name: 10x-cellranger-matrix-integration
description: Use when starting from a completed cellranger count run on 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample and you need pathogen UMI/gene counts appended into the 10x matrix files for Seurat/Scanpy downstream analysis.

name: 10x-chromium-single-cell-read-counting
description: Use when 10x Chromium scRNA-seq reads must be counted against competing reference annotations to measure how a modified GFF3 (e.g., extended 3' UTRs) changes per-cell genes and UMI metrics.

name: 10x-count-matrix-handling-with-dropletutils
description: Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics count matrices (raw gene-barcode matrices) from multiplexed samples must be read into R and called cells extracted before barcode-swapping or sample-sharing analyses.

name: 10x-genomics-barcode-whitelist-processing
description: Use when processing raw 10x Genomics v3 scRNA-seq FASTQ reads (e.g. Arabidopsis root sample GSM4626009 from GSE152766) with scKB/kallisto/bustools and a barcode whitelist is needed for barcode correction and counting.

name: 10x-genomics-output-format-handling
description: Use when input data comes from a 10x Genomics run consisting of one barcoded BAM plus a barcodes.tsv.gz from outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/, and per-cell BAM files are needed before downstream per-cell analysis.

name: 10x-genomics-read-structure-processing
description: Use when raw 10x Genomics Chromium (e.g., 10xv3) scRNA-seq FASTQs must be converted into gene-by-cell spliced/unspliced count matrices quickly, especially for Arabidopsis with a TAIR10-based index.

name: 21-nt-phasirna-prediction-configuration
description: Use when the goal is to predict 21-nt phasiRNAs and PHAS loci from sRNA-seq data mapped to cDNA (transcriptome) and/or gDNA (genome) references, e.g. rice SRR5049781 data against oryza_sativa_cdna.fa and oryza_sativa_gdna.fa.

name: 2c-like-cell-identification-zscan4c-tcstv3
description: Use when analyzing a murine embryonic two-cell stage single-cell RNA-Seq dataset where a 2C-like subpopulation must be defined and its differentially expressed transposable elements identified at locus level.

name: 2clc-population-marker-identification
description: Use when analyzing 10x mouse chemical reprogramming scRNA-seq to find a 2CLC population and its defining TE markers using locus-specific TE quantification with MATES.

name: 2d-embedding-stability-assessment
description: Decision support for judging whether a GraphDDP 2D embedding depends critically on the class-confidence bias - required before trusting layouts built from prior cluster labels.

name: 2d-location-regression-neural-network-training
description: Use when you have ST data with spot-level gene expression and true 2D coordinates and need to predict 2D locations of scRNA-seq cells or held-out test spots by supervised regression.

name: 2d-shape-clustering-reproducibility
description: Use when validating or reproducing the Forest Fire Clustering benchmarks on ring-shaped, half-moon-shaped, or circular Gaussian-mixture synthetic datasets, where GMM is expected to fail and FFC should achieve top purity.

name: 2d-vs-3d-projection-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify whether cell types or clusters mix less in a 3D embedding (UMAP/tSNE) than in its 2D counterpart, e.g. choosing projection dimensionality for scRNA-seq data.

name: 3d-expression-surface-visualization
description: Use when consecutive ST slices have already been 3D-aligned (e.g., by Scube) and the goal is to model, test, and render per-gene expression as continuous surfaces over the stacked 3D spot/cell coordinates (e.g., STARmap mouse brain).

name: 3d-projection-angle-flattening-analysis
description: Use when comparing whether 3D single-cell dimension-reduction projections (UMAP/tSNE) separate annotated cell types or clusters better than 2D, quantified by pairwise Shannon-entropy mixing or convex-hull area overlap across swept viewing angles.

name: 3d-slice-alignment-and-stacking
description: Use when you have multiple consecutive ST slices (e.g., 33 MERFISH mouse primary motor cortex slices, Stereo-seq mouse embryo slices) and need to construct a 3D stack by aligning slice coordinate systems.

name: 3d-tissue-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when consecutive 2D ST slices contain defects (rotation, flip, translation, cropping) and you need to reconstruct or evaluate a stacked 3D tissue architecture against a ground-truth reference.

name: 3utr-apa-dynamics-analysis
description: Use when analyzing polyA-captured scRNA-seq data (Sierra or scAPAtrap PACdataset) to detect and visualize 3'UTR shortening/lengthening dynamics across cell states or differentiation trajectories.

name: a-to-i-rna-editing-site-classification
description: Use when you have tabix-indexed REDItools outTables from RNAseq BAM files and need per-site A-to-I vs SNP classification of A-to-G substitutions, benchmarking against ground truth sets, or evaluating robustness to missing flanking RNAseq data.

name: abc-model-ablation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify, by ablation, how much AUPRC improvement each individual ABC-model variant (adapted activity -q True, all-TSS gene window -i all_tss) contributes over the regular ABC baseline on perturbation-validated enhancer–gene interaction data.

name: abc-score-scaling-of-enhancer-activity
description: Use when scoring enhancer–gene interactions from candidate regions and a chromatin contact map, and you want enhancer activity adapted by enhancer–gene contact counts (adapted ABC), rather than plain activity-by-contact.

name: ablation-study-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you need to isolate the contribution of one method component (here, the similarity-enhancement step of SSRE) by comparing a full pipeline against its ablated baseline on the same labeled benchmark datasets using NMI and ARI.

name: ablation-study-model-training
description: Use when a published model is built from multiple interacting components (e.g., ZINB autoencoder + graph convolution + contrastive learning) and you need to isolate each part's contribution to clustering/imputation performance by training and comparing ablation variants.

name: ablation-study-performance-comparison
description: Use when a multi-input deep learning model (e.g., sequence + structure) needs validation that each input branch adds value, by training matched single-input CNN ablations on the same encoded data and benchmark folds.

name: ablation-variant-comparison-lazy-teleporting
description: Use when you must isolate the performance contribution of a specific algorithmic component (e.g., lazy-teleporting MCMC in VIA) by comparing a full-method run to an ablated variant and baselines on time-series single-cell data with day labels.

name: absorbing-markov-chain-branch-probability-estimation
description: Use when a SingleCellExperiment or Milo pseudobulk object with a VDJ feature space and a diffusion map is available and you need branch probabilities into defined terminal states (e.g. CD4+T/CD8+T tips) plus diffusion pseudotime in R.

name: absorbing-markov-chain-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when pseudobulked VDJ feature-space data (e.g. pb.milo from vdjPseudobulk with a 20-component PCA) needs pseudotime and branch probabilities toward defined terminal states in R.

name: acat-omnibus-input-preparation
description: Use when OTTERS Stage II output from testing.py contains per-gene TWAS Z-scores for the five training models and they must be genomic-control adjusted before ACAT-O omnibus aggregation.

name: accessible-chromatin-sequence-extraction
description: Use when scATAC-seq peak data must be converted into gene-associated accessible promoter/enhancer sequences as the substrate for TF motif scanning in CellOracle base-GRN construction.

name: accession-resistance-allele-ranking
description: Use when genotype data (e.g., SoySNP50k VCF) for a germplasm collection must be scored against curated resistance SNP loci to rank accessions by resistance allele burden per pathogen.

name: accuracy-aggregation-and-reporting
description: Use when benchmarking cell type classifiers over repeated stratified train/test splits and you must average per-repeat accuracy into a mean accuracy table and verify a reported method ordering.

name: accuracy-at-k-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating a cell type annotation or classification method that outputs ranked scores over a controlled vocabulary (e.g., Cell Ontology terms), and you need top-k correctness (Accuracy@3/Accuracy@5) rather than only AUROC.

name: accuracy-f1-score-computation
description: Use when comparing cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq data with known ground-truth labels, and per-method accuracy and F1-score rankings must be produced and verified.

name: accuracy-macrof1-metric-computation
description: Use when a benchmark produces per-cell predicted cell-type labels that must be scored against ground-truth annotations to rank annotation tools by accuracy and MacroF1.

name: accuracy-plateau-analysis
description: Use when you have a ranked gene/feature list and need to decide how many top-ranked features maximize classifier accuracy before additional genes add no benefit.

name: acinar-ductal-transdifferentiation-reference-direction-construction
description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods (scKINETICS vs scVelo/VeloVAE/UniTVelo) against a pseudotime-derived transdifferentiation axis in high dimensions, e.g. acute pancreatitis scRNA-seq.

name: across-plate-uncertainty-aggregation
description: Use when a per-plate swapping-fraction estimate has been derived (gradient of swapped reads vs. reads available for swapping) and a single pooled fraction with an uncertainty must be reported for the experiment.

name: active-gene-threshold-filtering
description: Use when normalized RNA-Seq FPKM matrices (e.g. TCGA KIRC/LIHC/PRAD, protein-coding and lncRNA genes) must be reduced to actively expressed genes prior to building gene co-expression networks.

name: active-learning-benchmarking-single-cell-annotation
description: Use when a single-cell expression dataset has a marker file (author-provided, data-derived, or PanglaoDB top-20) and you need an informative initial 20-cell training set for an active learning annotation loop, benchmarked against random initialization.

name: active-learning-cell-selection-benchmarking
description: Use when building small labeled training sets (e.g., 100–500 cells) from single-cell expression data and deciding between active learning, adaptive reweighting, and random sampling for annotation model training.

name: active-learning-representative-selection
description: Use when bulk sequencing data cover a large cohort (e.g., the 124-sample COVID-19 dataset) and the budget permits single-cell sequencing of only a small subset, so representatives must be chosen to minimize inference difficulty Dsc.

name: active-learning-uncertainty-sampling
description: Use when annotating single-cell expression data with a limited labeling budget: you have ground-truth labels available on demand, a training classifier (e.

name: active-subnetwork-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing subnetwork detection methods on simulated case/control expression data with known planted perturbed modules, so precision, recall, and F1 against the ground truth can be computed per replicate.

name: active-subnetwork-jaccard-similarity-comparison
description: Use when several active subnetworks are recovered from the same seed genes or gene P-values (e.g., on COVID-19 benchmark data) and you need to quantify node-set overlap between methods via pairwise Jaccard similarity.

name: activity-assay-combination-design
description: Use when deciding which chromatin-assay combination to feed as enhancer activity into ABC scoring, e.g. if only ATAC-seq (no DNase-seq + H3K27ac ChIP-seq pair) is available for the cell type of interest.

name: activity-regulated-gene-velocity-restriction
description: Use when pseudotime from velocity data must be validated against an externally measured elapsed process time (e.g., stimulation duration 0–120 min in scNT-seq neurons) and velocity should be estimated only on genes regulated by the perturbation.

name: acyclicity-verification-of-directed-graphs
description: Use when a kNN cell graph has been edge-oriented by pseudotime (e.g., DPT rooted at a given iroot) and the N×N adjacency matrix must be confirmed acyclic before Granger causal inference on cell states.

name: adapted-abc-activity-scaling
description: Use when scoring enhancer–gene interactions from activity assays (DNase-seq, H3K27ac/ATAC-seq) plus contact data and you want higher AUPRC than the regular ABC score, or when validating whether a single activity assay suffices.

name: adapted-abc-gabc-score-configuration
description: Use when scoring enhancer-gene interactions with STARE and you want the adapted (generalised gABC) variant instead of the regular ABC score — e.g., comparing gABC vs ABC recall against eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs.

name: adaptive-attractor-co-expression-scanning
description: Use when starting from a normalized, log-transformed single-cell expression matrix and you need unsupervised, seed-gene-driven co-expression signatures (ranked gene lists) to drive feature selection for clustering, as in CASCC.

name: adaptive-bandwidth-inverse-distance-kernel-construction
description: Use when building affinity/transition matrices for diffusion maps or geometry-preserving losses in a TensorFlow GAN pipeline, and gradients must flow through the kernel without saturating.

name: adaptive-bandwidth-kernel-tuning
description: Use when building cell-to-cell affinity matrices from raw or log-normalized scRNAseq count matrices in full dimensionality, and kernel bandwidths must adapt to local density via k-NN scaling rather than fixed global scales.

name: adaptive-binning-discretization-of-expression-data
description: Use when a raw or normalized time-series RNA-Seq count table (e.g. DREAM 4 In Silico, ~21 samples, 100 genes) must be binned into a limited number of states to make pairwise mutual-information GRN inference tractable.

name: adaptive-cluster-merging
description: Use when running scAce (or benchmarking against it) on scRNA-seq count data and the number of clusters is unknown: after VAE pre-training and cluster initialization, this criterion decides which Leiden-derived or split-derived clusters to merge and when to stop.

name: adaptive-kernel-bandwidth-estimation
description: Use when a sample-by-feature single-cell matrix (e.g., PBMC zheng17-preprocessed data, first 30 principal components) must be converted into a KNN-based affinity graph to feed label-propagation clustering, and a full pairwise L2 distance matrix would be computationally expensive (>1 million points).

name: adaptive-lasso-logistic-regression
description: Use when a binary outcome (e.g., invasive vs non-invasive bladder cancer subtype) must be regressed on thousands of molecular variables (e.g., ~8,024 mRNA Z-score entries) where ordinary logistic regression fails and variable selection with correct p-values is needed.

name: adaptive-reweighting-cluster-based-cell-selection
description: Use when a scRNA-seq or CyTOF training set is imbalanced (e.g. 450 vs 50 cells or 400 vs 25 per minority type) and you need a cell-selection baseline to rebalance it against active learning or random selection.

name: adaptive-reweighting-labeling-strategy
description: Use when a small labeled training set must be constructed from an imbalanced single-cell expression matrix (e.g., snRNA-Seq PDAC SCP1089) and rare cell types should be captured for annotation.

name: adaptive-uncertainty-threshold-estimation
description: Use when bimodality testing (bimodality coefficient, Hartigan's dip test) has confirmed novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data and a non-manual, data-driven cutoff is needed to separate known from unknown cells.

name: adipocyte-differentiation-biology
description: Use when the analysis goal is differential gene expression of genetically or pharmacologically perturbed MDI-induced 3T3-L1 adipocytes — e.g. Pparg knockdown vs control — or gene set enrichment over differentiation time points.

name: adipocyte-differentiation-gene-signature-interpretation
description: Use when a curated 3T3-L1 adipocyte dataset (e.g. from curatedAdipoArray) has differential-expression results available and the goal is to identify enriched GO terms among genes ranked by fold-change rather than test a single gene list.

name: adipocyte-differentiation-stage-annotation
description: Use when working with MDI-induced 3T3-L1 microarray samples from multiple GEO series whose raw study-specific metadata use inconsistent vocabulary, and you need comparable stage-of-differentiation labels before PCA, batch correction, or differential expression.

name: adipocyte-subpopulation-composition-analysis
description: Use when a cell-by-cell type annotation table (e.g., WATLAS/SCP2289 labels) must be converted to per-donor cell type fractions and tested for obesity, depot, or sex effects via covariate-adjusted linear models.

name: adipose-snrna-seq-expressionset-conversion
description: Use when starting a Bisque decomposition or bias-simulation task with adipose snRNA-seq counts plus bulk RNA-seq samples, and the inputs must be packaged as ExpressionSet objects with sample-to-individual and cell-type labels.

name: adjacency-list-construction
description: Use when a custom PPIN adjacency list is needed for a biological process or user-supplied gene set for ORIGINS2 activity() scoring, and only a gene ID list is available from which to subset the full_human_ppin edge list.

name: adjacency-list-network-export
description: Use when you need to derive a transcription factor co-expression network from a cell group selected during a CellexalVR VR session and export it as an adjacency list the in-session TF network generator can consume.

name: adjacency-matrix-network-export
description: Use when a mutual-information-inferred GRN needs to be refined with curated database interactions and persisted as an adjacency-matrix .csv (final_grn.csv) before downstream Boolean Network conversion.

name: adjacency-matrix-processing
description: Use when you have edge-weighted adjacency matrices of gene co-expression networks (e.g., built from TCGA expression with Euclidean distance or Pearson correlation) and need to prune them to a backbone before network fusion or community extraction.

name: adjacency-matrix-verification-at-alpha-extremes
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing the ClonoCluster α/β edge-weight combination and you need to prove the integration is anchored correctly before clustering at intermediate α values.

name: adjusted-mutual-information-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing clustering solutions (e.g., eeSNV- vs gene-expression-derived partitions of single cells) against known subpopulation labels and you need a chance-corrected agreement score over multiple bootstrap runs.

name: adjusted-pvalue-significance-filtering
description: Use when a pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value table (CSV with gene-name column, per-comparison padj columns) must be filtered by significance and fold-change cut-offs to identify extreme gene entries across pairwise conditions.

name: adjusted-pvalue-significance-quadrant-classification
description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values (per gene) must be partitioned into significant extreme/moderate up- or down-regulated quadrants across pairwise treatment-vs-control comparisons.

name: adjusted-rand-index-and-nmi-computation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has ground-truth cluster labels (e.g. a simulated pancreas dataset with 7 true clusters) and you must score predicted cluster assignments against them, as in the SCISSORS comparison workflow.

name: adjusted-rand-index-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics clustering method has produced per-spot domain labels and a manual layer/tumor annotation (e.g., DLPFC layers, tumor/non-tumor) is available as ground truth for ARI-based benchmarking.

name: adjusted-rand-index-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking clustering strategies on simulated scRNA-seq data with known ground-truth population labels, e.g. SymSim UMI datasets varying Sigma, alpha, depth, and rare-population proportion.

name: adjusted-rand-index-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a predicted scRNA-seq clustering against known cell-type labels to quantify accuracy — e.g., benchmarking DESC, scVI, or other methods on datasets with reference annotations like the GSE115746 macaque retina bipolar-cell data.

name: adjusted-rand-index-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing clustering accuracy of multiple single-cell methods on scRNA-seq datasets with known cell-type labels, and per-dataset ARI averages are needed to rank methods.

name: adjusted-rand-index-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression data with ground-truth cell-type labels and need a chance-corrected metric to compare clustering quality across imputation methods or against raw data.

name: adjusted-rand-index-cluster-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction or clustering methods on scRNAseq data that have published ground-truth cell-type annotations, and you need a single reproducible metric (ARI) to rank cluster recovery across datasets.

name: adjusted-rand-index-cluster-validation
description: Use when assessing whether repeated runs of an unsupervised clustering method (e.g., RCC with ConsensusClusterPlus/k-means base) yield consistent cluster counts and concordant assignments on bulk or single-cell expression matrices.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-accuracy-computation
description: Use when benchmarking clustering or spatial-domain methods against simulations that retain ground-truth cell labels, and you need a chance-corrected agreement score (ARI) per method per dataset, e.g. to reproduce the scSpace Fig. 1d-e comparison.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a task requires quantifying how well K-means clusters of imputed (or unimputed) log-transformed scRNA-seq expression matrices agree with known cell-type annotations via Adjusted Rand Index.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-agreement
description: Use when comparing multiple clustering methods' assignments against ground-truth cell-type labels on single-cell RNA-seq data, and per-dataset ARI values must be assembled into a benchmark table (e.g. CASCC vs. baselines, SIMLR excluded).

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-comparison
description: Use when comparing cell-type label predictions from multiple reference-mapping or clustering methods against manually curated ground-truth annotations, and you need per-cell-type accuracy plus ARI summary metrics to build a comparison table.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when multiple cell-type annotation labelings of the same cells (e.g., scanpy Ingest transfer vs Leiden variants) must be scored against expert annotations to rank methods on a single dataset.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing unsupervised clusterings (e.g., Louvain on 50 PCs from different gene sets) against known reference labels (cortical layer annotations) to quantify recovery, such as benchmarking SVG-based vs. HVG-based feature selection on Visium DLPFC.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when clustering or community-detection predictions must be scored against known true labels (e.g. z_mus_dynamic_true from simulate_mus_dynamic_dcbm) across multiple subjects and time points.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating the quality of cell-type clustering results on scRNA-seq data against known cell labels, or when comparing clustering configurations (e.g., ablations, seeds, methods) via ARI.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing clusterings (e.g., Leiden community detection on a q-diffused, Gaussian, or scVI-derived graph) against expert manual annotations across cell subtypes or organ tissues, and you need an ARI-based accuracy metric for benchmarking.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq clustering or batch-effect correction outputs against known cell-type labels (e.g., FACS-sorted labels), especially when assembling an ARI/silhouette comparison table across methods.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when a cell-classification or clustering output (e.g. scID target labels) must be quantitatively compared against published cell labels on the same cells, and a chance-corrected agreement score like ARI is needed.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing predicted cluster memberships from multiple clustering methods or simulation replicates against known/approximated truth labels and you need a chance-corrected accuracy score (ARI) per method per dataset.

name: adjusted-rand-index-clustering-validation
description: Use when 2D cell embeddings (t-SNE or UMAP) have been generated at both original and scDEED-optimized hyperparameters and you must quantify whether optimized embeddings align 2D clusters with annotated cell types.

name: adjusted-rand-index-computation
description: Use when evaluating a cell annotation/clustering result against known ground-truth labels on scRNA-seq data, especially when comparing methods in Monte Carlo splits and needing a chance-adjusted agreement metric beyond raw accuracy.

name: adjusted-rand-index-computation
description: Use when comparing clustering methods on single-cell data where a ground-truth label vector exists (e.g., Splatter simulations with known cell types), and you need a chance-corrected agreement metric like ARI (often alongside purity) for downstream paired tests.

name: adjusted-rand-index-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a single-cell clustering method (e.g. scDHA) against simulated ground-truth cell-type labels from sc_mosim/MOSim and you need a chance-corrected agreement metric over per-cell label vectors.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when comparing corrected scRNAseq matrices from multiple confounder-removal methods (scPLS, RUV, LMM, PCA, scLVM) and you need a single clustering-accuracy number per method against known labels.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cluster assignments (e.g., from K-means, hierarchical, K-medoids, SC3, or Seurat on GEM vs CNDM) against known cell-type or tissue-origin labels and a single external-validity score is needed, such as reproducing ARI = 0.73 on Tabula Muris.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has ground-truth cell-type annotations and you need a scalar score comparing predicted cluster labels against them, or when benchmarking clustering methods (e.g., scAce vs DESC vs scDeepCluster) via mean ARI.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq or tabular embedding has been clustered (k-means, Leiden) and you need a label-based agreement score, such as comparing CCSF cMAP clustering against PCA or Leiden baselines on data with known ground-truth cell labels.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when comparing clustering assignments from single-cell RNA-seq methods against known cell-type labels, or aggregating ARI across repeated runs to benchmark a clustering method against alternatives.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when you need to score how well cluster structure in synthetic data matches a ground-truth reference clustering, e.g. after mapping synthetic cells onto original-data clusters in UMAP space across pilot sizes.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation or clustering across timepoints and you need an ARI comparison (as in supplementary Figure 11) alongside per-cell accuracy for CASi vs scmap, CHETAH, scPred.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation
description: Use when a clustering method's predicted cell labels must be scored against ground-truth cell type annotations on single-cell RNA-seq data, or when assembling a per-dataset, per-method clustering accuracy benchmark table.

name: adjusted-rand-index-evaluation-against-reference-labels
description: Use when benchmarking a single-cell clustering method against reference cell-type or tissue labels and you need a chance-corrected agreement score (ARI) to compare methods or quantify gains from high-confidence label filtering.

name: adjusted-rand-index-normalized-mutual-information-evaluation
description: Use when a set of scRNA-seq clustering methods (e.g., SC3, CIDR, monocle, pcaReduce, Rphenograph, Seurat, SHARP, SINCERA, RaceID, scEFSC) has been run on datasets with published cell-type labels and you need to quantify and compare clustering accuracy.

name: adjusted-rand-index-partition-comparison
description: Use when a clustering or differential-abundance method must be benchmarked against a baseline on data with ground-truth cell-state/condition labels, and partition agreement needs to be quantified with ARI plus chi-square statistics.

name: adjusted-vs-raw-logcounts-benchmarking
description: Use when you have both an integration-adjusted expression matrix and the raw logcounts matrix with cell-type labels and per-sample metadata (e.g. severity), and need to quantify whether integration improves sample-level prediction.

name: admm-optimization-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or independently verifying the row-sparse FPS estimation path of SuffPCR (Algorithm 1 with AIRLB plus Algorithm 2 elbow thresholding), or when implementing an ADMM solver for sparse PCA loading matrices whose sparsity must match the suffpcr package.

name: admm-optimization-solver-implementation
description: Use when you must estimate a sparse, signed, weighted regulatory matrix from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) moment data — a sample mean vector and covariance matrix — and need a NumPy-only solver for the covariance-restricted L1-regularized regression objective.

name: ads-recall-metric-computation
description: Use when you need to score and compare cross-species cell type matching outputs (e.g., human–mouse, human–marmoset, mouse–marmoset motor cortex) with per-cell-type ADS and recall metrics, as in the TACTiCS benchmark against SAMap and Seurat.

name: adt-ambient-background-normalization
description: Use when raw ADT/protein count matrices from droplet-based single cell assays (CITE-seq, TEA-seq, ASAP-seq) show ambient antibody noise that masks biologically meaningful populations — e.g., empty-droplet signal correlating with CLR-normalized protein values.

name: adt-background-threshold-positive-cell-calling
description: Use when a CITE-seq dataset contains ADT counts alongside gene expression and per-cell antibody positivity must be called rather than inferred only from clustering, e.g. surface-marker phenotyping on 10x/cellranger data.

name: adt-clr-normalization
description: Use when processing CITE-Seq, TEA-Seq, or Multiome protein (ADT) counts that must be scaled and clustered on their own terms before multimodal integration with scTriangulate.

name: adt-distance-sigmoid-filtering
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with a limited number of ADT features (<50) where the ADT modality disproportionately dominates the joint cell-cell distance and masks transcriptomic differences between subsets.

name: adt-fastq-sample-multiplexing-setup
description: Use when ADT FASTQs from cell-hashing CITE-seq libraries must be organized per sample and converted into a cells-by-hashtags UMI count matrix before sample demultiplexing.

name: adt-relative-abundance-log-ratio-transformation
description: Use when CITE-seq or REAP-seq ADT/protein count matrices must be converted to relative-abundance training targets for cTP-net, or whenever per-cell protein log-ratios (vs. geometric mean) are needed instead of raw barcode counts.

name: adversarial-batch-classifier-training
description: Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq batches whose embeddings show batch separation: per-cell batch labels are available and a VAE latent space must be made batch-invariant without erasing biological variation.

name: adversarial-component-ablation-analysis
description: Use when you need to determine whether each adversarial component of an adversarial-VAE integration method (discriminator, batch classifier) contributes to integration, and what each contributes.

name: adversarial-discriminator-training
description: Use when training scButterfly-B (or -T/-C) on paired single-cell multi-omics count matrices to align modality-specific VAE latent spaces via translator–discriminator adversarial optimization before cross-modality prediction.

name: adversarial-variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices (Scanpy AnnData) and you need batch-corrected latent embeddings, especially with skewed cell-type distributions, nested batch effects, many batches, or developmental trajectories that must be conserved.

name: age-dynamic-gene-scoring
description: Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq data spanning multiple organismal ages and need to identify, per cell type, genes whose expression changes with age to build cell-type-specific senescence signatures.

name: age-group-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when single-cell AnnData objects annotated with cell type and age are available and the goal is to compute, per cell type, the fraction of senescence-score-positive cells in young vs old age groups and rank which markers (e.g., CDKN2A, CCL4) are most age-dynamic.

name: age-stratified-cell-proportion-analysis
description: Use when scoring cells (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis tongue keratinocytes) with senescence hub signatures and you need to test whether the proportion of senescence-outlier cells increases with organismal age.

name: agglomerative-clustering-of-copy-number-profiles
description: Use when scDNA-seq cells have copy-number (CNA) profiles but no prior clone labels, and a clone partition is needed as input to RNA-to-clone mapping (e.g., MaCroDNA cell2clone_assignment) or when benchmarking clone definitions across clustering/transformation configurations.

name: aggregated-bloom-comb-tree-construction
description: Use when many sequence datasets (FASTA/FASTQ, gzip-compressed or not) must be indexed together so later queries can list which datasets share k-mers with a query sequence, especially when index construction time and disk footprint must stay low.

name: aggregated-gradient-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when a trained SpatialDDLS deconvolution model exists and the goal is model interpretation: ranking which genes drive predicted cell type proportions and visualizing top per-cell-type gradient markers as a heatmap.

name: aging-comparative-network-visualization
description: Use when comparing predicted ligand-receptor communication networks across two conditions or ages (e.g. young vs old tissue) from single-cell expression data and you need differential edge counts and a delta network plot.

name: agretopicity-score-computation
description: Use when you have ScanNeo2 variant_effects.tsv entries plus typed HLA allele lists (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and need to rank mutant-vs-wildtype MHC binding predictions into agretopicity-scored neoepitope tables.

name: alcs-biology-conservation-metric-implementation
description: Use when benchmarking cross-species integration strategies (e.g. LIGER, LIGER UINMF, fastMNN, SeuratV4, scANVI, scVI, Harmony, Scanorama, SAMap) and you need to quantify how much integration blurs distinct cell types, i.e. overcorrection, on integrated embeddings with ground-truth cell type labels.

name: algorithmic-complexity-benchmarking
description: Use when a paper asserts a time complexity (e.g., Augusta's O(mn²D²) for MI-based GRN inference from RNA-Seq count tables) and you must verify it empirically by timing scaled inputs and fitting runtime to the parameterized model.

name: aligner-consistency-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two aligner runs of scPathoQuant (-align bbmap vs -align bowtie2) have produced per-gene pathogen UMI outputs for the same samples and you need to quantify their per-gene count consistency.

name: alignment-distance-and-atc-score-aggregation
description: Use when you need to characterize how a trajectory-tree alignment method's accuracy metrics (e.g., normalized alignment distance, ATC score) degrade as a function of controlled input perturbation such as Gaussian noise.

name: alignment-quality-metric-computation-mmd-mse
description: Use when two domain mappings (e.g. scRNA-seq to spatial transcriptomics) have been generated by GAN-based aligners and you must judge whether target distributions match (MMD) and whether point-wise correspondence with inputs is preserved (MSE).

name: all-vs-all-protein-alignment
description: Use when pooled protein FASTA files from annotated genomes must be converted into a bitscore-weighted gene similarity network to drive graph-based gene family clustering (e.g., MCL) and downstream absence/presence matrices.

name: allele-frequency-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have vireoSNP clone labels and a set of MQuad ΔBIC-selected mtDNA variants and need to visually confirm clonal discrimination, e.g. reproducing Fig. 4c for MKN-45 scDNA-seq data.

name: allele-specific-cna-detection
description: Use when analyzing PTA-amplified high-coverage (>20x) scWGS BAMs with matched bulk WGS, to call small (200 kb–5 Mb) allele-specific CNAs that RDR-only callers miss and to obtain integer copy-number states per allele per cell.

name: allele-specific-cna-detection-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when the goal is to infer haplotype-aware CNA states or tumor subclones from single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g., 10x Genomics droplet or Smart-seq2 tumor samples), especially when copy-neutral LOH or low tumor purity challenges expression-only methods.

name: allele-specific-copy-number-inference
description: Use when analyzing high-coverage (>20x) PTA-amplified single-cell WGS data where small (100 kb–Mb scale) somatic CNAs must be called with allele-specific copy states, and paired bulk WGS is available for phasing.

name: allele-specific-copy-number-state-inference
description: Use when per-cell copy gain/loss/LOH states must be inferred from raw scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts (10x or Smart-seq2), especially for tumour subclone dissection or when benchmarking XClone against InferCNV/CopyKAT/CaSpER/Numbat with AUROC.

name: allele-specific-expression-detection
description: Use when multi-sample VCF files (GATK HaplotypeCaller output) from RNA-seq of heterozygous individuals are available and the goal is to identify which biallelic SNPs show statistically significant allele-specific expression per tissue.

name: allele-specific-expression-gene-set-compilation
description: Use when you have VADT sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt call sets for multiple tissues and need gene-level ASE sets, cross-tissue overlap percentages, or a high-ASE-score gene list for pathway analysis.

name: allele-specific-peptide-prioritization
description: Use when patient-specific HLA allele lists (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and per-variant-type variant_effects.tsv files are available and predicted neoantigens must be ranked per allele by MHC binding affinity.

name: allele-specific-read-counting
description: Use when scRNA-Seq reads from a polymorphic F1 cross (e.g. CAST×B6) must be converted into per-allele gene counts, and you must decide between unique-read counting and multi-read weighted allocation before allelic classification.

name: allele-specific-short-read-alignment
description: Use when scRNA-Seq reads from an F1 hybrid cross (e.g. CAST×B6) must be assigned to maternal/paternal alleles for allele-specific expression counting, and multi-mapping reads should be retained rather than discarded.

name: allele-umi-count-analysis
description: Use when allele-level UMI counts from single-cell 3' RNA-seq (Cell Ranger output, SNVs called with Freebayes) must be converted into per-cell genotype calls or two-genotype mixture inference, e.g. donor/host chimerism in transplant or mixing datasets.

name: allelic-bursting-independence-testing
description: Use when you have allele-specific single-cell count matrices and want to test per-gene whether maternal/paternal bursting events are independent (logOR ≈ 0), positively correlated, or anti-correlated, with FDR control.

name: allelic-count-matrix-generation-from-bam
description: Use when starting from cell-barcoded BAM/CRAM files from a scRNA-seq experiment (e.g., 10x Genomics) and you need allele-specific AD/DP matrices to feed haplotype-aware CNA callers such as XClone's BAF module.

name: allelic-differential-splicing-statistical-modeling
description: Use when merged per-allele inclusion and skipping counts (IJC/SJC for reference and alternative alleles across samples) are available and the goal is to call significant ASAS events at FDR ≤ 10% from replicate or population-scale RNA-seq data.

name: allelic-dropout-modeling-single-cell-wgs
description: Use when a single-cell WGS CNA analysis must pick a per-dataset bin size that balances CNA detection resolution against amplification noise, e.g. before binning PTA- or MDA-amplified scWGS with HiScanner.

name: allelic-expression-state-classification
description: Use when allelic read counts from single-cell RNA-Seq (e.g., CAST×B6 F1 embryos) need per-cell, per-gene P/B/M state calls, and random monoallelic bursts and sparse coverage make naive read-ratio thresholds unreliable.

name: allelic-heterogeneity-multi-component-colocalization
description: Use when multiple studies or tissues (e.g., eQTLGen and GTEx whole blood) have summary statistics or individual-level genotypes/phenotypes for the same locus and you need to test whether signals colocalize despite possible multiple causal alleles and LD.

name: allelic-proportion-partial-pooling
description: Use when single-cell allele-specific RNA-Seq read counts are too sparse (e.g. <10 unique reads per gene) for reliable per-cell allelic proportion estimates, and classification of P/B/M expression states is needed.

name: allelic-read-uniqueness-qc-filtering
description: Use when RNA-seq reads aligned to two haplotype-modified personal genomes must be allele-assigned: filter multi-mapping or between-genome discordant reads, then assign haplotypes by SNP majority voting before ASAS counting.

name: allen-brain-atlas-dataset-handling
description: Use when validating or benchmarking a cell-type annotation method on external harmonized snRNA-seq query datasets such as the Allen Brain Atlas 10x (76,533 nuclei) and Smart-seq (49,495 nuclei) sets.

name: allen-brain-atlas-ish-cross-validation
description: Use when a reference-free or reference-based deconvolution yields an unlabeled cell type whose spatial localization is plausible but whose identity needs independent validation via in situ hybridization gene expression patterns.

name: alpha-convex-hull-density-quantification
description: Use when evaluating 2D scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., MDS/UMAP/t-SNE of 2000/4000/10000 highly variable genes) for trajectory inference suitability by quantifying cell coverage area as the alpha-convex hull proportion of the minimum enclosing circle (GOF).

name: alpha-parameter-optimization-purity-modularity
description: Use when running cell-attribute aware community detection (EVA/ELVAR) on a cell-cell kNN graph and an alpha value weighting attribute similarity must be chosen from multiple candidate partitions.

name: alpha-parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when you need to choose a maximum α for ClonoCluster hybrid clustering such that cluster number remains comparable to standard transcriptome clustering while still showing significant reorganization.

name: alra-low-rank-imputation
description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Drop-seq) contains abundant false zeros and you need zero-preserving imputation, or when validating imputation against RNA FISH Gini-coefficient correlations.

name: alra-rank-parameter-selection
description: Use when running ALRA (or a similar low-rank scRNA-seq imputation) on a library/log-normalized expression matrix and an automatic, data-driven rank k must be chosen instead of hand-tuning.

name: alt-splicing-event-read-support-verification
description: Use when novel splice junctions (e.g. novel acceptor/donor events) were detected by a spliced aligner on unmapped reads and you must confirm that an alternative quantifier's refined counts use the identical supporting read set.

name: altanalyze-icgs2-gene-expression-clustering
description: Use when single-cell FASTQ/count data needs gene-expression-defined cell population annotations as one modality-specific clustering input to a mix-and-match integration, prior to NMF splicing subclustering or scTriangulate reconciliation.

name: alternating-dictionary-embedding-minimization
description: Use when factorizing paired multi-omics count matrices (e.g., 10X Multiome RNA/ATAC, CITE-seq ADT) into simplex-constrained dictionaries H(p) and a shared low-dimensional cell embedding W with entropic OT coupling.

name: alternative-polyadenylation-gene-classification
description: Use when you have scUTRquant 3'UTR isoform count matrices (*.txs.Rds / *.genes.Rds) from 10x 3'-end scRNA-seq data and need to label genes as multi-UTR or IPA and tabulate per-category gene counts.

name: alternative-polyadenylation-isoform-comparison
description: Use when paired-end RNA-Seq from two or more conditions is available and the goal is to detect proximal APA transcripts (shifted/shortened 3' ends) induced by a perturbation, such as knockdown of a polyadenylation factor like CFIm25.

name: alternative-polyadenylation-transcript-annotation
description: Use when RNA-Seq alignments and a reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) are available and you need to identify expressed polyA sites or refine 3'-terminal exons without 3'-end sequencing data.

name: alternative-splicing-event-comparison
description: Use when CircAST_result.txt full-length circRNA assemblies exist for an RNase R-treated RNA-seq dataset and you need to count transcripts whose AS events differ from linear cognates or identify novel AS events.

name: alternative-splicing-event-identification-from-junction-reads
description: Use when starting from single-cell SMART-seq BAM or junction (SJ.out.tab) files and you need de novo alternative-splicing events and a per-cell AS probability matrix without relying on transcriptome annotation.

name: alternative-splicing-phasirna-isoform-interpretation
description: Use when an sRNA-seq analysis needs to distinguish PHAS loci predicted on transcript isoforms versus genomic sequence, e.g. to detect isoform-specific phasiRNA loss caused by alternative splicing or intron clipping.

name: alternative-splicing-vcf-conversion
description: Use when RNA-seq alignments are available and the neoantigen-prediction goal requires capturing alternative-splicing-derived variants (beyond SNV/indel calling), i.e., when the altsplicing module's activate flag is set in config/config.yml.

name: alzheimer-disease-pathway-interpretation
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq imputation methods on a disease dataset and you need biological evidence that one imputed matrix preserves or clarifies disease-relevant DEG patterns and KEGG pathways.

name: alzheimer-disease-scrnaseq-analysis
description: Use when analyzing two-group (case vs control) single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., late-stage AD vs healthy human brain — to infer differential cell-cell communication networks and rank the most active communicating cell types.

name: alzheimer-scrnaseq-dataset-analysis
description: Use when the task is to identify disease-specific (e.g., Alzheimer's vs normal) biomarkers from brain-region scRNA-seq datasets with scaLR's DNN-based pipeline and validate top-ranked genes against known neurological-disorder marker sets.

name: alzheimers-model-network-conservation-analysis
description: Use when two (or more) independently constructed co-expression networks exist — e.g. 5xFAD vs 3xTg-AD module-assignment tables — and the goal is to flag module pairs with significant gene overlap indicating conserved co-expression.

name: ambient-antibody-noise-quantification-from-empty-droplets
description: Use when you have raw ADT/UMI count matrices from both empty droplets and cell-containing droplets (e.g. raw vs filtered Cell Ranger output from a CITE-seq run) and need to characterize or validate ambient, unbound antibody background per protein.

name: ambient-background-noise-standardization-citeseq-protein-counts
description: Use when normalizing raw ADT/protein UMI matrices from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq droplet experiments where ambient unbound antibody noise and per-cell technical noise must be removed before clustering.

name: ambient-grna-noise-separation
description: Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in a single-cell CRISPR screen where ambient (extracellular) gRNA UMIs must be distinguished from endogenous in-cell expression before calling singlets vs multiplets, and per-guide thresholds are preferable to a fixed UMI cutoff.

name: ambient-noise-correction-citeseq
description: Use when raw ADT/protein UMI counts from droplet-based single cell assays (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) show substantial background noise from unbound antibodies and per-cell technical variation, and you need denoised, normalized protein values for downstream clustering or multimodal analysis.

name: ambient-noise-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing ADT normalization strategies (CLR vs dsb) for residual ambient antibody noise, or when assessing whether a protein cluster's normalized values track empty-droplet background levels.

name: ambient-rna-debris-filtering
description: Use when filtering a raw 10X droplet count matrix (feature-barcode MTX) for ambient RNA/debris contamination, especially snRNA-seq from frozen tissue, or when comparing DIEM vs EmptyDrops kept-droplet sets using MT% and MALAT1% metrics.

name: ambient-rna-fdr-threshold-testing
description: Use when 10x Genomics droplet UMI count matrices (e.g., parsed from molecule information files of HiSeq 4000-sequenced libraries) must be separated into real cells versus empty droplets at a specified FDR.

name: ambiguous-cell-removal
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., a list of per-donor gene-by-cell count matrices) must be turned into marker-labeled approximated ground-truth cell identities for adjusted-Rand-index clustering benchmarks.

name: ambiguous-date-term-disambiguation-marchf-mtarc
description: Use when an Excel-processed gene list contains date-converted symbols Mar-01 or Mar-02 that cannot be uniquely mapped to a single HGNC gene, and MTARC vs MARCHF assignment must be resolved from context.

name: ambiguous-mar01-mar02-date-term-disambiguation
description: Use when a .csv or .xlsx gene expression file contains date-converted entries Mar-01 or Mar-02 (including duplicate Mar-01/Mar-02 values), which cannot be auto-converted because they map to two candidate genes each.

name: aml-malignant-cell-annotation
description: Use when a cancer (e.g. AML) 10x scRNA-seq sample needs cell-type annotation plus a malignant vs non-malignant call, and bulk SNVs/CNVs must be linked back to individual cell barcodes and clusters.

name: aml-patient-immunophenotype-stratification
description: Use when AML (or other hematopoietic) scRNA-seq count matrices need imputed surface protein levels to assign malignant cells to myeloid differentiation stages or to flag aberrant immunophenotype clusters such as hyper-CD38.

name: aml-progenitor-single-cell-preprocessing
description: Use when scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., AML CD34+ aligned with Cell Ranger to hg19) must be split into expression-defined populations plus splice-junction PSI subclusters, and decision-level integration is needed to expose splicing-defined disease subtypes.

name: amq-index-sequence-querying
description: Use when you have batches of query sequences (e.g., human RefSeq transcripts in FASTA) and a prebuilt AMQ index over thousands of datasets, and you need to list candidate datasets per query while profiling query runtime, CPU usage, and memory footprint.

name: anchor-based-integration-execution
description: Use when integrating multi-sample or multi-study scRNA-seq data in Seurat where batch correction must preserve cell type structure, especially when partial cell type labels (e.g., scGate CD8_TIL gates) are available to guide anchor finding.

name: anchor-cell-identification-in-scrnaseq-partitions
description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets affected by batch effects and you need a parsimonious set of representative anchor cells per dataset before building a weighted bipartite graph for one-to-one matching.

name: anchor-score-weighting-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or validating how STACAS weights integration anchors during batch effect correction, or when you need to reproduce the sample guide tree that determines the order of multi-dataset Seurat integration.

name: anchored-targeted-read-alignment
description: Use when searching for fusions involving one known driver gene (e.g., BCR-ABL1, NSD2-IGH) in paired-end bulk or single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Smart-seq2) where de novo tools miss multi-mapping/homologous or shallow-depth reads.

name: angiogenesis-high-population-identification
description: Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Seurat object or counts matrix from csv/rds/h5/10X) for a pathway signature like angiogenesis to flag which TME cell subpopulations are pathway-high.

name: anglecbs-projection-filtering
description: Use when unrolling rolled intestinal tissue imaging data in IntestLine and misprojected points appear in the stretched output after backbone-based projection; the angleCBS parameter is the tool's dedicated control for removing them.

name: angular-distance-embedding-analysis
description: Use when you have a trained mvTCR joint model with specificity annotations and need to quantify each cell's or epitope group's TCR contribution to the shared embedding, or to test whether that contribution tracks TCR sequence similarity.

name: ann-data-gene-alignment-across-datasets
description: Use when a query AnnData with different or unordered var_names must be passed to TOSICA.pre() alongside a trained reference model, since the reference and query gene sets must match exactly.

name: annadata-expression-matrix-subsetting
description: Use when a query .h5ad dataset has a different gene set or gene count than the features a SIMS/TabNet reference model was trained on, and label-transfer prediction fails or would fail on feature mismatch.

name: annadata-h5ad-prediction-export
description: Use when a scDEAL single-cell prediction run (e.g. scmodel.py on GSE110894) has finished and the per-cell drug response predictions must be persisted and shared as an AnnData object for evaluation or visualization.

name: annadata-metadata-annotation
description: Use when preparing single-cell RNA-, ATAC-, or CITE-seq studies as .h5ad files for Cellenium import, and study-level metadata must be ontologized so studies can be semantically found and organized across the app.

name: annadata-object-manipulation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq analysis pipeline requires an AnnData object preprocessed via the scanpy standard workflow with log-cpm normalisation and high-resolution Leiden cluster labels as input to downstream tools.

name: annadata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets must be loaded, annotated with batch/cell-type labels, or passed between methods (e.g. scETM, scVI, transfer learning) as cells-by-genes AnnData objects with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' obs columns.

name: annadata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when multiplexed imaging data preprocessed with MCMICRO into a single-cell marker-intensity table (per cell × antibody channel) must be held in AnnData for SpatialCells gating, MPI scoring, or region-based TME measurement.

name: anndata-backed-mode-query-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing between AnnData backed-mode h5ad access and on-disk AnnSQL/DuckDB when filtering or querying large single-cell matrix datasets, especially when datasets exceed available memory.

name: anndata-backed-mode-subsetting
description: Use when a .h5ad dataset is larger than memory and you need boolean-mask cell/gene subsetting in AnnData backed mode, or when benchmarking that baseline against AnnSQL on-disk SQL filters.

name: anndata-backed-vs-ondisk-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking AnnSQL against AnnData on simulated single-cell data, or when testing whether runtime conclusions transfer from randomly generated matrices to sparser Splatter-simulated UMI-count datasets of the same shapes.

name: anndata-cell-metadata-handling
description: Use when the input is a single-cell dataset in AnnData/.h5ad format and a downstream tool needs per-cell metadata columns (samples_col, clusters_col, conds_col) extracted or validated before proportion analysis.

name: anndata-count-matrix-loading
description: Use when starting an XClone run and you need the RDR read-depth matrix, the BAF AD/DP allelic matrices, and genome-mode feature annotation assembled into AnnData objects before run_RDR/run_BAF.

name: anndata-expression-matrix-loading
description: Use when a scRNA-seq study is available as an AnnData/H5AD file (e.g. the blood_covid demo) and the cells x genes expression matrix must be restructured into a gene-centric sparse form for PostgreSQL-backed aggregation by cell type.

name: anndata-expression-matrix-manipulation
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be read, subset, smoothed, or scored within the scverse ecosystem — e.g. loading an h5ad or pbmc3k_processed() object, computing per-cell gene set scores that land in adata.obsm, or extracting activities with dc.get_acts.

name: anndata-h5ad-data-handling
description: Use when loading, formatting, or saving single-cell RNA/ATAC data as AnnData .h5ad files to feed scBridge or read back its Prediction and Reliability outputs.

name: anndata-h5ad-data-handling
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data arrives as an .h5ad file and must be loaded with Scanpy into an AnnData object before gene set scoring (e.g. gssnng score_method on a phagocyte scRNA-seq object with LPS-treated and untreated cells).

name: anndata-h5ad-io
description: Use when the input scRNA-seq count matrix is stored as an h5ad-formatted HDF5 file (or must be persisted as one) before denoising, normalization, or downstream Scanpy/DCA processing.

name: anndata-h5ad-object-handling
description: Use when building or persisting a single-cell count matrix (e.g. 10x PBMC 3k counts or Splatter-simulated 10000 genes x 3000 cells) as an AnnData object for downstream scanpy/Cytocipher analysis, or when writing/reading .h5ad files.

name: anndata-h5ad-result-handling
description: Use when a scDEAL run (bulkmodel.py/scmodel.py) must produce, load, or validate its single-cell output as a scanpy-readable .h5ad AnnData file under save/adata, or when downstream notebooks need cell-level sens_label predictions.

name: anndata-layer-table-querying
description: Use when an AnnData object (e.g. pbmc3k or pbmc68k_reduced .h5ad) has been converted to an on-disk or in-memory AnnSQL/DuckDB database and results must be retrieved with SQL, with output as pandas, AnnData, or Parquet.

name: anndata-log-cpm-normalised-data-handling
description: Use when loading a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. .h5ad AnnData) in scanpy/Jupyter before running Cytocipher, and you must confirm the matrix is log-cpm normalised and carries tentative Leiden cluster labels, preferably at high resolution.

name: anndata-metadata-handling-sample-cluster-condition
description: Use when an .h5ad/AnnData single-cell dataset must be passed to scanpro() and the per-cell metadata columns identifying replicate samples, clusters, and condition labels need to be specified or verified first.

name: anndata-object-handling
description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data with scBridge and you need to prepare, subset, or extract results from h5ad AnnData objects (cell types in obs, embeddings in obsm).

name: anndata-object-manipulation
description: Use when building or running a STREAM workflow (trajectory reconstruction or mapping of new cells onto a fixed reference graph) whose inputs must be represented as anndata objects holding count matrices and per-cell metadata.

name: anndata-object-processing
description: Use when the analysis input is or should be a Scanpy AnnData object (e.g. scanpyobj.h5ad) that must be loaded, sub-clustered, or transformed (log2 fold change vs. average expression) to feed CaDRReS-Sc or PRISM drug response prediction.

name: anndata-omics-matrix-loading
description: Use when the input is a raw protein-by-condition abundance matrix in TSV or CSV from scRNA-seq (Human Protein Atlas) or proteomics (PRIDE) data and it must be ingested into a scverse-compatible workflow for VAE-based network inference.

name: anndata-registry-handling
description: Use when training or applying TOSICA on scanpy AnnData objects: a reference AnnData must be paired with a query AnnData whose var_names (genes) match in identity and order, and model artifacts must be written to and read from a project folder.

name: anndata-scrnaseq-data-handling
description: Use when loading scRNA-seq count data (e.g. .h5ad files) into AnnData objects for model-based integration, or when batch and cell type information must be exposed in specific adata.obs columns for tools like scETM.

name: anndata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (qPCR, scRNA-seq, or scATAC-seq matrix plus optional graph/pseudotime) must be wrapped in a cells × features AnnData object before running STREAM or a stream-plot reconstruction.

name: anndata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq or scATAC data must be represented as an AnnData object with sample, cluster, and condition metadata columns before running proportion analysis or downstream Scanpy-based tools.

name: anndata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when an RNA velocity trajectory analysis must load, validate, and pass scvelo-processed AnnData (spliced/unspliced counts, velocity field) into Cytopath's Markov-chain simulation or between its workflow stages.

name: anndata-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when an analysis pipeline (e.g. gssnng score_cells.with_gene_sets) requires a Scanpy AnnData object stored as an h5ad file, with expression values in adata.X and cell group labels in adata.obs.

name: anndata-single-cell-marker-gating
description: Use when you have per-cell marker intensity tables from multiplexed imaging (e.g., MCMICRO output for the MEL1 CyCIF sample) and need to define marker-positive populations (SOX10+ tumor cells, Ki67+ proliferating cells, MITF-high state) before computing region-level composition metrics.

name: anndata-sparse-to-dense-conversion
description: Use when a scanpy-read .h5ad file (e.g. CITEseq.h5ad) returns a sparse matrix in adata.X and a downstream model such as MarkerMap's VAE expects a dense numpy array.

name: anndata-spatial-transcriptomics-data-handling
description: Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10X Visium spots) and a single-cell reference must be loaded into anndata format before deconvolution or multi-slice spatial domain analysis.

name: anndata-to-duckdb-database-conversion
description: Use when a single-cell AnnData/h5ad dataset is too large for memory (e.g. millions of cells) and SQL-based querying, filtering, or aggregation is needed instead of AnnData-backed-mode operations that fail or run ~700x slower.

name: annealed-langevin-dynamics-posterior-sampling
description: Use when decomposing aggregated spot-level ST expression (e.g. Visium/Slide-seq spots with multiple cells) into per-cell gene expressions given a scRNA-seq reference and a trained conditional score model.

name: annotated-splice-site-recombination-fragment-enumeration
description: Use when building an alignment-free splicing quantification pipeline that must first guess novel transcript fragments from a GTF annotation's splice sites, before pseudoaligning reads with kallisto.

name: annotation-accuracy-ari-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell annotation methods on scRNA-seq data with known reference labels — e.g. difficult PBMC splits with p = 10/20/50/80% training proportions or ASD vs control cross-condition directions — to rank methods by accuracy and ARI.

name: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how robust an automated cell-type annotation method is to dropout events, by benchmarking accuracy against known labels on simulated scRNA-seq data at graded dropout levels.

name: annotation-accuracy-benchmarking-against-original-labels
description: Use when validating an automated cell-annotation model on held-out, independently published cancer scRNA-seq datasets that carry original labeled cell information (e.g., MCC 11,024 cells, CRC 11,717 myeloid cells, LC 45,555 T cells) so predicted labels can be scored against expert ground truth.

name: annotation-accuracy-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when you have annotation accuracies (overall and per-cell-type) from multiple subsampling methods across sketch fractions 0.02–0.10 and need side-by-side boxplots showing accuracy vs. fraction per dataset-model pair.

name: annotation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantitatively evaluate how well automated cell-type annotation (reference-based or marker-based) reproduces manual cell-type assignments in plant single-cell datasets, especially across species.

name: annotation-accuracy-evaluation-against-predefined-labels
description: Use when a new or existing cell type annotation method must be benchmarked for accuracy against predefined labels on scRNA-seq datasets, e.g. reproducing deCS vs. SingleR/CHETAH/scPred/SciBet/Cell BLAST comparisons.

name: annotation-accuracy-metrics-computation
description: Use when CellGEP/cellgep has assigned marker-GEP labels to single cells and you must quantify how faithfully those assignments match original cell-type or clustering labels.

name: annotation-accuracy-quantification
description: Use when you need to measure whether a cell type annotation method (e.g., SingleR) is limited by its default reference databases, by re-running it with an alternative reference such as CellMatch and comparing consistency with benchmark labels.

name: annotation-based-cluster-composition-comparison
description: Use when comparing cluster purity before and after a decomposition/merging step: you have cell type annotations for each cell and two clusterings of the same cells, and need to know if rare types become more dominant within their clusters.

name: annotation-consistency-quantification
description: Use when you need to validate an automatic cluster annotation tool by computing the fraction of clusters whose predicted cell types match published manual annotations across one or more scRNA-seq datasets.

name: annotation-granularity-prediction-scoring
description: Use when evaluating whether a cell type classifier's predictions are acceptable at coarser annotation granularity, e.g. reproducing Supp. Fig. 7a of scTab on the donor hold-out test split.

name: annotation-label-similarity-assessment
description: Use when an automated annotation output (Census celltype predictions) must be quantitatively compared to curated expert cell-type labels to reproduce benchmark metrics like balanced accuracy 0.8 and label similarity 0.89.

name: annotation-overlap-validation
description: Use when automated region/community annotations (e.g. germinal centers from getCommunities/getBoundary) must be checked against an existing manual annotation to confirm boundaries and label agreement.

name: annotation-resource-gene-mapping
description: Use when you need to test whether CCC resources (Ramilowski, ConnectomeDB, OmniPath, Cellinker, etc.) are biased toward specific pathways or tissue-enriched proteins by enriching resource genes against annotation sets.

name: annotation-result-table-export
description: Use when a deCS.correlation or deCS.fisher annotation run has produced a result data frame and you need a machine-readable, tab-delimited annotation table (e.g. hipsc_decs_result.txt) with row-count and label checks.

name: annotation-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantify how robust an scRNA-seq cell-type annotation method is to marker-gene-set noise, by systematically degrading marker sets and comparing resulting annotations against ground-truth cell-type labels.

name: annotation-table-formatting-for-cci-inference
description: Use when a clustered single-cell count matrix needs cell-type labels before running scCrossTalk's find_lrpairs and downstream communication inference, and the labels must be formatted for create_scCrossTalk.

name: annotation-throughput-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation methods and you need quantitative runtime/throughput (cells/min) on held-out datasets with known cell counts, alongside predictive metrics like F1 and balanced accuracy.

name: annotation-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell type annotation methods on single-cell or spatial omics data that has a ground-truth annotation, e.g. a MERFISH mouse brain section with CCF-mapped labels.

name: annotation-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when a study claims a cell-annotation tool's ity and the claim must be reproduced on the same query datasets (e.g. Allen Brain Atlas snRNA-seq, T2D/NSCLC/AD disease data) with ranked accuracy/MacroF1 metrics.

name: annotation-tool-parameter-configuration
description: Use when reproducing the scRNA-seq annotation benchmark of Accordion vs marker-based tools, or when replicating its exact tool settings (e.g. max_n_marker = 30, SCINA 100-marker cap, 4 threads).

name: annoy-knn-triplet-sampling
description: Use when implementing or reproducing ivis-style siamese triplet training and you need positives drawn from each point's KNN vector and negatives from outside it, via approximate KNN search (AnnoyKnnMatrix).

name: annsql-on-disk-database-construction-from-anndata
description: Use when an .h5ad single-cell dataset is too large for memory and AnnData backed-mode reads are slow — e.g. filtering or aggregate queries on hundreds of thousands of cells — and persistent, SQL-queryable storage is needed.

name: annsql-vs-anndata-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or adapting the AnnSQL runtime benchmark: comparing in-memory AnnSQL vs in-memory AnnData query runtimes across simulated dataset sizes with a 45,000-cell crossover expectation.

name: anorexia-treatment-outcome-analysis
description: Use when a treatment-outcome dataset (e.g., anorexia patients with treatment group, pre-weight, and post-weight) needs subgroup identification via a DIPM tree with a categorical response and mixed covariate types.

name: anova-differential-expression-testing-across-time-points
description: Use when scRNA-seq data span ordered time points of a differentiation process (e.g., primary human myoblast GSE52529 at 0/24/48/72 h) and a gene set is needed to drive multi-branching trajectory reconstruction.

name: anova-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing a continuous performance score (e.g., sub-network detection sensitivity on simulated RNA-seq data) across three or more competing methods or simulation conditions and you need an omnibus test of mean differences.

name: anova-statistical-modeling
description: Use when you have binary driver-alteration calls (amplification or mutation) per sample plus continuous pathway activity scores and need to test which alterations activate which pathways.

name: anti-correlated-bp-group-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have ORIGINS2 PPIN activities for several biological processes and you need to test whether BPs cluster into distinct, potentially anti-correlated groups within a sample.

name: antigen-specificity-prediction-from-tcr-embeddings
description: Use when single-cell data has paired transcriptome and TCR sequences plus pMHC (e.g. SARS-CoV-2) specificity annotation and the goal is to predict or benchmark antigen specificity from cell-level embeddings.

name: apa-dynamics-gradient-overlay-plotting
description: Use when a PACdataset of single-cell poly(A) site counts (e.g., scPACds with SC/RS/ES celltype colData) has UMAP_1/UMAP_2 embeddings and you need cluster plots overlaid with per-gene or mean pA-count gradients.

name: apa-marker-detection-across-cell-types
description: Use when you have a PACdataset of poly(A) sites with cell group annotations (e.g., sperm differentiation stages SC/RS/ES) and need to identify and visualize per-cell-type APA usage differences such as 3'UTR shortening.

name: apa-usage-heatmap-visualization-across-cell-types
description: Use when you have a PACdataset of poly(A) site counts with cell-type annotations (e.g., sperm cell stages SC/RS/ES) and want to display which genes show differential APA usage (RUD/avg_log2FC) across cell types as a heatmap or companion rich plots.

name: apa-usage-ratio-quantification
description: Use when you have a poly(A) site-by-spot APA count matrix from spatially barcoded ST data (e.g. MOB ST) plus a gene-spot expression count matrix, and need dense per-spot APA usage (RUD) values for downstream spatial APA analysis.

name: approved-drug-annotation-filtering
description: Use when you have essential genes/gene pairs from an in silico knockout analysis and a drug-target interaction table (e.g. DrugBank V5) and need to derive approved single-drug and combination candidates.

name: approximate-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when an iSCMEBObj built from multiple Seurat objects (e.g. DLPFC Visium sections) needs a top-PC embedding (typically npcs=15) before spatial clustering with the hidden Markov random field model.

name: aptardi-transcript-set-comparison
description: Use when you have RSEM quantitations for the same samples against two transcriptome GTFs (aptardi-modified and original) and need to identify which differentially expressed transcripts are attributable to aptardi-added 3'-end annotations.

name: arabidopsis-root-correlation-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when quality-filtered Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq data (e.g. scKB/COPILOT output) needs cell type and developmental time annotations matched to the Shahan et al. 2022 root atlas.

name: arabidopsis-transcriptome-index-usage
description: Use when raw 10x v3 scRNA-seq reads from Arabidopsis thaliana (e.g. SRA runs like SRR12046119/SRR12046120) need pseudoalignment against the TAIR10 cDNA+introns kallisto index to produce spliced/unspliced count matrices.

name: archetypal-analysis-resolution-sweep
description: Use when a single-cell dataset must be decomposed without a priori choosing one number of archetypes, and the goal is to compare pattern-capture quality across resolutions (k=2..30) against a pruned multiresolution decomposition.

name: archetype-number-sweep-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to determine how many archetype components suffice to recover all ground-truth cell-identity patterns, e.g. synthetic scRNA-seq data with known activity patterns evaluated across noise levels.

name: archr-arrow-file-generation
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment files (e.g., BMMC fragments.tsv.gz) must be converted into an ArchR arrow file with QC-filtered cells and reduced to an LSI latent space for clustering and UMAP visualization.

name: arcsin-logit-transformation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when evaluating Scanpro on unreplicated single-cell proportion data and you must decide between arcsin and logit transformations, or choose how many pseudo-replicates the bootstrapping should use.

name: arcsin-transformed-proportion-testing
description: Use when a single-cell dataset annotated with cell type clusters (e.g. an AnnData object with cluster/condition/sample columns) must be tested for differential cell-type proportions, especially when replicates are missing or unbalanced across conditions.

name: argmax-subtype-assignment-validation
description: Use when a batch-corrected expression matrix with per-gene subtype means (cot.df_mean) is available and each gene must be scored and assigned to the subtype whose ideal-marker-gene definition its cross-subtype pattern most closely matches.

name: ari-clone-label-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when a per-cell clone labeling from a CNA-inference pipeline must be validated against an existing clone annotation, and a single agreement statistic (ARI) is needed to quantify concordance.

name: ari-clustering-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing TE quantification methods on scRNA-seq data in terms of downstream cell-clustering fidelity, e.g., testing whether a new method (MATES) beats scTE/SoloTE on ARI against gene-defined clusters.

name: ari-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing imputation or preprocessing methods on scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels, so that quality is measured as improvement in k-means clustering accuracy (ARI) rather than direct value error.

name: ari-nmi-benchmark-computation
description: Use when comparing the accuracy or robustness of scRNA-seq clustering methods (e.g., scAce vs. Leiden) on data with ground-truth cell-type labels, especially across repeated random-cell-subset repeats where median ARI/NMI per method is the target metric.

name: ari-nmi-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-type clustering results against retained ground-truth labels on simulated scRNA-seq data — varying cluster numbers, rare-cell proportions, and dropout — to quantify agreement via ARI, NMI, and silhouette scores.

name: ari-nmi-clustering-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating clustering quality of scRNA-seq cluster assignments against known ground-truth cell-type labels, or when comparing multiple clustering methods' accuracy (e.g. verifying whether a method like scAce achieves ARI = 1).

name: ari-nmi-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating clustering quality of an scRNA-seq imputation method (e.g. scGCL) where an h5 dataset provides both predicted clusters and true cell labels, and ARI/NMI scores must be reported per method-dataset pair.

name: ari-score-significance-testing
description: Use when you have paired per-dataset clustering accuracy scores (e.g. ARI) for a proposed method and one or more baselines over the same dataset set and need non-parametric significance testing.

name: ari-vs-parameter-curve-visualization
