description: Use when you must show that a method's clustering performance (ARI against true labels) remains stable as a hyperparameter is reduced, e.g. subsampling scPLS control genes to q = 10, 20, 30, 40 versus the full 50-gene baseline.

name: arithmetic-geometric-mean-dispersion-statistic
description: Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq training matrix with cell type annotations and need a fast, supervised feature-selection statistic to rank/select cell type-specific genes before training a classifier like SciBet.

name: arrayexpress-perturbation-data-curation
description: Use when building consensus pathway-response signatures from public perturbation data: ArrayExpress series must be searched, pathway-labeled, QC'd, and z-scored per experiment before signature fitting.

name: artificial-bulk-rnaseq-construction
description: Use when benchmarking bulk tissue cell type deconvolution with a single-cell reference and no gold-standard bulk samples with known cell type proportions are available, as in the Segerstolpe pancreatic islet setup.

name: artificial-chromosome-genome-construction
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads must be classified as tRNA-derived without ambiguity from non-tRNA loci, requiring a modified reference genome where tRNA regions plus flanks are separated into distinct artificial chromosomes.

name: artificial-doublet-simulation-from-cell-pairs
description: Use when building the real-artificial training set inside the Chord workflow after the overkill filter, i.e. when a prefiltered Seurat object of quality singlets must be converted into simulated doublet profiles to train the GBM/adaboost doublet classifier.

name: artificial-genome-masked-mapping
description: Use when identifying tRNA-derived small RNAs in plant sRNA-seq FASTQ data and ambiguous mapping to paralogous tRNA copies or non-tRNA genomic regions would otherwise inflate false-positive tncRNA calls.

name: artificial-scrnaseq-dataset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking or reproducing accuracy/runtime comparisons of DEG prediction methods on artificial single-cell RNA-seq data where the set of true DEGs is known by construction, such as validating that singleCellHaystack outperforms cluster-based methods.

name: as-event-count-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a merged allele-specific splicing count table (IJC/SJC counts for reference and alternative alleles plus effective isoform lengths) has been produced by PAIRADISE Step 4 and needs to be cleaned before running the paired ASAS statistical test.

name: as-probability-matrix-handling
description: Use when starting from single-cell SMART-seq BAM or junction files (or Leafcutter/SJ.out.tab junctions) and you need an AS probability matrix (rows = AS sites, columns = cells) with missing values imputed before cell clustering on splicing landscapes.

name: as-probability-quantification-per-splicing-event
description: Use when single-cell SMART-seq BAM files or junction files (LeafCutter output or STAR SJ.out.tab) must be converted into a per-cell AS probability matrix (normalized_matrix) as stage 1 of SCASL before imputation and spectral clustering.

name: asas-significant-event-filtering
description: Use when a PAIRADISE results table has been produced (e.g., for GM12878 or Geuvadis populations) and a statistically significant ASAS SNP/event list is needed for downstream GWAS-LD overlap or enrichment testing.

name: ase-snp-cross-tissue-intersection-analysis
description: Use when you have per-tissue lists of significant ASE SNPs (e.g., VADT meta-analysis significant variants with coordinates for two or more tissues) and need to quantify SNP-level and gene-level overlap across tissues via Venn/set-intersection analysis.

name: assembled-transcript-correctness-scoring
description: Use when you have assembled transcript GTF files from one or more assembly conditions and need to quantify how many assembled transcripts match reference annotations (correct transcripts) and compute precision per condition.

name: assembler-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing transcriptome assemblers on complex multi-isoform genes from short-read or barcoded linked-read RNA-seq, where the metric is the count of annotated isoforms receiving a unique IsoQuant assignment per assembler.

name: assembly-accuracy-comparison-across-assemblers
description: Use when you need to verify that a transcriptome assembler's performance advantage over baselines (e.g., StringTie2, Scallop) holds across multiple real RNA-seq datasets, or when re-testing a trend under a different alignment setting (e.g., Hisat2 without --dta).

name: assembly-graph-tip-clipping
description: Use when assembling full-length isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked-read data reference-free and per-barcode subgraphs contain short dead-end or dead-start edges, or tips with low barcode-specific coverage, that must be clipped before bulge removal and gap closing.

name: assembly-precision-recall-evaluation
description: Use when you have assembled contigs from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads (e.g. cloudrnaSPAdes output) plus a reference annotation, and need to quantify which isoforms were reconstructed accurately per gene.

name: assembly-sensitivity-precision-f1-evaluation
description: Use when simulated RNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth circRNA isoforms are available and you must quantify how well an assembly tool reconstructs full-length circular transcripts (sensitivity, precision, F1) across depths, read lengths, or RI bins.

name: association-inflation-assessment
description: Use when analyzing high-MOI single-cell CRISPR screen data (e.g., CROP-seq with thousands of gRNAs across >10,000 genes) and you need to assess whether gRNA cross-associations inflate FPRs in naive differential expression testing.

name: asw-silhouette-batch-mixing-scoring
description: Use when comparing integration/disentanglement methods on multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq latent factors and you have batch labels plus ground-truth cell-type labels to score batch mixing vs. cell-type preservation.

name: atac-peak-based-clustering
description: Use when clustering single-cell multiome PBMC data where the ATAC modality must be reduced to its most variable peaks before PCA, and high-confidence cluster labels (PEP < 0.1) are needed for downstream ARI evaluation.

name: atac-peak-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrices (AnnData) must be normalized and structured (peaks sorted per chromosome, intra-chromosomal pruning) before feeding scButterfly's ATAC encoder with 30% input masking.

name: atac-seq-ecdna-detection
description: Use when bulk ATAC-Seq datasets (tumor samples, cell lines, or normal negative controls) need screening for ecDNA/amplified circular structures and oncogene content, especially when WGS data or copy-number inputs are unavailable.

name: atac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when integrating scATAC-seq data with annotated scRNA-seq data via scBridge (or similar transfer-learning pipelines) and the target is only a peak-by-cell matrix that must first become a gene activity matrix suitable for cross-omics label transfer.

name: atac-seq-peak-binarization
description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData, cells × peaks) must be prepared for a variational autoencoder input — binarization, 0.5% peak-frequency filtering, TF-IDF, and [0,1] scaling are needed.

name: atac-seq-peak-to-tss-annotation
description: Use when building a candidate TF–target GRN mask from ATAC-seq peaks: motif sites in peaks must be mapped to nearby genes and intersected with an expressed-gene set to seed regulatory network inference (e.g., scKINETICS priors).

name: atacseq-background-read-blending
description: Use when a benchmark of an ATAC-Seq-based ecDNA detector requires positive controls with known ground-truth coordinates: simulated ecDNA reads must be blended into real ATAC-Seq background at controlled local depths and read lengths.

name: atacseq-gene-activity-score-computation
description: Use when a mosaic integration layout contains feature entities (e.g., chromatin regions and genes) that cannot be connected by any available input matrix, so a pseudo-scRNA-seq gene activity matrix must be derived from the scATAC-seq counts.

name: atc-score-paired-statistical-testing
description: Use when comparing trajectory-tree alignment quality (ATC scores) of CAPITAL against integration baselines and you need paired one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values over many synthetic dataset pairs, e.g. to reproduce the Fig. 4a benchmark.

name: atlas-query-label-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when two methods for TCR/transcriptome embedding or antigen specificity prediction must be compared on identical preprocessed atlas-query splits, and per-dataset F1-Score/NMI gains with p-values are the required deliverable.

name: atlas-scale-scrna-seq-data-processing
description: Use when you need clustering-independent DEG/DAF predictions on atlas-level scRNA-seq datasets (h5ad files, up to millions of cells), or to benchmark the continuous v1.0.0+ version against the binary v0.3.4 branch across many datasets.

name: atlas-scale-single-cell-data-integration
description: Use when integrating thousands of samples and millions of cells from multiple studies/technologies (scRNA-seq, CyTOF, CITE-seq) where reduced technical variation AND an adjusted expression matrix for downstream sample-level analysis are required.

name: attention-based-edge-weight-aggregation
description: Use when building a lineage-specific GRN from scRNA-seq expression (e.g., .h5ad) plus a prior gene interaction edgelist, where edge weights should derive from GNN attention rather than co-expression correlations.

name: attention-embedding-normalization-and-clustering
description: Use when TOSICA.pre() has returned new_adata with the attention matrix in .X and you need to trajectory-order or cluster cells on regulon/pathway token attention rather than raw gene expression.

name: attention-head-entropy-analysis-per-cell-type
description: Use when analyzing interpretability of the pretrained tGPT transformer ('lixiangchun/transcriptome-gpt-1024-8-16-64') over HCA per-cell gene ranking sequences, to test whether cell types show distinctive attention head entropy/importance patterns and to attribute scores to marker genes.

name: attention-head-entropy-quantification
description: Use when bulk tumor transcriptomes must be converted to gene-expression rankings and passed through pretrained tGPT (checkpoint lixiangchun/transcriptome-gpt-1024-8-16-64) with output_attentions=True to extract per-head entropy/importance features for clinical or molecular association testing.

name: attention-head-importance-ranking
description: Use when a pretrained tGPT checkpoint and per-cell gene ranking sequences (with cell type labels) are available and the goal is to characterize how attention heads behave per cell type and rank genes by attribution.

name: attention-head-selection-with-ridge-classifier
description: Use when a labeled ground-truth network (e.g. ChIP-seq or perturb-seq edges) is available and you want to bias scPRINT's averaged attention matrix toward the heads that recover known regulatory edges.

name: attention-head-significance-testing
description: Use when bulk transcriptomes are converted to tGPT gene-ranking token sequences and you need to identify which attention heads' entropy patterns differ between responder (CR/PR) and non-responder (SD/PD) immunotherapy patients.

name: attention-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have per-cell top-expressing gene ranking sequences with cell type labels and want to probe which transformer attention heads and genes drive tGPT's feature representation for each cell type.

name: attention-matrix-gene-network-extraction
description: Use when you have a pretrained single-cell transformer (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer v2) and want a zero-shot gene network for a cell type or cell line that must be scored against a directed ground-truth network.

name: attention-matrix-normalization
description: Use when you have run TOSICA.pre on query data and obtained the attention matrix (new_adata.X) that you intend to feed into scIB metric computation, PCA, nearest-neighbor graph construction, or UMAP visualization.

name: attractor-basin-identification-from-langevin-simulations
description: Use when you have snapshot data (simulated or single-cell) from a known multi-stable stochastic system and need to verify that a dynamical method recovers the true attractor-basin structure and highlights transition cells near saddles.

name: attribution-matrix-construction
description: Use when UMI-clustered Nanopore long-read isoform assignments show cross-isoform read leakage within clusters and per-gene attribution matrices are needed to identify and correct mis-mapped isoforms.

name: auc-against-ground-truth-evaluation
description: Use when a method's ability to detect differential regulation (or other binary labels) must be quantified on simulated data with known ground truth, and compared to baseline/alternative methods via AUC.

name: auc-classification-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-cell gene set scores and a binary cell-level label (treated/control, injured/control, cell-type vs rest) and need a single threshold-free metric of class separation, typically to test whether nearest-neighbor smoothing improved discrimination.

name: auc-computation-for-gene-signatures
description: Use when a fixed gene signature from TCGA RNA-seq data (tumor vs normal labels) must be scored for classification performance, and you need a concrete AUC value per cancer type as the deliverable.

name: auc-curve-computation-across-replicates
description: Use when benchmarking rare-cell detection sensitivity on scRNA-seq data by sweeping the number of DE genes (1–144) separating a known rare population from an abundant one, computing per-replicate AUCs and averaging across ~100 synthetic replicates.

name: auc-distribution-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when several gene/feature-selection methods must be ranked on the same synthetic datasets with known ground truth, e.g. simulated 20,000 gene x 2,000 cell NB/ZINB count matrices with embedded impure subpopulations.

name: auc-evaluation-of-type-detection
description: Use when query data are expected to contain cell types absent from a Symphony reference (e.g., ablated or held-out type scenarios) and you need to quantify how well mapping metrics flag those cells as novel rather than misannotating them.

name: auc-performance-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking communication-inference tools (e.g., MDIC3 vs CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK) against a curated literature-supported set of interactions to rank methods by support rate and AUC.

name: auc-precision-metric-computation
description: Use when multiple CCI prediction methods (e.g. DeepCCI, SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, CellPhoneDB, CellChat, CellCall, CytoTalk, NATMI) have produced predicted CCI lists on the same dataset and you must quantify accuracy via AUC and precision.

name: auc-ranking-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating DEG detection methods on simulated expression datasets that carry ground-truth DE labels, and you need per-method AUC over ranked significance scores to compare detection performance.

name: auc-roc-monte-carlo-estimation
description: Use when quantifying how sensitivity of a rareness scorer (e.g. FiRE scores) varies with the number of DE genes distinguishing a ~5% minor subpopulation, requiring mean AUC-ROC over many simulated replicates.

name: aucell-activity-scoring
description: Use when you need per-cell activity scores for gene-regulatory modules (one regulator + its targets) to build a cell-specific GRN from single-cell expression data, e.g. in the pySCENIC pipeline on dyngen simulations.

name: aucell-gene-set-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when you have a normalized UMI matrix in SingCellaR and pre-curated lineage signature gene sets (GMT) and need enrichment-based per-cell cell-type annotation rather than marker-gene-only labeling.

name: aucell-gene-set-scoring-per-cell
description: Use when you have single-cell/snRNA-seq expression data plus a partitioned gene regulatory network (e.g., Leiden subnetworks from a SCING GRN) and need per-cell module activity scores for phenotypic association or clustering.

name: aucell-gene-signature-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when single-cell expression data (SingleCellExperiment) must be converted into per-cell gene-signature enrichment scores, e.g. as classifier features, for state assignment, or for labeling Treg/CD4T/NKT/non-CD8 cells by curated signature enrichment.

name: aucell-gene-signature-scoring
description: Use when you need per-cell gene set activity scores (e.g., malignant up/down signature activity) to calibrate cell labels, define malignant clusters, or establish normal-cell baselines in scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data.

name: aucell-module-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have regulon-like gene modules (RGMs.csv) detected on a cell-lineage-specific GRN and need per-cell module activity scores over the scRNA-seq expression matrix for clustering or benchmarking against SCENIC regulons.

name: aucell-module-score-embedding
description: Use when a SCING GRN has been built and you need cell-level embeddings for clustering, phenotypic association, or batch-effect-corrected dimensionality reduction driven by regulatory modules rather than raw genes.

name: aucroc-aupr-performance-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a CSNI method (e.g. LIONESS, SSN, pySCENIC) against dyngen's cell-specific ground-truth regulatory networks and you need comparable AUROC/AUPR scores per dataset.

name: aucroc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a cell-proportion or differential-abundance method's performance across simulated dataset sizes — e.g. choosing how many pseudo-replicates Scanpro's bootstrapping should use for a given total cell count per condition.

name: aucroc-classifier-evaluation
description: Use when a set of high-weight pathways from a disease-related module must be validated as a predictive signature: bulk RNA-seq expression matrices with binary phenotype labels (e.g., MMR/MSI status) are available and held-out + external-cohort AUROC is the acceptance criterion.

name: aucroc-detection-discrimination-evaluation
description: Use when you have predicted miRNA expression values from mRNA profiles (e.g., miRSCAPE output) plus ground-truth detection calls (detected/non-zero vs undetected) per sample or cell type, and you want an auROC-based accuracy metric.

name: augmentation-vector-thresholding-and-clamping
description: Use when building scTab-style training data from donor- and cell-type-annotated, size-factor-normalized (10000 counts, log1p) scRNA-seq matrices and you need precomputed augmentation vectors for donor-difference data augmentation.

name: aupr-auroc-network-evaluation
description: Use when a reconstructed GRN or GCN (e.g., MCP score matrix like gnw2000.mcp4.h5, or output from Pearson/MI/DPI) must be scored for network quality against a known ground-truth edge list (e.g., gnw2000_truenet.

name: auprc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a single-cell cell-type classifier in a cross-dataset or unseen-term setting, where test labels include Cell Ontology terms absent from the training set.

name: auprc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing gene co-expression network inference methods on simulated single-cell data with known ground-truth edges (power-law, hub-based, or no-extra-sparsity controls) and quantifying accuracy with AUPRC and AUROC across repeats.

name: auprc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking the predictive accuracy or robustness of inferred cell-lineage-specific GRNs against ground-truth regulatory edges, e.g., testing AUPRC stability after randomly perturbing the prior network's edges.

name: auprc-distribution-statistics
description: Use when benchmarking GRN reconstruction against a gold-standard interaction network and you need AUPRC distributions under partial-groundtruth train/test splits (e.g. 0.5%-10% gold-standard fractions) rather than a single full-groundtruth AUPRC.

name: auprc-epr-network-metrics-computation
description: Use when comparing inferred gene regulatory networks (e.g., from scPRINT, scGPT, DeepSEM, Geneformer, GENIE3) against a binary ground-truth network and you need EPR and AUPRC scores to rank methods.

name: auroc-aupr-network-evaluation
description: Use when you need to score predicted cell-specific regulatory networks against dyngen ground-truth GRNs, e.g. benchmarking SSN, LIONESS, or pySCENIC on the 42-dataset dyngen CSNI benchmark.

name: auroc-auprc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing GRN inference tools on synthetic or real single-cell datasets where a ground-truth network exists (e.g. BoolODE toggle-switch simulations with known topology), so predicted edges can be scored as AUROC/AUPRC/EPR.

name: auroc-auprc-classification-evaluation
description: Use when two or more communication-inference methods must be compared fairly on identical ligand-target pairs and expression data, with AUROC/AUPRC ranking of aggregated and per-interaction-pair networks.

name: auroc-based-classification-evaluation
description: Use when GEDI-trained Qi parameters from a multi-sample, multi-condition dataset (e.g., two independent COVID-19 cohorts with COVID vs. healthy labels) must be validated via cross-cohort SVM classification with AUROC as the metric.

name: auroc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying how gene set size or expression variability (CV) affects MetaNeighbor AUROC for cross-dataset cell-type identification, or when validating that a gene set performs above chance (AUROC ~0.5).

name: auroc-benchmark-evaluation-against-curated-markers
description: Use when validating or reproducing marker gene identification quality for Cell Ontology terms — e.g. checking whether top-20 OnClass-ranked markers recover curated marker sets via AUROC for seen vs unseen cell types in Muris FACS/droplet data.

name: auroc-benchmark-evaluation-of-scrnaseq-barcodes
description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq cell-calling/filtering method against ground-truth barcode labels (e.g. HTO-derived singlet/doublet/negative or demuxlet genetic labels) via AUROC, especially under a hyperparameter sweep.

name: auroc-cluster-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying whether an over-clustered scRNA-seq clustering can be recovered by merging: compute AUROC of merged clusters against known cell-type labels, e.g. Tabula Sapiens artificial over-clusters (AUROC 0.9974/0.9976).

name: auroc-computation-for-barcode-classification
description: Use when a raw unfiltered gene-by-barcode count matrix has independent per-barcode ground-truth labels (e.g., demuxlet singlet probabilities or HTO singlet/doublet/negative calls) and you need to quantify how well competing cell-calling methods separate cell-free from cell-containing droplets.

name: auroc-cross-validation-scoring
description: Use when you need a quantitative, comparable score (AUROC) for how well a cell-type label replicates across independent scRNA-seq datasets, e.g. neuron vs non-neuron classification across eight diverse studies.

name: auroc-estimation-with-proc
description: Use when comparing droplet cell-calling predictions on a raw scRNA-seq count matrix against HTO-derived singlet/doublet/negative labels and you need a threshold-independent AUROC per method.

name: auroc-evaluation-against-wgs-ground-truth
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq CNA callers on a sample with WGS-derived clone labels (e.g., BCH869 glioma from Filbin et al. 2018) and you need gene-scale AUROC per CNA state (copy gain, copy loss, LOH).

name: auroc-metric-evaluation-of-gene-detection
description: Use when benchmarking cluster-free DE methods on single-cell data with known ground-truth DE labels (e.g., the simulated COVID-19 cohort 1 dataset) and you need per-method AUROC of up- and down-regulated gene detection alongside Pearson r.

name: auroc-model-evaluation
description: Use when a trained sequence classifier (e.g., a CNN scoring candidate polyA sites) must be benchmarked on held-out genomic test sets from independent databases, with AUROC as the accuracy metric.

name: auroc-performance-computation
description: Use when comparing novel cell type detection or cell-type classification methods on single-cell RNA-seq query/reference pairs and you need threshold-independent performance metrics such as AUROC, AUPR and FPR95 per method per setting.

name: auroc-performance-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking differential expression (or similar binary gene-label) detection methods against simulated data with known ground-truth DE genes, and you need rank-based performance metrics (AUROC, negative Spearman of p-values vs logFC) to compare methods.

name: auroc-replicability-scoring
description: Use when cell-type labels exist for multiple scRNA-seq datasets and you need to quantify cross-dataset replicability of a cell type (or validate a reconstructed scoring module) via AUROC from neighbor voting over a cell-cell correlation network.

name: auroc-statistical-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when several locus-gene link inference methods are scored on identical candidate peak-gene pairs and need a rigorous retrieval comparison against eQTL-supported ground truth with per-sample AUROC and statistical significance testing.

name: ausfc-auroc-baseline-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether accessibility-based TFBS predictions (e.g., from BIRD-predicted DH in GM12878) recover known binding sites better than motif-only or mean-DH baselines, using AUSFC and AUROC metrics.

name: autocrine-paracrine-interaction-classification
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor interaction data (e.g., CellPhoneDB output) for two or more conditions and want to find cell types whose total autocrine/paracrine interaction burden shifts between conditions.

name: autocrine-signalling-specificity-ranking
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix with cell-type annotations should be queried for within-cell-type co-expression of ligand–receptor pairs (self-signalling potential) and autocrine edges need to be ranked against intra-/inter-organ edges by specificity.

name: autoencoder-architecture-implementation
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (h5ad or CSV/TSV) need denoising/imputation in one step while respecting count overdispersion, sparsity, and dropout.

name: autoencoder-architecture-implementation
description: Use when highly sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., >80-95% zeros, masked .hd5 inputs like example.msk90.hd5) need imputation and you must build or reproduce the LATE autoencoder network in TensorFlow 1.x.

name: autoencoder-based-dimension-reduction
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices are noisy with high dropout and you need a low-dimensional, part-based cell representation to support unsupervised clustering (e.g., ARI benchmarking against SC3, Seurat, CIDR).

name: autoencoder-based-expression-denoising
description: Use when a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes) with simulated dropout or low sampling efficiency (e.g., 5–10%) needs a denoised reconstruction before imputation or downstream clustering.

name: autoencoder-based-multimapping-rate-regression
description: Use when Smart-seq2 or 10X single-cell RNA-seq/ATAC data must have multi-mapping reads accurately allocated to individual TE loci, rather than collapsed at subfamily level.

name: autoencoder-based-single-cell-multimodal-integration
description: Use when integrating unpaired (non-co-assayed) single-cell modalities such as scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, surface protein, CyTOF, smFISH, or morphology into a shared low-dimensional latent space for visualization, clustering, and cross-modality imputation.

name: autoencoder-classifier-composite-network-implementation
description: Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (e.g., genes x cells CSV) contains dropouts and other noise, and a distribution-free deep learning imputation that preserves cell-type signal is needed.

name: autoencoder-denoising-distribution-fitting
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes) is sparse due to dropout/low capture efficiency and you need denoised imputed expression values without training method-specific deep models per dataset.

name: autoencoder-denoising-of-scrna-seq-expression
description: Use when a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix with simulated dropout (low sampling efficiency, e.g. 0.1%–10%) must be denoised before downstream distribution learning or imputation, and you need a latent representation of the noisy data.

name: autoencoder-feature-extraction-scrna
description: Use when benchmarking autoencoder-derived latent features of scRNA-seq data against original profiles and correlation-based features (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman) via silhouette values against true cell-type labels.

name: autoencoder-feature-selection
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes) is high-dimensional and noisy, and you must remove uninformative genes before training a stacked variational autoencoder or graph-based clustering.

name: autoencoder-fine-tuning
description: Use when annotating normal (non-disease) scRNA-seq query data with a pre-trained SELINA model and the query distribution differs from the reference, requiring adaptation of pre-trained parameters before label transfer.

name: autoencoder-hyperparameter-grid-selection
description: Use when running AutoImpute's autoencoder imputation on a scRNA-seq count matrix and per-dataset hyper-parameters (lambda, hidden units, initial learning rate, threshold) must be chosen from Table 2-style settings.

name: autoencoder-imputation-model-training
description: Use when a pre-processed, log-transformed single-cell count matrix (cells x genes, CSV or .mat) has dropouts or artificially masked non-zero values that need imputation with an overcomplete autoencoder, or when benchmarking imputation recovery error.

name: autoencoder-latent-feature-analysis
description: Use when scRNAseq clusters need functional annotation — e.g., identifying cluster-specific transcription factors or minimal gene panels (≤4 genes) from a TF-SCA latent-space frequency matrix of a blood-cell dataset.

name: autoencoder-latent-vector-extraction
description: Use when segmented single-cell masks from multiplexed tissue imaging need quantitative shape descriptors, e.g., feeding cell-shape latent vectors into t-SNE analysis downstream of MIRIAM segmentation.

name: autoencoder-loss-weight-configuration
description: Use when building or retuning a BEENE get_hybrid_model_1 autoencoder for RNA-seq batch-effect estimation and you must choose λ1/λ2/λ3 and dropout based on feature count, dimensionality reduction, and biological variables.

name: autoencoder-low-dimensional-feature-extraction
description: Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices are noisy or high-dimensional (many cells, high dropout) and a compressed cell embedding is needed before clustering, visualization, cell classification, or pseudo-time inference.

name: autoencoder-masked-reconstruction-training
description: Use when a preprocessed sparse single-cell gene expression matrix (cells x top high-dispersion genes, .csv) contains dropout dropouts that must be imputed via overcomplete autoencoder reconstruction, e.g. blakeley.csv.

name: autoencoder-matrix-completion
description: Use when a log2-transformed, library-size-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. top 1000 high-dispersion genes, .csv/.mat) contains dropout zeros and needs imputation before clustering or expression-recovery analysis.

name: autoencoder-pretraining
description: Use when starting a DESC clustering workflow on preprocessed scRNA-seq data (log1p-transformed, top-1000 HVGs, scaled) and a low-dimensional embedding is needed to initialize cluster centers.

name: autoencoder-quality-metric-evaluation-qcm-qcc
description: Use when quantifying whether an SCA/SSCA latent space (built from TF, miRNA, kinase targets, or immune signatures) reconstructs a given single-cell cluster, or when comparing knowledge-group combinations (e.g., TF+miRNA vs TF alone) by QCM/QCC on a counts table with pre-computed clusters.

name: autoencoder-training-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when training the scDHA non-negative kernel autoencoder module on a genes-by-cells scRNA-seq matrix and you need to verify reconstruction-loss convergence before ranking genes by encoder weight variance.

name: autoencoder-training-on-coverage-vectors
description: Use when quantifying transposable elements at locus level in scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq data: multi-mapping reads must be allocated to specific TE loci using unique-read flanking context before counting.

name: autoencoder-training-on-gene-expression
description: Use when a normalized, log1p-transformed cell-by-gene scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. Klein dataset, top 5000 Seurat HVGs) still contains dropouts and you need a statistically grounded imputation via a two-part-generalized-gamma autoencoder.

name: autoencoder-training-on-sparse-counts
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data are highly sparse (typically >80-95% zeros) and the goal is to recover true expression behind dropout zeros via autoencoder-based imputation with no reference dataset.

name: autoencoder-variant-training
description: Use when you must choose the hidden-layer width of an autoencoder or a dropout-augmentation strength for DCNet by comparing train/test RMSE on log2(x+1)-transformed TCGA expression data.

name: automated-cell-type-validation-against-manual-annotations
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq dataset has published manual cell-type annotations and you need to check whether an unsupervised annotator (ScType) reproduces them from raw counts alone.

name: autoregressive-gene-ranking-language-modeling
description: Use when building a transformer language model whose autoregressive pretraining target is gene expression rankings (not counts) of single-cell transcriptomes, e.g. reproducing tGPT or adapting GPT2LMHeadModel to a gene-token vocabulary.

name: auxiliary-classifier-ensemble-consistency
description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells source-free with scEMAIL and you need per-cell uncertainty from the main classifier plus two auxiliary classifiers to later detect novel cell types via E-score bimodality.

name: average-gene-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two single-cell 3′ gene-expression datasets differ by a handling variable (freeze-thaw, library prep) and you must show equivalence of average expression and per-cell sensitivity (genes/UMIs) before downstream cell-type classification.

name: average-precision-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing alternative hierarchical correction algorithms for Cell Ontology-based classification and you need a threshold-free metric (average precision) plus per-cell-type PR curves to establish whether a correction degrades or preserves the baseline.

name: average-proportion-of-nonoverlap-computation
description: Use when comparing clustering methods on droplet-based scRNA-seq data and you need a quantitative cluster-stability metric from repeated perturbation runs.

name: awca-reference-construction
description: Use when classifying breast cancer RNA-seq samples into the five intrinsic subtypes (Luminal A/B, Basal, Her2-enriched, Normal-like) and the standard median-based PAM50 reference is sensitive to cohort composition or a single-sample, reference-independent caller is needed.

name: azimuth-reference-agreement-assessment
description: Use when scTriangulate final labels need external validation against a supervised reference annotation (Azimuth L2/L2-level atlas labels), or when a reference label-transfer annotation should be jointly integrated as a fourth conflicting annotation set.

name: azimuth-reference-based-cell-annotation
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., CD45+ immunotherapy cohorts) lack cell-type labels and downstream differential-state analysis such as scDist requires annotated cluster identities per cell.

name: b-allele-frequency-concordance-analysis
description: Use when validating single-cell CNA calls (RDR-based segmentation) by requiring concordant BAF shifts at phased gHETs, or when comparing allele-aware vs. BAF-agnostic CNA callers.

name: b-cell-clonotype-clustering
description: Use when RNA-seq-derived Ig transcript contigs (e.g. Trinity-assembled from a BWA/hg38-aligned BAM) need IGHV germline assignment, percent-identity-based SHM calls, and clonotype grouping to classify CLL samples as mCLL/uCLL.

name: b-cell-subset-cluster-annotation
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data from CD19+ B cells where surface protein expression must be integrated with transcriptome to resolve functionally distinct B cell subsets, e.g. spike-specific memory-like clusters in COVID-19 patient PBMC.

name: back-splice-junction-fragment-quantification
description: Use when you have ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq FASTQ (or a CIRCexplorer2 output plus HISAT2-aligned BAM) and need directly comparable circular vs. linear RNA expression values (FPB and CIRCscore) at shared gene loci.

name: back-splicing-junction-circrna-detection
description: Use when ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files must be screened for circRNAs via BSJ-spanning fragments, and quantification of circRNA expression relative to cognate linear RNA (CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear) is required.

name: back-splicing-junction-read-mapping
description: Use when quantifying circRNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files by detecting fragments spanning back-splicing junction sites, prior to FPB/CIRCscore quantification.

name: back-to-back-barplot-visualization
description: Use when two or more pre-computed CCI datasets from different conditions (e.g. CellPhoneDB output for critical vs moderate COVID-19) are loaded in InterCellar and the goal is to identify cell clusters with strikingly gained or lost interactions via per-cluster count comparison.

name: backbone-point-selection-center-outward
description: Use when processing imaging data of rolled (Swiss-roll) intestinal tissues — e.g. CODEX-exported .csv files or 10x spatial transcriptomics images providing x and y coordinates — where a curved spiral backbone must be manually defined before unrolling cells onto a line.

name: backbone-spiral-quality-assessment
description: Use when you are drawing or reusing a backbone over a rolled-intestine ROI (CODEX or 10x xy-coordinate CSV) and must confirm the selection traces a high-quality 3D spiral, starting from the spiral center and going outward, before running the Unroll step.

name: backbone-topology-configuration
description: Use when generating dyngen simulation datasets and a specific trajectory topology (linear, bifurcating, cyclic, converging, disconnected) must be configured to benchmark trajectory, RNA velocity, or CSNI methods.

name: background-corrected-permutation-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when per-cell TRS or module scores (e.g., Seurat AddModuleScore output) need statistically calibrated significance, because raw module scores lack a null model and cannot be thresholded (e.g., q<0.05) for calling trait-relevant cells.

name: background-cutoff-histogram-visualization
description: Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix (e.g. PIMENTo's preprocess.data.obj$quantile) shows a bimodal log2 intensity distribution and a background/signal valley must be identified to define a background-subtracted gene set.

name: background-droplet-definition-barcode-rank
description: Use when running dsb (DSBNormalizeProtein) on CITE-seq ADT data with both raw and filtered Cell Ranger output available, and a set of empty droplets must be defined to estimate ambient antibody background.

name: background-droplet-standardization
description: Use when raw CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq ADT count matrices are available together with raw (unfiltered) barcode matrices containing empty droplets, and ambient protein-specific noise must be removed prior to cell-level normalization.

name: bacterial-lifestyle-gene-association-analysis
description: Use when you have a binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix plus per-genome lifestyle labels and need to enumerate lifestyle-associated genes per group using bacLIFE's 70% prevalence / 2 log2FC rule.

name: bacterial-lifestyle-prediction
description: Use when you have a gene cluster absence/presence matrix for genomes with literature-derived lifestyle labels and need to (a) quantify lifestyle predictability via cross-validated AUC or (b) assign lifestyles to unknown-lifestyle genomes.

name: baf-binarization-at-germline-hets
description: Use when single-cell scWGS BAF data must be converted to a clean allelic state matrix at reliable germline SNPs — e.g., before ADO-event HMM decoding or allele-specific CNA calling — and phased gHET calls from SHAPEIT2 (shapeit/phased_hets.vcf) are available.

name: baf-concordance-classification
description: Use when you have single-cell CNA calls from a BAF-agnostic (read-depth-only) caller and phased bulk germline heterozygous SNPs, and you need to quantify how many calls are supported by local allelic (BAF) evidence per cell type.

name: baf-gene-scale-mapping
description: Use when running XClone's BAF module on phased scRNA-seq allele counts (AD/DP matrices) and the phased mega-gene-level allele states must be projected to per-gene resolution before run_combine merges them with RDR CNA probabilities.

name: baf-shift-integration-for-cnv-calls
description: Use when calling CNV events from bulk or single-cell RNA-seq where expression-based segmentation alone is ambiguous and BAF shift information from mapped reads (no heterozygous variant call set or SNV calls) should be integrated to confirm and consolidate calls at multiple scales.

name: baf-shift-signal-extraction
description: Use when RNA-seq BAM files (bulk or single-cell) must be converted into per-sample BAF shift profiles to supply the LOH/allelic-shift input for CaSpER CNV calling.

name: baf-shift-signal-generation-from-rnaseq-bam
description: Use when you have mapped bulk or merged single-cell RNA-seq BAM files and need a genome-wide BAF shift signal to correct/confirm CaSpER CNV calls, without a pre-existing heterozygous SNV call set.

name: bag-level-instance-label-relabeling
description: Use when candidate m6A site labels are uncertain and inputs are positive/negative bag-level datasets, so instance labels must be inferred via multiple instance learning.

name: bagged-subsample-network-consensus-merging
description: Use when a robust GRN is needed from scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data and many subsample networks have been built from supercells, so edges recurring across networks must be merged into a consensus before edge pruning.

name: balanced-accuracy-benchmark-computation
description: Use when evaluating an automated cell-type annotation method against curated expert labels on atlas-scale mouse or human tissue datasets, when balanced accuracy and label-similarity metrics must be reproduced from deposited code, or when benchmarking Census against annotators on droplet or FACS.

name: balanced-accuracy-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-querying or label-transfer methods on scRNA-seq datasets where some query cell types are absent from the reference, so both sensitivity (positive queries) and specificity (negative queries) must be measured.

name: balanced-accuracy-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying how cell type imbalance (e.g., 450:50 or 400:25 per cohort) affects the relative performance of selection strategies for single-cell type annotation, with results laid out as in Fig. 3C and Supplementary Figs. 13-30.

name: balanced-accuracy-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a malignant-cell annotation method on single-cell datasets that have per-cell ground-truth malignant/normal labels, and you need per-method accuracy and balanced accuracy values for a comparison table.

name: balanced-accuracy-sensitivity-rank-aggregation
description: Use when comparing multiple cell/training-set selection strategies evaluated across several datasets and classifiers, and you need a single robust overall ranking from per-combination balanced accuracy and sensitivity results.

name: balanced-unbalanced-simulation-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when comparing batch-effect correction methods on simulated scRNA-seq data with balanced and unbalanced batch conditions, and you need per-method kBET, ASW, and LISI metrics assembled into a benchmark table.

name: bam-alignment-file-io
description: Use when a pipeline must preprocess aligned reads in BAM format by opening the file, inspecting per-read FLAG and RG tags, and writing partitioned BAMs with a preserved header.

name: bam-alignment-file-processing
description: Use when a BAM produced by a spliced aligner (e.g. STAR realignment of unmapped reads) contains novel splice sites that must be incorporated into fortuna's cnt.tsv/alt.tsv signature counts and novel-event annotations.

name: bam-alignment-input-preparation
description: Use when running Tiglon on RNA-seq alignments: you have coordinate-sorted BAM files from Hisat2 and/or Star and must supply them as bamFiles_list text files with a library-correct strand flag.

name: bam-alignment-merging-across-aligners
description: Use when RNA-seq reads have been aligned independently by Hisat2 and STAR and a downstream integrative assembler (e.g., Tiglon) needs a combined BAM or a bamFile_list of the per-aligner BAMs as input.

name: bam-alignment-parsing-with-pysam
description: Use when you have a gRNA-aligned BAM file (e.g. gRNA.sorted.mapped.removedSecondaryAlignment.onlyMappedToGrnaChrom.bam) plus a filtered cell barcode list and need per-UMI consensus gRNA sequences for mutation calling.

name: bam-alignment-preprocessing
description: Use when starting from cellranger/STAR-aligned scRNA-seq BAMs and you need a combined, per-strand alignment to feed annotation-free TAR discovery or to compute the coverage cutoff n.

name: bam-alignment-processing
description: Use when a sorted BAM of small-RNA reads aligned to a tRNA-masked artificial genome and a matching reference FASTA are available and the goal is to predict modified nucleoside sites along tncRNAs.

name: bam-alignment-processing
description: Use when you have long-read cDNA/direct-RNA reads (FASTQ) plus a reference FASTA and need a splice-aware BAM alignment as input for isoform detection, quantification and tool benchmarking against a known isoform annotation.

name: bam-alignment-processing
description: Use when sorted, length-filtered RiboSeq BAM files (e.g. BAM.25-35 folder) and a GFF annotation are available and a gene-level count matrix is needed for downstream DESeq2 differential expression analysis.

name: bam-alignment-sorting-validation
description: Use when a BAM file is about to be fed into CRIS (or an analogous RNA-seq Ig reconstruction pipeline) and you must verify or produce hg38/GRCh38 alignment, coordinate sorting, and an index before running.

name: bam-cigar-softclip-parsing
description: Use when a BAM of aligned sequencing reads (e.g. 10x Chromium 3'-enriched data) must be mined for soft-clipped reads bearing polyA-tails to derive per-position truncation-point tallies for 3' UTR end determination.

name: bam-file-construction-and-merging
description: Use when benchmarking allele-specific CNA callers requires simulated single-cell scWGS BAMs with known ground-truth events (200 kb–5 Mb), preserved haplotype structure, and realistic amplification artifacts.

name: bam-file-processing
description: Use when input is a single 10x Genomics barcoded BAM plus a barcodes.tsv.gz from outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ and per-cell BAM files are needed for gene body coverage or per-cell QC.

name: bam-file-splitting-by-cell-barcode
description: Use when the input is a single 10x Genomics barcoded BAM (e.g. possorted_genome_bam.bam) plus a barcodes.tsv.gz from outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/, and per-cell BAM files are needed before gene body coverage analysis.

name: bam-file-strand-separation
description: Use when input is a strand-specific aligned BAM (e.g. Tb927_01_v5.1.slice.bam) and the next step is per-strand coverage/peak calling toward 3' UTR annotation.

name: bam-junction-read-support-quantification
description: Use when you have short-read RNA-seq alignments (BAM) from two or more splice-aware aligners (Hisat2, STAR) and need to quantify junction read support and assign aligner-capture labels to splice graph edges.

name: bam-level-allele-specific-read-injection
description: Use when a CNA-caller benchmark needs controlled ground truth: inject a known allele-specific chr3 copy loss into real 10x 5' scRNA-seq data and measure AUROC-based detection recovery.

name: bam-read-alignment-processing
description: Use when a GFF3/GTF canonical annotation must be extended with 3' UTRs using aligned reads (BAM) enriched at transcript 3' ends, e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq BAMs with ~10^8 reads.

name: bam-read-filtering-by-gene-assignment
description: Use when starting from a CellRanger or STAR scRNA-Seq BAM and you need unassigned (non-gene) reads to quantify locus-specific transposable element expression without gene-contamination artifacts.

name: bam-sorting-and-indexing
description: Reference for converting merged SAM alignments from Ribo-seq double-mapping (HISAT2 splice-aware followed by Bowtie2 mismatch-tolerant) into sorted, indexed BAM/BAI files ready for read counting and periodicity analysis.

name: bam-splice-coordinate-extraction
description: Use when a BAM/GFF3/BED6 long-read RNA alignment must be converted into a consensus set of splice-site/exon-boundary coordinates per gene, prior to isoform assembly and quantification.

name: bam-tag-parsing-cb-ub
description: Use when somatic SNVs from eWGS must be detected per-cell in 10x 5' scRNA-seq BAMs by pileup over reads carrying valid CB and UB_tag values, producing per-cell mutant counts.

name: bam-tag-parsing-chromium-barcode
description: Use when analyzing 10x Chromium scRNA-seq alignments (BAMs with CB/UB tags) or _counts_UB.tsv tables and you need per-cell, per-UMI molecule counts collapsed by genomic position — e.g., to profile coverage decay distal to the capture site.

name: barcode-count-quantification
description: Use when raw bulk cellular barcoding FASTQ (single- or paired-end) must be converted into a barcode-by-sample counts table, with documented QC metrics at each stage.

name: barcode-counts-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw FASTQ or a raw barcode counts table from a population-level cellular barcoding experiment must be QC-filtered before downstream clonal analysis, and low-quality samples or low-abundance barcodes must be removed.

name: barcode-discovery-from-long-reads
description: Use when cellular barcodes must be discovered de novo from noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. ONT reads) where only the flanking sequence of the barcode region is known and no barcode list is available up front.

name: barcode-frequency-distribution-visualization
description: Use when a barcode count table from Flexiplex barcode discovery needs visual inspection of the frequency-versus-rank curve to verify the empty-droplet cutoff before filtering.

name: barcode-gene-assignment-classification
description: Use when cloudrnaSPAdes contigs from barcoded (SPIso-seq-style) data must have their barcode-to-gene assignments classified as unique vs ambiguous, or when quantifying the fraction of ambiguous contigs removable by barcode-multiplicity filtering (e.g. Table 3 '1' vs '1-fixed' rows).

name: barcode-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when lineage predictions from scRNA-seq gene expression alone need quantitative validation against a known barcode lineage annotation, or when selecting a confidence cutoff with acceptable precision (e.g., precision = 1.0 at confidence 80).

name: barcode-group-partitioning
description: Use when validating a cell-calling filter (e.g., EmptyNN) by testing whether barcodes it uniquely retains are transcriptionally closer to confirmed cells than barcodes it removes, from a raw unfiltered count matrix.

name: barcode-knee-plot-inflection-detection
description: Use when a barcode count table (e.g. flexiplex_barcodes_counts.txt from flexiplex in discovery mode) must be filtered to keep only barcodes above the empty-droplet knee, and a whitelist such as 3M-february-2018.txt is to be intersected with the cutoff.

name: barcode-preprocessing-novelty-scoring
description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference exists (e.g. healthy 54 cell types) and a query dataset may contain rare cell types absent from the reference (e.g. 10 COVID-only types) that must be auto-detected.

name: barcode-rank-plot-parameter-inspection
description: Use when running CellBender cell calling on a raw scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count matrix and the required 'expected number of cells' / 'total-droplets-included' parameters must be chosen for a new dataset with no prior defaults.

name: barcode-sequence-clustering-error-correction
description: Use when raw barcode FASTQ reads contain sequencing errors that would inflate unique-barcode counts, and you need to derive a consensus barcode repertoire (per-sample counts table) before population-level quantification or cross-tool comparison.

name: barcode-specific-edge-coverage-estimation
description: Use when assembling isoforms de novo from bulk barcoded RNA-seq linked reads and you need edge support quantified per barcode/read cloud, because an edge erroneous for one barcode's isoform may be correct for another barcode's isoform.

name: barcode-swapping-molecule-identification
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries were sequenced on patterned flow-cell Illumina machines (HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq) and swapped molecules must be excluded from per-sample count matrices.

name: barcode-total-umi-count-filtering
description: Use when a raw unfiltered droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (mtx or h5) must be split into known-empty barcodes and unlabeled barcodes prior to PU-learning-based cell calling, or when a simple total-UMI cutoff defines empty droplets.

name: barcode-umi-cdna-region-extraction
description: Use when a preprocessing tool such as kallisto|bustools or simpleaf/alevin-fry needs its technology string derived from a seqspec spec.yaml plus the FASTQ read names for a single-cell modality.

name: barcode-whitelist-filtering
description: Use when you have a barcode count table from barcode discovery on single-cell reads (FASTQ/FASTA) and need to keep only whitelist-matching barcodes and drop empty droplets before assigning reads to cells.

name: barcoded-lineage-cell-pairing
description: Use when scRNA-seq data comes with barcode lineage annotations (e.g. GEO GSE74923 L1210 or CD8+ T-cell datasets) and you need to verify that related cells are more transcriptomically similar than random pairs.

name: barcoded-linked-read-contig-filtering
description: Use when you have a cloudrnaSPAdes contigs FASTA from barcoded (SPIso-seq) RNA-seq data plus a barcode-to-gene assignment table, and you need to remove contigs with multiply-assigned barcodes and quantify the removal rate per assignment class.

name: barcoded-read-cloud-subgraph-extraction
description: Use when assembling reference-free isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads: you have a shared SPAdes assembly graph plus per-read barcode tags and need barcode-specific subgraphs for simplification.

name: barcoded-rnaseq-isoform-assembly
description: Use when input is paired-end barcoded RNA-seq FASTQ (e.g. SPIso-seq human brain, ~181.8M read pairs / 584,399 barcodes) and full-length isoform contigs must be assembled without a transcript reference.

name: barcoded-rnaseq-read-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic barcoded RNA-seq linked reads from genes with known isoform structure (e.g. GYPC, MAPT, BIN1) to evaluate reference-free isoform assembly and barcode-filtering strategies.

name: barretts-esophagus-biopsy-heterogeneity-assessment
description: Use when evaluating MaCroDNA cell-to-cell assignments on BE biopsy scDNA-seq/scRNA-seq data in the absence of ground truth, to test statistical significance and quantify assignment stability across resampled runs.

name: barretts-esophagus-multiomic-reanalysis
description: Use when single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA expression tables from Barrett's esophagus biopsies (NDBE, LGD, HGD, EAC) need cross-modality cell-to-clone assignment and per-gene phylogenetic signal (K*) analysis to test whether genomic mutations drive transcriptomic heterogeneity.

name: base-grn-construction-from-scatac-seq
description: Use when preparing scGATE inputs from paired scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq data: you need a base GRN parquet (e.g. Buenrostro2018_base_GRN_dataframe.parquet) of candidate TF–target edges derived from scATAC-seq peaks and TF motifs before running scGATE_edge()/scGATE_gate().

name: base-grn-integration-from-scatac-motif-hints
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data must be combined with a scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN (.parquet) to filter candidate TF-target pairs prior to directed TF-gene network or Boolean logic gate inference with scGATE.

name: base-grn-integration-with-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have a base GRN edge list derived from scATAC-seq (e.g., the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas) plus an scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP) and need cluster-specific pruned GRNs.

name: base-level-pileup-processing
description: Use when RNA-seq alignment files (BAM) for a sample cohort must be converted to a transcript-independent, base-level coverage matrix for downstream shape-change or structural-variation analysis with SCISSOR.

name: base-quality-score-recalibration
description: Use when a tumor-normal WES/WGS SAM/BAM alignment (GRCh37 or GRCh38) needs base quality score recalibration and repeat-sequence removal before Mutect2 somatic SNV/INDEL calling.

name: basecaller-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a modification-aware basecaller (e.g. NanoSpeech inosine-only or multi-mod models) detects modified bases as accurately as a baseline such as Guppy or Dorado+ModiKit on synthetic or IVT ONT dRNA datasets.

name: basecaller-model-development
description: Use when pretrained NanoSpeech model weights (.h5 with .h5.cfg files) must be turned into an executable Keras/TF architecture, or when developing a transformer basecaller that maps raw ONT dRNA signals to kmers over an expanded vocabulary.

name: baseline-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a deep learning filter (e.g. HVLD for chimeric-read/fusion-gene classification) genuinely improves over bi-LSTM, Transformer, MLP, SVM, or a no-distillation ablation on identical training splits.

name: baseline-classifier-comparison-chetah-svmrejection
description: Use when comparing cell-type classifiers on benchmark scRNA-seq data (simulated, PBMC-FACS, AMB2018) to quantify hierarchical F1-scores and unseen-population rejection rates for scHPL's linear vs one-class SVM against CHETAH and SVMrejection.

name: baseline-classifier-reproduction-across-datasets
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend a head-to-head comparison of malignant-cell identification tools on .h5ad scRNA-seq datasets that carry ground-truth malignant/normal labels, and report per-method accuracy and balanced accuracy.

name: baseline-clustering-algorithm-comparison
description: Use when a new general-purpose clustering algorithm must be validated against standard baselines on simulated datasets with known ground-truth labels, producing a per-algorithm, per-dataset metric table for publication-style comparison.

name: baseline-clustering-method-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking a new scRNA-seq clustering method against published baselines on the same down-sampled cell sets, or when verifying that scDCC with pairwise constraints outperforms competing methods on the four small 2100-cell datasets.

name: baseline-confounder-removal-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a confounder-removal method for single-cell RNA-seq outperforms PCA, LMM, RUV, and scLVM baselines on simulated data with known latent confounders and cell labels.

name: baseline-grn-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a new GRN inference method for time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data must be compared to baselines like SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, and SINGE using early precision against BEELINE ground truth networks.

name: baseline-imputation-method-reproduction
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq imputation methods on simulated dropout: non-zero expression entries are masked at 10/30/50% rates and imputed values must be compared against retained ground truth.

name: baseline-integration-method-execution
description: Use when benchmarking a new single-cell diagonal-integration method against established baselines on paired-modality datasets (e.g. scRNA-scATAC 10X Multiome or CITE-seq scRNA-surface protein PBMC data) where identical inputs and metrics are required for a fair comparison.

name: baseline-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when proposing a graph-based single-cell method and you need to demonstrate it consistently outperforms a published baseline across a sweep of graph-construction hyperparameters (k neighbors, distance measures) using ARI/NMI.

name: baseline-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a new multi-batch multi-condition integration method against a baseline (e.g., scDisInFact vs scINSIGHT) on identical data, needing quantitative metrics like ASW-batch and ARI.

name: baseline-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a new trajectory/pseudotime method must be validated against published baselines on shared datasets, especially to quantify robustness under random cell subsampling (e.g. 90% ME subsampling over 50 repeats).

name: baseline-method-benchmarking-across-datasets
description: Use when a new latent-process or pseudo-time method must be shown to outperform existing methods across several labeled scRNA-seq datasets with a shared accuracy metric and comparison table.

name: baseline-method-benchmarking-comparison
description: Use when multiple SC-to-ST spatial mapping methods must be compared on the same preprocessed SC/ST inputs where ground-truth spatial coordinates and cell-type labels exist, so coordinate error (MAE), neighbor-recovery (hit-number@K), and cell-type proportion fidelity (PCC) can be tabulated per.

name: baseline-method-benchmarking-in-scrnaseq
description: Use when clustering droplet-based multi-individual scRNA-seq UMI count data and you need to quantify whether a proposed method outperforms established baselines via adjusted Rand index against approximated truth labels.

name: baseline-method-comparison
description: Use when a time-course scRNA-seq dataset has been processed with CellST and a head-to-head comparison against a baseline method (Pearson correlation alignment or tradeseq) is needed to justify the OT-based lineage construction.

name: baseline-method-default-parameter-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing novel cell detection/classification baselines on scRNA-seq reference-query splits, especially cross-platform settings where batch effects may degrade competitor methods like scLearn.

name: baseline-metric-coupling-comparison
description: Use when two-time-point (or adjacent-time-point) scRNA-seq matrices are available and you need to evaluate whether OT-based cell-to-cell coupling outperforms Euclidean or Pearson-correlation matching, or when high-dimensional noisy expression data makes classical distance metrics suspect.

name: baseline-spatial-mapping-method-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking a new spatial-relationship reconstruction method for single-cell RNA-seq data against SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, and Tangram and each baseline must be run under its authors' own settings.

name: bash-based-scrna-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw 10xv3 scRNA-seq FASTQ reads need alignment and quantification into spliced/unspliced count matrices, especially when CellRanger is too slow or RNA velocity / splicing-dynamics downstream analyses are planned.

name: batch-aware-deep-learning-clustering
description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data spanning multiple batches where batch effect must be removed jointly with clustering, and no reliable batch annotation is available (DESC does not explicitly require batch information).

name: batch-corrected-kernel-reduction
description: Use when merging multiple scRNA-seq count matrices from independent studies and you need a shared low-dimensional cell embedding in which batch/study-of-origin effects are removed before clustering or label propagation.

name: batch-correction-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you have multi-sample/single-batch-annotated scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq embeddings and need a quantitative benchmark of how well alternative embedding/correction methods mix batches while retaining phenotypic information such as diagnosis, sex, or disease stage.

name: batch-correction-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a pretrained single-cell embedding model's batch insensitivity against batch-correction baselines, e.g. computing kBET acceptance rates on multi-donor data such as the HCA Census of Immune Cells bone-marrow set (n=282,588 cells, 64 healthy donors).

name: batch-correction-model-conditioning
description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData contain multiple sequencing batches and you need batch-corrected RNA velocities and latent cell states that preserve gene expression dynamics, e.g. with ltv.models.VAE(batch_correction=True, batches=n).

name: batch-correction-multiomics-integration
description: Use when paired multi-omics data (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or CITE-seq via 10X Multiome) are profiled across multiple batches or centers and you need to train, evaluate, and compare batch-corrected versus uncorrected Mowgli embeddings.

name: batch-correction-scenario-benchmarking
description: Use when a cell-attribute-aware DA-testing workflow (e.g. ELVAR/EVA clustering) must be stress-tested for robustness to whether batch correction is applied beforehand, and to quantify how correction shifts significance of DA-test results.

name: batch-covariate-signal-extraction
description: Use when raw multi-batch scRNA-seq count data (e.g., Kolodziejczyk mESC across culture media) must be decomposed so the low-dimensional representation clusters by a known biological variable while dependence on batch is measured and removed.

name: batch-effect-assessment
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq raw count data have technical batches that are partially confounded with biology (e.g., each patient/biological replicate processed in a separate batch) and you must remove batch effects without erasing the biological signal.

name: batch-effect-correction-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare how well foundation-model cell embeddings remove batch effects, measured by the scIB avgBIO aggregate, across open-problems batch-correction datasets such as human pancreas and lung.

name: batch-effect-correction-combat-scanorama
description: Use when building context-wise 4D-communication tensors from multi-donor single-cell data (e.g. 12 BALF COVID-19 patients) where batch effects across samples could confound LR communication scores, and you need batch-corrected representations before tensor decomposition.

name: batch-effect-correction-vector-arithmetic
description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData objects with a trained GeneVector cell embedding (cell_embed) contain batch/treatment labels (e.g., control vs interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) and batch effects must be removed while retaining stimulus-driven variation for downstream UMAP and silhouette benchmarking.

name: batch-effect-correction-with-harmony
description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain multiple batches (e.g., patients or samples, with a metadata CSV batch column such as 'PatientID') and the top PCs must be batch-corrected with Harmony before Louvain clustering in the scDrug/Scanpy pipeline.

name: batch-effect-correction-with-mnn-and-cca
description: Use when multi-individual droplet-based scRNA-seq UMI count matrices show batch effects (e.g., same-batch samples clustering together in t-SNE of 50 PCs) and you need corrected/aligned data as input to downstream clustering baselines.

name: batch-effect-correction-with-mofa-plus
description: Use when single-cell-derived pseudobulk feature matrices (e.g., scPAFA PAS aggregated per sample) contain clearly known technical batch effects and you need unsupervised factor analysis that separates batch from biological/disease variance.

name: batch-effect-detection-in-microarray-samples
description: Use when normalized microarray intensity data (e.g. quantile- or LOESS-normalized samples from example_unnorm.txt) must be screened for systematic processing artifacts such as date, operator, or reagent lot effects before downstream analysis.

name: batch-effect-diagnostic-assessment
description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression data are collected across multiple batches or replicates and batch effects must be diagnosed before z-score normalization and clustering.

name: batch-effect-embedding-estimation
description: Use when integrating multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets (e.g. DLPFC or seqFISH sections) whose low-dimensional embeddings contain batch effects that must be estimated jointly with spatial clustering.

name: batch-effect-integration-across-tissue-sections
description: Use when analyzing multiple SRT tissue sections (e.g. six mouse embryo seqFISH sections or twelve human DLPFC sections) where cross-sample batch effects must be estimated simultaneously with spatial domain clustering, and integrated clustering metrics are needed.

name: batch-effect-quantification-ilisi
description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods (e.g., BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, Scanorama) on integrated scRNA-seq datasets and you need a numeric mixing-vs-structure tradeoff score such as mean iLISI and mean 50-RNN.

name: batch-effect-quantification-scoring
description: Use when comparing imputed vs. raw scRNA-Seq matrices for batch correction on datasets with known batch and cell-type annotations (e.g., Villani PBMC GSE80171, Baron pancreatic islet) and numeric batch-merging scores are needed.

name: batch-effect-quantification-via-kl-divergence
description: Use when per-cell batch labels and a low-dimensional representation (e.g., DESC's X_Embeded_z in adata.obsm) or derived quantities such as Monocle3 pseudotime are available, and you need a numeric, distribution-level measure of whether batches are well mixed.

name: batch-effect-removal-across-protocols
description: Use when combining scRNA-seq count matrices generated by different library-preparation protocols or batches, and the goal is cell-type clustering with batch effect removed in a single joint analysis (measured by ARI and cell-type classification accuracy).

name: batch-effect-removal-cross-assay
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq and ST count matrices measured on the same shared gene space from different experiments or patients, and a domain-invariant latent feature is needed before spatial projection or joint clustering.

name: batch-effect-removal-cross-dataset-integration
description: Use when combining two scRNA-Seq datasets generated in different labs/protocols (e.g., Hockley GSE102962 target with Usoskin GSE59739 source) prior to clustering, and you want to test whether batch correction improves cluster recovery.

name: batch-effect-removal-evaluation
description: Use when assessing whether a scRNA-seq clustering method removes batch effects: you have count matrices with multiple batch metadata fields (e.g., donor, region, sample IDs) and reference cell-type labels to score with ARI.

name: batch-effect-removal-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq integration methods on held-out <condition,batch> matrices and you need ARI/ASW-batch values on shared vs condition-specific latent factors to judge batch-removal quality.

name: batch-effect-robust-cell-annotation
description: Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Smart-seq2) must be annotated against a clustered reference (e.g. Drop-seq) across technologies with batch effect and strongly imbalanced cell numbers or library sizes per cell.

name: batch-effect-scaling-scenario-design
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods or metrics and you need controlled ground truth where batch effect strength and cell type DE are known by construction (e.g., testing whether iLISI rewards overcorrection).

name: batch-effect-scenario-design
description: Use when benchmarking batch integration/correction methods requires controlled simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with tunable batch-effect magnitude, dropout, batch-size imbalance, or cell-type composition.

name: batch-effect-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking CITE-seq clustering methods under controlled regimes (clustering signal, dropout, batch effect) where simulated paired mRNA/ADT data with ground-truth cell-type labels are needed for reproducible comparison.

name: batch-effect-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking batch-effect removal, condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection, or perturbation prediction methods and ground-truth data with known condition effects and batch labels are required.

name: batch-effect-simulation-parameter-design
description: Use when a benchmark of batch-correction or multi-source integration methods needs simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with known cell-type and batch effect magnitudes instead of real data lacking ground truth.

name: batch-effects-correction-single-cell-rna-seq
description: Use when integrating raw scRNA-seq read count matrices across multiple batches or platforms (e.g., GEO datasets like GSE85241 or GSE86473) where cell-type labels are unknown and batch effects and dropout events must be corrected before clustering.

name: batch-entropy-mixing-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking multiple scRNA-seq integration/annotation pipelines on batch-involved datasets and you need quantitative batch-mixing and cell-type-structure metrics plus significance testing between pipelines.

name: batch-integration-metric-computation
description: Use when you have latent embeddings from one or more single-cell batch-integration methods plus per-cell batch and cell type labels, and need quantitative ASW scores to rank integration quality.

name: batch-integration-metric-computation-kbet-ilisi
description: Use when comparing velocity models across batches on example_bifurcation.h5ad and you need quantitative evidence that batch correction improved both cell-state mixing (kBET, iLISI, cLISI) and velocity fidelity (CBDir, ICCoh, NN velocity cosine).

name: batch-integration-workflow-comparison
description: Use when you have one or more scRNA-seq perturbation datasets (e.g. drug-treatment vs control) with ground-truth labels and need to compare ICAT against conventional integration workflows quantitatively by ARI, LISI, and DB.

name: batch-lisi-computation
description: Use when you have aligned joint embeddings from multiple single-cell modalities (e.g., Full PBMC, Partial PBMC, BM datasets aligned by scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, or SCOTv2) and need to quantify modality mixing for benchmarking.

name: batch-mixing-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have embeddings from ≥2 batch integration methods (e.g. JOINTLY, scVI, Harmony, Scanorama, LIGER, fastMNN, Seurat, scGPT) run on the same multi-batch sxRNA-seq datasets with cell type labels and need a comparable rank table.

name: batch-mixing-metric-evaluation-asw
description: Use when a multi-patient, multi-condition scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 6-patient GBM, DMSO vs 0.2 uM panobinostat) has been factorized and you must score batch effect removal (ASW-batch) and cell-type separation (ARI) across methods.

name: batch-mixing-quantification-kbet
description: Use when an scRNA-seq/velocity dataset spans multiple sequencing batches (e.g. 3 mouse gastrulation batches) and you need to verify that a latent embedding corrects batch effects without destroying velocity signal.

name: batch-parallel-cell-classification
description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) of tumor biopsies and need fully unsupervised, automatic malignant/non-malignant cell classification without manually picking reference cell clusters, ideally across many samples in parallel.

name: batch-partitioned-single-cell-preprocessing
description: Use when preprocessing large scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. PBMCs-SLE >1.25M cells, PBMCs-HED >2M cells) in .h5ad/anndata format where full in-memory loading would exceed available RAM and low-resource execution is required.

name: batch-query-throughput-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify query scalability of an indexed sequence-collection structure (e.g. PAC) by timing batches of many sequences — from tens to hundreds of thousands — against a fixed index and compiling runtime and memory measurements.

name: batched-graph-computation
description: Use when building k-NN graphs over thousands of single cells (or other large point sets) where full pairwise distance computation would exhaust memory, and downstream label propagation must run on the graph.

name: bayes-factor-based-edge-ranking
description: Use when you have preprocessed scRNA-seq expression (counts rescaled into (0,1)) with a small refined candidate TF set and need a ranked, directed TF-gene edge list or top logic gates per target gene.

name: bayes-factor-confidence-scoring
description: Use when scGATE has fit a zero-inflated mixture likelihood to a target gene's expression and you need a confidence score to select or rank the most probable Boolean logic gate among candidate regulatory TFs.

name: bayes-factor-differential-module-testing
description: Use when comparing per-cell gene module variational (GMV) activities inferred by VEGA between two cell groups (or one-vs-rest across annotated cell types) to call significantly activated pathways, TF regulons, or cell type marker sets.

name: bayes-factor-model-comparison
description: Use when comparing probabilistic phase-inference models (Tempo vs Cyclops, Cyclum, PCA) on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, per-cell-type measure of the evidence favoring one model's phase estimates over another's.

name: bayes-mean-score-computation
description: Use when you have reCAT's test_exp (cycle base genes, log2(TPM+1)) and a consensus-TSP ordIndex, and need Bayes- and mean-scores to segment cells into cycle stages or to compare pseudo-time methods via correlation-scores/change-index values.

name: bayesian-cell-genotype-mixture-assignment
