description: Use when scRNA-seq data (e.g. 10x/GemCode 3' gene-barcode matrices from bone marrow mononuclear cells of transplant patients) must be decomposed into host vs donor cell genotypes without a prior known genotype.

name: bayesian-colocalization-prior-configuration
description: Use when testing whether cis-eQTL signals are shared across tissues (e.g., GTEx v8) and LD inflation from distinct causal variants must be accounted for via Bayesian colocalization.

name: bayesian-confidence-interval-inference
description: Use when smoothed individual cell fate trajectories from time-course scRNA-seq are available and the goal is a time-resolved gene-gene network plus identification of critical (differentially expressed) genes during differentiation.

name: bayesian-cycler-gene-threshold-selection
description: Use when after Tempo Step 1 phase inference, you must expand the core-clock cycler set de novo — i.e., classify which currently non-cycling genes from a scRNA-seq anndata matrix are described by 24 h phase variation before refitting the model.

name: bayesian-dirichlet-multinomial-modeling
description: Use when per-sample cell-type counts from scRNA-seq (or similar compositional count data) must be tested for differential abundance across conditions, especially with few replicates.

name: bayesian-fdr-gene-selection
description: Use when a fitted BUSseq SingleCellExperiment object is available and the goal is to rank genes by posterior cell-type-effect indicator mass and control Bayesian FDR at a stated alpha (e.g. 0.05) to call intrinsic genes.

name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-fitting-scrnaseq
description: Use when you have per-gene summary statistics (beta and beta variance, or p-values convertible via qnorm) from a scRNA-seq DE tool such as zingeR-DESeq2 and want joint DE + gene set enrichment analysis with permutation-based empirical FDR.

name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-mcmc-inference
description: Use when raw multi-batch scRNA-seq read count matrices contain unknown cell subtypes with batch effects and dropouts, and you need simultaneous batch correction and clustering without prior normalization or subtype labels.

name: bayesian-hierarchical-model-posterior-use
description: Use when you have a fitted BUSseq model object (e.g., sce_BUSseqfit from BUSseq_MCMC) and need corrected count data free of batch effects and dropout for downstream analysis, cell-type-colored t-SNE, or DE testing.

name: bayesian-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when base classifiers were built with pre-set, experience-derived hyperparameters and you need to systematically tune them to maximize k-fold cross-validation accuracy before stacking or comparison.

name: bayesian-log-expression-mmse-estimation
description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq UMI read count matrix (e.g. GSE120861 highmoi, Cell Ranger sparse mtx or tsv) and normalized log expression is needed as the basis for Normalisr's downstream association testing.

name: bayesian-matrix-factorization-imputation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has high dropout (the article notes 40%-90% missing values) and downstream goals are cell clustering, pseudotime/trajectory inference, or visualization that depends on recovering cell-to-cell relationships.

name: bayesian-mixture-model-clustering
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from several individuals (e.g. 10x Genomics Chromium libraries) show batch effects or individual-level heterogeneity and single-individual methods like DIMM-SC or naive merging produce unreliable clusters.

name: bayesian-mixture-model-em-inference
description: Use when inferring cell-type-specific TF-gene networks and Boolean logic gates from a small, pre-selected set of TFs and target genes in single-cell expression data, given a candidate base GRN.

name: bayesian-mixture-model-selection
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq SNV calls yield a per-cell fraction of reads supporting each species/genotype and you must decide if the population is a mixture of two genotypes, assign cells, and quantify multiplets.

name: bayesian-model-averaging-de-evidence
description: Use when scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (beta, se_beta) are already fitted with iDEA.fit and you want gene-level posterior DE probabilities that exploit consistent DE evidence across overlapping gene sets rather than gene-by-gene testing.

name: bayesian-model-averaging-posterior-inclusion-probability
description: Use when gene-level DE summary statistics (beta coefficients and variances) from tools like MAST, edgeR, or zingeR are available and you want to strengthen per-gene DE calls by aggregating evidence across gene set fits rather than testing one gene at a time.

name: bayesian-model-comparison-bayes-factor
description: Use when a 3D-aligned spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., STARmap mouse brain slices stacked by Scube) is available and you need to flag spatially variable genes by testing directional expression variation in 3D.

name: bayesian-model-evidence-evaluation
description: Use when an unsupervised variational inference loop (e.g., Tempo phase inference) needs a principled termination criterion, or when deciding whether adding de novo detected cycler genes improves or worsens model fit to core clock genes.

name: bayesian-network-ontology-correction
description: Use when benchmarking generative Bayesian-network correction (BNC, URSA) of per-term Cell Ontology classifier probabilities against discriminative baselines (independent classifiers, IR, TPR) on human RNA-seq data.

name: bayesian-parametric-comparator-design-implementation
description: Use when benchmarking a novel phase I/II dose-finding design against established Bayesian parametric designs (Thall–Cook P1, Yin et al. P2) in Monte Carlo simulations with a fixed highest acceptable DLT rate phi.

name: bayesian-posterior-rule-inference
description: Use when you have a preprocessed (0,1)-rescaled scRNA-seq matrix for one cell type/context, a small candidate TF list (k<=5) per target gene, and you need the combinatorial Boolean rule (not just directed edges) linking TFs to each target.

name: bayesian-posterior-significance-thresholding
description: Use when you have a fitted PhenoPath model (phenopath_fit) and need to rank and call significant covariate-trajectory interaction effects per gene, e.g. stimulant-pseudotime interactions for LPS vs PAM in the Shalek dendritic cell data.

name: bayesian-spike-and-slab-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when testing cell-type compositional changes across few biological replicates (e.g. 7 supercentenarian vs 5 control PBMC samples) from an NxK cell-type count matrix with a binary covariate, where univariate tests would inflate false positives.

name: bayesian-spike-and-slab-effect-selection
description: Use when scRNA-seq samples (or other count compositional data) are aggregated per sample into cell-type counts and you need differential abundance testing that controls the FDR, especially with a low number of experimental replicates.

name: bayesian-variational-phase-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq counts (e.g., droplet-based 10X data stored as anndata) must be ordered over the circadian cycle without sample-time labels, and phase point estimates plus uncertainty are needed.

name: bayesspace-spatial-clustering
description: Use when a SeqScope/Slide-seq/VISIUM digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates has too few UMIs per spatial barcode for direct cell-type clustering and barcodes must be aggregated into grids before Seurat/BayesSpace clustering.

name: bcell-tcell-marker-contamination-assessment
description: Use when validating a segmentation method's biological accuracy on non-Xenium SST platforms (NanoString CosMx lung, Vizgen MERSCOPE melanoma) by quantifying cross-cell-type marker contamination and cell-type homogeneity.

name: bcr-repertoire-inference-from-rnaseq
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq reads (ribo-depleted or polyA, ≥25M reads/sample) from B-cell/CLL samples must be converted into full-length IGHV gene reconstructions with SHM/hypermutation (IGHV-mutated vs unmutated) classification.

name: bcv-noise-corruption-of-simulated-counts
description: Use when benchmarking feature selection or trajectory inference methods under quantitatively controlled signal-to-noise regimes, requiring simulated scRNA-seq count data with known ground-truth genes and labels.

name: bed-format-count-output-generation
description: Use when you have a UMI-to-genomic-position mapping (umi_positions.txt) and need position-level UMI counts in BED format for downstream annotation intersection.

name: bed-genomic-interval-intersection
description: Use when preparing a custom gene model BED for SkewC gene body coverage and rRNA/tRNA sequences must be removed from a reference gene annotation.

name: beene-nonlinear-embedding-training
description: Use when you have a gene expression matrix (samples x genes) with batch labels (and optionally biological labels) and need a nonlinear embedding to detect or quantify batch effects, especially when PCA may miss nonlinear batch structure.

name: benchmark-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a new or existing cluster-level cell type annotation method must be quantitatively benchmarked on scRNA-seq datasets whose true cluster labels are known from published literature.

name: benchmark-auc-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare cell-cell communication inference methods (e.g., MDIC3 vs CellChat) on the same scRNA-seq dataset using literature-supported ground truth and AUC, rather than relying on qualitative claims.

name: benchmark-cell-label-processing
description: Use when you need ground-truth positive/negative cell–cell interaction labels from scRNA-seq data (e.g. panc8 with benchmark cell labels) to supervise training of an interaction inference model via a majority vote of statistical L-R methods.

name: benchmark-comparison-across-integration-methods
description: Use when you have paired scDNA-seq copy-number and scRNA-seq expression data with partially known clone labels and need to compare integration methods' cell-to-clone assignment accuracy.

name: benchmark-comparison-against-published-metrics
description: Use when a paper reports headline metrics (e.g. MCC/F1 on named test datasets) and you have access to the model or code deposit, so you can recompute metrics and diff them against the published benchmark values.

name: benchmark-comparison-against-reported-metrics
description: Use when a paper reports concrete per-sample quantitative results (e.g., identified-read counts/ratios) on named public datasets (e.g., SAMN accessions) and you must independently reproduce and compare them.

name: benchmark-comparison-of-cell-annotation-methods
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare automated cell-type annotation methods on the same clustered scRNA-seq datasets, with controlled marker inputs, accuracy counts, and runtime measurements.

name: benchmark-comparison-of-de-methods
description: Use when you must validate a temporal differential expression method's detection performance against established DE tools on simulated single-cell counts with a known ground-truth gene set.

name: benchmark-comparison-of-scoring-approaches
description: Use when evaluating whether Cytocipher's cluster-merge can discriminate significant vs non-significant cluster pairs on simulated over-clustered scRNA-seq data, or when comparing scoring methods via AUROC against known subcluster labels.

name: benchmark-comparison-table-compilation
description: Use when several malignant-cell classifiers must be evaluated on identical scRNA-seq datasets with shared ground-truth labels and their metrics need compiling into one reproducible comparison table.

name: benchmark-comparison-table-generation
description: Use when a new clustering method must be benchmarked against existing ensemble and single-cell baselines across multiple datasets and an ARI/NMI comparison table with per-dataset rankings is the deliverable.

name: benchmark-count-reproduction
description: Use when validating or benchmarking a published bioinformatics pipeline by re-executing its workflow steps on the same inputs and checking that every reported count matches the original paper's numbers.

name: benchmark-curve-visualization
description: Use when reproducing label-noise robustness curves for (semi)supervised integration methods: you have integration scores at 0–100% shuffled or 0–100% 'unknown' label corruption and need method-comparison curves per task.

name: benchmark-dataset-evaluation-across-repositories
description: Use when you need to evaluate a filter-based feature-selection algorithm on standard UCI/ASU benchmark datasets and compare out-of-sample classification performance as a function of the number of selected features.

name: benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Reference for when you need the standard scSHARP evaluation datasets (two Splatter simulations, mouse testis, human PBMC) to reproduce or compare cell-type annotation results.

name: benchmark-dataset-method-comparison
description: Use when evaluating how a new trajectory-inference method's predicted topology compares to established methods (Slingshot, TinGa) on benchmark single-cell datasets with ground-truth clustering and known milestone networks.

name: benchmark-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you must show that a spatially aware colorization method (e.g. Spaco's graph-guided palette) yields significantly more discernible colors than a default palette, using pairwise color-difference distributions.

name: benchmark-figure-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or validate published rare-cell detection benchmarks on the 68k PBMC subsampled rare-cell (99) and doublet (140) datasets, or to re-derive F1, runtime, and peak-memory comparisons across RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS, FiRE and GapClust.

name: benchmark-gene-list-mapping
description: Use when you have driver gene prediction lists for multiple tools (e.g. from DriverDBv2) and need to rank them against curated benchmark sets (CGC 616 genes, NCG 711 genes, PMH 501 genes) with an F-measure.

name: benchmark-ground-truth-label-chaining
description: Use when a cell hashing Seurat object and published SNP-based (scSplit) ground-truth labels are both available and you need to correlate hashing singlet groups with genotype clusters to produce validated per-cell sample identity labels.

name: benchmark-method-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when comparing label-transfer methods (e.g., scID vs scmap, CaSTLe, scVI) that map cells from a target scRNA-seq dataset to clusters of a reference dataset, and you need coverage and accuracy metrics on a common benchmark.

name: benchmark-method-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when multiple active subnetwork detection methods have each recovered a subnetwork from the same seed (disease) genes or gene P-values and you must quantify method-to-method structural overlap via pairwise Jaccard similarity.

name: benchmark-method-comparison
description: Use when you must objectively compare a new CCI inference method against existing ones (e.g. SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, CellPhoneDB, CellChat, CellCall, CytoTalk, NATMI) on a shared scRNA-seq dataset with a literature-supported ground-truth interaction set.

name: benchmark-method-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when a new analysis tool claims parity with existing tools and the claim must be validated by running both on identical inputs (e.g. .h5ad AnnData with sample/cluster/condition columns) and comparing per-feature significance calls.

name: benchmark-method-comparison-against-ground-truth
description: Use when paired scDNA-seq (CNA) and scRNA-seq (gene expression) data from the same cells provide partial ground-truth clone labels, and multiple integration methods must be ranked on cell-to-clone assignment accuracy and clonal prevalence prediction.

name: benchmark-method-comparison-single-cell
description: Use when a new single-cell fate-mapping method must be validated against a published baseline (e.g., CellRank) by checking whether known terminal states, such as hormone-producing α, β, and ε cells, are consistently recovered.

name: benchmark-method-power-comparison
description: Use when validating a statistical detection method's false discovery rate calibration and power against existing methods using simulated signal spiked into a null dataset with known gold-standard positives.

name: benchmark-metric-reproduction
description: Use when a task specifies a published numeric benchmark (e.g. accuracy 0.94, specificity 0.98, sensitivity 0.90 on a 30% held-out test set) that must be verified by re-running the classifier end-to-end.

name: benchmark-metric-reproduction-across-species
description: Use when replicating a published lncRNA-vs-PCT classifier's benchmark table on multi-species transcript datasets to check reported ACC, SEN, SPE, F1, PRE, MCC, and AUC values.

name: benchmark-performance-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods (e.g., SINGE, SINCERITIES, SCODE) across pseudotime/trajectory variants on ordered single-cell expression data, scored with AUROC/AUPRC overall and per regulator.

name: benchmark-performance-table-assembly
description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation tools across benchmark single-cell datasets with reliable ground truth, to produce a comparable performance/runtime table.

name: benchmark-performance-visualization
description: Use when comparing IPA-detection tools (InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder) on simulated RNA-seq data with known ground-truth polyA sites, and you need sensitivity/precision-vs-coverage figures and IPA-usage error plots.

name: benchmark-precision-curve-visualization
description: Use when you have ranked driver-regulator lists (with influence scores) from multiple methods and curated ground-truth gene sets (e.g. GO:0045165, GO:0019827, GO:0007492) and need to compute/plot top-k precision curves for benchmarking.

name: benchmark-result-aggregation-across-omics
description: Use when you have per-method activity score matrices from decoupleR benchmark runs (e.g. run_rna_bench.R / run_php_bench.R outputs on Zenodo record 5645208) and need to quantify whether different inference methods produce similar regulator activity estimates.

name: benchmark-result-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to verify a published quantitative claim (e.g. that scMGCA attains the highest ASW on 'QS Trachea' and 'QS Heart') by re-executing the full method-vs-baseline comparison on the original benchmark scRNA-seq datasets.

name: benchmark-result-tabulation
description: Use when comparing isoform-assembly tools on the same dataset and you need a machine-readable, validated summary table (e.g. assembler vs. uniquely_assigned_isoforms) derived from IsoQuant assignment files.

name: benchmark-result-tabulation
description: Use when timing a pipeline (e.g. scSPARKL on Spark) across multiple dataset sizes or executor/driver memory configurations and you need a per-subsample runtime table comparable to a sequential implementation.

name: benchmark-result-tabulation
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (CPU time and wall-clock time) of pathogen-quantification tools for 10x single-cell data on one identical sample, to produce a ranked runtime table.

name: benchmark-results-aggregation-and-visualization
description: Use when a perturbation benchmark has produced per-regulator activity scores for multiple decoupleR methods and you must aggregate them into per-method performance metrics and ranking comparisons.

name: benchmark-results-tabulation
description: Use when replacing a full SVD routine (e.g. base R svd) with a partial/truncated SVD (e.g. RSpectra::svds) inside an iterative algorithm like JIVE, and you need runtime evidence that the substitution preserves the computation while cutting cost.

name: benchmark-results-visualization
description: Use when multiple automatic cell-type identification methods have been run over shared train/test scRNA-seq splits (e.g., Smart-seq2 training, 10x testing in Tabula Muris) and you must rank them by accuracy, F1-score, and unlabeling rate and render comparison figures.

name: benchmark-runtime-aggregation-and-visualization
description: Use when comparing execution runtimes of multiple analysis tools (e.g., AnnSQL vs AnnData) across a series of dataset sizes and you need statistical comparison plus a visualized, tabulated runtime summary.

name: benchmark-runtime-measurement
description: Use when evaluating an automated cell-type annotation method against curated expert labels on atlas-scale tissues and you need reproducible metrics (balanced accuracy, label similarity) plus wall-clock run time for comparison against published benchmarks.

name: benchmark-runtime-profiling-and-comparison
description: Use when a claim about an optimal-transport or sample-level single-cell method's scalability to millions of cells must be validated by measuring and comparing end-to-end wall-clock runtimes across competing pipelines.

name: benchmark-scaling-curve-reconstruction
description: Use when comparing how runtime and peak memory scale with read count for an alignment-free pseudoaligner (fortuna) versus spliced-align-and-count baselines (Whippet, STAR + sigcount) on subsampled FASTQ data.

name: benchmark-score-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-run score tables (e.g., KMD silhouette vs. accuracy for every scanned k value) over repeated dataset instances and need to quantify score–performance agreement, e.g., median Pearson correlation across instances.

name: benchmark-score-aggregation-and-ranking
description: Use when benchmark results from multiple cross-species integration strategies must be reduced to a single ranked score per task, e.g. after running scIB metrics on integrated embeddings from tasks like Pancreas_hs_mm or Hippocampus_hs_mu_ss.

name: benchmark-score-normalization-tabulation
description: Use when comparing colorization or spatial-metric performance across cluster-pair configurations and you need per-metric normalized scores tabulated (e.g., a Figure 2B/2C-style benchmark of DOI vs Wasserstein vs LISI vs KDE-Jaccard).

name: benchmark-score-reproduction
description: Use when a published cell-cell communication score (e.g., ICELLNET score 1527 for CM3->CT3b vs 1123 for CM3->CT0a) must be exactly reproduced from raw expression data to validate a pipeline or benchmark a method.

name: benchmark-score-table-aggregation
description: Use when cluster label assignments from multiple scRNA-seq clustering methods must be scored against ground-truth cell-type annotations and compiled into a per-dataset, per-method ARI/AMI/NMI comparison table.

name: benchmark-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when comparing module-detection or sub-network-inference methods on RNA-seq data where ground-truth sub-networks are known or embedded, and sensitivity/robustness must be quantified and statistically compared.

name: benchmark-sensitivity-evaluation
description: Use when you need to benchmark TF activity inference methods against perturbation experiments (e.g. Holland et al. 2020 transcriptomics) and rank methods like ULM, MLM, VIPER, AUCell by sensitivity.

name: benchmark-sensitivity-precision-f1-computation
description: Use when comparing fcircRNA or fusion-junction detection tools against a simulated ground truth and you need sensitivity, precision, and F1 per tool to demonstrate ity (e.g., INTEGRATE-Circ 87.3% sensitivity vs Fcirc 57.1%).

name: benchmark-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when a miRNA/small RNA detection method must be benchmarked against a reference truth set (e.g., SRP120169) and you need quantitative sensitivity/specificity, including per-abundance-tier performance.

name: benchmark-table-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports head-to-head quantitative scores (ARI/ASW/kBET) for multiple integration methods on a shared dataset and the goal is to regenerate that table from raw data within rounding tolerance.

name: benchmark-tool-score-comparison
description: Use when you have an annotated scRNA-seq count matrix with a known stem/progenitor compartment and need to compare ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR and CytoTRACE scores across cell types to judge which tool identifies stem cells correctly.

name: benchmark-versus-real-dataset-comparison
description: Use when you have HTO count matrices from multiple published or in-house datasets plus benchmark/simulated references, and need to know if real data quality (component overlap) is comparable to benchmarks or degraded enough that demultiplexing results are method-sensitive.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when a differential expression meta-analysis yields one combined P value per gene per cell subtype and you must control multiplicity before ranking marker genes (e.g., recovering Sst, Pvalb, Vip, Cck, Htr3a as subtype discriminators).

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when many candidate biomarkers (e.g., 16 gene expression programs or transferred qPHATE coordinates) each yield a Cox regression treatment-effect contrast and the family of p-values must be FDR-corrected before declaring significance.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when you have raw per-gene p-values from a two-group differential expression test (e.g. a Wilcoxon rank-sum test between user-defined cell groups) and need FDR-corrected values before ranking marker genes.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when you have raw p-values from multiple testing methods (e.g., progressionTest, fateSelectionTest, DAseq, milo) on the same features/genes and need binary differential calls at a controlled false discovery rate of 5% for downstream performance evaluation.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-correction
description: Use when a gene-list enrichment run (E.PAGE compute/compute_sets over the curated 522-module, 25,789-gene database) produces many raw hypergeometric p-values that must be adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing before filtering significant environmental modules.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-estimation
description: Use when testing differential regulatory relations between two conditions from paired single-cell data and needing calibrated p-values/FDR for the likelihood ratio statistic, especially when the standard Chi-square null appears anti-conservative.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many parallel hypothesis tests must be thresholded with false-discovery-rate control — e.g., hundreds of GO over-representation tests on top-ranked communities per donor per time point — and an adjusted-p (BH FDR 0.05) significance call is required.

name: benjamini-hochberg-fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when PAIRADISE's Step 5 statistical model (LRT on delta_i) has produced thousands of raw event-level p-values and you must control the false discovery fraction across tests to call ASAS event-SNP pairs at FDR <= 10%.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-adjustment
description: Use when a hypothesis-testing co-expression method (CS-CORE, Pearson, Spearman, locCSN, normalisr, NoiseRegularization) yields one p-value per gene pair across a p x p matrix, and the network must be thresholded or PR curves computed.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a single analysis produces many pathway-enrichment p-values (e.g. 100 scETM topics tested against MSigDB Canonical Pathways or PsyGeNET gene sets) and significant topic-pathway associations must be controlled for false discovery.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a gene-set activity analysis tests many gene sets simultaneously and raw empirical p-values (e.g. ppv L1, ppv Median Exp from rROMA) must be adjusted before classifying modules as significant.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many paired statistical tests (e.g., matched perturbed-vs-control Wilcoxon tests over hundreds of TF-gene edges) have been run and raw p-values must be FDR-adjusted before calling significant edges.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a gene-wise statistical test (e.g., limma moderated t-statistics across 46 cases and 23 controls) yields thousands of raw P-values that must be FDR-adjusted before ranking seeds or thresholding DEGs.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many gene-set (GO_BP/KEGG) enrichment tests are run in parallel — e.g., one test per detected RGM or SCENIC regulon on the hESC, mESC, or mHSC lineage datasets — and per-module significance must be assessed with a threshold that accounts for multiple testing.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when you have thousands of per-gene isoform (or TSS/polyA) chi-square p-values from a scisorseqr region-vs-region comparison and need FDR-controlled DIE calls with an effect-size (delta-PI) filter.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many hypothesis tests (e.g., GSEA on 22 KEGG-derived LR pathway sets per factor) produce raw P-values per condition, and FDR-controlled adjusted P-values are needed for a factor-by-pathway results table.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when hundreds of module-vs-term hypergeometric tests are performed (e.g., 137 MCA GEPs against GO/MP gene sets) and enriched terms must be reported with BH-adjusted p-values alongside raw p-values and enrichment ratios.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when NeuronChat (or analogous permutation-based cell-cell communication inference) has produced raw per-interaction p-values across many ligand-receptor pairs and you need FDR-controlled significance calls before retaining or zeroing links.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a tncRNA count matrix with ≥3 biological replicates per condition is being tested for differential expression across many tncRNA loci and per-locus p-values must be corrected for multiple testing before significance calling.

name: benjamini-hochberg-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many parallel significance tests have been run (e.g. one hypergeometric GO over-representation test per bicluster across 151 UniBic biclusters) and enrichment calls must control the false discovery rate before tallying proportions.

name: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-adjustment
description: Use when a per-cluster marker gene list has been tested against cell-type gene sets (e.g. easyct with test='fisher') and the family of candidate cell-type p-values within each cluster must be FDR-adjusted before ranking annotations.

name: benjamini-hochberg-pvalue-correction
description: Use when many per-gene hypothesis tests (e.g. Fisher's exact tests on gene-cluster absence/presence per lifestyle) yield a vector of p-values that must be FDR-corrected before ranking candidate lifestyle-associated genes.

name: bernoulli-direction-enrichment-testing
description: Use when an analysis reduces to binary directional calls per gene or exon — TSS shift direction in pairwise DIE comparisons, or same/opposite delta-PSI between single-cell and spatial measurements — and an exact enrichment p-value against a 50/50 null is required.

name: bernoulli-dropout-simulation-single-cell
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell clustering robustness on in silico mixtures (e.g., GM12878/K562) by injecting controlled dropout into expression E and openness O matrices at rates such as 0, 0.5, 0.8, 0.9.

name: bert-peptide-sequence-embedding
description: Use when transcript-derived peptide sequences (e.g., translated longest ORFs from Orfipy with transl_table=1) must be converted into fixed-size contextual vectors to augment ORF-attention features for lncRNA vs PCT classification.

name: best-algorithm-per-dataset-identification
description: Use when a reproduced benchmark table of random-forest misclassification percentages (1…min(M,30) selected features per FS algorithm) is available and you need to name the algorithm per dataset and compare binary vs multi-class winners.

name: beta-binomial-cna-state-mixture-inference
description: Use when phased allelic counts (integer 'AD'/'DP' layers) are available for scRNA-seq cells and you need to infer per-cell, per-bin allele-imbalance CNA state probabilities that are robust to sparse, low-coverage variant counts.

name: beta-binomial-mixture-classification
description: Use when estimating per-cell per-gene allelic expression states (P/B/M) from low-coverage allele-specific scRNA-Seq counts (e.g., F1 hybrid CAST×B6 data), where U-shaped allelic-proportion distributions and sampling zeros require borrowing information across cells.

name: beta-binomial-psi-estimation
description: Use when you have a cell-by-isoform count matrix from single-cell Nanopore long reads and need to estimate inter-cell splicing heterogeneity (phi) versus psi at exon/splice sites, distinguishing isoform co-expression within cells.

name: beta-binomial-read-count-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic bulk DNA and single-cell RNA read counts with known ground-truth clonal trees (Z, Ps) to quantify reconstruction error of tumor phylogeny inference methods.

name: beta-binomial-zero-inflation-modeling
description: Use when single-cell mutation read counts (e.g., Rs/Xs matrices) show excess zeros from transcriptional bursting or dropout, and you need overdispersed counts modeling that decomposes zeros rather than a plain binomial likelihood.

name: beta-cell-subset-construction-pancreas
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods (scETM, Harmony, Scanorama, Seurat, LIGER, scVI, scVAE-GM) for over-correction, by removing a cell type (beta cells) from all Human Pancreas batches except CelSeq2.

name: beta-poisson-gene-expression-modeling
description: Use when preparing Canopy2 inputs from single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Smart-seq2 data such as GBM10_preproc): you need mutation-specific alpha/beta bursting rates to model stochastic zeros before running get_trees(), and you have a gene expression count matrix.

name: between-group-expression-difference-verification
description: Use when single reference gene normalization (ERgene.normalizationdata) has been applied and you must show, via before/after boxplots and density plots, that the between-group spectral density difference (e.g., SHED vs salt injection) is reduced relative to raw data.

name: betweenness-centrality-analysis
description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods on topology: you have inferred network graphs (edges between genes) and need scale-free fit R-squared, edge/gene counts, betweenness centrality variance, and split-half edge overlap scores.

name: bgc-gene-cluster-family-clustering
description: Use when you need biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) detection and Gene Cluster Family-level absence/presence encoding across many bacterial genomes, as a comparative-genomics feature matrix.

name: bhattacharyya-kernel-construction
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix has already been converted to a stationary diffusion distribution matrix S via RWR and you need a valid inner-product kernel plus 2D/3D embedding for pseudotime ordering.

name: bhattacharyya-kernel-feature-decomposition
description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix with developmental stage labels must be embedded in low dimensions for pseudotime trajectory visualization, e.g. ordering mouse embryo cells across the 1-cell to 64-cell stages.

name: biaxial-protein-expression-plotting
description: Use when dsb-normalized protein values (and cell cluster labels) are available and you need cytometry-style biaxial plots to verify that clusters and UMAP reproduce expected immune cell population structure.

name: bic-based-model-order-selection
description: Use when single-cell CITE-seq / ADT protein count distributions (after dsb step-I log(pseudocount 10) transformation and empty-droplet standardization) must be modeled with Gaussian mixtures and the number of mixture components needs a principled, per-cell choice.

name: bic-based-model-selection-over-cell-type-number
description: Use when fitting BUSseq to a multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrix and the true number of cell types K is unknown, so the latent subtype count must be chosen by comparing BIC values across candidate K.

name: bic-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when fitting Gaussian mixture models to principal components of scCRISPR-seq control/perturbation expression data and the number of cell clusters K is unknown and must be chosen objectively.

name: bic-regularization-parameter-selection
description: Use when fitting scLink's weighted graphical lasso (QUIC) and a sparsity level must be chosen objectively: run sclink_net over lda = seq(0.5, 0.1, -0.05) and pick the lambda minimizing BIC from the summary output.

name: bic-subclone-model-selection
description: Use when inferring a tumor phylogeny from bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq SNV data and the number of subclones K is unknown and must be chosen by a model-selection criterion rather than fixed a priori.

name: bicluster-gene-set-extraction
description: Use when a run of UniBic/runibic has produced trend-preserving biclusters on expression data (e.g. the eight GDS datasets) and you must determine which biclusters are significantly GO-enriched and report their overall proportion.

name: bicluster-relevance-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a biclustering algorithm (e.g. UniBic via runibic) on synthetic matrices with implanted ground-truth biclusters and you need quantitative relevance/recovery scores to compare tools.

name: bicluster-significance-filtering
description: Use when a biclustering run (e.g. UniBic on GEO microarray matrices like GDS589) has produced candidate trend-preserving biclusters and only statistically significant ones should be reported or counted downstream.

name: biclustering-algorithm-parameter-configuration
description: Use when you need to run UniBic/runibic on a continuous gene expression matrix (or discrete data with BCUnibicD) and must set its algorithm parameters (significance level, extension error rates, number of output biclusters) correctly or reproduce published runs.

name: biclustering-result-verification
description: Use when you have biclusters (e.g. trend-preserving biclusters from UniBic/runibic with significance p < 0.05) and need to verify they are biologically meaningful by GO enrichment testing and comparison against published proportions.

name: bicubic-gene-expression-overlay-interpolation
description: Use when a single-cell dataset already has an inferred branching graph and pseudotime (e.g. from STREAM/ElPiGraph stored in anndata) and you must render a density-level trajectory visualization with gene-expression overlays.

name: bidirectional-edge-deduplication
description: Use when counting or intersecting edges from a FAVA (favapy) predicted interaction network — favapy emits each protein pair twice (in both directions), so raw-row counts inflate edge totals and must be deduplicated first.

name: bifurcation-simulation-data-validation
description: Use when validating that MuTrans TCS distinguishes stable from transition cells on the saddle-node bifurcation simulation, or when reproducing the Fig. 2a sharp-transition ordering from example_saddle_node.mlx.

name: bifurcation-timing-inference-from-scseq
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq timecourse or pseudotyped dataset captures a binary lineage branching (e.g. hepatoblast to hepatocyte vs cholangiocyte) and the goal is to locate the transition/tipping point along pseudotime.

name: big-data-train-test-knn-clustering
description: Use when the scRNA-seq input matrix has more than 5,000 cells (e.g. Zilionis with 34,558 cells) and a full network-fusion spectral clustering run is too expensive, so clustering must be learned on a subsample and extended to the rest.

name: bilinear-neural-network-training
description: Use when training an OnClass model on annotated scRNA-seq data (h5ad) with Cell Ontology-mapped labels, to obtain a saved model file that supports seen-term classification and unseen Cell Ontology term prediction.

name: bilinear-resampling-patch-consistency
description: Use when a matrix has been imputed patch-wise (e.g., per-ROI histogram equalization in SERM) and the per-window outputs must be merged into a single globally consistent expression matrix before downstream analyses.

name: bilstm-artifact-scoring-model-training
description: Use when building scFusion's deep-learning artifact-scoring stage: chimeric/fusion candidates extracted from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq alignments must be classified as technical artifacts vs. real fusions before final fusion calls.

name: bimodal-distribution-assessment
description: Use when you need to validate that the top edges (e.g. top 150 filtered edges) of a BoostDiff differential network show condition-specific correlation patterns in the original expression matrix, i.e. bimodal vs unimodal KDE distributions across target conditions.

name: bimodal-gene-distribution-visualization
description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq data generated from small pilot sub-samples (384–2304 cells) must be checked against the original data's per-gene distributions, especially to detect missed bimodal gene patterns.

name: bimodality-test-interpretation
description: Use when annotating a target scRNA-seq dataset in open or open-partial settings and you must decide, from the E-score (entropy/confidence/consistency) distribution alone, whether target-private cell types exist before partitioning cells into known vs unknown groups.

name: bimodality-testing-of-uncertainty-scores
description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a pre-trained source model and you must decide—without manual thresholds or prior information—whether the target contains unseen (novel) cell types based on per-cell uncertainty scores.

name: bin-size-optimization-scwgs
description: Use when configuring scWGS CNA calling resolution: you must choose a bin size for RDR/BAF-based single-cell copy-number analysis or decide if a dataset's coverage (e.g., ~0.5× low-coverage vs >20× PTA-amplified) supports sub-Mb CNA detection.

name: binary-classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing multiple binary classifiers (e.g., lncRNA prediction tools) on a common labeled test set and you need reproducible per-tool accuracy values for a benchmark table.

name: binary-classification-concordance-analysis
description: Use when a per-sample binary call (e.g., mCLL vs uCLL from RNA-seq IGHV percent identity) must be compared sample-by-sample against matched clinical gold-standard labels to quantify agreement.

name: binary-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing binary RNA-modification classifiers (e.g., m5C predictors on A. thaliana or M. musculus datasets) and you need side-by-side Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, AUC tables from TP/TN/FP/FN counts.

name: binary-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing differential detection methods on simulated trajectory data with known ground truth, where each method's per-gene (or per-state) calls must be scored as binary classification metrics.

name: binary-classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have a simulated or labelled scRNA-seq AnnData object with known per-cluster memberships and need to rank enrichment scoring methods by binary classification performance (accuracy, precision, recall, F1) per cluster.

name: binary-classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you need unbiased performance estimates (AUC, accuracy, balanced accuracy) for a binary classifier fitted on high-dimensional transcriptomic data via nested cross-validation with nestedcv, e.g. to compare against vignette-reported values.

name: binary-classifier-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a binary classifier has produced per-site predictions on a labeled, held-out dataset and you must quantify performance as mean accuracy, AUC, specificity, and precision against gold-standard positives/negatives.

name: binary-classifier-auc-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a trained fusion-read filter (e.g., HVLD retrained per dataset on artificial chimeric negatives and PCAWG positives) and comparing its AUC to competing models on held-out single-cell RNA-seq test samples.

name: binary-classifier-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g. a Keras/TensorFlow viral-read model) must be scored on a labeled held-out test partition and compared to baselines under identical data.

name: binary-classifier-performance-metrics
description: Use when several tuned binary classifiers (e.g. LR, DT, SVM, RF, XGBoost) must be ranked on a held-out labeled test set to decide which algorithm a tool should adopt, as in LncDC's five-algorithm selection on H-Test.

name: binary-classifier-power-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a binary classifier trained on simulated OU-process expression data (or any two-class problem) must be scored for power and accuracy on a balanced test set, especially after training on skewed/unbalanced training data.

name: binary-fate-classification-auroc-evaluation
description: Use when validating whether a trajectory/fate model's predicted fate-bias probabilities match observed clonal outcomes on a held-out progenitor set (e.g. the 335-cell Weinreb day-2 test set), where AUROC, Pearson r, and covered fraction are the acceptance metrics.

name: binary-gene-detection-binarization
description: Use when preparing an expression matrix (e.g. dat.expression, genes x cells) as input to singleCellHaystack's haystack() or DKL computation, which accepts only binary detection data per cell.

name: binary-gene-set-matrix-construction
description: Use when iDEA-based GSE analysis requires pre-defined gene set annotations whose gene identifiers must match the identifier type (gene symbols or MGI IDs) of DE summary statistics.

name: binary-indicator-vector-construction
description: Use when converting fixed-length nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt RNA 5hmC windows) into numerical feature vectors via position-specific binary occurrence indicators of k-mer and gapped k-mer patterns before classifier training.

name: binary-integer-programming-optimization
description: Use when you have a differential gene co-expression network with per-edge P-values and must select a minimum dominating set of driver nodes, weighting nodes by degree and co-expression difference significance.

name: binary-mixed-integer-program-optimization
description: Use when cells measured only by scRNA-seq (expression) must be associated one-to-one with cells measured only by scDNA-seq (CNA), and the matching can be cast as a binary MIP over Pearson-correlation edge weights when |RNA cells| ≤ |DNA cells|.

name: binary-pattern-gene-clustering
description: Use when a sparse, dropout-prone scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. SMARTer-protocol data such as Xin GSE81608) must be converted into a binary low-dimensional cell representation for cell-type clustering, and dropouts should be leveraged as weak signals rather than imputed.

name: binary-random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when you have a binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix plus lifestyle metadata labels per genome and want to quantify lifestyle predictability (AUC) or assign lifestyles to unlabelled genomes.

name: binary-sensitivity-specificity-computation
description: Use when comparing automatic scRNA-seq cell-type classifiers on a binary malignant-vs-non-malignant detection task, where 'unknown'/'unassigned' predictions must be scored as malignant positives against held-out ground-truth labels.

name: binary-versus-multiclass-comparison
description: Use when a feature-selection benchmark table (misclassification percentage as a function of number of selected features) must be scanned to find per-dataset winners and summarize how recommendations differ between binary and multi-class classification problems.

name: binding-affinity-mlp-training
description: Use when labeled oligo(dT) priming windows (paired-end alignments indicating primer sites) from scRNA-seq data are available and a sequence-based binding-affinity predictor must be trained or reproduced (e.g. the pa6with1mm model).

name: binomial-co-occurrence-statistic-implementation
description: Use when hunting for genes expressed almost exclusively in one cell cluster (bDEGs) in a scRNA-seq Seurat object, and when per-cluster marker scores must be normalized to [0,1] so they are comparable across clusters.

name: binomial-detection-probability-modeling
description: Use when planning a single-cell RNA-seq experiment to determine the cell number N needed to detect a rare population (e.g., 5% prevalence) while accounting for within-population variability and capture efficiency.

name: binomial-enrichment-testing-with-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when you have cell-attribute-aware clusters (Eva_partitions output over an igraph cell-cell nearest-neighbour graph) and need to flag which communities are significantly enriched for a condition label before downstream DoDA regression.

name: binomial-mixture-model-variant-selection
description: Use when single-cell mtDNA AD/DP matrices (from cellsnp-lite or cellSNP) are available and you must distinguish clone-discriminative heteroplasmic variants from noisy, non-inherited SNVs before clonal reconstruction with vireoSNP.

name: binomial-mixture-variant-scoring
description: Use when you have a SNP-by-cell AD/DP count matrix (e.g. from cellsnp-lite/cellSNP over mtDNA) and need to separate clone-discriminative heteroplasmic mtDNA variants from noisy background variants before clonal assignment.

name: binomial-probability-threshold-modeling
description: Use when computing minimizer-sharing thresholds for (w,k)-minimizer queries whose minimizer count varies per read (e.g. m in 15-35), so that random sharing can be separated from true matches at significance level 0.99.

name: binomial-test-allele-count-analysis
description: Use when you have a multi-sample VCF with raw allele depths per sample and need to classify biallelic SNPs as showing allele-specific expression versus equal (50/50) allelic balance.

name: bio-conservation-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating a signal-filtering or cell-cycle-removal method on annotated single-cell data and you need to quantify, alongside a removal score, whether the corrected expression matrix preserves the biology of interest (e.g., subclone structure).

name: bioanalyzer-trace-area-quantification
description: Use when BioAnalyzer Expert traces from plate-based scRNA-seq library preparation are available and you need per-sample free-barcode-to-cDNA ratios to test their association with estimated barcode-swapping fractions.

name: biofilm-transcriptome-visualization
description: Use when you have pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns (CSV) for several pairwise biofilm experimental conditions (e.g. AGXX vs silver vs V2A steel, or sucrose/glucose/lactose/xylitol) and need data-driven, quadrant-grouped identification of extremely changing genes.

name: bioinformatics-classifier-metric-evaluation
description: Use when comparing candidate classifiers (e.g., SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree, GBDT), feature selection methods (F score, MRMD, PCC), or feature dimensions on a balanced sequence classification dataset and you need cross-validated Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC tables.

name: biological-conservation-scoring
description: Use when comparing single-cell batch-correction or integration methods on scRNA-seq or spatial (e.g., MERFISH–scRNA-seq) embeddings and you must quantify whether cell types and biological structure survive correction, not just whether batches mix.

name: biological-process-edge-set-selection
description: Use when computing per-cell biological-process activities from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix and you must decide which of ORIGINS2's 18 BP adjacency edge sets (or a custom PPIN) to use for a given research question.

name: biological-process-gene-list-curation
description: Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process of interest and need to derive the corresponding PPIN edge set (adjacency list) for downstream PPIN activity scoring in ORIGINS2.

name: biological-process-network-selection
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cells) and need per-cell activity scores for a biological process such as cell differentiation, cell cycle, DNA repair, or immune response, or when you must build a custom PPIN from a gene ID list.

name: biological-sequence-umap-visualization
description: Use when a trained Keras model (tmpMod./tmpWeight.bin from autoBioSeqpy, parameters.txt) must be inspected by embedding its hidden-layer activations for encoded protein/DNA/RNA test sequences in 2D UMAP space.

name: biological-zero-symmetry-thresholding
description: Use when a low-rank approximation of a sparse scRNA-seq expression matrix has been computed and technical zeros must be completed while keeping true biological zeros at exactly zero.

name: biologically-informed-loss-function-implementation
description: Use when implementing, re-implementing, or validating BIDCell's biologically-informed loss functions on subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE) and you need per-component loss values and correctness checks.

name: biology-conservation-metric-scoring
description: Use when you have joint latent embeddings of two or more species' scRNA-seq data from an integration algorithm (e.g. scVI, scANVI, SeuratV4) and need to score species mixing versus biology conservation in the BENGAL benchmark.

name: biomarker-comparison-across-annotation-tools
description: Use when two trained cell-annotation models (e.g. scaLR DNN vs CellTypist-Logistic) must be compared on how many literature-validated cell-type biomarkers appear in their top-K ranked feature lists.

name: biomarker-direction-validation
description: Use when reproducing a gene-expression signature where the expected direction of change is known (e.g. MCEMP1 up, HLA-DRA down), and you must verify that multiple perturbation conditions (viral proteins vs GFP control) recapitulate that pattern on a majority basis.

name: biomarker-gene-list-generation
description: Use when a large network-derived gene community (IC genes) must be reduced to a compact, classification-ready biomarker list and you have per-community gene files plus normal/cancer expression matrices available.

name: biomarker-novelty-classification
description: Use when IC gene symbol lists from the fused co-expression pipeline must be triaged into drug-actionable versus literature-novel candidate biomarkers per cancer type (KIRC, LIHC, PRAD).

name: biomarker-recovery-verification-against-supplementary-figures
description: Use when a clustering method claims to support downstream DEG analysis and you must verify that recovered marker genes match those reported in the paper's supplementary figures.

name: biomarker-threshold-cell-classification
description: Use when evaluating a marker-gene thresholding baseline for cell-type mapping: target cells must be assigned to reference clusters using top cluster markers alone, and the Classified/Ambiguous/Orphan fractions must be quantified.

name: biomaterial-exposure-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when transcriptomic CSVs contain pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for multiple treatment-vs-control biomaterial comparisons (e.g., AGXX® vs silver vs V2A steel), and you need quadrant classification plus time-course tracking of extreme genes.

name: biosynthetic-gene-cluster-prediction
description: Use when you have annotated genome assemblies (.gbk) across a genus-scale dataset and need BGC predictions, GCF clustering at a defined distance cutoff, and a binary GCF-by-genome matrix for lifestyle association testing.

name: bipartite-graph-construction-from-clusterings
description: Use when you have K base partitions of a cell-by-feature latent embedding (e.g. from a dual denoising autoencoder) and need a single consensus cell clustering that exploits cell-to-cluster relationships.

name: bipartite-graph-construction-with-euclidean-edge-weights
description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets via minimum-weight matching: after Seurat V3.0-style log-count pre-processing and anchor identification, a cross-dataset weighted graph must be built before matching.

name: bipartite-network-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually explore bipartite relationships between two entity types, such as KEGG pathways and the top-ranked eeSNV genes annotated to them, following enrichment analysis.

name: birth-death-score-estimation
description: Use when you need proliferation-rate estimates for single-cell time-series modeling but lack direct lineage-traced descendant counts — e.g. supplying growth weights (data_pt['w']) to PRESCIENT from expression data only.

name: bisulfite-read-alignment
description: Use when single-cell RRBS (bisulfite) FASTQ reads must be aligned and per-cell SNVs called before building an n_cells x n_SNVs matrix for eeSNV inference with SSrGE.

name: bivariate-gaussian-fitting-unspliced-spliced-space
description: Use when selecting reliable cycling-gene inputs for DeepCycle: candidate genes from a GOterm cell_cycle list must be checked in unspliced-spliced space (scVelo Ms/Mu layers) for multiple maxima before phase inference.

name: bladder-cancer-invasion-prediction-modeling
description: Use when analyzing high-dimensional TCGA mRNA expression data with a binary outcome (e.g., invasion subtype) and you need candidate genes selected by penalized regression with correct post-selection p-values.

name: bladder-cancer-invasion-subtype-classification
description: Use when classifying bladder cancer patients into invasive vs non-invasive subtypes from TCGA mRNA expression Z-scores, or when validating a penalized-regression gene panel (e.g., adaptive Lasso with FDR screening) as a multivariate predictor with cross-validated AUC.

name: blast-based-contig-gene-mapping
description: Use when you have a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g., Trinity contigs from FASTQ reads) and a reference transcript set, and need to identify which contigs are chimeric, correct, or unidentified to benchmark chimera-removal pipelines.

name: blast-gene-orthology-matrix-construction
description: Use when running a gene-matching ablation in cross-species scRNA-seq analysis: you need BLAST-derived gene similarity distance matrices to replace ProtBERT matches as input to TACTiCS on datasets such as human-mouse motor cortex.

name: blast-homology-rank-analysis
description: Use when a cross-species gene-matching benchmark needs a sequence-alignment baseline: you have two species' protein sequences (e.g. human and mouse) and must assign per-gene BLAST hits and match ranks to compare against embedding-based matches.

name: blast-result-taxonomic-aggregation
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads unmapped to the human genome (e.g. *_Aligned_UnMapped.bam) have been BLAST-aligned to the UCSC nt database and per-taxon microbial read counts must be tabulated.

name: blastn-expectation-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you have Trinity-assembled transcript contigs from RNA-seq and need to separate bona fide immunoglobulin IGHV-containing transcripts from non-Ig contigs and assign each to its closest germline IGHV gene.

name: blastn-sequence-homology-annotation
description: Use when you have differentially expressed uTARs (Wilcoxon rank-sum, e.g. >=25-50% of cluster cells expressing, >=0.25-1 log-e fold change) and need gene-level or functional annotations from nucleotide sequence homology.

name: blastn-viral-database-annotation
description: Use when you have predicted viral contigs (FASTA output from virnatrap-predict) and need to assign viral taxonomy per sample, e.g. to confirm HR-αHPV, HBV, or HCV detections in TCGA tumor types.

name: blastocyst-scrnaseq-data-handling
description: Use when evaluating estimation precision of allelic proportions under reduced sequencing depth, or when a low-coverage replicate of full-depth allele-specific counts is needed for an MSE benchmark.

name: blastocyst-stage-fraction-computation
description: Use when scBASE per-cell P/B/M posteriors are available for the Deng et al. CAST×B6 F1 pre-implantation data (286 cells) and you need per-gene, per-stage ASE class assignments or the PBM-region fraction at blastocyst.

name: blastp-gene-presence-mapping
description: Use when you need to know which genomes in a pan-genome gene-cluster absence/presence matrix contain homologs of a defined reference gene set, using paper-standard BLASTP annotation thresholds.

name: blastx-database-screening
description: Use when translated nucleotide contigs or extracted genomic loci (e.g., HERVd-annotated HERV regions from hg19) must be screened against a protein database like NCBI NR to detect retroviral POL/RT, GAG, or ENV protein motifs, or to verify viral contig classification.

name: block-matrix-computation-for-large-gene-datasets
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (Pandas DataFrame) is too large to screen endogenous reference genes in a single pass and needs to be split into 1000-gene blocks for variance-of-ΔF computation.

name: block-permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when a TE-based (or other feature-based) cell clustering must be compared to a reference clustering (e.g., gene-expression-based Leiden/Louvain labels) and a raw ARI alone is insufficient — an empirical significance p-value is needed.

name: blood-stroma-cancer-prediction-mapping
description: Use when benchmarking automated scRNA-seq annotators on tumour-microenvironment samples and you need tool-agnostic, three-class (blood/stroma/cancer) F1 comparisons such as the scATOMIC Fig. 2c evaluation.

name: blood-trait-association-interpretation
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics for a blood cell trait (e.g., lymphocyte count, ieu-b-31 monocyte count) have already been run through scPagwas and you need to prioritize trait-relevant genes and quantify their GO-BP enrichment versus MAGMA/TWAS-based gene sets.

name: blood-transcriptome-cohort-clustering
description: Use when multiple blood transcriptome cohorts or disease/physiological states need to be compared and grouped by shared immune-response patterns, e.g. to test whether a state like acute HIV infection forms its own cluster via aggregate-level fingerprints.

name: blood-transcriptome-module-annotation
description: Use when you need per-module functional annotations or titles for BloodGen3 modules, or need to annotate a normalized blood expression matrix (e.g. GSE13015/EH5429) with module membership for aggregates A1–A38.

name: blood-transcriptome-repertoire-construction
description: Use when building or reproducing a fixed whole-blood co-expression module repertoire from multiple reference transcriptome datasets, or when partitioning modules into higher-level aggregates (A1–A38) for fingerprint grid plots.

name: bloom-filter-aggregated-encoding
description: Use when compressing per-dataset Bloom filters of a sequence collection into a run-length-encoded (Aggregated) Bloom filter, or building left/right Bloom comb trees for a PAC-style approximate membership index over thousands of FASTA/FASTQ datasets.

name: bloom-filter-approximate-membership-query
description: Use when benchmarking approximate membership query structures (e.g., PAC, Cobs, HowDeSBT) on large collections of FASTA/FASTQ genomes, or when deciding how many Aggregated Bloom Comb trees to enable for sequence search.

name: bloom-filter-size-parameterization
description: Use when building a PAC index over a collection of FASTA/FASTQ datasets and you must choose the Bloom filter size (-b) trade-off, e.g. 2^27-bit vs 2^29-bit filters, balancing false positive rate against index size and RAM.

name: blosum62-filtered-peptide-search-parameterization
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a non-model eukaryotic species must be quantified at the KO level via translated search, and the Seq2Fun search thresholds (mismatches, matching length, BLOSUM62 score) need to be chosen or replicated.

name: bona-fide-editing-site-contrasting-rnaseq-wgs
description: Use when you need an independent labeled benchmark of A-to-G positions from a cell line/sample with matched RNAseq and WGS/WES data, to evaluate editing classifiers like REDInet on data never seen during training.

name: bone-disease-cell-state-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when scRNA-seq query cells from a disease-vs-control bone/cartilage context must be ordered along a developmental trajectory (e.g., HomC → preHTC → HTC chondrocyte maturation) and the key question is whether an attention-defined regulatory transition fails in the disease state.

name: bone-marrow-hematopoiesis-lineage-annotation
description: Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories of two related bone-marrow/hematopoiesis scRNA-seq datasets that branch, and you must match lineage leaf clusters (erythrocytes, megakaryocytes, pre-B-cells, dendritic cells) without manually selecting linear paths.

name: bone-marrow-subpopulation-shift-analysis-across-transplant-timepoints
description: Use when analyzing paired pre/post-transplant bone marrow mononuclear cell scRNA-seq (e.g., SRP073767 AML027/AML035) and you need per-cell host/donor genotypes plus cell-type composition changes across timepoints.

name: bonferroni-corrected-paired-t-test-comparison
description: Use when comparing method runtimes (or similar paired measurements) across multiple dataset sizes — e.g., AnnSQL vs AnnData filter/query timings at 14 simulated cell counts — and per-size significance must be controlled for multiple testing.

name: bonferroni-corrected-t-test-comparison
description: Use when comparing per-step removal (or depletion) rates of a spiked/known-positive class against the background class across replicates, and multiple filter steps require multiplicity correction.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when thousands of genes are tested in parallel by CTMM (e.g., REML JK and HE Wald p-values per gene) and a strict family-wise-error-controlled gene hit list is required before ranking or cross-method intersection.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a large family of statistical tests (e.g., 1641 motif enrichment Wilcoxon tests over a gene set) must be jointly thresholded, and raw p-values would otherwise yield inflated false positives.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when testing many source–sink causal paths per subnetwork (SEMace effect='source2sink') or declaring perturbed nodes/edges in SEMtree modules, and family-wise error control at alpha=0.05 is needed.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a per-gene model (e.g., the negative binomial GLM with Time, Group, and Time-by-Group interaction) yields thousands of raw p-values that must be Bonferroni-adjusted before calling tDEGs at p.cutoff = 0.05.

name: bonferroni-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many module-level or gene-set-level statistics (e.g., dozens of leiden-derived GRN module scores) are tested against the same phenotype and individual uncorrected p-values would inflate the false positive rate.

name: boolean-logic-gate-inference
description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix and a refined candidate TF list (or base GRN from scATAC-seq + motifs) for <200 target genes, and you need the combinatorial Boolean rule (not just TF-target edges) governing each target in a specific cell type or tissue.

name: boolean-logic-rule-assignment
description: Use when a refined GRN adjacency matrix is available and a draft Boolean Network model in SBML-qual format is needed for further manual editing or simulation.

name: boolean-network-attractor-analysis
description: Use when you have scBONITA-learned Boolean rules for a pathway (e.g., a GRAPHML KEGG topology like hsa00010) plus binarized single-cell expression states and need to map each cell to a characteristic signaling state.

name: boolean-network-inference-from-grn
description: Use when a refined GRN adjacency matrix is available and a draft Boolean model suitable for further manual editing (SBML-qual) is needed, especially for organisms with or without models in the Cell Collective database.

name: boolean-rule-inference-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether Boolean rule sets inferred from a scRNA-seq cell cluster are stable to the number of training cells, i.e. whether performance degrades below a critical training fraction (e.g. after downsampling to 1%).

name: boolean-rule-inference-genetic-algorithm
description: Use when you have binarizable single-cell expression data and a pathway topology and need executable Boolean rules describing signal integration at each network node, with node importance/uncertainty scores.

name: boolean-rule-inference-on-kegg-pathway-topologies
description: Use when you have a cells x genes log2(TPM+1) scRNA-seq matrix with cell-level condition labels (1/0 metadata) and want topology-constrained Boolean rule inference and dysregulated-pathway calls per cell type, rather than conventional ORA/DE.

name: boolode-gene-knockout-simulation-forecasting
description: Use when you have BoolODE (or similar) simulated single-cell gene-expression count matrices with known time points and a defined single-gene knockout, and need to benchmark whether a neural ODE forecaster extrapolates to post-perturbation states absent from training.

name: boolode-gene-regulatory-network-simulation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking transcriptomic forecasting methods on simulated gene regulatory networks where true future cell states and lineage splits are known, or when determining how far ahead recursive predictions stay accurate before diverging from simulated dynamics.

name: boolode-toggle-switch-simulation-data-handling
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference tools (scGATE vs GRNBOOST2, LEAP, CellOracle) on synthetic single-cell data where a known ground-truth network and simulated expression matrices are available.

name: boostdiff-differential-tree-ensemble-execution
description: Use when you have paired disease/control tab-separated gene expression matrices (genes as rows, samples as columns, identical feature sets) and need to infer a differential network between the two conditions.

name: boosted-tree-ensemble-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when inferring a differential gene regulatory network from two condition-specific gene expression matrices with BoostDiff and you must set ensemble size, regulator pool size, subsample count, and AdaBoost loss.

name: boosted-tree-ensemble-training
description: Use when you have two matched tab-separated expression matrices (rows = genes, columns = samples, first column 'Gene') from disease vs. control conditions and need a condition-specific differential network with regulator-to-target edges.

name: bootstrap-branch-uncertainty-estimation
description: Use when a multi-sample scRNA-seq trajectory (e.g. TSCAN cluster-based MST on HCA-BM data) contains branches whose stability is uncertain, and you need per-branch detection rates or sample-level branch-proportion variability before testing differential topology.

name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when aggregating per-dataset performance metrics (e.g. ROC AUCs of the MCEMP1/HLA-DRA Z-score across GSE155454, Bibert 2021, GSE161731, GSE157103, GSE152418, GSE172114, GSE164805) and you need a 95% CI that reflects cohort-level variability rather than subject-level sampling.

name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when estimating inter- vs intra-cell splicing heterogeneity (phi) from single-cell Nanopore isoform counts and you need to distinguish statistically confident phi estimates from unstable ones before plotting or interpretation.

name: bootstrap-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when fitting COSMIC v3.1 reference signatures (e.g., SBS1/SBS2/SBS5/SBS8/SBS9/SBS13/SBS18/SBS-MM1) to WGS SNV catalogs in 5-column format and you must decide whether low-contribution signatures are truly present versus fitting noise.

name: bootstrap-correlation-estimation-of-lfc-concordance
description: Use when evaluating whether a denoising/imputation method (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) brings single-cell log fold changes closer to matched bulk RNA-seq LFCs, e.g., on the Chu et al. H1 vs definitive endoderm data.

name: bootstrap-edge-confidence-thresholding
description: Use when inferred GRN edges need confidence scores before final network selection, and when precision/recall must be characterized as a function of an edge-confidence threshold rather than at a single arbitrary cutoff.

name: bootstrap-estimator-aggregation
description: Use when you have bootstrapped COSLIR regression coefficient matrices plus first-moment vectors μ̂_1 and μ̂_2 from two consecutive time points and must rank which interactions drive the cell-state transition.

name: bootstrap-fdr-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing two scLink co-expression networks (e.g., normal vs tumor immune cells) and you must annotate differential edges' statistical significance, distinguishing reliable normal-only or tumor-only edges from chance changes in scLink correlation.

name: bootstrap-null-distribution-estimation
description: Use when identifying genes or cell subclusters that vary significantly along pseudotime in time-series scRNA-seq data and a nonparametric null distribution is needed for a curve-vs-flat-line F statistic.

name: bootstrap-null-distribution-qvalue-calculation
description: Use when calling differentially expressed genes or subclusters along pseudotime in scTITANS and you need calibrated p-values/q-values for time-dependent expression via a bootstrap null instead of a parametric assumption.

name: bootstrap-pseudoreplicate-generation
description: Use when a single-cell dataset in AnnData (.h5ad) format lacks biological replicates — i.e., samples_col is None or one sample per condition — and differential cell-type proportion analysis between conditions is still required.

name: bootstrap-resampling-sample-imbalance-correction
description: Use when scoring perturbation impact from per-cell topic distributions in single-cell CRISPR screens (e.g., crop_stimulated CROP-seq data) where perturbed and CTRL cell numbers differ and a sample-imbalance-corrected ranking (TPDS/TPDR/CS) is required.

name: bootstrap-resampling-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when scRNAseq cells within a ZT time point must be converted to pseudobulk replicates to overcome dropout, so bootstrapped tauFisher circadian-time predictions can be compared for phase-heterogeneity differences between cell types.

name: bootstrap-resampling-stability-analysis
description: Use when comparing feature representations (e.g., eeSNV vs gene expression matrices) for subpopulation identification in scRNA-seq and you need stability of clustering accuracy quantified across resampled runs rather than a single clustering outcome.

name: bootstrap-significance-testing
description: Use when you must decide which principal components of a log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrix represent the cell-cycle effect, by testing loading differences between cell-cycle genes (XA) and control genes (XB) via resampling.

name: bootstrap-significance-testing-cross-sample
description: Use when comparing the distribution of cTP-net-imputed surface protein abundances between two independent scRNA-seq samples (e.g., cord blood vs bone marrow mononuclear cells) to test whether imputed protein levels differ biologically across samples.

name: bootstrap-variability-estimation-of-tf-activities
description: Use when TF activities have been inferred along FateCompass stochastic trajectories (e.g., mouse E15.5 pancreatic endocrine differentiation) and you need per-TF variability estimates before applying Z-score/variability/dynamic-correlation lineage-specificity criteria.

name: bootstrapped-cell-type-profile-sampling
description: Use when scRNA-seq data stored in a Seurat object must be converted into non-sparse per-cluster pseudo-bulk mRNA profiles (rows = genes, gene names as row names) before miRNA prediction with miRSCAPE.

name: bootstrapped-pseudobulk-cell-type-aggregation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data are sparse (high dropout) and miRNA activity must be inferred per cell type/cluster, e.g. profiling 523 miRNAs across all 56 HCL cell types with a global miRSCAPE model.

name: bootstrapping-robustness-assessment
description: Use when TF activities inferred with FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation must be robustness-tested across bootstrap resamples before calling differentially active TFs on differentiation trajectories.

name: borda-count-edge-aggregation
description: Use when multiple ranked directed networks from ensemble Granger regression runs (e.g., SINGE GLG outputs across lambda, kernel-width, lag, family, and replicate settings) must be merged into one ranked edge list.

name: boundary-condition-handling-density-estimation
description: Use when a nx1 vector of pseudotime values and a nx1 vector of marker signals from n single cells must be turned into a joint density p_s(s,y) on a regular grid as MAPiT input, especially when domain edges distort plain KDE.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: bowtie-index-generation
description: Use when building the reference index for tncRNA (tRF/tRNA-half) detection from small RNA-seq, where reads must be classified only if they map exclusively to tRNA-derived artificial chromosomes rather than non-tRNA genomic loci.

name: bowtie2-reference-indexing
description: Use when RNA-seq reads (e.g., GDC TCGA tumor BAMs) must be filtered against hg19 and the phiX contaminant to produce *_unmapped.fastq files feeding viRNAtrap or similar alignment-free viral detection.

name: bowtie2-short-read-alignment
description: Use when adapter-trimmed Ribo-seq FastQ reads (e.g. the 25-35 nt RPF fraction) may still contain contaminant RNA (rRNA, tRNA, viral RNA) and must be filtered against an unwanted-sequence reference before genome/transcriptome mapping.

name: boxplot-comparison-visualization
description: Use when you have replicate-level null statistics (e.g., 1000 random pairwise overlap counts) computed under several permutation backgrounds and need to visually compare their distributions to justify which background a colocalization test should use.

name: boxplot-visualization-of-gene-variability
description: Use when comparing imputation methods on single-cell RNA-seq data by measuring which one reduces gene-wise variability across cells of the same type, replicating the variance-stabilization analysis (Fig. 4) of the AutoImpute paper.

name: brain-cell-type-annotation-from-markers
