description: Use when clusters from scCAN (or similar unsupervised clustering) lack true cell type labels and a marker-gene reference table (e.g. PanglaoDB brain cell types) is available to assign each cluster a known cell type.

name: brain-rnaseq-module-functional-annotation
description: Use when a brain RNA-seq WGCNA analysis has produced gene-to-module assignments and you need the biological functions enriched per module plus significant module–trait correlations (e.g., coral module vs. age progression at P < 0.05).

name: brain-tissue-marker-database-querying
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq clusters from brain or nervous-system tissue by querying differential-expression marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers, only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) against CellMarker.

name: branch-assignment-in-differentiation-trajectories
description: Use when an Mpath trajectory contains a branching event and you must isolate which cells commit to each distinct differentiation path, such as muscle versus non-muscle fates in myoblast differentiation.

name: branch-dependent-gene-detection
description: Use when a branching single-cell trajectory has been inferred (e.g., STREAM on scRNA-seq) and you need to identify marker genes enriched on each branch to validate the topology or annotate lineage identities.

name: branch-topology-reconstruction-evaluation
description: Decision support for selecting a trajectory inference method when a scRNA-seq dataset has known branch structure (e.g., 8 branches in the CMP myeloid progenitor data) and downstream time-series analysis needs single-cell pseudotime.

name: branched-cell-fate-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is suspected to contain a branched developmental trajectory and pseudotime has already been inferred with redPATH's redpath() function, so multiple Hamiltonian path solutions (norm_res_new) are available to combine.

name: branching-event-detection-against-gold-standard
description: Use when evaluating whether a trajectory inference method (e.g. STREAM, Monocle2, TSCAN, DPT) correctly detects known bifurcations and recovers true pseudotime on a synthetic single-cell dataset with ground-truth topology.

name: branching-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when pseudotime trajectories contain branches (e.g. human vs mouse bone marrow scRNA-seq) and you need to visualize trajectory trees or a globally aligned tree to inspect conserved/divergent lineage marker kinetics.

name: branching-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when single-cell data (transcriptomic or chromatin-accessibility) is expected to contain branching developmental structure, and you need to learn, assign cells to, and visualize a branching trajectory graph with pseudotime.

name: brca-drug-repurposing-candidate-confirmation
description: Use when a BRCA (MCF7) GSFM active matrix and drug-induced GSFM matrix are available and the goal is to rank compounds by RSGSFM and confirm a reported top candidate such as WYE-354 against IC50 and FDA-approved/investigational drug benchmarks.

name: breakpoint-preservation-qc-in-cnv-matrices
description: Use when a gene-by-cell relative expression matrix (after baseline subtraction from confident normal cells) must be denoised before copy number segmentation while retaining breakpoints needed for joint segmentation and clone detection.

name: breast-cancer-de-gene-interpretation
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has cells assigned to mtDNA-defined clones (e.g., TNBC1 T0 vs T1 subclones) and you need to test whether the subclones show detectable transcriptional differences via differential expression.

name: breast-cancer-er-status-stratified-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when you have bulk (or single-cell) expression data from a cohort with a binary sample-level covariate (e.g. ER status in TCGA-BRCA) and want to detect covariate–pseudotime interaction genes rather than a single averaged trajectory.

name: breast-cancer-intrinsic-subtype-classification
description: Use when you have processed breast cancer RNA-seq expression profiles (e.g., TCGA RSEM or GSE96058 FPKM-normalized) and need single-sample intrinsic subtype calls without building a cohort-specific reference.

name: breast-cancer-pam50-subtype-classification
description: Use when classifying breast cancer samples into PAM50 molecular subtypes from gene expression data, especially cross-platform prediction where signature genes are missing or single-sample classification is needed.

name: breast-cancer-receptor-status-annotation
description: Use when DeepCC-predicted breast cancer subtype labels are available for validation cohorts with ER/PR and HER2 receptor-status metadata plus disease-free survival outcomes, and you must demonstrate clinical relevance against the PAM50 benchmark.

name: breast-cancer-scrna-seq-dataset-handling
description: Use when a task requires the exact breast-cancer scRNA-seq inputs of the ASGARD study (GSE123926, GSE113197 epithelial cells) loaded via Seurat with the paper's cell/gene filters.

name: breast-cancer-subtype-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq tumour biopsies are already annotated as Breast Cancer Cell by the base scATOMIC pan-cancer model and the goal is to assign ER+/HER2+/TN subtype labels per sample, including mixed double-positive calls.

name: breast-cancer-subtype-group-comparison
description: Use when you have a normalised count matrix plus metadata for TCGA-BRCA (or similar) samples with a SUBTYPE column, and the goal is to find gene–gene interactions whose correlation differs between two phenotypic subgroups.

name: breast-epithelial-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) from breast tissue has per-cell type labels and the goal is to characterize or annotate cell populations by PPIN activity of biological processes rather than marker genes alone.

name: breeding-accession-prioritization
description: Use when you have accession-level SNP genotype data (e.g., VCF from Soybase SoySNP50k) plus a curated table of resistance-SNP effect sizes per pathogen, and need to rank breeding accessions by predicted resistance.

name: broad-cell-type-taxonomy-renaming
description: Use when training a reference-based identifier on a pre-annotated dataset and applying it to a test dataset whose cell populations include types absent from the reference taxonomy, requiring label harmonization before evaluation of unknown-population rejection.

name: bsj-fragment-count-quantification
description: Use when quantifying circRNAs by back-splicing junction (BSJ)-supporting fragment counts from ribo− RNA-seq, or when cross-comparing circRNA call sets from CIRCexplorer2/CLEAR, MapSplice, and DCC under a >= 3 BSJ-fragment filter.

name: bsj-overlap-relation-index-computation
description: Use when evaluating how overlapping BSJ sites from CircAST output (or similar circRNA lists) affect full-length assembly sensitivity/precision and FPKM/TPM quantification accuracy, e.g. in simulation benchmarking.

name: bspline-null-statistics-smoothing-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when re-implementing or validating singleCellHaystack's per-gene significance pipeline: you have observed D_KL values per gene plus randomized null D_KL replicates and need smoothed p-values via B-splines instead of per-gene empirical tests.

name: bulk-alternative-splicing-comparison
description: Use when Nanopore long-read alignments (e.g., minimap2 v2.24 spliced alignments to GRCh38) show inflated PSI or suspected false-positive small internal exons, and you need to quantify the PSI shift from Longcell's consensus correction on bulk isoform quantification.

name: bulk-barcode-count-extraction
description: Use when raw bulk NGS FASTQ files contain expressed synthetic lineage barcodes and you need reference-free barcode detection and quantification into a per-sample counts table.

name: bulk-barcode-counts-normalization
description: Use when a bulk barcode counts table (e.g., counts/all_counts_combined.tsv from BARtab) must be normalized across samples and treatments compared by clonal composition, diversity, or replicate concordance.

name: bulk-dna-wes-read-alignment
description: Use when raw bulk DNA WES FASTQ files (e.g., SRA SRP067248 or EGA EGAS00001001880) must be aligned to a reference genome to enable downstream somatic SNV calling and read count matrix construction.

name: bulk-expression-gene-set-scoring
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq/microarray expression matrix (e.g., pdacR's TCGA-PAAD $ex) and a named gene signature (e.g., Bailey ADEX), and need a per-sample signature score to correlate with continuous metadata like ABSOLUTE purity.

name: bulk-expression-reference-processing
description: Use when building or verifying deCS CTGene reference panels from bulk (BlueprintEncode, DICE, MonacoImmune) or single-cell (HCL, HCAF) expression references, or when the ref_panel_markers_ratio cutoff must be re-derived.

name: bulk-guided-single-cell-inference-fine-tuning
description: Use when a cohort has bulk RNA-seq data for all samples plus processed single-cell data from one representative sample, and single-cell profiles must be inferred for the remaining target samples.

name: bulk-hic-dci-overlap-analysis
description: Use when scHi-C DCI calls (e.g., from scHiCDiff.ZINB pvalue.adj.FDR) need external validation against bulk Hi-C DCI sets and differential TAD regions before being reported as reliable findings.

name: bulk-jtkcycle-cycler-integration
description: Use when comparing a cell-type-specific cycler gene set (e.g., 189 SMC, 109 fibroblast, 87 endothelial, 28 macrophage, 117 hepatocyte de novo cyclers) to an independent bulk cycler reference to quantify overlap enrichment with empirical p-values.

name: bulk-microarray-cycler-definition
description: Use when building simulated circadian scRNA-seq data that needs a realistic, non-sinusoidal set of true cyclers, or when validating unsupervised cycler detections (e.g., Tempo de novo cyclers) against a bulk microarray-derived ground truth.

name: bulk-microarray-gene-signature-scoring
description: Use when you need to compute a gene-signature score per sample from a bulk microarray expression matrix (e.g., the 309 FFPE primary PDAC samples in Puleo 2018) and correlate it against sample-level metadata such as predicted mean VAF to test purity dependence.

name: bulk-mirna-mrna-gradient-boosted-model-training
description: Use when you have paired bulk mRNA and miRNA expression matrices for a tissue/cancer cohort and need a trained model to later infer miRNA expression in scRNA-seq clusters.

name: bulk-multiomics-count-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic bulk RNA-seq count matrices with coupled regulatory omics layers and ground-truth regulatory interactions to benchmark GRN inference, multi-omics integration pipelines, or DE/clustering methods.

name: bulk-rna-clustering-representative-selection
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq data for a cohort (e.g., 124-sample COVID-19 dataset) and must choose a small set of informative samples to receive real single-cell sequencing before semi-profiling the rest.

name: bulk-rna-deconvolution-cell-fraction-estimation
description: Use when single-cell cluster gene expression profiles (GEPs) must be mapped onto bulk drug-perturbed transcriptomes (e.g. LINCS L1000 anti-log GEPs) to quantify per-sub-cluster proportions before and after treatment.

name: bulk-rna-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you need to rebuild or validate the gene feature panel behind the sc_xgboost malignancy classifier, e.g. you have TCGA bulk counts with malignant/normal labels plus an integrated scRNA-seq matrix and must reproduce GbulkDE ∪ GscHV.

name: bulk-rna-seq-activity-score-computation
description: Use when a cluster-specific gene signature (e.g., top 20 DEGs of a scRNA-seq tumor cluster such as Cluster 4 with PTMA and STMN1) must be translated into a bulk cohort metric to stratify patients for Kaplan-Meier/log-rank survival testing.

name: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-decomposition
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq/snRNA-seq data from the same tissue must be decomposed into cell-type proportions, especially when single-cell vs bulk technical biases are expected or when only marker genes (not a reference profile) are available.

name: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-deconvolution
description: Use when bulk or pseudobulk RNA-seq samples need cell type proportions estimated, and a single-cell reference (real or semi-profiled) is available, or when benchmarking deconvolution methods against ground-truth proportions.

name: bulk-rna-seq-cell-type-deconvolution
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression matrix plus sample metadata and an annotated plant single-cell reference (e.g. Seurat object from Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq), and need cell-type fraction estimates per sample.

name: bulk-rna-seq-co-expression-network-analysis
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., a 192-sample count/TPM matrix) plus sample trait metadata (age, genotype, tissue, sex) must be partitioned into co-expression modules and those modules related to traits.

name: bulk-rna-seq-count-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 38 3xTg-AD/WT female hippocampus samples across three ages) must be formatted and cleaned—filtering low-expression genes—before module detection in PyWGCNA.

name: bulk-rna-seq-deconvolution
description: Use when marker-gene sets must be evaluated for how well they support estimating cell-type proportions from bulk or pseudo-bulk expression mixtures.

name: bulk-rna-seq-expression-normalization
description: Use when normalized bulk RNA-seq profiles must be converted into a z-scaled markers_expression matrix as query input for deCS correlation-based cell type annotation (e.g., Figure S12 iPSC-NPC/neuron differentiation-quality assessment).

name: bulk-rna-seq-latent-feature-extraction
description: Use when bulk tumor RNA-seq (e.g. 298-patient urothelial carcinoma ICB cohort, Mariathasan et al. 2018) needs biologically meaningful latent features derived from a single-cell-trained Miscell model for response association testing.

name: bulk-rna-seq-network-construction
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., TCGA LUAD tumor vs normal) must be transformed into per-sample gene-gene association networks to compare pathway connectivity (e.g., EGFR/EGF degrees) at single-sample resolution.

name: bulk-rna-seq-reference-comparison
description: Use when a paired bulk RNA-seq dataset exists for the same cell-type or condition contrast as scRNA-seq data, and you need to quantify whether imputation improves DE gene-list concordance rather than relying on qualitative checks.

name: bulk-rna-seq-subtype-classification
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq tumor expression matrices must be classified into known molecular subtypes using single-cell-derived gene signatures, and when subtype survival differences (e.g., basal-like vs. classical in PAAD) need to be quantified.

name: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating human primary-cell RNA-seq samples (bulk or single-cell) with Cell Ontology terms, or when auditing whether independent one-vs-rest classifiers produce probabilities inconsistent with the ontology's 'is a' edges.

name: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-deconvolution
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq read counts must be deconvolved into cell type proportions using a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, especially for tissues with closely related cell types (e.g., pancreatic islet alpha/beta/delta/gamma, kidney nephron segments).

name: bulk-rnaseq-cell-type-deconvolution
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq or pseudo-bulk expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) and need to estimate abundance of hundreds of cell types for downstream TME clustering or survival analysis.

name: bulk-rnaseq-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have simulated or ground-truth-annotated bulk RNA-seq and ATAC-seq count matrices plus a known regulator-gene interaction list and need to quantify whether modelled activator/repressor effects manifest as strong expression-accessibility correlations.

name: bulk-rnaseq-count-normalization
description: Use when a raw bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GEO GSE23649: 8 DBD EAD vs 8 DBD non-EAD) must be made cross-sample comparable before computing per-sample gene-signature scores for group tests such as EAD vs non-EAD.

name: bulk-rnaseq-cpm-normalization
description: Use when raw bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., DLPFC paired bulk samples) must be converted to Biobase ExpressionSet objects, filtered, and CPM-normalized prior to BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition or benchmarking against CIBERSORT/MuSiC/BSEQ-sc.

name: bulk-rnaseq-deconvolution-interpretation
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq gene-by-sample expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) and need cell-type composition estimates covering >400 cell types, e.g., to compare TME cell abundance across tumor subtypes.

name: bulk-rnaseq-deconvolution-with-single-cell-references
description: Use when estimating cell-type proportions in bulk or simulated bulk RNA-seq samples with a single-cell reference, and when choosing which subsampling/sketching method should build that reference from a large scRNA-seq atlas.

name: bulk-rnaseq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have matched scRNA-seq and bulk RNA-seq counts for the same biological system and want to quantify whether imputation improves differential expression concordance with bulk.

name: bulk-rnaseq-dropout-noise-simulation
description: Use when bulk count data must be degraded with simulated scRNA-seq-like dropout (targeting ~80% zero entries) to create a denoising benchmark against the original unperturbed matrix.

name: bulk-rnaseq-expression-preprocessing
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq or microarray expression matrix for a cell population of interest must be reformatted (gene-symbol-indexed) before computing ICELLNET cell-cell communication scores against reference partner cells.

name: bulk-rnaseq-expressionset-conversion
description: Use when running BisqueRNA::ReferenceBasedDecomposition or MarkerBasedDecomposition on bulk RNA-seq counts with a single-cell reference, and the inputs are still raw matrices, Seurat objects, or data frames that must first be cast into Biobase ExpressionSet format.

name: bulk-rnaseq-highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when a raw bulk expression matrix (e.g., TCGA log2(TPM+1) from GDC) must be reduced to a highly variable gene set before fitting a PhenoPath covariate-pseudotime model.

name: bulk-rnaseq-pathway-activity-scoring
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq normalized expression matrix (e.g. edgeR cpm) needs gene-set/module activity scores, and you must choose or benchmark among rROMA, GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA and z-score for differential pathway activity testing.

name: bulk-rnaseq-predictor-training
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression with binary drug response annotations is available and a drug sensitivity predictor must be trained (or resumed from a checkpoint) before transfer to scRNA-seq data.

name: bulk-rnaseq-read-qc-trimming
description: Use when raw bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. anti-PD-1 vs control CD8 TIL samples from GEO/SRA, such as GSE62771) need QC and trimming before Salmon quasi-mapping quantification.

name: bulk-rnaseq-reference-correlation
description: Use when a single-cell pattern/decomposition method (ACTIONet archetypes, cNMF components) must be benchmarked against labeled bulk cell-sorted RNA-seq profiles to test whether learned cell states match known cell-type signatures.

name: bulk-rnaseq-signature-scoring
description: Use when single-cell-derived cell-type signatures (e.g. from scDist differential-state analysis) must be validated in bulk transcriptome cohorts with matched survival and radiologic-response metadata.

name: bulk-rnaseq-top-gene-validation
description: Use when a single-cell trait-association pipeline (scPagwas gPAS/TRS) has ranked candidate risk genes and you need external bulk-expression evidence that they are disease-relevant.

name: bulk-rnaseq-training-set-curation
description: Use when you need to verify or reproduce the curated training-set composition of CellO's human primary cell bulk RNA-seq data (sample, study, and Cell Ontology term counts) from the Zenodo deposit.

name: bulk-sample-potency-scoring
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices and/or matched single-cell RNA-Seq profiles and need to score differentiation potency, identify cancer stem-cell or drug-resistant populations (e.

name: bulk-scrnaseq-domain-adaptation
description: Use when predicting per-cell drug response labels for a drug-treated scRNA-seq dataset by leveraging pre-trained bulk RNA-seq models built from GDSC/CCLE drug sensitivity databases.

name: bulk-single-cell-correlation-cellline-assignment
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters (from scanpyobj.h5ad with a cluster-wise GEP, GEP.txt) must be linked to a specific bulk cancer cell line before deconvolving LINCS L1000 perturbation samples for subpopulation fractions.

name: bulk-single-cell-gene-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when scDEAL IG matrices exist at both bulk and single-cell levels and you need to quantify how many top contributing genes are shared between the two scales for sensitivity vs. resistance.

name: bulk-single-cell-matched-analysis
description: Use when matched bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data exist for the same biological system and the goal is to distinguish biologically-driven true zeros from technical dropout zeros after imputation.

name: bulk-single-cell-rnaseq-integration
description: Use when predicting single-cell drug sensitivity/resistance labels from scRNA-seq (h5ad/AnnData) by leveraging bulk-level drug-response training data, e.g. reproducing the GSE110894 I-BET case study with scDEAL.

name: bulk-single-cell-transcriptomic-integration
description: Use when evaluating whether scRNA-seq denoising brings single-cell expression profiles into closer agreement with matched bulk RNA-seq data, e.g. comparing imputation methods by LFC correlation on a dataset with paired bulk and single-cell samples from the same populations.

name: bulk-to-single-cell-transfer-learning-model-training
description: Use when training scDEAL from scratch for a drug-treated scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. GSE110894 with I.BET.762) using the methods-table hyperparameters, instead of resuming a shipped checkpoint, to predict per-cell drug sensitivity.

name: bulk-transcriptome-connectivity-normalization
description: Use when you have one or more bulk cell-population transcriptomes (microarray probes or gene-level RNA-seq) and need to quantify their communication potential with many partner cell types via ligand-receptor scoring rather than co-expression of genes across cells.

name: bulk-transcriptome-preprocessing-normalization
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq or microarray expression data with matched clinical event/time-to-event survival information must be filtered, log-transformed, gene-wise median normalized, and converted into marker pair scores before Cox-based immune prognostic analysis.

name: bulk-tumor-immune-deconvolution
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq or microarray tumor cohort with matched survival data (event + time-to-event) should be scored for immune cell infiltration and linked to Cox-model hazard ratios to detect co-infiltration-driven prognostic bias.

name: bulk-tumor-latent-feature-extraction
description: Use when a pre-trained Miscell checkpoint is available and bulk tumor expression (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer) should be encoded into latent features and tested for association with overall survival adjusting for Age, Sex, and TNM stage.

name: bulk-tumour-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a bulk tumour expression matrix (log2(TPM+1), highly variable genes) with a per-sample covariate such as MSI or ER status must be mapped onto a 1D pseudotime and genes with covariate-pseudotime interactions identified.

name: bulk-vs-single-cell-fusion-call-comparison
description: Use when scRNA-seq (Smart-Seq) fusion calls from scFusion must be validated against known spike-in fusions or against fusion calls and chimeric-read support from bulk methods, e.g. to reproduce the Fig 5 comparison of fusion counts and bulk-support fractions.

name: bulk-vs-single-cell-platform-annotation
description: Use when building or auditing a multi-dataset transcriptomic compendium where each dataset must be labeled by measurement type (MA/RNAseq/scRNA) and checked for sample/feature counts before analysis, e.g. when deciding whether TCGA-PAAD should be whitelisted to histologically confirmed PDAC samples.

name: bursting-kinetics-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting Canopy2's beta-Poisson bursting model and mutation-specific gene activation/deactivation rates (alpha, beta) must be estimated from single-cell gene expression counts (e.g. featurecounts.qc of GBM10_preproc) before running get_trees().

name: busco-completeness-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g. Trinity-assembled H. subflexa pheromone gland) with BUSCO ortholog counts, especially to verify that chimera/redundancy filtering reduces duplicated BUSCO groups.

name: ca-biplot-visualization-with-feature-labeling
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., SingleCellExperiment) reduced with standard CA and want a geometric joint display of cells and genes to identify which features (e.g., top 20 by loading L2 norm) drive cell-population separation.

name: cad-gwas-locus-fine-mapping
description: Use when a GWAS locus has a known/validated target gene or tissue and you need to determine which tissue's eQTL explains the trait association, especially under suspected allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants per locus).

name: caf-subset-communication-comparison
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq or microarray expression matrices of CAF-S1 (n=6) and CAF-S4 (n=3) subsets are available and the goal is to test whether one subset emits stronger signals to epithelial, endothelial, pDC, or B cell partners via ICELLNET scoring.

name: caf-subtype-marker-gene-annotation
description: Use when reclustering a broad stromal/mesenchymal cluster has produced subclusters and each must be assigned a CAF subtype identity, especially when validating a rare subcluster against a reference marker set.

name: cafeh-genotype-mode-bayesian-fine-mapping
description: Use when individual-level genotype and phenotype matrices are available for multiple eQTL studies or tissues and you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization that can resolve multiple causal variants (allelic heterogeneity) that mislead standard colocalization.

name: cafeh-summary-statistic-colocalization
description: Use when you have GWAS/eQTL summary statistics (z scores or betas+SEs), a reference LD matrix, and per-study sample sizes, and need joint colocalization/fine-mapping across tens of traits or tissues to prioritize a causal target tissue.

name: cage-peak-proximal-tss-annotation
description: Use when building an enhanced long-read isoform annotation and you need to confirm read 5'/3' ends against CAGE peak (FANTOM, mm10) and polyA site (polyASite 2.0) BED intervals before collapsing novel intron chains.

name: cageminer-candidate-gene-prioritization
description: Use when you need to rank candidate genes underlying GWAS resistance loci by integrating gene coexpression modules and defense-related guide genes, e.g. genes within 2 Mb of resistance SNPs in soybean.

name: calinski-harabasz-cluster-ranking
description: Use when Totem has generated a large set of candidate clusterings (k-medoids/CLARA over many k values) and one must automatically select clustering(s) to feed Slingshot MST construction, using Calinski-Harabasz scores combined with cell connectivity.

name: cancer-associated-fibroblast-subtype-annotation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq stromal/CAF clustering partition contains low-ROGUE (impure) clusters and finer subtypes — such as myCAF splits or CD74/MHC-II+ apCAFs — must be resolved and annotated.

name: cancer-biomarker-signature-generation
description: Use when raw TCGA-style RNA-Seq gene count matrices for paired normal vs cancer samples (e.g., KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) must be turned into a differential-expression baseline signature to benchmark other gene sets by classification.

name: cancer-cell-line-drug-response-analysis
description: Use when you have matched gene expression profiles for cancer cell lines plus drug sensitivity (IC50) data (e.g., the GDSC panel) and want to identify which signaling pathway activities explain drug response.

name: cancer-cell-line-expression-data-harmonization
description: Use when a bulk cancer cell-line expression matrix (GDSC Affymetrix U219 microarray, CCLE RSEM RNA-seq) must be log2(x+1)-normalized and aggregated over TMG/NMG gene sets for correlation with IC50 drug sensitivity.

name: cancer-cell-of-origin-annotation
description: Use when annotating epithelial cells in a cancer scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., liver, pancreatic, colon, kidney, lung, mammary tumors) to identify malignant cells and infer their cell of origin from a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction.

name: cancer-database-annotation-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a pretrained malignant-cell annotation model (Cancer-Finder, checkpoints/sc_pretrain_article.pkl) against database-curated tumor annotations across many scRNA-seq datasets to test generalization at scale.

name: cancer-driver-benchmark-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing predicted pan-cancer driver genes from cTaG (or similar RandomForest-based TSG/OG classifiers) against established tools like TUSON, 20/20+ and DriverNet using curated driver lists such as Bailey et al. and CGC.

name: cancer-driver-gene-benchmark-scoring
description: Use when ranking driver-gene prediction lists (your own or tools like PNC, DawnRank, MutSigCV) against curated CGC, NCG or PMH benchmark gene sets with precision, recall and a precision-weighted F0.2 score across TCGA cancer types.

name: cancer-driver-gene-classification
description: Use when genes must be classified cancer driver vs non-driver from multi-omics features averaged per gene over a directed GRN such as DawnNet, KEGG, or RegNetwork, e.g. to reproduce the DGMP 5-fold cross-validation benchmark.

name: cancer-driver-gene-classification
description: Use when somatic mutation data (e.g. COSMIC MAF-style coding mutations) must be converted into per-gene mutation-type features and genes classified as TSG vs OG, especially to nominate low-frequency candidate drivers among unlabelled genes without background-mutation-rate bias.

name: cancer-driver-gene-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when you have DGMP (or similar) gene-level driver-probability predictions (e.g., 'logits' from './code/result/') and need to assess whether top-ranked, unannotated predictions show cancer-like multi-omics alteration patterns versus known cancer genes.

name: cancer-gene-census-reference-list-validation
description: Use when a driver-gene prediction method must be benchmarked for precision against curated reference driver sets (Bailey et al. pan-cancer list or CGC), especially to rank methods like cTaG, TUSON, 20/20+ and DriverNet on the same evaluation genes.

name: cancer-gene-coexpression-analysis
description: Use when a panel of cancer genes (e.g., 40 genes from >10K TCGA pan-cancer samples) must be screened for co-expression and visualized as a clustered pairwise correlation heatmap.

name: cancer-gene-expression-data-loading
description: Use when reproducing the GNIAP gene co-expression network workflow and the study's breast or prostate cancer expression data files must be located, loaded, and fed into the GCN inference step in R.

name: cancer-genomics-significance-table-construction
description: Use when a MAF-format mutation dataset must be tested per-gene between two sample groups defined by a continuous factor (e.g., hypoxia GSVA score strata) to yield a p-value/FDR significance table.

name: cancer-invasiveness-deg-validation
description: Use when analyzing human breast cancer scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE148093) with GEMLI to discriminate symmetric vs asymmetric DCIS/inv_tumor cell fates and call DEGs marking the onset of invasiveness.

name: cancer-molecular-subtype-classification
description: Use when assigning established molecular subtype labels (e.g., CRCSC CMS, PAM50) to tumor RNA-Seq or microarray samples, especially cross-platform validation where signature-gene classifiers fail due to batch effects or unpaired gene annotation.

name: cancer-multiomics-feature-integration
description: Use when you need to merge gene alteration, survival, GO-similarity, and protein-RNA binding evidence for candidate RBPs into one feature matrix before unsupervised clustering of circRNA regulators.

name: cancer-normal-biomarker-evaluation
description: Use when a predefined gene set must be scored for its ability to distinguish tumor from normal samples in TCGA RNA-seq cohorts, and per-cancer-type AUC or classification accuracy is the target output.

name: cancer-primary-origin-prediction-from-metastatic-scrnaseq
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from metastatic tumour biopsies (e.g. breast, kidney, lung, ovarian, skin cancer metastases) lack a known primary and the goal is to infer each sample's cancer tissue of origin at the cancer-cell level.

name: cancer-scrna-seq-dataset-quality-and-label-handling
description: Use when a labeled cancer scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object or counts matrix in csv/rds/h5/10X format) must be quality-controlled, run through scWizard's two-step annotation, and its predictions graded against the original study's cell labels to compute per-cluster accuracy.

name: cancer-scrnaseq-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a labeled cancer scRNA-seq test set (e.g. T/NK_BRCA, T/NK_KIRC, Mye_PAAD, LYM) must be annotated with a pretrained hierarchical DNN and you need to reproduce or compare cluster-after-annotate vs direct annotation accuracy.

name: cancer-scrnaseq-workflow-execution
description: Use when analyzing cancer scRNA-seq data (Seurat object, counts matrix in csv/rds/h5, or 10X folder) and you need automated TME cell-type annotation plus downstream analyses instead of manual marker-based labeling.

name: cancer-signature-baseline-thresholding
description: Use when building a supervised malignant-vs-normal training set from scRNA-seq data whose 'Malignant'/'Tumor' labels were assigned by upstream studies of variable quality, and you need to remove mislabeled cells before classifier training.

name: cancer-signature-calibrated-training-data-handling
description: Use when building a malignant-cell classifier's feature matrix from a multi-dataset calibrated training set: you have malignant/normal-annotated cells (e.g. adata.obs['Raw_annotation'] with 'Malignant'/'Tumor' vs 'Normal') and need union-based DEG feature selection rather than intersection.

name: cancer-subtype-stratification
description: Use when you have a bulk tumor cohort expression matrix (e.g., TCGA) and want unsupervised patient stratification into subpopulations without pre-selected gene subsets, or when studying intra-cohort heterogeneity beyond single-cell applications.

name: cancer-transcriptome-novel-lncrna-discovery
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-Seq from a tumor cohort (e.g., 180 TARGET-OS samples) plus normal controls and need to discover novel, tumor-specific lncRNA transcripts absent from existing annotations.

name: cancer-type-agnostic-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a query cancer type and drug pair must be pushed through secDrug's greedy set cover pipeline to rank secondary combination candidates with confidence scores in [0,1].

name: cancer-vs-normal-classification
description: Use when a binary Cancer/Normal classification must be run on a pan-cancer transcriptomic matrix using a fixed biomarker gene set (e.g., Wx-14-UGCB, Peng-14, DEG-14), with LOOCV accuracy as the reported metric.

name: candidate-gene-conservation-assessment
description: Use when you have a binary presence/absence (PAV) matrix over 204 cultivated soybean accessions and a list of prioritized candidate resistance genes, and need per-gene conservation frequencies and a >99% core-gene fraction.

name: candidate-gene-filtering-for-grn-inference
description: Use when building a GRN from paired snRNA-seq/snATAC-seq multiomic data with scMEGA and you need to restrict network inference to genes varying along a pseudotime trajectory that have at least one linked peak.

name: candidate-gene-prioritization
description: Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk CTMM results are available for many genes and you need a ranked, replicated list of variance-differentiation hits, including variance-only genes without mean differentiation.

name: candidate-gene-ranking-per-pathogen
description: Use when a set of high-confidence candidate genes per pathogen species must be converted into an ordered per-species ranked list (e.g., top-10 shortlist) using network/annotation-based weighting and prior GWAS-expression association scores.

name: candidate-k-skewness-selection
description: Use when running GapClust on a scRNA-seq count matrix to flag rare cell clusters (e.g. the 29-cell tuft-cell R2 cluster), and you need the criterion that turns per-k gap statistics into candidate rare clusters.

name: candidate-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have a uniform-format list of already annotated plus newly predicted miRNA/precursor candidates and need to label promising candidates via parallel HT criteria and one-class SVM sets and compute their overlap.

name: candidate-tf-pool-filtering
description: Use when scRNA-seq data alone must be augmented with context-specific regulatory hints — specifically when scATAC-seq peak data and TF motif annotations are available and a filtered candidate TF–target table is needed before logic-gate inference.

name: candidate-tf-set-scaling-analysis
description: Use when planning or auditing scGATE runs on scRNA-seq data: you need to know how many cells and how many candidate regulatory TFs per target are required for reliable (AUROC/EPR-validated) logic-gate inference before committing to a full-scale run.

name: canonical-exon-boundary-matching
description: Use when running INTEGRATE-Circ fusion detection and you must decide whether spanning-read breakpoints represent canonical exon-boundary junctions versus non-canonical (alternative-splicing/backsplice) junctions for a gene fusion.

name: canonical-lymphocyte-marker-validation
description: Use when a trained SpatialDDLS neural network deconvolution model must be interpreted or sanity-checked: after trainDeconvModel, to confirm predicted cell type proportions are driven by canonical markers via gradient-based ranked gene lists per cell type.

name: canonical-wnt-signaling-pathway-annotation
description: Use when CellChat-predicted signaling pathways for scRNA-seq cell groups include WNT, and the canonical WNT ligand-receptor pairs and pathway-level aggregates must be extracted, ranked by communication probability, and validated against known dominant pairs.

name: carbohydrate-metabolism-gene-signature-interpretation
description: Use when a reconstructed scorecard from S. mutans (SMU) transcriptomic comparisons under different dietary carbohydrates must be annotated/validated against known PEP-PTS and carbohydrate-metabolism gene families.

name: cardiac-progenitor-lineage-annotation
description: Use when a bifurcating or low-population-fate trajectory (e.g., Isl1+ cardiac progenitors splitting into cardiomyocyte and endothelial branches) must be resolved across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, or multi-omic-integrated data and standard TI tools miss one fate.

name: cardiomyocyte-marker-expression-profiling
description: Use when assigning biological identity to day-60 terminal subpopulations on a TCM latent map of hiPSC-to-cardiomyocyte scRNA-seq data by overlaying log-expression of TNNT2, MYL2, NPPA, NPPB, NR2F2 and CDH11.

name: cart-cluster-combination-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether visually adjacent or suspicious clusters in a t-SNE/UMAP embedding (e.g. CAR-T clusters 3+4+9+11) should be merged, by comparing per-cluster ROGUE purity scores against the merged cluster's ROGUE score.

name: cascc-attractor-based-clustering-pipeline-execution
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq count matrices with a co-expression-assisted method: gene-by-cell matrices needing attractor-based feature selection, cluster-number prediction, and UMAP visualization with cluster correspondence.

name: case-control-phenotype-simulation
description: Use when a benchmark with known ground-truth genetic meta-markers is needed to test pattern-mining tools like HOGImine, e.g. for the simulation study of Section 4.1.1.

name: case-control-small-rna-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample small RNA-seq read-count files from COMPSRA's Annotation module and samples are labeled as case and control groups, and you need per-RNA differential expression p-values.

name: categorical-metadata-autocorrelation-on-phylogeny
description: Use when you have a rooted single-cell phylogeny (e.g., a Cassiopeia-reconstructed Newick tree) plus cell-level categorical metadata (e.g., sampleID, tissue site) and want a per-cell numeric score of how homogeneous or mixed that category is along each cell's ancestral path.

name: categorical-treatment-enrichment-g-test
description: Use when you have categorical cluster assignments (Louvain or sslouvain) plus a binary treatment label (control vs perturbed) and need per-cluster enrichment/depletion statistics to judge whether a clustering resolves treatment responses.

name: causal-controller-deterministic-inference
description: Use when a trained GRouNdGAN checkpoint (.pth) and an imposed GRN are available and you need to test whether knocking out a regulating TF significantly changes its target gene's expression in simulated cells (interventional sampling, not observational generation).

name: causal-gan-model-training
description: Use when a preprocessed, library-size-normalized (20,000) scRNA-seq train split and a formatted causal graph exist and a reference-based GAN must be trained to later generate realistic single-cell expression data.

name: causal-gan-scrna-seq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference algorithms (GRNBoost2, GENIE3, PIDC, PPCOR) needs realistic scRNA-seq simulations with a known imposed ground-truth GRN, or when performing in silico TF perturbation/knockout experiments on reference data such as PBMC-CTL.

name: causal-graph-mask-encoding-from-pickled-nested-dictionary
description: Use when you need to impose a GRN on GRouNdGAN training: convert TF→gene edges into the pickled causal graph (nested dict of gene index -> set of regulating TF indices) that fixes the masked causal generator's per-target-gene connectivity.

name: causal-graph-pickled-dictionary-formatting
description: Use when preparing a TF-gene regulatory network to impose on GRouNdGAN training: you have TF-gene rankings (e.g., GRNBoost2 output) or a custom GRN and must convert it to the causal_graph.pkl nested-dictionary format.

name: cca-based-single-cell-integration
description: Use when query cells lack surface-protein measurements (mRNA-only scRNA-seq) but a multimodal CITE-seq reference atlas of the same tissue (e.g. memory T cells) exists and per-cell protein abundance must be predicted by reference mapping.

name: cca-rpca-data-integration
description: Use when multiple single-cell transcriptomic matrices from different plant species must be co-embedded on a shared UMAP to test whether cell identities are preserved across species.

name: ccc-interaction-perturbation-robustness-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify the stability of ligand-receptor interaction rankings inferred from single-cell RNA-seq under perturbed cell composition, shuffled cell-type labels, or corrupted prior-knowledge resources.

name: ccc-method-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and want to validate that a CCC method's top-ranked ligand-receptor interactions are coherent with an independent modality such as predicted cytokine activity.

name: ccc-method-resource-decoupling-benchmark
description: Use when assessing how much the choice of CCC inference method versus prior-knowledge resource drives disagreement in ligand-receptor predictions from single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: ccc-resource-comparison-across-databases
description: Use when the goal is to quantify how much a set of ligand-receptor CCC resources (e.g., CellChatDB, CellPhoneDB, Ramilowski, ConnectomeDB, LRdb) overlap or differ in unique interactions, receivers, and transmitters before choosing one for downstream inference.

name: ccc-tool-benchmark-runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational cost and predictive power of CCC tools across multiple samples/contexts, e.g. benchmarking Tensor-cell2cell vs CellChat on runtime, peak memory, and AUC for phenotypic classification.

name: cci-bayes-factor-score-computation
description: Use when a clustered scRNA-seq target population (e.g. AML1_cluster1) must be assigned a healthy counterpart from a reference atlas via a composite-likelihood/Bayes-factor score.

name: cci-dataset-formatting-for-intercellar
description: Use when InterCellar analysis is required but no CCI dataset exists yet, and ligand-receptor interactions must be pre-computed with CellPhoneDB v2 from a scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type annotations, per condition.

name: cci-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions from one or more conditions (e.g., CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR output) and need functional annotation of int-pairs plus statistically significant condition-specific terms.

name: cci-interaction-filtering-by-cell-type-viewpoint
description: Use when starting from CellChat/CellPhoneDB/ICELLNET/SingleCellSignalR-inferred CCI data and the analysis goal requires isolating interactions sent or received by one cell type (e.g., outgoing interactions of malignant cells) before module definition.

name: ccle-depmap-gene-effect-analysis
description: Use when you have a set of ecDNA calls (e.g., from the circlehunter Snakemake pipeline) and need to quantify oncogene content and test enrichment against CCLE/DepMap functional genomics data.

name: ccsn-conditional-independence-network-inference
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be transformed into per-cell gene-gene association networks where indirect (non-direct) edges are filtered out via conditional-independence hypothesis tests, e.g. before computing NFE or CNDM-based analyses.

name: cd-hit-est-redundant-contig-clustering
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g. Trinity output in FASTA) contains redundant, highly identical contigs that must be deduplicated as part of the Bellerophon filtration sequence (TPM -> CD-HIT-EST -> TransRate-C).

name: cd4-cd8-t-cell-label-consolidation
description: Use when cell-type predictions from scCancer2 predCellType (or a reference metadata scheme) emit CD4/CD8-split T-cell labels but the evaluation targets a coarse five-major-cell-type taxonomy across datasets and sequencing technologies.

name: cd4-t-cell-naive-memory-discrimination
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data (e.g., GSE100866 CBMCs) where naive vs. memory CD4+ T cells (or CD8−/CD8+ NK cells) co-cluster under RNA-only or ADT-only clustering and joint multimodal clustering is needed to resolve them.

name: cd4-t-cell-subset-cluster-visualization
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with a limited number of ADT features (e.g., <50) where a single surface protein modality dominates the joint distance, and you need to test whether applying the sigmoid filter to ADT distances separates RNA-defined subsets (e.g., memory vs naive CD4+ T cells).

name: cd8-t-cell-subcluster-marker-interpretation
description: Use when Cytocipher merging of Leiden resolution-2 over-clusters on PBMC 3K scRNA-seq leaves two T cell sub-clusters unmerged and you must confirm with cluster-specific markers (e.g. GZMK, GZMH) that the split is biologically real.

name: cd8-til-state-annotation-from-reference-map
description: Use when murine CD8 T cell scRNA-seq data (e.g. Smart-seq2 or 10X counts) must be assigned to reference CD8 TIL states (exhausted, memory-like, EM-like, naïve) prior to clonotype or state-composition analyses.

name: cd8-til-state-classification
description: Use when you have a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 T cell scRNA-seq profiles (mouse or human) and need to assign each cell a probability of belonging to a reference CD8 TIL state (exhausted, memory-like, naive, EM-like).

name: cdf-difference-optimality-assessment
description: Use when running scISR's data perturbation module on a filtered training gene-by-cell expression matrix and you must decide how many gene-subspace groups to retain before subspace regression imputation.

name: cdi-differential-expression-marker-identification
description: Use when you have a clustered (or resolution-swept) Seurat scRNA-seq object and need per-cluster top markers ranked by the co-dependency index (CDI) to score cluster specificity or benchmark cluster configurations.

name: cds-versus-utr-read-density-enrichment
description: Use when validating RiboSeq alignment output (length-selected BAM/BED files) to confirm that ribosome-protected fragments accumulate in coding sequences rather than untranslated regions before downstream statistical analysis.

name: celery-2d-location-prediction-training
description: Use when you need to recover 2D spatial coordinates of scRNA-seq cells (or held-out ST spots) by training a supervised model on a reference ST dataset with known locations, e.g. 10x Visium mouse brain sections.

name: cell-annotation-method-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-type annotation methods on multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data, especially when later-timepoint cell types may shift in composition, disappear, or emerge as novel types.

name: cell-atlas-annotation-agreement-evaluation
description: Use when a cell-atlas scRNA-Seq dataset carries multiple conflicting annotation columns (e.g., ICGS2, Seurat3, Monocle3, curated labels) in adata.obs and you need to quantify whether an integrated solution reproduces or refines the reference atlas clusters.

name: cell-attribute-aware-community-detection
description: Use when performing DA-testing of cell-types from scRNA-Seq/snRNA-Seq data where condition labels (age, disease stage, severity, phenotype) exist per cell and standard Louvain, Milo, or DA-seq clustering yields weakly significant composition shifts.

name: cell-barcode-based-cross-modality-label-transfer
description: Use when paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. SNARE-seq chromatin + expression) share cell barcodes across modalities, and clusters computed on one modality (here the cell-by-peak chromatin side) must be copied to the other for DE/enrichment.

name: cell-barcode-calling-and-filtering
description: Use when raw 3' droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., GemCode/10x data such as SRA SRP073767) must be turned into a cell-filtered gene-barcode UMI matrix, deciding which barcodes represent cells versus empty droplets.

name: cell-barcode-extraction-from-short-reads
description: Use when reads are FASTQ/FASTA and a known sequence of interest (barcode, fusion, variant) must be located with tolerated sequencing errors, and reads must be assigned to cell barcodes for single-cell quantification or genotyping.

name: cell-barcode-extraction-scrna-seq
description: Use when processing raw 3'-end tag scRNA-seq FASTQ (e.g., MCA GSE108097 or HCL GSE134355) where cell barcodes/UMIs must be extracted from merged inserts and corrected against a whitelist before isoform quantification.

name: cell-barcode-posterior-error-correction
description: Use when raw 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ reads must have their 16 bp cell barcodes error-corrected (or discarded) prior to UMI filtering and building a gene-barcode count matrix.

name: cell-barcode-sharing-hypergeometric-testing
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq samples (e.g. HiSeq 4000-sequenced libraries) must be tested pairwise for more shared cell barcodes than expected by chance, to flag barcode-swapping artefacts.

name: cell-barcode-umi-extraction-specification
description: Use when sequencing reads embed cell barcodes and UMIs at variable-length or non-fixed positions (e.g. 10x Chromium v2/v3, concatenated barcodes) and must be normalized to a simple fixed-position geometry before mapping and quantification.

name: cell-barcode-umi-quantification
description: Use when you have 10x CellRanger output (filtered_feature_bc_matrix, possorted_genome_bam.bam) and need per-cell pathogen UMI counts for an infected scRNA-seq sample, e.g. HIV EGFP+ cell detection.

name: cell-barcode-whitelist-matching
description: Use when single-cell amplicon FASTQ data contain a fixed cell barcode+UMI pattern in R1 (e.g. 16bp barcode + 10bp UMI) and a known cell barcode whitelist is available that extracted barcodes must be matched against.

name: cell-by-cluster-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when an AnnData object has log-cpm normalised scRNA-seq data with tentative (ideally over-clustered) Leiden labels and you need per-cell enrichment scores against every cluster's marker signature to support significance-based cluster merging.

name: cell-by-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a per-cell sparse k-mer abundance matrix (from jellyfish counts) and a CKG look-up table (from simhash), and need a normalized cells-by-CKGs feature matrix for downstream cell type classification.

name: cell-calling-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a raw unfiltered gene-by-barcode count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA/snRNA-seq needs cell-calling, and multiple callers must be compared against ground-truth labels (HTO singlet/doublet or demuxlet genotypes).

name: cell-cell-communication-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing ligand-receptor scoring rules for cell-cell communication inference on scRNA-seq data and you need an apples-to-apples benchmark on the same interaction database, same input matrix, and same permutation/significance pipeline.

name: cell-cell-communication-inference-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has cluster/cell-type annotations and the goal is to compute transcriptome-based communication scores between sender and receiver clusters and rank specific ligand-receptor pairs (e.g., checkpoints, chemokines).

name: cell-cell-communication-matrix-factorization
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression (genes x cells) plus cell labels and need species-agnostic cell-cell communication inference, especially when no curated L-R database exists for the species or condition-specific shared vs unique signals are of interest.

name: cell-cell-communication-method-benchmarking
description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq data must be interrogated for ligand-receptor interactions with multiple CCC methods, or when per-method interaction scores need to be combined into a robust consensus ranking via LIANA.

name: cell-cell-communication-module-interpretation
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor CCI predictions (e.g., from CellChat on a scRNA-seq dataset such as GSE72056 melanoma) and need to biologically interpret which interaction groups/signals characterize a specific sender or receiver cell type.

name: cell-cell-communication-network-analysis
description: Use when you have clustered scRNA-seq cell groups and need to infer significant ligand-receptor communication between them, quantify pathway-level signaling, identify dominant senders/receivers, and group coordinated outgoing/incoming patterns.

name: cell-cell-communication-network-inference
description: Use when single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., seqFISH+ mouse cortex, Seq-Scope mouse colon) with a gene expression matrix plus cell spatial coordinates and cell-type labels is available, and the goal is to estimate which neighboring cell types regulate HVG expression.

name: cell-cell-communication-score-computation
description: Use when you need to quantify communication potential between an input cell population and partner cell types from transcriptomic data, e.g. comparing outward signaling of CAF-S1 vs CAF-S4 or LPS-stimulated DCs against the Primary Cell Atlas.

name: cell-cell-distance-based-communication-analysis
description: Use when you have non-spatial scRNA-seq data plus a limited spatial measurement of a few genes, and need to infer cell-cell communication or the spatial distance/range of a signaling pathway (e.g. Wg ~100 µm, Dpp ~125 µm).

name: cell-cell-distance-inference-from-transport-plan

description: Use when a normalized single-cell tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix needs cell subtype labels beyond the five major TME types, using pretrained subtype templates rather than reference-free clustering.

name: cell-subtype-similarity-map-construction
description: Use when fine cell subtype annotations from different published references must be related quantitatively, or when subtypes from a reference (e.g., the PBMC multimodal reference) must be transferred onto tumor-derived cells and compared across datasets.

name: cell-subtype-supervised-classification
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object from tumor tissue needs fine-grained cell subtype labels within the five TME compartments (T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial), or when cross-dataset subtype label similarity must be quantified.

name: cell-to-cell-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have SClineager genotype-inference outputs (inferred VAF matrix and covariance from run_sclineager) and need to partition cells into lineages based on similarity of inferred genotypes.

name: cell-to-cell-pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have imputed (or raw) gene-by-cell count matrices plus cell type labels and need to measure whether dropout recovery improves same-cell-type Pearson correlation and clustering separation without over-homogenizing cell types.

name: cell-to-cell-similarity-matrix-symmetrization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering pipeline needs a dense, undirected cell-to-cell similarity matrix: the ADMM-learned coefficient matrix is sparse and asymmetric, and zero entries must be imputed (Weighted Adamic/Adar over KNN) before spectral clustering.

name: cell-to-clone-assignment
description: Use when you have matched scDNA-seq copy-number data, scRNA-seq gene-expression data, and a clone-label table mapping each DNA cell to a clone id, and you need to predict which clone each RNA cell belongs to.

name: cell-to-landmark-pair-assignment
description: Use when a landmark-labeled low-dimensional expression matrix is available and you must quantify neighborhood-based cell state transitions between landmark pairs to build a weighted transition graph.

name: cell-to-region-assignment
description: Use when single-cell coordinates with marker intensities (e.g. MCMICRO-processed CyCIF data in an AnnData object) must be annotated with region labels derived from marker-defined cell populations like SOX10+ tumor cells.

name: cell-to-trajectory-assignment-entropy-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on a branching (bifurcating) dataset with close, fine lineages, where purity of cell-to-trajectory assignments and per-path pseudotime accuracy must be quantified.

name: cell-type-abundance-comparison-across-culture-media
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples were grown under different differentiation media (e.g. UNC vs SC air-liquid interface cultures) and you need to verify or estimate cell type composition shifts, such as ciliated vs secretory cell abundance, from gene signatures rather than deconvolution tools.

name: cell-type-abundance-thresholding
description: Use when building a supervised cell-type annotation model from a reference scRNA-seq matrix whose cell-type counts are imbalanced, and minority types risk being ignored during training.

name: cell-type-aggregate-score-verification
description: Use when per-cell pluripotency/differentiation scores from multiple methods (ORIGINS, LandSCENT, CytoTRACE) must be averaged within annotated cell types and their orderings compared for consistency, e.g. on the breast epithelial sample.

name: cell-type-aggregation-of-per-cell-scores
description: Use when per-cell stemness scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) have been computed on annotated scRNA-seq data and you need per-type averages and rankings to benchmark which method correctly identifies stem cells.

name: cell-type-annotated-reference-construction
description: Use when a large cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq reference (.h5ad) must be reduced to a representative sketch to serve as the reference matrix for deconvolution of pseudobulk/bulk RNA-seq samples, and sketch quality must be judged by proportion-estimate accuracy.

name: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., GEO/E-MTAB pancreas, PBMC) must be used to annotate one or more independent testing studies and per-method annotation accuracy needs to be quantified across all train-test combinations.

name: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a trained cell-type annotation model (e.g. a DNN on .h5ad scRNA-seq data) must be scored against ground-truth labels on a held-out test set, or when comparing annotation tools for accuracy and run feasibility on large datasets (>0.6M cells).

name: cell-type-annotation-accuracy-validation
description: Use when GeneVector phenotype_probability annotations must be trusted before downstream analyses like latent-space arithmetic; trigger when an independent label source (e.g., CellAssign) exists for concordance checking.

name: cell-type-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing Table 1-style accuracy comparisons of cell type annotators across multiple tissue scRNA-seq datasets, or when evaluating how sequencing depth affects single-cell annotation accuracy on a labeled test set.

name: cell-type-annotation-by-gsea
description: Use when you have Seurat cluster marker lists (only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) from scRNA-seq data and need automated, database-backed cell-type annotation for each cluster.

name: cell-type-annotation-from-marker-genes
description: Use when scRNA-seq cluster assignments produced by an unsupervised method (e.g. scBGEDA) lack cell-type labels and a curated marker database such as CellMark can be matched against per-cluster DEGs.

name: cell-type-annotation-from-signature-scores
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq object (e.g., SingCellaR Human_HSPC) needs cell-type labels from lineage signature gene sets rather than marker-gene inspection or reference mapping.

name: cell-type-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have a rooted lineage tree in Newick plus per-cell cell-type labels and want to quantify which cell types co-occur within subtrees (e.g., after cutting the LinRace embryo tree at depth 26).

name: cell-type-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (genes x cells) must be paired with a cell-annotation metafile before running NATMI ExtractEdges.py, or when cell-type labels need to be validated so edges are attributed to the right cell types.

name: cell-type-annotation-marker-genes
description: Use when you have a cell-by-factor or low-dimensional embedding from paired multi-omics data (e.g., Mowgli on TEA-seq PBMC) and need per-cell type labels grounded in canonical gene/protein markers plus an independent reference annotation.

name: cell-type-annotation-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a cell type annotation tool's accuracy on reference-to-query label transfer, or when assessing whether annotation performance depends on expert-knowledge masks vs. parameter-matched random masks.

name: cell-type-annotation-model-training
description: Use when benchmarking how subsampling/sketching (e.g. scValue sketches at 0.02–0.10 fractions) affects supervised cell-type annotation accuracy on .h5ad scRNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth labels.

name: cell-type-annotation-model-training
description: Use when confident cell type labels from a consensus of annotation tools must be spread to unlabeled cells in scRNA-seq data via a graph convolutional network, or when tuning GCN hyperparameters per dataset.

name: cell-type-annotation-pipeline-comparison-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify resource/accuracy trade-offs of cell type annotation pipelines on identical feature subsets of an scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., reproducing a Table-3-style comparison of accuracy, memory, and execution time).

name: cell-type-annotation-plotting
description: Use when comparing imputed vs. unimputed scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., Jurkat-293T or Zeisel datasets) to assess whether imputation improves clustering of annotated cell-type subpopulations, as in Fig. 5 of the AutoImpute paper.

name: cell-type-annotation-scoring-against-reference-database
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., from Seurat) need automatic, knowledge-free cell type annotation by scoring cluster marker genes against a tissue-specific cell taxonomy reference database rather than manual marker inspection.

name: cell-type-annotation-standardization
description: Use when combining scRNA-seq studies whose free-text cell annotations differ, e.g. before rendering a cross-study comparison of expression across aligned cell types in Cellenium (H5AD-imported studies with ontologized metadata).

name: cell-type-annotation-transfer-with-mlp-classifier
description: Use when semi-profiled single-cell data (e.g. scSemiProfiler output for a COVID-19 cohort with Healthy/Asymptomatic/Mild/Moderate/Severe/Critical conditions) is unlabeled, and annotated representative single-cell reference data exists to train a classifier for label transfer.

name: cell-type-balanced-subset-allocation
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. a 428k-cell gut atlas in .h5ad) must be subsampled to a fixed sketch size while preserving cell-type diversity and rare populations for downstream annotation/ML tasks.

name: cell-type-biomarker-ranking-extraction
description: Use when a trained scRNA-seq cell-type classifier (e.g. scaLR DNN on anndata .h5ad data) must be converted into per-class ranked gene lists, or when top-100 biomarkers must be checked for recall against a curated reference like CellMarker2.0.

name: cell-type-bootstrap-association-testing
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics and an annotated single-cell Seurat object are available and the goal is to rank predefined cell types for trait/disease association at FDR < 0.05 (e.g., AD vs. OPCs/microglia, severe COVID-19 vs. PBMC subsets).

name: cell-type-classification-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters have been produced and reference cell-type labels exist, and you need ARI plus per-cell-type classification accuracy (e.g., alpha/beta cells) to quantify clustering fidelity.

name: cell-type-classification-accuracy-computation
description: Use when benchmarking supervised cell-type classifiers on annotated scRNA-seq data and you need repeatable accuracy and balanced-accuracy estimates for SciBet, scmap, and Seurat v3 across many datasets.

name: cell-type-classification-evaluation
description: Use when a labeled single-cell RNA-seq AnnData (cell x gene, 'class_label' column) needs automated cell-type label transfer with measurable accuracy/F1, including imbalanced, many-class (e.g., 42-type mouse brain) or small-training-set settings.

name: cell-type-classification-evaluation
description: Use when you have a set of k selected marker genes on a labeled scRNA-seq AnnData object and need to quantify how well those markers discriminate cell types via classifier performance.

name: cell-type-classification-macro-f1-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell type annotation models on a held-out test set and you need donor-generalizing performance metrics such as macro F1-score and cross-entropy loss.

name: cell-type-classification-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing or benchmarking the running time of automatic scRNA-seq cell-type identification methods on subsets of varying training/testing sizes, e.g. reproducing the Fig. 4 speed ranking on the mouse brain dataset GSE116470.

name: cell-type-clustering-ari-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing the LUAD/HCC827-H1975-H2228 scRNA-seq clustering benchmark across three platforms with the 2267 common HVGs, or when comparing ARI of unsupervised batch-correction clustering to published values.

name: cell-type-clustering-assessment
description: Use when an scRNA-Seq matrix has been corrected for the cell-cycle effect and you must verify that cell-type signal was retained while cell-cycle heterogeneity was removed, comparing original vs corrected matrices.

name: cell-type-clustering-unknown-subtypes
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq read count matrices from multiple batches contain cell types that are unknown a priori, and clustering plus batch-effect correction must be performed jointly without preliminary normalization.

name: cell-type-colored-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a 2D ivis embedding of scRNA-seq data has been computed and you need to visually validate cell-type segregation and global cluster relationships against published figures.

name: cell-type-composition-input-construction
description: Use when preparing seq-based ST data (e.g., 10X Visium slices such as the 12 human DLPFC slices) for Splane spatial domain identification, which requires per-spot cell type composition rather than gene expression.

name: cell-type-composition-quantification-across-conditions
description: Use when comparing cell-state or cell-type proportions between conditions (e.g., KO vs WT) in scRNA-seq data where cells have been projected onto a reference atlas and assigned discrete cell-state labels.

name: cell-type-composition-regression-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell/nucleus atlas has cell-type or cell-state annotations plus per-donor covariates, and the goal is to test whether cell-type fractions differ across a condition (e.g. obesity, depot) while controlling for covariates.

name: cell-type-consistency-rate-computation
description: Use when evaluating how accurately an automatic cell-type annotation method labels clusters of scRNA-seq data against manually curated cell types, and a comparable consistent-rate table across multiple methods is needed.

name: cell-type-correlation-strategy-selection
description: Use when training a supervised single-cell label-assignment model on scRNA-seq data with known cell types and you must decide between a flat vs hierarchical classifier based on how highly correlated the training cell types are.

name: cell-type-correspondence-mapping
description: Use when visualizing two or more cellular-resolution SRT sections jointly (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl DPI-10 vs DPI-15) and cell-type labels differ across sections, so naive default palettes misalign colors between biologically related or confusable cell types.

name: cell-type-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have a cell-by-feature scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq count matrix with per-cell type labels and need across-cell-type expression/accessibility profiles for Spearman/k-medoids clustering or Kendall's Tb correlation validation.

name: cell-type-deconvolution-method-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell type identification or gene expression decomposition methods on simulated single-slice spatial transcriptomics benchmarks with paired scRNA-seq references and ground-truth per-cell assignments.

name: cell-type-deconvolution-wnnls
description: Use when estimating cell type proportions from bulk RNA-seq read counts with a multi-subject single-cell reference, especially for closely related cell types and without pre-selected marker genes.

name: cell-type-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell dataset contains annotated cell types and two conditions, and you need per-cell-type DE gene counts and magnitudes to rank the biological response across populations.

name: cell-type-disjoint-cross-validation-splitting
description: Use when benchmarking cross-modality translation methods (e.g., scRNA-seq to scATAC-seq) for generalization to cell types absent from training, mimicking the MB/MCC/MK/PBMC unseen-cell-type evaluation.

name: cell-type-drug-response-ranking
description: Use when you need to identify which cell type in an untreated disease scRNA-seq dataset is most responsive to a drug with a known target gene, without paired treated/untreated samples.

name: cell-type-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when SINCERA hierarchical clustering has produced cell clusters and each cluster must be annotated with a predicted cell type using differentially expressed genes and a Fisher's exact test against the EBI Expression Atlas annotation table.

name: cell-type-entropy-coefficient-of-variation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing segmentation methods on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERSCOPE melanoma, CosMx lung) where no pixel-level ground truth exists and you need reference-based homogeneity vs cell-size consistency metrics.

name: cell-type-expression-aggregation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq study stored as an AnnData/H5AD object must be loaded into a relational sparse expression table and queried for gene-level per-cell-type averages, e.g. to replicate Cellenium's server-side aggregation.

name: cell-type-expression-specificity-ranking
description: Use when a query gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') must be matched to the annotated cell types that specifically express it, within one study or across multiple ingested scRNA-seq studies.

name: cell-type-f1-score-computation
description: Use when comparing label-transfer accuracy of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq integration methods on cells with held-out ground-truth annotations, especially under varying annotation budgets.

name: cell-type-fraction-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples have been deconvolved against a single-cell reference (e.g., via scPlant decomposeBulk on an annotated Seurat object) and you need a heatmap of per-sample cell-type fractions to compare compositions across conditions.

name: cell-type-functional-annotation
description: Use when an unsupervised clustering (e.g., Leiden) of scRNA-seq data has produced clusters with no labels and you must assign a cell type from the functional enrichment of cluster-specific genes.

name: cell-type-gene-signature-definition
description: Use when cell types have been annotated across merged datasets (e.g., after Harmony-kernel integration and label propagation) and a unified marker-gene signature per type/subtype is needed, such as neuronal (LINGO2, CUX2, SST) and glial (SLC1A2, MBP, CLDN5) markers.

name: cell-type-ground-truth-precision-evaluation
description: Use when a real scRNA-seq dataset has trusted cell-type labels serving as ground truth and you need to quantify how precisely a gene-set or pathway score (TRS, scDRS) retrieves the trait-relevant cell type.

name: cell-type-held-out-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods on two datasets with known cell-type compositions and you want to verify that a cell type present in only one dataset is left unmatched instead of incorrectly aligned.

name: cell-type-hierarchy-construction
description: Use when training a custom Census cell-type annotation model from a scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Tabula Sapiens plus CCLE) that requires inferring the cell-type hierarchy and fitting node classifiers.

name: cell-type-homology-annotation
description: Use when integrating single-cell datasets from multiple species whose cell type annotations use different or dataset-specific ontology terms, and a shared cell type homology mapping is required before integration and scoring.

name: cell-type-identification-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether joint (all-slices) inference improves cell type labeling accuracy of spatial transcriptomics methods, or when comparing ST cell type identification methods on simulated Visium data with known ground-truth single-cell labels.

name: cell-type-identification-performance-metrics
description: Use when comparing or tuning a scRNA-seq cell type identifier on annotated datasets and you need to quantify correct/erroneous assignments for known and unknown cell populations (C, E, EA, CUA, EUA).

name: cell-type-identification-potts-model-map-inference
description: Use when you need per-cell (not per-spot) discrete cell type labels for ST spots (Visium, Slide-seq), given nucleus segmentation outputs and a labeled scRNA-seq reference, with spatial smoothness enforced.

name: cell-type-importance-visualization
description: Use when you have dsCellNet-inferred ligand-receptor networks across multiple developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis stages) and need per-cell-type incoming/outgoing/total edge counts to rank the most communicating cell types per stage.

name: cell-type-interaction-overlap-statistics
description: Use when gABC/ABC-scored enhancer-gene interactions have been predicted per cell type from snATAC-seq candidate enhancers and you need per-cell-type interaction counts plus cross-cell-type overlap/shared fractions.

name: cell-type-isoform-usage-aggregation
description: Use when SingleCellExperiment 3'UTR isoform count matrices (*.txs.Rds, *.genes.Rds) from scUTRquant must be summarized per cell type and genes labeled multi-UTR vs IPA under a ≥10% isoform-fraction cutoff.

name: cell-type-label-alignment-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-cell embeddings (e.g., tGPT transformer features) plus ground-truth cell type annotations and must quantify clustering alignment via NMI, ARI, and FMI.

name: cell-type-label-guided-bayesian-matrix-factorization
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices come with trusted cell type labels and the goal is dropout imputation that leverages those labels, e.g. benchmarking silhouette/Pearson clustering metrics against scImpute, DrImpute, PBLR.

name: cell-type-label-hierarchy-classification
description: Use when benchmarking marker gene panels against a two-layer cell-type label hierarchy on scRNA-seq data, or when testing whether fewer hierarchy-aware markers match a one-vs-all baseline panel.

name: cell-type-label-permutation-ablation
description: Use when benchmarking NeuronChat's projection prediction on retrograde-labeling ground truth and you must rule out that benchmark performance is driven by node cell-type labels rather than the specific ground-truth graph topology.

name: cell-type-label-permutation-testing
