description: Use when constructing a cell–cell communication network from scRNA-seq data and you need to decide which sender–receiver L–R interactions are statistically significant rather than keeping all expression-product edges.

name: cell-type-label-prediction
description: Use when annotating cell types in scRNA-seq data without training on the test dataset, or when benchmarking a zero-shot label predictor against supervised classifiers like CellTypist on a multi-batch atlas such as the open-problems pancreas dataset.

name: cell-type-label-propagation-across-datasets
description: Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., three cortex studies totaling ~105,099 cells) are jointly integrated and one or more reference annotations must be propagated to unlabeled cells without re-clustering from scratch.

name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a cell-type-specific gene network (weighted edge matrix) for one of 26 cell types and need to verify that its node scores recover the correct pangaloDB cell-type markers.

name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-annotation
description: Use when scQA clustering (labels.txt) has assigned cells to clusters and you must confirm each cluster's key genes overlap known markers, hub genes, and DEGs (e.g., endothelial ADTRP, CDH5, CLEC14A, ACVRL1).

name: cell-type-marker-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have a gene marker list selected from scRNA-seq phenotypes and need to verify it recovers the correct tissues and cell types by enrichment against a curated reference set such as HuBMAP_ASCTplusB_augmented_2022.

name: cell-type-marker-gene-matrix-handling
description: Use when reconstructing or fine-tuning the DCNet network and you need to wire 9078 marker genes to 434 cell-type hidden neurons via the zero-one relation matrix and align input/output neuron ordering with index.pkl.

name: cell-type-marker-gene-selection
description: Use when you have a raw/normalized scRNA-seq count matrix paired with manually annotated cell-type labels and need a per-cell-type positive marker gene list to drive marker-based or marker-learning cell-type prediction.

name: cell-type-marker-gene-validation
description: Use when scBridge (or a baseline such as scJoint, Seurat or GLUE) has produced predicted cell-type labels on target scATAC/ADT data and you need marker-based evidence that the predicted populations (e.g. Naive vs Effector CD4+ T cells) are biologically correct.

name: cell-type-marker-gmv-inference
description: Use when you have an annotated single-cell dataset (e.g., the Field et al. week-2 cortical organoid data, GEO GSE106245) plus a cell type marker GMT file and want interpretable, module-level per-cell cell type activity rather than opaque clustering.

name: cell-type-marker-validation
description: Use when a single-cell TE matrix (scTE .h5ad output from scRNA-seq or scTEATAC output from scATAC-seq) has been clustered and you must confirm cell-type assignments or marker-TE specificity.

name: cell-type-marker-verification-from-loadings
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. SingleCellExperiment) has been embedded with correspondence analysis and you want to check whether high-loading genes correspond to known cell-type markers (e.g. GNLY, TYROBP, LYZ, S100A8, CD74, HLA-DRA) and interpret cell-population associations.

name: cell-type-matching-metric-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cross-species cell type matching pipelines (e.g., human vs mouse vs marmoset primary motor cortex scRNA-seq) and you need reproducible ADS/recall metrics, including gene-matching ablations that test whether ProtBERT gene matches outperform BLAST matches.

name: cell-type-mean-expression-profile-computation
description: Use when preparing labelled scRNA-seq training data (e.g. SingleCellExperiment objects with known cell labels) and you need per-cell-type mean expression profiles plus a cross-cell-type correlation matrix to decide a classifier strategy.

name: cell-type-neighborhood-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when single-cell data have been pseudo-spatially mapped onto ST spots (e.g., via STEM's netsc2st mapping) and the goal is to quantify spatial proximity/colocalization between rare cell types such as TSKs, endothelial cells, or pDCs.

name: cell-type-nomenclature-standardization
description: Use when combining marker gene sets from multiple published databases or cell-sorting sources whose gene symbols and cell type labels follow non-standard, inconsistent nomenclature, and you need harmonized, comparable sets.

name: cell-type-perturbation-detection
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix with per-cell metadata assigning condition, patient, and cluster, and need to identify which predefined cell types are transcriptomically perturbed between two conditions.

name: cell-type-perturbation-ranking
description: Use when you have untreated diseased scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and a known drug target gene, and need to identify which cell types are drug-responsive or resistant without paired treated/untreated samples.

name: cell-type-phenotype-association-testing
description: Use when cell-type proportions have been estimated from bulk RNA-seq (via BisqueRNA bulk.props or BisqueMarker) and you need to test associations with phenotypes such as BMI, Matsuda index, or Braak stage, replicating reported cell-composition associations.

name: cell-type-positive-fraction-quantification
description: Use when single-cell AnnData atlases spanning multiple ages (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis, 328K cells, 19 tissues, 1-30 months) must be scored for senescence and aggregated into per-cell-type positive-cell proportions or old/young ratios.

name: cell-type-potency-ranking-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq count matrix with malignant/non-malignant or cell-type annotations is available and the goal is to estimate and rank differentiation potency of cell types without marker genes, feature selection, or training.

name: cell-type-probability-classification
description: Use when single-cell expression data has a small labeled training set and you need probabilistic cell type predictions plus predictive entropy to guide cell selection or evaluate annotation uncertainty.

name: cell-type-probability-expression-correlation
description: Use when you need marker genes for cell types absent from training data, given OnClass prediction matrices (pred_Y_all.released.npy) and single-cell expression data such as Tabula Muris Senis FACS cells.

name: cell-type-profile-matching
description: Use when ST pixels are cell mixtures and you need to assign reference-free deconvolved cell-type transcriptional profiles to known cell populations and compare them across conditions (e.g., aged vs young) for perturbation-driven gene changes.

name: cell-type-proportion-accuracy-evaluation
description: Decision support for validating false-positive control of Scanpro proportion analysis on null simulations, and for choosing pseudo-replicate counts (2–14) based on total cell counts per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells).

name: cell-type-proportion-computation-per-condition
description: Use when comparing cell-type composition of an AI-generated (semi-profiled) cohort against real-profiled single-cell ground truth across defined conditions, e.g. COVID-19 severity states (Healthy, Asymptomatic, Mild, Moderate, Severe, Critical).

name: cell-type-proportion-controlled-synthetic-data-generation
description: Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq count matrix with known ground-truth cell-type labels and controlled per-type cell numbers — e.g. to benchmark clustering methods on a rare cell type (<5% of cells).

name: cell-type-proportion-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating SC-ST mapping outputs (SC-ST / ST-SC mapping matrices) against ground-truth ST cell-type labels, to quantify whether each method preserves cell-type composition of spots rather than just coordinate accuracy.

name: cell-type-proportion-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a decomposition method's estimated cell-type proportions (e.g., BisqueRNA's res$bulk.props) must be scored against known or reference proportions per individual and cell type using Pearson correlation and RMSD.

name: cell-type-proportion-quantification
description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq UMI counts from a heterogeneous cell suspension (e.g. 68k PBMCs) and need cluster-level cell-type composition percentages validated against a published population breakdown.

name: cell-type-proportion-statistical-testing
description: Use when single-cell resolution data (AnnData with sample, cluster, condition metadata columns) needs differential compositional analysis of cell-type proportions, with or without biological replicates.

name: cell-type-proportion-summarization
description: Use when per-cell DA scores (or similar per-cell condition-association statistics) have been computed on an integrated single-cell dataset with cell-type annotations and you need to rank cell types by the fraction of cells linked to a condition such as severe disease.

name: cell-type-purity-evaluation
description: Use when a joint latent embedding (e.g. scConfluence latent in mdata.obsm['latent']) must be quantitatively validated against known cell-type labels, as in diagonal-integration benchmarks or hyperparameter sensitivity sweeps.

name: cell-type-rank-dimension-reduction-visualization
description: Use when a scRank analysis has produced a ranked list of drug-responsive cell types (obj@cell_type_rank) and you need to check or display how the ranking distributes across single cells on a dimension-reduction embedding.

name: cell-type-recovery-assessment-across-graining-levels
description: Use when selecting a graining level for metacell construction and you need to check that rare cell populations are not merged into other types, especially in datasets of varying complexity or size.

name: cell-type-recovery-auc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing pathway activity scoring methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cell labels exist (e.g., SERGIO simulations or annotated datasets), to measure cell-type recovery AUC and accuracy.

name: cell-type-rejection-thresholding
description: Use when annotating single-cell RNA-seq cells via marker counting and you must conservatively reject low-confidence assignments (possible unknown cell types) before downstream cluster reassignment.

name: cell-type-relationship-tree-inference
description: Use when you need to assess whether a subsampled ('sketched') single-cell dataset preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, by harmonizing labels with CellHint and comparing the inferred relationship tree against a full-data reference tree.

name: cell-type-relative-interaction-quantification
description: Use when several pre-computed cell-cell communication (CCI) datasets from different conditions must be compared cell-type-wise, to test whether a cell type (e.g., mast cells or NKT-p) consistently mediates more interactions in one condition.

name: cell-type-replicability-subsampling-simulation
description: Use when you must stress-test whether a cross-dataset cell-type identification method still recovers a target type that is rare (1–20% of cells) and only subtly different from the out-group, rather than well-separated abundant types.

name: cell-type-scaling-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a transcriptomic perturbation score (e.g., number of DEGs, scDist distance) scales with the number of cells per cell type in single-cell RNA-seq data, or when benchmarking speed of differential-state methods.

name: cell-type-scatter-plot-visualization
description: Use when a small marker-gene panel has been selected and you need a visual check that the reduced-dimensional projection separates known cell type labels into distinct clusters, e.g., reproducing a published t-SNE of cells projected onto 15 markers.

name: cell-type-score-aggregation-across-clusters
description: Use when you have a cell-type-by-cell score matrix (es.max) from sctype_score() and Seurat cluster identities and must assign a single label per cluster, with an Unknown fallback for low-confidence assignments.

name: cell-type-score-computation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq analysis requires scoring cells against known cell-type markers (e.g., producing per-cell scores/labels for MASI-based annotation or for pipeline variants in integration benchmarks).

name: cell-type-score-space-centroid-distance-analysis
description: Use when transferring labels from a reference atlas with MASI and query data may contain cell types not present in the reference: cells whose closest-centroid distance approaches their farthest-centroid distance (ratio near 1, certainty near 0) should be flagged as unassigned.

name: cell-type-separation-visualization
description: Use when a VEGA (or similar interpretable VAE) model has been trained on single-cell RNA-seq with gene-module-wired latents and you must check that latent dimensions separate annotated cell populations before interpreting module activities.

name: cell-type-signature-deconvolution
description: Use when you need to infer relative cell type composition from bulk RNA-seq by scoring curated cell-type gene signatures (GMT module lists) with sample-level PC1 module activity rather than a regression-based deconvolution tool.

name: cell-type-silhouette-and-batch-entropy-metrics
description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation or integration methods on the same labeled multi-batch scRNA-seq datasets and you need standardized scores (silhouette, batch entropy, F1, accuracy) plus statistical significance.

name: cell-type-similarity-quartile-stratification
description: Use when evaluating BIRD-predicted differential DH between many cell-type pairs and you need to know how prediction–truth correlation (Pearson, all loci vs differential loci) depends on the similarity of the two cell types' DH profiles.

name: cell-type-spatial-distance-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been projected into a spatially informed pseudo-space and you need to test whether the spatial proximity between annotated cell types differs between biological conditions (e.g., normal vs. disease).

name: cell-type-specific-co-expression-inference
description: Use when raw UMI-count scRNA-seq data need cell-type-specific co-expression networks, when correlation-based methods give inflated false positives due to sequencing depth confounding, or when differential co-expression between disease groups is sought.

name: cell-type-specific-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. BALF or PBMC count matrices from GEO) has been clustered and cell-type-annotated, and the goal is to test candidate genes (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) for differential expression between severity groups per cell type.

name: cell-type-specific-gene-thresholding
description: Use when running deCS.fisher on a marker gene list or GWAS trait-associated gene list and you must first convert a cell type specificity score panel into discrete per-cell-type gene sets via a score cutoff.

name: cell-type-specific-ipa-usage-comparison
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq alignments and InPACT-derived IPA usage estimates are available and the goal is to flag IPA events whose usage is restricted to one cell type versus others.

name: cell-type-specific-model-validation
description: Use when a model trained on paired bulk omics data (e.g., TCGA miRNA-mRNA) must be validated for cell-type-specific inference against scRNA-seq data with known cell-type miRNA profiles (e.g., Isakova Kidney-Breast-Skin GSE151334).

name: cell-type-specific-network-annotation
description: Use when you have cell-type-specific gene/GRN networks (edge-score matrices per cell type) and need to validate biological relevance via TF, cell-type-marker, and ENCODE TF-target enrichment before benchmarking inference methods.

name: cell-type-specific-pseudobulk-mixed-model-fitting
description: Use when per-individual, per-cell-type scRNA-seq data must be aggregated into CTP/ctnu/P pseudobulk inputs and fit with CTMM linear mixed models to quantify or test cell type-specific interindividual variance (and its differentiation between cell types/stages).

name: cell-type-specific-regression-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when predicted and true count matrices must be scored per cell type for multiple prediction scenarios (within-batch/cross-batch, in-sample/out-of-sample) and compared against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN.

name: cell-type-specific-spatial-de-testing
description: Use when the goal is to identify genes whose spatial expression varies within a specific cell type — e.g. testing whether imputation of non-MERFISH genes into a MERFISH slice increases detectable cell-type-specific spatially DE genes.

name: cell-type-specific-variance-component-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq counts with cell and individual metadata need to be summarized into cell type-specific pseudobulk and tested for genes with significant cell type-specific interindividual expression variance.

name: cell-type-specificity-reference-panel-matching
description: Use when a preprocessed, z-scored cluster-level marker-gene expression matrix (clusters as columns) needs automatic cell type labels matched against a human cell type reference panel such as MonacoImmune or BlueprintEncode.

name: cell-type-specificity-score-implementation
description: Use when annotating clusters of a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with scaled matrix) against a tissue-restricted marker database using both positive and negative markers, or when verifying a from-scratch reimplementation of the ScType scoring algorithm.

name: cell-type-specificity-tscore-estimation
description: Use when building or verifying deCS CTGene reference panels: you need per-cell-type ranked gene lists derived from bulk (t-score) or single-cell (z-score) specificity scores before annotation or enrichment.

name: cell-type-stratified-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you have an integration-adjusted expression matrix plus raw logcounts, consensus cell-type labels and per-sample severity metadata, and need to quantify whether integration improves cell-type-stratified prediction accuracy.

name: cell-type-stratified-integration-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq integration methods on datasets with imbalanced cell type proportions, where a cell type-aware batch-mixing metric (rather than plain iLISI) is needed to score batch mixing per cell type.

name: cell-type-stratified-prediction-assessment
description: Use when predicting held-out condition/batch scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., PW034-705) and you must judge prediction accuracy separately per cell type under both condition-only and condition-plus-batch scenarios.

name: cell-type-stratified-pvalue-aggregation
description: Use when a per-sample EMBEDR p-value sweep across kEff/perplexity exists for an annotated single-cell dataset and you need to determine whether cell types are embedded at different neighborhood scales.

name: cell-type-subpopulation-stratification
description: Use when simulating perturbed trajectories from a differentiation time series and you need fate-outcome shifts computed per starting cell state rather than per whole timepoint.

name: cell-type-subset-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking phase inference on heterogeneous droplet-based scRNA-seq where per-cell-type accuracy (e.g., median phase error per population) must be computed against known sampling times.

name: cell-type-subset-cohort-analysis
description: Use when analyzing droplet-based multi-subject single-cell count data where the goal is to test a cell-level predictor (like APOE expression) or subject-level genotype group within one annotated cell type, while accounting for hierarchical subject structure.

name: cell-type-subsetting-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object or raw UMI count matrix contains mixed cell types and the analysis target is cell-type-specific co-expression inference or null-data simulation for one cell type.

name: cell-type-supervised-classification
description: Use when a labeled .h5ad scRNA-seq dataset needs per-cell informativeness scores (data values) for value-based subsampling, quality assessment, or identifying ambiguous/atypical cells relative to their annotated cell types.

name: cell-type-te-marker-identification
description: Use when a locus-level TE quantification matrix (cell × TE counts) has been produced by MATES and the goal is to find TEs that mark specific cell populations recovered by clustering or by a gene-expression reference clustering.

name: cell-type-term-mapping
description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets carry heterogeneous free-text cell annotations (e.g., Tabula Muris Senis-style labels) that must be normalized to Cell Ontology terms before ontology-based classification or cross-dataset annotation.

name: cell-type-text-embedding-similarity
description: Use when you have Cell Ontology text embeddings (cl.ontology.nlp.emb), the ontology graph (cl.obo), and per-cell-type expression profiles, and you want to test whether ontology/text/expression similarity agree.

name: cell-type-tree-comparison-against-published-hierarchy
description: Use when a learned or predicted cell-type hierarchy must be verified against a published cluster-correspondence figure, e.g. checking that AMB2016/AMB2018 visual cortex populations attach to the correct parents.

name: cell-type-unbalancing-simulation
description: Use when evaluating whether a single-cell diagonal integration method (scRNA with scATAC or surface protein) remains robust as cell populations become unbalanced or absent from one modality.

name: cell-type-vector-magnitude-ranking
description: Use when you have a GEDI model fitted to a multi-sample, condition-contrast scRNA-seq atlas (e.g., Harmony-integrated COVID-19 cohort 1) and need a cluster-free, cell-type-level ranking of response strength to a condition.

name: cell-type-vs-rest-contrast-computation
description: Use when preparing single-cell study data for interactive exploration (e.g. Cellenium import) and marker genes must be served instantly per annotated cell type: annotated scRNA expression matrix in H5AD plus cell-type labels are available offline.

name: cell-variance-estimation-and-variance-normalization
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq UMI count data for Normalisr association testing and mean-level (lcpm/normcov) normalization is done but per-cell variance effects of library-size covariates still confound expression.

name: cell2location-deconvolved-data-handling
description: Use when the input is a Visium spatial transcriptomics dataset deconvoluted with Cell2location (spot-level cell-type compositions in AnnData) and the goal is SpatialCells region-based analysis, e.g. community clustering and boundary delineation.

name: cellchat-database-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq cell groups have been clustered and differentially expressed signaling genes identified, and you need to map over-expressed ligands/receptors onto a curated pathway-level interaction database before computing communication probabilities.

name: cellchatdb-signaling-pathway-annotation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has already been clustered into cell groups and you need significant ligand-receptor pairs classified into curated signaling pathways (e.g., reproducing the 60 pairs / 25 pathways day-12 wound result).

name: cellexalvr-input-file-conversion
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq object (Seurat or AnnData) with dimension-reduction coordinates must be exported into CellexalVR input files, including 7-column .mds trajectory files for RNA velocity visualization.

name: cellmarker-marker-confidence-classification
description: Use when you have a ranked DEG list (e.g. singleCellHaystack log.p.vals from scRNA-seq data) and want to validate biological relevance by checking whether known cell type markers are over-represented among the top ranks rather than uniformly distributed.

name: cellmatch-reference-database-querying
description: Use when annotating cell types for identified scRNA-seq clusters (human or mouse) by matching cluster marker genes against a literature-derived, tissue-specific cell taxonomy database, or when boosting SingleR/CellAssign accuracy with a curated reference.

name: celloracle-links-object-construction
description: Use when you have a base GRN edge list (e.g. from the Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas) plus a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP scRNA-seq) and need per-cluster context-dependent GRN configurations.

name: cellphonedb-cci-data-upload
description: Use when you already have pre-computed, inferred ligand-receptor interactions from CellPhoneDB (or CellChat, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR) and need to load them into InterCellar for interactive CCI analysis.

name: cellphonedb-statistical-analysis
description: Use when you need to infer cell-cell interactions from a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type annotations, and must generate one CCI dataset per condition (e.g., control vs moderate vs critical) for downstream InterCellar analysis.

name: cellranger-grna-assignment-comparison
description: Use when a CROP-seq / single-cell CRISPR screen has both Cell Ranger feature-barcode gRNA calls and GiRAFR output, and you need to quantify how many cells carry mutant gRNAs or lack any gRNA call under the default pipeline.

name: cellranger-host-genome-alignment
description: Use when raw 10x scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. HBEC SARS-CoV-2 time-course samples at 1-3 dpi) must first be aligned to the host genome (GRCh38) with cellranger count to produce the 10x output folders and unmapped host reads required by scPathoQuant.

name: cells-per-subject-qc-evaluation
description: Decision support for choosing between NEBULA-LN and NEBULA-HL per gene in multi-subject snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data, when cells-per-subject counts (e.g., CPS ~380–700) may make the large-sample LN approximation unreliable for some genes.

name: celltag-lineage-tracing-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data from CellTag-barcoded reprogramming experiments where early cell states must be linked to later conversion outcomes via clonal lineage tracing and GRN comparison.

name: celltype-annotated-velocity-modeling
description: Use when RNA velocity must be inferred on spliced/unspliced scRNA-seq data (AnnData) with reliable cell-type annotations, especially when the default VAE requires hyperparameter adjustment (larger latent_dim, cell-type-annotated model, or gene subsetting).

name: celltype-identity-parcellation-for-network-nodes
description: Use when building a ligand–receptor edgelist from a Seurat 3.0 scRNAseq object (e.g., panc8) and the nodes must correspond to cell types rather than individual cells or clusters.

name: celltype-label-matching-evaluation
description: Use when you have aligned single-cell embeddings from two modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) with cell-type labels available post hoc, and need to quantify alignment quality across competing methods.

name: celltypist-model-training-and-label-transfer
description: Use when cell-type labels must be transferred from a large labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (.h5ad AnnData with a cell_type key and X_pca representation) to a query dataset, and annotation fidelity should be benchmarked against a full-reference transfer.

name: cellular-barcode-demultiplexing
description: Use when input is single-cell FASTQ/FASTA reads with embedded cellular barcodes/UMIs (10x Chromium, Visium) and the goal is read-to-cell-barcode assignment, optionally with barcode discovery or whitelist filtering.

name: census-hierarchical-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a Seurat object with a UMAP reduction needs automated cell-type labels (normal or cancer tissues), or when you must test how many cells per cluster (e.g. 5–500) are required for stable Census annotations.

name: centrality-based-network-node-ranking
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis needs to identify the driving forces (key nodes) of specific cell types after cell types and signatures have been defined, e.g., ranking TFs regulating a cluster.

name: cerna-network-module-detection
description: Use when you have case/control RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. TCGA tumor vs normal) plus an RBP-ncRNA interaction network (ENCORI CLIP-seq evidence) and need to identify condition-specific, globally or locally optimal RBP-ncRNA sub-networks.

name: certainty-score-threshold-optimization
description: Use when MASI-annotated query data contains cell types absent from the reference (e.g., Oetjen et al. 16 cell types vs. 12-type 10x PBMC reference) and you must recover the unseen types by tuning the certainty-score threshold in the 0.5–0.6 range.

name: cetuximab-response-stratification
description: Use when assigning CMS labels to CRC PDX/cell-line expression data with CMScaller and testing whether CMS2-classified models respond more to cetuximab than non-CMS2 models.

name: chain-status-quality-control
description: Use when a SingleCellExperiment object merged with scVDJ-seq contig data contains non-productive receptors or ambiguous VDJ chain annotations that must be removed before VDJ feature-space or pseudobulk analyses.

name: champ-minfi-workflow-benchmark-timing
description: Use when you need to reproduce or validate the reported runtimes (~3 min ChAMP, ~4 min minfi) of a methylR DNA methylation array analysis on the testData dataset under minimal hardware constraints.

name: champ-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw DNA methylation array IDAT files (450K/EPIC, e.g. from GEO accession GSE207426) must be processed through ChAMP to call differentially methylated CpGs (DMCs) and validate counts against a published analysis.

name: chemokine-couplet-uniqueness-analysis
description: Use when comparing cell-cell communication predictions across multiple patient conditions (e.

name: chemokine-ligand-communication-visualization
description: Use when pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions from scRNA-seq data (e.g., COVID-19 CCI datasets) need targeted visualization of a chemokine ligand family's communication between defined cell clusters, to test enrichment in disease vs. healthy controls.

name: chetah-hierarchical-cell-annotation
description: Use when benchmarking cell type annotation on scRNA-seq data with a labeled reference/training set, and you need CHETAH as a baseline label-assignment method to compare accuracy against neural-network or scmap-based classifiers.

name: chi-square-asymptotic-null-comparison
description: Use when computing p-values and FDR for sc-compReg differential-regulation LR statistics and you need to decide whether the asymptotic Chi-square null is miscalibrated relative to a fitted (Gamma) empirical null.

name: chi-square-boundary-enrichment-testing
description: Use when spot-level positive/negative pathway labels from GSDensity (e.g., BIOCARTA granulocyte or mesenchyme morphogenesis) must be tested for enrichment at anatomical boundaries in Visium ST data.

name: chi-square-contingency-testing
description: Use when you have per-cell binary calls (e.g. cells exceeding a hub-score outlier cutoff of mu + 3 sigma) stratified by a categorical variable such as donor age, and you need to test whether the outlier proportion shifts across categories.

name: chi-square-differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when cell communities (from EVA or Louvain clustering) must be tested for differential enrichment between two conditions (e.g. perturbed vs normal cells), and you need chi-square P-values plus ARI to quantify clustering recovery.

name: chi-square-independence-testing
description: Use when comparing overlap of two gene-level hit sets (e.g., DGE calls from Welch t-tests and DUL calls from scUTRboot WUI tests) and you need to test whether their intersection exceeds chance expectation.

name: chi-square-proportion-testing
description: Use when comparing categorical read-assignment proportions (isoform, TSS, or polyA-site usage) between two biological groups per gene, and you need a gene-level significance call with FDR control and a minimum effect size (delta-PI).

name: chi-squared-variance-testing
description: Use when you already have an RMT eigen-decomposition of a single-cell covariance matrix partitioned into noise-bulk and signal-outlier eigenvectors and need to classify individual genes as signal- versus noise-responsible.

name: chi2-gene-cluster-feature-selection
description: Use when training lifestyle-prediction classifiers on large gene cluster absence/presence matrices (e.

name: chimera-identification-blast-alignment
description: Use when you need to label contigs in a de novo transcriptome assembly as chimeric vs. correct and have (or can build) a reference transcriptome of known, truly expressed transcripts.

name: chimera-removal-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly pipeline's chimera-removal performance must be quantified against a reference where chimeras and correct contigs are already classifiable.

name: chimera-removal-count-analysis
description: Use when a Trinity de novo transcriptome assembly (with paired Illumina RNA-Seq reads) must be screened for chimeric contigs and you need per-step chimera removal counts, e.g. testing filter orders or validating ~97% chimera removal.

name: chimera-removal-from-de-novo-transcriptomes
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity-built from Illumina RNA-Seq reads) is suspected of containing chimeric or redundant contigs and no reference genome is available to assess assembly quality.

name: chimeric-aware-rna-seq-alignment
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a tumor sample must be aligned for fusion detection (Arriba) or for RNA-side variant callers (transIndel, ScanExitron) and chimeric events such as gene fusions must not be missed.

name: chimeric-contig-classification-and-count-tabulation
description: Use when you have a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g., Trinity contigs) plus a reference transcript set and need to quantify how many chimeric vs. correct vs. unidentified contigs a filter removed.

name: chimeric-read-artifact-modeling
description: Use when detecting gene fusions from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq FASTQ data where PCR amplification produces artificial chimeric reads that inflate false-positive fusion candidates.

name: chimeric-read-classification
description: Use when building or evaluating the false-positive filter of a targeted fusion-detection pipeline that must distinguish true fusion reads from artificial chimeric reads in paired-end RNA-seq data.

name: chimeric-read-correlation-analysis
description: Use when STAR alignment logs from RNA-seq samples grouped by tissue show anomalous unmapped ('too short') rates and you need to test whether chimeric reads co-occur with unmappable reads, e.g. to diagnose genome-build or annotation-driven mapping failures in one tissue.

name: chimeric-read-local-alignment
description: Use when running Anchored-fusion on paired-end RNA-seq (FASTQ) data and you have candidate chimeric reads whose mates fail to map to the anchored target gene, requiring precise fusion-partner localization and breakpoint resolution.

name: chimeric-read-negative-sample-generation
description: Use when retraining the HVLD false-positive filter of Anchored-fusion on a new RNA-seq dataset and dataset-specific artificial fusion reads are needed as negative training samples alongside PCAWG positive samples.

name: chimeric-read-splitting
description: Use when demultiplexing long reads (e.g. Ebrahimi et al. 2022 simulated FASTQ) that may contain more than one barcode construct per read, and each detected construct must be reported separately.

name: chimeric-read-supporting-evidence-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking fusion-gene detectors on simulated paired-end FASTQ inputs and you need per-tool counts of spanning reads, split reads, and lowest coverage at which BCR-ABL1, CIC-DUX4, or DUX4-IGH is detected.

name: chimeric-rna-hyb-record-parsing
description: Use when input is hyb-format chimeric RNA sequence data (optionally with paired Vienna/CT fold files) from CLASH or qCLASH experiments and records must be integrity-checked, filtered, and annotated with segment types and miRNA identities before analysis or plotting.

name: chimeric-rna-hybrid-subset-selection
description: Use when a hyb-format file (with optional associated vienna/CT fold files) from CLASH/qCLASH microRNA/target ligation experiments must be subset to records matching identifier substrings, segment-type criteria, or de-duplicated by record id.

name: chimeric-rna-qclash-data-handling
description: Use when input is hyb-format hybrid (chimeric) sequence data from qCLASH/CLASH experiments — e.g. GEO-derived GSE101978 data — that must be integrity-checked, filtered, evaluated for miRNA/segment types, or merged with predicted secondary structure in Vienna dot-bracket format.

name: chimeric-rna-segment-type-annotation
description: Use when input is a hyb-format hybrid (chimeric RNA) file from miRNA/target ligation methods such as CLASH/qCLASH and records need seg1_type/seg2_type and miRNA_seg annotations before quantification or filtering.

name: chimeric-transcript-identification
description: Use when tumor RNA-Seq FASTQ reads are available and fusion-derived neoantigen candidates are needed alongside WES/WGS-based SNV/INDEL neoantigen prediction in TSNAD.

name: chip-seq-gold-standard-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether predicted chromatin accessibility (e.g., BIRD-predicted DH) can rank TF motif sites correctly, by comparing against ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks for known TFs such as ELF1 in GM12878.

name: chip-seq-ground-truth-network-construction
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference methods (scPRINT, scGPT, DeepSEM, Geneformer, GENIE3) against cell type-specific ChIP-seq or perturb-seq ground truths such as MCalla et al. ESC networks or K562 gwps.

name: chip-seq-ground-truth-network-evaluation
description: Use when a ranked TF–gene edge list has been produced from scRNA-seq data (e.g. Tabula Muris tissue data) and needs quantitative validation against ChIP-Atlas-derived ground-truth GRNs per cell type using AUROC and EPR.

name: chip-seq-peak-overlap-annotation
description: Use when peak-gene pairs (e.g., GrID-Net vs correlation baselines on 10x Multiome) must be validated for enhancer priming states, requiring H3K4me1/H3K27ac ChIP-seq overlap of ATAC peak coordinates.

name: chip-seq-regulatory-potential-annotation
description: Use when a data-learned gene program (e.g., one of the 86 MeCs) needs candidate transcriptional regulators, and TF ChIP-seq binding potentials (Lisa) can be combined with per-gene program weights.

name: chipseq-ground-truth-network-evaluation
description: Use when an inferred gene regulatory network from scRNA-seq data must be quantitatively validated against a ChIP-seq ground-truth network using AUPRC and EPR on BEELINE lineage benchmarks.

name: chord-diagram-visualization
description: Use when you have per-cluster or per-cell-type SNV scores from ScType/vartrix for a tumor scRNA-seq sample and need a visual, similarity-based separation of malignant vs non-malignant cell populations.

name: chromatin-3d-model-coordinate-conversion
description: Use when a cudaMMC simulation output file containing 3D coordinates of chromatin beads must be turned into a parseable structural file, particularly for whole-chromosome models whose bead counts exceed legacy PDB format limits.

name: chromatin-accessibility-peak-calling
description: Use when DC3 has assigned single cells to subpopulations and you need subpopulation-specific open peaks and motif enrichment scores to nominate candidate key regulatory transcription factors.

name: chromatin-contact-based-scoring
description: Use when candidate enhancer regions need enhancer-gene interaction scores that incorporate chromatin contact data (e.g. Hi-C maps), such as ranking CRISPRi-validated enhancer-gene pairs on the three validation datasets or comparing against model-based scores like Enformer in-silico mutagenesis.

name: chromatin-modeling-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two chromatin modelling tools must be compared for computational performance or run-to-run stability, and per-run execution times are available across repeated simulations on defined chromosomes.

name: chromosome-level-3d-genome-reconstruction
description: Use when you have ChIA-PET anchor/cluster/singleton files (e.g. GM12878 CTCF Rep1) and need per-chromosome 3D chromatin structure ensembles faster than 3D-GNOME, with a CUDA GPU (compute capability >= 6.0) available.

name: chromvar-transcription-factor-activity-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-Seq-derived lineage-priming predictions (e.g. DICE primed cells and their TFs such as GATA1, KLF1, IRF8) need independent validation against matched scATAC-Seq accessibility and chromVAR TF activity (TFA) data.

name: chromvar-transcription-factor-activity-estimation
description: Use when inferring transcription factor activity from single-cell chromatin accessibility peaks (scATAC-seq or multiome), as a prerequisite for linking TF motif deviation scores to gene expression in enhancer-based gene regulatory network construction.

name: chu-liu-edmonds-arborescence-reconstruction
description: Use when a fully connected directed graph over measured variables must be collapsed into a single rooted directed tree, and data-driven edge weights (e.g., from bivariate SEM or spline fits) are available or can be estimated per edge.

name: chunked-estep-vectorized-computation
description: Use when fitting scPLS to large scRNAseq count matrices (thousands of cells × tens of thousands of genes) where the naive full-matrix EM becomes CPU-prohibitive and a scalable block-wise EM is needed.

name: chunked-processing-of-large-scrnaseq-matrices
description: Use when a per-cell computation (e.g. ranking-based PAS scoring over >1000 pathways) must run on a cell-gene expression matrix too large to hold as a dense matrix in memory.

name: ci-graph-merging-across-sections
description: Use when visualizing two or more spatially resolved tissue sections with shared cell-type labels (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl regeneration time points) and default per-section colorization mismatches or visually confuses corresponding cell types across sections.

name: ci-graph-umap-embedding-cielab
description: Use when coloring cellular-resolution spatial transcriptomics (SRT) data where a default palette (e.g., Scanpy's) makes spatially adjacent cell types perceptually ambiguous, and you need colors chosen to maximize CIELab contrast among neighboring clusters.

name: cibersort-immune-fraction-comparison
description: Use when testing whether inferred immune composition (e.g., CIBERSORT CD8+ T-cell and Treg fractions) differs between two predefined sample groups, such as viral-positive vs viral-negative TCGA tumor samples.

name: cibersort-signature-based-fraction-estimation
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix plus sample metadata and an annotated single-cell reference atlas, and you need to quantify per-sample cell-type fractions across conditions.

name: ciede2000-color-difference-computation
description: Use when quantifying how visually distinguishable two colors (or two whole palettes) are — e.g. adjacent cell-type pairs in spatial-omics plots, image-extracted vs. default palettes, or DOI-driven color assignments.

name: cielab-color-space-frequency-binning
description: Use when a coloring palette must be derived from a reference image (e.g., a journal cover figure) so that visualizations preserve the image's theme while remaining discriminable against baselines like matplotlib tab20.

name: cigar-like-mutation-string-annotation
description: Use when consensus gRNA sequences (consensus.sequence.gRNA.txt) must be compared to a designed gRNA-cassette reference and each mutation pinpointed relative to annotated cassette structures, producing a variant table for downstream mutation-aware cell assignment.

name: circadian-cycler-de-novo-detection
description: Use when scRNA-seq counts lack labeled clock-controlled genes and you need unsupervised phase inference: run Tempo in de novo cycler-detection mode, cross-check calls against an independent rhythmicity test (e.g., JTKCycle q<0.05), and re-estimate phase.

name: circadian-phase-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (droplet or plate based) has an unknown or partially known circadian phase per cell and you need to quantify how accurately different unsupervised phase-inference methods recover it.

name: circadian-phase-prediction-pseudobulk
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomic data lack timestamps and you need per-cell-type circadian time estimates, e.g., comparing circadian phase heterogeneity across cell types via bootstrapped pseudobulk tauFisher predictions.

name: circadian-phase-stability-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking unsupervised circadian phase inference on scRNA-seq data and you need to quantify how stable per-cell phase point estimates are across repeated runs of competing methods, as in Fig. 2f/5d stability distributions.

name: circadian-phase-uncertainty-quantification
description: Use when you have approximate posterior phase samples from Tempo alongside known true or sample-collection phases and need to verify that reported phase uncertainty (credible intervals) is calibrated in sparse single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: circadian-time-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing circadian phase-prediction methods (e.g., tauFisher vs ZeitZeiger vs TimeSignatR) on timestamped bulk RNA time-course data, or when needing standardized accuracy/RMSE metrics with a ±2-hour correctness rule.

name: circadian-time-series-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw bulk transcriptomic time-series matrix with time-encoded column names must be converted into tauFisher training/testing inputs — e.

name: circbase-id-mapping
description: Use when building RBP-ncRNA edge lists from ENCORI/starBase interaction tables and node identifiers must be normalized to Ensembl gene IDs, miRBase MIMAT* accessions, or circBase IDs before module detection.

name: circrna-back-splice-junction-detection
description: Use when you have name-sorted accepted_hits.sorted.sam from TopHat2 paired-end RNA-seq data and need a CircAST-format circRNA_list.txt of back-spliced junctions (chromosome, start, end) before running full-length circRNA isoform assembly.

name: circrna-call-coordinate-intersection
description: Use when you have circRNA call sets from ≥2 detection pipelines on the same ribo− RNA-seq data and need coordinate-based overlaps, Venn counts, or per-circRNA BSJ fragment comparisons.

name: circrna-detection-from-rnaseq-alignments
description: Use when raw FASTQ/alignment data from knockdown (shRNA/siRNA) or condition-controlled RNA-seq experiments must be mined for back-splice circRNAs to test whether knocking down a candidate RBP changes global circRNA expression.

name: circrna-expression-quantification
description: Use when you need to quantify circRNA expression and compare it to cognate linear RNA expression from ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files, e.g. to distinguish tumor vs paired-normal circRNA profiles where standard fragment counts fail.

name: circrna-full-length-isoform-assembly
description: Use when paired-end RNA-seq alignments and a back-splice junction list exist and the goal is to reconstruct full-length circular transcript sequences (including isoforms) and estimate FPKM/TPM expression per circRNA locus.

name: circrna-isoform-distribution-statistics
description: Use when CircAST output tables (per-transcript junction reads, assigned reads, FPKM/TPM) are available for multiple samples and the goal is to characterize how many and how diverse the circular isoforms are across cell lines or tissues.

name: circrna-isoform-quantification-accuracy-analysis
description: Use when simulated RNA-seq data with known ground-truth circRNA isoforms have been processed by CircAST and you must quantify how BSJ overlap complexity (relation index) affects assembly and quantification accuracy.

name: circrna-linear-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when validating circRNA quantification from ribo− RNA-seq against RT-qPCR or existing FPKM/FPM measures, or when reproducing published Pearson correlations (e.g. r=0.92, 0.78, 0.72, 1.00, 0.93) for FPB and CIRCscore values.

name: circrna-output-table-parsing
description: Use when a CircAST result file (tab-separated, 13 columns ending in junction read counts, FPKM, TPM, assigned reads) must be loaded and structured for downstream RI stratification, isoform comparison, or expression-accuracy analysis.

name: circrna-protein-interaction-mapping
description: Use when building protein–circRNA interaction counts (C values) from predicted RBP–RNA interactomes plus circRNA annotations, e.g. as an input feature for candidate regulator scoring or clustering.

name: circrna-regulator-candidate-validation
description: Use when a list of predicted circRNA regulators (e.g., CRIT NMF cluster output) must be tested for over-representation of circRNA-binding RBPs from CLIP databases (POSTAR3, ENCORI) via one-sided Fisher's exact tests.

name: circrna-tool-output-format-conversion
description: Use when a circRNA junction list from a BSJ detector (CIRCexplorer2 annotated_circ.txt, CIRI2 result.txt, UROBORUS, or any similar tool) must be reshaped into CircAST's circRNA_list.txt (chromosome/start/end) before full-length assembly.

name: circrna-transcript-structure-construction-from-bsj
description: Use when back-spliced junction records (e.g., 2923 Hs68 BSJs from SRA SRR444974 in CircAST junction-list format) must be converted into full circular transcript structures on a UCSC hg19 GTF annotation.

name: circscore-computation-from-fpb-ratios
description: Use when ribo− RNA-seq data has been mapped (HISAT2 + TopHat-Fusion), circRNAs annotated via CIRCexplorer2, and FPBcirc/FPBlinear values are available per gene locus and a relative circRNA expression level is needed.

name: circular-autoencoder-pseudo-time-inference
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain a latent periodic process such as the cell cycle and linear PC-based or regression-based representations cannot accurately represent the circular timing of cells.

name: circular-embedding-visualization-of-cell-cycle-phases
description: Use when single-cell data carry a priori labels along a cyclical process (e.g., G1.S, S, G2, G2.M, M.G1 cell-cycle phase scores) and the goal is a supervised, interpretable circular embedding plus phase-classification accuracy rather than an unbiased clustering.

name: circular-latent-autoencoder-training
description: Use when an scRNA-seq dataset preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments (Ms/Mu layers) should be given a continuous circular cell-cycle phase per cell, rather than a discrete marker-based G1/S/G2M label.

name: circular-linear-rna-expression-comparison
description: Use when quantifying circRNA expression from ribo− paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs and comparing it against cognate linear RNA expression at the same gene loci (CIRCscore = FPBcirc/FPBlinear).

name: circular-manifold-autoencoder-modeling
description: Use when scRNA-seq (or qPCR) expression matrices should be characterized for a periodic/circular latent process (e.g., cell-cycle staging with Hoechst-validated labels), especially where linear methods (PCA, NMF, ICA) or marker-gene methods (Cyclone, reCAT) underperform.

name: circular-manifold-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be assigned circular/periodic pseudo-time (e.g., cell-cycle stages) or when periodic-process-associated genes must be identified without marker genes.

name: circular-phase-variable-comparison
description: Use when comparing circular cell-cycle phase assignments from two DeepCycle runs (e.g. ablated inputs or replicate fits) to quantify phase consistency or reproduce the Supplementary Fig. S8 inconsistency.

name: circular-phase-wraparound-handling
description: Use when computing credible intervals or coverage statistics over 24 h circadian phase estimates whose posterior density straddles phase 0/24 (midnight), e.g. validating Tempo's uncertainty calibration on scRNA-seq time-course data.

name: circular-pseudotime-gene-ranking
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells plausibly follow a periodic process (e.g., cell cycle) and you need to identify the associated genes ab initio from expression kinetics rather than marker genes, then benchmark the ranking against PCA-based alternatives.

name: circular-pseudotime-wrapping
description: Use when a Cyclum sinusoidal autoencoder has been trained on log2(x+1)-transformed, variance-1-scaled scRNA-seq data and the circular latent stage of each cell must be converted into a wrapped [0, 2π] pseudo-time.

name: circular-rna-back-splice-junction-quantification
description: Use when ribo− depleted RNA-seq FASTQ (or a CIRCexplorer2 circRNA output plus a HISAT2 BAM) needs circRNA quantification per BSJ with readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and CIRCscore per locus.

name: circular-rna-backsplice-detection
description: Use when RNA-Seq BAM reads may contain gene fusions and you need to call the primary fusion junction plus secondary splice-variant/backsplice junctions and fcircRNAs, e.g. sim56-like or TMPRSS2::ERG-style data.

name: circular-statistics-angular-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when comparing two or more groups of predicted circadian times (angles on a 0-24 h clock) to formally test whether the angular distributions differ in homogeneity or dispersion, e.g., bootstrapped tauFisher predictions per cell type at each ZT time point.

name: circular-statistics-ordering-assessment
description: Use when recursive neural ODE forecasts (e.g., RNAForecaster 72-step predictions) must be validated for biologically ordered progression along a circular trajectory such as cell-cycle position from tricycle.

name: circular-statistics-standard-deviation-computation
description: Use when quantifying run-to-run stability of circular quantities (e.g., circadian phase in hours on a 24 h cycle) by computing per-cell circular standard deviation across five or more replicate runs of a phase-inference method on scRNA-seq data.

name: circular-theta-variable-binning
description: Use when an AnnData object already carries a continuous circular cell cycle phase (obs['cell_cycle_theta']) and discrete phase assignments plus per-phase fractions are needed for validation against flow cytometry.

name: circular-trajectory-evaluation
description: Use when you have inferred a circular latent time (e.g. adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta']) from cycling genes in scRNA-seq data and need to verify the fits, phase-transition angles, and agreement with discrete/continuous baseline methods.

name: circular-variable-handling
description: Use when cells carry a circular phase annotation (obs['cell_cycle_theta']) from DeepCycle and you must bin, average, or fit quantities (e.g. total UMI counts) across the full cell cycle without breaking the 0/2π wrap-around.

name: cis-eqtl-variant-filtering
description: Use when summary-level eQTL statistics must be converted into per-gene cis-window SNP sets and LD-clumped reference inputs for PRS/TWAS Stage I weight training from summary data.

name: cis-nat-identification-from-genome-annotation
description: Use when the task is to comprehensively extract cis-NAT pairs from genome annotation (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns, e.g. from Ensembl) with optional RNA-seq expression profiling (TPM, FPKM, fold_change, padj), and to classify them into EB/FO/HH/TT structural types.

name: cis-nat-overlap-extraction
description: Use when a gene annotation (CSV with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) must be mined for opposite-strand cis-NAT pairs, especially fully-overlapped (FO) pairs where one gene's transcribed interval completely contains its partner's.

name: cis-nat-pair-count-tabulation
description: Use when a CCIVR run has produced Table.csv with cis-NAT pairs carrying fold_change and padj expression columns, and you need expression-combination counts (down-down, down-up, up-down, up-up) per EB/FO/HH/TT type or a down-up pair set.

name: cis-nat-pair-partner-gene-selection
description: Use when you have CCIVR output from an RNA-seq dataset (e.g. Huh-7 cells with TGFβ stimulation) and need to partition differentially expressed cis-NAT partner genes by direction (fold_change/padj) into gene lists for enrichment analysis.

name: cis-nat-type-frequency-quantification
description: Use when genome annotations (e.g. Ensembl GTF releases 105/104 or Ensembl plants/fungi release 52) must be converted and screened with CCIVR to tabulate cis-NAT type counts and percentages per organism.

name: cis-regulatory-distance-decay-modeling
description: Use when preprocessing paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq for cnmf joint clustering and you need a peak-gene coupling matrix that weights open chromatin peaks by distance to genes (d0 = 40 kb decay).

name: cis-regulatory-motif-enrichment-filtering
description: Use when converting co-expression modules into directed gene regulatory networks: after GRNBoost2 proposes candidate TF–TG edges from single-cell expression data, to retain only edges with cis-regulatory motif evidence.

name: cisbp-motif-database-query
description: Use when you have a set of ATAC-seq/DNase peak sequences and need TF motif hits to construct a candidate TF–target regulatory mask as a prior for GRN inference.

name: cite-seq-adt-count-processing
description: Use when raw ADT/CITE-seq FASTQ files (I1/R1/R2) from hashed samples need to be converted into antibody-by-cell UMI count matrices, optionally after removing index-hopped reads from combined NovaSeq GEX+ADT data.

name: cite-seq-adt-normalization
description: Use when raw ADT/protein UMI counts from droplet-based single-cell assays (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) must be normalized and denoised before clustering, or when comparing dsb against CLR normalization for protein-based analyses.

name: cite-seq-adt-relative-abundance-transformation
description: Use when preparing paired transcriptome–surface protein (CITE-seq or REAP-seq) data as training targets for cTP-net or comparable protein-imputation models: raw ADT barcode counts must be converted to per-cell relative abundances before model training.

name: cite-seq-atac-seq-multimodal-integration
description: Use when clustering cells measured across multiple modalities (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT, or SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq RNA+ATAC) and you need integrated unsupervised embeddings comparable to totalVI/MultiVI/MOFA+ methods.

name: cite-seq-batch-correction-comparison
description: Use when combining two or more CITE-seq datasets (e.g., pbmc_1k_protein_v3 and pbmc_10k_protein_v3) and you need to decide whether Seurat batch correction changes the cell groups identified by multimodal LinQ-View clustering.

name: cite-seq-cell-embedding-clustering-subsetting
description: Use when scME joint embeddings from CITE-seq BMNC data must be subdivided into cell-type subclusters and the subdivision needs validation from differential protein (CDT ADT) markers like CD69 and CD25 rather than genes.

name: cite-seq-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when raw ADT/protein UMI count matrices from a CITE-seq experiment are available (e.g., raw and filtered Cell Ranger outputs) and you need to characterize ambient antibody background before normalization, or verify that empty-droplet background reflects protein levels in cells.

name: cite-seq-dual-modality-model-implementation
description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq RNA gene counts and raw protein ADT counts (CSV, rows=cells) and need a joint cell embedding that retains modality-specific complementary information, not just shared structure.

name: cite-seq-expression-normalization
description: Use when raw CITE-seq or scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO GSE100866 CBMC data) must be normalized with log2(1+X) before marker selection or k-NN label classification.

name: cite-seq-hashtag-count-normalization
description: Use when cell-hashing CITE-seq data must be demultiplexed: a hashtag count matrix per cell barcode exists and each cell needs a sample identity call plus doublet/negative classification before downstream GEX/ADT analysis.

name: cite-seq-hashtag-umi-counting
description: Use when hashed CITE-seq ADT FASTQs (I1/R1/R2 per sample) must be converted into per-cell hashtag UMI count matrices prior to demultiplexing sample identities in a gExcite/Snakemake workflow.

name: cite-seq-multimodal-clustering
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with both transcriptome and surface-protein (ADT) modalities and the goal is joint cell-population clustering plus quantitative purity scoring in both modalities.

name: cite-seq-multimodal-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw CITE-seq data (paired scRNA-seq and ADT counts from platforms like 10X Chromium) must be filtered, normalized, and packaged for joint multimodal clustering benchmarking.

name: cite-seq-multimodal-distance-fusion
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with a limited number of ADT features (e.g. <50) where unimodal or naive joint analysis fails to separate subsets (e.g. memory vs naive CD4+ T cells), or when distinguishing antigen-specific B cell populations

name: cite-seq-multimodal-embedding-generation
description: Use when CITE-seq or other multimodal single-cell data (same cells measured across modalities, e.g. RNA + ADT matrices) needs integrated embeddings to cluster cells into major and minor cell types.

name: cite-seq-multimodal-integration
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing multimodal CITE-seq integration, specifically testing whether ALRA imputation of RNA counts improves agreement between RNA-space and ADT protein-space pairwise cell distances.

name: cite-seq-multimodal-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing integration algorithms (e.g. scMerge2, scMerge2-h, Seurat, Harmony, scVI, Scanorama) on a multi-batch CITE-seq or scRNA-seq dataset where both batch labels and cell-type annotations are available for evaluation.

name: cite-seq-multimodal-reference-building
description: Use when a CITE-seq reference with paired mRNA and surface protein measurements is available but query samples are mRNA-only, and you need to infer query surface protein levels from reference mapping.

name: cite-seq-protein-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a CITE-seq dataset contains cell-surface protein abundance (e.g., PBMC antibody-derived tags) and trusted cell-type labels are needed as reference ground truth for benchmarking clustering or label-validation methods.

name: cite-seq-protein-differential-activity-analysis
description: Use when analyzing a multimodal CITE-seq/PBMC h5ad atlas (>200k cells, 228 proteins) to rank surface proteins by differential activity in PCA space without clustering, and to compare that ranking against cluster-based DE baselines.

name: cite-seq-protein-distance-constraint-generation
description: Use when a CITE-seq dataset provides protein (ADT) measurements on the same cells as mRNA counts, and the goal is to improve mRNA clustering accuracy or enforce biologically consistent cluster labels (e.g., CD4/CD8 T cell subtypes) via pairwise constraints.

name: cite-seq-protein-imputation-from-scrna
description: Use when you have a UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrix and want per-cell relative abundance estimates of surface protein immunophenotype markers, or when benchmarking imputation against raw/denoised RNA baselines or Seurat v3 anchor transfer.

name: cite-seq-protein-mrna-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a denoising/imputation method improves scRNA-seq data using CITE-seq ADT protein abundances as ground truth, e.g. reproducing Fig. 6 protein-mRNA co-expression and CD3E detection-rate analyses.

name: cite-seq-protein-rna-integration
description: Use when CITE-seq data pairs surface-protein abundance (e.g. CD16/CD56 ADTs) with RNA counts for the same genes and the goal is to test whether RNA denoising recovers protein-defined sub-population structure.

name: cite-seq-raw-count-preprocessing
description: Use when a holdout CITE-seq UMI count matrix must be quality-filtered and LogNormalized without SAVER-X denoising to run the denoising-ablation of cTP-net and measure the correlation drop versus the denoised baseline.

name: cite-seq-surface-protein-expression-summarization
description: Use when you have scMM output from CITE-seq (transcriptome & surface protein) data and need cluster-level multimodal feature heatmaps to interpret a high-resolution latent-space clustering, e.g. reproducing the PBMC ~54-cluster figure.

name: citeseq-adt-normalization-empty-droplets
description: Use when normalizing droplet-based single-cell protein (ADT) counts — e.g. CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq — where raw and filtered Cell Ranger matrices are available so empty droplets can estimate ambient antibody background.

name: citeseq-paired-multimodal-data-handling
description: Use when you hold paired UMI-based scRNA-seq and ADT (protein) count matrices from CITE-seq or REAP-seq and need normalized RNA features plus CLR-transformed protein targets before surface-protein imputation with cTP-net.

name: citeseq-protein-expression-distribution-analysis
description: Use when CITE-seq/ADT counts have been dsb step-I normalized (log10 pseudocount 10, standardized by empty-droplet background mean/SD) and you need to determine the number of Gaussian components per cell or extract the fitted background mean µ1.

name: citeseq-rna-adt-count-data-preparation
description: Use when raw paired CITE-seq (or SMAGE-seq) mRNA + ADT count matrices must be converted into the structured H5 input (X1 = RNA, X2 = ADT) that scMDC expects before deep clustering.

name: ckg-feature-construction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (BAM/FASTA) must be converted into alignment-free features for cell type classification, especially when a reference genome is incomplete or insufficient; also for comparing k-mer sizes (e.g., 21-mer vs 16-mer) under fixed fingerprints, classifiers, and read types.

name: ckg-to-gene-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have CKG cell features (reference-free k-mer groups) plus a CKG look-up table and need to interpret CKGs at gene level, e.g. to overlap them with gene expression feature rankings.

name: ckg-versus-gene-expression-feature-comparison
description: Decision support for whether reference-free CKG features should replace gene expression features when classifying cell types in scRNA-seq data, particularly when the reference genome may be incomplete or insufficient.

name: clade-based-distance-cid-computation
description: Use when assessing whether a lineage-reconstruction method recovers the true topology for cells sharing an identical barcode but belonging to different true clones (barcode homoplasy), via CID versus random-tree baselines.

name: clara-kmedoids-mst-topology-inference
description: Use when inferring a tree-shaped trajectory (linear, bifurcation, multifurcation, tree) from single-cell data in a low-dimensional embedding, and clustering quality (not manual tuning) must determine the milestone topology.

name: class-average-vector-inner-product-analysis
description: Use when a labeled gene-expression matrix (e.g., TCGA RNA-seq tumor vs. normal) must be reduced to a ranked feature list, and ranking should reflect a classifier's learned weights rather than differential-expression p values.

name: class-balanced-cell-downsampling
description: Use when assembling a training corpus of annotated single-cell data from multiple tumor datasets (e.g., TISCH) where malignant and non-malignant cell counts differ per tissue and a balanced classifier must be trained.

name: class-imbalance-loss-weighting
description: Use when training a SIMS classifier on annotated scRNA-seq data (h5ad AnnData with a 'class_label' column) whose cell-type distribution is imbalanced and rare populations must still be learned.

name: class-imbalance-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating a cell-type annotation or novelty detector on scRNA-seq data where novel/rare cells form a small positive class and you need threshold-free ranking metrics (AUROC, AUPR) plus a tail metric (FPR95).

name: class-imbalance-random-under-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-type classifier (e.g., SciBet vs. scmap/Seurat v3) on datasets with unequal cells per type, where rare or closely related subtypes could be hidden by class imbalance in the confusion matrix.

name: class-imbalance-smote-oversampling
description: Use when building an lncRNA/mRNA classifier from a training set where the two transcript classes are imbalanced (e.g. H-Train or a self-trained model via lncDC-train.py), prior to running RFECV feature selection or XGBoost training.

name: class-imbalanced-neural-network-training
description: Use when testing robustness of the CLOUDe neural network classifier to class imbalance: training data are skewed toward 'Redundant' or 'Unique' classes, but evaluation must occur on a balanced test set.

name: class-informed-graph-embedding
description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. intestinal epithelial or myeloid progenitor cells) plus class labels from a prior clustering, and need a 2D visualization preserving both cluster separation and differentiation pathways.

name: class-probability-table-generation
description: Use when you have a trained random forest TSG/OG model set with per-fold model files and a feature matrix of unlabelled genes, and need a consolidated consensus table of TSG/OG labels with per-class probabilities.

name: class-separation-benchmarking-across-datasets
description: Use when comparing supervised dimensionality-reduction visualizations across multiple single-cell datasets to verify that a reduced feature set preserves or improves a priori class-label separation relative to a full-feature baseline.

name: class-size-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a user-supplied cluster/class assignment file for GraphDDP or GraphEmbed contains rare or over-sized classes, and the embedding pipeline must drop classes with fewer than min_threshold (default 5) or cap classes at max_threshold (default 300) instances before layout.

name: classification-accuracy-aggregation-across-replicates
description: Use when you must fairly compare gene/feature-selection methods for cell type identification: hold the classifier constant, repeat randomized train/test splits many times, and aggregate per-repetition accuracies into per-dataset means before ranking methods.

name: classification-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you have per-cell gene set scores (e.g., summed_up scores from gssnng) for both unsmoothed and NNG-smoothed AnnData objects plus per-cell condition labels, and need to quantify whether smoothing improves a simple median-cut-point classifier.

name: classification-accuracy-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when a gene-expression matrix with pre-existing reference labels (e.g. original CMS classes for TCGA primary colorectal cancers, n = 143) must be re-classified and agreement quantified as accuracy with confidence intervals and per-class sensitivity/specificity.

name: classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you must benchmark competing fixed gene-signature (biomarker candidate) sets for cancer-vs-normal classification on a labeled TCGA-style expression matrix, and check each signature's LOOCV accuracy against published values.

name: classification-concordance-analysis
description: Use when replicating or validating a subtype/classification pipeline where novel calls must be compared against published labels and pairwise stability across repeated instances must be quantified as concordance percentages.

name: classification-error-benchmarking
description: Use when a selected or curated gene marker panel must be quantitatively compared against baselines by held-out cell label classification error in the marker-reduced feature space.

name: classification-metric-computation
description: Use when cell-type predictions from identification methods (e.g. Seurat, SingleR, SciBet, CELLBLAST) must be scored against manual ground-truth labels to rank methods by accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate in a cross-validation or cross-platform evaluation.

name: classification-metric-computation
description: Use when you have binary lncRNA/mrna prediction labels (e.g., LncDC CSV outputs or baseline tool outputs on H-Test/M-Test) and must quantify accuracy, precision, specificity, or MCC for benchmark tables or ablation comparisons.

name: classification-metric-computation
description: Use when you have predicted cell-type labels from one or more annotators on the Peng 2019 pancreatic cancer dataset and author-provided ground-truth annotations, and need per-method F1, balanced accuracy, accuracy, label similarity, and runtime in a comparison table.

name: classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when a binary cell-level classifier (e.g. PreCanCell k-NN predictions, or CHETAH/SciBet/SCINA/scmap/SingleR/ikarus outputs) must be scored against ground-truth malignant/non-malignant labels using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy and AUROC.

name: classification-metric-evaluation-f1-accuracy
description: Use when a Symphony mapQuery/knnPredict annotation transfer must be quantitatively validated against known reference labels, e.g. reproducing the reported median F1 of 0.83 and accuracy of 85.0% at k = 30.

name: classification-metrics-aggregation-accuracy-macro-f1
description: Use when comparing cell-type classification methods on pre-annotated single-cell RNA-seq datasets and you need per-fold held-out accuracy and Macro F1 aggregated into a method-by-dataset benchmark table.

name: classification-metrics-computation
description: Use when demultiplexing assignments from hashing methods (HTOreader, HTOdemux, MULTI-seq, GMM-Demux, DropletUtils, BFF) must be validated quantitatively against known per-cell sample labels.

name: classification-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when a supervised cell type or cell state classifier has been trained on labeled scRNA-seq data and its predictive quality must be quantified on a test set, especially when comparing pipelines on accuracy alongside resource metrics.

name: classification-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when a trained cell-type classifier (e.g., a Keras neural network on CKG or gene-expression features) must be scored against known labels, or when comparing classifiers across dataset pairs.

name: classification-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-type identifiers (MarkerCount, SingleR, scmap, CaSTLe, CHETAH) across annotated scRNA-seq dataset pairs where some test populations are absent from the reference, so both assignment accuracy and unknown-population rejection must be scored.

name: classification-performance-metric-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a binary cell-level drug-response predictor (e.g. scDEAL on scRNA-seq data with 'sens_label' in adata.obs) and you need multi-metric accuracy plus variation over repeated 80/20 stratified samplings.

name: classification-performance-visualization
description: Use when you have trained classifier outputs (per-cell probabilities and binary decisions) plus ground-truth cell-type labels and need to compare classification algorithms via per-type F1, precision, and average precision.

name: classification-tree-pruning
description: Use when a dipm() or spmtree() tree was fitted (possibly with default pruning disabled) and the resulting node structure needs simplification into a parsimonious subgroup tree before printing, plotting, or saving the fitted object.

name: classifier-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you have candidate subnetworks (e.g. Steiner-tree or r2z-weighted variants from SEMtree) plus a binary patient label vector and need to compare subnetwork detection methods by out-of-sample classification accuracy and predictor-gene parsimony.

name: classifier-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a trained cell-state classifier (e.g. TILPRED) and an independent scRNA-seq dataset with consensus labels from multiple clustering methods (SNN, K-means, hierarchical), and need a quantitative accuracy estimate of the classifier's agreement with that ground truth.

name: classifier-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when the goal is to compare cell-classification accuracy of a learned scRNA-seq representation (e.g., scDHA embedding) versus standard ML classifiers across multiple train-test dataset combinations.

name: classifier-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when a previously selected feature set must be stress-tested for classifier dependence — i.e., compare accuracy of two algorithms (e.g., XGBoost vs SVM) on the exact same features and splits.

name: classifier-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a binary cell-state classifier (malignant vs normal) against published baselines on labeled gold standard datasets and unlabeled silver standard datasets with weighted accuracy metrics.

name: classifier-accuracy-specificity-precision-evaluation
description: Use when a per-site classifier output (SNP vs editing probability/label for A-to-G candidates) must be scored against a ground truth set such as HEK293T KO-WT, KO-OE, or A549 bona fide editing sites.

name: classifier-auroc-evaluation
description: Use when a sample's RNA-seq BAM must be classified into skipped vs composite intronic terminal exon candidates and classifier performance (AUROC, TPR, F1, MCC) must be quantified against held-out annotated regions.

name: classifier-baseline-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a new cell type annotation method on a labeled scRNA-seq dataset and you need a simple baseline (1NN) plus tools (scMatch, SingleR) for fair comparison via median F1.

name: classifier-benchmark-metrics-computation
description: Use when a trained cell-type classifier (e.g., CellO IR or CLR models) and a labeled single-cell test set must be compared against a baseline by computing F1-score, precision, and average precision per Cell Ontology term.

name: classifier-branch-ablation-comparison
description: Use when you must attribute an imputation/denoising method's performance to a specific architecture component and need an ablation control (e.g., AutoClass vs. a plain autoencoder) on simulated scRNA-Seq data.

name: classifier-confusion-matrix-evaluation
description: Use when a trained or packaged classifier (e.g. TILPRED on a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 TIL profiles) must be validated on a held-out test split by computing accuracy, per-class specificity/sensitivity from a confusion matrix against annotated labels.

name: classifier-confusion-matrix-evaluation
description: Use when a Pollock model has been trained on annotated scRNA-seq data (e.g. BRCA pan-immune states) and you must quantify which cell states a withheld validation partition classifies poorly.

name: classifier-f1-evaluation-across-random-seeds
