description: Use when you have a continuous outcome (e.g., a signature score) and continuous predictors (e.g., reaction fluxes) per sample and need effect-size estimates with 95% CIs rather than only p-values.

name: confidence-threshold-application
description: Use when you have per-cell label predictions from multiple annotation tools and need to separate high-confidence (majority-agreed) from unconfident cells before propagating labels.

name: confidence-threshold-unknown-class-assignment
description: Use when a trained SIMS/TabNet checkpoint's raw logits must be turned into calibrated per-cell classification probabilities and cells below a confidence cutoff should be flagged as 'unknown' instead of receiving a cell-type label.

name: confidence-thresholding-interaction-matrix
description: Use when reconstructing sparse directed GRNs from time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell expression data with COSLIR and you must suppress unstable or spurious interaction estimates via bootstrapped confidence and magnitude clipping.

name: confidence-weighted-edge-length-contraction
description: Use when a supervised 2D embedding must balance cluster separation against trajectory structure: discrete class labels exist per instance and the strength of trust in those labels (clean vs noisy single-cell data) needs an explicit, tunable bias.

name: conflicting-annotation-construction
description: Use when benchmarking decision-level cluster integration on a simulated dataset with a known ground truth, or when constructing multiple partially matching annotation solutions to test whether a method can reconcile over- and under-clustered inputs.

name: confounded-model-contrast-analysis
description: Use when batch and biology are partially confounded (e.g., each patient processed in a separate batch) and you need to show whether latent factors extracted by ZINB-WaVE capture unwanted technical variation or the biological signal of interest.

name: confounder-adjusted-linear-modeling
description: Use when you have donor-aggregated single-cell type/state counts (e.g. WATLAS annotations for 46 donors) and must test whether a condition such as obesity shifts cell-type composition while controlling for covariates like depot and sex.

name: confounder-score-correction-in-single-cell-pipelines
description: Use when preprocessing scRNAseq data (10X matrix.mtx/gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) with robustSingleCell, after read.data quality filtering and get.variable.genes, to attach covariate scores before PCA and clustering.

name: confusion-matrix-accuracy-auc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two or more supervised classifiers on the same held-out test split and you need comparable metrics (confusion matrix, accuracy, AUC) to rank them, e.g. malignant vs nonMalignant cell prediction.

name: confusion-matrix-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when predicted cell type labels from marker-based scoring (e.g., GeneVector phenotype_probability) must be validated against reference annotations via a confusion matrix with per-type accuracy and overall misclassification rate.

name: confusion-matrix-construction-single-cell
description: Use when you have hybrid clustering assignments from ClonoCluster (over alpha = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), beta = 0.1, res = 1) plus a barcode table, and need to quantify how well clusters recapitulate clonal origin.

name: confusion-matrix-evaluation-against-source-labels
description: Use when predicted single-cell clone labels (e.g., from vireoSNP on mtDNA variants) must be validated against ground-truth source/population labels, and a concordance percentage or confusion matrix is the required benchmark output.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-calculation
description: Use when you have TP/TN/FP/FN counts (or raw positive/negative predictions plus labels) from m5C site predictors on the Chen et al. A. thaliana or Yang et al. M. musculus training/independent test sets and need Table 3/Table 4-style benchmark metrics.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-calculation
description: Use when an inferred GRN must be quantitatively scored against an undirected typed gold standard (e.g., DREAM 4) using edge-level confusion-matrix metrics.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-computation
description: Use when a benchmark provides ground-truth labels (e.g., simulated DEG genes in the 40%-doublet DataDEG dataset) and you must quantify how well a method's binary calls match truth via TPR, TNR, and accuracy.

name: confusion-matrix-metric-computation
description: Use when binary classification predictions (lncRNA vs PCT) with raw scores need to be converted into confusion-matrix metrics such as MCC, F1, PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, and AUC for benchmark comparison against published LncCat values.

name: confusion-matrix-normalization-and-binarization
description: Use when two aligned, labeled scRNA-seq datasets (AnnData with label and batch metadata) have been cross-predicted by scHPL classifiers and you must decide which population labels match, merge, split, or are new before updating the classification tree.

name: confusion-matrix-normalization-and-visualization
description: Use when validating a supervised cell-type classifier (e.g., SciBet) via repeated stratified train/test splits and you need normalized confusion matrices to show discrimination of close subtypes and rare cell types.

name: connectivity-auroc-auprc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a ligand-receptor-inferred cell-cell communication network must be validated against a ground-truth anatomical connectivity map, reporting AUROC and AUPRC against the 0.5-chance AUROC baseline.

name: connectivity-map-signature-matching
description: Use when cluster- or patient-level DEG lists from scRNA-seq case-vs-control contrasts must be converted into ranked drug candidates by comparing against L1000 Level5 perturbational profiles (GSE70138/GSE92742 gctx).

name: connectivity-matrix-aggregation
description: Use when a preprocessed gene-by-cell expression matrix must be split into gene subspaces before regression-based imputation, and the cluster count k is unknown and must be chosen from the data structure itself.

name: connectivity-score-drug-repurposing
description: Use when case/control scRNA-seq differential expression signatures (e.g., limma moderated t-statistics) are available per cell cluster and the goal is to rank repurposed drugs, optionally restricted to FDA-approved candidates, across heterogeneous cell types.

name: connectivity-vector-normalization-and-averaging
description: Use when you have a set of Minimum Spanning Trees (one per clustering from Totem/Slingshot) and need per-cell connectivity values in [0,1] to rank clusterings or pinpoint trajectory leaves and branching points.

name: connectome-edge-attribute-validation
description: Use when auditing, extending, or re-deriving Connectome edgeweight attributes (weight_sc vs weight_norm) on a Seurat scRNA-seq object and you must prove how weight_sc is computed from scaled ligand/receptor z-scores.

name: connectome-edge-filtering-by-expression
description: Use when a CreateConnectome edgelist from single-cell RNA-seq data contains low-confidence ligand-receptor edges (low percent-expressed or weakly scaled expression) that must be pruned before centrality, network plotting, or circos visualization.

name: connectome-output-consistency-verification
description: Use when independently reimplementing a Connectome edge statistic (e.g. weight_norm) and needing proof of numerical agreement with CreateConnectome output on a shared edge set.

name: consecutive-multi-omics-chain-inference
description: Use when you have scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq batch data plus a separate paired scRNA-seq/ADT (CITE-seq) dataset and need to predict protein (ADT) abundance for cells measured only by scATAC-seq, chaining epigenome→transcriptome→proteome inference.

name: consecutive-time-point-pair-grn-modeling
description: Use when input is time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data (no true longitudinal linkage) and the goal is a GRN driving cell-state transitions between consecutive time points.

name: consensus-cdf-plateau-analysis
description: Use when clustering transcriptome data (bulk or single-cell) with an unknown number of clusters and you must algorithmically decide the optimal k and when to stop subdividing clusters, as done inside RCC_clus.

name: consensus-clustering-combination
description: Use when you have multiple cell embeddings (e.g. VAE snapshot embeddings from CITE-seq or SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq modalities) or clusterings over the same cells and need a single consensus cluster label per cell.

name: consensus-clustering-of-bulk-transcriptomes
description: Use when you have a curated bulk PDAC expression dataset (e.g. TCGA-PAAD whitelisted to 150 PDAC samples) and gene-symbol-level subtype signatures, and you need to assign subtype labels or compare concordance between subtyping schemes.

name: consensus-clustering-of-gene-expression
description: Use when validating whether a published gene signature is PDAC-specific: cluster genes (not samples) across two or more curated bulk RNAseq datasets and measure cross-signature overlap fractions to expose tissue-nonspecific or contaminant gene subsets.

name: consensus-clustering-subtype-discovery
description: Use when a sample-by-feature landscape (e.g. DCNet-inferred 434-cell-type abundances for ~10,176 TCGA bulk RNA-seq samples) should be partitioned into robust molecular subtypes testable against clinical survival.

name: consensus-decomposition-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark with planted generative patterns (identity and activity states) is available and you need to quantify whether a decomposition method recovers them better than consensus NMF, LDA, ICA, or Louvain baselines.

name: consensus-ensemble-scoring
description: Use when multiple decoupleR methods (e.g., ULM, MLV, weighted mean) have been run simultaneously on the same network and transcriptomic/phospho-proteomic data and a single regulator-level activity estimate per regulator is needed.

name: consensus-exon-coordinate-frequency-filtering
description: Use when building isoform models from long-read RNA-seq alignments (BAM/GFF3/BED6) and you must define consensus splice-site coordinates from read start/end positions before isoform classification, without prior annotation.

name: consensus-exon-coordinate-threshold-tuning
description: Use when a single-locus long-read RNA-seq analysis (BAM/GFF3/BED6 input) misses known isoforms under VIsoQLR's default 2% CEC threshold, or when a documented sensitivity/quantification trade-off curve for the threshold is needed before manual curation.

name: consensus-exon-coordinate-tuning
description: Use when a VIsoQLR automatic run misses known or expected isoforms for a single-gene locus, or when isoform sets must be compared across read-threshold values (e.g. 2% vs 3%) on GMAP- or Minimap2-aligned BAM/GFF3/BED6 long-read data.

name: consensus-hamiltonian-path-inference
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq gene-by-cell expression data must be ordered along a linear pseudo-developmental time axis without cell type labels, e.g. neural stem cell differentiation.

name: consensus-landmark-vector-construction-scrna
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix must be reduced to a quantitative low-dimensional cell representation via clustering of genes with akin (quasi-trend-preserved) expression-rank trends, e.g. as the LC2 step feeding scQA's cluster constructor.

name: consensus-nmf-factorization-of-single-cell-counts
description: Use when benchmarking GEP-identification methods on a single-cell transcriptome dataset: you need to decompose counts into transcriptional programs and classify each program as cell-type-specific (identity) versus shared-usage (activity) to compare with SingleCellGGM output.

name: consensus-prediction-consolidation
description: Use when multiple random forest classifiers (e.g. per CV fold or per random iteration) each label the same unlabelled genes as TSG or OG, and a single stable per-gene consensus prediction with a consensus score is needed.

name: consensus-trajectory-averaging
description: Use when you have an ensemble of simulated cell state sequences (e.g., from Markov sampling of an RNA-velocity transition matrix) and need a single consensus trajectory per terminal region.

name: consensus-traveling-salesman-ordering
description: Use when you have log2(TPM+1) scRNA-seq expression filtered to cycle base genes and need to order unsynchronized cells along the cell cycle without synchronization.

name: consensus-tsp-ordering
description: Use when an unsynchronized scRNA-seq matrix restricted to cell-cycle base genes (log2(TPM+1) test_exp) must be converted into a cell time-series ordering for downstream G1/S/G2/M segmentation or pseudo-time scoring.

name: consistency-weighted-marker-scoring
description: Use when a Seurat object or count matrix from human/murine single-cell or spatial data needs automated, interpretable cell type, cell cycle, or pathway annotation from consistency-weighted markers.

name: consistent-inconsistent-cell-labeling
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-type annotation method against original study labels on labeled scRNA-seq test sets, and you need per-cluster accuracy plus a consistent/inconsistent/unknown triage of each prediction.

name: constant-region-adapter-trimming
description: Use when raw barcode amplicon fastq reads still carry flanking constant sequences upstream/downstream of the barcode and must be trimmed before alignment to a barcode reference library (e.g. SPLINTR_mCHERRY_V2).

name: constitutive-exon-psi-validation
description: Use when validating that UMI-cluster misalignment/truncation correction improved isoform assignments in single-cell or spatial Nanopore long-read data, e.g. by checking VPS28-201 exon-8 read attribution and constitutive-exon PSI consistency in the CRCLM sample.

name: constitutive-internal-exon-filtering
description: Use when quantifying bulk PSI from Nanopore long reads aligned to GRCh38 and you need to isolate constitutive internal exons (read count > 30) and correct minimap2 mapping errors before computing splicing-in ratios.

name: constrained-maximum-likelihood-estimation
description: Use when binary joint toxicity-efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) are available per dose and closed-form MLEs of π_jkl are needed subject to a monotonicity order constraint on toxicity probabilities.

name: constrained-vs-unconstrained-clustering-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether integrating partial prior knowledge as soft pairwise constraints into a scRNA-seq deep clustering model improves clustering or marker-gene specificity versus an unsupervised baseline.

name: constraint-based-flux-balance-analysis
description: Use when you have expression data from infected vs. mock tissue (e.g. GSE147507, GSE148729) and need to infer metabolic gene essentiality or drug targets via constraint-based modeling of an infected host model.

name: constraint-based-metabolic-modeling
description: Use when RNA-seq expression data from infected and mock (control) tissue/cell samples must be turned into context-specific metabolic models for knockout-based essentiality prediction and drug-target screening.

name: constraint-based-model-statistics-verification
description: Use when RNA-seq datasets from multiple conditions (e.g. GSE147507, GSE148729) must be converted to one context-specific COBRA model per sample, and per-model metabolite/reaction counts must be tallied and checked against published medians.

name: constraint-perturbation-robustness-analysis
description: Use when a clustering pipeline consumes prior pairwise constraints and you need to verify that noisy or partially incorrect domain knowledge does not hurt performance relative to running the method without constraints.

name: constraint-score-wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when you have gene sets defined by a genomic property (e.g., tissue-specific vs shared CAFEH colocalization) and continuous constraint scores (LOEUF, pLI) per gene, and you need to test whether the sets differ in selective pressure.

name: constraint-set-construction-from-label-pairs
description: Use when you have a labeled expression matrix (e.g., the scGeneFit spectral toy dataset) and need to translate pairwise label relationships into linear constraints for a marker-selection LP solved with scipy.optimize.linprog.

name: containerized-pipeline-execution
description: Use when executing the SkewC workflow (0_split10XbyBarcode.sh, 1_geneBodyCoverage.sh, 2_SkewC.sh) on pbmc_8k or other 10x/ E-MTAB-2600 data, especially on systems without admin rights where the R 'stringi'/libicui18n.so.

name: contaminant-rna-sequence-filtering
description: Use when processing Ribo-seq FastQ reads after Cutadapt trimming/length filtering and before genome alignment, to remove reads derived from rRNA, tRNA or other contaminant sequences prior to double-mapping.

name: contaminated-cell-marker-based-detection
description: Use when building the SINCERA S4 object from a raw expression matrix (genes x cells, FPKM/TPM) and you suspect mixed-cell wells or droplets, e.g. cells coexpressing markers of two lineages such as Epcam and Pecam1.

name: context-specific-metabolic-model-analysis
description: Use when RNA-seq data from multiple disease/control conditions (e.g., SARS-CoV-2 infected vs mock lung samples) must be converted into per-sample context-specific metabolic models and queried by FBA for essential genes or drug targets.

name: contig-count-tabulation
description: Use when auditing or reproducing assembler-vs-annotation statistics for a barcoded RNA-seq assembly: counting >300 bp isoform contigs from contigs.fasta and their per-class IsoQuant assignment counts against GENCODE v32/GRCh38.

name: contig-to-isoform-assignment
description: Use when you have assembled isoform contigs from barcoded or bulk RNA-seq (contigs.fasta) and need to quantify which annotated GENCODE isoforms they recover, per gene, with assignment-class statistics.

name: contingency-table-background-selection
description: Use when validating an over-representation claim: a predicted/clustered gene list must be tested for significant overlap with a curated binding list (e.g., 112 POSTAR3 CLIP RBPs or ENCORI stringency sub-lists) against a defined background set.

name: continuous-population-evf-modeling
description: Use when you need simulated scRNA-seq data with a known continuous trajectory (true pseudotime from the root and branch labels) to evaluate trajectory inference methods under varied sigma (within-population variability) and alpha (capture efficiency).

name: continuous-variable-median-split-grouping
description: Use when a survival factor (e.g. a continuous GSVA score) must be converted into high/low groups to draw K-M curves or compare survival between extreme halves of samples.

name: continuous-variable-sample-dichotomization
description: Use when a survival or group-comparison factor is continuous (e.g. per-sample GSVA scores) and a two-group (high vs low) split is needed for K-M curves or differential analysis in ARMT.

name: contour-overlap-dispute-resolution
description: Use when stabilizing raw hierarchical cell-type predictions on a scRNA-seq dataset where overlapping label regions in UMAP space indicate disputed cells, and an iterative contour-dispute loop is needed to produce converged annotations.

name: contrastive-learning-model-training
description: Use when you have an ST reference AnnData (e.g., 10X Visium or Stereo-seq spots) with truth coordinates in .obs[['x','y']] and need spatially preserved representations for query single-cell data lacking coordinates.

name: contrastive-learning-training-on-spatial-transcriptomics
description: Use when you have an ST dataset with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']] (AnnData h5ad) and want to reconstruct spatial relationships or neighbor structure of query single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: contrastive-loss-design-cell-and-cluster-level
description: Use when implementing or reproducing scCobra-style integration: you must attach contrastive heads computing l_cell, l_cluster, and combined L_c on latent embeddings alongside BCE reconstruction, KL regularization, and a domain discriminator.

name: contrastive-spatial-representation-learning
description: Use when you have unspatial single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., scRNA-S1, GSE87038) plus a matching ST reference with truth coordinates (e.g., Stereo-seq E9.5 E2S1 .h5ad with obs x/y) and need pseudo-spatial coordinates or SC-SC distance estimates for downstream spatial analyses.

name: control-gene-set-subsampling
description: Use when assessing how robust an scPLS confounding-correction workflow is to the number of available control genes, e.g. when only a subset of a full control-gene panel can be measured.

name: control-guided-semi-supervised-clustering
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq perturbation data (e.g. treatment vs control, gene knock-outs) where the goal is to find perturbation-unique cell states without a priori marker knowledge, and integration approaches would erase treatment-specific signal.

name: controlled-single-cell-simulation-generation
description: Use when a multi-omics integration method must be benchmarked against a known ground truth, e.g. simulating mixed or rare populations and controlled sparsity (82/90/96%) in paired scRNA/scATAC cell-line data.

name: conventional-cluster-center-mapping-benchmark
description: Use when evaluating whether a perturbation-effect estimator corrects 'infected proportion bias' better than clustering-based mapping, via synthetic two-cluster and four-cluster scCRISPR-seq simulations with known ground truth.

name: convergence-criterion-sweep-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether a simple k-NN majority-vote label propagation baseline matches a GCN annotation method, by sweeping k and convergence criteria against reference cell-type labels.

name: convergence-score-threshold-decision
description: Use when both cell-hashing singlet labels and SNP-based genotype labels (e.g. from scSplit) exist for the same cells and per-cell sample identities must be reconciled via a convergence-score cutoff decision.

name: convergent-topology-trajectory-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq data exhibit a convergent differentiation topology (e.g., the 157-cell neonatal mouse inner ear dataset, Burns et al., GSE71982) that violates the topology-related assumptions of tree-based trajectory methods.

name: conversion-efficiency-estimation-from-spike-ins
description: Use when benchmarking sensitivity of a droplet-based 3' mRNA counting system with ERCC spike-ins, or when validating that detected UMI counts track expected molecule inputs.

name: converted-feature-matrix-scaling
description: Use when modalities were converted to shared gene-level features (scATAC peaks via gene activities, protein names mapped to coding genes, scRNA/smFISH subset to shared genes) and need to be put on a comparable range before computing the cross-modality cost matrix.

name: convex-combination-dataset-mixing
description: Use when a small target scRNA-Seq dataset must be improved for downstream clustering by mixing in structure learned from a large annotated source dataset via NMF, without concatenating source and target cells.

name: convex-supervised-unsupervised-loss-balancing
description: Use when training MarkerMap on single-cell (e.g. CITE-seq .h5ad) data and you must choose between supervised, unsupervised, or joint marker selection within one differentiable-sampling VAE model.

name: convolutional-feature-map-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when dissecting a trained CNN for biological sequence classification: you want to visualize what convolutional filters learned by reducing the conv-layer output tensor over 'Filtered sequence length' and 'Channel' axes and embedding with UMAP.

name: convolutional-neural-network-training
description: Use when classifying tissue-specific RNA m6A modification sites from 41-nt nucleotide sequences and you need a CNN trained on one-hot encoded inputs with cross-validation and independent-test evaluation.

name: coordinate-ascent-variational-bayesian-fitting
description: Use when fitting a PhenoPath model to an expression matrix (e.g. 284 TCGA-COAD tumour samples x 4801 highly variable genes, log2(TPM+1)) with a sample-level covariate such as MSI status, and convergence must be checked via the ELBO.

name: coordinate-ascent-variational-inference-fitting
description: Use when you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization across multiple studies/traits from either individual-level genotype/phenotype data or summary statistics (LD matrix plus effect sizes/SEs or z-scores and sample sizes), especially under suspected allelic heterogeneity.

name: coordinate-permutation-null-testing
description: Use when benchmarking SVG detection methods on spatially-resolved transcriptomics data and you need to verify that reported p-values are calibrated by measuring false positive rates on coordinate-permuted null simulations.

name: coordinate-system-transformation-of-st-slices
description: Use when consecutive 2D ST slices (e.g., STARmap, MERFISH, Stereo-seq) must be aligned into a 3D stack, especially when slices carry defects such as rotation, flipping, translation, or crop ratios up to 0.25.

name: cophenetic-distance-matrix-computation
description: Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group aggregates too many genes across species for gene-level insight and must be split into smaller clusters based on phylogenetic distance.

name: cophenetic-distance-neighbor-merging
description: Use when a breadth-first clustering of leaves over internal nodes of a single-cell phylogeny yields more candidate clusters than the user-defined target (default target := 10) and the count must be reduced while preserving phylogenetic coherence.

name: copula-based-joint-toxicity-efficacy-data-generation
description: Use when simulating phase I/II trials with correlated binary toxicity and efficacy outcomes, or when reproducing Table 3-style comparisons (e.g., Gumbel association parameter 0.2) between dose-finding designs like TSNP and U-BOIN.

name: copy-loss-auroc-benchmarking-across-cna-callers
description: Use when a simulated scRNA-seq dataset has known ground-truth CNA labels (e.g. allele-specific chr3 loss injected across subclones) and you must quantify which caller (XClone, InferCNV, Numbat) recovers the loss via AUROC.

name: copy-number-aberration-burden-analysis
description: Use when CMScaller CMS subtype assignments exist for a pre-clinical CRC cohort (e.g. Gao PDXs, Fujii organoids) and you need to test whether mutation burden, CNA burden, BRAF mutation status, or MSI is enriched in specific subtypes.

name: copy-number-aberration-inference-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when malignant identity of a scRNA-seq subcluster must be validated via CNV inference from a gene-expression count table (10X 5'/3'-tagged or full-transcript data) without a matched normal control, e.g. after SCISSORS reclustering of epithelial tumor clusters.

name: copy-number-alteration-inference-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have an annotated cancer scRNA-seq Seurat object and want to identify malignant cells by their copy-number alterations relative to a non-malignant reference population.

name: copy-number-expression-correlation-mapping
description: Use when you have paired single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) with no direct cell correspondence and need cell-to-cell or cell-to-clone assignment, e.g. to link genomic mutations to transcriptomic states.

name: copy-number-profile-correlation-with-bulk-truth
description: Use when scRNA-seq copy number inferences (SCEVAN, CopyKAT, inferCNV) need quantitative validation against matched bulk WGS or WES segmented profiles, e.g. for benchmarking tools on GBM or Multiple Myeloma cohorts.

name: copy-number-segmentation-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or extending runtime/efficiency benchmarks of scRNA-seq copy-number (CNV) tools such as SCEVAN, CopyKAT, and inferCNV, or when justifying tool choice on large droplet datasets by measuring per-stage wall-clock runtimes.

name: copy-number-segmentation-variational-minimization
description: Use when a smoothed, gene-coordinate-sorted scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. MGH106 from GSE131928) must be segmented into copy number regions to infer clonal CNA profiles, as in SCEVAN steps D and G.

name: copy-number-state-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data from a tumor sample has been segmented (e.g. via getBreaksVegaMC/computeCNAmtx) and each segment must be assigned an integer CNV state label for tumor/normal or clonal analysis.

name: copykat-copy-number-inference
description: Use when a tumor-derived scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. the AML patient sample) must be split into diploid non-malignant vs aneuploid malignant cells by inferred copy-number profiles, validating SNV-score malignancy calls.

name: copykat-vs-scevan-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing automatic aneuploidy-based malignant cell callers (SCEVAN vs CopyKAT) on real scRNA-seq count matrices from GBM, HNSCC or colorectal tumors across Smart-seq2 and 10X Chromium platforms, with per-sample F1 aggregation.

name: copynumber-based-malignancy-classification
description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix from a tumor biopsy and need automatic malignant/non-malignant cell segregation without manually identifying reference normal cell clusters.

name: cord-blood-mononuclear-cell-cluster-annotation
description: Use when a CITE-seq dataset of cord blood mononuclear cells needs cluster-level annotation of immune subsets (e.g., NK and CD4+ T cells) and multimodal integration quality must be benchmarked against methods like MOFA2, Seurat 4, and SNF.

name: core-upstream-downstream-node-partitioning
description: Use when a DC3-derived subpopulation-specific TF-target network (directed weighted adjacency matrix W_ij) is too large to interpret and you need the dense core regulatory circuitry plus its upstream/downstream effectors identified and significance-tested.

name: correlated-gene-count-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when comparing trajectory-inference methods on identical single-cell RNA-seq input (real or Splatter-simulated) and you need quantitative smoothness metrics — correlated-gene counts and lag-1 autocorrelation — per method.

name: correlation-analysis-of-baf-and-expression-signals
description: Use when you have CaSpER outputs from bulk RNA-seq (BAF shift signal from BAFExtract plus multiscale smoothed expression per chromosome arm) and need to quantify whether LOH/bajo-allelic-imbalance arms co-vary with expression loss, e.g. chr1p/chr6q/chr22q in meningioma.

name: correlation-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a normalized, scaled gene expression profile (cluster-average z-scored markers or per-cell scaled matrix) needs automatic cell type labels against human reference panels such as MonacoImmune, BlueprintEncode, DICE, HCL, or HCAF.

name: correlation-based-classifier-strategy-selection
description: Use when training a supervised cell-type annotator (NeuCA) on scRNA-seq data with known labels and you must decide whether high inter-cell-type correlations require a hierarchical neural-network strategy instead of a plain feed-forward classifier.

name: correlation-based-decomposition-validation
description: Use when a bulk expression decomposition run has produced estimated cell proportions (e.g. res$bulk.props) and ground-truth proportions exist (from simulated data with known avg.props) so accuracy can be quantified.

name: correlation-based-edge-computation
description: Use when a filtered RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., soybean samples across five fungal-pathogen stress conditions) must be converted into a weighted coexpression network whose edges are correlation-based, as a prerequisite for candidate gene or module mining.

name: correlation-based-feature-gene-selection
description: Use when building cell-line kernel features for drug response prediction (e.g., PRISM models) and you need to reduce the expression matrix to genes informative of drug sensitivity rather than using all ~19k genes.

name: correlation-based-gene-representative-selection
description: Use when a combined DEAPA/LSAPA/SVAPA gene set must be reduced to representative genes and assigned to spatial APA usage patterns across tissue layers of spatially barcoded ST data.

name: correlation-based-predictor-selection-per-locus
description: Use when reconstructing BIRD's per-locus prediction model from ENCODE RNA-seq training data, i.e., when building a binary model file that predicts DNase I hypersensitivity at ~1M genomic loci from genome-wide gene expression.

name: correlation-based-quantification-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking Nanopore long-read isoform quantification pipelines (Longcell, IsoQuant, FLAMES, Sicelore2, wf-single-cell) against a supervised ground-truth count matrix on the same cells.

name: correlation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to reproduce or verify the reported HTO-count vs detected-gene correlations (e.g. brain tagging r = 0.67–0.86, background r = 0.07–0.13; CSF PBMC r = 0.48, CSF r = 0.18) before feeding the gene covariate into demuxmix.

name: correlation-coefficient-computation-scipy
description: Use when benchmarking pseudotime accuracy of trajectory methods (e.g., STREAM/ElPiGraph vs Monocle2) by correlating inferred pseudotime with known marker gene expression from scRNA-seq data in anndata objects.

name: correlation-distance-cost-matrix-computation
description: Use when two modalities have been converted to a shared feature space (e.g. peaks→gene activity, proteins→coding genes) and a cell-by-cell cost matrix is needed for unbalanced OT alignment.

name: correlation-distribution-visualization
description: Use when validating filtered BoostDiff differential networks: you have top edges (e.g. percentile=3, n_edges=150) plus disease/control expression matrices and need to check whether edge correlations are target-condition-specific (bimodal vs unimodal distributions).

name: correlation-distribution-visualization
description: Use when a gene-expression (GTEx/TCGA-style) feature table is available and the goal is to see how one focal feature correlates with all others, including the shape of the correlation distribution.

name: correlation-distribution-visualization
description: Use when comparing denoising/imputation methods on a time-course expression matrix and you need a distribution-level readout of recovery for genes most strongly correlated with time, rather than a single aggregate score.

name: correlation-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have estimated cell type proportions for a set of bulk samples (e.g., MuSiC Est.prop.weighted from 105 rat renal tubule segments) and need to visually validate that samples within each segment/condition show concordant deconvolution profiles.

name: correlation-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when comparing cell-abundance deconvolution methods on pseudo-bulk single-cell data where true per-cell-type fractions are known, and results must be visualized as a per-cell-type Pearson correlation heatmap across methods and datasets.

name: correlation-of-topic-score-with-log-fold-change
description: Use when a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic (e.g., Topic 14) appears to describe a cell identity and its top-associated genes must be checked against HuBMAP ontology membership and cell-type log-fold changes.

name: correlation-range-feature-scoring
description: Use when selecting an initial candidate feature gene set for single-cell RNA-seq clustering via gene-gene correlations, after filtering out mitochondrial, ribosomal, spike-in, and pseudogenes from log-normalized count data.

name: correlation-score-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing pseudo-time/cell-cycle ordering methods on unsynchronized scRNA-seq data by scoring agreement with experimental stage labels (correlation-score) across clustering k sweeps.

name: correspondence-analysis-embedding-computation
description: Use when starting from raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g., SingleCellExperiment objects) and you need a dimension-reduction embedding for clustering, cell-type annotation, or visualization that avoids distortive log(x+1) transformation.

name: correspondence-analysis-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether CA is computationally feasible as a PCA substitute in an scRNAseq pipeline, or when justifying a dimension-reduction method choice on wall-clock runtime grounds for datasets with tens of thousands of cells.

name: correspondence-analysis-svd-dimension-reduction
description: Use when you need dimension reduction of raw scRNA-seq count matrices (SingleCellExperiment) and want a chi-squared-residual-based embedding (CA) instead of log(x+1)+PCA, e.g. for clustering or biplot visualization.

name: cortical-cell-subclass-subsetting
description: Use when preparing the cortex_data example dataset (Yao 2021) for NeuronChat benchmarking or region-specific communication inference, when cells must be restricted to one cortical region (e.g., ALM or VISp) and to Glutamatergic CTX subclasses before network inference.

name: cortical-depth-laminar-distribution-analysis
description: Use when single-cell coordinates have been mapped onto layered tissue (e.g., human MTG cortex with L1–L6 annotations) and you must verify that reconstructed cell positions reproduce laminar organization rather than layer compression or offset.

name: cortical-layer-annotation-comparison
description: Use when evaluating spatial transcriptomics methods on the 12 human DLPFC Visium slices with manually annotated cortical layers (1-6, WM) as ground truth, e.g. comparing SPACEL modules against PRECAST, STAligner, or other deconvolution/domain-identification baselines.

name: cortical-layer-marker-gene-visualization
description: Use when a pseudo-space reconstruction of a layered tissue (e.g., DLPFC) must be validated and rendered as a figure showing layer ordering and marker-gene patterns alongside numeric correlation metrics.

name: cortical-layer-ranked-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq cells must be assigned to ordered tissue layers or spatial domains (e.g., human DLPFC cortical layers) and Visium ST sections with layer labels are available as training data.

name: cortical-neuron-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when scMoMaT cell factors from the MOp_5batches dataset (6 matrices + 2 GxR.npz pseudo-scRNA-seq inputs) have been Leiden-clustered and clusters must be annotated to cortical cell types via marker scores.

name: cosine-angle-velocity-concordance-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking velocity methods against a known biological axis: you have per-cell velocity vectors, a pseudotime-inferred endpoint, and need to quantify whether vectors align with or are orthogonal to the reference direction.

name: cosine-deviation-velocity-comparison
description: Use when assessing whether velocity estimates from scKINETICS (or a comparable EM-fitted velocity model) remain stable under technical noise, such as reduced transcript-capture depth simulated by random downsampling of raw counts.

name: cosine-distance-activity-quantification
description: Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A and per-cell transcriptional velocities) and need per-cell, per-TF activity scores via in silico knockout rather than expression-based TF activity inference.

name: cosine-distance-computation-on-pca-embeddings
description: Use when you have a Seurat object with PCA embeddings (e.g. RunPCA output on pbmc3k) and need cosine distances between cells to feed silhouette-score computation or cluster-heterogeneity evaluation.

name: cosine-distance-local-inconsistency-metric
description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods on the same cell set and you need a quantitative, cluster-resolved measure of how well a method's velocity vectors agree with neighbors in the phenotypic manifold.

name: cosine-distance-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have cohort-shared ICA gene z-weight profiles for independent components and need a component-to-component similarity matrix to support reproducibility filtering and graph-based meta-component construction.

name: cosine-similarity-benchmarking-across-scoring-methods
description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate that a fast or reimplemented pathway scoring method reproduces the outputs of an established method on the same cells and pathway set, e.g. via per-cell cosine similarity of PAS vectors.

name: cosine-similarity-decomposition-evaluation
description: Use when a spot-level aggregated expression profile has been decomposed into per-cell expressions (e.g., via annealed Langevin posterior sampling) and you must quantify reconstruction accuracy against simulated ground truth.

name: cosine-similarity-expression-reconstruction-assessment
description: Use when you need to measure how much a GRN inference method (e.g., SCING vs ppcor, PIDC, GRNBOOST2) overfits, by comparing per-gene expression reconstruction quality (cosine similarity) on train vs held-out test cells from snRNA-seq or scRNA-seq data.

name: cosine-similarity-one-sample-testing
description: Use when a batch-corrected multi-subtype expression or proteomics matrix (e.g. FP/FS/NL vascular specimens) must be screened for subtype-specific marker proteins/genes and existing test statistics do not satisfy the MG definition.

name: cosine-similarity-range-validation
description: Use when cot.df_cos has been produced by COT's generate_cos_values() (or the XOR-basis SDG variant) and the cosine values must be checked against theoretical bounds before ranking markers or writing sdg_cos_values.csv.

name: cosmic-signature-reference-curation
description: Use when fitting reference signatures to WGS catalogs from hematological malignancies or other cancers where the default COSMIC signature set contains processes that are biologically implausible for the cohort (e.g., platinum exposure absent) or where genome-wide vs exome context matters.

name: cost-performance-curve-generation
description: Use when evaluating a semi-profiling or representative-selection pipeline: you have real-profiled single-cell data for a cohort, inferred or copied data for non-representatives at multiple representative counts, and you need a normalized error vs. cost curve.

name: count-based-statistical-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq count matrix plus sample metadata with infected vs mock conditions (e.g., GEO GSE147507) and need DEGs for downstream pathway or metabolic model mapping.

name: count-based-transcript-quality-filtering
description: Use when an aptardi or StringTie-derived transcriptome has been quantitated with RSEM across multiple samples and a high-quality subset of transcripts is needed before re-quantitation and DESeq2 differential expression testing.

name: count-concordance-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two or more barcode pre-processing pipelines have been run on the same FASTQ samples and you need to quantify agreement — overlap of detected barcodes and correlation of counts against a published dataset.

name: count-data-log-transformation
description: Use when raw simulated count matrices must be transformed before correlation- or clustering-based validation, e.g. prior to Pearson/Kendall Tb regulator-gene correlations, Spearman-distance k-medoids clustering, or PCA in MOSim workflows.

name: count-data-log-transformation-for-glmnet
description: Explains how to preprocess large count-based single-cell expression matrices (e.g. .mat X with gene_list and regix) before SINGE GLG Granger regression so that glmnet_matlab does not hit memory segmentation violations.

name: count-expected-molecule-correlation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking detection sensitivity and quantitative linearity of a UMI-based scRNA-seq protocol against ERCC spike-ins with known molecule concentrations loaded into GEMs.

name: count-matrix-construction-and-export
description: Use when a scisorseqr pipeline has produced LongReadInfo/AllInfo and IsoQuantOutput files and you need a cell_type × isoform count matrix plus a per-read assignment table exported as CSV.

name: count-matrix-corpus-representation
description: Use when a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix needs to be represented as a topic model corpus to discover latent biological functions with pLDA.

name: count-matrix-denoising
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (h5ad/CSV/TSV) is sparse and dropout-heavy and the goal is a denoised count matrix with the same gene x cell dimensions plus optional 32-dim latent representations.

name: count-matrix-downsampling
description: Use when comparing gene expression between barcode groups of unequal size or total UMI content (e.g., All-retained vs EmptyNN-removed) so that DE results are not biased by depth or cell-number imbalance.

name: count-matrix-driven-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking read-level bioinformatics tools (UMI deduplication, peak calling, alignment/coverage) needs synthetic scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq reads whose counts are grounded in a fitted synthetic count matrix.

name: count-matrix-file-io
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns, e.g. a csv like raw_count.csv) must be read into scImpute and an imputed count matrix of the same dimension must be produced for downstream analyses.

name: count-matrix-log2-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq or proteomics count matrices (TSV/CSV) must be transformed to the 0–1 range expected by FAVA's sigmoid-scaled VAE output layer, before running favapy network inference.

name: count-matrix-melting-to-tall-format
description: Use when the input is a wide gene-by-cell count matrix (CSV or Parquet) that must be reshaped to tall format before running the scSPARKL pipeline stages of QC summaries, filtering, and normalization.

name: count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when raw bulk RNA-seq count matrices plus sample metadata must be normalized and tested for differential expression (DESeq2/edgeR negative-binomial GLMs) between untreated baseline and 17-AAG/Ixazomib-treated HMCLs at p<0.05 with |FC|>2, FDR<0.05 reporting.

name: count-matrix-normalization-scaling
description: Use when a raw or normalized count matrix (genes x cells) from scRNA-seq or spatial data must be normalized, scaled, and clustered prior to automatic cell-type annotation with consistency-weighted markers.

name: count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when you have a raw multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics pixel-by-gene count matrix (e.g. ST, 10X Visium, DBiT-seq) that needs cleaning and feature selection before LDA deconvolution.

name: count-matrix-preprocessing-and-filtering
description: Use when a raw gene-by-sample count matrix is the input to PyWGCNA and lowly expressed genes must be removed per the Data_format tutorial so network construction (adjacency, TOM, dynamic tree cut) is not driven by noise.

name: count-matrix-processing
description: Use when a raw or simulated RNA-seq count table (genes as rows, samples as columns, with control/treatment conditions) must be validated and prepared as input for DEG detection in the ExpHunter Suite.

name: count-matrix-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells, e.g. from GEO/ArrayExpress/GSA) is about to be used as a training or testing input for cell-type identification and needs QC, normalization and label curation first.

name: count-matrix-quality-filtering
description: Use when raw spliced/unspliced scKB count matrices need background-noise cell removal without arbitrary thresholds, e.g. downstream RNA velocity or trajectory inference on scRNA-seq data.

name: count-matrix-reconstruction-error-analysis
description: Use when you have imputed scRNA-Seq count matrices plus ground-truth true counts or known cell-group labels and need to quantify reconstruction accuracy and clustering recovery.

name: count-normalization-and-log-transformation
description: Use when starting from a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (10x mtx directory or CSV) that must be depth-normalized and log-transformed before clustering or differential expression in a Scanpy-based pipeline.

name: count-per-million-normalization
description: Use when per-sample RNA read counts from small RNA-seq annotation (COMPSRA Annotation Module tab-delimited count files) must be library-size normalized before differential expression testing between case and control samples.

name: count-transformed-rud-matrix-statistical-testing
description: Use when the imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix from stAPAminer must be tested for global spatial variation to identify SVAPA genes in spatially barcoded ST data.

name: counting-method-contrast-validation
description: Use when scRNA-Seq allele-specific expression counts could be produced either by keeping only uniquely mapping reads or by resolving multi-reads, and you need to quantify the bias introduced by discarding multi-reads.

name: counting-tool-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the computational performance (wall-clock runtime) of feature-counting tools on the same SAM/BAM alignment inputs, especially small RNA-seq reads with collapsed duplicates.

name: counts-to-tpm-normalization
description: Use when the input is a raw counts matrix (.csv, rows = Ensembl gene IDs, columns = sample IDs) that must be normalized to TPM and log2(TPM+1) before GSVA, correlation analysis, or integration with clinical/mutation data.

name: countsimqc-count-distribution-comparison
description: Use when simulated single-cell count matrices must be checked against a real scRNA-seq reference (e.g., Cuomo et al. 2020 iPSC data) on per-gene mean-variance and zero-fraction distributions before downstream analyses.

name: countsimqc-fidelity-assessment
description: Use when simulating multi-sample multi-group scRNA-seq data anchored to a reference SingleCellExperiment and you must verify simulation fidelity against the reference before downstream method benchmarking.

name: coupled-nmf-clustering-baseline-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether adding bulk HiChIP loop data (DC3) improves subpopulation clustering of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq cells, by comparing against coupled NMF (no loop data) and separate per-datatype NMF under the same conditions.

name: coupled-nmf-multi-omic-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and bulk H3K27ac HiChIP samples from the same heterogeneous cell population are available and the goal is coupled clustering plus deconvolution of bulk HiChIP/RNA/ATAC signals into subpopulation-specific profiles.

name: coupled-nonnegative-matrix-factorization-clustering
description: Use when you have one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq sample of the same heterogeneous population (e.g. healthy donor BMMC) and need consistent cluster assignments across both modalities before running sc_compreg, rather than clustering each modality separately.

name: coupled-vae-optimal-transport-training
description: Use when integrating heterogeneous single-cell datasets (e.g. paired 10x PBMC scATAC/scRNA, MERFISH + scRNA) with nonlinear cross-modality deformations, or when common genes alone are insufficient and dataset-specific HVGs must be retained.

name: covariance-moment-based-network-inference
description: Use when you have time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data (qPCR or RNA-seq) from two consecutive time points and need to infer a sparse, directed, signed transition matrix A_t without constructing pseudo-time trajectories.

name: covariance-restricted-sparse-linear-regression
description: Use when you have TSCS single-cell expression data (qPCR or RNA-seq) sampled at consecutive time points and need to infer the transition-driving GRN without pseudo-time trajectory construction.

name: covariance-spectrum-decomposition-single-cell
description: Use when a single-cell count matrix is heavily sparse (e.g. ~95% zeros) and you need to quantify how much of the covariance eigen-spectrum departs from Marchenko-Pastur/Tracy-Widom expectations and partition that departure into sparsity artifacts versus biological signal.

name: covariance-spectrum-eigendecomposition-analysis
description: Use when a sparse cell-by-gene expression matrix has been eigendecomposed and you must decide which eigenvalue/eigenvector pairs are noise, sparsity artifacts, or true biological signal — including discarding delocalized eigenvectors whose eigenvalues fall outside the MP bulk.

name: covariate-adjusted-genotype-association-testing
description: Use when genotype data and transcript expression (e.g., GTEx V7 per-tissue) are available and the goal is to detect variants affecting the global splicing pattern of genes rather than single univariate splicing traits.

name: covariate-adjusted-linear-regression-fdr
description: Use when you have per-cell module-specific expression scores from a GRN (e.g. SCING Leiden modules scored with AUCell) plus per-cell clinical metadata (trait labels and confounders such as sex), and need FDR-controlled module-trait association statistics.

name: covariate-adjusted-spatial-modeling
description: Use when analyzing spatially-resolved transcriptomics data (e.g., SpatialExperiment objects) where known spatial domain labels exist and you need to detect SVGs adjusted for domain structure, or benchmark SVG detection against SPARK-X, HVGs, and Moran's I.

name: covariate-encoded-trajectory-modelling
description: Use when a cross-sectional single-cell expression cohort carries a sample-level covariate (stimulant, mutation, drug) that may modulate progression, and pseudotime must be inferred without explicit time-series labels.

name: covariate-gene-interaction-significance-testing
description: Use when a cross-sectional expression cohort (e.g. TCGA-BRCA log2(TPM+1) matrix of 4579 HVGs x 1135 samples) must be ordered along a pseudotemporal trajectory while testing which genes' loadings interact with a sample covariate such as ER status.

name: covariate-pseudotime-interaction-ranking
description: Use when a PhenoPath fit is available and the goal is to rank genes by covariate-pseudotime interaction effect size and identify significant interactions (e.g. Shalek LPS/PAM genes, TCGA MSI analysis).

name: covariate-regression-from-gene-expression
description: Use when comparing the wall-clock scalability of nuisance-covariate removal methods (SiFT, scVI, scanpy regress_out) on large scRNA-seq data, e.g. continuous covariates regressed from the expression matrix across subsamples up to ~500,000 cells.

name: covariate-regression-on-sample-parameters
description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model for a multi-sample single-cell dataset (e.g., PBMCsca) and need to visualize sample-level manifold parameters or verify that GEDI disentangled donor from technology effects, as in Fig. 2a/2d UMAPs.

name: covariate-regression-residualization-limma
description: Use when a per-cell technical covariate (e.g. dsb's PC1 of isotype controls and fitted Gaussian-mixture background means µ1) must be regressed out of normalized protein/ADT values to return denoised residuals.

name: coverage-based-bulge-removal
description: Use when assembling isoforms per read cloud (barcode) from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads and the extracted barcode subgraph contains parallel (bulge) paths between the same node pairs that must be resolved using barcode-specific coverage instead of aggregate graph coverage.

name: coverage-based-missingness-handling
description: Use when a scRNA-seq mutation (VAF) matrix paired with a per-cell sequencing-coverage matrix must be marked and filtered for low-coverage/unobservable observations before SClineager lineage inference.

name: coverage-downsampling-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing bin size and sequencing depth before running a scWGS CNA calling pipeline, especially when balancing detection of small (<500 kb) or single-copy events against per-bin read-depth noise at lower coverage.

name: coverage-limit-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when comparing fusion-detection tools on simulated paired-end RNA-seq reads titrated across coverage levels, to rank methods by the lowest coverage at which each still detects a known fusion such as BCR-ABL1 or CIC-DUX4.

name: coverage-log-transformation-normalization
description: Use when raw base-level coverage pileup matrices (e.g. from build_pileup) must be variance-stabilized and normalized across a cohort prior to SCISSOR global/local shape change detection.

name: coverage-normalization-and-variance-stabilization
description: Use when base-level pileup coverage matrices from RNA-seq BAM files must be transformed and normalized before cohort-level outlier or structural-variation analysis, e.g. as the input step to Scissor() shape change detection.

name: coverage-rate-varying-gene-set-construction
description: Use when evaluating gene-set enrichment method calibration or power as a function of gene set size, by building synthetic gene sets at fixed coverage rates (e.g., 1%, 2%, 5%, 10%) over a fixed gene universe of null summary statistics.

name: covid-19-differential-gene-interpretation
description: Use when novel cell subtypes (e.g. the three CD163-high macrophage clusters 3, 5, 12 from the GSE171524 COVID-19 dataset) have been identified and you need to know which GO biological pathways are significantly up- or downregulated in disease vs. control samples.

name: covid-19-severity-biomarker-association-analysis
description: Use when whole-blood transcript measurements for candidate severity biomarkers must be aligned sample-wise with clinical/lab variables (CRP, lymphocyte counts, type I IFN score) and tested for Pearson correlation sign and significance.

name: covid-19-severity-prediction
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency and classification accuracy of multi-context cell-cell communication tools on multi-sample single-cell data, e.g. predicting patient COVID-19 status/severity from communication features.

name: covid-19-therapeutic-candidate-evaluation
description: Use when a disease/trait-associated gene co-expression module or GRN (e.g. M11 with TFs GATA2, MAFF, FOSB) has been inferred and you need candidate repurposable drugs targeting its key driver proteins.

name: covid-patient-status-stratified-expression-comparison
description: Use when you have scNovel-detected (or otherwise annotated) cell clusters from a single-cell atlas with patient-level COVID/healthy status labels and need disease-status-stratified marker genes per cluster plus a cross-cluster consistent gene set.

name: covid-pbmc-t-cell-subset-annotation
description: Use when analyzing 10x Genomics PBMC scRNA-seq from COVID-19 patients (e.g. accession E-MTAB-9357) to subset naive/CD8+ T cells, construct pseudotime, and detect TDE/XDE gene expression or TCD/XCD cell-proportion changes between mild and moderate severity groups.

name: covid19-cell-cell-communication-pattern-verification
description: Use when you have pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellChat/CellPhoneDB/ICELLNET/SingleCellSignalR output) for multiple conditions (control, moderate, critical COVID-19) and need to compare per-cell-type interaction profiles across conditions to verify condition-specific communication patterns.

name: covid19-epithelial-immune-communication-interpretation
description: Use when you have pre-computed CellChat CCI outputs for multiple COVID-19 phenotypes (control, moderate, critical) and need to quantify chemokine couplets unique to each condition per cell cluster.

name: covid19-lung-scrnaseq-subpopulation-annotation
description: Use when control vs COVID-19 lung scRNA-seq cells must be spatially localized against a 10X Visium normal-lung reference to detect spatially variated subpopulations (e.g. MDM/TMDM macrophages) and quantify myeloid–epithelial proximity.

name: covid19-scrnaseq-cci-interpretation
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor interactions (CCI data) from multiple COVID-19 scRNA-seq conditions and need to test whether a specific ligand family (e.g., chemokines) drives communication between defined cell-type pairs across conditions.

name: covid19-severity-biomarker-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or validating the timing of severe-COVID-19 prognostic gene-expression changes (MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) in a longitudinal whole-blood microarray cohort aligned to days relative to respiratory nadir.

name: covid19-severity-group-comparison
description: Use when moderate-vs-severe group abundance differences must be quantified at single-cell resolution on scMerge2-integrated COVID-19 data, e.g. to find which annotated cell types carry the highest proportion of severe-outcome-associated cells.

name: covid19-subnetwork-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when a case-vs-control RNA-seq dataset must be reduced to a perturbed active subnetwork connecting seed genes at minimum cost, and performance must be measured against a reference gene or GO term list.

description: Use when you have BoostDiff edge lists from both target-condition sub-analyses (e.

name: cox-proportional-hazards-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when you have per-sample features (e.g. Miscell latent features computed from TCGA bulk expression) joined to overall survival time/status plus confounders such as Age, Sex and TNM stage, and need covariate-adjusted prognostic associations per feature.

name: cox-proportional-hazards-regression
description: Use when you have per-sample survival time/status merged with continuous molecular scores (e.g. GSVA) or clinical covariates and need to determine which factors independently predict survival.

name: cox-proportional-hazards-survival-analysis
description: Use when a bulk expression cohort (e.g. TCGA SKCM06 RNA-seq with clinical info) has matched event/time-to-event survival fields and you need per-feature hazard ratios with BH-adjusted significance for cell types or genes.

name: cox-proportional-hazards-survival-modeling
description: Use when testing whether a candidate biomarker (e.g. binarized GEP weights or transferred embedding coordinates) has a statistically significant differential effect on patient outcomes between two treatment arms in a randomized trial with PFS/OS endpoints.

name: cox-proportional-hazards-survival-modeling
description: Use when pathway activity scores (e.g., PROGENy scores for EGFR, MAPK, PI3K, Hypoxia, Trail) must be tested against overall survival time and event status in a tumor cohort such as TCGA, with covariate adjustment.

name: cpg-genomic-feature-annotation
description: Use when you have a table of differentially methylated CpGs from a 450K/EPIC Illumina array analysis and need to join CpG IDs to probe annotations, subset by genomic feature (TSS/5'UTR), or validate a published feature-restricted DMC count.

name: cpg-significance-thresholding
description: Use when a DMC results table from methylR's ChAMP- or minfi-based differential analysis must be thresholded on adjusted P-value and logFC to identify significant CpGs and visualize them on a volcano plot.

name: cpg-to-gene-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have a differentially methylated CpG list (DMC output from ChAMP/minfi in methylR) and need gene-level identifiers to run gene ontology or pathway enrichment analysis.

name: cpm-expression-threshold-application
description: Use when filtering ligand–receptor pairs from single-cell or bulk expression data (e.g. Tabula Muris) with NATMI's --detectionThreshold and --expressionThreshold arguments before predicting communication edges.

name: cpp-branch-and-bound-threshold-modification
description: Use when mining significant genetic meta-markers with HOGImine and the |T|·δtar Tarone bound is too conservative — replace the threshold update with a Westfall–Young FWER estimate from pre-computed label permutations.

name: cpp-command-line-tool-execution

name: cpu-gpu-training-speedup-measurement
description: Use when you need to measure the device speed-up of GPU vs CPU training for a scETM model, e.g. timing 1000 training steps on the 1886-cell Mouse Pancreas AnnData object.

name: cpu-time-benchmarking-of-em-variants
description: Use when a fitted model's E-step is too slow on large scRNAseq data and you need to verify that a chunked EM variant matches the naive EM's estimation error while lowering CPU time.

name: cramer-von-mises-nonparametric-testing
description: Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) split into two condition groups, and want distribution-free DCI detection per bin pair.

name: crc-subtype-biology-annotation
description: Use when you have extracted deep features from the last hidden layer of a trained CRC DeepCC model and need to interpret which biological characteristics (MSI, metabolic, EMT) each feature group encodes relative to CMS subtypes.

name: credible-effects-evaluation-at-specified-fdr
description: Use when a fitted scCODA CompositionalAnalysis result (CAResult) is available and you must decide which cell-type compositional effects are credible at a specified FDR level.

name: credible-interval-calibration-analysis
description: Use when a Bayesian phase-inference method (e.g., Tempo) returns posterior phase samples per cell and you must verify whether its uncertainty quantifications are well-calibrated on sparse droplet-based scRNA-seq data.

name: credible-set-variant-selection
description: Use when you have CAFEH fine-mapping output tables for GTEx gene-tissue pairs and need per-tissue credible-set test variants plus a matched lead-eQTL background for enrichment tests against Roadmap regulatory annotations.

name: crispr-barcode-mutation-dropout-modeling

name: crispr-barcode-simulation
description: Use when a lineage-reconstruction benchmark needs paired barcode-and-expression data with a known true tree, e.g., sweeping mutation rates on the C. elegans L1 tree or TedSim-simulated phyla.

name: crispr-screen-null-calibration
description: Use when you need to verify that a differential-expression pipeline (e.g., Normalisr on a Perturb-seq/CRISPR screen dataset) produces uniformly distributed null P values across gene expression levels before trusting its significance calls.

name: crispr-screen-trans-regulatory-inference
description: Use when you have gRNA assignment and UMI count matrices from a high-MOI CRISPRi screen (e.g., GSE120861 K562) and want to infer causal trans-gene regulations from TSS-targeting gRNAs.

name: critical-gene-identification
description: Use when analyzing time-course scRNA-seq data (e.g. zebrafish embryogenesis Drop-seq with 38,731 cells x 11,588 genes) to discover genes that dynamically regulate cells into mature cell types via gene-gene network edges.

name: critical-gene-identification-from-trained-networks
description: Use when a trained deep drug-response predictor must be interpreted — i.e., you need ranked lists of genes contributing to sensitivity vs resistance predictions and want to measure bulk-vs-single-cell overlap (reported ~46% / 53%).

name: cross-age-label-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating supervised cell-type label transfer across developmental ages or samples in scRNA-seq, e.g. testing whether a classifier trained on one age generalizes to another.

name: cross-algorithm-consistency-comparison-with-confidence-intervals
description: Use when a downstream transformation or trajectory conclusion must be shown to be robust to the choice of pseudotime algorithm, e.g. MAPiT-transformed Ki-67, RNA or p27 spatial profiles derived from Wanderlust vs DPT orderings.

name: cross-algorithm-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare signature-detection performance of multiple fitting algorithms against ground-truth contributions, e.g., validating a new error-suppression rule (bootstrap 95% CI) against fixed contribution thresholds.

name: cross-algorithm-lineage-comparison-visualization
description: Use when two trajectory-inference algorithms (e.g., CellRouter flow networks vs Monocle 2 DDRTree) must be compared on the same count matrix to test whether underrepresented or rare lineage bifurcations are resolved or collapsed.

name: cross-algorithm-pseudotime-comparison-table-construction
description: Use when you have pseudotime orderings from two or more trajectory-inference algorithms run on the same single-cell RNA-seq dataset and need a quantitative smoothness benchmark (correlated-gene counts and lag-1 autocorrelation of lineage markers) to compare them.

name: cross-aligner-density-plot-visualization
description: Use when you need to test whether a UMI-read mapping-shift pattern is specific to one alignment algorithm by re-aligning the same quality-filtered, UMI-clipped FASTQ reads with STAR, GSNAP and HISAT2 and overlaying the resulting shift-distance density curves.

name: cross-batch-condition-effect-prediction
description: Use when you need to predict gene-expression count matrices for unseen condition/batch combinations (e.g., ctrl/healthy vs stim/severe) from multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq data, including out-of-sample held-out cell subsets.

name: cross-batch-consistency-validation
description: Use when a low-dimensional embedding claimed to remove batch effects must be validated: compute pseudotime or another per-cell quantity per batch and test cross-batch consistency via regional KL divergence of batch mixing.

name: cross-batch-gene-feature-intersection
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq count tables from multiple platforms/batches whose gene sets differ, and a shared gene universe must be established before multi-table CA (corralm) or before comparing against PCA/Harmony baselines.

name: cross-batch-highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when integrating multiple independently preprocessed single-sample scRNA-seq batches in the scdrake integration pipeline and a joint HVG set is needed before running batch integration methods.

name: cross-batch-prediction-scenario-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a model can predict single-cell expression toward an unseen condition-batch combination (e.g., <moderate, 40-65> in batch Lee_2020) and comparing it against baselines across multiple prediction scenarios.

name: cross-benchmark-method-ranking-comparison
description: Use when ranking GRN inference algorithms against a known ground-truth GRN on simulated scRNA-seq data (BoneMarrow, PBMC) and checking whether the resulting method ordering reproduces BEELINE's experimental-benchmark results.

name: cross-boundary-direction-correctness-evaluation
description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods (e.g., UniTVelo vs scVelo stochastic/dynamical) on a dataset with known cell-type annotations and expected lineage transitions, to score direction correctness across cluster boundaries.

name: cross-caller-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing a new or existing single-cell CNA caller against HiScanner, Ginkgo, CHISEL, SCYN, and SCOPE on high-coverage (≥20x) PTA-amplified scWGS with simulated ground-truth CNAs or a known aneuploid single cell.

name: cross-cancer-label-transfer
description: Use when a query single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., six-cancer-type myeloid cells) needs cell-type labels transferred from a differently sourced reference (e.g., KIDNEY/UCEC/ESCA pan-cancer myeloid), especially across batches or cancer types where annotation consistency and interpretability matter.

name: cross-cancer-type-deg-classification
description: Use when building or auditing a pan-cancer malignant-vs-normal single-cell classifier from unioned cross-dataset DEG features, and you need to quantify whether cross-cancer-type common DEGs (≥2 cancer types) drive performance versus cancer-type-unique DEGs.

name: cross-cancer-validation-benchmarking
description: Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices from cancer types disjoint from the training data (e.g., P1_BC through P11_Melanoma) and need to reproduce or extend reported malignant vs non-malignant prediction performance metrics.

name: cross-cell-type-benchmarking-of-grn-methods
description: Use when multiple GRN inference methods must be compared on identical single-cell datasets and the goal is to rank them by biological validity, e.g. disease subnetwork modeling accuracy across tissues or cell types.

name: cross-cell-type-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have DH profiles (predicted or imputed) for the same set of cell types from two methods and need genome-wide cross-locus and cross-cell-type agreement metrics, plus differential-DH comparison for similar cell type pairs.

name: cross-cell-type-phase-heterogeneity-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNAseq data from multiple cell types is sampled across circadian time points and the goal is to test whether circadian phase heterogeneity (not just mean phase) differs between cell types.

name: cross-cell-type-rhythmic-gene-overlap
description: Use when comparing circadian rhythmicity between annotated cell types in single-cell RNAseq time-course data, e.g., counting rhythmic genes per cell type and their shared overlap.

name: cross-classifier-rejection-comparison
description: Use when evaluating which classifier variant better rejects cells from unseen cell populations: you have a labeled hierarchical dataset, can hold out one population (e.g. Group 3 / four AMB nodes), and need per-variant rejection rates.

name: cross-cluster-zscore-normalization
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset has been clustered and per-cluster marker gene expression must be put on a comparable, standardized scale (z-scores) before correlating against deCS reference panels or before ranking cell-type-specific genes.

name: cross-cohort-component-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a component model (e.g., 86 MeCs learned by ICA from integrated TME scRNA-seq) must be shown to be reproducible rather than an artifact of any single training dataset, by testing exclusion of each cohort in turn.

name: cross-cohort-dataset-scaling
description: Use when an scRNA-seq dataset exceeds available RAM (e.g. >0.6M cells on a 128GB machine, or ~11.5M-cell cross-cohort data) and you must run or benchmark annotation pipelines like scaLR, scBalance, scvi, devCellPy, or CellPLM under that limit.

name: cross-cohort-expression-consistency-check
description: Use when a derived gene read-count or DE table from one RNA-seq cohort must be validated against a second public cohort (e.g. dbGap vs TCGA) before downstream pathway interpretation.

name: cross-cohort-gene-expression-correlation
description: Use when the same RNA-seq pipeline has been run on two independent patient cohorts and you must quantify whether node-level (FunHoP-aggregated) pathway results — dominant genes and read-count ratios — are consistent across cohorts.

name: cross-cohort-single-cell-integration
description: Use when a pan-cancer single-cell integration stage has produced per-cohort ICA z-weight matrices and you must derive cohort-shared transcriptional meta-components instead of dataset-specific components.

name: cross-cohort-single-cell-integration
description: Use when several scRNA-seq cohorts with responder-status annotations must be jointly scanned for perturbed cell populations, and naive per-cell-type testing would be confounded by individual-to-individual and cohort-to-cohort variability.

name: cross-cohort-statistical-reproducibility
description: Use when a published finding links a categorical subtype/label (e.g., CMS2 from CMScaller) to a binary drug-response outcome across multiple independent cohorts and the target is to reproduce the reported p-values and odds ratios per cohort.

name: cross-cohort-subtype-classification
description: Use when independent breast cancer RNA-seq cohorts (e.g., GSE96058, PanCA, GSE81538, TCGA) must be assigned PAM50 intrinsic subtypes using a reference computed on a different cohort, and subtype-call concordance must be quantified.

name: cross-cohort-svm-disease-classification
description: Use when you have a trained GEDI model on a multi-sample, multi-condition dataset (e.g., two independent COVID-19 cohorts) and need to predict sample-level disease labels in an unseen cohort from learned parameters.

name: cross-cohort-tcga-data-pooling-and-harmonization
description: Use when you have paired bulk mRNA/miRNA expression matrices spanning several TCGA cancer types and need one harmonized pooled cohort (genes/miRNAs as row names, patients as columns) to compare per-miRNA prediction accuracy across methods.

name: cross-cohort-transcriptome-clustering-interpretation
description: Use when multiple blood transcriptome cohorts need to be compared at the module-aggregate level using the fixed BloodGen3 repertoire, e.g. to cluster disease states by aggregate activity or reproduce the aggregate abundance heatmap.

name: cross-comparison-gene-occurrence-tracking
description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values spans several pairwise comparisons and you must identify which genes recur across conditions or appear only in one (e.g. VAN-specific Q3 down-regulation).

name: cross-condition-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when comparing a model's prediction/assignment accuracy across input preprocessing conditions or batch-effect regimes, e.g. testing whether raw scRNA-seq counts outperform normalized inputs for cell type labeling.

name: cross-condition-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference from one biological condition (e.g., ASD patients) must annotate cells in another condition (e.g., controls), and accuracy/ARI of competing supervised and unsupervised annotators must be benchmarked.

name: cross-condition-cell-type-specific-comparison
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data from two or more conditions plus pre-classified cell-type labels, and need to determine which pathway-level dysregulations (not single genes) are shared or specific to a condition within each cell type.

name: cross-condition-communication-comparison
description: Use when the same scRNA-seq communication inference (e.g., MDIC3) has been run on two matched conditions of a dataset (e.g., GEO GSE147424 LS and NL skin) and the goal is to distinguish condition-specific communications from shared ones.

name: cross-condition-gene-expression-comparison
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. anti-CD4-treated vs isotype-control P14 cells in chronic LCMV) must be compared for cell subtype frequencies or gene expression within a defined subtype, using a curated reference atlas as the common coordinate system.

name: cross-condition-scorecard-aggregation
description: Use when a main folder already holds one sub-directory per pairwise comparison with scorecard outputs, and the goal is to rank genes by total occurrences across all comparisons versus genes found only in isolated conditions.

name: cross-condition-scrnaseq-communication-comparison
