description: Use when you have two pre-built CommPath objects from matched scRNA-seq conditions (e.g., tumor vs normal) and need to identify communication chains up- or down-regulated between them.

name: cross-database-annotation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify or compare annotation accuracy across alternative marker gene databases for a single-cell cluster annotation workflow with known ground-truth cell-type labels.

name: cross-database-candidate-overlap-counting
description: Use when a combined list of annotated plus newly predicted miRNA precursors must be tallied against miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, and PsRNA to count database-specific overlaps and identify previously unannotated candidates.

name: cross-database-gene-label-mapping
description: Use when you have a candidate HVG list (e.g. ~16,000 genes from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, M3drop) and need database-derived communication-relevance labels to retain only genes involved in cell-cell communication.

name: cross-database-interaction-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have a FAVA (favapy) predicted protein-pair network with Pearson-correlation confidence scores and need to quantify how many of its high-confidence edges are novel vs. supported by STRING, hu.MAP 2.0, or the IDG Tdark catalogue.

name: cross-database-polya-site-comparison
description: Use when a set of predicted polyA sites or 3'-end bins must be benchmarked against public polyA site annotations (PolyASite, PolyA_DB) instead of a sample-specific gold standard.

name: cross-dataset-batch-effect-evaluation
description: Use when comparing reference-based cell-type mapping methods across two single-cell datasets with batch effect and strong asymmetry in cell number and library depth (e.g., whole-cell scRNA-seq reference to ultra-sparse snRNA-seq nuclei target).

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing competing feature sets or representations for cell clustering across several scRNA-seq datasets, requiring replicate-level metrics (AMI) against known subpopulation labels to show consistency.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating an automatic cluster annotation method on several independent published scRNA-seq datasets with known manual annotations, to report per-dataset consistency rates and an overall average.

name: cross-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a classifier's robustness must be benchmarked across multiple independently sequenced scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 6 cross-platform human pancreas training-test pairs), comparing 2+ annotation methods by mean classification accuracy.

name: cross-dataset-cell-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when you have 2+ annotated scRNA-seq reference datasets with batch effects and a held-out unlabeled target dataset, and you need cross-dataset cell-type annotation plus an evaluation against known labels.

name: cross-dataset-cell-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets with overlapping cell types must be integrated and you need to quantify dataset mixing vs. cell-type resolution for competing correction methods (e.g., ComBat, MNN, CCA, Harmony, scVI, DIRECTi).

name: cross-dataset-cell-label-integration
description: Use when per-dataset cell subtype fine labels have been produced (fine-labels.RDS per dataset) and you need to reconcile or compare subtype label definitions across published references by constructing a cross-dataset Jaccard similarity matrix.

name: cross-dataset-cell-population-matching
description: Use when two or more annotated scRNA-seq datasets (batch-corrected/aligned, e.g. with scVI or Seurat) must have their cell population labels matched and a hierarchical classification tree learned, especially when name-based matching fails (e.g. different labs, resolutions, or nomenclatures).

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-mapping
description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset and an unlabeled target dataset (e.g., Drop-seq reference to Smart-seq2 target, or Smart-Seq2 to CEL-Seq pancreas) must be mapped across technologies or batch conditions.

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-prediction
description: Use when a labeled training scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad) must annotate cells from a different dataset — same species or cross-species — where the test set contains cell types with no annotated cells in the training data.

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-replicability-assessment
description: Use when you need to measure whether cell types (e.g., neurons vs non-neurons, excitatory vs inhibitory, interneuron subtypes) identified in one scRNA-seq study replicate in independent studies, or to find reciprocal top-hit cell-type pairs across datasets.

name: cross-dataset-cell-type-transfer
description: Use when a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., .h5ad from GEO) must be used to label cells in a different test dataset whose taxonomy may contain unseen cell types, and errors from noise/batch effects need suppression.

name: cross-dataset-classifier-comparison
description: Use when a new cell-annotation or classification method must be compared against established algorithms on the same ground-truth-labeled scRNA-seq test sets with ranked, per-dataset metrics.

name: cross-dataset-clustering-benchmark-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking a clustering model across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and random seeds (e.g. 20 datasets, seeds 1111–10000) and you must assemble per-dataset mean/median ARI comparisons into one table.

name: cross-dataset-clustering-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare a scRNA-seq cell clustering method's accuracy (ARI) against published tools across many datasets with known cell type labels, e.g. benchmarking scQA on GEO/ArrayExpress data such as GSE57249 or E-MTAB-5061.

name: cross-dataset-coexpression-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when multiple methods infer cell-type-specific co-expression from scRNA-seq data and you must test which method's significant gene pairs replicate in an independent dataset.

name: cross-dataset-component-comparability-handling
description: Use when decomposing individual tumor scRNA-seq expression matrices with ICA (n_components=100) and you need gene loading scales and orientations comparable across components and datasets before downstream clustering or pan-cancer integration.

name: cross-dataset-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when the goal is to identify genes consistently dysregulated across several public transcriptomics cohorts (e.g. severe vs mild COVID-19 peripheral blood RNA-seq) instead of relying on a single-dataset DE result.

name: cross-dataset-drug-response-scale-transformation
description: Use when drug response data come from datasets with incompatible units (e.g., GDSC IC50 vs PRISM Repurposing 19Q4 AUC) and must be placed on a common sensitivity scale before model training or cross-dataset correlation.

name: cross-dataset-expression-comparison
description: Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data reproduce a protocol-specific expression property (e.g., gene length bias in non-UMI data) by direct comparison against a matched experimental dataset.

name: cross-dataset-expression-correlation-mapping
description: Use when unsupervised BUSseq clusters need biological labels beyond FACS labels — e.g., verifying an intermediate CMP-MEP cluster or mapping a CLP/LMPP-like cluster to Haemopedia progenitor populations.

name: cross-dataset-gene-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to classify which of the top-2000 Seurat FindVariableFeatures() HVGs participate in cell-cell communication, and compare the classified gene counts across independent spatial transcriptomics datasets.

name: cross-dataset-gene-clustering
description: Use when a published gene signature (e.g. Bailey ADEX) may be confounded by tissue-nonspecific or non-tumor genes, and you have ≥2 independently parsed bulk RNAseq datasets to test cross-dataset reproducibility of gene groupings.

name: cross-dataset-gene-set-intersection
description: Use when building robust cancer-cell classification features by intersecting malignant-vs-non-malignant DEGs across multiple training scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) rather than relying on a single dataset.

name: cross-dataset-intensity-normalization
description: Use when combining probe-level microarray intensity data from multiple GEO series (e.g. 3T3-L1 differentiation studies) where per-study platforms and processing differ and cross-study comparability is required.

name: cross-dataset-metadata-tabulation
description: Use when a collection of parsed expression datasets must be inventoried into a single annotation table with consistent columns (measurement type, sample description, n samples, n features, Used flag), e.g. to audit a compendium or reproduce a published dataset table.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer
description: Use when a trained scRNA-seq cell-type classifier must be transferred to a second dataset with different cells but overlapping cell-type labels, and prediction accuracy/F1 must be quantified against the target dataset's known labels.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer-assessment
description: Use when a pre-trained model (e.g. aptardi's HBR model.hdf5) must be tested for generalizability across RNA-Seq datasets differing in tissue, organism, library preparation, or sequencing depth.

name: cross-dataset-model-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when you have candidate-feature tables (e.g. dsRID_whole.tsv) from multiple ENCODE long-read RNA-seq datasets and need to decide whether a self-trained random forest or the PacBio AD-trained transferred model performs better under 20-fold cross-validation.

name: cross-dataset-network-consistency-analysis
description: Use when you have several bulk transcriptomic cohorts with matched survival data (e.g., metastatic melanoma datasets like TCGA SKCM06) and need to test whether inferred cell-cell interaction networks are reproducible across cohorts and across different cell-type marker annotations.

name: cross-dataset-node-importance-comparison
description: Use when you have scBONITA rule-inference node importance scores for KEGG pathway networks from one or more scRNA-seq datasets and need to check whether importance scores carry context-dependent signaling information beyond topology alone.

name: cross-dataset-overlapping-gene-selection
description: Use when a reference dataset (e.g. annotated HuBMAP data such as HBMP3-spleen-CC3) is being used to transfer labels to a query dataset (e.g. HBMP2-spleen-2) whose AnnData object has a different gene set, or when comparing clusterings across the two objects.

name: cross-dataset-promoter-comparison
description: Use when two or more transcription start site (TSS) datasets for the same organism must be benchmarked against each other, and a motif-positioning-based quality comparison of nascent vs. annotated TSSs is desired.

name: cross-dataset-read-length-stability-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether an RNA-seq expression quantification parameter is robust to sequencing length or strategy differences, by building virtual short-read/single-end derivatives from paired-end data and comparing median quantification values.

name: cross-dataset-reference-evaluation
description: Use when you need to evaluate or tune a reference-based cell-type identifier (e.g. MarkerCount_Ref) without holding out a dedicated training set, by rotating multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets through test/reference roles.

name: cross-dataset-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq h5ad files annotated with adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta'] from a DeepCycle run and need to verify cell cycle annotation or the RNA-doubling prior by quantifying UMI-vs-phase fold change across multiple cell systems.

name: cross-dataset-shared-gene-merging
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq AnnData objects with partially non-overlapping (or homologous but differently ordered) gene lists must be merged into a single cells-by-genes matrix before integration, transfer, or runtime benchmarking.

name: cross-dataset-single-cell-embedding-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to test whether predicted cell-type annotation scores (cell-by-Cell-Ontology-type matrix from OnClass Predict) integrate multiple heterogeneous scRNA-seq datasets better than expression-space integration (Scanorama), quantified by silhouette coefficient.

name: cross-dataset-subpopulation-separation-analysis
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction/visualization methods for temporal scRNA-seq data on their ability to resolve subpopulations within the final time point, using dip-test multimodality scores across multiple datasets.

name: cross-dataset-subtype-similarity-mapping
description: Use when you need to compare/relate cell subtype label schemes across published TME scRNA-seq references, or to cross-validate a subtype annotation model and report fold-wise accuracy and kappa within each dataset.

name: cross-dataset-tf-set-intersection-analysis
description: Use when two FateCompass differential motif activity results exist for orthologous cell fates (e.g., beta cells) in distinct species or systems, and you need to compute the intersection fraction and label species-specific TF groupings.

name: cross-dataset-weight-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing between raw-CT optimization and external-dataset (e.g. TCGA) weight optimization when only ~20–30 qPCR samples and a few internal controls are available.

name: cross-design-operating-characteristics-comparison
description: Use when two phase I/II dose-finding designs (e.g., TSNP vs U-BOIN) must be compared on the same simulated scenarios: generate correlated outcomes with Gumbel() in R, run both designs with matched seeds, and tabulate OBD selection and patient-allocation percentages.

name: cross-disease-cohort-generalisation-testing
description: Use when a severity biomarker score built from one disease's transcriptomic cohorts must be validated for discriminative power (severe vs mild) in independent cohorts of other pathogens, treating AUC~0.5 as no discrimination.

name: cross-disease-isoform-specificity-check
description: Use when a candidate isoform switch (e.g. HSPH1-001↔HSPH1-002, SLC25A25-005) found in one CanIsoNet disease dataset must be checked for absence in the OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and Behcet's Disease datasets to claim disease specificity.

name: cross-disease-module-intersection-analysis
description: Use when two or more disease gene lists have each been run through E.PAGE enrichment and you need the set of significantly enriched environmental gene modules common to all queries.

name: cross-embedding-dr-quality-comparison
description: Use when two or more dimensionality-reduction algorithms (e.g. t-SNE vs UMAP) have been run on the same dataset and you need a statistical, per-cell measure of which embedding and which hyperparameter setting better preserves high-dimensional neighborhoods.

name: cross-embedding-lineage-structure-comparison
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has multiple candidate embeddings (feature selection x dimension reduction choices) and you must decide which embedding yields the optimal trajectory — e.

name: cross-entropy-loss-evaluation
description: Use when training or evaluating cross-tissue cell type classifiers (scTab/TabNet) on the CELLxGENE Merlin store and you need the cross-entropy loss and macro F1-score on unseen-donor test data, e.g. to compare training-dataset-size scaling regimes.

name: cross-entropy-loss-negative-sampling
description: Use when a similarity matrix (e.g. EDGE's ensemble similarity matrix S) has been built and the initial spectral embedding must be refined so rare and common cell groups separate in the low-dimensional plot.

name: cross-entropy-method-feature-selection
description: Use when you have a phenotype x feature score matrix M from scRNA-seq data (e.g., IPF, mouse cortex, or human cell atlas datasets) and need a discriminative marker set covering all phenotype pairs at a fixed coverage, especially when comparing against or substituting for the greedy G-PC solution.

name: cross-entropy-method-optimization
description: Use when you need a small global biomarker set that distinguishes between all pairs of phenotypes (e.g., cell type × tissue combinations in scRNA-seq) from a phenotype-feature score matrix, and a greedy approximation (G-PC) is insufficient.

name: cross-experiment-cv-quantification
description: Use when you need to quantify technical variability across replicate sequencing runs or ERCC spike-in experiments, e.g. computing CV2 across ERCC experiments and correlating mean UMI counts with expected molecule counts.

name: cross-experiment-standardized-metric-interpretation
description: Use when a DemuxmixResult (fitted HTO mixture model) is available and you need a per-HTO data quality metric of droplet separability that can be compared across experiments or used for QC filtering.

name: cross-feature-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when you have cell coordinates in a common low-dimensional embedding (e.g., 2D UMAP) from multiple feature spaces for the same cells, plus reference cell-type labels, and need to score how well each feature space reproduces the reference structure.

name: cross-file-gene-identifier-reconciliation
description: Use when a gene expression dataset (.csv or .xlsx) opened in Excel contains date-like terms or outdated gene symbols in the first column that fail pathway-database lookups (Enrichr, GSEA, Ingenuity) and need mapping to HGNC-approved names.

name: cross-genome-scrna-seq-comparison
description: Use when comparing how two TE-expression quantification tools (e.g., SoloTE vs scTE) recover known cell populations across two genome builds (hg38, mm10) using Seurat clustering and UMAP on simulated or ground-truth matrices.

name: cross-implementation-communication-probability-verification
description: Use when a reimplemented ligand-receptor communication probability model (Hill/mass-action form) must be checked against CellChat's computeCommunProb reference outputs to confirm numerical and statistical agreement.

name: cross-implementation-segmentation-agreement-analysis
description: Use when the same segmentation pipeline exists in two implementations (e.g. Matlab vs Python) and you need to demonstrate the outputs are largely similar before distributing or adopting either version on multiplexed image data.

name: cross-language-python-r-pipeline-execution
description: Use when an analysis requires tools from both ecosystems — e.g. simulating scRNA-seq data with splatter in R and scoring cells with the FiRE Python module — and the intermediate expression matrix must be exchanged between languages.

name: cross-language-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a Python reimplementation is faster or more memory-robust than its R reference: you have matched expression datasets, both packages installed, and need replicate-timed scaling runs across feature-count subsets.

name: cross-language-runtime-comparison-r-python
description: Use when the same analysis toolkit exists in both an R/Bioconductor and a Python implementation and you need to quantify how execution time scales with dataset size, expressed per sample and regulator.

name: cross-lineage-driver-regulator-overlap-analysis
description: Use when CEFCON has been run independently per lineage on scRNA-seq trajectory data and you need to determine which driver regulators (e.g., top-20 per lineage) are common versus lineage-specific, and how overlapping sets affect control metrics.

name: cross-method-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a scRNA-seq cell-type annotation method head-to-head with published baselines under multiple label-overlap settings, and accuracy values must be matched against a reference table.

name: cross-method-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when a new method claims improved accuracy on a task (e.g., circadian phase inference from scRNA-seq) and you must quantify how close its errors are to a theoretical optimum versus baseline methods on simulated data with ground truth.

name: cross-method-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a supervised annotator (NeuCA) outperforms existing clustering/annotation methods across training-size and testing-size regimes on scRNA-seq data with known labels.

name: cross-method-annotation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing source-free scRNA-seq annotation methods on target datasets containing target-private (novel) cell types, to test whether adaptive unknown-cell detection outperforms user-defined thresholds.

name: cross-method-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq dataset with author/expert-provided cell-type annotations is available and you need to compare the prediction quality and speed of several automated annotation methods on identical inputs.

name: cross-method-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when the goal is to quantitatively compare cell-type annotation tools on the same reference/query dataset splits, reproducing accuracy and MacroF1 tables like SELINA vs ACTINN, SingleCellNet, mtSC, CellTypist, Cell BLAST, SingleR, scmap, Seurat, SVM, RF, kNN.

name: cross-method-annotation-comparison
description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation/classification methods on labeled scRNA-seq data and you need a fair, repeated train/test benchmark (accuracy and balanced accuracy) across multiple datasets.

name: cross-method-annotation-comparison
description: Use when a pretrained annotation model (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs) must be validated against baseline annotators (Seurat CIBERSORT-based labeling, SingleR with Human Primary Cell Atlas / Blueprint-ENCODE) on the same held-out scRNA-seq cells.

name: cross-method-annotation-comparison
description: Use when several prior-knowledge cell-type annotation methods must be compared under identical marker-database perturbations, e.g. quantifying how often each method falsely assigns a removed (unknown) cell type.

name: cross-method-auroc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing novel cell detection or open-set cell-type classifiers on scRNA-seq benchmarks where novel-class cells are positives and imbalance makes AUROC/AUPR/FPR95 the appropriate metrics.

name: cross-method-batch-correction-benchmarking
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset with a batch/condition covariate (e.g. control vs interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) has cell embeddings from GeneVector and you need to quantify batch alignment versus preservation of treatment-related transcriptional variation across correction methods.

name: cross-method-benchmark-accuracy-tabulation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend the scCancer2 Fig. 2B benchmark: comparing cell-type annotation accuracy of scCancer2 against baseline methods across multiple datasets and sequencing technologies.

name: cross-method-benchmark-aggregation
description: Use when a benchmark must compare pathway-activity/cell-type recovery performance of multiple gene set scoring methods across many simulated or real datasets into one ranked results table.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new clonal-inference method must be evaluated head-to-head against predecessor methods on identical patient datasets, using a shared downstream metric such as cell-to-clone assignment coverage.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new temporal single-cell embedding method must be benchmarked head-to-head against established dimension-reduction tools on the same gene-by-cell count matrices, with a quantitative per-dataset comparison metric and a method-by-dataset results table.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a newly proposed sequence-classification method must be validated against a published baseline on shared benchmark splits, and per-tissue metric deltas (e.g., AUC) must be tabulated with significance markers.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a scRNA-seq annotation-transfer method must be compared head-to-head against alternatives on shared reference/query data, using balanced accuracy for cell typing or JSD for continuous-label transfer.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing two or more count-estimation or preprocessing variants (e.g. unique vs weighted multi-read allocation, with vs without partial pooling) by feeding each through an identical downstream statistical test and reporting matched result counts.

name: cross-method-benchmark-comparison-of-pluripotency-tools
description: Use when per-cell stemness/pluripotency score tables (ORIGINS activity, activity-HVF, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) already exist for multiple datasets and the goal is to quantify agreement between scoring methods via mean Pearson correlations.

name: cross-method-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a new cell-type annotation tool against ready-to-run baselines on a shared single-cell test set, especially when tools use different reference sets and label vocabularies that must be reconciled via an ontology.

name: cross-method-benchmark-jaccard-overlap
description: Use when multiple GSE or DE methods (e.g., iDEA, fGSEA, GSEA, CAMERA, PAGE) are run on identical DE summary statistics and you need quantitative concordance metrics such as Jaccard overlap to compare their outputs.

name: cross-method-benchmark-ranking-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking several single-cell integration methods on the same dataset collections and you need a reproducible global ranking from batch-mixing and bio-conservation metrics computed on each method's latent embedding.

name: cross-method-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a claim that 'method A outperforms methods B and C' must be reproduced end-to-end: re-running all quantifiers on the same mapped reads, rebuilding feature matrices under multiple perspectives, and statistically testing the performance gap.

name: cross-method-benchmarking-of-cell-annotation-tools
description: Use when multiple malignant-cell classifiers (e.g. scMalignantFinder, PreCanCell, ikarus, Cancer-Finder, CopyKAT) must be compared on the same labeled scRNA-seq datasets to reproduce or verify reported sensitivity/specificity benchmarks.

name: cross-method-benchmarking-of-reference-mapping-algorithms
description: Use when you must compare reference-mapping methods (Symphony vs Seurat vs scArches) on the same query/reference pair, quantifying integration via LISI and annotation transfer via F1 against true labels.

name: cross-method-cell-mapping-comparison
description: Use when comparing how cell-querying/mapping time of methods like Cell BLAST, scmap, and CellFishing.jl scales with reference size, from 1,000 to 1,000,000 cells.

name: cross-method-chromatin-accessibility-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether expression-based DH prediction (BIRD, log2(x+1) scale) performs comparably to multi-data-type imputation (ChromImpute) on shared test cell types, or when comparing differential DH between similar cell type pairs.

name: cross-method-cluster-comparison-visualization
description: Use when multiple integration or clustering methods have been run on the same control/perturbed single-cell dataset and you must determine which method's clusters recover treatment-responsive cell states (e.g. sm50/pks2 PMC responses to MK-886).

name: cross-method-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a general-purpose clustering algorithm against domain-specific scRNA-seq clusterers on datasets with known cell-type labels, to quantify whether the general method matches or beats specialized tools.

name: cross-method-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when you must rank several rare-cell-type or clustering methods over a common set of annotated scRNA-seq datasets and report F1 plus rare-type recovery counts in a single benchmark table.

name: cross-method-clustering-performance-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or extend a supervised-by-labels clustering benchmark that compares multiple scRNA-seq clustering tools on datasets with known cell types using ARI.

name: cross-method-cna-call-comparison
description: Use when a task asks to compare ROC-AUC performance of CNA callers on snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data, or to reproduce published AUC benchmark values against a single-cell DNA copy-number ground truth.

name: cross-method-colocalization-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or comparing multi-trait colocalization/fine-mapping methods on eQTL summary statistics, especially to test whether allelic heterogeneity (multiple causal variants) changes method ranking via FDP-power curves.

name: cross-method-consensus-scoring
description: Use when multiple per-method ligand-receptor score tables (e.g. truncated mean, weight_norm, LRscore, CellChat probability) are available and a single method-agnostic consensus ranking of interactions is needed.

name: cross-method-deg-list-comparison
description: Use when an annotated multi-timepoint scRNA-seq dataset (binary Group factor plus a Time variable) needs DE genes identified by both a temporal method (CASi FindTemporalDEGs) and a conventional tool (Seurat) so their result lists can be intersected and compared.

name: cross-method-dimensionality-reduction-comparison
description: Use when you need an empirical ranking of dimensionality reduction methods on the same scRNA-seq datasets with ground-truth cell labels, judged by Louvain-cluster NMI.

name: cross-method-drug-sensitivity-correlation
description: Use when validating a single-cell drug repurposing pipeline against an independent bulk drug-response predictor (e.g., TRANSACT vs. ASGARD) or when quantifying how removing one annotated cell type changes per-patient drug scores.

name: cross-method-f1-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing rare-cell detection algorithms on scRNA-seq mixtures with a known rare population, so that continuous rareness scores and binary cluster calls can be converted to a common F1-score comparison.

name: cross-method-fusion-comparison
description: Use when scRNA-seq fusion calls from scFusion must be benchmarked against bulk callers (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, EricScript, FusionCatcher) for sensitivity or CPU-time comparison across Smart-Seq datasets.

name: cross-method-gene-overlap-comparison
description: Use when comparing whether a trajectory-based scRNA-seq DEG method identifies a higher fraction of literature-verified genes among its top-ranked DEGs than a competing method on the same preprocessed expression matrix.

name: cross-method-gene-ranking-comparison
description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. 10x Visium or HDST h5ad with 2D spatial coordinates) and need to compare which top-scoring spatially variable genes one method detects that another misses.

name: cross-method-gene-set-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a ground-truth scRNA-seq dataset with known trait-relevant cells and want to test whether one method's prioritized gene set improves a second scorer (e.g., scDRS) relative to a baseline gene set (e.g., MAGMA-derived).

name: cross-method-gep-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare activity GEPs from a baseline method (e.g., cNMF at k=137 factors on MCA) with SingleCellGGM GEPs to assess cell-type specificity and shared-program recovery.

name: cross-method-grn-comparison-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a GRN inference method on time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell data against competitors (e.g., SINCERITIES, SCODE, SCRIBE, SINGE) using early-precision curves.

name: cross-method-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when a new or existing scRNA-seq imputation method must be quantitatively compared against competing imputers by masking known non-zero values and measuring recovery error (RMSE/MAE/NMSE).

name: cross-method-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when two scRNA-seq batches must be integrated and several correction tools should be compared quantitatively on the same inputs using iLISI (batch mixing) and 50-RNN (local structure retention) against an uncorrected Original baseline.

name: cross-method-integration-evaluation
description: Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth cell labels (e.g., GSE118767 sc_mixology) must be integrated and clustered by several competing methods and their accuracies compared via ARI.

name: cross-method-integration-score-aggregation
description: Use when comparing >=2 cell-type annotation or integration methods across multiple scRNA-seq datasets and you need standardized per-method metrics plus a statistical verdict (paired t-tests, p < 0.05).

name: cross-method-local-structure-preservation-comparison
description: Use when comparing batch-correction/integration methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a quantitative measure of local structure preservation (e.g., before adopting an integration method for a two-dataset comparison).

name: cross-method-macro-f1-comparison
description: Use when comparing discriminative power of marker-selection methods on scRNA-seq phenotype classification: you need each selector's features (e.g., 42 genes on IPF) scored identically via logistic regression macro-F1.

name: cross-method-mapped-read-count-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a SPLiT-seq preprocessing method against the original barcode-filtering method by comparing STAR uniquely-mapped read counts across the five SPLiT-seq samples (SAMN08567259-64, mm10/hg19).

name: cross-method-model-comparison
description: Use when a new classifier (e.g. Pollock) must be evaluated head-to-head against multiple established methods on identical annotated single-cell datasets with predefined train/validation splits, using F1 as the comparison metric.

name: cross-method-network-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a gene co-expression network inference method against alternatives on scRNA-seq data and you need quantitative computational-efficiency and robustness comparisons rather than only accuracy metrics.

name: cross-method-network-consistency-evaluation
description: Use when true gene networks are unknown for real single-cell data and inferred TF–gene edges must be validated against ChIP-seq references, comparing scLink with PIDC, Pearson, Spearman, and glasso variants per cell type.

name: cross-method-pas-scoring-comparison
description: Use when PAS must be computed on large-scale scRNA-seq data (>10^3 pathways, up to million-cell atlases) and an original vs. accelerated implementation comparison is needed.

name: cross-method-pathway-concordance-analysis
description: Use when a large-scale scRNA-seq study requires validating that a fast pathway-activity method (scPAFA/fast_Ucell) detects the same disease-related differential pathways as a slower reference (SCPA), while quantifying compute cost.

name: cross-method-pathway-rank-comparison
description: Use when a labeled RNA-seq expression matrix must be benchmarked across sample-wise pathway quantification methods to rank a target pathway (e.g., TNFa signaling in IL17+TNFa-treated vs control samples) by significance.

name: cross-method-pathway-ranking-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell differential comparison (e.g., stimulated vs control PBMCs) has been scored for pathway/gene-module activity by both a Bayes Factor test (VEGA) and a ranked-list enrichment method (GSEA) and the goal is a side-by-side significance comparison.

name: cross-method-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (peak memory and total runtime) of unsupervised single-cell manifold alignment methods such as scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA, and SCOT on one or more pre-processed single-modality datasets.

name: cross-method-performance-table-assembly
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq clustering methods (e.g., scDCC, CIDR, DCA+k-means, DEC, MPSSC, PCA+k-means, SIMLR, SC3, Seurat) have been run on the same labeled datasets and their per-method metric values must be tabulated for comparison.

name: cross-method-prediction-overlap-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking ligand-receptor inference tools on the same scRNA-seq dataset, e.g. comparing CellChat vs CellPhoneDB/SingleCellSignalR/iTALK predictions, overlap, or robustness to cell subsampling.

name: cross-method-quantification-benchmarking
description: Use when an organism has a reference genome/transcriptome (e.g., zebrafish GRCz11, Homarus americanus GMGI_Hamer_2.0) and you must validate that Seq2Fun ortholog-based quantification reproduces Kallisto-based results.

name: cross-method-rare-cell-detection-comparison
description: Use when comparing rare cell-type detection accuracy across methods on scRNA-seq data, e.g. testing sensitivity to the number of DE genes distinguishing a rare population, or reproducing reported rare clusters in the 68k PBMC dataset.

name: cross-method-runtime-comparison
description: Use when a study must rank GRN-inference algorithms fairly on one dataset — e.g., AUROC/AUPRC vs. a reference network plus per-method runtime on identical hardware.

name: cross-method-runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when two or more gene co-expression network inference methods must be compared on the same single-cell expression matrix, with runtime/memory and downstream module quality (GEP counts, GO enrichment) as head-to-head metrics.

name: cross-method-scrnaseq-mapping-comparison
description: Use when several single-cell reference-mapping methods must be compared head-to-head on the same reference/query dataset pairs, e.g. to judge whether a new mapper (ProjectSVR) matches Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs, iNMF or SCALEX.

name: cross-method-speed-comparison
description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency of scDist, Augur, and nDEG on the same scRNA-seq data — full datasets, subsamples of varying size, or large simulated cohorts (~1M cells) — to record timing ratios.

name: cross-method-speed-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare prediction runtime of automatic cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq data, especially to assess how runtime scales with training/testing set size or to select a fast method for large prediction tasks.

name: cross-method-stability-scoring
description: Use when two HVG-selection or gene-classification methods (e.g. CPPLS-MLP and CCPLS) must be compared for selection stability on spatial/single-cell datasets with cell-type clusters, and per-cell-type Y HVG lists are available.

name: cross-method-svg-rank-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare the agreement of two or more spatially variable gene detection methods on identical spatial transcriptomics data, or to verify whether a method under-ranks genes with strong spatial expression patterns.

name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell pseudotime/branching result from one method (e.g., DTFLOW RSKG) needs to be validated or contextualized against branch assignments from alternative tools such as Scanpy or Monocle2.

name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on spliced/unspliced AnnData from complex differentiation scenarios (cell cycles, sparse cell types, multi-branch lineages) to decide which tool's trajectory matches expected biology.

name: cross-method-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when a simulated dataset with known pseudotime and branching structure is available and you need to quantify which TI method assigns cells to branches most purely and reconstructs pseudotime most accurately.

name: cross-method-transcript-classifier-comparison
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend head-to-head evaluation of lncRNA coding-potential classifiers on sORF-enriched test sets, computing PRE, SEN, SPE, ACC, F1, MCC, and AUC per species.

name: cross-method-twas-result-comparison
description: Use when two TWAS frameworks have been run on identical reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=574) and GWAS data and you must count independently significant genes per method and their overlap.

name: cross-method-velocity-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking two or more RNA velocity methods on the same dataset and you need comparable per-gene metrics (e.g., phase-portrait fitting quality, directional coherence) restricted to commonly modeled genes.

name: cross-metric-benchmark-comparison-scrna-seq
description: Use when you must decide which similarity metric (posterior distance vs. Euclidean) better distinguishes same-type nearest neighbors between query and reference scRNA-seq cells within a fixed embedding space.

name: cross-metric-droplet-alignment
description: Use when you have per-droplet DIEM debris scores from an snRNA-seq run and a per-droplet contamination proxy (e.g., percent spliced reads) and need to verify the debris score tracks extranuclear RNA contamination.

name: cross-modal-decoder-generation
description: Use when a trained scMM model's latent dimensions need interpretation: sweep each latent dimension independently through the mixture-of-experts decoder to link genes, surface proteins, and chromatin accessibility peaks to individual dimensions.

name: cross-modal-gan-domain-mapping
description: Use when two separately measured single-cell modalities of related cells must be aligned or a missing modality predicted — e.g., spatial transcriptomics to scRNA-seq or paired ATAC-seq/RNA-seq — while preserving data geometry.

name: cross-modal-gene-list-comparison
description: Use when a target gene's correlated-gene ranking from original spatial data must be compared against the same ranking computed on a GAN-mapped scRNA-seq output to flag spurious vs. newly discovered candidate associations.

name: cross-modal-protein-generation-from-transcriptome
description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq transcriptome and surface protein counts (RNA_count.mtx/gene.tsv and Protein_count.mtx/protein.tsv with barcode.tsv) and need to predict protein measurements for cells whose protein data is withheld, given transcriptome observations alone.

name: cross-modal-rna-protein-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/ADT data are available and you must quantify whether a prediction (or RNA signal itself) tracks measured protein levels cell-by-cell — e.g. comparing imputation methods or raw/denoised RNA baselines per protein.

name: cross-modal-similarity-validation
description: Use when you need to check that structurally-derived relationships (ontology graph distances) are recapitulated by an independent data modality (gene expression or text embeddings) before trusting the structure for downstream inference.

name: cross-modality-alignment-robustness-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how robust a cross-modality alignment (e.g. scATAC-to-scRNA via scTopoGAN) is to cell-number imbalance, by generating downsamples from 90% to 10% of cells and measuring alignment quality per fraction.

name: cross-modality-benchmark-table-generation
description: Use when each single-cell modality (e.g., PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) must be projected to a low-dimensional latent by multiple methods and compared in one table of KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 and Silhouette metrics.

name: cross-modality-cell-pairing
description: Use when single-nucleus RNA and ATAC data from the same tissue were captured in separate assays (no shared barcodes) and downstream pseudotime or eGRN analysis needs each ATAC cell paired to an RNA cell.

name: cross-modality-common-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq inputs for scBridge: the target gene activity matrix and the source count matrix must be reduced to their common gene set before encoding.

name: cross-modality-correlation-metric-computation
description: Use when two modalities are jointly measured (e.g. DBIT-seq spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) and you must score whether a learned cross-domain mapping preserves point-wise correspondence, not just distributional similarity.

name: cross-modality-cost-matrix-construction
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq or surface protein counts) that share only a weak, partial set of features, and a cell-level coupling cost is needed for Optimal Transport-based alignment.

name: cross-modality-encoder-input-preparation
description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData, rows=cells, columns=peaks) must be converted into a VAE-compatible, [0,1]-scaled matrix before feeding a cross-modality translation model's ATAC encoder.

name: cross-modality-feature-connection-computation
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with smFISH or scATAC-seq) where features are only weakly connected across modalities and a feature-level cost matrix is needed for rIOT-based alignment.

name: cross-modality-label-matching-evaluation
description: Use when you have aligned source/target single-cell latent manifolds (e.g. ATAC projected onto RNA space by scTopoGAN) plus cell type labels, and need a metric of alignment quality or a stability check across random GAN initializations.

name: cross-modality-marker-enrichment-testing
description: Use when after multi-omic integration you have reclustered cells (e.g. B cells and monocytes at Louvain resolution 0.2) and need statistical evidence that subcluster markers are shared across modalities (scRNA vs scATAC) rather than an alignment artifact.

name: cross-modality-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a single-modality dataset (e.g., scATAC-seq from BMMC batches) must be translated consecutively to a downstream modality (ADT via CITE_BMMC) and compared head-to-head with alternative translator pipelines under a labeled ground truth.

name: cross-modality-pseudo-count-generation
description: Use when a mosaic multi-omics dataset (e.g. CITE-seq + ASAP-seq batches) has batch–modality slots with no count matrix and you need pseudo-counts for those slots before running scMoMaT first-stage training.

name: cross-modality-scatac-seq-annotation
description: Use when the target data are single-cell multi-omic counts (10x Genomics PBMC CITE-seq with antibody-derived tags, or scATAC-seq such as mouse bone marrow) and only pre-trained scEMAIL source weights (encoder h, classifier c, auxiliary c1/c2) are available.

name: cross-modality-segmentation-transfer
description: Use when a segmentation pipeline validated on one multiplexed imaging modality (e.g., MIBI, IMC, imaging mass cytometry) must be evaluated on another platform or marker set to demonstrate cross-tissue/platform transferability.

name: cross-modality-shared-gene-subsetting
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC, smFISH, or surface protein/CyTOF data) whose native features differ, so modality-specific features must be converted to gene-level common features to compute a cross-modality cell distance for Optimal Transport.

name: cross-modality-single-cell-cluster-label-consistency
description: Use when you have one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq sample from the same heterogeneous population and need linked subpopulations with identical cluster labels across both modalities before comparative gene regulatory analysis.

name: cross-modality-translation-model-training
description: Use when paired single-cell count matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq genes and scATAC-seq peaks as AnnData) are available and a held-out single-modality profile must be translated into the other modality while preserving cellular heterogeneity.

name: cross-modality-translation-scrna-scatac
description: Use when paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data are available and ATAC-only profiles must be converted to RNA-like profiles, e.g., to annotate scATAC-seq cell types via translated RNA expression.

name: cross-model-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when multiple virus-read-classification models must be compared fairly on identical RNA-seq fragment data, e.g. to reproduce the finding that viRNAtrap beats baselines on all measures except precision, where DeepVirFinder wins.

name: cross-model-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing prediction accuracy of a new model or aggregation scheme (e.g., cluster/pathway-level) against a baseline model like BIRD at multiple DHS cluster resolutions.

name: cross-model-reconstruction-evaluation
description: Use when comparing marker-selection or latent-variable models on their ability to reconstruct full gene expression from a small marker panel (k markers), with per-cell-type and overall reconstruction metrics such as Jaccard Index, Spearman rho, and l2 distance.

name: cross-model-synthetic-quality-evaluation
description: Use when comparing synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple deep generative models against an original count matrix to assess per-gene univariate distribution fidelity, including bimodality failures.

name: cross-normalization-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when scRNA-seq raw count matrices with known cell-type labels are available and the question is how much normalization method (RAW/TC/TMM/FQ) vs. dimensionality-reduction method (PCA/ZIFA/ZINB-WaVE) affects downstream clustering quality.

name: cross-omics-label-transfer-benchmarking
description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (or CITE-seq/ASAP-seq) h5ad data and you need to benchmark label-transfer F1/accuracy under reduced annotations, noisy labels, or novel cell-type discovery.

name: cross-omics-prototype-alignment
description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq data (e.g., CITE-seq source + ASAP-seq target .h5ad) and you need to progressively align modalities without treating all cells homogeneously.

name: cross-pipeline-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to position a new single-cell analysis tool against existing Python ML/DNN pipelines by comparing accuracy, memory usage, and wall-clock execution time on a shared dataset and VM.

name: cross-pipeline-cell-annotation-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to validate a barcode annotation pipeline by re-running an alternative published pipeline on the same single-cell amplicon FASTQs and comparing per-cell barcode calls and clone sizes.

name: cross-platform-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq query dataset from one sequencing platform must be labeled using a reference built from other platforms, or when benchmarking annotation tools on externally harmonized datasets such as the Allen Brain Atlas.

name: cross-platform-cell-type-classification
description: Use when evaluating which automatic cell-type identification method transfers across scRNA-seq platforms: labeled training data from one platform, held-out or cross-platform test data from others, ranked by accuracy, F1 and unlabeling rate.

name: cross-platform-circadian-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a bulk transcriptomic time series with labeled circadian times (microarray or RNAseq) must predict circadian time of samples from a different assay platform, e.g. RNAseq or scRNAseq pseudobulk, and accuracy/RMSE must be reported.

name: cross-platform-classifier-benchmarking
description: Use when a gene-expression subtype classifier trained on one platform (e.g., TCGA RNA-Seq) must be evaluated on independent cohorts from other platforms, or when robustness to unmatched/missing genes is assessed by random gene subsampling.

name: cross-platform-correlation-validation
description: Use when a newly produced poly(A) site or APA quantification matrix (e.g., polyA_sites.tsv from scAPAtrap on ST-MOB data) must be checked for agreement against a second transcriptomic platform.

name: cross-platform-expression-rescaling
description: Use when classifying a single gene expression sample with a pre-trained DeepCC model, or when the input sample's platform differs from the RNA-Seq-based TCGA training reference (e.g., microarray data).

name: cross-platform-gene-expression-correlation
description: Use when a cell-gene expression matrix from segmented spatial transcriptomics data needs benchmarking against a matched scRNA-seq reference (e.g. Chromium scFFPE-seq of the same tissue) via expression-profile correlation.

name: cross-platform-gene-identifier-harmonization
description: Use when assembling circadian time-course datasets from different GEO platforms (e.g., GSE54651 with Ensembl IDs, GSE54650 raw CEL files) whose identifiers must be unified to uppercase gene names before tauFisher training or cross-method benchmarking.

name: cross-platform-gene-symbol-intersection
description: Use when a downstream model (e.g. an xgboost malignancy classifier) requires a reference gene panel that must be reconciled between TCGA bulk RNA-seq feature space and single-cell count matrix gene symbols.

name: cross-platform-generalisability-visualization
description: Use when testing whether a segmentation method trained on Xenium transfers to other SST platforms (CosMx, MERSCOPE) or tissue types, and when plotting cross-platform benchmark panels.

name: cross-platform-isoform-matrix-joining
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell isoform quantification methods against a cross-platform gold standard (e.g., Nanopore output vs a matched PacBio IsoSeq reference) and per-cell accuracy metrics are needed.

name: cross-platform-label-transfer
description: Use when a labeled training count matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) plus an unlabeled testing matrix must be annotated by routing each method to one of three wrappers by its category.

name: cross-platform-rnaseq-microarray-comparison
description: Use when the same gene signatures must be evaluated in both an RNA-seq and a microarray PDAC dataset (e.g., paired ICGC PACA-AU primary/metastasis/cell-line samples, or Moffitt 2015 tissue-compartment datasets) to confirm a signature trend is platform-independent.

name: cross-platform-runtime-comparison
description: Use when reproducing or extending runtime/memory comparisons of a tool across computational environments (laptop vs HPC) or across competing implementations (e.g. AnnSQL vs AnnData backed mode vs Seurat) on the same dataset.

name: cross-platform-scrna-protocol-comparison
description: Use when scRNA-seq FASTQ data from multiple UMI-based platforms (Chromium, Drop-seq, ICELL8, SmartSeq3) has been processed by both UniverSC and its vendor pipeline and you need to quantify concordance of the resulting GBMs.

name: cross-platform-scrna-st-integration
description: Use when a paired scRNA-seq reference and spatial transcriptomics spots (e.g. ST, Visium, MERFISH) need cell-type deconvolution/label transfer, especially when datasets share only partially overlapping genes or are heterogeneous (e.g. PDAC ST + inDrop scRNA).

name: cross-platform-scrnaseq-data-integration
description: Decision support for choosing between a unified processing pipeline and platform-specific pipelines when integrating scRNA-seq data generated on different UMI-based technologies.

name: cross-platform-scrnaseq-parameter-comparison
description: Use when multiple publicly available scRNA-seq count datasets from different protocols (e.g., UMI-based 10x/droplet vs. plate-based read counts) are available and the goal is to test whether distributional assumptions such as the Tweedie index p differ by platform.

name: cross-platform-single-cell-data-processing
description: Use when paired-end FASTQ files (R1 barcode/UMI, R2 transcript) from a non-Chromium UMI platform must be processed with Cell Ranger, or when cross-platform scRNA-seq datasets must be integrated under identical parameters.

name: cross-platform-transcriptome-model-training
description: Use when a training set from one transcriptomic platform (e.g., RNA-seq GSE151189 .csv with sample names in the first column and labels in the last) must yield a model that predicts clinical outcomes on samples from a different platform (e.g., GSE59098 microarray).

name: cross-platform-variant-concordance-comparison
description: Use when RNA-seq-derived variant calls (multi-sample VCF from GATK) must be quality-checked against an independent genotyping platform (e.g., Axiom array VCF) to confirm sample identity and call accuracy.

name: cross-population-trajectory-mapping
description: Use when comparing the state/progression of an unseen cell population against a labeled reference population along shared axes — e.g., asking whether CD57high senescent T cells overlap CD57low cells at days 2–3 of TCR stimulation on LD axes.

name: cross-predictor-performance-comparison-across-species
description: Use when comparing Staem5's m5C prediction performance against SVM/RF-based baselines on the same A. thaliana and M. musculus training and independent test datasets to reproduce Tables 3 and 4.

name: cross-protocol-protein-prediction-validation
description: Use when testing transfer of a trained protein-imputation model to data whose cell types are not perfectly aligned with training, or generated by a different antibody-tagging protocol (CITE-seq vs REAP-seq).

name: cross-protocol-scrnaseq-integration
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data generated by multiple scRNA-seq protocols where batch effects confound cell-type separation, and you need batch-corrected embeddings plus cluster assignments evaluated with silhouette metrics.

name: cross-reference-version-signature-exposure-comparison
description: Use when fitting mutational signatures to a mutation catalog and you need to assess sensitivity of per-sample signature exposures to the reference signature set version (e.g. COSMIC v2 vs v3.1), or to justify which reference version's cleaner signature definitions to report.

name: cross-replicate-agreement-analysis
description: Use when two or more replicate sections from the same platform (e.g., Xenium-BreastCancer1 and Xenium-BreastCancer2) have been segmented with BIDCell and you need to quantify whether cell segmentation and cell-type annotation results are concordant across replicates.

name: cross-replicate-apa-profile-correlation
description: Use when you have spatially barcoded ST poly(A) site data for multiple tissue-section replicates (e.g., ST-MOB Replicates 5, 11, 12) and need to test whether spatial APA patterns and gene-level DEAPA calls reproduce across sections.

name: cross-replicate-st-training-scenario-design
description: Use when benchmarking 2D location or spatial domain recovery on ST data with replicate sections, and you need training scenarios ranging from same-section splits to cross-replicate transfer with merged training sets.

name: cross-run-clustering-consistency-measurement
description: Use when scRNAseq cells have been clustered by Sparsely-Connected Autoencoder (SCA) across repeated runs and you must quantify cluster reconstruction reproducibility (QCC/QCM >= 0.5) or validate the autoencoder's clustering stability.

name: cross-run-feature-set-comparison
description: Use when repeating a marker-selection procedure (e.g., phenotype-cover G-PC/CEM-PC) over multiple resampled runs and you need a stability index showing how much of the feature set is retained across runs.

name: cross-run-pseudotime-robustness-assessment
description: Use when pseudotime/trajectory output from RNA velocity-based methods must be validated: repeated runs of a stochastic method (e.g., 10 Cytopath initialisations) need robustness checks and known cell type orderings are available for correlation.

name: cross-sample-cell-library-loss-quantification
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet data sequenced on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) needs per-sample assessment of how many cell calls are artefactual after swapped-molecule removal.

name: cross-sample-label-transfer
description: Use when you have an annotated single-cell/nuclei RNA-seq dataset (e.g., .h5ad with 'class_label' in AnnData.obs) and need to predict cell-type labels on cells from a different donor or sample using SIMS label transfer.

name: cross-sample-network-coordinate-comparison
description: Use when you already hold two denoised scGRNs (sparse dgCMatrix X and Y over the same gene set) and need commensurable per-gene coordinates to detect differential regulation between conditions.

name: cross-sample-variability-adjustment
description: Use when comparing pseudotemporal gene expression dynamics across two or more conditions where each condition has multiple biological sample replicates, and cell-level methods would inflate false discoveries.

name: cross-scale-cell-type-label-transfer
description: Use when a sub-micrometer-resolution ST dataset (e.g. Seq-Scope, >1M spatial barcodes per mm2) has too few UMIs per spatial barcode for direct clustering, and cell-type labels from coarse bins must be transferred to finer overlapping sliding-window bins.

name: cross-screen-reproducibility-filtering
description: Use when reconstructing a causal gene regulatory network from gRNA-to-gene perturbation data where multiple gRNAs per regulator and replicate screens are available, and only regulations surviving all four Q ≤ 0.2 tests should be kept.

name: cross-slice-batch-effect-mitigation
description: Use when integrating multiple spatial transcriptomics slices (e.g., 11 human breast cancer 10X Visium slices) whose batch effects would confound slice-by-slice domain identification, and uniform cross-slice domains are required.

name: cross-source-pair-merge-deduplication
description: Use when building or extending a ligand-receptor reference database from multiple prior L-R resources and you must reconcile, deduplicate, and verify literature support per pair before publishing the merged set.

name: cross-species-aging-atlas-analysis
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend cell-type-by-age analyses of cellular senescence in single-cell atlases spanning multiple ages/species, e.g. scoring cells with SenePy signatures and comparing old vs young marker-positive proportions per cell type.

name: cross-species-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when scRNA-seq FASTQs from multiple organisms must be assessed for how much transcriptional signal falls outside current genome annotations, or when reproducing reported uTAR read fractions (e.g., hg38 2%, lemur 7.1%, mole rat 4.2%, sea urchin 10.7%).

name: cross-species-cell-fate-annotation-transfer
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset from one species must receive continuous cell fate (differentiation potential) annotations from a curated reference dataset in another species, requiring cross-batch and cross-species distribution alignment.

name: cross-species-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when training labels exist only in one species (e.g., mouse Tabula Muris) and you must annotate scRNA-seq cells from another species (e.g., human pancreas) using a shared one-to-one orthologue gene space.

name: cross-species-cell-type-matching
description: Use when matching/aligning cell types between two species from scRNA-seq count data (e.g., human–mouse, human–marmoset, mouse–marmoset cortex), especially when homologous gene lists are incomplete and protein-sequence-based gene similarity is needed.

name: cross-species-conservation-comparison
description: Use when you have predicted core promoter element records (position, score, TSS) for multiple species and want to test whether element positioning — e.g. TATA, dInr, PB relative to CAGE-annotated TSSs — is conserved across metazoans.

name: cross-species-cross-tissue-model-validation
description: Use when a tissue-specific RNA modification predictor (e.g., im6A-TS-CNN on 41-nt m6A segments) must be shown to generalize across species-tissue combinations before deployment or comparison.

name: cross-species-embedding-integration-interpretation
description: Use when trained cross-species cell embeddings exist and you need to judge cell-type-level alignment across species, e.g. homologous types (Vip, Sncg) mixing while species-specific types (Meis2, pericytes, SMC) stay separated.

name: cross-species-expression-pattern-comparison
description: Use when interpreting differential expression results from ExpressAnalyst across taxonomically diverse species lacking reference transcriptomes, where KO-based mapping could double-count homologous genes as separate DE ortholog groups.

name: cross-species-gene-homolog-mapping
description: Use when scRNA-seq gene identifiers come from a species (e.g., mouse) whose names must be mapped to homologs (e.g., human) before matching against a default L-R pair database such as dsCellNet's 5,744-pair list.

name: cross-species-gene-matching-comparison
description: Use when comparing how ortholog/gene matches from protein-embedding distances (ProtBERT) differ from BLAST sequence-alignment hits across two species, e.g. human vs mouse protein FASTA plus embeddings.

name: cross-species-gene-ortholog-mapping
description: Use when training data and query data come from different species (e.g. mouse reference, human query) and cell type labels must be transferred across species via orthologous genes.

name: cross-species-gene-orthology-mapping
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples from one species (e.g., rat micro-dissected renal tubule segments, GSE56743) must be deconvolved with a single-cell reference from another species (e.g., mouse kidney scRNA-seq, GSE107585), which first requires homologous-gene mapping.

name: cross-species-genome-coordinate-processing
description: Use when building training data for RNA modification site prediction from RMBase v2.0 BED/GTF annotations across multiple species, requiring genome-coordinate extraction of flanking sequence windows.

name: cross-species-lncrna-model-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-species trained lncRNA classifiers and independent FASTA test sets from multiple species, and need to measure homologous vs. divergent transfer (e.g., animal vs. plant) via an MCC matrix.

name: cross-species-ortholog-gene-mapping
description: Use when a human single-cell query must be interpreted against a mouse reference atlas — e.g., projecting human tumor biopsy T cells onto the murine TIL map to test human-mouse T cell subtype conservation.

name: cross-species-ortholog-mapping
description: Use when the query scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq dataset is from a different species than the available reference cell map (e.g., wheat query vs. rice reference) and reference-based annotation is required.

name: cross-species-orthology-inference
description: Use when building or reproducing an ortholog database (e.g. EcoOmicsDB) from many species' proteomes, or when non-model-species RNA-seq reads must be quantified against cross-species ortholog groups rather than a reference transcriptome.

name: cross-species-pretrained-model-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when you have human-trained miRSCAPE models (xgboost-based) and need to test transfer to non-training transcriptomic contexts — e.g. ENCODE cell-line mRNA profiles or mouse scRNA-seq clusters — with binary detectability labels for miRNAs.

name: cross-species-promoter-element-profiling
description: Use when you have high-confidence TSS coordinates (e.g. from csRNA-seq or other nascent-transcription data) for any species and need to detect core promoter elements and assess motif positioning around the TSS.

name: cross-species-scrna-seq-integration
description: Use when integrating single-cell RNA-seq datasets from different tissues or species where a pretrained embedding model (scETM) should be applied to a target AnnData without retraining, and clustering quality (ARI) and batch mixing (kBET) must be benchmarked.

name: cross-species-senescence-signature-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to derive or validate species-level 'universal' senescence gene panels from SenePy's 72 mouse / 64 human cell-type signatures, or to compare a derived merged panel against the distributed Universal_mouse.txt / Universal_human.txt references.

name: cross-species-single-cell-integration
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression matrices from two or more plant species and need to test whether homologous cell types co-embed after integration using orthologous genes as anchors.

name: cross-study-cell-type-annotation-comparison
description: Use when query scRNA-seq datasets from two or more biological groups (e.g., Ctrl vs RPL decidual immune cells) have been projected onto a shared reference atlas and you need to compare cell-type label composition across groups.

name: cross-study-cell-type-integration
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq studies (e.g. H5AD inputs like the public blood_covid example) must be compared at cell-type level and their heterogeneous annotations need to be mapped to a shared standardized Cell Ontology vocabulary.

name: cross-study-clustering-meta-analysis
description: Use when you have expression data from multiple independent studies/cohorts (possibly across species) and need to test whether a shared reference annotation, rather than batch/study/species identity, drives transcriptional clustering.

name: cross-study-expression-normalization
description: Use when you have a gene-level collapsed intensity matrix from multiple microarray studies (e.g. GEO-derived 3T3-L1 arrays) and need comparable, log-scale normalized expression across arrays/studies.

name: cross-study-gene-overlap-normalization
description: Use when a classifier trained on one scRNA-seq study must predict labels on an independent dataset (different platform/study), since the two count matrices typically contain different gene sets that must first be normalized and intersected.

name: cross-study-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when an interpretable latent-space model (e.g., VEGA) has been trained on one single-cell study and you must quantify generalization to held-out cell types/conditions or to a completely unseen second study.

name: cross-study-label-harmonization-with-cellhint
description: Use when evaluating whether a subsampled scRNA-seq sketch (e.g. 10% scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler) preserves cross-study cell-type subtype relationships, via CellHint harmonization trees built from .h5ad inputs with X_pca representations.

name: cross-study-marker-gene-search
description: Use when a specific gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') is given and the goal is to find which annotated cell types specifically express it across multiple imported single-cell studies in Cellenium's integrated database.

name: cross-study-metadata-vocabulary-harmonization
description: Use when aggregating metadata from multiple public datasets (e.g., GEO series) whose experimental designs are described inconsistently, and you need a unified vocabulary to compare or pool samples across studies.

name: cross-study-scrna-seq-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known labels from one study and need to annotate cells from a different, independently collected study of the same tissue (inter-study annotation), or to benchmark label-assignment methods.

name: cross-subgroup-network-edge-intersection
description: Use when you have a DEGGs subnetworks object built over multiple subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 and BRCA_LumA from TCGA-BRCA) and need each subgroup's network restricted to interactions not significant in all groups.

name: cross-subject-gene-weighting
description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq cell type proportions with a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, and gene weights must reflect cross-subject consistency rather than pre-selected marker genes.

name: cross-subtyping-concordance-analysis
description: Use when the same curated PDAC bulk expression samples must be labeled under multiple published subtype schemes (Moffitt, Collisson, Bailey) to measure pairwise overlap between analogous subtypes.

name: cross-technology-scrnaseq-benchmarking
description: Use when query scRNA-seq data from multiple sequencing technologies/protocols must be mapped onto a shared reference atlas and you need to quantify batch-effect correction with a cell-type mixing metric such as LISI.

name: cross-time-module-similarity-analysis
description: Use when you have per-subject, per-time-point community label predictions from a MuDCoD fit on donor-specific scRNA-seq networks and need a cross-time module-persistence score per donor, stratified by a donor-level phenotype such as differentiation efficiency.

name: cross-timepoint-cell-annotation
description: Use when you have labeled scRNA-seq data at an initial time point (t0) and unlabeled expression data at a later time point (t1) from the same study, and you need to assign cell-type labels to the t1 cells (e.g., pre- vs post-treatment samples).

name: cross-tissue-biosample-suitability-analysis
description: Use when you have .results.mrsd.txt scores for multiple GTEx-derived biosamples and a one-per-line gene list (GENCODE v19 symbols/Ensembl IDs), and need to determine which genes/variants are assayable or low-MRSD (≤100 M reads) in at least one tissue.

name: cross-tissue-gene-coverage-comparison
description: Use when per-tissue MRSD score tables (*.results.mrsd.txt) are available for two or more biosamples and you must rank tissues by the fraction of low-MRSD genes within a gene panel.

name: cross-tissue-gene-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have per-tissue ASE SNP call sets (e.g. VADT sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt files) mapped to gene IDs and need to test whether the same genes show ASE across multiple tissues and what pathways they share.

name: cross-tissue-mirna-activity-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq profiles lack miRNA measurements (poly(A) capture precludes mature miRNAs) and paired bulk mRNA-miRNA training cohorts exist for the tissue(s) of interest, so miRNA expression can be predicted from mRNA profiles.

name: cross-tissue-model-transfer-to-single-cell-data
description: Use when you need to chart miRNA activity across many cell types in a scRNA-seq atlas using a model trained on diverse bulk paired miRNA-mRNA cohorts, rather than tissue-matched training.

name: cross-tissue-protein-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when cell types in training and test single-cell multi-omic data are not perfectly aligned and you need to test whether a trained protein-imputation model generalizes across tissues or across CITE-seq/REAP-seq protocols.

name: cross-tissue-qval-variance-ranking
description: Use when you have a multi-tissue single-cell atlas (e.g. blood, bone marrow, lymph node, lung) with a shared cell-type annotation and want to find pathway-level features unique to one tissue site rather than testing tissue pairs in isolation.

name: cross-tissue-sqtl-effect-size-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL results (e.g. GTEx sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv tables) and need to quantify, cluster, or visualize cross-tissue sQTL sharing, especially to test whether brain tissues share sQTLs differently from non-brain tissues.

name: cross-tool-alignment-consistency-comparison
description: Use when a 10x scRNA-seq sample has been analyzed for pathogen reads by more than one alignment strategy and you need to verify that EGFP+/pathogen+ cell calls and per-cell UMI counts are consistent across methods.

name: cross-tool-annotation-agreement-quantification
description: Use when you have 3' UTR predictions from multiple annotation tools plus a trusted canonical annotation (e.g. WormBase chrI GFF) and need to quantify which tool agrees with the reference.

name: cross-tool-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare annotation pipelines head-to-head on million-cell datasets (>1 million cells) and quantify accuracy together with resource metrics (training time, peak memory, GPU requirement) to derive cost-efficiency conclusions.

name: cross-tool-barcode-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have barcode count tables produced by two or more pre-processing tools on the same FASTQ dataset and need to benchmark their detection concordance, quantify three-tool overlaps, and compare runtime/memory.

name: cross-tool-capability-benchmarking
description: Use when selecting among gene-name/date correction tools: you need an apples-to-apples capability matrix covering multi-file processing, dd/mm/yy vs mixed date formats, and HGNC name updating.

name: cross-tool-cell-call-overlap-analysis
description: Use when validating a new pathogen-detection tool for 10x scRNAseq against established tools by measuring concordance of infected-cell calls and correlating per-cell pathogen read/UMI counts.

name: cross-tool-circrna-quantification-comparison
description: Use when comparing alternative circRNA quantification tools on the same ribo− RNA-seq data to decide whether a CIRCscore-style normalized ratio is more accurate than CLR-style back-splice counting, e.g. for loci with RT-qPCR validation values.

name: cross-tool-comparison-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a malignant cell annotation method against published baselines on shared gold/silver standard scRNA-seq datasets, or when benchmarking inference runtime and memory scaling with dataset size.

name: cross-tool-driver-prediction-comparison
description: Use when comparing multiple driver-gene prediction tools' gene lists against known driver sets (e.g. CGC 616 genes, NCG 711 genes, PMH 501 genes) over matched datasets, and recall-weighted performance must be quantified and ranked.

name: cross-tool-execution-time-comparison
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency (CPU time and wall-clock time) of multiple pathogen-quantification pipelines for scRNAseq data, and a measured ranking must be reproduced on an identical input sample.

name: cross-tool-factor-similarity-correlation-index
description: Use when several cell-cell communication scoring methods (e.g., CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, rank-based cell2cell scores) have been applied to the same multi-sample dataset and you need to assess whether Tensor-cell2cell decompositions agree across tools.

name: cross-tool-isoform-abundance-comparison
description: Use when a single-locus long-read splicing assay (e.g. a minigene) has been aligned once and you need to compare how two isoform callers (VIsoQLR vs StringTie2) disagree on isoform counts, abundances, and isoform lengths.

name: cross-tool-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing the runtime and RAM footprint of ORIGINS, LandSCENT, and CytoTRACE on the same GEO scRNA-seq count matrices to reproduce or extend the paper's Table 1 performance benchmark.

name: cross-tool-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing computation time of a new GPU-accelerated implementation against its CPU predecessor on the same workstation, inputs, and settings (e.g. cudaMMC vs 3D-GNOME on GM12878 CTCF ChIA-PET data).

name: cross-tool-prediction-comparison
description: Use when you hold a labeled RNA transcript FASTA test set (e.g., H-Test mRNAs vs lncRNAs) and need to verify or replicate reported accuracy differences across multiple lncRNA-coding-potential predictors rather than run just one tool.

name: cross-tool-prediction-overlap-analysis
