description: Use when a task requires benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools by comparing the number and overlap of predicted 21-PHAS genes from multiple tools on the same small RNA-seq dataset with a shared reference sequence.

name: cross-tool-probability-collection
description: Use when benchmarking two or more RNA editing detection tools on a shared bona fide site set and you need per-site predictions aligned by genomic position to compute head-to-head ROC curves, AUC, or FNR.

name: cross-tool-pseudotime-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to benchmark or validate trajectory-inference consistency across multiple pseudotime tools on a preprocessed plant scRNA-seq Seurat object with known root-state cell types (e.g., meristem).

name: cross-tool-quantification-comparison
description: Use when comparing the runtime or throughput of competing read-counting/quantification tools on the same SAM/BAM alignment files and reference annotations, e.g. to decide whether a specialized counter's overhead is acceptable.

name: cross-tool-result-aggregation
description: Use when several annotation tools have been run on the same scRNA-seq train/test splits and their per-cell predictions must be harmonized, scored against study labels, and aggregated into a single comparison table.

name: cross-tool-runtime-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when comparing the IGHV-reconstruction completeness or runtime of competing BCR reconstruction tools across the same set of RNA-seq samples, e.g. reproducing the CRIS vs V'DJer/TRUST/MiXCR benchmark on GSE66228 CLL samples.

name: cross-tool-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing batch-integration methods on the same datasets and you must report both integration quality (iLISI/cLISI/RNN) and wall-clock runtime per tool in a single comparison CSV.

name: cross-tool-speedup-factor-comparison
description: Use when reproducing or extending runtime/speedup benchmarks of SCEVAN against CopyKAT, inferCNV, DNAcopy, or CNVkit on scRNA-seq count matrices, timing classification and segmentation stages separately.

name: cross-tool-te-marker-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a locus-resolved TE quantification tool outperforms a family-level TE tool for detecting cell-type marker TEs in scRNA-Seq clusters.

name: cross-validated-auc-evaluation
description: Use when you have a binary gene cluster absence/presence matrix with literature-assigned lifestyle labels and need to quantify how predictable each lifestyle is via cross-validated AUC.

name: cross-validated-binary-classifier-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a fitted penalized regression model on high-dimensional genomic covariates with a binary outcome (e.g., NMIBC vs MIBC invasion subtype) needs an unbiased estimate of prediction performance.

name: cross-validated-classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a trained LDA or HSS-LDA model with a priori labels (e.g., cell-cycle phase, day, cell type) must be validated by cross-validated classification accuracy and analysis of which classes are confused.

name: cross-validated-concordance-index-estimation
description: Use when evaluating the predictive performance of penalized Cox regression (Ridge, Lasso, adaptive Lasso) fitted to high-dimensional genomic covariates (e.g., 9,548 mRNA entries or 670 mutated genes vs. 316 patients' survival times) with a 5-fold cross-validated concordance index.

name: cross-validated-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when a multivariate logistic or Cox model has been built from genes selected by first-step screening (e.g., adaptive Lasso with FDR) and you need an unbiased estimate of prediction power via cross validation.

name: cross-validated-regularization-tuning
description: Use when training a penalized multinomial classifier (e.g. glmnet) on per-cell signature-score features and the regularization strength must be tuned by k-fold cross-validation rather than fixed a priori.

name: cross-validated-regularization-tuning
description: Use when fitting suffPCR (row-sparse PCA + OLS/logistic) on high-dimensional, correlated omics data like the DLBCL expression set and the penalty lambda / subspace dimension d must be chosen by 5-fold cross-validation before extracting sparse loadings.

name: cross-validated-threshold-estimation
description: Use when predicting labels for an unlabeled scRNA-seq dataset against a trained hierarchical classifier and you need a data-driven cutoff to reject cells that belong to no known population.

name: cross-validation-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when evaluating how training-cohort composition (tissue-specific vs pooled multi-cancer cohorts) changes the cross-validation accuracy of a trained miRNA-inference model such as miRSCAPE.

name: cross-validation-and-independent-test-evaluation
description: Use when a new sequence-based predictor (e.g., a stacked ensemble for m5C sites in A. thaliana or M. musculus) must be benchmarked against tools on identical training and independent test datasets.

name: cross-validation-benchmark-evaluation-scrnaseq
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type classifiers on scRNA-seq data with predefined hierarchical trees, requiring k-fold cross-validated HF1-scores, rejection rates of unseen populations, and comparison to published baselines.

name: cross-validation-benchmark-of-cell-classifiers
description: Use when benchmarking automated single-cell cell-type classifiers (e.g., SIMS vs scANVI, Seurat, Scnym, SingleR, SciBet) on pre-annotated datasets to quantify accuracy and Macro F1 under cross-validation.

name: cross-validation-fold-model-consensus
description: Use when classifying unlabelled genes as TSGs or OGs from a gene-by-feature mutation matrix (e.g. 37 ratio-metric/entropy features) where a single model would risk overfitting the small CGC-labelled training set.

name: cross-validation-grid-search-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when choosing among several candidate classifiers on a high-dimensional expression matrix (e.g. 19,737-gene TCGA RNA-seq with subtype labels) and you need unbiased per-model hyperparameter selection plus held-out generalization estimates.

name: cross-validation-hyperparameter-stability
description: Use when training a classifier on a small labelled gene set (e.g. 136 TSGs and 76 OGs from CGC) where overfitting risk is high and hyper-parameters must be estimated stably before predictions are trusted.

name: cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a cancer driver gene prediction model on directed gene regulatory networks (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) with multi-omics gene features and you need 5-fold CV metrics (AUPRC, AUROC, accuracy) comparable to graph-based baselines.

name: cross-validation-neural-network-training
description: Use when you need to train or robustness-test EmptyNN's PU-learning classifier over a grid of threshold T (50-400), cross-validation folds k (5-20), and iterations N (5-20) on raw droplet scRNA-seq count matrices.

name: cross-validation-of-probabilistic-models
description: Use when a probabilistic distribution model (e.g. the cubic-spline fragment length model in Forseti) must be trained on empirical measurements and its accuracy/variation on held-out data must be quantified with RMSE and k-fold cross-validation.

name: cross-validation-parameter-selection
description: Use when fitting FateCompass's linear model of gene regulation on single-cell data and needing to control model complexity via the diffusion step t, which must be tuned by cross-validation rather than set heuristically.

name: cross-validation-partitioned-feature-selection
description: Use when you need to identify which sequence-position features (e.g., position-specific gapped k-mer descriptors on 41-nt RNA sequences) are consistently, not just incidentally, predictive across repeated cross-validation resampling.

name: cross-validation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking a small-sample gene-classification model (e.g. 136 TSGs and 76 OGs labelled from CGC) and you need stable, class-wise performance metrics under k-fold cross-validation rather than a single train/test split.

name: cross-validation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when validating an m5C site prediction model on a balanced training set (e.g., 5,298 pos/5,298 neg A. thaliana or 4,563 pos/4,563 neg M. musculus 41-bp sequences) and reporting 10-fold cross-validation metrics.

name: cross-validation-performance-metric-computation
description: Use when a curated gene set or biomarker panel must be validated computationally by measuring normal-vs-cancer classification performance (Accuracy, AUC, F1) under cross-validation against competing gene signatures.

name: cross-version-runtime-benchmarking

description: Use when benchmarking or training DEG-combination methods (e.g. Naïve Bayes vote classifiers) and you need simulated count tables paired with known ground-truth DEG labels.

name: deg-list-comparison
description: Use when you have two or more ranked or unranked gene lists (e.g., Wx DI-ranked UGCBs, edgeR DEGs sorted by adjusted p value, published biomarker signatures) and need to measure their overlap to assess method concordance.

name: deg-literature-validation
description: Use when a ranked DEG list (e.g., scTITANS output at fdr level 0.01) must be confirmed as biologically meaningful, via literature surveys plus GO BP enrichment of the top genes.

name: deg-method-consensus-combination
description: Use when a count table must be analyzed for differential expression and robustness matters, or when evaluating which DEG detection method/combination strategy to trust on RNA-seq data.

name: deg-method-performance-evaluation
description: Use when simulated RNA-seq count matrices with known differentially expressed gene labels are available and you need to compare DEG detection methods by AUC, or to benchmark a combined/integrated method against individual tools.

name: deg-method-rank-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two DEG-prediction methods (one clustering-independent like singleCellHaystack, one clustering-based like Seurat FindAllMarkers) must be benchmarked on the same scRNA-seq dataset and their top gene lists compared for agreement.

name: deg-method-vote-threshold-evaluation
description: Use when you have simulated RNA-seq count data with known DE/non-DE labels and need to choose a consensus combination strategy (vote threshold vs combined-FDR) across DESeq2, NOISeq, and limma results.

name: deg-rank-binning-analysis
description: Use when a ranked DEG list (sorted by p-value, e.g. log.p.vals from show_result_haystack) needs benchmarking against a curated marker database to test whether top hits are enriched for known cell-type markers.

name: deg-result-ranking-and-export
description: Use when a haystack run has completed and you need to extract, rank, and export its DEG results ordered by log p-values / D_KL divergence for downstream inspection or verification of the top-ranked gene.

name: deg-set-overlap-and-agreement-analysis
description: Use when you have two DEG result tables from alternative paired linear mixed model fits (e.g. with and without a kinship covariance random effect) and need to quantify how model specification changes detection at a fixed FDR cutoff such as 0.05.

name: deg-threshold-filtering
description: Use when raw RNA-seq read counts with infected-vs-mock sample metadata are available and a stringent list of differentially expressed genes (|log2FC| > 1, adjusted p-value < 0.05) is needed for downstream pathway or modeling analyses.

name: deg-volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have already called DEGs between two cell-fate groups (e.g., sym_DCIS vs asym_DCIS from GEMLI lineage predictions) and need to visualize genes with significant adjusted p-values and log-fold changes such as CDH2, DCAF7, and LINC01999.

name: degraded-sample-outlier-exclusion
description: Use when a cohort of base-level RNA-seq coverage data must be screened for degraded samples whose 3'-to-5' decay slopes would create spurious outliers in downstream shape/outlier analyses.

name: degree-corrected-block-model-parameterization
description: Use when you need simulated multi-subject dynamic networks with known community labels to benchmark community detection — e.g. sweeping r_time, r_subject, and time_horizon T for MuDCoD evaluation.

name: degree-of-interlacement-graph-construction
description: Use when single-cell spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl brain with 16 cell types) with per-cell coordinates and cluster labels must be summarized as a weighted cell-type-by-cell-type graph of spatial interlacement before spatially aware colorization.

name: degree-of-interlacement-quantification
description: Use when you need a scalar score describing how interlaced, adjacent, or isolated two cell-type clusters are in single-cell spatial coordinates (e.g., SRT data), or when choosing which spatial-relationship metric to drive color assignment or further spatial analysis.

name: degree-preserved-random-network-null-generation
description: Use when benchmarking whether an inferred GRN models disease gene sets (e.g., DisGeNET Immune, Metabolic, Neuronal categories) better than chance, and a degree-matched random network null is needed to compute performance gain.

name: delta-aic-model-comparison
description: Use when RNA-seq data come from related/paired samples and you need to quantify, per gene, whether adding a kinship covariance random effect improves mixed model fit via AIC.

name: delta-network-differential-analysis
description: Use when comparing two single-cell expression conditions (e.g. 3- vs 18-month mammary gland CPM-normalized matrices) to identify which ligand-receptor edges are gained, lost, or fold-changed between them.

name: delta-pi-cell-type-tracing
description: Use when gene-wise bulk DIE results (e.g., HIPP vs PFC) must be attributed to the cell types that drive them, i.e., deciding Single-/Both-/No-Cell-Type-Model for each DIE gene from per-cell-type isoform usage.

name: delta-pi-percent-isoform-usage-calculation
description: Use when comparing per-gene isoform proportions between two conditions (e.g., bulk or single-cell HIPP vs PFC) from long-read ScISOrSeq count tables to identify genes with significant shifts in isoform, TSS, or polyA-site usage.

name: delta-psi-calculation
description: Use when comparing alternative-splicing changes between two regions/conditions (e.g. hippocampus vs prefrontal cortex) at exon level, especially when validating that single-cell ScISOrSeq dPSI values reproduce in spatial long-read data.

name: delta-svm-variant-scoring
description: Use when sQTL (or other regulatory) variants need to be assessed for whether they alter RBP binding sites rather than splice-site consensus sequences, using per-RBP sequence classifiers and deltaSVM effect scores.

name: delve-dynamic-module-identification
description: Use when you have a preprocessed cells x genes single-cell matrix (.h5ad or similar) and need to select features that preserve cell-state transitions, e.g. modules of genes with dynamic expression along a differentiation or activation trajectory.

name: demultiplexing-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when a task requires reproducing or extending the Fig. 1D-style accuracy comparison of demultiplexers on data with true barcode labels — e.g. the Ebrahimi et al. 2022 simulated 5-million-read/5000-cell long-read single-cell dataset with barcode_list.txt as the whitelist.

name: demultiplexing-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a cell-hashing HTO count matrix (e.g. 8-hashtag Stoeckius-2018, GSE108313) must be demultiplexed by multiple tools and their sample assignments compared to scSplit-derived ground-truth labels.

name: demultiplexing-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cellular-barcode discovery/demultiplexing tools on noisy long-read single-cell FASTQ data and a short-read-derived barcode whitelist is available as withheld ground truth for sensitivity/specificity scoring.

name: demuxlet-genotype-based-demultiplexing
description: Use when a multiplexed scRNA-seq dataset has genetically distinct individuals pooled together, and per-barcode genotype-derived labels (singlet/doublet/negative, cell-free versus cell-containing) are needed as ground truth to benchmark cell-calling methods.

name: demuxlet-ground-truth-matching
description: Use when evaluating or comparing demultiplexing methods (e.g., demuxmix vs HTODemux, hashedDrops, MULTI-seq, GMM-Demux, DemuxEM) and genotype-derived ground-truth labels from demuxlet are available for the same (HTOs x droplets) count matrix.

name: dendritic-cell-progenitor-lineage-branching-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset of dendritic cell progenitors (CDP through preDC stages) must be checked for a branching event separating cDC1- versus cDC2-committed preDC subsets, and when benchmarking which trajectory method recovers that branch.

name: dendritic-cell-subtype-annotation
description: Use when FiRE-scored ~68k human PBMC profiles have yielded a rare-cell subset (~4238 cells) and you need to resolve which Villani dendritic sub-types (DC1, DC3, DC4, DC6) the rare dendritic clusters correspond to.

name: dendrogram-cut-parameter-tuning
description: Use when a clustering-based trajectory method (e.g. Mpath) requires choosing a dendrogram cut depth and a diversity/aggregation cut, and you must confirm that downstream landmarks, branches, or networks are robust to those parameter choices.

name: dendrogram-iterative-cutting
description: Use when designating landmark clusters from single-cell expression data by cutting a Ward.D hclust dendrogram at multiple candidate k values and selecting the cut via a purity-versus-number-of-clusters inflection criterion.

name: dendrogram-visualization
description: Use when you have a symmetric pairwise distance matrix (e.g., scDist distances between cell types) and need to cluster it hierarchically and render a dendrogram to check whether distances recapitulate known biological relationships such as immune cell lineages.

name: denoising-autoencoder-training
description: Use when predicting single-cell drug responses from scRNA-seq by transferring a model trained on bulk cell-line drug response data (GDSC/CCLE), e.g. scoring GSE110894 AML cells for I.BET.762 sensitivity.

name: denoising-autoencoder-training
description: Use when you need a denoised, low-dimensional latent embedding of a scRNA-seq count matrix for downstream cell clustering, especially with dropout-heavy zero-inflated counts.

name: denoising-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare scRNA-seq denoising/imputation methods (DCA vs MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) on count matrices, either by recovery of a known signal (e.g., time-correlated genes after simulated dropout) or by runtime scaling across downsampled cell counts.

name: denoising-multimodal-autoencoder-implementation
description: Use when clustering paired single-cell multimodal data (CITE-seq RNA+ADT or SMAGE-seq RNA+ATAC) with an end-to-end deep model that jointly optimizes reconstruction, KL, and clustering losses.

name: denovo-ccg-identification
description: Use when after Tempo Step 1 has produced cell phase posterior distributions for a scRNA-seq dataset, you must expand the circadian cycler set by identifying which previously non-cycling genes are described by phase variation.

name: dense-subnetwork-extraction
description: Use when you have a subpopulation-specific directed TF-target score matrix (e.g., from DC3 deconvolved expression, ATAC, and HiChIP profiles) and need to identify the densely cross-regulating core regulatory network plus its upstream/downstream effectors.

name: densenet-encoder-architecture-configuration
description: Use when training a self-supervised feature encoder on a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix of highly variable genes and a DenseNet-based MoCo architecture with contrastive queue settings must be configured.

name: density-adaptive-neighbor-selection
description: Use when constructing a single-cell cell–cell network from archetypal/multilevel decomposition outputs (H*) and you need neighborhood sizes to adapt to local density and heterogeneity rather than fixing k in advance.

name: density-based-cluster-seed-selection
description: Use when initializing label-propagation clustering of single-cell RNA-seq data without a predetermined number of cell types, and seed cells must be selected from a directed kNN graph built on a quantitative cell-landmark matrix.

name: density-gradient-edge-construction
description: Use when you have single-cell expression data with a prior (e.g. RaceID3-derived) cluster assignment and need a 2D embedding whose topology encodes both class separation and density-gradient-based differentiation paths.

name: density-gradient-shift-edge-interpretation
description: Use when a graph-embedding visualization with prior class labels must reveal continuous differentiation orderings between clusters, e.g. resolving meta-cluster C7-C1 in myeloid progenitor single-cell data.

name: density-index-computation-pc-space
description: Use when tuning DUBStepR feature selection on scRNA-seq data without reliable cell type labels: sweeping feature set sizes and needing a label-free criterion whose argmax agrees with the silhouette index.

name: density-index-optimization
description: Use when running DUBStepR with optimise.features = TRUE and you must decide how many correlated feature genes to keep beyond the seed set, e.g. after computing a gene-gene correlation (GGC) matrix on log-normalized scRNA-seq counts.

name: density-regression-gene-expression-association
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq cells genotyped for an expressed somatic SNV (e.g., via cb_sniffer or Vartrix on _counts_UB.tsv data) and want to test which genes track a mutant subclone across the whole sample, including non-genotyped cells.

name: dentate-gyrus-granule-cell-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when applying CellPath to the dentate-gyrus dataset (GSE95753, P12/P35, ~2,930 cells) to extract multiple high-resolution granule-cell trajectories with RNA velocity and quantify DE genes along within-population paths.

name: depth-importance-score-computation
description: Use when you need to rank or select candidate splitting variables at nodes of a DIPM classification tree or forest for precision-medicine subgroup identification, from fitted dipm tree structures over a covariate dataset.

name: deseq2-count-based-de-testing
description: Use when benchmarking differential expression methods on scRNA-seq case-vs-control data prior to ASGARD drug repurposing, specifically to generate a DESeq2-derived Gene.list (score/p-value per gene) as an alternative to Limma, Seurat, or edgeR rankings.

name: deseq2-log2foldchange-ecdf-comparison
description: Use when you have a filtered DESeq2 results data frame (gene_id, log2FoldChange, padj) and defined gene sets (e.g. seed-match targets vs. non-targets, or miRNA predicted targets vs. background) and need to test whether the target set shows a cumulative positive or negative log2FC shift.

name: deseq2-result-filtering
description: Use when a raw DESeq2 results data.frame (e.g., 32883-row Schlegel_2022_Ttr_D1_30mkg output) must be cleaned of NA rows and thresholded on log2FoldChange, padj, and baseMean before seed-match counting or deseq_fc_ecdf.

name: deseq2-wald-statistic-gene-specificity-scoring
description: Use when you need to quantify how specifically a set of marker genes (e.g., the 55 uniquely assigned human liver marker genes) maps to clusters produced by two or more alternative clustering solutions, and to test whether one solution yields higher marker-gene specificity.

name: deseq2-wald-test-count-modeling
description: Use when raw UMI count data for single cells are split into two pre-defined clone groups (e.g., by mtDNA variants from MQuad/vireoSNP) and you need a ranked DE gene list with FDR control.

name: detection-count-reproducibility-comparison
description: Use when a published COMPSRA serum small RNA-seq result (molecule counts per RNA class at a read-count threshold of 5) must be re-derived from raw 50 nt FASTQ reads and validated against reported figures.

name: detection-f1-score-evaluation
description: Use when comparing rare-cell detectors (GapClust, RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS, FiRE) on simulated count matrices that carry ground-truth rare-cell labels and you need per-method F1 scores.

name: detection-rate-threshold-filtering
description: Use when constructing cell-to-cell communication networks from single-cell expression data and you need to decide which ligands/receptors count as expressed in each cell type before edge extraction.

name: developmental-erythropoiesis-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when multi-batch single-cell RNA-seq of a continuous differentiation process (e.g. erythroid development) must be ordered along a trajectory and batch-corrected, interpretable factors should be validated against an RNA-velocity latent time.

name: developmental-hematopoiesis-marker-interpretation
description: Use when temporal scRNA-seq of developing mesoderm/hematopoiesis (e.g. E7.5/E7.75 mouse Cd41+ cells) has been projected with TCM and you must identify and biologically interpret subpopulations within one time point using marker genes.

name: developmental-lineage-ordering-by-embryonic-stage
description: Use when SCASL clusters of a developmental scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. 486-cell embryonic hepatoblasts) need biological validation by checking whether cluster orderings recapitulate known lineage progression across embryonic days.

name: developmental-lineage-timing-verification-across-hpf-stages
description: Use when integrating time-course embryo scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., zebrafish Wagner et al. and Farrell et al.) to verify or compare the developmental time point at which major lineages first emerge.

name: developmental-potency-monotonicity-analysis
description: Use when validating that a network-based potency metric like signalling entropy (SR) genuinely relies on the PPI network: the goal is a null ablation showing SR loses pluripotency discrimination and stage monotonicity after network-constrained reshuffling.

name: developmental-series-scrnaseq-analysis
description: Use when you have time-series single-cell RNA-seq spanning multiple developmental or aging time points (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis series) and need to infer L-R interactions and how they change across time points.

name: developmental-stage-composition-visualization
description: Use when query scRNA-seq cells have been mapped onto a developmental reference atlas (e.g., mTCA) and you need to show stage/cell-type composition per condition (treatment day) to detect meiotic entry, progression, or developmental arrest.

name: developmental-stage-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell dataset carries known developmental stage/time labels and the goal is to validate that a low-dimensional embedding recovers them chronologically or to check which method resolves an intermediate state.

name: developmental-time-course-communication-comparison
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq time points of a developing tissue are available with cell-type labels, and the goal is to identify stage-shared vs stage-specific communications and shifts in dominant communicating cell types (e.g., dermal-to-epidermal).

name: developmental-time-series-interaction-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple developmental time points and you need per-cell-type sender/receiver communication scores at each stage to identify the most active cell types over development.

name: developmental-timecourse-ase-dynamics
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-Seq allelic read counts from cells sampled along a developmental time course (e.g., 286 CAST×B6 F1 pre-implantation embryo cells) to quantify how stage-wise ASE patterns change.

name: developmental-timecourse-bifurcation-timing
description: Use when a multi-stage (e.g. 5W-24W fetal retina) scRNA-Seq time-course shows a bifurcation into two competing lineages that trajectory methods like diffusion maps cannot resolve in time, and the exact transition stage must be identified.

name: developmental-trajectory-cell-sorting
description: Use when a Mpath landmark graph and cell-to-landmark transition assignments are available and a pseudo-temporal ordering of individual cells along each developmental path is required for downstream dynamics analysis.

name: developmental-trajectory-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset represents a time-course (e.g., 86,024-cell C. elegans embryo GSE126954) and you need to test whether a hyperbolic embedding's radial coordinate (distance-to-origin) recapitulates developmental time as pseudotime.

name: developmental-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when you have a dropout-affected scRNA-seq matrix from a differentiating or developing cell population (e.g., zebrafish embryos, embryoid bodies) and need to recover pseudotime ordering and state transitions that imputation may distort.

name: deviance-residual-count-transformation
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq .h5ad objects) are about to be encoded by a MIRA/CODAL topic model and a continuous, variance-stabilized expression representation is required instead of raw or log-normalized counts.

name: deviation-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you have two competing cell-distance/similarity measures over the same labeled cells and need to quantify and plot which one separates same-type cells more strongly than random expectation (e.g., ACTIONet JSD similarity vs. HVG+PCA Euclidean distance).

name: dexseq-subexon-count-transformation
description: Use when you already hold a fortuna signature-counts table (cnt.tsv with subexon-ID signatures and counts) and need DEXSeq-compatible per-subexon counts for alternative splicing analysis.

name: dhs-cluster-level-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when you have BIRD-predicted DH plus measured DNase-seq signal for the same cell types and need to quantify prediction accuracy at pathway/DHS-cluster level (rC, fraction of clusters with rC>0.5/0.75) rather than per-locus.

name: dice-coefficient-segmentation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when predicted cell segmentation masks (e.g. MIRIAM, Mesmer, or nuclei-based Voronoi) must be quantitatively scored against manually annotated cell borders on tiled multiplexed immunofluorescence TMA images.

name: diebold-mariano-model-comparison-testing
description: Use when two or more deconvolution/clustering methods have been run on the same pixels with known ground-truth cell-type proportions and you must test whether one method's per-pixel RMSE is significantly lower than another's.

name: differentiable-rescaling-operation-design
description: Use when a generative model (e.g. scGAN/cscGAN generator) must explicitly output expression vectors with a fixed total read count, and the rescaling must remain differentiable for end-to-end backpropagation in TensorFlow.

name: differential-abundance-comparison-with-sccoda
description: Use when testing whether cell type proportions shift between conditions (e.g. ischemic vs control) in a clustered single-cell AnnData object, especially when samples are unreplicated and bootstrapped calls need concordance checks against scCODA on replicate pairs.

name: differential-abundance-local-neighborhoods
description: Use when comparing cell condition compositions in single-cell data with a shared low-dimensional representation but no trajectory assumed, or when computing per-cell imbalance scores for a visual diagnostic.

name: differential-abundance-negative-binomial-testing
description: Use when scRNA-Seq cells have been clustered into communities (Louvain or EVA) and you must test whether the abundance of specific cell-type/cluster labels changes between biological conditions while accounting for per-sample replicate variability.

name: differential-abundance-scoring-knn-graph
description: Use when comparing cell abundance between patient conditions on an integrated single-cell dataset — e.g. finding which cell types are enriched in severe versus moderate COVID-19 samples.

name: differential-abundance-testing
description: Use when testing which cell types credibly change abundance between conditions (e.g., COVID-19 BALF severity groups) from per-sample cell-type counts, especially with few replicates where univariate tests give false positives.

name: differential-activity-rank-comparison
description: Use when you need to validate a clustering-independent DAF/DEG method (singleCellHaystack) against cluster-based baselines (Wilcoxon rank-sum, t-test) by comparing rankings of the same features on shared normalized data.

name: differential-activity-testing-along-1d-trajectory
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data have been ordered along a 1D pseudotime trajectory (e.g. monocle3 learn_graph/order_cells from DN to SP thymocytes) and you need genes with biased expression along that axis rather than cluster-marker DEGs.

name: differential-analysis-html-reporting
description: Use when a ribosome profiling pipeline has produced a per-transcript count matrix (e.g. from htseq-count) and conditions are defined in config.yaml, and you need DESeq2-based differential calls plus a consolidated HTML report.

name: differential-apa-usage-analysis
description: Use when you have an imputed 3' UTR RUD (relative usage of distal poly(A) site) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data with layer annotations and need to classify genes with spatial APA usage patterns.

name: differential-apa-usage-analysis-between-anatomical-layers
description: Use when a spatially barcoded ST dataset already has poly(A) site annotations and layer labels (e.g., MOB morphological layers), and you need genes with differential or spatially patterned APA usage between those layers.

name: differential-cell-abundance-analysis
description: Use when you have a cell-type-by-sample abundance matrix (e.g., DCNet-inferred landscapes from bulk RNA-seq) with two labeled patient subtypes and need to find significantly differentially abundant cell types or build a subtype classifier from them.

name: differential-cell-subcluster-abundance-analysis
description: Use when you have pseudotime-ordered single-cell data from trajectory inference (e.g., Monocle3) with cluster/cell-type annotations, and need to detect which cell subclusters expand or deplete significantly over pseudotime rather than at discrete time points.

name: differential-chromatin-interaction-detection
description: Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) from two conditions and need per-bin-pair differential interaction statistics (pvalue, pvalue.adj.FDR) plus a consensus DCI set.

name: differential-co-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have single-cell UMI count data with per-cell group labels (e.g. disease status) and per-cell donor/sample labels, and need to test whether gene co-expressions within a specific cell type differ between conditions.

name: differential-co-expression-network-analysis
description: Use when you have matched two-condition gene expression matrices (rows = gene symbols, columns = sample IDs) plus a reference interaction network, and you need driver-node selection by network controllability rather than hub ranking.

name: differential-coexpression-z-testing
description: Use when you have FPKM-normalized expression matrices for two physiological conditions (e.g. TCGA_BLCAtumor vs TCGA_BLCAnormal, rows=gene symbols, columns=sample ids) and need to call significant differential co-expression edges on a fixed reference network.

name: differential-communication-analysis
description: Use when testing whether cell-cell communication strength mediated by specific candidate eLR pairs depends on a developmental process, by comparing interaction scores between a perturbed condition (e.g., ZGA-inhibited embryos) and unperturbed time-point conditions.

name: differential-communication-analysis-between-conditions
description: Use when two or more single-cell/single-nucleus expression matrices with cell-type annotations from distinct biological conditions (e.g., ASD vs control cortex) must be compared at the level of inferred ligand-receptor communication networks.

name: differential-connectomics-analysis
description: Use when two single-cell RNA-seq conditions (e.g. ifnb interferon-stimulated vs. control PBMCs from SeuratData) must be compared at the ligand–receptor level, and each edge needs a magnitude-of-perturbation score that is sign-agnostic for ligand/receptor changes.

name: differential-detection-analysis
description: Use when the goal is to detect subpopulation-specific changes in the fraction of cells expressing a gene (differential detection) across conditions from multi-sample scRNA-seq data, e.g. with muscat's pbDD.

name: differential-exon-usage-analysis
description: Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) FASTQs have short-read cell-type assignments and you need per-exon PSI quantification and HIPP-vs-PFC delta-PSI tests, or single-cell-vs-spatial ΔΨ concordance.

name: differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when raw or imputed scRNA-seq count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns, e.g. GSE75748 ESC/DEC) need DE gene lists between subpopulations, or when imputation impact on DE accuracy must be benchmarked against a bulk RNA-seq reference.

name: differential-expression-analysis-bulk-and-single-cell
description: Use when comparing single-cell vs bulk differential expression agreement for a two-population scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. H1 vs DEC), or when benchmarking denoising methods (DCA, MAGIC, SAVER, scImpute) by bulk-LFC correspondence.

name: differential-expression-analysis-endothelial-cells
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell batch-integration methods on multi-condition mixtures and you need a quantitative readout of whether across-condition biological differences (e.g. tissue-specific endothelial DE genes) survive integration.

name: differential-expression-analysis-of-tumor-infiltrating-lymphocytes
description: Use when comparing bulk or single-cell RNA-seq of CD8 TILs between immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) and control conditions, or when scoring an input scRNA-seq dataset for CD8 TIL transcriptomic states to test EM-like signature enrichment.

name: differential-expression-analysis-with-deseq2
description: Use when comparing two conditions (e.g., BNLx vs SHR strains) at transcript level after RSEM quantitation, especially to test whether a modified transcriptome changes the DE call set.

name: differential-expression-aucpr-assessment
description: Use when evaluating an imputation or preprocessing method's effect on differential expression accuracy in scRNA-seq data where a ground-truth set of DE genes is known, especially as a function of the zero-count (dropout) proportion.

name: differential-expression-auroc-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a feature selection algorithm (e.g., DUBStepR vs. HVGDisp, HVGVST, trendVar, devianceFS, HLG, M3Drop/DANB, GiniClust) on scRNA-seq data and you need a DE-detection AUROC against independently ascertained cell type annotations.

name: differential-expression-based-node-scoring
description: Use when you have case/control RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. TCGA ESCA tumor vs normal) and need to weight nodes of a CLIP-derived RBP-ncRNA network before running fRNC's global or local module search.

name: differential-expression-candidate-regulator-screening
description: Use when you have a scRNA-Seq matrix with a multipotent cell population and competing downstream lineages (e.g. SHARE-Seq hair-follicle TACs vs IRS/HS, or Ranzoni fetal-liver MPPs vs GP/MEMP), and you need to shortlist overexpressed regulatory factors to feed into DICE priming analysis.

name: differential-expression-cluster-validation
description: Use when RCC (or a consensus clustering run over candidate k values) has produced clusters and you must decide whether each cluster is a genuine subtype before subdividing further, using differential gene expression as the quality gate.

name: differential-expression-feature-extraction
description: Use when a simulated bulk multi-omics dataset (e.g. MOSim RNA-seq + miRNA-seq + TF) must yield a defined DEG/regulator feature set with ground-truth regulatory signs (activator vs repressor) for downstream validation.

name: differential-expression-fold-change-calculation
description: Use when you have a SAM significance output (samr-based Significance Analysis of Microarrays) plus a quantile-normalized expression matrix and need heatmaps of top-ranked gene lists that cluster samples by response class.

name: differential-expression-fold-change-ranking
description: Use when you have differential expression results (gene-level log fold-changes) from perturbed 3T3-L1 adipocyte microarray data and need a fold-change-ranked gene list as input to clusterProfiler GSEA for GO term enrichment.

name: differential-expression-gene-identification
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices with known rare-cell labels (e.g., artificial splatter data with group.prob = c(0.99, 0.01) or the packaged 1%Jurkat.h5) and need a validated set of DE genes and non-DE background genes for robustness/sensitivity tests.

name: differential-expression-gene-list-extraction
description: Use when a CCIVR Table.csv/Summary.csv of cis-NAT pairs carries RNA-seq expression columns (TPM, fold_change, padj) and the goal is to split partner genes into up/down lists for GO enrichment (e.g., DAVID GOTERM_BP_FAT).

name: differential-expression-gene-overlap-statistics
description: Use when you have cluster-derived key genes from scQA (e.g. labels.txt chained from a prior clustering task) and need to confirm they agree with published marker genes, hub genes, or DEGs for the same cell type.

name: differential-expression-gene-scoring
description: Use when validating single-cell drug-response predictions on a drug-treated scRNA-seq dataset by scoring DEGs and correlating scores with Monocle3-style pseudotime or sensitive/resistant probability labels.

name: differential-expression-gold-standard-annotation
description: Use when benchmarking DE detection methods on simulated scRNA-Seq data where ground-truth differential genes must be extracted from known true counts (e.g. SymSim population pairs 1v2, 1v4, 2v4) before any observed-count analysis.

name: differential-expression-group-planting
description: Use when you need a controlled synthetic scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth cell groups defined by distinct DE gene combinations, e.g. to benchmark cluster-merging or cluster-significance tools against planted truth.

name: differential-expression-log-transform-visualization
description: Use when signed differential-expression scores for a PCa-vs-normal RNA-seq contrast must be rendered as a Cytoscape color gradient (−1200 to 600) over expanded KEGG pathway nodes to show up/down regulation per gene or aggregated node.

name: differential-expression-logfc-extraction
description: Use when a completed multi-method DEG results table (e.g. ExpHunterSuite output with vote-threshold calls and log2FC columns) needs a specific gene's logFC record extracted for reporting, validation, or downstream GSEA-style reuse.

name: differential-expression-method-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating which multi-sample trajectory differential expression method controls false discoveries on single-cell data, especially by counting called genes on a null dataset where no gene is truly differential.

name: differential-expression-method-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or selecting a cluster-free differential expression method for multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell data where a simulated cohort with known ground-truth DE labels is available for validation.

name: differential-expression-modeling
description: Use when you need per-gene DEG testing on RNA-seq count data with an unpaired design (no within-subject pairing, no kinship/random effects), using kimma's kmFit run_lm=TRUE on TMM-normalized log2 CPM.

name: differential-expression-module-filtering
description: Use when you already have a cell-lineage-specific GRN plus driver regulators with influence scores and need gene modules tied to those regulators, then per-cell activity scores via AUCell.

name: differential-expression-profile-labelling
description: Use when building a synthetic bulk RNA-seq time-course with ground-truth DEG classes — e.g. seeding a simulator from a real sample's NB mean/dispersion and needing labelled induction/repression/flat temporal profiles.

name: differential-expression-pvalue-seeding
description: Use when you have case/control RNA-seq data (e.g. GSE172114 COVID-19, 46 critical vs 23 non-critical cases), have computed per-gene DE P-values, and need to extract a perturbed subnetwork from a reference interactome such as the KEGG graph (5007 nodes / 44755 edges).

name: differential-expression-quadrant-classification
description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values for two Treatment-vs-Control comparisons must be screened to identify extreme or moderate expression variations by fold-change thresholds and significance.

name: differential-expression-results-filtering
description: Use when a DESeq2 results table (with gene_id, log2FoldChange, padj, baseMean) contains NA rows or unfiltered fold changes and must be cleaned before annotating siRNA seed matches or running deseq_fc_ecdf comparisons.

name: differential-expression-signature-querying
description: Use when you have a short DE gene signature (e.g. 27–71 genes from GEO/MSigDB C7 studies of disease, smoking, or toxic-chemical exposure) and want to identify statistically enriched environmental gene modules.

name: differential-expression-similarity-based-cell-filtration
description: Use when preprocessing Perturb-seq/CROP-seq data (e.g., crop_stimulated expression_profile.txt + perturb_information.txt) to purge cells carrying invalid sgRNA edits before topic-model building in MUSIC.

name: differential-expression-summary-statistics-generation
description: Use when you have a two-group scRNA-seq comparison (e.g. DEC vs EC, CD4+ vs CD8+ T cells) and need per-gene beta/se summary statistics as input to iDEA or other GSE methods that consume DE summary statistics.

name: differential-expression-summary-table-generation
description: Use when a main folder hosts one sub-directory per pairwise comparison (each with pre-computed scorecard outputs) and you need per-gene totals across all comparisons to separate common gene-expression changes from condition-specific ones.

name: differential-expression-t-test-analysis
description: Use when you have a simulated two-group scRNA-Seq dataset with known truly differentially expressed gene labels and need to quantify how imputation (e.g., AutoClass) restores DE signal lost to dropout.

name: differential-expression-table-querying
description: Use when a gene of interest (e.g. 'insulin') must be matched to the cell types in which it is specifically expressed, using precalculated per-cluster differential expression/marker scores already ingested into Cellenium's database across one or more scRNA-seq studies.

name: differential-expression-testing
description: Use when DC3 subpopulation-specific FPKM profiles are available and transcription factors must be tested for differential expression between subpopulations to build a key-regulator candidate list.

name: differential-expression-testing-after-doublet-removal
description: Use when a doublet-contaminated scRNA-seq dataset with known or expected DEG labels is available and you need to quantify whether doublet removal (by Chord, DoubletFinder, scds, etc.) improves differential expression results.

name: differential-expression-testing-single-cell
description: Use when you have a single-cell TAR or gene expression matrix with cell-cluster labels and need to identify features (uTARs or genes) that are differentially expressed per cluster, e.g. to direct annotation efforts to biologically significant transcripts.

name: differential-expression-threshold-filtering
description: Use when building cancer cell-intrinsic subtype marker gene sets for pre-clinical model subtyping, i.e. when DE results from tumor cohorts must be stripped of stromal/immune signals absent from cell lines, organoids and PDXs.

name: differential-expression-thresholding
description: Use when raw RNA-seq count data from infected and control conditions (e.g. GEO GSE147507 / GSE148729 lung samples) must be reduced to binary expressed/not-expressed gene lists under |log2FC|>1, padj<0.05 thresholds to drive rFASTCORMICS model pruning.

name: differential-expression-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when a longitudinal cohort has per-patient timepoints relative to a clinical event (respiratory nadir) and you need to determine how early differential expression of candidate genes emerges and when levels return to baseline.

name: differential-expression-utar-filtering
description: Use when a single-cell TAR expression analysis has produced differentially expressed uTARs (e.g., from Wilcoxon rank-sum testing across clusters) that need functional or gene-level annotations via sequence homology.

name: differential-fate-selection-testing
description: Use when a single common trajectory (e.g., slingshot sds) spans multiple conditions and the goal is to test whether condition-level cell abundance differs between lineages (differential fate selection), after topologyTest has not rejected a common topology.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a batch-correction method on scRNA-seq data (e.g. two healthy samples from the same condition) and you need DEG counts, survival-relevant DEG signatures, or a comparison of over-correction vs. batch-noise removal across methods.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when comparing gene-level expression between exactly two user-defined cohorts from a parsed PDAC expression dataset and you need per-gene logFC and padj values plus a volcano plot.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a gene-level count table from an RNA-seq experiment (real, spike-in, or simulated) and need robust DEG calls whose method-specific assumptions are unknown or likely to matter.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object with annotated clusters/subclusters (e.g. PBMC3k) needs cluster-specific marker genes, and genes expressed in any non-target cluster must be excluded from the marker set.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when scRNAseq clusters (e.g., from LCMV1/LCMV2 CD44+ T cell 10X data) already exist and you need genes defining each cluster versus all others, plus subtype label assignment.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (.h5ad) with cell-type and condition/disease annotations and need per-cell-type DEG calls between conditions (e.g. COVID-19 vs normal, infarct vs control), with ranked gene lists and volcano plots.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a single-cell gene expression matrix plus cluster labels (e.g., SSRE-inferred cell type labels) and need to detect marker genes per cluster, expecting recovery of known markers.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq case/control data must be reduced to per-cell-cluster DEG profiles before connectivity-based drug repurposing (ASGARD GetDrug/DrugScore), or when benchmarking which scRNA-seq DE method maximizes downstream AUC.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a Seurat object with graph-based clusters (e.g. severe vs healthy COVID-19 bronchoalveolar/peripheral cells) and need DE gene lists plus their enriched environmental/gene modules with padj and fold enrichment.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when building a malignant-vs-normal epithelial classifier feature set from multiple annotated scRNA-seq training datasets, or when you need to combine per-dataset DEG lists into one pan-cancer gene panel.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when validating predicted perturbation-response transcriptomes (e.g., scButterfly-B output on PT_PBMC) by comparing per-cell-type DEG profiles to ground truth with top-100 DEG overlap and R2 metrics.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq expression matrices for two or more FACS-sorted or annotated cell subsets are available and signature genes distinguishing terminal cell types are needed for fate prediction or marker discovery.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a normalized gene/ortholog expression matrix with sample metadata is available and the goal is a ranked table of DEGs at a defined FDR threshold (e.g., FDR < 0.05 with |log2FC| > 1.5, or FDR < 0.1 for salamander-style analyses).

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when cells have already been assigned to clusters by SINCERA cluster.assignment and you need per-cluster differentially expressed genes to characterize cell types or build gene signatures.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a raw read count matrix plus sample metadata (e.g. GSE147507 severity study) must be tested for infected-vs-mock differential expression under |log2FC|>1 and adj p<0.05 thresholds.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have GEMLI-predicted symmetric/asymmetric cell fate lineages with cell type annotations and need to identify DEGs between cells of the same type that followed different fate decisions.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when rare cells detected from a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. 4238 FiRE-detected PBMC cells) have been clustered and specific clusters must be biologically characterized and assigned to known reference sub-types.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a gene-by-cell Smart-seq2 (or comparable) scRNA-seq count matrix is paired with per-cell mtDNA clone/subclone labels and the goal is to test if two subclones are transcriptionally distinct and which Hallmark pathways separate them.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when comparing gene expression between two groups of RNA-seq samples (e.g., high vs low GSVA-score strata or tumor vs normal) and you need DEGs filtered by p-value, FDR and logFC thresholds.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis-of-novel-cluster
description: Use when a Cell BLAST query leaves query cells unassigned (rejected under the default hit cutoff), indicating a putative novel cell type that must be validated by differential expression of marker genes.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis-of-t-cell-subsets
description: Use when you have clustered an mvTCR joint embedding of paired scRNA-seq/TCR data into antigen-specific and bystander T cell clusters and need to characterize their transcriptional differences, e.g. effector CD8+ T cells from SARS-CoV-2 PBMCs.

name: differential-gene-expression-analysis-riboseq
description: Use when ribosome profiling FastQ data from at least two conditions (reference vs comparison) must be processed end-to-end to identify genes with significant differential translational regulation.

name: differential-gene-expression-marker-extraction
description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq dataset with known cluster labels must yield per-cluster marker gene sets to score or assign target cells, e.g. before scid_multiclass mapping or a top-N-marker thresholding baseline.

name: differential-gene-expression-query-processing
description: Use when you have a DE gene list from a disease-vs-control contrast (e.g., GEO microarray study) and need to identify statistically enriched environmental pathway gene modules via Fisher exact test with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction.

name: differential-gene-expression-testing
description: Use when a merged, quantile-normalized (preprocessCore 'normalize.quantiles') expression matrix of staged cells must be reduced to a gene set that captures developmental variation before trajectory/pseudotime analysis.

name: differential-gene-expression-testing
description: Use when pseudo-bulked gene-level count matrices from 3'-tag scRNA-seq (scUTRquant output) are available and you need to identify genes whose mRNA abundance differs between two cell types or conditions.

name: differential-gene-expression-testing
description: Use when simulated or real single-cell data contain a binary covariate (e.g. stimulant/mutational status) and you need to quantify how well DE-based tests recover genes with covariate-pseudotime interactions versus a dedicated interaction model.

name: differential-gene-expression-ttest
description: Use when you have Spark-normalized scRNA-seq expression (tall/wide format) plus K-means cluster assignments, and need per-gene two-sample t-test DE rankings between every pair of clusters.

name: differential-gene-gene-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have normalized sequencing count data plus sample metadata with a categorical subgroup variable (e.g. TCGA-BRCA SUBTYPE = BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and need group-specific gene-gene interaction networks.

name: differential-gene-module-activity-testing
description: Use when single-cell gene module activities (GMVs) have been inferred per cell in a VEGA latent space and you need statistically testable, per-module activity differences between conditions (e.g., Trametinib vs. DMSO).

name: differential-gene-regulation-testing
description: Use when you have manifold-aligned network coordinates for genes from two single-cell conditions (scTenifoldNet output) and need to call significantly differentially regulated genes with p-values and FDR.

name: differential-gene-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when you have two gene expression matrices (tab-separated, rows = genes, columns = samples, first column named 'Gene') from two conditions and want a context-specific differential network beyond plain differential expression.

name: differential-hub-gene-identification
description: Use when you have scPRINT-derived gene networks (GRnnData objects) for two cell states or conditions — e.g. BPH-associated vs normal prostate fibroblasts — and need to flag genes whose hub status changes between conditions.

name: differential-isoform-expression-testing
description: Use when you have per-gene isoform (or TSS/polyA-site) count tables for two cell types or regions and need to identify genes whose percent-isoform usage shifts significantly between them.

name: differential-marker-expression-testing
description: Use when clustering results (e.g. 19 scCAN clusters on the Brain 1.3M dataset, GSE93421) lack true cell type labels and must be biologically validated and mapped to known cell types via marker genes.

name: differential-methylation-calling
description: Use when raw IDAT files plus a sample sheet from an Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array study (e.g. from GEO) need differential methylation calling between groups, and a GUI-driven, reproducible pipeline is acceptable.

name: differential-methylation-results-filtering
description: Use when you have a DMC results table from Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation analysis and need to restrict CpGs to promoter/5'UTR features or apply adjusted-P/logFC thresholds before visualization or enrichment.

name: differential-mutation-frequency-analysis
description: Use when you have a TCGA-style MAF mutation file and sample groups defined by a continuous factor (e.g. top/bottom hypoxia GSVA score) and need per-gene mutation p-values and FDR between groups.

name: differential-network-edge-analysis
description: Use when you have single-cell count matrices from two matched conditions (e.g., 211 normal vs 656 tumor immune cells from GSE114727) and want to detect co-expression edges present in one condition but absent in the other.

name: differential-network-inference-boosted-trees
description: Use when you have two tab-separated gene expression matrices (same genes, rows=genes, columns=samples) from two biological conditions and need a condition-specific differential network for downstream pathway enrichment.

name: differential-network-inference-from-transcriptomics
description: Use when two tab-separated gene expression matrices (genes as rows, first column named 'Gene') from two conditions are available and the goal is a condition-specific differential regulatory network with enriched disease-relevant pathways.

name: differential-pathway-activation-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters and candidate LR pairs are available and the goal is to determine which intracellular signaling pathways are significantly activated per cluster and which LR interactions are functionally associated with them.

name: differential-pathway-activity-prediction
description: Use when you have spot-level (or cell-level) continuous feature values such as Seurat module scores plus 2D/3D spatial coordinates, and you need to rank gene sets or features by how non-randomly their activity is distributed across the tissue.

name: differential-pathway-activity-testing
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomic data has been embedded in VEGA's pathway-informed latent space and you need to test which gene modules differ in activity between defined cell groups or conditions.

name: differential-pathway-activity-testing-between-condition-groups
description: Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two condition groups (e.g., CF vs non-CF, or treated vs control) needs a benchmarked differential pathway activity comparison across rROMA and sample-wise scoring methods.

name: differential-pathway-ranking-comparison
description: Use when comparing the computational efficiency (runtime, memory) and sensitivity of pathway activity scoring / differential pathway methods (scPAFA vs SCPA) on million-cell-scale scRNA-seq data with >1000 pathways, or when assessing whether downsampling-based tools lose disease-relevant pathway.

name: differential-progression-testing
description: Use when scRNA-Seq data from two or more conditions share a common trajectory (topologyTest fails to reject it) and the goal is to detect condition-specific shifts in pseudotime distributions along lineages.

name: differential-pseudotime-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples per condition need differential pseudotime analysis of gene expression, cell abundance, or trajectory topology, and sample-to-sample variation must be modeled to avoid false discoveries.

name: differential-regulatory-factor-overexpression-analysis
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-Seq data of a bifurcating multipotent population (e.g. MPPs vs. two downstream lineages) to find which regulatory factors are overexpressed in one lineage's progenitors and may encode primed states prior to computing distance covariance entropy.

name: differential-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when you have one scRNA-seq plus one scATAC-seq sample from each of two conditions (e.g., a CLL donor vs a healthy control, as log2-transformed O/E matrices with cluster indices) and need subpopulation-specific differential regulatory networks and hub TF rankings.

name: differential-state-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and condition labels (e.g., immunotherapy responder status per patient) must be screened for which annotated cell type shows the largest transcriptomic shift between conditions, accounting for patient/replicate structure.

name: differential-state-gene-spiking
description: Use when building synthetic two-condition, multi-batch single-cell benchmark datasets that require a known set of DS genes with controlled log fold-change and proportion, e.g. to evaluate integration or DS-detection pipelines.

name: differential-state-ground-truth-design
description: Use when benchmarking DS analysis methods on multi-sample, multi-group scRNA-seq data and reproducible ground truth (which genes are DS, at what logFC) must be generated by simulation anchored to a real reference.

name: differential-tad-region-enrichment
description: Use when validating scHi-C DCI calls (e.g. from scHiCDiff.ZINB) against orthogonal bulk Hi-C DCI sets and differential topologically associating domain (TAD) regions to assess biological support of single-cell detections.

name: differential-te-expression-across-cardiac-lineage-branches
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq BAMs from a branching differentiation system need TE-level quantification and comparison of TE expression between annotated cell-fate branches (e.g., contracting vs non-contractile cardiomyocyte lineages).

name: differential-te-expression-testing-between-cell-types
description: Use when single-cell BAM/SAM files from distinct cell types (e.g. ESCs and MEFs) need per-cell TE counts from scTE and a list of cell-type-specific differentially expressed TEs.

name: differential-te-locus-expression-analysis
description: Use when single-cell full-length scRNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-Seq2 glioblastoma BAMs) require locus-level TE quantification and downstream clustering/marker testing that subfamily-level TE counts cannot resolve.

name: differential-topic-abundance-testing
description: Use when AnnData outputs from a trained scETM model (normalized cell topic mixtures in obsm['theta'], topic embeddings in uns['alpha']) are available with obs metadata labeling disease condition and cell type, and you need to identify which learned topics are differentially enriched between groups.

name: differential-topology-testing
description: Use when you have pseudotime trajectories inferred from multiple samples (e.g., 8 HCA-BM donors) and want to know whether covariates change which trajectory branches exist, with uncertainty-aware, sample-level statistical inference.

name: differential-topology-testing
description: Use when comparing single-cell dynamic processes across conditions and you must first decide whether conditions share a common trajectory topology before testing differential progression, fate selection, or gene expression.

name: differential-topology-testing-sc-rna-seq
description: Use when you have multi-sample scRNA-seq (e.g., the 8-donor HCA bone marrow dataset with a sex covariate) and need to test whether trajectory tree topology or branch cell proportions change between conditions.

name: differential-transcript-usage-analysis
description: Use when you have condition-grouped RNA-seq samples (e.g., 3 control vs 3 LPS-stimulated monocytes from GSE118165) with sample-level IPA usage estimates and need to identify differentially used IPA isoforms between groups.

name: differential-transcription-factor-activity-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq differentiation data (adata with cluster annotations and RNA velocity or differentiation potential) must be analyzed to identify time- and fate-specific transcription factor regulators along stochastic trajectories.

name: differential-transcription-factor-expression-analysis
description: Use when you need candidate regulatory factors for bifurcation/priming analysis from scRNA-Seq: e.g. picking top TFs per lineage (retina: 7 neuronal + 7 epithelial; liver: top-4 hepatocyte + top-4 cholangiocyte) before CompDICE.

name: differential-translation-analysis-negbin-glm
description: Use when the input is a merged ribosome-profiling count matrix (e.g. HTSeq-count output like count_matrix_by_transcript_IDs.csv) plus biological conditions, and the goal is calling up/downregulated features with DESeq2.

name: differential-treatment-effect-z-testing
description: Use when you have patient-level biomarker values (e.g., binarized GEP weights or qPHATE-coordinate thresholds) from a randomized trial with PFS/OS outcomes and two treatment cohorts, and you need to test for a statistically significant differential treatment effect.

name: differential-tree-recursive-partitioning
description: Use when you must identify regulators whose predictive relationship with a target gene differs between two conditions (e.g. disease vs. control) and have two tab-separated expression matrices with matching gene feature sets.

name: differential-utr-length-testing
description: Use when SingleCellExperiment objects from scUTRquant are available and the goal is to call genes with significant 3'UTR length changes (DUL) between two cell types and compare them to DGE gene sets.

name: differential-variance-improvement-tree-splitting
description: Use when two matched gene expression matrices (disease/target and control/baseline, rows = genes, columns = samples, first column 'Gene', tab-separated) are available and the goal is to find condition-specific predictor genes via tree-based differential network inference.

name: differentially-expressed-gene-count-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking whether per-PC mixed-model distances (scDist) outperform nDEG gene counts on sorted immune cell types with deliberately unbalanced cell-type sizes, e.g. after downsampling CD14 monocytes to test dendrogram consistency.

name: differentially-expressed-gene-counting
description: Use when comparing perturbation of multiple extracted subnetworks (e.g., seven CAT modules on COVID-19 GSE172114 RNA-seq) and you need per-subnetwork DEG counts plus path-level ACE statistics to rank which module is most perturbed.

name: differentially-expressed-gene-stratification
description: Use when a differential expression table (FDR-adjusted p < 0.05, |log2 FC| > 1.5) is available and direction-specific pathway enrichment counts are required.

name: differentially-expressed-gene-substitution
description: Use when benchmarking a rare-population detector (e.g., FiRE) on synthetic single-cell data and you need to control the 'difficulty' of detection by varying the number of DE genes distinguishing a ~5% minor subpopulation.

name: differentiation-efficiency-group-contrast-analysis
description: Use when multi-dimensional (subject x time point) community label predictions exist from a MuDCoD fit_predict run on donor networks and the goal is to relate donor-level cross-time module similarity to a donor phenotype such as differentiation efficiency.

name: differentiation-potency-violin-visualization
description: Use when single-cell differentiation datasets (e.g. progenitor vs. mature stages) need a per-cell potency score to orient trajectory direction, and NFE distributions must be compared across stages with non-parametric statistics.

name: differentiation-potential-trajectory-inference
description: Use when RNA velocity profiles are inconclusive or noisy in a single-cell differentiation dataset and prior biological knowledge defines progenitor and terminal cell states (e.g. NKX6-1+ progenitors toward SC-β fates), so trajectories can be biased by a differentiation-potential gradient.

name: differentiation-trajectory-pathway-interpretation
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq or protein expression profiles with prior RaceID2/cluster class labels and need a 2D visualization that exposes differentiation pathways and lineage relations (e.g. stem cell clusters, branch points) beyond what unsupervised t-SNE/PCA/MDS shows.

name: diffusion-distribution-similarity-analysis
description: Use when single-cell data has been converted into per-cell stationary diffusion distributions (RWR matrix S) and a kernel-based, unit-diagonal similarity embedding is needed for pseudotime ordering or 2D/3D visualization.

name: diffusion-embedding-single-cell
description: Use when comparing imputed vs. observed scRNA-seq data for trajectory preservation — e.g., after SERM or MAGIC imputation of zebrafish development or EB differentiation matrices — to check whether the developmental manifold and state transitions survive imputation.

description: Use when a labelled single-cell expression matrix needs a low-dimensional diffusion-based embedding that must preserve chronological stage order (e.g. 1-cell through 64-cell ME stages) or resolve branching intermediates visually.

description: Decision support for benchmarking a trajectory-inference method: when you need to test whether standard dimensionality-reduction embeddings (diffusion map, PCA) recapitulate a known lineage-branching event in progenitor scRNA-seq data.

name: diffusion-map-eigenvector-embedding
description: Use when you need a manifold-aware low-dimensional embedding of single-cell (or other high-dimensional) data, or diffusion coordinates to quantify how well a mapping preserves intrinsic geometry.

name: diffusion-map-eiplgraph-trajectory-inference
description: Use when sample-level distances (e.g., PILOT's Wasserstein matrix over single-cell or pathomics samples) should be ordered into a disease trajectory rather than clustered, e.g., lupus PBMC, kidney IgAN, or myocardial infarction cohorts.

name: diffusion-map-pseudotime-computation
description: Use when static single-cell flow cytometry data (e.g. DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27 stainings) must be ordered along a developmental or spatial trajectory to serve as input to pseudotime-to-real-time transformation.

name: diffusion-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when you have cell-level feature embeddings (e.g., tGPT features in AnnData) plus cell-type labels and need to resolve developmental branches or lineage order from the representation space.
