name: dilution-series-simulation-design
description: Use when quantifying detection sensitivity of a mutational signature fitting algorithm (e.g. mmsig) for low-abundance signatures, by generating simulated mutation catalogs with known ground-truth signature admixtures.

name: dimension-reduction-method-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating which dimension reduction method separates subpopulations of cells within the final time point of temporal single-cell expression datasets, especially for trajectory-visualization benchmarking.

name: dimension-reduction-visualization
description: Use when input is a single-cell or cohort expression matrix (e.g., scRNA-seq with noise/dropout, or TCGA patient expression) and you need unsupervised clustering plus 2-D visualization without pre-selecting gene subsets.

name: dimension-reduction-visualization-comparison
description: Use when you must benchmark a dimension-reduction method for temporal single-cell data against t-SNE and diffusion map, evaluating how well each 2D embedding separates cells from different lineages across simulated differentiation conditions.

name: dimensionality-reduction-ablation-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell deep clustering pipeline has two modules (a latent embedding and an ensemble/consensus clustering step) and the goal is to test whether each module independently improves clustering on labeled scRNA-seq datasets.

name: dimensionality-reduction-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a deep embedding for scRNA-seq cells must be compared to classical dimensionality-reduction baselines (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, full SCANPY/Seurat pipelines) using ground-truth cell labels and a quantitative embedding-quality metric such as ASW.

name: dimensionality-reduction-baseline-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type resolution of scRNA-seq cell embeddings — comparing Cell BLAST/DIRECTi against DCA, PCA, and tSNE — via mean average precision (MAP) on query-reference pairs.

name: dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing dimensionality reduction methods for scRNA-seq embeddings on sparse or high-CV data, or when evaluating whether automatic PC/signal-dimension selection (e.g., RMT-based) beats fixed-PC baselines.

name: dimensionality-reduction-coordinate-export
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq object (Seurat or AnnData) with 2D/3D DR embeddings (UMAP, tSNE, PHATE, DDRTree) must be converted into CellexalVR-compatible input files for VR visualization.

name: dimensionality-reduction-embedding-scvi-simlr
description: Use when you have simulated or observed scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. SymSim UMI counts with known population labels) and need to compare embedding methods (PCA, scVI, SIMLR) for clustering accuracy or rare-population detection.

name: dimensionality-reduction-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you have multi-sample or multi-condition single-cell count matrices (dgCMatrix) needing an interpretable latent embedding, or when projecting prior-knowledge gene signatures (DoRothEA TF regulons, pathways) onto per-cell activities for visualization.

name: dimensionality-reduction-pca-umap
description: Use when you need to cluster droplets from a snRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., after DIEM/EmptyDrops or quantile filtering) to detect residual background RNA-driven debris clusters via per-cluster median percent spliced reads.

name: dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq object (e.g. SingCellaR Human_HSPC) has clustering and reduced-dimension results ready and you need publication-style 2D plots colored by cluster, gene expression, cell type annotation, or pseudotime.

name: dimensionality-reduction-visualization-of-single-cell-clusters
description: Use when SCASL (or similar splicing-landscape clustering) has produced an imputed AS probability matrix and cluster labels, and you need a 2D embedding to inspect cluster separation, coloring either by SCASL clustering results or user-supplied ground-truth labels.

name: dimensionality-reduction-visualization-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when a normalized, scaled scRNA-seq matrix with detected variable features needs to be compressed for visualization or as input to clustering, and 2D/3D cell projections (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP) must be produced.

name: dimensionality-reduction-with-kmeans-and-ward-agglomeration
description: Use when comparing how well alternative feature spaces (eeSNV vs gene expression) retrieve known cancer cell subpopulations in scRNA-seq data, or when benchmarking clustering pipelines (PCA/FA + K-means, PCA/FA + agglomerative WARD, SIMLR) with AMI.

name: diploid-transcriptome-alignment
description: Use when single-end scRNA-Seq reads from an F1 hybrid (e.g. CAST×B6) must be assigned to parental alleles without discarding multi-mapping reads, as a prerequisite for ASE counting and classification.

name: dipm-decision-tree-fitting
description: Use when a precision-medicine question asks which treatment is optimal for which patient subgroups: e.g., a treatment indicator plus covariates (such as anorexia pre-weight) and a continuous response like post-weight are available.

name: directed-communication-matrix-interpretation
description: Use when you have run MDIC3 (or an equivalent A=RΣW decomposition with a GRN-derived left submatrix R) on scRNA-seq data and must convert the resulting W matrix entries into directed, sender-to-receiver communication strengths between cells or cell types.

name: directed-edge-ranking-by-weight
description: Use when you have a bootstrapped COSLIR coefficient matrix A plus the two consecutive-stage mean vectors mu1 and mu2, and need to rank directed regulator→target edges for early-precision evaluation.

name: directed-gene-network-construction
description: Use when you have a bulk gene expression matrix (RNA-seq or microarray) with matched survival data and cell-type marker genes, and need to construct a directed gene-gene network whose edges encode favorable prognostic associations.

name: directed-graph-convolution-on-gene-regulatory-networks
description: Use when reproducing cancer driver gene identification or ablation studies on a directed GRN (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) with multi-omics features, using the DGMP DGCN+MLP model.

name: directed-graph-convolutional-network-training
description: Use when you need to reproduce or benchmark cancer driver gene identification on a directed GRN with multi-omics gene features, comparing AUPRC/AUROC against EMOGI, NRFD, DeepWalk+SVM, PageRank, HotNet2, or MutSigCV.

name: directed-graph-manipulation-with-igraph
description: Use when the analysis input is a directed reference network (igraph object, e.g. alsData$graph or kegg) plus expression data, and the goal is to weight, filter, or convert that digraph into a DAG or directed tree (arborescence) for SEM fitting or Chu–Liu–Edmonds recovery.

name: directed-graph-quadratic-program-optimization
description: Use when you have a directed weighted TF-target score matrix derived from subpopulation-specific profiles (e.g., DC3-derived HiChIP peak-gene pairs) and need the densely cross-regulating core subnetwork plus upstream/downstream effectors.

name: directed-knn-graph-construction
description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data with scQA and a directed cell-cell graph over the LC2-derived quantitative representation is needed as the substrate for seed generation and label propagation.

name: directed-network-graph-construction
description: Use when an undirected co-expression module (e.g. from WGCNA/BioNERO) must be converted into a directed TF→target regulatory graph whose edges need motif-level validation.

name: directed-network-graph-visualization
description: Use when a TF–gene edge list (tf/gene/weights columns) from scMEGA or similar eGRN inference must be visualized as a directed, weighted network with TF nodes annotated by trajectory position.

name: directed-path-perturbation-fitting
description: Use when a significant causal ACE pair (e.g. after Bonferroni correction at alpha = 0.05) defines a source and sink node in a directed SEMtree subnetwork, and you must recover the connecting directed path and assess which of its nodes/edges are group-perturbed.

name: directed-tree-conversion-causal-additive-trees
description: Use when active subnetworks are returned as undirected graphs by multiple detection methods (e.g., from the Ma et al. 2011 simulation benchmark with 500 genes, 20 samples per condition) and you need directionality to compare them or fit tree-based SEMs.

name: directed-tree-conversion-chu-liu-edmonds
description: Use when subnetworks recovered from seed (disease) genes or gene P-values by different methods are undirected modules and must be expressed as directed trees for a like-for-like comparison of directed active subnetworks (e.g. 21 pairwise Jaccard values across 7 methods).

name: directi-reference-model-training
description: Use when a raw or subsampled scRNA-seq reference dataset (AnnData/h5ad, or legacy h5) must be embedded with DIRECTi before building a Cell BLAST BLAST index for cell querying.

name: directional-concordance-analysis
description: Use when two orthogonal per-cell label assignments (e.g., copy-number-based vs mutation/expression-based) exist for the same cell barcodes and you need to quantify how well one predicts the other, directionally.

name: dirichlet-latent-space-encoding
description: Use when scRNA-seq counts from batched experiments (e.g. NEURIPS bone marrow data) need topic compositions and an unconfounded latent representation that separates technical covariates from biological cell states.

name: dirichlet-multinomial-count-simulation
description: Use when you need controlled simulation benchmarks for multi-individual scRNA-seq clustering: you must vary individual-level heterogeneity and donor count to test whether a method (e.g., BAMM-SC vs SIMLR/SC3/DIMM-SC) benefits from more individuals.

name: dirichlet-multinomial-map-estimation
description: Use when converting per-sample cell-cluster count vectors from single-cell AnnData into probability distributions over clusters as input to optimal transport, especially when some samples lack counts for certain clusters and zero probabilities would break downstream distance computations.

name: dirichlet-multinomial-mixture-modeling
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., 10x Chromium droplet scRNA-seq) must be jointly clustered without prior batch correction, and posterior per-cell clustering uncertainty is needed.

name: disconnected-and-cyclic-trajectory-inference
description: Use when single-cell data is expected to contain disconnected populations, cyclic/circular processes, or converging multifurcations that tree-only trajectory inference methods would merge or break.

name: discordant-read-pair-uniform-likelihood-modeling
description: Use when reconstructing ecDNA breakpoints from ATAC-Seq data where junction evidence consists of discordant read pairs with anomalous orientation/insert size and soft-clipped or supplementary-aligned read piles, and realignment is too costly.

name: discordant-sample-characterization
description: Use when scATOMIC malignant/non-malignant calls for external tumour biopsies must be cross-checked against CopyKAT aneuploid/diploid ploidy status and discordant biopsies need causal characterization.

name: discrete-selector-layer-implementation
description: Use when building or re-implementing a neural gene/marker selector on scRNA-seq data (e.g. CITE-seq .h5ad) where selecting a discrete subset of k genes must remain differentiable for joint gradient-based optimization with a VAE-style reconstruction or classification objective.

name: discriminant-analysis-cell-classification
description: Use when a target scRNA-seq dataset lacks cell-type labels while a reference dataset with known clusters exists, especially when the two differ in protocol, batch effect, cell number, or library depth (e.g., Smart-Seq2 reference mapped to CEL-Seq1/CEL-Seq2 targets).

name: discriminative-index-gene-ranking
description: Use when you need to prioritize genes from high-dimensional RNA-seq data (e.g. TCGA pan-cancer, 20,501 genes) by classification power rather than differential-expression p-values, to build a compact biomarker panel.

name: discriminative-index-score-computation
description: Use when ranking genes from high-dimensional labeled RNA-seq/expression matrices by classification power, as an alternative to DEG analysis (e.g., edgeR) for selecting biomarker candidates.

name: disease-biomarker-identification
description: Use when the input is disease-vs-control scRNA-seq data in .h5ad (anndata) format with a 'disease' target column, and the goal is to rank condition-specific biomarker genes rather than annotate cell types.

name: disease-informative-subpopulation-identification-across-cell-types
description: Use when case-control single-cell RNA-seq data have a healthy control population usable as a reference trajectory, and the goal is to expose disease-related cells and dynamics masked by healthy shared signal.

name: disease-marker-based-aberrant-cell-scoring
description: Use when single-cell data from a diseased tissue (e.g., AML bone marrow) must be screened for aberrant/disease-critical cell populations defined in NCIT, and per-cell disease scores must be compared across conditions such as healthy vs AML or pre- vs post-treatment relapse.

name: disease-scrnaseq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating cell types in a disease scRNA-seq query (e.g., type 2 diabetes, NSCLC, Alzheimer's) against a normal-cell reference where batch/treatment effects make standard label transfer unreliable.

name: disease-specific-dmdt-retrieval
description: Use when a transcript isoform switching event (e.g. an ENST identifier such as HSPH1-002 / ENST00000380405 in Alzheimer's disease) must be queried in CanIsoNet and its disrupted STRING interactions quantified.

name: disease-specific-network-overlay
description: Use when RNA-seq transcriptome data for a disease has yielded isoform switching events / dMDT genes with lost protein domains, and you need to map those domain losses onto a protein interaction network to expose functional disruptions.

name: disease-subnetwork-random-walk-modeling
description: Use when a inferred GRN (e.g., from SCING, GRNBOOST2, ppcor, or PIDC) needs biological validation by testing how well it models disease gene subnetworks from DisGeNET versus degree-preserved random network nulls.

name: disease-vs-control-separation-analysis
description: Use when an imputed or latent scRNA-seq expression matrix from a disease dataset (e.g. the adam h5 file) must be checked for AD-versus-control cell separation and clustering quality (ARI/NMI).

name: disentangled-latent-factor-extraction
description: Use when a multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 6-patient GBM, DMSO vs panobinostat) must be decomposed into shared vs condition-specific latent factors for batch-effect removal or cell-type/batch-mixing evaluation.

name: disentanglement-test-holdout-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking whether a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq model separates cell types while removing batch effect in shared factors, and removes batch effect from condition-specific (unshared-bio) factors.

name: disgenet-disease-gene-set-mapping
description: Use when evaluating whether an inferred single-cell GRN captures disease biology: you have one or more inferred networks and want a quantitative, per-disease-category score of how well the network models disease gene subnetworks versus matched random nulls.

name: distance-correlation-statistics
description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix and a redPATH pseudotime ordering and need to rank/select genes whose expression correlates with the developmental trajectory, such as markers of transitions between cell states.

name: distance-covariance-entropy-computation
description: Use when a multipotent progenitor population (e.g. MPPs, TACs) plus competing downstream lineages are available in log-normalized scRNA-Seq data, and the goal is to quantify priming or locate a bifurcation point by entropy of expression covariation.

name: distance-decay-weighting-of-regulatory-regions
description: Use when region-level TF affinities (TRAP, 818 PFMs from JASPAR 2022 / HOCOMOCO v11 / Kheradpour & Kellis) must be summarised to gene level using a TSS-centred window (default 50 KB gene-window, 5 MB ABC-mode) with activity × exponential distance decay weighting.

name: distance-dependent-variant-gene-linking
description: Use when fine-mapped noncoding GWAS variants (with posterior probabilities) overlap scATAC-seq peaks and you must assign distal regulatory target genes beyond the nearest gene, accounting for distance-dependent effects.

name: distance-function-indicator-sequence-validation
description: Use when validating per-read barcode calls from SPLiT-seq reads after sliding-window index location: each of the three 8-nt indicator barcodes must satisfy Dist < 2 against its whitelist entry, otherwise the Read2 must be abandoned.

name: distance-metric-benchmarking
description: Use when sketching a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x features/PCs) with Sphetcher and you need to decide which distance metric for the sketching objective preserves cluster structure for downstream clustering.

name: distance-metric-parameter-sweep
description: Use when you have hidden-layer embeddings from a trained Keras model (e.g. RFCN on single-cell gene expression) and need to check that two-dimensional UMAP cell-type separation does not depend on the choice of distance metric before reporting the visualization.

name: distance-metric-sweep-analysis
description: Use when building a KNN cell graph from sparse scRNA-seq expression data and you must choose k (e.g., 5–25) and a distance measure (cosine, euclidean, city-block, manhattan, L2) based on clustering ARI/NMI.

name: distance-outlier-filtering-and-averaging
description: Use when scRNA-seq neighbour-distance matrices produce sporadic distance spikes that would dominate ∆∆D statistics, and candidate rare-cluster sizes k must be scored via per-k skewness for GapClust-style rare cell detection.

name: distributed-pipeline-execution-timing
description: Use when measuring how runtime of a distributed single-cell analysis pipeline scales with dataset size (e.g. 2K–10K cell subsamples) under different cluster/memory configurations versus a sequential implementation.

name: distributed-scrnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts arrive as a wide-format .csv too large for in-memory tools (Seurat/Scanpy constrained by RAM) and downstream Spark-based QC, filtering, normalization, PCA or clustering is planned.

name: distributional-similarity-metric-interpretation
description: Use when evaluating GRouNdGAN-simulated single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., 10000 cells from PBMC-All) and you need thresholds for deciding if RF AUROC ~0.5, miLISI ~2, and MMD/Cosine values comparable to the two-halves test-set control indicate realistic generation.

name: distributional-similarity-metrics-computation
description: Use when GRouNdGAN-simulated scRNA-seq cells (e.g., 10,000 generated from a Dahlin, Tumor-All, or Tumor-malignant checkpoint) must be compared against the real reference data on both training and test splits.

name: diverging-and-transition-gene-detection
description: Use when a STREAM elastic principal graph has been fitted to scRNA-seq data (e.g., AnnData expression matrix) and you need to identify which genes diverge at branch points and which transition along branches.

name: divide-and-conquer-metacell-scaling
description: Use when planning metacell construction on large scRNA-seq atlases (hundreds of thousands of cells) and you need to know which method/variant is computationally tractable at a given cell count and graining level.

name: dmap-lineage-label-transfer
description: Use when you need per-cell lineage or cell-type labels from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data without marker genes or supervised training, and a hematopoietic reference profile set (e.g. DMAP) is available for correlation-based matching.

name: dmc-count-validation
description: Use when validating that an Illumina 450K/EPIC differential methylation analysis reproduces a published DMC count, especially counts restricted to promoter-proximal CpG feature groups such as TSS200, TSS1500, and 5'UTR.

name: dmdt-differential-transcript-usage-analysis
description: Use when you have disease and control transcriptome RNA-seq FASTQ data and want to identify isoform switching events and assess whether they disrupt protein interactions pathogenically.

name: dna-methylation-array-data-processing
description: Use when raw Illumina 450K or EPIC methylation array files (IDAT plus sample sheet) need loading, QC, normalization, and differential methylation analysis, or when reproducing a published DMC analysis.

name: dna-methylation-array-downstream-analysis
description: Use when raw or normalized Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array data (e.g., GSE207426) must be analyzed for differentially methylated CpGs, or when reproducing published DMC counts restricted to TSS200/TSS1500 + 5'UTR annotated probes.

name: dna-seq-short-read-alignment-with-bwa
description: Use when raw DNA-seq/WES FASTQ read groups from (sample, seqtype, group) rows of a Snakemake sample sheet must be mapped to a reference genome before SNV/indel calling or neoantigen variant detection.

name: dna-sequence-motif-scoring
description: Use when scoring a DNA sequence against a position weight matrix and the GC content of the input sequence must be accounted for via a background model P(G)=P(C)=GC/2, P(A)=P(T)=(1-GC)/2.

name: dna-storage-encode-decode-pipeline-implementation
description: Use when implementing or verifying a DNA-based storage system pipeline in simulation: you have a digital file to encode into DNA strands, noisy simulated sequencing reads to decode, and need a fault-injection test bed with round-trip validation.

name: dna-storage-fault-injection-simulation
description: Use when you need to evaluate a DNA-based data storage pipeline design (encoder/decoder choice) under controlled error injection — e.g. varying fault rates, error distributions, or pipeline stages like multiple sequence alignment — and collect decode-failure and error-location statistics.

name: dna-storage-pipeline-simulation
description: Use when you need to simulate DNA storage pipelines under fault injection (i.i.d. or nanopore/DNArSim error models) and compare read/write density Pareto fronts across pipeline configurations.

name: dnn-training-resource-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking how much training time, runtime, and memory a cell-type annotation pipeline consumes on large (>1 million cell) scRNA-seq datasets, especially to compare low-resource (CPU-only) tools against GPU-dependent pipelines.

name: docker-containerized-bioinformatics-workflow
description: Use when you need to execute methylR locally on raw Illumina 450K/EPIC methylation array data (IDAT plus sample sheet) via its Docker image, e.g. to reproduce published differential methylation results such as DMC counts on a GEO dataset.

name: docker-containerized-pipeline-execution
description: Reference for executing a Shiny/GUI bioinformatics pipeline locally via its published Docker (or Singularity/Apptainer) image when reproducing authors' analyses or benchmarking runtimes without installing R dependencies.

name: dockerized-genomics-tool-execution
description: Use when you need to execute VIsoQLR on long-read sequencing alignments (BAM/GFF3/BED6) for isoform identification and quantification of a single gene or minigene, and want a reproducible containerized run on any OS including Windows/WSL2.

name: domain-adversarial-discriminator-optimization
description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g. 9-batch pancreas, 10-batch immune) where batch effects must be removed while preserving inherent biological differences across batches, and over-correction by MNN-style methods is a concern.

name: domain-domain-interaction-network-construction
description: Use when linking transcript abundance changes (isoform switching) to protein interaction disruptions: you have dMDT gene lists per disease and want to flag PPI edges that can no longer occur because a Pfam domain is lost in the disease isoform.

name: domain-generalization-model-evaluation
description: Use when validating a pre-trained scRNA-seq cancer classifier against an annotated pan-cancer benchmark (e.g., TISCH tissues) to confirm reported accuracy and per-tissue generalization.

name: domain-generalization-risk-extrapolation-training
description: Use when training a malignant-cell classifier on multi-tissue scRNA-seq data where the model must generalize to unseen tissue domains — i.e., when optimizing the combined variance-plus-average risk objective over tissue domains is needed.

name: dominant-b-cell-clone-identification
description: Use when Trinity-assembled contigs from an RNA-seq sample (e.g. CLL patient BAM aligned to hg38) must be filtered for Ig transcripts and the highest-TPM productive transcript marked as the dominant clone.

name: dominant-cell-type-occupy-rate-quantification
description: Use when auditing whether an iterative cluster decomposition/merging pipeline (e.g., scCAD) increased the purity of rare cell type assignment: you have cell-type annotations plus I-cluster and M-cluster labels and need dominant-type occupy rates per cluster.

name: dominant-gene-ratio-comparison
description: Use when FunHoP node-level pathway analysis has been run on RNA-seq data from two independent patient cohorts (e.g. TCGA and Prensner prostate cancer) and you need to verify that dominant genes and very-high/very-low abundance-ratio genes in multi-gene KEGG nodes reproduce across cohorts.

name: dominant-gene-read-count-verification
description: Use when a pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes and you must determine which enzyme dominates the reaction and whether the aggregated node-level regulation is trustworthy, e.g., after collapsing RNA-seq read counts in FunHoP networks.

name: donor-based-holdout-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cell type classifiers on scRNA-seq data where generalization to unseen donors must be quantified and donor-level label leakage between train and test sets must be prevented.

name: donor-difference-data-augmentation-ablation
description: Use when evaluating whether data augmentation improves generalization of a tabular single-cell cell type classifier to unseen donors, or when reproducing the scTab augmentation ablation (test loss 0.797→0.659, macro F1 0.7755→0.7841).

name: donor-holdout-generalization-testing
description: Use when a cell type annotation model trained on CELLxGENE census data must be tested for generalization to held-out donors, or when comparing performance across label granularity or sequencing protocols.

name: donor-level-cell-fraction-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-cell cell type/state labels plus per-donor metadata (donor id, sex, depot, lean/obese status) and need to test how tissue cellular composition differs between donor groups while controlling for covariates such as depot and sex.

name: dose-escalation-counts-matrix-aggregation
description: Use when you have a raw bulk barcode counts table (e.g. from GEO GSE246611) and need to replicate the dose-escalation QC pipeline that removes low-quality samples and low-abundance barcodes before downstream bartools analysis.

name: dose-escalation-decision-rule-simulation
description: Use when evaluating or reproducing the operating characteristics (e.g., early-termination probability, P1/P2 dose-selection percentages) of the TSNP phase I/II dose-escalation design under a specified toxicity/efficacy scenario.

name: dose-toxicity-order-constraint-estimation
description: Use when per-dose DLT proportions from a dose-escalation trial violate the monotone increasing toxicity constraint and monotone (isotonic) toxicity estimates are needed for dose-escalation/de-escalation decisions.

name: dot-plot-and-pie-chart-visualization
description: Use when int-pair/cluster-pair couplets from a multi-condition CCI comparison (e.g., critical vs non-critical COVID-19 CellChat output subset to a ligand subfamily in InterCellar's gene-verse) must be visualized as per-cluster dot plots and per-condition proportion pie charts.

name: dot-plot-visualization-of-annotation-results
description: Use when EasyCellType has produced annotation test results (from easyct with test='GSEA' or Fisher) and you need a dot plot plus top-five candidate cell-type rankings per cluster to judge annotation quality.

name: double-centering-of-distance-matrices
description: Use when quantifying priming or bifurcation dynamics in a multipotent scRNA-Seq population (e.g. Ranzoni MPP cells) by measuring entropy of covariation among candidate regulatory factors via the DICE framework.

name: doublet-detection-and-removal
description: Use when raw spliced/unspliced gene-by-cell count matrices from the scKB pipeline are being quality-filtered with COPILOT and doublets must be detected and removed (remove.doublet=TRUE) before downstream Seurat analysis.

name: doublet-detection-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need to compare doublet detectors on datasets with experimental doublet annotations (e.g., cell-hashed DM-A/DM-B/DM-C, HTO12/HTO8, multiplexed DM-2.1/DM-2.2), or when choosing between detectors where spurious trajectory branches matter.

name: doublet-detection-ensemble-classification
description: Use when processing droplet-based scRNA-seq count data (Seurat object or SingleCellExperiment) where doublets are a suspected technical artefact and a stable doublet set is needed before downstream clustering or DEG analysis.

name: doublet-rate-estimation-and-removal
description: Use when preprocessing raw scRNA-seq data with scKB/COPILOT and quality-filtered gene-by-cell matrices must be purged of doublets without manually specifying a doublet rate.

name: doublet-rate-estimation-per-cell-count
description: Use when running Chord (or any simulated-doublet method) on droplet scRNA-seq data without experimental doublet labels (no demuxlet/cell hashing) and you must supply an expected doubletrate before calling doublets.

name: doublet-removal-effect-on-trajectory-branching-comparison
description: Use when you need to benchmark doublet detection methods by their downstream effect on developmental trajectory inference, especially on synthetic data with known doublet labels and a bifurcating trajectory.

name: doublet-score-integration-across-methods
description: Use when a Seurat/SCE dataset has already been run once through chord() and you want to boost the ensemble with additional doublet detectors' per-cell score columns.

name: doublet-score-rank-filtering
description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq dataset has an estimated doublet proportion and doublet scores from one or more tools (Chord, Scrublet, bcds, cxds, doubletCells), and you need to remove doublets by score cutoff and assess the effect on trajectory/branch inference.

name: doublet-simulation-from-pbmc-data
description: Use when constructing controlled doublet-detection benchmarks: you have the 68k PBMC dataset with NK, B and CD14+ monocyte labels and need synthetic doublets at known abundance gradients (e.g. 2 monocytes at 0.08%-5%) to evaluate F1 of rare-cell detectors.

name: doubletfinder-artificial-nearest-neighbor-scoring
description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq Seurat/SingleCellExperiment object needs DoubletFinder pANN doublet scores — either to prefilter likely doublets before Chord simulates its artificial-doublet training set, or as one of three predictors (with cxds and bcds) for the GBM ensemble.

name: doubletrate-estimation-for-droplet-scrnaseq
description: Use when running Chord's chord() call (or simulating artificial doublets generally) on 10X-style droplet scRNA-seq data and an input 'doubletrate' must be supplied before doublet detection can proceed.

name: downsampled-dataset-reproducibility
description: Use when validating that a cluster-significance/merging method retains test performance (AUROC) and acceptable runtime at reduced cell counts, e.g. reproducing Cytocipher's Tabula Sapiens 483152-cell benchmark and its 7385-cell downsample.

name: downsampled-matrix-comparison
description: Use when comparing normalized scRNA-seq matrices across downsampling or imputation conditions and you need a rotation-invariant measure (subspace angle of signal PCs) of whether multivariate structure is preserved.

name: downsampled-scrnaseq-matrix-handling
description: Use when you need to compare zero-preserving imputation methods on scRNA-seq count matrices by quantifying whether imputation improves cell-type separability via out-of-bag classification error.

name: downsampling-based-method-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a tool that downsamples cells per condition (e.g. SCPA's default 500 cells) loses information or gains speed relative to a full-dataset method on million-cell-scale scRNA-seq data with >1000 pathways.

name: downsampling-correlation-analysis
description: Use when validating that a cluster-purity metric or entropy-fit parameter (e.g. S in ROGUE) remains stable under varying cell numbers or sequencing-depth differences (2- to 100-fold) between replicates.

name: downsampling-heuristic-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking runtime scaling of supervised dimensionality reduction (HSS-LDA) vs unsupervised methods across increasing single-cell counts (up to ~50,000-200,000 cells), or when deciding whether to keep the runHSS downsample=TRUE default.

name: downsampling-mse-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a pooling or counting strategy improves single-cell allelic proportion estimates from sparsely sequenced scRNA-Seq data, using down-sampled reads and MSE against full-data estimates as the accuracy metric.

name: dpr-training-cell-selection
description: Use when classifying target scRNA-seq cells against reference clusters with scID and you need to select c+/c- training cells and estimate gene signature weights, especially when data have batch effect.

name: dpt-trajectory-inference-on-simulated-scrnaseq
description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction methods on simulated scRNA-seq lineage data with a known ground-truth cell ordering, and you need pseudotime inferred on each embedding and quantified by Kendall-tau correlation.

name: drake-pipeline-target-execution
description: Use when running or re-running a scdrake single-sample or integration pipeline stage (input QC, integration, clustering, cluster_markers, contrasts) where incremental, reproducible target execution via drake is needed.

name: driver-alteration-pathway-association-testing
description: Use when you have TCGA-style expression, MAF mutation calls, and GISTIC copy-number calls per sample and want to verify that a driver alteration activates its corresponding signaling pathway at the transcriptomic-footprint level.

name: driver-gene-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when one or more predicted driver gene lists (from WMDS.net, unweighted MDS, or degree-only ranking) must be scored against a curated cancer gene benchmark to compare precision/recall trade-offs.

name: driver-gene-frequency-stratification
description: Use when you have per-patient personalized driver gene lists from sample-specific networks (e.g., WMDS.netP on TCGA RNA-seq) and need to tabulate how often each driver gene recurs across patients by cancer type.

name: driver-gene-precision-metric-computation
description: Use when you have driver-gene prediction lists from one or more methods and need to quantify and rank their precision against a curated reference driver set such as the Bailey et al. pan-cancer list or CGC.

name: driver-node-weight-computation
description: Use when you have a differential co-expression network with per-edge differential co-expression P-values p_ij and need node weights for a weighted minimum dominating set formulation of driver-node selection.

name: driver-regulator-module-filtering
description: Use when you have a CEFCON-inferred cell-lineage-specific GRN plus identified driver regulators with influence scores and need their gene modules (out-degree and in-degree types) with per-cell AUCell activity.

name: driver-regulator-ranking
description: Use when a cell-lineage-specific GRN has already been constructed and attention-based gene embeddings are available, and you must produce a ranked driver-regulator list using network control theory (MFVS + MDS candidates scored by influence score).

name: driver-regulator-topk-precision-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a ranked list of predicted driver regulators against ground-truth gene sets (e.g., GO:0045165, GO:0019827, GO:0007492) by computing top-k precision for k=1–20 and comparing multiple methods' precision curves.

name: drop-one-out-cluster-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-patient ASGARD drug scores across annotated cell clusters and want to quantify how sensitive those scores are to each cell type by excluding one cluster at a time.

name: drop-seq-fish-distribution-comparison
description: Use when evaluating an imputation method on Drop-seq data against RNA FISH measurements of the same cell line, using Gini-coefficient correlation across shared genes as the agreement metric.

name: droplet-barcode-quantile-thresholding
description: Use when you need to quantify what fraction of droplets removed by a hard count cutoff (knee/quantile-style) are background versus nuclear droplets — e.g., benchmarking a knee-point cutoff against EmptyDrops or DIEM using percent spliced reads in a raw 10X snRNA-seq matrix.

name: droplet-based-scrna-seq-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when processing raw droplet-prepared 10x Genomics mouse data (e.g. ArrayExpress E-MTAB-6854) into UMI count matrices and defensible cell calls, or when needing to correct for cross-sample barcode swapping on patterned flow-cell instruments such as the HiSeq 4000.

name: droplet-based-scrnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw 10X droplet count matrices (CellRanger raw_feature_bc_matrix or 10X feature-barcode output) show extranuclear RNA contamination (elevated MT%/MALAT1%) or spurious cell types after hard-count-cutoff filtering of snRNA-seq data.

name: droplet-classification-probability-thresholding
description: Use when a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq must be split into cell-free vs cell-containing droplets and ambient RNA causes low-count droplets that simple total-count cutoffs misclassify.

name: droplet-demultiplexing-qc-metrics
description: Use when an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix has been demultiplexed with negative binomial regression mixture models and you need a per-HTO separability/QC metric or want to discard droplets with high assignment error probabilities.

name: droplet-filtering-benchmark-tabulation
description: Use when benchmarking droplet-filtering methods (DIEM, EmptyDrops, hard-count cutoffs) on a raw 10X droplet count matrix and you need to quantify what fraction of removed droplets are background vs. nuclei via percent spliced reads.

name: droplet-quality-metric-visualization
description: Use when quantifying extranuclear RNA contamination per droplet in snRNA-seq, or when a sample-specific midpoint separating nuclear and background droplets must be estimated from a bimodal percent-spliced (or percent-mitochondrial) distribution.

name: droplet-scrna-seq-cell-barcode-extraction
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet count matrices must be reduced to per-sample sets of called cell barcodes (e.g. to test for excess inter-sample barcode sharing on HiSeq 4000 vs HiSeq 2500).

name: droplet-scrnaseq-count-preprocessing-with-xcltk
description: Use when starting from raw 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq BAM/CRAM files of a tumor sample and you need RDR read-depth and BAF allelic AD/DP matrices to run XClone or similar allele-specific CNA inference.

name: dropout-and-distributional-noise-injection
description: Use when benchmarking imputation/denoising methods against known ground truth: you need noisy variants of a simulated true count matrix (1000 genes, 500 cells, six groups) spanning dropout and five noise distributions to compute MSE and ASW recovery.

name: dropout-event-modeling
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) contains excessive false zeros from dropout events and downstream tasks like dimension reduction, clustering, or differential expression analysis are degraded by them.

name: dropout-event-modeling-with-gumbel-distribution
description: Use when input is a noisy single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix with many zero/near-zero values that would mislead PCA or t-SNE, and the goal is dropout-aware low-dimensional embedding or 2D visualization of cell populations.

name: dropout-identification-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g., CPM/TPM/FPKM values) contains zero entries that must be classified as dropout artifacts or true zeros before imputation or downstream clustering.

name: dropout-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when a scRNA-seq matrix with dropout zeros needs imputation quality assessment: compare imputed vs raw clustering (ARI), evaluate robustness across dropout rates, normalization (FPKM, CPM, TPM, RPM), or simulated sparsity (e.g., Splatter negative-binomial, 84-93%).

name: dropout-masking-benchmarking
description: Use when a single-cell AS probability matrix (sites × cells) with NA entries is available and you need to quantitatively validate an imputation strategy (e.g., SCASL's weighted KNN) against held-out ground truth under graded dropout levels.

name: dropout-noise-robustness-assessment
description: Use when evaluating how a tumor/normal cell classifier degrades under increasing dropout noise in scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth labels, or when reproducing F1 benchmarks like SCEVAN's 0.948/0.943/0.909/0.824 vs CopyKAT's 0.798/0.792/0.763/0.726.

name: dropout-noise-simulation
description: Use when you need ground-truth scRNA-Seq data with known DE genes to quantify how much dropout degrades differential expression (e.g. median t-statistic collapse) and how well imputation methods such as AutoClass, SAVER, scImpute, or DCA recover it.

name: dropout-non-detection-probability-estimation
description: Use when computing gene-gene co-expression correlations from sparse, zero-inflated single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. ~70% zeros) where naive Pearson/Spearman correlations are distorted by dropout zeros.

name: dropout-parameter-sweep-design
description: Use when you must quantify how robust a cell-type annotation method is to dropout by sweeping Splatter's dropout.shape/dropout.mid parameters over simulated datasets with known ground-truth labels.

name: dropout-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when simulating CRISPR lineage barcodes (e.g., TedSim SimulateCIFs) and you need to measure how dropout events degrade barcode quality — via Qr/Qh — or how they change relative performance of reconstruction methods like LinRace, DCLEAR, or Cassiopeia.

name: dropout-perturbation-benchmarking
description: Use when you must test whether a denoising method preserves or recovers biological structure (celltypes) in scRNA-seq data corrupted by dropout, using simulated ground truth rather than real data.

name: dropout-recovery-assessment
description: Use when you have imputed single-cell expression matrices (hd5, log10(count+1) scale) plus a ground truth, and need to verify that dropout imputation recovers nonlinear gene-gene patterns rather than blurring them.

name: dropout-robust-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq matrix shows high noise/dropout and you need to identify the genes that explain differences across inferred sample populations, downstream of SIMLR similarity learning.

name: dropout-robust-graph-diffusion
description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain high noise and dropout events that weaken cell-to-cell similarity measures, and an unsupervised distance metric is needed for clustering heterogeneous populations (e.g., PBMC subpopulations).

name: dropout-robustness-benchmarking
description: Use when stress-testing a cross-omics integration/label-transfer method against simulated dropout noise in scRNA-seq data, or when reporting stability of scBridge under count down-sampling regimes.

name: dropout-robustness-evaluation-across-simulated-scenarios
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering/dimensionality-reduction method's robustness to dropout (zero-inflation) must be quantified, i.e. simulated count matrices at multiple dropout rates with ground-truth cell labels are available and NMI versus true labels is the target metric.

name: dropout-tolerant-consensus-landmark-computation
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data are sparse with high dropout rates and a robust binary low-dimensional cell representation is needed before clustering, e.g. SMARTer or CEL-Seq2 data such as Xin GSE81608.

name: dropout-zero-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking network inference methods on synthetic scRNA-seq data where excess zero counts (dropout) must be introduced at controlled rates, or when ground-truth power-law/hub network topologies are needed for AUPRC/AUROC evaluation.

name: dropout-zero-inflation-simulation
description: Use when building a benchmark simulation for confounder-removal or normalization methods in scRNA-seq: you need count matrices with known latent factors, a group signature of 200 DE genes, and controlled zero inflation via dropout.

name: dropout-zero-rate-estimation-scrna-seq
description: Use when validating that a Bayesian scRNA-seq model's dropout (zero-inflation) component captures observed zero-count rates, or when quantifying how much model misfit a negative-binomial-only model incurs under non-UMI protocols.

name: dropout-zero-recovery-quantification
description: Use when a simulated scRNA-Seq dataset was generated by applying dropout noise to a known true count matrix (e.g., a Splatter simulation) and you need a scalar measure of imputation recovery at dropout positions.

name: drosophila-embryo-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when analyzing Drosophila embryo scRNA-seq (Synapse syn15665609) with a SpaOTsc-derived cell–cell distance matrix and the goal is to infer which gene in one cell regulates a gene in a neighbor cell across spatial distances.

name: drosophila-embryo-spatial-coordinate-processing
description: Use when mapping scRNA-seq cells to spatial positions of the Drosophila embryo (bdtnp.txt, geometry.txt, dge_normalized.txt) and you need the dissimilarity/distance matrices for an unbalanced structured optimal transport plan.

name: drug-combination-coverage-computation
description: Use when computing percent cell-line coverage of proteasome-inhibitor backbone + secondary drug (secDrug) combinations over GDSC1000-derived resistant B-cell cancer cell lines to rank combination candidates.

name: drug-combination-prioritization-scoring
description: Use when you have predicted essential single genes and gene pairs (e.g. from in silico knockout of context-specific metabolic models) and need to convert them into candidate single drugs and drug combinations from an approved-drug database like DrugBank V5.

name: drug-efficacy-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-compound reversal scores (e.g., RS_GSFM) for LINCS drug perturbations and independent efficacy measurements (IC50 from ChEMBL) and need to test score–efficacy agreement per cell line.

name: drug-perturbation-response-analysis
description: Use when analyzing single-cell transcriptomic data from drug-treated cancer cell lines (e.g., MIX-Seq with multiple drugs and a DMSO control) and you need interpretable pathway-level response readouts rather than generic latent embeddings.

name: drug-repositioning-candidate-curation
description: Use when a set of essential single genes and gene pairs from FBA knockout analysis (e.g. reducing viral biomass without affecting host biomass) must be converted into druggable candidates and curated drug combinations.

name: drug-repurposing-pipeline-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing drug-repurposing pipelines on scRNA-seq case-control data (e.g. GSE123926/GSE113197 breast epithelial, GSE132509 Pre-T ALL, GSE145926/GSE158055 COVID-19 BALF) to assess whether a multi-cluster drug score beats cluster-level signature ranking.

name: drug-response-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset captures a time-course or drug-treatment progression and you have predicted per-cell response probabilities in adata.obs that you want to validate against trajectory inference (pseudotime).

name: drug-response-gene-signature-analysis
description: Use when comparing which genes a bulk-trained drug response model versus its single-cell transferred counterpart identify as IG-contributing, to test consistency of learned signatures across bulk and scRNA-seq levels.

name: drug-response-ic50-analysis
description: Use when CMS labels from CMScaller for pre-clinical models must be linked to drug response (e.g. 5-FU IC50) to test whether subtypes predict chemotherapy sensitivity in MSS CRC cell lines.

name: drug-response-prediction-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) and need clusterwise drug sensitivity predictions — e.g., IC50 from GDSC or AUC from PRISM — to rank drug candidates against tumor subpopulations.

name: drug-response-transfer-learning
description: Use when you must predict single-cell drug sensitivity/resistance labels and signature genes for a drug-treated scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Cisplatin GSE117872, Gefitinib GSE112274, I-BET-762 GSE110894) using bulk cell-line training data.

name: drug-sensitivity-anova-modeling
description: Use when you have matched drug-sensitivity measurements (e.g., IC50 values from GDSC) and gene-expression-derived pathway scores for the same cell lines and want to test which pathways explain drug response.

name: drug-sensitivity-fold-change-analysis
description: Use when GDSC drug sensitivity IC50 values, cell-line mutation calls, and a cell-line expression compendium are available and the goal is to test whether pathway activity scores refine drug-sensitivity stratification beyond driver mutation status alone.

name: drug-sensitivity-pharmacogenomics
description: Use when testing whether a gene-expression signature (e.g., TMG/NMG aggregate scores) is associated with drug response (IC50) across a cell-line panel, requiring per-compound Spearman correlations with FDR control.

name: drug-signature-reversal-repurposing
description: Use when you have case-vs-control scRNA-seq clusters with differential expression profiles and want FDA-approved drug candidates that reverse disease signatures across multiple cell populations, e.g. TNBC, leukemia, or COVID-19 BALF data.

name: drug-target-actionability-annotation
description: Use when you have a candidate gene list from a network or biomarker pipeline and need to flag which genes are targets of pharmacologically active drugs (DrugBank) and which lack prior literature links to a disease.

name: drug-target-annotation-mapping
description: Use when applying scRank to a drug perturbation analysis and only a drug name (not a target gene) is available, or when deciding between antagonist (inhibitor) and agonist MOA settings for CreateScRank.

name: drug-target-gene-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive vs drug-resistant myeloma samples (e.g., U266P vs U266VR) must be screened to rank combination candidates by subclonal enrichment of specific drug-target genes.

name: drug-target-gene-module-visualization
description: Use when scRank has ranked cell types for a drug target (e.g., Smo for vismodegib, SLC6A4 for fluoxetine) and you need to see which perturbed gene modules — especially the target-containing module — differ between top- and bottom-ranked cell types.

name: drug-target-gene-ranking-and-downregulation-validation
description: Use when a drug's direct target is known (or a drug-responsive cell type has been ranked) and you must prioritize additional candidate target genes from the cell-type-specific GRN and confirm them against treated-vs-untreated expression data.

name: drug-target-interaction-database-mapping
description: Use when a gene co-expression or regulatory network module has driver/hub genes and you need to retrieve known or experimental drugs targeting them for mechanistic drug repurposing.

name: drug-wise-spearman-correlation-filtering
description: Use when evaluating CaDRReS-Sc drug response predictions trained on GDSC/PRISM cell line data and you need to remove poorly predicted drugs (bottom-quartile drug-wise Spearman correlation) before reporting results.

name: drugbank-target-interaction-mapping
description: Use when you have a list of disease-specific essential genes/gene pairs from constraint-based knockout analysis and want to identify approved drugs or drug pairs targeting them via DrugBank.

name: dsrna-positive-training-set-construction
description: Use when building a labeled positive training set of endogenous dsRNA regions from A-to-I RNA editing site annotations, and when structural curation via RNAfold secondary-structure filters is needed before model training.

name: dsrna-region-feature-classification
description: Use when you have PacBio long-read RNA-seq (BAM) derived feature tables of candidate dsRNA regions and need to train/validate a classifier, or reproduce reported performance (89% 20-fold CV accuracy) and feature importances (Skip_ratio 75.4%, Len_skip 15.9%).

name: dsrna-region-threshold-filtering
description: Use when you need to predict dsRNA regions in silico from PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM files genome-wide, and classify predicted windows into candidate dsRNAs, novel long dsRNAs, and structured RNAs.

name: dual-branch-cnn-architecture-implementation
description: Use when reproducing or porting the MU-PseUDeep pseudouridine-site classifier: input is paired 51×4 sequence and 51×6 RNAshapes structure one-of-K matrices that must be encoded by separate Conv1D branches and fused in Keras.

name: dual-genome-transcriptome-riboseq-alignment
description: Use when processing Ribo-seq FastQ data that has already passed QC and contaminant removal and must be mapped to a reference genome and transcriptome before CDS-level read counting and differential expression.

name: dual-reference-viral-read-counting
description: Use when you have 10x cellranger output from infected-cell scRNA-seq and need per-cell pathogen read/UMI counts integrated into filtered_feature_bc_matrix, or when validating an alignment strategy against a combined host+pathogen cellranger reference.

name: dual-route-consensus-transcript-filtering
description: Use when assembling a de novo transcript set from RNA-Seq (e.g. 180 TARGET OS tumor samples plus 9 normal bone controls) and you need a high-confidence novel candidate set prior to lncRNA/mRNA classification with LncDC.

name: dual-tool-circrna-call-concordance-analysis
description: Use when public shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq datasets (e.g., GEO/ENCODE FASTQ) are available for candidate RBPs and you must decide which regulators affect global circRNA expression via mCRI change and dual-tool (CIRI2 + find_circ) concordance.

name: dual-virus-read-differentiation-within-sample
description: Use when a 10x scRNAseq sample may harbor a co-infection and you need to detect, differentiate, and quantify reads for more than one pathogen genome within the same cellranger-processed output.

name: dubious-cell-embedding-detection
description: Use when visualizing single-cell RNA-seq data with t-SNE or UMAP in Seurat and you need to quantify which cell embeddings are dubious vs trustworthy, or to optimize perplexity/min.dist/n_neighbors.

name: dubious-embedding-reliability-scoring
description: Use when a Seurat-processed scRNA-seq dataset has 2D t-SNE or UMAP embeddings and you need to detect which cell embeddings are unreliable or choose embedding hyperparameters (perplexity, min.dist, n_neighbors) that minimize dubious cells.

name: duckdb-in-process-database-access
description: Use when single-cell data stored as AnnData layers must be filtered or aggregated with SQL through an in-process or on-disk DuckDB database (.asql), with results returned as pandas DataFrames, AnnData objects, or Parquet files.

name: duckdb-relational-schema-design
description: Use when converting an AnnData (.h5ad) single-cell object into an on-disk relational DuckDB database and you need the layer-to-table mapping, key columns, and naming conventions for each AnnData slot.

name: duplicate-hybrid-record-removal
description: Use when a .hyb file (optionally with an associated vienna/CT fold file) contains repeated hybrid records and you need a deduplicated subset before type/miRNA, target, or fold analysis.

name: duplicate-probe-gene-mapping-across-modules
description: Use when annotating a gene expression matrix with BloodGen3 module membership and some probes/genes map to multiple modules, and a sanctioned duplicate-handling strategy must be chosen before running Groupcomparison.

name: duplicate-read-marking
description: Use when SAM/BAM files from RNA-seq alignment (e.g. STAR two-pass output) feed into GATK HaplotypeCaller variant calling and duplicates must be flagged before Base Recalibration and calling.

name: dv-threshold-bin-prioritization
description: Use when implementing or reproducing scValue's step-3 cell selection (FB/MTB binning) from per-cell DV scores in adata.obs['dv'] or dv_values.csv, given a per-type sketch quota S_m.

name: dynamic-expression-cutoff-annotation
description: Use when a reference set of cell-type-specific marker GEPs (e.g., 70 MCA identity GEPs from mca.marker.geps.txt) must directly annotate cells in an independent single-cell dataset without clustering, enabling universal cell-type label transfer.

name: dynamic-feature-module-permutation-testing
description: Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data must be reduced to dynamically covarying gene modules before trajectory inference, and noisy or low-variance lineage-specific features (e.g., transcription factors) would otherwise be missed by HVG or variance-based selection.

name: dynamic-network-community-detection
description: Use when you have personalized adjacency matrices for multiple subjects over multiple time points (e.g., S x T x n x n numpy array of gene co-expression or similarity networks) and need time-varying, subject-specific community assignments.

name: dynamic-programming-arm-level-phasing
description: Reference for reconstructing XClone's BAF phasing hierarchy when a workflow must collapse gene-bin-level B-allele counts to chromosome-arm mega-features before beta-binomial CNA-state calling.

name: dynamic-time-warping-gene-kinetics-alignment
description: Use when two single-cell pseudotime trajectories (typically already tree-aligned with CAPITAL) need marker-gene expression trends compared along pseudotime, e.g. matching erythrocyte, megakaryocyte, pre-B-cell, or dendritic-cell lineage kinetics between Setty et al. and Velten et al.

name: dynamic-time-warping-trajectory-alignment
description: Use when an ensemble of simulated cell state transitions (e.g. from Cytopath Markov sampling) must be converted into per-terminal-region consensus trajectories, or when simulations of unequal length need temporal alignment before averaging.

name: dynamic-tree-cut-module-detection
description: Use when you have a gene-by-sample RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., the 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex and hippocampus bulk RNA-seq dataset) and need to detect clusters of highly correlated genes that can be related to sample traits such as age, genotype, tissue, and sex.

name: dynamics-preserving-cell-aggregation
description: Use when running MuTrans dynamical_analysis on large datasets (e.g., 10x Chromium human bone-marrow hematopoiesis with tens of thousands of cells) where full cell-cell rwTPM computation is too slow, and approximate transition probabilities are acceptable.

name: dyngen-ground-truth-network-comparison
description: Use when a quantitative CSNI benchmark with complete cellwise ground-truth networks is needed and real single-cell data cannot provide that ground truth — i.e. comparing network inference methods on dyngen-simulated transcriptomics.

name: dyngen-synthetic-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing velocity estimation methods on synthetic data with known ground-truth velocities and diverse developmental topologies (linear, bifurcation, trifurcation, binary tree), e.g. validating a deep-learning velocity method against linear baselines.

name: dyngen-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic dyngen-simulated trajectory datasets with known ground-truth condition differences to benchmark differential progression, fate selection, or differential abundance methods against simulated reality.

name: dynverse-trajectory-scoring
description: Use when inferred trajectories (e.g. from Totem, Slingshot, or TinGa) must be scored against dynverse gold-standard trajectories with known milestone/branch structure, as in the 216 tree-shaped dynverse benchmark or the 10 dynverse Zenodo datasets (doi:10.5281/zenodo.1443566).

name: e-score-uncertainty-measurement
description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a source-free transfer learning model and you need per-cell uncertainty scores to drive downstream novel cell-type detection (bimodality testing) and known/unknown partitioning.

name: e-test-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when building a supervised single-cell classifier from labeled scRNA-seq data and you need a small, cell-type-discriminative gene set before fitting the multinomial model.

name: ead-biomarker-validation-in-independent-cohorts
description: Use when a cell-type-based biomarker or immune niche identified in a discovery scRNA-seq cohort (e.g., EAD vs non-EAD liver transplant samples) must be verified for association with a clinical outcome in an independent cohort.

name: ead-group-statistical-comparison
description: Use when validating a single-cell-defined cell-population signature in an independent bulk RNA-seq cohort with a binary phenotype group (e.g., EAD vs non-EAD), requiring per-sample scoring and group-comparison statistics.

name: ead-vs-nonead-group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when per-sample scalar summaries (cell-type percentages, niche scores, LR-pair counts or scores) must be compared between non-EAD and EAD patient groups within a transplantation stage, mirroring the paper's one-sided Welch's test design.

name: early-precision-curve-evaluation
description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods on time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell data where a reference regulatory network (e.g. BEELINE hESC/mESC ground truth) exists and performance at the top of the ranked edge list matters more than full-network accuracy.

name: early-precision-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods that each output a ranked edge list over the same gene set and a gold-standard regulatory network is available to compute average precision and early precision for benchmarking.

name: earth-mover-distance-solving-single-cell-samples
description: Use when each sample is represented as a vector of cell-cluster (or tissue-structure) proportions and you need a pairwise, unsupervised sample-level distance matrix (e.g. for downstream Leiden clustering or diffusion-map trajectories).

name: ecclip-alignment-signal-extraction
description: Use when starting from eCLIP/STAMP IP and size-matched input BAM files and you need per-nucleotide transcript-level diagnostic signals (read coverage or CIT/CIM summation) before metagene averaging.

name: ecdf-log2fc-distribution-comparison
description: Use when you have DESeq2 differential expression results from an siRNA perturbation and want to test whether transcripts carrying seed matches (e.g. mer7m8/mer8) show a cumulative log2FC shift versus background.

name: ecdna-breakpoint-concordance-comparison
description: Use when circlehunter has been run on ATAC-Seq samples (e.g. GBM39, PC3, COLO320DM) with known WGS- and FISH-validated ecDNA, and you must verify that predicted ligation relationships and breakpoints match the reference structures.

name: ecdna-breakpoint-posterior-inference
description: Use when ATAC-Seq reads already support a candidate ecDNA junction (discordant pairs with anomalous orientation/insert size plus soft-clipped/supplementary-aligned pileups) and you need an exact breakpoint MAP estimate with a 95% CI, without full read realignment.

name: ecdna-detection-from-atacseq
description: Use when ATAC-Seq libraries from tumor/cancer samples must be scanned for ecDNA (focal circular amplifications, often >1 Mb carrying oncogenes like MYC, MYCN, EGFR) without WGS, or when comparing ecDNA callers like circlehunter vs Circle_finder.

name: ecdna-gene-annotation
description: Use when you have ecDNA interval calls (e.g., circlehunter Snakemake output) over tumor ATAC-Seq samples and need to count amplified genes, flag known oncogenes, and test their functional enrichment.

name: ecdna-genome-segment-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking ecDNA-calling tools on ATAC-Seq data and you need simulated ground-truth ecDNA amplicons spanning controlled local depths (e.g. 10×–30×+) and read lengths (e.g. 35–150 bp).

name: ecdna-size-chromosome-distribution-profiling
description: Use when you have per-sample ecDNA calls from tumor ATAC-Seq (e.g., circlehunter predictions over hundreds of GEO samples) and need cohort-level counts, ecDNA-positive sample percentages, and size/chromosome/segment distributions.

name: eclip-peak-filtering
description: Use when testing whether sQTLs alter RNA-binding protein binding sites: you have ENCODE eCLIP peak calls, a sQTL catalog (e.g. sQTLseekeR2/GTEx), and need per-RBP SVM classifiers to score allelic binding impact.

name: eclip-signal-metagene-visualization
description: Use when you have eCLIP IP and size-matched input bigWig/bedGraph signal tracks from ENCODE plus GENCODE annotations and need a metagene density summary over transcript features to infer RBP binding localization.

name: ecoomicsdb-subgroup-database-selection
description: Use when quantifying raw RNA-seq reads from a non-model eukaryotic species into KO-level counts and you must pick which of EcoOmicsDB's 29 NCBI-taxonomy-based taxonomic sub-group databases to align against.

name: edge-level-network-score-computation
description: Use when analyzing a DifferentialConnectome output (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control ifnb PBMCs) and you need a sign-independent per-edge magnitude of perturbation for ranking, filtering, or heatmap/circos visualization of differential ligand–receptor signaling.

name: edge-specificity-weight-ranking
description: Use when you have NATMI ExtractEdges output carrying both mean-expression and specificity weight columns and need to assess whether ranking metric choice alters the top-ranked ligand–receptor pairs per cell-type pair.

name: edge-weight-linear-combination-modeling
description: Use when clustering barcoded single-cell data where a hybrid graph must weight both transcriptome nearest-neighbor similarity and shared clone-barcode relationships with a continuous α parameter.

name: edger-deseq2-dispersion-estimation
description: Use when a dyngen simulation must be shown to match a real single-cell RNA-seq reference dataset (e.g. the zenodo_1443566 bone-marrow mesenchyme MCA counts) in library size, fraction of zeros, and dispersion characteristics.

name: edger-limma-deseq2-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing between edgeR, limma and DESeq2 for RNA-seq differential analysis and computational run time matters, or when reproducing the ARMT Fig. 1B speed comparison on a shared counts matrix.

name: edger-negative-binomial-glm-testing
description: Use when per-cell-type case-vs-control DE gene lists are needed as ASGARD GetDrug inputs and edgeR should be compared against Limma, Seurat, and DESeq2 modes on the same integrated Seurat object.

name: editing-enriched-region-merging
description: Use when A-to-I RNA editing site annotations (e.g., REDIportal) must be converted into candidate dsRNA training regions via windowed enrichment detection, spatial merging, and RNAfold secondary-structure filtering.

name: edlib-edit-distance-flank-search
description: Use when reads (FASTQ/FASTA) must be demultiplexed against a barcode whitelist by error-tolerant sequence matching, or when reproducing Flexiplex's flank-search/Levenshtein-match/chimeric-split logic on simulated long-read data such as the Ebrahimi et al. 2022 reads.

name: eesnv-feature-transformation
description: Use when you have paired per-cell SNV (n_cells x n_SNVs binary) and gene expression (n_cells x n_Genes) matrices from scRNA-seq and need filtered, effective SNV features instead of noisy gene expression for subpopulation analysis.

name: effect-size-confidence-interval-reporting
description: Use when per-trait fgwas annotation model fits have been obtained and you must report the annotation effect sizes (with 95% CIs) to test whether sQTLs show stronger GWAS association than expression-only variants.

name: effective-text-ratio-estimation
description: Use when computing or validating effective text ratios r(k) for a binned nucleotide sequence collection (e.g., Raptor's artificial dataset with 64 or 1,024 bins) across k-mer sizes k=12..20 using Raptor's minimizer approach.

name: egfr-clinical-association-testing
description: Use when a sample-level trajectory or progression score (e.g., PILOT EIPLGraph ranking of pathomics samples) must be shown to predict a clinical outcome such as kidney failure or eGFR category, and benchmarked against a multivariate baseline.

name: egfr-pathway-connectivity-analysis
description: Use when bulk or single-sample RNA-seq data (e.g., TCGA-LUAD tumor and adjacent-normal samples) must be converted into per-sample gene-gene association networks so that pathway-level connectivity (e.g., EGFR pathway, EGF/EGFR degrees) can be compared sample-by-sample.

name: eigen-peak-index-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when running MuTrans and the number of attractors (K_cluster) is unknown: compute the EPI spectrum on the Gaussian-kernel cell-cell rwTPM and pick K at the clearest eigen-gap before DynamicalAnalysis.

name: eigengap-cluster-number-estimation
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with scCAN (or a similar spectral/network-fusion pipeline) and the true number of cell types is unknown, so k must be estimated from the fused similarity network before spectral clustering.

name: eigengap-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when running MuDCoD community detection on multi-subject dynamic networks (S subjects x T time points adjacency tensors) and the number of communities per subject/time must be chosen without a known ground-truth label count.

name: eigengap-heuristic-cluster-number-estimation
description: Use when a learned cell-to-cell similarity or affinity matrix is available and the number of cell types must be estimated without labels, or when comparing spectral-cluster-number estimates against pre-annotated cluster numbers.

name: eigenvalue-ratio-gene-selection
description: Use when running marker-based decomposition (BisqueRNA::MarkerBasedDecomposition) and you must choose how many/which unique markers per cell type support a rank-1 abundance estimate from bulk expression.

name: eigenvector-component-normality-testing
description: Use when eigenvectors of a single-cell covariance matrix must be classified as informative vs non-informative — e.g. eigenvalues outside the Marchenko-Pastur bulk whose components still look Gaussian and may be sparsity-driven artifacts.

name: eigenvector-correlation-robustness-scoring
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data have passed RMT-based noise filtering but a data-driven decision is still needed on which signal eigenvectors are robust versus dropout-driven, prior to dimensionality reduction/embedding.

name: eigenvector-localization-quantification
description: Use when a highly sparse single-cell expression matrix (e.g. ~95% zeros, 6,573 PBMCs x genes) shows localized eigenvectors or an unexpected elbow in a PCA scree plot, and you must decide whether these are sparsity artifacts or biological signal.

name: eigenvector-sign-correlation-check
description: Use when computing a correspondence or geometry-preserving loss over diffusion map eigenvectors, or comparing eigendecompositions of two related Markov transition matrices, where eigenvector sign is arbitrary.

name: eigenvector-smoothing-dynamic-networks
description: Use when you have networks from multiple subjects sampled over multiple time points (e.g., personalized gene co-expression networks from population-scale scRNA-seq) and need community detection that shares signal across subjects and time.

name: eiplgraph-principal-graph-pseudotime-fitting
description: Use when a PILOT sample-level distance matrix (Wasserstein distances between patient samples, e.g. myocardial_infarction.h5ad) must be converted into an ordered disease-progression pseudotime so that cell-population and gene changes can be regressed along disease progression.

name: elastic-net-coefficient-extraction
description: Use when a nested CV analysis (nestcv.glmnet) has finished and you need the final whole-dataset glmnet fit's retained genes and their ranked coefficients, e.g. for reproducibility checks or reporting a response signature.

name: elastic-net-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when fitting regularised glmnet models on high-dimensional data (P >> n, e.g. >16,000-gene RNA-seq with n=68) and both the mixing parameter alpha and shrinkage lambda must be cross-validated without biasing outer-CV accuracy.

name: elastic-net-perturbation-target-regression
description: Use when you have an inferred GRN (from SCING, GRNBOOST2, PIDC, or ppcor) plus Perturb-seq data with guide-to-gene assignments, and you need to quantify how accurately the GRN predicts downstream perturbed genes.

name: elastic-net-regularized-matrix-decomposition
description: Use when you have a large labeled source scRNA-Seq expression matrix (genes x cells) with ground-truth cluster labels and need a gene-level dictionary H_src to adjust a smaller target dataset for clustering.
tools: scikit-learn NMF (elastic-net regularized, as cited in the paper)

name: elastic-principal-graph-fitting
description: Use when scRNA-seq (or scATAC-seq) expression data in an AnnData object must be ordered into a branching trajectory/pseudotime and the number of bifurcations is unknown a priori.
