description: Use when a simulated or real multi-batch single-cell dataset has cell types confounded with batch (e.

name: elbow-criterion-sparsity-selection
description: Use when a Fantope/sparse PCA loading matrix must be made row-sparse and the hard-threshold t on row ℓ2 norms cannot be set by hand — e.g. estimated subspace V̂d rows must be split into signal vs noise without a known sparsity level.

name: elbow-point-detection
description: Use when a runHSS() result (hss.result) contains an HSSscores table over subsetted feature-set sizes and you must pick the elbow-optimal number of markers to define the final HSS-LDA model.

name: element-centric-clustering-similarity-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking DR embeddings (e.g., scLENS vs Seurat/Scanpy/scVI PCs) against known cell-type labels and you need per-element clustering agreement (ECS) plus silhouette scores to rank methods across sparsity levels.

name: elementwise-statistical-mean-computation
description: Use when AE-TPGG has been run with return_info=True on semi-continuous normalized scRNA-seq data (e.g. per-cell normalized and log1p-transformed Klein data) and the alpha/beta/gamma/pi parameter matrices must be converted into a dropout-free imputed expression matrix.

name: em-algorithm-parameter-estimation
description: Use when per-HTO droplet count distributions (e.g., an (HTOs x droplets) HTO count matrix) must be decomposed into unobserved signal/noise components, i.e., mixture parameters and posteriors must be estimated before classifying droplets to samples.

name: em-based-isoform-quantification
description: Use when RNase R-treated paired-end RNA-seq reads have been aligned (TopHat2), back-spliced junctions are listed from CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS, and you need full-length circRNA isoform sequences plus per-isoform FPKM/TPM expression.

name: em-estimation-of-logic-combination-priors
description: Use when inferring which Boolean logic gate (e.g. TF1 AND TF2, TF1 AND NOT TF2) regulates a target gene from scRNA-seq profiles, and you need to replace per-rule likelihood computations with a single mixture model whose combination priors are updated by EM.

name: em-iterative-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when fitting a Bayesian beta-binomial mixture to maternal read counts x_gk from single-cell RNA-Seq (P/B/M states) and you need the state assignments and pooled allelic proportions to reach a mutually consistent solution before writing per-cell per-gene calls.

name: embedding-benchmark-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when comparing a novel single-cell dimension-reduction embedding (e.g., GEP-averaged expression) against established methods like PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA on the same labeled dataset with identical clustering-quality metrics.

name: embedding-connectivity-evaluation
description: Use when candidate 2D embeddings (e.g., PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, diffusion maps of scRNA-seq data) must be screened for disconnected cell clusters before being accepted for trajectory inference scoring in Escort.

name: embedding-evaluation-pipeline
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has multiple candidate embeddings (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, diffusion maps) from varied feature-selection/dimension-reduction choices and you must score which are suitable for trajectory fitting with Escort.

name: embedding-mapping-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have aligned SC and ST embeddings in a shared latent space (e.g. from a trained STEM netE encoder) and need per-cell spatial coordinates or spot-to-cell correspondence probabilities.

name: embedding-quality-statistics
description: Use when per-cell quality scores are needed for 2D embeddings (t-SNE or UMAP) of high-dimensional data such as scRNA-seq or MNIST, to distinguish real structure from algorithm-induced noise.

name: embedding-recommendation-scoring
description: Use when multiple 2D embeddings (from different dimension-reduction, feature-selection, or hyperparameter choices) exist for a scRNA-seq dataset and you need a data-driven classification of which are suitable for trajectory inference.

name: embedding-silhouette-quality-evaluation
description: Use when an integrated scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq joint embedding has been produced and you need to verify that cells of the same type (or same omics) cluster together, e.g. to reproduce scBridge-vs-baseline comparisons.

name: embedding-stability-assessment
description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction methods on synthetic or single-cell datasets and you must verify that cluster shapes, relative positions, and noise handling are reproducible across runs rather than artifacts of a single initialization.

name: embedr-pvalue-threshold-tabulation
description: Use when you have per-cell EMBEDR p-values for dimensionality-reduced scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g. t-SNE vs UMAP on ~4,800 Tabula Muris bone marrow cells) and need to quantify, per p-value threshold, how many cells exceed the random-null quality expectation.

name: embryo-development-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when a 2D latent embedding of single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., VASC features of the Petropoulos pre-implantation embryo dataset) is available and the goal is to find and functionally annotate genes whose expression tracks embryo developmental dynamics.

name: embryo-developmental-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from staged embryos (e.g. E3–E7 pre-implantation stages) must be visualized in 2D to check whether developmental stage ordering, lineage separation, and pseudo-time structure are recovered, and to compare against PCA, t-SNE, ZIFA, or SIMLR.

name: embryonic-skin-cell-state-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from E14.5 embryonic skin must be split into spatially colocalized dermal states (placode, pre-DC, DC1, DC2) prior to cell-cell communication inference.

name: embryonic-stage-labeled-figure-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to visually validate learned cell-to-cell similarity matrices by re-embedding them with a modified t-SNE and comparing stage-colored panels across competing methods on embryo-development datasets (e.g., Goolam, Yan).

name: empirical-bayes-batch-adjustment
description: Use when a merged, cross-study normalized expression matrix (e.g. GEO-derived microarray data collapsed to gene symbols) shows batch structure driven by known covariates such as data series or microarray platform that must be removed before downstream analyses.

name: empirical-bayes-batch-effect-removal
description: Use when combining multi-study microarray data (e.g. GSE12929 and GSE14004 from curatedAdipoArray) where study of origin or platform confounds the analysis, and you need to verify that a biological variable separates samples after correction.

name: empirical-cdf-error-visualization
description: Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth circadian phases and multiple phase-inference methods (e.g., Tempo vs Cyclops/Cyclum/PCA) whose point-estimate errors you need to compare across conditions.

name: empirical-covariance-rank-truncation
description: Use when the sample covariance of a high-dimensional transcriptomic matrix (p >> n, e.g. 116 obs × 6283 genes) is rank deficient and you need a full-rank empirical covariance Φ or a pseudo-true β* to test whether marginal-correlation screening recovers true predictive genes.

name: empirical-distribution-estimation-scrna-seq
description: Use when time-course scRNA-seq data sacrifice cells at each time point (no cell-to-cell correspondence) and you need to set up the discrete OT problem for CellST's cell_name_traj lineage alignment.

name: empirical-distribution-sampling
description: Use when a ground-truth null scRNA-seq read-count matrix is needed to benchmark confounder-detection or normalization methods — specifically a homogeneous, co-expression-free null for testing nonlinear library-size effects in Normalisr.

name: empirical-false-positive-rate-estimation
description: Use when you must verify that a marker-gene or association test controls type-I error at the nominal 0.05 level across subject-level overdispersion levels — e.g. benchmarking NEBULA against naive glm.nb on unbalanced multi-subject single-cell groupings.

name: empirical-fdr-estimation-by-gene-label-permutation
description: Use when running gene set enrichment on scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (e.g. zingeR-DESeq2 beta/beta-variance) and a calibrated, overlap-aware empirical FDR (e.g. 5% threshold) is needed instead of nominal p-value cutoffs.

name: empirical-null-hypothesis-testing-via-marginal-resampling
description: Use when a t-SNE or UMAP embedding of single-cell omics data (e.g. ~4,800 Tabula Muris marrow cells) must be judged for real vs. algorithm-induced structure, requiring a per-sample significance test rather than a global quality score.

name: empirical-null-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when you need per-sample empirical p values that separate real structure in a DR embedding (t-SNE/UMAP) from algorithm-induced distortions, e.g. on Tabula Muris bone marrow scRNA-seq.

name: empirical-null-random-gene-set-sampling
description: Use when testing whether an unsupervised or bulk-derived gene set (e.g., cyclers with q < 0.05) is enriched for a reference set such as circadian clock genes, without a parametric enrichment model.

name: empirical-power-estimation-at-fixed-fdr
description: Use when comparing detection rates of gene set enrichment methods on simulated summary statistics where the truth (which replicates are enriched) is known and power must be computed at a fixed FDR threshold (e.g. 5%).

name: empirical-pvalue-computation-genesets
description: Use when quantifying significance of coordinated gene-set expression in a normalized expression matrix, and needing to classify gene sets as shifted (Median Exp) or overdispersed (L1) against random-set nulls.

name: empirical-pvalue-fdr-correction
description: Use when you have many gene signatures scored for phylogenetic autocorrelation (e.g., Geary's C on a KNN graph of cophenetic distances) and need multiple-testing-corrected significance before reporting which signatures track the phylogeny.

name: empirical-vaf-parameter-estimation
description: Use when parameterizing simulated single-cell mtDNA data: you need empirically grounded background SNPs, depths, and heteroplasmy distributions sampled from real cells rather than arbitrary values.

name: empty-droplet-filtering-single-cell
description: Use when you have a barcode frequency count table (e.g. flexiplex_barcodes_counts.txt) from single-cell long-read or short-read data and need to distinguish real cell barcodes from empty droplets before demultiplexing.

name: empty-droplet-noise-correlation-assessment
description: Use when raw and filtered Cell Ranger ADT matrices are available, empty droplets can be defined from the raw barcodes, and you must decide whether CLR normalization of protein data is confounded by ambient noise (e.g. misinterpreting MAIT-like clusters).

name: empty-droplet-removal-inflection-point
description: Use when flexiplex discovery mode has produced a read-barcode assignment and barcode count file (flexiplex_barcodes_counts.txt) from long-read single-cell FASTQ and true cell barcodes must be separated from empty-droplet barcodes.

name: emptydrops-cell-calling

name: encode-dnase-seq-truth-standard-selection
description: Use when a cell type has two ENCODE DNase-seq replicates and the goal is to quantify whether BIRD-predicted DH adds signal to the observed replicate in low signal-to-noise or few-replicate settings.

name: encoder-decoder-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when a DNA storage pipeline design must be evaluated under injected errors (i.i.d. or nanopore DNArSim channel faults), including parameter sweeps over encoder/decoder settings, to compare pipeline stage choices across error rates.

name: encori-clip-evidence-stringency-filtering
description: Use when constructing an RBP-ncRNA edge list from ENCORI/starBase interactions (human or mouse) for downstream RNC module detection and identifiers must be standardized and CLIP-evidence filtered.

name: enhancer-based-gene-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when you have paired or integrated scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (or 10x Multiome) data for a cell trajectory and need to infer which TFs regulate which genes via enhancer binding, e.g. reconstructing GRNs across pseudotime or validating predicted cell pairings.

name: enhancer-chromatin-state-classification
description: Use when you have genomic intervals (e.g., ATAC peaks from adata.var) plus H3K4me1 and H3K27ac ChIP-seq peaks and need to label each interval as a poised vs active enhancer to test priming.

name: enhancer-gene-pair-recall-evaluation
description: Use when comparing candidate enhancer–gene interaction rankings (e.g. ABC vs gABC vs co-accessibility) against an independent gold standard such as fine-mapped eQTL credible-set pairs, to measure which method recovers more supported pairs.

name: enhancer-priming-ratio-analysis
description: Use when validating that causally prioritized peak-gene pairs (e.g., GrID-Net Granger pairs) show epigenomic evidence of enhancer priming, by comparing H3K4me1-only vs H3K4me1+H3K27ac ChIP-seq overlap with ATAC peaks and comparing ratios across prioritization methods.

name: enriched-term-interpretation-for-rna-modification-genes
description: Use when you have a gene list derived from transcriptome-wide prediction of modification sites (e.g. 2441 genes with MU-PseUDeep-predicted Ψ sites) and need to identify which molecular functions, pathways, or diseases are over-represented.

name: enrichment-network-visualization
description: Use when you have a list of predicted target proteins and enrichment analysis results (GO/pathway terms) that need to be organized into a visual similarity network with cluster annotations, as done for common plant tRF-5/tRF-3 targets.

name: enrichment-odds-ratio-computation
description: Use when testing whether sQTLs alter annotated splice-site strength more frequently or more strongly than non-sQTL variants, via PWM scores of reference vs alternative alleles and a 2×2 odds ratio at FDR 0.05.

name: enrichment-p-value-multiple-testing-interpretation
description: Use when you have a gene list submitted to an enrichment tool (e.g. Enrichr against GO Biological Processes) and must decide which returned terms are significant, using adjusted p-value < 0.05 rather than raw p-values.

name: enrichment-pvalue-aggregation
description: Use when you have top-N gene lists (e.g., top 100 SSrGE-ranked eeSNV genes) from 5+ datasets and need a single cross-dataset pathway enrichment ranking, e.g., to reproduce Fig. 5-style KEGG pathway-gene graphs.

name: enrichment-result-comparison-across-marker-methods
description: Use when you have marker gene lists from two or more selection methods and need to determine which method's markers better recover known tissue/cell-type biology via enrichment q values against a reference gene set library.

name: enrichment-results-table-reporting
description: Use when per-cluster up/down-regulated marker gene lists (cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon-style testing, e.g. PBMC3k) from SCALA's differential expression step are available and per-cluster GO/KEGG enrichment plus TF activity must be computed and exported as a table.

name: enrichment-score-comparison-across-feature-sets
description: Use when two gene-selection strategies (e.g., scRNA-seq-only top-1000 vs scRNA-seq+HiChIP Fisher-combined top-1000) must be compared via GO enrichment -log10(p) per subpopulation and term.

name: enrichment-score-significance-testing
description: Use when an AnnData object with log-cpm normalized counts and high-resolution (over-clustered) Leiden labels needs statistical determination of which clusters represent genuinely distinct cell populations versus clusters to be merged.

name: enrichment-statistics-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when you have two E.PAGE enrichment result objects (results$stats tibbles) from distinct gene lists and need to identify which enriched gene modules are common to both, comparing padj and fold enrichment per module.

name: enrichment-table-reproduction-from-figure

name: enrichr-api-gene-list-query

name: enrichr-api-pathway-query

name: ensembl-gene-id-mapping

name: ensemble-aggregation-network-inference
description: Use when reconstructing a directed, signed GRN from time-stamped cross-sectional single-cell expression data and the raw A_t estimate is unstable because the sample mean and covariance must themselves be estimated.

name: ensemble-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether decision-level integration (scTriangulate) of conflicting clustering solutions outperforms consensus ensemble methods (HGPA, MCLA, HBGF) against a ground truth or reference annotation.

name: ensemble-coefficient-grid-search
description: Use when you have multiple MCP path-capacity score matrices (2-, 3-, and 4-path) plus partial groundtruth interactions, and want the optimal ensemble weighting that maximizes AUPRC.

name: ensemble-consensus-clustering
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression matrices where the number of cell types is known and no single algorithm is consistently , and a consensus label per cell is needed with NMI/ARI benchmarking against published labels.

name: ensemble-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a cells-by-genes scRNA-seq count matrix needs simultaneous 2D embedding and feature gene extraction, especially to separate rare cell types or to benchmark against t-SNE and UMAP with silhouette indices.

name: ensemble-feature-gene-ranking
description: Use when a simulated or real scRNA-seq count matrix needs a ranked list of feature genes via EDGE, and detection accuracy must be scored against known differentially expressed genes (top-15/top-30 counts).

name: ensemble-feature-selection-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when a preprocessed, log-normalized cells x genes scRNA-seq matrix plus initial cluster labels are available and a compact gene subset (up to ~4000 genes) is needed before rare-cell anomaly detection or clustering.

name: ensemble-machine-learning-doublet-scoring
description: Use when raw Seurat/SCE droplet scRNA-seq data contains suspected technical doublets and you need stable, accurate doublet calls (AUC-based) that outperform any single tool like DoubletFinder or scds.

name: ensemble-median-aggregation
description: Use when forecasting future transcriptomic states from paired time-point single-cell expression matrices with RNAForecaster and single-network predictions are unstable or degrade over recursive time steps.

name: ensemble-size-scaling-analysis
description: Use when evaluating snapshot-ensemble embedding generation on multimodal single-cell omics (e.g., CITE-seq RNA+ADT) and you need to determine which ensemble size and epoch budget reproduces conventional VAE-ensemble clustering performance at minimal cost.

name: ensemble-tree-grn-inference
description: Use when you need a strong classical baseline for GRN inference from a gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. 8000+ expressed genes in K562 perturb-seq data) to compare against foundation-model-derived networks like scPRINT or scGPT.

name: ensemble-weak-learner-averaging
description: Use when you have a log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix and need a bounded (0-1) cell-by-cell similarity matrix to seed downstream k-NNG, spectral embedding, or dimensionality reduction.

name: entrez-gene-id-mapping
description: Use when network nodes, ACE tables, or path outputs from SEMgraph/SEMtree are keyed by Entrez IDs (e.g., ATG16L1 = 55054, CCR5 = 1234) and must be labeled with gene symbols for reporting or benchmark counting.

name: entrez-to-symbol-gene-identifier-mapping
description: Use when an stAPAminer RUD/APA count matrix or PACdataset is keyed by ENTREZID and downstream labeling, clustering, or DEAPA reporting needs gene SYMBOLs (mouse data).

name: entropic-optimal-transport-ground-cost-design
description: Use when training Mowgli on paired single-cell multi-omics data (RNA, ADT, ATAC) and you need to configure the OT loss — ground-cost metric, entropic regularization, sparsity weights, and latent dimension k — or extend it, e.g. with batch-aware cost reweighting.

name: entropy-analysis-of-cluster-label-distributions
description: Use when hybrid clusters from ClonoCluster runs (alpha = 0 vs low alpha) must be compared against known cell-type ground-truth labels to demonstrate clonal information increases cluster purity.

name: entropy-and-divergence-computation
description: Use when benchmarking label-transfer/annotation accuracy on datasets with known cell type label distributions and you need dataset-level characteristics (size, type count, entropy, DKL) to correlate with accuracy.

name: entropy-based-confident-cell-selection
description: Use when a small actively- or randomly-selected labeled training set exists for cell type annotation and additional unlabeled cells are available to boost classifier F1 via pseudo-labeling.

name: entropy-based-differentiation-potential-quantification

name: entropy-based-feature-scoring

name: entropy-based-transcriptome-purity-scoring

name: entropy-confidence-classifier-scoring
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq target cells with a pre-trained source classifier and you need a per-cell uncertainty score in [0,1] to detect novel cell types without source data.

name: entropy-estimation-from-gene-expression
description: Use when starting from a normalized gene-expression count table (e.g. DREAM 4 time-series, units-to-tens of time points) and you need to rank gene-gene relationships by mutual information to seed GRN inference.

name: entropy-feature-computation
description: Use when raw somatic coding mutation data (e.g. COSMIC v79) must be converted into a per-gene/transcript feature matrix with entropy and frequency statistics for mutation types, for driver gene classification or feature-importance analysis.

name: entropy-pseudotime-correlation-analysis
description: Use when single-cell clustering results must be checked against a developmental trajectory: e.g. testing whether label entropy is high at transition states and decreases with differentiation pseudotime.

name: epigenetic-mark-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a scHiCDiff DCI results data frame is available (bin_1/bin_2 pairs with pvalue.adj.FDR) and the goal is to characterize detected DCIs by epigenetic mark changes and GO enrichment, e.g. Astro vs Endo.

name: eqtl-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when summarystatistic-level eQTL data (z-scores or betas+SEs) for many tissues, reference LD matrices, and a question of tissue sharing or GWAS target-tissue prioritization are available, especially when loci may harbor multiple causal variants.

name: eqtl-groundtruth-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a peak-gene (locus-gene) inference method must be quantitatively benchmarked against eQTL-supported ground-truth pairs on paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data with multiple samples per dataset.

name: eqtl-lead-variant-background-matching
description: Use when evaluating whether CAFEH fine-mapped credible-set variants are enriched in active regulatory elements (Roadmap chromHMM) and a size-balanced, gene-matched lead-eQTL background is needed for comparison.

name: eqtl-mapping-genotype-expression
description: Use when you have SNP genotype data plus RNA-seq counts from (possibly related) individuals across conditions (e.g. infection), and need per-SNP–gene eQTL effect sizes, P-values, and FDR calls rather than plain DEG calls.

name: eqtl-retrieval-auroc-benchmarking
description: Use when you have peak-gene scores from one or more causal-inference configurations (GrID-Net, linear Granger, correlational baselines) on the SHARE-seq mouse skin dataset and need a quantitative gold-standard comparison against significant eQTLs from the eQTL Catalogue.

name: eqtl-summary-statistics-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking fine-mapping/colocalization methods on summary statistics and you need simulated loci with a controlled number of causal variants and signal strengths.

name: eqtl-trained-logistic-model-training
description: Use when GrID-Net Granger scores for peak-gene pairs need distance-aware calibration before linking variants to genes, and an eQTL dataset (e.g., SHARE-seq skin) is available to define positive pairs.

name: eqtl-weight-based-grex-association-testing
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics and pre-trained eQTL weights (per-gene SNP effect sizes from a reference panel) are available and the goal is to identify genes whose genetically regulated expression associates with a trait.

name: eqtl-weight-training-from-summary-statistics
description: Use when eQTL summary statistics (CHROM, POS, A1, A2, Zscore, TargetID, N) plus an LD reference panel are available but individual-level genotype/expression data are not, and gene-level eQTL weights are needed for TWAS.

name: equivalent-rule-set-computation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data and a prior knowledge network (e.g., KEGG pathways like hsa00010/hsa00020) are available and executable Boolean regulatory rules are needed, especially when multiple rule sets can explain the data.

name: er-status-stratified-survival-modeling
description: Use when bulk tumour samples (e.g. TCGA-BRCA) have a continuous pseudotime score from PhenoPath plus overall survival time/status and ER status, and the goal is to test pseudotime as an independent survival predictor.

name: ercc-mitochondrial-fraction-annotation
description: Use when tall-format melted scRNA-seq expression data (CSV or Parquet) has been loaded in Spark and per-cell/per-gene QC metrics — percent ERCC, percent mitochondrial, counts, and dropouts — are needed before filtering.

name: ercc-spike-in-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation method (e.g., scImpute on raw read counts with drop_thre = 0.5) recovers true expression levels masked by dropout events, using ERCC spike-ins with known concentrations as ground truth.

name: ercc-spike-in-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking droplet scRNA-seq conversion efficiency or linearity using ERCC spike-ins: ERCC FASTQ from SRA SRP073767 is available and conversion efficiency, UMI-vs-molecule Pearson r, and CV2 must be recomputed.

name: erdos-renyi-network-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic genotype-phenotype data with known planted higher-order (multi-gene) associations to benchmark network-guided interval miners such as HOGImine against their statistical power and runtime.

name: error-tolerant-sequence-search
description: Use when searching FASTQ/FASTA reads for a known sequence (e.g. a variant, transgene, or fusion junction) where base errors are expected and an exact string matcher would miss true matches.

name: ers-rule-sampling-for-network-simulation
description: Use when scBONITA Boolean rules and a GRAPHML pathway topology are available and cells must be mapped to characteristic pathway-specific signaling states via attractor analysis of the learned discrete-state models.

name: ers-size-quantification
description: Use when testing the robustness of Boolean rule inference to training-set size: input is a pre-processed scRNA-seq cluster (genes x cells matrix), and the goal is to detect at which training fraction the ERS size degrades.

name: erythrocyte-marker-expression-profiling
description: Use when a rare-cell analysis of the 68k PBMC dataset has produced a candidate CD34+/megakaryocyte cluster (e.g. ~185 cells) and its reported erythrocyte-marker signature must be verified against remaining CD34+ cells.

name: erythrocyte-marker-expression-validation
description: Use when a rare-cell cluster from LSH-based rareness scoring (FiRE) plus dropClust clustering must be assigned a cell-type identity, and candidate marker genes (e.g. erythrocyte markers Alas2, Hba-a1, Hba-a2, Hbb-bt) are available to confirm the assignment.

name: escort-embedding-scoring
description: Decision support for choosing among multiple 2-D embeddings (e.g., MDS, UMAP or t-SNE computed on 2000, 4000 or 10000 highly variable genes) before trajectory inference, when you need a data-driven recommended/not-recommended verdict per embedding.

name: essential-gene-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have a defined gene list (e.g., TimeTalk's 430 eLR genes) and reference gene sets, and need to test whether the list is significantly enriched/depleted (e.g., essential/ZGA enriched, housekeeping depleted) against a gene-universe background.

name: essentiality-safety-scatter-visualization
description: Use when you have single-gene deletion results from both infected and mock context-specific models and must rank knockouts on an essentiality-vs-safety plane to select low-toxicity antimetabolic drug targets.

name: estimated-versus-annotated-cluster-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when benchmarking similarity-learning clustering methods (e.g., SSRE vs. SSR and four comparison methods) and you must judge how reliably each method recovers the known number of cell types on pre-annotated scRNA-seq data.

name: estimator-bias-mse-visualization
description: Use when you need to assess robustness of ZINB-WaVE estimates of ln(mu) and pi to misspecification of the number of latent covariates K or the gene-level covariate matrix V, by comparing refits to simulated ground truth.

name: euclidean-cluster-center-merging
description: Use when an iterative cluster decomposition (as in scCAD) has over-split major clusters into D-clusters and you must consolidate them into stable M-clusters before scoring rare sub-clusters.

name: euclidean-distance-knn-graph-construction
description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2 and Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2 log-count matrices) and you need to build Euclidean-distance neighbor sets to match anchors across datasets or quantify neighborhood retention after batch correction.

name: euclidean-distance-neighbor-weighting
description: Use when a cell-by-feature matrix has sparse NA entries (e.g., single-cell AS probability dropouts) and missing values must be imputed before downstream clustering such as spectral clustering.

name: euclidean-distance-network-percentile-thresholding
description: Use when building condition-specific (normal vs cancer) gene co-expression networks from TCGA RNA-Seq expression data and you need a distribution-based, top-percentile sparsification of Euclidean-distance similarity edges before network fusion.

name: euclidean-minimum-spanning-tree-cell-graph-construction
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell trajectory methods on a progenitor dataset with a known branching event (e.g. cDC1 vs cDC2 preDC commitment) and a conventional tree-based baseline is needed to compare against neighborhood-based methods like Mpath.

name: eukaryotic-protein-sequence-retrieval
description: Use when building or extending a protein ortholog database from KEGG eukaryotic proteomes — i.e., you need per-organism FASTA files for downstream all-vs-all orthology binning.

name: eva-alpha-parameter-optimization
description: Use when running ELVAR/EVA clustering on a cell-cell nearest-neighbor graph with a vertex attribute (age, disease stage/severity) and an optimal alpha balancing attribute-similarity against state-manifold topology must be chosen before downstream DA testing.

name: evidence-based-cell-type-scoring
description: Use when clusters from scRNA-seq data need automatic cell type labels without prior knowledge, and candidate cluster marker genes have been identified and matched against the CellMatch reference database.

name: evidence-linking
description: Use when an article claims a tool exists with stated capabilities (here, RCAT for circadian clock genes) and you must verify which repository, release package, and usage instructions substantiate the claim, and record what is still missing.

name: evolutionary-index-visualization
description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData objects need gene age-weighted evolutionary index (TEI) scores per cell and stage-wise plots, e.g. to reproduce hourglass patterns with lowest TEI at 12 hpf in zebrafish.

name: exact-kmer-overlap-extension
description: Use when assembling viral contigs from unmapped RNAseq FASTQ reads without an aligner, using model-predicted viral reads as seeds and exact k-mer overlap extension to grow contigs.

name: excel-date-artifact-correction
description: Use when a gene expression dataset opened in Excel contains date-like tokens (Dec-01, Mar-01–Mar-11, Sep-01–Sep-15) or pre-2017 HGNC symbols (SEPT1, MARC1) in its gene-name column that must be restored to updated HGNC names before pathway analysis.

name: excel-date-conversion-detection
description: Use when supplementary .csv or .xlsx gene-expression files contain date-like tokens (Mar-01, Mar-02, or numeric values at the top of an ascending-sorted gene-name column) that must be mapped back to HGNC symbols.

name: excel-date-conversion-gene-list-recovery
description: Use when a .csv or .xlsx gene expression list opened in Excel contains gene symbols auto-converted to dates (e.g. Mar-01, Mar-02) or outdated gene names that pathway enrichment tools like Enrichr or GSEA cannot recognize.

name: execution-time-memory-profiling
description: Use when scaling claims about a feature selection or clustering method must be quantified: run the method on downsamplings (10k, 100k cells) and the full dataset (1M+ cells) and record per-method runtime and peak memory.

name: execution-time-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of network inference pipelines on genome-wide RNA-Seq data and you need per-tool and per-pipeline-step runtime metrics to populate a benchmark results table.

name: execution-time-variability-analysis
description: Use when comparing the consistency (not just the speed) of execution times between two methods or implementations across repeated benchmark runs, e.g. GPU-accelerated vs CPU-based pipelines on the same workstation.

name: exemplar-gene-call-reconciliation
description: Use when re-implementing scBASE's seven-region gene classification on the Deng et al. CAST×B6 F1 pre-implantation data and you need to validate your mixture-weight thresholds and P/B/M posterior assignments against the paper's exemplar gene calls.

name: exhaustive-split-search-tree-construction
description: Use when you need a classical, deterministic single--split classification tree (e.g. on anorexia weight-change data with treatment/coding/interacting variable types) rather than the DIPM random-forest-based node fitting.

name: exitron-splicing-event-detection
description: Use when RNA-seq alignments are available and the goal is to capture neoantigen sources beyond SNVs/indels, specifically exitron-splicing events that most neoantigen-prediction tools overlook.

name: exon-inclusion-count-length-normalization
description: Use when you have per-event inclusion (IJC) and skipping (SJC) junction counts for reference and alternative alleles plus effective isoform lengths, and need length-normalized exon inclusion levels for ASAS testing.

name: exon-intron-structure-annotation
description: Use when PHAS loci predicted from sRNA-seq data must be annotated by exon/intron structure against a genome gff3, especially when comparing transcriptome-based vs genome-based phasiRNA prediction results.

name: exon-skipping-event-count-filtering
description: Use when preparing exon inclusion/exclusion count matrices (e.g., from a SingleCellExperiment with raw_M1 and raw_M2 assays) for GEDI splicing-mode integration, to drop low-sequencing-depth cells and low-coverage events before model fitting.

name: exon-skipping-variation-modeling
description: Use when you need simulated circRNA isoform panels with known full-length sequences and expression levels — e.g. benchmarking assembly or quantification tools like CircAST across depth, read-length, or multi-condition series.

name: expectation-maximization-parameter-estimation
description: Use when smoothed per-cell segment-level expression means from scRNA-seq data must be discretized into a fixed set of copy number states via unsupervised mixture-model fitting with EM.

name: expectation-maximization-read-assignment-quantification
description: Use when you have a name-sorted paired-end SAM from TopHat2, a UCSC-format GTF, and a back-spliced junction list from CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS, and you need full-length circRNA isoform sequences plus isoform-level expression (FPKM/TPM).

name: expected-classification-error-model-selection
description: Use when demultiplexing HTO-labeled scRNA-seq droplets with demuxmix and both a naive NB mixture and a genes-detected regression mixture have been fit per HTO, so the model with the lower expected classification error must be chosen for classification.

name: experimenthub-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis workflow requires downloading a normalized GEO expression dataset and its sample annotation (e.g., GSE13015/EH5429) into R as a SummarizedExperiment to feed into module-level fingerprinting functions.

name: expert-review-preparation
description: Use when an article package pairs a tool paper with a GitHub release and the goal is an expert review: connect each stated claim (e.g. a packaged Windows RCAT release) to the actual repository artifact and log gaps.

name: exponential-family-harmonium-parametrization
description: Use when fitting a deep Boltzmann machine (scDBM) to raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k, 4182 cells × 1000 highly variable genes) and per-gene negative-binomial inverse dispersion parameters must be estimated during training.

name: exponential-trend-fitting
description: Use when h5ad cells carry a continuous cell-cycle angle (cell_cycle_theta) and you must verify whether total UMI counts per cell double (fold change ~2.0-2.1) across the transcriptional phase before mitosis.

name: expression-based-regulome-prediction
description: Use when you have RNA-seq (FPKM matrix) or exon array gene expression for a sample and need genome-scale chromatin accessibility predictions, e.g., to pseudo-replicate DNase-seq or convert GEO expression samples into regulomes.

name: expression-bin-stratified-logfc-regression
description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately normalization/DE methods estimate effect sizes (logFC) on simulated single-cell data with known ground truth, especially to detect expression-level-dependent bias.

name: expression-binned-zscore-normalization
description: Use when selecting well-correlated candidate feature genes from a log-normalized scRNA-seq matrix, and gene-level correlation statistics must be normalized against expression-level confounding by binning genes by mean expression.

name: expression-data-adjustment-preprocessing
description: Use when filtered RNA-seq expression matrices from multiple infection-condition samples must be distribution-adjusted (quantile normalization) before computing gene-gene correlations or building coexpression modules.

name: expression-data-binning-entropy-estimation
description: Use when starting from an RNA-Seq time-series count table (e.g., C. beijerinckii 5442 genes × 6 time points) and you need an initial genome-wide GRN via mutual information between gene pairs.

name: expression-feature-extraction-from-simulated-data
description: Use when OU-simulated deletion-event expression data (or empirical data in the same format) must be transformed into the p=3m feature file that CLOUDeClassifyNN/XGB/RF/SVM and CLOUDePredict* require.

name: expression-matrix-construction
description: Use when reproducing the paper's infection expression matrix: you have TPM estimates from the Soybean Expression Atlas plus supplementary infection RNA-seq samples and need a filtered gene x sample matrix as coexpression network input.

name: expression-matrix-pca-input-preparation
description: Use when a single-cell dataset must be formatted as a cell-by-feature CSV (genes, transcripts, or principal components) before running Sphetcher at a given sketch size.

name: expression-skewness-gene-classification
description: Use when a barcode-annotated (lineage-labeled) scRNA-seq matrix must be screened for genes with unusually stable expression across related cells, and each hit classified as quantitative or qualitative memory.

name: expression-variation-filtering-in-cell-lines
description: Use when building a subtype/classification gene template from bulk tumor data that must generalize to cell lines, organoids or PDXs lacking human stromal/immune compartments.

name: expressionset-construction-from-single-cell-and-bulk-counts
description: Use when raw bulk RNA-seq and single-cell/single-nucleus counts from the same tissue need to be packaged as ExpressionSet objects for BisqueRNA decomposition with overlapping individuals.

name: expressionset-single-cell-data-formatting
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts with cell-type and subject labels plus paired bulk RNA-seq counts for BisqueRNA decomposition, e.g. a Seurat v3 object or count matrices needing ExpressionSet conversion.

name: external-clustering-metrics-computation
description: Use when evaluating how well unsupervised clusters derived from tGPT (or similar) embeddings match known cell type annotations, and you need quantitative NMI/ARI/FMI values reproducible as a clustering_metrics.csv table.

name: external-cohort-validation-of-classifiers
description: Use when pre-trained RNA-seq subtype classifiers must be benchmarked on an independent external cohort processed with the same normalization, reproducing Table 2 external-testing results.

name: external-doublet-detector-scoring
description: Use when Chord's built-in tools (DoubletFinder, scds) are insufficient and you want to boost the GBM ensemble with an additional detector such as Scrublet or solo via the addmethods1/addmethods2 port.

name: external-reference-score-integration
description: Use when you have computed performance metrics for your method on a shared benchmark dataset and need to integrate them with previously published scores of competing algorithms so all methods can be compared on identical data and metrics.

name: extra-domain-validation-checkpoint-selection
description: Use when training a multi-domain deep-learning model (e.g. Cancer-Finder on 13 TISCH tissue domains) and you need to choose the saved checkpoint by generalization to an unseen domain rather than internal-validation loss.

name: extracellular-matrix-term-interpretation
description: Use when functional enrichment results from a DEG list (e.g. PMM2-CDG DEGs selected by a minimum vote threshold of three) must be filtered and interpreted for basement membrane, extracellular matrix, or collagen-related biological process terms.

name: f-measure-classification-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating a DEG-calling method or combined classifier (e.g. Naïve Bayes over multi-method p-value vectors) against a spike-in dataset with known DEG/non-DEG truth labels, to quantify performance as an F-measure.

name: f-measure-precision-recall-computation
description: Use when ranking gene-prediction tools by F0.2-measure against curated driver gene lists (CGC 616 genes, NCG 711 genes, PMH 501 genes) over multiple TCGA cancer-type prediction sets.

name: f-score-feature-selection
description: Use when a fused high-dimensional sequence-encoding feature matrix (e.g., PCPseDNC + PSP + k-mer + PseEIIP) must be reduced before training classifiers and you need a fast filter-type ranking such as the F score used by Staem5.

name: f1-benchmark-comparison-across-annotation-methods
description: Use when comparing cell type annotation classifiers on single-cell expression data with ground-truth labels, especially to measure whether adding confidently self-labeled (pseudo-labeled) cells improves held-out F1 relative to ground-truth-only training.

name: f1-benchmark-evaluation-across-sequencing-conditions
description: Use when a detector's calls (e.g. ecDNA callers on ATAC-Seq data) must be validated against known ground truth, especially to characterize performance sensitivity to local sequencing depth (e.g. 10x–30x+) and read length (e.g. 35–150 bp).

name: f1-classification-performance-comparison
description: Use when comparing malignant-vs-non-malignant cell classifiers on scRNA-seq count matrices with bulk WES/WGS-derived copy number ground truth, and you need per-sample F1 aggregation across cancer types and platforms.

name: f1-cross-parental-origin-read-tagging
description: Use when processing scRNA-Seq reads from a CAST×B6 F1 cross where reads must be assigned to maternal vs. paternal transcript copies, e.g., before EMASE-based multi-read allocation or unique-read allele counting.

name: f1-improvement-aggregation-across-splits
description: Use when two active learning classifiers (e.g., random forest vs logistic regression) have been evaluated with F1 across multiple train/test splits and you must aggregate into a single relative improvement metric per search/threshold combination.

name: f1-metric-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a classifier's predicted cell labels must be scored against held-out true labels, e.g. comparing Symphony-based predictions to benchmarked classifiers via per-cell-type F1 and median F1 across train-test experiments.

name: f1-precision-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a cell type annotation method against baselines and you need per-class F1/precision distributions that are fair across methods with different reference sets.

name: f1-score-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing a generalized model trained on merged multi-dataset training data against disease-specific counterparts on each cancer type's validation set, using macro-averaged F1 deltas.

name: f1-score-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating annotation or classification accuracy of single-cell labels — e.g. Census predictions vs original cluster-level labels — across perturbations such as cell-number down-sampling (5–500 cells per cluster), producing F1 distributions and non-parametric significance tests.

name: f1-score-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing cell annotation algorithms (e.g., CellO IR/CLR, 1NN, scMatch, SingleR) on a labeled single-cell dataset, or when testing whether classification performance is stable across parameter settings such as Leiden clustering resolution.

name: f1-score-computation-across-dropout-levels
description: Use when benchmarking a pretrained Pollock module's tolerance to artificial sequencing dropout — e.g., you have .h5ad/.rds validation data with ground-truth 'cell_type' annotations and need an F1-versus-dropout robustness curve.

name: f1-score-computation-against-ground-truth-labels
description: Use when comparing automatic malignant-vs-non-malignant classification methods on single-cell count matrices that come with known tumor/normal ground-truth labels, and you need a single harmonic-mean accuracy number per condition.

name: f1-score-evaluation-of-rare-cell-calls
description: Use when benchmarking rare-cell or doublet detection on subsampled scRNA-seq data with known planted cells, to compare methods like GapClust, RaceID, GiniClust, CellSIUS, and FiRE by F1 score.

name: f5c-eventalign-kmer-anchoring
description: Use when building training data from ONT direct RNA reads that pairs variable-length raw current chunks with reference kmers — e.g. before NanoListener dataset construction, simulated-randomer augmentation, or IsolationForest training on f5c eventalign output.

name: facs-label-mapping-for-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq batch-correction or clustering methods on data with FACS-sorted cell-type labels, to quantify clustering consistency (ARI) and separation (silhouette) against true labels.

name: facs-label-vs-cluster-composition-assessment
description: Use when single-cell expression data have accompanying FACS-sort labels for each cell and an unsupervised clustering must be validated/optimized by how purely each cluster recapitulates the sorted subsets.

name: facs-purified-population-purity-assessment
description: Use when you have expression matrices from FACS-sorted or otherwise purified cell populations (or a control such as ERCC spike-ins) and need a quantitative, thresholded measure of cluster/population purity before downstream analysis.

name: facs-sorted-pbmc-data-processing
description: Use when benchmarking cell-label assignment methods (e.g., NeuCA vs scmap, CHETAH, Seurat, SC3) on labeled 10X PBMC scRNA-seq data with Monte Carlo training/testing splits.

name: factor-disease-association-statistics
description: Use when a trained MOFA/scPAFA model over pseudobulk pathway activity scores must be linked to disease state — i.e., you have sample-level clinical metadata (SLE vs healthy) and latent factors whose variance needs statistical testing against condition.

name: factor-loading-group-comparison-statistics
description: Use when a tensor decomposition of cell-cell communication scores yields context loadings and you must determine which factors differ significantly between phenotypic groups or whether samples group by condition.

name: factor-loading-pattern-recovery
description: Use when a simulated or real 4D-communication tensor has known embedded latent patterns and you need to verify that tensor decomposition recovers them from context, LR-pair, and cell-type factor loadings.

name: factor-similarity-correlation-index-comparison
description: Use when two or more 4D-communication tensors (contexts x LR pairs x senders x receivers) have been decomposed under different preprocessing, batch-correction, or parameter settings, and you need to test whether recovered communication factors are consistent.

name: fairness-constrained-cell-sketching
description: Use when a large single-cell expression matrix must be subsampled for trajectory or clustering analysis while preserving a minimum number of cells per collection time point or class label, e.g. to remove outlier cells whose transcriptomic state disagrees with their time point.

name: false-discovery-rate-calculation
description: Use when evaluating a demultiplexer's read-barcode assignments against known truth barcodes and you need an error-rate metric (FDR) plus correct-assignment counts, e.g. comparing Flexiplex, scTagger, and FLAMES at edit distances 0–3.

name: false-discovery-rate-computation
description: Use when benchmarking filter feature-selection algorithms on synthetic datasets where the truly relevant features are known, so the fraction of irrelevant probes among the selected features (FDR) can be measured.

name: false-discovery-rate-control
description: Use when a table of per-cell candidate fusion supporting-read counts must be tested against a background-noise model, and multiple-testing-adjusted (FDR) significance calls are required to control false positives.

name: false-discovery-rate-control
description: Use when you have per-gene Wald test p-values from per-feature Tweedie (CPLM/ZICP) GLM fits of scRNA-seq UMI or read counts and must convert them into FDR-adjusted q-values for DE calls at α = 0.05.

name: false-discovery-rate-control
description: Use when calling differential (XDE) genes along pseudotime from multi-sample single-cell RNA-seq with two or more conditions per contrast, and you must demonstrate FDR control at FDR.overall < 0.05 on a null dataset or spike-in simulation.

name: false-discovery-rate-correction
description: Use when many per-gene statistical tests (e.g. chi-squared variance tests of signal vs noise eigenvector projections) must be multiple-testing corrected before ranking or selecting genes.

name: false-discovery-rate-estimation
description: Use when a SingleCellGGM GGM network has been computed (~20,000 iterations) and edge cutoffs (pcor >= 0.03, co-expression in >= 10 cells) must be validated by a permutation-based FDR estimate before network clustering.

name: false-discovery-rate-meta-analysis
description: Use when you have raw per-sample allele depths (AD field) for biallelic SNPs in a VCF, per-sample binomial p-values testing allelic imbalance against probability 0.5, and need a per-variant significance call with FDR control.

name: false-discovery-rate-thresholding
description: Use when you have a fitted scCODA CAResult (HMC posterior samples of spike-and-slab indicators) and must call credible cell-type effects while controlling the expected false discovery rate at a chosen level.

name: false-discovery-rate-thresholding
description: Use when a background-subtracted microarray expression matrix has two known response classes (e.g. wild-type vs. mutant samples) and you need a statistically ranked list of differentially expressed genes under a permissive FDR cutoff such as 0.4.

name: false-negative-rate-estimation
description: Use when evaluating an RNA editing predictor (e.g. RDDpred) against a curated set of validated editing positives and negatives, and you need per-tool missed-site rates or ROC-AUC to rank competing classifiers.

name: false-positive-count-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking approximate sequence search or binning tools (e.g., Raptor vs. COBS vs. Mantis) where search results are probabilistic and false-positive rates must be counted against known ground-truth bin memberships.

name: false-positive-false-negative-benchmark-counting
description: Use when you need to measure how an approximate sequence search index (e.g., a minimizer interleaved Bloom filter with probabilistic thresholding) trades off false-positive and false-negative bin assignments across different index sizes or bin counts.

name: false-positive-false-negative-rate-evaluation
description: Use when you must estimate how many RNA editing positives are missed (FN) and negatives accepted (FP) by REDInet — e.g. validating robustness under degraded inputs like >30% missing flanking positions.

name: false-positive-rate-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-type perturbation detection method under null conditions (beta=0) to test whether individual-to-individual variability inflates false positives, or to validate that a mixed-effects alternative controls FPR.

name: false-positive-rate-assessment
description: Use when evaluating how the size of a Raptor interleaved Bloom filter (e.g. 1, 2, 4, 8 GiB), minimizer choice, or compression affects the number of false-positive bin assignments and run time/memory when searching large read collections.

name: false-positive-rate-estimation
description: Use when you need to quantify how many false-positive differential-proportion calls Scanpro produces — e.g., when choosing the number of bootstrapping pseudo-replicates (2–14) for a given total cell count per condition (~1,000 to ~50,000 cells).

name: false-positive-rate-estimation-in-healthy-controls
description: Use when validating a scRNA-seq mutation-calling pipeline: apply it to cells known to lack the somatic variants (e.g., 8057 bone marrow cells from four healthy donors) to measure per-site false-positive rates and confirm no spurious calls in wild-type cells.

name: fantope-projection-eigendecomposition
description: Use when replicating or auditing how suffPCR turns a sparse PCA (FPS) solution into a row-sparse loading matrix V̂d — i.e., Fantope projection via truncated eigendecomposition, ADMM soft-thresholding, and Algorithm 2 elbow threshold selection.

name: fasta-identifier-count-embedding
description: Use when raw demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be reduced to unique sequences with embedded counts (FASTX-Toolkit-style headers) before alignment and counting, e.g. preparing collapsed.fa for tinyRNA.

name: fasta-sequence-file-curation
description: Use when assembling tissue-specific m6A benchmark FASTA datasets — 41-nt RNA segments from human/mouse/rat brain, liver, kidney, heart, or testis — need redundancy removal (CD-HIT <80%) and balanced train/test splits before model training.

name: fastq-adapter-and-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw Illumina short-read FASTQ (single-end or paired-end, DNA-seq or RNA-seq) must be quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed, and QC-reported before alignment or genotyping in a pipeline.

name: fastq-downsampling-depth-analysis
description: Use when quantifying how isoform-quantification accuracy degrades with sequencing depth: you have simulated Nanopore FASTQ reads with 10x-style cell barcode/UMI, a ground-truth cell-by-isoform matrix, and need depth-response curves of per-cell accuracy.

name: fastq-naming-schema-validation
description: Use when raw GEX/ADT FASTQ files must be staged before a gExcite/cellranger run and you need to confirm the per-sample directory layout and SAMPLENAME_S[Number]_L00[Lane]_[ReadType]_001.fastq.gz naming before execution.

name: fastq-preprocessing-and-downsampling
description: Use when starting from published scRNA-seq resources (e.g. Cell Ranger 1.1.0 BAMs from Chromium, or oversized FASTQs from ICELL8) that must be converted, reduced to chromosome 21, or downsampled to a fixed read count before pipeline benchmarking.

name: fastq-quality-assessment
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files (e.g. SRA accessions SRP058295, SRP255211) must be QC-checked before STAR alignment or variant calling, or when read origin needs verification via sampled BLAST.

name: fastq-read-barcode-annotation
description: Use when FASTQ reads must be filtered for reads containing a known sequence/variant (with mismatches tolerated) and then annotated with cell-barcode and UMI assignments in a single command-line pipeline.

name: fastq-read-preprocessing-and-counting
description: Use when raw paired-end SPLiT-seq FASTQ files need barcode/UMI identification and you must count identified labeled reads and compute identified-read ratios per sample.

name: fastq-read-region-indexing
description: Use when preprocessing single-cell genomics FASTQs (e.g. dogmaseq-dig RNA/tag/atac/protein splits) and you need the per-tool technology string describing where barcodes, UMIs, and cDNA lie in R1/R2/R3 before kb count or alevin-fry.

name: fastq-read-sequence-collapsing
description: Use when a small RNA-seq FASTQ(.gz) file must be reduced to unique sequences with per-sequence counts before alignment and counting, e.g. producing collapsed.fa as consumed by tiny-count in the tinyRNA pipeline.

name: fastq-sample-folder-organization
description: Use when preparing raw 10x-style GEX and ADT (CITE-Seq) FASTQs for the gExcite or scAmpi Snakemake pipelines, which require one sub-directory per sample and SAMPLENAME_S[Number]_L00[Lane]_[ReadType]_001.fastq.gz naming before cellranger count.

name: fastq-umi-clipping
description: Use when the input is a quality-filtered single-end FASTQ whose reads carry the UMI at the 5' start and you must move it into the read header before alignment and UMI counting.

name: fasttree-dendrogram-inference
description: Use when an oversized EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (too many genes aggregated for gene-level insight) must be split by phylogenetic distance: given protein sequences plus species assignments, infer the dendrogram needed for cophenetic-distance k-means clustering.

name: fastx-toolkit-compatible-header-formatting
description: Use when you hold demultiplexed small RNA FASTQ reads and need a count-annotated collapsed FASTA (collapsed.fa) to feed the alignment and counting steps of a small RNA-seq pipeline such as tinyRNA/tiny-count.

name: fate-detection-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing whether VIA recovers both branches of a bifurcating lineage (e.g., Isl1+ progenitor to cardiomyocyte and endothelial fates) where SlingShot, Palantir, STREAM or Monocle3 merge or fragment lineages across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq and Seurat-integrated data.

name: fate-outcome-statistical-significance-testing
description: Use when PRESCIENT perturbation ensembles initialized from a defined starting population (e.g., day-0 cells) must be evaluated for statistically significant, magnitude-dependent shifts in endocrine vs exocrine or alpha vs beta fate fractions.

name: fate-probability-estimation-from-differentiation-potential
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (AnnData with 'cluster' annotations) covers a differentiation system with known terminal-fate marker genes (e.g. Target62, C5-TF1, D6-TF1) and no robust RNA velocity, so transition probabilities must be biased by differentiation potential.

name: favorable-hazard-ratio-bias-quantification
description: Use when bulk transcriptomic profiles with matched survival data are available and you need to test whether immune co-infiltration makes most cell types and immune marker genes appear prognostically favorable regardless of their anti-/pro-tumor function.

name: fclip-seq-dsrna-region-processing
description: Use when validating in silico dsRNA predictions against experimental J2 fCLIP-seq data, or when computing the fraction of captured dsRNAs overlapped by dsRID predictions (expected 73.3%, 7803 regions).

name: fdp-power-curve-visualization
description: Use when evaluating fine-mapping or colocalization methods on simulated loci with known causal variants (ground truth), to quantify the FDP-power trade-off across varying numbers of causal variants (q) and signal strengths (rho).

name: fdr-based-hit-calling-thresholding
description: Use when you have per-cluster pseudobulk differential state results (gene, cluster_id, logFC, p-value) from muscat::pbDS/edgeR and must declare significant hits, e.g. filtering the mouse cortex LPS dataset at FDR < 0.05 and |logFC| > 1.

name: fdr-calibration-plotting
description: Use when testing differential regulatory relations across two linked single-cell subpopulations and you need to check whether the Chi-square null for the LR statistic is well calibrated or a Gamma-fitted null gives better FDR control.

name: fdr-coefficient-filtering
description: Use when a CPPLS regression model has produced a coefficient matrix W of neighboring-cell-type effects on HVGs and statistically significant communication edges must be retained before k-means clustering or MIMO graph construction.

name: fdr-multiple-hypothesis-correction
description: Use when a gene-list query (e.g. 291 T1D or 229 RA DE genes) is tested against hundreds of gene modules simultaneously and raw Fisher/hypergeometric p-values must be FDR-adjusted before filtering significant modules.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-control-survival-genomics
description: Use when a regression analysis with survival or binary outcomes has high-dimensional genetic covariates (on the order of thousands of variables, e.g. ~9,548 mRNA entries) and the multiple-testing problem must be addressed before Ridge/Lasso/adaptive Lasso penalized regression.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when performing thousands of per-gene group comparisons (e.g. t-tests across all probes in a blood expression matrix) where module-level hits would otherwise be inflated, and a BH-FDR-adjusted p-value cutoff must be applied instead of raw p-values.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when calling significant sQTLs (or other high-multiple-testing association scans) from a nominal association pass over GTEx-style transcript-expression and genotype files, where per-test P-values must be converted to empirical, permutation-calibrated FDR values.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a per-feature hypothesis test (e.g., Wald test on Tweedie/CPLM/ZICP model coefficients) produces many p-values that must be FDR-adjusted to make differential-expression calls across genes or taxa.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when performing large-scale single-cell hypothesis testing (co-expression edges, DE, CRISPR screen P values, or pathway enrichment over network edges) where thousands to millions of simultaneous tests require explicit FDR or Bonferroni correction before calling significance.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when calling significant differential state (DS) or differential detection genes across many cell clusters/genes in multi-sample multi-condition scRNA-seq data, where per-gene p-values must be adjusted to control FDR before hit calling.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many statistical tests (e.g., Fisher's exact tests of resource-annotation enrichment across SignaLink, NetPath, CancerSEA terms) are run simultaneously and per-test p-values must be corrected before calling over-/underrepresentation.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when many TF perturbation simulations each yield a p-value and you must correct across all tested targets before calling significant hits (e.g., FDR < 0.01 plus log2FC > 0.5 in a 200+ TF screen).

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a DE analysis (limma on RNA-seq counts, e.g., ExpressAnalystR PerformDEAnal output) yields thousands of raw p-values and DEGs must be called at a defensible multiple-testing-adjusted threshold matching a reference publication.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when a per-gene test across many genes (e.g. 100-gene Lamian XDE/TDE permutation likelihood-ratio tests) yields raw p-values that must be corrected for multiplicity before calling genes at FDR.overall < 0.05.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-first-step-screening
description: Use when regression covariates number in the thousands to ~hundred thousand (TCGA mRNA entries or mutated genes), the multiple-testing problem is of concern, and variables must be screened before penalized regression.

name: fdr-multiple-testing-thresholding
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics DE method (C-SIDE, SPARK-X) returns per-gene p-values across many genes and cell types, and significant gene calls must be tabulated at a controlled FDR level such as 1%.

name: fdr-significance-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a differential expression or enrichment result table contains per-feature FDR-adjusted p-values and you must classify features as significant using a study-defined threshold (e.g., FDR < 0.1 for the salamander ortholog-level results).

name: fdr-threshold-gene-intersection
description: Use when comparing DS/DE method outputs across replicates to assess concordance of significant gene calls (p_adj < 0.05) and classify shared versus method-unique hits as true or false discoveries.

name: fdr-threshold-sweep-analysis
description: Use when comparing imputation methods (Bfimpute, scImpute, SAVER, VIPER, DrImpute, MAGIC) on a paired scRNA-seq/bulk dataset by measuring how imputation changes agreement between single-cell and bulk DE gene sets.

name: fdr-thresholded-credible-effects-interpretation
description: Use when scRNA-seq cell-type count tables per sample (e.g. from Scanpy) have been modeled with scCODA and you must decide which cell-type abundance changes survive FDR control, e.g. FDR 0.2 in the Salmonella/H. polygyrus SCP44 dataset.

name: fdr-thresholded-differential-expression-calling
description: Use when you have per-gene FDR result tables from RNA-seq mixed model fits (e.g. kimma lme/lmerel models) and need to define DEG sets at FDR < 0.05, or compare DEG detection between two model formulations.

name: fdr-thresholded-droplet-calling
description: Use when you need a model-based baseline droplet filter for raw 10X (CellRanger raw_feature_bc_matrix) snRNA-seq or scRNA-seq count matrices, or when comparing EmptyDrops calls to DIEM debris-score or quantile filtering on the same droplets.

name: fdr-thresholded-power-estimation
description: Use when simulations provide a known set of true DE genes and you must quantify detection power at a controlled FDR level (e.g., true FDR 5%) and compare methods.

name: fdr-thresholded-significance-calling
description: Use when Normalisr association outputs (gRNA-gene TSS-repression, trans-association, differential expression, or co-expression P values) must be filtered into significant hits using stated Q-value and logFC thresholds.

name: feature-dimension-sweep-cross-validation
description: Use when a fused feature matrix built from multiple sequence encodings (e.g., PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP) must be reduced by a filter criterion (F score, MRMD, PCC) and swept over candidate dimensions with cross-validated metrics to pick the smallest accurate feature subset.

name: feature-dimension-validation
description: Use when you have generated a position-specific (gapped) k-mer feature matrix from fixed-length 41-nt RNA sequences and must verify per-pattern-type feature counts and the total matrix width before model training.

name: feature-downselection-benchmark-design
description: Use when comparing computational scalability (wall-clock time) of dimension-reduction methods on scRNAseq count data, and you need a controlled design that fixes feature count (e.g., 1500 features) across benchmark datasets.

name: feature-importance-analysis
description: Use when a trained dsRID random-forest model on PacBio AD long-read RNA-seq regions (dsRID_data.tsv or /data/Pacbio_AD_data.tsv) needs feature importance ranking and cross-validation accuracy reported.

name: feature-importance-ranking-expression-features
description: Use when a trained CLOUDe classifier (e.g. Training.nn.2.classifier.hdf5) exists and you need to know which of the 18 expression features—derived (eD), survived (eS), or lost (eL) gene columns—drive the Redundant/Unique class discrimination.

name: feature-module-clustering-with-kmeans-plusplus
description: Use when you have a preprocessed cells x features single-cell matrix (.h5ad) and need to identify dynamically co-expressed feature modules that seed trajectory-preserving feature selection.

name: feature-ranking-intersection-analysis
description: Use when a ranked feature/gene list (e.g. Wx top genes by average DI score) must be compared against baseline gene sets such as Peng-14-UGCB, Martinez-7-UGCB, or edgeR DEG-14-UGCB to quantify gene-level agreement.

name: feature-selection-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when comparing high-dimensional regression methods on omics data where both predictive accuracy (out-of-sample MSE) and correctness of the selected gene subset matter, e.g. reproducing Figure 3-style semi-synthetic benchmarks.

name: feature-selection-benchmark-concordance-analysis
description: Use when determining the optimal number of DUBStepR-ordered feature genes for clustering scRNA-seq data, and for testing whether a label-free criterion (Density Index) agrees with label-based silhouette index across benchmark datasets.

name: feature-selection-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare filter feature-selection algorithms (e.g. RRCT, mRMR, CFS, CMIM, JMI, RELIEF, HITON) on the same data matrix and response, matching true feature sets or ranking them by downstream classifier performance.

name: feature-selection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing unsupervised feature selection methods for trajectory preservation in scRNA-seq or iterative immunofluorescence (4i) data with known ground truth labels (cell types, cell cycle phase, latent pseudotime).

name: feature-selection-leakage-bias-assessment
description: Use when validating a high-dimensional (P >> n) classification pipeline where a feature-selection filter precedes model fitting, to check whether reported accuracy is inflated by information leakage from the test set into the filter.

name: feature-selection-method-comparison
description: Use when the goal is to benchmark which gene/feature-selection method (e.g., E-test vs F-test vs M3Drop) yields the highest cell-classification accuracy, holding the classifier and train/test protocol fixed across methods and multiple labeled scRNA-seq datasets.

name: feature-selection-precision-recall-analysis
description: Use when comparing feature-selection quality of penalized or latent-factor regression methods on simulated data where the true nonzero coefficients are known and you need precision/recall or ROC curves.

name: feature-space-alignment-single-cell
description: Use when running SIMS label-transfer prediction on a query .h5ad dataset whose gene set differs in size or ordering from the genes the reference TabNet model was trained on.

name: feature-space-clustering
description: Use when clustering a large single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix where direct clustering on raw gene expression is computationally prohibitive, and reduced O(n) complexity via subsampling plus Spearman-correlation feature projection is desired.

name: feature-space-dimensionality-verification
description: Use when a milo pseudobulk object has been processed with vdjPseudobulk and you must confirm the resulting Feature_space assay has the expected genes-by-pseudobulks dimensions before PCA.

name: feature-space-normalisation-vdj-counts
description: Use when a miloR pseudobulk object has been processed with vdjPseudobulk and the raw V/D/J gene usage counts must be normalised into the Feature_space assay prior to runPCA and trajectory inference.

name: feature-subset-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when an scaLR-trained model on top-K features must be evaluated for DGE sensitivity, specifically when asked whether running dge_pseudobulk/dge_lmem on all samples rather than test samples changes DEG counts.

name: feature-subset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking how a co-expression or module-detection tool's runtime scales with the number of features: build nested gene/transcript subsets from a fixed-sample expression matrix (e.g., 100-sample ENCODE matrices, up to 16,000 genes or the full 96,000 transcripts).

name: feature-to-genome-coordinate-projection
description: Use when transcriptome elements (e.g. m6A sites, RNA-binding protein target sites from POSTAR3) are known only by genomic positions and the specific isoform they originate from is unclear.

name: feature-wise-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when you have a merged feature matrix (e.g. CRIT's MATRIX.txt) plus group labels (e.g. NMF cluster membership separating 90 predicted regulators from 916 other RBPs) and need to identify which features distinguish the two groups.

name: feed-forward-neural-network-training-keras
description: Use when training data with known cell-type labels exist and the Pearson correlation matrix over averaged K cell-type profiles has all off-diagonal values below tau = 0.95 (no highly correlated types).

name: ferroptosis-gene-role-annotation
description: Use when a list of in-silico knockout essential genes includes ferroptosis-related candidates (e.g. SLC3A2, SLC7A11, SLC7A5) and their FerrDb roles and KEGG pathway enrichment must be determined.

name: fetal-liver-hematopoiesis-trajectory-projection
description: Use when a query dataset (e.g., a 10x 5' fetal liver sample) must be positioned along a continuous reference-defined differentiation gradient — such as fetal liver hematopoiesis — instead of, or in addition to, per-cluster annotation transfer.

name: fgwas-genomic-annotation-modeling
description: Use when genome-wide GWAS summary statistics (P-values per SNP) are available together with a catalog of sQTLs and eQTLs, and the goal is to compare their GWAS enrichment per trait.

name: fibroblast-to-iep-reprogramming-data-analysis
description: Use when reprocessing the Biddy MEF-to-iEP reprogramming time course (or an analogous fibroblast-to-iEP scRNA-seq time course) to reproduce Figure 1F-style trajectory structure with manually annotated clusters and marker overlays.

name: fibrosis-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when analyzing spatial transcriptomics (e.g., Visium) sections from tissue undergoing fibrosis (e.g., post-myocardial-infarction heart) to determine whether senescence-burden spots colocalize with fibrotic regions and are spatially clustered.

name: fickett-score-coding-potential-scoring
description: Use when reconstructing LncDC feature extraction from H-Train-style mRNA/CDS/lncRNA FASTA inputs, or when needing an alignment-free coding-potential value per transcript to feed a coding/noncoding classifier.

name: figure-4-fraction-reproduction
description: Use when validating a network-based driver gene predictor by quantifying what fraction of its CGC-overlapping predictions are rarely-mutated (<0.05 SNV frequency) versus frequently-mutated across TCGA cancer types.

name: figure-reproduction-from-published-curves
description: Use when a published clustering paper claims a hyperparameter (e.g., a penalty ratio rho/lambda) is stable over an interval and you must verify that claim by sweeping the parameter on its original benchmark datasets.

name: filter-based-feature-selection-rank-correlation
description: Use when a data matrix plus response vector (e.g., fat datasets like Relathe 1,427×4,322 or SRBCT 63×2,308) needs ranked feature selection and out-of-sample classification performance assessment.

name: filter-feature-ranking-mrmd-pcc-fscore
description: Use when a fused high-dimensional sequence-encoding feature matrix (e.g., PSP + k-mer + PCPseDNC + PseEIIP for RNA modification data) must be ranked and reduced by filter selection, and when comparing F score vs MRMD vs PCC to pick the subset dimension.

name: filtered-cell-proportion-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking or auditing MUSIC-style preprocessing on single-cell CRISPR screening data and you need per-dataset QC-filtered and sgRNA-filtered cell proportions comparable to published Fig. 4a statistics.

name: filtering-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when two or more droplet/background-filtering methods (e.g., DIEM and EmptyDrops) must be compared on the same scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq count matrix to determine which retains dying/debris-contaminated droplets.

name: filtering-sensitivity-assessment
description: Use when a pipeline applies an automatic filtering step (e.g., dropping perturbations whose target gene is zero in all cells) and you must determine whether that filter materially alters the final rankings or is a minor edge-case removal.

name: fine-mapping-method-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying whether a multi-trait fine-mapping/colocalization method (e.g. CAFEH) improves power or FDP over CAVIAR, eCAVIAR, FINEMAP, or SuSiE under allelic heterogeneity in simulated loci.

name: fire-score-thresholding
description: Use when you have a continuous FiRE rareness score for every cell (np.array [nCells]) and need a binary rare-cell annotation per cell, because downstream validation or visualization (e.g., t-SNE overlay of detected rare cells) requires discrete 0/1 calls rather than raw scores.

name: fisher-combined-probability-testing
description: Use when per-individual (or per-replicate) ASAS p values must be merged into one event-level p value, or when a non-paired baseline is needed to benchmark a paired differential AS model such as PAIRADISE.

name: fisher-exact-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating Seurat-derived cluster marker lists (positive markers with avg_log2FC scores, Entrez-mapped) against CellMarker via easyct(test='fisher'), or when comparing Fisher vs GSEA annotation accuracy.

name: fisher-exact-cell-type-enrichment-analysis
