description: Use when the query input is a list of genes rather than an expression matrix — e.g., top-N cluster marker genes from Seurat FindAllMarkers, or trait-associated genes mapped from GWAS SNPs — and cell type membership must be tested for enrichment.

name: fisher-exact-co-infection-enrichment-testing
description: Use when two binary per-sample viral/infection status calls (e.g., IIV31 positivity and Trichomonas vaginalis positivity in TCGA-UCEC) must be tested for enrichment using an exact 2x2 test.

name: fisher-exact-contingency-table-testing
description: Use when two WGCNA/PyWGCNA co-expression networks from different datasets must be compared at the module level — i.e., you need to identify which module pairs share significantly more genes than expected by chance.

name: fisher-exact-contingency-testing
description: Use when testing a categorical association between CMScaller CMS class assignments (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2, CMS1 vs non-CMS1) and a binary phenotype (drug responder status, MSI status, BRAF mutation) across PDX, organoid, or cell line cohorts.

name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when comparing the composition of ligand-receptor sets from CCC resources against annotation terms (pathways, cancer genes, tissue-enriched proteins), or when testing whether top-ranked CCC interactions overlap significantly with active cytokines.

name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when validating a predicted gene/RBP set (e.g., an NMF cluster from CRIT's MATRIX.txt features) against a curated reference list such as gold_regulators.xlsx or POSTAR3/ENCORI CLIP-derived circRNA-binding RBPs via 2x2 overlap tests.

name: fisher-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when a fitted SSrGE model must be probed for subgroup-specific genotype markers — e.g., after separating normal vs. cancer cell indices, to find eeSNVs/genes significantly enriched in one subgroup (Fisher's exact test p < 0.05).

name: fisher-exact-pooled-read-testing
description: Use when simulating or benchmarking ASAS/differential splicing methods and a simple read-pooled baseline is needed to quantify the power gained by modeling replicates, particularly with injected outlier samples.

name: fisher-exact-proportion-enrichment-testing
description: Use when a gene set (e.g., DEGs from rank_genes_groups) must be tested for over-representation within a genomic annotation stratum (e.g., XClone-defined LOH vs non-LOH regions) using proportional counts and an exact test.

name: fisher-exact-test-differential-gene-enrichment
description: Use when you have imputed surface protein abundances (cTP-net output) that split one cell type into two subgroups, and you need to test whether the genes differential between those subgroups are enriched, e.g. CD56-high/CD16-low vs CD56-low/CD16-high NK cells.

name: fisher-exact-test-enrichment
description: Use when a per-cluster differential marker list (genes + cluster labels + expression scores such as logFC) needs to be converted into ranked cell-type annotations via overrepresentation testing against a marker database.

name: fisher-exact-test-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a binary gene-cluster absence/presence matrix plus per-genome lifestyle labels and need to find genes significantly enriched in one lifestyle group versus the rest.

name: fisher-exact-test-gene-set-enrichment
description: Use when the deCS query input is a list of genes — e.g., a top-N cluster marker gene table with 'cluster' and 'gene' columns or trait-associated genes — rather than a gene expression profile matrix.

name: fisher-exact-test-outlier-filtering
description: Use when running rROMA/Roma PC1-based gene set activity analysis on normalized expression matrices and needing to protect outlier-gene removal (leave-one-out L1 z-scores) from incorrectly excluding genes whose apparent outlier status is not specific to individual gene sets.

name: fisher-exact-toxicity-admissibility-testing
description: Use when implementing or simulating the TSNP two-stage dose-finding design and you must decide which dose levels are sufficiently safe (not overly toxic) to remain candidates for the OBD.

name: fisher-information-standard-error-estimation
description: Use when fitting per-gene Tweedie (Compound Poisson) GLMs to scRNA-seq counts and Wald-type standard errors, p-values, or confidence intervals are needed for regression coefficients after estimating (ϕ, p) by profile likelihood.

name: fisher-lda-gene-weight-estimation
description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq dataset has cluster-specific gene signatures and you need to weight those genes by discriminability before scoring target cells, especially with batch effect or imbalanced library sizes.

name: fisher-pvalue-combination
description: Use when a subpopulation-specific gene ranking must integrate expression evidence from scRNA-seq with enhancer-promoter contact evidence from bulk HiChIP loop counts, e.g. to improve GO enrichment of subpopulations at low sequencing depth.

name: fisher-r-to-z-network-weighting
description: Use when a directed/undirected reference network must be re-weighted from case-control high-throughput data (e.g., GSE172114 COVID-19 RNA-seq) so edge costs encode between-group correlation differences prior to Steiner tree or perturbation extraction.

name: fisher-scoring-optimization
description: Use when fitting a scDBM or negative-binomial count model to a scRNA-seq UMI count matrix and the per-gene inverse dispersion parameter θ needs to be estimated or periodically refreshed during training.

name: fisher-z-transformation-statistics
description: Use when you have two condition-specific FPKM expression matrices and a fixed reference network, and need to test whether each edge's Pearson correlation differs significantly between conditions.

name: fishers-exact-contingency-testing
description: Use when discrete, mutually exclusive counts form a 2x2 table needing an exact P-value — e.g. insertion-carrying vs wild-type reads split by intronic/exonic class at a SCISSOR-flagged junction, or co-altered gene counts between cohorts.

name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when comparing a set of cell-type co-localization pairs detected on reconstructed or predicted spatial coordinates against a reference set of supported co-localizations, to quantify concordance with a p-value.

name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when two sample groups yield sets of candidate regions (e.g., predicted dsRNA regions per sample) and you need to test whether the shared vs group-specific overlap fractions differ significantly between groups.

name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when a single-cell dataset has categorical clone assignments (e.g., mitochondrial clones from vireoSNP at probability >0.8) and independent cell labels (tumor vs non-tumor, CNV subclones) and you need to test enrichment of one clone in one label.

name: fishers-exact-enrichment-testing
description: Use when testing whether a lead variant set (e.g. sQTLs at FDR < 0.05) is enriched in discrete annotation categories relative to matched non-sQTLs or intron sets, and you need odds ratios with Fisher's exact p-values.

name: fishers-exact-receptor-association-testing
description: Use when you have predicted molecular subtype labels (e.g., from a DeepCC model via get_DeepCC_label) plus cohort clinical metadata with ER/PR/HER2 receptor status and survival outcomes, and need to demonstrate clinical relevance.

name: fitch-hartigan-small-parsimony-scoring
description: Use when you have a single-cell phylogeny (cells as leaves) plus cell-level categorical metadata and need a per-cell numeric score of plasticity/local state heterogeneity on the tree.

name: fitsne-visual-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have high-dimensional per-cell feature vectors (e.g., Miscell latent features from scRNA-seq data) and need a fast, reproducible 2D t-SNE embedding for visualization and cluster extraction.

name: five-fold-cross-validation-cell-subsampling
description: Use when you must quantify how a cross-modality translation model's performance degrades with limited paired training cells, or when testing whether data augmentation compensates for reduced sample size.

name: five-fold-cross-validation-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a graph-based driver-gene predictor (e.g., DGMP on DawnNet/KEGG/RegNetwork) with 5-fold CV and you need per-gene probability logits aggregated into mean±std AUPRC/AUROC across folds.

name: five-fold-cross-validation-partitioning
description: Use when comparing cross-modality translation methods on paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq datasets and a by-cell resampling design is needed so per-fold metrics can feed paired statistical tests (one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank).

name: five-fold-cross-validation-splitting
description: Use when a single labeled scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. PBMC SCP424) must be split into train/test subsets to benchmark supervised cell-type identification methods under self-projection, before computing accuracy, F1-score and unlabeling rate.

name: fixed-length-feature-vector-construction
description: Use when raw nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt m6A positive/negative samples from tissue-specific benchmark datasets like h_b, m_k, r_l) must be encoded as fixed-length numeric matrices before feeding a deep-learning model.

name: fixed-size-cell-shape-resizing-128x128
description: Use when segmented single-cell masks (e.g. from MIRIAM's membrane-extended segmentation) must be converted into uniform binary matrices to train or apply a deep learning-based cell shape descriptor.

name: flow-cytometry-marker-profile-analysis
description: Use when a static, unsynchronised flow cytometry dataset of a heterogeneous population (e.g. dissociated HCT116 spheroids stained for DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) must be mapped from pseudotime onto a real spatial (distance-from-surface) or temporal (cell age) scale.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: flow-cytometry-quality-gating
description: Use when raw FCS flow cytometry measurements (e.g. spheroid-derived HCT116 cells stained for DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27 and forward scatter) must be cleaned of doublets, dead cells and outliers before computing pseudotime ordering.

name: flow-network-trajectory-reconstruction
description: Use when snapshot single-cell RNA-seq data span multiple cell states (e.g., HSPC differentiation to erythroid, myeloid, and lymphoid lineages) and you need multi-lineage trajectories between user-chosen source and target subpopulations, plus transition-specific genes and regulators.

name: flow-network-transition-trajectory-inference
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq count data must be resolved into distinct lineage trajectories toward rare or underrepresented cell fates, especially when a branching method like Monocle 2 collapses two lineages onto one branch.

name: flowsom-clustering-of-cytof-data
description: Use when multi-sample IMC/CyTOF protein expression matrices and a manual cell-type annotation are available and you need sample-integrated, annotation-concordant clustering to quantify batch-removal benefit.

name: flux-balance-analysis-essentiality-scoring
description: Use when context-specific metabolic models of infected and healthy cells (e.g., rFASTCORMICS models with a VBOF) are available and you need to rank which gene knockouts reduce viral biomass without impairing host biomass.

name: flux-consistency-analysis
description: Use when a generic genome-scale reconstruction (e.g., Recon2.04, Recon3D_01 from VMH) — possibly augmented with a custom biomass reaction such as a viral biomass objective function (VBOF) — must be made flux-consistent before context-specific reconstruction.

name: flux-profile-clustering-umap-visualization
description: Use when per-sample reaction fluxes (e.g., METAFlux compute_flux output) are available and the goal is to discover metabolically coherent sample subgroups, visualize them in UMAP, and relate them to phenotypes like glucose uptake or survival.

name: fmeasure-precision-recall-scoring
description: Use when a predicted gene list (e.g., driver genes from WMDS.net) must be quantitatively compared against a benchmark gene set such as the 616-gene CGC list, and a precision-weighted Fβ score is the desired metric.

name: fold-change-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when two or more single-cell expression quantification tools must be benchmarked on simulated data against a known ground truth of cluster-marker TEs and their log2(FC) values.

name: fold-change-correlation-between-scrnaseq-clusters
description: Use when two or more scRNAseq datasets have been independently clustered (e.g., TIL, dLN, and acute viral Arm CD4+ T cells) and you need to identify which populations share transcriptomic profiles across datasets.

name: fold-change-count-transformation
description: Use when simulating bulk multi-omics count data with MOSim and you need to impose temporal DEG fold-change profiles on negative-binomial counts and couple regulatory-layer features to gene expression patterns.

name: fold-change-gene-ranking
description: Use when a Leiden/louvain cluster must be annotated by function and you need a compact, high-confidence gene list: rank Welch t-test DE results by log2 fold-change and keep the top 500 genes for enrichment analysis.

name: fold-change-qvalue-threshold-filtering
description: Use when assigning reproducible cell-cluster identities from scRNAseq differential expression output, e.g. selecting cluster-defining genes across LCMV1/LCMV2 replicates before naming clusters with curated T-cell markers.

name: fold-change-threshold-based-differential-expression
description: Use when analyzing human blood transcriptome expression matrices (e.g. SummarizedExperiment objects like GSE13015/EH5429) to classify each fixed BloodGen3 module as increased or decreased per group or per individual sample against a control reference.

name: fold-change-threshold-filtering
description: Use when comparing inferred cell abundance matrices between two sample groups (e.g., LUAD vs LUSC tumor samples) and you need a list of significantly and substantially shifted cell types meeting explicit FC and q-value cutoffs.

name: fold-change-threshold-parameterization
description: Use when comparing two experimental conditions against a common control with pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values (CSV with gene ID column), and you need to tune standard vs. extreme fold-change cut-offs and the p-value significance level before scorecard classification.

name: fold-enrichment-calculation
description: Use when a set of differentially expressed genes (e.g. from SCLC samples, cobalt-exposed rat liver cells, or a Seurat object) must be tested for over-representation in curated gene-environment modules, and fold enrichment with FDR-corrected significance is the required output.

name: force-directed-2d-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a single-cell or labeled expression matrix (CSV) already has discrete cluster assignments and you need a 2D visualization that integrates cluster membership with trajectory-like transitions between clusters (e.g. differentiation pathways).

name: force-directed-graph-layout-implementation
description: Use when a supervised 2D embedding must preserve both graph connectivity (knn and k_shift edges) and prior class labels, e.g. laying out a nearest-neighbor graph with Kamada-Kawai spring-energy minimization and class-confidence-contracted same-class distances.

name: force-directed-graph-layout-visualization
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (e.g., a 27,663-cell, 8-time-point scRNA-seq time course) has been partitioned with PAGA into clusters and you need a 2D embedding that draws both cells and cluster-level edges to visualize trajectory and dead-end structure with marker overlays.

name: force-directed-layout-embedding-visualization
description: Use when tGPT-derived feature embeddings and cell type annotations (e.g. AnnData objects loaded with Scanpy) must be ordered along developmental trajectories and the branch structure rendered as a trajectory visualization.

name: forced-dropout-robustness-testing
description: Use when you need to quantify the robustness and stability of cell clusters from SCASL AS profiles (or any clustering labels) under forced dropout or random cell sub-sampling, with a gene-expression comparator.

name: forecast-log-mse-error-analysis
description: Use when comparing forecast accuracy of single-network vs ensemble neural ODE predictions over recursive time steps, or when validating that forecast error stays within a bounded threshold over long horizons.

name: forecast-mse-benchmarking
description: Use when a forecaster's accuracy must be quantified against known future expression states — e.g., recursive predictions over BoolODE trajectories, comparing two forecasting variants, or testing whether KO forecasts degrade.

name: forensic-mixture-contributor-characterization
description: Use when scRNA-seq reads from a multi-person mixture have already been deconvoluted into per-individual cell clusters and each cluster must be assigned sex, maternal/paternal haplogroups, and ancestry fractions.

name: forensic-mixture-separation-validation
description: Use when validating or stress-testing a single-cell mixture deconvolution pipeline against in silico mixtures with known contributor ratios (e.g. 1:10–1:99) and ground-truth cell-to-individual labels.

name: forest-plot-visualization
description: Use when Cox regression results (single- or multi-variable, e.g., GSVA scores with clinical covariates) need to be visualized as a forest plot to judge which factors are independent prognostic factors.

name: forest-plot-visualization-across-traits
description: Use when per-trait fgwas annotation effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals (e.g. fgwas_sQTL_effect_sizes.csv) must be compared visually to show sQTL enrichment exceeding expression-only variants.

name: formula-verification-against-reference-implementation
description: Use when reproducing or validating a published scoring/ranking method: you have the paper's formula definitions, the reference package (e.g. MUSIC's Rank_overall/Rank_specific), and a shared test dataset (e.g. crop_stimulated).

name: foscttm-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating or tuning a diagonal integration method's shared latent embeddings: FOSCTTM quantifies cross-modality alignment by measuring each cell's nearest-neighbor agreement across modalities, e.g. when sweeping the unbalanced OT parameter m.

name: four-cluster-cell-partitioning
description: Use when preparing selected cells in a CellexalVR session for pseudotime trajectory calculation: slingshot analysis requires the selected cells to first be partitioned into exactly four clusters before pseudotime ordering.

name: four-dimensional-communication-tensor-construction
description: Use when you have per-sample/per-context LR communication scores from one or more CCC tools (e.g., CellChat, CellPhoneDB, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, cell2cell built-in) and need a 4D tensor input for Tensor-cell2cell factorization or cross-tool consistency checks.

name: fourier-inversion-density-evaluation
description: Use when fitting Tweedie (CPLM) or zero-inflated Tweedie (ZICP) models to scRNA-seq counts with the index parameter p constrained to (1, 2), where the Tweedie density is semi-continuous with a point mass at zero and its normalizing constant must be computed numerically.

name: fov-nuclei-image-stitching
description: Use when input nuclei images are separated into FOVs (e.g., NanoString CosMx Lung5-1 data) and a whole-section image is needed before model.segment_nuclei() in the BIDCell pipeline.

name: fpb-expression-normalization
description: Use when quantifying circRNA and cognate linear RNA expression from ribosomal-RNA depleted RNA-seq so both can be directly compared on a common scale, or when reproducing FPB/CIRCscore-based correlation or tissue-enrichment analyses.

name: fpkm-to-zfpkm-log-normalization
description: Use when normalized RNA-Seq FPKM expression matrices (e.g., TCGA KIRC/LIHC/PRAD protein-coding and long non-coding genes) must be reduced to actively expressed genes before building co-expression networks.

name: fragment-geometry-string-parsing
description: Use when single-cell FASTQ reads come from protocols whose barcode/UMI layout is not simple fixed-position (e.g. repeated barcode segments like b[16]...b[4], or 10x-style 1{b[16]u[12]x:}2{r:} geometry strings) and must be normalized before mapping.

name: freeman-tukey-residual-count-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., SingleCellExperiment objects) are overdispersed and you need a chi-squared-residual-based dimension reduction or multi-batch integration embedding that outperforms log-transform PCA.

name: frequency-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you have RSCanner structure counts (positions above BPC percentile cutoff and below Shannon entropy percentile cutoff) and need to visualize how structural content is distributed along the transcript.

name: frequent-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when building an EmptyNN-style classifier on a raw unfiltered scRNA-seq count matrix and you need a data-driven, ambient-informed gene subset (top frequent genes of empty droplets) instead of the full gene space.

name: fresh-versus-cryopreserved-sample-comparability-assessment
description: Use when deciding whether cryopreserved (frozen-thawed) PBMC or similar single-cell suspensions can be substituted for fresh specimens in droplet scRNA-seq profiling and cell-type classification, or when comparing two sample preparations for sequencing-depth-matched equivalence.

name: frobenius-norm-distance-metrics
description: Use when you must choose the optimal gene feature set size for single-cell clustering from a label-free curve, sweeping DUBStepR feature set sizes and comparing a label-free metric like the Density Index against the label-dependent silhouette index.

name: frobenius-norm-loss-minimization
description: Use when you have a weighted cluster interlacement adjacency matrix (CI-graph) from Spaco's DOI modeling plus a selected color palette, and need an optimal cluster-to-color mapping.

name: frozen-encoder-linear-probing
description: Use when a trained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder exists and cluster-specific marker genes must be recovered by quantifying per-gene influence on cluster predictions rather than by differential-expression testing.

name: ftest-model-comparison-statistics
description: Use when ranking candidate causal peak-gene pairs by Granger causal strength from paired scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq data on a cell-state DAG, or when quantifying forecasting improvement of a full model over a reduced model per candidate pair.

name: full-length-isoform-count-tabulation
description: Use when comparing bulk-mode short-read transcriptome assemblers on simulated or real genes (e.g. GYPC, MAPT, BIN1) and you need a per-gene, per-assembler tally of uniquely recovered full-length isoforms.

name: full-length-read-completeness-criteria
description: Use when filtering long-read (PacBio/ONT) alignments for ScISOrSeq analysis and you need to decide which reads have confirmed transcript boundaries before collapsing novel isoforms.

name: full-length-transcript-tar-annotation
description: Use when analyzing full-length Smart-seq2 (or similar plate-based paired-end) scRNA-seq from an organism with an incomplete genome annotation, and you need to detect cell-type-specific unannotated transcripts (uTARs) beyond the reference annotation.

name: fully-overlapped-antisense-pair-identification
description: Use when you have a CSV gene annotation with id, Chr, Strand, Start, End columns and need to classify opposite-strand overlaps as fully-overlapped (FO) cis-NAT pairs, e.g. reproducing the Xist/Tsix example.

name: functional-annotation-spreadsheet-curation
description: Use when you need to build or reproduce a consolidated per-module functional annotation table for a fixed transcriptional module repertoire, attaching a functional title to each module based on top-ranked enrichment terms.

name: functional-annotation-submission
description: Use when you have top-ranked genes (e.g., the top 100 SSrGE-ranked eeSNV genes per dataset) and need to identify enriched KEGG pathways and link genes to pathways in a bipartite network.

name: functional-concurrent-gene-network-construction
description: Use when time-course scRNA-seq data have been aligned into individual cell fate trajectories (e.g., via CellST smoothing) and the goal is to infer dynamic gene-gene regulatory relationships and critical genes along differentiation.

name: functional-concurrent-linear-model-estimation
description: Use when you have smoothed individual cell fate trajectories from time-course scRNA-seq and need to identify dynamic pairwise gene-gene relationships and critical genes across differentiation time.

description: Use when training tauFisher on a bulk transcriptomic time course (e.

name: functional-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a gene list from differential expression analysis (e.g. DEGs from a vote-threshold consensus across DEG methods) needs to be converted into overrepresented biological processes, such as ECM or basement membrane terms.

name: functional-enrichment-qvalue-interpretation
description: Use when a ranked or filtered gene list (e.g., top-correlated marker genes) needs functional interpretation via GO biological process enrichment with reported q-values, such as genes linked to latent features from dimension reduction.

name: functional-group-geometric-mean-aggregation
description: Use when computing ligand or target abundance for NeuronChatDB interaction entries (especially non-peptide neurotransmitters like glutamate or GABA) from per-group ensemble-averaged gene expression, when contributing genes must be combined across functional groups.

name: functional-homolog-gene-annotation
description: Use when KEGG KGML pathway files loaded into Cytoscape (KEGGScape) render only the first gene per multi-gene node, and the analysis goal is to surface all functionally homologous genes responsible for enzymatic reactions.

name: functional-module-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when raw cancer or drug-induced gene expression matrices must be converted into functional module activity scores before computing reversal scores (e.g., RSGSFM) against disease signatures.

name: functional-similarity-network-visualization
description: Use when a plant single-cell atlas contains clusters with unknown marker genes or unclear identity and you want to infer their cell type from GO-term enrichment profiles via topic modeling and a functional similarity network.

name: functional-spectra-computation
description: Use when raw gene-level expression matrices (rows = samples, columns = Entrez IDs) must be converted to pathway-activity features before training or applying a DeepCC classifier, or when classifying a single sample that requires a reference expression profile.

name: functional-spectra-interpretation
description: Use when a trained DeepCC model's deep features must be validated biologically: samples have CMS (or analogous) labels and you need to show deep-feature space is more compact than signature-gene space and that feature groups map to known subtype characteristics.

name: functional-spectrum-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw gene expression profiles (data.frame with Entrez-ID columns, one row per patient) must be converted into pathway-level feature vectors before training or applying a DeepCC cancer subtype classifier.

name: functional-topic-enrichment-annotation
description: Use when interpreting MUSIC topic model output from Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CRISP-seq data: after Get_topics()/Select_topic_number() have fit topics, to assign each topic a functional label via enrichment before computing perturbation impacts.

name: fusion-breakpoint-annotation
description: Use when Smart-Seq single-cell FASTQ files need fusion detection and breakpoint calling, and when fusion-bearing versus fusion-negative cells must be compared for oncogene overexpression (e.g. WHSC1 after IgH-WHSC1).

name: fusion-call-cross-reference-validation-ccle
description: Use when scRNA-seq fusion calls (e.g., from scFusion on Smart-Seq data) need benchmarking against known fusion catalogs (CCLE, TMPRSS2-ERG in prostate cancer) or when fusion positivity must be tested for association with a cell-level phenotype.

name: fusion-caller-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or comparing RNA-seq fusion callers on data with known ground-truth fusions, especially simulated single-cell datasets containing technical chimeric reads, to quantify precision/recall/F-score differences.

name: fusion-caller-performance-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a circRNA/fusion caller against a simulated RNA-Seq truth set, or when estimating a maximum achievable sensitivity ceiling (e.g. Acfs' 86.6% after excluding same-strand, same-chromosome gene-pair backsplices).

name: fusion-candidate-artifact-filtering
description: Use when screening raw STAR chimeric alignments from single-cell Smart-Seq data to remove artifact-driven fusion candidates and retain true fusions such as TCR V(D)J recombinations or recurrent IgH-WHSC1.

name: fusion-candidate-table-generation
description: Use when tumor RNA-Seq fastq reads are available as part of a neoantigen prediction workflow and gene fusion candidates must be identified to support downstream fusion-derived neoantigen calling.

name: fusion-gene-annotation-interpretation
description: Use when an INTEGRATE-Circ (or compatible BEDPE-style) fusion-caller output contains junction definitions for fcircRNAs and exon-level backsplice visualizations with cytoband context are needed for interpretation.

name: fusion-gene-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing fusion gene caller sensitivity across simulated or real paired-end RNA-seq data, especially when testing detection limits under progressive subsampling or shallow sequencing depth.

name: fusion-individual-level-weight-training
description: Decision support for benchmarking FUSION's individual-level training against summary-level OTTERS/PRS methods, or whenever individual-level genotype and expression reference data are available for TWAS Stage I weight estimation.

name: fusion-junction-primary-secondary-annotation
description: Use when a fusion caller produces multiple spanning-read clusters per candidate fusion and you must decide which junction is primary versus which represent alternative-splice or backsplice (fcircRNA) junctions, e.g. annotating INTEGRATE-Circ summary.tsv entries for a fusion like TMPRSS2::ERG.

name: fusion-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking fusion-gene detection sensitivity across tools on paired-end bulk or single-cell RNA-seq (e.g., Smart-seq2 FASTQs), especially when shallow depth or sequence homology suppresses de novo caller recall.

name: fusion-transcript-reference-construction
description: Use when benchmarking a fusion-detection tool (e.g., Anchored-fusion) and you need ground-truth test FASTQs containing reads spanning a known fusion junction embedded in realistic background RNA-seq data.

name: fuzzy-c-means-time-series-clustering
description: Use when you have a matrix of DTW-computed expression changes for L-R pairs across developmental time points and need to identify which interactions are active at a given stage (e.g., cluster 1 = E12.5 pluripotency-related interactions).

name: fuzzy-clustering-of-temporal-gene-expression
description: Use when you have L-R pair (or gene) expression changes across ordered developmental time points and need to group them into temporal expression clusters and identify the peak time point of each cluster.

name: g0-like-cell-detection
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset may contain quiescent G0-like cells that confound trajectory inference, and reCAT cell-cycle scores (G1, S, G1/S, G2, M, G2/M) are available for the cells.

name: g1-fraction-quantification-aging-hsc
description: Use when comparing cell-cycle phase distributions (especially G1 fraction) of stem-cell populations between conditions, e.g., young vs old LT-HSC scRNA-seq data, using unsynchronized single-cell transcriptomes.

name: g2m-cell-cycle-geneset-scoring
description: Use when scRNA-seq tumor cell data (e.g., GSE161529 TNBC count matrices) must be classified into dividing vs non-dividing cells via the G2M checkpoint gene set without clustering, to support pathway-associated comparisons such as TYRO3 expression.

name: galaxy-workflow-execution
description: Use when annotating plant miRNAs from a reference genome plus sRNA-Seq datasets (SRA accessions or FASTQ) and you need to chain database aggregation, prediction, selection, and curation steps in a reproducible web-based environment.

name: gam-based-pseudotime-expression-modeling
description: Use when cells have been ordered along a developmental trajectory (e.g., early CDP to late cDC2- or cDC1-committed preDC) and you need to identify distinct temporal waves of gene regulation from path-specific differentially expressed gene lists.

name: gamma-distribution-fitting-to-null-statistics
description: Use when testing differential regulatory relations between two linked single-cell subpopulations and the asymptotic Chi-square null for the likelihood-ratio statistic is suspected to be miscalibrated, i.e. empirical FDR exceeds nominal FDR.

name: gamma-distribution-quantile-fitting
description: Use when computing p-values and FDR for likelihood ratio statistics testing differential regulation across two linked subpopulations and the standard Chi-square null approximation fails.

name: gamma-normal-mixture-em-estimation
description: Use when estimating gene co-expression strength from sparse, zero-inflated single-cell count matrices where excessive zero counts make ordinary Pearson/Spearman correlations unreliable, and you need to separate low-confidence zeros from genuine expression.

name: gamma-normal-mixture-model-fitting
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) contains suspected dropout zeros and you need per-entry dropout probabilities to decide which values to impute rather than imputing everything.

name: gamma-poisson-count-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq batch-integration tools requires synthetic paired-batch count matrices with controlled batch strength, dropout rate, or batch-size imbalance rather than real data.

name: gan-architecture-implementation
description: Use when simulating single-cell RNA-seq data that must honor a user-provided causal gene regulatory network, or when implementing a CausalGAN-derived generator with masked connectivity from a pickled causal graph.

name: gan-based-cross-modal-data-alignment
description: Use when two discrete single-cell datasets measuring different modalities (scRNA-seq, spatial transcriptomics, proteomics) of related samples must be mapped into each other's feature space while retaining per-sample correspondence, not just distribution-level similarity.

name: gan-based-cross-modality-alignment
description: Use when integrating two single-modality single-cell datasets (e.g. scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) profiled on different cells with no shared features, and an unsupervised joint embedding is needed.

name: gan-generator-loss-regularization
description: Use when training a GAN to map between separately measured single-cell modalities and the adversarial loss alone leaves the generator over-parameterized — enforce geometry preservation via the λc-weighted correspondence term.

name: gan-training-loop-implementation
description: Use when training a GAN-based single-cell modality alignment model (e.g. scMMGAN) and you need to structure the alternating generator/discriminator optimization session loop with periodic loss monitoring.

name: gan-training-loss-monitoring
description: Use when training an scGAN/cscGAN model on .h5/.h5ad scRNA-seq data in TensorFlow and you need to verify stable adversarial convergence (via loss curves) before generating cells or accepting t-SNE validation plots.

name: gan-training-on-scrna-seq-data
description: Use when a scRNA-seq population (e.g. an erythrocyte cluster of 150 cells in GSE72857 bone marrow data) has been downsampled or is too sparse, and you need to generate matched synthetic cells in .h5ad format to restore pseudo-time/PAGA graph structure or improve classifier robustness.

name: gan-training-on-single-cell-data
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (.h5/.h5ad, e.g. Fresh 68k PBMCs Donor A or a 1.3M-cell mouse brain dataset) must be augmented or realistic cells must be generated in silico, either unconditionally or conditioned on cell type.

name: gap-distance-score-computation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. 4491 non-irradiated intestinal crypt cells) must be scanned for rare cell types, and you need to compute the nearest-neighbour distance profile and second-order derivative gap score to nominate candidate rare-cluster sizes k.

name: gap-penalty-scoring-design
description: Use when designing or reimplementing the scoring function for aligning branched pseudotime trajectory trees (or any bounded-degree unordered rooted labeled trees) via tree-alignment dynamic programming, and you must define match costs and deletion/insertion penalties.

name: gapdh-housekeeping-normalization
description: Use when comparing single-cell expression distributions (e.g., Gini coefficients) between platforms like Drop-seq and RNA FISH, and a shared housekeeping gene (GAPDH) is available to control for cell-level sampling depth differences.

name: gapped-kmer-svm-sequence-classification
description: Use when the goal is to test whether sQTLs alter splicing by modifying RNA-binding protein binding sites, quantified as differences in |deltaSVM| between sQTLs and non-sQTL variants.

name: garnett-pretrained-classifier-annotation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation accuracy on PBMC scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth labels and a pre-trained Garnett classifier is available for the tissue.

name: gatk-rnaseq-variant-recalling
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQs (e.g., chicken SRP058295/SRP255211 samples) need per-sample variant calls in g.vcf format for downstream ASE analysis, or when reference allele bias must be reduced by re-calling variants against a masked genome.

name: gatk-variant-calling-pipeline
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., paired-end broiler samples from SRA SRP058295/SRP255211) need variant calls in VCF/g.vcf format to support downstream per-sample ASE or genotype-concordance analyses.

name: gaussian-affinity-estimation
description: Use when you have a high-dimensional data matrix (e.g. mnist2500_X.txt) plus data/null 2D t-SNE or UMAP embeddings and need a local, per-cell measure of how faithfully each cell's neighborhood survives embedding.

name: gaussian-convolution-imputation-for-sparse-contact-maps
description: Use when raw single-cell Hi-C contact matrices (N*N dat_HiC) are too sparse for differential testing and a bias-aware normalized count matrix is needed before scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB detection.

name: gaussian-graphical-model-inference-large-scale
description: Use when a log-normalized single-cell gene expression matrix with >5000 cells needs partial-correlation (GGM) co-expression network inference, or when benchmarking SingleCellGGM against pcor-based methods like ppcor and SILGGM on an identical input matrix.

name: gaussian-graphical-model-penalized-estimation
description: Use when a single-cell read-count matrix must be turned into a sparse, undirected gene co-expression network that separates direct gene-gene dependencies from indirect ones, and standard Pearson/Spearman correlations plus plain glasso are unreliable due to excessive zero counts.

name: gaussian-graphical-model-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking gene co-expression network inference methods on synthetic data where the ground-truth adjacency matrix must be known, especially for sparse scRNA-seq-like data with simulated dropouts.

name: gaussian-hmm-baum-welch-training
description: Use when a single-cell WGS analysis must pick a data-driven bin size before segmentation: specifically, when gHET calls phased by SHAPEIT2 are available and the amplification assay's ADO length distribution must be measured to set the minimum resolvable CNA bin.

name: gaussian-kernel-affinity-computation
description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix (N cells x D genes) must be converted into a probabilistic neighborhood graph or Markov transition matrix as the substrate for diffusion/random-walk based analyses such as RWR, diffusion pseudotime, or trajectory inference.

name: gaussian-kernel-nearest-neighbor-graph
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g. 438 cells x 48 genes) must be converted into a Markov transition matrix as input to diffusion-based manifold learning such as BKFD or diffusion pseudotime.

name: gaussian-kernel-reference-distribution-on-grid
description: Use when computing per-gene differential expression significance from cell positions in a multidimensional space (t-SNE, PCA, spatial or pseudotime coordinates) without clustering cells.

name: gaussian-kernel-spatial-smoothing
description: Use when you have ST spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv from the Figshare deposit DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.24452812) and need the normalized adjacency matrix that serves as STEM's prediction goal for spot-level spatial relationships.

name: gaussian-likelihood-scoring-of-clusters
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics clusterings must be ranked without ground-truth labels, e.g. to pick the alpha/beta configuration by the goodness score v(y,Cα) instead of ARI.

name: gaussian-mixture-ambient-noise-modeling
description: Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) counts from CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq where ambient unbound-antibody noise and cell-level technical noise must be removed before clustering or differential expression.

name: gaussian-mixture-cell-classification
description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset with cluster-specific gene signatures and weights (e.g., from scID_weight) is available and unlabeled target cells must be assigned to reference clusters from per-cell signature scores.

name: gaussian-mixture-clustering-of-surface-protein-markers
description: Use when CITE-seq data provides surface-protein ADT levels for markers (e.g., CD16/CD56) whose RNA is dropout-obscured, and you need protein-derived sub-population labels to quantify or benchmark RNA-based (or denoised) recovery of that structure.

name: gaussian-mixture-denoising-of-adt-data
description: Use when normalizing droplet-based protein (ADT) data from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq where ambient antibody noise and cell-to-cell technical variation confound protein values and raw/CLR values track empty-droplet signal.

name: gaussian-mixture-em-decoupling
description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq cell-by-gene matrices where perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups have differing cluster proportions, so naive fold-change estimation is distorted by infected proportion bias and the true cellular response must be decoupled.

name: gaussian-mixture-em-fitting
description: Use when quantifying extranuclear RNA contamination per droplet in droplet-based snRNA-seq: the percent of reads spliced is bimodal with nuclear and background droplets straddling ~50%, and a sample-specific midpoint separating the two distributions must be estimated per experiment.

name: gaussian-mixture-fitting-of-hashtag-distributions
description: Use when demultiplexing cell hashing experiments and per-hashtag cutoffs must distinguish true positive from background signal, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-clustering-of-gene-expression-pcs
description: Use when expert-provided scribble annotations are unavailable and you need an initial non-spatial domain labeling of Visium or ST spots from principal components of raw gene expression as input to automated scribble generation.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-clustering-of-single-cell-transcriptomes
description: Use when you need to partition unsynchronized single-cell transcriptome data (e.g. log2(TPM+1) cycle-base-gene expression) into a user-defined number of clusters k before reconstructing a pseudo time-series.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-em-estimation
description: Use when scCRISPR-seq perturbation vs control groups differ in cluster proportions (infected proportion bias) and you need per-gRNA cellular responses decoupled from that bias on selected infection-biased PCs.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting
description: Use when a user-supplied CSV gene-expression data frame (gene identifiers plus log-fold-change values) must be partitioned into distinct expression-pattern clusters using unsupervised, probability-based Gaussian mixture modelling.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting
description: Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in a single-cell CRISPR screen and per-guide UMI count distributions must be split into endogenous vs ambient components without a user-defined fixed UMI threshold.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-fitting-per-cell
description: Use when normalizing CITE-seq/ASAP-seq/TEA-seq ADT data with dsb step II, or when validating that k=2 Gaussian mixtures fit per-cell protein distributions via BIC.

name: gaussian-mixture-model-subclone-separability
description: Use when comparing how accurately different cell-cycle correction methods (Cyclum, Seurat, ccRemover, PC1–5) preserve or recover subclone structure in scRNA-seq data containing two known subpopulations.

name: gaussian-mixture-rejection-threshold-fitting
description: Use when binarized scRNA-seq marker counts per cell type show a bimodal distribution and a defensible cutoff is needed to label clusters as 'unassigned' (unknown) rather than force an annotation.

name: gaussian-mixture-reliability-modeling
description: Use when transferring labels from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq and you must decide per-cell which target cells can safely be merged into the annotated source during iterative integration.

name: gaussian-mixture-simulation-on-unit-circle
description: Use when benchmarking clustering algorithms on non-convex synthetic shapes (rings, half-moons) where ground-truth labels are available and purity scores against GMM, K-means, DBSCAN, OPTICS, or spectral clustering baselines are required.

name: gaussian-mixture-technical-component-denoising
description: Use when ADT/protein counts have already been ambient-corrected against empty droplets and residual cell-to-cell technical noise (correlated with isotype controls and background mean) must be regressed out before clustering or UMAP.

name: gaussian-mixture-umi-threshold-fitting
description: Use when assigning gRNAs to cells in single-cell CRISPR screens whose per-gRNA UMI distributions vary widely (low vs high UMI experiments), where a fixed min_umi threshold over- or under-assigns cells; triggered by UMI-histogram bimodality or inter-experiment differences in average gRNA UMIs.

name: gaussian-noise-perturbation-of-scrnaseq-data
description: Use when you need to quantify the noise robustness of a single-cell trajectory inference or alignment pipeline by sweeping Gaussian noise levels on synthetic scRNA-seq data and recording performance-metric distributions per noise level.

name: gaussian-process-length-scale-estimation
description: Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Visium DLPFC counts plus coordinates) must be screened for SVGs whose spatial expression ranges differ, or when per-gene length scale parameters are the analysis target.

name: gaussian-process-regression-3d-expression-modeling
description: Use when consecutive ST slices have been 3D-aligned by Scube (e.g., the STARmap mouse brain dataset) and you need to model continuous gene-expression surfaces in 3D and identify spatially varying genes via Bayes Factor scoring.

name: gaussian-rbf-kernel-regression
description: Use when noisy per-cell scVelo RNA velocity must be aggregated to a lower-resolution representation (meta-cells) and smoothed via regression on averaged spliced expression before trajectory graph construction.

name: gbm-ensemble-refitting
description: Use when a prior chord() run's saved objects (seu.robj, sce.robj, overkilled.robj) exist and additional external doublet detector scores should be integrated into a refit GBM ensemble for improved doublet calls.

name: gc-bias-amplification-modeling
description: Use when simulating Nanopore single-cell/spatial long-read FASTQ from a known cell-by-isoform matrix and you need realistic GC-dependent amplification, truncation, and error profiles to benchmark isoform quantification accuracy.

name: gc-bias-correction-evaluation
description: Use when preprocessing scWGS read-depth data for CNA calling, or when benchmarking CNA callers whose segmentation shows bin-level read-depth trends correlated with GC content, e.g. CHISEL-preprocessed 100 kb RDR.

name: gc-bias-read-depth-normalization
description: Use when preparing raw single-cell (or paired bulk) WGS BAMs for read-depth-based CNA calling and GC-biased depth must be corrected before segmentation, e.g. as the normalize step of a HiScanner pipeline.

name: gc-content-background-normalization
description: Use when scoring DNA sequences against a nucleotide position weight matrix (e.g., core promoter motifs like those in ElemeNT) and the user's sequence has a known GC fraction, so background nucleotide frequencies must be GC-normalized before log-odds scoring.

name: gc-content-calculation
description: Use when building position-specific k-mer feature vectors from fixed-length (41-nt) RNA sequences for 5hmC site prediction and a per-sequence GC-content descriptor is required as an additional feature block.

name: gc-content-frame-feature-engineering
description: Use when encoding transcript FASTA sequences (lncRNA vs PCT classification) and GC-composition descriptors are needed as classifier inputs, e.g. feeding CatBoost-style models like LncCat.

name: gcf-absence-presence-matrix-construction
description: Use when you need BGC-level absence/presence features across a genome set — e.g. after annotating genomes with Prokka and predicting BGCs with antiSMASH, to feed downstream lifestyle or comparative analyses.

name: gcf-presence-absence-fisher-testing
description: Use when you have a GCF absence/presence matrix (e.g., from BiG-SCAPE at 0.70 distance) plus binary lifestyle labels and need to rank BGC families significantly enriched in one lifestyle group.

name: gcn-biological-assessment
description: Use when an inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) has been produced (e.g. for breast or prostate cancer expression data) and its performance must be measured via overlap analysis, topological assessment, and biological assessment using GNIAP.

name: gcn-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when a semi-supervised GCN (e.g. scSHARP EdgeConv label propagation) must be tuned on scRNA-seq data with a set of confident consensus labels and you need the -validation-accuracy architecture recorded per dataset.

name: gcn-interaction-model-training
description: Use when you need to train DeepCCI's interaction model on processed ligand-receptor pair features and verify its generalizability for identifying significant CCIs via cross-validation metrics.

name: gcn-neuron-targeted-attribution
description: Use when a trained scSHARP GCN model must be interpreted at the feature level — e.g. to recover which genes drive classification of specific cell types (CD8 T Cells, testis spermatogenic stages) after label propagation.

name: gcn-overlap-analysis
description: Use when an inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) needs its performance measured, and agreement with reference co-expression edges, network topology, and biological relevance of modules must be quantified.

name: gcn-topological-assessment
description: Use when a previously inferred gene co-expression network (GCN) needs its performance measured via topological assessment as part of the GNIAP overlap/topological/biological evaluation pipeline.

name: gencode-annotation-filtering
description: Use when building a pseudoalignment target (UTRome) from a GENCODE or other GTF/GFF annotation and transcripts must be restricted to protein-coding features with verified 3' ends before truncation.

name: gencode-transcript-3prime-end-window-parsing
description: Use when building or validating a cleavage site (CS) catalog from 3′-end scRNA-seq data and you need GENCODE-annotated transcript 3′ end coordinates as reference intervals for overlap-based classification.

name: gencode-transcript-annotation-matching
description: Use when comparing de novo isoform assemblies (e.g. cloudrnaSPAdes, rnaSPAdes, Trinity, RNA-Bloom) by counting uniquely assigned GENCODE annotated isoforms per gene from IsoQuant assignment output files.

name: gene-absence-presence-matrix-modeling
description: Use when you have binary gene cluster absence/presence matrices plus literature-based lifestyle labels and need to train lifestyle classifiers or predict lifestyles of genomes from species with no representative in the training set.

name: gene-accessibility-aggregation-from-atac-peaks
description: Use when matched peak-level scATAC-Seq counts must be summarized to per-gene accessibility (3kb-upstream+gene-body aggregation around RNA-defined marker genes) to validate primed states or compare chromatin opening across cell groups.

name: gene-activity-score-integration
description: Use when snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq come from unpaired samples and you need a shared low-dimensional representation before cell pairing or downstream GRN inference; the ATAC assay must be converted to a gene activity matrix.

name: gene-age-class-count-summarization
description: Use when you already have a gene-to-gene-age-class orthomap table for a focal species (e.g. from oggmap of2orthomap on OrthoFinder output) and need per-age-class gene counts for quality checking or downstream plotting.

name: gene-age-class-relative-expression-normalization
description: Use when a TEI-annotated AnnData (h5ad) with gene age class annotations is available and you need a table of relative expression shares per gene age class per observation group (cell type, timepoint).

name: gene-age-orthomap-matching
description: Use when an AnnData/scRNA object must be annotated with per-gene evolutionary ages (an orthomap) before computing a transcriptome evolutionary index (TEI), e.g. reproducing hourglass or young-gene-peak patterns across embryo stages.

name: gene-age-weighted-expression-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq AnnData objects need an evolutionary age metric (TEI or partial TEI profiles) per cell, especially for large datasets (~90,000+ up to 1e6 cells) where per-cell computation must stay tractable.

name: gene-alteration-proportion-zscoring
description: Use when building the CRIT feature matrix for candidate genes and you have per-sample TCGA mutation (data_mutations_extended.txt) and CNV (data_CNA.txt) files that must be dichotomized into per-gene alteration proportions and Z-scored.

name: gene-annotation-gtf-processing
description: Use when preparing a reference for splicing-status prediction of scRNA-seq reads: you have a gene annotation GTF and matching genome FASTA and need an augmented spliced+unspliced transcriptome (spliceu.gtf, spliceu.fa, t2g_3col.tsv).

name: gene-annotation-overlap-classification-of-tars
description: Use when you have groHMM-predicted TAR BED files from scRNA-seq alignments and need to partition them into aTARs vs uTARs relative to a refFlat annotation, or quantify the fraction of reads assigned to uTARs.

name: gene-ase-profile-class-verification
description: Use when per-cell allelic state posteriors (P/B/M) from a beta-binomial mixture on F1-hybrid scRNA-Seq cells are available and genes must be assigned to seven ASE profile classes and validated.

name: gene-barcode-matrix-harmonization
description: Use when comparing gene-barcode matrices from two scRNA-seq processing pipelines (e.g., UniverSC vs Cell Ranger/dropSeqPipe/CogentAP/zUMIs) before correlation, clustering, or integration analysis.

name: gene-barcode-matrix-reconstruction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQ/BAM reads (e.g. from SRA SRP073767 or 10x datasets site) must be converted into gene-cell-barcode matrices, or when matrices from different preparations must be regenerated under identical counting settings before comparison.

name: gene-based-association-result-processing
description: Use when Stage II TWAS output from testing.py (per-gene Z-scores from five eQTL-weight training models) must be calibrated via genomic control so median test p values equal 0.5 before ACAT-O aggregation.

name: gene-biomarker-survival-association-testing
description: Use when TCGA-style gene expression matrices are paired with patient survival metadata (vital status, days to death, days to follow-up) and candidate gene sets (e.g., Extracted/IC_<tumor>.csv vs DE genes) must be screened for significant survival association and compared by Concordance statistic.

name: gene-body-coverage-bias-verification
description: Use when RNA-seq BAM files from multiple tissue groups (e.g. broiler liver, abdominal fat, breast muscle) must be checked for systematic gene-body coverage bias before variant or expression analyses.

name: gene-body-coverage-computation
description: Use when you have per-cell BAM files split from a 10x Genomics barcoded BAM and need normalized gene body coverage profiles (100 values per cell) as input to SkewC quality assessment.

name: gene-body-coverage-data-loading
description: Use when starting the SkewC R Markdown analysis chain on gene body coverage output (e.g. coverage.r) and a compact per-cell percentile-coverage matrix (Coverage_means_DF) is needed for plotting or trim clustering.

name: gene-body-coverage-skewness-classification
description: Use when you have per-cell gene body coverage data (Coverage_means_DF_Clust derived from coverage.r in the SkewC workflow) and need to partition cells into typical vs. skewed groups for quality filtering.

name: gene-category-expression-profiling
description: Use when a per-gene scalar metric (e.g. nucleotide diversity, Tajima's D, F-statistics) is available and you want a cell-level weighted expression index using those bins as weights in place of evolutionary gene age classes.

name: gene-cell-nonzero-fraction-filtering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. h5 expression files for the scGCL pipeline) must be quality-controlled before normalization and graph construction, and a scGNN-style >1% non-zero expression filter is the desired gene/cell exclusion criterion.

name: gene-centric-sparse-storage
description: Use when a large single-cell expression matrix (AnnData/H5AD) must be persisted in a relational database so per-gene and per-cell-type expression queries run efficiently server-side.

name: gene-cluster-absence-presence-matrix-generation
description: Use when starting from quality-filtered bacterial genome FASTAs and needing a gene-cluster-by-genome binary matrix as the foundation for pan-genome analyses or lifestyle-associated gene (LAG/pLAG) prediction.

name: gene-co-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a gene-expression or feature table (e.g., GTEx Gene-Tissue Expression data) needs to be queried for which features correlate with one prime feature, with coefficients and p-values for each.

name: gene-co-expression-correlation-computation
description: Use when two FPKM-normalized expression matrices (rows=gene symbols, columns=sample ids) for two physiological conditions are available and differential co-expression edges between gene pairs must be quantified and significance-tested.

name: gene-co-expression-network-construction
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 38 3xTg-AD/WT female hippocampus samples across three ages) and need to identify co-expression modules correlated with traits such as genotype or age.

name: gene-co-expression-network-inference
description: Use when raw gene expression data (e.g. breast or prostate cancer expression matrices) must be turned into a weighted gene co-expression network and the resulting GCN's performance needs to be assessed via overlap, topological, and biological criteria.

name: gene-co-expression-network-inference
description: Use when you have a raw UMI count matrix from a defined cell population (e.g. dysfunctional CD8+ T cells from MARS-seq melanoma, GSE123139) and want gene-level co-expression edges that recapitulate known functional annotations.

name: gene-co-expression-network-pruning
description: Use when edge-weighted gene co-expression adjacency matrices (normal/cancer conditions per cancer type) are too dense for downstream fusion or community detection and must be pruned to their backbone.

name: gene-co-expression-robustness-half-sampling
description: Use when comparing gene network inference methods (e.g., scLink, PIDC, GENIE3) for edge-stability across cell subsamples and for wall-clock runtime/memory on matched scRNA-seq inputs.

name: gene-coexpression-network-degree-analysis
description: Use when you have constructed gene co-expression (or differential co-expression) networks and need to validate their topology as approximately scale-free before downstream hub/driver-node analyses.

name: gene-coexpression-network-hub-derivation
description: Use when deriving cell-type-specific senescence (or age-dynamic) gene signatures from aggregated single-cell RNA-seq spanning multiple tissues and ages, requiring weighted hub gene lists rather than simple marker lists.

name: gene-coexpression-network-inference
description: Use when filtered RNA-seq expression data from stress conditions (e.g., soybean tissues infected with C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi) must be converted into a coexpression network for downstream gene-module and candidate-gene mining.

name: gene-community-modularity-detection
description: Use when you have a fused gene co-expression network (e.g., Gephi-format .gexf from the GeneNetFusion pipeline) and need to partition genes into communities for biomarker extraction.

name: gene-count-frequency-summarization
description: Use when scorecard single-quadrant analyses have been run for multiple comparisons (e.g., VAN/CPT/DEL/LZD vs untreated in S. aureus dataset 1) and you need a tabulated count of genes per quadrant per comparison.

name: gene-database-label-extraction
description: Use when a list of candidate HVGs (e.g. from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scannpy, M3drop) must be classified as communication-related or not, using database-derived gene tags as the labeling criterion.

name: gene-degree-ranking-baseline-comparison
description: Use when you must reproduce or benchmark an ablation of a network driver-gene method against degree-only and unweighted baselines, scoring each list against a curated benchmark like the 616-gene CGC set.

name: gene-deletion-class-prediction
description: Use when you have a space-delimited expression file (N+1 rows, 3m columns: eD1-eDm, eS1-eSm, eL1-eLm) for gene deletion events and need to classify each event as 'Redundant' or 'Unique'.

name: gene-detection-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a raw digital gene expression matrix (e.g., Cell Ranger output UMI counts) has not been filtered or normalized, signaled by indication='none' in scTITANS_full, and a cleaned, normalized matrix is needed before trajectory inference.

name: gene-dropout-probability-thresholding
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix (csv) from scRNA-seq contains dropout zeros — genes observed at moderate expression in some cells but undetected in others — and only high-confidence dropouts should be imputed without altering unaffected values.

name: gene-drug-interaction-mapping
description: Use when a trait- or cell-type-associated co-expression module or GRN (e.g. the M11 network with TFs GATA2, MAFF, FOSB) has already been inferred and needs to be linked to repurposable drugs through drug-target interaction databases.

name: gene-embedding-cosine-neighbor-ranking
description: Use when a trained GeneVector embedding (genes.vec) is available and you must rank a query gene's nearest neighbors by cosine similarity to confirm pathway co-membership or seed a metagene.

name: gene-embedding-entropy-ranking
description: Use when trained graph-embedding outputs (e.g., DGMP logits and ZF, Zin, Zout, ZMLP vectors) are available and you need to isolate genes with dissimilar neighbors to diagnose embedding class separation.

name: gene-embedding-learning
description: Use when constructing cell-lineage-specific gene embeddings from scRNA-seq data and a prior gene interaction network, e.g. inputs to downstream driver-regulator or RGM analysis.

name: gene-environment-module-annotation
description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed human genes (from microarray, bulk RNA-seq, or a clustered Seurat single-cell object) and want to test which curated environmental gene modules (infection, diet, cigarette smoking, toxic chemicals) are statistically over-represented.

name: gene-expression-baseline-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking whether incorporating VDJ features into trajectory inference yields higher fate-prediction accuracy than expression-only trajectory analysis, e.g. on fetal immune atlas DP-to-CD4/CD8 T-cell data.

name: gene-expression-biclustering
description: Use when the input is a continuous (or discretized) gene expression matrix and the goal is to discover overlapping trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters and compare them against planted ground truth or other algorithms.

name: gene-expression-binarization
description: Use when preprocessing sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices (e.g. Xin GSE81608) to build a binary low-dimensional representation of cells, where dropouts must be handled as signals rather than imputed away.

name: gene-expression-binning
description: Use when you have null (e.g., gRNA-free or split-group) P values from single-cell DE or co-expression testing and need to check P-value uniformity across expression levels via expression-stratified KS tests.

name: gene-expression-binning-from-bulk-replicates
description: Use when matched bulk RNA-seq replicates and a single-cell count matrix are available and you need to partition genes by bulk expression level (true-zero silent genes vs. expressed bins) to test whether an imputation method retains biological zeros while imputing dropouts.

name: gene-expression-clinical-variable-correlation
description: Use when whole-blood gene expression measurements and matched per-sample clinical laboratory values (e.g. CRP, lymphocyte counts, IFN scores) are available and you need to test whether gene abundance is linearly associated with disease-severity markers.

name: gene-expression-clustering
description: Use when a CSV gene-expression data frame with gene identifiers and log-fold-change (LFC) values must be partitioned into distinct expression-pattern clusters with per-gene membership probabilities.

name: gene-expression-clustering-and-go-enrichment
description: Use when a Lamian lamian_test run has produced significant TDE or XDE genes (FDR.overall < 0.05) and you need to organize them into expression-dynamics clusters and interpret each cluster via GO enrichment.

name: gene-expression-cohort-aggregation
description: Use when building a subtype reference for PAM50-style classification from multiple subtype-labeled RNA-seq cohorts and the goal is a cohort-composition-independent centroid table (e.g. matching Supplementary Material Table S3).

name: gene-expression-contour-overlay-on-tsne
description: Use when a pooled t-SNE embedding of scRNAseq clusters needs annotation with expression contours of marker genes (e.g. Cd4, Cd8a) to identify compartment or lineage identity of clusters.

name: gene-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix (imported from H5AD into Cellenium's PostgreSQL backend) is loaded for one study and you need to find all genes whose expression is highly correlated to a query gene, transcriptome-wide, within that study.

name: gene-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a bulk expression matrix (e.g. TCGA AML) and a subclone-associated gene list from scRNA-seq (e.g. GATA2R361C subclone) must be linked to test whether a marker gene like VIM defines a co-expressed regulon.

name: gene-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing gene-gene correlation landscapes between an original measurement domain and a cross-modality mapping (e.g., scMMGAN spatial output), to flag spurious correlations and surface novel candidate associations like SLC2A1–P2RX7.

name: gene-expression-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when two gene-matching approaches (e.g. protein-embedding distance and BLAST hits) disagree for a set of ortholog candidates and raw count scRNA-seq data is available to score candidates by expression correlation.

name: gene-expression-csv-formatting
description: Use when preparing cross-platform transcriptome data (e.g., GEO series such as GSE151189 or GSE59098) for ingestion by Ciclops, whose --train_path/--valid_path inputs must be .csv files with sample names as the first column and labels as the last column.

name: gene-expression-data-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw expression matrix from NGS/microarray experiments (e.g., TCGA, GTEx-style gene-by-sample data frames) shows PCR artifacts, heteroskedasticity in high-signal features, or non-normal/multimodal feature distributions before correlation analysis.

name: gene-expression-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw TCGA-style FPKM gene expression matrices must be reduced to actively expressed genes before co-expression network construction, to remove background/noisy genes.

name: gene-expression-data-separation-and-granulation
description: Use when input is a continuous gene-expression microarray or RNA-seq matrix to be clustered for trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters, and many genes are inactive under some conditions, so raw-value biclustering would be distorted.

name: gene-expression-dataframe-normalization
description: Use when a raw gene-expression matrix (e.g., tab-separated GSE-style text or CSV loaded as a Pandas DataFrame) needs an internal reference gene identified and single-gene normalization to reduce between-group sample variation.

name: gene-expression-decoder-implementation
description: Use when re-implementing or extending the scGAE decoder stack: you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix plus a KNN cell-graph adjacency matrix and need a single autoencoder that reconstructs both X and A from a shared latent embedding.

name: gene-expression-dissimilarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when connecting an scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. zebrafish GSE66688/GSE112294 or Drosophila dge_normalized.txt) to spatial gene measurements and you must supply cost_matrix, sc_dmat, and is_dmat to SpaOTsc.

name: gene-expression-distribution-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have per-gene MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) plus TPM values for the same genes and want to test whether expression level alone predicts required sequencing depth or full-transcript coverage.

name: gene-expression-feature-classification
description: Use when the goal is to predict evolutionary targets of gene deletion events ('Redundant' vs 'Unique' classes) from two-species expression data, or to benchmark classifier power across four added-noise SD levels (0.001, 0.01, 0.1, 1).

name: gene-expression-feature-ranking
description: Use when you need to rank/ prioritize genes from a labeled high-dimensional gene-expression matrix (e.g., TCGA RNA-seq) as biomarker candidates, instead of traditional DEG analysis.

name: gene-expression-feature-subsetting
description: Use when the scRNA-seq dataset is too large (e.g. >1 million cells) or resource-limited to train a feature-selection model on all genes at once, and you need an importance-ranked feature set before final classifier training.

name: gene-expression-filter-based-feature-selection
description: Use when training mLR subtype classifiers on whole-transcriptome RNA-seq matrices where a reduced, informative gene space is needed and filter scores or limma DE statistics can define the feature set.

name: gene-expression-filtering
description: Use when raw gene-by-cell UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., human PBMC, mouse lung, human skin 10x Chromium data) must be filtered of lowly-expressed genes and reduced to a top-1000-HVG feature space before clustering or benchmarking.

name: gene-expression-filtering-of-network-priors
description: Use when you have a motif- and TSS-derived candidate TF–target mask built from ATAC-seq peaks and need to restrict it to genes detectably expressed in your scRNA-seq dataset prior to EM-based GRN inference.

name: gene-expression-gradient-visualization
description: Use when you have cross-modality latent embeddings (e.g. from scConfluence's diagonal integration of morphology and scRNA-seq) and need to inspect whether a marker gene such as Fezf2 shows a graded pattern along a biological manifold (e.g. apical-dendrite organization of IT neurons).

name: gene-expression-heatmap-generation-by-response-class
description: Use when you have SAM/samr significance-ranked gene lists and a quantile-normalized expression matrix from microarray data and need a dendrogram heatmap to check sample clustering by biological class.

name: gene-expression-log2-normalization
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) is about to be fed into DCNet or a deconvolution baseline, and raw counts/TPM values are not yet log-scaled.

name: gene-expression-matrix-export
description: Use when a cleaned, batch-corrected gene-by-sample matrix of the MDI-induced 3T3-L1 microarray data must be written to disk for downstream differential expression or gene set enrichment analysis.

name: gene-expression-matrix-filtering
description: Use when a raw or quantile-normalized microarray matrix (e.g. the PIMENTo example_unnorm.txt tab-separated file) contains a large low-intensity background population that must be separated from signal before differential analysis.

name: gene-expression-matrix-imputation
description: Use when preparing .csv gene expression matrices (e.g., GSE151189 training and GSE59098 validation) with missing values for cross-platform model training in Ciclops, where train and test data must share aligned gene distributions.

name: gene-expression-matrix-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE65525 Buettner, GSE74547 Kolodziejczyk, GSE75748 Chu-time) must be normalized before c-CSN/CNDM construction or before clustering comparisons against GEM.

name: gene-expression-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when building gene expression inputs for the GSFM FM active matrix: raw tumor/normal matrices (TCGA, GEO) and LINCS drug-induced profiles must be sample-filtered for cell-line correlation before STEP 2 transformation.

name: gene-expression-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells, count- or FPKM-like values) needs cleaning before dropout analysis, imputation, or clustering, and value range/gene sparsity must be normalized first.

name: gene-expression-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when the input is raw or non-conforming bulk RNA-seq expression data that must be reshaped into a gene (symbol) x sample matrix before reaction activity scoring or flux analysis.

name: gene-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when perturbation gene-expression series (e.g., ArrayExpress submissions) must be normalized, QC'd, assembled into an expression matrix, and converted to z-scores for pathway-activity modeling.

name: gene-expression-memory-based-lineage-prediction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data lacks lineage information and you need to infer small cell lineages, or when validating GEMLI lineage predictions against barcoding ground truth (e.g., GSE99915 MEF data) with precision/sensitivity/FPR metrics.

name: gene-expression-memory-validation
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq matrix with barcode lineage annotations is available and you need to quantify whether lineage-related cells are transcriptomically more similar than random pairs before trusting lineage predictions.

name: gene-expression-network-structure-learning
description: Use when you have a directed reference graph (e.g., the 32-node/47-edge ALS KEGG graph or KEGG/Reactome interactomes) plus an RNA-seq expression matrix, and need to recover or convert it into a valid directed spanning tree (arborescence).

name: gene-expression-normalization-centering-scaling
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (e.g. GEO/ArrayExpress pre-clinical CRC datasets, TCGA pCRC, organoid or PDX matrices) is to be classified with CMScaller or its NTP algorithm, since input must be centered and scaled before prediction.

name: gene-expression-permutation-null-generation
description: Use when a scDEED-style reliability analysis needs a null distribution of cell-embedding similarity scores to classify 2D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings as dubious or trustworthy.

name: gene-expression-phenotype-simulation
description: Use when you need controlled simulation benchmarks for TWAS training methods: you have a real genotype panel and want to vary causal variant proportion and heritability to compare out-of-sample test R2 and TWAS power across methods.

name: gene-expression-profile-aggregation
description: Use when a clustered scRNA-seq AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) must be reduced to per-cluster average expression profiles for cell-type annotation or to match a cell line for LINCS L1000 deconvolution.

name: gene-expression-profile-z-score-normalization
description: Use when preparing a Seurat-clustered scRNA-seq query whose top-N marker genes' average expression must be z-scored (e.g. via t(scale(t(...))) in R) before running deCS.correlation against a reference panel.

name: gene-expression-program-cell-type-specificity-assessment
description: Use when you have a program usage matrix (e.g., cNMF usage values for k factors) plus known cell-type labels and need to count identity vs. shared-usage activity GEPs or compare methods on activity-program recovery.

name: gene-expression-program-estimation
description: Use when a (genes x cells) log-normalized scRNAseq matrix must be decomposed into a small set of interpretable, nonnegative gene expression programs whose cell weights are regularized toward similarity of nearby cells in a q-diffused graph.

name: gene-expression-program-recovery-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing between ICA- and NMF-based decomposition of scRNA-seq matrices, or for validating a program-recovery pipeline by matching recovered components to known embedded gene expression programs (GEPs).
