name: gene-expression-radar-visualization
description: Use when you have a Seurat query object projected onto a reference TIL atlas and need to compare gene-expression profiles (e.g. exhaustion vs naive-like markers) across predicted cell states, or to verify subtype assignments.

name: gene-expression-ranking-serialization
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices (e.g., HCL, GSE134355) must be converted into token sequences for a GPT-style autoregressive transformer that models gene-expression rankings rather than expression values.

name: gene-expression-reconstruction-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a trained multimodal generative model (e.g. scMM on paired SHARE-seq scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq) has decoded predicted expression profiles that must be quantitatively scored against observed transcriptome counts and compared to a GAM baseline.

name: gene-expression-replacement-simulation
description: Use when quantifying how much transcriptional identity (number of DE genes) a rare cell type needs before a detection method can still recover it, via controlled replacement of DE genes in subsampled scRNA-seq data.

name: gene-expression-scaling
description: Use when preparing a gene expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cell populations) as input to ICELLNET interaction scoring, to bound per-gene influence before computing ligand–receptor and global communication scores.

name: gene-expression-stratification-plotting
description: Use when you have scMMGAN-generated scRNA-seq profiles (output_fake2) from spatial transcriptomics input and need to test whether k=5 spectral k-means clusters or marker-gene strata (SLC2A1/CDK11A) retain the spatial organization of the tissue.

name: gene-expression-subsetting-to-selected-cells
description: Use when a user has defined a cell group during a CellexalVR VR session and downstream backend calculations (e.g. TF-TF correlation networks with propr rho) need the expression matrix restricted to exactly those selected cells.

name: gene-expression-time-series-simulation
description: Use when a forecasting or trajectory method needs ground-truth future expression states for benchmarking, by simulating noisy single-cell time-series data with BoolODE from random gene networks.

name: gene-expression-tpm-filtering-of-neoantigens
description: Use when TSNAD v2.0 has produced DeepHLApan-scored candidate neoantigens from WES/WGS and matched tumor RNA-Seq is available, so that neoantigens from genes with TPM < 1 must be removed before ranking high-confidence candidates.

name: gene-expression-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when a DESC-embedded single-cell dataset (e.g. 10,878 human monocytes across three processing batches) needs pseudotime ordering and per-batch visualization of a marker gene such as S100A8 along that trajectory.

name: gene-expression-z-score-normalization
description: Use when raw perturbation-series microarray data must be normalized per series and converted to z-scores so expression changes from different perturbation experiments (e.g. ArrayExpress submissions) can be pooled for signature construction.

name: gene-expression-zscore-normalization
description: Use when an FPKM/TPM expression matrix (genes x cells) from scRNA-Seq has been quality-filtered and expression-floored (expr.minimum = 0.01) and a scale-free gene profile is needed before correlation-distance-based cell clustering.

name: gene-functional-annotation
description: Use when a ranked disease-vs-control gene list (e.g. top-100 or top-10 biomarkers from scaLR's eval_and_analysis_pipeline) must be checked for enrichment of known disease or neurological-disorder genes to validate biomarker discovery.

name: gene-fusion-and-exitron-detection
description: Use when RNA-seq data must be mined for gene-fusion and exitron-splicing events as variant inputs to neoantigen prediction, beyond the SNV/indel sources most tools cover.

name: gene-fusion-detection
description: Use when tumor RNA-Seq FASTQ reads are supplied to TSNAD v2.0 and fusion-derived neoantigen candidates must be generated alongside WES/WGS-based SNV/INDEL neoantigens.

name: gene-fusion-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational time of scFusion against bulk fusion detection methods (Arriba, STAR-Fusion, EricScript, FusionCatcher) on real Smart-Seq scRNA-seq datasets.

name: gene-gene-association-network-construction
description: Use when you need per-cell, direct gene-gene association networks from a scRNA-seq expression matrix, e.g. to remove CSN's indirect-association overestimation or to identify hub genes in differentiation modules.

name: gene-gene-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to validate denoised/imputed single-cell expression by comparing gene-gene Pearson correlations before and after imputation, or to detect spurious marker expression in a specific cell population.

name: gene-gene-correlation-matrix-analysis
description: Use when building or analyzing a gene-gene correlation matrix from log-normalized scRNA-seq data to score genes, identify well-correlated marker genes, or derive feature sets for cell-type clustering.

name: gene-gene-correlation-preservation-in-simulation
description: Use when a clustering benchmark needs a simulated scRNA-seq dataset that retains realistic gene-gene correlation structure and per-type marginals, with controlled group sizes including a rare cell type (<5% of cells).

name: gene-gene-interaction-extraction
description: Use when you have a DEGGs subnetworks object of class Deggs (e.g. from generate_subnetworks on TCGA-BRCA counts) and need the significant gene-gene pairs listed per subgroup as candidate features.

name: gene-genomic-coordinate-annotation-and-sorting
description: Use when a filtered gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. SCEVAN input after removing cells with <200 genes and genes in <1% of cells) lacks genomic coordinates or is not yet ordered by genomic position prior to CNV segmentation.

name: gene-hit-tracking-across-experimental-comparisons
description: Use when several pairwise Treatment-vs-Control RNA-seq comparisons (e.g., oxacillin, loratadine, Cmpd8 co-treatments vs Control in MRSA USA100) need screening for genes extreme in log2 fold-change and padj<=0.05.

name: gene-homology-mapping
description: Use when preparing single-cell RNA-seq count matrices from two or more species for integration and you must decide which homologous gene sets (O2O vs in-paralog-including HE/SH) define the shared feature space.

name: gene-identifier-mapping
description: Use when you have a gene ID list associated with a biological process of interest and need to derive its PPIN adjacency edge list for downstream PPIN activity scoring in ORIGINS2.

name: gene-identifier-mapping
description: Use when an RNA-seq counts matrix carries Ensembl gene IDs but downstream GSVA, .gmt gene-set matching, TPM integration, or differential analysis in ARMT requires gene-symbol identifiers.

name: gene-importance-ranking
description: Use when a trained Cancer-Finder checkpoint exists (e.g., ST model with 5000-gene input) and the goal is to explain malignant-vs-normal spot classification by extracting a ranked, per-gene importance list from spatial transcriptomics slides.

name: gene-importance-stability-analysis
description: Use when you need to verify that a trained SIMS/TabNet classifier's sparse gene-selection masks for a specific cell class (e.g., Pvalb+ interneurons) are consistent across independent runs, or to recover an interpretable marker-gene set.

name: gene-influence-quantification-per-cluster
description: Use when marker genes must be identified for clusters from pretrained deep learning embeddings (e.g., Miscell) and you need per-gene, per-cluster influence scores rather than t-test/Wilcoxon differential expression.

name: gene-influence-score-computation
description: Use when you have a CEFCON-constructed cell-lineage-specific GRN with learned attention coefficients and need to rank MFVS/MDS driver gene candidates by importance to output driver regulators.

name: gene-interaction-network-subsetting
description: Use when building a differential co-expression network from TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices and a prior gene-interaction network is available to restrict which gene-pair correlations are computed and tested.

name: gene-interaction-table-export
description: Use when a fitted PhenoPath model exists and you must rank genes by |covariate-pseudotime interaction effect|, label interactions of interest, and write the results as a per-gene CSV table.

name: gene-length-bias-quantification
description: Use when validating that a simulated non-UMI scRNA-seq dataset recapitulates gene length bias, or when contrasting length-biased full-length protocols against UMI-based protocols that lack it.

name: gene-length-read-count-normalization
description: Use when raw featureCounts gene-level read counts (TopHat2/hg19 alignments, TCGA or Prensner PCa cohorts) must be corrected for sum-of-exons gene length before FunHoP node aggregation or Voom differential expression.

name: gene-level-cnv-matrix-construction
description: Use when a CaSpER run has produced final.objects from runCaSpER and you need gene-level amplification/deletion calls (e.g. to benchmark 69% TPR / 0.3% FPR gene-based deletion detection against a genotyping array gold standard).

name: gene-level-differential-expression-along-lineages
description: Use when a common multi-condition trajectory (slingshot sds) already exists and the goal is to find genes whose expression patterns differ between conditions along its lineages after topology, progression, and fate-selection tests.

name: gene-level-dispersion-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking imputation methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a transcriptome-landscape preservation metric — e.g. comparing median gene-level normalized intra dispersion across raw and imputed matrices over multiple datasets.

name: gene-level-pvalue-table-preparation
description: Use when a downstream pareg regression call needs a gene-by-pvalue dataframe and you only have raw matched tumor/normal expression data (e.g. GSE62944 TCGA-BRCA) that still requires a differential expression test per gene.

name: gene-level-read-count-quantification
description: Use when starting from raw RNA-seq FASTQ files of a patient cohort and per-gene read counts plus DE statistics (P value, regulation direction) are needed as downstream input for node-level pathway aggregation, e.g. FunHoP/KEGG network analysis.

name: gene-list-over-representation-analysis
description: Use when you have a differential-expression gene list (up- or down-regulated DEGs), especially from a non-model species, and need to identify which KEGG/GO pathways are significantly over-represented.

name: gene-list-overlap-contingency-table-analysis
description: Use when the query input is a list of genes (cluster marker genes with 'cluster' and 'gene' columns, or trait-associated genes) rather than an expression profile, and a cell type label is needed for each gene set.

name: gene-loading-norm-ranking
description: Use when you have a CA-embedded scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Zhengmix8eq SingleCellExperiment with corral output) and need to identify which genes carry the highest weight in the first two CA dimensions and interpret their association with cell populations.

name: gene-loading-z-score-standardization
description: Use when you have gene loading (weight) vectors from an ICA decomposition of log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression and need comparable loading scales across components before downstream clustering or meta-component mapping.

name: gene-location-file-preparation
description: Use when running the scWizard 'inferCNV' module on an annotated cancer scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., the ICC case study) and a gene-to-chromosomal-coordinate mapping file must be prepared before copy number analysis.

name: gene-locus-isoform-filtering
description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblies against a reference annotation and you need per-locus counts of uniquely assigned isoforms, especially for high-isoform-diversity genes like ATP6AP2.

name: gene-mapping-variance-quantification
description: Use when a trained noise-augmented GAN mapping between transcriptomic and proteomic domains is available and you need to quantify which genes' generated values are stable vs. unstable under stochastic z draws.

name: gene-marker-selection
description: Use when scRNA-seq data contains many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) with overlapping DE genes and a single global marker set is needed that distinguishes every phenotype pair, not just markers per individual cell type.

name: gene-marker-selection
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix with categorical cell labels (flat or hierarchical) and must design a minimal gene panel that discriminates all labels jointly with high precision.

name: gene-median-expression-filtering
description: Use when a raw TPM expression matrix (e.g. from the Soybean Expression Atlas plus supplementary infection RNA-seq data) must be filtered to remove lowly expressed genes before building a coexpression network.

name: gene-membership-table-matching
description: Use when two WGCNA/PyWGCNA networks built from different datasets (e.g., 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD MODEL-AD mouse RNA-seq) must be compared module-by-module to find conserved co-expression signatures via significant gene-set overlap.

name: gene-metric-bin-assignment
description: Use when you have a per-gene metric table (e.g. Tajima's D or nucleotide diversity per gene) and a nematode/zebrafish scRNA count object (AnnData via Scanpy), and want a binned gene-category-weighted expression index instead of a gene-age-weighted one.

name: gene-model-reference-file-verification
description: Reference for reproducing or validating the SkewC gene-model filtering step when the default hg38/mm10 .norRNAtRNA.bed references cannot be used, e.g. a new assembly or GENCODE release.

name: gene-module-activity-inference
description: Use when you have a single-cell count matrix (AnnData/scanpy) plus a GMT gene-module file and need per-cell, interpretable activity scores for pathways or marker sets, including out-of-sample inference on unseen cells or studies.

name: gene-module-activity-inference-single-cell
description: Use when you have a preprocessed single-cell dataset (e.g., Scanpy AnnData) and a GMT gene-set file and need pathway-level activity per cell, with downstream testing of which modules are significantly activated.

name: gene-module-annotation-count-audit
description: Use when you have the E.PATH GitHub data files (database and annotations) and need to verify or recompute the reported dataset, gene-module, gene-count, and per-environmental-factor statistics before downstream enrichment work.

name: gene-module-detection
description: Use when the input is a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes) with cell metadata and the goal is to infer gene co-expression networks and detect trait-associated gene modules.

name: gene-module-interpretation-for-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when you have run JOINTLY and need to interpret its learned factors as gene modules — e.g., to annotate cell types, confirm marker genes (DCN for IMR90, CD3B for Jurkat), or discover active biological processes per cluster.

name: gene-module-membership-outlier-exemption
description: Use when applying leave-one-out outlier detection (L1OutExpOut) to gene sets and needing to prevent over-removal of genes, e.g. genes flagged as outliers in many collections or belonging to only a few gene sets.

name: gene-module-variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (AnnData/scanpy) must be embedded in a biologically interpretable latent space defined by prior gene annotations (MSigDB, Reactome, GO, cell type markers), e.g. for pathway activity or drug-response interpretation.

name: gene-name-alias-mapping
description: Use when refining an inferred GRN against curated databases (OmniPath, Signor, SignaLink, TRRUST) and gene/organism labels from a GenBank file may miss synonyms, causing incomplete interaction retrieval.

name: gene-network-benchmarking-metrics
description: Use when comparing gene network inference methods or model variants against a curated directed binary ground truth (e.g. Omnipath) and reporting AUPRC and EPR per cell type or condition.

name: gene-network-centrality-analysis
description: Use when you have weighted, cell-type-specific gene network adjacency matrices (e.g., GRnnData objects from scPRINT) and need to identify differential hub genes or functionally enriched network communities, as done for the BPH fibroblast ion-exchange/senescence module.

name: gene-network-heads-selection
description: Use when extracting a gene regulatory network from a pretrained transformer's attention matrices and you must decide which attention heads to average, using a literature ground truth such as Omnipath.

name: gene-network-inference-from-attention-matrices
description: Use when inferring genome-wide gene regulatory networks from a single-cell transformer model's attention matrices and benchmarking against ChIP-seq/perturb-seq gold-standard networks with EPR and AUPRC metrics.

name: gene-network-scoring-analysis
description: Use when you have a data frame (CSV format) of significantly changed genes with log-fold-change values from single-cell RNA-seq or proteomics experiments and need per-gene LFC scores for GMM-based gene-network exploration in OmicInt.

name: gene-neuron-correspondence-mapping
description: Use when reconstructing or retraining DCNet: you need to wire the 9078x434 zero-one gene-cell matrix into the network's input-to-hidden weights and align input/output neuron ordering with the gene index.

name: gene-ontology-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have mouse gene clusters/modules (e.g., co-expression GEPs) and need to determine which GO or MP terms are statistically enriched, with enrichment ratios and BH-adjusted p-values.

name: gene-ontology-annotation-mapping-mouse
description: Use when mouse (3T3-L1) differential expression results need to be translated into GO terms — e.g. ranking genes by log fold-change and testing which adipogenic GO categories (BP/CC/MF) are significantly enriched.

name: gene-ontology-annotation-via-biomart
description: Use when a pre-computed cell-cell interaction (CCI) dataset of enriched int-pairs must be annotated with Gene Ontology functional terms, as a prerequisite for ranking terms by annotated int-pair occurrence.

name: gene-ontology-biological-process-enrichment
description: Use when you have a ranked or significant gene list (e.g., SigGenes at fdr level 0.01) and need to confirm it is biologically meaningful via GO biological-process term enrichment.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-along-trajectory
description: Use when you have LatentVelo cell trajectories (z_traj, times from ltv.cell_trajectories) for a lineage such as beta cell differentiation and need biological validation of the trajectory via enriched GO terms.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a gene list derived from differential IPA usage (or another differential transcript event) and want to identify enriched GO biological-process terms explaining which functions the affected genes share.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have cluster labels from single-cell RNA-seq clustering (e.g., scEFSC wMetaC output) plus a normalized expression matrix, and need to interpret clusters biologically via GO/KEGG enrichment of top DE genes.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when comparing functional enrichment of subpopulation gene sets derived from scRNA-seq alone versus scRNA-seq combined with bulk HiChIP loop data, to quantify whether loop information improves GO enrichment (Table 2).

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a small detected gene set (e.g., EDGE feature genes below the μ − 1.5 × σ entropy cutoff) and need to test whether it is enriched for GO biological processes relative to an appropriate background universe.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-analysis-via-toppfun
description: Use when a subclone-associated gene list (e.g. GATA2R361C subclone genes) overlaps a co-expression module (e.g. TCGA VIM-correlated genes, 2191 genes at q < 0.001) and the intersecting genes need biological interpretation via GO terms.

name: gene-ontology-enrichment-comparison
description: Use when scCRISPR-seq analysis needs to judge whether decoupled perturbation responses (vs the naive OC estimate) yield better pathway enrichment and perturbation-related gene rankings, e.g. for TCR-related genes like CD69 and RELA on Jurkat CROP-seq data.

name: gene-ontology-gaf-annotation-parsing
description: Use when DE summary statistics must be paired with pre-defined gene set annotations (e.g. for iDEA GSE input) and no annotation matrix matching the required gene identifier type exists yet.

name: gene-ontology-geneset-scoring
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels across datasets and want to test whether specific functional gene sets (e.g., GO terms) carry enough cell-type signal to recover labels via cross-dataset neighbor voting.

name: gene-ontology-pathway-annotation-mapping
description: Use when assigning functional titles to gene-set or module gene lists by consolidating enrichment evidence (GOTERM, KEGG, BioCarta, GSAn, RcisTarget motifs) across all 382 BloodGen3 modules.

name: gene-ontology-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a list of predicted mRNA/protein targets of small RNAs (e.g. tRF-5 and tRF-3 series tncRNAs of 18-25 nt) is available and you need to identify overrepresented biological processes such as metabolic and developmental pathways.

name: gene-ontology-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a ranked or top-N gene list per class/state (e.g. top 20 DWGs from Pollock feature attribution) and need to identify enriched GO pathways and verify biological plausibility.

name: gene-ontology-term-overrepresentation
description: Use when you have a gene list from differential expression (e.g. consensus DEGs selected by a minimum vote threshold) and need overrepresentation of biological processes such as basement membrane or ECM terms.

name: gene-overlap-across-sample-pairs
description: Use when you have ranked candidate reference gene lists from ERgene FindERG over multiple sample pairs of one dataset (e.g., 20 genes per pair) and need to quantify which genes recur across pairs.

name: gene-pair-deletion-screening
description: Use when you have mock and infected context-specific genome-scale metabolic models (e.g., built from GSE147507/GSE148729 lung expression data) and need to find knockouts that selectively impair viral biomass while sparing host biomass.

name: gene-pair-difference-normalization
description: Use when you must timestamp individual bulk or scRNAseq pseudobulk transcriptomic samples (e.g., microarray or RNAseq) whose circadian phase is unknown and no matched control series exists for cross-sample normalization.

name: gene-pair-prognostic-association-analysis
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq/microarray with matched survival data must be tested for whether immune cell types or immune marker genes appear spuriously favorable due to co-infiltration, as in TCGA SKCM06 melanoma.

name: gene-pair-score-computation
description: Use when a bulk transcriptomic cohort has been preprocessed with marker-gene selection and you need a pairwise logical-relational matrix of marker expression comparisons to feed Cox regression or enrichment of cell-cell interactions.

name: gene-pair-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when a set of candidate ligand-receptor pairs has been inferred between two cell types and you must determine whether each pair is restricted to that sender-receiver combination or also appears in other cell-type interactions.

name: gene-pair-to-drug-combination-mapping
description: Use when you have a list of essential genes and gene pairs (from single-/double-gene knockout analysis, e.g. FBA with a VBOF) and need to convert them into approved single-drug and drug-combination candidates via DrugBank target mapping.

name: gene-pairwise-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have a log2-transformed expression matrix (data frame) of multiple genes/features (e.g. 40 genes across ~10K TCGA Pan-Cancer samples) and need a pairwise correlation heatmap ordered by hierarchical clustering into feature clusters.

name: gene-panel-intersection-across-datasets
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq AnnData has a different gene count or ordering than the SIMS TabNet reference model's training features, and cell-type label prediction must proceed without feature-mismatch errors.

name: gene-panel-tissue-optimality-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing the RNA-seq biosample for a disease gene panel: you have per-tissue MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) and a panel gene list, and need the tissue minimizing required sequencing depth.

name: gene-periodicity-magnitude-quantification
description: Use when you have Cyclum-inferred circular pseudo-time for cells in two or more conditions (e.

name: gene-presence-absence-feature-selection
description: Use when building lifestyle or metadata classifiers from a binary gene cluster presence/absence matrix (e.

name: gene-presence-fraction-filtering
description: Use when preparing a raw scRNA-seq/CITE-seq count matrix (e.g., an AnnData .h5ad loaded with scanpy) for marker selection, and you need to discard genes expressed in too few or too many cells before normalization and z-scaling.

name: gene-program-discovery-network-analysis
description: Use when the goal is unsupervised discovery of gene programs/modules from normalized scRNA-seq data, especially when benchmarking against ICA/NMF or seeking GO-term/PPI-enriched gene modules.

name: gene-protein-correspondence-mapping
description: Use when constructing an intercellular communication database from protein-centric PPI sources (e.g., STRING) that must be expressed as gene pairs to match scRNA-seq gene expression matrices for human or mouse.

name: gene-ranking-and-top-k-selection
description: Use when a labeled single-cell training matrix with cell type annotations needs supervised feature selection before building SciBet (or similar multinomial) classifiers.

name: gene-ranking-matrix-construction
description: Use when a normalized UMI matrix from scRNA-seq data (e.g., SingCellaR Human_HSPC) must be converted into AUCell rankings to score lineage signature gene sets loaded from a GMT file.

name: gene-recall-curve-analysis
description: Use when you have per-cell-type ranked biomarker lists (e.g. top-100 from scaLR ClasswiseAbs) and a curated cell-type-specific reference marker database, and need to quantify/plot how many validated markers each tool recovers.

name: gene-regulator-correlation-validation
description: Use when you have simulated or inferred multi-omics data with a ground-truth list of regulator–gene interactions and need to confirm that modelled regulatory effects produce detectable correlations distinct from a no-effect background.

name: gene-regulatory-network-backbone-design
description: Use when simulating single-cell dynamics with dyngen and the user must define or choose a module network backbone that drives the topology (e.g. bifurcation, loop) of the resulting gene regulatory network.

name: gene-regulatory-network-centrality-analysis
description: Use when cluster-specific GRN Links objects are available and you need to rank TFs by network position (degree/eigenvector centrality) or classify network configuration (cartography) across a reprogramming trajectory.

name: gene-regulatory-network-construction
description: Use when analyzing full-scale or small-scale CROP-seq/Perturb-seq CRISPRi screens with TSS-repression and trans-association tables from Normalisr, and the goal is a causal gRNA->target->trans-gene regulatory network reproducible across gRNAs and screens.

name: gene-regulatory-network-edge-pruning
description: Use when a base GRN built from single-cell epigenomic data (e.g., Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas peaks) must be converted into cluster-specific, weighted GRNs using a matched scRNA-seq expression matrix with defined cell clusters.

name: gene-regulatory-network-edge-ranking
description: Use when an overall precision-recall evaluation of a GRN inference method (e.g., SINGE Borda-aggregated edge ranks) looks acceptable but you need to check whether performance is driven or hidden by the prevalence of individual regulators in the gold standard.

name: gene-regulatory-network-edge-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when a reconstructed GRN (directed signed edges/weights) must be scored against a known ground-truth network — e.g., oracle-case simulations with known true mean and covariance matrices — to quantify edge recovery via precision and recall.

name: gene-regulatory-network-ensemble-evaluation
description: Use when you have a full synthetic/simulated groundtruth network plus expression data (HDF5/CSV/EXP) and need to test whether ensemble GRN coefficients remain reliable when optimized on only 0.5%-10% of the truth.

name: gene-regulatory-network-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when a new or reimplemented fate-inference or TF-activity method needs validation against a synthetic dataset with a known ground-truth GRN before application to real scRNA-seq data.

name: gene-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq (optionally with scATAC-seq/motif hints) must be turned into a cell-type-specific directed TF-gene network whose target genes are explained by Boolean logic combinations of <5 candidate regulators.

name: gene-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when a raw or preprocessed scRNA-seq reference dataset needs a TF-gene regulatory graph to guide causal GAN training (GRouNdGAN) or to serve as ground truth for benchmarking GRN inference methods.

name: gene-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when you have pseudotime-ordered single-cell expression data (a .mat file with X, ptime, gene_list, optional regix/branches) and need a ranked list of directed regulator-gene interactions.

name: gene-regulatory-network-inference-from-pseudotemporal-single-cell-data
description: Use when input is pseudotemporal single-cell gene expression (a .mat file with sparse matrix X, ptime array, optional regix regulator indices) and the goal is a ranked list of transcriptional regulator-target interactions.

name: gene-regulatory-network-inference-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when a pre-inferred co-expression module (GCN module, e.g. WGCNA/BioNERO-derived gene lists) must be converted into a directed, motif-validated GRN to identify its key transcription-factor regulators.

name: gene-regulatory-network-inference-via-expectation-maximization
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster labels) requires joint inference of a gene regulatory network and per-cell RNA velocities, especially to resolve directional dynamics like state transdifferentiation that standard methods miss.

name: gene-regulatory-network-informed-decoder-wiring
description: Use when you have single-cell transcriptomics plus a prior gene regulatory network (e.g. ARACNe-derived TF-target modules) and want an interpretable latent space whose dimensions correspond to transcription factor / pathway activity rather than abstract factors.

name: gene-regulatory-network-module-partitioning
description: Use when you have a merged, edge-pruned GRN from single-cell or spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., snRNAseq or Visium) and need to identify gene modules, compute per-cell/spot module scores, and link modules to traits or pathways.

name: gene-regulatory-network-neighborhood-extraction
description: Use when you have an inferred lineage-specific GRN plus driver regulators with influence scores and need gene modules around those regulators with per-cell activity scores.

name: gene-regulatory-network-perturbation-scoring
description: Use when untreated scRNA-seq data from diseased tissue has a known drug target (e.g. Brd4 for BET inhibitors) and you must rank which cell types are most drug-responsive via in silico target perturbation of GRNs.

name: gene-regulatory-network-prior-integration
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq count data must be embedded with prior knowledge from a TF regulatory network (e.g., DoRothEA) so latent variables correspond to TF regulon activities, e.g., to score TF activity per cell or benchmark TF perturbation inference.

name: gene-regulatory-network-refinement
description: Use when an initial GRN inferred from RNA-Seq expression data needs refinement with TFBM predictions and curated database interactions, especially for non-model organisms lacking database coverage.

name: gene-regulatory-network-representation-learning
description: Use when the input is a directed GRN edge list (e.g. DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) plus a gene feature matrix, and the goal is to capture directed regulation information and second-order neighbor structure as embeddings.

name: gene-regulatory-network-resource-handling
description: Use when a task needs a prior-knowledge GRN (DoRothEA or OmniPath) as input for TF-activity inference or perturbation benchmarking with decoupleR/decoupleRBench, and the network's sign and weight annotations must be preserved.

name: gene-regulatory-network-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference, RNA velocity, trajectory alignment, or cell-specific network inference methods requires simulated single-cell data with completely known ground truth for GRN dynamics and cellular progression.

name: gene-scoring-baseline-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to show that genes prioritized by a new GWAS-by-scRNA-seq method are more functionally enriched than top genes from established gene-scoring baselines such as MAGMA or eQTL-based TWAS methods.

name: gene-scoring-per-cell-type-from-deconvolution-model
description: Use when a trained SpatialDDLS deconvolution model exists and you need to know WHICH genes the network uses to predict each cell type's proportions, e.g. to recover canonical markers (Cd8/Cd8b1, Foxp3) from predicted spot compositions.

name: gene-selection-by-encoder-weight-variance
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) must be reduced to a compact informative gene set before dimension reduction or clustering, and noise/dropout-driven genes need to be filtered by contribution to a part-based representation.

name: gene-set-activity-scoring
description: Use when projecting a scRNA-seq query onto a pre-built ProjectSVR reference model: the query must first be converted to gene set activity scores (via ComputeModuleScore with the model's stored gss.method, e.g. AUCell or UCell) before ProjectNewdata/MapQuery can predict embeddings.

name: gene-set-averaged-expression-scoring
description: Use when you need to translate a cell-state or pathway gene signature (e.g. a MetaTiME MeC weight table) into a per-sample numeric score in bulk RNA-seq data such as TCGA, for grouping samples into high/low signature classes.

name: gene-set-based-cell-type-identification
description: Use when the goal is to quantify cross-dataset replicability of known cell-type labels (e.g., neuron vs non-neuron across eight scRNA-seq studies) using gene sets and AUROC, rather than cluster-level unsupervised matching.

name: gene-set-consistency-filtering-across-clusters
description: Use when several related (e.g., subtype-level) cell clusters each yield a ranked COVID-vs-healthy biomarker list and you need the gene subset whose expression direction is consistent across all of them.

name: gene-set-coordination-testing
description: Use when you have a normalized cell-by-gene scRNA-seq or ST matrix and a list of gene sets, and need to decide which pathways are truly coordinated among cells without clustering, before pathway scoring or binarization.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a list of gene symbols — especially one recovered from Excel date-conversion errors (Mar-01, Mar-02) — must be functionally annotated via GO Biological Processes enrichment, with terms filtered at adjusted p < 0.05.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a ranked gene list (e.g. FDR-ranked conditionTest DE genes from a multi-condition trajectory analysis) and need to interpret which biological pathways explain between-condition differences.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have differential expression results from the curatedAdipoArray 3T3-L1 microarray data (e.g., Pparg knockdown) and need to rank all genes by decreasing log fold-change to identify significantly enriched GO terms via GSEA rather than overlap-based ORA.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (from a text list, microarray study, or clustered Seurat single-cell object) and want to find statistically enriched gene modules linked to environmental factors such as cigarette smoking, diet, infections, or toxic chemicals.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have per-factor gene rankings from a trained multi-omics factor model (e.g., Mowgli on TEA-seq) and need to interpret latent factors biologically by testing their top genes for enrichment against curated gene set databases.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a DMC (differentially methylated CpG) list from a 450K/EPIC Illumina array analysis needs to be translated into enriched biological pathways with per-database enrichment statistics.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq cluster (e.g., a Leiden cluster from Cellar) needs a cell-type label and differential expression has yielded ranked genes that must be interpreted against GO, KEGG, or MSigDB functional gene sets.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a selected gene list (e.g. RMT signal genes from Zeisel mouse cortex or Kang PBMC data) plus a discarded list, and need to test over-representation of biological gene sets against the full gene universe.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have ranked gene-level differential expression statistics (e.g., edgeR log2-fold-changes between two cell clones or conditions) and want to know which MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched at FDR < 0.05.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have CMScaller-classified (CMS1–CMS4) organoid, PDX or cell-line expression data and need to confirm the subtypes recapitulate known CMS biology (CMS2 HNF4A/MYC/WNT, CMS3 CDX2/metabolic, CMS4 TGFβ/EMT) via gene set enrichment.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a list of discriminatively selected marker genes needs functional/annotation validation against a curated tissue and cell-type gene-set library such as HuBMAP ASCT+B, or when comparing marker-selection methods by enrichment q values.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of mouse gene sets (e.g., co-expression modules or GEPs from SingleCellGGM) and need to test which GO or MP terms are statistically enriched at p <= 0.05.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-gsea
description: Use when genes ranked by an inferred latent process (e.g., Cyclum circular pseudotime match scores, or PCA components 1-2) must be validated against a curated gene set such as GO:0007049 to test whether the ranking captures cell-cycle biology.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-hallmark-pathways
description: Use when scMDC cluster assignments for a CITE-seq dataset (e.g., BMNC GSE128639) exist and you need per-cluster Hallmark pathway enrichment from differential gene rankings to interpret cluster biology.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-interpretation
description: Use when a gene list of temporal DEGs from multi-timepoint scRNA-seq (e.g., CASi tDEGs at p < 0.05) needs pathway-level interpretation (Hallmark/Reactome) and key-gene trajectory visualization.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-of-cluster-markers
description: Use when you have Seurat FindAllMarkers output (only.pos=TRUE, min.pct=0.25, logfc.threshold=0.25) for scRNA-seq clusters and need reference-database cell-type annotations that respect gene ranking rather than simple list overlap.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-scrnaseq
description: Use when you have gene-level differential expression summary statistics (beta, beta_var or p-values) from scRNA-seq data (e.g. MAST, SCDE, zingeR-DESeq2) and need calibrated gene set enrichment p-values and FDR estimates.

name: gene-set-enrichment-analysis-with-comet
description: Use when SCA (QCM/QCC > 0.5) has identified supported clusters and you must functionally annotate their cluster-specific genes against immune-signature or KEGG gene sets to validate cell identity.

name: gene-set-enrichment-annotation-scoring
description: Use when cluster-level marker tables (gene symbol, avg_log2FC per Seurat cluster) must be converted into per-cluster cell-type recommendations, and when comparing GSEA vs Fisher exact test accuracy across marker databases (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole).

name: gene-set-enrichment-auc-analysis
description: Use when projecting leukemia cell sub-clusters onto a reference hematopoietic atlas and you need the gene-set-enrichment AUC-difference component of the CCI composite score to measure similarity between compared sub-clusters.

name: gene-set-enrichment-auc-scoring
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has been clustered into CD8 TIL states and you need quantitative per-cell scores for phenotype axes defined by marker gene sets (e.g. Pdcd1/Havcr2 exhaustion, Gzmb cytotoxicity, Tcf7 stemness).

name: gene-set-enrichment-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when you have a Seurat object with clusters and a per-cluster positive marker list (e.g. FindAllMarkers output mapped to Entrez IDs) and need automatic, ranking-aware cell-type annotation instead of manual marker matching.

name: gene-set-enrichment-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a directed/undirected subnetwork extraction method must be quantitatively compared against active-subnetwork alternatives on a case-vs-control RNA-seq benchmark with known disease genes and GO term references.

name: gene-set-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when scRNA-seq topics/embeddings must be interpreted against known biological pathways, or when gene set/pathway knowledge should be directly embedded into a topic model so pathway-topic associations are learned rather than inferred post hoc.

name: gene-set-enrichment-of-dynamic-genes
description: Use when scLANE (or a similar trajectory DE tool) has called genes significantly dynamic along a Slingshot/Monocle3 trajectory at FDR-adjusted p < 0.01, and you need pathway-level interpretation of lineage-specific dynamics such as osteoblastic vs. apoptotic fates.

name: gene-set-enrichment-pvalue-calibration-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking GSE methods (e.g., iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) on scRNA-seq data and you must verify null p-value calibration rather than power, especially across varying gene set coverage rates.

name: gene-set-enrichment-score-computation
description: Use when an AnnData object processed via the scanpy standard workflow (log-cpm normalised, high-resolution Leiden labels) needs per-cluster enrichment scores to assign cells to marker-defined clusters, or when comparing which scoring method discriminates clusters defined by unique gene combinations.

name: gene-set-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when raw gene expression profiles (rows = samples, columns = Entrez gene identifiers) must be transformed into pathway activity features — e.g., to train or apply a DeepCC subtype classifier, or to make batch/platform-robust single-sample predictions.

name: gene-set-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when annotating clusters in a Seurat scRNA-seq object against a heterogeneous catalog of variable-sized cell-type marker gene sets, and you need bias-corrected per-cluster enrichment scores with statistical significance calls.

name: gene-set-enrichment-spectra-computation
description: Use when converting raw gene expression matrices (rows=samples, columns=Entrez gene IDs) into pathway-activity features using MSigDB gene sets, prior to training a DeepCC subtype classifier or classifying new/individual samples.

name: gene-set-enrichment-statistics
description: Use when a gene list derived from a co-expression module (e.g., a PyWGCNA module correlated with an external trait at P < 0.05) needs GO/KEGG/REACTOME functional enrichment to identify the biological functions the module represents.

name: gene-set-enrichment-summary-statistics-testing
description: Use when you have per-gene DE summary statistics (e.g., z-scores from MAST/SCDE/zingeR) plus gene set annotations and need a calibrated p-value testing whether each gene set is enriched in differentially expressed genes.

name: gene-set-enrichment-testing-via-fishers-exact-test
description: Use when a fitted topic model (e.g., CODAL/MIRA β matrix) yields a ranked gene list and you need to test overrepresentation of a curated cell-type ontology set — e.g., HuBMAP CD16+ monocyte membership — among the top-ranked genes.

name: gene-set-enrichment-validation-with-vam
description: Use when a rare, newly recovered single-cell subcluster must be confirmed against a published marker gene set — e.g., an apCAF subcluster (23 cells, 0.092% of the Elyada PDAC dataset) that was absent from the original analysis.

name: gene-set-mask-construction
description: Use when training TOSICA on a reference AnnData and you must pick or construct the gmt-path mask (human_gobp, human_immune, human_reactome, human_tf, mouse_gobp, mouse_reactome, mouse_tf, or a custom .gmt path) that defines gene-to-pathway-token connectivity.

name: gene-set-module-score-computation
description: Use when the goal is to convert annotated gene sets (pathways) into continuous per-spot or per-cell activity features for downstream KLD-based differential-activity testing, e.g., on Visium spatial transcriptomics data.

name: gene-set-outlier-thresholding
description: Use when computing PC1/SVD-based gene set (module) activity from a normalized expression matrix and you must remove aberrant genes that would distort the percentage of variance explained by PC1 (L1) before scoring module activity.

name: gene-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when comparing a ranked or selected gene list against published biomarker signatures or DEG lists (e.g., top-14 UGCB sets) to report overlap counts, percentages, and shared gene symbols.

name: gene-set-overlap-jaccard-analysis
description: Use when comparing significant gene-set or DE gene call lists from two or more enrichment/DE methods and you need a set-level concordance metric to confirm that a more method's extra hits are consistent with existing calls.

name: gene-set-overlap-quantification
description: Use when auditing whether a published PDAC signature (Bailey ADEX, Exocrine, Immunogenic) is confounded by non-tumor-specific genes, or when you need to reproduce signature-vs-signature overlap fractions across curated pdacR bulk RNAseq datasets.

name: gene-set-overlap-rate-computation
description: Use when evaluating whether a feature-selection strategy (Seurat-style HVG, random-forest HIG, or scCAD ensemble) preserves a reference rare-cell-type DE gene set, using OR1/OR2/OR3 overlap rates.

name: gene-set-overrepresentation-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a filtered gene list (e.g. markers exceeding an AUC threshold) and need to test whether defined gene sets (GO CC/MF terms) are overrepresented at FDR < 0.05.

name: gene-set-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell GEX matrix has already been QC-filtered, clustered, and cell-type classified within the gExcite/scAmpi workflow, and differentially expressed genes per cluster must be assigned biological pathway context.

name: gene-set-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have JOINTLY factor/module gene sets (liver$modules) or factor-associated genes and need to know which biological processes or pathways each interpretable factor represents.

name: gene-set-pca-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix (RNA-seq cpm/vst or proteomics) plus gene sets (GMT/MSigDB or custom signatures) and need per-sample module activity scores with statistical significance.

name: gene-set-permutation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate a gene-set-scoring cell-type annotation pipeline — i.e., measure how annotation accuracy (sensitivity/specificity) degrades as marker sets are corrupted with random genes at increasing replacement rates.

name: gene-set-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when RNA-seq expression data with case/control group labels (e.g. GEO GSE172114) must be mapped onto extracted network submodules and compared for perturbation strength via source-sink path ACEs and Bonferroni-combined P-values plus DEG counts.

name: gene-set-score-computation
description: Use when building or applying a ProjectSVR reference model: you need a gene-set (signature) score matrix — e.g., from cNMF-derived or overexpression-tested gene sets, top 25 genes per set — as regression input features.

name: gene-set-score-computation-across-bulk-transcriptomic-datasets
description: Use when you have bulk genes-by-samples expression matrices (microarray or RNAseq, e.g. pdacR $ex objects) with sample-level tissue metadata, and you need per-sample gene-set scores to compare signature activity across compartments like normal pancreas, primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, and metastases.

name: gene-set-score-feature-augmentation
description: Use when preparing representative single-cell reference data for scSemiProfiler's deep generative model, where raw normalized expression alone under-constrains in silico inference of target samples.

name: gene-set-size-filtering
description: Use when preparing gene-by-gene-set annotation matrices (e.g. binary 0/1 data.frames from MSigDB or MGI GO GAF 2.0 files) as inputs for iDEA GSE analysis, and sparse sets below the size threshold must be removed first.

name: gene-set-size-null-model-fitting
description: Use when scoring cell-type marker gene sets of widely varying sizes against scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., Miko scoring on a Cell Catalog or permuted marker sets) and raw enrichment scores must be corrected for gene set-size bias before significance calling.

name: gene-set-size-stratified-summary-statistics
description: Use when comparing gene-set scoring methods across multiple BP sets and you need overall plus Ngenes-stratified (e.g., Ngenes>200) summary statistics such as mean Pearson correlation.

name: gene-set-spatial-relevance-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a pathway activity scoring method's ability to detect spatially relevant gene sets, by benchmarking delta-KLD separation between true and random gene sets across simulated ST spatial organization patterns (hotspot, gradient, streak).

name: gene-set-specificity-scoring-jsd
description: Use when you already have per-cell pathway activity weights (e.g. from run.rwr on an MCA co-embedding) and spot/cell group annotations, and need a numeric JSD-based score of how specific each gene set is to a cluster or anatomical annotation.

name: gene-set-transcription-factor-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have gene programs (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs) with gene-level weights and want to identify putative upstream TF regulators by intersecting TF binding/potential scores with the program's TF weights.

name: gene-set-variation-analysis-scoring
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells need pathway-level activity scores (e.g. MSigDB angiogenesis or a user GMT gene set) to flag pathway-high subpopulations within a tumor microenvironment.

name: gene-set-variation-analysis-scoring
description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, .csv) and want gene-set-level activity scores (e.g. hypoxia/glycolysis) per sample to enable group comparisons, KM/Cox analysis or correlation of pathway activity.

name: gene-signature-aggregate-scoring
description: Use when you have a gene set (TMGs/NMGs or other DEG-derived signature) and a matched expression-plus-phenotype matrix (e.g., 962 GDSC cancer cell lines x 265 compound IC50 values) and need a single signature-level score per sample to correlate with the phenotype.

name: gene-signature-based-sample-annotation
description: Use when bulk PDAC expression samples need subtype calls under one or more published signatures, or when concordance between Moffitt, Collisson, and Bailey subtype labels must be quantified per sample.

name: gene-signature-based-training-label-calibration
description: Use when building or retraining a malignant-vs-normal scRNA-seq classifier and the initial malignancy labels come from heterogeneous original annotations that may contain mislabeled cells.

name: gene-signature-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when RCC clusters (e.g. CT/PAN glioblastoma clusters or SKCM subtypes) must be validated against a known transcriptional signature to confirm biologically distinct subtype identity.

name: gene-signature-geneset-handling
description: Use when assembling gene signatures for UCell/AddModuleScore_UCell scoring — e.g. building Tcell, Myeloid, NK, Plasma_cell marker lists on a scRNA-seq matrix, marking negative markers with '-', or deciding how absent genes should be treated.

name: gene-signature-merging
description: Use when you have multiple cell-type- or tissue-specific gene signatures (e.g., SenePy hub signatures) and need to derive a consolidated universal or tissue-level signature with statistically filtered, weighted genes.

name: gene-signature-per-cell-scoring
description: Use when you have an annotated Seurat object with condition metadata and want per-cell scores and top genes for a pathway signature (e.g., innate immune response) across conditions and cell types.

name: gene-signature-reproducibility-checking
description: Use when a published nested-CV transcriptomic model reports a final fitted gene signature (ranked nonzero coefficients) and you need to verify your refit retains the same genes in the same order.

name: gene-signature-scoring
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix plus a set of pre-defined gene signatures (.gmt) and want per-cell signature Z-scores and a statistic of whether signature variation tracks a cell similarity structure such as a phylogeny or KNN graph.

name: gene-signature-scoring-for-exhaustion
description: Use when a cell population (e.g., 2064 melanoma T cells) has been partitioned into subpopulations (C1–C5) in reconstructed pseudo-space and you must test whether the subpopulation nearest malignant cells carries a higher functional signature score (exhaustion) than a distant one.

name: gene-signature-scoring-from-degs
description: Use when a single-cell cluster's DEGs (e.g., scanpyobj.h5ad / cluster_DEGs.csv) must be tested against bulk RNA-seq cohorts (e.g., TCGA-LIHC) for prognostic significance via signature scoring and survival analysis.

name: gene-signature-scoring-pdac-tumors
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq tumor expression matrix plus two competing gene signatures (basal-like vs classical) and need per-sample subtype calls comparable to published schema, followed by survival testing.

name: gene-signature-specificity-partitioning
description: Use when a curated gene signature needs to be audited for tissue- or tumor-specificity confounders — e.g., checking if ADEX/Immunogenic genes are driven by non-PDAC or adrenal (ACC) signal before using the signature for subtyping.

name: gene-signature-weight-estimation
description: Use when mapping target scRNA-seq cells to reference clusters and you need discriminative weights for cluster-specific gene signatures — e.g. before scid_multiclass scoring or when batch effect/strong asymmetry in cell number and library size means weights should come from the target data.

name: gene-significance-filtering
description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values for two treatments vs a common control must be partitioned into significance-filtered regions of interest (quadrants A–E, or M/R/S in the full scorecard) by fold-change magnitude.

name: gene-significance-selection-thresholding
description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell expression matrix and a redPATH pseudotime ordering and need to rank or filter genes for significance along the trajectory using dCor and MIC statistics.

name: gene-similarity-distance-matrix-computation
description: Use when preparing the gene-similarity input required by the TACTiCS class in tactics.py: you have protein sequences for the genes of two species' scRNA-seq datasets and need the distance matrix describing gene similarities.

name: gene-similarity-scoring
description: Use when two single-cell pseudotime trajectories (e.g., human and mouse bone marrow) have been aligned by CAPITAL tree alignment and you need to score which marker genes show conserved versus species-biased expression kinetics.

name: gene-space-batch-correction-combat-scgen
description: Use when evaluating RNA velocity models on multi-batch data and you need gene-space batch-corrected baselines (ComBat or scGen feeding UniTVelo) to compare against dynamics-based correction such as LatentVelo's batch_correction=True VAE.

name: gene-space-reconstruction-via-domain-specific-batch-normalization
description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., log1p-normalized pancreas matrix, 2000 HVGs) and you need corrected outputs in the original gene space instead of only latent embeddings, avoiding the interpretability loss of latent-space-only methods.

name: gene-specific-bulk-expression-transformation
description: Use when decomposing bulk RNA-seq into cell-type proportions using a scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference where technical differences between single-cell and bulk chemistries introduce gene-specific biases that break direct proportionality assumptions.

name: gene-specific-latent-time-inference
description: Use when the dataset contains complex branching, cycling progenitors, or sparse cell types where a single transcriptome-wide latent time is inappropriate, and per-gene time is needed to recover trajectory structure.

name: gene-specific-length-scale-gaussian-process-modeling
description: Use when identifying spatially variable genes in spatially-resolved transcriptomics data (e.g., Visium DLPFC, ST mouse OB) where genes may have different spatial ranges (length scales) and scalable fitting over thousands of spots is required.

name: gene-specific-linear-bias-simulation
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking bulk RNA-seq cell-type decomposition methods under simulated single-cell-vs-bulk technical bias, especially with snRNA-seq reference data such as adipose nuclei.

name: gene-subset-model-retraining
description: Use when you must determine whether a reduced or stratified gene feature set (e.g., pan-cancer-common vs. dataset-unique DEGs) retains a trained malignant-vs-normal classifier's performance.

name: gene-subspace-assignment
description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq training gene set (genes expressed in at least two cells with at least one percent non-zero entries) must be partitioned into gene subspaces so that dropout-imputation regression can be run within each group.

name: gene-symbol-cross-referencing
description: Use when you have gene symbol lists from a network/biomarker pipeline and need to annotate each gene with drug-actionability status (e.g., DrugBank active targets) and literature association to identify novel candidate biomarkers.

name: gene-symbol-disambiguation-widget-implementation
description: Use when building or extending Gene Updater–style date-to-gene conversion and input data contains duplicate Mar-01 or Mar-02 terms that could each map to two genes (MTARC1/MARCHF1, MTARC2/MARCHF2), requiring user-assigned resolution.

name: gene-symbol-standardization
description: Use when combining marker gene sets from multiple published marker databases or cell-sorting collections and you need consistent gene nomenclature and cell type labels before computing cross-source overlaps or integrating markers.

name: gene-tf-matrix-construction-with-peak-features
description: Use when you have open-chromatin candidate regions (e.g. ATAC/DNase peaks) with activity scores and need a gene-level TF affinity matrix (genes as rows, TFs as columns) whose scaling follows the chosen region–gene mapping mode.

name: gene-time-correlation-analysis
description: Use when ranking genes by Pearson correlation with a continuous time variable (e.g., a 12-hour C. elegans developmental course) and comparing top-N correlation distributions to score denoising recovery.

name: gene-to-cell-type-score-conversion
description: Use when you have a ranked per-cell-type marker list from reference data and a LogNormalized query/reference expression matrix (AnnData) that must be converted into a per-cell cell-type score matrix for label transfer or integration.

name: gene-to-token-weight-mapping
description: Use when you have run TOSICA.pre on a query AnnData and need to trace attention weights back to gene sets (e.g., reactome.gmt, GO_bp.gmt tokens) to interpret why cells received particular cell type predictions.

name: gene-token-attribution-scoring
description: Use when you have per-cell top-expressing gene ranking sequences with cell type labels and want to rank genes by their attention-derived attribution scores to find cell-type-specific markers.

name: gene-topic-probability-interpretation
description: Use when you have a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix and want to decompose it into latent topics (biological functions) and obtain interpretable per-topic gene-probability distributions.

name: gene-transcript-id-mapping
description: Use when scRNA AnnData var_names are transcript-level or otherwise inconsistent with the gene IDs in an orthomap/OrthoFinder-derived gene age table, and IDs must be collapsed or matched before computing gene age-weighted TEI.

name: gene-updater-local-streamlit-deployment
description: Use when csv or .xlsx gene expression files contain gene symbols auto-converted to dates by Excel (e.g. SEPT1, MARC1 becoming date strings, or ambiguous Mar-01/Mar-02 terms) and need to be converted back to HGNC-approved gene names.

name: gene-variability-ranking
description: Use when you have a gene expression matrix (e.g. GSE125792, 1968 genes) and need to screen or rank stable endogenous reference genes for qPCR normalization in Python.

name: gene-variance-based-feature-subsetting
description: Use when evaluating a pathway-activity classifier's robustness to missing data or cross-platform gene annotation gaps, by testing whether balanced accuracy stays high (>90%) with far fewer genes than the full annotated set.

name: gene-verse-chemokine-subfamily-filtering
description: Use when you have pre-computed cell-cell interaction data from multiple biological conditions and need to isolate one ligand-receptor subfamily (e.g., CXC/CC chemokines) and compute which interactions are unique to each condition.

name: gene-verse-int-pair-filtering
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor interaction (CCI) data loaded in InterCellar and need to test whether a specific ligand family (e.g. chemokines) or set of cluster-pairs (e.g. secretory-to-neutrophil) drives communication in one condition versus another.

name: gene-weight-top-contributor-ranking
description: Use when a rROMA analysis flags a module as over-dispersed or shifted and you need to identify which individual genes carry the largest PC1 weights, e.g. to nominate a lead gene for follow-up in a CF vs healthy comparison.

name: gene-wise-linear-regression-on-perturbation-indicators
description: Use when building consensus pathway-response signatures from a compendium of perturbation experiments: per-gene z-scores and a binary perturbation indicator matrix are available and pathway-responsiveness coefficients are needed.

name: gene-wise-overdispersion-estimation-qc
description: Use when NEBULA (NEBULA-LN or NEBULA-HL) has been run gene-wise on multi-subject scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts and per-gene summary statistics include convergence codes plus subject-level and cell-level overdispersions that must be screened before downstream interpretation.

name: gene-wise-permutation-randomization
description: Use when analyzing a sparse single-cell expression matrix where you must separate sparsity-induced spurious eigenvector localization from true biological signal before RMT denoising.

name: gene-wise-z-score-scaling
description: Use when building a Connectome edgelist whose edgeweights must reflect cell-type-specific expression roles (weight_sc/weightscale) rather than raw connectivity (weight_norm), e.g. before CreateConnectome on scRNA-seq data.

name: gene-zweight-averaging-into-mec-profiles
description: Use when a cohort-shared ICA gene z-weight matrix (task_inputs port 'ica_zweight_matrix') is available and the goal is to collapse reproducible ICs into consensus meta-components for tumor microenvironment annotation.

name: genecards-gene-annotation-querying
description: Use when a gene list (e.g. 16,000 HVGs from FindVariableFeatures(), variance, scranpy and M3drop) must be classified by database annotation into communication-related vs. function-only categories before downstream filtering.

name: generalized-em-iteration-rna-velocity
description: Use when fitting TF-based gene dynamics and latent times on scRNA-seq data with TFvelo, or when reproducing/tuning the EM optimization loop (weight updates, dynamics updates, time assignment) for RNA velocity without splicing counts.

name: generalized-linear-model-count-modeling
description: Use when raw single-cell gene count data (e.g. Smart-seq2) has cells assigned to clone/subclone groups and you must test which genes differ between groups while accounting for plate and detection-rate confounders.

name: generated-cell-quality-evaluation-rf-auc-mmd
description: Use when you have cscGAN/scGAN-generated scRNA-seq cells (e.g. .h5ad output for specific PBMC clusters) and need to judge whether they are realistic and indistinguishable from real cells of the target clusters.

name: generative-adversarial-network-training
description: Use when aligning two non-overlapping single-cell modalities (e.g. Full PBMC source/target manifolds) whose topoAE embeddings must be mapped into a common space, especially when GAN-to-GAN variability across initializations is too high.

name: generative-adversarial-network-training
description: Use when the goal is to train a GAN on single-cell RNA-seq data (.h5/.h5ad) so that generated cells are hard to distinguish from real cells by t-SNE embedding, marker-gene correlation, MMD, and classifier AUC.

name: generative-model-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq data from a trained generative model must be quantitatively compared to held-out real cells and rival simulators (e.g., 10x Genomics PBMC-CTL, 1000 generated cells vs 1000 test cells).

name: generative-model-online-fine-tuning
description: Use when transferring cell annotations (discrete types or continuous fate probabilities) from a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset to an independent query dataset whose batch or distribution differs, e.g. cross-species or cross-platform queries in h5ad format.

name: generative-model-training-single-cell
description: Use when you have a reference scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad/AnnData) and need unbiased low-dimensional cell embeddings robust to batch effect, as input for Cell BLAST querying, benchmarking, or annotation transfer.

name: geneset-overlap-scoring
description: Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq cells for membership in a gene signature (e.g. LM22 cell-type sets from a .gmt file) by counting genes expressed above a threshold, especially on sparse pbmc3k-style count matrices where smoothing should boost detection.

name: geneset-signature-scoring
description: Use when per-cell gene set scores from sparse scRNA-seq count matrices are too noisy for downstream tasks (e.g. AUC discrimination of cell types), and you want scores computed on neighbor-smoothed data in a Scanpy AnnData workflow.

name: genetic-constraint-score-interpretation
description: Use when per-gene statistics such as CTMM cell type-specificity or mean-difference measures must be related to gene-level annotations like LOEUF, pLI, enhancer domain score (EDS), or enhancer count.

name: genetic-interaction-pattern-mining
description: Use when genotype data (SNPs x samples, binary or additive encoding), binary phenotype labels, covariate classes, and a gene-interaction priors file (PPI edges, pathways, complexes) are available, and the goal is to discover higher-order (k>=2) multi-gene meta-markers associated with the phenotype.

name: genetic-meta-marker-ground-truth-annotation
description: Use when benchmarking higher-order genetic meta-marker miners: you need synthetic SNP data (n=3000 samples, per-gene SNP counts U[3,10]) where the true associated connected subgraph of the gene-interaction prior is known.

name: genetic-meta-marker-pattern-mining
description: Use when a case/control GWAS-style dataset has SNPs mapped to genes plus a gene-interaction prior (PPI edges, 3-cliques, protein complexes) and you need significant multi-gene marker combinations stronger than FastCMH or SiNIMin can find.

name: genome-annotation-csv-validation
description: Use when preparing a CSV of genome annotation for cis-NAT identification with CCIVR and you must confirm the required id/Chr/Strand/Start/End columns (and optional expression columns) exist before running.

name: genome-annotation-index-building
description: Use when preparing scTE (or scTEATAC) quantification for single-cell RNA/ATAC-seq alignments and a prebuilt index for the genome assembly (mm10, hg38, panTro6, macFas5, dm6, danRer11, xenTro9) is not yet available.

name: genome-annotation-statistics-verification
description: Use when reproducing a published annotation result (e.g. peaks2utr 3' UTR counts on T. brucei scRNA-seq) and you must confirm your output GFF3/GTF matches reported totals and new/altered/unchanged partitions.

name: genome-annotation-strand-filtering
description: Use when preparing a genome annotation CSV for CCIVR-style cis-NAT extraction and you need to restrict candidate antisense partners to same-chromosome, opposite-strand genes (e.g., selecting the 1,352 minus-strand X-chromosome genes for the Xist/Tsix FO example).

name: genome-browser-coverage-visualization
description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads must be visually validated against real reads at the read-sequence level, e.g. comparing coverage tracks of scReadSim BAM output vs minnow/bowtie2-aligned FASTQ over binned genomic windows.

name: genome-build-version-matching
description: Use when quantifying transcript abundances from RNA-seq FASTQ files that feed isoform-level analyses (e.g. CanIsoNet), and transcript identifiers must match a specific Ensembl genome build such as human GRCh37.p13.

name: genome-collection-index-construction
description: Use when a collection of FASTA/MultiLine FASTA/FASTQ datasets (gzipped or not) must be indexed so that future sequence queries can list which datasets contain the query, with bounded RAM, disk footprint, and construction time.

name: genome-coordinate-liftover-harmonization
description: Use when annotation reference databases or BED/GFF resources are provided in different genome builds (e.g. hg18, hg19, hg38) than the genome used for read alignment, and coordinates must be converted before overlap-based annotation.

name: genome-coordinate-mapping-of-mirna-loci
description: Use when merging miRNA annotations from multiple public databases and sRNA-Seq predictions for a species with a reference genome, and all loci must be expressed in a single uniform genome coordinate system before selection.

name: genome-coordinate-windowing-and-extraction
description: Use when a genome annotation (GTF) and reference genome (e.g., hg19 FASTA) must be turned into fixed-length, strand-corrected sequence fragments centered on candidate residues for downstream model prediction.

name: genome-fasta-preprocessing-and-header-normalization
description: Use when a plant reference genome FASTA must be fed into the tncRNA Toolkit or any Bowtie-based small-RNA pipeline that requires 'chr'-prefixed headers, masked tRNA loci, and an index under lib/indexes/<species>.

name: genome-guided-transcriptome-assembly
description: Use when assembling transcripts from RNA-seq reads aligned to a reference genome and single-aligner assemblers (StringTie2, Scallop) miss transcripts because no single alignment covers all splice junctions, or when benchmarking assembler accuracy.

name: genome-metadata-table-augmentation
description: Use when you have a gene cluster absence/presence matrix plus literature-derived lifestyle labels, and genomes labeled 'unknown' need a predicted lifestyle appended to the metadata table.

name: genome-personalization-from-phased-vcf
description: Use when RNA-seq reads must be assigned to a specific haplotype (e.g. for allele-specific alternative splicing counting) and per-sample phased VCFs plus a reference FASTA are available.

name: genome-scale-metabolic-modeling
description: Use when transcriptomic data (bulk RNA-seq matrix, Seurat object, or cell-cluster expression profiles) must be converted into reaction-level flux distributions under a defined nutrient medium, e.g. nutrient-aware cancer metabolism analysis of TCGA or single-cell TME data.

name: genome-sequence-reconstruction-with-variant-masking
description: Use when performing allele-specific expression (ASE) analysis in an F1 hybrid cross (e.g., CAST×B6) and reads must be assigned to parental origin via a strain-specific or diploid reference rather than a single generic reference genome.

name: genome-space-modification-aggregation
description: Use when NanoSpeech basecalled fasta/q read headers carry modification (inosine or multi-mod) indexes and you need them mapped to reference coordinates and aggregated into per-site modification counts/frequencies.

name: genome-transcriptome-coordinate-transform
description: Use when phasiRNA/siRNA clusters were predicted separately against a reference genome and a reference transcriptome and need to be unified into a single, deduplicated PHAS locus set with gene annotations.

name: genome-wide-dh-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when you have BIRD-predicted DH matrices (log2(x+1)) plus true DNase-seq profiles for multiple cell types and need to quantify prediction accuracy overall, for differential DH, or versus ChromImpute.

name: genomic-alteration-significance-testing
description: Use when you have per-sample attention-head features from a pretrained tGPT model over tumor bulk transcriptomes and need to link them to mutation, HRD, genome-doubling, TMB, or survival annotations.

name: genomic-annotation-command-line-workflow-execution
description: Use when you have a GFF/GTF gene model plus a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) and need to annotate or refine 3' UTR features at the genome level.

name: genomic-annotation-cross-referencing
description: Use when a set of variants or genes identified by identifiers (GENCODE v19 gene symbols and/or Ensembl gene IDs) must be joined to per-gene quantitative scores (MRSD read depths) across biosamples to yield a per-variant classification and an aggregate fraction.

name: genomic-bias-correction-with-local-features
description: Use when raw N*N single-cell Hi-C contact matrices are sparse and biased by local genomic features (effective length, GC content, fragment-end mappability) and must be normalized before DCI testing with scHiCDiff.KS/CVM/NB/ZINB.

name: genomic-control-inflation-assessment-lambda-gc
description: Use when benchmarking DE or gene set enrichment methods on scRNA-seq summary statistics and you need to check p-value calibration via a genomic control factor (lambda_gc), as in the iDEA paper's Fig. 4 comparison.

name: genomic-control-inflation-factor-estimation
description: Use when benchmarking whether a competitive GSE method (iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) yields well-calibrated p-values under null simulations on zero-inflated scRNA-seq data.

name: genomic-coordinate-alignment-of-prediction-tracks
description: Use when two genome-wide DH or regulome track sets (e.g., BIRD predictions and ChromImpute imputations) must be compared across shared loci and cell types, requiring coordinate/locus matching before correlation.

name: genomic-coordinate-binning
description: Use when per-nucleotide scores (e.g. RSCanner structure counts) must be aggregated into fixed non-overlapping windows along a transcript to rank regions, e.g. locating high-structure-density segments in a long RNA.

name: genomic-coordinate-format-unification
description: Use when merging already annotated miRNAs from heterogeneous databases (miRBase, PmiREN, sRNAanno, PsRNA) with novel sRNA-Seq-derived precursor predictions that use inconsistent coordinate representations.

name: genomic-coordinate-overlap-comparison
description: Use when comparing predicted UTR (or other interval) coordinates from multiple tools against a reference annotation and you need a tolerant agreement fraction rather than exact-match counting.

name: genomic-coordinate-overlap-detection
description: Use when you have CSV gene annotations (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) for a genome and need to enumerate all antisense gene pairs whose loci overlap, stratified by overlap structure.

name: genomic-coordinate-translation-of-mirnas
description: Use when annotated miRNA records from public plant databases and newly predicted precursors from sRNA-Seq must be merged into one non-redundant candidate set on a common reference genome.

name: genomic-feature-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-region expression estimates (e.g., uTAR pseudo-bulk coverage) plus a PCA loading matrix from single-cell expression data and need to ask whether the most highly expressed features are also the ones that define cell types.

name: genomic-flanking-sequence-retrieval
description: Use when you have coordinate-annotated modification sites (e.g., BED-format Ψ sites from RMBase) and need fixed-width sequence fragments centered on each site from a matching reference genome for downstream ML feature encoding.

name: genomic-interval-extraction-around-editing-sites
description: Use when you have REDItools outTables of candidate A-to-G substitutions and need fixed-length 101-nt centered sequence contexts (with per-position nucleotide frequencies) to feed a deep-learning editing classifier such as REDInet.

name: genomic-interval-intersection
