description: Use when predicted genomic features (e.g., aptardi polyA-site bins in BED format) must be validated against reference annotation intervals (PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3) to derive TP/FP classifications and precision/recall metrics.

name: genomic-interval-merging
description: Use when strand-specific predicted intervals (e.g., groHMM TAR predictions on BED files) must be consolidated into non-overlapping features within a distance threshold such as 500 bp before coverage filtering.

name: genomic-interval-nearest-matching
description: Use when predicted genomic intervals (e.g. IPA sites from InPACT, APAIQ, IPAFinder) must be validated against reference polyA site sets (A-seq, 3P-seq, polyA-seq, Iso-seq) by nearest-feature distance rather than exact overlap.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis
description: Use when validating predicted genomic regions (e.g., dsRID dsRNA BED files) against an experimentally derived interval set (e.g., J2 fCLIP-seq peaks) by intersecting coordinates and quantifying overlap fractions.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you already have a scHiCDiff DCI results data frame (bin pairs with pvalue.adj.FDR) and need downstream functional annotation: epigenetic mark association at DCI bins and GO enrichment of DCI-linked genes.

name: genomic-interval-overlap-classification
description: Use when phasiRNA/PHAS loci predicted against both a transcriptome and a genome reference must be de-duplicated into reference-unique sets and each unique locus classified by exon/intron structure from a gff3 annotation (e.g. mirroring Supplementary Fig. S3).

name: genomic-interval-overlap-counting
description: Use when comparing null distributions of random overlap counts between region sets over different genomic or transcriptome backgrounds, e.g., quantifying how many overlaps arise by chance over DNA vs mRNA permutation spaces.

name: genomic-interval-sequence-extraction
description: Use when converting tabix-indexed REDItools outTables into per-site 8×101 feature matrices for TCN-based editing classification, e.g. filtering candidates (cov≥50, ≥3 Gs, A-to-G freq≥0.01) and pulling flanking sequence from a faidx-indexed genome.

name: genomic-region-masking-with-bedtools
description: Use when building a reference for tncRNA (tRF/tRNA half) detection where reads mapping to non-tRNA loci would otherwise be misattributed, and tRNA regions plus 50 nt flanks must be masked before adding artificial tRNA chromosomes.

name: genomic-resolution-matching-resampling
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq inferred copy number profiles against bulk WGS/WES ground truth whose native resolution differs from the single-cell profile bins, requiring harmonization before correlation.

name: genomic-sequence-bin-feature-extraction
description: Use when you need per-position (binned) DNA sequence and/or RNA-Seq coverage features over transcript 3' terminal exons from a GTF to feed a sequence+coverage machine-learning model such as aptardi's biLSTM.

name: genomic-track-alignment-and-integration
description: Use when one or few DNase-seq (or ChIP-seq) replicates are available and a BIRD-predicted DH track can be merged with observed signal on shared genomic bins, then benchmarked against a held-out truth replicate via genome-wide Pearson correlation.

name: genomic-variant-interval-overlap
description: Use when you have a list of genetic variants (e.g. lead sQTLs from sQTLseekeR2) and two disjoint genomic interval sets, and need to test whether variants are preferentially located in one set (e.g. ps introns) versus the other (cs introns).

name: genomics-assay-library-structure-annotation
description: Use when you need to write or schema-validate a machine-readable specification (spec.yaml) of a sequencing assay's library structure — regions, region types, sequences, and onlists — before preprocessing FASTQs with cellatlas/kb.

name: genorm-normfinder-stability-measure-computation
description: Use when benchmarking candidate reference-gene (RG) combinations from a qPCR array (raw CT matrix, e.g. data_GSE78870/data_GSE50013) and you need GeNorm and NormFinder stability measures for each weighted k-gene combination.

name: genotype-based-single-cell-deconvolution
description: Use when you have 10X scRNA-seq data (possorted_genome_bam.bam + barcodes.tsv) from a multi-person blood mixture, with live cells, and need genotype-based single-cell separation of contributors — especially imbalanced mixtures at ratios up to 1:60.

name: genotype-maf-filtering
description: Use when a raw genotype matrix (columns chr, start, end, snpId; alleles coded 0=REF/REF, 1=REF/ALT, 2=ALT/ALT, -1=missing) must be filtered to well-powered biallelic variants before sQTL association testing.

name: genotyping-array-data-processing
description: Use when raw genotyping array CEL files need conversion to a filtered VCF, or when RNA-seq variant calls must be validated against an independent genotyping panel by sample-level concordance.

name: geo-accession-data-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark or reproduction task names a published dataset only by its GEO accession code (e.g., GSE125970 for colon epithelial cells) and the original count matrix must be obtained before scoring cells.

name: geo-accession-data-retrieval
description: Use when a GEO-deposited bulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., GSE23649: 8 DBD EAD vs 8 DBD non-EAD liver transplant samples) must be retrieved in R to validate single-cell signatures.

name: geo-accession-data-retrieval
description: Use when a reproducibility or benchmarking task requires the CBMC CITE-seq RNA counts and ADT counts from GEO accession GSE100866, e.g. to test whether ALRA imputation improves gene-expression-space consistency with protein distances.

name: geo-count-matrix-loading
description: Use when a downstream tool requires a raw/normalized scRNA-seq count matrix from GEO (genes as rows, cells as columns) as its expression_matrix input, e.g. before running ORIGINS activity or benchmarking against LandSCENT/CytoTRACE.

name: geo-dataset-acquisition-and-loading
description: Use when a task requires downloading a specific GEO-accessioned single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., GSE141259) and preparing raw count matrices as a Seurat object for embedding or hyperparameter-optimization analyses.

name: geo-dataset-acquisition-and-processing
description: Use when starting from a public GEO scRNA-seq accession (e.g. GSE81682, GSE129788, GSE100866, GSE87038) and the goal is a processed Seurat/AnnData object ready for export to CellexalVR input files.

name: geo-dataset-preprocessing
description: Use when raw GEO expression matrices (RNA-seq or microarray .csv with sample names as first column and labels as last column) contain missing gene values or platform distribution differences that must be resolved before cross-platform training with Ciclops.

name: geo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce a published differential methylation analysis from raw array data, and the source dataset (e.g., GSE207426) is available on GEO as IDAT files with a sample sheet.

name: geo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a task specifies a public scRNA-seq dataset by GEO accession (e.g. GSE119945) and the raw count matrix must be downloaded, QC'd, log-normalized, and loaded into Seurat before downstream feature-selection benchmarking.

name: geo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis requires real published HTO datasets — e.g., surveying typical dataset quality with an overlap score (ovs) or correlating HTO counts with detected genes across datasets — and GEO accessions or 'recently published' HTO data must be downloaded.

name: geo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a task requires the original macaque retina bipolar-cell count matrix and sample metadata (macaque id, region id, sample id) needed to reproduce DESC clustering ARI benchmarks.

name: geo-encode-dataset-retrieval-and-reprocessing
description: Use when candidate circRNA regulators (e.g. CRIT-predicted RBPs) need experimental validation via reanalysis of public knockdown RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENCODE, with global circRNA abundance compared between knockdown and control conditions.

name: geo-expression-data-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs subtype-labeled bulk expression profiles as raw input for marker-gene detection or deconvolution benchmarking, and the dataset is identified by a GEO accession number such as GSE28490.

name: geo-expression-data-retrieval
description: Use when a workflow needs bulk gene expression data for public pre-clinical CRC datasets identified by GEO (GSE*) or ArrayExpress (E-MTAB-*) accessions, as input to downstream classification or subtyping.

name: geo-expression-dataset-handling
description: Use when raw/processed RNA-seq lung expression data must be fetched from GEO accessions (e.g. GSE147507, GSE148729) and converted into per-sample binarized gene expression vectors to drive context-specific metabolic model reconstruction.

name: geo-expression-matrix-loading
description: Use when starting from a GEO-deposited microarray dataset (tab-delimited probe-level matrix such as gse.txt) and the downstream analysis requires ERgene's DataFrame-format input for reference gene screening or normalization.

name: geo-microarray-data-retrieval
description: Use when the analysis needs a real-world disease gene list (e.g. for enrichment testing) and GEO accession IDs are known or discoverable via MeSH-term queries, as with RA microarray datasets GSE12021/GSE55457/GSE55584/GSE55235.

name: geo-microarray-download-and-metadata-curation
description: Use when a meta-analysis needs to harvest multiple public microarray studies from GEO (series matrix or raw probe intensities) and requires unified, cross-study sample metadata before normalization or batch correction.

name: geo-mirna-expression-ranking
description: Use when you need to identify the most abundantly expressed endogenous miRNAs from a GEO expression accession (e.g., GSE172269 rat liver) so their predicted targets can be tested for cumulative expression shifts against a background in DESeq2 results.

name: geo-rnaseq-count-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis needs raw (unnormalized) RNA-seq count data plus sample metadata from a public GEO series to run a bulk-RNA-seq contrast such as SARS-CoV-2-infected vs mock lung cells.

name: geo-rnaseq-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis requires public embryo-development RNA-seq data — e.g. a specified GEO accession (GSE71434) or GEO-deposited scRNA-seq from cited references — that must be fetched and normalized before communication-strength or delta computation.

name: geo-scrna-seq-dataset-preprocessing
description: Use when a public GEO single-cell dataset (e.g., GSE84465) must be acquired, normalized, and log-transformed into a scanpy AnnData object to serve as input for an interpretable VAE such as VEGA.

name: geo-scrnaseq-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis requires reproducing a published single-cell result from raw public data, specifically when a GEO accession (e.g., GSE122043) must be converted into MDIC3's exp.txt/metadata.txt input format.

name: geo-series-data-retrieval
description: Use when starting from a GEO accession (GSE series) and you need the raw probe-level intensity matrix, its probe annotation table, and per-sample metadata to feed a curation or normalization pipeline.

name: geo-series-sample-subsetting
description: Use when a combined multi-study dataset (multiple GEO series merged into one SummarizedExperiment) must be narrowed to specific studies/conditions — e.g. isolating Pparg-knockdown samples across GSE12929 and GSE14004 for batch-removal or variance analyses.

name: geo-single-cell-dataset-acquisition-and-preprocessing
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation methods on the ScType paper datasets, or when standardized GEO/10x scRNA-seq download plus Seurat v4.0 normalization and clustering is needed as input to annotation.

name: geo-transcriptomic-clinical-data-harmonization
description: Use when a GEO accession (e.g. GSE78220) provides a raw/processed transcriptome matrix plus separate clinical or treatment-response metadata that must be aligned per sample before survival or responder-vs-non-responder analysis.

name: geo-transcriptomics-data-retrieval
description: Use when a analysis requires raw microarray/RNA-seq expression data hosted on GEO (a GSE accession) and it must be converted into per-condition gene-by-sample tab-separated matrices with a 'Gene' first column before downstream modeling.

name: geodb-transcriptomic-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when you need a reproducible annotation/inventory table (dataset, type, sample description, sample count, feature count, Used flag) for the thirteen human PDAC expression datasets housed in the pdacR R package, or when verifying curated dataset metadata against a published compendium table.

name: geometric-mean-expression-scoring
description: Use when ground-truth (supervised) CCI labels must be constructed for training a cell-cell interaction model: candidates come from a shared LRIDB over clustered scRNA-seq data (e.g. panc8 with Human labels, label_mode True) and no trusted label file exists yet.

name: geometric-mean-score-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking multiple trajectory inference methods (e.g., Totem vs Slingshot vs TinGa) scored with the four dynverse metrics against dynverse gold standards, and a single comparable overall score per method/topology is needed.

name: geometric-sketching-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking stability of communication-inference or clustering results against reduced cell counts, e.g. re-running CellChat on geometric sketches at 90/80/70% and scoring TPR/FPR/ACC vs full-data predictions.

name: geometric-versus-spherical-sketch-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare cell-subsampling (sketching) strategies on scRNA-seq data by quantifying how faithfully a sketch of 1%-10% of cells represents the full transcriptomic space or preserves cell-type separability.

name: geometry-preserving-correspondence-loss-implementation
description: Use when training a cross-modality GAN (e.g. scMMGAN) where the mapping must keep nearby points nearby across domains — e.g. aligning scRNA-seq with spatial transcriptomics while preserving manifold structure.

name: geoscrna-dataset-retrieval-and-preprocessing
description: Use when starting a scRNA-seq analysis from a public GEO accession (raw UMI count matrix) and a graph-based deep-learning method like scGAE requires scTransform-preprocessed input data.

name: gep-averaging-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomes (e.g. MCA count matrix) need a low-dimensional, biologically interpretable embedding built from known marker GEPs, and when benchmarking that embedding against PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA with clustering metrics.

name: gep-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a novel single-cell count matrix should be annotated per cell using reference marker GEPs (e.g., mca.marker.geps.txt) instead of clustering, and annotation purity against reference labels must be quantified.

name: gep-functional-classification
description: Use when you have gene co-expression modules (GEPs, e.g. MCL clusters of a GGM network) and need per-module GO/MP enrichment significance and a functional category split (identity vs. activity vs. morphogenesis).

name: gep-sparsity-screening
description: Use when you have run kernel-regularized NMF (e.g., par_estimate_nmf at rank ~16) on a log-normalized genes x cells matrix and must filter out degenerate gene expression programs before downstream use (e.g., biomarker binarization).

name: germ-cell-meiosis-stage-annotation
description: Use when a germ-cell query dataset (e.g. in vitro induced meiosis, Ythdc2-KO or Zfp541-KO germ cells) must be assigned meiotic stages by mapping onto the mTCA reference, and day-resolved meiotic entry rates or developmental arrest must be quantified.

name: germline-cna-region-removal
description: Use when constructing euploid-baseline single-cell inputs for simulated CNA benchmarking (e.g., SDX chrX pooling from male oligodendrocyte BAMs) or when donor cells carry germline CNAs that would confound somatic CNA calling.

name: germline-sirna-mutant-vs-wildtype-count-comparison
description: Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ data from wild type and mutant samples (e.g. C. elegans germline, mut-16) must be quantified per-gene by small RNA class defined by length, 5′ nucleotide, and antisense strandedness, with classes resolved from the same loci.

name: gff3-annotation-based-cluster-classification
description: Use when phasiRNA/siRNA cluster predictions exist in multiple coordinate systems (cDNA vs gDNA mapping) and must be merged, deduplicated, and annotated with GFF3 gene features into a unified PHAS loci catalog.

name: gff3-annotation-parsing
description: Use when a workflow requires reading gene models from a GFF3/GTF canonical annotation, merging tool-annotated 3' UTR features (source=peaks2utr) with original features, or comparing predicted UTRs against a canonical GFF truth set.

name: gff3-feature-annotation-handling
description: Use when supplying reference annotations (GFF3/GFF2/GTF) to tiny-count or tinyRNA for hierarchical small RNA-seq quantification, and feature IDs, Parent relationships, or genome/annotation identifier matching must be validated first.

name: gff3-genomic-feature-annotation-writing
description: Use when you must write a GFF3 annotation file that preserves existing gene model features and appends newly called 3' UTR features derived from BAM-aligned reads.

name: gff3-gtf-genomic-coordinate-parsing
description: Use when a feature list (e.g., miRNA precursors in table, GFF3/GTF, and FASTA formats) must be mapped to chromosome coordinates or assigned to subgenomes of a polyploid genome such as hexaploid bread wheat.

name: ggplot2-comparative-panel-visualization
description: Use when a synthetic single-cell count matrix must be visually validated against a real reference dataset by plotting comparative panels of dispersions, library sizes, fraction of zeros, and sample/feature correlations.

name: ggplot2-curve-visualization
description: Use when a per-cell scalar measurement (methylation rate, expression score) must be binned and smoothed along an ordered circular pseudo time-series (ordIndex/HMM phases G1, S, G2/M) and rendered as an annotated curve figure.

name: gibbs-sampler-implementation
description: Use when clustering droplet-based UMI count matrices from multiple individuals with BAMM-SC and you must run, tune, or validate the MCMC/Gibbs sampler (burn-in, iteration budget, log-likelihood tolerance) behind the hierarchical Dirichlet multinomial mixture.

name: gibbs-sampler-two-genome-mixture-modeling
description: Use when single-cell allele-level UMI counts at filtered SNVs are available and the goal is to detect a minor genotype, quantify mixing fraction, or decide K=1 vs K=2 in in silico or wet-lab chimerism mixtures.

name: gibbs-sampling-mcmc-implementation
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices contain pervasive dropouts (40%-90% missing values) and cell-to-cell relationships must be recovered via Bayesian matrix factorization with MCMC, optionally leveraging cell labels or bulk side information.

name: gibbs-sampling-synthetic-count-generation
description: Use when a trained scDBM (BoltzmannMachines.jl-based model on scRNA-seq count data) must be turned into synthetic observations of a target cell count, and when comparing sampling strategies such as Gibbs sampling against scVI prior/posterior sampling.

name: gillespie-ssa-cell-simulation
description: Use when dynamic cellular processes must be simulated in silico from a known GRN with ground-truth molecule counts (pre-mRNA, mRNA, protein) in the low-copy-number regime typical of single-cell omics.

name: gini-coefficient-cell-type-balance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing subsampling/sketching methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a single numeric score of how well each method preserves cell-type balance, especially capture of rare cell types.

name: gini-coefficient-computation
description: Use when you have factor loadings from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition (e.g. rank=10 BALF COVID-19 tensor) and need a scalar inequality statistic per factor to characterize loading concentration across contexts or LR pairs.

name: gini-coefficient-computation
description: Use when comparing how imputation (e.g., ALRA vs. SAVER vs. raw) changes the gene-expression distribution of scRNA-seq data toward an orthogonal gold standard, via Gini coefficients over shared genes.

name: glm-based-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when pre-processed SingCellaR objects (e.g. eFL_1, eFL_2) have been QC-filtered and normalized with normalize_UMIs, and a set of highly variable genes is needed before PCA, UMAP, and Louvain clustering.

name: glm-pca-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking dimension-reduction methods on scRNAseq counts and a fast, scalable non-CA baseline (glmPCA) is needed to compare runtime or cluster accuracy against standard CA in corral.

name: glmnet-lasso-model-fitting
description: Use when fitting lasso or elastic-net glmnet models on high-dimensional data (P >> n, e.g. transcriptomics) where unbiased performance estimation requires nested CV with feature selection embedded in the outer loop.

name: global-optimization-dual-annealing
description: Use when a scalar hyperparameter (e.g. a target separation Delta) of an optimization-based method like scGeneFit must be tuned by maximizing a noisy, non-convex objective such as test-split label recovery accuracy, under a positivity constraint.

name: global-spatially-variable-gene-detection
description: Use when you have single-cell-resolution spatial expression (e.g. ~1,938-gene SpatialScope-imputed MERFISH mouse1_slice180 matrix) and need genes significantly spatially variable, not just cell-type-composition artifacts.

name: global-structure-preservation-assessment
description: Use when a 2D embedding (ivis or a comparable method) of high-dimensional single-cell data must be verified for preservation of global inter-cluster geometry, e.g. after embedding scRNA-seq (hippocampus, melanoma SCP11, retinal bipolar) or CyTOF (Levine-32-dim) data.

name: global-structure-visualization
description: Use when a high-dimensional dataset (e.g. nine-feature synthetic benchmarks, CyTOF, or scRNA-seq expression matrices) must be visualised in 2D without artificial cluster artifacts, and relative cluster locations and shapes must be preserved.

name: glomeruli-tubuli-morphometric-feature-regression
description: Use when pathomics AnnData objects (e.g., Kidney_IgAN_G.h5ad, Kidney_IgAN_T.h5ad) already carry a PILOT/EIPLGraph trajectory and you need to test which glomerular or tubular morphometric features change along the disease progression score.

name: glucose-uptake-flux-extraction
description: Use when METAFlux flux outputs (bulk RNA-seq samples run under human_blood medium) are available and a per-sample glucose uptake quantity is needed for correlation with FDG-PET SUV or subgroup survival analysis.

name: gmap-reference-index-construction
description: Use when raw long-read FASTQ data must be aligned to unspliced reference sequences (e.g. MANE Ensembl 108) with GMAP as the first step of a VIsoQLR isoform analysis workflow.

name: gmm-based-baf-shift-threshold-estimation
description: Use when CNV calls from RNA-seq expression-based HMM segmentation need to be validated or corrected by an allelic shift (LOH) signal, and a threshold for calling a BAF shift 'significant' must be learned from the data rather than fixed a priori.

name: gmm-based-cell-reliability-modeling
description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq (source) with unlabeled scATAC-seq gene-activity (target) h5ad data and you must decide per-cell which scATAC-seq cells are trustworthy for label transfer or are candidate novel cell types.

name: gmm-based-pseudo-time-reconstruction
description: Use when benchmarking cell-cycle pseudo-time inference on scRNA-seq data — e.g., five melanoma patient 10X Chromium samples (Mel78–Mel88) — and a model-free GMM baseline ordering is needed for GSEA NES comparison against a circular model such as Cyclum.

name: gmm-based-pseudotime-reconstruction
description: Decision support for comparing model-free pseudo-time reconstruction against model-based methods: use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., mESC, log2(x+1), scaled variance=1, centered mean=1) and need GMM-based cell-cycle pseudo-time or a robustness baseline.

name: gmt-gene-module-mask-assembly
description: Use when building a VEGA model or similar annotation-guided VAE: you have GMT-format gene set files (e.g., MSigDB) and a Scanpy AnnData matrix, and need the decoder mask linking GMVs to member genes.

name: gmt-gene-set-parsing
description: Use when a SingCellaR workflow requires curated signature gene sets from a .gmt file (e.g. lineage signatures for AUCell scoring or hematopoiesis sets for fGSEA) and the sets must be read in and verified first.

name: gmt-gene-set-parsing
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq analysis must encode cells over a priori annotated latent variables, requiring GMT gene-set files (pathways, cell type markers, GRNs) to be converted into VEGA's decoder membership matrix.

name: gmt-gene-set-signature-handling
description: Use when scoring single-cell AnnData with a curated signature (e.g., a 12-gene injury signature) that must be encoded in a .gmt gene set file with _UP/_DN nomenclature before calling gssnng scoring functions.

name: gmt-geneset-file-parsing
description: Use when a single-cell analysis needs per-cell gene set scores from a .gmt file (e.g. LM22 signatures on pbmc3k AnnData), and the gene sets must be extracted and direction-resolved before scoring.

name: gmv-activity-inference-per-cell
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data must be projected onto a prior gene module set (e.g., an ARACNe TF-target network in GMT format) to obtain per-cell module or master regulator activity scores with an interpretable latent space.

name: gmv-overlap-quantification
description: Use when reproducing VEGA's Fig. 4 generalization results: a trained VEGA model on PBMC scRNA-seq (Kang et al. GSE96583) must be evaluated on unseen cells (held-out cell type/condition or the Zheng et al. study) by measuring top-50 differential GMV overlap and reconstruction R2.

name: go-based-gene-subsetting
description: Use when preparing a raw single-cell expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns, gene_type 'gene_names') for redPATH pseudotime reconstruction and you need to subset to GO development genes before filtering.

name: go-biological-process-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when comparing trait-relevant gene sets from GWAS-to-single-cell gene prioritization methods and you need GO BP over-representation term counts (FDR < 0.01) as the functional-quality benchmark.

name: go-biological-process-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have many subject-/time-point-specific gene sets (e.g., 316 CRank-prioritized MuDCoD communities from Soskic-2022 CD4+ T cell activation networks) and need to identify which GO BP terms are recurrently enriched.

name: go-biological-process-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes or WGCNA co-expression module members and need to identify over-represented GO Biological Process terms linking gene sets to phenotypic traits.

name: go-biological-process-enrichment-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq lineage predictions must be functionally validated by checking whether GO BP terms recovered from memory genes of predicted lineages match those from ground-truth lineage annotations (e.g., Spearman correlation of enrichment scores, Fig. 3a).

name: go-biological-process-pathway-querying
description: Use when you hold a curated list of human gene symbols (e.g. date-converted genes recovered from Excel auto-conversion) and need to identify which GO Biological Process terms they enrich at adjusted p < 0.05.

name: go-cellular-compartment-annotation-filtering
description: Use when building or curating a ligand-receptor database from published L-R sources and you need to verify subcellular localization (secreted vs membrane) before accepting a pair.

name: go-enrichment-analysis-of-dmc-annotated-genes
description: Use when you have a DMC results file from a methylR differential methylation run (ChAMP or minfi) and need functional interpretation via GO term enrichment of the genes annotated to those CpGs.

name: go-enrichment-analysis-of-gene-lists
description: Use when you have gene lists flagged as critical by a drug-response model (e.g., scDEAL integrated-gradient gene output) and need functional interpretation via GO term enrichment with adjusted p-values.

name: go-enrichment-analysis-of-gene-modules
description: Use when co-expressed gene modules (e.g., from WGCNA cutreeDynamic on CS-CORE co-expression or differential co-expression matrices) need functional annotation via GO enrichment to identify relevant biological pathways per module.

name: go-enrichment-analysis-splicing-genes
description: Use when fortuna alt.tsv (or any novel-event table keyed by gene_id) has produced a list of genes with novel splicing events and you need functional interpretation or enrichment testing.

name: go-enrichment-gene-module-analysis
description: Use when you have gene co-expression modules (GEPs, e.g., from MCL clustering of a SingleCellGGM network) as gene-id/cluster-id pairs and need to quantify functional enrichment via GO/MP terms in mouse.

name: go-enrichment-signature-comparison
description: Use when two single-cell cohorts must be compared at the pathway/signature level — e.g., validating that inferred or semi-profiled data reproduces GO/Reactome enrichment from real-profiled data.

name: go-gene-set-benchmark-curation
description: Use when a ranked list of predicted regulators (e.g., CEFCON vs VIPER/ANANSE/SCENIC/CellRouter/CellOracle) must be validated against GO biological-process gene sets such as GO:0045165, GO:0019827, and GO:0007492.

name: go-kegg-edge-over-abundance-testing
description: Use when you have a filtered gene co-expression network (e.g. Normalisr coex edges at Q ≤ 1e-15) and want to test whether genes annotated to the same GO or KEGG pathway are connected more often than expected by chance.

name: go-kegg-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have gene modules or regulons (e.g., CEFCON RGMs or pySCENIC regulons) and need to quantify their biological meaningfulness via GO_BP/KEGG enrichment precision for benchmarking.

name: go-kegg-overrepresentation-enrichment
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering pipeline has produced per-cluster marker gene lists (e.g. cluster-vs-rest Wilcoxon-style DE on PBMC3k) and you need to know which GO biological processes and KEGG pathways are enriched in each cluster.

name: go-ontology-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when you have paired transcriptome-only and hybrid ClonoCluster cluster assignments plus a count matrix, and need genes predicting cluster rearrangement and their GO CC/MF enrichment.

name: go-semantic-similarity-network-construction
description: Use when you have a list of predicted modification-site genes (e.g. 2441 genes with Ψ sites at >0.99 precision) and need over-representation enrichment plus a similarity-scored GO network to expose functional modules such as nucleotide/protein binding or neurodegeneration pathways.

name: go-semantic-similarity-scoring
description: Use when scoring candidate genes for functional relatedness to a specific GO term (e.g., spliceosome-mediated circRNA biogenesis) so the semantic similarity becomes a per-gene feature for downstream clustering or ranking.

name: go-term-overrepresentation-analysis
description: Use when you have a CAFEH results table (cafeh.{mode}.results with pip, top_component, alpha, rank, p_active per SNP-study pair) and want to test whether tissue-specific vs shared eQTL regulation differs in constraint, disease association, and functional pathways.

name: go-term-recovery-jaccard-scoring
description: Use when comparing unsupervised gene program/module discovery outputs (e.g., SSN gene modules, ICA components, NMF factors) for their ability to recover known functional annotations such as GO terms or PPI enrichments.

name: gobp-gene-perturbation-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking batch-correction/integration methods for over-correction risk: you need a known implanted biological signal (GOBP term in one cell type of one batch) that a good integrator must preserve, not erase.

name: gold-standard-interaction-mapping
description: Use when a ranked GRN prediction (e.g., SINGE_Ranked_Edge_List.txt) must be audited per regulator against a gold standard, to check whether aggregate precision-recall conceals poor performance for individual regulators.

name: gold-standard-polya-site-labeling
description: Use when training a custom aptardi model (Mode 2) or benchmarking polyA site predictors against 3'-sequencing-derived gold-standard polyA sites that need to be mapped to label columns.

name: gold-standard-regulator-validation
description: Use when a set of candidate RBPs (e.g. CRIT-derived non-physically-associated candidates) must be connected to known circRNA regulators through binding-motif similarity, given circRNA sequences and a gold-regulator motif set.

name: gold-standard-topology-graph-distance-comparison
description: Use when comparing a trajectory inference method's inferred topology, pseudotime, and cell-fate predictions against known synthetic ground truth (e.g., dyntoy multifurcating, cyclic, or disconnected datasets) to quantify accuracy.

name: goodness-of-fit-diagnostic-visualization
description: Use when evaluating whether a zero-inflated count model (e.g., ZINB-WaVE on scRNA-seq counts) actually fits observed mean counts, dropout rates, and genewise dispersions better than simpler negative binomial or hurdle alternatives.

name: goodness-of-fit-r2-evaluation-per-gene
description: Use when validating RNA velocity model fits (UniTVelo with spliced/unspliced AnnData) by scoring per-gene R2 goodness-of-fit, e.g. to check that velocity fields and latent time are supported by dynamically informed genes.

name: gpr-based-reaction-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have a bulk gene x sample RNA-seq expression matrix (human gene symbols as row names, non-negative normalized values) and need reaction-level activity scores to feed compute_flux in a METAFlux/Human-GEM workflow.

name: gpu-accelerated-latent-variable-model-training
description: Use when a large single-cell dataset (e.g. Heart Cell Atlas, ~500,000 cells) must undergo covariate-removal correction via a latent-variable model, or when wall-clock runtimes of scVI vs SiFT vs regress_out must be measured across increasing cell counts.

name: gpu-based-dnn-model-training
description: Use when a .h5ad anndata scRNA-seq dataset must be classified (e.g. cell_type or disease target) by a DNN on constrained hardware (e.g. 12GB GPU / 128GB RAM), where memory-heavy pipelines like scVI-tools fail on full feature sets (e.g. 22,858 features).

name: gpu-bead-chain-energy-minimization
description: Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin structures from ChIA-PET anchors, PET clusters, and singletons on an NVIDIA GPU (Pascal or newer, CUDA_ARCH >= 60) and you need warp-parallel per-bead Monte Carlo energy minimization.

name: gpu-chromatin-3d-structure-simulation
description: Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin models from ChIA-PET anchors/PET clusters/singletons (e.g. GM12878 CTCF GRCh37/GRCh38) for single chromosomes or 100-model ensembles on an NVIDIA GPU (compute capability >= 6.0), especially when CPU 3D-GNOME runtimes (hours to days) are prohibitive.

name: gpu-cpu-memory-and-runtime-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking scLENS or similar single-cell pipelines for memory footprint and speed on CPU vs. GPU, or when evaluating whether median scaling can replace z-score scaling to cut resource cost.

name: gpu-cpu-performance-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking cudaMMC against 3D-GNOME timing on the same workstation and you have per-run execution times for ≥10 repeated runs per chromosome-method pair, and need a reproducible stability metric (CoV) rather than a single wall-clock time.

name: gpu-cpu-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether an imputation pipeline scales to large scRNA-seq datasets: time identical LATE runs on GPU and CPU builds of TensorFlow and compare against other imputation methods' runtimes.

name: gpu-deep-clustering-execution-profiling
description: Use when you must characterize how a deep single-cell clustering method's runtime scales with cell count, or benchmark empirical runtimes (e.g., scMDC at ~7 min/10K cells, ~1 hr/100K cells) on GPU hardware.

name: gpu-deep-embedding-training
description: Use when raw CITE-seq (RNA+ADT) H5 files must be converted into a low-dimensional latent embedding whose clusters separate cell types and mix batches, and GPU-accelerated deep training is feasible.

name: gpu-deep-learning-training
description: Use when you must reproduce or adapt scBridge's iterative label transfer from annotated scRNA-seq to unlabeled scATAC-seq (h5ad AnnData) on a single GPU, e.g. the SNARE-seq mouse cortex benchmark.

name: gpu-deep-learning-training-and-inference
description: Use when a segmentation mask assigning transcripts to individual cells is needed from SST imaging data (e.g., Xenium transcripts.csv.gz + morphology_mip.ome.tif) and a ≥12GB VRAM GPU is available to train the UNet3+ model.

name: gpu-multimodal-model-training
description: Use when a >60k-cell 10x Genomics-style dataset with paired gene expression and TCR sequences must be fused into a single cell-level multimodal embedding, or when reproducing mvTCR benchmarks on GPU hardware.

name: gpu-parallel-pairwise-kernel-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a q-diffused or Gaussian kernel over a full n×n cell-pair affinity matrix on a (genes × cells) matrix, and the pairwise gene-to-gene computation is too slow on CPU (the paper reports 20 min to 3 h per affinity matrix).

name: gpu-training-environment-setup
description: Use when a deep-learning model such as mvTCR must be trained on GPU, and no environment with the pinned Python, pip package, and matching CUDA PyTorch version exists yet; scale RAM to dataset size.

name: gradient-boosted-tree-model-training
description: Use when building a custom Census cell-type classifier from a scRNA-seq reference: reference data must be aggregated to pseudo-bulk per cell type, a cell-type hierarchy inferred, and one binary xgboost model trained per internal node.

name: gradient-boosting-classifier-training
description: Use when you must train and benchmark GBDT (and sibling boosting classifiers like XGBoost/LightGBM) as base learners on sequence-encoded feature matrices and compare accuracy before vs. after Bayesian parameter tuning via 10-fold cross-validation.

name: gradient-boosting-expression-regression
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference methods (e.g., SCING vs ppcor, PIDC, GRNBOOST2) for overfitting by comparing goodness-of-fit on training cells versus generalization to held-out test cells.

name: gradient-boosting-grn-edge-inference
description: Use when building a genome-scale directed GRN from a full single-cell transcriptome count matrix (e.g., snRNA-seq of a specific cell type like microglia), where sparse expression and cell-to-cell heterogeneity make standard GRN tools computationally intractable or inaccurate.

name: gradient-boosting-model-training-catboost
description: Use when a tabular feature matrix encoded from transcript sequences (e.g. Fickett score, GC1/GC2/GC3, k-mer/CTD, Mw/PI/Gravy, BERT ORF-attention vectors) must be fit with a gradient-boosting classifier for binary lncRNA vs PCT prediction.

name: gradient-boosting-model-tuning
description: Use when OU-simulated gene-deletion training data (training_prefix.features/.classes from GenerateTrainingData) must be fit with an xgboost classifier and hyperparameters (eta, log10(lambda), gamma, max_depth) need five-fold cross-validated selection.

name: gradient-boosting-regression-network-inference
description: Use when a gene co-expression module (e.g. WGCNA/BioNERO module gene list) must be converted into a directed TF-to-target regulatory graph, with candidate edges pruned by cis-regulatory motif enrichment.

name: gradient-descent-distribution-fitting
description: Use when the input is a sparsity-filtered single-cell cell-gene expression matrix and the goal is to detect the part of the dataset that behaves like a random matrix by fitting Marchenko-Pastur universality to its covariance eigenvalue spectrum.

name: gradient-interpretation-class-vs-loss-methods
description: Use when a trained SpatialDDLS deconvolution model must be made interpretable at the gene level — e.g., to recover which input genes (such as Cd8/Cd8b1 or Foxp3) drive the predicted cell type proportions in spatial transcriptomics spots.

name: granger-causal-inference-on-dags
description: Use when inferring causal noncoding locus-gene relationships from paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (or other multimodal single-cell) data undergoing a dynamic process, where a DAG of cell states can be oriented by pseudotime.

name: granger-causal-inference-single-cell-multimodal
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq (e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq) from a dynamic process and need causal locus-gene links beyond correlation, or to validate/enrich enhancer-priming annotations of prioritized peak-gene pairs.

name: granger-causal-peak-gene-linking
description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data from a dynamic process (e.g. 10x Multiome corticogenesis) must be prioritized for causal peak-gene or variant-locus-to-gene links beyond correlation-based proximity.

name: granger-causality-network-inference
description: Use when you have single-cell expression data ordered by pseudotime (e.g., a .mat file with sparse X, ptime, optional regix/branches) and need to rank candidate regulator-target interactions as a directed network.

name: granger-causality-testing
description: Use when you have aligned, interpolated temporal profiles of ligand-receptor pairs and TF-cluster activity (e.g. from cellAlign) and need to infer directionality — LR->TF, TF->LR, or bidirectional feedback — between them.

name: graph-attention-model-training
description: Use when constructing a lineage-specific gene regulatory network from scRNA-seq expression (h5ad/csv), a prior interaction network, and differential expression, and benchmarking GRN quality with AUPRC/EPR against ChIP-seq ground truth.

name: graph-attention-network-encoder-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reconstructing the scGAE encoder: you have a cells × genes count matrix, a KNN cell graph (default K=35), and need a graph-attention latent embedding Z in TensorFlow/Spektral that supports joint feature and adjacency reconstruction.

name: graph-attention-network-grn-inference
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression data for one developmental lineage plus a prior gene interaction network (edgelist) and need a lineage-specific GRN, e.g. for downstream driver regulator identification.

name: graph-autoencoder-embedding
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be embedded for visualization, clustering, or trajectory inference while preserving inter-cell topological structure (e.g., keeping transcriptionally similar populations close), and deep-learning competitors lose cell-cell relationships.

name: graph-autoencoder-model-training
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be embedded in a topology-preserving low-dimensional space with simultaneous cluster assignment, i.e., a cell graph is built and latent features plus cluster labels are learned jointly.

name: graph-autoencoder-training-on-single-cell-rna-seq
description: Use when you have a preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq count matrix and need a topology-preserving low-dimensional embedding for cell clustering or trajectory/visualization tasks where deep methods like DCA, scVI, or scDeepCluster lose cell-cell relationships.

name: graph-based-batch-correction-bbknn
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq matrices from multiple batches (e.g., GSE70630 oligodendroglioma samples MGH36-MGH97) and you need a fast, graph-based alternative that builds connections between analogous cells across batches without altering counts or PCA space.

name: graph-based-clustering-of-spatial-locations
description: Use when a spatially-resolved transcriptomics dataset (e.g., Visium human DLPFC SpatialExperiment with manual layer labels) must be clustered into spatial domains, and you need to compare feature-selection strategies (nnSVG, SPARK-X, Moran's I, HVGs) as clustering inputs.

name: graph-based-color-assignment-optimization
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics colorization step must assign colors from a fixed palette to cell-type clusters such that adjacent or interlaced clusters (quantified by Degree of Interlacement) get perceptually contrasting colors.

name: graph-based-iterative-louvain-umi-clustering
description: Use when quantifying isoforms from single-cell/spatial Nanopore long reads whose UMIs carry high sequencing error, and fixed edit-distance collapsing (e.g., Sicelore2, FLAMES, DBSCAN) inflates UMI counts at high PCR amplification.

name: graph-centrality-analysis
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object has been converted to a filtered Connectome edgelist and you need to identify cell types that dominate sending vs. receiving positions for specific signaling families (e.g. PDGF, EGF, VEGF) within a single tissue.

name: graph-community-detection-clustering
description: Use when you have a trained SDDA latent embedding of scRNA-seq data (e.g. 256-32 dims, 2000 highly variable genes) and need cell-type clusters via graph-based consensus or community detection, or when ablating the bipartite graph ensemble clustering component of scBGEDA.

name: graph-contrastive-learning-imputation-run
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices in h5 files (expression values, true labels, metadata) have dropout artifacts and the goal is imputation plus clustering benchmarked by ARI/NMI against methods like MAGIC or scTAG.

name: graph-contrastive-representation-learning
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices stored as h5 (expression values plus true labels) suffer from dropout and existing imputation methods that ignore topological structure cannot comprehensively utilize relationships between cells.

name: graph-convolutional-autoencoder-clustering
description: Use when clustering raw scRNA-seq count matrices (AnnData) across platforms, especially with rare cell types/small clusters, or when comparing against deep embedding methods (scDeepCluster, DESC, scVI) with ARI/NMI/ASW.

name: graph-convolutional-clustering
description: Use when clustering raw scRNA-seq count matrices (CSV or h5 format) into cell types, especially when high sparsity/heterogeneity defeats Seurat Louvain/Leiden, K-means, Spectral, scTAG, scGNN, scDCC, or other baselines and ARI is the accuracy metric.

name: graph-convolutional-network-adversarial-training
description: Use when multiple spatial transcriptomics slices (e.g., 33 MERFISH MOp slices) need jointly identified, uniform spatial domains that are coherent across slices and serve as the basis for downstream 3D alignment.

name: graph-degree-permutation-testing
description: Use when validating that discovered gene modules (e.g. DELVE dynamic vs. static modules) have statistically significant experimental evidence of co-regulation, by testing network degree against random size-matched gene sets.

name: graph-edge-coverage-validation
description: Use when running Tiglon's label-based dynamic path extension on a labeled splice graph and you need to confirm no junction (edge labeled 1, 2+, or 2-) was left unrecovered by the assembled transcript paths.

name: graph-edge-labeling-and-filtering
description: Use when integrating BAM alignments from multiple splice-aware aligners (e.g., Hisat2 and STAR) to assemble transcripts requires building a labeled splice graph with junction edges labeled by capturing-aligner agreement and filtered against spurious junctions.

name: graph-embedding-autoencoder-training
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be clustered while preserving cell-cell topological structure — especially datasets with rare cell types, batch effects, or >25,000 cells requiring batched learning.

name: graph-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you have a data matrix plus a user-defined cluster/class assignment (CSV) and need a supervised 2D layout that simultaneously reveals cluster structure and density-gradient differentiation trajectories, as in the intestinal epithelial and myeloid progenitor datasets.

name: graph-laplacian-eigendecomposition
description: Use when two networks over the same node set (e.g., denoised scGRNs for samples X and Y) must be aligned so each node's coordinates can be compared across conditions.

name: graph-neural-network-model-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a graph neural network (e.g., DGMP vs. MutSigCV, EMOGI, deepDriver) on gene regulatory networks with multi-omics gene features, or when evaluating generalization to an independent driver-gene test set.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when training a GNN on a directed gene regulatory network with per-gene multi-omics features (SNVs, CNAs, DNA methylation, gene expression) to predict binary gene labels such as driver/non-driver, or when reproducing ablation studies of DGCN/MLP components.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when you have paired scATAC-seq peak accessibility (N x C) and scRNA-seq expression (N x T) matrices, a candidate peak-gene pair list, and a cell-state DAG, and need to rank Granger causal links.

name: graph-neural-network-training
description: Use when constructing a lineage-specific GRN from scRNA-seq data (e.g., h5ad/adata with 1,000 HVGs) given a prior gene interaction network, and downstream driver-regulator analysis requires reliable inferred regulatory edges.

name: graph-signal-smoothness-analysis
description: Use when you have single-cell data (.h5ad, e.g. scRNA-seq or protein iterative immunofluorescence) plus a small set of dynamic seed features from Step 1 of DELVE, and you need to rank all measured features by their smoothness over the cell trajectory graph.

name: graph-topology-estimation-from-clustering
description: Use when you have a set of cluster assignments for single cells plus a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. LMDS with 5 dimensions) and need a tree-shaped trajectory backbone connecting the clusters.

name: graph-vertex-set-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two or more subnetworks (e.g., edge lists recovered by different active subnetwork detection methods such as pathfindR, BioNet, STr2z) must be compared on node membership to decide which methods find overlapping vs. distinct network structures.

name: graphical-lasso-precision-matrix-estimation
description: Use when testing whether marginal-correlation feature screening recovers predictive genes in p>>n transcriptomic data (e.g. the aml dataset, 116 observations x 6283 genes) by benchmarking screening FNR against a graphical-lasso-derived pseudo-true β*.

name: graphical-model-regularization-tuning
description: Use when inferring a sparse gene co-expression network from normalized single-cell expression data and the penalization strength (lda) of a Gaussian graphical model must be selected by BIC.

name: graphml-network-topology-analysis
description: Use when the analysis requires supplying pathway topologies (KEGG-derived or custom networks from non-KEGG sources) in GRAPHML format to scBONITA's pathway-analysis stage, especially when scoring node importance from in-silico knock-in/knock-out perturbations of learned Boolean rules.

name: graphql-database-querying-for-scrnaseq
description: Use when you need to retrieve per-cell-type differential expression or marker scores for a gene (e.g. insulin) from ingested H5AD-derived single-cell studies stored in Cellenium's PostgreSQL backend, especially for cross-study comparisons.

name: greedy-approximate-matching-on-weighted-graphs
description: Use when a minimum-weight one-to-one matching is needed on a large weighted bipartite graph (e.g. many anchor cells across two scRNA-seq batches) and the exact blossom algorithm is too slow; accepts up to 2x suboptimality.

name: greedy-combination-treatment-search
description: Use when a set of tumor sub-cluster gene expression profiles (GEPs) must be matched against LINCS L1000 perturbation bulk profiles to build a minimal combination therapy covering as many sub-clusters as possible.

name: greedy-feature-ranking-scoring
description: Use when a data matrix and response vector must be reduced to a small ranked feature subset, and plain mRMR is insufficient because feature interactions (complementarity) should be explicitly scored.

name: greedy-set-cover-feature-selection
description: Use when you need a global, discriminative marker set across many overlapping phenotype pairs (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in scRNA-seq data) rather than per-group differentially expressed genes, and can supply a phenotype-pair × feature score matrix.

name: greedy-set-cover-implementation
description: Use when you need a compact, globally discriminative marker set from a phenotype × feature score matrix (e.g., scRNA-seq cell-type × gene scores) such that every phenotype pair is covered (distinguished) at least K times.

name: greedy-set-cover-optimization
description: Use when predicting novel secondary drug combinations for a chemotherapy-resistant cancer, given pharmacogenomics drug-response data (e.g., GDSC1000 IC50) partitioned into resistant/sensitive groups and a standard-of-care primary drug query.

name: greedy-set-cover-sphere-center-selection
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes/PCs, e.g. CSV of principal components) must be reduced to a fixed number of representative cells that evenly cover transcriptomic space before downstream clustering or trajectory inference.

name: greedy-vs-cross-entropy-marker-solver-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how reproducible the feature sets selected by G-PC or CEM-PC are across repeated runs on randomly sampled scRNA-seq data, e.g. IPF lung, mouse cortex, or Human Cell Atlas matrices.

name: grex-imputation-weight-training
description: Use when the goal is TWAS Stage I: estimating per-gene eQTL weights from a reference panel, especially when only summary-level eQTL data (e.g., eQTLGen, GTEx V8) are available instead of individual-level genotype/expression data.

name: grid-based-transition-probability-estimation
description: Use when ranking candidate transcription-factor perturbations from CellOracle GRN simulations: simulated KO/overexpression transitions must be scored against a reference differentiation trajectory on a low-dimensional embedding.

name: grid-pseudo-spot-coordinate-generation
description: Use when you have single-cell data with global x/y spatial coordinates (e.g. seqFISH slides) and need simulated ST spot data with known cell-type ground truth to benchmark or validate single-cell-to-spatial mapping methods.

name: grid-search-map-confidence-interval-estimation
description: Use when reconstructing exact ecDNA breakpoints from ATAC-Seq junction evidence (discordant read pairs, soft-clipped/supplementary reads) and quantifying breakpoint confidence intervals across read lengths, e.g. down to 35 bp.

name: grn-based-cell-identity-transition-simulation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data and a CellOracle Links/GRN object are available and the goal is to predict, in silico, how knocking out or overexpressing a candidate TF (e.g., Fos) redirects cells among known clusters or attractors before committing to experiments.

name: grn-baseline-comparison-against-scenic
description: Use when a GRN/gene-module method needs a functional benchmark against SCENIC regulons on single-cell lineages, comparing enrichment precision and NMI of clustering.

name: grn-benchmark-against-ground-truth-networks
description: Use when a Bayes-Factor-ranked scGATE edge list (from/to/BF_score) must be scored against ground-truth networks such as Cus_KO/Cus_Chip or ChIP-Atlas-derived GRNs using precision-recall/AUPR, or when comparing scGATE against other network-inference tools on single-cell multi-omics data.

name: grn-benchmark-auroc-auprc-evaluation
description: Use when comparing multiple GRN-inference algorithms on the same scRNA-seq input matrix (e.g., BEELINE GSD 19 genes x 2,000 cells or SERGIO-simulated 100-gene matrices) where ground-truth regulatory edges exist and AUROC/AUPRC/runtime ranking is the goal.

name: grn-benchmark-auroc-tpr-evaluation
description: Use when you have one or more inferred GRNs and Perturb-seq count matrices (e.g., Dixit GSE90063 or Papalexi GSE153056) and need a quantitative, comparable ranking of network accuracy via perturbation-target prediction.

name: grn-benchmark-evaluation-against-gold-standard
description: Use when an inferred gene regulatory network (e.g., from Augusta on DREAM 4 or time-series RNA-Seq) needs quantitative evaluation against a reference edge set, using sensitivity/specificity/accuracy metrics.

name: grn-benchmark-evaluation-auroc-aupr
description: Use when benchmarking cell-specific network inference (CSNI) methods such as pySCENIC, LIONESS, or SSN on simulated single-cell data where the ground-truth cellwise regulatory network is known.

name: grn-benchmark-metric-computation-epr-auprc
description: Use when comparing inferred gene networks (from scPRINT, GENIE3, scGPT, DeepSEM, Geneformer, etc.) against a binary perturb-seq or literature ground truth and you need comparable AUPRC/EPR scores.

name: grn-confusion-matrix-evaluation
description: Use when one or more predicted GRNs (e.g., Augusta MI-only, Augusta with TFBM/DB refinement, GENIE3, TDAracne, KBoost) must be quantitatively compared against a gold-standard network with directed-edge ground truth.

name: grn-edge-conflict-resolution
description: Use when refining a MI-inferred GRN with curated database interactions and the same regulator-target pair receives contradictory edge types (e.g., activation vs. inhibition) from inference or from multiple databases.

name: grn-edge-significance-quantification
description: Use when GRouNdGAN has been trained with an imposed GRN (e.g., GRNBoost2- or PPCOR-derived) on PBMC-CTL or a similar reference dataset and you need to test whether knocking out each regulating TF significantly changes its target genes' simulated expression.

name: grn-guided-gan-training
description: Use when you need reference-based simulation of scRNA-seq data that retains the regulatory dynamics of a user-provided causal GRN, e.g. for benchmarking GRN inference or pseudo-time preservation studies.

name: grn-in-silico-knockout-analysis
description: Use when a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A plus per-cell velocities) is available and you need per-cell TF activity scores across all regulators to identify regulators driving a transition, such as acinar-to-ductal metaplasia.

name: grn-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to decide how many cells and how many candidate TFs per target are sufficient for reliable scGATE logic-gate inference, or when reproducing runtime/saturation curves like Figure 5C before committing to a full-network run.

name: grn-inference-benchmarking-with-genie3-and-grnboost
description: Use when a workflow depends on a GRN inferred from a single-cell gene expression matrix and you need to test whether the downstream results (e.g., cell-type communication matrices) are robust to swapping the GRN inference algorithm.

name: grn-inference-gniplr
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells, .txt, rows = genes, columns = cells) must be converted into a GRN adjacency matrix to serve as the left submatrix R in MDIC3, or when benchmarking GNIPLR against GENIE3/GRNBoost as GRN sources.

name: grn-inference-with-gradient-boosting
description: Use when a co-expression module (e.g. a WGCNA module correlated with a trait or cell type) must be converted into a directed TF–target regulatory network to identify the transcription factors controlling it.

name: grn-inference-with-grnboost2
description: Use when preparing a GRN-guided causal GAN run: you have a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix (e.g., 1000 highly variable genes, library-size normalized to 20,000) and need a causal graph of TF-gene edges to impose during GRouNdGAN training.

name: grn-network-object-handling
description: Reference for handling scPRINT-derived gene networks loaded as GRnnData objects when you need differential hub detection (eigenv centrality), Louvain community detection, or prerank Enrichr enrichment on network communities.

name: grn-reproducibility-overlap-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking multiple GRN inference methods on single-cell (snRNAseq/scRNAseq) expression matrices and you need quantified edge reproducibility, scale-free topology fit, network characteristic metrics, and runtime per method.

name: grn-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods on snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data and you need quantitative topology fit (scale-free R-squared), reproducibility of inferred edges, and computational runtime benchmarks per method.

name: grn-simulation-knockdown-perturbation
description: Use when a new differential network inference method must be benchmarked against existing methods and no real dataset with a known ground-truth GRN is available; simulated knockdown perturbation data provides verifiable true edges.

name: grn-tool-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a new or modified GRN inference pipeline against established tools on a dataset with a known gold-standard network, to quantify accuracy and runtime trade-offs.

name: grna-cell-assignment-umi-thresholding
description: Use when you have a filtered gRNA BAM (UMI + cell barcode aware) from a droplet CRISPR screen (e.g. CROP-seq) and need per-cell gRNA calls that include mutant gRNAs missed by Cell Ranger feature barcoding.

name: grna-competition-covariate-modeling
description: Use when analyzing high-MOI single-cell CRISPR screens (e.g. the 207,324-cell K562 CRISPRi CROP-seq screen with 13,186 gRNAs) where multiple gRNAs are assayed per cell and FPR of gRNA-gene associations must be controlled against NTC-based estimates.

name: grna-gene-association-filtering
description: Use when you have gRNA-gene association tables (TSS-repression and trans-association Q-values and logFC) from Normalisr on a high-MOI CRISPRi screen and need to call high-confidence putative gene regulations for GRN reconstruction.

name: grna-library-mutation-profiling
description: Use when analyzing single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM files where mutant gRNAs may go undetected by default Cell Ranger annotation, or when quantifying per-experiment mutant gRNA frequencies.

name: grna-library-sequencing-downsampling
description: Use when estimating the minimum gRNA library sequencing depth needed for accurate gRNA-to-cell assignment in a CROP-seq experiment, by comparing annotation accuracy and UMIs per cell across downsampled saturation levels.

name: grna-variant-calling-against-cassette-reference
description: Use when you have a filtered gRNA BAM from a single-cell CRISPR screen (e.g. CROP-seq) and need to detect which gRNA molecules carry mutations versus the designed oligo pool, beyond the intact-only assignment Cell Ranger provides.

name: grna-variant-calling-structure-annotation
description: Use when processing a gRNA library bam file from a single-cell CRISPR screen (e.g., CROP-seq or Perturb-seq) and you need to detect mutant gRNAs that the default Cell Ranger pipeline labels as intact, prior to assigning gRNAs to cells.

name: grna-variant-calling-with-cigar-like-encoding
description: Use when single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA alignments need mutation-aware calling — i.e., you have a consensus.bam of UMI-cell barcode consensus sequences and an oligo_pool_plasmid.fa reference, and must distinguish intact from mutant gRNAs before assigning gRNAs to cells.

name: grnboost2-ranking-based-control-grn-construction
description: Use when building positive/negative control ground-truth GRNs from GRNBoost2 TF-gene importance rankings to impose on GRouNdGAN-simulated single-cell data for AUPRC-based recoverability benchmarking.

name: ground-truth-community-label-generation
description: Use when benchmarking MuDCoD (or similar multi-subject dynamic community detection) and you need simulated S x T x N adjacency tensors paired with ground-truth node community labels.

name: ground-truth-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a simulation provides a known cell-by-isoform ground truth and you need to quantify how accurately a long-read isoform quantification method recovers per-cell isoform expression across error regimes or sequencing depths.

name: ground-truth-deg-label-derivation
description: Use when benchmarking DEG prediction accuracy on artificial Splatter datasets: simulated count matrices exist but lack reference labels, and each gene's simulated DEFac value is available to define the DEG ground truth.

name: ground-truth-grn-validation
description: Decision support for ranking gene regulatory network inference methods when synthetic single-cell data with an imposed causal ground-truth GRN is available, or when reproducing BEELINE-style benchmark comparisons.

name: ground-truth-label-annotation
description: Use when generating synthetic benchmark data (e.g. two-condition, two-batch scRNA-seq simulations) that require known injected signal — DS genes at specified proportions (5%/10%) and logFC ranges — to be written alongside the counts as label annotations.

name: ground-truth-regulatory-relationship-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when validating GRN inference or denoising methods against a simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known regulatory relationships, e.g., quantifying recall gains from CP tensor denoising of multilayer scGRNs.

name: ground-truth-trajectory-extraction
description: Use when benchmarking methods that require known ground truth (RNA velocity via velocity correlation/arrow cosine, trajectory inference, CSNI) on simulated single-cell data where the true trajectory is available by construction.

name: group-by-pseudotime-interaction-modeling
description: Use when performing XDE (covariate-associated differential expression along pseudotime) on scRNA-seq data with a trajectory method like Monocle2 that lacks native XDE support and needs group-specific intercept/trend tests.

name: group-comparison-differential-expression
description: Use when a normalized, non-log2 blood transcriptome matrix (e.g., GSE13015/EH5429 from ExperimentHub) with sample annotation must be compared between two sample groups to get per-module percent-increase/decrease values.

name: group-specific-interaction-filtering
description: Use when DEGGs generate_subnetworks has produced per-subgroup significant edge lists (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and you must restrict each network to interactions specific to one group rather than links common to all groups.

name: group-wise-median-comparison-across-tools
description: Use when a supplementary table (e.g. Dataset EV2) lists a numeric parameter per study along with the tool that produced it, and the goal is to test whether the parameter differs between tool families.

name: grouped-subject-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a modification to MuDCoD's subject-smoothing term (e.g., replacing the global all-subject mean with group-specific means) improves community recovery, measured by ARI against known true labels on simulated networks.

name: gsa-rank-based-gene-set-analysis
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq DE contrasts (e.g., 17-AAG-sensitive vs -resistant HMCLs, 17-AAG response, combination response) need to be converted into ranked gene lists and gene-set/upstream-regulator signals to interpret drug-response mechanisms.

name: gsea-enrichment-score-calculation
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (samples x genes, Entrez IDs) must be converted into per-sample pathway activity vectors (functional spectra) as classification or visualization features.

name: gsea-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a cluster from joint mRNA/protein WNN clustering (e.g., Seurat FindClusters algorithm=3, resolution=2) needs identity confirmation: rank its transcript signature and test enrichment against a curated cell-type gene set (e.g., MAIT-cell signature).

name: gsea-normalized-enrichment-score-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing pseudo-time/trajectory inference methods on scRNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, gene-set-based metric: run GSEA with a cell-cycle gene set on each method's cell ordering and rank methods by NES.

name: gsea-prerank-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a ranked gene list from a differential expression comparison and need per-pathway enrichment FDR values, especially to benchmark model-based module activity tests (e.g., VEGA Bayes Factors) against a standard enrichment method.

name: gsva-family-sample-level-geneset-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking sample-wise pathway quantification methods (GSVA, PLAGE, ssGSEA, z-score) against rROMA module activity on a normalized RNA-seq matrix to test which method recovers an expected treatment- or disease-driven pathway shift.

name: gsva-geneset-scoring
description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, e.g. TCGA-LUAD) and a curated gene set (e.g. a 14-gene hypoxia or 22-gene glycolysis signature) and need per-sample pathway/hallmark scores for downstream grouping, survival or differential analysis.

name: gsva-pathway-score-computation
description: Use when a bulk transcriptomic cohort (e.g., GSE39582 or TCGA COAD-READ expression matrices) must be scored for a curated pathway list (e.g., high-weight pathways from scPAFA/MOFA modules) to build or validate a disease-status classifier.

name: gsva-score-based-sample-stratification
description: Use when a continuous process signature (e.g., hypoxia or glycolysis gene set) must be turned into patient sample groups — e.g., to compare mutation burdens or survival between hypoxia-high and hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD tumors.

name: gsva-score-differential-analysis-limma
description: Use when RNA-seq gene-set (pathway) activity must be compared between sample groups — e.g. glycolysis GSVA score between hypoxia-high and hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD samples — and the test variable is continuous decimal scores.

name: gtex-eqtl-finemapped-pair-intersection
description: Use when validating enhancer-gene interaction predictions against orthogonal genetic evidence: intersect method-ranked enhancer-gene lists with fine-mapped GTEx eQTL credible sets to compute and compare eQTL-pair recall per method and cell type.

name: gtex-expression-reference-modeling
description: Use when GReX imputation weights must be trained from whole-blood eQTL reference data (eQTLGen summary statistics or GTEx individual-level genotypes/expression) and compared by number of valid models (test R2 > 0.01).

name: gtex-multitissue-sqtl-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing multi-tissue GTEx transcript expression (TPM) and genotype tables as sqtlseeker2-nf inputs, i.e., when the goal is cis-sQTL mapping and raw tissue, gene, transcript and variant sets must be filtered first.

name: gtex-tissue-expression-analysis
description: Use when GTEx TPM values and MRSD scores are available for the same genes and you need to test whether relative expression alone predicts required sequencing depth for transcript coverage.

name: gtex-tissue-transcript-expression-preprocessing
description: Use when building a per-tissue sQTL catalog from GTEx V7 transcript expression and genotypes, or when reproducing the Garrido-Martín et al. counts of 210,485 cis sQTLs across 6,963 sGenes at 0.05 FDR.

name: gtf-annotation-file-authoring
description: Use when long-read alignments must be converted into novel transcript records in a valid GTF enhanced annotation, with TSS/polyA end-support filtering against external interval BEDs.

name: gtf-annotation-guided-splice-correction
description: Use when assembling or correcting isoforms from long-read RNA-seq alignments (e.g. GMAP-aligned PacBio BAM) where a trusted GTF annotation with exon coordinates is available and detection accuracy against known isoforms must be benchmarked.

name: gtf-annotation-parsing
description: Use when a set of lead sQTL variants must be mapped to annotated intron/gene coordinates to test whether sQTLs are enriched in post-transcriptionally spliced introns.

name: gtf-transcript-annotation-formatting
description: Use when transcript paths recovered from a labeled splice graph (edges labeled 1, 2+, 2-) must be written out as an annotation file, and output candidates need to be filtered by coverage and length thresholds before downstream use.

name: gtf-transcriptome-annotation
description: Use when a sample-specific GTF/GFF transcriptome (e.g., StringTie output) needs refined 3' ends / expressed polyadenylation sites before quantitation or differential expression analysis.

name: gtmse-error-metric-computation
description: Use when quantifying imputation accuracy of scRNA-seq methods: comparing MSE/gtMSE against a ground-truth matrix, or evaluating real datasets (e.g. PBMC_G5561, PBMC_G9987) where ground truth is set equal to the input.

name: guilt-by-association-feature-expansion
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering pipeline needs a final feature gene set from DUBStepR seed features, i.e., when optimise.features=TRUE and the optimal number of feature genes must be determined.

name: gumbel-softmax-differentiable-marker-selection
description: Use when selecting a minimal, informative set of k gene markers from single-cell RNA-seq or CITE-seq data (.h5ad AnnData) such that markers are differentiably learned end-to-end and support both cell-type classification and whole-transcriptome reconstruction.

name: gumbel-softmax-dropout-modeling
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq expression matrices with frequent zero/near-zero dropout events (e.g. Pollen, 10x Genomics datasets) and nonlinear low-dimensional representations are needed for visualization or downstream lineage analysis.

name: gvcf-merging-into-global-vcf
description: Use when per-sample gVCF outputs from GATK HaplotypeCaller must be combined into one multi-sample VCF to support joint downstream analyses such as reference masking or allele-specific expression testing.

name: gwas-catalog-ld-proxy-annotation
description: Use when testing whether a variant catalog (e.g., GTEx sQTLs at FDR < 0.05) is enriched for GWAS Catalog hits via LD proxies, alongside annotation-based enrichments like splice donor/acceptor or H3K36me3.

name: gwas-catalog-snp-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a PAIRADISE (FDR <= 10%) significant ASAS SNP list from GM12878 or Geuvadis population data needs to be linked to GWAS-catalog SNPs via LD (1000 Genomes phase 3) and tested for enrichment against random controls.

name: gwas-gene-mapping-and-preprocessing
description: Use when you have GWAS summary statistics (or preprocessed trait-associated gene lists) and want to identify which human cell types are significantly associated with a complex trait or disease.

name: gwas-snp-interval-mapping
description: Use when GWAS SNP results for a trait (e.g., soybean resistance to phytopathogenic fungi) need to be converted to a per-pathogen high-confidence candidate gene set by scanning a fixed genomic window around significant SNPs.

name: gwas-summary-statistics-gene-prioritization
description: Use when you have GWAS summary statistics (e.g., monocyte count, IEU ID ieu-b-31) and a normalized scRNA-seq matrix, and you need a ranked trait-relevant gene set (n_topgenes = 1,000) to feed cell-scoring methods like scDRS or Seurat AddModuleScore.

name: gwas-summary-statistics-harmonization
description: Use when only summary-level eQTL statistics (e.g., eQTLGen), GWAS summary statistics (e.g., UK Biobank), and a PLINK LD reference are available and TWAS weights must be trained without individual-level reference expression/genotype data.

name: gwas-summary-statistics-processing
description: Use when per-trait GWAS summary statistics (SNP coordinates and association P-values) must be annotated with sQTL vs expression-only labels and tested for annotation enrichment of splicing effects.

name: gwas-variant-peak-genomic-intersection
description: Use when fine-mapped GWAS variants with posterior probabilities (e.g., Trubetskoy SCZ FINEMAP PP >= 0.05) must be intersected with scATAC-seq peaks and linked to candidate regulated genes beyond nearest-gene assignment.

name: h5ad-count-matrix-loading-and-cell-subsetting
description: Use when a raw single-cell count matrix (10X/h5ad/GSE accession) must be loaded into an anndata object and cells filtered by a compositional threshold (e.g. % human UMI counts) or zero-expression criteria before denoising or analysis.

name: hamiltonian-monte-carlo-posterior-inference
description: Use when estimating covariate effects on cell-type proportions from compositional scRNA-seq count data with scCODA, where HMC (or NUTS) posterior sampling is needed to obtain credible effects relative to a reference cell type.

name: hamming-distance-cell-to-attractor-mapping
description: Use when scBONITA-inferred Boolean rules and binarized single-cell expression states exist and you must map sequenced cells to characteristic signaling states (attractors) of a pathway.

name: hamming-similarity-gene-graph-construction
description: Use when converting a sparse, dropout-prone scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. Xin GSE81608, 2000 highly variable genes, entries in [0,1]) into a binary gene-gene similarity graph to derive qualitative cell landmarks.

name: haplotype-phasing-em-gene-binning
description: Use when building allele-specific CNA calls from scRNA-seq allelic counts (AD/DP matrices) and single-SNP BAF signals are too sparse/noisy, requiring aggregation from SNPs to genes, gene bins, and chromosome arms before HMM smoothing.

name: harmonizome-association-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a list of newly predicted candidate RBPs (e.g., CRIT NMF cluster candidates) must be functionally connected to a gold-standard regulator set via physical interaction, co-expression, or shared transcription factor modulation evidence.

name: harmony-batch-corrected-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when comparing how well alternative single-cell embeddings (TCR-only, RNA-only, Harmony-corrected RNA, mvTCR joint) preserve pMHC antigen specificity, quantified by NMI of Leiden clusters and per-cluster antigen purity.

name: harmony-batch-correction
