description: Use when unpaired snRNA-seq and snATAC-seq cells from multiple patients, regions, or technologies have been co-embedded (e.g. via Seurat CCA in CoembedData) but remain separated by batch, and a corrected embedding is needed for sub-clustering, PairCells, or trajectory analysis.

name: harmony-batch-correction-of-single-cell-embeddings
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq samples must be integrated: the SingCellaR object already has Supervised PCA embeddings and cell metadata covariates (e.g. sample batch) that need correction before downstream clustering and UMAP visualization.

name: harmony-batch-integration
description: Use when a held-out query dataset from a different technology or batch must be projected into a stable reference embedding built from the other datasets, and the mapping quality must be quantified against a de novo Harmony integration.

name: harmony-batch-integration
description: Use when a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GSE149689 PBMCs) pooled from multiple samples/donors shows batch effects that would confound clustering and cell-type annotation prior to differential-expression localisation.

name: harmony-benchmark-integration-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a new integration/annotation method's batch-effect removal and you need a head-to-head LISI-based comparison against Harmony on the same merged datasets.

name: harmony-cross-dataset-integration-colocalization
description: Use when cells in two independent scRNA-seq datasets have been assigned labels from a common set of marker GEPs (e.g., 70 MCA GEPs annotating 94,582 TMS cells) and the transfer must be validated in a joint embedding.

name: harmony-integration-baseline-execution
description: Use when benchmarking a new batch-integration method (e.g., BATMAN) against Harmony on two single-cell datasets projected into a shared PCA space, and you need mixing (iLISI) and local-structure (RNN) metrics plus runtimes.

name: harmony-multidonor-integration-of-scrnaseq-batches
description: Use when building an integrated single-cell reference atlas from expression matrices spanning multiple donors or technologies (e.g., pancreatic islet donors across four protocols), where donor/batch covariates must be removed before downstream reference mapping.

name: hartigan-dip-statistic-multimodality-testing
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction methods on temporal scRNA-seq data and you need a distribution-level statistic quantifying whether cells from a single time point separate into multiple subpopulations on a 2D latent space.

name: hartigan-dip-test-statistics
description: Use when a per-cell uncertainty score distribution (e.g. scEMAIL E-scores from entropy, confidence, consistency) must be tested for bimodality to declare the presence of novel cell types without user-defined thresholds.

name: hartigans-dip-test-multimodality-testing
description: Use when PCA scores from a control-group scCRISPR-seq matrix must be triaged so that only multimodal, high-variance PCs are decoupled for infected proportion bias, while remaining PCs use observed change directly.

name: haseman-elston-regression-scrna-seq
description: Use when you need a fast, method-of-moments cross-check of cell type-specific variance differentiation calls from REML-based LMM fits on scRNA-seq pseudobulk data, e.g. to confirm Bonferroni-significant genes across two independent fitting methods.

name: hash-based-sketch-vector-construction
description: Use when you need cell-to-cell similarity scores from a log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix without full pairwise distance computation, e.g. building the similarity matrix S that feeds EDGE's k-NNG and spectral embedding.

name: hashing-deconvolution-count-generation
description: Use when hashed CITE-seq ADT FASTQ files (I1/R1/R2 per sample) need to be converted into per-cell hashtag UMI count matrices before hashtag deconvolution, e.g. for multiplexed PBMC samples in gExcite.

name: hashing-demultiplexing
description: Use when analyzing hashed single-cell multiome data (e.g. cell hashing antibody oligo tags) that requires sample demultiplexing plus combined GEX and ADT/CITE-seq processing from raw FASTQ reads onward.

name: hashtag-cutoff-calling-for-cell-hashing-demultiplexing
description: Use when a Seurat object carries an 'HTO' assay from a cell hashing experiment and per-hashtag cutoffs separating true-positive from background signal are needed to assign singlet/doublet/negative identities, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes.

name: hashtag-cutoff-calling-quality-assessment
description: Use when a Seurat object with an 'HTO' assay has been demultiplexed (or is about to be) with HTOreader and you need to verify each hashtag's cutoff, especially with imbalanced sample sizes, many hashtags, or suspected poor hashtag staining.

name: hashtag-demultiplexing-cell-assignment
description: Use when input contains a cell-hashing (hashtag oligo) ADT count matrix — e.g. CITE-seq-Count output for multiple hashed samples — and each cell barcode must be assigned to a sample, a doublet, or a negative before downstream single-cell analysis.

name: hausdorff-distance-distributional-fidelity-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell sketching methods and you need a distribution-fidelity metric comparing a subsample's feature distribution (e.g. PCA embeddings in adata.obsm['X_pca']) against the full dataset.

name: hausdorff-distance-simulation-clustering
description: Use when an ensemble of simulated cell-state sequences from the Cytopath Markov sampler must be partitioned into sub-trajectory clusters (per terminal region) before dynamic time warping alignment and consensus averaging.

name: hausdorff-distance-sketch-quality-evaluation
description: Use when you have a sketch (subset of cells) and the full single-cell expression/PC matrix and need to quantify how well the sketch covers the original transcriptomic space, or to compare competing sketching methods.

name: hazard-ratio-estimation-survival-genes
description: Use when high-dimensional genomic covariates (e.g., TCGA somatic mutation matrix) must be related to a survival outcome, and penalized Cox selection with FDR screening, hazard ratios, and C-index evaluation is needed.

name: hazard-ratio-interpretation
description: Use when patient-level survival metadata (vital status, days to death, days to follow-up) is available alongside per-gene expression sets, and you need to rank gene panels (e.g. IC vs DE genes) by prognostic association via hazard ratios and C-statistics.

name: hca-dataset-acquisition-and-harmonization
description: Use when benchmarking batch-effect insensitivity of a representation method on a large multi-donor dataset, or reproducing the tGPT vs. ComBat/MNN/Harmony/Seurat/BBKNN/Scanorama/Pegasus/scVI/scArches/iMAP/DESC kBET comparison on HCA bone marrow.

name: hdf5-single-cell-matrix-export
description: Use when running scTE on 10x-style or plate-based scRNA-seq BAM files and you need the resulting TE count matrix in anndata-compatible .h5ad format for cell-type-level TE aggregation and marker-TE identification.

name: heart-cell-atlas-dataset-subsampling
description: Use when reproducing or extending the runtime scalability benchmark on the Heart Cell Atlas: measuring how SiFT, scVI, and regress_out runtimes scale with subsample size from 5,000 to ~486,134 cells.

name: heat-based-label-propagation-clustering
description: Use when you need to cluster a preprocessed sample-by-feature matrix (e.g., PBMC scRNA-seq reduced to 30 PCs) with a method that yields per-point posterior label confidences and works on a KNN affinity graph.

name: heatmap-visualization-of-enrichment-scores
description: Use when you have pre-ranked differential gene tables for every cluster in an integrated scRNA-seq dataset and need to assign cell type identities/states from enrichment of curated signature gene sets (e.g., the 75 hematopoiesis GMT sets).

name: held-out-cell-type-ablation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a Symphony reference mapping flags query cell populations absent from the reference as novel, or when reproducing the ablation benchmark of per-cell/per-cluster mapping-confidence metrics (AUCs, Supplementary Fig. 9).

name: held-out-cell-validation-model-selection
description: Use when training a custom cTP-net model on paired scRNA-seq/CITE-seq data and you must pick optimal network weights via held-out cells rather than training loss.

name: held-out-condition-splits-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a multi-condition scRNA-seq model predicts held-out condition combinations (e.g. <ctrl,severe> cells) correctly, comparing against baselines like scGen and scPreGAN.

name: held-out-donor-validation-design
description: Use when validating that a reference-mapping pipeline (e.g., Symphony) can transfer annotations (such as surface proteins) to query cells lacking the modality, and you need a donor-level split so query donors are never seen during reference construction.

name: held-out-prediction-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating crossmodal generation quality of scMM (or similar multimodal VAEs) on CITE-seq data: need to quantify how precisely surface protein abundance can be predicted from transcriptome observations in held-out test cells via correlation.

name: held-out-test-set-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when a supervised classifier trained with 10-fold stratified CV on the TCGA 19,737-gene training matrix must be assessed for true generalization on unseen held-out TCGA test samples (e.g. confirming mLR's 85% test accuracy).

name: held-out-timepoint-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a trained trajectory model must be validated on held-out progenitor states and ranked against existing methods on clonal fate-bias prediction metrics.

name: held-out-timepoint-validation
description: Use when a longitudinal scRNA-seq dataset has ≥3 time points and you need to test whether a trained trajectory model can generate an unobserved intermediate population, comparing against an optimal-transport baseline.

name: hematopoiesis-gene-set-interpretation
description: Use when clusters from an integrated hematopoietic (e.g. HSPC) scRNA-seq dataset need objective cell-type labels, and a curated GMT of hematopoiesis signature gene sets is available.

name: hematopoiesis-qpcr-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when comparing branching trajectory inference methods on a small single-cell qPCR dataset where sorted population labels can serve as ground truth for lineage-specific marker genes such as Gata1 and Pax5.

name: hematopoiesis-single-cell-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing large-scale single-cell RNA-seq hematopoiesis data (e.g., human bone marrow from 10X Chromium) where cell-fate dynamics must be reconstructed efficiently and aggregation is needed to make multiscale transition analysis tractable.

name: hematopoietic-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a single-cell hematopoiesis dataset (e.g., Weinreb et al. Kleind2ws murine HSC differentiation data) has ground-truth cell-type labels and you need to quantify cluster purity via per-cluster label entropy under different clustering schemes.

name: hematopoietic-hierarchy-reconstruction
description: Use when input is a raw single-cell chromatin-accessibility (scATAC-seq) k-mer or peak count matrix and the goal is to infer a branching developmental trajectory with pseudotime and identify transcription-factor regulators along branches.

name: hematopoietic-lineage-annotation
description: Use when raw mouse bone marrow or HSPC scRNA-seq count data (e.g., GSE76983) must be segmented into subpopulations and transitions from HSCs toward mature neutrophil/erythroid fates must be annotated with lineage-specific gene dynamics.

name: hematopoietic-lineage-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from hematopoietic subpopulations (HSCP/LSK, CMP, GMP, LKCD34+) needs an unbiased lineage hierarchy with per-branch gene expression, without prior time points, start cell, or branching count.

name: hematopoietic-lineage-fraction-comparison
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq of murine bone marrow under hematopoietic perturbation (gene knockout or drug inhibition such as Mettl3 KO/STM2457) must be compared to a control for changes in lineage composition, cell cycle phase fractions (G0), or innate immune response signatures.

name: hematopoietic-lineage-interpretation-erythroid-megakaryocytic
description: Use when two processed SingCellaR single-cell HSPC objects (e.g., eFL and FL) must be compared for differential abundance of annotated subpopulations such as erythroid, megakaryocytic, lymphoid, and myeloid progenitors, with results visualized on a shared UMAP.

name: hematopoietic-lineage-marker-interpretation
description: Use when a fitted branching trajectory on sorted hematopoietic scRNA-seq data (e.g., Nestorowa HSC dataset) needs biological validation via marker detection at bifurcations into lymphoid, myeloid, and erythroid fates.

name: hematopoietic-progenitor-cell-type-ranking
description: Use when per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores must be compared across hematopoietic progenitor types (HSC, MPP, GMP, etc.) to check whether a method orders cells according to the classical HSC-first hierarchy.

name: hematopoietic-progenitor-hierarchy-interpretation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data of hematopoietic progenitors (e.g. the Velten multipotent progenitor dataset with RaceID3 cluster assignments) needs a lineage-hierarchy readout, or when benchmarking pseudotime tools like Monocle2 against a class-informed graph embedding.

name: hematopoietic-progenitor-lineage-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data of hematopoietic progenitors (FACS-sorted LK, LSK, CMP, MEP, CLP/LMPP fractions) has been clustered by BUSseq and unknown clusters must be annotated as specific progenitor stages using marker genes and Haemopedia reference profiles.

name: hepatocyte-zonation-landmark-gene-interpretation
description: Use when single cells have been assigned pseudo-spatial coordinates along the hepatic lobule PV-CV axis (e.g. via STEM's netsc2st mapping and all_coord) and you need to identify regionally expressed genes per cell type and confirm zonation biology with landmark markers.

name: herv-expression-survival-association
description: Use when per-sample viral/HERV contig calls from RNAseq (e.g. viRNAtrap FASTA contigs) must be dichotomized into HERV-positive vs HERV-negative groups and tested against TCGA overall survival or somatic driver mutations.

name: herv-locus-sequence-extraction
description: Use when a study needs a reference set of intact/potentially functional HERV sequences from the human genome to serve as an alignment target for endogenous retroviral expression analysis in transcriptomic data.

name: hesc-npc-potency-population-comparison
description: Use when analysing snapshot scRNA-Seq populations (e.g. hESC vs progenitor/NPC) where differentiation potency must be inferred without marker genes or timepoint labels, and population-level potency heterogeneity (Shannon index) is the target output.

name: heterogeneous-drug-target-network-construction
description: Use when a detected gene co-expression module (GCN) or gene regulatory network (GRN) from scRNA-seq analysis must be linked to repurposable drugs — i.e., after module selection and hub gene detection, when pharmacological targeting of driver mechanisms is the goal.

name: heterogeneous-network-integration
description: Use when you have an inferred gene network (e.g. a co-expression module GCN or a TF–TG GRN) and need to connect its genes/proteins to drugs to propose mechanistic repurposing candidates.

name: heteromeric-complex-filtering
description: Use when constructing or extending a ligand-receptor pair list (e.g., connectomeDB2020) from CellPhoneDB (v2.0, IDs 'CPI-SSxxx') and the downstream analysis tool cannot represent heteromeric complexes, so only simple protein-to-protein pairs should be retained.

name: hexamer-usage-table-scoring
description: Use when building coding-potential features for lncRNA/mRNA classification and you need a training-set-calibrated hexamer usage score (SIF) for each transcript, as in LncDC's H-Train feature matrix.

name: hf1-hierarchical-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating hierarchical cell-type classifiers on scRNA-seq benchmarks where predictions must be scored with hierarchical F1 and the fraction of cells rejected as unseen populations must be reported per fold.

name: hg19-annotation-background-extraction
description: Use when a permutation-based colocalization or randomization analysis in RgnTX/regioneR needs matched genome and transcriptome background region sets built from hg19 annotation for a defined gene set.

name: hgnc-gene-symbol-conversion-validation
description: Use when Excel auto-conversion turned gene symbols (e.g. SEPT1, MARC1) into dates such as Mar-01/Mar-02 in .csv or .xlsx expression files, or when old gene symbols need updating to new HGNC names before pathway analysis or data sharing.

name: hgnc-gene-symbol-mapping
description: Use when a gene-expression table (.csv/.xlsx) has a gene-name column containing Excel date artifacts (Dec-01, Mar-01..Mar-11, Sep-01..Sep-15) or pre-2017 HGNC symbols that must be converted to current HGNC names before pathway analysis.
tools: Mark Ziemann's gene name errors dashboard

name: hichip-binomial-loop-testing
description: Use when bulk H3K27ac HiChIP enhancer-promoter interactions (gene index, enhancer index, loop counts) are available alongside subpopulation cluster assignments and you need per-gene p-values quantifying subpopulation-specific loop signal.

name: hidden-factor-associated-gene-discovery
description: Use when an IA-SVA run has produced a significant surrogate variable (e.g., SV1 on alpha-cell scRNA-seq counts) and you need the marker genes that explain that hidden factor, such as contamination/doublet genes (COL4A1, COL4A2) or cell-cycle genes.

name: hidden-layer-activation-extraction
description: Use when a trained Keras model (tmpMod. + tmpWeight.bin + parameters.txt) is available and you need to inspect or validate what its hidden layers learned, e.g. UMAP plots of last-hidden-layer activations colored by class labels.

name: hidden-markov-model-cell-cycle-stage-segmentation
description: Use when an ordered single-cell pseudo time-series (reCAT ordIndex) plus bayes_score/mean_score must be partitioned into cell cycle stages, and judged phase regions are available from score plots.

name: hidden-markov-model-transcribed-region-calling
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq alignments (e.g. STAR-aligned 10x or Smart-seq2 BAMs) to discover transcriptional activity outside a genome annotation, especially for organisms with incomplete gene annotation.

name: hidden-markov-random-field-empirical-bayes-modeling
description: Use when integrating and spatially clustering multiple SRT sections (e.g., 12-sample DLPFC Visium or 6-section mouse embryo seqFISH) where batch effects must be estimated jointly with domain/cell-type detection.

name: hierarchical-batch-integration
description: Use when integrating atlas-scale scRNA-seq collections (many studies, thousands of samples, millions of cells) where rapid methods like Harmony or scVI return only embeddings, and an adjusted expression matrix plus preserved biological condition signal is required.

name: hierarchical-bayesian-count-modeling
description: Use when raw per-sample cell-cluster count vectors n_lk (from an AnnData of single-cell samples) must be converted into sample-level probability distributions over clusters before optimal-transport or distance computations.

name: hierarchical-bayesian-em-mcmc-fitting
description: Use when gene-level DE summary statistics (beta, beta_var) plus gene set annotations are available and you need calibrated per-gene-set enrichment p-values that borrow information across genes rather than analyzing one gene at a time.

name: hierarchical-bayesian-joint-de-gse-modeling
description: Use when you have gene-level summary statistics (beta coefficients and coefficient variances) from a scRNA-seq DE method and want joint DE + GSE analysis with calibrated gene set p-values.

name: hierarchical-cell-ontology-label-aggregation
description: Use when comparing cell-label predictors (e.g. zero-shot scPRINT vs CellTypist vs supervised baselines) on labels whose granularity differs across methods or annotation schemes, and you need ontology-consistent, coarser-grained evaluation.

name: hierarchical-cell-type-annotation-scoring
description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix from a tumour biopsy must be annotated into cancer, immune, and stromal cell types/subtypes across a pan-cancer hierarchy with intermediate per-class confidence scores.

name: hierarchical-cell-type-classification
description: Use when annotating human single-cell or bulk RNA-seq cells against the Cell Ontology, especially when flat classifiers would be inconsistent with the ontology hierarchy or when cells should be placed at an internal (ancestral) ontology node rather than a leaf.

name: hierarchical-cell-type-classification
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq data (Seurat v4 objects with a UMAP reduction) at the cell-type level, or when identifying malignant cells and predicting their likely cell of origin in normal or cancer tissues.

name: hierarchical-cell-type-marker-selection
description: Use when scRNA-seq data comes with a multi-level cell-type label hierarchy and the goal is a minimal marker panel that discriminates all levels jointly (e.g. selecting 30–40 markers for the Zeisel mouse cortex labels).

name: hierarchical-cell-type-model-classification
description: Use when bulk DIE genes (from an Iso-based differential isoform test) must be attributed to constituent cell types — deciding whether a region-specific isoform shift originates in one cell type, multiple cell types, or no cell type.

name: hierarchical-classifier-configuration
description: Use when annotating human scRNA-seq cells against the Cell Ontology with a pre-trained, ready-to-run classifier, or when benchmarking CellO against scMatch/SingleR by projecting flat labels onto ontology term IDs.

name: hierarchical-classifier-rejection-step
description: Use when a labeled single-cell training set and an unlabeled test set must be screened for cells that do not belong to any known population, i.e., rejection of potential unseen cell populations before hierarchical classification.

name: hierarchical-classifier-training
description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., simulated AMB data or PBMC-FACS/AMB2018 from the scRNA-seq benchmark Zenodo) must be classified through a hierarchical tree and cells from held-out or unknown populations must be flagged as 'unseen' rather than misassigned.

name: hierarchical-cluster-structure-generation
description: Use when benchmarking transfer-learning clustering on scRNA-Seq data requires synthetic count matrices with known ground-truth labels and controlled complete/incomplete/no-overlap between source and target cell types.

name: hierarchical-cluster-then-annotate-cell-classification
description: Use when annotating tumor-microenvironment cell subtypes in cancer scRNA-seq data and direct per-cell subtype prediction is inaccurate; apply after major-type classification to boost subtype accuracy on T/NK or myeloid cells.

name: hierarchical-clustering-cutree-cutoff-application
description: Use when a batch-corrected (Supervised Harmony) embedding matrix with one row per cell is available and you need a single flat cluster assignment per cell to feed get_clusters() downstream in SingCellaR.

name: hierarchical-clustering-dendrogram-interpretation
description: Use when normalized microarray intensity samples need QC for systematic batch effects: the analysis goal is to see whether samples group by date, operator, or reagent lot rather than by response class before downstream testing.

name: hierarchical-clustering-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL tables (sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv) indexed by geneId-snpId variant-gene pairs and need to test whether sQTL effect sizes are shared across tissues and whether tissue groups (e.g. brain vs non-brain) cluster apart.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-cell-types
description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq cell type proportions with MuSiC and the scRNA-seq reference contains closely related cell types (e.g., PT vs DCT, CD-PC vs CD-IC) where collinearity destabilizes single-stage W-NNLS estimates.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-correlation-values
description: Use when you have log-e-normalized expression of candidate uTARs plus canonical cell-type marker genes (e.g., HBZ, TNNT2, COL1A1) over matching spots/cells and need to test which uTARs are cell-type specific or spatially colocalized, and to visualize groupings as a dendrogram.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-marker-genes
description: Use when generating an in-session CellexalVR heatmap after a user defines two or more cell groups, and the top-ranked marker genes and cells need to be ordered by hierarchical clustering for visualization.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-sample-decay-rates
description: Use when a base-level RNA-seq cohort shows 3'-to-5' coverage decline in some samples and you must identify and exclude degraded samples so they do not appear as spurious shape-change outliers.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-single-cell-transcriptomes
description: Use when you must group individual cells from a single-cell expression matrix into an initial set of discrete cell-state clusters prior to defining Mpath landmark clusters, using FACS-sort labels to judge cluster quality.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-single-cells
description: Use when you already have SClineager MCMC output (results.RData with inferred `genotype_mat` and `sigma`) and need to assign each cell to a discrete lineage cluster.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-somatic-cna-profiles
description: Use when you have per-cell allele-specific integer copy-number calls across single cells and need to define clone structure, especially to cross-validate CNV clones against SNV-genotype clusters.

name: hierarchical-clustering-of-transcription-factors
description: Use when a time-course scRNA-seq trajectory needs its developmental regulatory programs reduced to TF clusters — e.g., recovering Fig. 2f-style tTF groupings after eLR/communication inference.

name: hierarchical-clustering-sample-class-visualization
description: Use when a ranked significant-gene list (e.g. top 50/100/150 from samr SAM output) is available alongside a quantile-normalized expression matrix and you need to visualize whether samples cluster by phenotype class.

name: hierarchical-clustering-tumor-origin-classification
description: Use when scRNA-Seq cells from multiple tumor samples should be grouped by tumor of origin, and you need to test whether removing the cell-cycle effect (scLVM/ccRemover) raises clustering accuracy over uncorrected data.

name: hierarchical-feature-selection-rule-configuration
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads mapping to the same loci must be split into distinct classes (e.g., 22G- vs 26G-RNAs by length 22/26, 5′G, antisense alignment) or resolved at single-nucleotide precision, rather than bulk-counted to features.

name: hierarchical-gradient-boosted-tree-classification
description: Use when annotating cell types in a Seurat scRNA-seq object (with UMAP computed) for human or mouse tissues, or when identifying malignant epithelial cells and their cancer cell-of-origin, without manual marker curation.

name: hierarchical-guide-tree-construction
description: Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq samples with STACAS/Seurat and you need to reproduce or customize the automatic integration order derived from anchor scores instead of using an arbitrary or manual dataset order.

name: hierarchical-integration-ordering
description: Use when integrating many samples/studies (thousands of samples, millions of cells, e.g. COVID-19 CITE-seq collections) where a single flat integration is computationally infeasible or mixes heterogeneous studies.

name: hierarchical-linkage-algorithm-implementation
description: Use when the desired linkage function (e.g. k-minimal-distance linkage generalizing single and average linkage) has no existing O(n^2)-time implementation, so a custom heap-based generic-linkage agglomerative routine must be built and validated against SciPy baselines.

name: hierarchical-neural-network-classifier-training
description: Use when building or reproducing automated cancer scRNA-seq cell-type annotation with a hierarchical deep-learning classifier, or when benchmarking major-type vs subtype annotation accuracy via cross-validation on the scWizard training reference.

name: hierarchical-node-classifier-training
description: Use when you need to train a custom Census cell-type classification model from a reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Tabula Sapiens) rather than using the pretrained model, inferring the cell-type hierarchy from the reference and fitting one binary classifier per node.

name: hierarchical-pathway-clustering
description: Use when pathway module scores (e.g., Seurat AddModuleScore over msigdbr BioCarta gene sets with >=10 genes) have already been scored per spot and ranked by singleCellHaystack KLD-based FDR in 2D spatial data, and the top pathways (e.g., top 25) need to be grouped by spatial-pattern similarity.

name: hierarchical-prior-conditioning-on-cell-type-labels
description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g. AnnData of normalized, log-transformed cells) where some or all cell type annotations are available and a supervised/semi-supervised latent space with label prediction is desired.

name: hierarchical-random-forest-tme-annotation
description: Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices from individual tumour biopsies need pan-cancer TME cell-type labels, including malignant cells and their tissue of origin across 19 cancer types.

name: hierarchical-sample-clustering-by-barcode-composition
description: Use when you have a normalized barcode counts table (samples x barcodes) and need to test whether samples group by treatment condition based on overall clonal composition rather than single-clone abundance.

name: hierarchical-subtype-discovery-verification
description: Use when unsupervised transcriptomic data (bulk or single-cell RNA-seq) has an unknown number of clusters and the goal is to discover and verify novel, biologically meaningful subtypes without manual k selection.

name: hierarchical-tree-split-merge-update
description: Use when a new labeled scRNA-seq dataset (AnnData with cell population labels and batch indicators) must be progressively integrated into an existing scHPL classification tree, and you need to determine which populations match, merge, split, or are new.

name: hierarchical-two-step-cell-annotation
description: Use when annotating unlabeled cancer scRNA-seq cells against the tumor microenvironment reference (113,976 cells, 13 cancer types) — e.g., MCC/CRC/LC datasets — and when major-type and subtype labels are both needed.

name: hierarchy-aware-confusion-matrix-analysis
description: Use when a classification tree (e.g. scHPL trained on multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets) has predicted labels for a held-out dataset and you need to quantify which cross-node and within-subtree misclassifications occur, as in the PBMC Bench10Xv3 evaluation.

name: high-definition-spatial-transcriptomics-analysis
description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics count matrix (e.g., mouse olfactory bulb HDST from the Broad Single Cell Portal, SCP420) with 2D spatial coordinates and need to detect spatially variable genes or reconcile rank disagreements between SVG callers.

name: high-dimensional-expression-matrix-neighborhood-search
description: Use when a pre-processed, normalized scRNA-seq HVG expression matrix must be converted into a cell-to-cell graph (one node per cell, kNN edges) as input to graph-based contrastive learning or downstream imputation.

name: high-dimensional-gene-expression-feature-selection
description: Use when the task is selecting a small, sparse set of predictive genes from high-dimensional, correlated omics/expression data (p >> n) for regression or classification, and unknown feature groupings (e.g. ribosomal or MHCII genes) should be respected.

name: high-dimensional-genomic-covariate-regression
description: Use when fitting Cox or logistic regression with thousands of gene-expression/mutation covariates (e.g., TCGA mRNA Z-scores) and you need penalized variable selection, optional FDR screening, and cross-validated AUC/C-index.

name: high-dimensional-microarray-regression-benchmarking
description: Use when a high-dimensional regression or classification task on correlated omics/microarray feature data needs a quantitative benchmark of sparse linear methods — e.g. reproducing the paper's Table 2 test-MSE and feature-count comparison across the five public microarray datasets.

name: high-dimensional-mse-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing prediction methods (e.g. SuffPCR vs sparse linear models vs non-sparse PCR) on high-dimensional omics data where both out-of-sample MSE and correct feature selection must be evaluated.

name: high-dimensional-nested-cross-validation
description: Use when a dataset has far more predictors than samples (P >> n, e.g. RNA-seq with >16,000 genes in n=68 samples) and you need hyperparameter tuning plus an unbiased estimate of model accuracy or AUC.

name: high-dimensional-noise-data-simulation
description: Use when validating a cross-validation workflow for leakage bias: you need a null dataset (no true signal, P >> n) where any AUC above ~0.5 from filtered models demonstrates information leakage.

name: high-dimensional-omics-cross-model-gene-intersection
description: Use when fitting regression models with survival (or binary) outcomes against ~thousands to hundred-thousands of genomic covariates (e.g., 9,548 TCGA ovarian mRNA entries) and a robust, intersection-based candidate gene list with concordance estimates is needed.

name: high-dimensional-omics-latent-embedding-generation
description: Use when input is a high-dimensional protein x condition omics matrix (TSV/CSV, AnnData-compatible) with sparseness and redundancy, and a dense low-dimensional per-protein embedding is needed before network inference.

name: high-dimensional-predictor-ranking
description: Use when a numeric predictor matrix x has far more columns than rows (transcriptomics-style P >> n) and you must rank/select predictors by univariate tests (t-test, Wilcoxon, ANOVA, correlation) before model fitting inside nested cross-validation.

name: high-dimensional-rnaseq-predictive-modeling
description: Use when the dataset has far more predictors than samples (P >> n, e.g. RNA-Seq like E-MTAB-11611), an unbiased estimate of model accuracy is required, and feature selection must be nested within CV to avoid leakage bias.

name: high-dimensional-screening-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when you need to demonstrate or benchmark that marginal-correlation screening fails to recover predictive genes in a high-dimensional transcriptomic setting where p >> n (e.g., AML: 116 samples, 6283 genes).

name: high-dimensional-shape-similarity-measurement
description: Use when base-level RNA-seq pileup matrices must be compared per sample against a gene mean shape reference, e.g. to derive per-gene on/off statistics or exclude genes with many off samples before shape-change analysis.

name: high-dimensional-simulated-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking or stress-testing penalized regression (Ridge/Lasso/adaptive Lasso logistic or Cox) and you need synthetic n×p covariate grids with matching outcome columns instead of real patient data.

name: high-dimensional-simulation-design
description: Use when evaluating whether a sparse supervised dimension-reduction method still predicts well and recovers features when the marginal-correlation screening assumption is deliberately violated (zero-marginal-correlation, non-zero-coefficient features).

name: high-dispersion-gene-selection
description: Use when a raw single-cell count matrix must be reduced to a manageable, informative gene set (highest-dispersion genes) before autoencoder-based dropout imputation with AutoImpute.

name: high-memory-genome-alignment
description: Use when QC-filtered small RNA-seq FASTQ reads (e.g., 17–50 nt post-trimming from 50 nt serum reads) must be mapped to hg19/hg38 with STAR under a ~30 GB RAM budget, or when per-sample runtime must be compared against web-based pipelines like exceRpt run with identical parameters.

name: high-order-gene-interaction-term-expansion
description: Use when building a cell-to-cell affinity matrix from raw scRNAseq counts where the analysis goal is full-dimensionality similarity — capturing high-order gene interactions without feature selection, PCA, or marker-gene filtering.

name: high-resolution-ortholog-group-splitting
description: Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group aggregates too many genes across species (e.g. vitellogenin s2f_0005567) to permit gene-level insight and needs subdivision into phylogenetically coherent clusters.

name: high-resolution-spatial-image-rendering
description: Use when you have a Seq-Scope (or similar sub-micrometer) spatial DGE with per-barcode spatial coordinates and want to visually resolve cell-type (e.g., periportal vs. pericentral) or subcellular spatial patterns via marker-gene images.

name: high-throughput-criteria-filtering-mirna

name: high-throughput-fastq-preprocessing-benchmarking

name: high-throughput-read-query-evaluation
description: Use when you need to characterize how partitioning a large IBF index (e.g., 8 GiB) into x parts affects wall-clock build time, query time, peak memory, and specificity, before choosing a partition count for large-scale read search.

name: highly-correlated-t-cell-subset-simulation

name: highly-variable-gene-and-transcription-factor-feature-selection

name: highly-variable-gene-detection-vst

name: highly-variable-gene-feature-selection

name: highly-variable-gene-filtering

name: highly-variable-gene-preprocessing

name: highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing raw per-individual UMI count matrices (e.g., human PBMC, mouse lung, human skin droplet-based datasets) for clustering with BAMM-SC or competitors, and a reduced gene feature space must be defined before clustering.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when a Spark-based scRNA-seq pipeline has produced normalized (CPM-like or quantile) tall-format counts and you need to restrict downstream PCA to a informative gene subset before clustering.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq expression matrices from multiple time points as features for supervised cross-timepoint cell-annotation, and you must reduce thousands of genes to a manageable, informative subset before neural-network training.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes, log2(x+1) normalized, genes in ≥3 cells retained) needs dimensionality reduction to a gene subset that preserves signal for rare cell type detection.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when preprocessing raw UMI count matrices (e.g., GSE115746 macaque retina bipolar cells) for DESC clustering, or whenever a compact set of informative genes is needed before deep-embedding or low-dimensional representation.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. h5ad from a multi-batch atlas) for integration or clustering and you need to restrict analysis to informative genes before embedding methods like scCobra, scVI, or Harmony.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection

name: highly-variable-gene-selection

name: highly-variable-gene-selection

name: highly-variable-gene-selection-by-mean-dispersion
description: Use when preparing a raw single-cell UMI count matrix (e.g. gene-cell-barcode matrix from Cell Ranger) for dimensionality reduction or clustering, and you need a compact set of informative genes.

name: highly-variable-gene-selection-comparison

name: highly-variable-gene-selection-filter-genes-dispersion

name: hill-function-ligand-receptor-probability-modeling

name: hiseq-4000-barcode-swapping-characterization

name: hmm-transcribed-region-calling-from-sc-rna-seq

description: Use when a qCLASH/CLASH dataset consists of a .hyb file with a paired Vienna-format predicted-secondary-structure file, and per-record fold patterns or predicted binding energies of miRNA-containing hybrids must be computed and plotted.

name: hybkit-api-segment-type-evaluation
description: Use when input is hyb-format chimeric (hybrid) RNA sequence data from miRNA/target ligation experiments (e.g. CLASH/qCLASH) and records need segment-type and miRNA annotations assigned before analysis or filtering.

name: hybrid-analysis-result-plotting
description: Use when you have completed a hybkit analysis (e.g., Target Analysis of kshv-miR-k12-5 qCLASH hybrids) and need the counts exported as CSV tables and distributions visualized as plots.

name: hybrid-cluster-rearrangement-comparison
description: Use when you already have paired transcriptome-only and ClonoCluster hybrid cluster assignments plus a count matrix, and need to find genes driving cluster rearrangements and test them for GO enrichment.

name: hybrid-record-flag-annotation
description: Use when a .hyb file from CLASH/qCLASH miRNA-target ligation experiments contains unannotated records and you need seg1_type, seg2_type, and miRNA_seg flags added to each record's flags column before type/miRNA, target, or fold analysis.

name: hybrid-segment-type-and-mirna-criteria-matching
description: Use when a hyb-format file of CLASH/qCLASH hybrids must be subset to records whose segment types, miRNA assignments, or sequence identifiers match specified criteria (e.g. keep only miRNA-containing hybrids or hybrids with 'kshv' in any segment).

name: hybrid-sequence-quality-control
description: Use when input is a hyb-format chimeric RNA file (e.g. from CLASH or qCLASH) with an associated Vienna/CT fold file, and data integrity must be checked (malformed columns, disallowed lines, hyb/fold sequence mismatches) before type/miRNA, target, or fold analyses.

name: hybrid-sequence-record-iteration
description: Use when qCLASH/CLASH hybrid records in hyb format must be combined record-by-record with predicted secondary-structure data held in a paired Vienna dot-bracket or CT file — e.g. before fold analysis or any record-level fold-aware filtering.

name: hybrid-subset-selection-feature-selection
description: Use when high-dimensional single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF cells-by-markers tables) has a priori class labels and you need a reduced, interpretable feature set for supervised dimensionality reduction with LDA.

name: hydra-dataset-cell-classification-analysis
description: Use when reproducing scDEED dubious/trustworthy embedding percentages on a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Hydra) at a known original versus optimized t-SNE perplexity, or when validating hyperparameter optimization by counting cell classifications.

name: hydra-neuron-subtype-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify whether merging visually defined single-cell clusters (e.g., five Hydra neuron ectodermal subtypes, or CAR-T clusters 3+4+9+11 under the scDEED-optimized t-SNE) preserves or reduces cluster purity as measured by ROGUE.

name: hypergeometric-dropout-significance-testing
description: Use when an scRNA-seq count/normalized expression matrix contains many zero entries and you must decide which zeros are true biological zeros versus dropout artifacts before imputation.

name: hypergeometric-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have a list of differentially expressed genes (from text, GEO/MSigDB, or a clustered Seurat object) and want to find statistically enriched environmental gene modules with adjusted p-values and fold enrichment.

name: hypergeometric-gene-set-enrichment
description: Use when you have DE genes from clustering corrected scRNA-Seq data (e.g., 2-means clustering at FDR 0.01) and a known signature gene set, and need enrichment statistics to judge biological meaningfulness.

name: hypergeometric-gene-set-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you need to statistically validate that a candidate gene list (e.g., identified LR pairs) is over- or under-represented for known functional categories like essential, housekeeping, or developmental-stage genes.

name: hypergeometric-go-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have a gene list of interest derived from a filtering step (e.g., 533 cell-type-specific IPA events mapped to their host genes) and a defined background universe of genes, and you need GO term enrichment significance.

name: hypergeometric-overrepresentation-testing
description: Use when you have RMT-selected signal gene lists and discarded gene lists from a single-cell dataset (e.g. mouse cortex Zeisel or PBMC Kang) and need to confirm the retained genes enrich for tissue-specific pathways rather than generic or sparsity-driven ones.

name: hypergeometric-overrepresentation-testing
description: Use when a clustering or biclustering step has produced groups of genes (e.g. UniBic trend-preserving biclusters from GDS expression matrices) and you must quantify what proportion is significantly GO-enriched.

name: hypergeometric-phase-enrichment-testing
description: Use when predicting PHAS loci/phasiRNAs from a preprocessed sRNA map file against a transcriptome or genome reference and you need statistically phased clusters (e.g. 21-nt phasiRNAs) rather than heuristic-only phase calls.

name: hypergeometric-statistical-testing
description: Use when given a list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. 229 RA genes from GSE12021/GSE55457/GSE55584/GSE55235) and you need statistically enriched environmental or infection gene modules with FDR-adjusted p-values.

name: hyperparameter-configuration-from-grid-search
description: Use when running AutoImpute.py on a pre-processed scRNA-seq count matrix and dataset-specific hyperparameters must be set from the paper's grid search (e.g., the ~68,000-cell PBMC dataset values in Table 2).

name: hyperparameter-configuration-scrnaseq
description: Reference for setting MarkerCount/HiCAT hyper-parameters (N, fth, score exponent, reassignment cutoff) when running reference-based or marker-based cell-type identification on scRNA-seq count matrices.

name: hyperparameter-ensemble-borda-aggregation
description: Use when reconstructing gene regulatory networks from pseudotemporal single-cell expression data (.mat files with sparse X, ptime, optional regix/branches) and you need SINGE's GLG-then-Aggregate two-stage ensemble workflow with ranked edge output.

name: hyperparameter-grid-configuration
description: Use when preparing a hyperparameter file for SINGE's GLG tests on pseudotemporal single-cell expression data, choosing lambda, dT, num-lags, kernel-width, family, and replicate settings for the ensemble.

name: hyperparameter-optimization-deep-learning
description: Use when training a Keras CNN (e.g., for RNA modification site prediction) and you need to search dropout rates, kernel regularizer weights, optimizer choice, and learning rate to maximize validation F1-score.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a model's default hyperparameter (e.g. the unbalanced OT transported mass m=0.5 in scConfluence) lacks justification for your dataset and you need to demonstrate that embeddings are insensitive to its choice across progressively unbalanced modality scenarios.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when reproducing hyperparameter robustness analyses (Fig. 6, Supplementary Figs. 6-8, 10) or when verifying that a deep imputation method's clustering and imputation metrics are stable across bottleneck size, pre-clustering number, or classifier-weight settings.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-calling or PU-learning classifier whose defaults (e.g., EmptyNN T=100, k=10, N=10) need sensitivity testing against ground-truth labels before deployment on new data.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when deciding how many SINGE ensemble members (replicates/hyperparameter combinations) are necessary, or when checking whether simplifying the hyperparameter grid (e.g., 2–5 replicates instead of 10) degrades precision-recall performance on pseudotemporal single-cell data.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you must quantify how sensitive integration performance (e.g. scMoMaT's NMI/ARI/GC on the human PBMC dataset) is to choices like latent dimension d, lambda, KNN neighborhood size k, or radius r.

name: hyperparameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a pipeline contains a tunable clustering/embedding parameter (e.g. Leiden resolution) whose default needs empirical justification across multiple benchmark datasets via ARI/NMI sweeps.

name: hyperparameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when a method has a tunable hyper-parameter (e.g. number of markers per cell type) whose value must be chosen empirically by sweeping candidate values and comparing performance measures across datasets.

name: hyperparameter-sweep-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking unsupervised manifold-alignment methods on single-cell multi-modal datasets and you need fair, article-specified hyperparameter sweeps (Methods 2.7) plus scTopoGAN model selection over 20 candidate GANs.

name: hyperparameter-tuning-for-marker-selection
description: Use when a marker-selection pipeline (e.g. scGeneFit) exposes a tunable separation parameter Delta that controls how closely same-label samples must sit in the selected-marker subspace, and you must locate the Delta maximizing label-recovery accuracy.

name: hyperspherical-kl-divergence-computation
description: Decision support for validating or reimplementing VAE training objectives where latent variables are vMF-distributed on a unit hypersphere and the KL term to a uniform hyperspherical prior must be computed in closed form.

name: hypoxia-signature-association-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample flux features from METAFlux and a hypoxia signature score table for the same TCGA samples, and need to quantify flux–hypoxia associations via OLS regression.

name: hypoxia-signature-sample-stratification
description: Use when a counts matrix of tumor RNA-seq samples (e.g., TCGA-LUAD from GDC) must be split into hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low groups before differential expression or survival analysis, using a gene-set score rather than a single marker gene.

name: ibf-partitioning-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify how partitioning a large fixed-size IBF index (e.g., 8 GiB) into x parts trades wall-clock construction/search time against peak RAM, as in Table 2 of the Raptor paper.

name: ic50-based-compound-efficacy-labeling
description: Use when a drug retrieval evaluation needs binary efficacy ground truth per compound — e.g., computing ROC AUC and PR AUC for GSFM reversal scores against CMap/XSum/ZhangScore/RS baselines.

name: ic50-to-cell-death-efficacy-conversion
description: Use when you have per-cell or cluster-level IC50 predictions from CaDRReS-Sc GDSC pre-trained model and need to express drug kill efficacy as cell death percentages per cluster and drug.

name: ica-component-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when you have gene z-weight vectors for independent components derived from multiple tumor scRNA-seq cohorts and must keep only cross-cohort-reproducible components before building consensus meta-components.

name: ica-decomposition-of-scrna-seq-expression
description: Use when you have a single log-transformed tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix and need reproducible, independent transcriptional directions (meta-components) rather than manual marker-based cell labeling.

name: ica-discriminant-dimension-analysis
description: Use when comparing two projected query conditions (e.g., knockout vs WT) on a shared reference atlas and you need to find which latent dimensions/gene programs shift, beyond changes in cell-state composition.

name: ica-meta-component-decomposition-single-cell
description: Use when you have a large pan-cancer tumor scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. thousands to millions of cells across many cohorts) and want reproducible, low-dimensional gene programs for cell-state annotation rather than marker-based manual labelling.

name: ica-nmf-factor-decomposition
description: Use when scRNA-seq gene programs must be discovered by independent component analysis or NMF — e.g., as ICA/NMF comparators in a benchmark against SSN gene programs scored by GO and PPI enrichment.

name: icat-upweighted-gene-space-analysis
description: Use when you have an ICAT-processed AnnData (obsm['X_icat'] upweighted matrix, ICAT gene list, 'control' vs 'perturbed' treatment labels) and need to test whether ICAT-selected marker genes are differentially expressed between treatments.

name: icb-response-immune-signature-interpretation
description: Use when bulk tumor RNA-seq profiles from ICB-treated patients have been projected through a single-cell-trained encoder and latent features must be tested for responder/non-responder association and biologically interpreted.

name: icgc-paca-au-sample-metadata-handling
description: Use when a task requires paired-sample analysis of the ICGC PACA-AU cohort (primary vs metastatic vs derived cell line comparisons) across both RNAseq and microarray platforms using pdacR-parsed objects.

name: icm-em-algorithm-execution
description: Use when multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics datasets (e.g. Visium or seqFISH sections) have APCA low-dimensional embeddings and spatial adjacency matrices already built, and you need joint spatial clustering with batch-effect estimation and a data-driven choice of cluster number.

name: identifier-based-sequence-classification
description: Use when hyb-format records from miRNA/target ligation experiments (e.g. CLASH/qCLASH) need segment-type classification from segment reference identifiers, or when miRNA_seg flags ('N','5p','3p','B','U') must be set for downstream analysis.

name: identity-versus-activity-gep-classification
description: Use when comparing GEP-identification methods on a single-cell dataset with known cell-type labels, specifically to quantify how many programs are cell-type-specific identity programs versus shared activity programs across cell types.

name: iedb-antigen-specificity-annotation
description: Use when paired scRNA-seq + TCR data from patients with known epitope exposure (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 PBMCs) and donor HLA types are available, and clusters in a mvTCR joint embedding must be labeled antigen-specific vs bystander.

name: ifn-response-pathway-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq case-control data has been signal-filtered (e.g., SiFT healthy-trajectory removal) and you need a gene-set readout to confirm which cell types carry the recovered disease signal.

name: ig-locus-read-extraction-from-bam
description: Use when starting from a BWA-aligned, coordinate-sorted, indexed hg38 RNA-seq BAM (e.g. ribodepleted or polyA-selected, ≥25M reads) and you need Ig-locus reads extracted and assembled into IGHV-D-J transcript contigs before SHM/IGHV mutation-status analysis.

name: ig-transcript-tpm-sorted-contig-selection
description: Use when a CRIS run has produced Ig-transcript outputs (.ig-transcripts.sortedbyTPM.txt/.fasta and .IgBLAST_out.txt) and the top-expressed contig must be selected and assigned to a germline IGHV gene (e.g. IGHV3-74) for percent-identity comparison.

name: igblast-germline-vdj-alignment
description: Use when you have RNA-seq-derived Ig transcript FASTAs (TPM-ranked) or contigs from a BCR/CLL sample and need to assign a germline IGHV gene, compute percent identity, and call mCLL/uCLL SHM status.

name: ighv-gene-assembly-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing immunoglobulin variable-region reconstruction tools on RNA-seq data, specifically measuring percent IGHV gene assembled and runtime on the same BAM inputs at identical thread counts.

name: ighv-germline-alignment-percent-identity-computation
description: Use when you have de novo assembled Ig-transcript contigs from RNA-seq and need to assign each contig to a germline IGHV gene, compute percent identity to the germline allele, or benchmark whether reconstruction length affects reported identity.

name: ighv-germline-homology-search
description: Use when you have de novo-assembled transcript contigs (e.g., Trinity FASTA) and need to find which contigs are immunoglobulin IGHV-derived and which expressed Ig transcript is the dominant clone by TPM.

name: ighv-mutation-status-classification
description: Use when CLL RNA-seq BAMs (≥25M reads, ribodepleted or polyA) aligned to hg38/GRCh38 with BWA need an IGHV mutation status call, and clinical Sanger genotyping is unavailable or should be cross-checked from transcriptome data.

name: ilisi-batch-mixing-metric-computation
description: Use when you need a quantitative batch-mixing score (complementary to kBET rejection rates) for comparing embeddings such as BEENE vs. PCA on batch-corrected vs. uncorrected scRNA-seq data.

name: ilisi-clisi-metric-computation
description: Use when two preprocessed scRNA-seq datasets have been integrated (e.g., by BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, or Scanorama) and you need quantitative batch-mixing (iLISI) and cell-type-consistency (cLISI) scores to compare correction methods.

name: ilisi-degradation-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing robustness of signal-removal methods (SiFT, regress_out, scVI) to partial or noisy marker gene priors, with iLISI percentage degradation as the metric on single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: ilisi-rnn-integration-metric-computation
description: Use when you have integrated (batch-corrected) single-cell expression or PCA-space embeddings from ≥2 batches and need quantitative iLISI/RNN scores plus runtime to compare integration methods.

name: illumina-nanopore-cross-platform-umi-comparison
description: Use when validating Nanopore single-cell isoform quantification after adaptive UMI cluster pruning (e.g., Longcell step 4) by checking that pruned cluster-size distributions reproduce a matched short-read Illumina reference distribution.

name: illumina-sequencing-error-simulation
description: Use when building simulated scRNA-seq read benchmarks from a spliceu (spliced + unspliced) reference and the simulated FASTQs must carry realistic sequencing errors to faithfully mimic experimental ambiguity.

name: image-based-palette-extraction
description: Use when the goal is to adopt a coloring theme from a publication figure or cover image and apply it to spatial transcriptomics cell-type plots while keeping palette discernibility comparable to standard palettes like matplotlib tab20.

name: image-like-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when fixed-length protein or RNA sequences must be turned into 2D numeric matrices that preserve positional dependencies among residues/nucleotides before feeding a CNN classifier.

name: imaging-mass-cytometry-data-integration
description: Use when integrating multi-sample CyTOF/imaging mass cytometry protein-expression data (e.g. 23-sample COVID-19 IMC with 38 protein markers) to remove sample/dataset variability before clustering against manual cell-type labels.

name: imbalanced-cell-type-downsampling
description: Use when stress-testing a cell-type perturbation method (scDist vs nDEG) against unbalanced cell-type sample sizes in single-cell RNA-seq data with condition, patient, and cluster annotations per cell.

name: imbalanced-class-bootstrapping
description: Use when Ψ site training data are heavily negative-skewed (e.g. 10:1 non-Ψ to Ψ built from RMBase v2.0) and you need bin-balanced training subsets with metrics averaged over bootstrap iterations.

name: imbalanced-class-oversampling-bias-analysis
description: Use when an imbalanced binary classification dataset (e.g. 150 samples, 20,000 predictors, weak signal in ~30 predictors) is being balanced before model fitting and you must check whether balancing outside the CV loop leaks data and inflates ROC AUC.

name: imbalanced-classification-metric-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a cell-type auto-annotation or novelty-detection model on scRNA-seq query sets where novel classes are rare, so accuracy is mis and AUROC (main metric), AUPR and FPR95 must be reported per held-out class.

name: imbalanced-dataset-construction
description: Use when benchmarking cell selection or annotation methods under controlled cell type imbalance, e.g. building artificial 450:50 or 400/25 datasets from cohorts with known ground-truth cell type labels.

name: imbalanced-negative-sampling-rna-sites
description: Use when building Ψ-site classification datasets from RMBase v2.0 annotations and hg19/mm10/sacCer3 genomes where Ψ-free negative RNA regions must be sampled (e.g., 10:1 imbalanced configuration) before model training.

name: immune-cell-community-delineation
description: Use when analyzing CyCIF/MCMICRO-derived single-cell data with marker annotations (e.g., CD3D+, SOX10+) and coordinates, to define immune subregions and quantify tumor cell localization relative to immune infiltrates.

name: immune-cell-marker-signature-annotation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq or microarray tumor profiles need per-sample immune cell-type abundance estimates from a published marker signature (LM22 or similar), e.g. to link co-infiltration to survival outcomes.

name: immune-cell-state-annotation-handling
description: Use when the input is annotated single-cell RNA-seq with fine-grained immune cell state labels (e.g. exhausted CD8 T cell, NKT, Treg) and you need to train a Pollock classifier and report per-cell-state confusion/accuracy.

name: immune-cell-state-classification-interpretation
description: Use when annotated or unannotated single-cell expression data (Seurat .rds, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x cellranger output) needs immune cell type/state labels, or when you need per-gene importance scores explaining which genes drive a cell-state classification.

name: immune-cell-state-marker-recovery-validation
description: Use when a trained Pollock cell-type classification model must be validated biologically by checking whether its per-state gene attribution (DWG) rankings recover literature-known markers such as FOXP3, LAG3, or PDCD1.

name: immune-cell-subpopulation-clustering-visualization
description: Use when raw droplet-based scRNA-seq count data (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC) merges closely related cell types such as cytotoxic/naive cytotoxic or naive/memory T cells in clustering or t-SNE plots, and dropout imputation should resolve them.

name: immune-cell-transcriptome-preprocessing
description: Use when raw single-cell (e.g. HCA bone marrow, Tabula Muris, GSE96583) count matrices must be cleaned of low-quality cells, mitochondrial/ribosomal/non-coding genes, and restricted to HVGs before clustering, tGPT embedding, or batch correction.

name: immune-cell-type-hierarchy-mapping
description: Use when cell-type interpretability scores from Pollock explain mode (captum feature scores) need validation against a curated marker database such as PanglaoDB, and cell states must be mapped to marker sets through a hierarchical parent-state fallback.

name: immune-cell-type-proportion-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices with per-cell cell-type annotations are available and a per-sample composite score of specific immune populations (e.g. an EAD-associated niche score) is needed to compare patient groups across stages.

name: immune-checkpoint-blockade-response-group-comparison
description: Use when a bulk-tumor transcriptome cohort has RECIST/ICB response annotations and you want to test whether pretrained tGPT attention-head entropy differs between responders (CR/PR) and non-responders (SD/PD).

name: immune-cluster-annotation
description: Use when annotating clusters from Seurat WNN joint mRNA+ADT analysis of PBMC CITE-seq data by matching protein markers (CD14, CD86) to immune cell identities and confirming phenotypes with differential gene expression.

name: immune-inflammatory-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when WGCNA module eigengenes (or DEG lists) from a rare-disease RNA-seq experiment correlate with a phenotypic trait and you must translate the module gene lists into GO Biological Process terms to confirm immune/infiltration biology or nominate targets.

name: immune-niche-signature-scoring
description: Use when an independent bulk RNA-seq (e.g. GSE23649) or scRNA-seq cohort (e.g. SRP313633) of liver transplant recipients with EAD vs non-EAD labels must be scored for the niche cell populations and tested for association with EAD occurrence.

name: immune-reference-panel-matching
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., PBMC 3k with 9 Seurat clusters) need automatic cell type labels against a curated human immune reference panel, or when comparing concordance of correlation- vs enrichment-based annotation approaches.

name: immune-repertoire-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when analyzing paired scRNA-seq + single-cell VDJ-seq data (e.g. Suo et al. fetal immune atlas T cells) to reconstruct T or B cell differentiation trajectories and assign per-cell pseudotime and branch fate probabilities.

name: immune-response-gene-restriction-analysis
description: Use when you need intercellular interaction predictions tied to a specific biological function (e.g., immune response GO: 0006955) on scRNA-seq data, rather than the fixed built-in criteria of tools like CellPhoneDB or CellChat.

name: immune-signature-cluster-validation
description: Use when single-cell clusters (e.g., setA clusters 4 NK cells and 5 naïve T cells) must be confirmed as supported by a cancer-immune-signature encoded space, requiring QCM/QCC > 0.5 and COMET p-values for signature/KEGG enrichment.

name: immunoglobulin-fusion-classification
description: Use when analyzing Smart-Seq scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. myeloma, T cells) to detect recurrent gene fusions per cell and test whether fusion carriage drives target-gene overexpression.

name: immunoglobulin-heavy-chain-locus-subsetting
description: Use when starting from a bulk RNA-seq BAM aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) with BWA, coordinate-sorted and indexed, and the goal is to subset reads from putative Ig loci and de novo assemble IGHV-D-J transcript contigs prior to SHM analysis.

name: immunoglobulin-transcript-de-novo-assembly
description: Use when CLL RNA-seq BAMs aligned to hg38 (GRCh38) must yield the dominant IGHV gene, its percent identity to the germline, and mCLL/uCLL status, and partial-IGHV tools (e.g. V'DJer) are insufficient.

name: immunotherapy-response-cohort-comparison
description: Use when comparing tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq cohorts split by immunotherapy condition (e.g., BCC pre vs post-ICB, BLCA ICB responders vs non-responders) to test which cell-state or signaling signature programs differ between groups.

name: immunotherapy-response-stratification
description: Use when you have pre-treatment bulk RNA-seq from immunotherapy (anti-PD-1) patients with survival and clinical response metadata, and need to test whether a published gene-signature risk score separates responders from non-responders.

name: implanted-pathway-benchmark-design
description: Use when comparing sensitivity of single-cell pathway analysis methods against a ground-truth perturbation, i.e. the analysis goal is a controlled simulation where the true significant pathway is known by construction.

name: impossible-barcode-combination-quantification
description: Use when a plate-prepared scRNA-seq library was sequenced on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) and you need to estimate the sample index swapping fraction from the raw FASTQ/BCL data.

name: imprinted-locus-verification
description: Use when RNA-seq data from parthenogenetic (pESC) and androgenetic (aESC) embryonic stem cells (or other allele-biased expression settings) must be screened to confirm a known imprinted cis-NAT pair is identified and expressed from opposite parental alleles.

name: imputation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when an imputed hd5 matrix (e.g. step2/imputation.step2.hd5) and a ground-truth matrix (e.g. example.hd5) with a masked input (e.g. example.msk90.hd5) are available and entrywise imputation accuracy must be quantified and decomposed by zero class.

name: imputation-accuracy-evaluation-correlation-mse
description: Decision support for choosing an imputation method to fill missing ctp/ctnu entries (individual-cell type pairs with <=10 cells, set to missing via preprocess.pseudobulk with ct_cut=10) before fitting CTMM to pseudobulk data.

name: imputation-accuracy-metric-computation
description: Use when you have an imputed scRNA-seq expression matrix plus the original values and a known synthetic-dropout mask, and need per-method accuracy scores (median L1, RMSE, cosine similarity) at each dropout rate.

name: imputation-accuracy-r2-evaluation
description: Use when comparing TWAS weight-training methods (summary-level PRS methods vs FUSION) by imputation accuracy, and a held-out individual-level genotype+expression reference (e.g., GTEx V8 whole blood, n=315) is available to compute per-gene test R2.

name: imputation-baseline-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare gene expression imputation accuracy across multiple ST integration methods by holding out measured genes and computing MAE against ground truth.

name: imputation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a dropout-affected scRNA-seq matrix and its dropout-free reference counterpart are available, and you need to rank competing imputation techniques by recovery accuracy and computational efficiency.

name: imputation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new or existing scRNA-seq imputation method needs head-to-head evaluation against published imputers on simulated or real developmental datasets, scored by downstream pseudotime, clustering, or correlation metrics.

name: imputation-correlation-analysis-vs-measured-proteins
description: Use when training and test single-cell multi-omic data are not perfectly cell-type aligned or come from different tissues/protocols (PBMC vs CBMC, CITE-seq vs REAP-seq), and per-protein imputation accuracy must be quantified against measured protein levels.

name: imputation-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing how much different imputation strategies (scImpute, drImpute, MAGIC, AutoImpute) improve cell-type clustering of sparse scRNA-seq count matrices, measured by ARI against original cell annotations.

name: imputation-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing whether an imputation method improves downstream clustering quality over raw data and competitor imputers on real scRNA-seq datasets, using clustering-quality indices and significance tests.

name: imputation-method-benchmarking-across-datasets
description: Use when raw scRNA-Seq count matrices with known cell-type labels are available and you need to quantify whether imputation improves downstream clustering versus raw data and control methods.

name: imputation-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing runtime/scaling of scRNA-seq imputation methods on large datasets (tens of thousands of cells), e.g. to decide which imputer is tractable for >10,000-cell matrices on a single core.

name: imputation-method-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when you have imputed scRNA-seq matrices from multiple methods on log10(count+1) scale plus ground truth, and need to visually compare which methods recover nonlinear gene-gene patterns for selected gene pairs.

name: imputation-method-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare the computational scalability of scRNA-seq imputation methods across increasing cell counts (e.g. 5000–50000 cells) and report a runtime-vs-cell-count table.

name: imputation-mse-assessment-against-true-counts
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising methods on simulated data where a ground-truth count matrix exists, and you need a quantitative recovery metric (MSE) plus cell-structure recovery (ASW) per noise type.

name: imputation-ordering-robustness-evaluation
description: Use when an imputation method claims arrangement-invariant recovery of scRNA-seq expression values and you must verify that permuted cell/gene orderings yield near-identical imputation correlations with minimal accuracy loss.

name: imputation-quality-evaluation
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data with ERCC spike-in transcripts of known concentrations are available and you need to verify that scImpute imputation recovers true spike-in expression rather than introducing bias.

name: imputation-recovery-error-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking an imputation method on scRNA-seq count matrices: you need controlled dropout recovery curves (error vs masking percentage) comparable to Fig. 3 of the AutoImpute paper.

name: imputation-result-table-compilation
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq imputation methods have been run on identical masked inputs and you must quantify imputation accuracy as MSE against ground truth, or gtMSE when no ground truth exists.

name: imputation-robustness-analysis-across-dropout-scenarios
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq imputation methods for robustness across dropout rates, normalization techniques, or quantification scenarios — e.g. Splatter-simulated negative-binomial datasets where ARI against known cell-type labels must be aggregated per method and scenario.

name: imputation-signal-preservation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing an imputed scRNA-seq matrix to its original counterpart to quantify whether imputation preserved the dominant biological structure captured by the principal components.

name: imputed-matrix-completeness-validation
description: Use when a sparse spot-by-poly(A) site RUD matrix has been imputed and you must confirm no missing entries remain and that imputed values preserve the known spatial structure (e.g., MOB layers).

name: imputed-merfish-transcriptome-analysis
description: Use when you have a SpatialScope-implemented (imputed) image-based ST dataset such as MERFISH mouse1_slice180 with paired snRNA-seq cell type labels and want cell-type-specific or global spatially DE genes beyond the original gene panel.

name: imputed-vs-raw-scrnaseq-comparison
description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq counts plus one or more imputed versions of the same matrix (e.g. scGCL, GraphSCI h5/h5ad outputs) and want to judge imputation quality by DEG patterns and disease-pathway recovery.

name: in-cluster-coherence-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity methods on h5ad developmental datasets and you need to score the directional coherence of inferred velocities within clusters, e.g. LatentVelo vs scVelo.

name: in-silico-cell-generation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation is too sparse (e.g. 13 of 150 cells after downsampling) to support trajectory or downstream analyses, and realistic cells must be generated in silico to restore population structure.

name: in-silico-cell-mixing-simulation
description: Use when quantifying how low a minor donor genotype an SNV-based chimerism method can detect, by simulating cell mixtures from single-cell allele UMI counts and comparing model selection (K=1 vs K=2) and detection metrics per mixing ratio.

name: in-silico-cell-mixture-clustering-benchmark
description: Use when evaluating whether incorporating bulk HiChIP loop data via DC3 improves single-cell clustering over coupled NMF or plain NMF as scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq dropout rises, using an in silico two-subpopulation mixture with known ground-truth labels.

name: in-silico-drug-perturbation-scoring
description: Use when untreated single-cell transcriptomic data plus a known drug target gene must be converted into a ranking of drug-responsive cell populations, without disease-treatment paired samples.

name: in-silico-gene-knockout-simulation
description: Use when you have mock and infected context-specific FBA models with a viral biomass objective function and need to rank host genes/gene pairs as antiviral targets by essentiality-vs-safety trade-off.

name: in-silico-gene-perturbation-simulation
description: Use when you have a trained PRESCIENT model and a serialized data_pt torch object and need to predict how overexpression or knockdown of specific genes (TFs or non-TFs) alters terminal cell-fate proportions.

name: in-silico-mixture-deconvolution-validation
description: Use when validating mixture-deconvolution performance on in silico scRNA-seq mixtures of known composition (5-9 contributors) where the ground-truth contributor count can be compared against the number of deconvoluted cell clusters.

name: in-silico-mutagenesis-perturbation-prediction
description: Use when enhancer–gene assignments must be validated against CRISPR perturbation measurements and a sequence-model counterfactual (predicted expression change after enhancer removal) is needed as an alternative to activity-by-contact scoring.

name: in-silico-scrnaseq-mixture-assembly
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell genetic mixture deconvolution (e.g. de-goulash) against controlled imbalance levels, by pooling barcoded cells from two known scRNA-seq donors at defined ratios such as 1:10–1:99.

name: in-silico-sensitivity-analysis-of-rule-inference
description: Use when you need to determine whether scBONITA Boolean rule determination is robust to the size of a cluster's scRNA-seq training data, or to choose how many cells a training subset must contain before inference degrades.

name: in-silico-single-cell-data-simulation
description: Use when a single-cell computational method needs validation against a known ground truth (e.g., a known gene-regulatory network with planted fate-driving TFs) before applying it to real scRNA-seq data.

name: in-silico-single-cell-mixture-construction
description: Use when benchmarking deconvolution or coupled clustering of bulk/single-cell RNA-seq, ATAC-seq, and HiChIP data and true subpopulation-specific profiles are needed as ground truth for computing PCC against predicted profiles.

name: in-silico-single-cell-simulation
description: Use when you need simulated single-cell RNA-seq data that preserves gene identities, cell trajectories, pseudo-time ordering, and noise of a reference dataset, or ground-truth GRNs for benchmarking GRN inference.

name: in-silico-single-gene-deletion-analysis
description: Use when you have context-specific genome-scale metabolic models (e.g. built with rFASTCORMICS on Recon2.04/Recon3D_01) with a VBOF and need to find genes essential to viral biomass but not host growth.

name: in-silico-tf-knockout-simulation
