description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a reprogramming or differentiation process has state-annotated cells and inferred GRNs, and you need to rank candidate TF regulators by simulating knockouts before experimental validation.

name: in-silico-tf-knockout-simulation
description: Use when you have a trained GRouNdGAN checkpoint and an imposed (e.g., GRNBoost2- or PPCOR-derived) bipartite TF-gene GRN, and you want to test whether knocking out each TF significantly alters its target genes in simulated cells.

name: in-silico-transcription-factor-perturbation-simulation
description: Use when CellOracle in silico TF perturbation simulations must be converted into quantitative perturbation scores to rank candidate regulators (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) for experimental validation.

name: in-vivo-in-vitro-trajectory-result-comparison
description: Use when two FateCompass differential TF activity result sets exist (e.g. mouse in vivo E15.5 and human in vitro beta differentiation) and the goal is to quantify shared versus system-specific beta-cell regulators.

name: incoming-outgoing-edge-quantification-per-cell-type
description: Use when dsCellNet has inferred developmental series cell-cell interaction networks (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis time points) and you need to rank cell types by incoming/outgoing/total interaction counts per time point to identify the most communicating sender and receiver cell types.

name: incremental-index-update
description: Use when a previously built PAC index must grow with additional sequence datasets — e.g. appending the next batch of SRA FASTQ/FASTA samples via update mode to reach ~32,000-sample scale where competitors (SeqOthello, HowDeSBT) fail.

name: indel-proximity-exclusion
description: Use when filtering a VCF for allele-specific expression analysis and SNPs must be excluded if they fall within a user-defined base-pair window of an indel.

name: indel-tolerant-oligo-position-detection
description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq or similar combinatorial-barcode single-cell FASTQ data and reads may contain a single mismatch or INDEL inside the barcode/index regions, so naive exact matching would discard them.

name: independent-cohort-validation
description: Use when a classifier trained on one cohort's features must be shown to generalize — e.g., an L1 LinearSVC on GSVA scores of MMR-module pathways needs AUROC confirmation on both a 30% held-out GSE39582 split and the independent TCGA COAD-READ cohort.

name: independent-cohort-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a trained subtype classifier must be assessed on external validation cohorts with known labels, or when cross-platform robustness to missing genes must be quantified.

name: independent-component-analysis-decomposition
description: Use when a single-dataset TME scRNA-seq expression matrix must be decomposed into independent gene-expression programs (MeCs), or when benchmarking ICA vs NMF recovery of known gene expression programs across pooled cohorts.

name: independent-dataset-testing
description: Use when a trained model (e.g., im6A-TS-CNN on 41-nt RNA sequences) must be evaluated on a separate benchmark test set, and per-dataset Sn/Sp/Acc/MCC/AUC values must be compared against cross-validation results.

name: independent-hypothesis-weighting-multiple-testing
description: Use when you have a large family of test p-values (e.g., ~20k genes from edgeR or 50 camera gene-set tests) plus an independent continuous covariate like average expression, and you need FDR-controlled calls (FDR < 0.1 or < 0.05) with maximal power.

name: individual-sample-transcriptome-fingerprinting
description: Use when the goal is to stratify individual subjects within a cohort by their module-level expression fingerprint — e.g., detecting which patients carry an interferon (A28) signature when group-level tests show no overall change.

name: induced-vs-uninduced-logfc-comparison
description: Use when a controlled induction experiment (e.g. doxycycline-inducible miRNA in scRNA-seq) yields induced vs uninduced cell profiles and you must quantify whether a miRNA-inference method recovers the induction as logFC with significance.

name: infected-proportion-bias-decoupling
description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data where perturbation (Y) and control (Z) groups show differing cell-cluster proportions, so naive fold-change / observed-change (OC) estimates of perturbation effect are contaminated by infected proportion bias and the true cellular response must be recovered.

name: infection-proportion-bias-quantification
description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq perturbation vs. control data where cluster proportions differ between groups, and you need to measure or validate how much fold-change estimates are contaminated by infected proportion bias.

name: infection-sample-subset-selection
description: Use when building a soybean–fungal infection expression matrix from Soybean Expression Atlas TPM data plus supplementary infection RNA-seq samples and a gene-level noise filter is needed before coexpression network construction.

name: infercnv-copy-number-profiling
description: Use when Splane-identified spatial domains (e.g., D1–D9 across 11 breast cancer Visium slices) need orthogonal validation via copy-number aberration signatures and histology-based immune-spot enrichment.

name: inference-difficulty-benchmarking
description: Use when a cohort bulk dataset has candidate representative-selection strategies and you must quantify which strategy yields lower single-cell inference difficulty at a fixed representative budget.

name: inferred-vs-true-network-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a fitted GRN matrix A is available and you need a quantitative recovery benchmark via noise-added in-silico expression simulations refit through the same model.

name: inflection-point-based-cluster-set-selection
description: Use when reconstructing a single-cell trajectory that needs discrete cell-state landmarks, and the number of clusters k must be chosen objectively from clustering-purity or landmark-count curves (e.g. FACS-label-guided cuts of hclust dendrograms).

name: information-content-label-coarsening
description: Use when evaluating a cell type classifier on a label hierarchy — e.g. mapping ~164 Cell Ontology fine labels to ~31 coarse classes via information content and comparing macro F1 across granularity levels.

name: information-flow-distance-profiling
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has been equipped with a spatial cell–cell distance matrix and the goal is to infer which gene in one cell affects which gene in a neighboring cell, and at which spatial range.

name: information-flow-quantification-of-signaling-pathways
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. lesional vs nonlesional AD skin, E13.5 vs E14.5 embryonic skin) each have a CellChat object and you need to rank which signaling pathways change their information flow between conditions.

name: information-flow-ranking-of-interaction-pairs
description: Use when a NeuronChat run has produced per-interaction communication networks and you need to rank all significant interaction pairs by information flow (weight and/or count) to report the top-ranked neuron-neuron signaling interactions.

name: information-leakage-avoidance-in-cv
description: Use when building predictive models on high-dimensional data (P >> n) where univariate feature filters like ttest_filter are applied inside nested cross-validation and unbiased outer-fold accuracy is required.

name: information-theoretic-correlation-transformation
description: Use when you must quantify association strength between continuous/ordinal features and a response, and overlapping information between feature pairs, from Spearman rank correlations without expensive mutual-information density estimation.

name: informative-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when preparing a scRNA-seq expression matrix (loaded into an AnnData object) for STREAM trajectory inference, so that only informative genes drive the low-dimensional embedding and subsequent branching-tree reconstruction.

name: informative-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing a normalized scRNA-seq reference matrix for supervised cell-type classification (e.g., SciBet Learn/Bet) and a compact marker gene set is needed to discriminate close subtypes or rare populations.

name: inner-bandwidth-estimation-from-gene-scatter
description: Use when constructing a DeformedKernel/AdaptiveKernel affinity matrix on a log-normalized (genes x cells) scRNAseq matrix and a data-driven inner bandwidth is needed instead of hand-tuning φ.

name: inner-product-perturbation-scoring
description: Use when scoring systematic in silico KO/overexpression simulations (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) against a reference differentiation trajectory to prioritize TF regulators for validation.

name: input-channel-ablation-analysis
description: Use when you need to test whether DeepCycle's accurate transcriptional phase inference depends on training with both the spliced (Ms) and unspliced (Mu) scVelo moment layers, by ablating one input channel and comparing the resulting cell_cycle_theta values between single-channel runs.

name: input-preprocessing-benchmark-design
description: Use when evaluating how input matrix preprocessing (raw vs log1p vs size-factor normalized variants) affects a downstream embedding or cell type annotation pipeline, or when validating that a method's raw-count requirement holds under batch perturbation.

name: int-pair-functional-annotation
description: Use when a pre-computed CCI dataset (e.g. from CellChat, CellPhoneDB, ICELLNET, SingleCellSignalR) has been loaded into InterCellar's function-verse and enriched int-pairs need GO/pathway functional annotation.

name: int-pair-module-definition-via-umap-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when a pre-computed CCI dataset (e.g., from CellChat) has been subset to a specific cell-viewpoint in the cluster-verse and enriched interaction pairs need to be grouped into functional modules for biological interpretation.

name: integer-linear-programming-formulation
description: Use when a directed gene regulatory network must be reduced to control-theoretic driver-node candidates, i.e., an MFVS that breaks all directed cycles and an MDS that covers every node are needed as optimization problems.

name: integrated-gradient-attribution-scoring
description: Use when cluster-specific marker genes must be recovered from a trained self-supervised scRNA-seq encoder (e.g., Miscell latent features) and attributed to individual genes via an attribution method.

name: integrated-gradient-gene-attribution
description: Use when a trained STEM model and spatial trajectory (e.g., the 11-segment E1z2 spinal-cord pseudo-spatial coordinates) are available and you need to identify which genes determine individual cells' spatial locations, beyond expression-based DEGs.

name: integrated-gradients-feature-attribution
description: Use when a trained Pollock cell-type/state model needs interpretable gene-level attributions — e.g. to identify driving genes (DWGs) for predicted immune cell states on held-out annotated cells.

name: integration-baseline-pipeline-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking whether a clustering/integration method resolves perturbation-unique cell states in control/perturbed single-cell transcriptome data with known ground-truth labels, across perturbation-severity, marker-gene, and cell-proportion conditions.

name: integration-benchmark-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing single-cell diagonal integration methods (e.g. scRNA-scATAC or scRNA-surface protein) on unpaired data and you need quantitative, per-method performance scores to produce a ranked benchmark table.

name: integration-benchmark-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing multiple single-cell batch-integration methods (e.g., scDREAMER vs. scVI, Harmony, Seurat v3) on the same AnnData embedding and you need quantitative, composite-scored benchmark metrics.

name: integration-benchmark-metric-visualization
description: Use when evaluating or visualizing how well integrated scRNA-seq embeddings mix batches while preserving cell types, especially to detect overcorrection where batch mixing destroys biological structure.

name: integration-method-benchmarking
description: Use when two or more single-cell datasets (scRNA-seq batches or spatial/scRNA pairs) must be integrated and a defensible choice among integration methods is needed, measured by batch-removal vs biological-conservation metrics.

name: integration-method-benchmarking-across-repetitions
description: Use when comparing how robust filtering/integration methods are to incomplete prior knowledge (e.g., a partial cell-cycle marker gene set), quantified as mean percentage degradation of iLISI across repeated runs.

name: integration-method-ranking-aggregation
description: Use when comparing multiple single-cell integration methods on the same dataset and you need a reproducible multi-metric ranking (batch/cell-type ARI and ASW) summarised into a single benchmark table.

name: integration-method-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you must justify or tune PILOT's optimal-transport cost matrix: i.e., before reporting sample-level Wasserstein distances/Leiden clusters, to test whether the cosine similarity and integration choice materially affect clustering or trajectory concordance.

name: integration-metric-computation-and-composite-scoring
description: Use when you have integrated embeddings from multiple single-cell integration methods (e.g. scDREAMER, scVI, INSCT) and need quantitative batch-mixing, bio-conservation, and runtime comparisons across atlas-scale datasets.

name: integration-metric-evaluation-cilisi-asw
description: Use when you have integrated (or uncorrected) scRNA-seq embeddings and true cell type annotations and need to quantify batch mixing (CiLISI) and preservation of biological variance (celltype ASW) across methods such as ssSTACAS, scANVI, scGen, or Harmony.

name: integration-metric-evaluation-kbet-pcr
description: Use when you have latent embeddings from one or more single-cell integration methods and need comparable bio-conservation and batch-correction scores (NMI/ARI/ASW/kBET/PCR) to rank methods or justify ablation choices.

name: integration-metric-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking whether an integration method (e.g. GEDI) removes technical/batch effects while preserving biological variability against competitors across multiple datasets and latent-dimension settings.

name: integration-metric-visualization-across-methods
description: Use when per-cell UMAP embeddings from several integration methods are available together with batch and cell-type annotations, and you need to objectively compare how well each method mixes batches while preserving AUCell-derived cell types.

name: integration-quality-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have latent embeddings from integrating scATAC-seq and scRNA-seq (e.g. uniPort coupled-VAE + Minibatch-UOT output) and must quantify alignment via Silhouette, FOSCTTM, and ARI/NMI/F1.

name: inter-gene-feature-segmentation
description: Use when building scReadSim's feature space from a scRNA-seq BAM file and a GTF annotation (e.g. gencode.vM10.annotation.gtf), and you need non-overlapping gene and inter-gene regions to construct gene-by-cell and inter-gene-by-cell count matrices.

name: interaction-evidence-channel-filtering
description: Use when building or filtering a protein–protein interaction database for intercellular communication analysis and you must separate STRING interactions by evidence channel (experiments > 0, database > 0, predicted low-evidence sources) with credibility/action annotations.

name: interaction-family-classification-verification
description: Use when building or auditing a cell-cell communication database and you must confirm that curated ligand-receptor interactions are complete, counted correctly, and classified into the expected molecular families before running inference.

name: interaction-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has annotated cell clusters (e.g., Seurat Louvain clusters) and the goal is to score, rank, and visualize bona fide ligand-receptor interactions between a sender and a receiver population.

name: interactive-report-state-save-restore
description: Use when an analyzed PhyloVision/VISION object must be delivered as an interactive HTML+JSON web report, or when a previously rendered report's saved state (differential expression cache, selections) must be restored before serving.

name: interactome-complexity-quantification
description: Use when a gene cluster table of significantly changed genes with LFC values needs interactome-level assessment of key interactors, e.g. to characterize cellular perturbation events or prioritize network targets.

name: interactor-function-assessment
description: Use when a completed interactome/GMM analysis has produced a list of key interactor genes/proteins and you need to annotate each interactor with protein type and subcellular location to interpret the cluster biologically.

name: intercellular-communication-inference
description: Use when the goal is to infer and benchmark intercellular/ligand–receptor interactions between annotated cell clusters from scRNA-seq count matrices, especially with user-defined gene filters such as GO terms or subcellular location cutoffs.

name: interferon-gene-module-scoring
description: Use when validating that an integration method (e.g. JOINTLY, Harmony, scVI) resists over-correction: score a biologically meaningful module, such as interferon signalling, on cells from different conditions and check whether condition-specific signal remains separable after integration.

name: interferon-module-subject-stratification
description: Use when the goal is to detect individual subjects with increased abundance of interferon (A28) modules in blood expression matrices, especially when group-mean comparisons show no significant overall change.

name: interferon-response-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data contain control vs interferon-beta-stimulated cells and you need to rank cell types by IFN-beta response magnitude while verifying batch effects were removed without erasing true biological variation.

name: interferon-signaling-pathway-geneset-annotation
description: Use when evaluating or annotating a gene embedding learned from interferon-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq data against the Reactome Interferon Signaling pathway R-HSA-913531 or MSigDB C8 co-membership, e.g. comparing MI vs Pearson training objectives.

name: interferon-stimulated-gene-program-interpretation
description: Use when analyzing interferon beta-stimulated PBMC scRNA-seq (or a similar perturbation dataset) and you need to extract a co-regulated gene program and verify it is not confounded by cell type composition.

name: interindividual-covariance-partitioning-across-differentiation-stages
description: Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk data span ordered cell types or stages and the goal is to test whether interindividual expression correlations between adjacent stages exceed those between more distant stages.

name: interindividual-variance-partition-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data across multiple individuals and cell types (e.g. differentiating iPSCs) must be partitioned into cell type-specific vs shared interindividual variance components using cell type-specific pseudobulk linear mixed models.

name: interleaved-bloom-filter-indexing
description: Use when many NGS reads or transcripts must be searched against a large binned collection (e.g., 64/1,024-bin NCBI RefSeq sets) and an IBF index with (k,w)-minimizers must be built and searched.

name: internal-membrane-detection
description: Use when multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images yield watershed cell labels that are bisected by internal membrane segments (e.g., columnar epithelial or Mucin 2+ goblet cells) and need resegmentation into single objects.

name: internal-priming-artifact-filtering
description: Use when building or curating a candidate cleavage-site catalog from 3'-tag scRNA-seq data (e.g. Microwell-seq) where genomic A-rich stretches downstream of a candidate site could indicate internal priming rather than a genuine polyadenylation event.

name: internal-reference-gene-normalization
description: Use when a raw microarray or gene-expression DataFrame (e.g., GEO series such as GSE4786) needs an empirically selected endogenous reference gene for single-gene normalization and before/after distribution comparison.

name: interval-data-structure-implementation
description: Use when interval-overlap queries (features overlapping an alignment/read interval) are a measured bottleneck in a Python counting pipeline, and the stock container (e.g., HTSeq StepVector) creates excessive intermediate objects per query.

name: interval-overlap-equivalence-testing
description: Use when a Python interval/feature data structure (e.g. HTSeq StepVector) is a measured bottleneck in read-to-feature assignment and a compiled (Cython) replacement must be proven query-equivalent before adoption.

name: intestinal-tissue-linearization
description: Use when a CODEX-exported .csv of per-cell x/y coordinates from rolled (spiral/Swiss-roll) intestinal tissue needs to be unrolled onto a line so cell types and markers can be assessed along proximal–distal and serosa-luminal axes.

name: intnmf-copy-number-clustering
description: Use when scDNA-seq copy-number data must be partitioned into clones (clone labels for DNA cells) before evaluating or running cell-to-clone assignment of scRNA-seq cells, and multiple clustering algorithms/transformations should be compared.

name: intra-cluster-gene-selection
description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq with a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference in which closely related cell types cause collinearity (e.g., 13 mouse kidney cell types), so proportions must be resolved hierarchically rather than in a single NNLS fit.

name: intronic-polyadenylation-site-identification
description: Use when analyzing coordinate-sorted RNA-seq BAM files (bulk or SMART-seq2 single-cell) to discover novel skipped or composite IPA events, reconstruct IPA isoforms, and estimate per-site PAU usage not present in the RefSeq annotation.

name: intronic-splicing-kinetics-classification
description: Use when you have lead sQTL variants mapped with sQTLseekeR2 plus an intron annotation, and need to test whether splicing QTLs localize preferentially in post-transcriptionally vs co-transcriptionally spliced introns.

name: intronic-terminal-exon-classification
description: Use when you must identify previously unannotated intronic terminal exons / IPA sites from a standard RNA-seq BAM aligned to GRCh38 with RefSeq annotation, and need sample-specific classification of skipped vs composite candidates.

name: intronic-transcriptome-index-building
description: Use when FASTQ files from 10x Genomics scRNA-seq (e.g. v2 chemistry) must be processed with scKB/kallisto-bustools and spliced AND unspliced counts (for RNA velocity or COPILOT input) are required.

name: inverse-dispersion-fisher-scoring-estimation
description: Use when training scDBM (BoltzmannMachines.jl) on scRNA-seq count matrices where the negative-binomial likelihood's inverse dispersion must be re-estimated during training rather than fixed, e.g. to support Gibbs sampling of synthetic cells.

name: inverse-distance-kernel-affinity-construction
description: Use when preparing inputs for scMMGAN's geometry-preserving correspondence loss: pairwise L1 distances on preprocessed modality matrices (MAGIC-corrected, zero-centered/unit-scaled, 50 principal components) must be converted to affinities via the inverse-distance kernel with adaptive kNN bandwidth.

name: inverse-pseudobulk-size-weighted-averaging
description: Use when a miloR neighbourhood object holds per-cell data and a pseudobulk milo object (pb.milo) carries pseudotime/branch probabilities in colData, and you need cell-level trajectory values.

name: inversely-correlated-pair-heatmap-visualization
description: Reference for when CCIVR Table.csv contains fold_change and padj columns for both strands and you need to classify cis-NAT pairs into expression combinations and visualize the down-up subset as a heatmap.

name: ipa-isoform-assembly-annotation
description: Use when sorted RNA-seq or scRNA-seq BAM alignments (BAM against GRCh38 with RefSeq GTF) have yielded InPACT-predicted novel IPA terminal exons and you need assembled isoform GTFs plus per-site IPA usage values.

name: ipa-site-benchmarking-against-3p-end-sequencing
description: Use when RNA-seq-derived IPA site predictions from multiple tools need accuracy assessment against experimentally determined polyA site coordinates, or when deciding which IPA caller to adopt.

name: ipa-site-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when comparing RNA-seq-based IPA site prediction tools for sensitivity, precision, and IPA-usage quantification accuracy, especially when ground-truth polyA sites are known and simulated reads at controlled coverage (10X–50X) are feasible.

name: ipa-usage-error-distribution-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing an IPA quantification method: you have simulated RNA-seq (Polyester, 10X–50X coverage, ≥5 replicates) with predefined polyA sites and known ground-truth relative usage, and need to compare tools' quantification error via |ΔPAU| distributions.

name: ipsc-differentiation-quality-assessment
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq profiles of iPSC-derived cells (e.g., hiPSC-NPC n=13, hiPSC-neuron n=11) need cell type assignment to judge whether differentiation toward a target lineage succeeded or stalled.

name: iqr-based-anomaly-thresholding
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix may contain outlier cells that should be flagged and removed before dropout imputation, based on their distance to the nearest neighboring cell in PC space.

name: iqr-based-outlier-flagging-of-count-data
description: Use when initializing demuxmix model fitting on an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and a per-droplet detected-gene vector, and droplets with extreme HTO counts or abnormally many detected genes must be flagged as outliers before mixture fitting.

name: iqr-outlier-detection
description: Use when you have a per-cell continuous FiRE rareness score vector and need to convert it to binary rare-cell calls via a distribution-based IQR cutoff.

name: iqr-threshold-dichotomization
description: Use when you have a continuous rareness score per cell (FiRE, LOF) and need binary rare/non-rare calls for a scRNA-seq dataset, or must compare against binary predictors like RaceID and GiniClust.

name: iqr-threshold-rare-cell-selection
description: Use when FiRE (or an equivalent LSH-based density estimator) has produced a per-cell rareness score array and a binary rare/abundant cell label is needed for downstream clustering of candidate rare subpopulations.

name: iqr-threshold-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a rare-cell or doublet detection method whose outlier-calling threshold is adjustable (e.g. FiRE's default vs relaxed IQR threshold) and you need to show the comparison is not an artifact of a single cutoff choice.

name: irlba-partial-svd-computation
description: Use when a large single-cell count matrix (e.g., 1500 features x >20,000 cells) needs fast, scalable dimension reduction or when comparing wall-clock runtime of CA against glmPCA on benchmark datasets.

name: islet-non-islet-separation-visualization
description: Use when after applying BUSseq to multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., the four human pancreas datasets), you need a heat-map view of corrected counts over intrinsic genes to confirm that islet and non-islet cell populations separate cleanly rather than clustering by batch.

name: ismara-linear-motif-activity-inference
description: Use when you need to infer TF motif activity trajectories across single-cell cell-cycle phases from unspliced scRNA-seq counts and promoter-annotated motif binding sites.

name: iso-f1-biology-conservation-scoring
description: Use when scoring cross-species scRNA-seq integration strategies (e.g. BENGAL outputs) for biology conservation, specifically to detect overcorrection where nearest-neighbour methods merge cell types present in only a few species datasets.

name: isoform-abundance-assignment
description: Use when RNA-seq data contain circRNA back-spliced junctions detected by CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS and you need isoform-level relative expression (read counts, FPKM, TPM) rather than locus-level junction counts.

name: isoform-abundance-cosine-similarity-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking isoform detection and quantification accuracy of long-read transcript tools against a set of known reference isoforms (e.g. SIRV spike-ins with PacBio data), needing detection counts plus cosine similarity of abundance profiles.

name: isoform-abundance-quantification
description: Use when a GMAP- or minimap2-aligned BAM from long-read (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT) data needs per-isoform abundance quantification for a single gene/locus, and the read-threshold parameter must be tuned or its sensitivity characterized against a known isoform profile.

name: isoform-ambiguity-aware-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when region sets are defined only by genomic positions without clear isoform association (e.g., POSTAR3/RBP or RNA modification sites) and you need transcriptome-level association testing against picked regions like 5'UTR, CDS, or stop codons.

name: isoform-ambiguity-fractional-overlap-scoring
description: Use when a region set (e.g. m6A sites from POSTAR3/miCLIP-seq) has genomic positions but no known transcript isoform association, and you need an overlap score or permutation test against transcriptome regions of interest such as stop codons.

name: isoform-ambiguity-handling
description: Use when transcriptome elements (e.g. POSTAR3 RBP sites or miCLIP-seq m6A sites) have known genomic positions but no clear isoform association, and a permutation-based colocalization test at the transcriptome level is required.

name: isoform-assembly-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing the Table 3 '1' vs '1-fixed' comparison on real SPIso-seq contigs: you have a cloudrnaSPAdes contig FASTA plus a barcode-to-gene assignment table and must measure how many ambiguously assigned contigs a duplicate-barcode filter removes.

name: isoform-assignment-parsing-from-alignment-tools
description: Use when comparing de novo transcriptome assemblers by counting uniquely assigned reference isoforms from IsoQuant assignment output files against a GENCODE annotation for a specific gene locus.

name: isoform-contig-removal-rate-quantification
description: Use when you have cloudrnaSPAdes assembled contigs (FASTA) plus a barcode-to-gene assignment table and need to measure what fraction of ambiguous barcode assignments a filtering script removes.

name: isoform-coordinate-quantification
description: Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) alignments in BAM, GFF3, or BED6 format for one or a few genes must be converted into consensus splice sites and quantified isoforms without prior knowledge of splice sites.

name: isoform-count-filtering
description: Use when preparing a transcript-level TPM expression matrix (e.g. GTEx V7 trId/geneId table) for multivariate sQTL mapping and you must keep only genes expressed with at least two isoforms.

name: isoform-count-matrix-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating long-read (Nanopore) isoform quantification methods on single-cell or spatially barcoded data where an independent short-read ground-truth cell barcode/UMI matrix is available for comparison.

name: isoform-count-table-processing
description: Use when per-cell-type long-read isoform count tables (IsoQuantOutput-style 'Modality-ModalityID.csv', NumModalityPerCluster files, or an AllInfo file) must be converted into pairwise differential isoform expression results with dPI and FDR statistics.

name: isoform-detection-and-quantification
description: Use when low-throughput long-read (PacBio/ONT) data mapped to a single gene or locus needs isoform detection and quantification without prior splice-site knowledge, e.g. PAX6/TP53 PacBio UHR analysis at a 3% read threshold.

name: isoform-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing isoform detection/quantification performance of long-read transcript tools against a known isoform annotation (e.g., SIRVs), or reproducing the VIsoQLR benchmark where VIsoQLR detects ~72% of isoforms with 99% exon coordinate accuracy.

name: isoform-dominant-transcript-calling
description: Use when you have a gene-by-transcript TPM expression matrix from a case/control RNA-seq dataset and need to identify per-sample dominant transcript isoforms and derive disease-specific isoform switching events.

name: isoform-expression-count-aggregation
description: Use when you need per-sample isoform-switch frequencies or isoform-expression prevalence counts from CanIsoNet's precomputed dMDT tables, e.g. verifying paper-reported values like '21% of samples' or '11 of 39 samples' for a specific transcript pair.

name: isoform-level-te-count-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a deep-learning TE quantifier recovers locus- and isoform-specific counts (e.g., 300 bp simulated Alu repeats, simple repeats, HERVK-int isoform pairs) against a known simulated ground truth.

name: isoform-path-extraction-from-assembly-graph
description: Use when assembling full-length isoforms reference-free from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads: after per-barcode subgraph simplification (tip clipping, bulge removal, gap closing) you need to read out simple isoform paths per read cloud.

name: isoform-proportion-psi-estimation
description: Use when you have per-sample, per-allele inclusion/skipping junction counts (IJC_REF/SJC_REF/IJC_ALT/SJC_ALT) with effective isoform lengths from a merged PAIRADISE count table, and need psi estimation plus an allelic-difference p-value aggregated across individuals.

name: isoform-quantification-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how accurately a long-read isoform detection/quantification tool recovers and quantifies known transcripts from aligned PacBio/ONT reads, using spike-in references like SIRVs as ground truth.

name: isoform-rich-contig-group-selection
description: Use when benchmarking a transcriptome chimera-removal pipeline (e.g. Bellerophon filter orders) and you need a targeted, chimera-rich test set built from isoform-rich contig groups rather than the whole assembly.

name: isoform-structure-comparison-across-tools
description: Use when two long-read isoform callers have been run on the same alignments and you must reconcile their call sets — e.g., quantifying outer-boundary extensions or missing central exons between VIsoQLR and StringTie2 isoform coordinates.

name: isoform-switch-frequency-quantification
description: Use when you need the per-sample prevalence of an isoform switching event in a CanIsoNet disease dataset (PCAWG cancers or the OIH, Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, Behcet's RNA-Seq datasets), e.g. 'what fraction of AD samples switch HSPH1-001 to HSPH1-002?'

name: isoform-switch-interaction-loss-assessment
description: Use when a dMDT or isoform switching event (e.g. transcript ENST00000380405) is identified and you need to determine which high-confidence STRING interactions are lost because the switched isoform lacks domains mediating them.

name: isoform-switching-event-detection
description: Use when transcript-level TPM abundances (e.g. Kallisto-quantified FASTQ from GEO/ENA) must be converted into per-sample dominant-transcript calls and disease-vs-control isoform switching event tables, as done for the 31 CanIsoNet disease types including Alzheimer's GSE203206.

name: isoform-transcript-assignment-to-genome-annotation
description: Use when raw long-read FASTQ reads from barcode-deconvolved ScISOrSeq libraries must be aligned, filtered for full-length spliced poly-exonic reads, and assigned intron/exon chains relative to GENCODE annotation.

name: isolation-forest-anomaly-detection-of-modified-reads
description: Use when you have event-aligned ONT direct RNA reads from paired CTRL and COND samples and need per-read modified/unmodified labels at bona fide modification positions without a pretrained modification-aware basecaller.

name: isolation-forest-anomaly-scoring
description: Use when quantifying the rarity of M-clusters after cluster decomposition/merging in scRNA-seq data, i.e., scoring how anomalous cells are on a cluster's differential genes and calling rare clusters via an independence score.

name: isomir-5p-offset-classification
description: Use when counting small RNA-seq reads where miRNAs must be distinguished from isomiRs by single-nucleotide 5' end shifts — e.g. you have collapsed reads (SAM/FASTA), a GFF3 annotation, and need hierarchical 5'-offset-based assignment.

name: isotonic-dlt-rate-estimation
description: Use when a phase I/II dose-finding analysis needs toxicity probabilities at each dose that satisfy a monotonic order constraint, and when joint toxicity-efficacy probability estimates must be computed in closed form without Bayesian modeling, MCMC, or numerical optimization.

name: isotonic-regression-pava
description: Use when per-dose toxicity (DLT) proportions from a dose-escalation trial violate the order constraint p1 ≤ p2 ≤ ... ≤ pJ and monotonicity-constrained dose-toxicity estimates are needed for dose-escalation/de-escalation decisions.

name: isotonic-regression-probability-calibration
description: Use when per-cell-type binary classifier outputs over a Cell Ontology term set violate the 'is a' hierarchy (child probability exceeds parent), and calibrated probabilities are needed for 10x/TSV/CSV/HDF5 RNA-seq expression matrices.

name: isotonic-toxicity-estimation-pava
description: Use when estimating dose-toxicity (DLT) probabilities in a phase I/II dose-finding design such as TSNP, where isotonic estimates p̂j must satisfy a monotone increasing order constraint before escalation decisions or utility-based OBD selection.

name: isotype-control-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to verify that a cell-intrinsic technical noise estimate for droplet-based protein (ADT) data is robust — e.g. correlating fitted background means µ1 with isotype controls or checking k=2 vs k=3 mixture-model concordance before building the dsb technical component.

name: iterative-cluster-decomposition
description: Use when a scRNA-seq workflow needs to split large initial clusters (>R*n cells, R=0.01 or 30/n for small datasets) into finer sub-clusters to expose rare cell populations that one-time global clustering overlooks.

name: iterative-clustering-lineage-inference
description: Use when you have a quality-controlled, normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix (genes x cells) and want to infer close lineage relationships (1-5 cell divisions) without dedicated lineage-tracing assays, ideally with a barcode dictionary available for validation.

name: iterative-constraint-relaxed-assignment-heuristic
description: Use when associating single-cell RNA-seq expression profiles to single-cell DNA-seq CNA profiles one-to-one and the number of RNA cells exceeds the number of DNA cells, so a single bipartite matching cannot assign every RNA cell.

name: iterative-de-bruijn-graph-transcriptome-assembly
description: Use when bulk barcoded RNA-seq (e.g. SPIso-seq) paired-end FASTQ reads must be assembled into isoform contigs without a reference genome, and contigs are needed for downstream transcript-to-reference assignment.

name: iterative-gene-parameter-fitting
description: Use when estimating single-cell circadian phases unsupervised from scRNA-seq expression (e.g., anndata matrices) and unknown clock-controlled genes must be identified de novo while quantifying phase uncertainty.

name: iterative-go-pathway-covariate-removal
description: Use when a Normalisr co-expression network from UMI scRNA-seq (e.g. dysfunctional CD8+ T cells from MARS-seq GSE123139) is dominated by generic GO programs and you want to regress them out before pathway over-abundance testing.

name: iterative-reliable-cell-selection
description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq (source) with unlabeled scATAC-seq (target) h5ad data and cell heterogeneity means some target cells are easy to bridge while others differ strongly across omics.

name: iterative-subnetwork-module-mining
description: Use when building a fixed blood transcriptome module repertoire from multiple GEO cohort expression datasets: transcripts must be grouped by co-clustering across cohorts and mined from a weighted graph into stable modules and aggregates.

name: ivis-siamese-embedding
description: Use when a high-dimensional dataset (e.g. single-cell expression, CyTOF, or synthetic benchmarks with redundant polynomial features) must be embedded in 2–3 dimensions while preserving global cluster shapes and relative locations, or when t-SNE's spurious clustering is a concern.

name: ivis-triplet-loss-embedding-training
description: Use when a high-dimensional single-cell expression matrix (e.g. melanoma 4,645 x 23,686 from SCP11, hippocampus, retinal bipolar) needs a 2D embedding that preserves both local cell-type clusters and global inter-cluster relationships.

name: jaccard-ari-shifting-distance-computation
description: Use when comparing spatial domain labels against layer annotations on multi-slice ST data (e.g., 12 DLPFC Visium slices) to quantify accuracy via JI, median ARI, and average shifting distance.

name: jaccard-coefficient-cell-level-overlap-quantification
description: Use when evaluating how well an automated tissue-cell segmentation (e.g. MIRIAM, Mesmer, Voronoi) agrees with manual cell-boundary annotations on multiplexed images, at both the individual-cell and 512x512 sub-image level.

name: jaccard-index-cluster-distance-assessment
description: Decision support for judging whether a 2D embedding (e.g. PCA, UMAP, t-SNE of normalized scRNA-seq data) is suitable for trajectory inference, by detecting disconnected cell clusters or homogeneous cells lacking a trajectory signal before fitting a trajectory.

name: jaccard-similarity-analysis-of-regulon-rankings
description: Use when two gene regulatory network inference tools (e.g., MINI-EX and SCENIC) have produced per-cell-type regulons and you need to quantify their overlap per cluster and validate specific regulon TF calls.

name: jaccard-similarity-computation
description: Use when comparing which interactions are shared versus distinct across CCC inference methods, resources, or datasets — e.g., to measure how much top-ranked predictions from CellChat vs NATMI (or CellChatDB vs Ramilowski) overlap.

name: jaccard-similarity-computation
description: Use when quantifying overlap between marker gene sets for the same cell types across multiple marker databases or cell-sorting marker collections to assess database consistency.

name: jaccard-similarity-matrix-construction
description: Use when a pathway enrichment analysis needs inter-pathway dependencies quantified from gene set overlaps — e.g. before fitting pareg with network regularization, or for rendering a pathway network view — and the input is a term-to-gene mapping (df_terms) such as GO BP terms of size 50-500.

name: jaccard-similarity-matrix-construction
description: Use when comparing label vocabularies across published single-cell references (e.g. is HCC 'Lymphoid-B' closer to naive or memory B cells?) or harmonizing subtype annotations from multiple atlases.

name: jaccard-similarity-module-overlap-quantification
description: Use when two PyWGCNA objects (e.g., the 5xFAD and 3xTg-AD networks) have been built with module assignments and you need to find which module pairs significantly overlap, indicating conserved co-expression signatures across datasets.

name: jaccard-similarity-of-top-ranked-regulators
description: Use when comparing activity-inference methods (e.g. the 11 decoupleR methods) on the same omics benchmark to measure whether methods nominate the same top regulators, complementing median Spearman correlation of activity scores.

name: jackknife-based-wald-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq data have been summarized to CTP/ctnu/P inputs and you need per-gene p-values for cell type-specific interindividual variance differentiation that are robust at modest sample sizes.

name: jackknife-model-stability-assessment
description: Use when fitting per-gene PLS1 regression models on multi-omics GRN data (e.g., voom-transformed RNA-seq response against miRNA-seq and TF predictor layers) and you need to separate regulations stable across resampled fits from spurious single-fit associations.

name: jackstraw-pc-significance-testing
description: Use when you must choose how many PCs to retain in a scRNA-seq PCA objectively (jackstraw p-values), or quantify whether imputation/denoising preserved the signal subspace via subspace angles.

name: jensen-shannon-cell-type-distribution-comparison
description: Use when evaluating spatial reconstruction of single-cell data (e.g., CellContrast on SeqFISH mouse gastrulation sections) and you need to score whether reconstructed neighbors reproduce the reference local cell-type composition.

name: jensen-shannon-distance-computation
description: Use when constructing a cell-cell similarity network from ACTIONet multilevel decomposition outputs: cells are represented as convex archetype-mixing weight vectors and a distribution-aware, bounded distance is needed for density-dependent k*-NN edge selection.

name: jensen-shannon-divergence-benchmarking
description: Use when transferring continuous annotations (e.g. 7-dimensional cell fate probabilities) between batches or datasets and you need a distribution-level metric to rank annotation-transfer methods.

name: jensen-shannon-divergence-proportion-evaluation
description: Use when you have deconvolution-predicted cell-type proportions (e.g., from CIBERSORT nu-SVR runs) and known true proportions for pseudo-bulk mixtures, and need a single distributional metric to rank marker sets.

name: jensen-shannon-divergence-similarity-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking whether a cell-similarity measure captures same-type cell similarity more strongly than a baseline such as HVG+PCA Euclidean distance, with permutation-labeled null models on PBMC data.

name: jensen-shannon-neighborhood-divergence-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a spatial reconstruction method for single-cell data: a predicted neighbor structure exists for query cells with known truth locations, and you need a local, neighborhood-composition quality metric beyond raw neighbor hits.

name: jive-joint-individual-variation-decomposition-scrna
description: Use when multi-source or multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices need batch-effect correction with preservation of cell-type signal, or when benchmarking JIVE against Seurat v5, Harmony, LIGER, and ComBat-seq under balanced versus unbalanced batch conditions.

name: jive-multi-source-decomposition
description: Use when you have two or more data matrices (e.g., scRNA-seq batches, or matched gene expression/methylation/miRNA sources like BRCA TCGA data) sharing samples/cells and need to separate shared signal from batch-specific variation.

name: jive-multi-source-rank-selection
description: Use when you have multiple matched data matrices (e.g. BRCA gene expression, methylation, miRNA) and must decide the joint rank and per-source individual ranks before interpreting a JIVE decomposition.

name: joint-density-change-of-variables
description: Use when a pseudotime-ordered single-cell dataset needs marker trajectories expressed on a real time or spatial scale, and a prior cell-density distribution on that true scale is available.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: joint-gene-antibody-clustering
description: Use when a hashed PBMC-style CITE-seq dataset has passed GEX QC and cellranger/CITE-Seq preprocessing, and you need joint gene-plus-antibody clustering, UMAP embeddings per modality, and antibody-positive cell calls.

name: joint-leiden-clustering-across-spatial-slides
description: Use when per-slide clustering of spatial transcriptomics data hides a global migratory/regenerative subpopulation behind local spatial neighborhoods, and you need clusters comparable across multiple APAP-injury slides (GSE223561).

name: joint-reconstruction-loss-implementation
description: Use when reproducing or extending scGAE: a graph autoencoder for scRNA-seq must simultaneously reconstruct the expression count matrix and the KNN cell-graph adjacency matrix in a single multitask loss.

name: joint-toxicity-efficacy-probability-derivation
description: Use when dose-finding trial data contain per-dose bivariate toxicity-efficacy outcome counts (x_jkl) and monotone-constrained joint response probability estimates are needed to feed a utility-based OBD selection.

name: joint-tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you have CoupledNMF H matrices (cnmf.output$H1, cnmf.output$H2) from a paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq run and need a joint embedding plot to check cluster coherence and cross-modality integration.

name: joint-variation-decomposition-integration
description: Use when integrating multi-batch or multi-source scRNA-seq data (e.g., Zilionis mouse lung two-batch data) where you need an unsupervised decomposition separating shared biological signal from batch effects, and when benchmarking against Seurat v5/Harmony.

name: journal-level-error-count-tabulation
description: Use when quantifying the prevalence of Excel date-converted gene symbols across published supplementary files, or benchmarking what fraction of date-related gene name errors a correction tool can resolve per journal.
tools: Mark Ziemann's gene name errors dashboard

name: json-workflow-manifest-parameterization
description: Use when a user needs to run a configurable multi-step alevin-fry single-cell pipeline end-to-end but wants a templated, parameterized workflow manifest rather than hand-composing simpleaf/alevin-fry/piscem commands.

name: jtk-cycle-rhythmicity-detection
description: Use when you have normalized pseudobulk expression matrices across circadian time points per cell type and need to identify genes with significant 24-hour periodicity (JTK_pvalue < 0.05) and compare rhythmic gene sets between cell types.

name: julia-jld2-data-loading
description: Use when the input is a JLD2 (.jld2) file containing labeled/unlabeled/total scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. scEU-seq rpeExampleData) and they must be loaded into Julia for RNAForecaster training or t0 estimation.

name: junction-read-count-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a circRNA isoform quantification method outperforms naive junction-read counting, using simulated loci with two or more splicing isoforms and known theoretical expression values across conditions.

name: junction-read-quality-control
description: Use when building a single-cell AS probability matrix from junction reads (e.g., SCASL/Leafcutter output) and sparse, biased coverage must be filtered prior to KNN imputation and spectral clustering.

name: jupyter-notebook-headless-execution
description: Use when preparing AnnData import files for Cellenium from its example notebooks, or when study notebooks must be executed non-interactively (e.g. inside make targets or CI) to generate .h5ad study data.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a hierarchical cell-annotation classifier must be trained and validated on a labeled scRNA-seq reference (H5 matrix, genes in rows, cells in columns) and per-fold accuracy at major and subtype levels is required.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a sequence classifier on balanced positive/negative RNA 41-nt segments and you need both 5-fold cross-validation metrics and an independent-test comparison of Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and AUC.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a dsRID random-forest model must be evaluated on candidate dsRNA region feature tables (dsRID_data.tsv / dsRID_whole.tsv) and you need per-fold accuracy, AUC, and AUPRC rather than a single train/test split.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-metrics-computation
description: Use when a labeled sequence-derived feature table (e.g., All_Features_Dataset.csv) must be benchmarked with repeated 5-fold cross-validation and a multi-metric performance table (Accuracy/Precision/Sensitivity/Specificity/F1/MCC) is required.

name: k-fold-cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when comparing classifier candidates (SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree, GBDT) or stacking-vs-voting ensembles on balanced RNA modification training data to select the optimal model before independent testing.

name: k-means-baseline-clustering
description: Use when benchmarking a constrained or deep clustering method on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need an unsupervised k-means baseline computed in a marker-gene ZIFA latent space for NMI/CA/ARI comparison.

name: k-means-cell-clustering
description: Use when you need to quantify whether an imputation method (e.g. scISR vs MAGIC, scImpute, SAVER, scScope, scGNN or raw data) improved cell-type clustering of an scRNA-seq dataset with known cell-type labels, measured by ARI.

name: k-means-clustering-of-cell-embeddings
description: Use when cells measured across multiple omics modalities (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT or RNA+ADT+ATAC) must be grouped into cell types, and per-modality clustering quality must be compared against an integrated-multimodality baseline using ARI/NMI.

name: k-means-clustering-of-embedded-representations
description: Use when comparing dimension reduction methods on labeled single-cell RNA-seq datasets and you need reproducible quantitative clustering scores (NMI/ARI) from low-dimensional (e.g., 2D) representations.

name: k-means-clustering-of-pca-latent-space
description: Use when simulated (or real) scRNA-seq count matrices must be partitioned into known discrete cell populations and a simple, reproducible PCA + k-means baseline is needed for benchmarking against scVI, SIMLR, or Seurat Louvain clustering.

name: k-means-clustering-of-scrna-data
description: Use when simulating artificial doublets from quality singlets after an overkill/filter step, and cells must be grouped so sampled pairs come from transcriptionally similar cells to make realistic training doublets.

name: k-means-clustering-with-jump-statistic
description: Use when building a fixed co-expression module repertoire from multiple transcriptome cohorts by clustering each dataset independently (k-means with jump statistic) and tabulating cross-cohort co-clustering of transcripts.

name: k-means-medoid-sample-selection
description: Use when training miRSCAPE on paired bulk miRNA–mRNA matrices spanning thousands of tumor and normal samples and you need a compact, representative training set (k-means medoids) before xgboost model fitting.

name: k-means-pathway-grouping
description: Use when a CellChat object with an inferred communication probability network is available and signaling pathways must be classified into functionally coherent groups, e.g. to reproduce CellChat's four-group pathway classification on the wound skin dataset.

name: k-medoids-clustering-generation
description: Use when building tree-shaped trajectory inference from single-cell data and you need many alternative clusterings (rather than one) to explore topologies, e.g. linear, bifurcating, or multifurcating trajectories in a SingleCellExperiment object.

name: k-medoids-clustering-of-pathway-curves
description: Use when a set of coordinated pathways has per-cell PAL scores along a trajectory (pseudotime) and you want to discover shared stage-activity patterns, e.g. developmental stage-specific pathway modules.

name: k-medoids-clustering-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when building trajectory-inference input for Totem: you have a SingleCellExperiment with a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. 5-dimensional LMDS) and need many candidate clusterings with varying k to construct MSTs and rank clusterings.

name: k-medoids-clustering-with-clara
description: Use when the input is a preprocessed SingleCellExperiment with an embedding and the goal is tree-shaped trajectory inference where clustering quality — not a single clustering — determines the milestone topology.

name: k-medoids-clustering-with-gap-statistic
description: Use when comparing normalization strategies (e.g., dsb vs CLR) on protein-only ADT data via clustering coherence, or when selecting the number of protein-defined clusters in a PBMC CITE-seq matrix.

name: k-mer-compressed-group-feature-generation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data must be classified without aligning reads to a reference genome, or when the reference genome is incomplete or insufficient to represent subject genomes — convert k-mer abundance profiles into CKG features.

name: k-minimal-distance-cluster-pair-tracking
description: Use when implementing hierarchical clustering with an arbitrary linkage function (e.g., KMD linkage), where naive agglomerative recomputation is impractical and you need linear-time linkage updates and k-independent memory.

name: k-scan-silhouette-evaluation
description: Use when clustering with KMDHierarchicalClustering and k is unknown: fit across a k_scan_range, compute KMD silhouette per k, and verify the silhouette is predictive of accuracy/NMI/ARI against ground-truth labels.

name: kallisto-bus-pseudoalignment-to-utrome
description: Use when raw FASTQ/BAM files from 10x Genomics 3'-end tag scRNA-seq libraries must be quantified at 3'UTR isoform resolution against the UTRome annotation rather than the whole transcriptome.

name: kallisto-pseudoalignment-indexing
description: Use when quantifying reads against annotated plus novel transcript fragments without an aligner, deriving signature counts from kallisto equivalence classes, or detecting/quantifying novel splicing events alignment-free.

name: kallisto-pseudoalignment-quantification
description: Use when raw RNA-Seq FASTQ reads (e.g. from GEO/SRA/ENA accessions) must be converted to transcript-level TPM abundances for downstream isoform-based analyses such as CanIsoNet.

name: kallisto-reference-assembly-pseudoalignment
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ samples come from an organism with a published reference assembly and you need gene-level counts to benchmark against reference-free (Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst) quantification, or to produce reference-based count tables for normalization, PCA QC, and limma differential.

name: kallisto-transcriptome-index-construction
description: Use when building a kallisto index for scRNA-seq that must distinguish spliced (cDNA) from intronic (unspliced) reads — e.g., before running scKB to emit spliced and unspliced count matrices for COPILOT or RNA velocity analysis.

name: kalman-smoothing-pseudotime-expression
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from unsynchronized cells needs a denoised, phase-resolved (G1/S/G2/M) expression time-series along a TSP-recovered cell-cycle order, e.g., to surface cycle genes missing from curated bases like Cyclebase.

name: kaplan-meier-cohort-survival-estimation
description: Use when DeepCC subtype labels exist for validation cohorts (TANSBIG, UNT, UPP, NKI) with clinical metadata containing disease-free survival outcomes, and you need to show the classification has prognostic value.

name: kaplan-meier-logrank-testing
description: Use when TCGA bulk tumor samples have RSEM-normalized expression for a gene signature (e.g., the 73 TMGs) plus matched clinical OS/DSS time-status data, and you must test if high vs low signature expression separates survival.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
description: Use when TCGA clinical data (survival time, status) has been merged with a continuous sample-level factor such as GSVA scores, and you need to test whether high vs low factor levels associate with poorer survival probability.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
description: Use when a tumor cell subcluster (e.g., Louvain Cluster 4 from scanpyobj.h5ad) has cluster-specific DEGs and you need to test whether its gene signature stratifies TCGA patient cohorts (e.g., TCGA-LIHC) into high- vs low-survival groups.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
description: Use when a cell-type or gene signature identified in single-cell data must be validated for association with overall survival and radiologic response in independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts with clinical metadata.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
description: Use when a per-sample grouping (subtype label or risk score) must be validated against patient overall survival, requiring KM curves plus a log-rank p-value as the success criterion.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-analysis
description: Use when patient samples have been partitioned into subgroups (e.g., from METAFlux flux-profile clustering of TCGA LUAD/LUSC) and you must test whether group membership predicts time-to-event survival outcomes.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-curve-analysis
description: Use when per-sample viral or HERV presence calls (from viRNAtrap contigs) must be tested for association with TCGA overall survival by Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank tests.

name: kaplan-meier-survival-curve-estimation

name: knn-classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have selected a feature subset from single-cell data (e.g., top p = 50–2000 genes per method) and need a quantitative, label-supervised metric of how well the subset preserves cell types or cell-type transitions.

name: knn-classifier-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a pre-built single-cell reference atlas exists and new query datasets (e.g., pancreas GSE114297, GSE85247, GSE83312) must be cell-type annotated by mapping onto frozen embeddings without retraining the generative model.

name: knn-classifier-cell-type-prediction
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset has been mapped into a Symphony reference embedding with mapQuery and you need cell type labels for query cells without retraining from raw reference data.

name: knn-classifier-evaluation
description: Use when single-cell data has specificity annotation (e.g. pMHC binding labels on a 10x Genomics T cell dataset) and you need to score embedding quality by antigen-specificity prediction.

name: knn-correlation-mapping-quality-assessment
description: Use when a query dataset has been mapped into a reference embedding (e.g., with Symphony mapQuery) and you need a per-cell metric quantifying whether the mapped coordinates reproduce the local neighborhood structure of a de novo integrated gold standard.

name: knn-cross-validated-classification-benchmark
description: Use when you have a low-dimensional cell embedding (e.g., scPhere 'wn' latent coordinates) plus per-cell labels such as embryo collection time, and need a quantitative time-continuity comparison across embedding methods.

name: knn-cross-validation-classification
description: Use when you must benchmark the k-NN (k = 5) DEG-feature classifier's malignant vs non-malignant performance (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, AUROC) within the five cancer scRNA-seq training datasets under 10-fold cross-validation.

name: knn-distance-null-distribution-permutation-testing
description: Use when projected query cells (e.g. PBMC query mapped onto the DISCO PBMC reference via ProjectNewdata) need a statistical per-cell mapping-quality score before downstream label transfer or filtering.

name: knn-ensemble-cell-classification
description: Use when you need to label individual cells in a normalized scRNA-seq matrix (genes as rownames, cells as colnames) as malignant or non-malignant, especially when you have no annotated training cohort of your own, since five pretrained k-NN (k = 5) classifiers are shipped.

name: knn-ensemble-majority-voting
description: Use when classifying cells from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) as cancer vs non-cancer, and per-cell voting frequencies (freq_cancer/freq_non_cancer) are needed for downstream accuracy/sensitivity/AUROC evaluation.

name: knn-ensemble-model-training
description: Use when a normalized single-cell expression matrix must be classified as malignant vs non-malignant using PreCanCell's five-dataset k-NN (k=5) ensemble with majority vote over common DEG features.

name: knn-extrinsic-profile-simulation
description: Use when deconvolving spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Visium spots) with a trained SpatialDDLS model and you want neighbor-aware, spatially regularized cell type proportions for each spot.

name: knn-graph-branch-detection
description: Use when a pseudotime-ordered single-cell trajectory (e.g., DTFLOW pseudotime with root cell indices) must be split into sub-branches at bifurcation points, and existing tools detect only a single bifurcation.

name: knn-graph-clustering-hematopoiesis-scrna-seq
description: Use when you need to test how sensitive an automated terminal-state/fate-detection method (VIA) is to graph parameters (KNN, ncomps) on a small annotated scRNA-seq hematopoiesis dataset, or to recover rare dendritic lineages and validate them by marker gene trends.

name: knn-graph-construction
description: Use when comparing velocity inference methods (e.g., scKINETICS, scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on local smoothness of their velocity fields, or when a kNN neighborhood structure over cells is needed for neighborhood-aggregated metrics.

name: knn-graph-construction-for-million-scale-scrnaseq
description: Use when a scRNA-seq or CyTOF expression matrix exceeds ~100k cells (e.g. 1.3M-cell 10X mouse brain data) and a neighbourhood structure is needed for triplet-based dimensionality reduction where scikit-learn Barnes-Hut t-SNE would not finish within 24 hours.

name: knn-graph-construction-from-cell-embeddings
description: Use when paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data need a cell-state DAG (not just a clustering or trajectory) so that Granger causal locus-gene inference can be run over an acyclic cell ordering.

name: knn-graph-construction-from-cophenetic-distances
description: Use when you have a single-cell lineage tree (e.g., Cassiopeia Newick with cells as leaves) plus expression data and need a cell-neighborhood metric for phylogenetic autocorrelation with Hotspot.

name: knn-graph-construction-from-embeddings
description: Use when you need a subpopulation-aware network over single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., hematopoietic progenitor snapshots) so that trajectory search between any chosen source and target subpopulations, including rare cell types, can be performed.

name: knn-graph-construction-from-pca-embeddings
description: Use when you need a cell-cell similarity graph for label propagation or GNN classification on scRNA-seq data, and cells are represented as PCA-reduced expression embeddings.

name: knn-graph-construction-from-similarity-matrix
description: Use when a precomputed cell-by-cell similarity matrix (e.g., EDGE's averaged weak-learner matrix S) must be converted into a k-NNG before spectral embedding or graph-based dimensionality reduction.

name: knn-graph-construction-on-single-cell-data
description: Use when you have a pre-processed N-cell × D-gene expression matrix and need a cell-to-cell transition probability graph (Markov matrix) as input to random walk or diffusion-based trajectory methods.

name: knn-graph-edge-construction
description: Use when a labeled single-cell or feature matrix must be turned into a graph whose edges capture both same-class proximity and cross-class density-gradient transitions prior to force-based 2D embedding.

name: knn-graph-layout-visualization
description: Use when you need a class-label-agnostic baseline visualization of single-cell expression data that mixes clusters, to contrast with class-informed graph embeddings like GraphDDP.

name: knn-graph-leiden-clustering
description: Use when cell/gene feature embeddings (e.g. from tGPT) must be clustered into groups and quantitatively compared with known cell type annotations using NMI, ARI, and FMI metrics.

name: knn-graph-leiden-clustering-single-cell
description: Use when you have extracted per-cell latent factors from a multi-omics integration model (e.g. scMoMaT extract_cell_factors) and need discrete cluster labels plus a 2D UMAP visualization to interpret populations.

name: knn-graph-post-processing
description: Use when you have extracted cell factors (zs) from a first-stage scMoMaT model and need a KNN graph plus Leiden cluster labels for benchmarking (NMI/ARI/GC) or for second-stage retraining.

name: knn-graph-trajectory-path-finding
description: Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data (with scVelo/velocyto spliced-unspliced velocity) contains multiple or branching trajectories whose direction and topology cannot be resolved by expression-only TI methods.

name: knn-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing imputation methods for highly sparse APA ratio (RUD) matrices from spatially barcoded ST data, e.g. deciding whether stAPAminer's k-nearest-neighbor imputation or scDaPars better recovers APA signals.

name: knn-kernel-construction-from-marker-genes
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset contains unwanted biological variation (e.g., cell cycle, sex) that can be encoded by curated marker gene lists, and you need a cell-cell similarity kernel for SiFT gene-level filtering or covariate scores for regress_out/scVI baselines.

name: knn-kernel-construction-in-harmonized-pca-space
description: Use when filtering a biological signal from scRNA-seq data via reference mapping — i.e., disease cells must be linked to their nearest healthy reference cells before projection-and-subtraction with SiFT.

name: knn-label-propagation-to-full-dataset
description: Use when clusters or labels have been assigned only to a sketched subset of cells (e.g., Sphetcher spherical or geometric sketch) and you need to infer labels for all cells of the original expression/PCA matrix.

name: knn-label-transfer-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing reference mapping methods (e.g. ProjectSVR, Seurat, scArches, Symphony, ProjecTILs) on reference/query pairs where query cells have manually curated labels and you need accuracy/ARI benchmark numbers.

name: knn-label-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when you have uniPort latent embeddings from two heterogeneous single-cell datasets (e.g. scATAC gene activity vs scRNA) and need quantitative ARI+NMI+F1 and Silhouette metrics to judge integration quality, including unbalanced-matching cases where cell types are missing from one modality.

name: knn-label-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when paired TCR+transcriptome query single-cell studies must be annotated by mapping them into a pre-trained mvTCR reference embedding, and accuracy of kNN label transfer for metadata labels (e.g. cancer source, tissue type) must be quantified against a baseline projection.

name: knn-label-transfer-large-dataset
description: Use when the scRNA-seq matrix exceeds scCAN's 5,000-cell training threshold and full network fusion on all cells is impractical, but per-cell cluster assignments are still needed for every cell.

name: knn-label-transfer-to-reference-atlas
description: Use when new query datasets have been integrated onto an annotated reference (e.g., a STACAS seed map) and cell subtype labels must be propagated to unlabeled cells using nearest-neighbor voting in the shared embedding.

name: knn-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a spot-by-poly(A)-site RUD (relative usage difference) matrix derived from spatially barcoded ST data is too sparse for downstream clustering or spatial-pattern tests, and a companion gene-spot count matrix is available to define spot neighborhoods.

name: knn-nearest-neighbor-distance-calculation
description: Use when quantifying how closely inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data matches real-profiled ground truth across representative counts, e.g. benchmarking scSemiProfiler against a selection-only baseline that merely copies each representative's cells.

name: knn-neighbor-graph-construction
description: Use when a velocity or trajectory pipeline needs a cell-neighborhood graph over preprocessed scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. after scvelo pp.filter_and_normalize with top-2000 highly variable genes) to support moment smoothing or local averaging.

name: knn-neighbor-graph-construction-scrna-seq
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix yields a sparse cell-to-cell similarity (e.g., from ADMM-solved sparse subspace representation) whose zero entries must be imputed within K-nearest-neighbor neighborhoods to obtain a dense similarity for spectral clustering.

name: knn-neighbor-voting-label-propagation
description: Use when annotating individual cells directly from marker GEPs (no clustering) and you need to smooth/consolidate per-cell GEP assignments using a precomputed KNN neighbor index.

name: knn-neighborhood-preservation-assessment
description: Use when comparing two embedding configurations (e.g., t-SNE perplexity 100 from scDEED vs 1000 from EMBEDR) by measuring retention of pre-embedding neighbor structure.

name: knn-neighborhood-score-computation
description: Use when comparing embedding methods on a multi-sample single-cell dataset for batch-effect correction versus biological signal retention, e.g. scoring SCING module AUCell embeddings against FastMNN/Harmony/Seurat on snRNA-seq cell annotations.

name: knn-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when validating that a graph-based trajectory-inference result is robust to the KNN hyperparameter on time-labeled single-cell data (e.g., ~90K-cell CyTOF panels with day annotations) by correlating inferred pseudotime against known sampling days across a KNN sweep.

name: knn-protein-abundance-inference
description: Use when a query dataset measures only mRNA (no CITE-seq ADT counts) but you need surface protein levels, and a multimodal CITE-seq reference atlas with a joint mRNA/protein embedding is available.

name: knn-purity-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods (e.g. Monocle, Slingshot, dynverse MST) on simulated continuous single-cell populations where gold-standard branch labels are available and ordering-only metrics are insufficient.

name: knn-state-manifold-graph-construction
description: Use when preparing single-cell RNA-Seq data (e.g. a Seurat object) as an undirected kNN graph input for EVA/ELVAR community detection and DA testing, or when reproducing the paper's lungCD4T or Tabula Muris Senis pipelines.

name: knockdown-perturbation-differential-testing
description: Use when candidate RBPs (e.g., from CRIT NMF clusters) need experimental validation via public shRNA/siRNA knockdown RNA-seq data: detect circRNAs per dataset, compute per-sample mCRI, and run group t tests knockdown vs control.

name: knockout-vs-control-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when contrasting two small RNA-seq conditions (e.g., wild-type control vs ZSWIM8-knockout human cell lines) and the goal is a filtered differential expression table of miRNA/isomiR features, starting from FASTQ reads plus GFF3 miRNA reference annotations.

name: knowledge-base-integration
description: Use when a gene list (e.g., IC genes from the Extracted folder as 'IC_'+str(tumor)+'.csv') must be cross-referenced against DrugBank pharmacologically active targets and PubMed to flag actionable genes and novel candidate biomarkers per cancer type.

name: known-driver-gene-prediction-validation
description: Use when a trained TSG/OG random forest model exists and you need consensus predictions on unlabelled genes, with sanity checks against known Cancer Gene Census driver genes.

name: known-unknown-cell-partitioning
description: Use when bimodality testing (bimodality coefficient and Hartigan's dip test) on target-cell E-scores confirms novel cell types, and cells must be split into known vs. unknown groups without a manually defined empirical threshold.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-cumulative-shift-testing
description: Use when you have a DESeq2 results table plus gene sets (e.g., mer7m8/mer8 seed-match targets vs. background) and need to test for cumulative down-regulation attributed to siRNA seed region activity.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-distribution-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a synthetic-data simulator against real single-cell data by testing whether distributions of per-peak and per-cell summary statistics (mean, variance, CV, zero proportion, library size) deviate from the real matrix.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have DESeq2 differential expression results annotated with seed-match counts (e.g. mer7m8 or mer8 matches, or a curated miRNA-target list) and want to test whether the target gene set shows a cumulative shift in log2FC relative to background.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-goodness-of-fit-testing
description: Use when validating that null P-value distributions from a statistical association method are uniform (unbiased), e.g. stratifying gene pairs into expression-level bins and testing each bin's P-value histogram against Uniform[0,1].

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-null-uniformity-testing
description: Use when validating that a DE method (e.g. Normalisr linear models) produces uniformly distributed null P values across gene expression levels, using replicate null groupings such as gRNA-free cells split randomly.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-pseudotime-distribution-comparison
description: Use when a common trajectory (e.g. slingshot lineages with slingPseudotime) has been inferred across multiple experimental conditions and you need to test whether pseudotime distributions differ between conditions per lineage or globally.

name: kolmogorov-smirnov-two-sample-testing
description: Use when comparing scHi-C contact counts per bin pair between exactly two cell groups (e.g. oocyte vs zygote), as a non-negative count.table matrix with a group factor, and no distributional assumption on counts is desired.

name: krnn-nearest-neighbor-retention-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating scRNA-seq integration quality beyond batch mixing: you have matched pre- and post-integration log-count matrices and need to quantify how many of each cell's original top-k neighbors survive correction.

name: kruskal-wallis-hypothesis-testing-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq gene expression matrix plus non-parametric cluster labels (e.g., from SSRE clustering) and need to detect differentially expressed genes across those clusters without assuming normality.

name: kshv-microrna-target-hybrid-identification
description: Use when analyzing hyb-format chimeric RNA data from a miRNA/target ligation experiment (e.g., qCLASH) to isolate hybrids containing a specific miRNA such as kshv-miR-k12-5 and enumerate its experimentally observed targets.

name: kta-ari-correlation-analysis
