description: Use when you need to check that KTA-based unsupervised selection of the transfer mixture parameter theta coincides with the theta maximizing supervised ARI in simulated scRNA-Seq transfer learning experiments.

name: kullback-leibler-divergence-annotation
description: Use when annotating log-normalized single-cell RNA-seq profiles against a labeled reference and you need a fast, portable multinomial MLE classifier (top-k entropy-selected genes, KL-divergence decision rule).

name: kullback-leibler-divergence-deg-detection
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells) plus a multidimensional cell embedding (PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, pseudotime, or 2D spatial coordinates) and need DEGs without defining cell clusters beforehand.

name: kullback-leibler-divergence-scoring
description: Use when predicting DEGs from single-cell data without clustering cells, by scoring each gene's detection pattern against cell positions in a multidimensional space (t-SNE, PCA, pseudotime, or spatial coordinates) with Kullback–Leibler divergence.

name: l1-loss-regression-optimization
description: Use when training a cTP-net MB-DNN to map a LogNormalize-normalized, SAVER-X-denoised scRNA-seq matrix to relative-abundance-transformed surface protein counts and a per-protein regression loss must be selected.

name: l1-regularized-linear-svm-training
description: Use when you need to validate single-cell-derived pathway modules as biomarkers: a small set of high-weight pathways must be converted into predictive features on independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts with binary disease labels.

name: l2-cell-vector-normalization
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq count matrices (CSV, JLD2, or 10x mtx.gz) where log normalization may introduce TGC-bias-driven artificial signals — e.g., detected eigenvalue counts unexpectedly high after log normalization on biased or synthetic data.

name: l2-regularized-neural-network-training
description: Use when you need to train a neural autoencoder on preprocessed (log2(x+1), variance=1, mean=1) single-cell expression data to infer circular/periodic pseudo-time, and MSE+L2 regularization is the fitting objective.

name: label-aware-compressive-classification-configuration
description: Use when you have a cells x genes scRNA-seq expression matrix plus cell-type labels (e.g., 40 classes) and need to select a specific number of markers (e.g., 50) that jointly discriminate the labels, including on large synthetic panels (10,000 genes).

name: label-based-dynamic-programming-path-extension
description: Use when transcript-representing paths must be recovered from a labeled splice graph whose junction edges are annotated by which aligners captured them (1, 2+, 2-), e.g., after integrating Hisat2 and Star BAM alignments.

name: label-corruption-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when you need to validate or reproduce the entropy-based confidence criterion for self-training by simulating annotation mistakes: perturbing known ground-truth labels and testing whether predictive entropy separates corrupted from correct cells.

name: label-guided-single-cell-imputation
description: Use when an scRNA-seq count matrix has pervasive dropouts and cell-type labels are available, and the goal is to improve downstream DE analysis concordance against a bulk RNA-seq reference.

name: label-propagation-cell-clustering
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq cells must be clustered from dual low-dimensional cell-landmark representations (binary Q1 from LC1 and quantitative Q2 from LC2) with an unknown number of cell types.

name: label-similarity-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation methods (e.g., Census vs scType) on datasets with harmonized ground-truth labels and you need a per-dataset label-similarity score that captures partial agreement between label vocabularies, not just exact-match accuracy.

name: label-transfer-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell diagonal integration methods (scConfluence, Seurat, rliger, MultiMAP, Uniport, scGLUE) on unpaired modalities and you need a label-based accuracy score for cell-type agreement in the joint embedding, especially under unbalanced population scenarios.

name: label-transfer-across-scrna-seq-methods
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq methods must be compared head-to-head for cell-type annotation and integration, using standardized metrics and paired statistical tests across datasets.

name: label-transfer-agreement-visualization
description: Use when comparing label transfer from a large reference (e.g. the 428k-cell human Gut scRNA-seq dataset) to a query (e.g. immune T-cell populations) across multiple subsampling methods, and you need a per-cell-type agreement dot plot against the full-reference baseline.

name: label-transfer-method-comparison
description: Use when evaluating which supervised cell-type annotation method (SciBet, Seurat v3, scmap) transfers labels across scRNA-seq datasets generated by distinct sequencing technologies.

name: labeled-cell-type-guided-imputation
description: Use when the scRNA-seq count matrix comes with trusted cell type labels (e.g., a published dataset like GSE118068 with annotations) and you want group-wise dropout imputation instead of unsupervised spectral clustering.

name: labeled-splice-graph-transcript-assembly
description: Use when RNA-seq reads are spliced-aligned to a reference genome with more than one aligner (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) and a full-length transcript assembly (GTF) is needed that recovers transcripts missed by single-aligner assemblers like StringTie2 or Scallop.

name: lag-1-autocorrelation-computation-along-pseudotime
description: Use when comparing pseudotime orderings produced by multiple trajectory-inference algorithms on the same scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., GSE72857 myeloid progenitors or Splatter simulations) and you need a quantitative smoothness score per algorithm.

name: lancaster-p-value-combination
description: Use when building reference cell-type markers from multiple DE tests and you need a significance-driven consensus (p-value combination) rather than rank-only aggregation of top-N markers.

name: landmark-based-approximation
description: Use when the scRNA-seq dataset has many cells so that solving the optimal transport problem (Eq. 2) for every cell pair over all m spatial positions is computationally intractable, and an approximate n x n spatial distance matrix is acceptable.

name: landmark-gene-expression-annotation
description: Use when an LDA (or HSS-LDA) embedding orders cells along a known biological axis (e.g., villus zone labels) and you must validate or interpret the axis using marker genes with distinct spatial or temporal expression patterns.

name: landmark-set-reproducibility-assessment
description: Use when an Mpath trajectory analysis on single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. mouse DC progenitors) needs its landmark clusters and branching topology checked for robustness to clustering/cut parameters before downstream interpretation.

name: landscent-signal-rank-computation
description: Use when scRNA-seq count/normalized expression matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns) need per-cell stemness/pluripotency ranking, e.g. to select stem/progenitor origins for trajectory inference or to benchmark against ORIGINS activity scores.

name: laplace-smoothing-parameter-estimation
description: Use when training a multinomial cell-type classifier on single-cell expression data and zero mean expression for some genes would otherwise yield zero likelihood; i.e., building a SciBet Learn model from log-normalized counts.

name: laplacian-score-feature-ranking
description: Use when a preprocessed single-cell dataset (e.g. .h5ad from scRNA-seq or 4i imaging) already has dynamic seed features and you need to rank all features by trajectory smoothness before trajectory inference.

name: large-dataset-subsampled-clustering
description: Use when a clustering task involves very large datasets (e.g. 100k-1M cells/objects, such as mass cytometry or scRNA-seq) where full-dataset KMD clustering is computationally infeasible, and the number of populations is known.

name: large-point-cloud-selection-scaling
description: Use when building interactive selection over dense 3D/2D scatter plots of single-cell DR coordinates (>30k points) where per-cell colliders would be too slow and freehand per-cell capture is required.

name: large-scale-cell-distance-matrix-computation
description: Use when sketching or sampling cells from an expression matrix with >1 million cells (rows = cells, columns = genes/PCs) and you need cell-cell distances or a timing comparison of the distance-computation stage.

name: large-scale-count-matrix-io-optimization
description: Use when benchmarking inference time or memory of scRNA-seq annotation tools on matrices ranging from 100 to 1,000,000 cells, and you need to isolate file-parsing overhead from model runtime.

name: large-scale-dataset-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method's runtime and memory footprint across dataset sizes (e.g., 10k → 100k → 1M cells) on a single large source dataset.

name: large-scale-dataset-scalability-testing
description: Use when benchmarking whether a method (e.g. a VAE-based network inferencer like FAVA vs. scLink, hdWGCNA, PCC) can process a very large scRNA-seq or proteomics matrix without failure, and where competitor methods break down.

name: large-scale-expression-matrix-subsampling
description: Use when you need to derive augmentation vectors from a very large cross-tissue scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. the 22.2M-cell CELLxGENE corpus) and full-data centroid computation is infeasible, so a donor/cell-type-annotated subsample is required.

name: large-scale-rna-seq-dataset-indexing
description: Use when indexing very large collections (thousands to ~32,000+) of RNA-seq or other sequence datasets where Bloom-filter-based AMQ tools hit construction-time or memory barriers, and the index must grow incrementally as batches of samples arrive.

name: large-scale-scrna-database-benchmarking
description: Use when reproducing or extending runtime comparisons between AnnSQL (in-process DuckDB) and AnnData backed-mode filtering on datasets larger than memory, such as the 4.4 million cell Macosko Mouse Atlas Single Nuclei h5ad.

name: large-scale-scrna-trajectory-inference
description: Use when analyzing a million-scale single-cell transcriptomic atlas (e.g., 1.3M cells stored as PCs in adata.obsm['X_pca']) and you need trajectory inference, automated terminal-state detection, and runtime comparison against PAGA/Palantir/STREAM/Monocle3 without losing global connectivity.

name: large-scale-scrnaseq-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether Python-based annotation pipelines (CellTypist, devCellPy, SingleCellNet, scBalance, ACTINN, CellPLM, scvi, scaLR) can process datasets with >0.6 million cells under a stated memory limit, or when reproducing cross-cohort benchmark tables.

name: large-scale-scrnaseq-clustering
description: Use when an scRNA-seq expression matrix exceeds the memory/runtime limits of standard deep-learning clustering (tens of thousands to >1 million cells, e.g., mouse brain 1,306,127 cells) and graph-neural-network competitors crash or exceed a 24-hour budget.

name: large-scale-scrnaseq-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when a clustering method for scRNA-seq count matrices must be benchmarked against competitors on datasets with ground-truth cell-type labels, or when robustness on downsampled large-scale data must be quantified with ARI/NMI and significance tests.

name: large-scale-scrnaseq-data-processing
description: Use when a single-cell dataset is too large for data-dependent sampling methods (e.g., millions of cells) and you need a fast preprocessing sketch whose representativeness can be compared to geometric sketching via Hausdorff distance.

name: large-scale-scrnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multi-batch scRNA-seq datasets (thousands to tens of thousands of cells) must be normalized, log-transformed, scaled, and filtered to highly variable genes before deep-learning clustering such as DESC.

name: large-scale-single-cell-backed-mode-data-loading
description: Use when an .h5ad single-cell dataset exceeds available memory (millions of cells) and must be opened with scanpy's backed mode before building an AnnSQL .asql database for SQL-based analysis.

name: large-scale-single-cell-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when profiling runtime and memory of AnnSQL preprocessing procedures on a large single-cell atlas (e.g. 4.4 million cell h5ad) and comparing against AnnData/Seurat equivalents that may fail on the same hardware.

name: large-scrnaseq-dataset-handling
description: Use when input is a large single-cell expression matrix (e.g. 1,000 to ~68,000 cells, such as the 68k PBMC dataset) and the goal is rare cell detection under tight runtime/memory budgets, or a scaling benchmark of time and peak RAM across rare-cell tools.

name: largest-remainder-integer-allocation
description: Use when fractional allocations (e.g. per-cell-type sketch sizes from value-weighted proportions) must be rounded to integer counts while guaranteeing the total equals a fixed budget S.

name: lasso-cox-regression-feature-selection
description: Use when building an IMGP-based prognostic model and you need to test whether cell-cell-interaction-enriched gene pairs are preferentially retained by LASSO Cox regression compared with pairs chosen only for prognostic p-value significance.

name: lasso-cox-survival-regression-fitting
description: Use when regressing a survival outcome (survival time plus censoring indicator) on high-dimensional molecular covariates (e.g. TCGA gene-level features far outnumbering patients) and a sparsity-inducing penalty is needed for variable selection.

name: lasso-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when a gene community or candidate gene set (e.g. IC genes from Gephi community extraction) must be reduced to a sparse, discriminative signature prior to supervised classification on expression data.

name: lasso-logistic-regression-fitting
description: Use when fitting lasso or elastic-net logistic regression to binary outcome data with predictors far outnumbering samples (P ≫ n, e.g. 150 samples × 20,000 predictors), and hyperparameter tuning must be nested within CV to avoid leakage.

name: lasso-multinomial-logistic-regression-training
description: Use when building a single-cell state classifier from gene-signature enrichment scores: cells are scored against several pairwise DEG signatures (e.g. via AUCell) and must be assigned to one of 3+ annotated states.

name: lasso-penalized-cox-model-building
description: Use when deriving a prognostic risk score from bulk tumor transcriptomes: fit LASSO (glmnet alpha=1) Cox regression on Cox-preselected marker gene pairs (e.g., top 21 CD8-Tem IMGPs) and validate across independent survival cohorts.

name: lasso-regression-velocity-prediction
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with scVelo-computed velocities and want to test whether per-gene velocity is recoverable as a linear combination of TF expression levels (ENCODE/ChEA candidates).

name: lasso-regularized-linear-regression
description: Use when you have coupled single-cell SNV (or VCF-derived) and gene expression matrices and need sparse SNV-to-expression models, feature selection, and eeSNV/gene rankings for subpopulation or genotype-phenotype analysis.

name: latent-dimension-filtering-gene-extraction
description: Use when you have trained scMGCA (two GCN layers, 128-dim latent space) on a scRNA-seq dataset and need a biological interpretation of the compressed transcription space via gene ranking and enrichment.

name: latent-dimension-hyperparameter-selection
description: Use when benchmarking or deploying paired single-cell multi-omics integration methods and a defensible number of latent dimensions must be chosen before comparing methods on silhouette score, ARI, and kNN purity.

name: latent-dimension-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when a VASC (or similar deep variational autoencoder) latent representation must be validated for robustness: you have labeled scRNA-seq data (e.g., Pollen), need to pick a latent dimension, and must show NMI/ARI stability across sampling fractions and read depths.

name: latent-dimension-traversal-pseudocell-generation
description: Use when a trained scMM model's latent space needs biological interpretation: to link individual latent dimensions to gene expression programs, surface protein levels, or chromatin accessibility motifs from CITE-seq/Atlas-seq multimodal single-cell data.

name: latent-dimensionality-sweep-analysis
description: Use when you have denoised single-cell expression matrices plus known phenotype labels and need to compare methods by cluster resolution, sweeping latent-space dimensions and reporting mean silhouette scores per method and dimension.

name: latent-dirichlet-allocation-inference
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes) and want to decompose it into interpretable latent biological function topics via a penalized LDA topic model in R.

name: latent-dirichlet-allocation-topic-modeling
description: Use when ST pixels are multi-cellular (e.g. Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) and no suitable scRNA-seq reference exists, or cell-type proportions and marker-enriched transcriptional profiles must be inferred in an unsupervised manner.

name: latent-embedding-connectivity-assessment
description: Use when you have a shared low-dimensional embedding from unpaired multiomic integration (e.g. scConfluence latents in mdata.obsm['latent']) and must quantify alignment quality or hyperparameter sensitivity (e.g. unbalanced-OT m) using purity, FOSCTTM, and graph connectivity.

name: latent-embedding-decoding-for-scrna-seq
description: Use when decoding a latent cell embedding back to gene space for scRNA-seq count data where dropout-heavy zeros must be accounted for by explicit Bernoulli dropout probabilities instead of ZINB modeling.

name: latent-embedding-extraction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices must be compressed into a low-dimensional feature representation for downstream clustering, explicitly modeling zero inflation via a ZINB likelihood.

name: latent-embedding-extraction-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when you have log1p-normalized, multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., pancreas: 16382 cells, 14 cell types, 9 batches; 2000 highly variable genes with batch labels) and need harmonized latent embeddings plus corrected outputs in original gene space.

name: latent-embedding-tsne-visualization
description: Use when you have per-cell latent feature vectors (e.g. 64-dim Miscell/MoCo embeddings) and need a 2D t-SNE visualization plus clustering assignments for a large scRNA-seq dataset such as the 43,095-cell 10x PBMC data.

name: latent-factor-inference-via-partial-least-squares
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data contain suspected unmeasured technical or cell-cycle confounders and a set of control genes is available; goal is confounder estimation and corrected expression for downstream clustering.

name: latent-factor-misspecification-analysis
description: Use when assessing how sensitive a ZINB-WaVE fit is to choosing the wrong number of latent factors K or omitting the gene-level intercept in V, e.g. before trusting low-dimensional outputs from scRNA-seq counts.

name: latent-factor-removal-from-expression-matrices
description: Use when a normalized log-transformed scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows within-cell-type heterogeneity suspected to arise from cell-cycle effects, and a known cell-cycle gene annotation set is available to guide removal before clustering.

name: latent-factor-removal-sclvm
description: Reference for removing dominant latent factors (e.g. cell cycle) from log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrices via scLVM's Python script, choosing K = 1 or the scree-plot value, and comparing corrected vs. original data.

name: latent-factor-sweep-benchmarking
description: Use when a multi-sample single-cell integration method must be shown competitive against alternatives (Seurat, Harmony, LIGER, scVI, Scanorama, BBKNN, CSS) across datasets while sweeping the number of latent factors K.

name: latent-ode-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a spliced/unspliced AnnData (h5ad) needs directional developmental trajectories or latent-time ordering, especially with multiple lineages, time-dependent rates, or batch effects that break linear RNA velocity.

name: latent-regulatory-state-analysis
description: Use when a LatentVelo model with zr_dim > 0 has been trained on spliced/unspliced AnnData and you need to test whether the latent regulatory state predicts divergent cell fates or lineage outcomes.

name: latent-regulatory-state-structured-dynamics
description: Use when building an RNA velocity model that must capture lineage-dependent or time-dependent kinetics on single-cell spliced/unspliced data, e.g. bifurcating developmental systems where steady-state or linear dynamical models fail.

name: latent-space-coordinate-export
description: Use when a fitted TCM model (e.g. mf <- tcm(X, time.table)) must be archived as a per-cell 2D coordinate table and a reproducible scatter plot colored by cell metadata such as source.name or developmental stage.

name: latent-space-correlation-network-inference
description: Use when the input is a high-dimensional, sparse and redundant omics matrix (e.g. scRNA-seq cell-by-gene counts such as GSE75748, or Human Protein Atlas / PRIDE proteomics) and the goal is a ranked protein-protein association network rather than raw co-expression links.

name: latent-space-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when a multi-batch single-cell dataset has been integrated with a disentangling model (e.g., CODAL) and you need to judge whether the new latent space corrects technical batch effects while preserving or improving biological cell-type separation, relative to a baseline latent space.

name: latent-space-mixing-quality-assessment
description: Use when evaluating scConfluence integration output — after model.fit() on a MuData object — to decide whether cell embeddings in mdata.obsm['latent'] are acceptably aligned across modalities (e.g. scRNA vs scATAC) before downstream clustering or imputation.

name: latent-space-quality-assessment
description: Use when a scRNA-seq study produces multiple low-dimensional embeddings (e.g., scMGCA graph-autoencoder latents vs PCA/t-SNE/UMAP) and you must quantify which embedding preserves cell-type structure.

name: latent-space-structural-validation
description: Use when a fitted TCM model (from tcm(X, time.table)) must be verified against a simulated or real temporal scRNA-seq dataset before exporting or interpreting its 2D latent space and prototype layout.

name: latent-space-vector-arithmetic-site-comparison
description: Use when comparing the same cell type across two sample sites or conditions in scRNA-seq AnnData objects and you need site-/condition-specific gene signatures, such as EMT gain and MHC class I loss in metastasis.

name: latent-time-estimation
description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData (scVelo-preprocessed) yields reversed or distorted trajectory directions from scVelo's stochastic/dynamical modes, and a unified latent time is needed to correct directionality.

name: latent-time-grid-search-assignment
description: Use when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics models (RNA velocity from TF expression) and you need per-cell latent times that must be re-assigned as TF weights and dynamics parameters (alpha, beta, theta, gamma) are updated each EM iteration.

name: latent-time-inference-verification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced mRNA counts (AnnData/.h5ad) must be assigned a directed trajectory and latent time without metabolic-labeling priors, and the velocity fit needs per-gene R2 verification.

name: latent-variable-map-estimation
description: Use when bulk HiChIP enhancer-promoter loop counts must be deconvolved into subpopulation-specific profiles and a model-based alternative to DC3's simple plug-in method is desired, with single-cell RNA/ATAC profiles available as known inputs.

name: latent-variable-model-optimization
description: Use when fitting a generative latent embedding (GEDI) to raw single-cell counts (dgCMatrix) with optional prior knowledge matrix, needing explicit K, mode, oi_shrinkage, randomSeed and iteration settings plus convergence checks.

name: latent-velocity-space-visualization
description: Use when a trained LatentVelo model (VAE or AnnotVAE) needs its latent-space velocities and latent time visualized to verify differentiation trajectories, branching structure, or batch-disentangled dynamics.

name: law-of-mass-action-signaling-model-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or validating CellChat's computeCommunProb step: you have clustered scRNA-seq data, a ligand-receptor-cofactor database (CellChatDB), and need communication probabilities plus p-values between cell groups.

name: layer-specific-apa-marker-detection
description: Use when you have a layer-annotated stAPAminer object built from an imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix and need to detect DEAPA, LSAPA, and SVAPA gene sets, e.g. for ST-MOB replicates or merging into stAPA sets.

name: layer-wise-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have a Seurat-clustered stAPAminer object (MOB spots labeled into layers like GCL, GL, ONL, OPL, MCL) and need a per-layer correlation score to verify imputation quality or benchmark two imputed RUD matrices.

name: lbfgs-dual-variable-optimization
description: Use when implementing or reproducing Mowgli's alternating minimization: nonnegative factors H(p) and shared embedding W must satisfy simplex constraints while minimizing the entropic OT-regularized objective (Eqs. 5-11).

name: ld-clumping-of-eqtl-summary-statistics
description: Use when OTTERS Stage I input preparation is needed: eQTL summary statistics (CHROM, POS, A1, A2, Zscore, TargetID, N) plus a gene annotation file must be cis-window restricted and LD-clumped at r2=0.99 before P+T/lassosum/SDPR/PRS-CS weight training.

name: ld-clumping-pvalue-thresholding
description: Use when eQTL summary statistics (e.g., eQTLGen, n=31,684) must be converted into per-gene expression imputation weights via P+T with LD clumping, and valid-model counts (test R2 > 0.01) compared across PRS-based trainers.

name: ld-computation-from-haplotype-data
description: Use when a set of significant SNPs (e.g., PAIRADISE ASAS events at FDR <= 10%) must be tested for enrichment of linkage disequilibrium with GWAS-catalog trait/disease SNPs against a random-control null.

name: lda-class-separation-scoring
description: Use when fitting LDA on single-cell data with known a priori labels (e.g., day0–day5 CyTOF markers) and you need to score candidate feature subsets to pick the subset with the class separation.

name: lda-model-fitting
description: Use when you have a cells-by-markers dataframe (e.g., CyTOF Morphometry, T cell metabolic regulome, or Chromotyping data) with an a priori class-label vector (cell type, cell-cycle phase, time point) and want supervised dimensionality reduction onto LD axes.

name: lda-topic-model-deconvolution-of-spatial-transcriptomics
description: Use when input is a pixel-by-gene count matrix from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data (e.g., 10X Visium, DBiT-seq, MERFISH-derived pixels) and cell-type proportions/profiles are needed but no suitable scRNA-seq reference exists.

name: lda-topic-model-fitting
description: Use when a pixel-by-gene spatial transcriptomics matrix (e.g. Spatial Transcriptomics, 10X Visium, DBiT-seq) must be deconvolved into cell-type proportions without a single-cell reference, after overdispersed-gene feature selection.

name: lda-topic-modeling-of-st-pixels
description: Use when the input is a pixel-by-gene count matrix from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST (e.g., ST, 10X Visium, DBiT-seq, MERFISH) and cell-type proportions/profiles are needed without a matched scRNA-seq reference.

name: lda-topic-modeling-on-single-cell-clusters
description: Use when single-cell clusters contain unannotated populations with unknown marker genes and you need functional annotation from GO enrichment signatures plus topic-model-based similarity, especially for plant scRNA-seq.

name: leakage-free-cross-validation-fitting
description: Use when a pipeline includes data-driven steps such as feature ranking, selection, or scaling that must be re-fit inside every CV fold to avoid information leaking from held-out data into the model.

name: learning-curve-convergence-analysis
description: Decision support for whether a knowledge-informed model component (e.g. pathway/TF masks) actually drives performance, by benchmarking it against parameter-matched random alternatives via learning-curve comparison.

name: learning-rate-sensitivity-analysis-of-embeddings
description: Use when reproducing or extending the SnapCCESS hyperparameter sensitivity diagnostics — specifically when testing how the initial learning rate of the variational-autoencoder embedding step affects clustering performance on a multimodal single-cell omics dataset such as Swanson TEA-seq (GSE158013).

name: leave-half-samples-out-cross-validation
description: Use when you must quantify how accurately a reference-mapping method (ProjecTILs, Azimuth/Seurat 4, scmap) projects and classifies held-out scRNA-seq samples onto a reference atlas, by a sample-level split so no query cell was seen during reference construction.

name: leave-one-dataset-out-cross-validation
description: Use when assessing whether a cell type replicates across two or more scRNA-seq datasets: you have labeled cells per dataset, a gene set (e.g. GOmouse), and need an AUROC that reflects cross-dataset identity recovery rather than within-study clustering.

name: leave-one-dataset-out-cross-validation
description: Use when comparing cell-type annotation methods on multiple reference datasets and you need an unbiased estimate of generalization to an entirely unseen dataset, using accuracy and MacroF1 per tissue.

name: leave-one-out-cell-type-generalization-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a trained single-cell classifier (SIMS/TabNet checkpoint) can distinguish seen from unseen cell types, or when calibrating per-cell probabilities and flagging low-confidence cells as 'unknown' before label transfer.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation
description: Use when comparing cancer-vs-normal classification accuracy of alternative gene sets (e.g., Wx-14 vs Peng-14 UGCBs) on a small-to-moderate TCGA expression matrix, where every sample must serve as a validation case to estimate generalization performance.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation
description: Use when you must rigorously quantify tauFisher prediction accuracy on a small labeled time-series (e.g., GSE83855 time-restricted feeding schedules ZT5-ZT9 and ZT0-ZT4) without a separate test set.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation
description: Use when comparing cell-composition estimation methods (Bisque, CIBERSORT, BSEQ-sc, MuSiC, CIBERSORTx) on a cohort where a subset of individuals has both bulk RNA-seq and single-nucleus/single-cell data, to get global R and RMSD.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when you have a spatial dataset measuring a small panel of genes (e.g. bdtnp.txt in situ values at 3039 Drosophila embryo positions) and a matched scRNA-seq matrix, and you need to quantify how accurately an optimal-transport mapping reconstructs spatial expression of held-out genes.

name: leave-one-out-cross-validation-of-spatial-gene-expression
description: Use when scRNA-seq data are being mapped onto a spatial reference map of a small number of measured genes (e.g. 64-position in situ hybridization maps) and an unbiased estimate of spatial gene-expression reconstruction quality is needed.

name: leave-one-out-entropy-perturbation-ranking
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq snapshot contains a multipotent population (e.g. MPPs) with competing downstream lineages, candidate priming RFs have already been filtered (type-1, low MPP-expression frequency), and you must prioritize which RFs and RF pairs define the primed state.

name: leave-one-out-marker-gene-validation
description: Use when an image-based ST panel omits genes that are measured in a reference or validation set, and you need to quantify imputation accuracy (MAE) against measured expression for held-out marker genes.

name: leave-one-out-marker-subset-cross-validation
description: Use when a MAPiT (or other measure-preserving pseudotime) reconstruction must be shown to be robust to the choice of markers fed into the pseudotime algorithm — e.g. spheroid flow cytometry data with multiple stains where input-marker bias is a concern.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: leave-one-out-model-validation
description: Use when validating a PROGENy model built from the 11-pathway perturbation compendium (208 ArrayExpress submissions, 580 experiments): you need evidence that pathway scores recover the perturbed pathway for experiments not seen during model construction.

name: leave-one-out-network-differencing
description: Use when benchmarking cell-specific network inference methods (e.g. LIONESS, SSN) against known per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks generated by dyngen, using AUROC/AUPR.

name: leave-one-out-pc1-variance-outlier-scoring
description: Use when computing PC1-based gene set activity scores (e.g. rROMA on MSigDB Hallmark sets) and genes within a set distort the one-dimensional variance, so aberrant genes must be excluded before scoring.

name: leave-one-out-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when you have scRNA-Seq data with a multipotent (MPP/TAC) population and competing downstream lineages, and you need to rank which regulatory factors and RF pairs drive priming of one lineage over another.

name: leave-one-out-resampling-robustness-analysis
description: Use when a learned representation (e.g., MetaTiME MeCs trained on multi-cohort single-cell data) must be shown to be robust to the removal of any single training cohort before it is reused for annotation.

name: leave-one-species-out-model-validation
description: Use when evaluating whether a gene-cluster-based lifestyle classifier generalizes to a species entirely absent from training, e.g. potential novel species with no representative genomes in databases.

name: leave-study-out-cross-validation
description: Use when evaluating whether hierarchical cell-type classification probabilities are logically consistent with the Cell Ontology DAG, by reproducing inconsistency rates under study-level held-out validation.

name: leiden-cluster-label-processing
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be converted to log-cpm normalised AnnData with tentative Leiden cluster labels as the required input format for Cytocipher code-scoring and cluster merging.

name: leiden-clustering-of-aligned-single-cell-embeddings
description: Use when you have embeddings from single-cell manifold-alignment methods on datasets with known cell-type labels (e.g. Full PBMC RNA/ATAC, BM RNA/ADT) and need to quantify unsupervised structure recovery via ARI.

name: leiden-clustering-of-cell-embeddings
description: Use when you have precomputed cell-level embeddings plus per-cell specificity/clonotype annotations and need to quantify how compactly and purely the embedding groups cells by specificity, or when comparing embedding variants on a common clustering metric.

name: leiden-clustering-of-low-dimensional-embeddings
description: Use when you have a low-dimensional cell embedding (e.g., a Mowgli, integrative NMF, or MOFA+ latent space) and need cell clusters to quantify embedding and clustering performance.

name: leiden-clustering-of-novel-cells
description: Use when scNovel's query stage has flagged cells as novel (score > threshold λ = 0.5) and the flagged novel cells must be grouped into clusters for subtype identification via markers such as CD163.

name: leiden-clustering-resolution-sweep
description: Use when comparing single-cell integration or batch-correction methods (e.g., scCobra vs. Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) and you need resolution-robust ARI/NMI/ASW metrics on each method's embedding.

name: leiden-clustering-resolution-sweep
description: Use when you have QC-filtered multimodal single-cell data (RNA, ATAC, ADT/CITE-Seq) and need per-modality Leiden annotations at multiple resolutions as players for downstream decision-level integration (scTriangulate) or ensemble clustering.

name: leiden-community-detection-clustering
description: Use when cells have already been embedded via a kernel-induced affinity graph (e.g., the symmetrized q-diffused kernel matrix) and you need unsupervised cluster assignments scored against ground-truth annotations or stimulation labels.

name: leiden-graph-clustering
description: Use when a learned joint cell embedding (e.g. scMoMaT cell factors zs) needs to be converted into a neighborhood graph, Leiden clusters, and a 2D UMAP visualization in a mosaic single-cell multi-omics pipeline.

name: leiden-graph-clustering-scrna
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq cell-by-gene matrix in AnnData format) must be partitioned into cell clusters after dimensionality reduction, e.g. to reproduce Cellar's reported cluster counts.

name: leiden-graph-community-clustering-on-topic-embeddings
description: Use when clustering cells from single-cell epigenomics data such as SNARE-seq or scATAC-seq that has been reduced to a topic embedding (e.g., cisTopic topics), and cluster labels must be propagated to paired single-cell transcriptomic modality via shared cell barcodes.

name: leiden-graph-community-detection
description: Use when clustering single-cell protein or RNA data (AnnData object) into communities via a neighbors graph, especially when projecting clusters onto spatial images (e.g., 46,840-cell lymph node CODEX data).

name: leiden-high-resolution-over-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData is log-cpm normalized with a neighborhood graph and you need tentative fine-grained Leiden labels that over-cluster cells, as the required starting point for Cytocipher cluster-merge testing.

name: leiden-multiresolution-clustering
description: Use when you need multiple candidate cluster label sets for scTriangulate integration — no prior annotations exist and one single Leiden resolution will not capture all discrete cell states.

name: leiden-neighborhood-graph-clustering
description: Use when clustering cells in a learned latent feature matrix (e.g. Miscell encoder output loaded into an AnnData object) and a graph-based Leiden partition is preferred over DBSCAN clustering of the t-SNE embedding.

name: leiden-over-clustering-of-scrnaseq-data
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq data (e.g. PBMC 3K processed via the scanpy standard workflow) as input to Cytocipher, which requires deliberately over-clustered tentative labels from a high Leiden resolution before cluster merging.

name: leiden-pattern-graph-pruning
description: Use when a multiresolution archetypal decomposition (e.g., ACTIONet run_ACTIONet output) yields many overlapping archetypes across resolutions and you need a nonredundant set of cell-state patterns for downstream comparison or annotation.

name: leiden-resolution-annotation-generation
description: Use when preparing scTriangulate input or comparing clustering resolutions: count-matrix AnnData needs QC filtering (min_gene>300, min_count>500, pct_counts_mt<20%), CPTT log-normalization, 3000 HVGs, and Leiden labels at several resolutions.

name: leiden-resolution-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when validating that a cluster-based cell type annotation pipeline (e.g., CellO with pre-clustering via -p) is robust to the choice of Leiden clustering resolution, or when reporting sensitivity of F1-scores across clustering granularity settings.

name: leiden-resolution-sweep-clustering
description: Use when you have a numeric cell-embedding matrix (e.g. from Mowgli, MOFA+, or integrative NMF) and need clusterings at multiple granularities to compute resolution-dependent clustering metrics such as ARI.

name: leiden-sample-level-clustering-silhouette-selection
description: Use when you have a sample-level distance matrix (e.g., PILOT's Wasserstein W over scRNA-seq samples in an AnnData with patient/disease columns) and need to detect unsupervised patient sub-groups and pick the Leiden resolution.

name: leiden-subclustering-of-hematopoietic-progenitors
description: Use when a batch-integrated single-cell atlas (e.g. wild-type + Tal1-/- chimeric E6.5-E8.5 embryos in a CODAL topic latent space) contains a coarse Leiden cluster enriched for hemato-endothelial progenitors that must be split into finer perturbation-affected subtypes.

name: leukemia-counterpart-mapping-onto-hematopoietic-reference
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a leukemia (or carcinoma) cell subpopulation must be projected onto a healthy reference atlas to identify its healthy counterpart, subtype, and lineage/developmental stage.

name: levenshtein-barcode-matching
description: Use when demultiplexing long-read (FASTQ/FASTA) data against a known barcode whitelist and you need edit-distance-tolerant barcode matching with a unique--match assignment rule.

name: levenshtein-distance-read-assignment
description: Use when demultiplexing FASTQ/FASTA reads to a known list of cellular barcodes from noisy single-cell long-read data, where sequencing errors mean exact barcode matching fails and imperfect (edit-distance-tolerant) matching is required.

name: library-output-parity-verification
description: Use when a task requires reimplementing an algorithm from a paper's description and validating it against the official library's exported function (e.g. ERgene.FindERG) on the same input matrix, expecting identical ranked results.

name: library-size-and-dropout-characterization
description: Use when you need to verify that a simulated (synthetic) single-cell count matrix matches the data characteristics — library size, dropout/fraction-of-zeros, and dispersion — of a real single-cell RNA-seq reference dataset.

name: library-size-batch-effect-simulation
description: Use when an scRNA-seq AnnData with raw counts in .X (e.g. TICA) must be stress-tested for cell type annotation robustness under a synthetic library-size batch effect and competing preprocessing (log, normalized, normalized+log).

name: library-size-factor-modeling
description: Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq counts with scVI (e.g. from a PBMC4k pilot with 4182 cells and 1000 HVGs) and you must decide whether library-size factors come from the per-cell posterior or from the Normal(l_mu, 1) prior variant.

name: library-size-median-normalization
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv, cells as rows, genes as columns) must be library-size normalized with median-of-totals scaling to make counts comparable across cells prior to imputation or downstream analysis.

name: library-size-normalization-cp10k
description: Use when raw scRNAseq UMI counts must be summed over cells of each annotated cell type per sample/circadian time point and scaled to CP10K before running JTK_Cycle on pseudobulk series.

name: library-size-offset-estimation
description: Use when fitting per-gene/per-feature GLMs (e.g., Tweedie CPLM/ZICP) to raw scRNA-seq counts or semi-continuous omics data with unequal sequencing depth, so that differences in depth are absorbed by an offset log(S) rather than by transforming counts.

name: lifestyle-associated-bgc-identification
description: Use when a BiG-SCAPE GCF absence/presence matrix at 0.70 distance is available together with lifestyle metadata per genome, and the goal is to rank GCF families significantly enriched in one lifestyle group (e.g., plant pathogens vs non-plant-pathogens).

name: ligand-receptor-communication-inference
description: Use when you have clustered scRNA-seq data (discrete cell groups or pseudotime-ordered continuous states) and need to predict significant ligand-receptor interactions and signaling pathways between cell populations.

name: ligand-receptor-communication-inference-early-embryo
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq from developmental systems (e.g. EPI/PE lineages of blastoids or blastocysts) to infer autocrine/paracrine LR signaling dynamics and LR-to-TF causal relationships along pseudotime trajectories.

name: ligand-receptor-database-curation-validation
description: Use when you need to load, audit, or validate a manually curated ligand–receptor interaction database (e.g. ICELLNET Supplementary Data 1) before using it for cell–cell communication scoring, or when reproducing its family-level and subfamily-level interaction counts.

name: ligand-receptor-database-mapping
description: Use when inferring cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq and interactions must be restricted to literature-supported ligand-receptor pairs, or when comparing tools whose one-ligand/one-receptor assumptions mis-handle multi-subunit receptor complexes.

name: ligand-receptor-database-usage-human-brain
description: Use when inferring neural-specific ligand-receptor communication from human single-nucleus/single-cell RNA-seq of brain tissue (e.g., cortical ASD vs control) and you must pick the correct species-specific interaction DB.

name: ligand-receptor-downstream-gene-selection
description: Use when a signaling pathway's spatial range must be estimated from scRNA-seq data and the canonical ligand, receptor, and downstream target genes for that pathway are known and can be listed explicitly.

name: ligand-receptor-edge-quantification
description: Use when constructing or reproducing ligand-receptor edge weights from a normalised single-cell expression matrix plus cell-type annotations, e.g. to validate NATMI's ExtractEdges.py weighting scheme or recompute edge_weights.csv independently.

name: ligand-receptor-edge-weight-computation
description: Use when you need to reproduce, verify, or interpret the edge attributes Connectome emits for every celltype-to-celltype ligand–receptor mechanism, or when you must compute normalized-slot (w1) vs z-score-based (w2) weights independently from Seurat-normalized data.

name: ligand-receptor-expression-filtering
description: Use when building ligand–receptor communication edges from single-cell expression data and you need to decide which genes count as 'expressed' per cell type before edge extraction.

name: ligand-receptor-gene-normalization
description: Use when preparing a gene-by-cell-population expression matrix (microarray, bulk RNA-seq, or scRNA-seq) for ICELLNET communication scoring, so that highly expressed molecules like chemokines do not dominate interaction scores.

name: ligand-receptor-gene-pair-background-definition
description: Use when validating that an identified set of ligand-receptor genes (e.g. eLRs) is enriched or depleted for reference gene sets, and you need a defensible background universe — all protein-coding genes and/or an all-known-LR baseline.

name: ligand-receptor-gene-subsetting-against-fantom5
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq data for Connectome ligand-receptor mapping: the expression matrix must be subset to the union of ligand and receptor genes from ncomms8866_mouse/human before NormalizeData/ScaleData and CreateConnectome.

name: ligand-receptor-gene-time-series-profiling
description: Use when you have expression values for retained L-R pairs across ordered developmental time points (e.g., GSE153164 E12.5–E17.5 corticogenesis) and need to identify which interactions peak at which stage.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-curation
description: Use when building or updating a curated ligand-receptor pair list from existing resources (CellPhoneDB, RNA-Magnet, SingleCellSignalR/LRdb, ICELLNET) and prior connectomes, requiring PubMedID-level literature verification before network inference.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-detection-in-spatial-transcriptomics
description: Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium) have been resolved to single-cell resolution via SpatialScope decomposition and you need to identify significant ligand-receptor pairs between spatially co-located cell types, such as EC–SMC signaling in a vascular region of interest.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have multiple ligand-receptor interaction resources and want to detect over-/underrepresentation of pathway, cancer, or tissue-enriched protein annotations in each resource relative to a pooled background.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-functional-annotation
description: Use when you have pre-computed ligand-receptor CCI data (e.g. from CellChat on scRNA-seq) subset to a specific viewpoint such as directed outgoing interactions of one cell cluster, and you need to annotate enriched interaction pairs by biological function before grouping them into modules.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference
description: Use when a developmental-series scRNA-seq dataset (expression matrix + cell-type labels + time-point annotations) needs cell-cell interaction inference that distinguishes membrane- from secreted-ligand signaling and tracks dynamic interaction changes across time points.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference
description: Use when analyzing cell-cell communication in SC data lacking native spatial coordinates but with a matched ST reference (e.g., Stereo-seq E9.5), to compare gene-expression-only vs spatially-informed LRI detection.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-inference
description: Use when the goal is to infer cell-cell communication from normalized single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices plus cell labels, especially to identify pathway-mediated LR interactions (e.g., CXCL12/CXCR4 between CD8+ T cells and endothelial cells/fibroblasts in HCC).

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-pathway-filtering
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (e.g., library-size normalized, log-transformed gene-by-cell matrix plus cell labels) has candidate LR pairs and you must prioritize LR interactions by downstream pathway activation in receiver clusters.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-prediction-in-disease-skin
description: Use when comparing cell-cell communication between two disease states (e.g., lesional vs. nonlesional skin scRNA-seq) to identify significantly upregulated ligand-receptor interactions and shifted information flow.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-rank-aggregation
description: Use when multiple CCC method outputs for the same scRNA-seq dataset must be combined into a single consensus prioritisation of ligand-receptor interactions, especially when methods yield incomparable score scales.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-scoring
description: Use when single-nucleus or single-cell RNA-seq data with cell-type annotations and a curated ligand-receptor pair list (e.g. Human-2020-Jin-LR-pairs.csv) must be converted into per-context communication scores for tensor decomposition.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-scoring
description: Use when labeled ground-truth CCI interactions are needed to supervise training of an interaction-inference model (e.g., DeepCCI's Interaction_inference.py), i.e., a scRNA-seq matrix with benchmark cell labels (e.g., panc8, Human) plus a ligand–receptor interaction database.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-scoring
description: Use when testing whether cell-cell communication strength of candidate eLR pairs depends on a developmental perturbation, such as ZGA inhibition with alpha-amanitin across early/late 2-cell stages.

name: ligand-receptor-interaction-scoring
description: Use when a Seurat-processed scRNA-seq dataset has annotated cell clusters and the goal is to identify and rank ligands expressed by one cluster against receptors on another, filtering by >10% expression of ligands/receptors in the clusters of interest.

name: ligand-receptor-network-inference
description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix plus cell-type annotations and need to predict which ligand-receptor pairs mediate communication between cell types, including autocrine/self-signalling and network visualisation.

name: ligand-receptor-network-mapping
description: Use when you have a heterogeneous single-cell RNA-seq dataset with cell-type annotations and want to infer cell–cell communication as ligand–receptor edges (e.g., VEGF, PDGF, DLL3-NOTCH signaling) between cell identities.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-classification
description: Use when building a cell-cell communication network from scRNA-seq data and you must split a curated L-R pair database into membrane-ligand, secreted-ligand, and membrane-receptor classes before computing interaction weights.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-database-curation
description: Use when building or rebuilding the reference LR interaction database needed for cell-cell communication inference (e.g., CommPath, CellPhoneDB-style pipelines) from CellPhoneDB and FANTOM5 resources.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-enrichment
description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-type annotations and need to infer, rank, or visualize ligand-receptor-mediated cell-cell communication between annotated cell populations.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-filtering
description: Use when building a multi-method or multi-context cell-cell communication tensor and you must restrict inputs to LR pairs and cell types shared across all samples, e.g. the 172 shared LR pairs common to all five scoring methods on the BALF COVID-19 data.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-graph-construction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (CSV or h5) with cell-type labels must be converted into a ligand-receptor pair graph so a GCN model (e.g. DeepCCI's ResNet+GCN interaction model) can classify significant CCIs.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-mapping
description: Use when MDIC3 has produced celltype_communication.txt / cellular_communication.txt outputs and you need the specific L-R pairs (e.g., Cx3cl1-Cx3cr1, Apoe-Lrp1, CCL2-CCR2, SST-SSTR2) supporting each sender-receiver communication.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-prediction
description: Use when you have cluster-annotated scRNA-seq data (human or mouse) and need to infer candidate protein pairs mediating communication between two specific cell types, e.g. CAF1–myeloid interactions in melanoma.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-ranking
description: Use when you have factor loadings for ligand-receptor pairs from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition and need to rank them (descending by loading value) to identify top communication pairs or feed factor-specific pre-ranked lists into GSEA.

name: ligand-receptor-pair-screening
description: Use when analyzing time-course scRNA-seq with a reconstructed trajectory (e.g. monocle3 pseudotime) and a ligand-receptor database to identify which LR pairs co-vary along development.

name: ligand-receptor-perturbation-scoring
description: Use when comparing two Seurat/Connectome connectomes (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs control PBMCs) and you need a sign-agnostic per-edge magnitude of perturbation from ligand.norm.lfc and recept.norm.lfc values.

name: ligand-receptor-resource-loading
description: Use when an analysis needs to enumerate, compare, or overlap multiple CCC ligand-receptor resources (e.g., CellChatDB, CellPhoneDB, Ramilowski, ConnectomeDB, LRdb) before downstream inference or benchmarking.

name: ligand-target-communication-strength-computation
description: Use when reproducing or auditing NeuronChat's ligand/target abundance and communication-strength computation for small-molecule neurotransmitter signaling from single-cell expression data.

name: likelihood-ratio-differential-regulation-testing
description: Use when comparing gene regulatory networks between two conditions from paired single-cell data (one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq per condition) and you need subpopulation-specific differential regulation testing with p-values and FDR control.

name: likelihood-ratio-forensic-identification
description: Use when separated cell clusters from a mixed scRNA-seq sample must be attributed to specific contributors by matching cluster SNP profiles against WES reference VCFs, yielding a likelihood ratio per contributor.

name: likelihood-ratio-model-selection
description: Decision support for choosing between NB and ZINB noise models before running DCA on a scRNA-seq count matrix, when you need to test whether a zero-inflation component is statistically justified.

name: likelihood-ratio-statistic-null-calibration
description: Use when computing p-values/FDR for likelihood ratio statistics from a differential regulatory relation test between two linked subpopulations, and the standard Chi-square null is suspected to be anti-conservative or miscalibrated.

name: likelihood-ratio-test-classifier-construction
description: Use when benchmarking machine learning classifiers for 'Redundant' vs 'Unique' deletion-class prediction from two-species expression data and a classical maximum-likelihood baseline is needed for comparison.

name: limma-camera-rotational-gene-set-testing
description: Use when you have a CMScaller-classified expression matrix (organoids, PDXs, cell lines) and need per-subtype gene set enrichment statistics to confirm the subtypes recapitulate canonical CMS pathway signatures.

name: limma-differential-expression-bifurcation-feature-selection
description: Use when training a NeuCA cell-type classifier on scRNA-seq data whose cell-type Pearson correlation matrix contains off-diagonal entries at or above tau = 0.95, requiring the marker-guided hierarchical neural-network route.

name: limma-differential-expression-calling
description: Use when you have normalized bulk RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. MOSim-simulated with a two-group design) and need a DEG call to define true positives for benchmarking or to feed downstream GRN/regulator modeling.

name: limma-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when the analysis target is a GSVA score matrix (samples x genesets) and the goal is testing differential gene-set activity between two sample groups in RNA-seq/cancer data.

name: limma-empirical-bayes-differential-expression
description: Use when PILOT has detected sample-level sub-groups (e.g. 3 PDAC clusters at resolution 0.3) and you need cell-type-specific genes distinguishing one cluster from the others, as a gene-level follow-up to proportion testing.

name: limma-empirical-bayes-linear-modeling
description: Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two-group labels (e.g., 46 critical vs 23 non-critical COVID-19 samples from GSE172114) needs gene-level DEG P-values to seed active subnetwork detection or SEMtree perturbation analysis.

name: limma-linear-model-differential-expression
description: Use when you need differential expression between a genetic/pharmacological perturbation group and MDI-induced control samples from the curated 3T3-L1 microarray data, with per-gene log2FC, moderated p and BH-FDR.

name: limma-linear-modeling
description: Use when genome-wide bulk RNA-seq count data must be converted into ranked differential-expression gene lists per drug-treatment contrast (e.g., 17-AAG response, combination response) to support rank-based gene set analysis.

name: limma-moderated-gene-ranking
description: Use when ranking genes of an RNA-seq expression matrix with subtype labels to define a compact, DEG-based feature space (e.g. limma50) for regularized multiclass logistic regression subtyping.

name: limma-voom-count-normalization
description: Use when the input is a raw RNA-seq gene/ortholog count matrix (e.g., salamander samples SRR7499348–SRR7499365) and the goal is DE analysis with a primary factor plus a blocking factor at a defined FDR threshold.

name: lincs-l1000-perturbation-signature-extraction
description: Use when a scRNA-seq-derived tumor sub-clustering (GEP file) must be matched to LINCS L1000 perturbation experiments to identify which compounds or combinations kill which sub-clusters.

name: lincs-target-gene-mapping
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters from drug-sensitive and drug-resistant myeloma samples (e.g., U266P vs U266VR) need per-subclone drug-target gene enrichment scoring to rank combination candidates such as 17-AAG + FK866.

name: lineage-antagonistic-tf-selection
description: Use when preparing the regulatory-factor input for DICE/CompDICE bifurcation-timing analysis: after differential expression between terminal cells of competing lineages, to pick an equal number of antagonistic lineage-specific TFs per branch.

name: lineage-assignment-randomization
description: Use when validating differential-progression results against imperfect trajectory inference: you have ground-truth pseudotimes/lineages (e.g. from dyngen) and need to know how much pseudotime noise or cell misassignment the progression test tolerates.

name: lineage-barcode-counting-per-cell
description: Use when processing single-cell RNA-seq data with expressed synthetic lineage barcodes (e.g., 10X scRNA-seq FASTQs) to produce per-cell barcode annotation tables after removing PCR chimeras and UMI sequencing errors.

name: lineage-barcode-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating lineage tree reconstruction methods and you need simulated ground-truth trees, leaf barcodes (muts_leaves), and paired expression counts over a grid of mutation rates, dropouts, and cell counts.

name: lineage-bifurcation-analysis
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix with pre-defined cell clusters and want to reconstruct developmental lineages whose start point is chosen objectively as the most pluripotent cells rather than arbitrarily.

name: lineage-branch-probability-interpretation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq trajectory analysis must recover rare or small terminal populations (e.g., ~3% delta cells) and assign lineage labels from computed branch probabilities rather than manual annotation.

name: lineage-cluster-annotation-mapping
description: Use when a pseudotime trajectory (e.g., DTFLOW on the 2730-cell MMP MARS-seq dataset with 3451 informative genes) has been computed and detected sub-branches must be annotated against known progenitor clusters and cross-checked against Scanpy/Monocle2 branch calls.

name: lineage-differentiation-verification
description: Use when validating that a neural ODE forecaster trained on paired time points of a bifurcating single-cell simulation reproduces lineage commitment, or when testing how far before a fate switch training data stays predictive.

name: lineage-fate-prediction-from-signature-genes
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq of progenitor populations plus FACS-sorted mature/differentiated subsets from which end-stage signature genes can be derived, and the goal is to assign individual progenitor cells to lineage-committed branches of a branching trajectory.

name: lineage-marker-dynamics-analysis
description: Use when you have CellRouter subpopulations and reconstructed trajectories (e.g., from subpopulation 20 HSCs to neutrophil/erythroid) and need to score marker genes or regulators along each trajectory to confirm lineage identity and transition-specific dynamics.

name: lineage-marker-fold-change-quantification
description: Use when comparing normalization methods on CITE-seq protein data: after assigning cluster-level cell identities, compute lineage-marker fold changes per cluster to measure which normalization (dsb or CLR) yields sharper lineage separation.

name: lineage-marker-gene-activation-comparison
description: Use when validating simulated scRNA-seq data against a reference for trajectory preservation, e.g. hematopoietic differentiation (BoneMarrow, GSE72857), by checking that marker gene sets activate sequentially along PAGA-inferred branches and pseudo-time ordering is concordant.

name: lineage-marker-spearman-correlation-analysis
description: Use when continuous cell-fate probabilities have been transferred to query cells (e.g., mouse Tusi reference to human Velten via Cell BLAST) and you need to quantify per-fate prediction quality against lineage marker expression.

name: lineage-membership-weight-interpretation
description: Use when you have a common slingshot trajectory (sds) spanning multiple conditions and need to test whether lineage-membership weight distributions differ between conditions (differential fate selection).

name: lineage-path-pseudotime-reordering
description: Use when single-cell data have been mapped onto a multi-branching trajectory and you need to order cells along a specific branch and identify temporally phased waves of gene regulation along that branch.

name: lineage-prediction-validation-against-barcoding-ground-truth
description: Use when GEMLI (or another scRNA-seq lineage inference tool) has produced cell-vs-cell lineage predictions and an independent barcode-to-cell assignment table exists to quantify precision, sensitivity, and false positive rate.

name: lineage-priming-quantification-scrnaseq
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq dataset contains a multipotent progenitor (MPP) population plus competing downstream lineages (e.g. GP vs MEMP bifurcation) and you need to detect primed subpopulations and their regulatory factors without matched scATAC-Seq data.

name: lineage-relatedness-statistical-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression matrices are paired with cellular barcode lineage annotations (e.g., GEO GSE74923 L1210 or CD8+ T-lymphocyte data) and you must statistically test whether lineage-related cells are transcriptionally more similar than random pairs.

name: lineage-separation-scoring
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction methods on temporal single-cell data to quantify which 2D embedding separates cells from distinct lineages across synchronized vs. asynchronized differentiation simulations.

name: lineage-specific-transcription-factor-driver-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data of a differentiating system has annotated clusters/terminal fates and you need to estimate fate probabilities and identify which TFs drive each final fate.

name: lineage-specific-transcription-factor-recovery-comparison
description: Use when comparing feature selection strategies on single-cell RNA-seq trajectories by counting lineage-specific transcription factors recovered per method, e.g., to show DELVE outperforms HVG and RNA velocity selection.

name: lineage-specific-transcription-factor-selection
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq timecourse with competing downstream lineages (e.g. hepatoblast -> hepatocyte vs cholangiocyte) requires choosing which lineage-restricted TF regulatory activity (TFA) features to feed into DICE or another priming/bifurcation quantifier.

name: lineage-tracing-clonal-fate-bias-prediction
description: Use when a longitudinal scRNA-seq dataset with lineage-tracing barcodes and time-point labels (e.g. days 2/4/6) is available and the goal is to predict the probability each progenitor cell enters a particular fate, quantifying whether proliferation estimates improve prediction.

name: lineage-tracing-descendant-count-correlation
description: Use when scRNA-seq time-series data with lineage-tracing annotations is available and per-cell proliferation rates must be estimated from expression alone and validated against empirical clonal growth (descendant counts).

name: lineage-tracing-phylogeny-preprocessing
description: Use when you have a single-cell phylogeny reconstructed from CRISPR-Cas9 lineage tracing (e.g., via Cassiopeia) plus cell-level categorical meta-data (e.

name: lineage-tree-depth-partitioning
description: Use when you have a rooted lineage-reconstructed tree (e.g., LinRace output in Newick) plus per-leaf cell-type labels, and want to assess whether barcode-defined subtrees are pure or mixed with respect to transcriptome-defined cell types.

name: lineage-tree-reconstruction
description: Use when you have paired single-cell lineage barcode data (character/allele matrix) and scRNA-seq expression for the same cells, and need a cell division tree with inferred ancestral cell states.

name: linear-classifier-training-on-embeddings
description: Use when you have a pretrained Miscell latent feature matrix (e.g. 43,095 PBMC cells) plus ground-truth cell-type labels and want to quantify how well a linear probe predicts each of the 7 PBMC cell types.

name: linear-correlation-assessment-of-simulation-parameters
description: Use when you have simulated perturbation (Y) and control (Z) scCRISPR-seq matrices spanning a synthetic (d, r) parameter grid and need to verify that a derived quantity depends linearly on both simulation parameters, per the paper's Equations 14-15.

name: linear-covariate-adjustment-scrnaseq
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has known unwanted covariates (e.g., patient/batch ID, library size) that must be adjusted for before inferring hidden factors or surrogate variables.

name: linear-deconvolution-of-bulk-rna-profiles
description: Use when you have latent variables (GEP weights or manifold embeddings) learned from a scRNAseq reference atlas and need to project them onto bulk RNA profiles from patients to build testable clinical biomarkers.

name: linear-discriminant-analysis-model-training
description: Use when you have single-cell measurements (e.g., CyTOF metabolic markers such as GLUT1 through HIF1A) plus a priori class labels and want supervised axes that optimally separate those labels for visualization or projection of unseen cells.

name: linear-discriminant-analysis-projection
description: Use when single-cell data (scRNA-seq PCs, mass cytometry markers) has trusted a priori class labels and the goal is a non-stochastic, linear, label-aligned visualization of heterogeneity or trajectory, e.g., reconstructing villus differentiation.

name: linear-discriminant-visualization-ggplot2
description: Use when a fitted LDA or HSS-LDA model on cells-by-markers CyTOF data must be rendered as a 2D scatter plot of LD axes colored by class labels, or when HSS-LDA separation must be visually compared against a plain-LDA baseline.

name: linear-gene-expression-prediction
description: Use when you have cell-type-specific gene-TF affinity matrices (e.g. STARE ABC-mode *_TF_Gene_Affinities.txt.gz derived from gABC, Hi-C, regular ABC or Cicero mappings) and need to quantify which enhancer-gene assignment approach predicts observed cell-type expression.

name: linear-mixed-effects-model-fitting
description: Use when detecting perturbed cell types between conditions (e.g., COVID-19 vs control, immunotherapy responders vs non-responders) from scRNA-seq data with replicated patients, where naive per-cell-type tests would inflate false positives.

name: linear-mixed-effects-modeling-of-patient-variability
description: Use when estimating cell-type-specific transcriptomic perturbation distances between conditions in single-cell RNA-seq data where multiple patients/replicates per condition require correcting sample-to-sample variability.

name: linear-mixed-effects-modeling-of-single-cell-pca-scores
description: Use when estimating the distance between condition means in gene-expression space for predefined cell types from scRNA-seq data with multiple replicate patients, and per-cell-type inference (CI, p-value) on that distance is needed.

name: linear-mixed-model-association-testing
description: Use when you have CAFEH per-(SNP, tissue) results (pip, p_active, top_component, rank, pi) across many tissues and traits, and need to quantify whether tissue-restricted eQTL components are enriched for activity in GWAS loci.

name: linear-mixed-model-variance-component-fitting
description: Use when scRNA-seq data have been summarized into OP or CTP pseudobulk per individual (with nu/ctnu noise variances and P cell type proportions) and the goal is to detect or quantify cell type-specific interindividual expression variance.

name: linear-mixed-model-with-kinship-correction
description: Use when you have per-sample cell-type proportion estimates (e.g., Bisque bulk.props) for a bulk RNA-seq cohort plus measured phenotypes and sample relatedness, and you need to test cell-proportion/phenotype associations while correcting for kinship, age, and sex.

name: linear-model-design-matrix-specification
description: Use when an RNA-seq count table has a primary condition of interest but samples also differ by a nuisance variable (batch, species, individual) that must be blocked in the limma design before calling DEGs.

name: linear-model-differential-expression
description: Use when performing differential expression or guide-gRNA association testing on single-cell UMI count data (e.g. Perturb-seq, CROP-seq) after Normalisr normalization, especially when unbiased null P values or control of gRNA cross-association FPR matters.

name: linear-model-tf-activity-inference
description: Use when TF activities must be inferred from a pre-processed adata object plus a TF binding-site matrix (rows = expressed genes, columns = TFs/motifs), e.g. within a fate-trajectory pipeline where downstream differential TF activity analysis is planned.

name: linear-program-objective-evaluation
description: Use when a pipeline parameter (e.g., a separation threshold Delta > 0) must be tuned by treating a downstream LP-solver/classifier accuracy as a black-box objective over a bounded search space.

name: linear-programming-formulation
description: Use when selecting a small, non-redundant gene-marker panel from labeled scRNA-seq data and the combinatorial marker problem must be relaxed to a solvable LP with a sparsity budget ||alpha||_1 <= s.

name: linear-regression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to estimate a per-sample swapped-read fraction from count data via regression gradients, or test whether a swapping rate correlates with a covariate such as free library barcode concentration across plates.

name: linear-regression-fitting
description: Use when you have DOI scores for cell-type pairs from a CI-graph plus Spaco-assigned colors, and need to quantify whether color differences track spatial interlacement via OLS regression.

name: linear-regression-goodness-of-fit
description: Use when you have a constructed co-expression network and must verify it satisfies the approximate scale-free topology criterion (R2 > 0.80 per Zhang and Horvath) before downstream node-controllability analysis.

name: linear-regression-imputation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix already has an imputable-entry mask from the upstream hypothesis-testing module and you need to fill those dropout-affected zeros with fitted values via subspace regression.

name: linear-regression-modeling
description: Use when you have a merged per-sample table of continuous predictors and a continuous response (e.g., 676 TCGA tumors with METAFlux flux features and Winter hypoxia scores) and need coefficient estimates, standard errors, p-values, and 95% CIs to test metabolic reprogramming associations.

name: linear-regression-of-cell-proportions-on-clinical-trait
description: Use when estimated cell type proportions from deconvolution (e.g., MuSiC music_prop output) must be tested for association with a clinical trait such as HbA1c via single-variable linear regression.

name: linear-regression-of-log-coverage-vs-base-position
description: Use when a base-level RNA-seq coverage dataset shows systematic 3'-end coverage decline per sample, and you need per-sample decay rates to identify degraded cases before shape change detection.

name: linear-regression-proportion-testing
description: Use when you need to test whether cell-type proportions shift between conditions in single-cell resolution data (.h5ad/AnnData), including unreplicated datasets where standard regression approaches fail.

name: linear-regression-reconstruction-loss-evaluation
description: Use when you have selected a minimal gene marker set from single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., .h5ad loaded via get_citeseq/get_mouse_brain/get_paul/get_zeisel) and need to quantify whole-transcriptome reconstruction quality as ℓ2/ℓ1 losses.

name: linear-regression-residual-computation
description: Use when an IA-SVA (or SVA-style) analysis must remove known-factor variation from single-cell log-transformed counts before extracting PCs, i.e., residualization of Y on the design matrix built via model.matrix(~patient_id + geo_lib_size).

name: linear-regression-runtime-extrapolation
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (runtime, peak memory) of scDNA–scRNA integration methods as input size scales, and you need a quantitative extrapolation beyond measured cell counts.

name: linear-regression-swapping-fraction-estimation
description: Use when quantifying the swapped-read fraction in plate-based scRNA-seq libraries sequenced on the HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq, where demultiplexing exposes impossible sample-barcode combinations to regress against.

name: linear-regression-transcript-counts
description: Use when you have paired labeled/unlabeled/total count matrices from metabolic labeling scRNA-seq (e.g., scEU-seq 4sU-treated cells) and need per-gene degradation rates to estimate pre-labeling expression.

name: linear-runtime-scaling-analysis
description: Use when estimating or validating SkewC gene body coverage compute cost for a 10x Genomics barcoded BAM (e.g. pbmc_8k), or when planning how many cells can be processed in a given time budget.

name: linear-scaling-regression-analysis
description: Use when a method's scalability claim (e.g., 'linear running time') must be verified empirically: you can generate or obtain datasets at multiple sizes and record wall-clock runtime per size for regression.

name: linear-svm-cell-type-classification
description: Use when annotating cells of an aligned, Seurat-v3-integrated scRNA-seq dataset whose integrated expression matrix (retaining many dimensions) is placed in the .X slot of an AnnData object, and a hierarchical classifier is trained per tree node in scHPL.

name: linear-svm-hierarchical-classification
description: Use when you have multiple aligned (batch-corrected), annotated scRNA-seq datasets with high-dimensional integrated expression matrices and need to construct or extend a hierarchical cell-population classification tree with per-node linear SVMs.

name: linf-norm-joint-distance-fusion
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data with RNA and surface-protein (ADT) modalities where modality fusion by L∞ norm of pairwise cell-cell distances is needed, especially with routine numbers of ADT features (<50).

name: linfinity-distance-matrix-fusion
description: Use when CITE-seq data with both transcriptome and surface-protein (ADT) modalities has been preprocessed and per-modality cell-cell distance matrices must be fused for joint Louvain clustering or dimensionality reduction.

name: linked-read-isoform-assembly
description: Use when input is barcoded bulk RNA-seq (e.g. SPIso-seq-style linked reads in FASTQ) and the goal is de novo full-length isoform reconstruction, especially for highly alternatively spliced genes such as GYPC, MAPT, or BIN1.

name: lioness-sample-perturbation-network-inference
