description: Use when evaluating cell-specific network inference (CSNI) methods on dyngen simulations: datasets carry transcriptomics plus per-cell ground-truth GRNs, and no motif data is available, so LIONESS must run with Pearson correlation rather than PANDA.

name: lisi-batch-mixing-quantification
description: Use when a query single-cell RNA-seq dataset carries explicit batch or technology-of-origin labels (e.g., three 10x protocols 3'v1/3'v2/5') and you need a numeric measure of how well batches mix before vs. after projecting cells into a reference atlas embedding.

name: lisi-entropy-score-computation
description: Use when evaluating scRNA-seq integration quality on datasets with batch origin and cell type annotations, especially when cell type imbalance across batches makes standard cell type-agnostic iLISI mis.

name: lisi-integration-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing single-cell batch integration methods on multi-sample, multi-condition data (e.g. pancreas + lung mixtures) and you need quantitative evidence of batch removal (iLISI) without over-correction (cLISI, condition separation, condition-specific DE genes).

name: lisi-integration-metric-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking whether mapped query cells (e.g., Symphony mapQuery output) mix with reference cells across technology or donor labels, by comparing LISI against a de novo integration baseline.

name: lisi-integration-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2 and Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2) have been integrated by batch-correction tools and you need numeric iLISI/cLISI scores, plus runtime, to rank the methods.

name: lisi-metric-computation-on-embeddings
description: Use when quantifying batch effects in scRNA-seq data via local batch-label diversity: you have an embedding (BEENE or PCA), per-cell batch labels across multiple batches/platforms, and need per-sample iLISI values for downstream kBET/iLISI comparison tables.

name: lisi-mixing-metric-computation
description: Use when per-cell UMAP embeddings from one or more integration methods (e.g. Supervised Harmony, Harmony, Seurat RPCA, Scanorama, Limma) must be benchmarked for batch/donor mixing versus AUCell-derived cell-type conservation.

name: lisi-neighborhood-continuity-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking spatially aware color assignments or spatial proximity metrics on 2D single-cell/cluster point data, and you need a neighborhood-mixing score that separates mixed/interlaced pairs from isolated ones.

name: literature-ground-truth-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-cell communication inference methods on the same scRNA-seq dataset and you need a quantitative, literature-grounded reliability metric (support percentage and AUC) for each method's predicted communications.

name: literature-ground-truth-network-construction
description: Use when benchmarking gene network inference methods and a literature-based directed binary ground truth (Omnipath source→target edges) is needed to compute AUPRC/EPR per cell type.

name: literature-support-verification
description: Use when building or validating a curated ligand-receptor interaction database where each pair must carry primary literature support, or when auditing merged resources for pairs whose cited PMID does not actually back the interaction.

name: liver-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a processed Seurat object of human liver scRNA-seq data (e.g. transplanted liver samples, cold perfusion/portal reperfusion stages) has PCA/UMAP clusters but no cell-type labels and needs annotation compatible with scCrossTalk's sc_celltype input.

name: lmds-dimensionality-reduction-for-trajectory-input
description: Use when preparing a single-cell dataset for tree-shaped trajectory inference (e.g., Totem CLARA k-medoids clustering) and a fast low-dimensional embedding is needed instead of PCA or full MDS on large datasets.

name: lncrna-classification-evaluation
description: Use when you have LncCat/CatBoost prediction scores for transcripts labeled lncRNA or PCT and need to reproduce or benchmark MCC/F1 classification results against the paper's fixed 0.5-cutoff baseline.

name: lncrna-coding-potential-classification
description: Use when you need to distinguish lncRNAs from PCTs in FASTA transcript sequences across species (human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, chicken), especially for transcripts containing sORFs where existing coding-potential tools perform poorly.

name: lncrna-coding-potential-feature-engineering
description: Use when building a coding-potential classifier for RNA transcripts and you must design the feature space (SIFs, SSFs, PFs, ORF-type features) or trim it down with recursive feature elimination while preserving accuracy.

name: lncrna-pct-class-separation-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually demonstrate that a fused feature representation (e.g. ORF-attention features from BERT-encoded ORF peptides) discriminates lncRNAs from PCTs in feature space, via per-species UMAP scatter plots colored by class.

name: lncrna-transcript-feature-extraction
description: Use when you have raw transcript FASTA files (mRNA sequences, their matching CDS sequences, and lncRNA sequences) and need to build a labeled feature matrix for training or reproducing an lncRNA/mRNA classification model such as LncDC's.

name: local-alignment-scoring-with-pairwise2
description: Use when you have tRF-5::tRNA interface sequences (tRF-5s of 15-19 nt) extracted from tncRNA Toolkit output and need to score their local alignments to detect a conserved cleavage motif across plant species.

name: local-score-smoothing-cubic-splines
description: Use when you need to visually assess whether condition labels (e.g., treatment vs. control) are locally imbalanced across a low-dimensional cell embedding, as the first diagnostic step before differential topology testing with condiments.

name: local-shifting-vector-batch-correction
description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Seurat V3.0 log-count matrices) where batch correction should move query cells toward matched reference anchors using per-anchor local shifting vectors rather than global or MNN-based correction.

name: local-structure-preservation-rnn-evaluation
description: Reference for judging integration quality when a method must both mix batches (iLISI) and retain local neighborhood structure (50-RNN), e.g. benchmarking BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, or Scanorama.

name: locality-sensitive-hashing-density-estimation
description: Use when a monolithic, clustering-free estimate of per-cell rareness/density is needed on ultra-large scRNA-seq data (tens of thousands of profiles) where pairwise-clustering methods like RaceID or GiniClust scale too slowly.

name: locality-sensitive-hashing-fingerprinting
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads must be transformed into reference-free cell features without genome alignment, and k-mers with similar abundance profiles need to be grouped via simhash fingerprints.

name: locus-level-annotation-extraction-with-flanking-genes
description: Use when a locus-level TE quantification matrix (e.g., MATES output with loci named chr|start|end) must be annotated with coordinates and flanking genes to interpret cell-type-specific TE markers such as RLTR44B in macrophages.

name: locus-level-linear-regression-model-fitting
description: Use when building a custom BIRD prediction model from training RNA-seq expression and DNase-seq DH data, or when cluster-level model performance is uncertain and the locus-level model must be used via BIRD_predict -l.

name: locus-level-te-count-correlation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a locus-specific TE quantification method (e.g., MATES, scTE, SoloTE) against simulated single-cell data with known ground-truth locus abundances, or when reproducing the controlled-simulation validation reported in a TE quantification paper.

name: locus-specific-te-expression-summarization
description: Use when processing single-cell RNA-Seq BAM files (CellRanger or STAR output) to detect locus-specific transposable element activity that standard pipelines discard, and to merge TE counts into a gene+TE expression matrix for downstream tools like Seurat.

name: loess-coverage-smoothing-genomic-tracks
description: Use when differentially expressed uTAR coverage tracks need smoothing and peak-coordinate extraction (FWHM) to define the nucleotide sequence that will be BLASTn-annotated.

name: loess-regression-residual-computation
description: Use when computing per-gene entropy-reduction statistics (ds) from a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix to feed the ROGUE cluster-purity calculation, or when modeling the expected mean-expression vs. sample-entropy relationship.

name: log-cosh-edge-preserving-regularization
description: Use when a gene-by-cell relative expression matrix (counts minus a normal-cell baseline) must be denoised before copy number segmentation while preserving piecewise-constant discontinuities (breakpoints) along genomic coordinates.

name: log-fold-change-gene-scoring
description: Use when you have a CSV data frame of significantly changed genes with expression values / log-fold-change values and need per-gene LFC scores to drive OmicInt's GMM clustering or gene-network exploration.

name: log-intensity-distribution-analysis
description: Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix contains a mixed background/signal distribution and a log2-scale histogram inflection must be identified to set a background cutoff (e.g. 6.1 in the PIMENTo pipeline).

name: log-l2-normalization-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (UMI or read count, e.g. CSV with cells x genes) must be normalized before PCA/RMT-based signal detection and you need to prevent log normalization from creating false variability from TGC bias.

name: log-log-distribution-visualization
description: Use when you have an adjacency network (e.g., a differential gene co-expression network) and must verify its degree distribution follows an approximate scale-free topology before downstream node-control analysis.

name: log-log-scaling-slope-fitting
description: Use when benchmarking computational scalability of a method: you have one large input dataset, need runtime as a function of size (e.g. number of cells), and want a fitted scaling exponent comparable across methods.

name: log-normal-batch-effect-injection
description: Use when building synthetic multi-sample multi-condition scRNA-seq benchmark data: condition-permuted counts must be given sample-level technical variation (batch structure) before ground-truth DS genes are injected.

name: log-normal-biological-variation-modeling
description: Use when a known-truth negative-control dataset is needed to test whether an scRNA-seq method (e.g., Normalisr) falsely detects co-expression or nonlinear library-size confounders when none exist.

name: log-normalize-count-transformation
description: Use when UMI-based scRNA-seq counts must be log-normalized (scale factor 10000) after SAVER-X denoising, or CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT protein counts must be converted to relative-abundance log-ratios before cTP-net protein imputation.

name: log-rank-hazard-ratio-estimation
description: Use when two patient subtype calls (e.g., basal-like vs classical from signature scoring of 150 TCGA PAAD tumors) must be validated against overall survival with KM curves, a log-rank P value, and a hazard ratio.

name: log-rank-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when a cell-type or gene signature discovered in single-cell data needs independent validation in bulk transcriptome cohorts that have matched overall survival time/status and radiologic response metadata.

name: log-rank-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when you have per-sample viral or HERV positivity calls (e.g., from viRNAtrap contigs) paired with TCGA clinical overall survival times, and the goal is to test survival differences between virus-positive and virus-negative patient groups.

name: log-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when a patient cohort has overall-survival metadata plus a continuous risk/enrichment score (e.g., ssGSEA signature score) and you must test high-vs-low group separation by survival.

name: log-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when cluster assignments (e.g., from RCC, k-means, hclust, or published subtype labels) must be validated for clinical relevance by testing survival differences across clusters within cancer-type strata.

name: log-rank-survival-analysis
description: Use when validating that predicted molecular subtype labels (e.g., DeepCC or PAM50 Luminal/HER2/Basal calls) are clinically meaningful by testing survival separation in cohorts with disease-free survival outcomes.

name: log-rank-survival-association-testing
description: Use when bulk tumor samples (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer) have matched overall survival time/status and clinical covariates (Age, Sex, TNM stage), and you need to test whether learned representation features are prognostic.

name: log-rank-survival-testing-of-gene-modules
description: Use when fRNC modules/RNCs (e.g., from runmodule local search on TCGA ESCA data) must be stratified by clinical outcome, requiring per-module Kaplan-Meier curves and log-rank p-values from TCGA survival annotations.

name: log-rank-test-statistics
description: Use when a cell-cluster DEG signature (e.g., Cluster 4 from GSE156625 with top DEGs PTMA and STMN1) must be validated against TCGA bulk cohorts (e.g., TCGA-LIHC) for prognostic survival separation.

name: log-rank-test-survival-comparison
description: Use when a workflow has partitioned patients (by consensus clustering, risk-score median split, or classifier label) and must show that the groups differ significantly in overall survival via Kaplan–Meier curves plus a log-rank test.

name: log-ratio-delta-derivation
description: Use when you have eLR pair interaction scores computed under a transcriptional perturbation (e.g. alpha-amanitin ZGA inhibition) and matched unperturbed conditions, and need a log-ratio delta per LR pair to call altered communication.

name: log-scale-imputed-data-backtransformation
description: Use when an imputation method (e.g. AutoImpute) was run on log-transformed count matrices but the downstream metric — like intra-subpopulation coefficient of variation for Fig. 4 variance stabilization — must be computed on linear-scale expression values.

name: log-scale-runtime-visualization
description: Use when comparing algorithm runtimes across dataset sizes that span orders of magnitude (e.g. 1,000–50,000 cells) and the speed advantage itself is the finding to visualize.

name: log-shift-parameter-grid-search
description: Use when base-level RNA-seq coverage pileup data retain strong right skew and a log transform is needed before SCISSOR shape change detection, but the pseudo-count added prior to log-transformation is unknown and must be chosen automatically.

name: log-space-expression-cap-enforcement
description: Use when performing recursive (multi-step) neural ODE expression forecasting with RNAForecaster, e.g. predicting scEU-seq RPE cell-cycle gene expression over 72 hourly steps, to prevent extreme predictions.

name: log-transformation-and-mean-centering-of-pileup-data
description: Use when you have base-level RNA-seq coverage (pileup) matrices from SCISSOR's build_pileup and need comparable, variance-stabilized per-gene coverage before shape change detection or decay-rate estimation.

name: log-transformation-of-adt-umi-counts
description: Use when raw ADT/UMI count matrices (cell-containing and/or empty droplets) from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq data must be transformed before estimating per-antibody ambient background or before computing ambient correlation summaries.

name: log-transformation-of-copy-number-data
description: Use when benchmarking cell-to-clone assignment accuracy across clustering algorithms and preprocessing choices, where both original and log-transformed copy-number values must be fed to intNMF or agglomerative clustering before running MaCroDNA.

name: log-transformed-count-error-metrics
description: Use when evaluating imputation accuracy on masked scRNA-seq data and you need to attribute ground-truth MSE to nonzero entries, biological zeros (true zeros), and technical zeros (masked nonzero values).

name: log10-library-size-count-normalization
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. raw_count.csv) must be normalized before fitting scImpute's mixture model or comparing expression across cells with differing library sizes.

name: log1p-expression-summary-transformation
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data (CSV or Parquet, melted tall format) has been reshaped in Spark and per-cell/per-gene QC summaries (total expression, genes expressed, percent ERCC, percent mitochondrial, dropout) need variance stabilization before filtering.

name: log2-expression-rescaling
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., FPKM/RPKM/CPM values from plate-based protocols like SUPeR-seq or Smart-Seq2) has a value range larger than 100 and will feed into subspace-regression imputation of dropout-affected zero entries.

name: log2-fold-change-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when two deconvolved or reference-free cell-type transcriptional profiles (beta matrices) from different biological conditions (e.g., aged vs young pseudo-pixels) must be compared gene-by-gene to validate recovered perturbation signatures.

name: log2-fold-change-prevalence-filtering
description: Use when given a gene cluster absence/presence matrix and per-genome lifestyle labels, you must identify lifestyle-enriched gene clusters using prevalence and log2 fold-change thresholds plus Fisher's exact test.

name: log2-fold-change-significance-thresholding
description: Use when a CSV already contains pre-computed log2 fold-changes and adjusted p-values per pairwise comparison and you need to narrow thousands of RNA-seq/transposon-insertion entries to extreme or moderately changing genes without preselecting candidates.

name: log2-pseudo-count-transformation
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes .csv) must be transformed into the normalized, log2-transformed <dataset_name>.{mat, csv} format expected by AutoImpute.py before imputation.

name: log2-transformation-of-gene-intensities
description: Use when a matrix of gene-level collapsed microarray intensities (e.g. from collapseRows across multiple GEO series) must be made comparable across arrays/studies prior to batch-effect removal or differential expression.

name: log2fc-intensity-computation
description: Use when inferring potential LR associations between cell clusters from scRNA-seq data and you need per-pair intensity and p-value statistics from cluster-pair differential expression results.

name: log2fc-regulation-direction-classification
description: Use when a DESeq2 differential expression table of tncRNA (or gene) counts across stress vs. control conditions must be filtered to significant hits and each hit labeled as up- or down-regulated by log2 fold-change direction.

name: logcounts-pca-baseline-embedding
description: Use when benchmarking a dimension-reduction method (e.g., CA via corral) on scRNA-seq counts and you need the canonical log(x+1)-then-PCA baseline embedding on the same datasets for ARI comparison.

name: logfc-correlation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking DEG methods on data with known fold changes (e.g. synthetic spike-in transcripts) and you need to verify that estimated logFC values are accurate, not just that DEG calls are correct.

name: logfc-outlier-validation
description: Use when a multi-method DEG consensus table (DESeq2, edgeR, limma) contains outlier or extreme logFC estimates that must be verified before downstream use such as qPCR target selection or GSEA.

name: logistic-regression-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantify how each of several engineered feature modes (position-specific k-mer/gapped k-mer descriptors plus GC-content) contributes to classifier performance via cross-validated Accuracy, Precision, Sensitivity, Specificity, F1-Score, and MCC.

name: logistic-regression-benchmarking-across-batch-correction-methods
description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods on scRNA-seq data with multilevel batch variables: train each method on the same counts and labels, then evaluate whether corrected embeddings preserve cell-type identity via supervised classification accuracy.

name: logistic-regression-cell-type-classification
description: Use when a selected marker gene set (e.g., 42 genes from GreedyPC on IPF) must be validated by training a logistic regression classifier on the same data subset used for feature selection and evaluating macro-F1 on left-out cells.

name: logistic-regression-coefficient-extraction
description: Use when you need per-gene importance from the 2707-DEG scMalignantFinder model (model.joblib) or must verify that a reduced feature set (common DEGs, top-1500 genes) matches full-model AUROC/balanced accuracy.

name: logistic-regression-f1-evaluation
description: Use when a feature/marker set (e.g., from GreedyPC at a fixed coverage) needs downstream validation of how well it distinguishes phenotypes, via classification F1 on held-out samples from scRNA-seq data such as the IPF, MC, or HCA datasets.

name: logistic-regression-gene-ranking
description: Use when cell clusters and cell types are already assigned in a SINCERA single-cell RNA-Seq analysis and marker genes per cell type are available, so gene signatures can be ranked and validated.

name: logistic-regression-model-retraining
description: Use when benchmarking an lncRNA identification tool whose shipped model (e.g., CPAT's logistic regression) was trained on a different dataset, and you have a labeled training set (H-Train) plus a test set (H-Test) to retrain and re-evaluate it.

name: logistic-regression-roc-fate-prediction
description: Use when a LatentVelo model with a zr_dim regulatory state has been trained on lineage-deciding data (e.g., fibroblast reprogramming) and you need to quantitatively test whether the latent regulatory state separates outcome classes such as reprogrammed versus dead-end cells.

name: logit-log-link-glm-model-fitting
description: Use when you need to distinguish true gene fusions from artificial chimeric-read noise by regressing per-cell fusion supporting-read counts on gene-expression covariates and GC-content splines, then testing candidates for significance.

name: logit-sr-gaussian-mixture-inference
description: Use when scRNA-Seq data must be stratified into discrete potency states using signalling entropy, e.g. to detect a low-potency subpopulation (like the ~4% hESC fraction) or compute a Shannon index of heterogeneity.

name: lognormal-log-ratio-distribution-analysis
description: Use when validating, teaching, or extending the theoretical assumptions behind SD and CV as reference-gene stability measures, or when checking numerically that argmax fZ(z=1) coincides with argmin of the respective stability measure under Gaussian or log-normal ratio models.

name: logrank-test-prognostic-interpretation
description: Use when integrating patient clinical survival data with continuous molecular scores (GSVA, expression TPM) and you need to test whether high vs low score groups differ in survival probability via Kaplan-Meier/log-rank.

name: loh-region-cna-stratification
description: Use when single-cell clone assignments and per-gene CNA/LOH states (e.g., from XClone) are available and you need to test whether DEGs between a tumour clone and normal cells concentrate in LOH regions.

name: long-indel-remapped-alignment-calling
description: Use when reconstructing ScanNeo2's variant-calling stage for long indels: matched DNA-seq and/or RNA-seq BAMs exist, config sets indel `type: long` (or `all`) with `mode: DNA|RNA|BOTH`, and long variants beyond Mutect2's short-indel reach are needed.

name: long-read-barcode-umi-extraction
description: Use when demultiplexing noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq reads or 10x Chromium/Visium short reads where barcodes/UMIs must be extracted, corrected, and assigned against a whitelist (barcode_list.txt).

name: long-read-demultiplexing
description: Use when noisy ONT long-read FASTQ/FASTA single-cell data needs cell-barcode demultiplexing or barcode discovery, e.g. 10x Chromium libraries where barcodes contain sequencing errors and a whitelist may or may not be known.

name: long-read-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when you need to validate or benchmark a short-read single-cell TE quantification method and matched long-read data (nanopore scNanoRNAseq or PacBio) from the same sample exists to serve as ground truth at the TE subfamily level.

name: long-read-isoform-consensus-repair
description: Use when Nanopore single-cell/spatial long reads are grouped into UMI clusters and you must fix misalignment or end truncation before isoform quantification, e.g. false-positive small internal exons or truncated read ends from high sequencing error.

name: long-read-isoform-detection
description: Use when BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments of long reads (PacBio Iso-Seq or ONT cDNA/direct RNA) from a targeted gene, minigene, or SIRV spike-in must be resolved into isoforms and quantified without prior splice-site annotation.

name: long-read-isoform-quantification
description: Use when Nanopore single-cell/spatial FASTQ reads (e.g., Jurkat GSP-targeted, MOB Visium, CRCLM) must be turned into cell-by-isoform count matrices, or when benchmarking isoform quantification methods against Illumina or PacBio IsoSeq gold standards.

name: long-read-isoseq-validation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking computationally predicted IPA/polyA sites from conventional RNA-seq (e.g., InPACT, IPAFinder) against long-read Iso-seq isoform annotations to obtain validation rates for a dataset such as GSE167486 small airway epithelial cells.

name: long-read-rna-seq-alignment
description: Use when you have raw long-read RNA FASTQ data (PacBio Iso-Seq, ONT) and unspliced reference sequences (FASTA) and need spliced alignments (BAM+BAI) as input for VIsoQLR isoform analysis.

name: long-read-rna-seq-feature-analysis
description: Use when a trained random forest model (e.g., dsRID trained on /data/Pacbio_AD_data.tsv) needs feature-level interpretation, specifically to rank features like Skip_ratio and Len_skip by permutation contribution score.

name: long-read-rnaseq-window-scanning
description: Use when the input is PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM alignments and the goal is a genome-wide scan for candidate endogenous dsRNA regions that feed into novel-long-dsRNA and structured-RNA classification (e.g. reproducing dsRID Fig. 3A counts).

name: long-read-splice-site-merging
description: Reference for defining consensus exon coordinates (splice start/end positions) from long-read BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments when splice sites are unknown a priori, e.g. SIRV or minigene splicing assays analyzed one gene at a time.

name: long-read-spliced-read-alignment
description: Use when long-read transcript sequencing reads (FASTQ, e.g. PacBio HiFi or ONT) must be spliced-aligned to a reference genome (FASTA) before isoform detection or benchmarking of tools such as VIsoQLR, FLAIR or StringTie2.

name: long-read-transcript-alignment-filtering
description: Use when raw PacBio/ONT FASTQ reads with single-cell barcodes must be splice-aligned to a reference genome and filtered to high-confidence full-length spliced isoforms before per-cell-type isoform quantification.

name: long-read-transcriptome-isoform-detection
description: Use when analyzing long-read RNA-seq (nanopore or PacBio Iso-Seq) BAM/GFF3/BED6 alignments of selected genes or spike-ins (e.g., SIRVs) to identify and quantify known or novel isoforms and tune detection thresholds.

name: long-tail-low-frequency-driver-detection
description: Use when you have a list of predicted driver genes for TCGA cancer types (e.g., BLCA, BRCA, COAD, HNSC, KICH, KIRC, KIRP, LIHC, LUAD, LUSC, PRAD, STAD, THCA, UCEC) and GDC somatic SNV data, and need to classify drivers as low- vs high-frequency mutations.

name: longest-common-subsequence-seed-detection
description: Use when clustering continuous gene expression microarray or RNA-seq matrix data to discover trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters hidden in complex, noisy data, e.g. GEO GDS datasets or BicatYeast.

name: longitudinal-gene-expression-tracking
description: Use when pairwise differential-expression comparisons form a time course or experimental series (e.g., log2 fold-change and padj CSVs at t=3–90 min) and you need to confirm which scorecard-identified genes stay stable or shift over time.

name: longitudinal-scrna-seq-simulation
description: Use when a method for multi-timepoint scRNA-seq (cross-timepoint annotation, novel-cell detection, or tDEG calling) needs a ground-truth benchmark with controlled temporal effects, since no real dataset has fully known labels/DEG truth.

name: longitudinal-scrnaseq-differential-expression
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices from two or more timepoints, a metadata table with a binary Group factor and a Time variable, and you need genes whose expression trends over time differ between strata (tDEGs).

name: loss-ablation-study-design
description: Use when a model's training objective combines multiple loss terms (e.g. scBGEDA's zero-inflated negative binomial reconstruction loss plus an MSE denoising reconstruction loss) and you need to isolate whether a specific term improves downstream performance such as cell-type clustering ARI.

name: loss-weight-ablation-study-design
description: Use when benchmarking how individual biologically-informed loss components of BIDCell contribute to segmentation performance, e.g. reproducing the ablation trends of Supplementary Figs. 4-5 on Xenium breast cancer data.

name: louis-method-pvalue-calibration
description: Use when testing whether a gene set is enriched in differentially expressed genes from scRNA-seq DE summary statistics (beta, beta_var) after fitting iDEA with iDEA.fit, and a properly calibrated enrichment p-value is required.

name: louvain-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you must quantify whether cell-attribute aware community detection (EVA/ELVAR) attains stronger significance for a known simulated or real DA shift than standard Louvain clustering on the same single-cell graph.

name: louvain-cell-type-clustering
description: Use when training scDesign2 in scReadSim on a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix whose cells lack predefined cell labels (no celllabel_file), since scDesign2 requires discrete cell types.

name: louvain-centroid-initialization
description: Use when training a graph autoencoder for scRNA-seq cell clustering (e.g. scGAE) and initial cluster centers are needed before soft-assignment/KL clustering training; also relevant to any DEC-style pipeline requiring centroid initialization.

name: louvain-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when a simulated or ground-truth-labelled scRNA-Seq dataset is available and you need to quantify whether cell-attribute aware EVA community detection recovers known labels better than a Louvain-analog, via ARI and chi-square DA statistics.

name: louvain-clustering-bio-conservation-scoring
description: Use when comparing the output embeddings of multiple scRNA-seq integration methods (e.g., scDREAMER, scVI, Harmony) and you need standardized, composite bio-conservation and batch-correction scores to rank them.

name: louvain-clustering-nmi-optimization
description: Use when evaluating integrated scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., scDREAMER vs. scVI/Scanorama/Harmony baselines) and you need per-method cluster assignments that are resolution-optimized before computing NMI, ARI, or ASW metrics.

name: louvain-clustering-of-control-cells
description: Use when a perturbation scRNAseq analysis requires reference cell-state labels from the control condition alone (scanpy neighbors + Louvain on control cells) before NCFS feature weighting and semi-supervised clustering.

name: louvain-clustering-of-embeddings
description: Use when a cell-level embedding matrix (e.g., scGAE latent representation of Splatter-simulated scenario3/4 scRNA-seq data) is available and discrete cell clusters must be recovered and scored by NMI.

name: louvain-clustering-of-simulated-trajectories
description: Use when an ensemble of simulated differentiation trajectories (from RNA-velocity Markov sampling) must be partitioned into sub-trajectory groups within each terminal state before DTW alignment and consensus construction.

name: louvain-community-clustering
description: Use when a scRNA-seq matrix (cells × features/PCs) has been reduced to a Sphetcher spherical sketch (indicator vector with sketch_size ones) and the sketched cells must be clustered into cell types.

name: louvain-community-detection-on-cell-graphs
description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized scRNA-seq object already carries variable features and PCA coordinates (e.g. PBMC3k with 25 PCs from 10-fold SVD cross-validation) and cell-population cluster labels are needed before marker-gene testing.

name: louvain-community-detection-on-gene-regulatory-networks
description: Use when you have a filtered differential GRN edge list (e.g., BoostDiff output post filter_network) and need to partition it into gene modules for pathway enrichment (gseapy Enrichr KEGG) or module-level interpretation.

name: louvain-community-detection-on-grn
description: Use when you have a weighted gene network (e.g. from scPRINT attention-based inference) and want to identify coherent gene modules for pathway/gene-set enrichment, as done for BPH fibroblast ion-exchange communities.

name: louvain-community-detection-on-single-cell-sketches
description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-sampling/sketching strategy (e.g., spherical thresholding vs. geometric/box sketching) preserves biological cell-type separability in large scRNA-seq datasets, by clustering sketched subsets and scoring against known cell-type labels.

name: louvain-graph-based-cell-clustering
description: Use when a Seurat object has been normalized (LogNormalize, scale factor 10,000) and PCA-reduced, and cell populations must be identified and later assigned labels (hepatocytes, endothelial cells, MAIT cells, GZMB+ GZMK+ NK cells, S100A12+ neutrophils).

name: louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when droplet-level counts (e.g., 10X sparse matrix from mouse brain snRNA-seq) have been filtered and converted to a Seurat object and you need data-driven clusters to detect residual debris/background droplets.

name: louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering step must discover data-driven cell groups from a PCA/KNN graph — e.g. generating I-clusters prior to scCAD's cluster decomposition or splitting clusters larger than R*n cells.

name: louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when QC-passed, SCTransform-normalized and integrated single-cell expression data needs unbiased cell-cluster identification prior to marker-based cell-type annotation.

name: louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when clustering cells from a log1p-normalized AnnData object into graph communities — e.g., defining control cell states prior to NCFS gene weighting, running sslouvain with fixed control labels, or clustering integrated embeddings to test whether a method detects perturbation-unique responses.

name: louvain-graph-clustering-of-gene-weights
description: Use when you have cohort-shared ICA gene z-weight vectors for independent components and need to collapse them into consensus, reproducible gene programs (meta-components) for downstream TME scRNA-seq annotation.

name: louvain-latent-space-clustering
description: Use when you have a MuData object with scConfluence latent embeddings in mdata.obsm['latent'] and need to discover subpopulations (e.g. memory/naive/plasma B cell subtypes in tri-omics PBMC data) that single-modality annotations miss.

name: louvain-purity-modularity-alpha-tuning
description: Use when running cell-attribute aware (EVA) community detection on a cell-cell nearest-neighbor graph and an optimal alpha must be chosen before attribute-aware clustering and downstream DA testing.

name: louvain-resolution-parameter-sweep
description: Use when comparing multimodal single-cell clustering methods on the same CITE-seq dataset and you need a fair resolution-matched comparison plus a resolution sweep to explain divergent subset recovery and time efficiency.

name: louvain-subpopulation-reclustering
description: Use when a biologically annotated cell subpopulation needs finer subdivision, and a low-dimensional embedding from scGAE (20-D latent space of scRNA-seq counts) is available; specifically to confirm substructure such as ≥2 subclusters within Ba/Eo/MaP cells.

name: louvain-two-group-iterative-reclustering
description: Use when CrossTimeAnnotation has assigned labels to t1 scRNA-seq cells but some cells may represent newly emerged cell types that the t0-trained neural network classifier would mislabel.

name: low-count-barcodes-recovery-filtering
description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq raw unfiltered count matrix (h5 or mtx) has been filtered by a total-count cutoff and you suspect real low-count cells (e.g., platelets) were discarded.

name: low-detection-gene-count-filtering
description: Use when preparing a counts matrix (e.g. 10x Visium spatial data or scRNA-seq) as input to haystack() and you need to eliminate very lowly expressed genes before running the DEG search.

name: low-dimensional-embedding-cell-ordering
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g. mouse embryo datasets Yan, Goolam, Deng) already have a scDHA low-dimensional representation and the goal is a developmental pseudo-time ordering whose accuracy can be scored as R-squared against known capture/stage time.

name: low-dimensional-embedding-construction
description: Use when two denoised, same-gene-set GRN adjacency matrices (e.g., sparse dgCMatrix networks X and Y from CP tensor decomposition) must be aligned into a shared low-dimensional space to compare each gene's regulatory positions across conditions.

name: low-dimensional-embedding-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple processing batches and you need pseudotime/trajectory inference on an embedding that suppresses technical batch differences (e.g. DESC X_Embeded_z feeding Monocle3).

name: low-dimensional-embedding-visualization
description: Use when comparing 2D embeddings of scRNA-seq count matrices across methods (EDGE vs UMAP vs t-SNE), especially to assess separation of rare cell types against dominant populations.

name: low-dimensional-representation-learning
description: Use when high-dimensional raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) with technical noise and dropout need to be compressed into a low-dimensional cell representation for clustering, visualization, classification, or trajectory analysis.

name: low-expression-gene-filtering
description: Use when running the scdrake single-sample pipeline on a droplet scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. 10x Cell Ranger output like PBMC 1k) and the gene dimension needs trimming before normalization and HVG selection.

name: low-expression-gene-prefiltering
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell FPKM/TPM expression matrix contains genes expressed (>5 FPKM/TPM) in fewer than two cells, and genes must be filtered before z-score normalization and clustering.

name: low-expression-transcript-recovery-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking a genome-guided transcriptome assembler (e.g. Tiglon vs StringTie2/Scallop) on RNA-seq alignments and you must show whether gains come specifically from recovering lowly expressed reference transcripts.

name: low-read-support-umi-filtering
description: Use when quantifying mutant gRNA molecule fractions in a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library and sequencing-error-derived molecules must be excluded before variant calling.

name: low-sequencing-depth-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when quantifying how a fusion caller's sensitivity degrades with shallower bulk or single-cell RNA-seq depth, e.g. testing detection limits on CCLE bRNA-seq subsampled below 1 million read pairs.

name: low-variance-gene-filtering
description: Use when preparing gene-by-sample expression matrices for differential network inference and the feature space is large relative to sample size — filter by per-gene variance (here a cutoff of 0.4) before running BoostDiff or similar tree-based methods.

name: lr-pair-database-mapping
description: Use when screening ligand-receptor pairs from a curated LR database against pseudotime-ordered scRNA-seq trajectories to identify co-varying LR pairs in temporal developmental data.

name: lrp-based-differential-gene-ranking
description: Use when scMDC (or a similar pretrained deep clustering model) has produced cluster assignments on single-cell multi-omics data and you need per-cluster marker genes or pathway-level enrichment from a directed gene rank.

name: lsi-dimensionality-reduction-scatac
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq fragment files (BAMMC-style fragments, hg19/hg38/mm9/mm10) must be converted to an ArchR arrow file, QC-filtered, peak-called with MACS2, and reduced to a low-dimensional LSI representation for clustering and UMAP embedding.

name: luad-therapeutic-candidate-verification
description: Use when a ranked RS-GSFM drug retrieval list for LUAD/A549 is available and you must confirm that perhexiline appears among the top-ranked reversal-score compounds, consistent with the paper's LUAD candidate identification.

name: lung-atlas-label-transfer
description: Use when integrating competing cell-atlas annotation labels from multiple lung scRNA/snRNA studies onto one base dataset, and when benchmarking integrated annotations against independent references (Azimuth CellRef, HLCA).

name: lung-cancer-subtype-classification
description: Use when you have TCGA LUAD and LUSC bulk RNA-seq expression matrices and want to classify lung cancer subtype from differentially abundant tumor microenvironment cell types rather than raw gene expression.

name: lupus-nephritis-cluster-profiling
description: Use when measuring how robust ICELLNET communication scores between lupus nephritis clusters (CM3 dendritic cells vs CT0a/CT3b T cells) are to random cell subsampling, i.e. when cluster size may inflate or destabilize inferred communication.

name: m5c-site-sequence-context-enumeration
description: Use when balanced m5C-positive/negative RNA fragment sets must be compared for position-specific nucleotide enrichment around a candidate cytosine, e.g., to test whether m5C sites carry distinctive flanking motifs before encoding features.

name: m6a-benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Use when reconstructing or reproducing the 11 species-tissue m6A benchmark datasets (e.g., h_b, h_k, m_t, r_k) from Zhang et al. antibody-independent m6A calls, or when preparing 41-nt RNA segments for CNN training/testing.

name: m6a-colocalization-visualization
description: Use when you have RgnTX permutation-test results linking m6A sites to stop codon regions and need to determine whether enrichment is localized at the original region positions or is an artifact, by examining the shifted z-score profile.

name: m6a-methylation-site-enrichment-testing
description: Use when genomic region sets such as miCLIP-seq m6A sites lack isoform annotation and you need a permutation test of their association with transcriptome features (e.g. stop codons) under a transcriptome-wide null model.

name: ma-plot-quality-assessment
description: Use when microarray intensity data (e.g., Illumina Bead array exports in a tab-separated file like example_unnorm.txt) need normalization-method selection and QC: compare quantile vs LOESS normalization via MA plots and check for batch effects via sample clustering.

name: machine-learning-classifier-power-evaluation
description: Use when assessing whether a trained CLOUDe classifier retains high power (fraction of correctly predicted Redundant/Unique labels) on new OU-simulated test data, including robustness checks under alternative evolutionary scenarios such as a distinct ancestral optimum theta0.

name: machine-learning-genomic-sequence-classification
description: Use when you need to identify expressed, sample-specific polyadenylation sites from genome-aligned RNA-Seq (sorted BAM) plus DNA sequence, especially de novo proximal APA isoforms that standard assemblers like StringTie miss at 3' terminal exons.

name: machine-learning-model-selection-and-hyperparameter-application
description: Use when building clinical outcome prediction models from cross-platform transcriptome datasets (RNA-seq trained, microarray transferred), when comparing multiple ML model types, or when needing quantile-normalized transfer learning between platforms.

name: machine-learning-model-training-polya-sites
description: Use when building a custom polyA-site prediction model from DNA sequence plus RNA-Seq coverage for a sample-specific transcriptome, or when ablation-testing feature sets (multi-omics vs DNA-only vs RNA-only).

name: machine-learning-noise-robustness-evaluation
description: Use when assessing robustness of a trained CLOUDe classifier (or similar expression-based ML classifier) by re-classifying noise-perturbed test feature sets and tabulating classification power versus noise level per method.

name: machine-learning-prediction-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a BAM file from PacBio long-read RNA-seq must be converted into predicted dsRNA regions with per-region probabilities, or when reproducing feature-importance (Skip_ratio 75.4%, Len_skip 15.9%) and cv_scores from the AD-trained model.

name: machine-learning-regression-across-architectures
description: Use when expression data for deletion events (3m-column absolute log10(x+1) format) is available and per-event continuous evolutionary parameters must be estimated and compared across multiple machine learning regressors rather than classified.

name: machine-readable-assay-specification-parsing
description: Use when raw single-cell FASTQ reads must be preprocessed and the read structure (barcode/UMI/cDNA positions and strand) must be derived from an assay specification file rather than hand-written for a specific chemistry.

name: macro-f1-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-type label predictors on a single-cell classification benchmark and you need comparable accuracy and macro-F1 per method across fine-grained and coarse ontology label levels.

name: macro-f1-and-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-type label-transfer or integration methods on scRNA-seq data and you need quantitative annotation metrics (macro F1, accuracy) plus integration metrics (silhouette, batch entropy) with statistical significance testing.

name: macro-f1-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking cell type classifiers on a large cross-tissue scRNA-seq corpus and you need macro F1-scores comparable to scTab (0.8295±0.0007), linear (0.7848±0.0001), XGBoost (0.8127±0.0005), and MLP (0.7971±0.0012).

name: macro-f1-class-imbalance-evaluation
description: Use when scoring cell type annotation predictions on heavily class-imbalanced single-cell datasets (e.g. 164 cell types, 22.19M cells) where accuracy would be dominated by abundant types and ontology subtypes should count as correct.

name: macro-f1-multiclass-classification-evaluation
description: Use when a semi-supervised single-cell label-prediction experiment has trained cell-type classifiers on partially annotated data and you need a balanced metric that weights rare and abundant cell types equally.

name: macrophage-marker-gene-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when validating that a cell sketch (e.g., a 20,000-cell Sphetcher-H sketch of the 254,941-cell umbilical cord blood dataset) preserved a rare cell population by scoring a candidate cluster against known marker genes.

name: macrophage-marker-gene-interpretation
description: Use when scNovel's query stage has flagged cells as novel (score > lambda = 0.5) and Leiden clusters of those novel cells need to be named by checking marker expression such as CD163.

name: macrophage-subtype-differential-pathway-analysis
description: Use when novel/rare macrophage subclusters have been identified in a COVID-19 scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., via scNovel on GSE171524) and you need to determine which GO pathways are significantly up- or downregulated in COVID versus healthy samples.

name: macrophage-subtype-prioritization-in-myocardial-infarction
description: Use when ranking diseased cell subpopulations by responsiveness to a drug from untreated scRNA-seq data — e.g. identifying the tanshinone IIA-responsive macrophage M∅-5 subpopulation in myocardial infarction — and prioritizing target genes beyond the known direct target.

name: macrophage-to-malignant-transition-marker-verification
description: Use when verifying transition-marker genes (e.g. CSF1R) between microglia/macrophage and malignant cell populations in glioma scRNA-seq using redPATH dCor/MIC statistics along pseudotime.

name: macs2-accessible-peak-calling
description: Use when processing scATAC-seq fragments (e.g., BMMC dataset) after QC/doublet filtering and a peak-by-cell count matrix is needed before iterative LSI and Louvain clustering in the SCALA/ArchR pipeline.

name: macs2-broad-peak-calling
description: Use when the analysis goal is to identify regions of significant read enrichment from BAM-format aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium 3' end-enriched signal) as candidate features, prior to downstream filtering or annotation.

name: macs3-peak-calling-qvalue-thresholding
description: Use when constructing a trustworthy feature space (peaks and non-peaks) from a scATAC-seq BAM file, or when peaks of differing confidence are needed for count-matrix construction or simulator training.

name: mada-domain-adaptation-pretraining
description: Use when merging multiple scRNA-seq reference datasets sequenced on different platforms and batch effects must be removed before training a cell-type annotation model or fine-tuning on query data.

name: mae-pcc-correction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when you have simulated technical dropouts (e.g., UMIs of marker genes subsampled to 50/100/200 counts) plus un-subsampled ground-truth expression, and you need to quantify and compare how well correction methods (e.g., SpatialScope vs Tangram) recover the true spatial expression profiles.

name: maf-file-processing-with-maftools
description: Use when mutation information is provided as a standard .maf file (e.g., TCGA LUAD) and you need per-gene mutation significance between groups (p-value, FDR) or mutation visualization such as forest plots and oncoplots.

name: magic-dropout-correction-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics count matrices contain dropout artifacts and must be smoothed prior to GAN-based cross-domain alignment or clustering pipelines.

name: magic-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when an scRNA-seq count matrix fed into the scDrug pipeline is too sparse/noisy for reliable clustering and the analyst opts into imputation via the --impute flag; default behavior is no imputation.

name: mahalanobis-distance-cluster-reassignment
description: Use when a marker-count-based annotation leaves cells 'unassigned' by a rejection threshold, and you want to recover labels by exploiting clustering structure (PCA + GMM clusters) with within-cluster expression similarity.

name: mahalanobis-distance-mapping-metrics
description: Use when a Symphony-mapped query may contain cell types missing from the reference and you need quantitative per-cell or per-cluster scores (with AUC evaluation) to flag unmapped/novel populations.

name: mahalanobis-like-between-cluster-distance-computation
description: Use when you have cell-to-cluster assignments plus a low-dimensional SingleCellExperiment embedding and need between-cluster distances that account for within-cluster covariance, to build an MST cluster topology.

name: mait-nkt-cell-population-visualization
description: Use when visualizing consensus clustering results on a CITE-seq embedding to highlight a specific minor cell population (e.g. MAIT-NKT cells) and reproduce the paper's Figure 3 / Supplementary Fig. S3.

name: major-minor-cell-type-label-splitting
description: Use when benchmarking a single-cell clustering method against curated cell-type annotations and you need to assess performance at both coarse (major) and fine-grained (minor) label granularity, e.g. resolving rare populations like MAIT-NKT cells.

name: majority-vote-ensemble-aggregation
description: Use when a single cell must be labeled malignant vs non-malignant from scRNA-seq expression and multiple base classifiers (one per training dataset) have produced per-cell predictions that need to be combined into a final consensus label.

name: majority-vote-sample-level-label-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-cell classification predictions across a sample and need a single sample-level call (e.g. predicted primary origin of a metastatic biopsy) from the majority cancer-cell annotation.

name: malat1-nuclear-localization-qc
description: Use when comparing droplet-filtering methods (e.g. DIEM debris-cluster mode vs EmptyDrops) on a 10x feature-barcode matrix and you need a quantitative extranuclear-contamination readout (MALAT1% alongside MT%) for kept vs removed droplets.

name: malignancy-probability-interpretation
description: Use when you have staged scRNA-seq expression matrices (.h5ad) from a cancerous epithelial lineage and want to test whether predicted malignancy increases with progression stage, rather than performing a one-off malignant/normal classification.

name: malignant-cell-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a new or existing malignant-cell annotation method outperforms CNV-based and machine-learning baselines on scRNA-seq tumor microenvironment datasets.

name: malignant-cell-classification
description: Use when annotating a tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq dataset where malignant cells must be identified but no confident internal reference malignant cells exist within the sample, or when testing whether the classifier generalizes to a cancer type (e.g. lung, gastric) held out of training.

name: malignant-cell-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying whether swapping a classifier's default gene signatures/training data for a signature-calibrated reference improves malignant-vs-normal cell identification accuracy on benchmark scRNA-seq datasets.

name: malignant-cell-communication-analysis-melanoma
description: Use when analyzing predicted ligand-receptor interactions from a tumor scRNA-seq dataset from the viewpoint of a specific malignant-cell population, and you need functionally grouped interaction modules (int-pair modules) rather than a flat interaction list.

name: malignant-cell-compartment-designation
description: Use when an annotated cancer scRNA-seq object (e.g., Seurat object from scWizard cell annotation) must be partitioned into malignant epithelial versus non-malignant compartments using inferred copy-number alterations.

name: malignant-cell-identification-scrna-seq
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a tumor sample (e.g., glioblastoma, lung adenocarcinoma) must be screened for aberrant/malignant cells and marker-based annotation must be compared to CNV-inference baselines.

name: malignant-cell-label-calibration
description: Use when building or cleaning a malignant-vs-normal training set for cancer scRNA-seq cell annotation — i.e., when 'Malignant'/'Tumor' labels from original studies may be noisy and curated cancer gene signatures are available to validate them.

name: malignant-cell-marker-gene-curation
description: Use when building malignant vs non-malignant cell classification features from annotated cancer scRNA-seq datasets, or when a pan-cancer marker gene set common across multiple tumor types is needed.

name: malignant-vs-nonmalignant-cell-classification
description: Use when you have a raw gene-by-cell count matrix from an individual patient/biopsy tumour sample and need per-cell malignant vs non-malignant (or detailed TME cell-type) annotations across the pan-cancer hierarchy.

name: mammalian-corticogenesis-temporal-biology
description: Use when a developmental-series scRNA-seq time course (e.g., GSE153164 corticogenesis spanning E12.5–E17.5) must be grouped into temporal expression clusters of L-R pairs to identify key time points.

name: mammalian-phenotype-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have mouse gene clusters/modules (e.g., gene co-expression GEPs) and need to test which MP phenotype terms are significantly over-represented, reporting enrichment ratios and adjusted p-values per module.

name: manifold-constraint-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when scKINETICS velocity outputs must be stress-tested against variation in the manifold-constraint parameter sigma or against noise injected into the coexpression prior A^, with all other inputs held fixed.

name: manifold-learning-of-signaling-networks
description: Use when comparing inferred signaling networks across two conditions (e.g., E13.5 vs E14.5 embryonic skin, lesional vs nonlesional AD skin) and you need to cluster pathways by functional similarity and rank up/downregulated signaling by differential information flow.

name: manifold-mixup-synthetic-pair-generation
description: Use when bimodality testing (bimodality coefficient or Hartigan's dip test) has confirmed novel cell types in target scRNA-seq data and cells must be split into known vs. unknown groups without a manually chosen E-score threshold.

name: manifold-mixup-threshold-estimation
description: Use when a source-free scRNA-seq annotation model's E-score distribution is judged bimodal (bimodality coefficient or Hartigan's dip test), and you must split target cells into known vs. unknown (novel-type) groups without a manually chosen cutoff.

name: manifold-parameter-extraction-from-gedi-model
description: Use when a fitted GEDI model (RDS file, e.g. from Zenodo accessions 8222040/8222698) must be converted into per-sample feature matrices for UMAP embedding of sample variability or cross-cohort SVM prediction of sample labels.

name: mann-whitney-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when you have per-sample small RNA-seq read-count files (tab-delimited, RNA molecules as rows, samples as columns) from COMPSRA's Annotation Module and need case-vs-control differential expression p-values per RNA.

name: mann-whitney-group-comparison-testing
description: Use when a continuous per-cell score such as ORIGINS2 PPIN activity must be compared between two cell-type-labeled groups (e.g., basal vs L2) with a non-parametric two-sided test, or when testing whether a significance call depends on a network-construction choice.

name: mann-whitney-u-group-comparison
description: Use when testing whether a SenePy sp_score (or similar cell-level score) differs between two independent sample groups — e.g., COVID-19 decedents vs controls — after aggregating per-cell scores to per-sample means with small, non-normal samples.

name: mann-whitney-u-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing a non-normally distributed continuous variable (e.g., predicted |theta1−theta2| from CLOUDe .predictions files) between two groups (Redundant vs Unique deletion classes) without assuming normality.

name: mann-whitney-u-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing a continuous, non-normally distributed variable (e.g., mutation counts, CNA burden) between two independent sample groups, such as CMS1 vs CMS2 colorectal cancer PDX subtypes.

name: mann-whitney-u-statistic-computation
description: Use when computing per-cell gene signature scores from a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (sparse matrix, SingleCellExperiment, or Seurat object) via rank-based Mann-Whitney U statistics, or when reimplementing/porting UCell's scoring mechanism.

name: mantel-test-distance-matrix-correlation
description: Use when comparing a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. ivis or t-SNE of CyTOF data) against the original high-dimensional space to test whether distances between manually annotated cell-population centroids are preserved.

name: manual-annotation-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when you have manually annotated cell borders for multiplexed imaging TMA cores and need to quantify how closely an automated segmentation (MIRIAM, Mesmer, Voronoi, or marker-subset variants) matches them.

name: manuscript-result-reproduction-scripting
description: Use when a task asks to verify or reproduce specific reported numerical results (e.g. cluster-purity scores) from a paper whose package and reproduction scripts are publicly available on GitHub.

name: map-inference-of-count-generative-models
description: Use when fitting count-based generative topic models (e.g., MIRA RP models) to single-cell multiome data and you need to compare model fit — via held-out log-likelihood — across single-batch vs multi-batch training, with or without technical effect correction.

name: mapping-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset carries free-text cell type annotations that must be converted to Cell Ontology terms, and you need to verify the text-to-ontology mapping accuracy before trusting downstream annotation.

name: mapping-quality-filtering
description: Use when cells have been projected into a reference UMAP space via ProjectSVR (ref.umap reduction with map-quality metrics attached) and you must retain only well-mapped cells before label transfer, pseudotime prediction, or cross-condition composition comparisons.

name: mapping-shift-distance-quantification
description: Use when quality-filtered, UMI-clipped FASTQ reads have been aligned with multiple aligners and you need to test whether reads sharing a UMI map to closely spaced, distinct genomic coordinates (the mapping shift artefact).

name: marchenko-pastur-distribution-fitting
description: Use when a sparsity-filtered cell-gene expression matrix is available and you need to identify the bulk eigenvalue spectrum predicted by random matrix theory so that departures (localized eigenvectors, outlier eigenvalues) can be read as signal.

name: marchenko-pastur-distribution-fitting
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq count data (log normalization with L=1, gene scaling, L2 normalization) and needing a data-driven signal/noise threshold from the eigenvalue spectrum of the cell similarity matrix, without subjective dimension selection.

name: marginal-correlation-screening-fnr-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether marginal-correlation (SPC-style) feature screening can recover predictive genes in a high-dimensional transcriptomic dataset (p >> n), by benchmarking its false negative rate against a pseudo-true coefficient vector.

name: marginal-histogram-density-plotting
description: Use when a deep dive into the relationship between exactly two features (e.g., RNASEH2A vs PCNA) is needed, requiring regression fit, Pearson correlation, and marginal density visualization on log2-transformed data.

name: marginal-resampling-null-embedding
description: Use when you need a biologically realistic null expectation for embedding quality (EMBEDR p-values) from single-cell omics data such as Tabula Muris scRNA-seq, before fitting data and null embeddings with a DRA like t-SNE or UMAP.

name: marker-based-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when Cell BLAST annotation transfer must be validated quantitatively (target MBA such as 0.873) or when unassigned/rejected query cells need confirmation as a novel cell type via marker gene enrichment.

name: marker-based-auc-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when a clustering (e.g., Louvain on a Sphetcher sketch) should be validated against a known rare cell type for which canonical marker genes are available, to quantify recovery of that population.

name: marker-based-bulk-decomposition
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix and a marker gene list (gene, cluster, optional fold-change weight) per cell type, but no scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference profile to decompose cell-type composition trends.

name: marker-based-cell-type-abundance-estimation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples need cell-type proportion/abundance estimates but no matched scRNA/snRNA-seq reference exists, and a validated marker gene list for the tissue's cell types is available.

name: marker-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating a scRNA-seq count matrix from a marker gene list — top 5 or 15 genes per cell type derived with Seurat, or canonical markers from PanglaoDB/CellMarker/CancerSEA — and no labeled training expression matrix is used.

name: marker-based-cell-type-assignment
description: Use when you have a log-normalized Seurat object of single-cell (snRNA-seq/RNA-seq) expression, a YAML marker file, and need a balanced subsample of cell IDs for manual or classifier labeling.

name: marker-based-cell-type-decomposition
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq cohort needs cell-type proportion estimates but no matched single-cell reference profile exists and only cell-specific marker genes (with weights such as avg_logFC) are available.

name: marker-based-cell-type-identification
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq cells or clusters with only external marker lists (no annotated reference), and you need conservative rejection of unknown cell types plus reassignment of uncertain cells.

name: marker-based-probabilistic-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when you need to annotate cell types in a scRNA-seq AnnData object without reference mapping — e.g., HGSOC adnexa/bowel samples — using marker gene sets and validating labels against an independent annotator such as CellAssign.

name: marker-centroid-reference-mapping
description: Use when aligning independent lung atlas annotations (GSE161383, GSE171524, GSE136831, EGAS00001004344) onto a base scRNA/snRNA dataset to feed competing reference classifications into scTriangulate.

name: marker-distance-profile-comparison
description: Use when you need to verify that MAPiT-transformed distance profiles of flow cytometry markers (e.g. DNA, RNA, Ki-67, p27) are robust to which markers are fed to the pseudotime algorithm, or when validating pseudotime-derived spatial arrangements against microscopy cross-sections.

name: marker-enrichment-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when FlowSOM clusters (e.g., 17 clusters on COVID-19 IMC data with 38 protein markers) must be visually validated against known marker biology to confirm cell-type identity after scMerge2 adjustment.

name: marker-enrichment-score-aggregation-per-cluster
description: Use when annotating unsupervised Seurat clusters of an scRNA-seq dataset with a marker database (e.g. ScTypeDB restricted to a tissue), requiring combined positive and negative marker scoring per cluster.

name: marker-enrichment-validation
description: Use when you have a ranked DEG list from scRNA-seq analysis and need to assess whether top-ranked genes are biologically meaningful by testing enrichment of known cell type marker genes by rank position.

name: marker-expression-based-cell-selection
description: Use when building the initial training set for active learning cell type annotation and a marker file (author-provided, data-derived, or PanglaoDB-derived) is available; especially beneficial when few cells will be labeled initially.

name: marker-expression-density-profiling
description: Use when validating a completed integration of CyTOF or similar single-cell datasets: you need to confirm dataset effects are removed by checking that per-marker density curves overlap across datasets while cell-type-specific marker expression is preserved.

name: marker-expression-overlay-visualization
description: Use when a spatial single-cell dataset (e.g., CODEX-exported .csv with x,y coordinates) has already been unrolled onto a linear structure and you need to visualize marker expression along organ length and wall thickness.

name: marker-expression-score-ranking
description: Use when converting per-cluster differential marker lists (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers output with Entrez IDs and scores) into ranked cell-type annotations, where significance-adjusted candidates must be ordered by marker expression significance.

name: marker-fidelity-roc-analysis
description: Use when you have hybrid cluster assignments from ClonoCluster at multiple α values and need to verify that cluster markers keep equivalent fidelity (median top-marker AUC) versus the α = 0 transcriptome-only baseline.

name: marker-file-preparation-panglaodb
description: Use when running marker-aware cell selection or active-learning initialization on scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq/CyTOF data and a marker gene set per expected cell type must be sourced, formatted, or validated.

name: marker-gated-cell-phenotyping
description: Use when the input is per-cell x/y coordinates plus multi-marker intensity values (e.g., MCMICRO output from a CyCIF whole-slide image in an AnnData object) and the analysis goal is to label each cell by marker-defined type (e.g., SOX10+ tumor cells) before spatial/region analyses.

name: marker-gene-annotation-of-cell-subclusters
description: Use when re-clustered scRNA-seq subpopulations must be biologically labeled by signature genes and their purity quantified with a quantitative statistic such as ROGUE before being trusted as subtypes.

name: marker-gene-auc-specificity-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell integrated/clustering result has interpretable gene modules (e.g. JOINTLY factors) and you need to test if module genes are more cell-type-specific than conventional marker genes, or to guide cell type annotation.

name: marker-gene-based-cell-type-classification
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., T/NK cells from BRCA/KIRC or myeloid cells from PAAD) needs cell-type/subtype annotation via a canonical marker-gene set, or when marker-based tools must be benchmarked against a learned classifier.

name: marker-gene-based-cell-type-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters have been identified (e.g., via robustSingleCell PCA/clustering on LCMV1/LCMV2 10X data) and need to be assigned biologically interpretable cell-type labels from a curated marker-gene panel.

name: marker-gene-based-cell-visualization
description: Use when IA-SVA (or similar SV analysis) has identified outlier cells via a surrogate variable, but standard all-gene visualizations (PCA, USVA, tSNE) fail to clearly separate those outlier cells in the embedding.

name: marker-gene-based-classification
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type label prediction on multi-batch scRNA-seq data, specifically to compare a marker/reference-database classifier such as CellTypist against zero-shot predictors using accuracy and macro-F1.

name: marker-gene-based-cluster-interpretation
description: Use when a re-clustering or clustering partition of scRNA-seq data (e.g. low-purity fibroblast clusters split by ROGUE) needs biological labels, and marker genes distinguishing subtypes such as myCAFs or antigen-presenting CAFs can be evaluated from the expression matrix.

name: marker-gene-based-confident-cell-selection
description: Use when building a labeled reference scRNA-seq training set for supervised TME cell subtype annotation and you need to filter cells down to those confidently belonging to T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, or Endothelial compartments.

name: marker-gene-branch-assignment
description: Use when you have an inferred branching trajectory over ~270 single-cell qPCR hematopoiesis cells (~170 transcription factors, six sorted populations) and need to quantitatively evaluate which branches correspond to marker-expressing lineages.

name: marker-gene-cell-fate-validation
description: Use when a trajectory-inference run has auto-detected terminal states that must be biologically labeled and validated, especially for rare populations like delta cells.

name: marker-gene-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a minor/rare cell cluster has been detected in a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. by GapClust on the 68k PBMC matrix) and must be annotated to a cell type via marker-gene expression (CD14, CD34) and benchmarked against GiniClust/FiRE.

name: marker-gene-collection-and-registration
description: Use when SINCERA cell types have been identified for a scRNA-Seq dataset and known positive/negative markers are needed as inputs to signature.prediction for cell type-specific signature prediction.

name: marker-gene-curation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression data must be decomposed into cell-type composition trends but no snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference profile exists and only cell-specific marker genes (gene, cluster, optional fold-change weight) are available.

name: marker-gene-database-annotation
description: Use when annotating clusters or cells in scRNA-seq or spatial (e.g., MERFISH) datasets from human or murine tissues, especially when marker-based annotation consistency and interpretability are needed.

name: marker-gene-database-matching
description: Use when you have cluster assignments from a scRNA-seq clustering method (e.g. scBGEDA) and need to assign biological cell-type identities by matching cluster DEGs to a curated marker gene database such as CellMark.

name: marker-gene-definition-vectorization
description: Use when you need a per-gene statistic that precisely matches the ideal marker-gene definition — a gene high in exactly one subtype and low in all others — across many subtypes in a batch-corrected expression matrix.

name: marker-gene-detection-cosine-similarity
description: Use when a batch-corrected gene/protein expression matrix with per-sample subtype labels is available and you need to identify subtype-specific marker genes across many subtypes, where one-vs-rest statistics (OVR t-test, Limma/EdgeR) yield inaccurate MG.

name: marker-gene-differential-expression
description: Use when a scRNA-seq query has been projected onto a reference atlas (e.g. murine TIL atlas) and you need subtype-level marker genes or perturbation-altered gene programs, such as KO-vs-WT shifts in Tnfrsf9/Ifng/Tcf7/Ccr7.

name: marker-gene-enrichment-code-scoring
description: Use when an AnnData with log-cpm normalised counts and over-clustered Leiden labels needs per-cluster marker genes and cell-by-cluster enrichment scores, e.g. to judge which cluster pairs are significantly different before merging.

name: marker-gene-expression-overlay-plotting
description: Use when you have a learned latent embedding (e.g. scMDC Z from CITE-seq data like BMNC or multi-batch SLN111) and need to visually verify cell-type separation, marker-gene concordance, and batch-effect removal.

name: marker-gene-expression-projection
description: Use when a PAGA-clustered single-cell reprogramming dataset needs visual validation that annotated clusters show expected marker enrichment, e.g., Apoa1 in iEP clusters and Col1a2 in fibroblast clusters.

name: marker-gene-expression-validation
description: Use when clusters have been assigned by SINCERA cluster.assignment and you must confirm predicted cell types are consistent with selectively expressed known marker genes before exporting assignments.

name: marker-gene-expression-validation
description: Use when BUSseq has been fit to scRNA-seq count data (e.g., the mouse hematopoietic study) and unknown clusters must be assigned biological identity via lineage marker genes and reference cell-type atlas correlations.

name: marker-gene-expression-visualization
description: Use when scRNA-Seq clusters or predicted cell type-specific signatures need quality assessment via known marker gene expression patterns, e.g. after cluster.assignment or signature.prediction in SINCERA.

name: marker-gene-expression-visualization-across-clusters
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices (raw vs imputed) must be compared at the cluster level by coloring t-SNE plots by cell type and overlaying curated marker genes (e.g., S100A8, FCER1A) to confirm subpopulation separation.

name: marker-gene-identification
description: Use when you need marker gene sets for Cell Ontology cell types — including types with no annotated cells in training data — from OnClass prediction matrices and single-cell expression data such as Tabula Muris Senis FACS.

name: marker-gene-identification-across-clusters
description: Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq matrix and need cluster-level marker genes free of pseudo markers (upregulated in multiple clusters) before automatic cell type annotation.

name: marker-gene-identification-for-immune-cell-populations
description: Use when an unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq data (e.g., k-means on PCs of PBMCs) yields clusters whose biological identities must be determined from cluster-enriched genes such as CD3D, NKG7, CD79A, S100A8/S100A9, PF4, FCER1A.

name: marker-gene-identification-via-rsq-regression
description: Use when an IA-SVA run has produced a significant surrogate variable (e.g., SV1 for 101 human alpha cells) and you need the marker genes driving that hidden factor for downstream interpretation.

name: marker-gene-list-validation
description: Use when a dimensionality-reduction/feature-selection method produces a ranked gene list that must be checked for biological plausibility against known cell-type markers before downstream use.

name: marker-gene-overlap-analysis
description: Use when a clustering method outputs per-cluster key genes and you must verify they are biologically meaningful by testing overlap with published cell-type markers and DEGs (|logFC| > 2, adjusted p < 0.01).

name: marker-gene-pair-cox-survival-regression
description: Use when you have bulk transcriptomic profiles (RNA-seq or microarray) with matched survival information and a cell-type marker set, and need to identify prognostic marker gene pairs as the basis for inferring cell-cell interactions in the tumor immune microenvironment.

name: marker-gene-pair-score-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a bulk transcriptomic profile (RNA-seq or microarray) plus a cell-type marker annotation and need expression-level pairwise relations as input to prognostic gene-pair analysis.

name: marker-gene-pairwise-comparison
description: Use when you have a cell-type marker gene list (e.g., scRNA-seq-derived T cell subtype markers) plus bulk RNA-seq/microarray data and need expression-level pairwise relations as input to survival modeling.

name: marker-gene-percent-expressing-aggregation
description: Use when validating scRNA-seq imputation on marker genes: you have a cell-by-gene normalized matrix (and optionally its imputed counterpart), cell-type labels, and need per-type percent-expressing fractions for genes like NCAM1 or CR2.

name: marker-gene-percentile-selection
description: Use when preparing positive/negative marker files for BIDCell training on spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Xenium breast cancer), or when defining cell-type markers by expression percentile cutoffs from a single-cell reference.

name: marker-gene-ranking-by-log2fc
