description: Use when Louvain/SNN cluster labels exist per cell and you must characterize each cluster by its top differentially expressed genes, e.g. to reproduce per-cluster marker depictions like the paper's Fig. 2E.

name: marker-gene-recovery-validation
description: Use when a redPATH pseudotime ordering exists for single-cell RNA-seq data and the goal is to discover and validate genes whose expression significantly associates with both cell proliferation and differentiation along the trajectory.

name: marker-gene-score-computation-from-rna-velocity-layers
description: Use when an AnnData annotated with DeepCycle's obs['cell_cycle_theta'] needs marker-gene-derived phase-transition landmarks (Cyclin E peak, G2M-vs-S crossover) to assign cells to G1, S, or G2/M.

name: marker-gene-selection-per-cell-type
description: Use when you have a pre-annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset and need to learn cell-type marker lists (with rejection thresholds) for downstream reference-based cell type identification instead of using a curated marker DB.

name: marker-gene-sensitivity-scoring
description: Use when NeuCA's hierarchical branch is triggered — off-diagonal Pearson correlations among cell-type mean profiles exceed tau = 0.95 — and test cells must be pre-assigned from highly sensitive markers before tree traversal.

name: marker-gene-set-preparation
description: Use when you need cell-type marker gene sets (positive and negative) from the ScTypeDB database restricted to a specific tissue type (e.g. 'Immune system', 'Liver', 'Eye', 'Brain') before running sctype_score or comparable marker-based annotation methods.

name: marker-gene-specificity-scoring
description: Use when harmonizing cell-type marker genes from multiple annotation sources (e.g., CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) and you need consistent, evidence-weighted marker scores for downstream cell type annotation.

name: marker-gene-test-statistic-implementation
description: Use when you have a batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression matrix with subtype labels and need to score genes by how closely their cross-subtype pattern matches an ideal marker gene (or an XOR-defined subtype-downregulated gene) profile.

name: marker-gene-top-rank-validation
description: Use when interpreting a trained single-cell classifier (e.g., scSHARP GCN) with DeepLIFT and you need to confirm the per-gene importance rankings recover known cell-type markers.

name: marker-gene-weight-assignment
description: Use when you have an upstream ranked marker list (e.g., MASI's marker_identification output) per cell type and need rank-discounted marker weights before computing a cell-type score matrix for annotation or integration.

name: marker-geneset-expression-quantification
description: Use when the analysis goal is to visualize spatial expression of specific marker gene sets at native sub-micrometer barcode resolution (e.g., Seq-Scope data with >1M barcodes/mm²), and you have an unaggregated digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates.

name: marker-gep-based-cell-label-transfer
description: Use when annotating cells in a novel single-cell dataset (e.g. TMS FACS) using pre-identified marker GEPs from a reference dataset (e.g. MCA) without cell clustering.

name: marker-informed-training-set-construction
description: Use when building a labeled training set for single-cell annotation without active learning, but prior knowledge of cell type marker genes (e.g. PanglaoDB markers) is available to guide sampling.

name: marker-intensity-correlation-analysis
description: Use when per-cell shape descriptors (autoencoder latent vectors) and per-cell marker quantifications from MIRIAM segmentation must be aligned cell-by-cell and tested for association, e.g. after t-SNE shows no obvious shape-marker patterns.

name: marker-list-curation-from-public-databases
description: Use when running marker-based cell type identification without a pre-annotated reference dataset and you must assemble cell-type marker lists from Panglao DB or CellMarker DB, choosing how many markers per type.

name: marker-pair-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq or microarray profile with matched survival (event + time-to-event) info and a cell-type marker geneset, and you need directed cell-cell interactions (FDR<0.05) plus per-cell prognostic favorability scores.

name: marker-panel-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when single-cell gene expression data (e.g. scRNA-seq, synthetic multimodal simulations) comes with cell type labels and the goal is to test whether jointly optimized marker panels recover labels better than one-vs-all gene-by-gene scoring.

name: marker-ranked-cell-sampling
description: Use when constructing an initial 10–40 cell training set for single-cell cell-type annotation and a marker gene file (positive/negative markers per expected cell type) is available to guide cell selection.

name: marker-recovery-benchmarking-against-ground-truth
description: Use when simulated or ground-truth-annotated single-cell TE expression matrices exist for multiple methods and you must quantify per-cluster marker recovery rates and log2(Fold Change) deviations, as in the SoloTE vs scTE Fig 3 comparison.

name: marker-score-computation
description: Use when a pre-annotated single-cell RNA-seq reference dataset (e.g. .h5ad count matrix with cell type labels) must be converted into per-cell-type marker gene lists and occurrence-frequency statistics before MarkerCount-based annotation.

name: marker-selection-from-single-cell-expression
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression data plus cell type labels (optionally a label hierarchy) and must choose a minimal gene panel that jointly discriminates the labels rather than testing genes one-vs-all.

name: marker-selection-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare how well different marker selection methods pick k gene markers from scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g., .h5ad from CITE-seq, Mouse Brain, Paul, Zeisel) by classification accuracy/f1 or by ℓ2/ℓ1 full-transcriptome reconstruction loss.

name: marker-selection-stability-analysis
description: Use when you need to compare the run-to-run stability of marker sets from phenotype-cover solvers (GreedyPC/CEMPC) against global methods (ReliefF, F values, mRMR) on multi-class scRNA-seq phenotype discrimination tasks.

name: marker-sensitivity-specificity-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing DE methods (e.g., CDI vs Wilcoxon) for cell-type-specific binary DEGs across scRNA-seq datasets, and you need DEG counts plus per-marker cluster-discriminating sensitivity/specificity benchmarking.

name: marker-specificity-scatter-visualization
description: Use when you have FlowSOM clusters (e.g. 17 clusters from the 23-sample COVID-19 IMC dataset with 38 protein markers) and must validate that clusters correspond to annotated cell types using marker-expression specificity plots.

name: marker-subset-ablation-analysis
description: Use when you need to test how the marker composition of multiplexed immunofluorescence TMA data affects segmentation quality — e.g., to justify which markers are mandatory for MIRIAM's membrane-driven cell-border reconstruction.

name: marker-table-validation
description: Use when a marker_5.csv or similar differential-marker table has just been generated from a training count matrix (e.g. GSE109774 liver 10x data) and must be verified before being passed to markersupervised methods.

name: marker-te-detection-in-disease-microglia
description: Use when scRNA-Seq from a disease-vs-control mouse model needs locus-level TE activity assessed in annotated cell clusters (e.g. DAM/microglia), beyond gene-level markers.

name: marker-vs-genotype-assignment-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq data from a mixture of two genotypically distinguishable cell populations and need to assign each cell to its genotype from transcriptome SNVs, then validate those assignments against marker-based cell classification.

name: marker-vs-random-gene-set-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a gene-set coordination or enrichment method's specificity: curated marker, mixed marker/random, and size-matched random gene sets are tested on real scRNA-seq data to confirm true sets rank highest.

name: markov-chain-coarse-graining
description: Use when a pre-processed N_cells x N_genes single-cell expression matrix must be reduced from cell-level random-walk dynamics to attractor-level (cluster-cluster) transition probabilities and soft membership assignments to quantify cell-fate transitions.

name: markov-chain-trajectory-sampling
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomics data (e.g., a Scanpy/scVelo-preprocessed AnnData with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field) must be converted into stochastic trajectories and fate probabilities toward defined terminal states.

name: markov-chain-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has reliable spliced/unspliced velocity estimates and the goal is trajectory inference across linear, circular, bifurcated, tree-like, or convergent topologies, especially where static-expression methods fail (e.g., cyclical cell-cycle patterns).

name: markov-chain-transition-probability-estimation
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be converted into stochastic differentiation trajectories and per-cell fate probabilities, especially when RNA velocity is noisy and a progenitor-defined differentiation potential gradient is available.

name: markov-clustering-coexpression-modules
description: Use when a weighted gene co-expression or GGM network (e.g., SingleCellGGM SigEdges from the MCA matrix) must be partitioned into gene modules/GEPs under the same MCL parameters across methods for fair comparison.

name: markov-clustering-gene-family-inference
description: Use when a large multi-genome protein set (e.g., Prokka-predicted proteins from thousands of RefSeq genomes) must be reduced to functionally coherent gene clusters and an absence/presence matrix for downstream comparative or machine-learning analyses.

name: markov-random-walk-transition-matrix-construction
description: Use when an scvelo-processed AnnData object with spliced/unspliced counts and a velocity field is available and root/terminal cell states must be identified (or supplied in supervised mode) before running Cytopath trajectory simulations.

name: markov-transition-matrix-normalization
description: Use when a pairwise affinity/similarity matrix over data points must be converted into a diffusion (random-walk) operator, e.g. before eigendecomposition for diffusion map coordinates in a geometry-preserving loss.

name: mars-seq-gene-expression-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw single-cell gene-count dataset (e.g., MARS-seq myeloid progenitor data with corrupted gene names) must be cleaned and shaped into an N×D expression matrix before DTFLOW trajectory or branch analysis.

name: masked-data-ground-truth-mse-evaluation
description: Use when comparing imputation methods (LATE, TRANSLATE, DCA, scVI, SAVER, MAGIC, ALRA, scImpute) on masked scRNA-seq data (e.g., example.msk90.hd5) with an unmasked ground truth available for error quantification.

name: masked-fully-connected-generator-construction
description: Use when building the GRouNdGAN/CausalGAN generator stack — instantiating per-target-gene masked generators from a pickled causal graph and pretraining the controller before the 1,000,000-step Wasserstein GAN training run.

name: masked-gene-to-pathway-embedding
description: Use when building an interpretable Transformer-based cell-type annotation model where input genes must be grouped into biologically relevant pathway tokens (from .gmt files such as GO_bp.gmt or reactome.gmt) before self-attention.

name: masked-input-encoder-construction
description: Use when constructing the basic scButterfly-B encoder/decoder stack for paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq translation and dropout noise must be denoised without data augmentation.

name: masked-neural-network-architecture-construction
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples) must be deconvolved into >400 cell-type abundances and an interpretable, marker-gene-masked network is needed instead of black-box deconvolution methods.

name: mass-action-signaling-probability-modeling
description: Use when inferring cell-state specific communication probabilities from scRNA-seq cell groups or continuous pseudotime states (e.g., E14.5 embryonic skin) and statistically testing which L-R pairs are significant.

name: mass-cytometry-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a clustering algorithm on mass cytometry data with known cell-type ground truth, or when comparing a new method to specialized cytometry clustering tools on the Levine15_13/Levine15_32/Samusik16 benchmarks.

name: mass-cytometry-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when a proteomic (CyTOF/mass cytometry) time-series single-cell dataset annotated with sampling-day labels needs pseudotime ordering, or when benchmarking whether lazy-teleporting MCMC (memory) improves pseudotime over TI baselines.

name: mast-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have an ICAT-processed AnnData with an ICAT-upweighted matrix (adata.obsm['X_icat']) and need to verify which weighted marker genes are differentially expressed between treatment groups.

name: master-regulator-analysis-with-rtn
description: Use when you need cell-type-specific master regulators (tTFs) from time-course scRNA-seq — e.g., to pair TF activity with inferred ligand-receptor signaling along an early-embryo developmental trajectory.

name: matched-bulk-single-cell-comparison
description: Use when matched single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices are available for the same cell population and the goal is to test whether bulk signalling entropy exceeds what random single-cell sampling would explain, i.e. regulated heterogeneity.

name: matched-case-control-expression-testing
description: Use when you need to test, edge by edge, whether knocking out a regulating TF via GRouNdGAN's --perturb mode significantly changes the expression of each gene it regulates in an imposed GRN.

name: matched-pairs-linear-regression
description: Use when a subset of individuals has both bulk RNA-seq and single-cell/scRNA-seq measurements (use.overlap=TRUE), so gene-specific bulk transformations can be learned from matched pairs before decomposition.

name: matched-tissue-accuracy-comparison
description: Use when quantifying how sample/tissue heterogeneity affects miRSCAPE cross-validation accuracy, e.g. comparing pooled multi-cancer TCGA training against tissue-specific or matched GTEx normal configurations.

name: matlab-python-pipeline-equivalence-testing
description: Use when a pipeline has dual implementations (e.g., Matlab and Python) and you must verify they yield similar segmentations on identical image inputs before deploying either version for downstream quantification.

name: matplotlib-categorical-plotting
description: Use when hyb-format records have already been evaluated with eval_types()/eval_mirna() and you need publication-ready categorical plots (pie/bar) of hybrid segment types or miRNA characteristics across qCLASH replicates.

name: matrix-block-computation
description: Use when screening endogenous reference genes over a large gene expression matrix (thousands of genes, e.g. GSE125792) and full-matrix pairwise computation would be too slow or depth-3+ screening risks no result.

name: matrix-decomposition-cell-cell-communication-inference
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data (exp.txt gene-by-cell matrix plus metadata.txt cell labels) for cell-cell communication in species beyond human/mouse, or when no prior L-R database should constrain the inference.

name: matrix-exponential-expression-dynamics-computation
description: Use when validating an inferred gene regulatory network (A matrix) by generating synthetic expression data — sample starting states x(0), propagate through the linear dynamics at known time points, add Gaussian noise (e.g. SD=5), and refit.

name: matrix-factorization-recommender-optimization
description: Use when you need to fit a latent-factor recommender model to a drug–cell-line response matrix (IC50 or AUC) and predict drug response from kernelized expression features, as in GDSC/PRISM pharmacogenomic modeling.

name: matrix-multiplication-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the runtime of dense matrix multiplication across R backends (%*%, RcppArmadillo, RcppEigen) with varying OpenMP core counts, or when justifying a faster backend for a computationally heavy R linear-algebra routine.

name: matrix-normalization-for-imputation
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Zeisel, Baron, Chen, La Manno downsampled matrices) is about to be imputed with ALRA or benchmarked against MAGIC/SAVER/DCA/scImpute and must first be library-normalized and log-transformed.

name: matrix-projection-filtering-of-single-cell-expression
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix carries an annotated nuisance signal (cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, batch, or healthy-vs-disease status) that must be removed at the gene expression level before downstream analysis.

name: matrix-row-normalization
description: Use when you have ST spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv) and need the normalized ground-truth adjacency matrix that STEM's predictors are trained to reconstruct from embeddings.

name: matrix-singularity-removal
description: Use when supplying a gene-by-geneset or TF-gene prior matrix (e.g., 'C_dorothea_tf_human.refined.rds') to a model like GEDI that requires a full-rank C, and singularity must be eliminated before model fitting.

name: matrix-sparsity-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you need to transform a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix into a pathway-by-cell activity score matrix via SVD (PC1 per pathway) and empirically verify that the pathway-level representation is less sparse than the gene-level matrix.

name: matrix-tri-factorization-retraining
description: Use when Leiden cluster labels are already available from the first-stage scMoMaT cell-factor KNN graph and you need per-cluster, per-modality marker scores (genes, ATAC regions, proteins) to annotate cell types.

name: matrix-trifactorization-cell-factor-training
description: Use when integrating multiple single-cell batches with partially missing modalities (mosaic scenario, e.g. scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq/protein with None placeholders) and you need a joint low-dimensional cell representation before clustering.

name: matthews-correlation-coefficient-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a binary transcript classifier (lncRNA vs. protein-coding transcript, lncRNA as positive class) on imbalanced five-species datasets and you need a single balanced metric, or when quantifying cross-species model transfer.

name: mature-mrna-region-shifting
description: Use when you have RgnTX permutation test results (e.g., m6A sites vs stop codon regions via permTestTxIA_customPick) and need to verify that the association peak sits exactly at the original ROI positions rather than reflecting generic 3'UTR enrichment.

name: maximal-information-coefficient-scoring
description: Use when gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrices and a redPATH pseudotime ordering are available and you need to rank genes by non-linear association with developmental/cancer trajectory, e.g. recovering CSF1R or Foxm1/Tubb5/Nek2.

name: maximum-likelihood-em-optimization
description: Use when inferring RNA velocity and latent time jointly from spliced/unspliced count matrices (AnnData) with a top-down dynamic model, especially when unified transcriptome-wide latent time or gene-specific time modes are needed.

name: maximum-likelihood-enrichment-estimation
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics for a trait are available together with binary functional annotations (e.g. sQTL vs expression-only variants) and you need to test whether associations are enriched in one annotation class via fgwas.

name: maximum-likelihood-under-order-constraints
description: Use when per-dose toxicity (or other monotone dose-response) proportions violate the increasing order constraint and you need monotonicity-constrained MLEs, e.g. isotonic DLT rate estimates for TSNP dose escalation decisions.

name: maximum-mean-discrepancy-computation
description: Use when benchmarking synthetic or simulated scRNA-seq data (e.g. from scGAN, Splatter, SUGAR) against a real reference dataset such as Fresh 68k PBMCs (Donor A) to quantify how close the generated distribution is to the real one.

name: maximum-mean-discrepancy-estimation
description: Use when comparing groups of cells as whole transcriptomic distributions (e.g., rexels from MERFISH spatial scRNAseq parcellization) so that spatial regions can be clustered or segmented on distributional rather than per-cell distance.

name: maximum-weight-bipartite-matching
description: Use when a set of uncontrolled free-text cell type annotations (synonyms, misspellings, abbreviations) must be converted one-to-one into Cell Ontology terms, and per-label nearest-neighbor retrieval alone may yield inconsistent or duplicated assignments.

name: maximum-weighted-bipartite-matching
description: Use when two single-cell modalities (scRNA-seq expression and scDNA-seq copy number) must be matched cell-to-cell or cell-to-clone with no ground-truth correspondence, i.e., the cell association problem.

name: mbic-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when fitting iSC.MEB to multi-sample SRT data and the number of spatial clusters K is unknown — e.g. grid-searching K=16:19 on six seqFISH embryo sections and picking the MBIC-minimizing K with c_penalty=0.2.

name: mca-cell-gene-coembedding
description: Use when starting any GSDensity pathway-centric analysis on a normalized cell-by-gene matrix (scRNA-seq or ST) — the MCA co-embedding is the required first step before compute.kld or compute.nn.edges.

name: mcc-based-confusion-matrix-evaluation
description: Use when a binary sequence classifier (e.g. lncRNA vs protein-coding transcript) produces probability scores on a test set and you must compute MCC and companion metrics against published benchmark values.

name: mcc-f1-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking lncRNA identification methods (or any binary sequence classifiers) on the human/mouse/zebrafish sORF test datasets and you need MCC/F1 values to compare against a published reference table (e.g. Tables 8–9, S12–S14 of LncCat).

name: mcl-graph-clustering-of-protein-networks
description: Use when you have an edge list of protein-protein functional associations (interactions given in both directions) and need to detect functional modules/communities for subsequent enrichment analysis in Cytoscape stringApp.

name: mcl-inflation-parameter-tuning
description: Use when a comparative-genomics pipeline needs proteins grouped into similar-function gene clusters to build an absence/presence matrix, and the Markov clustering inflation value must be selected and justified.

name: mcl-network-module-clustering
description: Use when a SingleCellGGM GGM network (e.g., MCA_GGM with 127,229 gene pairs or MouseBrain_GGM with 73,786 pairs) must be clustered into gene co-expression modules (GEPs) for enrichment analysis or cell-type annotation.

name: mclust-automated-scribble-generation
description: Use when running the ScribbleDom pipeline without expert-drawn manual_scribble.csv input, or when reproducing AutoScribbleDom baselines (e.g., melanoma ARI 0.74, breast cancer bcdc_ffpe ARI 0.83) on Visium or ST data.

name: mclust-em-algorithm-parameterization
description: Use when you need to model the distribution of dsb step-I ambient-corrected ADT values within each single cell as a Gaussian mixture and pick the number of components (k) per cell via BIC.

name: mcmc-based-bayesian-mixture-modeling
description: Use when clustering raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (each a genes x cells matrix in a list) where individual-level heterogeneity/batch effects exist, or when a trained model must predict cluster labels for held-out cells via a training-proportion split.

name: mcmc-based-hyperparameter-inference
description: Use when Canopy2 requires the 1 x M alpha and beta hyperparameter vectors and single-cell expression counts are available for the mutation-host genes (e.g., the featurecounts.qc slot of GBM10_preproc).

name: mcmc-based-spatial-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of spatial transcriptomics clustering methods (e.g. iSC.MEB vs MCMC-based BASS/BayesSpace) across multiple tissue sections and a sequence of K cluster numbers.

name: mcmc-convergence-diagnostics
description: Use when running get_trees() MCMC sampling in Canopy2 across a Klist of subclone counts and you must verify chain mixing and convergence before get__tree() selects the minimum-BIC configuration.

name: mcmc-gibbs-sampling-inference
description: Use when you need per-gene or per-cluster kinetic parameter distributions (kon, koff, s) estimated from real scRNA-seq count data to parameterize a two-state transcription bursting model, e.g. for SymSim simulation inputs.

name: mcmc-hyperparameter-configuration
description: Use when running Bfimpute on scRNA-seq count matrices and you must set or tune the MCMC factorization settings (D, totalepoch, burnin, threshold, sn_init/sn_max, priors) to reproduce published benchmarks or trade accuracy vs. compute time.

name: mcmc-lineage-refinement
description: Use when you need to reproduce or unit-test VIA's pseudotime computation and forward-biased MCMC lineage refinement on a PARC cluster graph (e.g. mESC CyTOF cell-cycle data) with explicit x_lazy/alpha_teleport settings.

name: mcmc-prior-estimation-single-cell
description: Use when analyzing allele-specific expression (ASE) from scRNA-Seq allele counts (e.g., CAST×B6 F1 embryo data) and you need population-informed priors to overcome low per-cell coverage before assigning P/B/M expression states per gene per cell.

name: mcnemar-significance-testing
description: Use when two classifiers predict the same labeled sample set (e.g., DeepCC CMS labels vs RF/SVM/GBM/MLR on 13 independent CRC validation sets) and you need a paired significance test on error counts.

name: mcp-score-network-scoring
description: Use when you need to reverse engineer a gene regulatory network from a gene expression matrix (HDF5/CSV/EXP) and quantify network quality via AUPRC/AUROC against a ground-truth interaction file, especially at genome scale where speed matters.

name: mcri-index-computation-per-sample
description: Use when assessing whether knocking down a candidate circRNA regulator (RBP) alters global circRNA expression, given paired knockdown/control RNA-seq datasets with raw FASTQ files available from GEO/ENCODE.

name: mds-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when aggregating single-cell counts into sample x cluster x group pseudobulks (e.g., Kang PBMC IFN-β data) and you need a low-dimensional check that pseudobulk profiles separate by cell cluster and stimulation condition before/after running pbDS.

name: mean-absolute-deviation-computation
description: Use when you need a scalar, per-gene measure of how well synthetic scRNA-seq data from a generative model matches the univariate expression distributions of an original dataset, especially to expose failures such as unreproduced bimodal genes like CD74 in PBMC4k.

name: mean-average-precision-cell-type-retrieval
description: Use when benchmarking batch-effect correction or dimension-reduction methods on scRNA-seq dataset combinations and you need a retrieval-style metric of cell-type resolution (preservation of cell type relationships) alongside a dataset-mixing metric.

name: mean-dispersion-heteroscedasticity-correction
description: Use when preparing a QC-filtered 10X scRNA-seq count matrix for PCA/clustering and you need highly variable genes selected with mean-dependence of dispersion corrected via expression-level binning.

name: mean-dispersion-parameter-estimation
description: Use when simulating bulk RNA-seq count data with MOSim: a seed RNA-seq sample must be converted into per-gene mean/dispersion NB parameters so that simulated counts, DEG profiles (continuous/transitory induction, repression, flat), and regulator couplings are statistically consistent with real data.

name: mean-dropout-mean-variance-comparison
description: Use when a simulation anchored to a reference scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Kang PBMC control samples via ExperimentHub EH2259) must be validated for faithful reproduction of mean-dropout, mean-variance, and sample-to-sample variability characteristics.

name: mean-expression-binned-background-gene-sampling
description: Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes (AnnData) against a gene signature and you need an expression-matched background control instead of naive whole-transcriptome averaging, e.g. re-implementing or validating SenePy score_hub.

name: mean-initialization-of-missing-entries
description: Use when a sparse single-cell AS probability matrix contains NA entries from dropouts and a complete matrix is needed as the starting point for downstream distance-based imputation or clustering.

name: mean-variance-fit-assessment
description: Use when single-cell counts have been simulated from a real scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., the Cuomo et al.

name: measure-preserving-pseudotime-to-real-scale-transformation
description: Use when snapshot single-cell data have been ordered in pseudotime (e.g. by Wanderlust or DPT) and marker trajectories must be interpreted on a real time or spatial scale for which a true-scale cell density distribution is available.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: measure-preserving-transformation-calibration
description: Use when you have an nx1 vector of pseudotime values (from Wanderlust, Monocle or Diffusion Pseudotime) plus single-cell marker signals, and a theoretically or empirically known cell-density distribution on a true real-time or spatial scale that the pseudotime ordering must be mapped onto.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: measurement-noise-variance-estimation
description: Use when preparing droplet scRNA-seq counts for CTMM: individual-level or individual-by-cell-type measurement-noise variances must be quantified before fitting op.free_REML or ctp.free_REML models.

name: mec-signature-scoring-in-bulk-rnaseq
description: Use when you need to project a single-cell-derived MetaTiME signature onto bulk tumor RNA-seq (e.g. TCGA with clinical survival metadata) and test whether higher MeC expression associates with prognosis.

name: median-auc-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have ClonoCluster cluster assignments across a range of α values plus a count matrix and need to verify that hybrid clustering did not degrade top-marker sensitivity/specificity (AUC) relative to transcriptome-only clustering.

name: median-pvalue-inflation-calibration
description: Use when OTTERS Stage II output (testing.py) has produced per-gene TWAS Z-scores from multiple eQTL weight training methods that must be calibrated per method before ACAT-O aggregation, e.g. UKBB cardiovascular disease GWAS with eQTLGen-derived weights.

name: median-robustness-curve-visualization
description: Use when stress-testing a trajectory-level differential test against trajectory-inference errors — you have a simulated reference with true pseudotimes/lineage labels and want sensitivity to pseudotime noise and lineage misassignment.

name: median-split-patient-stratification
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression matrices with clinical metadata (survival time/status, radiologic response) are available and a single-cell-derived gene signature (e.g., NK-2 from scDist) must be validated for association with outcome.

name: median-summary-statistics-by-subgroup
description: Use when drug response (e.g., 5-FU IC50) is available per sample and samples carry subgroup labels (CMS1-CMS4 from CMScaller), and you need per-group median summaries plus a CMS4-vs-CMS1/2/3 comparison.

name: median-threshold-binary-classification
description: Use when you have per-cell gene set scores for two experimental conditions and want a simple median cut point to quantify whether a smoothing or scoring change improves binary label prediction.

name: median-threshold-feature-filtering
description: Use when a sequencing (NGS/RNA-seq) or microarray expression data frame contains low-abundance or background-noise features that would distort correlation analysis, and you need to filter them by median expression (e.g. medianthres=1) prior to transformation.

name: medium-constraint-customization
description: Use when running METAFlux FBA on bulk RNA-seq MRAS scores and you must choose between cell_medium, human_blood, a custom-edited medium file, or a no-medium free-exchange control (known to yield only ρ=0.15 on NCI-60).

name: medium-exchange-reaction-configuration
description: Use when running METAFlux on bulk or single-cell RNA-seq data and the model must be constrained to a defined nutrient environment (cell culture vs. human-derived samples), or when customizing which nutrients are available for uptake.

name: melanoma-axl-mitf-state-marker-analysis
description: Use when testing drug-resistance program mutual exclusivity in melanoma scRNA-seq, especially in proliferating samples where cell-cycle signal masks the AXL–MITF anticorrelation (e.g., reproducing Mel78 R = -0.02 → -0.43 shift).

name: melanoma-cancer-vs-normal-cell-entropy-contrast
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-Seq count matrix has malignant vs non-malignant (and cell-type) annotations and you need to test whether cancer cells show higher differentiation potency/signalling entropy than microenvironment cells, without feature selection or training.

name: melanoma-prognostic-t-cell-subpopulation-analysis
description: Use when bulk transcriptomic data with matched survival (e.g., TCGA SKCM06) must be dissected at T cell-subpopulation resolution using scRNA-seq-derived markers to compare prognostic associations of Tex subtypes.

name: melanoma-tumor-cell-fraction-analysis
description: Use when per-cell MPI labels for MEL1 tumor cells (from a getMPI reconstruction) are available and the goal is the overall proliferating (MPI = 1) tumor-cell fraction to verify against the reported 7.4%.

name: membership-matrix-variance-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking condition-associated key gene (CKG) detection on multi-condition scRNA-seq data and a baseline ranking from an NMF-based method with known condition-specific modules is needed, or when ground-truth CKG labels allow AUPRC/early-precision comparison.

name: membrane-extension-cell-separation
description: Use when segmenting single cells from multiplexed imaging data (e.g., multiplexed immunofluorescence of colorectal adenomas or MIBI breast carcinoma TMAs) where cells have internal or incomplete membranes that defeat dilation- or Voronoi-based segmentation.

name: membrane-extension-geometry
description: Use when watershed or pixel-classification-based cell segmentation has split columnar epithelial cells along internal membrane segments, and cells need re-segmentation by extending incomplete membranes geometrically.

name: membrane-mask-overlap-metric-computation
description: Use when two segmentation algorithms or two implementations of the same pipeline have been run on identical multiplexed imaging data and you need a numeric overlap metric (DSC/JSC) to demonstrate cross-implementation reproducibility of membrane masks.

name: membrane-secreted-ligand-classification
description: Use when inferring ligand-receptor cell-cell interactions from scRNA-seq and you need to distinguish membrane-ligand vs secreted-ligand mediated receptor interactions, e.g. because product-of-sum aggregation misses rare cell types like endothelial cells or OPCs.

name: membrane-segment-angle-computation
description: Use when a watershed label mask contains cells whose interior was partitioned by internal membrane pixel-classification segments — i.e. cells where internal membranes occupy more than 10% of the cell area — and single-cell re-segmentation is needed.

name: membrane-versus-secreted-ligand-weight-computation
description: Use when constructing a single-time-point cell-cell communication network from scRNA-seq data and you need to score L-R candidate edges differently depending on whether the ligand is membrane-bound or secreted.

name: memory-constrained-large-dataset-training
description: Use when an scRNA-seq count matrix is too large (~68,000 cells) for standard imputation tools and the goal is to run autoencoder-based imputation within available RAM, per the AutoImpute PBMC scalability protocol.

name: memory-constrained-pipeline-execution
description: Use when an scRNA-seq dataset is too large to fit in RAM (e.g. >0.6 million cells, >1 million cells) and annotation, feature selection, or DGE analysis must run under a fixed memory cap such as 128 GB.

name: memory-failure-diagnostics
description: Use when a large RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. tens of thousands of transcripts) makes a co-expression tool slow or prone to out-of-memory failure, and you need to characterize the scaling limit empirically.

name: memory-gene-identification-from-lineages
description: Use when you have a quality-controlled scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-to-lineage annotations (cellular barcodes or GEMLI-predicted lineages) and want to enumerate and categorize heritably expressed genes.

name: memory-gene-set-enrichment-assessment
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix must be reduced to the GEMLI memory-gene candidate set, or when testing whether a quantile-based mean/CV2 selection rule enriches for gene-expression-memory genes.

name: memory-profiling-of-r-packages
description: Use when you must quantitatively compare computational efficiency (elapsed runtime and RAM usage) of R-based single-cell tools on identical count-matrix inputs, e.g. reproducing a Table 1-style runtime/memory benchmark.

name: memory-runtime-cost-comparison-across-pipelines
description: Use when choosing an annotation pipeline for million-cell scRNA-seq datasets under hardware or budget constraints, and you need measured accuracy, memory, runtime, and cost trade-offs across tools.

name: memory-usage-profiling-of-single-cell-models
description: Use when comparing the scalability of scRNA-seq/TCR integration models across dataset sizes, or when planning GPU/RAM allocation for training on atlas-scale (>60k cells) single-cell multimodal data.

name: merfish-cortical-tissue-segmentation
description: Use when segmenting high-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. MERFISH human cortical tissue) into spatial regions by comparing neighborhoods as transcriptome distributions, not single cells.

name: merfish-gene-imputation-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare gene imputation accuracy on image-based ST (e.g., MERFISH mouse1_slice180, 254 genes) against a paired snRNA-seq reference by leaving marker genes out and computing MAE.

name: merfish-single-cell-pixel-aggregation
description: Use when benchmarking pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics deconvolution against known single-cell composition: single-cell MERFISH counts must be aggregated into simulated multi-cellular pixels with ground-truth cell-type proportions for RMSE/correlation evaluation.

name: merfish-spatial-transcriptomics-preprocessing
description: Use when the input is a spatial scRNAseq/MERFISH sample with a cell-by-gene count matrix plus (dims x cells) spatial coordinates, and the goal is to segment tissue into region-level pixels (rexels) before distributional comparison.

name: merfish-spatial-transcriptomics-preprocessing
description: Use when handling an imaging-based spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., MERFISH) that requires standard Seurat preprocessing and alignment of cell spatial coordinates to a anatomical reference before annotation or benchmarking.

name: mesoderm-differentiation-lineage-mapping
description: Use when a temporal scRNA-seq dataset of hESC mesodermal differentiation (e.g., the 'loh' dataset from scDatasets) needs a 2D trajectory visualization that separates somite and cardiomyocyte lineages within each time point.

name: meta-component-gene-weight-ranking
description: Use when a task needs the gene members of a specific MetaTiME MeC ranked by z-weight — e.g., to build a signature score from the top 20 genes of MeC-42 or a top-100 gene set for Lisa ChIP-seq TF analysis.

name: meta-component-projection-scrna-seq
description: Use when annotating cell types/states in tumor immune microenvironment scRNA-seq data at higher resolution and consistency than marker-based references (CIBERSORT, Azimuth, Human Primary Cell Atlas) allow.

name: meta-splice-site-merging
description: Use when a single-cell Nanopore isoform quantification (Splice object from sc_iso_count.rds) contains multiple alternative exons or splice sites per gene, and downstream Beta-Binomial inter-cell heterogeneity (phi) estimation requires them merged into meta-splicing sites.

name: metabolic-flux-balance-analysis
description: Use when you have a gene x sample RNA-seq matrix (human gene symbols as row names, normalized, non-negative) and need nutrient-aware metabolic flux estimates for 13082 reactions, e.g., glucose uptake (HMR_9034), pathway activity, or TME cell-type community fluxes.

name: metabolic-flux-interpretation-from-gene-expression
description: Use when a KEGG pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g. the 21-gene PLA2G4B node) and you need to identify the dominant enzyme, node-level regulation, and net metabolic flux from RNA-seq data.

name: metabolic-gene-set-curation-and-application
description: Use when analyzing metabolic pathway activity in single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., across T cell activation time points or pseudotime trajectory nodes — where combined metabolic gene sets and distribution-based qvals are needed rather than simple enrichment.

name: metabolic-labeling-scrnaseq-data-processing
description: Use when input is metabolic labeling scRNA-seq (scEU-seq h5ad like rpeLabeling.h5ad) with labeled/total/unlabeled counts and a labeling time, and you must prepare paired t0/t1 matrices for RNAForecaster forecasting.

name: metabolic-labeling-t0-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data come from a metabolic labeling assay (e.g., scEU-seq) with separate labeled, unlabeled, and total count matrices, and you need a t=0 expression estimate to train RNAForecaster on paired time points.

name: metabolic-model-essentiality-analysis
description: Use when you have context-specific metabolic models of infected vs. mock tissue (built via rFASTCORMICS from GEO datasets such as GSE147507/GSE148729) and need to enumerate essential genes or synergistic double-knockout gene pairs to prioritize drug targets.

name: metabolic-reaction-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have a normalized, non-negative gene x sample bulk RNA-seq matrix (or bootstrapped single-cell average-expression profiles per cell type) with human gene symbols as row names, and need reaction-level activity scores before flux estimation.

name: metabolite-identifier-harmonization-across-reconstructions
description: Use when an external biomass objective function (e.g. the VBOF from Renz et al., 2020) must be added to a generic reconstruction such as Recon2.04 or Recon3D_01 whose metabolite identifiers use a different namespace, before running FASTCC and exporting consistent infected/control SBML models.

name: metacell-construction-graining-level-sweep
description: Use when building metacells and you must choose a graining level: sweep the graining parameter across a dataset and measure purity/cell-type recovery to pick a level that preserves rare populations without fragmenting the analysis.

name: metacell-construction-tool-taxonomy
description: Use when reviewing or benchmarking metacell construction tools and you need to quantify how coarse or fine published metacell analyses were grained, or compare target metacell sizes across tools (MetaCell vs SuperCell, SEACells, etc.).

name: metacell-level-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when comparing cell-type abundance or gene mean expression between conditions using aggregated metacell profiles, and you must ensure metacell size weights are applied to avoid inflated type I/II errors.

name: metacell-partitioning-from-cell-similarity-graph
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large or sparse for robust per-cell statistics and you need disjoint groups of cells of the same biological state as input for downstream analyses (trajectories, cell typing, differential analysis at the metacell level).

name: metacell-projection-based-reduction
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large for standard metacell construction (time/memory limits at hundreds of thousands of cells), or when built metacells must be projected onto a single-cell UMAP/embedding for visualization and QC.

name: metacell-purity-quantification
description: Use when metacells have been constructed (SuperCell/SEACells backends) and you need to check whether each metacell corresponds to a single cell type, e.g. when tuning graining level or comparing datasets of differing complexity.

name: metacell-quality-metric-computation
description: Use when a constructed metacell partition must be quantitatively assessed for quality, especially when no cell-type annotations are available and a latent-space-independent metric (INV) is needed.

name: metagene-clustering-and-hallmark-enrichment
description: Use when a trained GeneVector embedding must be turned into interpretable gene modules and ranked against a directional vector (e.g., Vadnexa − Vbowel in HGSOC cancer cells) to identify Hallmark-enriched programs.

name: metagene-clustering-from-gene-vectors
description: Use when you have a trained GeneVector embedding (genes.vec) from scRNA-seq AnnData and need to discover co-regulated gene modules (metagenes) and test whether their per-cell module scores change across conditions or treatment timepoints.

name: metagene-periodicity-qc-around-start-stop-codons
description: Use when length-selected Ribo-seq alignments (e.g. 25-35 nt RPF BAM/BED files) and a GFF3 annotation are available and you must verify footprints reflect active ribosomes before differential analysis.

name: method-accuracy-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when you must compare the robustness of two cell-cycle/pseudo-time methods by down-sampling an annotated scRNA-seq matrix to fewer cells (e.g. n=10, n=30) or fewer genes and plotting median accuracy against sample size.

name: method-benchmark-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when two methods were compared on differently sized datasets and you must re-run both on the same cell count subsets to isolate true performance differences from dataset-size effects.

name: method-benchmark-fdr-tpr-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking DS analysis methods for multi-sample, multi-group scRNA-seq data against simulated ground truth, especially to compare FDR/TPR under local (per-subpopulation) vs. global BH p-value adjustment.

name: method-comparison-visualization
description: Use when multiple cross-modality translation methods have been run on identical data splits and you must aggregate their per-fold metrics (e.g., calculate_cluster_index outputs) into a comparative table and figure to test whether a proposed method outperforms baselines.

name: method-of-moments-polygenic-regression
description: Use when you need per-cell, pathway-level estimates of genetic association from GWAS summary statistics and a normalized single-cell Seurat object, e.g. to compute scPagwas.gPAS.score for trait-relevant cell identification.

name: method-ranking-table-generation
description: Use when a paper's claim of one method outperforming baselines must be reproduced: multiple cell-type identification methods are run on identical data and ranked by accuracy and F1-score in a comparison table.

name: method-runtime-profiling
description: Use when you need to quantify how a DEG prediction method's detection accuracy and computational cost scale with dataset size, using artificial single-cell datasets with known planted DEGs as ground truth.

name: methylation-pipeline-runtime-comparison
description: Use when estimating or reproducing the computational cost of methylR's ChAMP or minfi methylation array pipelines on the paper's test dataset under stated hardware constraints, e.g. to plan capacity or validate the tool.

name: methylation-to-pseudotime-assignment
description: Use when you have paired single-cell methylation and transcriptome data and want to map methylation rates onto an independently recovered cell cycle ordering, or reproduce Fig. 4d-style methylation curves along G1/S/G2-M.

name: metric-space-distance-thresholding
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells x genes/PCs) is too large for downstream clustering, trajectory inference, or visualization, and a fixed-size representative subset that preserves rare cell states is needed.

name: metropolis-monte-carlo-trajectory-sampling
description: Use when scRNA-seq trajectories must be inferred beyond RNA velocity, e.g. propagating fates from progenitor (NEUROG3) clusters to terminal fates (SC-α, SC-β, SC-EC) using a potential-energy-biased Markov chain.

name: metropolis-within-gibbs-posterior-sampling
description: Use when jointly inferring tumor phylogeny from bulk DNA-seq and scRNA-seq SNV read counts and the joint posterior over Z, P^s, P^b admits no closed form, requiring iterative full-conditional MCMC sampling.

name: mgatk-vmr-strand-correlation-variant-calling
description: Use when benchmarking mtDNA variant callers on single-cell data, or when comparing an mgatk-based clone-assignment workflow against MQuad-based selection using concordance to known source labels.

name: mhc-class-i-allele-typing-with-optitype
description: Use when tumor FASTQ/BAM reads (DNA-seq or RNA-seq) need HLA class I genotyping to constrain MHC-I peptide binding predictions, or when custom allele files must be merged into typed allele sets.

name: mhc-peptide-binding-prediction-filtering
description: Use when TCR repertoires (paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq, e.g. PBMCs from SARS-CoV-2 patients) are clustered and clusters must be annotated as antigen-specific vs bystander using epitope database hits filtered by donor HLA binding.

name: mhc-region-exclusion
description: Use when preprocessing GWAS summary statistics (e.g. via scPagwas::GWAS_summary_input) before SNP-to-pathway linking, to drop SNPs in the MHC region that exhibit extensive LD and would bias pathway association estimates.

name: mi-lower-bound-estimation-mine
description: Use when training a topic/VAE model on multi-batch single-cell counts where cell states may be batch-confounded, and you must quantify or penalize the dependence between expression-rate predictions and batch covariates.

name: mibi-image-single-cell-segmentation
description: Use when segmenting single cells in MIBI or other multiplexed tissue imaging data (e.g., breast carcinoma TMA images) where cells have internal aberrant or incomplete membranes that defeat standard segmentation approaches.

name: micro-f1-multiclass-evaluation
description: Use when a per-cell assignment (e.g., inferred spatial layer L1-L6 for 15413 scRNA-seq cells) must be scored against ground-truth multiclass labels and compared to a chance/majority baseline.

name: microarray-background-subtraction
description: Use when a quantile-normalized microarray intensity matrix (e.g. PIMENTo's preprocess.data.obj$quantile from a tab-separated file like example_unnorm.txt) shows a distinct low-intensity background peak in its log2 histogram that must be filtered out before downstream expression analysis.

name: microarray-batch-effect-removal
description: Use when a normalized gene-level expression matrix aggregated across multiple GEO studies or platforms shows study-of-origin batch structure, and downstream comparison requires homogenized batch distributions while preserving perturbation/differentiation signal.

name: microarray-data-normalization
description: Use when raw microarray intensity data (e.g., a tab-separated file like example_unnorm.txt with gene IDs, symbols, and per-sample intensity columns) must be normalized before differential expression or background subtraction.

name: microarray-data-processing
description: Use when a longitudinal peripheral-blood transcriptomics dataset needs per-patient time alignment to clinical nadir, and trajectories of candidate prognostic transcripts must be extracted and plotted across disease phases.

name: microarray-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a background-subtracted microarray expression matrix (e.g. Illumina Bead array data like E-MTAB-2400 WT vs villin-gp130Act crypt samples) and a class vector, and need significant genes plus sample-separation plots.

name: microarray-expression-data-loading
description: Use when a transcriptomic regression/classification task needs a ready-made high-dimensional microarray expression matrix (p >> n, e.g. 6283 genes x 116 AML samples) packaged in the suffpcr R package rather than raw array files.

name: microarray-expression-data-retrieval
description: Use when an analysis requires baseline (non-perturbation) microarray expression profiles for GDSC cancer cell lines, e.g. to score pathway-responsive gene signatures against IC50 drug sensitivity, starting from ArrayExpress/cancerrxgene accessions.

name: microarray-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when the goal is differential gene expression (e.g. knockdown-vs-control contrasts) on MDI-induced 3T3-L1 microarray samples with curated, normalized gene-level intensities available as a SummarizedExperiment object.

name: microarray-intensity-filtering
description: Use when starting from a gene-level collapsed probe-intensity matrix (post-collapseRows) spanning multiple microarray studies, and a comparable normalized expression matrix is needed before batch-effect removal or downstream differential expression/gene set enrichment.

name: microarray-limma-moderated-statistics
description: Use when the selected pdacR dataset's experiment type is Array (microarray) and a two-cohort A-vs-B differential expression comparison is requested via a sample track and comparison control.

name: microarray-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when working with curated microarray datasets (e.g. 3T3-L1 adipocyte series) where you need to check whether batch effects (data series, platform) dominate sample variance and whether a biological covariate like stage of differentiation separates samples after correction.

name: microarray-probe-gene-symbol-mapping
description: Use when a downloaded GEO microarray series provides probe-level intensities with a probe-to-gene annotation table, and a gene-by-sample expression matrix (one row per unique gene symbol) is required for downstream analysis.

name: microarray-probe-to-gene-annotation
description: Use when input expression data are Affymetrix HG-U133 Plus 2.0 probe-level matrices (e.g., microarray CEL-derived probe IDs) that must be collapsed or mapped to gene symbols before downstream gene-name-based analysis.

name: microarray-significance-output-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have SAM significance output from samr testing on a microarray matrix and need tiered top-N gene lists plus a dendrogram heatmap to test whether samples cluster by phenotype/response class.

name: microarray-summarizedexperiment-data-access
description: Use when a task requires gene expression data from MDI-induced differentiating 3T3-L1 pre-adipocytes under genetic (knockdown/overexpression) or pharmacological perturbation, and needs it loaded as a SummarizedExperiment object in R/Bioconductor.

name: microbial-read-blast-alignment
description: Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ reads have been mapped to hg19/hg38 with STAR and an unmapped BAM/FASTA remains, and you need microbial taxon read counts for the four supported taxons archaea, bacteria, fungi and viruses.

name: microbial-read-classification
description: Use when you have unmapped reads (e.g., a STAR UnMapped.bam from human hg19/hg38 alignment of small RNA-seq FASTQ data) and need to profile fragmental microbial RNA content.

name: microrna-exploratory-analysis
description: Use when you have a manually curated/selected list of plant miRNA precursors (table + GFF3/GTF + FASTA) and need exploratory characterization — HTML summary reports, per-subgenome counts, or homologous-group/triad structure.

name: milestone-based-cell-population-binning
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset contains a continuous activation or differentiation process (e.g. naive CD4 T cells across 0 h/12 h/24 h stimulation with intermediate populations) and you need discrete per-node expression matrices for multisample pathway analysis.

name: milestone-network-export
description: Use when trajectory topologies inferred by multiple methods (e.g. Totem, Slingshot with ground-truth clustering, TinGa) must be compared or deposited as milestone network edge lists on datasets like multifurcating_4 or mouse thymus T cells.

name: milisi-dataset-mixing-quantification
description: Use when comparing synthetic scATAC-seq or scRNA-seq cells against real cells in UMAP space and a numeric dataset-mixing score (miLISI, closer to 2 = perfect mixing) is needed, e.g. benchmarking read simulators.

name: million-scale-scrna-atlas-scalability-testing
description: Use when benchmarking whether a single-cell auto-annotation or novel-cell-detection model scales to million-cell atlases, using a healthy-vs-disease atlas split where disease-only cell types serve as ground-truth novel classes.

name: milo-neighbourhood-pseudobulk-construction
description: Use when converting single-cell VDJ-seq data (e.g. SingleCellExperiment with complete TCR information) into a pseudobulked VDJ feature space so continuous VDJ gene-usage features can feed diffusion-map trajectory analysis.

name: milo-neighbourhood-pseudobulking
description: Use when a SingleCellExperiment with TCR contigs and a scVI/PCA embedding (e.g. X_scvi) needs neighbourhood-level pseudobulk VDJ features before trajectory inference.

name: milo-pseudobulk-vdj-feature-space-construction
description: Use when you have preprocessed scVDJ-seq data (e.g. SingleCellExperiment with X_scvi embeddings and complete TCR information) and need to build a VDJ feature space for trajectory analysis, as in the dandelionR abT workflow.

name: mimo-network-path-attenuation
description: Use when pairwise cell-cell communication networks (e.g., from CPPLS-MLP on Seq-Scope or seqFISH+ data) must be integrated into a single MIMO directed graph with attenuated multi-cell-type paths.

name: min-max-gene-expression-normalization
description: Use when preparing t0/t1 scRNA-seq count matrices for CASi's CrossTimeAnnotation neural network: features must first be restricted to the top 2000 highly variable genes and min-max normalized identically across timepoints so the ANN trains stably.

name: min-max-normalization-composite-score-aggregation
description: Use when comparing multiple integration methods with metrics on different scales (NMI, ARI, ASW, PCR batch, kBET, LISI) and you need normalized composite bio-conservation, batch-correction, and combined scores.

name: min-max-normalization-of-integration-metrics
description: Use when comparing multiple integration methods on shared benchmark metrics that have different scales/ranges, and composite scores (bio-conservation, batch-correction, combined) are needed to rank methods.

name: minibatch-graph-learning-for-million-cell-data
description: Use when clustering a scRNA-seq expression matrix larger than 25,000 cells (e.g., the 1.3-million-cell mouse brain dataset) where competing graph neural network methods fail or exceed a 24-hour budget.

name: minibatch-unbalanced-optimal-transport-implementation
description: Use when integrating unpaired or heterogeneous single-cell multi-omics datasets (e.g., scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq) whose heterogeneity must be handled with both common and dataset-specific HVGs via a coupled-VAE with an OT alignment loss.

name: minigene-splicing-isoform-validation
description: Use when you have nanopore long-read cDNA from a single-locus minigene (e.g. PAX6) splicing assay and need per-isoform detection, abundance and length estimates, plus a cross-check of splice-site calls against a transcriptome-based tool.

name: minimal-spanning-tree-visualization-in-umap
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq Seurat object already carries Louvain cluster assignments and reduced-dimension coordinates (PCA, UMAP, PHATE) and you need to infer and visually present cellular trajectories as a cluster-level MST.

name: minimap2-read-alignment
description: Use when NanoSpeech (or a comparable ONT) basecaller has produced fasta/fastq reads from direct RNA sequencing and the modification indexes carried in read headers must be mapped to a reference transcriptome or genome for per-read and genome-space modification calling.

name: minimax-adversarial-discriminator-optimization
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq batches with scDREAMER and batch-mixing must be achieved adversarially: the discriminator's Bhattacharyya minimax objective and encoder-vs-batch-classifier game drive batch-invariant latent embeddings.

name: minimizer-based-sequence-indexing
description: Use when many short reads/transcripts must be approximately searched against very large collections of nucleotide sequences (e.g., hundreds of bins/genomes) where FM-indexes are infeasible and word-based indexes cannot handle edit-distance searches.

name: minimizer-binning-directory-construction
description: Use when a large nucleotide sequence collection (e.g., thousands of SRA human RNA-Seq experiments) must be indexed into bins so many queries (reads or transcripts) can be approximately searched for set membership faster and with less memory than full-text indices like Mantis or COBS.

name: minimizer-index-construction
description: Use when indexing very large nucleotide reference collections (e.g. NCBI RefSeq bins) for approximate read/sequence queries and memory, not CPU, is the binding constraint.

name: minimizer-parameter-configuration
description: Use when building a Raptor binning-directory index and you must choose a winnowing minimizer variant (e.g., (19,19) vs. (23,19)) and an x-partitioned IBF (x=1, 2, 4, 8) to balance run time, memory, and specificity.

name: minimizer-partition-indexing
description: Use when needing to index thousands of FASTA/FASTQ sequence datasets into an approximate membership query (AMQ) structure and list which datasets may contain a query sequence, e.g. large collections like SRA or GenBank bacterial genomes.

name: minimizer-representative-kmer-computation
description: Use when reproducing or evaluating Raptor-style minimizer pre-filter sizing: you have a binned partitioning of nucleotide sequences (e.g., 64 or 1,024 bins) and need effective text lengths/ratios r(k) for k=12..20 as reported in Table 8.

name: minimizer-sharing-probability-estimation
description: Use when building or recalibrating a pre-filter over (w,k)-minimizer matches (e.g. an IBF binning directory) and you need, for each query minimizer count m, the tau distinguishing true error-tolerant matches from random sharing.

name: minimum-cost-flow-trajectory-search
description: Use when you need transition-centered trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations (e.g., HSPC to erythroid/myeloid/lymphoid fates) from single-cell RNA-seq, without knowing the number of branches a priori.

name: minimum-dominating-set-identification
description: Use when a directed cell-lineage-specific GRN has been constructed and driver-node candidates must be extracted via minimum dominating set / minimum feedback vertex set ILPs and ranked by attention-derived influence scores.

name: minimum-dominating-set-network-control
description: Use when you have a differential co-expression network (nodes, adjacency sets, per-edge differential P-values) and need a compact driver-node set rather than a degree-ranked top-k list.

name: minimum-feedback-vertex-set-identification
description: Use when a directed gene regulatory network (e.g. a lineage-specific GRN from CEFCON) must be decomposed with network control theory to find a minimum set of genes whose removal breaks feedback cycles, as candidates for driver regulators.

name: minimum-free-energy-threshold-screening
description: Use when a set of candidate genomic regions (e.g., editing-enriched windows) must be filtered for bona fide double-stranded RNA secondary structure before use as training positives or confident annotations.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-connectivity-computation
description: Use when a set of per-clustering MSTs (from Slingshot/Totem CLARA clustering) exists and you need a per-cell connectivity score in [0,1] to identify trajectory leaves and branch points.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-lineage-endpoint-validation
description: Use when inferring developmental lineages from single-cell RNA-seq clusters and you must verify that unsupervised trajectory endpoints match known mature cell types before trusting the lineage structure.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-network-trimming
description: Use when a complete weighted graph over cell states (landmarks) has been built from transitional-cell counts and must be reduced to a sparse, connected multi-branching trajectory network retaining only maximum-support edges.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-topology-estimation
description: Use when inferring tree-shaped trajectories from single-cell expression data where a good clustering must be found automatically and cell connectivity should guide selection of end points (leaves) and branch points.

name: minimum-spanning-tree-trajectory-inference
description: Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories that include branches across two or more scRNA-seq datasets, and a tree-structured cell-state transition map (rather than a single linear path) is needed before trajectory tree alignment.

name: minimum-weight-bipartite-matching
description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., log-count matrices pre-processed with Seurat V3.0) where batch correction must preserve local cell-to-cell structure, and a one-to-one matching of representative anchor cells across datasets is needed.

name: minimum-weight-matching-batch-correction
description: Use when integrating exactly two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., 10X PBMC 8k vs Pan T cells, or Splatter-simulated pairs) in gene or PCA space, prioritizing both batch mixing (iLISI) and local structure retention (RNN) over batch-effect removal alone.

name: minimum-weight-matching-blossom-algorithm
description: Use when integrating two scRNA-seq batches via BATMAN: anchors have been identified per dataset and a globally minimal one-to-one cell-to-cell correspondence (not mutual-nearest-neighbor) is needed to derive local shifting vectors for batch correction.

name: minimum-weight-matching-on-cell-graphs
description: Use when integrating exactly two single-cell RNA-seq batches (e.g. CEL-Seq2 vs Smart-Seq2 count matrices) where you need batch correction that maintains cell-to-cell (local) structure, and MNN-based tools underperform on iLISI/50-RNN.

name: mirbase-accession-mapping
description: Use when building an RBP-ncRNA edge list (e.g. from ENCORI/starBase CLIP data for human or mouse) whose nodes mix gene/lncRNA symbols, mature miRNA names, and circRNA IDs and must be converted to Ensembl, MIMAT*, and circBase identifiers.

name: mirna-annotation-against-mirbase
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads (e.g., 50 nt serum FASTQ with 3' adapter TGGAATTCTCGGGTGCCAAGG) have been STAR-aligned to hg19/hg38 and must be quantified against miRBase miRNAs to build a miRNA-by-sample count matrix.

name: mirna-database-aggregation
description: Use when annotating miRNAs in a plant species with a reference genome and you need a consolidated candidate precursor list combining public database annotations with novel sRNA-Seq-based predictions.

name: mirna-detection-comparison-across-pipelines
description: Use when two small RNA-seq miRNA identification pipelines (e.g. COMPSRA and exceRpt) have been run on identical FASTQ inputs and you need to quantify detection overlap and independently validate tool-unique miRNA calls.

name: mirna-expression-arm-selection-boxplotting
description: Use when manually curating candidate plant miRNAs and needing to inspect arm-specific expression and 5p/3p arm-switching events of a selected precursor across available sRNA-Seq samples, as part of the manualCuration HTML report.

name: mirna-expression-prediction-from-bulk-mrna
description: Use when you have paired bulk mRNA and miRNA expression matrices (genes as rows, samples as columns) and want to predict miRNA expression in samples or pooled single-cell clusters lacking direct miRNA measurement.

name: mirna-hybrid-target-summary-visualization
description: Use when you have multiple hyb (and associated fold/vienna) files from replicate miRNA/target ligation experiments (e.g. qCLASH) and need to analyze and plot targets of a defined set of miRNAs across pooled replicates.

name: mirna-isomir-hierarchical-read-counting
description: Use when you have demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads plus miRNA reference annotations (GFF3/GTF) and need to distinguish miRNAs from isomiRs at single-nucleotide resolution and test their abundance between conditions (e.g. control vs knockout).

name: mirna-marker-ranking-across-normalizations
description: Use when scRNAseq clusters must be functionally annotated with miRNA markers via a miRNA-target autoencoder latent space, and you need to know whether normalization of the input counts table changes which markers/scores emerge.

name: mirna-precursor-manual-curation
description: Use when annotating miRNAs in a plant species WITH a reference genome, by combining already annotated precursors from miRBase/PmiREN/sRNAanno/PsRNA with new predictions from public sRNA-Seq datasets (SRA accessions or FASTQ), and interactively selecting promising candidates.

name: mirna-read-alignment-with-star
description: Use when quality-controlled small RNA-seq reads (e.g., serum FASTQ processed with adapter trimming) must be mapped to hg19/hg38 before annotating mapped reads to miRBase miRNAs and building per-sample miRNA count matrices.

name: mirna-secondary-structure-visualization
description: Use when reconstructing or inspecting the manualCuration report generator of iwa-miRNA, or when visualizing a selected plant miRNA precursor's secondary structure, read support, arm expression, and targets in an HTML page.

name: mirna-segment-identification
description: Use when working with hyb-format chimeric RNA records from CLASH/qCLASH (or similar miRNA/target ligation) experiments whose seg1_type, seg2_type, and miRNA_seg annotations are missing, and downstream steps (target analysis, fold analysis, plotting) require knowing which segment is a miRNA.

name: mirna-selection-rule-encoding
description: Use when quantifying miRNAs and isomiRs from small RNA-seq reads with tiny-count and you must decide rule hierarchy, 5' offset, overlap range, and Partial flags for the selection-rules CSV.

name: mirna-target-binding-energy-analysis
description: Use when a qCLASH/CLASH hybrid-sequence dataset has paired hyb and Vienna (or CT) fold files and the goal is to quantify predicted miRNA-target binding energy and per-nucleotide intermolecular pairing patterns in miRNA-containing hybrids.

name: mirna-target-bipartite-network-construction
description: Use when curating a selected plant miRNA candidate (e.g., ath-MIR156b) in iwa-miRNA and you need to visualize its predicted target interactions as a bipartite network on the manualCuration HTML report page.

name: mirna-target-correlation-activity-scoring
description: Use when inferring miRNA activity from paired or single-sample mRNA profiles with correlation-to-putative-target scoring (miReact), or when benchmarking such target-only methods against a trained predictor like miRSCAPE.

name: mirna-target-count-tabulation
description: Use when hyb-format hybrid (chimeric miRNA/target ligation) records must be annotated by segment type and miRNA, then filtered to one miRNA of interest and its targets counted and tabulated per replicate.

name: mirna-target-functional-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters (e.g., setA PBMC clusters) must be functionally annotated via miRNA-target regulatory features, using the SCA encoded space to rank cluster-specific miRNAs and QC the reconstruction with QCM/QCC.

name: mirna-target-grouped-analysis
description: Use when you have miRNA/target hybrid data in hyb format (optionally with fold/vienna files) from multiple experimental replicates and need to quantify targets of a defined miRNA set across pooled replicates with tabular and plotted summaries.

name: mirna-target-prediction-integration
description: Use when you have filtered DESeq2 results (e.g., Schlegel_2022_Ttr_D1_10mkg) plus a set of predicted miRNA targets and want to test whether the target log2FC distribution shifts positively relative to background genes.

name: misclassification-curve-generation
description: Use when comparing filter feature-selection algorithms on a labeled dataset by measuring random-forest out-of-sample misclassification as a function of the number of selected features.

name: misclassification-rate-tabulation
description: Use when a reproduced benchmark table of random-forest misclassification percentages (multiple FS algorithms × number of selected features × datasets) is available and the goal is to identify the FS algorithm per dataset and compare binary vs multi-class winners.

name: mismatch-indel-tolerant-read2-index-alignment
description: Decision support for choosing SCSit's mismatch/indel tolerance parameters when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ data and questioning whether the default one-mismatch/one-indel setting sacrifices too many reads.

name: missing-data-simulation-in-genomic-windows
description: Use when evaluating robustness of a 101-base-window RNA editing classifier to missing RNAseq coverage — e.g. quantifying FP/FN rates after randomly swapping RNAseq nucleotide frequencies for genomic reference frequencies in >30% of flanking positions.

name: missing-exon-isoform-detection
description: Use when comparing isoform call sets from StringTie2 and VIsoQLR on long-read RNA-seq (e.g., SIRV or minigene assays) and you need to identify missed-exon isoforms and distinguish genuine boundary extensions from tool artifacts.

name: missing-value-imputation-omics
description: Use when an rROMA (or similar PCA-based gene set activity) analysis is run on an expression matrix that contains missing values, and PC1-based module scores require a complete global matrix.

name: missingness-indicator-matrix-encoding
description: Use when a sparse single-cell AS probability (PSI) matrix contains NA entries from dropouts and the downstream step (e.g. spectral clustering in SCASL) requires a complete feature matrix that also preserves original missingness information.

name: mitochondrial-content-qc-metric-assessment
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrix (e.g., 10x cellranger filtered_bc_matrix or tab-delimited gene-by-cell table) must be quality-filtered and per-cell mitochondrial percentage is needed to flag dying cells or doublets.

name: mitochondrial-expression-based-dying-cell-detection
description: Use when preprocessing raw spliced/unspliced gene-by-cell UMI count matrices (e.g. from scKB) and you need to flag dying cells via mitochondrial expression percentage before quality filtering.

name: mitochondrial-expression-qc-thresholding
description: Use when preprocessing raw scRNA-sev spliced/unspliced count matrices (e.g. from scKB) and a data-driven dying-cell cutoff based on mitochondrial read percentage is needed before downstream filtering.

name: mitochondrial-gene-filtering
description: Use when ranking per-gene interpretability/attribution scores (e.g., saliency maps) or building a gene signature, where mitochondrial transcripts could otherwise dominate or confound the top-ranked feature list.

name: mitochondrial-gene-qc-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing a SpatialExperiment gene-by-spot count matrix (e.g. Visium human DLPFC) before fitting nnSVG, where mitochondrial genes and genes with low UMI counts or detection in too few spots must be dropped to reduce runtime and improve p-value calibration.

name: mitochondrial-read-exclusion
description: Use when quantifying per-droplet contamination features (e.g., percent spliced reads, debris scores) in droplet snRNA-seq, where mitochondrial reads must be excluded so the metric reflects splicing status rather than extranuclear debris content.

name: mitochondrial-read-fraction-qc
description: Use when raw 10X droplet counts are loaded (sparse Matrix / SCE object) and you need per-droplet MT% or MALAT1% to assess extranuclear RNA contamination, tune debris-score filtering, or benchmark which droplets a filter (DIEM, EmptyDrops, hard cutoffs) retains.

name: mitochondrial-umi-quality-control
description: Use when preprocessing a raw single-cell UMI count matrix (e.g., from Cell Ranger) where low-quality cells enriched for mitochondrial transcripts must be removed before normalization and trajectory inference.

name: mitochondrial-variant-pileup-genotyping
description: Use when you have single-cell RNA/DNA/ATAC-seq BAM files (10x cell-barcode or Smart-seq2) and need per-cell mtDNA genotype matrices as input for clonal substructure discovery with MQuad or vireoSNP.

name: mixed-effects-distance-estimation
description: Use when detecting differentially perturbed cell types in scRNA-seq with patient replicates, especially when naive methods (Augur AUC, nDEG counts) risk false positives from individual-to-individual variability or cell-count confounding.

name: mixed-model-differential-expression-for-single-cell
description: Use when the goal is per-cell-type differential state testing directly on single-cell counts across multiple samples and conditions, especially when per-cell-level flexibility (e.g., mixed-model variance handling) is wanted instead of pseudobulk aggregation.

name: mixed-model-differential-state-testing
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq with multiple samples, groups, and cell subpopulations and cell-level (mixed-model) DS testing is preferred over pseudobulk aggregation, e.g. to compare mmDS against pbDS or when per-cell modeling is desired.

name: mixed-model-results-table-assembly
description: Use when kmFit has been run with run_lme enabled on paired/repeated-measure RNA-seq counts and the per-gene kimma_lme output (estimates, SE, P-values, AIC/BIC) must be compiled into one validated results table.

name: mixed-species-alignment
