description: Use when scRNA-seq FASTQ data from a mixed-species (e.g. human 293T + mouse 3T3) droplet experiment at ~100k reads per cell must be aligned to separate reference genomes and per-cell gene/UMI QC metrics computed.

name: mixture-model-soft-clustering
description: Use when compressing a Harmony-integrated reference atlas into a portable Symphony reference or when mapping query cells into that reference's embedding via soft cluster assignment.

name: mixture-of-experts-batch-correction
description: Use when mapping a query scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. 10x 5' PBMCs) into a pre-built Symphony/Harmony reference embedding (built from 10x 3'v1/3'v2 donors) and query batch effects must be corrected using stored reference parameters only.

name: mixture-of-experts-variational-posterior-implementation
description: Use when you need to infer a joint latent representation from paired single-cell multiomics raw count matrices (e.g. CITE-seq transcriptome + surface protein counts) with modality-specific encoders and a mixture-of-experts posterior.

name: mixture-parameter-selection-via-kta
description: Use when applying TransferCluster to a small scRNA-Seq target dataset: after learning Wtrg against the source NMF dictionary Hsrc, theta must be chosen without ground-truth labels to construct Xtrg_new = theta*Hsrc*W'trg + (1-theta)*Xtrg.

name: mixture-parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when transferring knowledge from a source scRNA-Seq dataset to a smaller target and needing to choose the convex-combination mixture parameter theta without ground-truth labels, or when validating that unsupervised KTA-based theta selection tracks supervised ARI.

name: mixture-weight-threshold-assignment
description: Use when per-cell P/B/M posterior classifications from scBASE must be summarized into per-gene, per-stage ASE profile classes using mixture-weight thresholds, e.g. to quantify the fraction of blastocyst genes in the PBM (dynamic bursting) region.

name: mlp-baseline-model-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a neural ODE transcriptomic forecaster genuinely outperforms a standard multi-layer MLP on paired two-time-point single-cell data, i.e., a controlled prediction-accuracy (MSE) ablation on held-out cells is needed.

name: mlp-gene-classification
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics HVGs (e.g. top 2000 from Seurat FindVariableFeatures()) restricted to a MIMO cell-communication network must be assigned binary communication-relevance labels and scored, in the CPPLS-MLP pipeline after network construction.

name: mlp-neural-projection-training
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells must be spatially mapped using an ST reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) — e.g., to place myeloid cells relative to epithelial cells in normal vs COVID-19 lung pseudo-space.

name: mlp-regression-with-continuity-loss
description: Use when single-cell reads must be allocated to individual TE loci: unique/multi coverage vectors (Vu/Vm) with U/M bin labels are available and per-locus α estimates are needed for read counting.

name: mlp-spatial-coordinate-prediction
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq count data and a spatial transcriptomics reference and need to assign spatial coordinates (pseudo-space) to individual single cells, e.g. to recover spatially heterogeneous subpopulations like atrial/ventricular cardiomyocytes.

name: mmcif-structure-file-generation
description: Use when a cudaMMC (or 3D-GNOME-style) chromatin simulation has produced a bead-coordinate model file that must be converted into a parseable PDBx/mmCIF structure, especially when bead counts exceed legacy PDB limits.

name: mmd-distribution-distance-evaluation
description: Use when you have trained a cross-modality mapping model (e.g. scMMGAN) between two domains and need to quantify both distributional fidelity (MMD) and point-wise correspondence preservation (correlation of columns known to correspond).

name: mmd-loss-transfer-learning-model-training
description: Use when you need to align single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics count data into a unified embedding space via deep transfer learning — e.g., before computing SC-ST mapping matrices or pseudo-spatial adjacency for single-cell spatial landscapes.

name: model-ablation-benchmarking
description: Use when a paper proposes a composite neural architecture (e.g., DGCN + MLP) and you must verify that each proposed component (directional convolution, MLP branch, multi-omics features) contributes to final task performance.

name: model-architecture-layer-dissection
description: Use when a trained Keras model (model JSON, weights, parameters.txt from an autoBioSeqpy run) must be inspected layer by layer to understand learned representations, e.g. dissecting a protein-CNN on typeIII secreted effector sequences or an RFCN on single-cell data.

name: model-comparison-via-simulated-zero-rates
description: Use when evaluating whether a Bayesian count model's zero-inflation (dropout) component is needed, by checking if posterior-simulated zero rates reproduce observed zero-count rates per batch.

name: model-embedding-comparison-across-architectures
description: Use when you have learned node embeddings from two graph-based architectures and need to qualitatively compare class separation (e.g., predicted driver vs non-driver genes) via 2D t-SNE projection.

name: model-ensemble-distribution-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when porting or re-implementing a stochastic 3D chromatin modelling tool and you need to demonstrate the new version produces statistically equivalent ensembles, by comparing within-ensemble similarity distributions.

name: model-evaluation-metric-computation
description: Use when a trained cell-type transfer model (e.g. TACTiCS) must be scored: build the per-cell-type matching score matrix between species and check reproduced recall values against published metrics.

name: model-fit-metrics-extraction-aic
description: Use when a paired/repeated-measure RNA-seq differential expression analysis needs per-gene fit metrics (AIC/BIC) to compare mixed-effects models, since kimma is the only tool among limma/dream that reports AIC for its models.

name: model-fit-metrics-interpretation
description: Use when running kimma/kmFit with multiple candidate model types and you need AIC or other fit metrics to decide which model (e.g. unpaired lm vs. kinship-aware lmerel) fits per-gene expression.

name: model-generalization-assessment-across-species
description: Use when you have per-species trained models and test datasets and need to quantify whether models transfer across related species (e.g., animal-to-animal) but degrade on distant taxa (e.g., animal-to-plant).

name: model-hyperparameter-config-serialization
description: Use when reimplementing or reproducing tGPT: you need the exact architecture dimensions (8 blocks / 1024 hidden / 16 heads) and training hyperparameters written into a config before building the PyTorch model.

name: model-selection-via-bic
description: Use when the true number of cell subtypes is unknown and you are fitting BUSseq to multi-batch scRNA-seq count data (e.g., LUAD cell lines profiled by CEL-seq2, 10x Chromium, and Drop-seq) and must choose K objectively before final clustering.

name: model-transfer-performance-testing
description: Use when you must determine the minimum sequencing depth at which a trained model retains acceptable accuracy, by training on descending random subsamples and comparing self-trained vs full-data-transfer accuracy curves.

name: modification-classification-precision-recall-assessment
description: Use when a modification-aware basecaller has been run on reads with ground-truth modified positions (e.g., synthetic IVT constructs) and you must quantify per-class precision/recall and cross-modification misclassification.

name: modification-detection-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a modification-aware basecaller on reads from synthetic constructs with known modification ground truth, to score per-position detection (accuracy/F1/AUC) and compare mappability vs standard basecallers.

name: modified-base-vocabulary-design
description: Use when building or adapting a deep-learning basecaller for ONT direct RNA data and the goal is single-step detection of modified bases (e.g. m6A, m1A, inosine) rather than modification-unaware basecalling followed by re-squiggling.

name: modified-fisher-exact-test-annotation
description: Use when annotating clusters from scRNA-seq differential expression results (e.g. Seurat FindAllMarkers output) and you want a gene-overlap-based annotation alternative to GSEA that still respects expression significance rather than plain list overlap.

name: modified-nucleoside-prediction-from-small-rna-seq
description: Use when quality-filtered, adapter-trimmed small RNA-seq reads have already been classified as tncRNAs (mapped exclusively to artificial tRNA chromosomes with 50 nt leader/trailer) and you need to annotate modified nucleoside sites per tncRNA from the mismatch patterns.

name: modular-method-port-configuration
description: Use when running Chord/ChordP on a Seurat scRNA-seq object and you want to augment the built-in ensemble (scds, DoubletFinder) with scores from additional doublet detectors to improve accuracy and stability.

name: module-aggregate-activity-quantification
description: Use when normalized blood expression data (e.g. GSE13015/EH5429) must be reduced to per-module or per-aggregate differential-expression percentages for cross-cohort fingerprinting and clustering.

name: module-aggregate-identifier-assignment
description: Use when building or reproducing the two-tier BloodGen3 repertoire structure: you have module-level activity/co-clustering profiles for the 382 modules and need aggregate IDs (A1–A38) and grid placement for fingerprint grid or heatmap plots.

name: module-eigengene-trait-correlation
description: Use when you have a PyWGCNA network with detected modules plus sample trait metadata (genotype, time point, brain region) and need to identify which modules are significantly associated with those traits before running module-level functional enrichment.

name: module-eigengene-trait-correlation-analysis
description: Use when RNA-seq count data with sample-level phenotypic metadata (e.g., mutant/wild-type labels from the Lafora disease dataset) is available and you want to find groups of co-expressed genes whose expression patterns correlate with the phenotype.

name: module-gene-list-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have the constitutive gene lists of a fixed transcriptome module repertoire and need per-module functional titles or consolidated enrichment annotations to organize modules by biological function.

name: module-level-percent-change-quantification
description: Use when you have a normalized (non-log2) blood expression matrix plus sample annotation and need per-module percent-increase/decrease values for fingerprinting, or when testing whether alternate gene-to-module assignments (e.g., duplicate-probe handling) change module-level results.

name: module-level-percentage-aggregation
description: Use when comparing blood transcriptome profiles between patient groups and results must be expressed as per-module percentage of increased/decreased constitutive genes for BloodGen3 fingerprint grids or heatmaps.

name: module-membership-annotation
description: Use when a normalized blood transcriptome expression matrix (non-log2, gene symbols as row names, e.g. Illumina HT12 v3 probes) must be mapped to the fixed 382-module BloodGen3 repertoire before module-level testing or fingerprint plotting.

name: module-percentage-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when the goal is to assess inter-individual variability in a blood transcriptome dataset at the module level for each individual subject — e.g., stratifying patients by individual molecular fingerprints rather than comparing pooled groups.

name: module-repertoire-abundance-quantification
description: Use when analyzing normalized human blood transcriptome matrices against the fixed BloodGen3 repertoire to score module-level increase/decrease percentages per sample or group, e.g., to detect individual subjects carrying an interferon signature.

name: module-trait-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset has per-cell trait labels (outcome, condition, cell type) and you have detected co-expression modules and need to know which modules associate with which trait.

name: modulo-hashing-similarity-estimation
description: Use when estimating cell-cell similarity for scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction (e.g. EDGE) without full pairwise distance computation, by hashing binary gene-expression sketches from many weak learners.

name: mofa-factor-stratification-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq PAS matrices from ≥15 samples must be reduced to interpretable multicellular pathway modules whose latent factors can statistically separate clinical phenotypes (e.g., MMRd vs MMRp).

name: mofa-factor-weight-feature-extraction
description: Use when a trained MOFA model over scPAFA-derived pathway activity scores has latent factors linking pathways across cell types to a disease phenotype, and you need to select the top-weighted pathways as features for classifier training or validation.

name: mofa-multi-group-factor-model-training
description: Use when a cell-level PAS matrix has been pseudobulked into a long-table dataframe with sample/donor, cell type, and technical batch columns, and you need latent factors capturing PAS variance among samples (≥15 samples required).

name: molecular-barcode-duplicate-collapsing
description: Use when calling somatic SNVs from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq BAMs (e.g., with cb_sniffer) and per-cell variant read counts must be deduplicated at the molecule level using the UB_tag before computing per-site false-positive rates.

name: molecular-function-classification-curation
description: Use when building or extending a protein/gene annotation database for intercellular communication analysis and you need to reduce hundreds of UniProt molecular function terms into a tractable, user-filterable set of functional classes.

name: molecule-information-to-count-matrix-parsing
description: Use when starting from 10x Genomics droplet molecule information (raw per-molecule records with cell barcode, UMI, gene) and you need per-sample UMI count matrices for cell calling or barcode-swapping exclusion.

name: molecule-level-barcode-swapping-exclusion
description: Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics count matrices sequenced on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X, NovaSeq) contain multiplexed samples and artefactual swapped cell libraries are suspected.

name: momentum-contrast-queue-management
description: Use when learning latent representations from a normalized highly-variable-gene scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. .npz of HVG profiles) via self-supervised momentum contrast instead of deep generative reconstruction.

name: monocle-ddrtree-pseudotime-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when scRNAseq clusters (e.g., robustSingleCell TIL subpopulations) need pseudotime/trajectory ordering, and you have overexpressed gene sets per group to seed Monocle DDRTree analysis.

name: monocle-pseudotime-analysis
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset (clustered cells with reduced-dimension coordinates, e.g. PCA/UMAP) needs a second, independent pseudotime ordering to validate or compare against Slingshot lineage inference.

name: monocle-pseudotime-branch-inference
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data along a developmental (bifurcating) trajectory needs pseudotime and branch structure inference, especially to check whether doublet removal preserved the lineage topology.

name: monocle-state-stratified-network-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data spanning a dynamic process (e.g., MEF-to-iEP reprogramming) has been annotated into Monocle states and you need state-resolved GRN models for perturbation simulation or network comparison across states and replicates.

name: monocle2-generalized-additive-model-fitting
description: Use when a Monocle2-style single-sample pseudotime analysis must be extended to covariate-associated differential expression (XDE), testing whether a sample-level group covariate shifts gene expression intercepts or pseudotime trends.

name: monocle2-trajectory-ordering
description: Use when benchmarking pseudotime inference: a single-cell gene expression matrix with a known or hypothesized developmental ordering is available and Monocle2 should be run as a comparison method whose cell ordering is evaluated against a reference ordering.

name: monocle2-trajectory-reconstruction
description: Use when a time-course or stage-ordered scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. 262 pre-implantation embryo cells from oocyte to late blastocyst) needs to be ordered along a pseudotime development trajectory with monocle2 DDRTree.

name: monocle3-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a single-cell expression or scATAC-seq dataset must be ordered along a differentiation hierarchy — e.g., testing whether a candidate feature set (DUBStepR peaks vs all peaks vs HVFs) recovers a known branching trajectory from a UMAP embedding.

name: monocyte-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when analyzing peripheral-blood or monocyte transcriptomics (GEO/ArrayExpress raw counts or series matrices, e.g. GSE186650, E-MTAB-9721) to quantify MCEMP1, HLA-DRA or ETS1 dysregulation in CD14+ cells across COVID-19 severity or viral-protein perturbation conditions.

name: mononuclear-phagocyte-subpopulation-annotation
description: Use when snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq datasets carry conflicting myeloid/MNP annotations from independent studies or reference atlases (e.g. Melms/Adams/Travaglini/Wang lung labels, MNP-Verse, HLCA) and a high-confidence myeloid subpopulation assignment is needed.

name: monotonicity-verification-of-mathematical-derivations
description: Use when you need to numerically verify a closed-form mathematical derivation (e.g., monotonicity between a likelihood/density objective and a stability measure) before relying on it in a pipeline.

name: monte-carlo-bias-mse-evaluation
description: Use when comparing co-expression estimators on scRNA-seq count data where a ground-truth correlation is known, to measure estimation bias and MSE as functions of gene expression level (e.g., reproducing Fig. 3a / Supplementary Fig. 4).

name: monte-carlo-clustering-validation
description: Use when a single-cell clustering result needs per-cell confidence or uncertainty estimates, e.g. to flag transition states along developmental pseudotime or to internally validate cluster labels without external ground truth.

name: monte-carlo-detection-shuffling-null
description: Use when computing per-gene differential expression significance from cell positions in an embedding (t-SNE, PCA, pseudotime, spatial 2D coordinates) and a per-gene parametric null is unavailable, so randomized shuffling of detection patterns is needed.

name: monte-carlo-label-propagation-validation
description: Use when a fitted FFC model's cluster_labels need per-cell confidence measures — posterior exclusion probabilities and label entropies — from Monte Carlo re-propagation on a single-cell sample-by-feature matrix.

name: monte-carlo-null-significance-testing
description: Use when a computed DICE value over candidate regulatory factors in a multipotent population (e.g. MPPs or TACs) must be tested against randomized data matrices to establish whether expression covariation indicates significant priming.

name: monte-carlo-posterior-likelihood-approximation
description: Use when you have latent posterior parameters (mean, variance per GMV) for two cell groups from a trained VEGA model and need Bayesian evidence (|log_e(BF)| > 3) for differential GMV activity.

name: monte-carlo-replicate-variability-assessment
description: Use when comparing stochastic unsupervised phase/cycle inference methods on scRNA-seq data and you must demonstrate that point estimates (e.g., circadian phase over the 24 h cycle) are reproducible across repeated runs rather than just accurate once.

name: monte-carlo-replication-aggregation
description: Use when comparing subnetwork detection methods (e.g., SEMtree ST/STr2z, BioNet, COSINE) on simulated gene-expression data where a planted perturbed module provides ground truth and per-replicate metrics must be aggregated over randomizations.

name: monte-carlo-replication-aggregation
description: Use when a paper reports averaged simulation results (e.g., Table 2 true-feature-gene counts over 100 replications) that must be reproduced, or when a stochastic pipeline's performance needs Monte Carlo error bounds.

name: monte-carlo-replication-analysis
description: Use when comparing cell annotation methods under stochastic simulation conditions and a single run would not capture sampling variability — e.g., benchmarking CASi vs scmap, CHETAH, scPred on simulated multi-timepoint scRNA-seq data.

name: monte-carlo-simulated-annealing-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing 3D chromatin structures from ChIA-PET anchors/clusters/singletons and a GPU-parallel Monte Carlo bead-fitting kernel with warp-level move selection must be implemented or revalidated.

name: monte-carlo-train-test-resampling
description: Use when comparing circadian-time prediction methods on the same time-course datasets and you need variance-controlled, partition-averaged accuracy/RMSE rather than a single train/test split.

name: monte-carlo-train-test-split-simulation
description: Reference for designing Monte Carlo simulation benchmarks of supervised cell annotation methods on labeled scRNA-seq data, e.g. when no fixed train/test split exists and repeated random splits with varying training proportions are needed.

name: monte-carlo-wald-p-value-estimation
description: Use when you need p-values (not just effect sizes) for per-cell-type between-condition transcriptomic distances from scDist mixed-model output, especially with few patients per group where MLE-based tests would be biased.

name: morans-i-spatial-autocorrelation-testing
description: Use when you have scored spots or cells (e.g., SenePy hub scores) on spatially resolved data and need to test whether the score is spatially clustered or colocalized with a marker-defined region such as Col1a1+ fibrosis.

name: morans-r-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when you have spatially reconstructed (or truth) single-cell coordinates with cell-type annotations and need to detect which cell-type pairs are significantly co-localized, e.g. after CellContrast spatial inference.

name: morisita-horn-repertoire-overlap-analysis
description: Use when paired single-cell RNA-seq with full-length TCR sequencing is available (e.g. plate-based smart-seq2, >3500 CD8 TILs) and you must test whether annotated CD8 TIL states share overlapping TCR clonotypes within a sample.

name: mosaic-dataset-label-annotation-matching
description: Use when re-annotated cell labels from an integration method (e.g., scMoMaT Leiden labels at resolution 0.9) must be compared against a paper's original published labels on the same mosaic dataset to argue annotation quality.

name: mosaic-missing-modality-imputation
description: Use when a mosaic scMultiome layout contains batches lacking a modality (e.g., no scRNA-seq or CITE-seq protein counts) and feature entities such as peaks and genes cannot be connected by the available input data matrices.

name: mosaic-multiomics-data-handling
description: Use when you already have Leiden cluster labels from scMoMaT's post-processed cell-factor KNN graph and need cluster-specific marker genes, marker regions, or marker proteins (e.g. from ASAP-PBMC RNA/ATAC/protein counts) to annotate clusters.

name: most-probable-path-tree-lineage-inference
description: Use when after MuTrans dynamical_analysis has identified attractor basins in a single-cell dataset and you need to infer the most probable transition trajectories between a starting state si and a final state sf for lineage reconstruction.

name: most-specific-cell-type-annotation-analysis
description: Use when reproducing or validating CellO's bulk RNA-seq training set curation counts (samples, studies, CL terms, most-specific terms) or when analyzing most-specific cell type annotations against the Cell Ontology hierarchy.

name: motif-activity-mrna-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to infer TF motif activities from scRNA-seq unspliced promoter counts and test whether a TF's motif activity tracks its own mRNA level across cell cycle phases.

name: motif-activity-result-integration
description: Use when you have differentially active TF sets from two or more FateCompass (or similar motif-activity) runs and need to quantify their intersection and partition factors into shared vs. system-specific groups.

name: motif-disruption-quantification
description: Use when a set of fine-mapped GWAS variants (e.g. linked to target genes via GrID-Net peak-gene links) needs to be prioritized by predicted TF binding disruption, using PWM-based motif scanning of alternate vs. reference alleles.

name: motif-enrichment-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have raw PMET paired-motif enrichment output (output/output.txt) from a plant scRNA-seq cluster analysis and need to identify and visualize cluster-specific enriched TF motif pairs as heatmaps and network plots.

name: motif-enrichment-testing-with-pwm-collection
description: Use when you need to identify which TF binding motifs are enriched among an upregulated gene set (e.g., the top 200 topic-4 proerythroblast genes), especially when motif signal may be masked by technical batch effects.

name: motif-position-distribution-analysis
description: Use when you have high-confidence TSS coordinates (e.g., HOMER-called csRNA-seq peaks, EPDnew/CAGE, RAMPAGE annotations) and need to quantify whether core promoter elements show preferential positional enrichment around the TSS.

name: motif-similarity-comparison-tomtom
description: Use when candidate RBPs lack physical interactions with gold regulators and you must test whether their circRNA-derived binding motifs statistically resemble known regulator motifs (E-value cutoff E < 0.01).

name: mouse-cortex-cell-type-grouping-analysis
description: Use when denoising a sparse single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., 3,005-cell mouse cortex from Zeisel et al.) with known cell-type labels and you need to quantify cluster resolution via mean silhouette score after RMT feature selection versus baseline denoising methods.

name: mouse-organogenesis-atlas-analysis
description: Use when running trajectory inference on a ~1.3-million-cell single-cell atlas (e.g., MOCA) and needing to confirm scalable runtime (~40 min) plus globally connected, multi-branch topology robustness across PC counts.

name: mouse-scrna-seq-aml-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing drug-treated mouse scRNA-seq (e.g., Mus musculus AML cells, GSE110894, I-BET-762) with a human-trained scDEAL model, or when correlating predicted response probabilities with Monocle3 pseudotime.

name: mpi-parallel-benchmark-execution
description: Use when a FrameD fault-injection configuration must be benchmarked for parallel scalability, i.e. when evaluating whether FrameD delivers measurable speedups from 1 core to 32 and 92 MPI ranks on the identical pipeline settings.

name: mpileup-allele-read-count-extraction
description: Use when you have sorted, indexed BAM files (bulk DNA WES and single-cell or bulk RNA-seq) plus a finalized, QC-passed SNV callset and need per-locus allele read counts to feed Canopy2 or a similar joint bulk/scDNA-scRNA clonal-inference model.

name: mras-reaction-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have a normalized, non-negative bulk gene x sample expression matrix with human gene symbols as row names and need reaction-level activity scores as the input to metabolic flux prediction (FBA) rather than gene-level expression.

name: mrmr-feature-ranking
description: Use when benchmarking marker-selection runtimes or ranking features on phenotype×feature score matrices, e.g. when reproducing Table 2 of the multiset multicover marker-selection paper on the IPF, MC, or HCA scRNA-seq datasets.

name: mrna-detection-fraction-quantification-against-protein-ground-truth
description: Use when validating scRNA-seq denoising/imputation against an orthogonal per-cell protein measurement (CITE-seq ADT), by comparing mRNA detection rates against protein-positivity as ground truth.

name: mrna-zscore-abnormality-scoring
description: Use when raw TCGA mRNA expression matrices must be reduced to abnormal-expression entries before FDR screening or Ridge/Lasso/adaptive-Lasso penalized regression in HDMAC.

name: mrsd-score-calculation
description: Use when you need gene- or transcript-specific predictions of RNA-seq depth required to survey splice junctions (e.g. low-MRSD <100 M reads classification) from bulk short-read poly-A RNA-seq reference datasets.

name: mrsd-sequencing-depth-prediction
description: Use when planning bulk short-read poly-A RNA-seq for splice-junction surveillance of Mendelian disease genes and you need to know how many reads (e.g. --number_reads 8 over --sj_prop 0.75 junctions) a given tissue requires.

name: msa-inclusion-tradeoff-analysis
description: Use when deciding whether MSA belongs in a DNA storage pipeline: you must compare HEDGES-MSA vs MSA-only configurations across error rates and error types to see where MSA helps or hurts.

name: mse-loss-regressor-validation
description: Use when single-cell latent features (e.g. TCA characteristic matrices) must be projected into spatial coordinates by regression against a spatial transcriptomics reference, and per-cell coordinate outputs need validation.

name: mse-training-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when training the DeepCycle autoencoder on scVelo moments (Mu/Ms) of cycling genes and you must confirm the loss plateaued rather than diverged before trusting the inferred cell_cycle_theta phases.

name: msigdb-gene-set-compilation
description: Use when iDEA GSE analysis is planned and a gene set annotation matrix is needed that matches the gene identifier type (symbols or MGI IDs) of the DE summary statistics.

name: msigdb-gene-set-database-handling
description: Use when transforming gene expression profiles into functional spectra with DeepCC and you must select, load, or swap the MSigDB gene set database (version, count, or custom msigdbr sets) used by getFunctionalSpectra.

name: msigdb-geneset-mapping
description: Use when scoring per-cell pathway activity (e.g., angiogenesis) from a scRNA-seq counts matrix or Seurat object using GSVA with MSigDB gene sets or a user-uploaded GMT file, to flag cell types with elevated pathway activity.

name: msigdb-geneset-retrieval-and-gmt-handling
description: Use when a pathway/module activity analysis (e.g., rROMA) needs a curated gene set collection and the user names a database like MSigDB HALLMARK or supplies a GMT file as the module list.

name: msigdbr-gene-set-formatting
description: Use when preparing pathway inputs for compare_pathways()/compare_seurat() SCPA analyses: you have a Seurat/SCE object or expression matrices and need MSigDB-derived gene sets formatted as pathway-name-plus-genes structures.

name: msle-regression-head-training
description: Use when cells have pMHC multimer read counts (continuous avidity annotations) alongside paired TCR and transcriptome data, and you must compare joint vs. unimodal embedding quality for avidity regression on the 10x dataset.

name: mtdna-clone-based-cell-subsetting
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has mtDNA-derived clone labels from MQuad/vireoSNP (e.g., TNBC1 clones MT0 vs MT1) and you need to split cells by clone for clone-level differential expression or comparison.

name: mtdna-variant-calling-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when scRNA-seq (e.g., Smart-seq2), scDNA-seq, or mtscATAC-seq BAM files from a population of single cells should be partitioned into mitochondrial clones, or when mtDNA variants must complement nuclear SNV/CNV clone calls for finer clonal resolution.

name: mtdna-variant-detection-binomial-mixture-model
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq, DNA-seq, or ATAC-seq BAM files must be genotyped across the mitochondrial genome to call heteroplasmic variants and select the subset informative for clonal substructure inference.

name: multi-algorithm-accuracy-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when a new clustering strategy or feature-space transformation must be validated against a baseline across several algorithms and benchmark datasets, with accuracy quantified by NMI at multiple subsampling rates.

name: multi-algorithm-single-cell-clustering
description: Use when the input is a preprocessed n × d scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) with a known number of cell types k, and no single clustering algorithm can be trusted to suit the dataset.

name: multi-aligner-ablation-comparison
description: Use when you must measure whether integrating alignments from multiple splice-aware aligners (e.g. Hisat2 and Star) improves genome-guided transcriptome assembly versus single-aligner mappings on the same paired-end/single-end RNA-seq datasets.

name: multi-aligner-alignment-integration
description: Use when short-read RNA-seq reads have been (or can be) aligned with more than one splice-aware aligner to the same reference genome and the goal is a genome-guided transcript assembly that recovers junctions and lowly expressed transcripts missed by any single aligner's assembly.

name: multi-assay-activity-integration
description: Use when you have candidate enhancer regions, several activity assay signals, a Hi-C contact matrix, and gene annotations (e.g. Gencode GTF), and need enhancer-gene interaction scores compared across assay/contact-matrix combinations.

name: multi-batch-cite-seq-clustering
description: Use when input is multi-batch multimodal single-cell data (H5 files with X1 RNA, X2 ADT, Y cell-type labels, Batch), and the goal is simultaneous cell-type clustering plus batch-effect removal in a latent embedding.

name: multi-batch-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a pretrained zero-shot label predictor (e.g. scPRINT) against supervised classifiers (CellTypist, openproblems logistic regression/xgboost) on multi-batch single-cell data where the test set comes from held-out batches.

name: multi-batch-data-integration-clustering
description: Use when input is paired multi-omics single-cell data (H5 files with X1 RNA, X2 ATAC, Y labels) spanning multiple batches, and the goal is integrated clustering with batch-effect correction rather than per-batch analysis.

name: multi-biosample-depth-comparison-analysis
description: Use when you need per-gene, per-tissue predicted RNA-seq depths (MRSD scores) for splice-junction coverage of a disease gene panel across several control biosample datasets.

name: multi-branch-network-architecture-implementation
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and CITE-seq/REAP-seq surface protein measurements and need to train a transcriptome-to-protein mapping model rather than apply the pre-trained cTP-net model.

name: multi-causal-variant-fine-mapping
description: Use when a locus may harbor multiple causal variants (allelic heterogeneity) across many tissues or studies and you need joint fine-mapping and colocalization rather than single-causal-variant meta-analysis.

name: multi-classifier-performance-comparison
description: Use when several candidate classifiers must be evaluated on identical training/test feature files, and you need to tabulate classification power (accuracy) per method, optionally across graded noise levels proxying shallower sequencing depth.

name: multi-cluster-drug-score-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-cell-type drug rankings from ASGARD GetDrug across multiple clusters of a patient's scRNA-seq data and need a single patient-level drug recommendation that accounts for heterogeneous cell populations.

name: multi-comparison-gene-occurrence-counting
description: Use when you have one sub-directory per pairwise experimental comparison, each with scorecard outputs, and you need a per-gene tally of how many scorecards/quadrants of interest each gene appears in across comparisons.

name: multi-condition-cci-comparison
description: Use when two or more pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB- or CellChat-derived) covering distinct biological conditions are available and the goal is to identify cell types or int-pairs whose communication is condition-specific, such as gain of interactions in critical vs moderate COVID-19.

name: multi-condition-count-matrix-prediction
description: Use when a multi-batch, multi-condition scRNA-seq count matrix plus meta_cells must yield predicted counts for held-out or out-of-sample condition combinations, with per-cell-type accuracy metrics.

name: multi-condition-dataset-merging
description: Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition scRNA-seq mixtures (e.g., different tissues from multiple donors) where batch effects within conditions must be removed without erasing across-condition biological differences.

name: multi-condition-multi-batch-dataset-construction
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-level metadata with >=1 condition columns and a batch/study ID column, and you need to train scDisInFact or run cross-batch perturbation prediction.

name: multi-condition-transcriptome-scorecard-visualization
description: Use when a CSV of gene IDs with log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for multiple treatment-vs-control comparisons must be screened for extreme or moderate expression variations across several experimental conditions (e.g., antibiotic, adjuvant, and co-treatment RNA-seq).

name: multi-database-small-rna-annotation
description: Use when FASTQ small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to hg19/hg38 with STAR and you need to classify and count reads into multiple small RNA classes (miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA, circRNA) in one pass rather than running separate single-class tools.

name: multi-dataset-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a deep learning filter (e.g., HVLD) against classifier baselines across multiple paired-end RNA-seq datasets, with per-dataset and averaged accuracy as the target metrics.

name: multi-dataset-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to compare multiple dimension-reduction or embedding methods across several labeled scRNAseq benchmark datasets to quantify which method recovers known cell populations.

name: multi-dataset-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a supervised ARI comparison of one scRNA-seq clustering method against multiple baselines is needed across a panel of labeled datasets (e.g., Tabula Sapiens organs) to establish relative performance.

name: multi-dataset-benchmark-harmonization
description: Use when a cell-type classifier (e.g. Pollock) trained on merged multi-cancer cohorts must be benchmarked against disease-specific models on each cancer type's validation set to quantify generalization loss.

name: multi-dataset-benchmark-rank-aggregation
description: Use when a dimension reduction method must be quantitatively benchmarked against baselines across 20 scRNA-seq datasets, scoring 2D embeddings via k-means NMI/ARI and aggregating per-method mean ranks.

name: multi-dataset-comparison-table-reconstruction
description: Use when a paper reports a benchmark table comparing methods across multiple datasets and the goal is to reproduce it end-to-end: run each method-dataset pair, compute the reported metric, and aggregate into a CSV table.

name: multi-dataset-deg-union-feature-selection
description: Use when building a supervised malignant-vs-normal classifier from multiple scRNA-seq training datasets and you need a robust, pan-cancer feature gene list that tolerates inter-tumor heterogeneity.

name: multi-dataset-method-comparison-table-generation
description: Use when a method's performance must be quantified against baselines across several real datasets with known trajectory directions, using trajectory-level metrics such as CBDir and ICCoh, and summarized into a per-dataset score table.

name: multi-dataset-score-aggregation
description: Use when per-cell scores from multiple stemness methods (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) have already been computed on several datasets and you need to quantify their agreement via averaged Pearson correlations.

name: multi-dataset-scrna-seq-reference-merging
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq reference datasets from different sequencing platforms must be merged and batch-corrected (e.g. five liver datasets with *_expr.txt and *_meta.txt files), or when reference-query batch effects must be quantified before label transfer.

name: multi-dataset-scrnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., IPF, MC, or HCA datasets) must be filtered, normalized, and log-transformed prior to running marker-selection methods such as GreedyPC or baseline selectors.

name: multi-encoding-feature-fusion
description: Use when building sequence-based ML predictors from labeled RNA segments (e.g., 41-bp m5C windows) and you need diverse informatic sequence profiles fused into one feature matrix.

name: multi-feature-hierarchical-clustering-of-st-regions
description: Use when annotating spatial transcriptomics spots as malignant vs non-malignant regions in tumor ST datasets, especially when pathologist-annotated regions are the benchmark and no ST-retrained classifier exists.

name: multi-format-scientific-figure-export
description: Use when a PIMENTo figure (e.g. the top-50-gene heatmap built from the SAM-ranked gene list and the quantile-normalized matrix) must be exported in multiple graphics formats (TIFF, PDF, Postscript, FIG) into a results subdirectory.

name: multi-gene-list-enrichment-with-upset-visualization
description: Use when you have up to 10 per-cluster up/down regulated gene lists from scRNA-seq differential expression and need to compare enriched GO/KEGG terms across clusters interactively.

name: multi-gene-node-expression-aggregation
description: Use when KEGG KGML pathway nodes contain multiple functionally homologous genes but per-gene RNA-seq counts exist, and node-level expression values are needed for pathway visualization or differential expression in Cytoscape.

name: multi-group-factor-analysis-training
description: Use when single-cell PAS matrices from multiple samples/donors and cell types must be integrated into low-dimensional factors that stratify clinical groups (e.g., MMRd vs MMRp) while correcting for known technical batch effects.

name: multi-individual-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when you must compare clustering accuracy across methods on multi-individual droplet scRNA-seq simulations (e.g., varying number of individuals, sigma_ik^2 heterogeneity, or Splatter group/batch-effect levels) and quantify results with ARI.

name: multi-input-combination-optimization-config
description: Use when reproducing DC3's Table 1 benchmark: an in silico GM12878/K562 mixture with scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and bulk HiChIP data must be deconvolved under four input-combination settings to compare PCC scores.

name: multi-kernel-clustering
description: Use when you need unsupervised clustering or sample stratification from a gene expression matrix where noise/dropout weaken standard distances, and the number of subpopulations is unknown.

name: multi-kernel-distance-metric-optimization
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (e.g., .RData workspace like Test_1_mECS.RData) must be converted into a cell-to-cell similarity matrix for clustering, dimension reduction, or visualization, especially under high noise and dropout.

name: multi-kernel-similarity-learning
description: Use when input is a single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix with high noise and dropout events, and the goal is de novo, unsupervised clustering or 2-D/3-D visualization of cell subpopulations.

name: multi-label-lda-axis-merging
description: Use when cells have two or more a priori labels capturing distinct biological variance (e.g., cell-cycle phase and cell line) and you want a single supervised-then-unsupervised embedding that preserves all label relationships.

name: multi-layer-perceptron-coordinate-regression-training
description: Use when reconstructing cell pseudo-space from scRNA-seq data: TCA characteristic matrices for ST reference and scRNA-seq exist, plus ST spot x-y coordinates, and per-cell spatial coordinates must be predicted.

name: multi-mapped-read-filtering
description: Use when assigning small RNA-seq FASTQ reads to tRNA-derived loci (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, tRH, tRNA halves) and ambiguous reads from repetitive tRNA-flanking regions or paralogous tRNA genes must be excluded before subtype classification.

name: multi-mapping-read-allocation-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell TE quantification methods that must resolve multi-mapping reads (e.g., Alu subfamilies, HERVK isoforms) across scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, or long-read datasets, using ARI/NMI clustering or simulation ground-truth accuracy as the comparison metric.

name: multi-mapping-read-allocation-neural-network
description: Use when quantifying transposable element expression at individual locus resolution in single-cell scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data where repetitive TE sequences generate multi-mapping reads that alignment-only tools (scTE, SoloTE, Telescope) cannot resolve per-locus.

name: multi-mapping-read-allocation-to-te-loci
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq or scATAC-seq alignments contain multi-mapping reads over repetitive TE loci and locus-specific (not subfamily-level) TE quantification or marker discovery is the goal.

name: multi-mapping-read-count-disambiguation
description: Use when quantifying small RNA-seq reads (miRNA/piRNA/tRNA/snRNA/snoRNA/circRNA) where reads map to multiple loci of one RNA or shared sequences create cross-RNA-type ambiguity and per-RNA read counts are the output.

name: multi-mapping-read-segregation-from-bam
description: Use when you have single-cell BAM files with multi-mapping reads to repetitive TE loci and need per-cell, per-locus coverage vectors and unique/multi read segregation before training a MATES model.

name: multi-method-annotation-comparison-across-datasets
description: Use when evaluating whether a cluster-based annotation method (scCATCH) outperforms cell-based annotation tools on benchmark scRNA-seq datasets with published cluster assignments and manually assigned cell types.

name: multi-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing a new cross-modality single-cell translation method against published baselines on identical data folds, needing per-fold paired statistics over AMI, ARI, HOM, and NMI clustering indices.

name: multi-method-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new method's paper claims ity over named baselines (e.g., 11 deconvolution tools or STAligner/PASTE) and you must reproduce or extend the head-to-head comparison on the paper's benchmark datasets.

name: multi-method-benchmark-table-reproduction
description: Use when replicating a published single-cell clustering benchmark: multiple clustering methods must be run on the same pre-annotated scRNA-seq matrices with known cluster counts and NMI/ARI assembled into a comparison table.

name: multi-method-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when comparing a new trajectory inference method's pseudotime accuracy against baselines on simulated single-cell datasets with ground truth, using Kendall rank correlation as the metric.

name: multi-method-cci-consensus-voting
description: Use when you need reliable positive/negative labels for candidate L-R interactions between cell clusters from a labeled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. panc8) to supervise a deep-learning CCI model, and no single statistical method's calls should be trusted alone.

name: multi-method-cell-cell-communication-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing performance of cell-cell communication inference tools (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, iTALK, SingleCellSignalR) on identical scRNA-seq datasets to quantify false-positive rates and robustness to cell subsampling.

name: multi-method-cell-type-benchmarking
description: Use when you have single-cell count matrices with manually annotated labels and need to quantitatively compare which automatic cell-type identification methods (eager, lazy or marker-based) perform , e.g. across platforms or tissues.

name: multi-method-clustering-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing several single-cell clustering methods on the same scRNA-seq datasets and you need quantitative stability (APN) and tightness (silhouette width) metrics for a benchmark table.

name: multi-method-clustering-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when a task requires comparing clustering quality of scSpace vs baselines (Louvain, K-means, Hclust, SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, DR-SC, scCoGAPS) on labeled simulated datasets via ARI boxplots.

name: multi-method-clustering-pipeline-execution
description: Use when clustering the 15 Krzak et al. 2019 real scRNA-seq evaluation datasets under R 4.0.5 and comparing CASCC against CIDR, RaceID3, SC3, Seurat V4, SIMLR, and TSCAN using ARI/AMI/NMI against ground-truth cell-type labels.

name: multi-method-comparison-table-compilation
description: Use when a gold-standard dataset with known branching topology (e.g., Rizvi et al. synthetic data with two bifurcations) is available and the goal is to rank multiple trajectory-inference methods on bifurcation detection and pseudotime accuracy.

name: multi-method-consensus-dci-identification
description: Use when scHi-C differential interaction results from multiple scHiCDiff detectors (KS, CVM, NB, ZINB) are available and a robust, cross-method-supported set of DCIs is needed rather than a single-method call.

name: multi-method-cross-dataset-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when you must objectively compare multiple patient-level single-cell/pathomics analysis methods across several public datasets, requiring per-method clustering and trajectory metrics plus statistically corrected method rankings.

name: multi-method-deg-consensus-voting
description: Use when a raw RNA-seq count table plus sample metadata must be screened for DEGs and no single method can be trusted, e.g. rare-disease model datasets like PMM2-CDG or Lafora disease where method choice strongly changes DEG counts.

name: multi-method-integration-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq RNA gene counts and raw protein ADT counts with ground-truth cell-type labels and need to quantify whether a multimodal joint embedding improves clustering (ARI/NMI) over unimodal or competing integration methods.

name: multi-method-integration-comparison-analysis
description: Use when a batch-corrected single-cell embedding must be quantitatively compared to other integration methods on cell type conservation (higher silhouette better) and batch mixing (lower silhouette better), e.g. replicating a Fig. 3d-style benchmark table.

name: multi-method-network-comparison
description: Use when a new differential network inference method must be validated against existing baselines on simulated gene regulatory networks with known ground truth, across multiple network complexity settings.

name: multi-method-quantification-agreement-analysis
description: Use when a 10x scRNA-seq dataset has been quantified for pathogen reads by more than one aligner or reference strategy and you must verify that positive-cell calls and per-cell UMI counts agree across methods.

name: multi-method-scrnaseq-comparison-table-construction
description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction or embedding methods on scRNA-seq data by a single downstream metric (e.g., pseudotime recovery), and a per-method-per-scenario results table with bounded scores is required.

name: multi-method-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing pseudotime/TI methods on datasets with known ground-truth cell ordering (e.g., VeloSim-simulated cycle-tree data), or when needing a per-path Kendall rank correlation benchmark against baseline velocity-based and expression-based methods.

name: multi-metric-similarity-feature-construction
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix with known cell-type labels is available and you must compare which cell-to-cell similarity metric (Euclidean, cosine, Pearson, Spearman, autoencoder) aligns engineered features with true labels via silhouette values.

name: multi-objective-loss-optimization
description: Use when a graph autoencoder latent embedding must be refined for clustering: after pre-training on reconstruction loss alone, when initial cluster centroids (e.g. from Louvain on embedded data) are available and soft-assignment KL refinement is needed.

name: multi-omic-batch-correction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods on paired single-cell multi-omic data (e.g., 10X Genomics PBMC scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq peak matrices) and need reproducible integration metrics like ARI, NMI, Batch ASW, and CellType ASW.

name: multi-omic-resampling-stability-analysis
description: Use when evaluating multi-omic single-cell integration output (e.g., MaCroDNA assignments on scRNA-seq/scDNA-seq pairs) in the absence of ground truth, to quantify statistical significance and assignment stability via resampling.

name: multi-omics-baseline-method-comparison
description: Use when you must show that a label-transfer method for unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data is robust to reduced annotation budgets, by comparing average per-cell-type F1 against a semi-supervised baseline such as scJoint.

name: multi-omics-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a multimodal single-cell clustering method against single-modality or concatenation-based ablations, or when reproducing ARI/NMI performance comparisons with statistical significance testing across multiple datasets.

name: multi-omics-feature-learning
description: Use when labeled driver/non-driver genes are available on a directed GRN (DawnNet, KEGG, RegNetwork) with per-gene multi-omics features, and the goal is to predict cancer driver genes via graph + feature learning.

name: multi-omics-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when building a feature table that integrates genomic alteration, survival, expression-correlation, functional-annotation, and protein-RNA interaction data across cancer samples for downstream clustering of candidate regulators.

name: multi-omics-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing integration methods on paired single-cell multi-omics data (scRNA+scATAC or RNA+ADT Muon objects) with clustering-quality metrics such as silhouette score, adjusted Rand Index, and kNN purity.

name: multi-omics-marker-score-extraction
description: Use when Leiden clusters from the post-processed scMoMaT cell-factor KNN graph are available and cluster-specific bio-markers across RNA/ATAC/protein modalities are needed to interpret and annotate clusters.

name: multi-omics-network-union-integration
description: Use when two or more FAVA-scored PCC networks (e.g., scRNA-seq and bulk proteomics tsv inputs) need to be converted to calibrated posterior probabilities and merged into one combined functional association network with STRING-style confidence cutoffs.

name: multi-order-local-affinity-loss-implementation
description: Use when fine-tuning a source-pretrained scRNA-seq annotation encoder on target data without source access and you need a self-supervised neighbor-based affinity loss on 'known' cells.

name: multi-order-neighbor-affinity-optimization
description: Use when adapting a pre-trained single-cell classifier to a target scRNA-seq/CITE-seq/scATAC-seq dataset with no access to source data, and batch effect must be mitigated self-supervised from target neighborhoods.

name: multi-panel-benchmark-plotting
description: Use when you have decomposition traces over an archetype-number sweep (k = 2..30) on data with known ground-truth activity patterns, and must quantify/report how many nontrivial archetype columns each method recovers per k.

name: multi-partition-feature-set-intersection-analysis
description: Use when a repeated cross-validation feature-selection experiment (e.g., 5-times 5-fold, 25 partitions) must be reduced to the features selected in every partition, to expose partition-invariant discriminative sequence patterns.

name: multi-path-cell-consistency-quantification
description: Use when a cell-level trajectory inference output (e.g. cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) assigns cells to more than one path and you need a per-dataset statistic of pseudotime agreement across those paths.

name: multi-phenotype-gwas-pattern-scan
description: Use when a binary/additive-encoded SNP x sample matrix with case/control labels, covariate classes, and a PPI/gene-interaction prior is available and the goal is to discover higher-order gene meta-markers associated with multiple phenotypes beyond single-interval methods like FastCMH or SiNIMin.

name: multi-platform-scrna-dataset-harmonization
description: Use when automatically classifying malignant vs non-malignant cells from raw scRNA-seq count matrices spanning different cancer types and sequencing platforms (Smart-seq2 vs 10X Chromium), and when benchmarking that classification against CopyKAT using per-sample F1 scores.

name: multi-platform-scrna-seq-data-integration
description: Use when raw read count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches or platforms must be integrated while cell-type labels are unknown, and batch effects, overdispersion, dropout events, and cell-specific sequencing depth need joint correction.

name: multi-platform-st-dataset-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating reference-free cell-type deconvolution on multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics data from multiple platforms (Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) and checking that known marker genes are recovered.

name: multi-probe-gene-collapsing-maxmean
description: Use when you have a probe-level microarray intensity matrix (e.g. a GEO series matrix) whose annotation table maps multiple probes to the same gene symbol, and you need one row per gene for downstream analysis.

name: multi-read-preserving-alignment-parameterization
description: Use when assigning single-cell RNA-Seq reads to parental alleles in a CAST×B6 F1 hybrid and you must preserve multi-mapping reads, since discarding them inflates allelic-proportion variability and produces spurious monoallelic calls.

name: multi-reference-annotation-integration
description: Use when annotating human scRNA-seq cells or clusters and a single reference is insufficient or composition differs from the query, requiring integration of annotations across multiple reference panels.

name: multi-reference-ctgene-panel-construction
description: Use when building or reproducing cell type specificity marker panels from deCS reference expression datasets, or when t-score/z-score-based CTgene lists are needed for cell type enrichment or annotation.

name: multi-reference-domain-adaptation-training
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset must be annotated against multiple reference datasets simultaneously, or when reproducing the leave-one-dataset-out benchmark of SELINA against comparator annotation tools.

name: multi-reference-genome-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when predicting tumor neoantigens from WES/WGS plus optional RNA-Seq of matched tumor-normal pairs and you need to test or control for reference genome build (GRCh37 vs GRCh38) effects on variant calling and downstream pMHC predictions.

name: multi-reference-label-transfer
description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq query matrix needs cell-type labels transferred from multiple heterogeneous reference datasets, especially with imbalanced/rare cell types or batch effects between reference and query.

name: multi-reference-phas-loci-integration
description: Use when sRNA-seq data must be mined for phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters against both a genome and a transcriptome reference, and when integrated multi-reference PHAS loci sets or alternative-splicing-derived phasiRNAs are the target output.

name: multi-reference-result-integration
description: Use when phasiRNA predictions have been run separately against cDNA, gdna, and/or flnc references (phase_a.txt/phase_o.txt outputs) and the goal is to merge them into one annotation-anchored result and quantify reference-specific loci.

name: multi-replicates-mouse-cohort-design
description: Use when DA-testing from scRNA-Seq data involves biological replicates (e.g. several mice per age group), where inter-mouse variability must be separated from the condition-specific cell-state frequency shift.

name: multi-run-repeatability-analysis
description: Use when a stochastic trajectory or pseudotime method (e.g. Cytopath on RNA velocity fields) is rerun across independent runs and stability or median performance across runs must be reported, e.g. Pearson correlation with elapsed stimulation time (0–120 min).

name: multi-sample-batch-effect-integration
description: Use when you have ≥2 SRT sections (e.g. the 12-sample DLPFC 10x Visium set) with batch/individual effects and need joint spatial domain detection or cross-sample integrated clustering.

name: multi-sample-batch-integration
description: Use when you need to remove technical/sample effects from multi-sample single-cell RNA-seq data while preserving cell-type variability, and to quantify how GEDI compares with other integration methods across datasets and latent-factor settings.

name: multi-sample-multi-condition-scrna-seq-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq data span multiple biological samples and experimental groups (e.g., vehicle vs LPS-treated mice) and the goal is cell-subpopulation-level differential state inference rather than across-cell comparisons.

name: multi-sample-preprocessing-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a new SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool against the original barcode/UMI filtering baseline across five or more samples, and you need per-sample identified-read overlap and 96-97% consistency rates as validation.

name: multi-sample-pseudotime-xde-testing
description: Use when analyzing multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime trajectories to identify genes whose expression along pseudotime differs across a covariate (e.g. sex, disease severity) while adjusting for batch effects.

name: multi-sample-scrna-seq-data-preparation
description: Use when preparing multi-sample scRNA-seq expression, pseudotime, and sample-covariate data for differential pseudotime (XDE/TDE) testing, or when a Monocle2 trajectory must be retrofitted for covariate-associated differential expression tests.

name: multi-sample-scrna-seq-differential-pseudotime-analysis
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples with covariates (e.g. sex, disease status) and a reconstructed pseudotime trajectory, and you need to test which genes or density patterns change along pseudotime in association with those covariates.

name: multi-sample-scrnaseq-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking differential state analysis methods on scRNA-seq data, or when ground-truth multi-sample multi-subpopulation counts with known DS genes/logFCs are needed.

name: multi-sample-srt-data-integration
description: Use when two or more SRT sections (e.g. Visium DLPFC sections or seqFISH mouse embryo sections) across batches, individuals, or conditions must be jointly clustered while correcting batch effects.

name: multi-sample-trajectory-statistical-modeling
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple biological samples per condition need pseudotemporal trajectory comparison across covariates (e.g. mild vs moderate COVID-19), and naive single-sample pseudotime methods would ignore sample-to-sample variation.

name: multi-scale-sliding-window-binning
description: Use when analyzing Seq-Scope/Slide-seq DGEs with spatial coordinates where simple square-grid aggregation is too coarse to resolve cell-type boundaries and finer, overlapping-bin clustering is desired.

name: multi-scheme-sequence-feature-encoding
description: Use when raw nucleotide sequence segments (e.g., 41-bp windows centered on candidate m5C sites in FASTA format) must be converted into informative numeric features to train or apply site-prediction classifiers.

name: multi-seed-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when a new scRNA-seq clustering method must be validated against baselines across multiple real datasets, and clustering quality must be measured as NMI/ARI averaged over repeated random-seed runs.

name: multi-seed-stochastic-evaluation-averaging
description: Use when benchmarking stochastic batch-correction/integration methods whose embeddings or scores vary run-to-run, and you need seed-averaged metrics (e.g. over-correction scores) comparable to a reference figure such as Fig. 3c.

name: multi-slice-spatial-alignment-evaluation
description: Use when multiple adjacent or replicated ST slices (e.g., simulated Visium Datasets 5-6) with paired scRNA-seq references are available and you need to decide whether analyzing slices jointly improves cell type labeling accuracy versus slice-by-slice analysis.

name: multi-slice-spatial-domain-identification
description: Use when analyzing multiple ST slices (e.g., 11 breast cancer 10X Visium slices or 33 MERFISH MOp slices) and you need a single set of spatial domain labels (D1–D9) shared across slices rather than per-slice clusters.

name: multi-slice-spatial-transcriptomics-integration
description: Use when you have multiple ST slices of the same tissue (e.g., 12 human DLPFC 10X Visium sections) and need unified spatial domain labels across slices rather than independent per-slice clustering.

name: multi-source-evidence-consistency-scoring
description: Use when integrating marker gene sets from multiple published databases (e.g. CellMarker2.0, PanglaoDB) and you need to quantify and reconcile source agreement/conflict to weight markers for cell type annotation.

name: multi-source-list-merging-deduplication
description: Use when a curated list must be assembled by unioning multiple published source databases and removing duplicate entries across sources, e.g. building a default L-R interaction database for cell-cell communication inference.

name: multi-source-reference-integration
description: Use when building a ligand-receptor reference by integrating multiple external LR resources (CellPhoneDB, FANTOM5) into one standardized, deduplicated, species-mapped table for cell-cell communication inference.

name: multi-species-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when validating or benchmarking a lncRNA-vs-PCT classifier (e.g., LncCat/CatBoost) whose published MCC/F1 results on human, mouse, zebrafish, wheat, and chicken test sets must be reproduced at a stated prediction-score cutoff, or when a cutoff sensitivity sweep is needed.

name: multi-species-pancreatic-islet-annotation-analysis
description: Use when a multi-donor or cross-species scRNA-seq query (e.g. inDrop human+mouse islets) must be mapped onto an existing human pancreatic islet reference and its cell types annotated via reference-label transfer.

name: multi-species-transcript-feature-engineering
description: Use when raw transcript sequences (FASTA, >=200 nt, CD-HIT filtered at 80%) from one or more species must be converted into a numeric feature matrix for coding-potential classification, especially when sORF-containing lncRNAs must be distinguished from PCTs.

name: multi-strategy-performance-comparison
description: Use when several integration algorithms (SAMap, fastMNN, Harmony, LIGER, LIGER UINMF, Scanorama, SeuratV4, scVI, scANVI) must be compared on identical cross-species scRNA-seq inputs with a common scoring scheme.

name: multi-subject-dynamic-network-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking multi-subject dynamic community detection (e.g., MuDCoD vs PisCES/static spectral clustering/Betzel-2019) or when ground-truth subject x time x node labels are needed for ARI evaluation on simulated S x T x n x n adjacency tensors.

name: multi-subject-network-tensor-formatting
description: Use when preparing adjacency matrices from multiple subjects sampled across multiple time points for MuDCoD fit_predict — input must be a numpy tensor with subject as the first dimension and time point as the second.

name: multi-subunit-complex-false-positive-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking ligand-receptor inference tools on scRNA-seq data and you need to measure how often a tool predicts single-gene interactions for receptors that are known heteromeric complexes, or when choosing a database that accounts for multimeric receptor structure.

name: multi-task-loss-optimization
description: Use when transferring bulk-level GDSC/CCLE drug response labels to scRNA-seq data with scDEAL, i.e. when training Eb, Es, and P simultaneously so single-cell and bulk embeddings are harmonized (MMD) while prediction accuracy is supervised.

name: multi-tf-regulome-gradient-comparison
description: Use when direct TF expression in spatial transcriptomics spots is too sparse to visualize, but an inferred fibroblast GRN edge list with target genes is available and TF regulome spatial patterns must be compared across tissue regions.

name: multi-tissue-expression-data-parsing
description: Use when you have absolute log10(x+1) expression values for gene deletion events across m conditions (e.g., 6 Drosophila tissues) and must build the EmpiricalData.data-style input required by CLOUDe's GenerateTrainingData, CLOUDeClassifyNN, and CLOUDePredictNN functions.

name: multi-tissue-expression-summary-statistics
description: Use when multiple ribo− RNA-seq samples have been quantified with CLEAR (FPBcirc/FPBlinear/CIRCscore) and the goal is cross-tissue comparison, per-tissue summary statistics, or reproducing tissue-enrichment patterns like Figure 5A.

name: multi-tissue-rna-seq-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when MRSD-predicted sequencing depths must be validated on independent RNA-seq cohorts: you have paired junction-count and sequencing-depth files for control biosamples and need PPV/NPV per parameter combination.

name: multi-tissue-significance-pattern-comparison
description: Use when you have Scanpro proportion-analysis results for several tissue subsets (e.g. heart, intestine, skeletal muscle) and need to verify that significant cell-type proportion shifts agree between the replicated design and the non-replicated bootstrapping mode.

name: multi-tissue-sqtl-sharing-analysis
description: Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL result tables (e.g. sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv) from GTEx or another multi-tissue cohort and want to measure cross-tissue sQTL sharing and cluster tissues by splicing-effect similarity.

name: multi-tool-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a new single-cell clustering method's accuracy against established tools on datasets with known cell-type labels, using ARI as the external validation metric.

name: multi-tool-comparative-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing execution time of phasiRNA prediction tools on the same sRNA library and reference sequences, and you need an apples-to-apples runtime comparison that isolates the prediction step from shared preprocessing.

name: multi-tool-consensus-voting
description: Use when multiple independent scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools have each produced per-cell label predictions on the same dataset and you need a consensus confidence mask separating confidently labeled cells from unconfident ones.

name: multi-tool-detection-overlap-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking circRNA/BSJ detection tools on identical ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ inputs and you need pairwise/three-way call-set overlaps plus per-tool BSJ fragment counts to expose sensitivity differences such as DCC misses.

name: multi-tool-detection-result-collation
description: Use when benchmarking fusion gene callers on the same input datasets under graded conditions (e.g., successive read subsampling) and you need a unified detection matrix to compare which tool calls which fusions at which depth.

name: multi-tool-fusion-caller-benchmarking
description: Use when a new or targeted fusion-detection method must be evaluated head-to-head against established callers (STAR-Fusion, FusionCatcher, Arriba, FusionInspector, scFusion) on shared FASTQ inputs with known positive fusion events.

name: multi-trait-colocalization-fine-mapping-modeling
description: Use when you have association data (individual-level genotypes/phenotypes, or summary statistics with LD + betas/SEs or z-scores and sample sizes) for multiple traits and need to fine-map causal variants while testing whether signals colocalize across traits.

name: multiclass-logistic-regression-cross-validation
description: Use when clusters from single-cell expression data must be tested for transitional relationships — e.g. estimating per-cell class probabilities and pairwise confusion scores to build ternary plots between putatively connected classes.

name: multiclass-logistic-regression-inference
description: Use when an already-normalized external RNA-seq breast cancer expression matrix (e.g. RSEM/FPKM processed like TCGA/GSE96058) must be subtype-called without a cohort-derived reference, using the published mLR models.

name: multicohort-prognostic-model-generalization
description: Use when a prognostic model derived from gene-pair (IMGP) scores in a training cohort (e.g., TCGA SKCM06) must be validated for risk stratification across several independent bulk transcriptomic cohorts with matched survival data.

name: multicore-parallel-scaling-analysis
description: Use when a compute-bound step (matrix multiplication, JIVE decomposition/rank estimation via bic.jive or jive.perm with a cores argument) dominates runtime and you need to quantify speedup across core counts 1/2/4/8 against a single-threaded baseline.

name: multilevel-batch-vector-specification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data have several batch covariates at once (e.g., 30 patients, 3 disease statuses, 2 locations) and single-factor methods like Harmony, LIGER, or Seurat3 CCA are insufficient.

name: multimapping-read-family-level-aggregation
description: Use when building a locus-specific TE expression matrix from scRNA-Seq BAMs (CellRanger/STAR) and reads overlap multiple TE copies, so locus-level counts would be unreliable for multi-mappers.

name: multimapping-read-removal-for-riboseq
description: Use when aligning ribosome-profiling footprints (25-35 nt) to a genome with the Hisat2 then Bowtie2 double-mapping strategy and you must retain only uniquely mapped reads before counting.

name: multimapping-read-te-subtype-collapsing
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq BAM/SAM reads multi-map to transposable element subtypes and a cell-by-gene/TE count matrix must be generated without double-counting ambiguous reads across subtypes or overlapping genes.

name: multimeric-complex-subunit-minimum-rule
description: Use when a curated ligand-receptor pair list annotates protein complexes (e.g. Human-2020-Jin-LR-pairs.csv from LewisLabUCSD/Ligand-Receptor-Pairs) and per-pair ligand/receptor scores must be computed from single-cell expression of individual subunits.

name: multimodal-annadata-concatenation
description: Use when an AnnData object must jointly carry a normalized expression matrix and one or more conflicting annotation columns (ADT-derived clusters, label-transfer results, or GoT clonal genotypes) before running scTriangulate.

name: multimodal-cell-embedding-integration
description: Use when paired single-cell multimodal data (e.g., scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq from the same cells, such as a 10x Multiome sample) must be unified into per-cell joint embeddings before trajectory or DAG construction.

name: multimodal-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing multimodal single-cell clustering methods under controlled simulation conditions — e.g. varying clustering signal or dropout rates — where simulated ground-truth cell-type labels enable AMI/NMI/ARI evaluation.

name: multimodal-embedding-snapshot-training
description: Use when you have multimodal single-cell omics data (RNA/ADT/ATAC measured on the same cells) and want to cluster cells by integrating modalities via ensemble VAE embeddings rather than clustering from any single modality alone.

name: multimodal-single-cell-distance-integration
description: Use when analyzing CITE-seq data where both RNA and surface protein modalities must be integrated — e.g., fusing pairwise distance matrices, clustering mixed modalities, or computing a quantitative cluster purity score.

name: multimodal-single-cell-embedding-generation
description: Use when the input is multimodal single-cell omics count data (RNA plus ADT or ATAC measured on the same cells) and the goal is an unsupervised shared latent space for clustering cells.

name: multimodal-single-cell-omics-clustering
description: Use when you have multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA + ADT matrices over the same cells) with no labels, and the goal is unsupervised consensus cell-type clustering via deep-learning embeddings.

name: multimodal-snare-seq-data-harmonization
description: Use when analyzing paired multi-omic SNARE-seq data where cells have both a chromatin (cell-by-peak) and expression modality, and cluster-level cell-type annotation must be supported by marker genes and GO enrichment.

name: multimodal-tcr-transcriptome-model-training
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and TCR sequencing data (with cell type, clonotype, or antigen specificity annotations) and need a joint cell-level embedding for clustering, antigen specificity prediction, or atlas-query label transfer.

name: multinomial-bootstrap-signature-fitting
description: Use when fitting reference signatures (e.g. COSMIC v3.1) to individual hematological cancer genomes with ≥500 mutations and you need contribution estimates with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and error suppression.

name: multinomial-decoder-network-implementation
description: Use when rebuilding or adapting the scMGCA decoder to model scRNA-seq count matrices with a multinomial likelihood plus Bernoulli dropout simulation instead of a zero-inflated (ZINB/NB) distribution, e.g. in TensorFlow re-implementations of the autoencoder.

name: multinomial-likelihood-cell-type-classification
description: Use when annotating newly sequenced single-cell RNA-seq cells (or clusters) against labeled reference data — including cross-species queries mapped to one-to-one orthologues — and a fast, portable supervised classifier is needed.

name: multinomial-logistic-timepoint-classification
description: Use when predicting the circadian time of a single transcriptomic sample (bulk or pseudobulk) after training on a paired-expression/timepoint time series, with rhythmic genes as platform-agnostic features.

name: multinomial-loop-count-allocation
