description: Use when you have bulk HiChIP loop counts (gene-enhancer pairs) plus scRNA-seq (E) and scATAC-seq (O) matrices with cluster labels from the same heterogeneous population, and you want subpopulation-specific HiChIP profiles with better interpretation than the plug-in baseline.

name: multinomial-read-sampling
description: Use when building a co-expression-free null read-count matrix with known ground-truth log expression proportions, e.g. to calibrate or benchmark detection of nonlinear library-size confounders in scRNA-seq association testing.

name: multiome-dataset-preprocessing
description: Use when applying TFvelo to a dataset not shipped with the package — e.g. a 10x multi-omics AnnData (.h5ad) file where you want RNA-only velocity without ATAC-seq — and the default pancreas demo branch cannot load it.

name: multiome-rna-atac-integration
description: Use when a paired RNA+ATAC (multiome) single-cell dataset needs decision-level integration of per-modality Leiden clusterings into stable cell populations, with V-Measure/Completeness benchmarking against individual resolutions.

name: multiomic-baseline-method-reproduction
description: Use when validating a causal peak-gene inference method on RNA+ATAC single-cell multimodal data and need a fair, pair-level AUROC comparison against Pearson/pseudocell correlation, linear Granger, GVAR, and ABC baselines.

name: multiomic-coembedded-data-handling
description: Use when single-nucleus RNA-seq and ATAC-seq from the same tissue (e.g. human heart post-myocardial infarction) are stored in separate Seurat objects and must be co-embedded, batch-corrected, and cell-paired before trajectory or GRN analysis.

name: multiomics-cluster-interpretability-annotation
description: Use when scMM latent representations from CITE-seq (transcriptome + surface protein) data have been clustered at high resolution and clusters must be characterized/annotated with coherent multimodal marker patterns.

name: multiomics-nmf-embedding-training
description: Use when you have paired single-cell multi-omics data (e.g., a Muon object with RNA, ATAC and/or protein modalities) and need a shared low-dimensional cell embedding with interpretable factors, as in the Mowgli workflow.

name: multipanel-figure-generation-from-module-scores
description: Use when you have run JOINTLY and scored cells with AddModuleScore_UCell and need to visualize factor activity per cell type or per covariate (e.g. factor 10 insulin-signalling boxplots by status and sex), or build module/marker AUC comparison panels.

name: multiple-hypothesis-fdr-correction
description: Use when you have two disjoint gene lists (algorithm-selected vs discarded genes) plus gene set annotations and need over-representation p values converted to FDR q values to validate that selection enriches specific biology.

name: multiple-hypothesis-pvalue-adjustment
description: Use when a large set of per-feature association tests (e.g., one Fisher's exact test per GCF in an absence/presence matrix) produces raw p-values that must be BH-corrected before ranking significant hits.

name: multiple-hypothesis-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
description: Use when a family of m raw p-values (e.g. from RgnTX permutation tests over m6A site groups) must be FDR-adjusted before declaring colocalization significant at alpha=0.05.

name: multiple-linear-regression-of-parameters-versus-ari
description: Use when you have ARI results from clustering methods evaluated across a SymSim parameter grid (N, Sigma, alpha, Depth, rare-population proportion) and need to attribute performance variation to individual simulation factors.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-decode-integration
description: Use when decoding DNA storage sequencing reads in FrameD and multiple noisy copies per strand must be consolidated before inner-code reversal, especially under fault injection.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-of-ortholog-protein-sequences
description: Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (like Seq2Fun 's2f_' groups) aggregates too many genes across species to allow gene-level insights, and the protein sequences plus species labels need alignment before clustering.

name: multiple-sequence-alignment-profiling
description: Use when constructing a curated database of potentially functional HERVs: genomic loci must be translated, screened against retroviral protein motifs (POL/RT, GAG, ENV), and filtered to retain only sequences with detectable homology.

name: multiple-testing-benjamini-hochberg-correction
description: Use when you have computed thousands of per-gene statistics in parallel (e.g., a Pearson correlation p-value for every gene vs. a marker gene like VIM) and must select a FDR-controlled gene set before overlap or enrichment testing.

name: multiple-testing-bonferroni-correction
description: Use when many topics/features are tested per contrast (e.g. scETM topic abundance across disease vs control or cell types) and a family-wise-error-controlled significance call is needed.

name: multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when calling significant hits across thousands of parallel gene-level tests (DGE or DUL) in scRNA-seq pseudobulk comparisons, or when testing set overlaps (chi-square independence) where unadjusted p-values would inflate false positives.

name: multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when thousands of genes are tested simultaneously (e.g., normal-vs-cancer DESeq2 tests on KIRC, LIHC, PRAD TCGA count matrices) and raw p-values must be converted into adjusted p-values before thresholding DE gene sets.

name: multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when performing many parallel statistical tests (e.g., one t test per feature across a multi-feature matrix) and you need adjusted p-values to identify which features genuinely differ between groups.

name: multiple-testing-correction-for-genomics
description: Use when a per-gene statistical test (e.g., Wilcoxon rank-sum between cell clusters) returns thousands of raw p-values that must be multiple-testing corrected before declaring significant DE genes or enrichment terms.

name: multiple-testing-correction-local-vs-global
description: Use when benchmarking or choosing the scope of FDR control (per-cluster vs. global BH correction) for gene-subpopulation differential state tests produced by muscat pbDS/mmDS across multiple samples and conditions.

name: multiple-testing-correction-of-enrichment-pvalues
description: Use when annotating clusters from a marker gene list with deCS.fisher: per-cell-type Fisher tests yield many raw p-values that must be corrected (e.g. bonferroni) before calling significant cell type assignments.

name: multiple-testing-correction-pvalues
description: Use when many hypothesis tests are run in parallel (e.g., scoring 64 latent features for association with ICB responder vs non-responder groups) and per-feature significance must be assessed with adjusted p-values to control false positives.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a per-gene test over hundreds/thousands of genes (mutation enrichment, DEG, or GSVA score difference) has produced raw p-values and you must report a defensible significant set, e.g. filtering mutation results with p < 0.05 and FDR < 0.01.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a differential expression test has been run across many genes (e.g. limma on a SummarizedExperiment of microarray intensities) and per-gene p-values must be converted to genome-wide FDR before thresholding.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when calling significant differential chromatin interactions from genome-wide scHi-C bin-pair test results, or when thresholding per-condition significance calls to build a set-difference baseline, so that thousands of simultaneous hypothesis tests are controlled with BH-adjusted p-values.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when per-spot significance tests (e.g., Local Moran's I across many spots and gene signatures) yield thousands of unadjusted P-values, and hotspots must be declared only after multiple-testing correction.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a group-comparison task yields one statistical test per feature (e.g., one per cell type in a DCNet-inferred TCGA abundance matrix) and per-feature p-values must be adjusted for multiple testing before filtering by effect size and q-value.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when a genome- or transcriptome-wide set of per-gene hypothesis tests (e.g., allelic burst-correlation logOR tests from SCALE) must be corrected for multiplicity before declaring significant genes at a fixed FDR level.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when an analysis tests many pathways (or pathway-by-alteration, pathway-by-drug, pathway-per-cohort combinations) simultaneously and a p-value family must be converted to FDR before declaring significance, e.g. the 10% FDR GDSC screen or pan-cancer driver/survival tables.

name: multiple-testing-fdr-correction
description: Use when running many parallel tests in the PreCanCell workflow — e.

name: multiple-testing-p-adjustment-selection
description: Use when running methylR's Association Study downstream modules such as GO or pathway enrichment on a DMC results file and an explicit multiple-testing correction choice must be made through the graphical interface before statistics and plots are generated.

name: multiplet-detection
description: Use when demultiplexing HTO-labeled pooled scRNA-seq droplets with demuxmix and droplets must be classified as singlets of a specific sample or as multiplets via posterior probabilities, with uncertain assignments discarded.

name: multiplet-rate-estimation-from-snv-fraction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data come from mixed cell populations (e.g. Jurkat/293T or 293T/3T3 mixing experiments, transplant chimerism samples) and an observed multiplet/doublet rate is needed from genotype rather than expression markers.

name: multiplexed-10x-sample-read-reassignment
description: Use when 10x Genomics droplet libraries from multiple samples were sequenced together on a patterned-flowcell machine (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) and barcode swapping between samples must be corrected at the molecule level.

name: multiplexed-image-cell-segmentation
description: Use when segmenting individual cells from multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images where columnar/epithelial morphology causes dilation- or Voronoi-based methods to undersegment, and per-cell marker quantification in nucleus/membrane/cytoplasm compartments is needed.

name: multiplexed-image-cell-shape-descriptor-pipeline
description: Use when segmented single-cell masks from multiplexed tissue imaging need to be converted into quantitative shape features via an autoencoder, e.g. for t-SNE or morphology-based cell characterization.

name: multiplexed-imaging-cell-phenotyping
description: Use when analyzing multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images where cells have irregular/elongated morphologies (e.g., columnar epithelial cells) and per-cell marker intensity plus shape phenotyping is needed.

name: multiplexed-imaging-cell-phenotyping
description: Use when you have single-cell data from multiplexed imaging (e.g. MCMICRO output from a CyCIF slide) and need to assign phenotypic identities via marker-intensity gates — e.g. separating SOX10+ tumor cells from CD3D+ immune cells or quantifying Ki67+ proliferation fractions.

name: multiplexed-imaging-marker-fraction-analysis
description: Use when you have MCMICRO-derived single-cell data from a multiplexed imaging sample (e.g. CyCIF MEL1, 1,110,585 cells) with per-cell region annotations and channel intensities, and need marker co-expression fractions per spatial subregion.

name: multiplexed-imaging-marker-intensity-thresholding
description: Use when you have a single-cell marker-intensity table (e.g., MCMICRO output from CyCIF imaging, ~1.1M cells x 30 antibody channels) and need to binarize marker expression into per-cell proliferation/arrest labels using user-defined thresholds.

name: multiplexed-imaging-single-cell-data-loading
description: Use when the input is multi-channel whole-slide imaging data already converted to single-cell form (per-cell x/y coordinates plus marker intensities, e.g. MCMICRO output from CyCIF) and it must be loaded into an AnnData object for SpatialCells workflows.

name: multiplexed-sample-barcode-deconvolution
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet UMI count matrices (e.g., HiSeq 4000 patterned-flow-cell data) must be split into real cells versus empty droplets, reporting per-sample called-cell counts and library-size distributions.

name: multiread-weighted-allocation-em
description: Use when allele-specific count matrices must be generated from diploid-transcriptome alignments containing genomic or allelic multi-mapping reads, and discarding multi-reads would lose the majority of available reads.

name: multiregional-gbm-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing multiregional GBM scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE131928 MGH samples) to detect clonal copy number substructure, classify malignant cells, or reproduce runtime benchmarking of SCEVAN vs inferCNV/CopyKAT.

name: multiregional-glioblastoma-scrna-processing
description: Use when processing multiregional GBM (or analogous tumor) scRNA-seq count matrices to infer clonal copy number substructure and benchmark inferred CNA profiles against bulk WGS/WES segmented ground truth.

name: multisample-pathway-distribution-testing
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression matrices for three or more populations (time points, trajectory nodes, or conditions) and want to identify which pathway classes show the largest distribution change across all conditions simultaneously.

name: multiscale-chromatin-model-configuration
description: Use when generating ensembles of chromatin 3D models from GM12878 CTCF ChIA-PET data (anchors, PET clusters, singletons) and CPU-based 3D-GNOME runtimes on large chromosomes such as chr1 are prohibitive.

name: multiscale-cnv-call-harmonization
description: Use when CaSpER (runCaSpER, method="iterative") has produced CNV calls from multiple smoothed expression scales paired with BAF shift evidence, and you must collapse N×M scale-wise calls into a single consistent set of chromosome-arm, segment, or gene-level CNV calls.

name: multiscale-coarse-graining-attractor-identification
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data must be decomposed into attractor basins and transition cells via stochastic dynamics — e.g., recovering EMT epithelial/mesenchymal/hybrid states or bifurcating iPSC lineages from a processed gene expression matrix.

name: multiscale-coarse-graining-of-stochastic-dynamics
description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data (e.g., an Anndata object or N_cells x N_genes expression matrix) must be dissected into meta-stable attractor basins versus transient/transition cells via stochastic dynamics rather than hard clustering.

name: multiscale-expression-signal-smoothing
description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample RNA-seq matrix (e.g. TCGA-GBM bulk or single-cell GBM) and need to detect both focal CNVs (e.g. PDGFRA amplification) and large-scale chromosome-arm events from expression alone.

name: multiscale-median-filtering-of-allelic-signals
description: Use when you have mapped RNA-seq BAM files and need an allelic shift (BAF/LOH) signal profile to correct or integrate with expression-based CNV calls, without a pre-existing heterozygous variant call set.

name: multiset-multicover-approximation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq or similar dataset has many phenotype groups (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations) with overlapping DE genes, and a global marker set is needed that discriminates every phenotype pair at least K times.

name: multisubunit-complex-coexpression-logic
description: Use when computing pairwise ligand-receptor communication scores between cell populations from scRNAseq, bulk RNAseq, microarray, or spatial transcriptomic profiles in which ligands or receptors (e.g. checkpoint, chemokine, cytokine complexes) have multiple subunits requiring co-expression logic.

name: multisubunit-complex-geometric-mean-aggregation
description: Use when computing ligand-receptor communication probabilities with CellChatDB and a ligand or receptor in the interaction is annotated as a multi-subunit complex whose subunits each have per-cell-group expression values.

name: multithreaded-fastq-preprocessing
description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ reads that require combinatorial barcode/UMI identification and the serial BLAST-based original method is too slow or CPU-bound; especially when runtime must be under 10% of the original.

name: multivariate-cox-model-concordance-evaluation
description: Use when ranked gene sets (e.g., IC genes from fused co-expression networks) must be validated against patient survival endpoints, comparing their Cox hazard ratios and Concordance statistics to a DE-gene baseline.

name: multivariate-gaussian-entropy-estimation
description: Use when you need to quantify randomness of expression covariation between candidate regulatory factors (TFs and chromatin-state modifiers) across cells of a multipotent population, e.g. to detect priming toward a lineage in scRNA-Seq data.

name: multivariate-sqtl-mapping
description: Use when RNA-seq transcript expression (transcript usage ratios) and genotypes from the same individuals are available and the goal is to identify genetic variants affecting alternative splicing genome-wide, e.g. GTEx V7 tissue-by-tissue sQTL catalogs.

name: mumford-shah-piecewise-constant-optimization
description: Use when you must segment a chromosome-ordered smoothed scRNA-seq expression matrix into copy number regions, exploiting shared breakpoints across cells/clones via multichannel Mumford–Shah minimization.

name: mutant-cell-fraction-estimation
description: Use when a per-cell somatic SNV genotype matrix from 10x scRNA-seq data must be summarized into per-variant mutation frequencies and benchmarked against bulk VAFs (eWGS or RNA-seq) to assess single-cell detection sensitivity.

name: mutant-cell-overlay-on-cluster-space
description: Use when a set of cells has been genotyped for a somatic SNV from scRNA-seq (via cb_sniffer/VarTrix on a 10x Chromium BAM) and you need to project that genotype onto the whole-sample expression embedding/clustering to ask which expression programs associate with the mutant subclone.

name: mutant-grna-fraction-quantification
description: Use when you need to estimate the fraction of mutant gRNA molecules in a CROP-seq/gRNA library BAM after consensus filtering that removes sequencing-error UMIs (min_reads threshold), to profile library quality or mutation-aware gRNA annotation.

name: mutant-peptide-extraction-from-variants
description: Use when VEP-annotated somatic SNV/INDEL calls (e.g. from GATK Mutect2) must be converted into amino-acid-level mutant peptide sequences for downstream neoantigen prediction.

name: mutation-aware-grna-annotation-classification
description: Use when analyzing CROP-seq / single-cell CRISPR screen data where gRNAs must be assigned to cell barcodes in a mutation-aware manner, e.g. to verify that spacer- or scaffold-mutant gRNAs are dysfunctional rather than mislabeled as intact.

name: mutation-aware-grna-variant-calling
description: Use when analyzing CROP-seq/single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library alignments (BAM) where mutant gRNAs need to be detected and assigned to cells, e.g. quantifying cells lacking a gRNA call under standard feature barcoding pipelines.

name: mutation-based-cell-line-stratification
description: Use when you have GDSC IC50 drug-sensitivity data plus cell-line mutation calls and gene expression, and you want to know whether pathway activity scores stratify drug response within mutant or wild-type sub-populations.

name: mutation-burden-comparison
description: Use when you have per-sample CMS subtype assignments plus molecular features (total mutation counts, CNA counts, BRAF status) and need to test whether alteration burden differs significantly between subtypes.

name: mutation-by-sample-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw bulk WES and scRNA-seq data must be converted into the M x N (mutation-by-cell) and M x T (mutation-by-bulk) alternative/total read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) required as Canopy2 input.

name: mutation-gene-annotation-mapping
description: Use when SNV callsets carry chromosome coordinates but the scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., the featurecounts.qc slot of GBM10_preproc) is keyed by gene identifier, and the two matrices must be row-aligned before bursting estimation.

name: mutation-rate-parameter-sweep
description: Use when validating lineage-reconstruction tools on real expression data paired with simulated barcodes, and you need robustness evidence across mutation rates (e.g., mu in 0.025/0.05/0.075) and dropout settings.

name: mutation-type-categorisation
description: Use when raw COSMIC somatic coding mutation data must be converted into per-gene mutation-type counts and missense functional-impact bins to construct the 37-feature matrix for TSG/OG classification.

name: mutation-type-entropy-feature-interpretation
description: Use when a trained random-forest TSG/OG classifier (37-feature matrix, e.g. FeatureMat.tsv) must be interpreted to identify which mutation-type features (entropy, frequency, ratio-metric) drive the classification.

name: mutational-signature-estimate-visualization
description: Use when you have run mm_fit_signatures on 96-channel trinucleotide catalogs and need to inspect per-sample signature contribution estimates or bootstrap confidence interval distributions before interpreting or reporting signature calls.

name: mutational-signature-fitting
description: Use when assigning reference mutational signatures (e.g. COSMIC v3.1 SBS1, SBS2, SBS5, SBS8, SBS9, SBS13, SBS18, SBS-MM1) to whole-genome or whole-exome SNV catalogs from hematological malignancies and deciding signature presence/absence without hard contribution thresholds.

name: mutsigcv-mutation-rate-comparison
description: Use when reproducing or extending the precision benchmarking of cTaG against MutSigCV, TUSON, 20/20+ and DriverNet on the Bailey et al. 92-gene pan-cancer evaluation set and the CGC driver gene list.

name: mutual-information-co-expression-target-computation
description: Use when building GeneVector gene embeddings from raw scRNA-seq counts in a Scanpy AnnData .X matrix and a co-expression training target is needed, especially to recover metagenes/transcriptional programs (e.g. TGF-beta metagene 24 in TNBC PDX cisplatin time series).

name: mutual-information-network-inference
description: Use when you have a raw or normalized RNA-Seq time-series count table (e.g., DREAM 4 100 genes x 21 samples, B. subtilis 3997 genes x 7 samples) and need a first-pass directed, signed GRN before TFBM/database refinement.

name: mutual-information-regularized-training
description: Use when training a topic model/VAE on multi-batch scRNA-seq (or multiome) data where cell states are batch-confounded and ELBO-only training entangles predicted expression rates with technical effect estimates.

name: mutual-nearest-neighbor-batch-correction
description: Use when extending cluster labels from an FFC-trained dataset to newly arriving (out-of-sample or streaming) test batches that show batch effects relative to the training data, prior to computing the joint affinity matrix.

name: mutual-nearest-neighbor-pair-identification
description: Use when combining scRNA-seq matrices from different batches (e.g., GSE70630 MGH53 & MGH54) and you need to detect which of the ~50 PCA subspaces carry batch effect before removal.

name: mutual-neighbor-graph-construction
description: Use when adapting a source-trained single-cell classifier to unlabeled target cells without raw source data and you need reliable self-supervised neighborhood structure for affinity regularization.

name: mxnet-symbolic-model-definition
description: Use when building an 'explainable' neural deconvolution model in mxnet where each hidden neuron must map to a defined biological entity (cell type) via a masked gene–cell relation matrix, trained with adam/ReLU/L2loss on bulk RNA-seq.

name: myc-copy-number-amplification-analysis
description: Use when analyzing ATAC-Seq samples from SCLC (or similar cancer) cell lines to determine whether MYC resides on ecDNA and whether that ecMYC status elevates MYC copy number and expression.

name: myeloid-differentiation-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when primary AML scRNA-seq samples need a cell-of-origin differentiation-stage call from imputed surface protein levels rather than transcriptome clustering alone.

name: myeloid-isg-variation-preservation-assessment
description: Use when a batch-corrected scRNA-seq embedding (e.g., interferon-beta stimulated PBMCs) must be checked for whether treatment-related variation in myeloid cells survives correction, or when comparing GeneVector batch correction against Harmony using silhouette scores and ISG program scoring.

name: myeloid-lineage-marker-validation
description: Use when CellPath has resolved parallel monocyte differentiation paths in the 6,555 day-4 in vivo mouse hematopoiesis cells and marker genes distinguishing each route must be recovered and verified via per-trajectory DE analysis.

name: myeloma-drug-response-genomics
description: Use when untreated-vs-treated bulk RNA-seq count matrices from drug-sensitive and drug-resistant HMCLs (e.g. 0.5 µM 17-AAG ± 15 nM Ixazomib at 24 h) must be converted into per-contrast DEG counts and ranked gene lists.

name: myoblast-differentiation-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on the Trapnell HSMM myoblast dataset, or when assessing pseudotime accuracy via correlations with differentiation marker genes (ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2) as in STREAM Fig. 5c-d.

name: naive-bayes-deg-classifier-training
description: Use when combining differential expression results from multiple DEG methods (e.g., DESeq2, NOISeq, limma) into a single robust DEG call, and a labelled training set can be generated from simulated data modelled on the target experiment.

name: naive-psi-estimation-from-inclusion-skipping-counts
description: Use when a merged allele-specific splicing count table with IJC/SJC inclusion and skipping junction counts plus effective isoform lengths (incLen, skpLen) is available and naive per-allele PSI (IncLevel) values are needed for quality filtering prior to ASAS testing.

name: nanopore-cell-barcode-umi-recovery
description: Use when raw Nanopore FASTQ reads from 10x 3'/5' or Visium-barcoded libraries need cell-barcode/UMI extraction and error-robust UMI deduplication before isoform or gene quantification.

name: nanopore-current-chunk-kmer-extraction
description: Use when building a training dataset from ONT dRNA fast5/pod5 signal data and you must pair variable-length raw current chunks with their reference kmers to train a modification-detection model.

name: nanopore-drna-basecalling
description: Use when raw ONT dRNA fast5/pod5 signals from SQK-RNA002 or SQK-RNA004 chemistries must be basecalled while simultaneously detecting modified bases (I, m6A, m5C, Psi) without re-squiggling or separate modification models.

name: nanopore-drna-modification-aware-basecalling
description: Use when raw ONT dRNA fast5/pod5 files (SQK-RNA002 or SQK-RNA004) must be basecalled while simultaneously detecting modifications (e.g., inosine, m6A) without re-squiggling or separate modification-scoring models.

name: nanopore-error-model-fault-injection
description: Use when evaluating DNA storage pipeline designs under a channel-with-memory (nanopore) error model, specifically to test whether MSA-only pipelines can compete with HEDGES-MSA when errors are bursty rather than i.i.d.

name: nanopore-long-read-isoform-alignment
description: Use when quantifying isoforms or PSI from single-cell/spatially barcoded Nanopore long reads (e.g., CRCLM sample) and raw minimap2 alignments show misaligned small internal exons inflating false-positive isoforms.

name: nanopore-long-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating long-read isoform quantification pipelines where real data lack gold-standard isoform counts, and a simulated cell-by-isoform matrix with known error profiles is needed as ground truth.

name: ncfs-sparse-gene-weighting
description: Use when clustering single-cell perturbation data where control-defined cell states are available and differential signal must be isolated from noisy genes prior to semi-supervised clustering.

name: nearby-gene-repression-exclusion
description: Use when assembling a putative trans-gene regulatory network from TSS-targeting gRNA association results in a high-MOI single-cell CRISPRi screen, and candidate regulations must be purged of nearby-gene repression signals that likely reflect local cis effects rather than causal trans regulation.

name: nearest-neighbor-cell-querying
description: Use when query scRNA-seq cells (h5ad) must be matched to annotated reference cells for label transfer or cell-type querying, and when similarity should account for posterior uncertainty rather than plain embedding distance.

name: nearest-neighbor-cellstate-classification
description: Use when a scRNA-seq query dataset (e.g., human tumor biopsies converted to mouse orthologs) has been projected onto a reference atlas via make.projection and you need per-cell state labels from the reference subtype vocabulary (e.g., CD8 Tex, Tpex, Treg) with a nearest-neighbor vote.

name: nearest-neighbor-cluster-label-mapping
description: Use when synthetic single-cell observations lack labels and you need ground-truth cluster assignments from a reference dataset to compute clustering-quality metrics such as the Davies–Bouldin index or adjusted Rand index.

name: nearest-neighbor-cross-modality-label-regression
description: Use when you have aligned latent embeddings of two single-cell modalities and need a quantitative downstream benchmark of alignment quality via cross-modality value prediction (Spearman correlations), complementing Leiden-clustering ARI.

name: nearest-neighbor-distance-analysis
description: Use when you must score how hard each cohort sample is to infer from representatives — e.g. comparing active-learning vs passive selection at equal representative counts, or deciding how many representatives are needed for a bulk cohort.

name: nearest-neighbor-distance-computation
description: Use when preparing a raw count matrix (genes x cells, e.g. raw_count.csv) for scImpute dropout imputation and aberrant/low-quality cells must be detected and excluded from the imputation procedure.

name: nearest-neighbor-gaussian-process-fitting
description: Use when you need to rank spatially variable genes in a spatial transcriptomics dataset (SpatialExperiment or coordinates + logcounts matrix), especially with thousands+ spots or within a priori defined spatial domains, and require a flexible per-gene length scale parameter.

name: nearest-neighbor-graph-construction
description: Use when you need a cell-cell similarity network whose neighbor count adapts to local neighborhood density and heterogeneity (e.g., after computing multilevel archetype encodings H*), without pre-specifying k.

name: nearest-neighbor-graph-construction-scrnaseq
description: Use when an annotated scRNA-Seq dataset processed through FindVariableFeatures/ScaleData/RunPCA needs a k-nearest-neighbor cell graph with vertex attributes (e.g. age, disease severity) before community-based differential abundance testing.

name: nearest-neighbor-graph-smoothing
description: Use when scoring sparse, noisy scRNA-seq count data with bulk-style gene set methods (e.g. singscore, ssGSEA, summed_up) and per-cell signal is too weak — e.g. signature genes missed or AUC degraded by downsampling.

name: nearest-neighbor-hit-miss-weighting
description: Use when you need a per-feature ranking by discriminative power from a labeled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. Zeisel et al. mouse cortex) to serve as a baseline against combinatorial marker-selection methods like phenotype cover.

name: nearest-neighbor-reference-profile-matching
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g., 10x Chromium barcoded cells in _counts_UB.tsv) need lineage or cell-type labels without marker genes or supervised training labels, and a suitable reference expression profile set exists.

name: nearest-neighbor-retrieval-cosine-similarity
description: Use when adapting a source-free scRNA-seq annotation model (e.g., scEMAIL) and you need globally-scoped neighborhood structure — bidirectional (mutual nearest), unidirectional, and extensional (neighbors-of-neighbors) sets — to regularize 'known' target cells.

name: nearest-neighbors-graph-construction
description: Use when a single-cell analysis pipeline needs a neighbors graph over cell embeddings (PCA/UMAP/cell-by-gene or protein matrices) as input for Leiden clustering, and dataset size makes exact kNN too slow.

name: nearest-neighbour-conservation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a batch-integration embedding (e.g., JOINTLY on a multi-donor scRNA-seq dataset) is robust to dropping input batches — subsample the donors and compare neighbour structure and metrics to the full reference.

name: nearest-neighbour-distance-computation
description: Use when building the distance layer of a rare-cell detection pipeline: you have a large scRNA-seq expression matrix and need per-cell nearest-neighbour distances (D<m,k>) feeding skewness>k>2 gap statistics.

name: nearest-neighbour-overcorrection-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking cross-species (or multi-dataset) integration strategies and you need to check whether integrated embeddings preserve distinguishability of cell types present in only a subset of input datasets, as species count increases.

name: nearest-template-prediction
description: Use when you need to classify pre-clinical colorectal cancer models (cell lines, patient-derived organoids, xenografts) into CMS1–CMS4 subtypes from a gene expression matrix, since the original CMS classifier fails on these stroma-free samples.

name: needleman-wunsch-umi-similarity-scoring
description: Use when recovering/collapsing UMIs from noisy Nanopore single-cell long reads where fixed edit-distance collapsing (e.g., DBSCAN eps=2, Sicelore2, FLAMES) overestimates UMI numbers, or when needing an alignment-score-based similarity graph for UMI clustering.

name: negative-binomial-autoencoder-denoising
description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. .h5ad from 10X Genomics) with dropout-affected counts that must be denoised/imputed before correlation, visualization, or differential analyses, or when benchmarking denoising methods.

name: negative-binomial-cell-count-simulation
description: Use when you need to validate the false-positive rate of a proportion analysis tool (e.g., Scanpro) on simulated null data with two conditions and unchanged cluster proportions, with or without real replicates.

name: negative-binomial-count-likelihood-modeling
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices (RNA_count.mtx, Protein_count.mtx) feed a deep generative model and you want likelihoods that match overdispersed count distributions, avoiding log-normalization preprocessing.

name: negative-binomial-count-simulation
description: Use when building a bulk RNA-seq simulator with realistic count distributions: you need NB draws per gene, time point and replicate, plus controlled DEG profiles (induction, repression, transitory, flat) and coupled regulator profiles.

name: negative-binomial-decoder-reconstruction
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices show noisy gene-gene relationships (e.g., low marker co-expression correlations) and a trained batch-invariant scPhere model is available whose decoder can impute denoised negative-binomial mean expression values.

name: negative-binomial-decoder-simulation
description: Use when synthetic single-cell count data must be generated without relying on copies of the original cells — e.g., enlarging a small pilot scRNA-seq dataset (such as PBMC4k, 4182 cells × 1000 HVGs) after a VAE like scVI has been trained on it.

name: negative-binomial-deep-boltzmann-machine-training
description: Use when you need to generate synthetic scRNA-seq count data from a small pilot dataset (a few hundred to ~2300 cells) with a generative model that avoids the posterior-sampling bias amplification seen in scVI, e.g. for pilot-study-based power analysis.

name: negative-binomial-dispersion-estimation
description: Use when training scDBM or similar NB-based generative models on scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k 4182 cells × 1000 HVGs) and per-gene inverse dispersion (θ) estimates are needed for the negative-binomial likelihood.

name: negative-binomial-dispersion-estimation
description: Use when modeling scRNA-seq count data requires comparing goodness-of-fit of zero-inflated NB vs negative binomial (edgeR) vs hurdle (MAST) models in terms of mean count, zero (dropout) probability, and dispersion estimation.

name: negative-binomial-gaussian-copula-count-simulation
description: Use when evaluating or benchmarking gene co-expression estimators (CS-CORE, rho-sctransform, locCSN, etc.) on synthetic UMI counts where a known true latent correlation must be held fixed across a grid of expression levels.

name: negative-binomial-gene-count-simulation
description: Use when evaluating whether a co-expression estimator applied to log-normalized scRNA-seq UMI counts produces false positives: simulate counts for an independent gene pair under a negative-binomial model with zero true co-expression and measure the spurious correlation each method reports.

name: negative-binomial-generative-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking circadian phase-inference methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data, or when choosing a count likelihood distribution for unsupervised phase inference from droplet scRNA-seq (e.g. 10X Genomics Chromium) data.

name: negative-binomial-glm-copy-number-fitting
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI/read counts must be transformed into copy-number states (loss/neutral/gain) per gene and cell via negative-binomial statistical modeling with HMM smoothing.

name: negative-binomial-glm-fitting
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple time points plus metadata with a binary Group factor and a Time variable, and need to detect genes whose expression trends over time differ between conditions (tDEGs).

name: negative-binomial-likelihood-ratio-testing
description: Use when comparing two single-cell Hi-C conditions (e.g., mouse oocyte vs zygote, Astro vs Endo) at bin-pair resolution from a normalized count table, and per-bin-pair differential interaction calls with raw and BH-adjusted p-values are needed.

name: negative-binomial-mean-extraction
description: Use when scMM has been trained on transcriptome + surface-protein CITE-seq counts and you must score held-out transcriptome-to-protein crossmodal generation via NB mean-parameter correlations.

name: negative-binomial-mixed-model-fitting
description: Use when analyzing droplet-based multi-subject scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., thousands of cells across dozens of subjects) where per-gene tests must account for hierarchical overdispersion, or when glmer.nb-style NB mixed models are too slow for genome-scale testing (~16,000 genes).

name: negative-binomial-mixed-model-overdispersion-estimation
description: Use when analyzing large-scale multi-subject droplet scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq count data (e.g., human frontal cortex snRNA-seq, PBMCs) where hierarchical overdispersion must be decomposed into between-subject and within-subject components per gene.

name: negative-binomial-model-fitting
description: Decision support for choosing between NB and ZINB noise models before denoising an scRNA-seq count matrix with DCA, when you need to test whether the zero-inflation component is required for your data.

name: negative-binomial-noise-baseline-simulation
description: Use when a synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark needs a noise-floor control: pilot sub-samples (384–2304 cells) exist and Davies–Bouldin indices of generative models (scDBM, scVI) must be judged against NB-noise-augmented pilot data.

name: negative-binomial-parameter-estimation
description: Use when building synthetic multi-sample scRNA-seq count data for benchmarking differential state (DS) methods and you have a real reference dataset (e.g. muscat's example_sce) to anchor the simulation.

name: negative-binomial-quantile-matching-correction
description: Use when raw read count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches must be converted into batch-effect-corrected, dropout-imputed counts for downstream analysis (t-SNE, clustering, DE) without further cell-specific normalization.

name: negative-binomial-regression-cell-counts
description: Use when testing whether counts of attribute-enriched cell communities (from ProcessEVA) shift with a biological condition across replicates, e.g. naive-vs-mature Cd4+ T-cells with age or stem/T-reg fractions with cancer stage.

name: negative-binomial-regression-da-testing
description: Use when significant condition-enriched cell communities (e.g. from EVA/ProcessEVA with a Bonferroni-thresholded binomial test) have been identified on a cell-cell kNN graph and their cell counts must be formally tested for differential abundance across a condition such as age or disease stage.

name: negative-binomial-regression-mixture-models
description: Use when you need to assign droplets from HTO-labeled pooled scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq experiments to their sample of origin (including multiplet detection) from an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix, optionally with per-droplet genes-detected counts as a covariate.

name: negative-binomial-zinb-expression-modeling
description: Use when a feature-selection or variable-gene method needs fair performance comparison on controlled synthetic scRNA-seq data, especially where subpopulations at fractions of 50%, 20%, 10%, and 1% must be embedded to test sensitivity to rare cell types.

name: negative-control-benchmarking
description: Use when assessing the false-positive rate of circlehunter ecDNA calls on non-cancer ATAC-Seq data (e.g., normal tissue) that lacks ecDNA amplification, or when validating a circlehunter installation before applying it to tumor samples.

name: negative-control-feature-selection-for-batch-correction
description: Use when integrating atlas-scale multi-sample multi-condition single-cell studies (e.g. >1M cells across cohorts like COMBAT and Geanon CyTOF) and you need control features to guide unsupervised batch/dataset-effect removal.

name: negative-gene-set-subtraction-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking gene-set enrichment scoring methods on scRNA-seq data where clusters are defined by unique gene combinations rather than single marker genes, and standard scoring underperforms on precision/accuracy.

name: negative-log-likelihood-loss-optimization
description: Use when pre-training a source classification model on raw scRNA-seq count matrices where dropout/dropout events require a probabilistic denoising loss (ZINB NLL) alongside supervised classification loss.

name: negative-log-likelihood-loss-optimization
description: Use when a single-cell graph convolutional autoencoder's decoder must model the scRNA-seq count distribution and simulate dropout events via a multinomial likelihood with dropout probabilities for zero-count entries, instead of a zero-inflated distribution.

name: negative-prediction-clamping-during-recursion
description: Use when running recursive multi-step predictions with RNAForecaster's predictCellFutures (e.g., 72 hourly steps on scEU-seq RPE data) and network outputs must be constrained to biologically realistic expression ranges.

name: negative-query-rejection-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type prediction methods on reference/query scRNA-seq dataset groups that include both positive queries and negative queries, so specificity (rejecting absent cell types) is scored alongside assignment accuracy.

name: negative-signal-subsampling-in-multi-hashtag-experiments
description: Use when demultiplexing a cell hashing experiment with more than 4 hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes, where negative-signal dominance degrades cutoff accuracy in HTOreader's HTOcutoff step.

name: neighbor-cell-type-score-computation
description: Use when building cell-cell communication networks from single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., seqFISH+ mouse cortex, Seq-Scope mouse colon) where a coordinate matrix and cell type label vector are available and neighbor exposure scores must precede regression modeling.

name: neighbor-joining-tree-initialization
description: Use when starting LinRace lineage reconstruction for a barcode group: you have a character matrix of mutated barcode loci and need an initial binary topology before likelihood-based local search.

name: neighbor-majority-label-propagation
description: Use when benchmarking a semi-supervised scRNA-seq label propagation model (e.g. scSHARP's GCN) against a simple nonparametric neighbor-voting baseline on PCA-embedded cells with reference labels.

name: neighbor-voting-cell-type-identification
description: Use when comparing cell types across two or more scRNA-seq datasets without shared labels, to identify reciprocal matches (AUROC >= 0.95) and assess how well novel subtypes replicate across studies.

name: neighbor-voting-label-prediction
description: Use when you need to quantify how well cell-type labels replicate across two or more scRNA-seq datasets by predicting labels for cells from one held-out dataset based on their similarity to labeled cells in training datasets.

name: neighborhood-based-cell-state-transition-mapping
description: Use when reconstructing multi-branching developmental trajectories from scRNA-seq (e.g. FACS-sorted progenitor populations like MDP/CDP/preDC or time-course myoblast data) where branching points and cell fates must be inferred without known temporal ordering.

name: neighborhood-based-transition-edge-weighting
description: Use when reconstructing cell-state transition graphs from landmark- or cluster-labeled single-cell data, where edge support should be quantified by counting cells whose two nearest landmark states define each candidate edge.

name: neighborhood-component-feature-selection-gene-weighting
description: Use when clustering single-cell perturbation data where control-defined cell states are already labeled, and non-explanatory gene variance must be down-weighted before assigning perturbed cells to states.

name: neighborhood-correspondence-statistical-testing
description: Use when you need to statistically judge whether local structures in a t-SNE/UMAP embedding reflect real high-dimensional signal rather than stochastic DR distortion, e.g. to color cells by embedding quality or pick DR hyperparameters.

name: neighborhood-count-probability-estimation
description: Use when building a conditional cell-specific network (CCSN) from a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix and you must estimate rho_xy|z(k) via scatter-diagram neighborhood counts given a conditional gene z.

name: neighborhood-regularization-in-transfer-learning
description: Use when adapting a pre-trained source classifier to unlabeled scRNA-seq target data source-free, and you need self-supervised regularization on 'known' cells using neighborhood structure to counter batch effect.

name: nematode-small-rna-class-assignment
description: Use when quantifying C. elegans small RNA classes (22G-/26G-RNAs) from genome-aligned small RNA-seq FASTQ data, especially when distinct classes derive from the same genes and must be separated by 5′ nucleotide, length, and strandedness rules.

name: neoantigen-confidence-ranking
description: Use when you have candidate peptide-MHC predictions with DeepHLApan binding and immunogenicity scores plus gene expression (TPM) values and need to select high-confidence neoantigens per sample.

name: neoantigen-immunogenicity-score-analysis
description: Use when you have a table of predicted pMHC scores (e.g., DeepHLApan binding and immunogenicity scores) with experimental immunogenicity labels, and need to test whether the score separates immunogenic from non-immunogenic peptides.

name: neoantigen-pipeline-hla-input-preparation
description: Use when preparing patient-level HLA class I typing from tumor-normal FASTQ inputs as a required input for MHC binding/immunogenicity neoantigen prediction (e.g., DeepHLApan in TSNAD).

name: neoantigen-prioritization-output-interpolation
description: Use when starting from raw WES/DNA-seq and RNA-seq FASTQ reads and you need per-sample predicted neoantigen output tables spanning SNVs, indels, alternative splicing, exitrons, and gene fusions.

name: neoantigen-threshold-filtering-and-ranking
description: Use when candidate mutant peptides (8–11 aa) already have DeepHLApan binding and immunogenicity scores and need to be filtered into potential vs high-confidence neoantigens.

name: neoepitope-kmer-extraction-from-variant-proteins
description: Use when HLA genotypes (mhc-I.tsv / mhc-II.tsv) and per-variant variant_effects.tsv files are available and predicted MHC-binding neoepitopes with mutant-vs-wildtype affinity scores must be produced.

name: nested-cross-validation-model-fitting
description: Use when fitting lasso/elastic-net or caret-based models on high-dimensional data (e.g. RNA-seq with far more predictors than samples) and you need unbiased performance estimates plus feature selection without information leakage.

name: nested-cross-validation-performance-estimation
description: Use when a small-n, high-predictor-count (P >> n) dataset needs unbiased model accuracy (e.g. ROC AUC) while feature selection or class balancing must be embedded inside the CV loop to avoid information leakage.

name: nested-model-likelihood-ratio-testing
description: Use when testing whether adding a sample covariate (group, condition) or its interaction with pseudotime significantly improves a gene-level generalized model, e.g., to call XDE/TDE genes.

name: network-based-drug-repurposing
description: Use when a trait- or cell-type-associated co-expression module or GRN has already been inferred (e.g. SCANet WGCNA modules like M11/M4) and you need mechanistic drug repurposing candidates targeting its hub/key-driver genes.

name: network-benchmark-auc-evaluation
description: Use when a directed TF-target network (e.g. from scGATE, CellOracle, Loregic) must be quantitatively scored against a known ground-truth GRN to reproduce or report AUROC/AUPRC benchmark performance.

name: network-cartography-classification
description: Use when cluster-specific GRN Links objects exist for a cell trajectory (e.g. fibroblast → reprogramming → iEP clusters) and you need degree/eigenvector centrality trajectories and cartography role classification to compare network configurations across clusters.

name: network-centrality-analysis-and-visualization
description: Use when a weighted TF-target network (edge table with correlation scores) has been inferred and you must identify the most important regulator(s) and visualize network modules, e.g. from scMEGA GetGRN output.

name: network-connected-component-analysis
description: Use when a cell type's driving forces (key nodes) must be identified and a gene-gene regulatory network needs to be inferred, checked for connectivity, and its key nodes ranked.

name: network-constrained-expression-permutation-testing
description: Use when you need to show that SR-based potency discrimination (e.g. pluripotent vs non-pluripotent cells) or its monotonic decrease with developmental stage collapses when expression values are reshuffled over the PPI network — i.

name: network-control-theory-driver-regulator-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data along a single developmental lineage plus a prior gene interaction network are available and the goal is to identify the driver regulators (e.g., top-20 per lineage) steering that cell fate trajectory.

name: network-cross-validation-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when fitting MuDCoD (or similar smoothed spectral community detection) to multi-subject dynamic networks and the eigenvector-smoothing penalty strengths alpha (over time points) and beta (across subjects) must be tuned rather than guessed.

name: network-degree-hub-identification
description: Use when scLink networks have been inferred for multiple conditions or time points and you need to identify genes whose connectivity (hub status) changes, e.g., 0 h vs 96 h of DE differentiation.

name: network-degree-matrix-computation
description: Use when per-cell CCSNs from c-CSN are available and the goal is to convert them into an m genes × n cells degree matrix (CNDM) so clustering, dimension reduction, or NFE analysis can operate on network data instead of the raw gene expression matrix.

name: network-diffusion-analysis
description: Use when cell-type-specific GRNs are already built (e.g. via scRank Constr_net on untreated scRNA-seq like GSE110894) and you must rank cell types by responsiveness to a drug with a known target gene (e.g. Brd4).

name: network-edge-filtering
description: Use when a raw BoostDiff output network (boostdiff_network_<keyword>.txt) must be reduced to condition-specific edges before Louvain module detection, KEGG enrichment, or network visualization.

name: network-edge-filtering-and-visualization
description: Use when a TF-gene correlation/eGRN edge table has been computed (e.g. via scMEGA GetTFGeneCorrelation) and needs threshold-based pruning and network visualization.

name: network-edge-perturbation-noise-analysis
description: Use when assessing sensitivity of regulator activity estimates to prior knowledge resource errors — e.g. simulating incomplete or spurious network edges before trusting downstream TF or kinase activity calls.

name: network-fusion-spectral-clustering
description: Use when you already have one or more low-dimensional cell representations (e.g. VAE latents) of scRNA-seq data and need cell-type clusters plus an estimate of the number of clusters from the fused similarity graph.

name: network-hub-gene-detection
description: Use when per-cell scRNA-seq gene expression data has been transformed into a CCSN/CNDM degree matrix and you need to detect modules and rank hub genes by network degree to pinpoint key regulators of differentiation.

name: network-inference-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantitatively validate a GRN inference method against ground truth — specifically when you have a fitted network matrix A and need to test whether refitting on simulated expression recovers the true regulator-target edges.

name: network-inference-method-comparison
description: Use when choosing a GRN construction method for scRNA-seq data, or when reproducing benchmark curves of accuracy/recall versus cell count against known regulatory edges.

name: network-method-prediction-thresholding
description: Use when benchmarking pan-cancer driver-gene predictions against published methods (TUSON, 20/20+, DriverNet) using precision TP/(TP+FP) against reference driver lists such as Bailey et al. or CGC.

name: network-metric-reimplementation
description: Use when a paper reports a per-protein network statistic (e.g. HSPH1's network density score of 78%) that must be independently recomputed from the underlying interaction network rather than taken on trust.

name: network-node-centrality-computation
description: Use when you have directed network topologies (e.g., KEGG GRAPHML pathways) plus a per-node data-driven importance score and need to test whether that score is decoupled from — or redundant with — network topology.

name: network-percolation-node-filtering
description: Use when constructing group-specific subnetworks from DEGGs differential interaction networks and needing to prune low-expression nodes via an expression-based percolation cut-off optimized for maximum significant links.

name: network-regularized-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when scoring differential-expression p-values against a large, redundant pathway database (KEGG, Reactome, GO) and you want enrichment estimates that exploit inter-pathway relations via a pathway-similarity network.

name: network-regularized-regression-fitting
description: Use when you have a gene-level p-value table (gene, pvalue) and a pathway database such as GO biological process (terms of size 50-500), and redundant/overlapping pathways make standard enrichment tests unstable or incoherent.

name: network-sparsity-comparison
description: Use when comparing per-cell edge counts of CSN versus CCSN built from a normalized scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., Buettner mESC) to verify that conditional independence testing yields sparser, direct-association-only gene–gene networks.

name: network-statistics-reproduction
description: Use when a task asks you to reproduce, verify, or cross-check reported network statistics (e.g. '16 of 90 genes with correlation >= 0.9', 'GRN regulators GATA2, MAFF, FOSB', Table 2 / Fig. 3B / Fig. 3D values) from a co-expression or regulatory network analysis.

name: network-topology-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing multiple GRN inference methods on single-cell expression data and you need quantitative, method-agnostic topology and reproducibility metrics (scale-free fit, edge counts, betweenness variance, edge overlap) to judge which method's networks are structurally most plausible.

name: network-transpose-normalization
description: Use when comparing predicted gene networks from attention- or regression-based inference methods to a directed source-to-target ground truth (e.g., Omnipath) whose regulators have sparse out-degree, so predicted edge matrices must be transposed to align regulator/target conventions.

name: network-validation-against-reference-databases
description: Use when you have a predicted protein interaction network with confidence scores (e.g. FAVA output filtered at ≥70% Pearson correlation confidence) and must quantify its novelty and agreement against STRING or hu.MAP 2.0.

name: network-weight-leveraging-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing enrichment/activity-inference methods that differ only in whether they leverage interaction weights, or when validating that weight-aware decoupleR methods outperform their weight-ignoring counterparts on perturbed-regulator prediction.

name: neural-attribution-gene-ranking-interpretation
description: Use when a trained scSHARP GCN cell-type classifier needs feature interpretation — i.e., you must rank genes by DeepLIFT attribution per cell type and/or validate those attributions against differential expression marker lists.

name: neural-cell-cell-communication-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq data with cell-type/subclass annotations from neural tissue (e.

name: neural-encoder-architecture-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking whether a denoising autoencoder with Leiden cell-cluster label regularization outperforms a plain AE or unregularized variant for single-cell drug sensitivity prediction.

name: neural-network-cell-annotation-training
description: Use when labeled training scRNA-seq data exist for the tissue and every cell type in the test sample is expected to be present in the reference, and exhaustive cell label assignment is needed.

name: neural-network-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating single cells from cancer scRNA-seq data (Seurat object, counts matrix csv/rds/h5, or 10X folder) into tumor microenvironment cell types without marker-gene curation or programming.

name: neural-network-cell-type-classification
description: Use when training cell labels exist for scRNA-seq reference data and every cell type in the test sample is expected to already exist in the reference, especially with closely correlated cell types or inter-study PBMC transfer.

name: neural-network-classifier-application
description: Use when simulated or empirical deletion-event expression data (space-delimited, N+1 rows x 3m columns with derived/survived/lost blocks) must be classified as 'Redundant' vs 'Unique' by the already-tuned CLOUDe neural network, e.g. when validating power under the alternative theta0 scenario.

name: neural-network-classifier-training
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq count matrices from two timepoints (t0/t1), labels for the t0 cells, and need supervised cross-timepoint cell-type annotation of t1 cells.

name: neural-network-classifier-training
description: Use when a labeled reference scRNA-seq matrix and an unlabeled query matrix must be processed through scNovel's two-stage pipeline, i.e. a trained cell-type probability classifier is needed before novel cell detection with threshold lambda = 0.5.

name: neural-network-classifier-training-scrnaseq
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq training data with known cell labels (e.g. Baron/Muraro/Seg/Xin pancreas or 10X PBMC) and need to assign labels to testing cells in an exhaustive supervised setting.

name: neural-network-convergence-verification
description: Use when running the ScribbleDom pipeline (run_other_visium.sh or run_other_st.sh) and you must confirm the training loop converged for each sample and that per-sample results were written to final_outputs/{dataset}/{samples[i]}/.

name: neural-network-deconvolution-training
description: Use when paired annotated scRNA-seq and spot-based spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Chromium + 10x Visium from GSE173778) are available and cell type proportions per spot must be learned from simulated mixtures.

name: neural-network-deconvolution-workflow-execution
description: Use when you have a paired scRNA-seq reference and spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. 10x Visium spots) and need cell type deconvolution via a trained neural network, including benchmarking runtime/RAM against RCTD and cell2location.

name: neural-network-dropout-perturbation
description: Use when training DCNet (or a similar gene-embedded ANN) on bulk RNA-seq data and you need to test whether zero-fill input perturbation improves generalization, or when comparing autoencoder sizes vs. dropout variants by RMSE.

name: neural-network-early-stopping-training
description: Use when training the DCA autoencoder (64-32-64 hidden layers, 32-dim bottleneck, ZINB loss) on raw scRNA-seq counts and you need a validation-driven early-stopping and learning-rate-reduction schedule.

name: neural-network-embedding-training
description: Use when a high-dimensional single-cell (scRNA-seq or CyTOF) expression matrix must be reduced to a low-dimensional embedding at scale — especially >100k cells where t-SNE is too slow.

name: neural-network-feature-selection
description: Use when you must rank/select genes from a high-dimensional labeled RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor/normal) and DEG analysis alone cannot pick an optimal biomarker combination.

name: neural-network-hyperparameter-cross-validation
description: Use when training the CLOUDe neural network on Ornstein–Uhlenbeck-simulated training data (p=3m expression features) and you must select optimal lambda, gamma, and number of hidden layers by five-fold cross-validation before classification.

name: neural-network-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when training an autoencoder-based imputation model (e.g., AutoImpute) on a sparse single-cell expression matrix and the cost-function regularization coefficient, hidden layer size, learning rate, or convergence threshold must be selected before final training.

name: neural-network-inference-in-r
description: Use when expression data for two-species gene deletion events (space-delimited 3m-column EmpiricalData.data format) must be classified and have OU evolutionary parameters predicted via pre-trained multi-layer neural network models.

name: neural-network-loss-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when training a deep generative model (e.g. VASC on the Pollen scRNA-seq dataset) and you need to verify that the loss curve has converged to a stable lower limit before saving weights or interpreting latent representations.

name: neural-network-proportion-prediction
description: Use when a trained SpatialDDLS model must predict cell type composition for 10x Visium spots, or when per-spot proportions need neighbor-aware spatial regularization using k.spots = 6 extrinsic profiles.

name: neural-network-training-hyperparameter-configuration
description: Use when building the VAE dimensionality-reduction stage of FAVA: input is a high-dimensional protein-by-condition omics matrix (TSV/CSV, AnnData-compatible) that must be compressed to a low-dimensional latent space before correlation-based network inference.

name: neural-network-transfer-learning-training
description: Use when you have paired transcriptome–surface-protein training data (e.g., CITE-PBMC, CITE-CBMC, REAP-PBMC) and want to train or fine-tune a model that imputes immunophenotype protein levels for transcriptome-only single-cell data.

name: neural-network-transfer-learning-training
description: Use when two species' scRNA-seq datasets must be matched at the cell type level: gene identities differ across species, so a cross-species gene similarity distance matrix (e.g. from ProtBERT protein embeddings) is available and a confusion-matrix-style label transfer is the goal.

name: neural-ode-forecasting
description: Use when you have paired time-point scRNA-seq count matrices from the same cells (e.g., metabolic labeling scEU-seq) and need to predict future single-cell expression states beyond the immediate observed changes that RNA velocity provides.

name: neural-ode-latent-dynamics-modeling
description: Use when estimating RNA velocity on datasets with multiple lineages, time-dependent transcription/splicing rates, or batch effects where strict steady-state/linear dynamical assumptions fail.

name: neural-ode-model-training
description: Use when paired time-point scRNA-seq count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns, e.g. BoolODE simulations or metabolic-labeling scEU-seq data) are available and the goal is to forecast future single-cell expression states.

name: neuron-layer-communication-validation
description: Use when a CPPLS-MLP cell–cell communication prediction on the seqFISH+ mouse cortex dataset links two cortical layer cell types (e.g., L5 eNeuron → L6 eNeuron) and a spatial expression visualization of a target gene is needed to confirm the predicted communication.

name: neuron-projection-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when validating inferred cell-cell communication networks against anatomical projection ground truth, or when checking whether benchmark performance depends on cell-type labels versus network topology via label-shuffling permutation.

name: neuronal-morphology-scrna-integration
description: Use when integrating unpaired morphology image features with scRNA-seq profiles (e.g. Patch-seq 625 morphologies with 589 RNA-only cells) to test whether scRNA-defined populations, like IT neurons, show molecular-morphological structure.

name: neuronchat-object-creation-and-network-aggregation
description: Use when starting from a normalized scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics count matrix with cell-type annotations and you need inferred neural-specific ligand-receptor communication networks aggregated by cell group (human DB='human', mouse DB='mouse').

name: neurotransmitter-ligand-abundance-scoring
description: Use when inferring neuron-neuron communication strength from scRNA-seq for neurotransmitter-type entries (glutamate, GABA, etc.) whose 'ligand' is a small molecule synthesized and vesicularly transported by the sender group, and you must convert gene expression into a ligand abundance score.

name: newick-tree-parsing
description: Use when simulating multiple discrete or continuous cell populations in SymSim, since SimulateTrueCounts requires a phyla tree object (Newick file read with ape::read.tree, or built-in Phyla5()/Phyla3()) to define population structure.

name: newton-raphson-likelihood-maximization
description: Use when fitting a zero-inflated Tweedie (ZICP) per-gene model to scRNA-seq read counts with excessive zeros and you need maximum-likelihood estimates of regression coefficients, dispersion, and the index parameter p.

name: nextflow-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw amplicon FASTQ data (population-level bulk or single-cell barcoding) must be processed through a reproducible, containerized Nextflow pipeline such as DaneVass/bartab, and execution profile/mode selection is needed.

name: nextflow-workflow-execution
description: Use when a publication provides a Nextflow workflow repository (e.g. guigolab/sqtlseeker2-nf) and you need to reproduce its containerized analysis on your own per-tissue input files.

name: nk-cell-marker-identification
description: Use when a Leiden-clustered scATAC-seq gene activity matrix needs cluster annotation, and you must confirm whether a known immune marker (e.g. KLRD1 for NK cells) appears among top differentially expressed genes per cluster.

name: nk-cell-subpopulation-differential-expression
description: Use when jointly analyzing multiple single-cell immunotherapy cohorts of CD45+ cells to identify which cell subpopulation (e.g., NK cells) differs transcriptomically between responders and non-responders.

name: nk-cell-surface-marker-phenotyping
description: Use when CITE-seq data shows protein (ADT) evidence of cell sub-populations, e.g. CD16/CD56 NK markers, that is hidden in the matching RNA counts by dropout, and you need to quantify whether denoising recovers it.

name: nmf-clustering-of-rbp-feature-matrices
description: Use when a merged candidate-RBP feature matrix (e.g., MATRIX.txt) must be partitioned into clusters whose enrichment for known circRNA regulators (gold_regulators.xlsx) is tested to select candidate regulators.

name: nmf-dictionary-learning-with-elastic-net
description: Use when a well-annotated source scRNA-Seq dataset (e.g. Usoskin et al. 2014, GSE59739, 622 cells) is available and its cluster labels should be encoded as a dictionary for subsequent transfer learning to a small target dataset.

name: nmf-signaling-pattern-discovery
description: Use when a CellChat communication probability network (cell groups x signaling pathways) is available and the goal is to decompose sender/receiver signaling into outgoing and incoming patterns and group signaling pathways by functional or structural similarity.

name: nmf-splicing-subcluster-discovery
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contains splice-junction evidence suggesting transcriptionally similar cells split by exon usage (e.g. pediatric AML blasts), and gene-expression clustering alone fails to resolve those subpopulations.

name: nmi-ari-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when a clustering method's predicted cell assignments must be scored against ground-truth labels (e.g., Splatter-simulated or annotated scRNA-seq datasets) with NMI and ARI to build benchmark comparison tables.

name: nmi-ari-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when quantitatively comparing dimension-reduction or clustering methods on labeled scRNA-seq datasets, e.g., scoring k-means on 2D latent representations with NMI/ARI against true cell labels.

name: nmi-ari-metric-computation
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq clustering results (e.g., SSRE/SSR/spectral-clustering assignments) against ground-truth cell-type labels and a reproducible NMI/ARI benchmark table is needed.

name: nmi-ari-metric-computation
description: Use when clustering solutions from multiple algorithms must be quantitatively compared against known ground-truth labels using accuracy, NMI, and ARI — e.g., benchmarking KMD clustering on simulated datasets where y_true is available.

name: nmi-clustering-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing whether gene modules or regulons from competing GRN methods better capture known cell states: you have an activity matrix per cell, reference cell-type labels, and need an NMI clustering benchmark.

name: nmi-clustering-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing how compactly and purely different single-cell embeddings (unimodal vs multimodal) group cells by a categorical label such as pMHC antigen specificity, using clustering quality metrics.

name: nmi-clustering-metric-computation
description: Use when you have predicted cluster labels from an scRNA-seq embedding (e.g. Louvain clusters on scGAE latent embeddings) plus ground-truth cell labels and need a single NMI score per condition, such as comparing clustering across dropout-rate variants.

name: nmi-clustering-quality-assessment
description: Use when comparing unsupervised feature selection methods (e.g., DELVE, Hotspot, Laplacian Score) on single-cell data and you need a clustering-based score of how well each top-p feature set recapitulates known cell states or phases.

name: nmi-cross-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing community detection methods on personalized dynamic networks and you need a subject-consistency metric (NMI between donors) plus a non-parametric significance test (Wilcoxon rank-sum) per time point.

name: nngraph-clustering-of-cell-embeddings
description: Use when you have a cell-by-dimension embedding matrix (e.g., CA embeddings from corral on counts, or PCA on log(x+1) logcounts) and need to assign cells to clusters to quantify recovery of annotated cell types by ARI.

name: nnls-cell-similarity-weighting
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix contains dropout zeros (gene moderate in some cells, undetected in others) and only the likely dropouts — not the rest of the data — should be imputed before clustering or differential expression.

name: nnls-cell-type-proportion-estimation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq read counts must be deconvolved into known cell type proportions using a single-cell reference, and an unweighted NNLS baseline (Est.prop.allgene) is needed to benchmark against weighted estimators like MuSiC.

name: node-degree-null-standardization
description: Use when reconstructing or reimplementing MetaNeighbor's neighbor-voting predictor from the Methods: you have a cell-cell similarity network plus a binary cell-type membership vector and need degree-normalized vote scores per cell for downstream AUROC computation.

name: node-level-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when RNA-seq read-count data must be analyzed per KEGG pathway node containing multiple functionally homologous genes, to identify which homolog dominates enzymatic activity and the node's overall up/down regulation (e.g., the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564).

name: node-level-read-count-aggregation
description: Use when KEGG KGML pathway nodes contain multiple functionally homologous genes catalyzing the same reaction and you need a single node-level RNA-seq read-count value plus identification of the dominant (most-expressed) gene per node.

name: node-panel-function-reconstruction
description: Use when a fitted dipm or spmtree tree object needs per-node subgroup visualization via partykit::plot, and the tree's outcome is continuous (e.g. anorexia) or survival (e.g. GBSG2).

name: noise-augmented-gan-generator-training
description: Use when training a cross-modal single-cell GAN where you need stochastic generator outputs to estimate mapping uncertainty, e.g. comparing per-gene variance for genes with vs without an analogous measured modality.

name: noise-correlation-assessment-single-cell
description: Use when reproducing or validating the dsb noise model on a droplet CITE-seq dataset: you have raw+filtered Cell Ranger ADT matrices, empty droplets, and want to confirm the µ1–isotype (Cor 1) and µ1–library-size (Cor 2) correlations across single cells.

name: noise-perturbation-robustness-evaluation
description: Use when a simulated tensor with known embedded patterns (e.g., 4 temporal patterns across 3 cell types, 300 LR pairs, 12 contexts) must be shown recoverable, or when rank selection must be stress-tested against measurement noise.

name: noise-robustness-assessment-across-instances
description: Use when you need to quantify how noise-tolerant a decomposition/clustering method is on scRNA-seq data: you have synthetic instances with known planted identity/activity patterns (e.g., 20 instances, 14 planted patterns, 3 noise levels) and want pattern-recovery purity per noise level.

name: noise-spacing-statistical-thresholding
description: Use when you must choose the rank k of a randomized-SVD low-rank approximation of a normalized scRNA-seq matrix and cannot identify the 'beginning of noise' by eye from the spectrum; 50–300 chars ok.

name: noisy-celltype-label-perturbation
description: Use when benchmarking supervised/semi-supervised single-cell integration methods that consume cell type labels, and you must quantify degradation under incomplete or imprecise annotations rather than only testing on curated ground truth.

name: noisy-single-cell-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking whether a GRN inference method (e.g., scKINETICS EM fitting) can recover a known ground-truth regulatory matrix A from simulated expression trajectories with added noise.

name: non-binary-information-quantification-delta-sil-shuffle
description: Use when benchmarking scLENS on real or simulated scRNA-seq datasets and you need to quantify the amount of non-binary (graded, non-zero-count) signal the embedding retains, e.g. to relate performance gains to dataset sparsity.

name: non-mammalian-scrnaseq-processing
description: Use when TE quantification must be benchmarked or applied on non-mammalian scRNA-seq data (e.g., Arabidopsis or Drosophila 10X alignments) and you need ARI-based comparison of TE-derived versus gene-derived cell clustering across MATES, scTE, and SoloTE.

name: non-model-species-ortholog-annotation
description: Use when the input gene IDs or RNA-seq reads come from a non-model eukaryotic species (e.g. salamander) and downstream KEGG/GO pathway analysis requires mapping those IDs to model-organism orthologs or KEGG ortholog (KO) IDs.

name: non-model-species-rnaseq-functional-profiling
description: Use when starting from raw paired-end FASTQ reads of a non-model eukaryotic species (no reference transcriptome needed) and the goal is a KO-level ortholog count matrix for downstream statistical analysis.

name: non-negative-autoencoder-implementation
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (genes x cells) must be filtered to an informative gene set and compressed to a ~50-dimensional representation before clustering, visualization, or classification with scDHA.

name: non-negative-least-squares-decomposition
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq (ExpressionSet) and single-cell/snRNA-seq data from the same tissue are available — including overlapping individuals — and cell-type proportions must be estimated while correcting single-cell technical biases.

name: non-negative-matrix-factorization-transfer-learning
