description: Use when clustering a small target scRNA-Seq dataset where a large well-annotated source dataset (shared gene space, non-negative counts) is available and rare cell types are hard to resolve with SC3 alone.

name: non-velocity-ablation-benchmarking
description: Use when a trajectory method uses RNA velocity and you need to quantify its contribution by ablating velocity (distance-only variant) and comparing pseudotime against an elapsed-time or known-ordering reference.

name: noncoding-variant-annotation
description: Use when fine-mapped noncoding GWAS variants (e.g., SCZ variants linked to genes by GrID-Net) need functional annotation of allele-specific TF binding disruption in accessible regulatory peaks.

name: nonlinear-autoencoder-embedding-batch-assessment
description: Use when batch effects in RNA-seq/single-cell data must be detected and quantified (kBET/iLISI) and PCA-space estimates may miss non-linear batch effects, e.g. multi-replicate inDrop mESC data.

name: nonlinear-embedding-based-batch-quantification
description: Use when detecting or quantifying the extent of batch effects introduced by technical non-biological factors in RNA-seq data, especially when existing PCA-based estimation may fail to capture non-linear batch effects.

name: nonlinear-library-size-covariate-selection
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices must be normalized so that library-size-dependent nonlinear confounding is detected and regressed out prior to linear association testing (DE, CRISPR screen, co-expression).

name: nonlinear-manifold-network-alignment
description: Use when two condition-specific scGRNs (e.g., mock vs morphine-treated neurons) have been denoised by CP tensor decomposition and you need a common embedding to quantify gene-wise regulatory differences.

name: nonnegative-kernel-autoencoder-gene-preselection
description: Use when an n × d scRNA-seq expression matrix has far more genes than needed (e.g., >20,000 detected genes) and a fixed-size, variance-informed gene subset (5000 genes) is required before filter-based feature selection or clustering.

name: nonnegative-matrix-factorization-decomposition
description: Use when comparing factorization choices for single-cell program recovery (NMF vs ICA), or when decomposing nonnegative scRNA count matrices into latent gene expression programs against simulation ground truth.

name: nonnegative-matrix-factorization-deconvolution
description: Use when estimating cell-type proportions from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data (e.g. simulated 100 µm² MPOA MERFISH-derived pixels) and comparing supervised (SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) vs reference-free (STdeconvolve) deconvolution accuracy by RMSE.

name: nonnegative-tensor-component-analysis
description: Use when you have communication scores assembled into a multi-dimensional tensor (e.g., 23 samples x 749 LR pairs x 16 x 16 cell types, or a simulated 3 x 300 x 12 tensor) and need to deconvolve latent context-driven communication patterns across multiple contexts simultaneously.

name: nonparametric-factor-site-association-testing
description: Use when trained MOFA latent factors (e.g., factors 4/5/6 from the 40-sample GSE164522 CRC-CRLM cohort) must be tested for association with sample-level clinical metadata such as tumor site, donor, or tumor status.

name: nonparametric-goodness-of-fit-testing
description: Use when comparing single-cell Hi-C interaction counts between two conditions on a bin-pair-by-cell normalized count matrix and you want DCI calls that make no assumption on the data distribution.

name: nonparametric-trend-testing
description: Use when METAFlux community fluxes (e.g., glucose exchange reaction HMR_9034 from a 4-cell-type TME model) must be tested against a pre-specified monotonic ordering across cell types, with non-normal flux distributions.

name: nontemporal-variance-decomposition
description: Use when benchmarking dimension reduction visualizations of temporal scRNA-seq data by measuring percent of non-temporal variance explained, e.g. reproducing Fig. 1c comparisons of TCM vs six tools across 11 time-course datasets.

name: normal-cancer-sample-labeling
description: Use when per-cancer-type gene communities (IC genes) must be reduced to representative genes and samples carry normal/cancer condition labels needed for classification-based validation.

name: normality-deviation-testing-of-gene-projections
description: Use when a cell-gene expression matrix is highly sparse (e.g. ~95% zeros) and you must separate spurious sparsity-driven eigenvector localization from true biological signal before denoising or feature selection.

name: normalized-alignment-distance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing branched pseudotime trajectories from scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., synthetic trajectory-tree pairs or replicate datasets) and you need a scalar, tree-level metric that captures whether two branching cell-state transition structures align.

name: normalized-ase-score-calculation
description: Use when ASE SNP call sets (e.g., VADT sig_meta_analysis_variants.txt per tissue) must be converted to gene-level ASE magnitudes to select strongly biased genes for pathway or PPI analyses.

name: normalized-count-thresholding
description: Use when selecting highly variable genes from normalized scRNA-seq count data at scale — e.g. after scSPARKL Global/CPM or Quantile normalization — where a robust MAD threshold (default k > 3) should decide gene retention.

name: normalized-coverage-vector-validation
description: Use when per-cell gene body coverage files (XXXXXXXXX.geneBodyCoverage, .geneBodyCoverage.txt) have been generated for split 10X BAM files and must be validated and aggregated into coverage.r before running 2_SkewC.sh.

name: normalized-entropy-label-agreement-computation
description: Use when you need to quantify how stable or reproducible two sets of cell cluster labels are — e.g., comparing labels from a perturbed matrix (masked AS values, sub-sampled cells) against reference labels.

name: normalized-expression-slot-edge-weighting
description: Use when reproducing or auditing Connectome-style ligand–receptor edgelists where each edge must carry a normalized-expression-derived weightnorm value computed from a Seurat object's active identity slot.

name: normalized-histogram-estimation-of-expression-values
description: Use when a denoised/reconstructed expression matrix is available and you need a parametric distribution fitted to the expression values before histogram-equalization imputation (SERM Fig. 1 steps 2-3).

name: normalized-mutual-information-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing how well competing scRNA-seq embedding methods (e.g. scGAE, scDeepCluster, DCA, scVI) recover known cell-type labels, and you need a single normalized clustering metric per method per dataset.

name: normalized-mutual-information-community-comparison
description: Use when you have per-subject, per-time-point community label vectors from a multi-subject dynamic community detection run (e.g., MuDCoD fit_predict) and need to measure cross-time or cross-condition module similarity per subject and compare it against subject-level phenotypes.

name: novaseq-index-hopping-removal
description: Use when combined GEX and ADT data from a NovaSeq run show sample misassignment due to index hopping and a clean per-sample count matrix is needed before running gExcite.

name: novel-cell-cluster-biomarker-selection
description: Use when a novel/rare cell cluster discovery step (e.g., scNovel) has produced candidate clusters and you need disease-vs-control differential genes within those clusters, or consistent biomarkers across related novel subtypes.

name: novel-cell-detection-mode-ablation
description: Use when benchmarking or configuring scNovel for novel rare cell-type discovery and you must choose among its four detection score modes (S^MSP, S^ODIN, S^SEQ, S^SIM) using AUROC/AUPR/FPR95.

name: novel-cell-type-detection
description: Use when a pre-trained source model must annotate target scRNA-seq cells without access to source data, and the target may contain cell types absent from the source label set, with no user-specified threshold allowed.

name: novel-cell-type-detection
description: Use when a labeled t0 scRNA-seq matrix has been cross-timepoint-annotated onto a t1 matrix (CrossTimeAnnotation) and you need to flag emerged/novel cell types or tumor subclones rather than force-assigning them known labels.

name: novel-cell-type-discovery-in-cross-omics-integration
description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq with unlabeled scATAC-seq (h5ad, gene activity matrices) and you suspect the target data contains cell types missing from the source annotations.

name: novel-cell-type-rejection-analysis
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad) may contain cell types absent from the curated reference, and you want annotation transfer to correctly reject those cells so the unassigned cluster can be characterized by marker genes.

name: novel-intron-chain-isoform-reconstruction
description: Use when long-read BAM/FASTQ alignments plus a reference annotation (e.g. GENCODE mm10 GTF) are available and the goal is to discover novel isoforms by requiring end-support from CAGE TSS and polyA site references before collapsing intron chains.

name: novel-rare-cell-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference exists but the query set may contain cell types absent from the reference, or when comparing novel-cell-detection methods (scNovel vs scmap/scPred/scLearn) with AUROC, AUPR and FPR95 across C^novel = 1–4 settings.

name: novel-splice-site-fragment-indexing
description: Use when quantifying reads on novel splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE) without a spliced aligner: you have a genome FASTA, a GTF annotation, and a known read length.

name: novel-splicing-event-annotation
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be quantified against a GTF annotation while simultaneously detecting unannotated splicing events (exon skipping, intron retention, alternative donor/acceptor) with per-event read counts, without a spliced aligner.

name: nu-svr-regression-tuning
description: Use when deconvolving pseudo-bulk or bulk RNA-seq mixtures with a signature matrix (e.g., built from G-PC/RankCorr/scGeneFit markers) and you need to fit cell-type fractions with CIBERSORT's linear nu-SVR approach.

name: nuclei-segmentation-from-he-histology-images
description: Use when processing seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium) that has a paired H&E image (~10000x10000 pixels) and you need per-spot cell counts and cell centroid locations before single-cell resolution reconstruction.

name: nucleotide-frequency-feature-matrix-perturbation
description: Use when stress-testing a sequence-window classifier (e.g. REDInet) for robustness to incomplete RNAseq coverage, by injecting reference-genome substitutions into feature matrices and re-scoring predictions against ground truth.

name: nucleotide-frequency-logo-analysis
description: Use when you have balanced positive/negative sequence fragments centered on a candidate site and need to visualize per-position nucleotide enrichment or depletion between the two classes.

name: nucleotide-one-hot-sequence-encoding
description: Use when converting tabix-indexed REDItools outTables into TCN input feature vectors for A-to-I RNA editing classification, i.e. when putative editing sites need 101-nt window encoding of reference base identity and RNAseq nucleotide frequencies.

name: nucleotide-read-mapping-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a minimizer-based pre-filter/read mapper against a k-mer baseline, or when validating that smaller interleaved Bloom filters (e.g., 15.2 GiB vs 16 GiB at 64 bins) do not cost mapping sensitivity.

name: nucleotide-sequence-dataset-partitioning
description: Use when a nucleotide sequence collection (FASTA bins, e.g. 64-bin or 1,024-bin partitionings) must be split into bins and the effectiveness of a minimizer-based pre-filter index (representative k-mer set) must be measured.

name: nucleotide-sequence-index-construction
description: Use when a very large collection of nucleotide sequences (e.

name: nucleotide-sequence-preprocessing
description: Use when raw 41-nt RNA sequences (FASTA or plain text) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature matrices before feeding a CNN-based m6A site predictor such as im6A-TS-CNN.

name: null-baseline-random-pair-comparison
description: Use when validating simulated or inferred gene–regulator relationships against ground truth, to establish whether modelled activator/repressor interactions show stronger correlations than random feature pairs with no simulated regulatory effects.

name: null-dataset-simulation-via-sample-partitioning
description: Use when benchmarking false discovery control of XDE/pseudotime methods on multi-sample scRNA-seq: you hold samples with no true condition differences (built via random partitioning) and must count FDR-cutoff false positives.

name: null-distribution-comparison-with-random-feature-pairs
description: Use when you have ground-truth regulator-gene interactions from simulated multi-omics data and need to verify that modelled activator/repressor pairs show stronger correlations than unmodelled pairs.

name: null-distribution-permutation-testing
description: Reference for building an empirical null distribution from shuffled/permuted single-cell data to classify embeddings or statistics (e.g., scDEED dubious vs trustworthy cells at dubious_cutoff=0.05 and trustworthy_cutoff=0.95).

name: null-distribution-simulation
description: Use when comparing colocalization/permutation-test null models over genomic vs transcriptomic backgrounds, or when establishing an empirical null distribution of overlap counts before running a permutation test.

name: null-gene-set-comparison-analysis
description: Use when validating a spatial pathway relevance method on simulated spatial transcriptomics data with known ground-truth gene sets, needing a null-gene-set separation metric.

name: null-hypothesis-dataset-construction-for-embedding-quality
description: Use when establishing the null expectation for embedding quality of scRNA-seq (e.g., Tabula Muris bone marrow) data: you need signalless data with preserved per-gene marginals to compute EMBEDR p-values.

name: null-p-value-uniformity-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a normalization/association method (e.g., Normalisr) on a synthetic null UMI count matrix and you need to verify null co-expression P values are uniform across expression levels.

name: null-phenotype-simulation
description: Use when validating that a gene-based association or omnibus test (e.g., OTTERS ACAT-O) is well calibrated under the null before applying it to real GWAS summary data.

name: null-simulation-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking differential-state or perturbation-detection tools under null conditions where no cell type should be detected as changed, to measure false-positive rates as patient-level variability grows.

name: numerical-convergence-testing
description: Use when solving the COSLIR Eq. 3 objective from only the first and second moments (sample mean vectors and covariance matrices) of two consecutive TSCS time points, and you must demonstrate numerically that the ADMM iteration converged before trusting the sparse A_t estimate.

name: numerical-formula-unit-testing
description: Use when a paper describes mathematical transformations (e.g. sigmoid filters, convex weight optimization, norm-based matrix fusion) that you must re-implement in code and you need unit tests to confirm boundary and ordering properties before applying them to real data.

name: numerical-invariant-verification
description: Use when a SiFT-filtered single-cell expression matrix (X~ = X − K·X with pseudocount α = min(X~)) must be algebraically validated before saving to .h5ad or feeding downstream analysis.

name: numerical-threshold-table-generation
description: Use when you need minimizer-sharing thresholds for a pre-filter query whose threshold must depend on w, k, the error budget, and the per-read minimizer count m (e.g. 15-35), rather than a fixed fraction of shared k-mers.

name: nye-similarity-tree-comparison
description: Use when comparing two or more phylogenetic/lineage trees (e.g., reconstructed vs. ground-truth cell division trees) and you need a branch-clade-split based similarity that is normalized to [0,1], as in the LinRace benchmark.

name: obd-selection-rate-analysis
description: Use when characterizing how the TSNP design's correct OBD selection percentage varies with maximum sample size (N=40, 50, 60), or when verifying whether a given N achieves at least 50% correct OBD selection across simulation scenarios.

name: observation-grouped-expression-summarization
description: Use when a Scanpy/AnnData scRNA object already carries gene age class annotations (e.g. from an oggmap orthomap) and the goal is a table of relative expression per gene age class grouped by an observation annotation like cell type or sampling timepoint.

name: octree-spatial-indexing
description: Use when you must make every cell individually selectable (e.g. freehand/controller selection) in VR dimension-reduction plots containing tens of thousands of scRNA-seq points, where attaching Unity native colliders per point is infeasible.

name: odds-ratio-association-analysis
description: Use when single-cell allelic count matrices (e.g., scBASE unique-read, weighted-allocation, or partial-pooled estimates) are available and the goal is to test whether maternal/paternal bursting is coordinated rather than independent.

name: odds-ratio-effect-size-estimation
description: Use when comparing a binary biomarker/class label (e.g., CMS2 vs non-CMS2 from CMScaller) against a binary drug-response annotation in PDX or cell line cohorts, and you need per-cohort p-values and odds ratios to quantify the association.

name: odds-ratio-enrichment-of-ranked-lr-interactions
description: Use when ranked ligand-receptor predictions from scRNA-seq must be validated against spatial transcriptomics: Visium spots with cell-type deconvolution, or seqFISH/merFISH cell-type maps, to test adjacency preference.

name: odds-ratio-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when comparing a ligand-receptor resource's membership in biological annotation terms (pathways, cancer gene sets, tissue-enriched proteins) against a pooled background to expose enrichment bias.

name: oligo-structure-mutation-localization
description: Use when a filtered gRNA BAM (gRNA.sorted.mapped.removedSecondaryAlignment.onlyMappedToGrnaChrom.bam) must be collapsed to per-UMI consensus gRNA sequences and mutations must be localized against a known oligo-pool cassette structure.

name: oligodendrocyte-lineage-trajectory-inference
description: Use when an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced counts and cell-type cluster labels covers a linear oligodendrocyte differentiation (e.g., P20 pons) and you must recover ordering and quantify directional correctness via CBDir.

name: oligonucleotide-background-quantification
description: Use when you have an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix alongside an RNA count matrix and need to quantify tagging vs background HTO signal per droplet, or to validate the positive association between HTO counts and detected genes before regression-based demultiplexing.

name: ols-meta-regression-analysis
description: Use when per-gene model measures (e.g., CTMM cell type-specificity, mean-difference) must be related to gene-level annotations such as EDS, enhancer count, LOEUF, or pLI via decile-binned regression.

name: omics-alteration-frequency-computation
description: Use when raw per-cancer-type multi-omics alteration matrices (SNV, CNA, methylation, expression) must be reduced to per-gene feature summaries, e.g., to test whether predicted driver genes differ from other genes.

name: omics-data-frame-format-validation
description: Use when a CSV gene-expression or proteomics data frame must be checked for the format OmicInt expects (significantly changed genes with their expression/LFC values) before scoring or GMM clustering.

name: omics-gene-cluster-interactor-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of key interactor genes/proteins produced by an interactome assessment and need to summarise their functional classes and typical cellular compartments.

name: omim-disease-gene-fisher-enrichment
description: Use when you have gene sets stratified by a regulatory metric (e.g., CAFEH top-component sharing across tissues) and want to test overrepresentation of curated disease genes from OMIM, separately for dominant and recessive inheritance modes.

name: on-disk-sql-database-construction
description: Use when a .h5ad single-cell dataset is too large for memory (e.g., 4.4M-cell atlas in backed mode) and needs a persistent, queryable SQL database for downstream runtime benchmarking or repeated SQL queries.

name: oncogene-copy-number-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have a set of ecDNA or focal-amplification gene calls and need to test whether known oncogenes are significantly enriched for amplification, expression, or functional effects.

name: oncogene-expression-quantification
description: Use when a gene fusion (e.g., IgH-WHSC1) has been detected per cell in scRNA-seq data and you must test whether the fusion partner oncogene is overexpressed in fusion-bearing cells.

name: one-class-svm-mirna-classification
description: Use when a uniform-format list of annotated plus newly predicted miRNA precursors (output of miRNATranslate) must be filtered into promising candidates using the one-class SVM classifier of iwa-miRNA's miRNASelection step with default parameters.

name: one-class-svm-novel-population-rejection
description: Use when constructing a scHPL hierarchical classification tree on annotated single-cell data where novel/unseen cell populations must be detected (rejection), or when reference batches may lack populations present in other batches.

name: one-class-svm-novelty-detection
description: Use when a hierarchical single-cell classifier must flag cells from cell populations that were excluded from training (novelty/unseen-population detection), e.g. testing whether held-out 'Group 3' AMB nodes are rejected.

name: one-hot-genomic-sequence-encoding
description: Use when a sequence-based classifier (e.g., the InPACT CNN sequence module) requires fixed-length genomic windows converted to binary one-hot nucleotide tensors, and you need reproducible positive/negative training and held-out test sets for polyA site prediction.

name: one-hot-nucleotide-sequence-encoding
description: Use when raw nucleotide sequences (e.g., 41-nt RNA segments centered on a candidate m6A site) must be converted to fixed-dimensional numeric feature vectors before feeding a CNN classifier such as im6A-TS-CNN.

name: one-of-k-encoding-of-rna-sequence-and-structure
description: Use when preparing Ψ-site candidate fragments (uridine-centered, 25 nt flanks each side) as fixed-length categorical matrices for a dual-branch 1D-CNN classifier that reads both sequence and secondary-structure context.

name: one-sided-f-test-variance-comparison
description: Use when two quantification methods have been benchmarked against a common ground truth (e.g., long-read TE counts) and you must show one method's residuals are significantly smaller, not just descriptively better.

name: one-sided-t-test-method-comparison
description: Use when two or more quantification/clustering methods have been run on the same datasets and per-seed metric distributions (e.g., ARI/NMI over 10 random seeds) are available, and the goal is to test whether the proposed method is significantly better, not just different.

name: one-sided-wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when validating whether cells predicted as primed for a lineage (e.g. GP/MEMP MPPs or HS/IRS TACs) show significantly higher fate probability, TF motif activity, or chromatin accessibility than unprimed or opposite-primed cells.

name: one-sided-wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when you have paired per-gene scores (e.g., marker-gene specificity with vs. without constraints) averaged over repeated clusterings and need a one-sided test of whether the constrained condition improves scores.

name: one-vs-all-marker-baseline-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking marker gene panels for cell type discrimination on labeled scRNA-seq data (e.g. Zeisel GSE60361) or synthetic multimodal simulations and you need the per-gene one-vs-all baseline to quantify scGeneFit's joint-selection gain.

name: online-inductive-label-inference
description: Use when newly arriving (streaming) data points must be assigned to existing clusters or evaluated for novel cluster emergence, without refitting the clustering model on the full combined dataset.

name: ontology-aware-cell-type-classification
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq cells against a controlled vocabulary (Cell Ontology) and the test set contains cell types absent from training data, or when benchmarking classifiers on unseen-term annotation.

name: ontology-aware-prediction-scoring
description: Use when evaluating cell type classifiers on CELLxGENE-style annotations where predictions of a more specific Cell Ontology subtype should count as correct against a parent true label.

name: ontology-based-cell-type-similarity-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking cell type annotation tools (e.g. Cell Marker Accordion vs ScType, SCINA, clustifyR, scCATCH, scSorter) and you need a Cell Ontology-aware similarity metric instead of exact label matching.

name: ontology-edge-consistency-analysis
description: Use when you need to measure logical inconsistency of independent binary classifiers against a hierarchy — e.g. comparing one-vs-rest vs hierarchical CellO outputs, or validating a probability matrix against ontology DAG constraints.

name: ontology-embedding-usage
description: Use when you must annotate scRNA-seq cells to Cell Ontology terms that lack annotated training cells (unseen terms), leveraging the ontology graph rather than per-term supervised training alone.

name: ontology-graph-classifier-training
description: Use when annotating human scRNA-seq or bulk RNA-seq cells against the Cell Ontology hierarchy, or when benchmarking hierarchical classifiers (IR, CLR) against flat baselines such as a Pearson-correlation 1NN.

name: ontology-graph-construction
description: Use when a scRNA-seq classifier must reason over a controlled vocabulary of cell type terms — e.g. to score unseen Cell Ontology terms or compute marker genes for all ontology categories — and raw obo/network files are available.

name: ontology-graph-distance-traversal
description: Use when you need to quantify how similar cell types are according to ontology structure (direct-neighbor vs multi-hop graph distance) and test whether ontology similarity tracks expression similarity.

name: ontology-leaf-node-cell-type-mapping
description: Use when DCNet abundance predictions must be restricted to or interpreted for specific terminal cell types (e.g. FGC, somatic cells) in a Cell Ontology hierarchy, rather than the full 434-type landscape.

name: ontology-membership-contingency-analysis
description: Use when you have a fitted topic model's gene association vector (Ntopics x Ngenes beta matrix) and an ontology/cell-type gene membership list, and need to test if a topic's top genes capture a known cell identity program.

name: ontology-metadata-mapping-ncbi-mesh-ncit
description: Use when preparing .h5ad study files for import into Cellenium (e.g. via the blood_covid.ipynb or heart_failure_reichart2022 notebooks) and study-level metadata must be mapped to NCBI taxonomy, MeSH, and NCIT ontologies.

name: ontology-term-projection
description: Use when comparing a hierarchical ontology-based classifier against flat annotation tools whose outputs are free-text cell-type labels, and you need a shared Cell Ontology term-ID space for hierarchical F1/precision scoring.

name: operating-characteristics-evaluation
description: Use when a phase I/II dose-finding design needs quantitative performance evaluation across dose-toxicity-efficacy scenarios, e.g. reproducing OBD selection or null-case early-termination rates from simulated trials.

name: optimal-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when clustering transcriptome data (bulk or single-cell expression matrix) with an unknown number of clusters and you need to determine the k for each recursive subdivision step.

name: optimal-matching-cell-pairing
description: Use when you have two unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. snATAC-seq and snRNA-seq) already co-embedded in a common low-dimensional space and need matched cell pairs to build a pseudo-multimodal dataset.

name: optimal-transport-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a generative model of single-cell time series is trained with an intermediate time point held out and you need to compare its simulated marginal against baselines (e.g., WOT linear interpolation) via Wasserstein distance.

name: optimal-transport-cell-lineage-alignment
description: Use when a time-course scRNA-seq matrix sacrifices cells at each time point (no cell-to-cell correspondence) and individual cell lineage paths between adjacent time points are needed before smoothing, fate prediction, or dynamic gene network construction.

name: optimal-transport-cell-matching
description: Use when control and perturbed single-cell RNA-seq profiles are unpaired (no per-cell ground-truth pairing) and a translator must be trained to predict stimulated-expression profiles, especially with held-out cell types.

name: optimal-transport-cell-to-position-mapping
description: Use when a non-spatial scRNA-seq dataset must be linked to spatial measurements of a small set of genes (e.g., seqFISH/in situ reference maps) to predict spatial expression patterns or assign cells to spatial regions.

name: optimal-transport-embedding-alignment
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.g. scRNA-seq with scATAC-seq, surface protein, morphology, or CyTOF) where cross-modality feature connections are weak, and a modality-mixed latent embedding is the desired output.

name: optimal-transport-latent-embedding
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell datasets with both common and dataset-specific HVGs — e.g., scATAC gene activity matrices vs scRNA counts with unmatched cell types — and you need latent embeddings plus robustness metrics.

name: optimal-transport-latent-space-tuning
description: Use when training scConfluence on unpaired single-cell multiomics data (e.g., scRNA-scATAC MuData objects) and the latent embeddings must be checked for modality mixing versus cell-type structure before benchmarking or downstream clustering.

name: optimal-transport-matrix-factorization
description: Use when you have paired multi-omics single-cell data (e.g. scRNA+scATAC from scCAT-seq or 10X Multiome, CITE-seq, or tri-omic TEA-seq Muon objects) and need a joint cell embedding with interpretable, cell-type-specific factors.

name: optimal-transport-plan-computation
description: Use when integrating non-spatial scRNA-seq data with spatial transcriptomics (e.g., in situ hybridization, seqFISH+) and a cell-to-position mapping is needed to recover spatial properties of single cells.

name: optimal-transport-sample-distance-estimation
description: Use when you have multiple single-cell/pathomics samples (.h5ad with per-cell cluster labels and sample IDs) and need an unsupervised, sample-level distance matrix to cluster patients or infer disease trajectories.

name: optimal-transport-unbalancedness-tuning
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities whose cell populations are unequally represented, and you need to verify that the chosen unbalanced-OT relaxation (transported mass m) yields robust, biologically meaningful embeddings.

name: order-preserving-biclustering
description: Use when the goal is to find trend-preserving (order-preserving) biclusters in noisy, complex gene expression microarray data, where rows share a consistent upward/downward trend rather than identical absolute values.

name: orf-attention-feature-scoring
description: Use when classifying transcript FASTA sequences (especially transcripts with small ORFs) as lncRNA or PCT, or when benchmarking coding-potential methods on sORF test sets where CPAT/CNCI/PLEK/CPC2/LncFinder/CPPred/mRNN/RNAsamba underperform.

name: orf-extraction-with-orfipy
description: Use when transcript sequences (e.g. CD-HIT-reduced lncRNA/PCT FASTA from RefSeq, Ensembl, or GENCODE) must be scanned for ORFs to compute ORF-derived coding-potential features or ORF-attention encodings.

name: orf-feature-extraction
description: Use when building a feature matrix from FASTA transcripts (e.g. H-Train mRNA/CDS/lncRNA files) for coding-potential classification and you need ORF-derived features beyond the single longest-ORF convention.

name: orf-feature-extraction
description: Use when encoding transcript sequences (e.g. lncRNA/PCT FASTA filtered to ≥200 nt) into numeric feature vectors where ORF content, not just global sequence composition, discriminates coding potential.

name: orf-length-based-transcript-filtering
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity FASTA contigs) must be filtered for likely non-coding or fragmented transcripts by predicted ORF length, as part of chimera-removal or assembly-cleanup filtering.

name: organ-specific-malignant-cell-model-application
description: Use when tumor scRNA-seq data (Seurat object with malignant epithelial cells pre-identified) must be assigned a cancer cell of origin using Census organ-specific CCLE-trained models for Liver, Pancreas, or Large_Intestine (colon).

name: organoid-cell-type-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying how accurately a supervised single-cell classifier (SIMS/TabNet) transfers cell-type labels across iPSC cell lines in cortical organoid scRNA-seq datasets, or when reproducing reported accuracy and radial glia misclassification rates from Figures 6C-D, 6E and Table S11.

name: original-spliseq-baseline-filtering-reimplementation
description: Use when benchmarking a SPLiT-seq preprocessing tool against the original identification method: paired-end FASTQ reads must be filtered with the original rules to define the baseline read set for overlap/consistency computation.

name: ornstein-uhlenbeck-expression-simulation
description: Use when you need simulated OU-process expression data with known Redundant/Unique deletion class labels (e.g., to train or benchmark CLOUDe classifiers) for Nk observations per class across m conditions, bounded by empirical expression ranges.

name: orthogonal-projection-onto-landmark-edges
description: Use when a Mpath landmark graph (landmark coordinates and connecting edges) and cell-to-landmark transition assignments exist and individual cells must be placed in pseudo-temporal order along developmental trajectories between neighbouring landmarks.

name: orthogroup-lca-annotation
description: Use when you have OrthoFinder (or eggNOG/PLAZA/orthomcl) orthogroup results for a query species (e.g. Danio rerio) and need per-orthogroup gene ages (LCA classes) or continuity scores of species representation.

name: ortholog-database-construction
description: Use when building a KO/protein ortholog reference from hundreds of eukaryote proteomes to support read-to-ortholog mapping for non-model species RNA-seq, instead of per-species transcript assembly and annotation transfer.

name: ortholog-gene-matching-with-blast
description: Use when matching cell types across a species pair requires gene/gene correspondences and a simple sequence-alignment-based ortholog map (e.g., BLAST one-to-one matches) is acceptable, or when benchmarking against embedding-based gene matching.

name: ortholog-group-clustering
description: Use when building or extending a protein ortholog database for non-model eukaryotic species (e.g., species lacking a reference transcriptome) so reads can be quantified against ortholog groups instead of transcript IDs.

name: ortholog-group-construction-o2o-he-sh
description: Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple species for integration and you must define homologous gene groups (one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many) before concatenating counts into a shared feature matrix.

name: ortholog-group-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when differential expression has been called on ortholog-group IDs (e.g. via Seq2Fun/ExpressAnalyst for species lacking a reference transcriptome) and you must validate whether the significant DEG list is inflated by reads from one gene mapping to different ortholog IDs in different species.

name: orthologous-gene-anchoring
description: Use when scRNA-seq datasets from different plant species must be integrated onto a shared UMAP/embedding while keeping cell identities consistent and detecting species-specific or conserved (e.g. meristem) cell types.

name: orthologous-group-lca-gene-age-interpretation
description: Use when a target species' genes need evolutionary age classes derived from precomputed or newly computed orthologous groups (OrthoFinder, eggNOG v6, PLAZA v5), e.g. to build an orthomap or count species gene-age coverage.

name: orthomap-gene-age-coverage-counting
description: Use when the task requires quantifying species coverage of precomputed gene age / orthomap assignments in oggmap, e.g. verifying that oggmap covers 317 (Ensembl release-110), 1322 (eggNOG v6), and 98 dicots + 52 monocots (PLAZA v5) eukaryotic species.

name: orthomap-species-membership-mapping
description: Use when you have an orthomap plus per-orthogroup species-membership table from OrthoFinder/oggmap and need lineage-continuity scores per orthogroup to spot candidate horizontal gene transfer along the LCA-to-focal-species path.

name: osqp-convex-optimization-solving
description: Use when estimating per-sample reaction fluxes from normalized MRAS scores with nutrient-aware bounds, i.e., when an E-Flux-constrained, parsimonious-FBA solution is needed over a genome-scale metabolic model.

name: ou-evolutionary-parameter-interpretation
description: Use when per-event CLOUDe predictions (test_prefix.*.classifications and test_prefix.*.predictions with theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha))) exist and you need to test whether predicted parameters differ between 'Redundant' and 'Unique' deletion classes.

name: ou-process-evolutionary-parameter-estimation
description: Use when absolute log10(x+1) expression data for derived, survived, and lost genes of deletion events (3m columns, space-delimited) must be converted into per-event evolutionary parameter estimates such as theta1, theta2, and log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)).

name: ou-process-gene-expression-simulation
description: Use when building CLOUDe training sets from simulated expression data under an OU process — e.g., when you need 'redundant-skewed' or 'unique-skewed' unbalanced training sets, or balanced training data, to train NN/XGB classifiers on expression evolution of deletion events.

name: out-of-bag-error-quantification
description: Use when you need an imputation-free supervised benchmark of cell-type separability: you have labeled scRNA-seq expression matrices (raw and imputed) and want a single quantitative error metric per method.

name: out-of-cell-type-generalization-testing
description: Use when benchmarking surface protein imputation (e.g. CITE-seq PBMC ADT prediction) for generalization to held-out cell types, rather than random cell-level holdout splits.

name: out-of-core-single-cell-data-processing
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (e.g., the 4.4-million-cell Macosko Mouse Atlas h5ad) exceeds available memory, making AnnData/Seurat operations fail or run ~700x slower, and SQL-based filtering/aggregation is needed.

name: out-of-distribution-score-function-implementation
description: Use when a trained cell-type classifier must flag query cells from unseen cell types, and you need to choose among maximum-probability, ODIN, or barcode-preprocessing (sequential/simultaneous) scoring modes.

name: out-of-sample-cell-type-evaluation
description: Use when a perturbation prediction model trained on unpaired control/stimulated scRNA-seq data must be tested on cell types absent from training (out-of-sample generalization), e.g., PT_PBMC response prediction with per-cell-type held-out evaluation.

name: out-of-sample-embedding-prediction-via-parametric-mapping
description: Use when labeled/unlabeled cells arrive after a dimensionality-reduction model was fit and you need to map them into the existing embedding (no refitting) and quantify how well the mapping generalizes as a function of training-set size.

name: outer-code-automatic-indexing
description: Use when reconstructing or designing a FrameD-style DNA storage encode path (file -> packets -> base-sequences -> DNA strands) and the outer code layer needs automatic index insertion across packets, including special indexes like Luby Seed.

name: outlier-aware-cluster-partitioning
description: Use when clustering noisy datasets where small spurious clusters are expected and you need automatic outlier detection plus re-assignment of outliers to core clusters rather than discarding them.

name: outlier-capping-transcriptomic-values
description: Use when preparing a gene-by-cell-population expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cell populations) for ICELLNET ligand–receptor scoring, and raw expression magnitudes would bias interaction scores toward strongly expressed molecules.

name: outlier-cell-classification-agreement-analysis
description: Use when independently re-implementing SenePy score_hub and needing to verify that your per-cell senescence scores classify the same outlier cells as the reference package output.

name: outlier-cell-identification-from-sv1
description: Use when a scRNA-seq cell population appears homogeneous but you suspect hidden heterogeneity (e.g., compromised/doublet cells), and known covariates (patient identity, geometric library size) fail to explain the residual variation.

name: outlier-cell-thresholding-gaussian-sigma
description: Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes with a senescence signature (e.g. SenePy hub scores) and you need to call individual senescent outlier cells and test whether their proportion shifts across groups such as donor age.

name: outlier-log-fold-change-correction
description: Use when comparing single-cell vs bulk differential expression log fold changes after DCA denoising and isolated genes show extreme LFC outliers in the denoised data that were not present in raw data or bulk samples.

name: outlier-replicate-perturbation-simulation
description: Use when evaluating whether a replicate-aware count model (e.g., PAIRADISE paired model) is more robust than a naive pooled-read baseline under outlier contamination, or when tracing power-versus-number-of-replicates curves for differential splicing detection.

name: outlier-spot-detection-in-time-course-spatial-data
description: Use when analyzing 10x Visium spatial spots from a tissue time course (e.g., myocardial infarction) to flag senescence-high outlier spots, test their colocalization with a spatial marker such as Col1a1 fibrosis, and quantify Moran's I spatial autocorrelation.

name: outlyingness-score-visualization
description: Use when SCISSOR has returned a ScissorOutput object with GSC$OS and LSC$OS outlyingness scores and you must identify and report which samples exceed the global/local shape-change cutoffs for a gene such as TP53.

name: over-clustered-annata-merging-benchmark
description: Use when a high-resolution Leiden-clustered scRNA-seq AnnData is intentionally over-clustered and you must quantify how well a merging method discriminates significant from non-significant artificial over-cluster pairs via AUROC.

name: over-clustering-ensemble-label-transfer
description: Use when transferring reference cell-type labels onto a large query single-cell dataset (AnnData) via marker-based cell-type scores, and you need robust consensus annotations by over-clustering across multiple MACA parameter settings rather than a single clustering run.

name: over-correction-assessment-via-deg-preservation
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell batch correction methods (scCobra, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, Seurat) on two same-condition samples and you need to detect over-correction by comparing DEG counts before vs. after correction.

name: over-correction-quantification-across-tissues
description: Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition (multi-tissue) scRNA-seq datasets and you need to check the chosen method (JOINTLY, Harmony, scVI, etc.) for over-correction of true biological condition differences.

name: over-correction-scoring-from-umap-embeddings
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell batch-correction methods (scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) for over-correction risk on data containing a known biological difference between batches, e.g., an implanted perturbation in GSE149614 immune cells.

name: overdispersed-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when preparing multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics counts (e.g., mOB, Visium, DBiT-seq, Slide-seq) before fitting LDA in STdeconvolve, and noisy, low-variance genes must be filtered out.

name: overdispersion-adjusted-ca-variants
description: Use when dimension-reducing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (SingleCellExperiment) whose counts are overdispersed and where log(x+1)+PCA pipelines underperform, or when benchmarking embeddings against ground-truth cell-type labels with ARI.

name: overkill-doublet-removal-prefiltering
description: Use when running Chord with overkill=T on a Seurat object and likely doublets must be removed before artificial-doublet simulation for training.

name: overkill-simulated-doublet-training-set-construction
description: Use when running Chord with overkill=T on a droplet-based scRNA-seq sample (e.g. a Seurat object) and you need the overkilled training data — doublets filtered out and simulated doublets generated from remaining cells — before GBM integration of method scores.

name: overlap-over-union-statistic-computation
description: Use when you have feature sets selected by a method (e.g., G-PC, CEM-PC, mrmr, ReliefF, F) over multiple runs on randomly sampled data and need to measure how reproducible the selected gene/feature sets are across runs.

name: overlap-score-computation-from-mixture-components
description: Decision support for judging per-HTO demultiplexing quality after fitting demuxmix regression mixture models: needed when you must rank HTOs by how well their negative and positive droplet populations separate before accepting classifications.

name: overlap-score-computation-hto-datasets
description: Use when you need a numeric, per-dataset quality metric for HTO demultiplexing data — e.g., to compare newly published GEO HTO datasets against benchmarks or simulated low-quality levels before choosing a demultiplexing method.

name: overlapping-gene-supergene-aggregation
description: Use when preprocessing a real scRNA-seq BAM file for count-matrix training and reads overlapping annotated genes must be assigned to mutually exclusive genomic features.

name: overlapping-sample-matching-in-paired-omics-data
description: Use when a cohort contains individuals with both bulk RNA-seq and scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq data and decomposition requires identifying which single-cell samples correspond to which bulk samples.

name: overrepresentation-enrichment-testing
description: Use when deriving a universal senescence gene panel from many cell-type-specific signatures and you need a statistical (rather than arbitrary overlap-count) cutoff for which genes are overrepresented across signatures.

name: p-value-integration-across-deg-methods
description: Use when multiple DEG detection method outputs (per-gene p-value vectors) are available and a machine-learning integration of DEG calls is needed, rather than a simple vote threshold cut-off.

name: p-value-integration-combination
description: Use when you need robust DEG detection from RNA-seq count matrices and no single DE method can be assumed appropriate, since methods 'behave quite differently depending on the properties of the data'.

name: p-value-multiple-testing-adjustment
description: Use when combining two independent differential-expression p-values (sender ligand, receiver receptor) into one LR-pair significance and needing a multiple-testing-adjusted p-value to filter candidate ligand-receptor associations.

name: p-value-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you need to compare per-gene p-value rankings produced by two versions or variants of a feature-scanning method across multiple datasets, to quantify whether a methodological change (e.g., binary detection vs continuous activity) preserves DEG predictions.

name: p-value-scatterplot-data-generation
description: Use when two DEG-prediction methods have been run on the same scRNA-seq dataset and you need per-gene p-value tables and top-N rank-overlap counts to quantify agreement.

name: p-value-significance-verification
description: Use when two SVG/DEG detection methods have been run on the same spatial dataset and you must verify and report which features agree or show discrepant ranks and p-values between them.

name: pacbio-isoseq-gold-standard-generation
description: Use when matched PacBio HiFi and Nanopore R10 reads exist for the same single-cell 5' cDNA library and you need an accuracy gold standard for evaluating isoform quantification methods like Longcell, FLAMES, Sicelore2, or wf-single-cell.

name: pacbio-long-read-rnaseq-downsampling
description: Use when deciding the minimum PacBio long-read RNA-seq depth needed for dsRID training/prediction: you have a full-depth BAM (e.g. 4.27M reads) and must justify how many reads (1.5–2M plateau) suffice.

name: packet-base-sequence-file-segmentation
description: Use when simulating or implementing a DNA-based data storage encode path that must convert an arbitrary binary file into addressable packets and base-sequences prior to inner-code DNA strand synthesis, e.g. when building or validating a FrameD-style pipeline.

name: paga-force-directed-graph-visualization
description: Use when you need to reconstruct or validate a coarse-grained trajectory/pseudo-time graph over scRNA-seq clusters, e.g. to check that augmented or downsampled cell populations preserve the original topology of a differentiation graph.

name: paga-trajectory-graph-partitioning
description: Use when reprocessing a published scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 10x Chromium data processed with Cell Ranger v6.0.1) and the goal is to partition cells into manually annotated clusters that recapitulate expected transition and dead-end trajectories.

name: paga-trajectory-inference
description: Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq data (e.g., GRouNdGAN .h5ad output) reproduce the trajectory structure and pseudo-time ordering of an experimental reference such as mouse BoneMarrow hematopoiesis (Paul et al., 2015; GSE72857).

name: paired-barcode-expression-lineage-tree-reconstruction
description: Use when you have paired single-cell lineage-barcode mutation matrices and gene expression counts and need to infer a cell division tree, or to resolve barcode homoplasy where identical barcodes span different true clones.

name: paired-cluster-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data are already clustered and you need reliable per-cluster marker genes to feed cell type annotation, especially when pseudo marker genes from one-against-all tests would corrupt downstream labels.

name: paired-differential-expression-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type drug-response prioritization methods on single-cell perturbation datasets with known responsive cell types, or when comparing untreated-only inference against paired pre/post-treatment DE-based baselines.

name: paired-distribution-statistical-comparison
description: Use when two palettes or measurement sets yield paired samples (e.g., pairwise CIEDE2000 distances for Spaco colors vs tab20 colors) and you must test whether their discernibility distributions differ, as in the Spaco axolotl benchmark.

name: paired-donor-random-effect-specification
description: Use when RNA-seq expression data contain paired samples or repeated measurements per donor (e.g. multiple libraries from the same patientID) and you need per-gene differential expression estimates that account for within-donor correlation.

name: paired-end-amplicon-read-merging
description: Use when the input is paired-end FASTQ data from a population-level cellular barcoding experiment whose overlapping mate pairs cover the barcode, and a single merged read per molecule is needed before trimming and quantification.

name: paired-end-fastq-generation-from-alignments
description: Use when an analysis needs FASTQ reads recovered from a subset of alignments in a coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM (e.g. reads mapped to putative Ig loci) so the reads can be fed to a de novo transcriptome assembler such as Trinity.

name: paired-end-fastq-generation-from-bed
description: Use when scReadSim has produced synthetic read-coordinate BED files (e.g., combined gene/inter-gene BED from scRNA_CombineBED) and you need actual paired-end FASTQ reads for downstream aligners or UMI-deduplication benchmarks.

name: paired-end-fastq-merging
description: Use when preparing paired-end RNA-seq unmapped reads (e.g., TCGA BAM reads failing alignment to hg19 and phiX NC_001422) as viRNAtrap input, since viRNAtrap treats each input FASTQ file as a distinct sample.

name: paired-end-fragment-extraction
description: Use when STAR-aligned paired-end scRNA-seq BAMs (e.g., Smart-seq2 data like gray mouse lemur testes cells) must be converted to strand-specific interval fragments before groHMM TAR discovery, because groHMM consumes read coverage intervals rather than raw BAM alignments.

name: paired-end-read-alignment-bwa
description: Use when running Anchored-fusion or its benchmark against de novo fusion callers: paired-end FASTQ (R1/R2) must be mapped with BWA-MEM (>=0.7.17) to a target-gene fasta and genome fa (hg38/hg19) with matching GTF.

name: paired-end-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq reads exist as unaligned FASTQ files (e.g., minnow output) and must be placed in genomic coordinates on mm10 to compare coverage against an aligned real BAM.

name: paired-end-read-group-organization
description: Use when a multi-sample sequencing workflow must ingest raw FASTQ inputs from a sample sheet into per-read-group QC and trimming steps, distinguishing paired-end (R1/R2) from single-end files for DNA-seq and RNA-seq.

name: paired-end-read-overlap-assembly
description: Use when processing paired-end, 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g. Microwell-seq FASTQ from Mouse Cell Atlas / Human Cell Landscape) where reads must overlap and be merged to recover the full insert containing the 3' cleavage site.

name: paired-end-rna-seq-alignment
description: Use when performing a targeted fusion search on paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ data by anchoring a gene of interest, and reads must be aligned to both the target gene transcript fasta and a whole-genome reference.

name: paired-end-splicing-label-derivation
description: Use when building an evaluation read set with definitive splicing ground truth from paired-end 10X scRNA-seq data (e.g., mouse/human scRNA-seq) to benchmark splicing-status predictors via AUC.

name: paired-model-comparison-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing a new causal-inference or prediction model against baseline configurations on the same candidate peak-gene pairs, and you need per-configuration retrieval AUROCs plus significance statistics for the differences.

name: paired-multiomics-data-preprocessing
description: Use when you have raw paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq count matrices (AnnData objects) that must be normalized and feature-processed before training or evaluating a scButterfly cross-modality translation model.

name: paired-multiomics-tnse-visualization
description: Use when you need qualitative visual confirmation that translated single-cell profiles (predicted scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq from a cross-modality translator) cluster by cell type and match true labeled profiles.

name: paired-nonparametric-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when two configurations of the same method (e.g. weighted vs unweighted decoupleR runs) yield paired scores over identical dataset/regulator combinations and a directional significance claim must be tested nonparametrically.

name: paired-replicate-differential-splicing-testing
description: Use when RNA-seq count data provide per-allele exon inclusion and skipping counts (IJC/SJC) with incLen/skpLen effective lengths for individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP, and the goal is to call significant ASAS events at FDR <= 10%.

name: paired-replicate-likelihood-ratio-testing
description: Use when per-event allele-specific inclusion/skipping counts (IJC/SJC for REF and ALT alleles) are available for multiple individuals sharing a heterozygous SNP and you need a combined ASAS p-value via a paired-replicate LRT on δi = 0.

name: paired-replicate-statistical-model-fitting
description: Use when you have per-allele exon inclusion (IJC) and skipping (SJC) counts plus effective isoform lengths (incLen, skpLen) from replicate RNA-seq samples sharing a heterozygous SNP, and need to test for differential splicing between alleles across replicates.

name: paired-sample-matching-across-datasets
description: Use when PDAC expression datasets contain patient-matched primary tumors, metastases, and/or derived cell lines (e.g., PACA-AU paired samples) and you need to compare signature scores across matched sample classes rather than across unrelated samples.

name: paired-scrnaseq-spatial-transcriptomics-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a spatial subpopulation identification method against baselines (Louvain, K-means, Hclust, SpaGCN, STAGATE, BayesSpace, DR-SC, scCoGAPS) on simulated data with known ground-truth subcluster labels, using ARI as the metric.

name: paired-scrnaseq-tcrseq-data-processing
description: Use when you have paired single-cell transcriptome and full-length TCR sequencing data (e.g. Smart-seq2 CD8 TILs) and need per-cell clonotype assignments to test clonal relatedness between transcriptional states.

name: paired-signature-estimate-statistical-comparison
description: Use when the same tumor samples have signature-fitting estimates from two matched contexts (e.g., WES capture-restricted vs WGS SNV catalogs) and you must quantify per-sample systematic differences, such as exome-vs-WGS shifts for SBS9.

name: paired-significance-testing-of-model-metrics
description: Use when comparing two model-training conditions (e.g. augmentation on/off) evaluated on the same holdout test set across matched random seeds, and you must report statistically significant differences in loss or macro F1.

name: paired-statistical-significance-testing
description: Use when two or more methods have been evaluated on the same set of datasets and a per-dataset paired comparison of scores (e.g., AMI/NMI/ARI) must establish statistically significant ity rather than just a higher mean rank.

name: paired-t-test-cross-dataset-comparison
description: Use when two hyperparameter-optimization or embedding-scoring methods must be compared across multiple matched datasets and per-dataset embedding-quality metrics (KNN/KNC preservation) need statistical significance testing via paired t-tests.

name: paired-t-test-differential-expression
description: Use when you have paired qPCR samples (e.g., 12 tumor/adjacent-normal breast cancer pairs) with raw CT values for a target miRNA and 2–3 internal controls, and you need to test differential expression under alternative reference-gene normalization schemes.

name: paired-ttest-method-comparison
description: Use when two or more methods are evaluated on the same datasets and you need a statistically grounded ranking: compute per-dataset metrics for every method, then run paired t-tests of the focal method against each baseline.

name: paired-wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when comparing a continuous per-sample score (e.g. signalling entropy SR from SCENT) between matched patient pairs, such as diagnostic–relapse AML bulk samples, and the score distribution is not assumed normal.

name: paired-wilcoxon-significance-testing
description: Use when you have paired per-fold metric values (e.g., AMI, ARI, HOM, NMI from 5-fold cross-validation) for two methods on identical folds and need a one-sided significance test of ity.

name: pairwise-cell-distance-computation
description: Use when a paired multimodal single-cell dataset (e.g., CITE-seq RNA counts + ADT antibody counts) needs a quantitative check that imputed RNA geometry matches protein-space geometry.

name: pairwise-celltype-comparison-statistics
description: Use when per-cell-type isoform or TSS count tables (e.g. 'Modality-ModalityID.csv', NumModalityPerCluster) are available and the goal is to test whether one cell type (e.g. choroid plexus epithelium) shows distinctive isoform regulation versus another via pairwise DIE tests.

name: pairwise-colocalization-baseline-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking a colocalization or target-tissue prioritization method against a classical single-causal-variant pairwise baseline on loci with experimentally validated target genes/tissues.

name: pairwise-complete-pearson-correlation-computation
description: Use when computing gene-gene co-expression correlations from sparse, zero-inflated scRNA-seq count matrices where excess zeros make ordinary Pearson/Spearman correlations unreliable, and a confidence-filtered pairwise-complete estimate is needed.

name: pairwise-condition-cell-population-comparison
description: Use when two processed, cell-type-annotated single-cell objects from distinct conditions are available and the goal is to identify which cell populations are enriched or depleted in one condition versus the other, e.

name: pairwise-constraint-generation
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with scDCC and partial labels or marker genes are available: hold out ~10% of labeled cells, then sample must-link/cannot-link pairs to guide the model's latent space toward biologically meaningful clusters.

name: pairwise-constraint-guided-deep-clustering
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data where purely unsupervised methods give biologically uninterpretable clusters and some prior knowledge (e.g., known same-type or different-type cell pairs) can be encoded as pairwise constraints.

name: pairwise-differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when a SingleCellExperiment of CD8 T cells has been assigned to reference states and you need gene signatures per state pair (or per state) to score/query cells or train a state classifier.

name: pairwise-distance-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a pseudo-space has been reconstructed from scRNA-seq data using an ST reference (e.g., 10X Visium DLPFC slice 151674) and the geometric fidelity of the reconstruction must be quantified before downstream interpretation.

name: pairwise-distance-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating recovered 2D cell/spot coordinates from scRNA-seq against a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, MERSCOPE, MERFISH) where true test-set coordinates are known and methods like CeLEry, Tangram, spaOTsc, and novoSpaRc are being compared.

name: pairwise-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq matrix with cell-type, condition, and patient metadata and need a cell-type-by-cell-type distance matrix (e.g., to cluster cell types by transcriptomic perturbation magnitude or lineage similarity).

name: pairwise-locus-level-correlation-computation
description: Use when evaluating BIRD predictions across multiple cell types: you have predicted and true DH matrices for ≥3 cell types and need pair-wise locus-level accuracy of differential DH, stratified by cell-type similarity.

name: pairwise-must-link-cannot-link-loss-configuration
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data where purely unsupervised clustering yields biologically uninterpretable clusters and partial prior knowledge (e.g., protein-level ADT distances or known marker subtypes like CD4/CD8) is available for a subset of cell pairs.

name: pairwise-similarity-computation-scrna-seq
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression data whose high dropout and noise make naive two-cell similarity unreliable, and a robust cell-to-cell similarity matrix is needed as input to spectral clustering.

name: pairwise-spearman-correlation-across-methods
description: Use when you have per-method regulator activity score matrices from decoupleR benchmarks and need to test whether different activity inference methods produce similar estimates.

name: pairwise-subtype-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you need to quantify how sensitive CMS subtype assignments (from CMScaller nearest-template prediction) are to template-development choices such as marker-selection p-value cutoffs, cell line panels, LFC thresholds, or gene-set composition.

name: pal-based-tumor-cell-binarization
description: Use when scRNA-seq tumor cells must be split into pathway-active vs pathway-inactive groups (e.g., G2M checkpoint-positive dividing TNBC cells) without clustering, so downstream per-group tests like a TYRO3 Wilcoxon rank-sum can be run.

name: pal-distribution-antimode-binarization
description: Use when a pathway's per-cell activity scores (PAL from GSDensity run.rwr) form a multimodal distribution and cells must be split into positive/negative pathway states for downstream differential tests, without relying on clustering.

name: palantir-cell-fate-probability-comparison
description: Use when DICE has already assigned primed vs unprimed cells toward competing lineages and you must validate those assignments against Palantir fate probabilities (and, for SHARE-Seq data, matched scATAC-Seq chromVAR TF activity).

name: palette-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantitatively justify a spatial color-assignment method over defaults: you have cell coordinates plus cluster labels from spatial transcriptomics (e.g., STARmap) and a set of candidate colorization methods sharing one palette.

name: pan-cancer-bulk-scrna-integration
description: Use when annotating malignant cells in tumor scRNA-seq data lacking an internal confident reference, or when testing classifier generalization to cancer types held out of training (e.g., lung or gastric cancer).

name: pan-cancer-driver-gene-model-training
description: Use when building or reproducing a pan-cancer TSG/OG classifier from somatic mutation features for labelled driver genes, especially when the training set is small (136 TSGs, 76 OGs) and overfitting is a concern.

name: pan-cancer-gene-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq expression of a predefined malignant-vs-non-malignant gene signature (e.g. TMGs/NMGs) must be correlated with ESTIMATE immune/stromal scores and tumor purity and tested for tumor-vs-normal elevation and survival impact in TCGA.

name: pan-cancer-gene-recurrence-filtering
description: Use when building a cross-cancer malignant-cell classifier reference and you need a gene panel selected from recurrent bulk-RNA-seq DE signals plus high-variance single-cell genes.

name: pan-cancer-reference-dataset-preparation
description: Use when a task requires building or curating a pan-cancer TME cell-classification training reference and matched external validation biopsies, or when retraining scATOMIC/SingleR/Seurat/scmap-cell/CHETAH/scType/SingleCellNet on identical data.

name: pan-cancer-scrnaseq-matrix-processing
description: Use when a large collection of uniformly processed tumor scRNA-seq matrices (e.g., TISCH-derived, 2,157,387 cells across 93 datasets) must be integrated into interpretable gene-expression components that transfer across cohorts and cancer types.

name: pancancer-cohort-survival-analysis
description: Use when a matrix of pathway activity scores (e.g. PROGENy footprints) over TCGA tumors must be associated with overall survival time and event status, pan-cancer or within individual cancer types.

name: pancancer-favorability-score-aggregation
description: Use when TimiGP interaction networks have been built per cohort (e.g., 23 TCGA cancer types) and you need to compare per-cell favorable/unfavorable degrees across cancer types to identify pan-cancer prognostic patterns.

name: pancancer-multiomics-comparison-analysis
description: Use when validating gene-level predictions (e.g., DGMP 'logits' top-100 drivers) by testing whether candidates differ from non-candidates in pan-cancer SNV, CNA, methylation, and expression alteration metrics.

name: pancreas-developmental-lineage-marker-interpretation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data are intentionally over-clustered (e.g. Leiden resolution 3.5) and the goal is to merge non-significantly different clusters and detect intermediate cell states along a developmental lineage from cell-by-cluster enrichment scores.

name: pancreas-endocrine-signaling-regulatory-analysis
description: Use when analyzing TFvelo output on the pancreas dataset to check whether high-|weight| transcription factors (REST, HMGN3) act with consistent signs on insulin secretion pathway genes and whether KEGG endocrine terms are enriched among -fitted genes.

name: pancreas-islet-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq dataset with published cell-type labels (e.g. Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2 pancreas) must be mapped onto a target dataset from a different protocol (e.g. Baron CEL-Seq1 or Muraro CEL-Seq2 pancreas) with strong batch effect and library-depth asymmetry.

name: pancreas-lung-dataset-preprocessing
description: Use when benchmarking batch effect removal of single-cell foundation model embeddings (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer v2, scFoundation) against open-problems SOTA on the human pancreas and lung datasets using scIB avgBIO.

name: pancreas-reference-atlas-construction
description: Use when you must build a reusable reference atlas from a multi-batch pancreas (or similar tissue) scRNA-seq dataset so that new query datasets can be mapped and annotated without retraining, as done for GSE114297, GSE85247 and GSE83312 with scCobra.

name: pancreas-scrnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw pancreas scRNA-seq count matrices (Muraro CEL-Seq2, Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2) must be converted to Seurat V3.0 log-counts before integration with BATMAN, Scanorama, Seurat V3.0, or MNNcorrect, or when building the 1-held-out condition.

name: pancreas-single-cell-data-processing
description: Use when building a single-tissue ligand–receptor connectome from the human pancreas scRNAseq data distributed by SeuratData, or when reproducing Connectome edgeweight columns (e.g. weight_sc) on a Seurat object.

name: pancreatic-cancer-cell-type-proportion-analysis
description: Use when sample-level Leiden clusters (e.g., the PDAC 11 control / 14 Tumor 1 / 10 Tumor 2 split at resolution 0.3) exist and you must test which cell types' proportions or marker genes separate them.

name: pancreatic-cancer-signature-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when interpreting the cellular origin of PDAC gene signatures across sample compartments (primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, cell lines, normal pancreas, metastasis) in bulk transcriptomic datasets.

name: pancreatic-endocrine-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq of pancreatic endocrine development (e.g., E15.5 Bastidas-Ponce pancreas data) must have rare hormone-producing fates like delta cells and Beta-1/Beta-2 subtypes detected without manual cell-fate assignment.

name: pancreatic-endocrine-differentiation-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when comparing lineage-specific TF sets inferred by FateCompass across two pancreatic endocrine differentiation datasets (e.g., mouse E15.

name: pancreatic-endocrine-lineage-annotation
description: Use when annotating mouse pancreatic endocrine scRNA-seq (e.g., E15.5 Bastidas-Ponce AnnData with 'clusters' and an scVelo RNA velocity field) into progenitor and terminal hormone-producing fates so downstream fate-probability or trajectory-sampling methods have defined terminal states.

name: pancreatic-islet-cell-type-biology
description: Use when deconvolving bulk pancreatic islet RNA-seq (e.g., Fadista/GSE50244 read counts) into alpha, beta, delta, gamma, acinar and ductal proportions with a healthy-human-islet scRNA-seq reference (E-MTAB-5060) and testing proportion–phenotype associations such as beta cell proportion vs HbA1c.

name: pancreatic-lineage-fate-outcome-analysis
description: Use when simulating transcription factor overexpression in single-cell time-series scRNA-seq of pancreatic/β-cell differentiation, and you need day-resolved or starting-population-resolved fate-bias shifts toward β-, α-, or EC-cell outcomes.

name: pancreatic-lineage-trajectory-interpretation
description: Use when a fitted scKINETICS model (gene regulatory network matrix A plus per-cell transcriptional velocities) is available and TF-level regulator activity across a pancreatic lineage transition such as acinar-to-ductal metaplasia must be inferred.

name: pandas-dataframe-result-handling
description: Use when SQL has been executed against an AnnSQL database (e.g. on an .asql file built from an .h5ad AnnData object) and the result must be captured as a pandas DataFrame, AnnData object, or Parquet file.

name: pandas-expression-matrix-handling
description: Use when a raw tab-delimited gene expression matrix (e.g. a GSE export like gse.txt) must be shaped into an indexed Pandas DataFrame as input to ERgene's FindERG or normalizationdata functions.

name: pandas-tabular-data-loading
description: Use when a CSV table of gene IDs with pairwise log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns (e.g. 'Treatment1vsCtrl_Log2FoldChange', 'Treatment1vsCtrl_padj') must be ingested before scorecard region-of-interest classification.

name: panel-gene-set-intersection-analysis
description: Use when you have per-gene MRSD scores for multiple biosamples and curated disease gene panel gene lists, and need to rank tissues per panel by fraction of low-MRSD genes.

name: pangenome-gene-cluster-assignment
description: Use when specific reference protein sequences must be located in a pan-genome gene-cluster matrix to build a per-genome presence/absence profile (e.g., mapping hrc/hrp genes across Pseudomonas genomes).

name: panglao-marker-gene-set-retrieval
description: Use when validating Pollock top-100 DWG lists (from captum feature scores) against a trusted external marker database, or when quantifying per-cell-state overlap percentages with known markers.

name: parallel-execution-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing runtime of a parallelized pipeline against slower baselines on the same input (e.g., A. thaliana microarray matrix), recording wall-clock time and memory alongside AUPRC to show a speed-quality trade-off.

name: parallel-multicore-scaling-evaluation
description: Use when comparing the wall-clock runtime and memory footprint of a fast re-implementation versus original scoring tools on large single-cell datasets, or when testing scaling in cell number and pathway number.

name: parallel-outer-loop-benchmarking
description: Use when timing nested CV fits of nestedcv (e.g. nestcv.train with random forest, nestcv.glmnet) on high-dimensional transcriptomic data and comparing serial (cv.cores=1) vs parallel (cv.cores=8) wall-clock times.

name: parallel-scaling-plateau-analysis
description: Use when nested CV fitting (e.g. 10 x 10-fold nestcv.train or nestcv.glmnet) is too slow serially and you need to quantify how much wall-clock time cv.cores parallelisation saves on multi-core hardware.

name: parallel-scoring-of-pathway-gene-sets
description: Use when a cell-by-gene expression matrix must be converted to a cell-by-pathway PAS matrix for >10^3 pathways across ≥10^5 cells and standard UCell/AddModuleScore would be too slow.

name: parallel-simulation-execution
description: Use when fault-injection simulation sweeps over DNA storage pipelines produce too many sequencing reads and iterations to run serially, and results must be collected across many independent jobs.

name: parameter-matched-mask-ablation-study
description: Use when validating that a knowledge-masked Transformer annotator (e.g., TOSICA on mPancreas, Supplementary Fig. 8) actually gains accuracy from curated .gmt masks rather than model capacity alone.

name: parameter-sensitivity-comparison
description: Use when scoring gene signatures on low-depth or downsampled single-cell data with UCell and you need to justify or reproduce a non-default maxRank setting, or to verify how missing signature genes affect scores under 'impute' vs 'skip'.

name: parameter-sensitivity-sweep-analysis
description: Use when validating a clustering or similarity-learning pipeline whose defaults (e.g. penalty ratio rho/lambda) need empirical justification, by sweeping parameters on benchmark datasets and plotting performance stability curves.

name: parameter-sweep-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how technical or biological simulation parameters (e.g., capture efficiency alpha, variability sigma) affect the relative performance of multiple methods that need simulated gold standards for scoring.

name: parameter-sweep-orchestration
description: Use when a DNA storage fault-injection experiment must vary encoder/decoder/fault/copy parameters systematically and each combination needs its own reproducible output directory with aggregated statistics.

name: parametric-probability-density-curve-fitting
description: Use when a denoised expression matrix (e.g., the SERM autoencoder output So) must be summarized as a single parametric probability distribution before histogram-equalization imputation, and you need to choose among Gaussian, Rayleigh, and exponential families objectively.

name: parc-cluster-graph-construction
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (e.g. mESC CyTOF, scRNA-seq) must be reduced to a cluster-level graph before trajectory inference, especially at atlas scale (10^2–10^6 cells).

name: parc-clustering-parameter-tuning
description: Use when constructing the PARC cluster-graph stage of a VIA trajectory-inference run (e.g., on a .h5ad AnnData with PCA in obsm['X_pca']) and needing to set pruning resolution, granularity, and terminal-state thresholds for scalable, globally connected TI.

name: pareg-regularized-regression-enrichment
description: Use when a study has per-gene differential expression p-values and a pathway database whose redundant, overlapping gene sets require coherent (inter-pathway-aware) enrichment scores rather than independent per-pathway tests.

name: parquet-columnar-storage-write
