description: Use when a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) has been melted to tall format in Spark and needs a columnar, compressed on-disk representation for subsequent scSPARKL pipeline stages.

name: parquet-io-for-single-cell-data
description: Use when a scRNA-seq pipeline must load or persist tall/wide count matrices (e.g. filtered tall csv/parquet input, normalized_wide.parquet/normalized_tall.parquet outputs) on Spark, especially when in-memory tools like Seurat/Scanpy hit RAM limits.

name: parquet-serialization-of-quality-tables
description: Use when you have cleaned, melted tall-format scRNA-seq expression data (CSV or Parquet) loaded as a Spark DataFrame and need per-cell and per-gene quality summaries (ERCC %, mito %, dropouts) persisted as Parquet tables for threshold-based filtering.

name: pars-tuberalis-subtype-identification
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (~tens of thousands of cells, e.g. ~20k Arc-ME mouse brain profiles from the Single Cell Portal) must be scanned for rare minor cell subpopulations that standard clustering would miss.

name: partial-annotation-benchmark-construction
description: Use when you must quantify how accurately a splice-aware tool detects junctions between annotated splice sites that are absent from the reference annotation: simulate reads from full transcriptomes, derive a partial ground truth by removing held-out event transcripts, and score recall/precision.

name: partial-correlation-complementarity-assessment
description: Use when implementing or validating a greedy feature-selection criterion (e.g., RRCT or an mRMR extension) that must account for feature interactions: candidate features need scoring via conditional relevance given the already-selected subset, not just marginal relevance and pairwise redundancy.

name: partial-correlation-edge-thresholding
description: Use when building a GGM-based co-expression network from a large single-cell expression matrix where weak co-expression signals and dropouts make ordinary Pearson correlation unreliable.

name: partial-correlation-network-inference-single-cell
description: Use when the goal is to construct a gene co-expression network from a raw single-cell expression matrix (e.g., MCA, >5000 cells) via GGM/pcor methods, and to identify gene expression programs (GEPs) from it.

name: partial-correlation-permutation-testing
description: Use when building a gene co-expression network (GGM) from a large single-cell expression matrix (>5000 cells recommended) and you need pcor estimates with permutation-based FDR control to select significant gene pairs.

name: partial-label-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how accurately a supervised single-cell integration method predicts cell-type labels for unannotated cells, against a baseline like scANVI, under partial-annotation settings (10%, 20%, or 50% of cells missing labels).

name: partial-least-squares-control-gene-modeling
description: Use when scRNAseq expression matrices contain unmeasured technical confounders (e.g. ERCC spike-ins available as controls), and a corrected matrix is needed for downstream clustering/analysis.

name: partial-least-squares-latent-factor-modeling
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression must be corrected for hidden confounders (e.g. cell cycle, batch/technical effects) and both control genes and target genes are available to inform factor inference.

name: partial-svd-computation
description: Use when a decomposition algorithm (e.g. JIVE) needs only the 1–10 singular components of a large dense matrix and full SVD is the runtime bottleneck.

name: partial-tei-stratified-computation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (Scanpy AnnData, .h5ad) must be decomposed into gene-age-stratified expression contributions — e.g. to test whether the youngest age classes (C. elegans classes 11–13) peak in early embryos.

name: partykit-tree-plot-customization
description: Use when a fitted subgroup tree (dipm/spmtree for continuous or survival outcomes) needs publication-ready visualization, and the default partykit terminal panels are insufficient because treatment-stratified distributions or survival curves must be shown per node.

name: partykit-tree-visualization
description: Use when a DIPM tree (e.g. fitted to the MASS::anorexia weight-change data) or a pmprune-pruned version of it needs to be rendered for inspection, so subgroup splits and optimal treatment assignments at each node can be visually verified.

name: pathogen-gene-umi-quantification
description: Use when 10x cellranger output exists for infected-cell scRNAseq data and per-cell UMI counts for individual pathogen genes (not just total pathogen reads) are needed, e.g. for Fig. 3J-style aligner consistency or gene-level infection analysis.

name: pathogen-genome-read-alignment
description: Use when you have 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample where cellranger count has already aligned reads to the host genome, and you need per-cell viral/bacterial counts in a single command.

name: pathogen-specific-candidate-count-verification
description: Use when reproducing or validating candidate gene counts from GWAS SNPs plus coexpression modules, e.g. after running cageminer on SoyFungiGCN data with defense guide genes and a 2 Mb SNP window.

name: pathologist-annotation-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when validating Cancer-Finder (or similar) spot-level malignancy predictions on 10x Visium slides against pathologist annotations, e.g. reproducing the reported per-slide accuracy of 82.00–97.37% (Fig. 4b,c).

name: pathologist-annotation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have tumor ST spot-level predictions (e.g., malignancy_probability, AUCell signature scores, image scores) plus pathologist-annotated malignant regions and need accuracy/balanced-accuracy benchmarking against expert labels or a competing classifier.

name: pathomics-trajectory-inference-with-eiplgraph
description: Use when you have per-sample cell-type/structure distributions from histopathology (e.g., .h5ad pathomics objects) and want an unsupervised disease progression ordering of samples plus associated morphometric changes.

name: pathway-activation-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when a CommPath object already contains scored pathways (scorePath) and differential activation results (diffAllPath), and you need to visualize the top differentially activated pathways per cluster as a heatmap PDF.

name: pathway-activation-score-computation-single-cell
description: Use when single-cell or semi-profiled cohort data (annotated cells with condition labels, e.g., Healthy/Asymptomatic/Mild/Moderate/Severe/Critical) must be compared for pathway-level fidelity, or when pathway activation patterns are a downstream deliverable.

name: pathway-activity-estimation-from-gene-expression
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (rows = samples, columns = Entrez gene IDs) must be converted into gene-set/pathway activity features for cancer subtype classification or to test robustness to incomplete gene annotation.

name: pathway-activity-inference-at-single-cell-level
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., AnnData-wrapped MIX-Seq drug treatment data) needs to be embedded in a biologically interpretable latent space defined by GMT gene sets, and per-cell pathway activity or differential pathway activity between conditions is the goal.

name: pathway-activity-inference-from-gene-expression
description: Use when you need to quantify signaling pathway activity from normalized gene expression (DESeq2 size-factor/VST RNA-seq, microarray, single-cell) for perturbation recall, driver mutation, drug-sensitivity, or patient-survival association analyses.

name: pathway-activity-likelihood-scoring
description: Use when you need single-cell pathway activity scores (PAL) for a gene set in scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics data without clustering, e.g., to fetch relevant cells or weight cells for spatial relevance tests.

name: pathway-activity-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively evaluate whether a pathway activity method outperforms alternatives (fGSEA, iDEA, GSVA, AUCell, Vision, ssGSEA) on controlled single-cell simulations with a known ground-truth perturbed pathway.

name: pathway-activity-network-propagation
description: Use when single-cell or spatial transcriptomics data must be scored per cell for pathway activity without clustering — e.g., to fetch cells active for a gene set (Hallmark G2M, GO BP terms) or to weight cells for spatial KDE testing.

name: pathway-activity-quantification-from-rnaseq
description: Use when you have a cpm-normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix with sample labels (e.g., CF vs healthy donors) and need to identify which gene sets show significantly shifted or over-dispersed activity between conditions.

name: pathway-activity-score-computation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of PAS scoring methods (fast_ucell, fast_score_genes vs UCell, AUCell, score_genes) across datasets scaling from 10,000 cells to over 1.2 million cells.

name: pathway-activity-scoring-across-methods
description: Use when you need to compare how well competing pathway activity scoring methods recover known cell types from scRNA-seq data, or to benchmark GSDensity against ssGSEA/GSVA/AUCell/VAM/scGSEA/CelliD on labeled or simulated datasets.

name: pathway-and-disease-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of genes carrying predicted Ψ sites (e.g. from a >0.99-precision transcriptome scan in Supplemental_table2.csv) and need to identify which molecular functions, pathways, or diseases are functionally over-represented.

name: pathway-cell-type-module-interpretation
description: Use when a trained MOFA model on pseudobulk pathway activity scores (PAS) must be interpreted: identifying which latent factors are disease-related and which pathway-cell type pairs drive them.

name: pathway-coordination-testing-kld
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (Seurat object) must be screened to determine which curated gene sets (KEGG, BIOCARTA, GO:BP) are genuinely heterogeneous across cells prior to pathway activity scoring or binarization, without pre-clustering the cells.

name: pathway-database-querying
description: Use when a table of enriched int-pairs from a cell-cell interaction analysis needs functional/pathway annotation of its ligand-receptor pairs, e.g. in InterCellar's function-verse.

name: pathway-dictionary-construction
description: Use when preparing pathway prior knowledge as input to scPAFA's fast_Ucell or fast_score_genes PAS computation, i.e., before Step1 'Calculate Pathway Activity Score'.

name: pathway-disease-association-interpretation
description: Use when you have trained a topic model (e.g. 100-topic scETM) on scRNA-seq data and need to show the learned topics correspond to known human gene pathways or disease gene sets via gene set enrichment analysis.

name: pathway-enrichment-annotation-of-gene-modules
description: Use when you have gene subnetworks/modules partitioned from a gene regulatory network (e.g., SCING GRN modules via Leiden) and need biological annotation or disease-relevant pathway interpretation for each module.

name: pathway-enrichment-dotplot-visualization
description: Use when a CCC decomposition factor's loadings (e.g., Factor 4 from the context x interaction x sender x receiver tensor built on GSE96583/EH2259 IFN-beta PBMCs) must be biologically interpreted via pathway enrichment dotplots such as JAK-STAT across STIM vs CTRL contexts.

name: pathway-enrichment-estimation
description: Use when a gene-level p-value table (gene, pvalue) and a pathway database (e.g., GO BP terms of size 50-500) must be converted into coherent pathway-level enrichment scores that account for redundant/overlapping gene sets.

name: pathway-enrichment-regularized-regression-modeling
description: Use when a pathway enrichment analysis must account for redundancy/dependencies between gene sets (e.g. large GO/KEGG/Reactome databases), or when benchmarking enrichment robustness to noise on synthetic pathway data.

name: pathway-flux-interpretation-from-dominant-genes
description: Use when a KEGG metabolic pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g. the four-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340) and read-count data must be aggregated per node to identify the dominant enzyme.

name: pathway-gene-matrix-filtering
description: Use when initializing p-scETM with trainable_gene_emb_dim set to zero, or whenever a known gene-set matrix must be size-filtered before being used as a fixed gene embedding in topic models.

name: pathway-geneset-formatting
description: Use when preparing pathway gene sets (MSigDB collections, csv, or gmt files) as input to SCPA or another pathway-analysis method that expects a structured pathway table mapping pathway names to gene sets.

name: pathway-gmt-gene-module-loading
description: Use when a single-cell dataset will be analyzed with VEGA or another annotation-informed latent variable model and a GMT file of gene module membership (Reactome, MSigDB, GO, PANTHER) must be loaded to define the decoder wiring.

name: pathway-network-visualization
description: Use when a pareg fit (or an enrichment result convertible via as_enrichplot_object) must be inspected for inter-pathway structure — clustered groups of related terms — rather than only a top-N term ranking.

name: pathway-node-expansion
description: Use when KEGG KGML pathway nodes carry multiple gene names (functional homologs/OR groups) and Cytoscape/KEGGScape shows only the first gene, hiding candidate enzymes for a reaction.

name: pathway-over-representation-analysis
description: Use when a DMC list from Illumina 450K/EPIC differential methylation analysis must be mapped to genes and tested for enriched biological pathways across KEGG, Reactome, and WikiPathways.

name: pathway-perturbation-association-testing
description: Use when you have a matrix of perturbation gene-expression experiments and a PROGENy model, and need to test that inferred pathway activations are specific to the experimentally perturbed pathway even when that experiment is held out of model building.

name: pathway-score-quartile-stratification
description: Use when you have cell-line drug sensitivity (IC50) data plus mutation calls and gene expression, and want to test whether PROGENy pathway activity further stratifies drug response within mutant vs wild-type sub-populations.

name: pathway-similarity-matrix-computation
description: Use when a regularized-regression enrichment method (pareg) needs a pathway similarity matrix for its network term, or when benchmarking whether an alternative similarity measure matches a Jaccard-based baseline.

name: pathway-topic-association-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData matrices (HP, AD, MDD) with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' need direct, functionally meaningful pathway-topic interpretations without sacrificing clustering performance relative to unregularized scETM.

name: patient-level-drug-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have per-cluster differential expression from multiple diseased scRNA-seq samples (PDX or patient) plus a tissue-specific LINCS L1000 drug reference, and you need patient-level drug recommendations and cross-cohort overlap of significant drugs.

name: patsy-design-matrix-construction
description: Use when fitting a scCODA Dirichlet-Multinomial model to cell-type count data and a covariate matrix must be constructed from a formula (e.g. 'x_0') with a specified or automatically selected reference cell type.

name: pattern-recovery-purity-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a decomposition or clustering method (e.g., ACTIONet, cNMF, cLDA, cICA, Louvain) on synthetic scRNA-seq benchmarks with planted patterns, to measure pattern-recovery purity against generative ground truth.

name: pbmc-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a raw PBMC single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. a GEO accession like GSE149689) must be clustered and annotated into immune cell subsets to localise gene-expression dysregulation to a cell type.

name: pbmc-cell-type-marker-validation
description: Use when Leiden cluster labels already exist for integrated scMoMaT cell factors and you need cluster-specific bio-marker scores per modality, or validation of those scores against known markers such as GNLY/NKG7 (NK) or MS4A1/CD79A/CD37 (B cells).

name: pbmc-cell-type-prediction
description: Use when a trained Miscell model's latent feature matrix and matching cell-type labels are available and you need to quantify how linearly separable the cell types are (AUC/accuracy per type).

name: pbmc-dataset-loading-with-scanpy
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell clustering on the 10x Genomics PBMC dataset (Zheng et al. 2017) or generating scDesign2 simulations fitted to PBMC data; input is raw gene-by-cell counts.

name: pbmc-immune-process-annotation
description: Use when a short list of EDGE feature genes (e.g., 35 genes from PBMC cells) needs biological-process interpretation, specifically testing whether they are enriched for immune- or stimulus-response-related GO terms.

name: pbmc-phenotype-label-clustering
description: Use when you have a denoised or imputed single-cell expression matrix with known phenotype labels and need a quantitative cluster-separation metric (mean silhouette score in [-1, 1]) to rank denoising methods.

name: pbmc-simulation-dataset-design
description: Use when benchmarking cell label assignment methods on PBMC scRNA-seq under controlled training-size and testing-size conditions, needing simulation splits and metrics like ARI.

name: pbmc3k-cell-type-discrimination
description: Use when evaluating whether gene set scores computed on sparsified/downsampled single-cell data remain discriminative between cell types, or when comparing smoothed vs non-smoothed scoring robustness.

name: pbmc3k-scrnaseq-data-processing
description: Use when a QC-filtered PBMC3k-style scRNA-seq count matrix must be processed in SCALA/Seurat through normalization, dimensionality reduction, Louvain clustering, and per-cluster marker-gene testing with Wilcoxon/MAST/DESeq2.

name: pc-count-robustness-benchmarking
description: Use when assessing sensitivity of trajectory inference / terminal-state detection to the dimensionality of the input PC representation, e.g. scATAC-seq (ChromVAR k-mer or TF-motif z-scores) swept across ~10–100 PCs to compare fate-detection F1 stability.

name: pc-count-selection-comparison
description: Use when evaluating how well an automatic dimension-selection criterion (RMT-based, elbow, or 95%-variance) preserves the local neighborhood structure of a scRNA-seq embedding, or when comparing PC counts across downsampled data.

name: pc1-based-geneset-shift-overdispersion-testing
description: Use when you have a normalized gene expression matrix (samples as columns, genes as rows) plus a module/GMT list (e.g. MSigDB HALLMARK) and need sample-level module activity scores with statistical shift/overdispersion significance.

name: pc1-module-activity-quantification
description: Use when you need sample-wise pathway/module activity scores and significance from a normalized gene expression matrix (e.g. edgeR cpm) and a collection of gene sets (GMT/MSigDB Hallmark), to find shifted or over-dispersed modules between conditions.

name: pc1-variance-geneset-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-sample expression matrix and gene sets (e.g., MSigDB GMT) and need sample-wise module activity scores with statistical significance distinguishing shifted vs overdispersed gene sets.

name: pca-based-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that imputation or preprocessing improves cell-subpopulation separation in scRNA-seq count matrices, by comparing PCA-based cluster compactness of raw vs imputed data against a known ground-truth clustering.

name: pca-cell-embedding-feature-set-sweep
description: Use when an scRNA-seq pipeline must decide how many top-ranked feature genes (DUBStepR-ordered) to retain before PCA and clustering, and cell type annotations may not exist for tuning that number.

name: pca-celltype-visualization
description: Use when evaluating whether a denoising method preserved or recovered celltype structure in scRNA-seq data with known labels, by comparing PCA embeddings of denoised vs. ground-truth matrices.

name: pca-clustering-validation
description: Use when you have clustered simulated (or ground-truthed) feature profiles with k-means/k-medoids and need an unsupervised confirmation that cluster assignments reflect the known simulation design before computing incorrect-assignment rates.

name: pca-component-gene-ranking
description: Use when benchmarking a periodicity- or trajectory-based gene ranking against a linear PCA baseline on the same scRNA-seq matrix, e.g., to test whether circular pseudo-time captures cell-cycle biology better than principal components.

name: pca-dimension-reduction-of-count-matrices
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix needs dimension reduction before distance- or similarity-based steps such as scImpute's outlier-cell detection via nearest-neighbor distances.

name: pca-dimension-reduction-of-scrna-counts
description: Use when you have a genes-by-cells scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. GSE45719, 268 mouse embryo cells) and need low-dimensional coordinates for downstream spectral clustering or comparison of imputation methods.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when evaluating imputation or preprocessing effects on single-cell clustering: after obtaining a gene-by-cell matrix (raw or imputed), reduce it with 50-component PCA prior to k-means clustering and ARI computation.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a cell-by-ontology-type score matrix (e.g. pred_Y_all from OnClassModel.Predict) or another high-dimensional per-cell feature table and need a low-dimensional embedding for clustering-quality benchmarks such as silhouette analysis.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-for-scrna-seq
description: Use when a raw single-cell counts matrix (csv/rds/h5, genes as rows and cells as columns) must be reduced to a lower-dimensional gene space before cell clustering or neural-network cell-type annotation in a cancer TME scRNA-seq pipeline.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-of-count-matrices
description: Use when a normalized or scaled cell-by-gene count matrix of barcoded cells needs a compact PC representation (e.g., npc = 25) to feed nearest-neighbor graph construction for ClonoCluster hybrid clustering.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-of-expression-matrices
description: Use when comparing dropout-imputation methods on scRNA-seq count matrices and you need a low-dimensional embedding for PCA/t-SNE visualization and spectral clustering against known cell-type labels.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-of-sc-rna-seq-counts
description: Use when a high-dimensional normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) must be embedded into a low-dimensional PC score space so per-PC mixed models can be fit for downstream cell-type distance estimation or inference.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-preprocessing
description: Use when raw Tabula Muris FACS scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 00_facs_raw_data/FACS/{Tissue}-counts.csv from the Figshare deposit) must be converted into a numeric 50-PC feature matrix as input to embedding methods such as EMBEDR.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-scrna
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., AnnData .h5ad) has been QC-filtered and normalized and you need a compact latent representation for clustering or UMAP visualization, such as reproducing HuBMAP spleen cluster counts.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-scrna
description: Use when a scRNA-seq preprocessing pipeline needs a compact PCA embedding (e.g., PC1-30) from scaled expression data before cell clustering, doublet simulation, or PC-count parameters for tools like DoubletFinder within Chord.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-scrnaseq
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (tall or wide format, e.g. CSV/Parquet) must be projected to a low-dimensional space to enable scalable clustering on large cell counts.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-single-cell
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq annotation pipeline has cells rejected as 'unassigned' after marker counting and needs a low-dimensional embedding (PCA) plus clustering to reassign them by cluster similarity.

name: pca-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when after a differential-expression test on background-subtracted microarray data, you need a low-dimensional (PCA) visualization to confirm that samples cluster by response class using only the significant genes.

name: pca-embedding-batch-assessment
description: Use when you need to quantify residual batch effects after correction (e.g. ComBat on two-technical-replicate mESC data) in a linear PC space, or to build the PCA baseline needed for a sensitivity comparison against a nonlinear embedding such as BEENE.

name: pca-embedding-of-trajectory-data
description: Use when pseudotime has been inferred with redPATH's consensus Hamiltonian path algorithm and you need to detect and visualize whether the developmental trajectory is linear or branched.

name: pca-feature-representation-extraction
description: Use when preparing a cell-typed scRNA-seq .h5ad (AnnData) as input to scValue or another OOB random-forest sketching step that expects a dense PCA feature matrix via use_rep='X_pca'.

name: pca-gmm-clustering-of-scrnaseq
description: Use when a marker-count-based cell type identifier leaves many cells unassigned and you need to reassign them by within-cluster expression similarity, or when reproducing the 0.1-0.9 rejection/reassignment threshold sweep.

name: pca-input-formatting-for-trajectory-inference
description: Use when preparing PC-reduced single-cell omics matrices (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq chromVAR k-mer or TF-motif z-scores) as input to VIA's via_wrapper, or when testing trajectory-inference robustness across PC counts.

name: pca-kmeans-cell-type-initialization
description: Use when running DIEM on 10X droplet-based snRNA-seq (or scRNA-seq) count data and you need to initialize k cell-type clusters via PCA and k-means before run_em debris-score estimation and call_targets filtering.

name: pca-latent-factor-detection
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows within-cell-type heterogeneity suspected to be a cell-cycle effect, and you need to test which principal components are cell-cycle driven before removing them while preserving cell-type signal.

name: pca-latent-space-coordinate-scoring
description: Use when you have normalized single-cell feature expression (protein counts, RNA, accessibility) plus a reduced-dimensional latent space (e.g., 50 protein-based PCs stored in an AnnData object) and need clustering-independent prediction of differentially active features.

name: pca-latent-space-embedding
description: Use when a library-normalized (scaled, non-log-transformed) genes x cells expression matrix must be embedded into a low-dimensional latent space before building a KNN graph or PhyloVision report, especially when cell counts exceed available memory (VISION 'pool' defaults to 'auto', micropooling.

name: pca-linear-baseline-ordering
description: Use when benchmarking a circular/periodic pseudo-time method against a linear baseline: scRNA-seq count matrices where cells should be ordered along a latent process and you need PCA-derived PC1/PC2 orderings for comparison (e.g. GSEA NES ranking as in Fig. 4a).

name: pca-linear-embedding-baseline-construction
description: Use when you need a standard linear embedding baseline in PC space to benchmark a learned nonlinear embedding's sensitivity for batch effect estimation metrics like kBET or iLISI on single-cell RNA-seq data.

name: pca-loading-versus-embedding-metagene-comparison
description: Use when a gene-embedding workflow has identified a candidate metagene (e.g. an IFIT1/ISG15/OAS1 cluster in interferon beta-stimulated PBMCs) and you need to demonstrate whether the program is cell-type-independent or an artifact of linear-model loading structure.

name: pca-multinomial-circadian-time-classification
description: Use when you have bulk or pseudobulk transcriptomic data with known circadian timestamps for training and need to predict the circadian time of single, untimestamped samples across assay platforms.

name: pca-neighborhood-distance-computation
description: Use when running scDEED and you need the pre-embedding neighbor distances against which 2D t-SNE/UMAP neighbor distances will be correlated — i.e., after RunPCA on a Seurat object and after generating the Permuted null (row-shuffled scale.data) PCA space.

name: pca-preprocessing-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix has thousands of features (e.g. ~23,686 genes) and must be scaled and compressed to PCA-50 prior to training ivis (k=15, model='maaten') for 2D embedding.

name: pca-reconstruction-error-rejection
description: Use when an unlabeled single-cell test set may contain cell populations absent from a labeled training set, and you need to reject (rather than force-classify) cells before hierarchical classification with scHPL.

name: pca-signal-equivalence-verification
description: Use when reconstructing scLENS's RMT noise-filtering module and you must prove that eigen-decomposition of the cell similarity matrix G = XX^T/N yields a signal subspace equivalent to PCA scores.

name: pca-tsne-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when you have an imputed single-cell expression matrix and known cell-type labels, and need a 2D embedding (t-SNE after PCA) to visually and quantitatively check cell-type separation.

name: pca-umap-cell-embedding-projection
description: Use when comparing synthetic scATAC-seq cells to real cells at the cell-embedding level: you have peak-by-cell count matrices for real and simulated cells (BAM/BED-derived) and need a quantitative mixing score such as miLISI.

name: pca-variance-structure-comparison
description: Use when two quantification pipelines have been run on the same RNA-seq FASTQ samples and you need to demonstrate equivalence by checking whether normalized count tables yield near-identical PCA variance structures and comparable DEG counts.

name: pca-versus-zinbwave-dimensionality-reduction-comparison
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices must be reduced to a low-dimensional space for clustering or trajectory inference, and dropouts/over-dispersion may make PCA representations miss lineage endpoints or cell types.

name: pca-visualization-of-imputed-expression
description: Use when comparing raw vs. imputed count matrices (Bfimpute, SCRABBLE, netNMF-sc, etc.) and you need a visualization-level and cell-relationship-level assessment of whether imputation improved cell-type separation.

name: pca-vs-nonlinear-embedding-batch-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying batch effects in single-cell RNA-seq data where PCA-space metrics may miss nonlinear batch structure — e.g., comparing uncorrected vs. ComBat/Harmony-corrected data with kBET and iLISI.

name: pcabased-cellcycle-component-removal
description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression matrices show within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by cell-cycle activity that obscures clustering of cell types, and you need a correction before downstream clustering.

name: pcawg-copy-number-coincidence-analysis
description: Use when validating ecDNA/amplification calls predicted from ATAC-Seq against an independent whole-genome sequencing cohort (PCAWG) by testing whether the same genes show copy-number gains.

name: pcawg-fusion-artifact-score-validation
description: Use when scoring candidate gene fusions from Smart-Seq scRNA-seq data for technical artifact likelihood, or when validating PCAWG fusion calls by assigning an artifact probability and filtering at a 0.5 cutoff.

name: pcr-amplification-and-fragmentation-simulation
description: Use when you have a true counts matrix from SimulateTrueCounts and need observed counts that reflect a specific scRNA-seq protocol (non-UMI vs UMI), or when testing whether simulated data reproduce protocol-specific artifacts like gene length bias.

name: pcr-amplification-fold-quantification
description: Use when quantifying isoform expression from single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore reads where PCR amplification scattering inflates UMI counts and fixed-edit-distance collapsing would overestimate UMIs under high sequencing error.

name: pcr-duplicate-marking-by-barcode-umi-gene
description: Use when converting aligned 10x droplet scRNA-seq reads (Read1/cDNA insert aligned with STAR, MAPQ=255) into a per-cell UMI count matrix and PCR duplicates must be removed before counting.

name: pdac-dataset-inventory-curation
description: Use when building or validating a dataset inventory table from pdacR's parsed .rds objects (e.g. verifying Table 1's 13-dataset compendium), or when auditing sample/feature counts and Used flags for PDAC transcriptomic datasets before analysis.

name: pdac-dataset-sample-filtering
description: Use when loading a public PDAC bulk expression dataset (e.g. TCGA-PAAD) from pdacR and the analysis requires only histologically confirmed adenocarcinoma samples; triggered by sample counts exceeding the whitelisted PDAC set or known contamination by non-PDAC tumors.

name: pdac-subtype-classification
description: Use when a bulk PDAC expression matrix (e.g. TCGA-PAAD) needs sample-level subtype calls under one or more of the Moffitt, Collisson, or Bailey schemas, or when comparing subtype assignments across these classification systems.

name: pdac-subtype-geneset-interpretation
description: Use when a PDAC transcriptomic analysis needs to check whether a subtype gene signature (Collisson Exocrine, Bailey ADEX, etc.) actually tracks tumor cellularity rather than tumor-intrinsic biology, using pdacR datasets with purity or VAF metadata.

name: pdac-subtype-signature-scoring
description: Use when comparing curated PDAC subtype signatures across matched/paired samples (primary vs metastatic vs cell line) or platforms (RNAseq vs microarray) to quantify signature retention or loss.

name: pdx-gene-expression-classification
description: Use when gene expression data from PDX models, cell lines, or organoids needs CMS classification without tumor stroma, or when assessing how sensitive subtype calls are to template construction choices.

name: pdx-model-identifier-mapping
description: Use when pre-clinical CRC cohorts (PDX or cell line) have CMS predictions from CMScaller and independently annotated drug-response labels that must be joined on sample/model identifiers before testing subtype-response associations.

name: peak-gene-candidate-pair-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq multiomic AnnData objects before GrID-Net-style causal inference, to define the bounded set of peak-gene pairs that will be scored.

name: peak-gene-pair-differential-prioritization
description: Use when you have GrID-Net peak-gene results plus correlation-method rankings and want to show that causally-prioritized pairs are biologically distinct, e.g., enriched for poised enhancers.

name: peak-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational cost (runtime, peak memory) of scDNA–scRNA integration methods as cell counts scale, or when you need to extrapolate MaCroDNA runtime to datasets larger than the measured ones.

name: peak-memory-profiling-of-decomposition-runs
description: Use when two alternative matrix-decomposition or joint-dimensionality-reduction implementations must be compared for computational efficiency on the same scenario, and runtime, memory, and rank-selection agreement are the metrics of interest.

name: peak-memory-usage-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking manifold alignment or single-cell integration methods for scalability, specifically to compare peak memory demand and runtime across multiple methods on the same datasets.

name: peak-to-gene-activity-conversion
description: Use when integrating scATAC (peaks) with transcriptomic modalities (scRNA/smFISH) in scConfluence: chromatin peaks must first be converted to gene activity scores to build the cross-modality common features matrix before computing the correlation-based cost matrix.

name: peak-to-gene-association-filtering
description: Use when building an enhancer-based GRN from paired snRNA-seq/snATAC-seq co-embedded cells and you need to restrict candidate genes to those both variable along pseudotime and linkable to at least one peak.

name: peak-to-gene-linkage-integration
description: Use when building an enhancer-based gene regulatory network from single-cell multiome data, where candidate TF–gene pairs must be filtered by enhancer–promoter linkage plus TF motif binding in linked peaks.

name: peak-to-gene-linking-from-multiome-data
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC multiome) cells ordered along a trajectory and need enhancer-to-promoter links to constrain TF-gene edges in an eGRN.

name: peak-to-gene-regulatory-linking
description: Use when you have scATAC-seq data (e.g. Cusanovich 2018 Spleen, GSE111586) plus a TF motif catalogue and need to filter out non-relevant TFs and build a per-target-gene candidate TF pool (base GRN parquet) for downstream logic-gate GRN inference.

name: peak-to-gene-strand-distance-matching
description: Use when MACS-called peaks from a 10x Chromium-like BAM must be filtered to gene-associated candidates — same strand as a gene and within a maximum distance — before designating 3' UTRs.

name: pearson-correlation-abundance-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when simulated RNA-seq data carry known theoretical circRNA isoform abundances and you must score how faithfully a quantifier (CircAST FPKM/TPM) recovers per-locus relative isoform fractions across conditions, or benchmark it against junction-read counting.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two features from a sequencing or microarray expression data frame (e.g., RNASEH2A vs PCNA in logTCGA40) need in-depth pairwise correlation with regression fit, correlation coefficient, and density/histogram visualization.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have a benchmark accuracy table plus per-dataset metadata (sizes, cell type counts, label distributions) and need to identify which dataset characteristics drive annotation accuracy.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis-of-bp-activities
description: Use when you have per-cell activity vectors for multiple ORIGINS2 biological-process PPINs (e.g. 18 BP edge sets) from a normalized scRNA-seq matrix and need to characterize cross-BP relationships such as anti-correlation between immune and replication programs.

name: pearson-correlation-analysis-of-sc-rna-seq-pluripotency-scores
description: Use when per-cell pluripotency scores from ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, and CytoTRACE are already computed and you need to quantify and validate their pairwise agreement via Pearson correlations across datasets.

name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-computation
description: Use when validating deconvolution output of bulk profiles into subpopulation-specific HiChIP/RNA-seq/ATAC-seq profiles by correlating predicted vs. true per-subpopulation profile vectors (e.g., in silico GM12878/K562 mixtures).

name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating a trajectory-inference method against ground-truth time points (e.g., annotated sampling days in a time-series CyTOF or scRNA-seq dataset) and you need a single quantitative score per method to compare against ablations and baselines.

name: pearson-correlation-benchmark-validation
description: Use when a deconvolution method's predicted cell-type abundances must be benchmarked against known true abundances from aggregated single-cell data to quantify accuracy per cell type.

name: pearson-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when a model predicts per-cell malignant labels on many externally curated scRNA-seq datasets and you must verify that aggregated per-dataset malignant fractions match those reported by the source database (e.g., CancerSCEM) using Pearson correlation.

name: pearson-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating predicted single-cell perturbation responses (e.g., control vs stimulated PBMC) against ground truth by DEG overlap and squared Pearson correlation per cell type.

name: pearson-correlation-benchmarking-across-modalities
description: Use when you have cell-level embeddings from multiple modalities (joint mvTCR, RNA-only, TCR-only) plus a continuous per-cell target such as pMHC multimer read counts, and need to quantify whether multimodality improves prediction.

name: pearson-correlation-cell-similarity
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq cells in scQA's CC stage and a cell-cell similarity graph is needed from the quantitative representation Q2; also as reference for choosing out-neighbor counts (0.1n vs 0.05n) by dataset size.

name: pearson-correlation-cell-type-matching
description: Use when a multi-timepoint scRNA-seq analysis must identify cells at t1 that do not match any t0-annotated cell type, after CrossTimeAnnotation has assigned preliminary labels and new cell types may have emerged over time.

name: pearson-correlation-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when you have Space Ranger-processed Visium spot-level expression for transcriptionally active regions (TARs/uTARs) plus known cell-type marker genes and need to test whether uTARs spatially colocalize with specific cell types across tissue sections.

name: pearson-correlation-computation
description: Use when you have two condition-specific expression matrices (rows = gene symbols, columns = sample IDs) and need per-patient differential co-expression edges for downstream WMDS.net driver-node ranking.

name: pearson-correlation-computation
description: Use when validating that CLEAR-derived FPB and CIRCscore values from ribo− paired-end RNA-seq reproduce published Pearson correlations against FPKM/FPM or RT-qPCR measurements.

name: pearson-correlation-computation
description: Use when you have two per-droplet numeric metrics (e.g., DIEM score.debris and percent spliced reads) aligned on shared droplet/barcode identifiers and need to quantify their linear agreement, expecting a high positive R (~0.7-0.99).

name: pearson-correlation-cutoff-network-filtering
description: Use when you have a PCC-scored functional association network (e.g. from FAVA on scRNA-seq or proteomics data) and need to extract a high-confidence subnetwork at STRING-style probability cutoffs.

name: pearson-correlation-deconvolution-assessment
description: Use when simulated bulk HiChIP mixtures have known subpopulation-specific loop counts and you must quantify deconvolution accuracy or benchmark a model-based inference against a simple plug-in baseline.

name: pearson-correlation-distance-computation
description: Use when you need a continuous cell ordering (pseudo-time) from a binary/transformed eeSNV matrix: Pearson correlation distance between cells feeds a minimum spanning tree that must recapitulate a primary-to-metastasis trajectory and expose subgroup ramifications.

name: pearson-correlation-distance-preservation-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a 2D embedding of high-dimensional single-cell (CyTOF/scRNA-seq) data retains global inter-cluster geometry, using manually annotated cell-population labels and centroid distance concordance.

name: pearson-correlation-feature-transformation
description: Use when preparing a scRNA-seq expression matrix (CSV) plus class labels for graph-embedding visualization with GraphDDP/graph_embed, after class filtering, normalization, and feature selection.

name: pearson-correlation-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have scPagwas per-cell gPAS scores for a GWAS trait and a normalized scRNA-seq matrix, and need to derive a ranked trait-relevant gene set (e.g., top 1,000 genes) for downstream enrichment or gene-set comparisons.

name: pearson-correlation-gene-selection
description: Use when imputing dropout-affected zero entries in an scRNA-seq expression matrix and you must choose which genes from a pre-defined gene subspace serve as regression predictors for a target gene.

name: pearson-correlation-grn-estimation
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-specific network inference method against dyngen's per-cell ground-truth regulatory networks and you need a simple correlation-differencing baseline (SSN) using Pearson correlation as the base estimator.

name: pearson-correlation-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when you have deep features from a trained DeepCC model and need to test whether features self-organize into biological groups (e.g., three groups mapping to CMS1 MSI, CMS3 metabolic, CMS4 EMT).

name: pearson-correlation-imputation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing gene imputation methods on paired observed/reference matrices (e.g. SERM vs MAGIC, SAVER, scVI on the cellular taxonomy dataset) and you need a quantitative accuracy score per sampling efficiency.

name: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation
description: Use when validating that a per-cell background/noise estimate (µ1) captures shared variance with isotype controls in CITE-seq ADT data, or when quantifying concordance of fitted parameters between alternative mixture-component definitions (k=2 vs k=3).

name: pearson-correlation-matrix-computation
description: Use when a supervised cell annotation pipeline must decide between model architectures based on cross-cell-type similarity, or when a K x K cell-type correlation matrix from averaged scRNA-seq expression profiles is required.

name: pearson-correlation-method-comparison
description: Use when multiple gene-set activity scoring methods (e.g. ORIGINS2 network activity, AUCell, mean expression) have been run on the same gene sets and you need to quantify their agreement with Pearson correlations and summary means.

name: pearson-correlation-of-count-matrices
description: Use when two raw gene-barcode count matrices produced by different scRNA-seq pipelines on the same FASTQ dataset must be compared numerically to validate that an alternative pipeline reproduces native-pipeline output.

name: pearson-correlation-of-per-protein-background-levels
description: Use when a CITE-seq (or ASAP-seq/TEA-seq) ADT dataset has both a raw empty-droplet matrix and a cell-containing matrix, and you need to verify that empty-droplet counts faithfully capture the ambient antibody background before using them for dsb step I correction.

name: pearson-correlation-of-perturbation-ranking-profiles
description: Use when comparing perturbation effect ranking lists produced under alternative MUSIC preprocessing settings (imputation on/off, Cell_filtering on/off) to measure ranking-list similarity and identify which strategy shifts the ranking most.

name: pearson-correlation-of-umi-counts
description: Use when two aligned gene-barcode matrices (same barcodes, zero-padded genes) from different processing pipelines must be quantitatively compared at the UMI-count level to assess processing concordance.

name: pearson-correlation-permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when building gene co-expression networks from RNA-Seq expression matrices where Pearson-correlation edges must be filtered for statistical significance before fusing with other similarity-based networks (e.g., Euclidean-distance networks).

name: pearson-correlation-protein-network-inference
description: Use when you need a plain co-expression/PCC baseline network on a protein-by-condition matrix (tsv/csv, e.g. HPA 566,109-cell scRNA-seq or PRIDE bulk proteomics) to benchmark against a learned method like FAVA.

name: pearson-correlation-scatter-visualization
description: Use when validating that clustering features (e.g., Spearman correlation features from sscClust) remain robust to subsampling fluctuations across multiple subsampling rates of an scRNA-seq dataset.

name: pearson-correlation-significance-testing
description: Use when you need to quantify and significance-test the association between two per-cell score vectors (e.g., AXL-high vs MITF-high program scores in scRNA-seq) and compare that association before vs after confounder correction.

name: pearson-correlation-similarity-assessment
description: Use when validating that computationally inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data reproduces the ground-truth cohort structure, by correlating per-condition cell-type proportion vectors and pathway activation scores between two cohorts.

name: pearson-correlation-stability-analysis
description: Use when a model has a stochastic component (e.g. random GAN initialization) and you must test whether an internal loss reliably predicts external alignment quality across repeated runs, via per-run Pearson correlations between loss and metric trajectories.

name: pearson-correlation-strategy-selection
description: Decision support for choosing NeuCA's annotation route when a labelled training scRNA-seq matrix is available: compute cross-cell-type correlations and check whether any off-diagonal element reaches tau = 0.95.

name: pearson-correlation-validation
description: Use when you have per-cell TCR-contribution scores from a trained mvTCR model plus TCRdist similarities per specificity group, and you must validate that TCR contribution quantitatively tracks TCR sequence similarity across epitope groups.

name: pearson-neighborhood-similarity-scoring
description: Use when you need to decide, cell by cell, whether a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) faithfully preserves pre-embedding neighborhood structure, or when optimizing hyperparameters like t-SNE perplexity by minimizing dubious embeddings.

name: pearson-residual-matrix-computation
description: Use when you have a raw scRNAseq count matrix and need the chi-squared residual matrix for CA dimension reduction, or when verifying a re-implementation of the corral_preproc count-to-residual pre-processing stage element-wise.

name: pedigree-kinship-matrix-preparation
description: Use when RNA-seq samples come from related individuals (family/pedigree cohort) and you want to model pairwise genetic relatedness as a covariance random effect, or to compare kinship vs non-kinship model fit via per-gene AIC.

name: penalized-cox-regression-survival-modeling
description: Use when predicting overall survival (time + censoring indicator) from thousands of genetic features per patient — e.g., Z-scored mRNA entries or mutated-gene matrices — and you need penalized Cox models with cross-validated prediction power.

name: penalized-lda-topic-model-fitting
description: Use when the goal is to decompose a scRNA-seq count matrix into latent topics whose topic-word probabilities and per-cell topic proportions yield biologically interpretable structure, via the penalized LDA model adapted from natural language processing.

name: penalized-likelihood-estimation
description: Use when you have a robust correlation/covariance matrix from single-cell gene expression data and need to distinguish direct gene-gene associations from indirect ones via a sparse concentration matrix estimate.

name: penalized-logistic-regression-variable-selection
description: Use when predicting a binary outcome (e.g., muscle-invasive vs non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer subtype) from thousands of genetic variables, and penalized regression with optional FDR screening is needed for variable selection and performance estimation.

name: penalized-probabilistic-estimation
description: Use when you have a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix and want an interpretable topic-model decomposition into latent biological functions with robust (penalized) estimation.

name: penalized-regression-competitor-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a high-dimensional regression method (e.g. SuffPCR) against feature-selecting penalized competitors on transcriptomic data where correlated features and small selected-feature counts matter.

name: penalized-spline-additive-model-edge-weighting
description: Use when you need data-driven weights for every directed edge of an input igraph network from RNA-seq-style expression data, as the first phase of CAT tree reconstruction in SEMtree(); trigger: fully connected or candidate digraph plus an n x p expression matrix.

name: peptide-mhc-binding-immunogenicity-prediction
description: Use when mutant peptides of length 8–11 aa derived from called SNVs, INDELs, or gene fusions must be scored for peptide-MHC binding and immunogenicity against patient HLA alleles to shortlist candidate neoantigens.

name: peptide-physicochemical-feature-calculation
description: Use when encoding transcript sequences for coding-potential prediction and putative peptide sequences translated from ORFs need to be converted into peptide-related numerical features (MW, pI, Gravy, instability index) for a classifier.

name: per-cell-annotation-accuracy-computation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq cell-type annotation tools (e.g. EasyCellType vs Garnett, scPred, SingleR) on simulated datasets with known ground-truth labels and you need per-cell accuracy tables.

name: per-cell-annotation-table-export
description: Use when an imported single-cell study needs standardized, ontology-resolved cell type labels per individual cell so that cross-study expression comparisons in Cellenium are semantically integratable.

name: per-cell-bam-processing
description: Use when starting from per-cell (barcode-split) BAM files from a 10x or non-10x scRNA-seq experiment and you need a per-cell normalized gene body coverage vector for SkewC quality/skewness analysis.

name: per-cell-correlation-evaluation-against-reference-matrix
description: Use when evaluating a single-cell long-read isoform quantification method against a matched gold-standard count matrix, e.g. Nanopore output vs PacBio IsoSeq truth for the same Jurkat 5' cDNA library.

name: per-cell-fusion-call-summarization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., K562 Smart-seq2, SRP291312) has been run through fusion detectors per cell and calls must be aggregated per cell per tool for benchmarking.

name: per-cell-genotype-matrix-quantification
description: Use when 10x Chromium single-cell BAMs aligned with cellranger must be genotyped at a pre-called somatic variant set (e.g. from eWGS tumor/normal) to assign variant evidence to individual cell barcodes.

name: per-cell-informativeness-scoring
description: Use when a cell-typed .h5ad single-cell dataset is too large for ML/DL training and you need a per-cell importance score before sketching, or want to rank ambiguous/atypical cells by OOB accuracy.

name: per-cell-kl-divergence-quantification
description: Use when you need a local, per-cell quality measure for a 2D embedding (t-SNE or UMAP) — e.g. to feed EMBEDR p-value estimation, compare DR algorithms, or tune perplexity/n_neighbors.

name: per-cell-optimal-neighborhood-scale-selection
description: Use when an EMBEDR perplexity (or n_neighbors) sweep has been fit on scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data and you want per-sample optimal scales, or a sample-wise optimal embedding, instead of a single global hyperparameter.

name: per-cell-pathogen-umi-quantification
description: Use when you have 10x scRNA-seq data from an infected sample for which cellranger count has already run against the host genome, and you need per-cell pathogen read and UMI counts appended to the 10x matrices for downstream single-cell analysis.

name: per-cell-prediction-table-generation
description: Use when scRNA-seq Seurat objects from tumor datasets (e.g. Massalha 2020, Peng 2019, Pelka 2021 liver/pancreatic/colon cohorts) need per-cell malignant classification and cell-of-origin labels compiled into one prediction table.

name: per-cell-qc-metrics-extraction
description: Use when two cellranger count runs on identical reads must be compared by per-cell QC summary statistics to quantify the effect of swapping the reference annotation (e.g. canonical vs. peaks2utr-augmented GFF3).

name: per-cell-regulator-activity-comparison-across-clusters
description: Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A + per-cell velocities) and need TF-level, per-cell activity scores to identify regulators whose influence varies across clusters, e.g. acinar vs transitioning vs duct-like populations.

name: per-cell-signature-score-visualization
description: Use when per-cell annotation or disease scores (e.g., LHSC_per_cell_score, Neoplastic_monocyte_per_cell_score) are stored in a Seurat object's metadata and you need to compare their spatial/UMAP distributions across biological conditions such as healthy vs AML or diagnosis vs relapse.

name: per-cell-tei-computation
description: Use when an AnnData scRNA-seq object and a gene-age orthomap (e.g. from OrthoFinder/oggmap) are available and you need gene age-weighted expression summaries such as per-cell or per-stage TEI to test developmental hourglass patterns.

name: per-cell-type-accuracy-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have cell-type label predictions for query datasets mapped onto a pre-trained reference (e.g., scCobra KNN label transfer on GSE114297/GSE85247/GSE83312 pancreas queries) and need a per-cell-type accuracy breakdown, such as reproducing the Fig. 6b-e ACC heatmap.

name: per-cell-type-auroc-evaluation
description: Use when you have a pretrained Miscell latent feature matrix (e.g. from PBMC scRNA-seq) with known cell-type labels and need to quantify how well those features separate 7 cell types via a linear probe.

name: per-cell-type-density-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells carry per-cell activity scores (from ORIGINS2 activity()) plus known cell-type labels, and you need density distributions per type to compare biological programs across clusters.

name: per-cell-type-doublet-proportion-quantification
description: Use when Chord (or another doublet caller) has output predicted doublet barcodes for annotated scRNA-seq samples and you need per-sample doublet rates and per-cell-type doublet proportions to identify doublet-enriched populations.

name: per-cell-type-isoform-quantification
description: Use when you have PacBio/ONT single-cell long-read fastq.gz files plus a barcode-to-cell-type assignment table (e.g. from Seurat short-read analysis) and need per-cell-type isoform, TSS, or polyA counts.

name: per-cell-type-mean-expression-computation
description: Use when you have a labeled scRNA-seq reference matrix (cells × genes with cell-type annotations) and need cell-type-level mean expression vectors to feed the E-test ΔS gene-selection statistic or a multinomial MLE classifier.

name: per-cell-type-scaled-expression-differential-analysis
description: Use when a gene metagene or embedding-derived gene program must be validated as cell-type-independent by comparing per-cell scaled expression of its member genes between conditions (e.g., stimulated vs control) within each annotated cell type.

name: per-cell-umi-count-statistical-testing
description: Use when two 10x scRNA-seq libraries must be compared for equal per-cell capture depth (genes/UMIs per cell), e.g. fresh vs cryopreserved PBMCs, after matching mean reads per cell by downsampling.

name: per-cell-viral-read-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-sample pathogen_al_counts.csv files from scPathoQuant runs over a multi-virus reference (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 + metapneumovirus) and need to aggregate per-cell counts into a per-virus infected-cell and read-abundance table.

name: per-class-f1-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking an annotation or classification model whose improvement is concentrated in minority classes, and aggregate metrics would hide the rare-class gains.

name: per-class-f1-score-computation
description: Use when you have predicted cell-type annotations from a tool like Census plus reference labels for the same cells and need per-class F1 scores, or need to test annotation robustness across embedding parameter grids.

name: per-class-f1-score-evaluation
description: Use when a multiclass or hierarchical cell-type classifier must be validated against labelled ground truth and reported per cell type, e.g. fivefold cross-validation on the pan-cancer training reference or the blood/stroma/cancer benchmark of Fig. 2c.

name: per-class-recall-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing classifiers trained on different gene feature spaces over the five PAM50 subtypes, and you need per-class (subtype) recalls, macro-averaged recall, and precision on a held-out test split rather than aggregate accuracy alone.

name: per-class-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when a CMS prediction (or any 4-class sample-subtype assignment) must be validated sample-by-sample against original reference labels on a held-out cohort and per-class sensitivity/specificity are required, not just a single accuracy figure.

name: per-cluster-interaction-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have pre-computed CCI datasets (e.g., CellPhoneDB output) for two or more conditions and want to identify cell clusters whose total interaction counts differ strikingly between conditions.

name: per-cluster-marker-ranking-by-ncdi
description: Use when analyzing a preprocessed Seurat object (e.g., Tyser 2021, 1195 cells) and the goal is cluster-specific binary markers — genes expressed exclusively in one cell population — rather than graded average-expression DE.

name: per-cluster-metric-aggregation
description: Use when a per-cell metric must be summarized per annotated cluster and globally to compare methods, e.g. local velocity inconsistency via mean cosine distance to k=30 neighbors across velocity methods.

name: per-cluster-metric-aggregation
description: Use when mapping a query single-cell dataset onto a Symphony reference and you need to detect query cell populations (clusters) that are absent from the reference, e.g. after holding out or ablating a cell type.

name: per-cluster-score-aggregation-and-thresholding
description: Use when a cell-by-cell-type score matrix (e.g. ScType es.max output on a clustered Seurat object) must be collapsed into one label per cluster, with a minimum-score threshold to flag unannotated clusters.

name: per-configuration-result-tabulation
description: Use when multiple segmentation configurations (e.g., loss-weight ablations) have been run and per-run metric values must be collected, tabulated, and compared against reference trends.

name: per-dataset-malignant-fraction-aggregation
description: Use when you have per-cell malignant-cell predictions from a scRNA-seq annotation model across many datasets and need to compare dataset-level malignant fractions against reference percentages (e.g., CancerSCEM database values).

name: per-donor-per-celltype-centroid-computation
description: Use when precomputing scTab data augmentation: per-cell-type, per-donor mean expression centroids must be derived from a size-factor-normalized, log1p CxG matrix to build donor-difference augmentation vectors.

name: per-factor-gene-count-aggregation
description: Use when a workflow must reproduce or audit the composition statistics of the E.PATH database — e.g. count unique gene sets, annotated modules, or genes assigned to each environmental factor from gs_genes/gs_info and annotations files.

name: per-gene-algorithm-dispatch-thresholding
description: Use when fitting NBGMMs with the nebula R package on multi-subject single-cell counts and you must decide, per gene, whether NEBULA-LN estimates suffice or NEBULA-HL re-estimation (full or partial, fixing phi) is required.

name: per-gene-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when RNA-seq count data include paired samples or repeated measures from the same donor/patient (e.g. a patientID variable) and per-gene differential expression with random effects and fit metrics like AIC is needed.

name: per-gene-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when raw pre-processed COSMIC v79 somatic coding mutation records must be converted into the paper's 37 ratio-metric, entropy and frequency features per gene/transcript for driver-gene classification.

name: per-gene-importance-aggregation-per-cell-type
description: Use when a trained scSHARP GCN model must be interpreted to identify which genes drive cell type classification, e.g. reproducing Figure 2 gene rankings for testis and PBMC cell types.

name: per-gene-linear-model-fitting
description: Use when you have a gene-by-sample count matrix plus sample metadata and need unpaired per-gene differential expression testing without random effects, kinship, or weights.

name: per-gene-marginal-distribution-comparison
description: Use when a marginally-resampled null data matrix has been generated from scRNA-seq counts and you must verify that each gene's empirical distribution is preserved before using the null for EMBEDR p-value estimation.

name: per-gene-off-fraction-quantification
description: Use when preparing base-level RNA-seq pileup data for cohort-wide shape-change analysis and you must define which genes are often 'not expressed' so they can be excluded from downstream SCISSOR analysis.

name: per-gene-zero-count-quantification
description: Use when validating ALRA imputation output: after thresholding the rank-k SVD approximation, to confirm that zeros at biologically non-expressed positions are retained and that technical (dropout) zeros have been imputed, on a per-gene basis.

name: per-grna-umi-threshold-estimation
description: Use when assigning CRISPR gRNAs to cells from UMI counts per cell barcode, when fixed UMI thresholds misclassify cells due to varying gRNA expression levels, or when discriminating ambient from endogenously expressed gRNAs.

name: per-label-error-and-f1-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two or more marker selection methods on labeled scRNA-seq data and you need per-label classification error and f1 metrics aggregated across all cell labels (e.g., 40 synthetic labels) rather than pooled accuracy.

name: per-lineage-pvalue-aggregation
description: Use when a common trajectory has been inferred across multiple conditions (e.g. with slingshot) and you need to test which lineages show differential progression — per-lineage pseudotime distribution shifts between conditions.

name: per-node-classifier-selection-svm
description: Use when constructing an scHPL hierarchical tree over aligned single-cell datasets and you must decide which classifier (linear SVM, kNN, or one-class SVM) to train per node, especially when unknown/new cell populations must be detectable via rejection.

name: per-nucleotide-folding-pattern-plotting
description: Use when analyzing CLASH/qCLASH hybrid RNA data in 'hyb' format that has a paired Vienna (or CT) predicted-structure file, and you need predicted miRNA/target folding patterns, per-nucleotide pairing, or binding-energy distributions.

name: per-nucleotide-shannon-entropy-mapping
description: Use when you have a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy list (two-column, tab-delimited, no header) and a pre-computed RNA secondary structure in CT or dot-bracket format, and need sliding-window structure-count maps.

name: per-patient-fusion-detection-rate-analysis
description: Use when a targeted fusion search has produced per-cell fusion calls across a multi-patient clinical cohort and you need per-patient recovery rates and cohort-level sensitivity to validate the calls.

name: per-patient-virus-detection-tabulation
description: Use when scPathoQuant has been run with a multi-virus reference fasta (up to 2 entries) on 10x cellranger count outputs and you must tabulate which viruses were detected per patient, with per-virus infected-cell counts and read abundances.

name: per-plate-linear-model-swapping-fraction-estimation
description: Use when quantifying sample-mislabelling (barcode swapping) rates in plate-based scRNA-seq libraries where the same or paired libraries were sequenced on both a non-patterned (HiSeq 2500) and a patterned flow-cell machine (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq).

name: per-protein-pearson-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a reference-mapping workflow predicts per-cell protein or other modal annotations from mRNA-only query cells and you need a quantitative per-feature accuracy metric against measured values.

name: per-protein-summary-statistics-across-droplet-populations
description: Use when you have a CITE-seq ADT count matrix split into empty (background) and cell-containing droplets and need to quantify or validate that per-protein ambient background levels are shared between the two populations.

name: per-read-modification-aggregation-to-genome-space
description: Use when NanoSpeech basecalled fasta/q read headers carry per-modification base indexes and you need per-read BED plus genome-space aggregated modification calls (counts, depth, frequency) for a reference transcriptome or genome.

name: per-read-modification-coordinate-extraction-from-bam
description: Use when NanoSpeech basecalled dRNA pod5/fast5 reads into fasta/fastq whose headers embed indexes of candidate modified nucleotides (e.g. inosines), and you need per-read and transcriptome-space modification coordinates to score calls against known modification positions.

name: per-sample-aberration-classification
description: Use when SCISSOR shape-change calls (per-sample GSC/LSC sample IDs) must be validated against an external mutation repository such as a TCGA MAF to label each call as a known or previously unrecognized aberration.

name: per-sample-count-matrix-merging
description: Use when per-sample RiboSeq alignments (BAM) exist and a single merged count matrix, one column per sample indexed by transcript/gene ID, is needed as input to DESeq2 differential expression analysis.

name: per-sample-dmdt-table-parsing
description: Use when a task requires computing the fraction of disease samples exhibiting a specific isoform switch (e.g. HSPH1-001 vs HSPH1-002) from CanIsoNet's per-sample dMDT tables with expression values, rather than gene-level summary statistics.

name: per-sample-outlier-detection
description: Use when per-cell SenePy hub scores must be summarized per biological sample and tested between disease groups, or when individual samples may distort group-level senescence comparisons.

name: per-sample-read-count-matrix-merging
description: Use when COMPSRA annotation has produced per-sample read-count files for multiple FASTQ inputs and you need a single merged RNA-molecule × sample count matrix (e.g., 12 serum samples × 6 RNA classes).

name: per-spot-module-expression-scoring
description: Use when you have a merged, edge-pruned SCING GRN divided into leiden subnetworks and need quantitative module activity scores per spatial spot or cell to support regional-specificity tests, clustering, or phenotype/plaque correlation analyses.

name: per-stage-expression-index-aggregation
description: Use when a per-cell gene age-weighted or gene-bin-weighted expression index has already been computed on a Scanpy AnnData object and the goal is to summarize it per developmental stage or cell-type group.

name: per-tissue-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when validating a pre-trained malignant-cell classifier (e.g. Cancer-Finder checkpoints/sc_pretrain_article.pkl) against per-cell malignancy labels from TISCH across multiple tissues, needing per-tissue and weighted-average accuracy.

name: per-tissue-allele-ratio-comparison
description: Use when ASE variant calls are available for multiple tissues and you need to quantify reference-allele mapping bias, or to validate that masking a reference genome with called variants reduces inflated reference allele ratios toward 50%.

name: per-tissue-ase-variant-counting
description: Use when you have per-tissue filtered biallelic SNP VCFs and need to quantify how many SNPs show allele-specific expression and what fraction of informative SNPs this represents.

name: per-tissue-informative-snp-identification
description: Use when you have per-tissue RNA-seq VCF files (e.g., GATK HaplotypeCaller g.vcf-derived) and need to count or extract biallelic SNPs eligible for binomial-test ASE analysis before running the ASE testing stage.

name: percent-spliced-read-droplet-classification
description: Use when filtering snRNA-seq droplets and you need to label retained or removed droplets as nuclear or background (e.g., to validate DIEM, EmptyDrops, or quantile filtering) using per-droplet spliced-read fractions.

name: percent-spliced-read-quality-assessment
description: Use when evaluating snRNA-seq droplet filtering on fresh/frozen nucleus data — e.g., to check what fraction of droplets removed by a hard count or quantile cutoff are truly background, using percent spliced reads as a nuclear-content proxy.

name: percent-spliced-reads-per-cluster-summary
description: Use when you have a droplet-filtered snRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., quantile-threshold-filtered) and need to test whether background RNA-driven debris clusters persist in downstream Seurat clustering.

name: percentile-based-maximum-estimation
description: Use when preprocessing a gene-expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cell populations) for ICELLNET ligand-receptor scoring and highly expressed molecules could otherwise dominate the communication score.

name: percentile-cutoff-embedding-classification
description: Use when per-cell 2D-embedding neighbor distances (original and gene-permuted data) and pre-embedding (PCA) distances are available and each cell must be labeled dubious/trustworthy/intermediate, e.g. for t-SNE perplexity or UMAP min.dist/n_neighbors optimization.

name: percentile-threshold-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you need to test how RSCanner's user-defined BPC percentile cutoff (raised from 0.25 to 0.75) and Shannon Entropy percentile cutoff (lowered from 0.75 to 0.25) change which nucleotide positions are called as structure counts in a CT or dot-bracket structure analysis.

name: percentile-threshold-suppression
description: Use when converting a LogNormalized single-cell gene expression matrix into a cell-type score matrix with MASI's gene2cell/PlinerScore, and low-level marker expression must be zeroed before summing weighted markers per cell type.

name: performance-gain-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have before/after F1 scores from a self-training (pseudo-labelling) experiment across multiple annotation methods and want to test whether the improvement correlates with baseline performance.

name: performance-gain-matrix-aggregation
description: Use when many inferred GRNs (one per cell type) have each been scored with a random-walk disease-subnetwork framework and you must aggregate gains into a cell-type-by-disease matrix for benchmarking methods like SCING vs GRNBOOST2, ppcor, PIDC.

name: performance-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when comparing automatic cell-type identification methods across tissues/datasets and the per-method, per-tissue metrics (accuracy, F1-score, unlabeling rate) from self-projection cross-validation need to be summarized as a comparable heatmap.

name: performance-index-computation
description: Use when benchmarking marker-gene detection methods on a labeled expression matrix (e.g. GSE28490) and you need a single quantitative quality score (P1) per method, compared against a known a priori marker-gene subset.

name: perl-script-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a sorted SAM file or umi_positions.txt from a UMI-tagged RNA-Seq run must be deduplicated, with reads sharing a UMI mapping within 3 bp grouped into UMI-read clusters and counted per position or per gene.

name: perl-single-cell-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a split barcoded 10X BAM set (one BAM per cell barcode) must be converted into per-cell gene body coverage profiles under SkewC, using either hg38 (Gencode V28) or mm10 (Gencode VM18) references.

name: permutation-based-empirical-pvalue-assessment
description: Use when mapping cis-sQTLs on transcript-ratio phenotypes and you need FDR-controlled significance calls — i.e., after a nominal pass you require permutation-calibrated empirical P-values at a target FDR such as 0.05.

name: permutation-based-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have pre-computed CCI datasets from two or more conditions (e.g., critical and moderate COVID-19) and need to call functional terms significant based on condition-unique ligand-receptor int-pairs.

name: permutation-based-fdr-estimation
description: Use when a SingleCellGGM GGM object has been constructed from a single-cell count matrix and edges need significance assessment or false discovery rate control before network clustering.

name: permutation-based-fdr-estimation
description: Use when testing many overlapping gene sets from summary-statistics-based enrichment (e.g., iDEA on scRNA-seq DE z-scores) and you need calibrated FDR estimates rather than naive p-value thresholds that ignore gene set non-independence.

name: permutation-based-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a trained topic model (e.g. 100-topic scETM) needs biological interpretation of its topics via GSEA of per-topic ranked gene lists against pathway databases such as MSigDB Canonical Pathways or PsyGeNET.

name: permutation-based-interaction-significance-testing
description: Use when inferring cell-cell communication from clustered scRNA-seq data and you need to call which ligand-receptor pairs are statistically significant rather than merely enriched or co-expressed.

name: permutation-based-likelihood-ratio-testing
description: Use when multi-sample scRNA-seq data with pseudotime and a design matrix require testing whether gene expression dynamics differ by a sample covariate (e.g., sex, disease severity) with controlled FDR.

name: permutation-based-pc-number-selection
description: Use when a scRNAseq pipeline needs to decide how many PCs to retain before clustering, and the choice must be justified by a shuffled-data null instead of an arbitrary elbow/scree cutoff.

name: permutation-based-signature-thresholding
description: Use when merging multiple cell-type-specific senescence hub signatures (e.g., all human or mouse hubs in hubs.metadata) into a universal signature and you need an automatic, statistically grounded overlap_threshold instead of hand-picking one.

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when you must test whether gene signatures (e.g., age-dynamic senescence genes in a cell type) exceed what null label permutations would produce, or set a data-driven overlap cutoff when merging SenePy hubs.

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when you need to test which scETM-learned topics are differentially abundant between labeled cell groups (e.g., AD vs control, suicidal vs healthy, or across cell types) and require nonparametric p-values with multiple-testing control.

name: permutation-based-significance-testing
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference methods (e.g., SCING, GRNBOOST2, PIDC, ppcor) on Perturb-seq data where significant downstream targets of guides must be identified to compute AUROC and TPR at FPR 0.05.
