name: permutation-based-significance-testing-of-hidden-factors
description: Use when running IA-SVA (or validating a reimplementation) on scRNA-seq read counts and you must decide whether an extracted PC1/SV is significant, or how many hidden factors (SVs) to retain via the significance index (SI).

name: permutation-based-threshold-calculation
description: Use when merging multiple SenePy senescence signatures (e.g., all mouse or human cell-type hubs) into a universal signature and you need an automatic, statistically grounded overlap threshold instead of an arbitrary overlap_threshold count.

name: permutation-based-topology-testing
description: Use when single-cell data from multiple conditions must be fitted to trajectories and you must decide, as Step 1 of the condiments workflow, whether trajectories differ fundamentally between conditions (differential topology).

name: permutation-control-statistics
description: Use when evaluating whether BIRD-predicted DNase I hypersensitivity correlations in held-out cell types reflect real expression–accessibility coupling, by benchmarking prediction-truth rL and rC against permuted-model controls.

name: permutation-enrichment-testing
description: Use when a set of significant events (e.g., ASAS SNPs at FDR <= 10%) needs to be tested for enrichment of overlap with an external annotation (e.g., GWAS catalog SNPs) against a matched random null.

name: permutation-matrix-optimization
description: Use when a weighted cluster interlacement graph (CI-graph) of cell-type spatial relationships and a color-difference target matrix (CD-graph) must be matched to assign contrasting colors to neighboring cell types.

name: permutation-null-count-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking co-expression estimators or p-value calibration on scRNA-seq data: you need null UMI count matrices with realistic depth variation but zero true co-expression, e.g. to reproduce bias curves or type-I error Q-Q plots.

name: permutation-null-distribution-analysis
description: Use when testing whether two transcriptome region sets (e.g., m6A RNA methylation sites and stop codon regions) colocalize more than expected by chance, especially when region-to-isoform association is ambiguous.

name: permutation-null-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when you must demonstrate that an observed cell-to-cell similarity/distance metric (e.g., ACTIONet JSD similarity) exceeds random expectation, by comparing it against a label-permuted null and a competing baseline metric (e.g., Euclidean distance on HVG+PCA coordinates).

name: permutation-null-significance-testing
description: Use when detected network modules (e.g. fRNC global/local RNCs from ESCA TCGA data) must be validated against a random null to confirm their scores significantly exceed chance at the detection FDR threshold (1e-5).

name: permutation-null-zscore-statistics
description: Use when you need to quantify whether colocalization between two transcriptome region sets (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A sites and stop codon regions) is statistically significant, via a permutation-derived null distribution, p-value, z-score and shifted z-score.

name: permutation-result-visualization
description: Use when a permutation test from RgnTX (permTestTx, permTestTx_customPick, or permTestTxIA_customPick) has produced a null overlap distribution and you need to plot observed vs. random overlaps, p-values, or z-scores for a transcriptome colocalization result.

name: permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when a NeuronChat run on scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics must identify which sender–receiver communication links are significant (p < 0.05) before aggregating networks, ranking interactions, or comparing conditions.

name: permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when you must attach an empirical significance level to an entropy- or potency-derived statistic — e.g. testing whether a bulk-sample signalling entropy (SR) significantly exceeds a matched single-cell SR distribution — without assuming a parametric null.

name: permutation-significance-testing-of-communication-links
description: Use when inferred ligand-receptor communication networks from scRNA-seq (NeuronChat objects) must be filtered for statistical significance, or when assessing stability of significant-link calls across permutation counts.

name: permutation-stability-comparison-analysis
description: Use when running NeuronChat's run_NeuronChat permutation test and you must verify that significance calls at a modest M (e.g., 100) are stable and consistent with a large-M reference run (e.g., 1000).

name: permutation-test-group-label-shuffling
description: Use when filtering inferred ligand-receptor interactions in scRNA-seq cell-cell communication analysis, i.e., after computing communication probabilities and needing a nonparametric null model to call interactions significant at p < 0.05.

name: permutation-testing-of-cell-group-interactions
description: Use when you have a CellChat object with overexpressed signaling genes across cell groups and need to determine which predicted ligand-receptor interactions are statistically significant rather than chance-level.

name: permutation-testing-of-clonal-state-enrichment
description: Use when single-cell time-course data has CellTag lineage barcodes and a fate label (e.g. Capybara-assigned iEP conversion), and you must split cells at an intermediate time point into clone groups enriched or depleted for successful fate conversion.

name: perplexity-based-k-selection
description: Use when deconvolving multi-cellular pixel-resolution spatial transcriptomics data with STdeconvolve and an appropriate number of cell types K must be set a priori for the LDA model.

name: persister-cell-gene-annotation
description: Use when a scorecard run on antibiotic-exposed bacterial biofilm transcriptomics (e.g. VAN comparisons yielding Q3 down-regulated SAUSA300 entries) needs gene-level functional interpretation as persistence or survival strategies.

name: personalized-differential-coexpression-analysis
description: Use when the goal is to find driver nodes/genes specific to individual patients from matched tumor-normal RNA-seq matrices (e.g., TCGA), and to assess patient-level tumor heterogeneity via driver-gene recurrence frequencies.

name: personalized-genome-alignment-with-star
description: Use when detecting allele-specific alternative splicing (ASAS) from RNA-seq fastq data and reads must be assigned to alleles via alignment to haplotype-modified personal genomes rather than a generic reference.

name: perturb-seq-bam-processing-with-snakemake
description: Use when starting from raw 3'-end tag-based scRNA-seq or Perturb-seq BAM files (10x-style chemistries) and you need 3'UTR isoform-resolved counts rather than gene counts, as the first step before pseudobulk aggregation and zdWUI testing.

name: perturb-seq-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw Perturb-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO accessions GSE90063 or GSE153056) must be converted into preprocessed inputs for GRN inference, or when benchmarking methods like SCING, GRNBOOST2, PIDC, or ppcor on perturbation-target prediction.

name: perturb-seq-guide-free-cell-selection
description: Use when a Perturb-seq/CRISPRi dataset needs guide-unassigned cells as a null cell population for evaluating null P-value calibration of single-cell DE methods.

name: perturb-seq-two-cluster-simulation
description: Use when you need a controlled two-cluster Perturb-seq benchmark with known true cellular response to evaluate whether a decoupling method beats naive fold-change estimation under infected proportion bias.

name: perturbation-benchmark-pipeline-execution
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or re-run a method-ranking benchmark that scores how well decoupleR methods recover experimentally perturbed TFs/kinases from perturbation experiments, or to run the associated network-noise robustness analysis.

name: perturbation-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing cell-state clustering methods on single-cell perturbation data (e.g. drug-treated vs control, IFN-beta stimulated PBMCs) where cluster quality must be quantified against ground-truth labels and mixing metrics.

name: perturbation-control-validation
description: Use when a generative trajectory model supports in silico gene perturbations and you must verify that perturbing known fate-regulating TFs moves lineage fractions in the expected direction while non-TF controls do not.

name: perturbation-correlation-analysis
description: Use when Perturb-seq/CROP-seq expression data plus perturbation labels (control labeled 'CTRL') have been topic-modeled with MUSIC and you need to quantify how two gene knockouts (e.g., Cebpb vs Rela) relate.

name: perturbation-effect-interpretation-in-til-subtypes
description: Use when comparing a perturbed scRNA-seq condition (e.g., Regnase-1-null vs WT CD8+ TILs) against a control to distinguish changes in cell-state abundance from subtype-specific gene-program deviations.

name: perturbation-effect-prioritization
description: Use when the input is a gene expression profile plus per-cell perturbation assignment (control cells labeled 'CTRL') and the goal is to rank perturbations and quantify their relationships at single-cell granularity.

name: perturbation-gene-ranking-evaluation
description: Use when comparing perturbation-effect estimators (scDecouple vs OC) on scCRISPR-seq data by measuring gene-ranking gains for TCR/pathway-related genes and enrichment significance.

name: perturbation-marker-stability-assessment
description: Use when a completed ICAT run (ICAT-upweighted matrix in adata.obsm['X_icat'], ICAT-weighted gene list, control vs perturbed labels) must be checked for marker-gene differential expression between treatments.

name: perturbation-prediction-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating perturbation-prediction accuracy of multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq methods on held-out conditions or batches, using cell-type-specific MSE, Pearson correlation, and R2 metrics.

name: perturbation-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how well regulator (TF or kinase) activity inference methods recover perturbed regulators from transcriptomic or phospho-proteomic perturbation data, or when statistically comparing method variants such as weighted vs unweighted scoring.

name: perturbation-response-auroc-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a single-cell TF perturbation dataset with true perturbation labels and a TF regulatory prior (e.g., DoRothEA), and need to quantify and compare how well activity-inference methods recover perturbation status via AUROC.

name: perturbation-response-error-comparison
description: Use when you must quantitatively compare perturbation-effect estimation methods (e.

name: perturbation-response-prediction
description: Use when you need to predict stimulated/perturbed single-cell expression profiles from unpaired control scRNA-seq data (e.g., PT_PBMC) and evaluate predictions per cell type against ground-truth DEGs.

name: perturbation-response-signature-scoring
description: Use when bulk or single-cell normalized gene-expression data (e.g. DESeq2 size-factor-normalized or variance-stabilized counts) should be converted into per-sample pathway activity scores for signaling pathways like MAPK, NFkB, PI3K, or TGFb.

name: perturbation-simulated-data-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare cell-state clustering methods on single-cell perturbation data where ground-truth population labels exist (real or simulated), especially under varying perturbation severity, marker-gene signal, or cell type proportions.

name: perturbation-transition-visualization-vector-field
description: Use when you have CellOracle Oracle objects with simulated KO or overexpression perturbations and need to visualize predicted cell-state transitions (e.g., early-transition vs. reprogrammed clusters) on an embedding.

name: perturbation-zero-expression-rate-quantification
description: Use when auditing MUSIC-style single-cell CRISPR screening pipelines: before or after the perturbation-filtering step, to identify which perturbations (e.

name: perturbed-cell-filtering-and-invalid-edit-removal
description: Use when preprocessing pooled CRISPR screening + scRNA-seq data (e.g. crop_stimulated Perturb-seq input) before topic modeling, to remove perturbed cells whose DE profile resembles controls and perturbations with too few remaining cells.

name: pfam-domain-domain-interaction-annotation
description: Use when a transcript isoform switching event must be characterized at the interaction level — specifically when deciding which of a transcript's STRING edges are physical, domain-mediated interactions disrupted by the switch.

name: pfam-domain-identifier-mapping
description: Use when building isoform-interaction or dMDT-based networks where transcript isoform switching loses Pfam domains, and you must connect Pfam DDI pairs to gene-level PPI networks to flag disrupted interactions.

name: phage-contaminant-removal
description: Use when preparing RNA-seq FASTQ input for viRNAtrap or similar viral-read detection: TCGA BAM files must be stripped of human (hg19) alignments and phiX phage contaminant reads before viral prediction.

name: pharmacogenomic-drug-response-model-training
description: Use when bulk drug response models must be trained or applied on GDSC/PRISM screening data with CCLE expression kernel features, e.g. reproducing cross-database correlation or scoring cluster-wise IC50/AUC predictions.

name: pharmacogenomics-ic50-response-classification
description: Use when raw drug IC50 values from a pharmacogenomics dataset (e.g., GDSC1000 cell-line panel) must be binned into sensitive/resistant/null classes per cell line before computing regimen coverage or selecting combination partners.

name: pharmacotranscriptomic-score-validation
description: Use when a computed reversal/ranking score for drug perturbation signatures must be checked against an external efficacy ground truth (IC50) before it is trusted for in silico drug candidate selection.

name: phase-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating a circadian phase inference method (e.g. Tempo) on simulated scRNA-seq data with known true phases, to quantify within-3h phase accuracy and test whether de novo cyclers improve point estimates.

name: phase-classification-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when scRNA-seq or qPCR single-cell data have Hoechst-based (or similar experimental) cell-cycle phase labels and you need to score and compare cell-cycle classification accuracy of competing pseudo-time methods.

name: phase-fraction-benchmarking-against-flow-cytometry
description: Use when a scRNA-seq cell cycle phase assignment (e.g. from DeepCycle cell_cycle_theta) needs independent validation against flow cytometry phase fractions, or when reproducing the paper's mESC (~19%/40%/41%) and fibroblast (~76%/15%/9%) phase proportion benchmarks.

name: phase-i-dlt-rate-estimation
description: Use when dose-escalation decisions in a phase I/II trial require per-dose DLT probability estimates that are guaranteed monotonically non-decreasing across dose levels, from raw cohort DLT counts.

name: phase-i-ii-dose-finding-simulation
description: Use when simulating a phase I/II trial with binary toxicity and efficacy outcomes to identify an optimal biological dose (OBD) for immunotherapy, or when benchmarking dose-finding designs on OBD selection and patient-allocation percentages.

name: phase-i-ii-operating-characteristics-evaluation
description: Use when reproducing or extending TSNP operating characteristics: you have scenario definitions with true joint toxicity-efficacy probabilities and need per-scenario OBD selection rates at multiple maximum sample sizes.

name: phase-i-ii-trial-design-implementation
description: Use when reproducing or executing a phase I/II immunotherapy dose-finding trial with the TSNP design — e.g., a hypothetical trial with J=5 doses, phi=0.3, max sample size 30, m=6 — to obtain per-dose utilities and a final OBD.

name: phase-portrait-co-expression-interpretation
description: Use when validating RNA velocity or TF-based gene dynamics fits: after running scVelo/TFvelo on scRNA-seq (e.g., E15.5 mouse pancreas), check phase portraits of -fitted genes for the clockwise TF–target traversal that evidences regulation.

name: phase-portrait-fitting-of-spliced-unspliced-rna
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data with both spliced and unspliced count layers (AnnData) to infer RNA velocity and cell-fate trajectories on multi-branching differentiation without labeling metadata.

name: phase-portrait-fitting-quality-evaluation
description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on the same scRNA-seq dataset and needing a quantitative, gene-level measure of phase portrait fit quality (e.g., reproducing Fig. 2d-g or benchmarking TFvelo against scVelo/Dynamo/UniTVelo/cellDancer).

name: phase-portrait-fitting-visualization
description: Use when you need to validate that a gene-regulation-based RNA velocity method fits gene dynamics correctly by inspecting phase portraits (TF representation vs. target) and UMAP pseudotime/streamplots, especially on multi-omics or scRNA-seq datasets.

name: phase-score-based-phasing-analysis
description: Use when small-RNA sequencing reads (19–25 nt) should be scanned for phased siRNA-producing loci (PHAS genes) against a reference transcriptome, genome, or full-length transcriptome, especially to recover phasiRNAs that only the phase score method detects.

name: phase-score-calculation
description: Use when detecting phased siRNA (phasiRNA) clusters/PHAS loci from sRNA-seq reads mapped to a transcriptome or genome and you need a combined phase-score + hypergeometric detection with bidirectional search.

name: phased-genotype-error-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking allele-specific CNA callers on scWGS data requires ground-truth simulations that preserve haplotype structure and phasing accuracy, e.g., testing sensitivity to 200 kb–5 Mb CNAs under controlled phase-switch error rates.

name: phased-heterozygous-snp-baf-estimation
description: Use when scWGS analysis requires allele-specific copy-number states or BAF-based validation, and you have single-cell BAMs plus a matched bulk WGS sample per individual to source and phase gHETs.

name: phased-sirna-loci-deduplication-and-merging
description: Use when phasiRNA prediction (phase module) outputs exist from mappings to more than one reference sequence — e.g. a cDNA map and a gDNA map — and clusters in different coordinate systems must be reconciled into one unified PHAS locus set.

name: phased-sirna-loci-prediction
description: Use when sRNA-seq reads (19–25 nt, e.g. rice SRR5049781) must be scanned for phased 21-nt siRNA stacks and PHAS loci, especially when genome- and transcriptome-based predictions should be combined to catch alternative-splicing or novel unannotated loci.

name: phased-sirna-prediction-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of phasiRNA/phased siRNA prediction tools, or when deciding whether PhasiHunter's parallel (-j) mode is needed for large genome-based 21-nt phasiRNA prediction workloads.

name: phasirna-cluster-integration
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads are already mapped to a reference (transcriptome and/or genome) and you need to call 21-nt or 24-nt phased siRNA loci and integrate multi-reference predictions into gene-level PHAS sets.

name: phasirna-cluster-integration-across-reference-sequences
description: Use when separate PhasiHunter phase runs on gDNA and cDNA (or full-length transcriptome) references have produced phase_o.txt and phase_a.txt outputs and the clusters must be merged into a single genome-annotated result set.

name: phasirna-phas-loci-prediction
description: Use when sRNA-seq libraries (e.g. 19–25 nt reads) need phased siRNA/PHAS locus prediction against one or more reference sequences (transcriptome and/or genome), or when comparing reference-based phasiRNA predictions.

name: phate-diffusion-embedding
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., a Seurat object carrying Louvain cluster assignments and PCA/UMAP reductions) needs a diffusion-based, trajectory-friendly embedding to support Slingshot trajectory inference and pseudotime visualization.

name: phemd-pipeline-execution-with-monocle-preprocessing
description: Use when benchmarking sample-level single-cell distance methods on multi-sample scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., .h5ad patient cohorts) and you need the PhEMD baseline with its required Monocle 2 preprocessing and measured runtime.

name: phenograph-clustering-ari-assessment
description: Use when 2D embeddings of preprocessed CyTOF data (arcsinh X/5, MinMaxScaler to [0,1]) must be partitioned into cell populations and quantitatively compared to manual gating labels via ARI, e.g. benchmarking dimensionality-reduction quality on BMMC/Samusik.

name: phenotype-cover-marker-selection
description: Use when you must select a small global feature/gene set that jointly distinguishes every pair of phenotypes (e.g., cell type × tissue combinations) from a phenotype × gene score matrix, where per-group DE genes overlap and pairwise discrimination matters.

name: phenotype-cover-optimization
description: Use when marker selection must produce a single global feature set that discriminates between many overlapping phenotypes (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in IPF, mouse cortex, or HCA scRNA-seq data), not just per-group DE genes.

name: phenotype-pair-coverage-scoring
description: Use when you need to select a global biomarker set that discriminates every phenotype pair in a phenotype x feature score matrix, or when scoring a gene set by the phenotype-pair coverage it attains (e.g., CEM-PC with I=500 iterations, Rs=1000 elite samples).

name: phenotype-prediction-f1-scoring
description: Use when you have cell embeddings (GRN module AUCell scores or batch-corrected PCs) plus cell-level phenotype labels and need a quantitative readout of biological signal retention, e.g., reproducing Figure S6-style embedding comparisons.

name: phenotypic-manifold-constraint-sampling
description: Use when fitting scKINETICS to single-cell transcriptomic data and a prior constraining cells' future states along the phenotypic manifold is needed to regularize the EM-learned gene regulatory network and velocities.

name: phosphoproteomics-perturbation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating which decoupleR methods recover perturbed kinases (regulators) from phospho-proteomics perturbation data, or when comparing phospho-proteomics method rankings against transcriptomics rankings.

name: phylogenetic-autocorrelation-analysis
description: Use when you have matched single-cell expression data and a reconstructed lineage tree and need to test whether user-defined gene signatures are heritable, i.e. associated with phylogenetic structure.

name: phylogenetic-node-completeness-scoring
description: Use when OrthoFinder rooted gene trees and an of2orthomap-derived orthomap (with LCA gene age classes) are available for a focal species such as Danio rerio, and you need per-orthogroup completeness along the lineage to flag low-continuity, HGT-suspect orthogroups.

name: phylogenetic-taxon-read-counting
description: Use when you have small RNA-seq reads that failed to map to the human genome (e.g. STAR *_Aligned_UnMapped.bam) and need microbial species-level read counts per taxon.

name: phylogenetic-tree-based-population-modeling
description: Use when simulating single-cell RNA-seq data for multiple discrete populations or continuous trajectories whose relationships should follow a lineage/phylogenetic tree, and you need to validate that the simulated heterogeneity (Sigma) preserves tree structure in low-dimensional embeddings.

name: phylogenetic-tree-breadth-first-clustering
description: Use when you have a single-cell lineage tree (Newick/phylo with cells as leaves) and need to partition tip cells into a fixed number of subpopulations that each correspond to a clade of the reconstructed phylogeny.

name: phylogenetic-tree-manipulation-in-r
description: Use when a reconstructed lineage or phylogenetic tree (e.g., Newick format from LinRace) must be partitioned at a specified depth and tip-level annotations (e.g., 34 cell types over 9707 mouse embryo cells) summarized per subtree in R.

name: phylogenetic-tree-topology-comparison
description: Use when several lineage or phylogenetic trees have been reconstructed from the same cell set (e.g., competing lineage-reconstruction methods) and you need to compare their local resolution via maximum root-to-tip depth and internal-node counts.

name: phylogenetic-tree-traversal-and-subtree-analysis
description: Use when a rooted phylogeny with cells as leaves must be traversed subtree-by-subtree (e.g., to compute per-cell plasticity of categorical meta-data such as GEO GSM4905334 annotations), or when per-leaf summaries require averaging node-level statistics along root-to-leaf paths.

name: phylogenetic-tree-visualization
description: Use when a single-cell lineage-tracing dataset has a reconstructed phylogeny (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 lineage trees from Cassiopeia) that must be interactively browsed, selected, and overlaid with UMAP/tSNE projections and metadata in a shareable web report.

name: phylogeny-preprocessing-and-pruning
description: Use when a single-cell phylogeny and an expression matrix must be reconciled before lineage-aware analysis — e.g., cells present in one modality but not the other, unifurcations in the tree, or raw UMI counts needing normalization.

name: pileup-based-snv-allele-frequency-extraction
description: Use when you have mapped RNA-seq reads (BAM) and need a genome-wide BAF/allelic-shift profile at germline SNP sites to support CNV or LOH inference, without a matched DNA variant call set.

name: pileup-nucleotide-frequency-normalization
description: Use when tabix-indexed REDItools outTables must be converted into per-site 8×101 feature matrices of reference-base one-hot and log2-normalized RNAseq pileup frequencies to feed REDInet or an equivalent TCN classifier.

name: pipeline-count-validation-against-reference
description: Use when reproducing a published pipeline (e.g., iwa-miRNA on maize B73) and you must confirm that intermediate counts (619 aggregated, 1241 predicted, 588/704 selected, 886 total) equal reported values.

name: pipeline-parameter-matching-across-tools
description: Use when comparing runtime or performance of two small RNA-seq analysis pipelines and you need a controlled benchmark: same FASTQ inputs, same parameters, same server resources (e.g. 30 GB RAM).

name: pipeline-resource-consumption-profiling
description: Use when comparing de-goulash's deconvolution accuracy and runtime/memory cost against ScSplit, Souporcell, and Vireo on the same in silico 2-person or 9-person scRNA-seq mixtures with known donor labels.

name: pipeline-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when two pipelines claim performance differences on the same data type and you need a fair head-to-head runtime comparison on a fixed FASTQ subset with identical references and comparable settings.

name: pipeline-runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing barcode pre-processing pipelines on identical input FASTQ data and you need wall-clock runtime, peak memory, and barcode-detection/correlation concordance metrics.

name: piscem-index-building
description: Use when you need to create a searchable reference index for alevin-fry/scRNA-seq quantification from a reference genome FASTA plus GTF annotation, e.g. preparing a splici reference for later `simpleaf quant` runs.

name: plant-cistarget-database-configuration
description: Use when building plant cell-type-specific GRNs with scPlant/pySCENIC from an annotated Seurat object and you need to obtain or build the required cisTarget databases and aux bundle before running GRN inference.

name: plant-go-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when clusters from a plant scRNA-seq atlas contain cells with unknown marker genes and you need GO-based functional annotation, or when you must test whether an unannotated cluster resembles a known cell type via functional similarity.

name: plant-microrna-precursor-prediction
description: Use when you need a genome-wide list of miRNA precursor candidates for a plant species with a reference genome, combining public annotations with novel predictions from small RNA sequencing (sRNA-Seq) data.

name: plant-pathogen-comparative-genomics
description: Use when you have a quality-filtered pan-genome set with gene-cluster absence/presence data and want to map reference gene families (e.g. secretion-system genes) across strains to test lifestyle-associated distribution patterns.

name: plant-pathogen-lifestyle-metadata-integration
description: Use when a binary GCF presence/absence matrix (e.g., from BiG-SCAPE at 0.70 distance) must be tested for statistical enrichment against per-genome lifestyle labels to find lifestyle-associated biosynthetic clusters.

name: plant-single-cell-data-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when you have a preprocessed plant Seurat object (e.g. Arabidopsis root cells) and need to infer and visualize developmental trajectories/pseudotime, especially to compare consistency across multiple trajectory tools.

name: plant-single-cell-reference-preparation
description: Use when a bulk RNA-seq deconvolution task in plants needs a cell-type-resolved scRNA-seq reference: an annotated single-cell dataset (e.g. Arabidopsis root Seurat object) must be processed and its labels/marker genes readied before running decomposeBulk.

name: plant-single-cell-transcriptomics-workflow-execution
description: Use when a plant scRNA-seq Seurat object must be run through a reproducible Nextflow-based GRN pipeline (MINI-EX) and its cell-type-specific regulons compared against SCENIC predictions, e.g. recovering bZIP44 (companion cells) and ANAC030 (xylem).

name: plant-transcription-factor-motif-pair-enrichment
description: Use when you have Seurat cluster-specific marker genes (e.g. DEG.txt for the photosynthetic cluster) from a plant scRNA-seq atlas and want to find which paired TF-binding motifs are enriched in their promoters.

name: plant-transcriptome-target-sequence-mapping
description: Use when you have 18–25 nt plant small-RNA sequences (e.g. conserved tRF-5/tRF-3 queries) and need predicted mRNA targets plus functional enrichment of those targets in metabolic/developmental processes.

name: plaque-burden-age-correlation-null-testing
description: Use when GRN modules from spatial transcriptomics (e.g., GSE152506 Visium AD vs WT mouse brain, 3-18 months) need to be tested for correlation with a continuous phenotype such as beta-amyloid plaque staining or age against a permutation null.

name: plate-based-scrna-seq-barcode-demultiplexing
description: Use when demultiplexing plate-prepared scRNA-seq FASTQ data from patterned-flowcell instruments (HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq) where index hopping may misassign reads between sample libraries, and swapped-read fractions must be estimated or artefactual cross-sample libraries identified.

name: platelet-reference-integration-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have recovered low-total-count barcodes (below an original Cell Ranger v.2-style threshold of 200) and need to confirm that a recovered cluster represents genuine cells of a known type rather than cell-free droplets.

name: platform-aware-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when quantifying cluster purity or selecting highly variable genes for scRNA-seq clusters, especially UMI-based (10x) data, and when purity metrics must be comparable across datasets, batches, or platforms.

name: platform-lisi-batch-mixing-quantification
description: Use when you need to verify that a batch-effect removal step (e.g., SELINA's MADA network or autoencoder fine-tuning) actually mixes platform batches while preserving cell-type separation, e.g., across merged liver reference datasets or reference-query pairs.

name: plaza-dicot-monocot-species-partitioning
description: Use when reproducing or updating species-coverage counts for precomputed gene age class assignments, specifically when the PLAZA source must be split into dicot vs monocot species blocks alongside Ensembl and eggNOG counts.

name: plink-ld-reference-processing
description: Use when training eQTL weights from summary-level data (OTTERS-style TWAS Stage I) and you must supply a PLINK 1.9 .bed/.bim/.fam LD reference panel plus gene annotation to drive LD clumping and per-gene extraction.

name: ploidy-relative-copy-number-conversion
description: Use when validating RNA-seq-derived CNV calls against matched DNA-seq absolute copy-number ground truth in single cells, so absolute copy numbers must be expressed relative to ploidy before computing TPR/FPR.

name: ploidy-vs-annotation-agreement-analysis
description: Use when you have per-cell malignant/non-malignant predictions from scATOMIC on tumour-biopsy scRNA-seq and want to benchmark them against CNV-inferred ploidy status from CopyKAT.

name: pluripotency-discrimination-assessment
description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq profiles (e.g. hESC vs progenitor/differentiated populations) must be ranked or classified by differentiation potency without marker genes, feature selection, or training labels.

name: pluripotency-score-computation-across-tools
description: Use when comparing runtime and memory footprint of pluripotency/potency scoring tools (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) on scRNA-seq count matrices from breast, colon, hematopoietic, or lung datasets.

name: pmhc-binding-immunogenicity-scoring
description: Use when 8–11-aa mutant peptides extracted from annotated tumor SNV/INDEL calls must be paired with OptiType-derived HLA alleles and ranked by pMHC binding plus immunogenicity to prioritize neoantigens.

name: pmhc-multimer-avidity-prediction
description: Use when a paired single-cell TCR + transcriptome dataset carries pMHC multimer read counts as a per-cell avidity annotation and the goal is to compare avidity regression across embedding modalities.

name: pmhc-specificity-cluster-purity-analysis
description: Use when comparing embeddings (TCR-only, RNA-only, Harmony-corrected, multimodal mvTCR) of paired scRNA/TCR-seq data by how compactly and purely they cluster cells sharing a pMHC specificity annotation.

name: pod5-raw-signal-processing
description: Use when raw ONT dRNA pod5 or fast5 signal files must be basecalled in a single step that simultaneously calls canonical (A,C,G,U) and modified bases (I, m6A, m1A, m5C, Psi), avoiding re-squiggling and separate modification models.

name: point-biserial-correlation-scoring
description: Use when you have high-confidence candidate genes linked to a binary resistance trait (e.g. GWAS-derived resistant vs susceptible accessions) and need an ordered, score-based ranking to pick a small validation set such as a top-10 per pathogen.

name: point-wise-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when two paired single-cell modalities (e.g., scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq of the same granulocyte cells) have been mapped between domains by scMMGAN, CycleGAN, or CMAE and you must verify that predictions retain point-wise correspondence with ground truth rather than only matching the marginal.

name: poisson-count-likelihood-modeling
description: Use when fitting a latent-space model to raw scRNA-seq count matrices with per-cell time labels, so the generative likelihood matches integer counts (Poisson) rather than Gaussian assumptions on log-transformed data.

name: poisson-count-noise-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking mutational signature fitting algorithms and you need simulated mutation count catalogs that reflect realistic sampling stochasticity rather than exact multinomial expectations.

name: poisson-count-resampling-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking type-I error control of scRNA-seq co-expression methods: you need null count matrices where genes are not co-expressed, in both constant-depth and depth-confounded variants.

name: poisson-gamma-negative-binomial-statistics
description: Use when you need to quantify the purity/homogeneity of an scRNA-seq cell cluster by fitting a per-gene entropy model on a gene-by-cell UMI count matrix and computing a ROGUE score.

name: poisson-measurement-model-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking co-expression detection methods on simulated scRNA-seq data that must preserve real co-expression structure — e.g., generating p x n UMI count matrices from a known sparse co-expression matrix to compute precision-recall curves and wall-clock runtimes per method.

name: poisson-model-hichip-deconvolution
description: Use when bulk HiChIP enhancer-promoter loop counts must be deconvolved into subpopulation-specific profiles using scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq profiles from the same population, and a principled model-based alternative to the plug-in baseline is acceptable despite ~24 h runtime.

name: polya-cluster-overlap-annotation
description: Use when you have candidate 3' end cleavage site coordinates from 3'-tag scRNA-seq (e.g., Microwell-seq) and need to label them against GENCODE 3' ends, PolyASite 2.0 clusters, and internal-priming risk.

name: polya-priming-window-scoring
description: Use when you need to predict the splicing status (spliced, unspliced, or ambiguous 'A') of individual scRNA-seq reads, especially reads aligned to a spliceu augmented reference and filtered to unique genome mappings.

name: polya-site-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when evaluating predicted polyA-site bins from an aptardi output GTF (or a StringTie/Ensembl baseline transcriptome) against curated polyA-site databases such as PolyASite 2.0, PolyA_DB 3, or PolyA-Seq tissue-specific ground truth.

name: polya-site-benchmark-dataset-curation
description: Use when a sequence-based polyA/IPA site predictor must be independently validated on external polyA databases (GENCODE, PolyA_DB 3, PolyASite 2.0) rather than on random splits of its own training annotations.

name: polya-site-benchmarking-against-polyaseq-gold-standard
description: Use when comparing predicted transcript 3'-end/polyA site calls from multiple tools (e.g., aptardi vs TAPAS vs APARENT) against a PolyA-Seq gold standard and quantitative accuracy metrics are needed.

name: polya-site-coordinate-liftover
description: Use when benchmarking IPA site callers against GEO-deposited 3'-end sequencing ground truth whose polyA site coordinates were produced on an older assembly and must be converted to GRCh38 before interval matching.

name: polya-site-fragment-read-simulation
description: Use when you need simulated paired-end scRNA-seq FASTQs with known ground-truth splicing status—especially reads that are ambiguous ('A', compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts)—to evaluate a splicing-status or read-origin prediction model.

name: polya-site-genome-track-visualization
description: Use when you have a PACdataset of poly(A) sites with per-cell or per-sample counts plus BAM alignments and genome annotation, and need to visually inspect proximal vs distal pA usage for a specific gene.

name: polya-site-quantification-in-spatial-transcriptomics
description: Use when raw spatially barcoded ST FASTQ reads (barcodes/UMIs in read 1) must be turned into a poly(A) site-by-spot matrix and per-spot APA usage ratios (RUD) before imputation or layer-level APA analysis.

name: polya-site-rud-index-computation
description: Use when a PACdataset contains multiple poly(A) sites per gene (3'UTR APA) and per-gene/per-cell RUD scores are needed to quantify 3'UTR shortening or lengthening across cells or cell types.

name: polya-site-usage-analysis
description: Use when long-read (PacBio/ONT) reads are annotated with polyA sites against a reference such as the polyasite.unibas.ch atlas or FANTOM CAGE peaks (mm10), and the goal is to find genes whose 3' end site choice differs between biological groups.

name: polya-site-usage-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when a gene's proximal vs distal poly(A) site usage (e.g., RUD scores from getAPAindexPACds) must be inspected as per-cell distributions across defined cell groups such as SC/RS/ES sperm stages.

name: polya-tail-motif-screening
description: Use when a strand-split BAM of aligned reads must be interrogated for reads with soft-clipped polyA/polyT tails to build truncation-point tallies that localize precise 3' UTR end bases.

name: polyadenylation-informed-transcriptome-analysis
description: Use when you need to test whether adding aptardi-predicted polyA transcripts to a GTF changes which transcripts are called differentially expressed between two conditions (e.g., BNLx vs SHR rat brain).

name: polyadenylation-site-feature-windowing
description: Use when eCLIP/IP signal should be visualized around polyadenylation sites (e.g. reproducing Supplementary Figs. S2/S3-style poly(A)-site metagenes) rather than around generic UTR/CDS transcript regions.

name: polyadenylation-site-prediction
description: Use when a sample-specific transcriptome (e.g. StringTie GTF) needs accurate 3'-end/polyA site annotation from genome-aligned RNA-Seq plus genome FASTA, and downstream APA or quantitation analyses require refined transcript termini.

name: polygenic-regression-celltype-inference
description: Use when you have GWAS summary statistics and a cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object or AnnData) and need to identify which cell types or single cells are statistically associated with a complex trait.

name: polygenic-score-model-fitting
description: Use when TWAS Stage I eQTL weights must be trained from summary-level eQTL summary statistics (with CHROM, POS, A1, A2, Zscore, TargetID, N columns) because individual-level genotype-expression reference data are unavailable or too small (e.g., GTEx V6 n=338 vs eQTLGen n=31,684).

name: polygenic-score-thresholding-with-ld-clumping
description: Use when only summary-level eQTL reference data (e.g., eQTLGen-style p-values + beta coefficients per gene) are available and individual-level genotype/expression cannot be used to fit GReX imputation weights.

name: polyphen2-functional-impact-binning
description: Use when building mutation-type feature matrices from COSMIC somatic mutation data where missense variants must be stratified by predicted functional impact (HiFI/MiFI/LoFI) before computing per-gene ratio-metric, entropy and frequency features for driver-gene classification.

name: pooled-versus-single-cell-prediction-strategy
description: Use when predicting miRNA activity from scRNA-seq data where single-cell profiles are too sparse for a pretrained bulk-trained model, and you want to contrast pooled-cluster predictions with per-cell predictions.

name: population-barcode-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a normalized barcode counts table (e.g. counts/all_counts_combined.tsv) is available and you need to test whether treatments, doses, or time points are distinguishable by global clonal composition, or to check replicate concordance before downstream diversity or clustering analyses.

name: population-genetic-allele-frequency-analysis
description: Use when a PAIRADISE results table of significant ASAS events (FDR <= 10%) must be tested for LD-based enrichment against GWAS catalog SNPs and quantified per dataset (e.g., GM12878, Geuvadis CEU/FIN/GBR/TSI/YRI).

name: population-level-barcode-count-table-filtering
description: Use when you have a raw barcode counts matrix (e.g. from BARtab output on SPLINTR/GEO data) and need to remove low-quality samples and low-abundance barcodes before downstream barcoding analysis.

name: position-specific-gapped-kmer-descriptor-grouping
description: Use when a combined feature table mixes several descriptor families (e.g., position-specific gapped k-mer and position-specific k-mer modes plus GC-content) and you need per-group Random Forest feature selection rather than ranking all features jointly.

name: position-specific-gapped-kmer-feature-ablation
description: Use when benchmarking which subsets of position-specific (gapped) k-mer feature blocks contribute to classifier performance on 41-nt RNA sequences, e.g. reproducing a Table 3-style ablation with Accuracy/Precision/Sensitivity/Specificity/F1/MCC.

name: position-specific-propensity-sequence-encoding
description: Use when building machine-learning inputs for m5C site prediction from labeled 41-nt RNA sequence segments (e.g., A. thaliana or M. musculus benchmarks) and you need positional, compositional, and physicochemical feature encodings fused into one matrix.

name: position-weight-matrix-log-odds-scoring
description: Use when scoring nucleotide sequences against a PWM for motif detection and the scoring must be normalized to the GC fraction of the user-supplied sequence to avoid GC-bias in motif hits.

name: positive-negative-marker-scoring
description: Use when clusters of closely related cell subtypes (e.g. naive vs effector T cells, immature B vs plasma cells) collapse to near-equal scores under positive-only markers, and negative marker evidence is needed to resolve them.

name: positive-negative-sample-balancing
description: Use when building benchmark datasets for a tissue- or species-specific site-prediction model and you need equal positive and negative sequence counts in both training and testing partitions to avoid class-imbalance bias.

name: positive-negative-set-contrast-analysis
description: Use when you have two balanced sets of centered, fixed-length nucleotide fragments (e.g., 5,298 vs 5,298 A. thaliana; 4,563 vs 4,563 M. musculus) and need to test whether the positive class shows position-specific residue enrichment or motifs relative to the negative class.

name: positive-unlabeled-learning-classification
description: Use when you have a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq and need to distinguish cell-free from cell-containing droplets, including recovering genuine cells with total counts below a fixed cutoff.

name: positive-unlabeled-neural-network-cell-calling
description: Use when given a raw unfiltered gene-by-barcode count matrix (mtx or h5) from droplet-based scRNA-seq and you need to classify barcodes as cell-free vs cell-containing, or recover cell-containing droplets below common count cutoffs.

name: positive-unlabeled-set-partitioning
description: Use when starting from a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) and you must assign each retained barcode to a positive (cell-free) or unlabeled (mixed cell-containing/cell-free) set before PU-learning-based cell calling.

name: post-hoc-cluster-label-inference
description: Use when a dataset is too large to cluster directly (e.g. Levine15_32dim, 104,184 cells; Samusik16, 86,864 cells) and a KMD model has been fit on a subsample whose labels must be propagated to the unsampled objects.

name: post-hoc-fishers-exact-testing
description: Use when you have tabulated control vs. perturbed cell counts per Louvain cluster (from any integration embedding or ICAT sslouvain assignments), a G-test has flagged clusters with significant treatment enrichment, and you need per-cluster direction of enrichment for a Fig 5C-style comparison.

name: post-integration-single-cell-clustering
description: Use when a single-sample scRNA-seq pipeline has already produced an integrated multi-sample SingleCellExperiment object (with HVGs and reduced dimensions) and you need post-integration clustering, cell-type annotation, and an HTML report.

name: post-selection-p-value-inference
description: Use when p-values are needed for variables selected by Lasso or adaptive Lasso penalized regression on high-dimensional genomic covariates, since standard software p-values are invalid after variable selection.

name: posterior-assignment-of-regulatory-combinations
description: Use when you have a preprocessed (0,1)-scaled scRNA-seq matrix with a shortlist of candidate TFs per target gene and need to infer which Boolean logic combination (e.g., TF1 AND NOT TF2) regulates each target without per-gate likelihood enumeration.

name: posterior-confidence-label-filtering
description: Use when FFC cluster labels and pval_list are available for single-cell data (PBMC CITE-seq, multiome, MCA) and you want to quantify ARI/purity gains from restricting evaluation to high-confidence (PEP < 0.1) labels.

name: posterior-distance-cell-similarity-search
description: Use when transferring cell type or continuous fate annotations from a labeled reference scRNA-seq dataset (AnnData/h5ad) to unlabeled query cells, especially across batches or species with batch effects.

name: posterior-distribution-distance-computation
description: Use when querying scRNA-seq cells against a reference embedding (e.g., DIRECTi or scVI latent space) and you need a model-aware similarity metric that accounts for posterior uncertainty rather than Euclidean distance between embedding vectors.

name: posterior-effect-size-significance-classification
description: Use when a fitted PhenoPath variational model (phenopath_fit) contains posterior interaction coefficients and you must rank and call significant gene-covariate (e.g. MSI-pseudotime) interactions.

name: posterior-label-distribution-estimation
description: Use when FFC cluster labels (cluster_obj.cluster_labels after fit(fire_temp=100)) need point-wise confidence quantification, e.g., posterior exclusion probabilities and label entropies to flag transition cells along developmental pseudo-time.

name: posterior-predictive-simulation-of-count-data
description: Use when you have posterior samples from a count-based scRNA-seq model (e.g., BUSseq fits of hematopoietic/pancreas read counts) and need to test whether the model reproduces observed zero-count rates, or whether dropout events must be explicitly modeled.

name: posterior-probability-cell-classification
description: Use when demultiplexing pooled single-cell RNA-seq experiments whose cells were labeled with hashtag oligonucleotides (HTOs), and per-droplet sample assignments with error probabilities are required.

name: posterior-probability-cutoff-subtype-classification
description: Use when reproducing or comparing cancer molecular subtype classification rates on gene expression data, specifically to quantify how many samples remain unclassifiable under a posterior probability > 0.5 criterion (e.g., DeepCC vs. the 273-gene random-forest CMS classifier).

name: posterior-probability-uncertainty-quantification
description: Use when BAMM-SC (or DIMM-SC) clustering of droplet-based scRNA-seq data must report which individual cells have uncertain cluster-type assignments, e.g. per-cell posterior probabilities rather than only hard labels.

name: postgresql-backend-table-ingestion
description: Use when preparing a single-cell study (H5AD expression matrix plus cell-type annotations) for import into Cellenium and interactive marker-gene lookup must return without recomputation at query time.

name: postgresql-study-data-retrieval
description: Use when a downstream analysis (e.g. ranking genes correlated to a query gene) needs the expression vector of a gene and of every other gene across all cells of one imported Cellenium study.

name: potential-energy-landscape-construction-cell-graph
description: Use when inferring differentiation trajectories without reliable RNA velocity, e.g. from progenitor clusters (NEUROG3-early/mid/late) to terminal fates (SC-α, SC-β, SC-EC) in a preprocessed AnnData object.

name: potential-landscape-model-training
description: Use when you have preprocessed longitudinal scRNA-seq (normalized expression, integer timepoint labels, cell type annotations) and need to fit a potential landscape for fate prediction or perturbation simulation.

name: potts-model-smoothness-grid-search
description: Use when multiple SRT sections need integrated spatial clustering and the number of domains K is unknown — e.g. after APCA reduction (npcs = 15) and CreateNeighbors adjacency, with batch effects to estimate jointly.

name: potts-model-spatial-prior-implementation
description: Use when a clustering of spatial transcriptomics spots must be scored/compared without ground-truth labels — e.g. sweeping alpha_options/beta_options/seed_options in ScribbleDom configs to pick the alpha without computing ARI.

name: power-and-false-positive-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how the power and type-I error of variance-differentiation tests (LRT, Wald, jackknife Wald) for cell type-specific pseudobulk data depend on sample size and measurement-noise misestimation, e.g. reproducing Figures 1-2 of the CTMM paper.

name: power-law-distribution-fitting
description: Use when a large-scale biological grouping result (e.g., ortholog group sizes from OrthoFinder over hundreds of species) needs its size distribution characterized and validated against a power-law expectation.

name: power-law-hub-topology-network-generation
description: Use when benchmarking network inference methods (e.g. scLink vs glasso, PIDC, GENIE3, thresholded Pearson/Spearman) on simulated sparse single-cell data where the true adjacency matrix must be known, especially to compare power-law vs hub-based topologies and varying sparsity levels.

name: pparg-target-gene-set-validation
description: Use when a gene-perturbation microarray analysis must be validated against a known transcription-factor target set, e.g. confirming Pparg knockdown effects by recovering previously validated PPARG targets among significant DE genes.

name: ppi-connectome-transcriptome-correlation-scoring
description: Use when you have single-cell expression data (e.g. Chu et al. scRNA-Seq matrix) and a PPI connectome, and need to rank cells by differentiation potency without running the expensive full signalling entropy computation.

name: ppi-network-differentiation-activity-computation
description: Use when you have a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix and need a per-cell pluripotency/potency score to rank or select stem and progenitor cells, e.g. as trajectory-inference origins.

name: ppi-network-integration-with-transcriptome
description: Use when the goal is to estimate or rank differentiation potency of single cells from scRNA-Seq profiles (e.g. discriminating pluripotent hESCs from progenitors) where marker expression or timepoint labels are unavailable or unreliable due to dropouts.

name: ppin-activity-computation
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes as rows, cells as columns) and need per-cell activity scores for biological-process PPINs, e.g. for cell annotation, UMAP maps, or correlation of process activities.

name: ppin-activity-quantification-per-cell
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells) and need per-cell activity scores for biological processes via PPIN edge sums, e.g. to build BP activity matrices for correlation or cell-type annotation.

name: ppin-diffusion-activity-scoring
description: Use when you have a normalized genes-by-cells scRNA-seq count matrix and need a per-cell pluripotency/differentiation score to rank cell types (e.g. basal vs. L1/L2) or to root pseudotime inference in the most stem-like cells.

name: ppin-network-activity-computation
description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix and need per-cell pluripotency/stemness scores to identify stem or progenitor cells as trajectory origins.

name: ppmi-graph-weighting
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be converted into a weighted cell–cell adjacency for graph-embedding clustering, and an unweighted KNN adjacency is insufficient to capture cell–cell transition probabilities.

name: ppv-npv-validation-metrics-computation
description: Use when validating MRSD-predicted required sequencing depths against observed junction coverage in held-out samples (e.g. 12 blood, 4 LCL, 52 muscle) across a grid of --number_reads, --sj_prop, --mrsd_param, --read_type parameter combinations.

name: pre-clinical-cms-subtype-classification
description: Use when gene expression matrices from CRC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, or PDXs need CMS1-CMS4 assignment and the original classifyCMS.RF classifier fails or leaves many samples unclassified (e.g., missing CMS4).

name: pre-post-immunotherapy-patient-sample-matching
description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain paired pre-/post-immunotherapy (ICB) samples per patient and you must select patients with both timepoints and adequate cell counts before testing whether a CD8 TIL state (e.g. EM-like) expands upon therapy in responders.

name: prec-recall-curve-benchmarking
description: Use when scored enhancer–gene interactions must be quantitatively compared across activity setups or models using an imbalanced CRISPR perturbation gold standard, where AUPRC is the appropriate metric.

name: precision-at-k-differentially-expressed-gene-recovery
description: Use when benchmarking feature selection on simulated single-cell data with known ground-truth DE genes and you need an objective overlap score between the top-k ranked features and the truth set.

name: precision-at-k-feature-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a feature selection strategy that returns a ranked top-p feature list and you have ground truth labels (e.g. cell cycle phase) to build a supervised reference ranking.

name: precision-benchmark-evaluation-against-simulated-ground-truth
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare per-cell precision of trait-relevant cell identification methods against a known ground truth, e.g. testing whether scPagwas-prioritized genes improve scDRS.

name: precision-curve-analysis-across-datasets
description: Use when you have ranked predicted interaction lists (e.g. top 100000 pairs from a latent-space or correlation method) and a gold-standard set like KEGG, and need to quantify precision across both scRNA-seq and bulk proteomics data.

name: precision-medicine-subgroup-tree-fitting
description: Use when the goal is a treatment-subgroup analysis: a treatment/coding/interacting variable structure must be encoded via the types argument of dipm(), and a tree over baseline covariates (e.g. MASS::anorexia weight-change data) must be grown, split by depth-importance, and optionally pruned.

name: precision-recall-auc-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare competing gene set enrichment methods on synthetic studies where the true positive pathways are known by construction, across a noise/similarity grid.

name: precision-recall-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a predicted sample-specific transcriptome (e.g., name_aptardi.gtf) must be quantitatively scored against gold-standard polyA sites to confirm cross-dataset generalizability.

name: precision-recall-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when ranked per-gene scores from competing methods must be compared against a known ground-truth gene set (simulated or curated) to quantify ranking accuracy via AUPRC and early-precision metrics.

name: precision-recall-caveat-analysis
description: Use when a GRN method's aggregate precision-recall curve looks acceptable and you need to check whether that summary hides poor edge-rank recovery for individual regulators in the gold standard.

name: precision-recall-curve-analysis
description: Use when comparing variant-calling or classification tools against a known ground truth, and you need cutoff-independent metrics (AUPRC/AUROC) plus PR/ROC curves across simulation settings.

name: precision-recall-curve-analysis
description: Use when inferred GRN edge lists (TF, Gene, importance from PIDC, GENIE3, GRNBoost2, etc.) must be evaluated against a ground-truth GRN to rank inference methods by precision@k and AUPRC.

name: precision-recall-curve-auprc-evaluation
description: Use when a reconstructed GRN (TF/Gene/importance rankings) must be scored against an imposed or curated ground truth GRN, and ranked edges need precision-recall quantification with a random-predictor baseline.

name: precision-recall-curve-evaluation
description: Use when comparing discriminative vs. hierarchy-corrected cell-type classifiers (independent, IR, TPR, BNC) on labeled bulk or single-cell RNA-seq with Cell Ontology term labels, and average precision or PR curves are the scoring metrics.

name: precision-recall-curve-evaluation
description: Use when you have ranked enhancer–gene interaction scores (e.g., STARE_ABCpp gABC or regular ABC output) and binary ground-truth labels from CRISPRi perturbation datasets, and need to quantify or compare predictive accuracy via AUPRC/ROC AUC.

name: precision-recall-curve-evaluation
description: Use when comparing gene co-expression detection methods (e.g., CS-CORE, Pearson, Spearman, locCSN, normalisr, NoiseRegularization) that output p-values, using a known ground-truth sparse co-expression network as the reference.

name: precision-recall-curve-metric-extraction
description: Use when benchmarking pathway enrichment methods against known true-positive pathways (e.g. similarity_sample-activated terms) and you need a recall-fixed precision summary under a specified noise level such as η=0.25.

name: precision-recall-f1-computation
description: Use when comparing per-cell predictions of malignant-cell identification tools (marker-based or CNV-based) against a published ground-truth label vector, and accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 with wall-clock runtime must be reported.

name: precision-recall-f1-computation
description: Use when comparing trajectory inference methods (e.g. STREAM, Monocle2, ElPiGraph) on a branching single-cell dataset where sorted population labels serve as ground truth, to rank methods by per-marker precision/recall/F1 on lineage-specific branches.

name: precision-recall-f1-evaluation
description: Use when comparing differential network inference methods (e.g., BoostDiff vs GENIE3, ARACNE, RF Difftrees, EBcoexpress) on data with known ground-truth edges and you need precision/recall/F1 per network-size setting.

name: precision-recall-fmeasure-benchmarking
description: Use when you have simulated RNA-seq count data with known DE/non-DE gene labels and need to compare DEG-calling consensus strategies (vote thresholds of 1–4 or combined-FDR) by precision, recall and F-measure.

name: precision-recall-fscore-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to judge whether an scRNA-seq preprocessing step (e.g., dropout imputation with scImpute, MAGIC, or SAVER) improves downstream differential-expression agreement with a bulk RNA-seq ground truth, via F-score comparison.

name: precision-recall-metric-computation
description: Use when multiple active-subnetwork detection methods are run on simulated datasets with a known perturbed module, and quantitative precision/recall/F1 benchmarking against the ground truth is required.

name: precision-recall-metric-computation
description: Use when a set of predicted genomic intervals (e.g., polyA-site bins from aptardi output GTF at probability >= 0.5) must be scored for precision and recall against annotated reference databases such as PolyASite 2.0 or PolyA_DB 3.

name: precision-sensitivity-computation
description: Use when benchmarking CNA callers (HiScanner, CHISEL, Ginkgo, SCOPE, SCYN) on simulated scWGS/bulk WGS data with known ground-truth CNAs and you need per-type, per-size precision and sensitivity curves.

name: precision-sensitivity-fpr-metric-computation
description: Use when a lineage prediction matrix must be quantitatively scored against ground-truth barcode assignments, e.g. reproducing GEMLI's cutoff-50 precision 80%±15%, sensitivity 22%±12%, FPR <1% on GSE99915 MEF data.

name: precision-sensitivity-fscore-computation
description: Use when benchmarking HTO-based demultiplexing methods: you have per-droplet sample-of-origin/multiplet calls from one or more methods plus an independent ground truth (demuxlet-derived SSDs or RNA-profile cluster labels) and need precisionSSD, sensitivitySSD, and F-score averaged across conditions.

name: precision-sensitivity-threshold-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq lineage predictions from GEMLI (or a similar predictor) must be validated against an independent lineage-tracing ground truth, such as a CRISPR barcode dictionary, to find an optimal confidence cutoff.

name: precomputed-orthogroup-resource-data-loading
description: Use when you need to enumerate which eukaryotic species have precomputed LCA-derived gene age assignments in oggmap's shipped Ensembl, eggNOG, or PLAZA resource files rather than re-running orthology inference.

name: precomputed-rankings-score-acceleration
description: Use when you need to score multiple or evolving gene signatures on the same single-cell dataset and want to avoid recomputing the expensive gene-ranking step for every new signature.

name: precomputed-result-table-serialization
description: Use when an interactive analytics application must return analysis results (e.g. differential expression per annotated cell type) instantly on user selection, and precomputing contrasts at data-import time is acceptable.

name: predicted-abundance-correlation-analysis
description: Use when bulk-aggregated single-cell samples with known per-cell-type abundances are available and you must quantify how faithfully a deconvolution method (e.g. DCNet, CIBERSORTx, xCell) recovers each cell type's abundance via per-type Pearson correlations.

name: prediction-accuracy-and-rmse-evaluation
description: Use when you have predicted vs. true circadian times (ZT hours) from a transcriptomic time-prediction pipeline and need standardized 2-hour accuracy and RMSE metrics, e.g. for 80/20-split benchmarks or leave-one-out cross-validation.

name: prediction-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a trained cell type annotation model (e.g., TOSICA) has predicted labels on a query dataset and you need to quantify annotation quality as a fraction of correctly predicted cells against known query/test labels.

name: prediction-confidence-thresholding
description: Use when classifying genomes (e.g., unknown-lifestyle Burkholderia/Paraburkholderia or Pseudomonas strains) with random-forest per-lifestyle probability outputs where an assignment cutoff must separate confident calls from uncertain ones.

name: prediction-contour-estimation
description: Use when initial per-cell cell-type predictions from Census's hierarchical models are noisy and need stabilization via UMAP-space contours and cluster label propagation before descending to the next hierarchy node.

name: prediction-error-distribution-analysis
description: Use when you need to evaluate the accuracy and precision of regression-based parameter estimators by comparing predicted-minus-true error distributions across multiple model architectures on simulated data with known ground truth.

name: prediction-score-cutoff-thresholding
description: Use when converting LncCat/CatBoost prediction probabilities into binary lncRNA vs PCT labels, or when sweeping cutoffs (e.g. 0.1-0.9) to check that reported MCC/F1 benchmarks hold at the fixed 0.5 cutoff.

name: prelu-convolutional-layer-configuration
description: Use when reconstructing or retraining a dual-branch 1D CNN for nucleotide-modification site prediction from one-hot encoded sequence plus secondary-structure matrices, or when the target model must report 661,118 trainable parameters.

name: preprocessing-for-protein-imputation
description: Use when you have raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts plus paired ADT (CITE-seq/REAP-seq) protein counts and need the normalized denoised expression matrix and relative protein abundance response vectors required to run or train cTP-net.

name: prerank-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a weighted gene network or community of genes (e.g., a GRnnData network across the 26 benchmarked cell types or a Louvain community) and need to test whether its genes are enriched for TFs, cell-type markers, ENCODE targets, or GO molecular-function terms.

name: preranked-gene-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when annotated cell type identities must be assigned to clusters of an integrated scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., human HSPCs) using curated signature gene sets rather than manual marker inspection.

name: preranked-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when factor loadings from a Tensor-cell2cell decomposition (e.g., 6 ASD factors) need functional interpretation by ranking LR pairs and testing enrichment of pathway-level LR gene sets.

name: presence-absence-matrix-construction
description: Use when comparing which of the top-ranked ligand-receptor predictions are shared across the 7 CCC methods or 16 prior-knowledge resources, i.e., when the analysis goal is overlap of predicted interaction sets rather than score correlation.

name: pretrained-checkpoint-inference
description: Use when you have an expression matrix (scRNA-seq or 10x Visium spots), a Cancer-Finder pre-trained checkpoint (e.g., checkpoints/sc_pretrain_article.pkl), and need reference-free malignant-cell/spot predictions.

name: pretrained-checkpoint-shape-validation
description: Use when reconstructing a published deep learning model from its paper's architecture description and you possess a pretrained checkpoint (e.g. Zenodo 5895221) to validate the reconstruction against layer-by-layer.

name: pretrained-classifier-inference-on-st-spots
description: Use when the input is a tumor ST dataset (h5ad spots with spatial coordinates and H&E image) and per-spot malignant-vs-normal malignancy probabilities are needed as features for malignant-region calling.

name: pretrained-model-inference-on-ann-data
description: Use when you have raw-count AnnData (.h5ad) scRNA-seq data with cells from a cancerous lineage already identified and need automated malignant-vs-normal cell calls plus a malignancy probability from a pretrained model.

name: pretrained-model-inference-scrnaseq
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (.h5ad) from progression-stage samples (normal mucosa, polyps, tumors) must be scored for malignancy with a pretrained classifier instead of retraining, and per-stage malignant-cell percentages are needed.

name: pretrained-model-transfer-to-scrna-data
description: Use when scRNA-seq data lack miRNA measurements (poly(A) capture precludes miRNA profiling) and you need to infer miRNA expression per cluster or per cell using a model pretrained on paired bulk miRNA-mRNA cohorts such as TCGA, GTEx, or CCLE.

name: pretrained-neural-classifier-inference
description: Use when new gene expression profiles (a batch data.frame with Entrez ID columns, or a single-sample profile) must be classified with an already-trained DeepCC model without retraining, e.g., assigning CMS labels to colorectal cancer samples.

name: pretrained-neural-model-inference
description: Use when a test scRNA-seq expression matrix must be labeled against the Cell Ontology without retraining, especially when the query may contain cell types absent from any training annotations.

name: pretrained-neural-network-model-loading
description: Use when a trained TACTiCS PyTorch model must be loaded from the Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.7582460) to extract cell embeddings for motor cortex scRNA-seq cells without retraining.

name: pretrained-pollock-module-inference
description: Use when cell type labels must be predicted for raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. artificially dropout-masked validation datasets) using a pretrained disease/tissue-specific Pollock module, so F1 can be computed against annotated cell types.

name: pretrained-transformer-zero-shot-inference
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix needs denoising, label prediction, embedding/batch correction, or gene network extraction without labeled training data, e.g. rare cell states where smoothing-based methods lose signal.

name: prevalence-scatter-plot-visualization
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-to-scDNA clone-assignment methods against ground-truth clone labels and you need to compare predicted vs. true clonal prevalence concordance across methods.

name: primary-cell-atlas-reference-profiling
description: Use when you have a gene-symbol-indexed transcriptome of one cell population of interest and need to infer its emitted (outward) communication toward reference partner cell types via ICELLNET.

name: prime-feature-correlation-statistics
description: Use when you need to observe the correlation of a single feature of interest against many features in an NGS or microarray expression table, obtaining per-feature coefficients and p-values plus a distribution plot.

name: primed-cell-state-calling
description: Use when a multipotent cell population (e.g. MPPs or TACs) has been shown by CompDICE/CompPrimingPval to be significantly primed (empirical P < 0.05 from nMC >= 1000 randomizations) and top RF pairs are known, and you need per-cell primed-state assignments from scRNA-Seq alone.

name: primed-cell-state-cross-modality-validation
description: Use when you have DICE-predicted primed cells and regulator TFs from scRNA-Seq plus a matched scATAC-Seq dataset for the same cell types, and need epigenomic confirmation that primed cells show higher accessibility/motif activity of the predicted TFs' targets.

name: primed-state-cross-omic-validation
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis has assigned primed states (e.g. via DICE FindPrimedCells) and matched scATAC-Seq profiles exist for the same or equivalent cells, and you must confirm that priming leaves an epigenomic signature.

name: principal-component-analysis-implementation
description: Use when a normalized, log-transformed, gene-centered scRNA-Seq matrix must be decomposed into principal components to identify dominant directions of unwanted variation (e.g. cell-cycle effect) prior to removal or clustering.

name: principal-component-based-domain-scoring
description: Use when evaluating multiple spatial-domain clustering outputs (e.g., over alpha_options/beta_options/seed_options grids) and ground-truth labels are unavailable, so clustering quality must be ranked by a model-based score instead of ARI.

name: principal-component-based-variation-identification
description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression data (log-transformed, gene-centered) shows a suspected dominant systematic effect and you must test whether PCs are cell-cycle effects before removal, using annotated control vs cell-cycle gene sets.

name: principal-component-multimodality-selection
description: Use when running scDecouple on perturbation matrix Y and control matrix Z from scCRISPR-seq (e.g. CROP-seq) data and you must pick which control-group PCs carry infection bias before the Gaussian-mixture decoupling step.

name: principal-component-preprocessing-for-lda
description: Use when the input feature matrix exceeds ~100 dimensions (e.g., transcriptomic data with thousands of genes) so HSS feature selection cannot run, yet a priori class labels exist and a supervised linear-discriminant visualization is wanted.

name: principal-component-regression-gene-adjacency-estimation
description: Use when constructing cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks from untreated scRNA-seq expression profiles as the network-construction stage of scRank, prior to in silico drug-perturbation ranking.

name: principal-component-technical-noise-estimation

name: prior-grid-sampling-with-class-labels
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix is too large (hundreds of thousands to millions of cells) for geometric sketching, prior class labels are available, and a fast, competitive subsample measured by Hausdorff distance is needed.

name: prior-latent-space-synthetic-generation
description: Use when generating a full-size synthetic scRNA-seq count matrix from a generative model trained on a small pilot sub-sample (e.g. 384–2304 cells), and you want to avoid amplifying pilot-specific artifacts that posterior sampling of p(z|x) introduces.

name: prism-scaled-auc-sensitivity-scoring
description: Use when you have a Scanpy AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) of drug-treated scRNA-seq samples with tumor clusters, and need PRISM-based per-cluster AUC sensitivity predictions to compare against observed cell proportion changes.

description: Use when the input is a multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST count matrix (e.

name: probabilistic-cluster-assignment
description: Use when a gene-expression data frame (CSV with gene identifiers and log-fold-change values) must be partitioned into expression-pattern types with probability-based cluster assignments.

name: probabilistic-in-silico-deletion

name: probabilistic-marker-based-cell-assignment
description: Use when raw-count scRNA-seq AnnData needs automated cell type annotation from curated marker gene sets, and predicted labels should be validated against existing published cell type annotations.

name: probabilistic-multimapping-read-allocation
description: Use when single-cell (scRNA, scATAC, Multi-Omics, Visium, or long-read) BAM files mapped by STAR/STARsolo contain multi-mapping reads over repetitive TE loci and locus-specific (not subfamily-level) TE counts are needed.

name: probabilistic-threshold-parameterization-for-sequence-search
description: Use when approximate sequence search needs a significance cutoff on shared minimizers — e.g. a query read with a sequence-dependent number of (w,k)-minimizers must be judged against random minimizer sharing at a fixed confidence level.

name: probe-identifier-verification
description: Use when a probe-level expression matrix (e.g. GEO microarray data like GSE4786) yields candidate reference probes from ERgene.FindERG and you must confirm a specific probe ID exists in the output before normalizing.

name: profile-based-homology-search
description: Use when building a reference database of endogenous retroviral sequences that must each be backed by detectable retroviral protein motifs (POL/RT, GAG, ENV) before downstream alignment of assembled contigs.

name: profile-likelihood-index-parameter-optimization
description: Use when fitting per-gene Tweedie (CPLM/ZICP) models to UMI or read-count scRNA-seq data and the index parameter p must be estimated rather than fixed, e.g. to compare gene-specific p across experimental protocols.

name: progeny-model-application
description: Use when you need to infer signaling pathway activity (e.g. MAPK, PI3K, NFkB, TGFb, JAK-STAT) from bulk or single-cell gene expression, especially in perturbation experiments where pathway activity must be validated against controls or phospho-protein measurements.

name: prognostic-risk-score-computation

name: prognostic-signature-benchmarking

name: progression-stage-stratified-analysis
