name: progressive-biological-knowledge-integration-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing which combination of biological knowledge (TF, miRNA, IS, Kinase) to embed in an SCA/SSCA latent space when single-knowledge spaces fail to reconstruct specific single-cell clusters.

name: progressive-learning-cell-annotation-across-batches
description: Use when multiple annotated single-cell datasets (e.g., simulated batches or PBMC-FACS) must be merged into one hierarchical classifier, especially when some batches may lack cell populations and you need to assess whether the learned tree stays stable.

name: progressive-learning-tree-construction
description: Use when multiple annotated single-cell datasets (e.g., from different labs or protocols, such as Saunders, Zeisel, Tabula Muris brain data) must be combined into one consistent cell-population hierarchy, especially when annotation terminologies differ between studies.

name: projection-accuracy-metrics-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively validate how faithfully a method projects held-out scRNA-seq data onto a reference atlas and how accurately it transfers cell-state labels, relative to alternative mapping tools.

name: projection-pursuit-outlier-scoring
description: Use when a cohort of base-level RNA-seq pileup matrices at one gene must be screened unsupervised for samples with anomalous coverage shapes (splicing, intron retention, deletions, ATS/ATT) rather than differential expression.

name: proliferation-index-piecewise-scoring
description: Use when single-cell marker-intensity data from multiplexed imaging (e.g. CyCIF) must be scored per cell for proliferation vs. cell-cycle arrest, to derive the fraction of a cell type (e.g. SOX10+ tumor cells) with MPI = 1.

name: proliferation-weight-incorporation-in-fate-modeling
description: Use when modeling cell fate bias from time-series scRNA-seq data (e.g., day-2/4/6 lineage-tracing points) and empirical or gene-expression-derived growth rates are available to weight the learned differentiation landscape.

name: promoter-binding-site-mapping

name: promoter-binding-site-matrix-processing

name: promoter-sequence-extraction-from-genbank

name: proportion-estimate-correlation-accuracy-evaluation

name: proportion-estimation-of-duplicated-degs

name: proportion-of-variance-explained-estimation

name: proportion-statistic-reproduction

name: proportional-enrichment-testing

name: propr-rho-correlation-computation

name: prosstt-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when a benchmark requires synthetic scRNA-seq datasets with known developmental trajectory or cluster structure (e.g. ~2000 cells x 5000 genes) to evaluate dimensionality-reduction or clustering methods.

name: prostate-cancer-pathway-network-interpretation
description: Use when analyzing differential RNA-seq expression on KEGG metabolic pathways in Cytoscape, where nodes contain multiple functionally homologous genes and standard KGML readers show only the first listed gene, masking the true catalytic driver.

name: protein-association-score-posterior-probability-conversion
description: Use when raw correlation-based protein association scores (e.g., FAVA PCC scores) must be calibrated into interpretable confidence probabilities using a gold-standard benchmark like KEGG, or when STRING-style confidence cutoffs (15%, 40%, 70%) are needed for a combined network.

name: protein-based-clustering-umap-visualization
description: Use when you have dsb-normalized ADT/protein values (or want to validate a normalization against Figure 2-style results) and need to confirm the normalized data resolve interpretable protein-defined clusters and biaxial population structure.

name: protein-cluster-annotation-across-seven-enrichment-categories
description: Use when you already have a FAVA protein association edge list (interactions in both directions) and need to detect functional modules and annotate them with functional enrichment.

name: protein-complex-decomplexification

name: protein-complex-expansion

name: protein-complex-group-modeling

name: protein-embedding-distance-rank-statistics
description: Use when two species' protein sequences and ProtBERT embeddings are available and you need to quantify how embedding-based gene matches agree with BLAST -hit assignments and ranks (e.g., for TACTiCS gene-similarity input validation).

name: protein-embedding-gene-matching
description: Use when preparing cross-species single-cell comparisons that need a gene similarity distance matrix derived from protein sequence embeddings rather than sequence alignment tools like BLAST.

name: protein-expression-matrix-log-transformation

name: protein-gene-mapping-count-projection

name: protein-interaction-benchmarking-against-kegg-biogrid

name: protein-interaction-credibility-and-action-mode-filtering

name: protein-interaction-database-filtering
description: Use when building or subsetting a cell–cell interaction database from STRING/COMPARTMENTS/UniProt annotations, or when filtering candidate ligand–receptor and protein–protein pairs by localization, evidence source, action mode, or effect before intercellular analysis.

name: protein-interaction-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have gene sets (gene programs/modules) from scRNA-seq analysis and want to validate them functionally by testing enrichment of STRING PPI interactions, or when benchmarking methods like SSN vs ICA/NMF.

name: protein-interaction-network-based-potency-scoring
description: Use when scoring snapshot scRNA-Seq cells for differentiation potency or identifying cancer stem-cell-like phenotypes (e.g. cancer vs non-malignant cells in Tirosh melanoma) without prior marker knowledge or timepoints.

name: protein-interaction-network-confidence-filtering

name: protein-interaction-network-confidence-filtering

name: protein-interaction-network-construction-from-gene-lists

name: protein-interaction-network-scoring

name: protein-marker-concordance-verification
description: Use when you have a multimodal CITE-seq h5ad with normalized protein counts and protein-derived PCs, and need to validate clustering-free protein marker predictions against Seurat-style Wilcoxon/t-test baselines.

name: protein-network-cluster-size-distribution-verification
description: Use when a weighted protein association network edge list (e.g. from a favapy run) must be partitioned into functional clusters with MCL and the resulting cluster count and size distribution must be validated against published numbers before enrichment analysis.

name: protein-physicochemical-feature-computation
description: Use when building an LncDC-style lncRNA-vs-mRNA feature matrix and protein-level descriptors (e.g. ProtParam properties from translated ORFs) must be added to sequence and secondary-structure features.

name: protein-prediction-correlation-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking cTP-net surface-protein imputation on holdout CITE-seq cells and you need to isolate the contribution of SAVER-X denoising versus other preprocessing or training parameter choices, measured as correlation retraction.

name: protein-protein-interaction-network-enrichment
description: Use when you have a small, validated gene list (ideally with gene symbols) and need to test whether its members form a non-random interaction network and which KEGG pathways are enriched, as done for shared broiler ASE genes.

name: protein-protein-interaction-network-subsetting
description: Use when you need a PPIN edge list restricted to a specific biological process or custom gene list, to feed into PPIN activity scoring of scRNA-seq expression matrices.

name: protein-protein-interaction-overlap-testing
description: Use when you have a list of predicted candidate regulators (e.g. 73 CRIT NMF-cluster candidates) and a gold-standard regulator list (gold_regulators.xlsx), and need to quantify physical-interaction enrichment between the two sets.

name: protein-sequence-clustering
description: Use when you have Prokka-predicted protein FASTAs from many quality-filtered genomes and need function-based gene clusters plus a genome-by-cluster absence/presence matrix for comparative genomics or feature-based ML.

name: protein-sequence-embedding
description: Use when aligning genes across species (e.g. human vs mouse scRNA-seq) by protein sequence similarity and you need embedding-based gene matches or a gene distance matrix for TACTiCS, as an alternative to BLAST -hit matching.

name: protein-to-coding-gene-mapping
description: Use when integrating modalities measured on different feature spaces (e.g., scRNA-seq vs surface proteins or smFISH) and you need a common gene-level feature matrix to compute cross-modality cell distances.

name: proteomic-module-activity-clustering
description: Use when you have a normalized proteomic expression matrix (proteins x samples) and want to identify significantly shifted or overdispersed pathways and stratify samples into clusters based on their module activity profiles.

name: prs-method-weight-estimation
description: Use when only summary-level eQTL reference statistics (e.g., eQTLGen, n=31,684) are available and per-gene eQTL weights must be estimated for TWAS Stage I using P+T, lassosum, SDPR, and PRS-CS.

name: pseudo-bulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-expression
description: Use when validating that curated single-cell RNA-seq data agree with matched bulk profiles — e.g. pseudo-bulk vs low-input bulk Pearson correlation and kBET batch mixing across early embryo stages (Fig. 1a-b, Supplementary Figs. 1-3).

name: pseudo-bulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when scRNA-seq case/control data (e.g., GSE113197, GSE123926, GSE132509, GSE145926, GSE158055) must be collapsed per patient or disease class into pseudo-bulk profiles to run bulk baselines.

name: pseudo-bulk-construction
description: Use when integrating atlas-scale multi-sample multi-condition single-cell collections (millions of cells, thousands of samples) where per-cell processing of scRNA-seq or CyTOF matrices is computationally prohibitive.

name: pseudo-bulk-genomic-window-coverage-quantification
description: Use when validating that simulated scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads (BAM/FASTQ from scReadSim) resemble real reads, by comparing pseudo-bulk read coverage across fixed-width genomic windows against the real input data.

name: pseudo-bulk-mixture-simulation
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with known per-cell type labels and need pseudo-bulk mixtures with ground-truth proportions to benchmark deconvolution performance of competing marker sets or signature matrices.

name: pseudo-bulk-profile-aggregation-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq reference with per-cell cell-type annotations (e.g., Tabula Sapiens) and need pseudo-bulk per-type profiles as training input for a hierarchical annotation model.

name: pseudo-bulk-read-coverage-quantification
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq alignments and a set of TAR/uTAR intervals and need aggregate (pseudo-bulk) expression per region, e.g., to rank uTARs by total coverage and compare against cell-type-defining PC loadings.

name: pseudo-bulk-sample-level-expression-aggregation
description: Use when a single-cell atlas (e.g. the scMerge2-integrated COVID-19 collection of ~5 million cells, 963 donors, 1298 samples) must be reduced to per-sample, per-cell-type expression signatures for sample-level prediction or comparison of adjusted vs raw logcounts.

name: pseudo-marker-gene-detection
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters are annotated via one-against-all marker gene tests (e.g. Seurat Wilcoxon) and you need to flag markers upregulated in multiple clusters that could cause incorrect or inconsistent cell type annotation.

name: pseudo-replicate-assignment-with-phenotypes
description: Use when integrating multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell collections (e.g. millions of cells across many donors/studies) where batch effects must be removed without confounding biological differences between phenotypes or severity groups.

name: pseudo-replicate-bootstrapping-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or running Scanpro on unreplicated single-cell proportion data (no samples_col), or when determining how many pseudo-replicates (5-8 vs 8+) to use in bootstrapped differential composition analysis.

name: pseudo-space-projection-of-scatac-cells
description: Use when scATAC-seq cells (e.g., mouse cortex ISSAAC-seq) need spatial localization but no spatial ATAC-seq reference exists, and a matched scRNA-seq/ST tissue is available.

name: pseudo-space-reconstruction-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix and a matched spatial transcriptomics reference from the same tissue type, and need to identify spatially heterogeneous cell subpopulations or pairwise cellular spatial associations from single-cell-only data.

name: pseudo-time-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when a cell-cycle pseudo time-series has been recovered (e.g., via reCAT's get_ordIndex/get_hmm_order/get_start pipeline) and an independent benchmark ordering such as an Oscope-recovered series exists to quantify agreement.

name: pseudo-time-method-comparison
description: Use when multiple pseudo-time / cell-ordering methods must be ranked on data with known stage labels (e.g. cell cycle phases), by sweeping cluster numbers k and comparing correlation-scores against the labels.

name: pseudoalignment-signature-quantification
description: Use when you need alignment-free quantification of transcript splicing units or detection/annotation of novel splicing events from RNA-seq reads, and prefer pseudoalignment (kallisto equivalence classes) over STAR-style align-and-count pipelines.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-baseline-execution
description: Use when benchmarking sample-level single-cell methods on runtime or scalability: you need the cheaper aggregation-based baseline (cell-type proportion aggregation per patient) to time against PILOT/PhEMD on a large dataset such as the 1.26M-cell Lupus PBMC data.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-counts
description: Use when single-cell UMI counts per transcript isoform must be compared against bulk 3'-seq or other sample-level references, or when per-sample (not per-cell) abundance estimates are required for validation or downstream statistics.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when you have a cell-level PAS matrix from scPAFA ('fast_Ucell' or 'fast_score_genes') plus cell-level metadata and need sample-level input for MOFA-based multicellular pathway module discovery.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-of-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq counts must be aggregated per cell type into pseudobulk profiles as input for pathway/cytokine activity scoring (decoupleR mlm) or pseudobulk-level differential/statistical tests.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-per-cell-type
description: Use when scRNAseq data (e.g., GSE223109 mouse dermal skin) must be converted to pseudobulk per annotated cell type per time point before circadian rhythm detection or circadian-time prediction.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-per-perturbation
description: Use when Perturb-seq single-cell data have been quantified to 3'UTR isoform level with scUTRquant and per-perturbation (per-guide) bulk-level profiles are needed before computing differential UTR-length statistics.

name: pseudobulk-aggregation-scrnaseq
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts plus per-cell metadata (cell, individual, cell type) must be summarized to individual-by-cell-type pseudobulk expression before fitting LMMs such as CTMM's Free model on CTP data.

name: pseudobulk-count-aggregation-single-cell
description: Use when you have a SingleCellExperiment with sample_id, group_id and cluster_id metadata and need sample-level inference of subpopulation-specific state changes across experimental conditions.

name: pseudobulk-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a cohort-level single-cell count matrix with sample annotations and known or simulated differential expression ground truth must be analyzed cluster-free, or when comparing DE methods' accuracy per cell.

name: pseudobulk-differential-expression-counting
description: Use when benchmarking perturbation metrics for single-cell differential state analysis, or when you need a gene-count baseline (nDEG) to contrast against cell-count-confounded measures on datasets with variable cells per cell type.

name: pseudobulk-dispersion-mean-analysis
description: Use when validating that a scRNA-seq simulation anchored to a reference SingleCellExperiment reproduces sample-to-sample variability, specifically by checking whether pseudobulk dispersion-mean trends match between simulated and reference data.

name: pseudobulk-expression-normalization-scrnaseq
description: Use when integrating multiple public time-course mouse scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., pre-implantation stages from GEO) into one expression matrix that must be batch-harmonized before trajectory, TRN, or ligand-receptor inference.

name: pseudobulk-probability-projection-to-cells
description: Use when trajectory inference was performed on VDJ pseudobulks (e.g. miloR neighbourhoods from the Suo et al. fetal immune atlas data) and you need per-cell pseudotime and CD4/CD8 branch probabilities to score predicted cell fates against annotated labels.

name: pseudobulk-read-coverage-window-binning
description: Use when comparing synthetic scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq reads against real reads at the read-sequence level, or when benchmarking a read simulator's ability to mimic pseudo-bulk coverage patterns across genomic windows.

name: pseudobulk-sample-aggregation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq or simulated tissue samples must be collapsed into pseudobulk profiles and deconvolved against a sketch-derived single-cell reference, with per-sample cell-type proportion estimates compared to known true proportions.

name: pseudobulk-vs-bulk-rnaseq-correlation-validation
description: Use when you need QC of a curated scRNA-seq time-course against a matched bulk RNA-seq reference — e.g. testing pseudo-bulk profiles of embryo stages against low-input bulk profiles before downstream analysis.

name: pseudocount-regularization-of-sample-compositions
description: Use when converting per-sample single-cell cluster count vectors into probability distributions over clusters as input for optimal transport (Wasserstein/EMD) sample-level analysis, especially when some clusters are absent in individual samples.

name: pseudodinucleotide-physicochemical-encoding
description: Use when converting 41 bp RNA m5C sequence segments into numerical features via dinucleotide physicochemical properties, e.g. to reproduce Staem5's PCPseDNC feature block before fusing with PSP, k-mer, and PseEIIP encodings.

name: pseudoinverse-matrix-computation
description: Use when solving a matrix factorization W=(RΣ)+A where the GRN adjacency matrix R (m×m) times the singular matrix Σ of the expression matrix A (m×n) is not invertible, so W must be recovered via the pseudoinverse.

name: pseudotemporal-gene-clustering-and-visualization
description: Use when Lamian XDE test results (per-gene fdr.overall from lamian_test/lamian_test_h5, e.g. sex tested at testvar=2 with batch columns adjusted) are available and significant genes must be grouped into pseudotemporal pattern clusters and plotted.

name: pseudotime-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on simulated single-cell datasets with known ground-truth pseudotime, e.g. quantifying pseudotime accuracy via Kendall rank correlation.

name: pseudotime-based-condition-testing
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from two or more conditions (e.g., mock vs TGF-β treatment) must be compared along a shared developmental trajectory, and you need to test differential topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection, or condition-specific gene expression along lineages.

name: pseudotime-based-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when time-series scRNA-seq data already have (or need) Monocle3 pseudotime and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose abundance changes significantly along pseudotime.

name: pseudotime-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when pseudotime orderings from redPATH and baseline methods must be quantitatively compared on the same filtered expression matrix against known cell type/stage labels using CI, BI, KC, and POS scores.

name: pseudotime-benchmarking-on-real-datasets
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has a known number of branches and cell-type ordering (e.g., CMP GSE72857 with eight branches, HSMM with two, MEF with three) and you must choose which TI method to trust before pseudotime-based downstream analysis.

name: pseudotime-binned-pal-averaging
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has a cell pseudotime/trajectory ordering (e.g., monocle3) and the goal is to identify which MSigDB KEGG/BIOCARTA pathways are coordinated and active at successive developmental stages.

name: pseudotime-branch-visualization
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells from a new condition (e.g., Gfi1-/-, Irf8-/-, double-knockout GMPs) must be projected onto an existing wild-type branching trajectory to read off branch-level fate allocation.

name: pseudotime-branching-assignment
description: Use when you have run CellPath's all_in_one() on scRNA-seq data with scVelo-computed velocities and need per-cell pseudotime and branching assignments to identify lineage paths (e.g., α/β/δ endocrine fates) or run path-level differential expression.

name: pseudotime-capture-time-correlation
description: Use when a pseudotime method has been fit on scRNA-seq data whose cells have known physical capture/sampling times, and you need an external check that the latent ordering recapitulates real time progression.

name: pseudotime-cell-ordering
description: Use when you have a merged, quantile-normalized scRNA-seq matrix spanning sequential developmental stages (e.g. pre-implantation mouse embryos) and need cells ordered along pseudotime for trajectory-based or temporal-communication analyses.

name: pseudotime-cell-type-correlation-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has a known biological ordering of cell types along a lineage and you need to score pseudotime from Cytopath or baselines (Slingshot, Monocle3, PAGA, VeTra, Cellpath) against that ground truth.

name: pseudotime-concordance-metric-computation
description: Use when you have per-cell pseudotime and fate-probability values from two trajectory inference implementations run on the same single-cell VDJ dataset and need quantitative concordance metrics to benchmark them.

name: pseudotime-correlated-gene-heatmap-generation
description: Use when pseudotime trajectories are inferred for a CellexalVR cell selection (e.g. slingshot on four clusters) and a pseudotime-ordered heatmap of correlated marker genes with ten colour groups is required.

name: pseudotime-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a hyperbolic scPhere embedding of a time-course single-cell dataset (e.g., C. elegans embryo GSE126954, 86,024 cells) must be checked for whether latent geometry encodes progression time as a pseudotime signal.

name: pseudotime-correlation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking feature selection on simulated or labeled trajectory data where ground-truth latent progression (e.g., Splatter step vector, SymSim latent time) is available and pseudotime fidelity must be quantified.

name: pseudotime-correlation-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a trajectory inference method on dyntoy synthetic datasets where gold-standard pseudotime and cell-fate labels are known and you must quantify agreement of inferred pseudotime.

name: pseudotime-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data with known gold-standard pseudotime and branch labels, especially when quantifying how technical noise (sigma) or capture efficiency (alpha) affects method performance.

name: pseudotime-dag-construction
description: Use when single-cell multimodal (paired RNA-seq + ATAC-seq) trajectories need a cell-state partial ordering — not a total pseudotime — to support lagged message-passing causal inference over peak-gene pairs.

name: pseudotime-gene-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing trajectory-inference algorithms that each output a pseudotime ordering of the same scRNA-seq cells and you need a quantitative, gene-centric smoothness metric to rank them.

name: pseudotime-gene-expression-kinetics-comparison
description: Use when you need to ask whether cell-type marker gene expression dynamics are conserved or divergent between species/conditions along branched pseudotime trajectories, without manually selecting linear lineage paths.

name: pseudotime-gene-expression-track-visualization
description: Use when a supervised LDA embedding yields a circular or ordered cell arrangement (e.g., cell-cycle phases on LD axes) and you need to confirm phase ordering by tracking marker expression (e.g., CCNB1, CDK1, TPX2) along the inferred pseudotime.

name: pseudotime-kendall-correlation-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating inferred cell orderings on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data with known ground-truth pseudotime and branching structure, to rank TI methods (CellPath, VeTra, Slingshot, CellRank, Vdpt) by per-path Kendall correlation and assignment entropy.

name: pseudotime-lineage-fitting
description: Use when single-cell data from multiple conditions has been embedded (e.g., Dim1/Dim2 reduced-dimension coordinates with cluster and condition labels) and you must decide whether to fit one common trajectory or test for differential topology and differential progression between conditions.

name: pseudotime-lineage-preprocessing-and-filtering
description: Use when preparing multi-sample scRNA-seq data (e.g., HCA bone marrow counts with cell-to-sample annotation and Slingshot/TSCAN pseudotime) before running lamian_test() for trajectory differential expression or density testing.

name: pseudotime-marker-gene-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing trajectory inference methods on the HSMM scRNA-seq dataset, or when quantifying pseudotime accuracy via Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation against known marker genes such as ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2.

name: pseudotime-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing how pseudotime algorithms degrade as the fraction of genes with covariate-pseudotime interactions increases, or when validating a new trajectory method against standard ones on simulated data with a known latent time.

name: pseudotime-noise-injection
description: Use when you need to quantify how sensitive a trajectory-level differential progression test (e.g., condiments progressionTest) is to imperfect pseudotime estimates or incorrect cell-to-lineage assignments from upstream trajectory inference.

name: pseudotime-normalization-single-cell
description: Use when single-cell expression data has an ordering along an inferred trajectory and must be formatted (ptime array, 0-100 rescale, sparse X, optional branches/regix) before running SINGE GLG.

name: pseudotime-ordered-expression-extraction
description: Use when time-course scRNA-seq data have been trajectory-ordered (e.g. monocle3 pseudotime) and you need aligned per-gene expression series along pseudotime to test ligand-receptor co-variation.

name: pseudotime-ordering-with-monocle-and-scuba
description: Decision support for choosing a trajectory-inference method when a scRNA-seq progenitor dataset is suspected to contain a branching event and single-path pseudotime methods (SCUBA, monocle) may miss it.

name: pseudotime-ordering-with-slingshot
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object with Louvain cluster assignments and PCA/UMAP/PHATE reductions) needs trajectory orientation and per-cell pseudotime values along defined lineages.

name: pseudotime-oriented-trajectory-modeling
description: Use when paired single-cell multimodal data (e.g., scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq from the same cells) captures a dynamic process such as differentiation, and a temporally oriented cell-state graph is needed for causal or trajectory modeling.

name: pseudotime-percentile-normalization
description: Use when CellPath assigns a cell to more than one trajectory path (cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) and you need to quantify pseudotime consistency across paths per dataset, e.g. reproducing Figure S4G Diffpst category proportions.

name: pseudotime-perturbation-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when ordered single-cell expression data are available and you need to test whether inferred or assigned pseudotemporal values (rather than the expression matrix itself) drive the quality of pseudotime-based network inference.

name: pseudotime-projection-to-single-cells
description: Use when a miloR pseudobulk object carries pseudotime and branch probabilities computed in VDJ feature space, and per-cell values are needed for plotting, downstream analysis, or benchmarking against Palantir.

name: pseudotime-sample-ranking
description: Use when you have per-sample cell-type/structure cluster distributions (e.g. pathomics .h5ad with clusters_col='Cell_type', sample_col='sampleID', status='status') and need an unsupervised ordering of patients along disease progression.

name: pseudotime-scoring-with-tscan-pos-kendall
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq imputation methods by how well each imputed matrix recovers cell-to-cell trajectory order — e.g., scoring imputed 10x data with TSCAN POS and Kendall rank correlation to rank Bfimpute vs. competitors.

name: pseudotime-similarity-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cell lineage construction from time-course scRNA-seq: you have cells sampled at adjacent time points and want to quantify whether aligned trajectories show higher cell-to-cell similarity (smaller pseudo-time changes) than a baseline alignment.

name: pseudotime-spearman-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a trajectory/pseudotime method has been run on scRNA-seq data with a known cell type ordering and you must quantify agreement per lineage and check consistency across multiple independent runs.

name: pseudotime-stimulation-duration-correlation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset carries a known per-cell elapsed-time label (e.g. stimulation minutes) and you need to test whether velocity-derived pseudotime tracks biological process time, ideally against a no-velocity ablation.

name: pseudotime-to-spatial-scale-transformation
description: Use when single-cell flow cytometry data of radially symmetric multicellular spheroids have been ordered in pseudotime and marker profiles (Ki-67, p27, DNA, RNA) must be recovered versus distance from the spheroid surface.

name: pseudotime-to-vector-field-conversion
description: Use when in silico TF perturbation simulations (e.g., Gata1 KO on the Paul et al. 2015 hematopoiesis data) must be quantified as scores by comparing simulated transitions to the pseudotime differentiation gradient.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have a pseudotime/trajectory ordering (e.g. monocle3 on GSE153162 E17.5 mouse cortex) and the goal is to find which pathway gene sets are active at each developmental stage and how their activity curves cluster over pseudotime.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when a splicing-free velocity or trajectory method must be validated against a multi-omics baseline: compare pseudotime ordering, streamplot direction, and gene phase-portrait dynamics on a shared dataset.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-correlation
description: Use when comparing two single-cell cohorts (e.g., AI-generated/semi-profiled vs. real-profiled) to verify that developmental or disease-progression trajectories are preserved, via Monocle3 pseudotime computed on shared UMAP coordinates.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq captures a continuous biological transition (e.g. naive CD4+ T cell activation through intermediate populations at 0 h, 12 h, 24 h) and you need pathway dynamics along the trajectory rather than a two-group comparison.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq captures a continuous state-transition process (e.g., acinar-to-ductal transdifferentiation) and you need a pseudotime-anchored reference direction to benchmark velocity vectors against, as in the ADM-axis concordance task.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a single-cell multi-omic dataset has been co-embedded, batch-corrected (RunHarmony) and sub-clustered, and the goal is to order clusters along a differentiation continuum (e.g. progenitors to myofibroblasts) for GRN inference.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq data from two or more conditions must be placed on a common trajectory to ask whether conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection between lineages, or gene expression along lineages.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when you have single-cell counts with known developmental/staged time labels (e.g., Chu GSE75748, Scialdone GSE74994, Petropoulos E-MTAB-3929) and need to test whether imputation recovers true temporal cell order.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when dropout-affected scRNA-seq data has been imputed (e.g., with SERM vs. MAGIC) and the goal is to verify that developmental trajectories and state transitions are recovered, not just gene values.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-slingshot
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. GSE81682 mouse HSPC from Nestorowa et al., 2016) must be ordered along a pseudotime trajectory with slingshot and visualized as group-wise colour groups in CellexalVR.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-visualization
description: Use when evaluating whether pseudotime-based approaches such as TSCAN can identify differentiation pathways on single-cell RNA-seq data given the same number of clusters as a class-informed method, or when comparing trajectory inference to visualization baselines.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-inference-with-scfates
description: Use when you have SiFT-filtered AnnData expression (e.g. local spatial signal removed via a coordinate-based kernel) and need to order cells along a trajectory and split genes into early/late pseudotime groups.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-signaling-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells form continuous pseudotemporal trajectories (e.g. E14.5 embryonic skin dermal/epidermal states) and you need cell-state-specific ligand-receptor signaling rather than cluster-level communication.

name: pseudotime-trajectory-tree-alignment
description: Use when two scRNA-seq datasets each have branching pseudotime trajectories (multiple lineages) and you need to match corresponding clusters/lineages across datasets without pre-selecting which single lineages to compare.

name: pseudotime-tree-visualization
description: Use when a multi-sample scRNA-seq pseudotime tree has just been inferred (e.g. via infer_tree_structure with origin.marker and number.cluster) and you need to inspect or publish the trajectory's branch structure and cell ordering.

name: pseudotime-vs-collection-time-outlier-verification
description: Use when a scRNA-seq trajectory inference run shows cells whose pseudotime ordering contradicts their known collection time point, and you want to automatically remove such outliers via fair sampling.

name: pseudouridine-site-fragment-extraction
description: Use when constructing a training/testing dataset of RNA fragments centered on known Ψ sites from RMBase coordinates plus reference genome FASTAs, especially to train or benchmark Ψ site classifiers on human, mouse, or yeast data.

name: pseudouridine-site-gene-list-annotation
description: Use when you have a list of genes with predicted Ψ sites (e.g., MU-PseUDeep human transcriptome scan at >0.99 precision) and need GO/pathway/disease over-representation against a protein-coding background.

name: psi-quantification-from-splice-sites
description: Use when you have read-level splice-site tables from Nanopore long reads (e.g., aligned to GRCh38 with minimap2 v2.24) and need bulk PSI per internal exon, especially to quantify how UMI-consensus correction shifts PSI for constitutive exons.

name: pu-learning-cell-calling-inference
description: Use when you have a raw unfiltered droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (h5/mtx) and need to distinguish cell-free from cell-containing droplets, especially to recover genuine low-count cells below a total-count filtering threshold.

name: public-dataset-download-and-reformatting
description: Use when importing public scRNA-seq studies into Cellenium or preparing .h5ad study files whose .uns dictionary must contain ontologized metadata (title, description, NCBI taxonomy species, MeSH disease, NCIT tissue).

name: public-geo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a study needs raw or processed public transcriptomics data (e.g. GEO accessions, Zenodo archives, GitHub processed files) for re-analysis, meta-analysis, or reproduction of published findings.

name: public-geo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark requires 25 real scRNA-seq datasets with known cell-type labels and accession IDs (GSE/E-MTAB/SRP), or when populating the scISR ARI comparison pipeline with raw expression matrices from GEO/ArrayExpress.

name: public-rnaseq-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a new disease/control RNA-seq dataset is available via a public accession (GEO/ENA) and the goal is isoform-level quantification and dMDT switching analysis compatible with the CanIsoNet database schema.

name: public-scrna-seq-dataset-acquisition-from-geo
description: Use when an analysis needs the original public mouse pre-implantation time-course single-cell count matrices (e.g. GSE38495 for MII oocytes, GSE45719 for E1-E4.0 stages) plus matched low-input bulk RNA-seq held outside GEO in the TimeTalk Figshare deposit.

name: publication-figure-reproduction
description: Use when a target figure reports a specific statistic (e.g. a correlation between a geneset score and a sample-level covariate like VAF/purity) and the underlying parsed dataset and curated gene lists are available in pdacR's Data/ directory.

name: publication-figure-reproduction
description: Use when the goal is to validate or replicate a published quantitative figure by re-running its described pipeline on the original or equivalent data, and a qualitative match can be checked against the reported figure.

name: published-result-reproduction-verification
description: Use when a pipeline (e.g., methylR on a public array dataset like GSE207426) must be validated by reproducing a published count or statistic from an existing differential methylation results table.

name: published-statistics-reproduction

name: pyscenic-pipeline-execution

name: python-object-serialization-of-network-models

name: python-script-orchestration

name: pytorch-deep-clustering-training-scripting
description: Use when implementing an end-to-end deep clustering model in PyTorch for multimodal single-cell data (CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq) where autoencoder reconstruction, KL loss, and K-means clustering losses must be jointly optimized in one training loop.

name: pytorch-forward-pass-verification
description: Use when reproducing tGPT's architecture from the paper's reported hyperparameters and you must confirm the model runs end-to-end on rank-encoded gene sequences before pretraining or feature extraction.

name: pytorch-gradient-verification

name: pytorch-neural-network-implementation
description: Use when building a domain-generalization deep-learning classifier (e.g., Cancer-Finder) that must distinguish malignant vs. non-malignant cells from normalized single-cell gene-expression matrices.

name: pytorch-supervised-model-optimization
description: Use when you already have transfer component analysis (TCA) characteristic/latent matrices for paired spatial transcriptomics (ST) and scRNA-seq data plus ST spot x-y coordinates, and you need to learn a regression mapping to produce per-cell pseudo-space coordinates.

name: q-diffused-kernel-construction

name: q-value-fdr-correction
description: Use when converting bootstrap-derived p-values from pseudotime-based curve fitting (complete vs. flat-line null models) into q-values to call time-dependent DEGs and cell subclusters at a chosen fdr_level (0.01 in the paper).

name: qc-metric-correlation-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq low-dimensional components (e.g., ZINB-WaVE W factors, PCA or ZIFA scores) need to be benchmarked for residual technical effects by correlating them with QC measures like detection rate and total reads.

name: qc-plot-generation
description: Use when a raw Cell Ranger gene-expression matrix has been loaded into a SingCellaR object and you need QC plots (e.g. UMIs vs detected genes) to choose min/max UMI, gene, and mitochondrial-percentage filtering cutoffs before filter_cells_and_genes.

name: qclash-count-table-aggregation
description: Use when you have multiple qCLASH hybrid (.hyb) files (e.g. replicates from GEO GSE101978) and need per-replicate plus combined counts of hybrid segment types and 5p/3p miRNA segments with tabular and plotted output.

name: qclash-hybrid-qc-filtering
description: Use when input is a hyb-format chimeric RNA file from miRNA/target ligation experiments (CLASH, qCLASH) that needs integrity checking before downstream type, target, or fold analyses.

name: qclash-replicate-data-pooling-and-filtering
description: Use when multiple qCLASH or CLASH replicate hyb files (with associated vienna/fold files) must be QC-checked, filtered, and pooled for grouped analysis of miRNA targets across replicates.

name: qcm-qcc-model-quality-evaluation
description: Use when a sparsely-connected autoencoder analysis of scRNAseq clusters needs a quantitative verdict on whether the autoencoder model and a given cluster's reconstruction are trustworthy (e.g., verifying QCM/QCC > 0.5 for NK and naive T cell clusters of setA).

name: qdiffused-kernel-affinity-graph-construction
description: Use when you need full-dimensionality single-cell clustering or embedding without feature selection or dimensionality reduction — e.g., unsupervised clustering of small organ-tissue samples (< 10,000 cells) benchmarked against scVI/Seurat embeddings.

name: qphate-embedding-biomarker-thresholding
description: Use when transferring single-cell atlas latent structure (e.g., the stage-4 Human Colon Cancer Atlas c295) onto bulk RNA patient profiles to create binary biomarkers for survival/differential-treatment-effect testing, and standard PHATE or NMF-derived biomarkers lack statistical significance.

name: qq-plot-construction-for-pvalues
description: Use when you have a large set of null (permutation/simulated) association p-values and need to assess statistical calibration — e.g., verifying type I error control against identity-line expectations in the tails.

name: qq-plot-fdr-visualization
description: Use when a scTenifoldNet diffRegulation table (gene, distance, Z, FC, p.value, p.adj) needs visual goodness-of-fit assessment against chi-square(1) expectations, e.g. to reproduce the Figure 2C / readmeExample.png style H0-vs-HA comparison.

name: qtl-variant-classification-sqtl-versus-eqtl
description: Use when GWAS summary statistics are available and you need to compare the phenotypic contribution of splicing-associated variants against variants affecting only gene expression via functional annotation enrichment.

name: quad-to-decimal-barcode-encoding
description: Use when identifying fixed-length cell barcodes or UMI flanking sequences in SPLiT-seq reads and you need constant-time matching of 8-nt indicator sequences against a barcodeList instead of per-read alignment (e.g. BLAST/BWA).

name: quadratic-programming-flux-balance-analysis
description: Use when estimating per-sample metabolic reaction fluxes from bulk RNA-seq gene expression: you have MRAS reaction scores, a chosen medium file (human_blood or cell_medium), and need parsimonious fluxes across all 13,082 Human-GEM reactions.

name: quality-control-filtering-of-scrna-seq-counts
description: Use when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix is about to be fed into scATOMIC (or similar hierarchical classifiers), to drop cells whose mitochondrial read fraction exceeds 25% or which express fewer than 500 unique features.

name: quantile-based-gene-filtering
description: Use when you have a raw gene-by-cell count matrix (e.g. from GEMLI_example_data_matrix.RData) and need to pre-select a small set of highly expressed and variably expressed candidate memory genes before lineage inference.

name: quantile-bound-landmark-similarity-scoring

name: quantile-normalization-ablation-comparison
description: Use when building or validating a Ciclops cross-platform transfer model on transcriptomic datasets (e.g., RNA-seq train, microarray test) and you need to decide whether quantile normalization should be kept on or skipped via --no_quantile.

name: quantile-normalization-cross-platform
description: Use when preparing .csv training and validation expression matrices with unequal platform distributions and missing values before running Ciclops cross-platform clinical outcome prediction, or when reproducing the Ciclops preprocessing stage.

name: quantile-normalization-of-count-matrices
description: Use when tall-format filtered scRNA-seq count data must have per-cell expression distributions standardized across cells (e.g., to remove library-composition/distribution shifts) while preserving within-cell relative expression rank order, at scales requiring Spark.

name: quantile-normalization-of-merged-expression-matrices
description: Use when pseudo-bulk profiles computed from scRNA-seq (e.g. per pre-implantation stage from GSE38495/GSE45719) must be compared against bulk RNA-seq profiles from a different platform, where column-wise expression distributions differ and must be forced onto a common scale.

name: quantile-normalization-of-rna-seq-expression
description: Use when a filtered RNA-seq expression matrix spanning multiple stress conditions must be made distribution-comparable across samples prior to computing gene-gene correlations for network construction.

name: quantile-normalized-microarray-data-processing
description: Use when microarray intensity data has already been quantile-normalized via PIMENTo's Preprocess Data command and background noise must be separated from signal by choosing a log2 cutoff from the intensity histogram before downstream analysis.

name: quantile-quantile-calibration-plot-visualization
description: Use when validating p-value calibration of gene-set enrichment or DE methods under a permuted/simulated null: pooled null p-values per method must be inspected via lambda_gc and QQ plots before trusting real-data calls.

name: quantile-vs-loess-normalization-comparison
description: Use when raw microarray intensity data must be normalized and there is no a priori reason to prefer quantile or LOESS; compare both, inspect MA plots for linearity, and check the dendrogram for batch effects.

name: quartile-based-statistical-filtering
description: Use when you have a continuous per-cell FiRE rareness score vector and need a binary rare-cell label per cell (0/1) via a distribution-based, parameter-free cutoff on scRNA-seq data.

name: quasi-trend-preserved-gene-grouping
description: Use when building a quantitative low-dimensional representation of single-cell RNA-seq cells by clustering genes whose expression-rank vectors show akin (not identical) trends into landmark consensus vectors.

name: quasibinomial-power-curve-fitting
description: Use when planning scCODA case-control scRNA-seq experiments: compositional count data with known ground-truth changes have been simulated per (baseline abundance × fold-change × sample size), and per-setting detection rates are available.

name: query-based-cell-annotation-transfer
description: Use when new scRNA-seq data (h5ad/AnnData) needs cell type labels or continuous fate annotations transferred from a curated reference dataset, especially across batches or species, or when screening for putative novel cell types rejected by the query.

name: query-cell-projection-onto-reference-embedding
description: Use when a normalized query dataset (e.g., log(CP10k+1)) must be placed into an existing integrated reference embedding — e.g., a 10x 5' PBMC query against 3'v1/3'v2 donors, or annotation/trajectory localization against a saved Symphony reference.

name: query-expression-matrix-loading
description: Use when a new scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. the Lafleur Ptpn2-KO/WT P14 or Yao Tox-KO query matrices) must be loaded as a query object before Run.ProjecTILs projection onto a reference map.

name: query-latency-curve-visualization
description: Use when comparing the querying-time scalability of cell-querying tools across increasing reference sizes, e.g. validating that a method scales to 1,000,000-cell references before deployment on large scRNA-seq databases.

name: query-reference-gene-alignment
description: Use when preparing a query scRNA-seq AnnData for TOSICA.pre() prediction after training on a ref_adata, and the query's var_names (genes) may differ from or be ordered differently than the reference genes.

name: query-result-parquet-export
description: Use when a single-cell expression or annotation query (e.g. SELECT ... FROM X/obs with LIMIT or WHERE clauses) has been executed against an on-disk or in-memory AnnSQL DuckDB database and the result must be persisted as a Parquet file for reuse.

name: query-throughput-analysis

name: quic-convex-optimization
description: Use when inferring a sparse gene co-expression network from normalized single-cell expression data for a fixed gene set, after computing scLink's robust correlation matrix, and needing to select lambda by BIC.

name: quickhull-computational-geometry

name: qval-based-pathway-ranking

description: Use when gene-expression data from CRC pre-clinical models (cell lines, organoids, PDXs) needs CMS1-CMS4 subtype calls, and you must quantify how the original primary-CRC classifier's stromal/immune signal dependency leaves samples (notably CMS4) unclassified.

name: random-forest-classifier-inference
description: Use when you have a gene-cluster absence/presence matrix for genomes labeled 'unknown' and literature-derived lifestyle metadata plus trained binary random forest classifiers (scikit-learn, n_estimators = 50) to predict a lifestyle per genome at >0.8 confidence.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when you have PacBio long-read RNA-seq BAM data processed by dsRID into positive (dsRID_train.tsv) and negative (dsRID_null.tsv) dsRNA region tables and need to train and validate a classifier that discriminates candidate dsRNA regions.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when assessing whether augmenting a sparse or downsampled scRNA-seq cell population (e.g., cluster 2 from Fresh 68k PBMCs) improves downstream classification robustness, with F1 score as the metric.

name: random-forest-classifier-training
description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrix with trusted per-cell labels (cancer, immune, stromal) is available and the goal is to train a hierarchical supervised classifier or benchmark it via stratified cross-validation.

name: random-forest-cross-validation-classification
description: Use when benchmarking how well cell-cell communication features (tensor factor loadings or UMAP embeddings from LR communication scores) separate biological phenotypes such as COVID-19 status and severity.

name: random-forest-discrimination-auc
description: Decision support for quantifying how realistic synthetic scRNA-seq cells are: train a random forest on real-vs-generated labels and use the resulting AUC, where values near 0.5 (positive control ~0.52) indicate generated cells are indistinguishable from real PBMC cells.

name: random-forest-driver-gene-classification
description: Use when classifying unlabelled cancer genes into TSGs/OGs from somatic mutation feature matrices (37 ratio-metric/entropy features), e.g. pan-cancer or tissue-specific driver gene prediction with CGC training labels.

name: random-forest-ensemble-inference
description: Use when a small labelled gene set (e.g. 136 TSGs and 76 OGs from CGC) must be extended to unlabelled genes using somatic mutation-derived features, and consensus across ensemble fold models is needed to reduce overfitting.

name: random-forest-ensemble-training
description: Use when classifying candidate intronic terminal exons (or similar genomic regions) from conventional RNA-seq alignments, needing a supervised model with region-level features and held-out AUROC-style validation.

name: random-forest-feature-importance-ranking
description: Use when a small, class-imbalanced labelled gene set (e.g. 136 TSGs vs 76 OGs) must be ranked by which mutation-type features (entropy, frequency, ratio-metric) drive random forest classification, avoiding single-model importance instability.

name: random-forest-gene-importance-ranking
description: Use when a log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with initial cluster labels needs a supervised, label-aware gene ranking (HIG) to complement unsupervised HVG selection before rare cell type detection.

name: random-forest-gradient-boosting-classification
description: Use when classifying single-cell RNA-seq cells from CKG or gene expression feature matrices with supervised tree-based models, or when RF/GBM feature_importances_ rankings are needed to compare feature representations.

name: random-forest-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when classifying genes as TSGs vs OGs from a pre-processed mutation feature matrix (e.g. FeatureMat.tsv with 37 ratio-metric/entropy features) with CGC labels, and stable hyper-parameters are needed to avoid overfitting on a small labelled set.

name: random-forest-lifestyle-classification
description: Use when gene cluster absence/presence matrices paired with literature-based lifestyle metadata are available and the goal is to classify held-out genomes' lifestyle, including leave-one-species-out validation for novel species.

name: random-forest-normal-cancer-classification
description: Use when you need computational validation that gene communities extracted from fused networks are relevant, by testing whether they classify TCGA normal/cancer samples better than DE or random gene sets.

name: random-forest-out-of-sample-classification-evaluation
description: Use when you need a label-based, out-of-sample measure of embedding quality — e.g. scoring ivis embeddings of BMMC CyTOF subsamples with manually gated cell-population labels via held-out classification accuracy.

name: random-forest-permutation-feature-importance
description: Use when a random-forest model (e.g., dsRID trained on Pacbio_AD_data.tsv) needs per-feature contribution scores rather than generic impurity-based importance, to explain which molecular traits drive dsRNA region prediction.

name: random-forest-pixel-classification
description: Use when multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images need pixel-level compartment labeling (nucleus, membrane, cytoplasm) to seed single-cell segmentation and enable per-cell marker quantification.

name: random-forest-probability-score-summarization
description: Use when you have per-cell scATOMIC prediction scores from run_scATOMIC() across the pan-cancer TME hierarchy and need to convert raw class probabilities into per-layer confidence cut-offs and 'unclassified' relabelling.

name: random-forest-signaling-range-inference
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq data with a spatial cell–cell distance matrix (e.g. from a SpaOTsc optimal transport mapping) and known ligand, receptor, and downstream gene lists, and you need to estimate the spatial range of a signaling pathway in micrometers.

name: random-forest-vs-logistic-regression-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking which classifier (random forest vs logistic regression) better drives active learning cell selection from single-cell expression data when the initial training set is randomly chosen and may not contain all cell types.

name: random-gene-set-size-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type replicability (e.g., neuron vs non-neuron AUROC) with random gene sets and you need to test how set size (100 vs 800 genes) or cross-validation variability bins influence MetaNeighbor performance.

name: random-geneset-null-distribution-sampling
description: Use when quantifying pathway/module activity from a normalized gene expression matrix and you need empirical p-values for PC1-based activity statistics (L1, Median Exp) that distinguish shifted from overdispersed gene sets.

name: random-marker-set-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking a marker-selection method (e.g., scGeneFit on CBMC scRNA-seq) and a size-matched random-gene baseline is needed to show that reported classification error reflects informed marker choice rather than panel size.

name: random-matrix-eigenvector-localization-analysis
description: Use when denoising a sparse single-cell gene expression matrix (e.g. 95%-sparse scRNA-seq) and you need to decide which eigenvectors/gene sets reflect signal versus sparsity artifacts.

name: random-matrix-simulation
description: Use when you need a reproducible, size-controlled workload to benchmark linear-algebra implementations (SVD variants, matrix multiplication, core-count scaling) before applying them to real data.

name: random-matrix-theory-noise-filtering
description: Use when analyzing sparse scRNA-seq count data and a data-driven signal/noise cutoff on PCA-like dimensions is needed instead of subjective elbow-inspection of eigenvalues.

name: random-restart-optimization
description: Use when a discrete assignment problem (e.g., mapping cell clusters to palette colors) must be solved by minimizing a Frobenius-norm graph-matching objective, and local search alone risks poor local minima.

name: random-sampling-permutation-significance-testing
description: Use when judging whether an observed overlap between a candidate regulator list and a reference set (e.g. gold circRNA regulators in a Harmonizome interaction or co-expression dataset) exceeds chance, via random-sampling permutations.

name: random-seed-replicate-aggregation
description: Use when the method being benchmarked involves stochastic steps (random clustering, random subsampling) and you need seed-averaged scores or robustness estimates across parameter sweeps.

name: random-split-cross-validation-aggregation
description: Use when comparing model variants (multimodal vs unimodal) on a prediction task with specificity annotation and you need statistically robust mean performance across random splits rather than a single train/test result.

name: random-subsampling-stability-assessment
description: Use when you must demonstrate that a supervised single-cell drug-response predictor's performance is not an artifact of a single train/test split, by measuring metric variation across repeated random stratified samplings of labeled scRNA-seq cells.

name: random-surfing-transition-matrix-computation
description: Use when constructing a cell-cell relationship graph from a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix: after building the unweighted KNN graph, to compute transition probabilities and the PPMI-weighted adjacency.

name: random-tree-null-distribution-testing
description: Use when you must judge whether a reconstructed phylogeny (e.g., a LinRace subtree for cells sharing an identical barcode but from different clones) carries real topological signal, by comparing its distance to a reference against random trees over the same tip set.

name: random-trial-aggregation-across-datasets
description: Use when comparing two sketching/sampling methods across multiple single-cell datasets and sketch sizes, where robust Hausdorff distance to the full dataset quantifies representativeness and stochastic trials must be aggregated.

name: random-walk-hitting-time-computation
description: Use when reconstructing pseudotime/directionality on a PARC cluster graph for single-cell trajectory data (e.g., mESC CyTOF cell-cycle), where a root cluster is known and hitting-time-based ordering is needed.

name: random-walk-restart-label-propagation
description: Use when scoring per-cell pathway activity in normalized scRNA-seq data (e.g. Seurat objects) to fetch the cells most relevant to a curated gene set (GO, Hallmarks, KEGG, BIOCARTA) without clustering.

name: random-walk-restart-pathway-activity-scoring
description: Use when a gene set's spatial/density relevance has been established (compute.kld p.adj < 0.05) and per-cell pathway activity scores or positive/negative cell labels are needed for downstream spatial or classification analysis.

name: random-walk-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a lazy-teleporting random-walk/MCMC stage improves pseudotime accuracy on time-series single-cell (e.g., CyTOF) data against ablated variants and TI baselines.

name: random-walk-transition-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have a pre-processed N_cells x N_genes single-cell expression matrix and need to model cell-fate transition dynamics as a Markov random walk before attractor/coarse-graining analysis.

name: random-walk-transition-probability-matrix-coarse-graining
description: Use when single-cell snapshot transcriptome data must be decomposed into stable attractor basins versus transient/transition cells, e.g. Pro-B to Pre-B differentiation, EMT, or Langevin simulation wells, with basin count guided by the EPI eigen-gap.

name: random-walk-with-restart-diffusion
description: Use when a pre-processed N×D single-cell expression matrix must be converted into per-cell stationary diffusion distributions over a k-nearest-neighbor graph as a precursor to pseudotime ordering or BKFD dimensionality reduction.

name: random-walk-with-restart-embedding
description: Use when classifying scRNA-seq cells to Cell Ontology terms — including unseen cell types with no annotated training cells — or when cell type embeddings and cell-by-gene expression matrices must share one low-dimensional space.

name: randomized-svd-computation
description: Use when a large normalized single-cell expression matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) needs a rank-k SVD, or when the low-rank parameter k must be selected automatically from the top-100 singular-value spectrum.

name: rank-based-gene-set-scoring
description: Use when input is a scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) count matrix and per-cell gene set activity scores are needed using rank-based scorers such as ssGSEA, singscore, RBO, or summed_up ranks, especially where sparsity/noise motivates neighbor-graph smoothing first.

name: rank-based-gene-signature-scoring
description: Use when you need rapid per-cell pathway activity scores on large-scale scRNA-seq data (e.g., >100k cells, >10^3 pathways) and existing tools like UCell, AUCell, or AddModuleScore are too slow.

name: rank-based-mann-whitney-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when scoring cell-type or biological-process gene signatures on a gene-vs-cell scRNA-seq matrix, Seurat object, or SingleCellExperiment, and you need scores that are unaffected by dataset composition.

name: rank-based-vs-distance-based-pseudotime-comparison
description: Use when multiple bifurcation-capable trajectory inference methods (e.g., STREAM/ElPiGraph, Monocle2) have been run on a branching single-cell dataset and you need an objective, marker-gene-anchored measure of pseudotime accuracy to rank the methods.

name: rank-biased-overlap-scoring
description: Use when scoring single-cell RNA-seq cells (Scanpy AnnData h5ad) for membership in a gene set using a rank-based statistic, e.g. testing whether an _UP/_DN signature separates two cell states such as injured vs control endothelial cells.

name: rank-capping-zero-inflation-tail-correction
description: Use when scoring gene signatures on sparse single-cell RNA-seq matrices where thousands of zero-expression genes per cell would dominate per-cell gene rankings, and scores must be robust to dataset size and composition.

name: rank-constrained-matrix-optimization
description: Use when you have a raw single-cell expression matrix and need to learn cell-to-cell similarities robust to noise, outliers and dropouts, rather than using a fixed distance metric.

name: rank-correlation-feature-scoring
description: Use when a data matrix and response are given and features must be scored for relevance and redundancy with a fast, robust criterion — especially for fat datasets (e.g. 100x500, 1000x500) or mixed-type variables.

name: rank-correlation-pvalue-assessment
description: Use when evaluating a differential expression detection method against simulated data where true per-gene log fold changes (logFC_theoretical from getDEgenes) are known and ranking quality, not just binary detection, must be quantified.

name: rank-distribution-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when evaluating GRN inference on the SINGE retinoic acid mESC dataset and the overall precision-recall evaluation needs to be broken down per regulator against the ESCAPE gold standard.

name: rank-normalisation-and-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when combining interaction scores from multiple CCC methods with incomparable magnitudes and differing interaction coverage into a single consensus ranking, e.g. as the preprocessing stage before Robust Rank Aggregation in LIANA.

name: rank-overlap-analysis-of-ligand-receptor-interactions
description: Use when you must benchmark or stress-test CCC inference methods (CellChat, CellPhoneDB, Connectome, NATMI, SingleCellSignalR, iTALK, Cytotalk) for sensitivity to noisy cell data or corrupted ligand-receptor prior-knowledge resources.

name: rank-parameter-sweep-evaluation
description: Use when tuning the LinQ-View ADT purity score's rank hyperparameter, or when evaluating how a cluster-scoring metric's parameter behaves across datasets with different surface-protein (ADT) feature counts.

name: rank-preservation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking whether a cell-type perturbation metric keeps stable rankings under varying cells-per-cell-type subsampling, or when demonstrating cell-count confounding of differential-expression-count metrics.

name: rank-selection-by-reconstruction-error
description: Use when a 4D-communication tensor (cell types x LR pairs x contexts x cell types) has been built with cell2cell and the number of latent communication factors must be chosen before running non-negative tensor component analysis.

name: rank-sum-statistical-testing
description: Use when two independent sets of scores must be compared for a significant shift — e.g. donor-pair NMI values from MuDCoD vs. PisCES at one time point — and a nonparametric test on unpaired samples is appropriate.

name: ranked-feature-table-generation
description: Use when you have a labeled feature matrix (e.g. scRNA-seq expression with phenotype labels) and need a per-feature numeric score to produce a full descending feature ranking, as a baseline filter before or alongside marker-set methods like GreedyPC.

name: ranked-gene-list-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when scTenifoldNet's diffRegulation output (genes ranked by differential regulation distance with BH-adjusted p-values) is available and the goal is to identify enriched biological processes from that ranked list.

name: ranked-list-correlation-against-ground-truth
description: Use when simulated or controlled datasets have a known ground-truth set of condition-associated key genes and you must quantify how accurately competing gene-ranking methods recover them.

name: ranked-list-linear-discounting
description: Use when you have a ranked, per-cell-type marker list (e.g., MASI's cell_markers dict from marker_identification) and need to weight markers by rank before summing marker expression into cell-type scores.

name: rare-cell-cluster-identification
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (thousands to tens of thousands of cells, e.g. 68k PBMC or 4491-cell intestinal crypt) must be scanned for minor cell populations that bulk clustering toolkits like Seurat or Scater miss.

name: rare-cell-cluster-separation-assessment
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering comparison must determine whether any method can separate known rare subclusters, and when external metrics (ARI/NMI) and internal metrics (per-cell silhouette) should be reported against a Louvain resolution sweep.

name: rare-cell-clustering-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a new rare-cell or subcluster clustering method must be validated for label-recall ity on simulated scRNA-seq data with known ground-truth cell-type labels, comparing ARI/NMI/silhouette against clustering baselines.

name: rare-cell-clustering-with-dropclust
description: Use when you already have per-cell rareness scores (FiRE) and IQR-thresholded rare cells (e.g. 727 cells from ~20k Arc-ME profiles) and need to partition them into minor sub-clusters for marker-based annotation.

name: rare-cell-count-validation
description: Use when reproducing FiRE rare-cell calls on ~68k-cell scRNA-seq data and you must verify both the expected rare-cell count (4238) and cluster-level specificity of top-scoring cells.

name: rare-cell-detection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing rare-cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq data, or when quantifying how few differentially expressed genes a detector needs and how runtimes scale to tens of thousands of profiles.

name: rare-cell-detection-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify and compare rare cell detection accuracy of scCAD against FiRE, GapClust, and GiniClust3, e.g. reproducing the DE-gene robustness/sensitivity analysis (Supplementary Fig. 11) on artificial or 1%Jurkat.h5 data.

name: rare-cell-gap-distance-quantification
description: Use when you have a large scRNA-seq expression matrix and need per-cell nearest-neighbour distance statistics (D<m,k>, ∆D<m,k>, ∆∆D<m,k>, skewness<k>) to detect rare cell clusters via inter-cluster gaps.

name: rare-cell-identification
description: Use when you need per-cell rareness scores from a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (tens of thousands of cells) and clustering-based rare cell tools (RaceID, GiniClust) are too slow or memory inefficient.

name: rare-cell-population-denoising-assessment
description: Use when comparing denoising performance of single-cell methods on downsampled count data, especially when rare cell states (e.g., pericytes, microfold cells, microglial cells) are present and neighbor-smoothing may bias results.

name: rare-cell-population-detection
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset is too large for downstream analysis (e.g., >200k cells) and a rare cell population must be recovered without uniform subsampling that overlooks rare states.

name: rare-cell-population-identification
description: Use when a broadly-defined scRNA-seq cluster is suspected heterogeneous (e.g. a stromal/mesenchymal cluster that may hide CAF subtypes, or immune clusters hiding fine-grained subtypes) and rare, low-abundance subpopulations must be recovered from Seurat-processed data.

name: rare-cell-subtype-frequency-quantification
description: Use when clustering an already-annotated single-cell subset (e.g. SingleR-annotated T/NK cells from RA patient PBMCs) and the goal is to resolve rare subtypes and doublets and report their cluster frequencies.

name: rare-cell-type-cluster-purity-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether an iterative cluster decomposition/merging step improves the purity (occupy rate) of rare cell types in their dominant clusters, as in scCAD's I-cluster vs. M-cluster comparison (Supplementary Table 9).

name: rare-cell-type-embedding-separation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain dominant/common cell types plus rare populations and the goal is a 2D embedding that visibly separates the rare clusters, evaluated via silhouette index against t-SNE and UMAP baselines.

name: rare-cell-type-multistage-clustering
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq clustering run merges a rare annotated cell type into a larger cluster and a multi-stage re-clustering could isolate it.

name: rare-cell-type-recovery-quantification
description: Use when testing whether oversampling rare cell types (e.g. CD4T, mast, plasma, pDC, cholangiocyte) improves reference-based single-cell annotation accuracy, and you need a per-type F1/count comparison table.

name: rare-cell-type-representation-assessment
description: Use when a subsampled single-cell dataset (e.g. a scValue, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, TreeHopper, KH, or Uniform sketch) must be checked for loss of rare cell types before downstream ML/DL tasks such as cell-type annotation.

name: rare-celltype-balancing-for-classification
description: Use when preparing a cell-by-gene reference matrix (e.g., SELINA xx_expr.txt with paired xx_meta.txt labels) for supervised cell-type annotation and some cell types are far outnumbered by majority types.

name: rare-cluster-threshold-classification
description: Use when after cluster decomposition and merging in scCAD, you need to score each M-cluster's rarity from isolation-forest anomaly scores and decide which sub-clusters count as rare cell types.

name: rare-population-cluster-size-thresholding
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering result may hide rare cell types inside large clusters, and you need to recursively decompose oversized clusters (R*n threshold) and merge near-identical sub-clusters before rare-population scoring.

name: rare-population-detection-curve-visualization
description: Use when experimental-design questions ask how many cells (N) must be sequenced to detect a rare subpopulation (e.g., 5% or 10% of cells) and ARI-vs-N curves per method are needed.

name: rare-population-proportion-scaling
description: Use when benchmarking rare-cell detection tools across controlled rare-population sizes and DE strengths, or when deciding whether a detector (e.g. GapClust) retains accuracy as the planted minor cluster grows from 2 to 100 cells.

name: rarity-and-subtlety-parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when you must determine how far MetaNeighbor AUROC performance degrades as a held-out cell type becomes rare (1-20% incidence) or only subtly different from the out-group, before trusting a replicability call.

name: ratio-mode-latent-variable-modeling-of-paired-counts
description: Use when input consists of paired, cell-by-event count matrices (inclusion/exclusion or spliced/unspliced reads) from multi-sample single-cell data and the goal is a harmonized latent embedding plus imputed ratio (e.g., logit PSI) values.

name: raw-idat-test-data-ingestion
description: Use when reproducing or smoke-testing the methylR pipeline on the authors' distributed test dataset, or when Illumina 450K/EPIC raw methylation data (IDAT) must be ingested into a locally running methylR container.

name: raycast-collision-detection
description: Use when implementing per-cell selection in a VR scatter/DR plot where datasets with tens of thousands of points (e.g., the >30k-cell mouse gastrulation GSE87038 coordinates) make per-point Unity colliders infeasible.

name: rbf-gaussian-process-prior-specification
description: Use when fitting TCM to temporal single-cell RNA-seq data and you must configure the radial prototype landscape and the RBF-kernel Gaussian-process prior over prototype positions before variational EM fitting.

name: rbp-binding-site-disruption-analysis
description: Use when you have a catalog of splicing QTLs (e.g. from sQTLseekeR2 on GTEx) plus ENCODE eCLIP peak sets and want to identify which RBPs' binding sites are altered by sQTLs relative to non-sQTL variants.

name: rbp-candidate-validation-against-gold-standard
description: Use when an NMF (or other) clustering of candidate RBPs has produced cluster assignments and you must test whether any single cluster is significantly enriched for known gold-standard circRNA regulators before accepting the clustering strategy.

name: rbp-cluster-comparison-statistics
description: Use when a merged CRIT feature matrix plus NMF cluster membership labels are available and the goal is to rank features (e.g., Zg splicing similarity, Zp alteration proportion) that separate predicted circRNA regulators from other RBPs.

name: rbp-ncrna-interaction-network-construction
description: Use when building the prior interaction graph needed to search RBP-ncRNA circuits (RNCs) from multi-omics differential expression scores, e.g. TCGA ESCA/BRCA or APP/PS1 mouse data scored with fRNC.

name: rbp-ncrna-network-module-scoring
description: Use when detected RNC modules (global or local, e.g. from runmodule with FDR = 1e-5) need permutation-based validation of whether their summary scores exceed what random node sets of the same size would achieve.

name: rdr-baf-cna-state-combination
description: Use when both an RDR_Xdata and a BAF_merge_Xdata from XClone runs on the same cells/genes exist and per-cell haplotype-aware copy-number states (including copy-neutral LOH) are needed.

name: rdr-baf-module-configuration-and-execution
description: Use when allele- and haplotype-specific CNA states must be inferred from scRNA-seq RDR and BAF matrices already produced by the xcltk preprocessing pipeline, and per-cell clonal copy-number profiles are needed.

name: rdr-reference-cell-normalization
description: Use when running XClone's RDR module on a gene-by-cell count matrix that contains a known normal/reference cell population, and copy-loss/neutral/gain states must be called relative to that baseline.

name: reaction-activity-score-flux-bound-setting
description: Use when converting a gene-by-sample RNA-seq expression matrix into reaction-level upper/lower bounds for Human-GEM FBA, i.e., capping each of the 13,082 reaction fluxes by its GPR-derived normalized MRAS with a nutrient medium constraint.

name: read-abundance-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing per-cell pathogen read quantification across multiple scRNAseq tools (e.g. SPQ vs Venus/PathogenTrack/ViralTrack) on the same 10x sample to assess concordance of read-abundance estimates.

name: read-barcode-assignment-sc-rnaseq
description: Use when you have FASTQ or FASTA single-cell reads (e.g. 10x Chromium or Visium libraries, noisy long-read scRNA-seq) and need to identify cellular barcodes and UMIs and assign reads to them.

name: read-coverage-peak-calling
description: Use when a BAM of aligned 3'-end-enriched reads (e.g. 10x Chromium scRNA-seq) must be scanned for broad coverage peaks to serve as candidate 3' UTRs against an existing GFF3/GTF gene model.

name: read-depth-binning-at-100kb-resolution
description: Use when preparing high-coverage (>20x) single-cell WGS BAMs for CNA detection or tool benchmarking at small variant sizes (200 kb–5 Mb), where a fixed 100 kb bin resolution harmonizes read depth across callers.

name: read-depth-segmentation
