description: Use when segmenting high-coverage (>20x) PTA-amplified single-cell WGS read-depth profiles into CNAs at 200 kb–5 Mb scales, especially when allele-specific calls and comparison against BAF-agnostic RDR-only callers are needed.

name: read-group-barcoded-bam-splitting
description: Use when a BAM of aligned sequencing reads (e.g. from 10x Chromium single-cell runs) must be split by SAM FLAG reverse-strand bit and RG tag into per-strand, per-read-group BAMs before peak calling or coverage analysis.

name: read-haplotype-assignment-majority-voting
description: Use when performing allele-specific read assignment for ASAS analysis: you have phased per-chromosome VCFs, gzipped FASTQ reads, hg19.fa, and need to label each uniquely aligned read with haplotype 1, 2, or 'discarded'.

name: read-length-filtering-of-ribosome-footprints
description: Use when preprocessing Ribo-seq FastQ files and only footprints within a defined nucleotide-length window (e.g. 25–35 nt, or a user-fixed range such as 20–22 nt) should be retained for analysis.

name: read-overlap-degree-of-support-filtering
description: Use when annotating genome-mapped small RNA-seq reads against reference RNA databases and you must decide which read-gene overlaps count as real evidence for an RNA annotation or read count.

name: read-pair-segment-concatenation-parsing
description: Use when input FASTQ libraries follow sequencing protocols whose cell-barcode/UMI layout is variable-length, floating-position, or split across multiple segments — i.e., not expressible as a single fixed-position barcode+UMI geometry a mapper like piscem natively supports.

name: read-quality-control-and-paired-end-joining
description: Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ reads from a non-model eukaryotic species must be converted into per-sample ortholog (KO) count tables, replacing transcript assembly and annotation.

name: read-set-overlap-consistency-analysis
description: Use when validating a new SPLiT-seq barcode/UMI identification tool against the original baseline by computing the overlap fraction of identified reads per sample on paired-end FASTQ data.

name: read-write-density-frontier-analysis
description: Use when comparing multiple DNA storage pipeline designs (e.g., with/without MSA, with/without an inner code like HEDGES) on measured read density and write density outputs from fault-injection simulations, and you need the Pareto-optimal set.

name: read-write-density-pareto-front-computation
description: Decision support for choosing a DNA storage encoding pipeline (RS vs HEDGES vs HEDGES-MSA) when fault-injection simulation outputs are available and trade-offs between read density (reads required for recovery) and write density must be compared across error rates.

name: receptor-weighted-sample-fitting
description: Use when inferring the spatial distance of a signaling pathway from scRNA-seq data with a SpaOTsc-derived cell–cell distance matrix, and known ligand, receptor, and downstream target gene lists are available (e.g. Wg/fz in the Drosophila embryo).

name: recommender-system-pharmacogenomic-inference
description: Use when a Scanpy AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) from Single-Cell Data Analysis is available and you need cluster-wise IC50 and cell death percentage (drug kill efficacy) predictions for GDSC drugs.

name: recon3d-subsystem-background-mapping
description: Use when a predicted gene list (e.g. essential genes from SKO/DKO in silico deletion of context-specific metabolic models) needs pathway enrichment against KEGG with a Recon3D_01 subSystems background, plus ferroptosis annotation via FerrDb.

name: reconstruction-accuracy-comparison-across-fitting-algorithms
description: Use when comparing mutational signature fitting outcomes across reference signature versions (e.g., COSMIC v2 vs COSMIC v3.1) or across fitting algorithms (mmsig, deconstructSigs, MutationalPatterns) on WGS catalogs with more than 500 mutations.

name: reconstruction-r2-benchmarking
description: Use when testing whether a trained single-cell generative model (VEGA) generalizes to unseen cell type/condition pairs or to an entirely unseen second study, via GMV overlap and R2 metrics.

name: recursive-clustering-termination-logic
description: Use when implementing or reproducing RCC's decision logic for choosing the k per consensus clustering run and deciding when recursive cluster subdivision should stop on transcriptome data.

name: recursive-consensus-clustering-execution
description: Use when clustering transcriptomic datasets (e.g. TCGA pan-cancer, Ivy GAP, Neftel scRNA-seq) with an unknown number of clusters, and you need automatic k selection plus novel subtype identification.

name: recursive-feature-elimination-with-cross-validation
description: Use when a tabular feature matrix (e.g., 57 SIF/SSF/PF columns for mRNA vs lncRNA transcripts) must be reduced before training an XGBoost model, and class labels are imbalanced so oversampling must precede elimination.

name: recursive-multi-step-expression-forecasting
description: Use when you have paired single-cell count matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns) from two consecutive time points and need to predict future expression states beyond that interval, e.g., forecasting 50-100 recursive steps or anticipating lineage bifurcations.

name: recursive-transcriptomic-forecasting
description: Use when you have paired single-cell expression measurements of the same cells at two time points (e.g., metabolic labeling scEU-seq) and need to predict future expression states several steps beyond the observed horizon.

name: rediportal-a-to-i-editing-site-intersection
description: Use when per-read inosine calls from NanoSpeech basecalling (BAM + genome_space.tsv) must be validated against known A-to-I editing sites in REDIportal, or when comparing inosine burden across ADAR-modulated samples (e.g. hWT/hKO/hOE).

name: reditools-pileup-table-generation
description: Use when RNAseq BAM files must be converted into position-wise pileup tables of candidate substitutions (e.g. A-to-G events) in the tabix-indexed REDItools outTable format consumed by REDInet or REDItools-based editing callers.

name: reed-solomon-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when evaluating whether a Reed-Solomon (e.g. RS(9,47)) DNA storage encoding pipeline recovers data under injected faults, or when benchmarking FrameD's transparent MPI parallelism across fault-injection iterations.

name: reference-allele-bias-quantification
description: Use when analyzing allele-specific expression from GATK HaplotypeCaller VCFs and you need to measure or mitigate reference allele mapping bias in per-tissue reference allele ratios before trusting ASE calls.

name: reference-anchored-count-data-fitting
description: Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) analysis methods on simulated scRNA-seq data that must recapitulate real reference dataset characteristics such as library-size and dispersion structure across samples and subpopulations.

name: reference-atlas-cell-type-file-parsing
description: Use when you have the CCI reference atlas files (expression matrix, gene list, cell types, cell identity) in data_ref/ and need per-population cell counts or a healthy BMMC composition table matching reported values (e.g., T cells 53.11%).

name: reference-atlas-construction
description: Use when building a stable, annotated reference map (e.g. mouse TIL atlas, LCMV viral CD8 atlas) from multiple heterogeneous scRNA-seq studies so new query datasets can later be projected and cell-state-labeled with ProjecTILs.

name: reference-atlas-label-transfer
description: Use when a COPILOT-processed Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq Seurat object needs cell type and developmental stage labels without manual annotation, by leveraging the published root atlas reference.

name: reference-based-bulk-rna-decomposition
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq samples from a tissue plus paired (or at least same-tissue) single-cell or single-nucleus RNA-seq data with SubjectName and cellType labels, and need cell-type proportion estimates for downstream phenotype associations or benchmarking.

name: reference-based-cell-type-classification
description: Use when a clustered scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Seurat object such as demo_sc_data) lacks cell-type labels and cluster identities must be assigned via a pre-computed reference classifier before cell-cell communication analysis.

name: reference-based-cell-type-labeling-cibersort-singler
description: Use when annotating held-out TME single cells (e.g. Yost et al. BCC data from TISCH) with reference-derived cell type labels, or when establishing a marker/reference-based baseline to compare against higher-resolution learned annotations.

name: reference-based-cell-type-proportion-estimation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq cohort samples need cell-type proportion estimates and a matched snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference exists (ideally with overlapping subjects), e.g. to test microglia proportions against Braak stage.

name: reference-based-deconvolution-benchmarking
description: Use when simulated ST pixels with known ground-truth cell-type proportions are available and you need to quantify how deconvolution accuracy degrades for reference-based methods (SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) when the scRNA-seq reference is missing cell types or mismatched to the tissue.

name: reference-based-disease-signal-filtering-in-single-cell-data
description: Use when case-control scRNA-seq data (e.g., COVID-19 patient vs healthy control PBMCs) is available, healthy cells can serve as a reference in a harmonized joint latent space, and the goal is to remove the healthy signal to reveal disease-related dynamics and disease-informative subpopulations.

name: reference-based-label-transfer
description: Use when a pre-processed query Seurat object (e.g., Arabidopsis root PRJNA507252 or wheat root CRA008788) has clustered cells and a curated reference cell map (e.g., PRJNA517021 or PRJNA706435) is available for label transfer.

name: reference-based-label-transfer
description: Use when query cells or spatial spots carry only coarse labels (e.g., 'B.cells', 'T.cells', 'Myeloid.cells') and a well-annotated reference atlas exists to resolve finer subtypes such as plasmablasts, memory B cells, or dendritic cells.

name: reference-cci-output-validation
description: Use when reproducing InterCellar paper CCI inputs (COVID-19 control/moderate/critical) and generated CellPhoneDB outputs must be checked against the reference CCI data deposited in martaint/InterCellar-reproducibility.

name: reference-cell-type-selection
description: Use when running scCODA CompositionalAnalysis on aggregated per-sample cell-type counts and you must fix or auto-select the reference cell type before HMC sampling, so credible effects (Final Parameter, FDR e.g. 0.2) are interpreted relative to that reference.

name: reference-database-substitution-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether annotation accuracy of a cell-based method (e.g., SingleR) is reference-database dependent, or when testing whether substituting a curated tissue-specific reference such as CellMatch improves cluster annotation consistency.

name: reference-dataset-matching-scmatch
description: Use when a clustered Scanpy AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) needs cell type labels per Louvain cluster, or when single-cell clusters must be matched against a curated reference GEP dataset like FANTOM5.

name: reference-free-assembly-evaluation-with-reads
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (FASTA) must be quality-assessed but no reference genome is available, and the raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) are at hand.

name: reference-free-cell-type-deconvolution
description: Use when analyzing multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data (e.g., Spatial Transcriptomics, 10X Visium, DBiT-seq) and no appropriate scRNA-seq reference exists, or when the goal is to recover cell-type-specific gene-expression changes from mixed pixel measurements.

name: reference-free-cell-type-proportion-inference
description: Use when the input is a multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST count matrix (e.g. Spatial Transcriptomics, 10X Visium, DBiT-seq pixels) and no suitable matched scRNA-seq reference exists for supervised deconvolution.

name: reference-gene-combination-benchmarking
description: Use when you have raw CT qPCR array data with many candidate reference genes/miRNAs and need to select and benchmark the most stable weighted combination (virtual reference gene) across candidate weighting schemes.

name: reference-gene-screening
description: Use when you have a gene expression DataFrame (e.g. GEO microarray data like GSE125792 or GSE4786, probe-level or gene-level) and need to identify stable endogenous reference genes for qPCR/microarray normalization in Python.

name: reference-gene-stability-variance-ranking
description: Use when a raw gene expression matrix (tab-delimited GSE-style file or Pandas DataFrame) must be screened for stable endogenous reference genes by ranking ΔF variance, or when reproducing/validating ERgene's FindERG top-20 output.

name: reference-gene-weight-optimization
description: Use when raw CT values (or a compatible normalized high-throughput dataset) are available for 2 or more internal controls and a weighted mean must replace the unweighted geometric mean for ΔΔCT normalization.

name: reference-genome-binning-dataset-preparation
description: Use when benchmarking a sequence-search pre-filter or distributed read mapper against reference collections that must be partitioned into bins, or when reproducing the Raptor Table 7 DREAM-Yara experiments on clustered NCBI RefSeq data.

name: reference-genome-expanded-reference-construction
description: Use when preparing a reference for alevin-fry/simpleaf single-cell RNA-seq quantification: you have a genome FASTA plus GTF/GFF3 annotation and need a spliced+intronic (splici) or spliced+unspliced (spliceu) expanded reference with a piscem index.

name: reference-genome-indexing
description: Use when preparing an RNA-seq alignment reference: a genome FASTA plus Ensembl GTF must be compiled into a STAR index, or the reference must be re-built after masking known variant positions with Bedtools to reduce reference-allele bias.

name: reference-genome-masking-with-variants
description: Use when RNA-seq-based ASE or allele-count analyses show inflated reference allele ratios (e.g., >51%) and you need to quantify or mitigate mapping bias before calling ASE from biallelic SNP allele depths.

name: reference-label-overlap-comparison
description: Use when a clustering/statistical flagging step yields a candidate cell or feature set and a published reference set (count or labeled IDs) exists for the same dataset to verify against.

name: reference-label-transfer-evaluation
description: Use when prior reference-annotations (e.g., Azimuth label transfer, Seurat label transfer, cellHarmony) must be reconciled with Leiden clusters from one or more modalities, or when benchmarking clustering solutions against a reference atlas with Homogeneity/Completeness/V-Measure.

name: reference-map-projection-of-query-cells
description: Use when scRNA-seq query data (raw counts, 10x/h5 or Seurat objects) must be mapped onto a pre-built reference atlas — e.g. the LCMV viral CD8+ T cell atlas — to quantify how a perturbation (KO, infection condition) shifts cell subtype frequencies.

name: reference-mapping-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when choosing a reference-mapping tool for scRNA-seq data and you need quantitative evidence on projection fidelity and cell-state classification accuracy rather than qualitative UMAP comparisons.

name: reference-marker-database-mapping
description: Use when a trained cell-annotation model has produced ranked per-class feature/biomarker lists and you need to quantify how many of the top-K markers are literature-validated, or compare marker recall across tools.

name: reference-panel-selection-and-loading
description: Use when annotating single-cell clusters or bulk RNA-seq samples (e.g. iPSC-derived NPC/neuron profiles) against deCS built-in reference panels and you must choose and load the correct reference before running deCS.correlation().

name: reference-panel-selection-for-cell-annotation
description: Use when annotating single-cell clusters or gene lists against a human cell type reference panel and you must choose which built-in deCS panel (main vs fine) and CTgene cutoff (e.g. ref_panel_markers_ratio = 0.05) to apply.

name: reference-query-label-transfer
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset needs cell type labels consistent with an annotated reference, and gene-order-matched AnnData objects (ref_adata, query_adata) are available for label transfer.

name: reference-stability-assessment
description: Use when subtyping TCGA RNA-seq breast cancer samples with PAM50 and you need to test whether reference-construction strategy (AWCA vs median centroids) affects concordance and reproducibility of subtype calls.

name: reference-table-metric-comparison
description: Use when you have recomputed clustering/integration metrics (ARI, kBET, ASW, ASW-beta) for a batch-effect benchmark and need to verify them against the paper's published reference table before trusting the reproduction.

name: reference-table-result-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or validating published gene-marker panels derived from COMET on an SCA latent-space frequency matrix, where a reference table of expected panels and COMETsc/TP/TN statistics is available for comparison.

name: reference-table-value-reproduction
description: Use when a paper's reported numeric table values (e.g., effective text ratios r(k) per binning and k-mer size) must be independently recomputed and validated from a downloadable dataset with the authors' tool.

name: reference-transcript-annotation-handling
description: Use when setting up SkewC gene body coverage computation and you must select the species-appropriate norRNAtRNA BED reference, build its index, or reconcile chromosome naming between the reference and 10X BAM files.

name: reference-vector-validation
description: Use when a PAM50-style centroid reference must be rebuilt from subtype-labeled RNA-seq cohorts so that classification no longer depends on cohort composition, or when an existing reference table (e.g., Supplementary Table S3 format) must be structurally verified before downstream classification.

name: region-based-cell-composition-quantification
description: Use when a MCMICRO-derived single-cell table from multiplexed imaging (e.

name: region-gene-window-mapping
description: Use when building a gene-level TF affinity matrix from region-level TRAP affinities: to pick gene-window (default 50 kb around 5' TSS) vs ABC-based (5 Mb, i.e. ±2.5 Mb) mapping, or to decide scaling of promoter-proximal vs distant regions.

name: region-merging-pyramidal-segmentation
description: Use when a smoothed, gene-order-sorted expression matrix must be converted into a copy number segmentation with shared breakpoints across cells, as in SCEVAN's joint segmentation step.

name: region-specific-gene-identification
description: Use when a reconstructed single-cell spatial landscape is available and the goal is to find genes determining spatial location or restricted to specific regions (e.g., cortical layers L1-L6, hepatic lobule zones) rather than merely mapping cells.

name: region-targeted-cnv-call-extraction
description: Use when you need to determine whether specific focal or arm-level CNV events (e.g., an oncogene amplicon or a chromosome arm deletion) are recovered by CaSpER at particular expression smoothing scales in bulk or single-cell RNA-seq.

name: regional-specificity-statistical-testing
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics spot-level module scores (e.g., AUCell scores per Visium spot) need testing for regional specificity across annotated anatomical subregions or correlation with spatially mapped phenotypes such as plaque burden or age.

name: regression-model-training-on-multi-cell-type-genomic-data
description: Use when you have DNase-seq (or other genome-wide regulatory) measurements and matched gene expression matrices for tens of cell types and need cell-type-general predictive models of regulatory element activity.

name: regression-statistics-table-reporting
description: Use when per-gene CTMM results (cell type-specificity and mean-difference measures) must be compared against gene-level annotations such as enhancer domain score, enhancer count, LOEUF, or pLI to ask whether interindividual variance tracks genome features differently than mean-based cell.

name: regularization-parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when you must attribute performance contributions of individual regularization penalties in a regularized regression model, or determine how the network regularization parameter η affects enrichment performance under varying noise conditions.

name: regulated-heterogeneity-z-score-computation
description: Use when matched single-cell and bulk RNA-Seq expression matrices are available and the goal is to test whether a bulk population's signalling entropy is significantly higher than expected from its constituent single cells.

name: regulator-activity-inference
description: Use when a count table or expression matrix must be summarized into per-regulator (TF/kinase) activity scores via signed, weighted prior-knowledge networks, or when multiple inference methods must be combined into a consensus.

name: regulator-activity-score-matrix-analysis
description: Use when you have activity score matrices (regulators × methods) from decoupleRBench runs and need to reproduce manuscript-level agreement statistics such as median Spearman correlations, Jaccard overlap, or Wilcoxon weight tests.

name: regulator-gene-lagged-correlation-computation
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq and regulatory omics count matrices plus a ground-truth regulator–gene interaction list and need to quantify how strongly each modelled interaction manifests as a correlation.

name: regulator-list-construction-in-mat-files
description: Use when preparing SINGE inputs for pseudotemporal single-cell expression data and only a subset of genes (e.g., transcription factors) should be considered as candidate regulators rather than all genes in gene_list.mat.

name: regulator-recovery-sensitivity-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating which activity-inference methods recover perturbed regulators from phospho-proteomics perturbation data, or when reproducing the decoupleR phospho-proteomics method ranking.

name: regulator-specific-prediction-evaluation
description: Use when overall precision-recall evaluation of a GRN method looks acceptable and you need to check whether performance is uneven across individual regulators, using a gold standard with per-regulator target sets.

name: regulator-target-interaction-analysis
description: Use when single-cell trajectory progressions and a reconstructed GRN edge list are available and you need to identify transcriptional regulators driving or mediating specific cell-fate transitions at the network level.

name: regulator-target-profile-matching
description: Use when simulating bulk multi-omics regulatory layers with MOSim and you must decide how a regulator's simulated count/time profile relates to the expression pattern of its assigned target genes.

name: regulator-variable-importance-ranking
description: Use when you have BoostDiff output from two conditions (e.g., salt-stress target vs. SMM baseline) and need to rank regulator-to-target edges by aggregating weighted DVI across the boosted differential trees into a VIM table.

name: regulatory-element-annotation-overlap
description: Use when you have fine-mapped credible-set variants (e.g., CAFEH pip/alpha per SNP) and want to test whether they are enriched in active promoters/enhancers relative to a matched background, as in Figure 3D.

name: regulatory-interaction-rescaling
description: Use when you have bootstrapped COSLIR coefficient matrices plus first-moment vectors (mu1, mu2) from two consecutive time points and need to rank directed gene-gregulatory interactions by influence.

name: regulatory-network-em-refitting
description: Use when you need to test robustness of scKINETICS velocity/network outputs by sweeping sigma over an initiating grid or perturbing nonzero A^ coexpression-prior elements with Gaussian noise while holding all other inputs fixed.

name: regulatory-network-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when a fitted GRN matrix A (e.g. from scKINETICS EM fitting) must be validated for recovery accuracy by simulating noisy expression trajectories from random start cells and refitting the model.

name: regulatory-potential-model-technical-effect-augmentation
description: Use when a multi-batch single-cell multimodal (RNA+ATAC) dataset is being used to infer regulatory potential and TF motif enrichments, and technical/batch effects may confound motif-gene associations you want to compare between corrected and uncorrected models.

name: regulon-activity-score-computation-aucell
description: Use when you have an annotated plant (e.g., Arabidopsis TAIR10) scRNA-seq Seurat object and need to infer cell-type-specific regulons/GRNs and identify top regulon TFs per cluster.

name: regulon-enrichment-visualization
description: Use when MINI-EX or SCENIC regulons have been inferred on a plant single-cell atlas and you need to rank top regulons per cluster, render enrichment heatmaps, and quantify cross-tool regulon consistency.

name: regulon-like-gene-module-detection
description: Use when you have a cell-lineage-specific GRN plus identified driver regulators (e.g., from CEFCON's driver_regulators() step) and need gene modules and per-cell module activity matrices for downstream enrichment or clustering benchmarks.

name: regulon-membership-validation
description: Use when a differential network (e.g. from BoostDiff on salt/heat/ethanol stress vs. control) needs biological validation: check whether top hub genes belong to a known regulon such as SigB.

name: regulon-partitioning-from-inferred-grn
description: Use when an inferred GRN (e.g. from Augusta's mutual-information step) needs to be grouped into TF-specific regulons before promoter-based motif discovery, and small regulons must be pruned.

name: regulon-specificity-score-analysis
description: Use when you have an annotated plant single-cell atlas (e.g., Seurat object) and need to identify cell-type-specific gene regulatory networks and rank the top regulon transcription factor per cell cluster.

name: regulon-specificity-score-visualization
description: Use when a pyscenic auc.*.loom (AUCell regulon AUC scores over clustered scRNA-seq cells) is available and you need to identify and visualize which regulons are preferentially active per cluster.

name: rejection-fraction-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when benchmarking how a hierarchical classifier rejects cells from unseen populations held out of training, e.g. comparing one-class SVM vs linear SVM rejection fractions across tree nodes.

name: rejection-threshold-calibration
description: Use when training a reference-based identifier (MarkerCount_Ref) on a pre-annotated reference dataset whose taxonomy does not cover the test cells, and you need non-parametric per-cell-type thresholds tm on normalized marker counts for unknown-population rejection.

name: rejection-threshold-tuning-scrnaseq
description: Use when calibrating the unassigned-cells portion threshold that triggers cluster-basis reassignment in a marker-count-based scRNA-seq cell type identifier, and you need empirical justification for the chosen cutoff.

name: relative-correction-factor-matrix-computation
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (Pandas DataFrame, genes × samples) must be screened for stable endogenous reference genes by replicating ERgene's inverse internal-reference calculation rather than treating the library as a black box.

name: relative-factor-variation-ranking
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (pandas DataFrame) must be screened for stable internal reference genes, and candidate genes should be ranked by smallest variance of relative factor change with the top 20 returned.

name: relieff-feature-scoring
description: Use when you have a labeled expression matrix (samples x features with phenotype labels) and need an individual per-feature relevance score that reflects local neighborhood discrimination, e.g., as a baseline against phenotype-cover methods.

name: reml-mixed-model-fitting
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple donors has been aggregated into cell type-specific pseudobulk (CTP), ctnu, and cell type proportions P, and the goal is to partition interindividual expression variance into cell type-shared (hom2) vs cell type-specific (V) components and test genes for.

name: reml-variance-component-estimation
description: Use when per-gene, per-cell-type variance components must be estimated from pseudobulk scRNA-seq and stage- or cell type-specific interindividual variation (with calibrated Wald p-values) is the target signal.

name: reorganization-marker-auc-scoring
description: Use when you have paired transcriptome-only and ClonoCluster hybrid cluster assignments plus a count matrix, and need genes whose expression predicts cell reassignment (reorganization markers) between cluster pairs for downstream GO enrichment.

name: reparameterization-trick-sampling
description: Use when building or re-running the scDHA Stacked Bayesian Self-learning Network stage that converts the filtered non-negative kernel autoencoder representation into a low-dimensional latent embedding.

name: repeated-clustering-run-aggregation
description: Use when a stochastic deep-clustering pipeline (e.g., scDCC with random initialization) yields run-to-run variability and you must quantify whether a modification (e.g., adding pairwise constraints) consistently improves a downstream metric such as cluster-specificity scores of marker genes.

name: repeated-cross-validation-model-evaluation
description: Use when a new feature set (e.g. PSG k-mer, position-specific k-mer, GC-content) must be compared against baselines on a labeled sequence dataset, requiring averaged cross-validation metrics and ROC/PR curves rather than a single train/test split.

name: repeated-cross-validation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantify downstream benefit of an adjusted expression matrix: sample-level labels exist (e.g., Healthy / Mild-Moderate / Severe-Critical), and you must compare predictive accuracy between adjusted and raw data per cell type.

name: repeated-explain-value-aggregation
description: Use when you have a trained SIMS/TabNet classifier on single-cell RNA-seq data and need to quantify whether its sparse feature masks consistently select the same genes for a given cell type across independent explain runs.

name: repeated-measure-runtime-aggregation
description: Use when you need to quantify computational time requirements of a scRNA-seq trajectory-inference workflow (e.g., Escort) across dataset sizes such as 1000 vs 3000 cells, and report reproducible per-step runtime statistics.

name: repeated-run-stability-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when a stochastic deep model's dimension reduction varies across runs (e.g. VASC with variational/Gumbel-softmax optimization) and you must show whether an added component, such as the ZI dropout layer, improves median clustering scores and tightens their spread.

name: repeated-run-variance-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a stochastic clustering model (e.g., DeepCCI's GCN cluster model with random initialization) against baselines on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and you must control seed variance by averaging ARI over multiple repeats.

name: repeated-train-validation-test-split-resampling
description: Use when benchmarking predictive performance of sparse high-dimensional regression methods on small-n/large-p omics data, where a single train/test split would make MSE and feature counts unstable.

name: repeatmasker-annotation-filtering
description: Use when building a custom TE reference for scTE or scTEATAC and a genome lacks a prebuilt scTE index — e.g. mm10 rmsk.txt must be subset to LINE/SINE/LTR/Retroposon classes before index construction.

name: repeatmasker-repeat-class-filtering
description: Use when a user needs a custom gene-model BED for SkewC and must remove rRNA/tRNA RepeatMasker entries from a GENCODE annotation for a genome/assembly (e.g. hg38, mm10) not shipped in the repository's reference/ folder.

name: replicate-aware-da-statistics
description: Use when performing differential abundance testing on ELVAR-enriched cell communities where biological inter-subject variability must be modeled via replicates, e.g. regressing naive/mature cell counts on age in Tabula Muris Senis lung Cd4+ T-cells.

name: replicate-cluster-matching-across-biological-datasets
description: Use when two or more independently clustered scRNAseq datasets (e.g., replicates, tissues, or disease models like TIL vs dLN vs Arm CD4+ T cells) must be compared to find which clusters share transcriptomic profiles and which remain distinct.

name: replicate-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two biological replicates each yield a ranked list of perturbation scores (e.g. 180 active TFs from systematic KO simulations) and you must show the ranking is reproducible before nominating candidate regulators.

name: replicate-pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a normalized barcode counts table (e.g. counts/all_counts_combined.tsv) contains biological replicates per treatment (e.g. DMSO, IBET-151) and replicate concordance must be quantified before downstream clonal analyses.

name: replicate-quality-validation-pca-correlation
description: Use when RiboSeq samples have passed footprint QC (read-length ~28 nt, metagene periodicity, CDS enrichment) and you must decide which replicates are consistent before running DESeq2 differential expression.

name: replicate-reproducibility-correlation-analysis
description: Use when two or more biological RNA-seq replicates are available and you need to verify that novel IPA sites and assembled IPA isoforms detected per-replicate are consistent (overlapping sites, correlated expression).

name: reported-value-benchmark-verification
description: Use when a published numeric result (e.g., a network statistic like a network density score reported in Fig. 1C of Kahraman et al., Scientific Reports 2020) must be independently reproduced from raw network data to validate a pipeline or database-derived value.

name: reproducible-random-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking biclustering algorithms on synthetic data with known ground truth — e.g. implanting trend-preserving, shift-scale, or constant biclusters into random N(0,1) matrices with fixed seeds for reproducibility.

name: reproducible-random-seed-sampling
description: Use when a trajectory-inference or ensemble-clustering step requires many randomly initialized clusterings on a low-dimensional embedding and results must be bit-reproducible across runs via seeded RNG.

name: reproducing-kernel-hilbert-space-embedding
description: Use when two count matrices from different platforms (scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics .csv files) must be brought into a comparable feature space before joint downstream analysis such as pseudo-space projection.

name: reprogramming-factor-candidate-ranking
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data with annotated subpopulations (e.g., GSE75478 human HSPC data) is available and you need ranked candidate regulators to overexpress or knock down to convert one cell type (B-cells, mono/DCs) into another (HSPCs).

name: reprogramming-trajectory-network-comparison
description: Use when single-cell GRN Links objects exist for ordered cell-state clusters along a reprogramming trajectory and you need per-cluster topology metrics (centrality, cartography, specific TF edge strengths) to compare network configurations between states.

name: reprogramming-trajectory-te-expression-analysis
description: Use when analyzing single-cell RNA-seq of OKSM reprogramming (e.g. GSE115943) to test whether specific TE families are expressed in a branch-restricted manner across intermediate cell fates, or to identify TEs upregulated specifically in the successful reprogramming route.

name: resampling-based-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when a clustering dataset is too large for full hierarchical clustering (e.g. mass cytometry datasets with 86,864–265,627 cells) and you need repeatable resample-based clustering with performance metrics (accuracy, NMI, ARI) aggregated over resamples.

name: resampling-based-model-stability-analysis
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that biologically informed feature filtering (e.g., TimiGP-enriched cell-cell interaction pairs) makes LASSO Cox feature selection more stable than filtering on prognostic p-values alone.

name: resampling-based-statistical-significance-testing
description: Use when assignments from MaCroDNA (or a similar bipartite-matching integration method) must be validated on data lacking ground-truth DNA–RNA cell correspondence, especially single-cell data grouped into biopsies of varying heterogeneity.

name: resampling-robustness-evaluation
description: Use when comparing module-detection methods (fRNC, WGCNA, LncACT) for stability: you have ground-truth embedded sub-networks or matched case/control RNA-seq counts and need recovery consistency across resamples plus sensitivity comparisons via ANOVA.

name: resolution-elbow-identification
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data and an objective, marker-based criterion is needed to choose among candidate Louvain resolutions, rather than defaulting to a resolution like 0.8 or relying solely on author-curated annotations.

name: resource-constrained-gpu-execution
description: Use when training or evaluating scRNA-seq annotation models on datasets with millions of cells where the VM has limited resources (e.g., 12GB GPU, 128GB RAM, 8 CPUs) and full in-memory processing would fail.

name: resource-overlap-quantification
description: Use when you need to compare the content of multiple ligand-receptor CCC resources (e.g. CellChatDB, CellPhoneDB, Ramilowski, ConnectomeDB, LRdb) to quantify how many interactions, transmitters, or receivers are unique to each resource versus shared.

name: resource-usage-profiling-build-vs-query
description: Use when comparing index-based sequence search tools (e.g., Raptor vs Mantis) on a large experiment collection and you must quantify build resources and query speed, memory, and specificity per query set.

name: resource-usage-profiling-cpu-wallclock-ram
description: Use when measuring runtime and memory footprint of PAC queries against an indexed collection, e.g. validating that large transcript batches complete in under an hour.

name: respiratory-nadir-time-alignment
description: Use when a longitudinal COVID-19 transcriptomics cohort has per-sample clinical timing (respiratory function measurements) and the goal is to anchor expression trajectories to the day of respiratory nadir to determine how early severe-disease signatures emerge.

name: response-class-labeling-microarray-samples
description: Use when running PIMENTo's SigGenesSAM on background-subtracted microarray data where samples fall into two biological conditions and a class vector must encode which sample belongs to which response class.

name: restricted-maximum-likelihood-variance-component-fitting
description: Use when partitioning interindividual variance of scRNA-seq gene expression across cell types from pseudobulk matrices (OP or CTP, ctnu, P) is needed, e.g. quantifying cell type-specific variance or stage-specific covariance along the iPSC-to-endoderm trajectory.

name: retina-bipolar-and-amacrine-cell-subtype-annotation
description: Use when annotating clusters in mouse retina scRNA-seq data with ScType and you need to separate closely related subtypes (amacrine subpopulations; rod vs cone bipolar cells) beyond the original manual labels.

name: retinal-progenitor-branch-reconstruction
description: Use when analyzing a multi-branch developmental scRNA-seq dataset with a clear cell cycle phase (e.g., E15.5 retina) where scVelo's dynamical mode produces a disconnected terminal path and a gene-specific latent time is preferred.

name: retrograde-tracing-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating an inferred neuron-neuron communication network for a cortical region against gold-standard anatomical connectivity from monosynaptic retrograde-tracing labels.

name: retroviral-protein-motif-annotation
description: Use when building or validating a curated database of potentially functional HERVs by screening genomic endogenous-retrovirus loci for intact retroviral protein motifs (POL/RT, GAG, ENV).

name: reverse-complement-strand-scanning
description: Use when scanning a user-provided nucleotide sequence (e.g. FASTA) for core promoter elements (TATA, Inr, DPE, MTE) or user-defined motifs and hits on both strands must be reported without prior TSS determination.

name: reverse-nearest-neighbor-structure-metric
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq batch-effect correction methods (e.g. BATMAN vs Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, Scanorama) and you need to quantify retention of local structure alongside batch mixing (iLISI).

name: rhythmic-gene-identification-jtk-lomb-scargle
description: Use when a bulk RNAseq/microarray time series with known circadian timepoints needs candidate rhythmic genes before training a circadian-time predictor such as tauFisher.

name: rhythmic-gene-periodicity-detection
description: Use when you have a timestamped bulk transcriptomic time series (e.g., a GEO circadian dataset like GSE38622 or GSE157077 with samples ordered by adjusted circadian time) and need to identify a compact set of significantly rhythmic 24-hour-period genes as predictors.

name: ribo-depleted-rnaseq-alignment
description: Use when input is paired-end ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ data and the goal is circRNA/linear RNA expression analysis with CLEAR (FPBquantification, CIRCscore) or downstream circRNA detection (CIRCexplorer2, DCC).

name: ribo-depleted-rnaseq-circrna-quantification
description: Use when ribosomal-RNA depleted paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ must be converted into per-locus circRNA quantifications (readNumber, FPBcirc, FPBlinear, CIRCscore) that are directly comparable to cognate linear RNA expression.

name: ribo-minus-rnaseq-processing
description: Use when ribo− RNA-seq FASTQ files must be processed into per-circRNA FPBcirc, FPBlinear, and CIRCscore values, e.g. to compare circRNA expression between tumor and paired-normal samples such as the 20 HCC/paired-normal libraries from GSE77509.

name: riboseq-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when starting a Ribo-seq analysis project from raw FastQ files with RiboDoc: building the project folder, naming *.fastq.gz samples, choosing genome/rRNA fasta references, and setting config.yaml options (RPF lengths 25-35 nt, p-val, logFC, riboWaltz vs TRiP).

name: riboseq-sample-naming-convention-parsing
description: Use when organizing gzip-compressed FastQ inputs for RiboDoc-style Ribo-seq runs and sample filenames must be validated, parsed, or mapped to condition/replicate groupings before pipeline execution.

name: ribosomal-mitochondrial-artifact-filtration
description: Use when a hyb-format qCLASH/CLASH file (with optional paired vienna/CT fold file) contains artifactual rRNA- and mtRNA-derived hybrid records that would contaminate type/miRNA or target analyses.

name: ribosome-footprint-read-length-distribution-analysis
description: Use when aligned Ribo-seq footprints (e.g. length-split BAM files such as *.25-35.bam) must be validated as genuine ribosome-protected fragments before quantitative analysis or differential expression.

name: ribosome-profiling-alignment-file-indexing
description: Use when SAM alignment files from conjoint genome/transcriptome RiboSeq alignment (HISAT2 + Bowtie2) must be coordinate-sorted, filtered to uniquely mapped reads, converted to BAM, and indexed for downstream htseq-count or riboWaltz steps.

name: ribosome-profiling-count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when a ribosome profiling count matrix (e.g. count_matrix_by_transcript_IDs.csv from htseq-count) is available with replicate samples grouped into reference and comparison conditions, and differential translation/expression calls are needed.

name: ribosome-profiling-read-depletion
description: Use when a Ribo-seq pipeline needs contaminant RNA removed from Cutadapt-trimmed, 25–35 nt RPF-length-selected FastQ reads before the double-mapping step with Bowtie2/HISAT2.

name: ridge-regression-cross-validation
description: Use when you must estimate TF motif activities from a promoter-by-motif count matrix built on unspliced scRNA-seq reads (scVelo 'Mu'), and the ridge penalty needs to be tuned by cross-validation so motif activities can be correlated with mRNA abundance across cell-cycle phases.

name: rmarkdown-html-report-rendering
description: Use when a selected miRNA candidate (e.g., ath-MIR156b from manualCuration output) must be presented as a feature-rich, shareable HTML report page for manual curation in a Galaxy-based plant miRNA annotation workflow.

name: rmarkdown-reproducible-analysis-execution
description: Use when running the SkewC R Markdowns in the folder's listed order, especially 3-SkewC_TrimClustering.Rmd on Coverage_means_DF_Clust to partition cells into typical and skewed groups.

name: rmbase-site-masking-with-bedtools
description: Use when preparing a human (or other species) transcriptome scan for novel RNA modification sites and known experimentally validated sites from RMBase must be excluded from prediction, e.g. before scoring uridine-centered windows.

name: rmse-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need to validate that a fitted fragment length distribution model generalizes across scRNA-seq datasets, i.e., when fitting Forseti's spline model and quantifying held-out prediction accuracy via RMSE.

name: rmse-correlation-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing competing marker gene sets (e.g., COT-derived via obtain_subtype_markers(), one-vs-rest t-test, a priori lists) for deconvolving bulk expression mixtures where true cell-type proportions are known, and a head-to-head accuracy table is needed.

name: rmse-evaluation-against-simulated-ground-truth
description: Use when benchmarking deconvolution methods (STdeconvolve, SPOTlight, RCTD, spatialDWLS) on simulated multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data with known ground-truth cell-type proportions and a significance test for RMSE differences is required.

name: rmse-model-comparison-benchmarking
description: Use when multiple trained deep learning variants (e.g. autoencoders of different widths or dropout settings) must be compared by reconstruction RMSE on held-out and independent datasets to pick the deployment model.

name: rmse-performance-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-type proportion estimation methods on simulated spatial transcriptomics data with known ground-truth pixel-level proportions, and per-pixel RMSE plus pairwise statistical accuracy tests are needed.

name: rmt-eigenvalue-noise-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq count data (e.g., ZhengMix PBMC) and you need a data-driven, non-manual threshold to separate signal dimensions from noise before dimensionality reduction or UMAP embedding.

name: rmt-eigenvector-based-feature-selection
description: Use when a highly sparse single-cell expression matrix (~95% sparse, e.g. 6,573 PBMC or 3,005 mouse cortex cells) must be denoised and signal-like genes selected before clustering or latent-space embedding.

name: rmt-marchenko-pastur-bulk-screening
description: Use when eigenvectors from an eigendecomposition of a single-cell covariance matrix must be classified as signal candidates or noise, especially when eigenvalues lie outside the Marchenko-Pastur bulk yet may still be sparsity-driven, delocalized noise.

name: rna-5hmc-position-specific-gapped-kmer-feature-generation
description: Use when raw RNA sequences of length 41 (5hmC benchmark Dataset.csv) must be transformed into position-specific gapped/ungapped k-mer descriptors, or when the stability of position-specific discriminative k-mer patterns must be verified across cross-validation partitions.

name: rna-5hmc-site-classification
description: Use when RNA sequences of length 41 need to be classified as 5hmC site vs non-site using position-specific sequence descriptors, or when reproducing the iRNA5hmC-PS benchmark (78.3% accuracy, 0.56 MCC) on Dataset.csv.

name: rna-count-matrix-aggregation
description: Use when multiple small RNA-seq samples have been annotated by COMPSRA and per-sample tab-delimited RNA count files must be merged into one RNA-by-sample count matrix before downstream normalization or differential expression.

name: rna-coverage-angle-based-on-off-classification
description: Use when preparing base-level RNA-seq pileup matrices (e.g., TCGA cohort) for SCISSOR shape-change detection and genes with many non-expressed samples must be identified and excluded.

name: rna-editing-pileup-generation
description: Use when REDInet inference needs tabix-indexed REDItools outTables from coordinate-sorted RNAseq BAMs, or when benchmarking REDItools v1 vs v3 pileup runtime on very deep HEK293T libraries.

name: rna-editing-site-deep-learning-inference
description: Use when you have tabix-indexed REDItools outTables of candidate A-to-G substitutions from RNAseq BAMs and need to distinguish genuine ADAR-mediated editing sites from SNPs or artifacts, especially when matched DNAseq data is unavailable.

name: rna-editing-site-density-windowing
description: Use when constructing a positive training set of double-stranded RNA regions from A-to-I RNA editing evidence — i.e., when converting REDIportal editing-site annotations into structurally verified dsRNA coordinates for model training.

name: rna-m5c-sequence-dataset-handling
description: Use when the input is RNA cytosine-site sequence data (FASTA windows around candidate m5C sites) that must be split into species-specific positive/negative training and independent test sets for m5C prediction.

name: rna-m5c-sequence-feature-fusion
description: Use when building sequence-based RNA modification (m5C) predictors that need richer features than a single encoding, and fused-feature dimensionality or training cost must be reduced with a filter method such as F score, MRMD, or PCC.

name: rna-m5c-site-prediction
description: Use when query RNA sequences in FASTA format need m5C site prediction for A. thaliana or M. musculus, or when reproducing/benchmarking stacked-ensemble m5C predictors against SVM/RF baselines like m5CPred-SVM or iRNA-m5C.

name: rna-m6a-site-prediction
description: Use when you need to identify m6A modification sites from RNA sequences for specific tissues (brain, liver, kidney, heart, testis) in human, mouse, or rat, starting from FASTA sequences or the 11 benchmark datasets (h_b, h_k, h_l, m_b, m_h, m_k, m_l, m_t, r_b, r_k, r_l).

name: rna-modification-stoichiometry-aggregation
description: Use when you have modification-aware basecalled dRNA reads (pod5/fast5 basecalled to fasta/fastq with mod indexes in headers, aligned to sorted BAM) and need per-read plus aggregated modification stoichiometry.

name: rna-profile-cluster-ground-truth-labeling
description: Use when benchmarking HTO-based demultiplexing methods on a cell hashing dataset where HTO counts alone cannot be trusted as truth, and RNA profiles are available to establish droplet identities independently.

name: rna-pseudouridine-site-dataset-construction
description: Use when building positive/negative Ψ-site training and test sets from RMBase v2.0 annotations that require sequence-identity reduction across 10-fold splits, e.g. for evaluating RNA modification predictors under balanced and imbalanced class ratios.

name: rna-read-sequence-classification
description: Use when you have unmapped RNAseq reads (e.g., *_unmapped.fastq after removal of hg19/phiX alignments) and need an alignment-free binary viral-vs-human read classifier or predicted viral contigs.

name: rna-secondary-structure-feature-encoding
description: Use when building deep learning inputs for RNA site prediction where secondary structure context should complement sequence, e.g. 51 nt fragments centered on a uridine/Ψ site.

name: rna-seq-adapter-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., pESC/aESC reads retrieved from SRA per Supplemental Table S1) must be adapter- and quality-trimmed before alignment to GRCh38/hg38 with STAR and expression quantification with RSEM/DESeq2.

name: rna-seq-alignment-feature-extraction
description: Use when you have coordinate-sorted RNA-seq BAM alignments plus RefSeq GTF annotation and need to classify candidate terminal exons (skipped vs composite IPA) using read-based features rather than sequence motifs.

name: rna-seq-alignment-grch38
description: Use when the input is human (GRCh38/hg38) RNA-seq FASTQ reads that must be aligned to a RefSeq-annotated genome before IPA site prediction with InPACT or downstream transcript quantification with Salmon.

name: rna-seq-alignment-quality-assessment
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQ files from multiple tissue groups must be aligned and you need per-sample STAR alignment statistics (unique mapping %, unmapped 'too short' %, chimeric %) to compare alignment quality across groups before ASE or expression analysis.

name: rna-seq-alignment-quality-control
description: Use when raw RNA-seq reads (e.g. the six untreated/LPS-activated monocyte samples from GSE118165) must be aligned to GRCh38 and cleaned into coordinate-sorted BAMs before InPACT can predict novel IPA sites.

name: rna-seq-bam-preprocessing-and-merging
description: Use when you have mapped RNA-seq reads (bulk or merged single-cell BAM) and need a BAF shift profile without a heterozygous variant call set, e.g. to supply CaSpER's allelic-shift signal.

name: rna-seq-cancer-normal-classification
description: Use when you have cancer and normal RNA-seq expression matrices (bulk or single-cell) plus a fixed gene set and need to benchmark its generalization accuracy on independent GEO datasets with a neural-network classifier.

name: rna-seq-count-data-simulation
description: Use when you need simulated gene-by-sample RNA-seq count matrices with known differential-expression ground truth to benchmark DEG detection methods such as DESeq2, edgeR, limma, or NOISeq.

name: rna-seq-count-filtering-normalization
description: Use when raw or simulated RNA-seq count matrices (e.g. MOSim mosim() bulk output) must be filtered and normalized prior to limma/voom linear modeling, DE testing, or GRN-inference preprocessing.

name: rna-seq-count-matrix-alignment
description: Use when loading expression count data plus a sample metadata/design table (e.g. BRCA_normCounts and BRCA_metadata from DEGGs) prior to generate_subnetworks or any per-sample subgroup analysis.

name: rna-seq-count-matrix-preparation
description: Use when fitting SNP–gene eQTL or differential expression models with kimma's kmFit/kmFit_eQTL and you must assemble expression counts, sample metadata, and a kinship matrix into the expected dat/kin/counts/meta format.

name: rna-seq-count-normalization-deseq2
description: Use when starting from raw RNA-seq gene count data across contrasting conditions (e.g. perturbation vs. vehicle control) that must be put on a comparable scale before downstream signature or pathway-activity scoring.

name: rna-seq-count-statistics
description: Use when you have raw TCGA RNA-Seq gene count matrices split into normal vs cancer samples (e.g. KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) and need a DE-gene baseline signature to benchmark a novel biomarker-extraction method.

name: rna-seq-count-table-normalization
description: Use when raw RNA-Seq count tables (e.g. DREAM 4 In Silico time-series or C. beijerinckii NRRL B-598 data) must be normalized with CPM, RPKM, or TPM prior to mutual-information GRN inference, or when benchmarking normalization effects on network metrics.

name: rna-seq-coverage-classification
description: Use when you need to assess how accurately predicted splice junction coverage (e.g., MRSD scores) matches achieved coverage in independent RNA-seq samples, using PPV/NPV as validation metrics.

name: rna-seq-coverage-decay-quantification
description: Use when base-level pileup coverage from an RNA-seq cohort must be screened for degraded RNA — e.g. samples with steep 3'-to-5' coverage slopes that would masquerade as spurious shape-change outliers in downstream analysis.

name: rna-seq-coverage-feature-engineering
description: Use when training or reproducing aptardi Mode 2 models that need RNA-Seq coverage (alone or with DNA sequence) as features over 3' terminal exons for polyadenylation-site prediction.

name: rna-seq-coverage-variance-stabilization
description: Use when raw base-level RNA-seq coverage pileup matrices are skewed and must be variance-stabilized (log-transform with tuned pseudo-count) prior to SCISSOR global/local shape change detection.

name: rna-seq-de-novo-transcript-assembly
description: Use when the goal is to reconstruct full IGHV-D-J Ig transcripts from an RNA-seq BAM (e.g., for IGHV hypermutation status in CLL) rather than inferring the B-cell receptor repertoire from only a portion of the IGHV gene segment.

name: rna-seq-de-novo-transcriptome-assembly
description: Use when you have Illumina paired-end RNA-seq reads (e.g. 2x100bp FASTQ, possibly with 10x/barcode structure) and need reference-free recovery of full-length isoforms from high-isoform-diversity genes like GYPC, MAPT, or BIN1.

name: rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when modeling RNA-seq gene counts from paired/related sample designs where a genetic kinship matrix is available, and you need per-gene DEG calls plus AIC-based comparison of models with and without the kinship covariance random effect.

name: rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a normalized RNA-seq expression matrix with two-group labels (e.g., 46 critical vs 23 non-critical COVID-19 cases from SEMdata) must be turned into per-gene DEG P-values to seed network analyses.

name: rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when a raw RNA-seq counts matrix (.csv, Ensembl ID rows, sample ID columns) must be tested for differentially expressed genes between sample groups, or when edgeR/limma/DESeq2 runtimes must be benchmarked on identical input.

name: rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq count matrix plus sample metadata with a defined experimental design and need robust DEG calls that are not biased by one method's assumptions.

name: rna-seq-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell RNA-seq expression matrix (thousands of genes) with batch labels and need a lower-dimensional embedding that preserves batch-specific variation for batch effect detection/quantification.

name: rna-seq-exon-count-simulation-from-population-parameters
description: Use when benchmarking an alternative-splicing or ASAS detection method against competitors and you need simulated paired allelic count data with controlled variance and replicate number instead of real RNA-seq reads.

name: rna-seq-expression-classification
description: Use when you need to evaluate whether genes from extracted active subnetworks discriminate between two patient groups (case/control) and to compare classifier performance (accuracy, predictor gene set size) across subnetwork detection methods.

name: rna-seq-expression-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw TCGA RNA-Seq gene expression matrices must be filtered and normalized before computing gene co-expression networks, and only protein-coding/lncRNA genes with sufficient expression (mean zFPKM > -3.0) should be kept.

name: rna-seq-expression-feature-representation
description: Use when a TCGA-style RNA-seq expression matrix with five intrinsic subtype labels (Luminal A/B, Basal, Her2-enriched, Normal-like) must be turned into a classifier feature space for supervised single-sample subtyping.

name: rna-seq-expression-matrix-loading
description: Use when you have a raw RNA-seq expression matrix (genes or transcripts x samples, e.g. ENCODE matrices with ~100 samples) that must be formatted, cleaned, and loaded into PyWGCNA before co-expression module identification.

name: rna-seq-expression-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw TCGA RNA-seq data for multiple cancer types must be assembled into a single tumor/normal gene-expression matrix before feature selection or classification, e.g. to compute per-gene DI scores over 20,501 genes.

name: rna-seq-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when a pre-trained RNA-seq subtyping model (mLR with PAM50, limma50, or limma50_BWE features) must be applied to a wholly unseen external expression matrix, or when reproducing external testing accuracies like Table 2.

name: rna-seq-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when the input is raw RNA-Seq data from a high-dimensional transcriptomics experiment (P >> n, e.g. ArrayExpress E-MTAB-11611) that must be converted into a predictor matrix x and outcome vector y for glmnet/nestedcv modelling.

name: rna-seq-fastq-download-from-geo-ena
description: Use when raw RNA-seq reads for a published study must be fetched from public archives — GSE accessions via GEO/SRA or a BioProject via direct ENA run downloads — before transcript-level quantification.

name: rna-seq-gene-id-mapping
description: Use when the input expression matrix is a .csv counts file with Ensembl gene IDs as row names and TCGA-style sample IDs as columns, and downstream GSVA, integration, or correlation analysis requires gene-symbol-keyed TPM data.

name: rna-seq-linear-mixed-effects-modeling
description: Use when RNA-seq differential expression data contain paired or repeated samples from the same donor (e.g., pre/post or within-patient designs) and you need per-gene mixed-model P-values plus AIC/BIC fit metrics.

name: rna-seq-outlier-sample-exclusion
description: Use when reproducing a published RNA-seq differential expression analysis whose original authors identified an outlier sample via QA/QC, or when PCA/box-plot diagnostics reveal a mislabeled or poorly separated sample before fitting a DE model.

name: rna-seq-paired-end-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a circRNA full-length assembly or isoform quantification method against known ground truth, requiring simulated paired-end reads with controlled depth, read length, and per-condition isoform abundances.

name: rna-seq-pileup-shape-change-interpretation
description: Use when a list of publicly reported splice-site mutation calls (e.g. TCGA HNSC MAF-style calls for TP53) must be cross-checked against SCISSOR shape-change outliers to flag likely mis-annotated calls.

name: rna-seq-pileup-table-preparation
description: Use when sorted RNAseq BAM files must be converted into position-by-position variant/invariant nucleotide frequency tables (REDItools outTables, bgzip+tabix indexed) to feed REDInet or other RNA editing classifiers.

name: rna-seq-preprocessing-and-normalization
description: Use when expression data (microarray, bulk or single-cell RNA-seq, e.g. TCGA-like sample-by-gene matrices) has a non-normal, bimodal, or multimodal feature distribution and must be Z-score normalized before correlation analysis.

name: rna-seq-read-alignment
description: Use when raw paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs from chicken (or other species) must be spliced-aligned for downstream per-sample variant calling (g.vcf/HaplotypeCaller) or allele-specific expression analysis.

name: rna-seq-read-alignment
description: Use when you have raw FASTQ reads (paired-end, e.g., first-strand Illumina libraries) and need a sorted, genome-aligned BAM as input to downstream transcriptome reconstruction (StringTie) or aptardi polyA-site prediction.

name: rna-seq-read-alignment-gene-counting
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g. ArrayExpress E-MTAB-6854 droplet-prepared mouse epithelial libraries) must be converted into a per-gene exonic read-pair count matrix for each demultiplexed sample combination.

name: rna-seq-read-alignment-multi-aligner
description: Use when you need to demonstrate that a mapping-derived signal (e.g. a shift, bias, or clustering pattern) is algorithm-independent by repeating the same alignment on identical input FASTQ with multiple aligners and comparing downstream distributions.

name: rna-seq-read-alignment-star
description: Use when preprocessing labeled SPLiT-seq FASTQ reads (e.g., SCSit output with combinatorial barcodes and UMI) need to be aligned to mm10, hg19, or a combined mm10-hg19 reference to compare mapped-read yields.

name: rna-seq-read-count-aggregation-per-node
description: Use when a KEGG pathway node contains multiple functionally homologous genes (e.g., the 4-gene ALDH3A1 node in hsa00340 or the 21-gene PLA2G4B node in hsa00564) and you need one node-level read count and regulation value instead of per-gene ambiguity.

name: rna-seq-read-depth-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking fusion-gene detection sensitivity (or similar read-count-dependent callers) across decreasing sequencing depths from a single deeply sequenced paired-end FASTQ sample.

name: rna-seq-read-fragmentation
description: Use when training or fairly benchmarking fixed-length read classifiers (e.g., viRNAtrap vs DeepVirFinder, DeepViFi, ViraMiner, Seq2Seq) and you need viral and human transcripts converted into comparable 48 bp fragments with shared train/test splits.

name: rna-seq-read-pseudoalignment-quantification
description: Use when you need to quantify reads supporting annotated and novel splicing events from short-read RNA-seq FASTQ files faster than a spliced aligner (fortuna was ~7x faster and mapped reads with mismatches across novel junctions more accurately).

name: rna-seq-read-quantification
description: Use when raw FASTQ RNA-seq reads from a model or non-model eukaryote must be converted to a KO-level count table, especially when no reference transcriptome exists or when cross-version equivalence with Kallisto-based quantification must be checked.

name: rna-seq-read-realignment-to-masked-genome
description: Use when per-allele read counts at heterozygous biallelic SNPs show inflated reference allele ratios (e.g. ~51.8–51.9% instead of the expected 50%) and you suspect the reference genome biases alignment toward the reference allele.

name: rna-seq-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking junction/splicing-event detection accuracy on controlled data: you need simulated FASTQs with known held-out novel junctions and per-event-type recall/precision ground truth.

name: rna-seq-read-truncation-processing
description: Use when you need to generate derivative sequencing-length variants (single-end truncations of paired-end FASTQ reads) to test robustness of an expression quantification metric across sequencing lengths and strategies.

name: rna-seq-sequencing-depth-quantification
description: Use when you need gene- and tissue-specific sequencing depth predictions (in millions of reads) for splice junction coverage of a gene panel, e.g. deciding which GTEx biosample and depth to use for RNA-seq mis-splicing surveillance.

name: rna-seq-shape-change-annotation
description: Use when SCISSOR has flagged shape-change outliers (e.g., ScissorOutput$GSC / $LSC sample IDs) and you need to determine which detected aberrations correspond to existing mutation calls versus novel events.

name: rna-seq-signature-count-augmentation
description: Use when an RNA-seq quantification based on fortuna signature counts (cnt.tsv/alt.tsv from --quant) must account for novel splice junctions that an aligner like STAR found in previously unmapped reads.

name: rna-seq-spanning-read-cluster-analysis
description: Use when RNA-Seq read support at a fusion locus forms multiple spanning-read junction clusters and one must decide which cluster is the primary fusion junction versus alternative-splice or backsplice junctions.

name: rna-seq-splice-event-quantification
description: Use when you need to detect and count novel alternative splicing events (ES, IR, AA, AD, AP, IE) from RNA-seq FASTQs using only a GTF annotation and genome FASTA, without a spliced aligner, or when tissue-specific event catalogs (e.g. RPM >= 1) are needed.

name: rna-seq-spliced-read-alignment
description: Use when paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ files must be spliced-aligned before circRNA full-length assembly, e.g. SRA/GSA reads destined for CircAST, CIRCexplorer2/CIRI2/UROBORUS junction detection.

name: rna-seq-spliced-read-alignment
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files must be converted into per-gene read counts (e.g., for the Prensner PCa cohort from dbGap phs000443.v1.p1) prior to differential expression or pathway-node aggregation.

name: rna-seq-statistical-filtering
description: Use when a counts matrix plus a two-group factor (e.g. hypoxia-high vs hypoxia-low TCGA-LUAD samples) must be tested for differentially expressed genes and filtered at explicit p/logFC/FDR cut-offs.

name: rna-seq-tmm-normalization-log2-cpm
description: Use when you have raw gene-level counts (e.g. kimma's example.count) plus sample metadata (example.dat) and want per-gene unpaired linear-model DEG testing on TMM-normalized log2 CPM expression with fit metrics.

name: rna-seq-tpm-expression-retrieval
description: Use when building a soybean–fungal infection expression dataset (C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, P. pachyrhizi) from public TPM estimates to feed coexpression or differential analyses.

name: rna-seq-transcript-assembly
description: Use when you have splice-aware BAM alignments of RNA-seq reads from one or more aligners (e.g., Hisat2 and Star) mapped to a reference genome and need to assemble transcripts, especially lowly expressed ones missed by single-aligner assemblers.

name: rna-seq-transcript-assembly
description: Use when raw RNA-Seq FASTQ samples (e.g., 180 TARGET osteosarcoma tumors plus 9 normal bone controls) must be converted into a consensus transcript candidate set prior to novel lncRNA detection.

name: rna-seq-transcript-quantification
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files from GEO/ENA (disease and control samples) must be converted to per-sample isoform-level TPM abundances as input for isoform switching / dMDT calling in the CanIsoNet workflow.

name: rna-seq-treatment-response-classification
description: Use when classifying binary treatment response (e.g. rituximab responders vs non-responders in the R4RA E-MTAB-11611 cohort) from transcriptomic matrices where predictors vastly outnumber samples (P >> n) and an honest out-of-sample AUC is required.

name: rna-sequence-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw RNA sequences (fixed length, e.g. 41 nt FASTA or CSV) must be converted into position-specific k-mer/gapped k-mer binary feature vectors for ML-based modification-site prediction.

name: rna-sequence-feature-extraction
description: Use when raw RNA transcript sequences in FASTA format must be converted into the numeric feature set (SIFs, SS k-mer scores, ORF, protein features) that LncDC's XGBoost model consumes for lncRNA prediction, or when reproducing its SSF ablation experiments.

name: rna-sequence-identity-reduction
description: Use when building train/test splits of RNA fragments (e.g., 51-nt pseudouridine-site windows) where homologous sequences across folds would inflate prediction accuracy through leakage.

name: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding
description: Use when raw RNA sequence segments (e.g., 41-nt tissue-specific m6A positive/negative samples) must be converted into fixed-length numeric feature matrices before feeding a CNN or other fixed-input neural network model.

name: rna-sequence-one-hot-encoding
description: Use when preparing Ψ-centered 51-bp RNA fragments (sequence plus RNAshapes dot-bracket structure) from RMBase v2.0 as fixed-size one-of-K binary matrices to feed paired 1D CNN inputs like MU-PseUDeep.

name: rna-structural-content-figure-generation
description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure in CT (connectivity table) or dot-bracket FASTA format plus a tab-delimited per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file, and you need BPC/entropy plots and structure-count heatmap/histogram outputs.

name: rna-structure-basepair-content-filtering
description: Use when you have per-window BPC values and smoothed Shannon entropy values for an RNA (e.g., from HCV_Jc1 CT/dot-bracket structure plus a shannon.txt) and must designate structure counts under RSCanner's dual-threshold filtering.

name: rna-structure-lineplot-visualization
description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure (CT or dot-bracket format) plus a per-nucleotide Shannon entropy file and need per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE line plots (e.g. reproducing Supplementary Fig. S2A/B for HCV_Jc1).

name: rna-transcript-dataset-construction
description: Use when building training and test FASTA sets of mRNA, their CDS, and lncRNA transcripts from curated annotations (e.g., NCBI RefSeq or GENCODE) to train or benchmark lncRNA identification models.

name: rna-velocity-alignment-score-computation
description: Use when you have an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced layers, scvelo RNA velocity, and an ensemble of DTW-aligned simulated trajectories, and need per-cell scores, pseudotime, and cell fate probabilities.

name: rna-velocity-baseline-comparison
description: Use when you need to benchmark an RNA-velocity- or manifold-based cell-cycle method (scVelo dynamical, Cyclum, Cyclone, Revelio, DeepCycle) on mESC or human fibroblast h5ad data and quantify agreement of inferred trajectories with annotated phases or DeepCycle's cell_cycle_theta.

name: rna-velocity-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on real datasets with known trajectory directions, or when quantitative CBDir/ICCoh benchmark scores are needed to validate velocity estimates.

name: rna-velocity-best-fitted-gene-selection
description: Use when a TFvelo run has completed (rc.h5ad output exists) and you need to extract -fitted genes, test KEGG pathway enrichment among them, and verify the sign consistency of top-weighted TFs on specific pathway gene sets.

name: rna-velocity-dynamical-model-gene-ranking
description: Use when comparing unsupervised feature-selection methods on a differentiation trajectory and you have spliced/unspliced counts so ScVelo's dynamical model can produce a likelihood-ranked gene set.

name: rna-velocity-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced counts (e.g. SMART-Seq2 U2OS cell cycle data) must be converted into velocity vectors and a cell-to-cell transition matrix to support directionality-aware trajectory reconstruction.

name: rna-velocity-estimation
description: Use when you have spliced/unspliced count matrices (AnnData/h5ad) from differentiation datasets such as pancreas, dentate gyrus, retina, hindbrain, erythroid or bone marrow, and need directed cell transitions, latent time, or CBDir benchmarking against scVelo.

name: rna-velocity-estimation-spliced-unspliced
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced count layers is available and the goal is to visualize predicted transcriptional trajectories as animated arrows/particles in a 3D embedding (e.g., PHATE/UMAP) inside CellexalVR.

name: rna-velocity-fate-probability-inference
description: Use when a pre-processed AnnData with cell-type 'clusters' annotations and a scVelo RNA velocity field is available and you need per-cell fate probabilities or end-fate frequencies toward terminal states (e.g., E15.5 endocrine α, β, ε fates), or to benchmark against CellRank.

name: rna-velocity-inference
description: Use when single-cell spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and you need velocity fields, latent trajectories, batch-corrected dynamics embeddings, or fate separation across multiple lineages where steady-state RNA velocity assumptions fail.

name: rna-velocity-intron-transcript-extraction
description: Use when preparing a kallisto/bustools index for RNA velocity or splicing-aware scRNA-seq quantification, so that pseudoalignment can separate spliced (cDNA) reads from unspliced (intronic) reads.

name: rna-velocity-latent-dynamics-modeling
description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData layers are available and the goal is RNA velocity on multi-lineage, time-dependent, or multi-batch data where strict steady-state assumptions of Velocyto/scVelo fail, or when batch-integrated velocities and latent trajectories are needed.

name: rna-velocity-latent-time-inference
description: Use when multi-batch single-cell transcriptomic data captures a continuous biological process (e.g., erythroid differentiation) and cells must be ordered in pseudo-time to validate that learned latent factors show distinct temporal profiles.

name: rna-velocity-moments-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing an scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. adata_mESC.h5ad from Zenodo) that lacks imputed 'Ms'/'Mu' layers, as a mandatory step before running DeepCycle or any unspliced-spliced RNA velocity analysis.

name: rna-velocity-pseudotime-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has pre-computed RNA velocity (scvelo/velocyto), root and terminal cell states are identifiable or supplied, and per-lineage pseudotime must be inferred and validated against a known cell type ordering.

name: rna-velocity-smoothing
description: Use when an scRNA-seq AnnData object with spliced counts and scVelo-derived RNA velocity must be denoised into meta-cell-level smoothed velocities as input for trajectory inference.

name: rna-velocity-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData object (with spliced/unspliced counts) needs trajectory inference: recovering parallel branches, within-population sub-flows, and cell pseudotime that direction-free TI methods (e.g., Slingshot) or velocity tools that lack path output (e.g., CellRank) cannot resolve.

name: rna-velocity-transition-matrix-construction
description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData with scvelo-computed RNA velocity is available and a probabilistic cell-state transition matrix is needed to sample differentiation trajectories or estimate root/terminal states.

name: rnafold-secondary-structure-curation
description: Use when candidate dsRNA/editing-enriched regions with genomic coordinates need structural validation or classification (e.g., stem >= 200 bp, <= 20% mismatches, adjusted MFE <= -0.35) before use as training labels or for final dsRNA annotation.

name: rnaseq-alignment-grch38
description: Use when RNA-seq reads (e.g. CLL samples like GSE66228) must be converted into an hg38-aligned, coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM suitable for CRIS or comparable BCR-reconstruction tools.

name: rnaseq-deseq2-count-modeling
