description: Use when computing gene-level differential expression between exactly two user-defined cohorts from a parsed pdacR dataset (GUI list format with $ex, $sampInfo, $featInfo with SYMBOL, $metadata), where the platform type determines the statistical backend.

name: rnaseq-dropout-characterization
description: Use when a cells-by-variants VAF matrix from scRNA-seq variant calling contains NA/missing entries and you need to quantify how much missingness is attributable to type I drop-out before lineage reconstruction or quality assessment.

name: rnaseq-expression-matrix-sample-feature-counting
description: Use when reproducing or auditing a published multi-dataset compendium table (dataset, type, sample description, n samples, n features, Used flag) from saved .rds expression objects rather than from publication text alone.

name: rnaseq-expression-median-cutoff-filtering
description: Use when starting from a raw RNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. >16,000 genes from ArrayExpress E-MTAB-11611) and low-abundance genes must be dropped by a median-expression cut-off before fitting models such as nestcv.glmnet.

name: rnaseq-expression-profiling-integration
description: Use when you have processed RNA-seq expression values for genes (e.g. from STAR/RSEM/DESeq2) and want them carried through a CCIVR cis-NAT identification run into Table.csv and Summary.csv outputs.

name: rnaseq-fusion-candidate-feature-extraction
description: Use when preparing spanning-read/split-read candidate fusion evidence (PCAWG positives, artificial chimeric negatives) as features for training or applying the HVLD filter in Anchored-fusion.

name: rnaseq-index-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a pre-filter such as Raptor can replace or complement an exact index like Mantis for membership queries of transcripts/reads against thousands of SRA RNA-Seq experiments, with resource and FPR metrics.

name: rnaseq-low-expression-gene-filtering
description: Use when a raw RNA-seq count matrix plus sample metadata (e.g., GEO GSE147507 infected vs mock lung cells) must be filtered for low-expression genes before DESeq2 DEG testing.

name: rnaseq-pileup-feature-extraction
description: Use when stranded RNAseq BAM files must be converted into per-position nucleotide frequency matrices (8 × 101) to feed a deep learning model for RNA editing site classification without coupled WGS/WES data.

name: rnaseq-read-alignment
description: Use when a human RNA-seq BAM (e.g., from TCGA/GDC) must be reduced to reads unmapped to hg19 and phiX so the resulting *_unmapped.fastq files can be fed to viRNAtrap for viral read detection.

name: rnaseq-splice-aware-variant-calling
description: Use when the goal is to call splicing-derived (SplAdder/ScanExitron/Arriba) plus SNV/indel variants from raw DNA/RNA sequencing reads as inputs to downstream neoepitope prediction.

name: rnaseq-time-series-network-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing gene regulatory network inference methods on a time-series RNA-Seq dataset with a known gold-standard GRN, requiring sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and runtime metrics per tool.

name: rnaseq-transcript-3prime-end-refinement
description: Use when a sorted, genome-aligned RNA-Seq BAM (e.g. HISAT2 + SAMtools) and a StringTie-reconstructed transcriptome (GTF) are available and you need de novo polyA site prediction and 3' end refinement without direct 3'-end sequencing.

name: rnaseq-transcript-quantitation-and-count-filtering
description: Use when a GTF transcriptome (e.g., from StringTie plus aptardi) contains many candidate transcript isoforms sharing 3' terminal exons and needs expression-based filtering before quantitation and differential analysis.

name: rnaseq-variant-call-validation
description: Use when RNA-seq-derived VCFs need validation against genotype array data (e.g., Axiom SNP array VCF from GSE131764) to confirm variant-calling fidelity before ASE or downstream analyses.

name: robinson-foulds-tree-distance-comparison
description: Use when evaluating inferred lineage/cell division trees (e.g., from LinRace, DCLEAR, Cassiopeia, Startle, LinTIMaT, or NJ-on-Hamming baselines) against a known ground-truth tree across simulation conditions such as mutation rate or dropout.

name: robust-huber-regression-cell-proportion-testing
description: Use when a sample-level trajectory (pseudotime from Wasserstein distances + diffusion maps + EIPLGraph) has been estimated on single-cell data (AnnData .h5ad) and you must rank which cell populations and genes change significantly along that trajectory.

name: robust-rank-aggregation-of-marker-lists
description: Use when building a final ranked marker list per cell type from reference scRNA-seq data where individual DE tests vary in their ability to predict cell types and a single consensus ranking is needed.

name: robust-regression-interaction-testing
description: Use when testing whether a gene-gene correlation differs between phenotypic subgroups (e.g. BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) in normalized RNA-seq count data, and per-link differential p-values are needed.

name: robust-subpopulation-identification-across-replicates
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices from two or more independent 10X replicates (e.g., matrix.mtx/gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) must be resolved into high-resolution cell subpopulations with a shuffled-data false-discovery control, and reproducible clusters must be matched across replicates.

name: robustness-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when stress-testing a trajectory-alignment method's robustness: synthetic single-cell trajectory pairs are available and the goal is to measure how alignment distance and conservation scores change as noise standard deviation increases.

name: robustness-sensitivity-analysis-of-prior-knowledge-networks
description: Use when a GRN-inference or network-based method consumes a prior gene interaction network and you must quantify how much method performance degrades when that prior is partially randomized or noisy.

name: roc-and-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a continuous per-cell score (e.g. signalling entropy rate) and binary or continuous ground-truth labels (pluripotent vs progenitor, or a pluripotency score) and need to quantify discriminative performance.

name: roc-auc-and-tpr-method-comparison
description: Use when ranking competing statistical detection methods on simulated count data with known positives, by comparing ROC AUC and TPR at a fixed 5% FPR across methods.

name: roc-auc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when simulated single-cell datasets with ground-truth covariate-pseudotime interaction labels are available and you must compare interaction-detection accuracy (AUC) of PhenoPath vs DE-based methods across varying fractions of interacting genes.

name: roc-auc-computation
description: Use when benchmarking a splicing-status predictor (e.g., Forseti splice_prob) with ROC AUC against trivial baselines on scRNA-seq reads carrying ground-truth spliced/unspliced labels.

name: roc-auc-computation-for-copy-number-detection
description: Reference for quantifying and comparing CNA-detection accuracy of scRNA-seq copy-number callers via ROC-AUC against single-cell DNA-seq ground truth, as done for XClone on the 4416-cell 2R astrocytoma minor clone.

name: roc-auc-computation-gene-ranking
description: Use when comparing accuracy and runtime of DEG prediction methods on artificial scRNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth DEGs, where genes must be ranked by method-specific significance scores and evaluated via ROC AUC.

name: roc-auc-curve-comparison
description: Use when two or more RNA editing detection tools (e.g. REDInet, EditPredict, RED-ML, RDDpred) must be compared head-to-head on the same labeled site set, and per-tool ROC curves, AUC, or FNR are the requested performance metrics.

name: roc-auc-curve-evaluation
description: Use when comparing ranked drug/compound predictions from two or more pipelines (e.g., ASGARD multi-cluster score vs. CLUE, DrInsight, Alakwaa's, Guo's) against a known positive-drug ground truth and the comparison must be quantified as ROC/AUC with statistical significance testing.

name: roc-auc-evaluation
description: Use when you need an unbiased performance estimate (ROC AUC) for a glmnet/caret model fitted on high-dimensional data (P >> n) by concatenating left-out outer CV fold predictions, or when comparing outer vs inner CV AUC to detect optimistic bias from whole-dataset filtering or unbalanced resampling.

name: roc-auc-evaluation-of-domain-markers
description: Use when you have identified spatial domains on multi-slice spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 12 human DLPFC Visium slices) with known cortical-layer marker genes and need a quantitative, comparable accuracy metric for domain-marker recovery.

name: roc-auc-evaluation-of-read-classification
description: Use when Forseti (or a similar per-read splicing-status classifier) has produced spliced/unspliced probabilities on reads with known ground-truth labels, and you need ROC/AUC to quantify predictive accuracy.

name: roc-auc-method-comparison
description: Use when two or more interaction-scoring methods are applied to the same candidate enhancer-gene set and you must decide which performs better against perturbation-based ground truth (e.g., CRISPRi) via ROC/PR curves.

name: roc-auc-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a trained binary classifier (e.g., CNN or SVM on 41-nt RNA segments) must be scored on balanced positive/negative test sets and reported via Sn, Sp, Acc, MCC, and ROC AUC.

name: roc-auc-pr-aupr-benchmark-computation
description: Use when validating a fusion/artifact classifier (e.g., scFusion's bi-LSTM) on held-out scRNA-seq candidates where median ROC AUC and PR AUPR across datasets quantify discrimination of artifacts.

name: roc-auroc-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantitatively benchmark cell-cluster scoring or cluster-merge significance methods as binary classifiers, by computing ROC curves and AUROC against known ground-truth subcluster labels on scRNA-seq data.

name: roc-based-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare two or more marker-based cell annotation methods on identical datasets, using author-curated cell labels as ground truth and AUROC as the comparison metric.

name: roc-based-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when a Seurat WNN joint mRNA-ADT clustering needs biological validation: after identifying a protein-defined cluster (e.g. CD14+ CD86-high monocytes) and you must confirm its identity via differentially expressed transcripts such as inflammatory and activation genes.

name: roc-curve-auc-evaluation
description: Use when you must decide whether a model-specific cell-to-cell similarity metric (e.g. NPD from a variational posterior) discriminates same-type query/reference neighbor pairs better than plain Euclidean distance in a learned embedding.

name: roc-curve-comparison
description: Use when you need to verify that a sparse regression method selects the correct features, by comparing feature-selection ROC curves over regularization paths against competitors on simulated data with known ground truth.

name: roc-curve-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a binary classifier built on DCNet-inferred cell-type abundance features (e.g., LUAD vs LUSC prediction) must be validated on a held-out test set with ROC AUC, precision, and an ROC curve.

name: roc-prc-and-partial-auc-computation
description: Use when benchmarking doublet detectors on experimentally annotated scRNA-seq ground truth and you need accuracy metrics (AUC, AUPRC, pAUC800/900/950/975) plus cross-dataset stability ranks.

name: roc-precision-recall-curve-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers (e.g. MACS3, HOMER, SEACR, HMMRATAC) on synthetic reads that come with designed ground-truth peaks, so that varying thresholds can sweep TPR/FPR and precision/recall.

name: roc-sensitivity-specificity-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking DE detection on simulated scRNA-Seq data with known DE gene labels and dropout noise, and you need ROC-based sensitivity at fixed specificity (0.90) to rank imputation methods.

name: rogue-guided-cell-reclustering
description: Use when a scRNA-seq cluster's purity is questionable (per-cluster ROGUE < ~0.8) and pure subtypes must be resolved by re-clustering that subpopulation, or when validating cluster homogeneity against a 0.9 ROGUE purity threshold.

name: rogue-intra-cluster-heterogeneity-scoring
description: Use when deciding whether visually distinct single-cell clusters should be unified or kept separate — compute per-cluster and merged-cluster ROGUE scores and compare them (e.g., Hydra neuron ectodermal subtypes vs. their unified cluster).

name: rogue-statistic-computation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq analysis needs to quantify whether an identified cell cluster is a pure population, or to compare cluster purity across batches, individuals, or re-clustering strategies.

name: roi-boundary-zero-padding
description: Use when per-ROI histogram-equalized imputation patches (from SERM's sliding-window stage) must be merged into a single expression matrix with globally consistent expression values.

name: roi-selection-histogram-equalization
description: Use when you have a sparse, dropout-affected scRNA-seq expression matrix plus a fitted PDF from a prior distribution-learning step, and you need to impute missing values by analytically enforcing self-consistency via ROI-based histogram equalization.

name: rolling-window-derivative-computation
description: Use when you need to convert a barcode count table (flexiplex_barcodes_counts.txt) into a filtered whitelist by finding the knee/inflection point of the barcode frequency-versus-rank curve, as in empty-droplet removal for single-cell data.

name: root-cell-constrained-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when simulated single-cell datasets (e.g. VeloSim cycle-tree, 785 cells x 600 genes) have known ground-truth pseudotime and a known root cell, and you need to quantify how accurately TI methods recover cell ordering.

name: root-cell-selection-from-activity-scores
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix needs a biologically motivated trajectory root: cluster identities are known (e.g., basal vs. differentiated epithelial cells) but the origin for pseudotime inference must be chosen objectively from pluripotency/differentiation activity scores.

name: root-cell-selection-from-marker-anchors
description: Use when generating a pseudotemporal ordering from flow cytometry single-cell data before MAPiT transformation and a trajectory algorithm such as Wanderlust requires root cells to define the trajectory start.

name: root-cell-selection-in-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a single-cell trajectory method requires a biologically early reference cell (e.g., stem/progenitor or earliest time-stage cell) to orient pseudotime before branch detection with RSKG.

name: root-terminal-state-probability-thresholding
description: Use when a scvelo-processed AnnData object with a velocity field must be decomposed into root and terminal cell sets before simulating Markov-chain differentiation trajectories with Cytopath, and no prior root/terminal annotations are supplied.

name: rooted-tree-data-structure-implementation
description: Use when the analysis requires representing branched single-cell pseudotime trajectories as rooted trees with node-level expression profiles so they can be compared via tree alignment rather than linear dynamic time warping.

name: row-max-scaling-to-unit-interval
description: Use when raw gene/protein count matrices (TSV or CSV) must be transformed to the 0–1 range expected by a sigmoid-output VAE, or when reproducing the FAVA preprocessed_matrix.tsv input format.

name: row-stochastic-normalization-of-cell-cell-kernels
description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix must be filtered by projecting it onto a cell-cell similarity kernel derived from an annotated attribute (cell type, spatial coordinates, cell cycle phase), before subtracting the projection.

name: row-wise-column-rank-ordering
description: Use when beginning a UniBic/runibic biclustering run on a continuous expression matrix: the input matrix must first be converted to an index matrix where each row lists column indexes sorted by that row's increasing values.

name: rpca-distance-based-anchor-filtering
description: Use when integrating multiple single-cell RNA-seq samples with STACAS/Seurat and you must remove anchors whose pairwise rPCA distance or inconsistent cell type labels make them unreliable before scoring anchors and building the integration guide tree.

name: rphenograph-graph-based-single-cell-clustering
description: Use when you have scMM latent representations of multimodal single-cell data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA + surface protein counts stored as RNA_count.mtx/Protein_count.mtx with gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) and need high-resolution, interpretable cluster assignments for downstream heatmap visualization.

name: rpkm-read-coverage-normalization
description: Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers on scReadSim synthetic reads and you need to compare read enrichment of called peaks vs ground-truth peaks (or non-peaks) in a length-normalized way via RPKM distributions.

name: rpm-normalization-counting
description: Use when per-sample tncRNA subclass counts (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH, tRNA halves) must be expressed in a library-size-independent unit or reconciled against the paper's species-level totals.

name: rrho-marker-overlap-analysis
description: Use when two single-cell cohorts of the same biological system must be compared at the level of per-cell-type differential marker rankings and downstream enrichment results, to verify that a computational surrogate (e.g., scSemiProfiler output) reproduces ground-truth analyses.

name: rrna-binding-protein-sequence-analysis
description: Use when candidate RBPs have no physical interaction with gold circRNA regulators (e.g., the 16 non-physically-associated candidates from CRIT) and motif-level functional connection must be established from circRNA sequences.

name: rrna-contaminant-read-depletion
description: Use when raw Ribo-seq FastQ reads have been adapter-trimmed and length-filtered, and abundant rRNA/tRNA contamination must be depleted before HISAT2/Bowtie2 alignment and htseq-count CDS quantification.

name: rsem-transcriptome-read-simulation
description: Use when a controlled benchmark of transcriptome assemblers is needed and a ground-truth transcriptome (e.g., hg38 NCBI RefSeq) must be paired with realistic simulated reads.

name: rseqc-tool-execution
description: Use when computing gene body coverage across many split per-cell scRNA-seq BAM files with RSeQC-equivalent output at ~10-fold lower cost, or when benchmarking geneBodyCoverage.pl vs geneBody_coverage.py on the same BAM/BED.

name: rsq-based-gene-weighting-for-factor-estimation
description: Use when reconstructing or adapting IA-SVA to estimate a surrogate variable for a hidden factor (e.g., patient or cell-type heterogeneity) from single-cell read counts after adjusting for known covariates such as patient_id and geo_lib_size.

name: rss-likelihood-summary-statistics-modeling
description: Use when only GWAS/eQTL summary statistics are available (no individual-level genotypes/phenotypes) and joint fine-mapping plus colocalization across multiple traits or tissues is needed, provided a reference LD matrix and sample sizes can be supplied.

name: rubins-rule-multiple-imputation-pooling
description: Use when a single-cell dataset lacks biological replicates and Scanpro's bootstrapping produces ~100 iterations of per-cluster regression statistics that must be pooled into a single robust result per cell type.

name: run-length-array-compression
description: Use when indexing many datasets with per-dataset Bloom filters whose nested merges along a comb tree must be stored compactly, and per-dataset membership must be recoverable from run-length aggregation values.

name: runtime-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when you need to quantify runtime and peak-memory costs of PAS computation (fast_ucell, fast_score_genes) vs UCell, AUCell, score_genes, or SCPA on datasets scaling from 10,000 up to 1,263,676 cells with 1383–14,300 pathways.

name: runtime-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of scRNA-seq clustering or batch-effect-removal methods on a fixed dataset size (e.g. 30,000 cells, 30 batches) and you need per-method runtime and peak-memory numbers.

name: runtime-and-memory-profiling-across-tools
description: Use when benchmarking computational pipelines on large-scale scRNA-seq data (e.g. >0.6 million cells) under a fixed RAM limit, and you need per-tool peak memory, runtime, and crash/completion outcomes as comparable metrics.

name: runtime-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when a new single-cell annotation or cell-calling tool must be validated against baseline tools on the same datasets, with per-cell predictions scored against ground-truth labels and runtimes recorded on identical hardware.

name: runtime-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when evaluating or reporting the computational cost of ERgene reference-gene screening on an expression matrix (e.g. GSE125792), especially when choosing a computational depth or comparing speed to geNorm/Normfinder/Keeper.

name: runtime-benchmark-measurement
description: Use when you have replaced or re-implemented a performance-critical component (e.g. an interval query structure) and must prove both functional equivalence with the original and a measured runtime improvement on the real workload.

name: runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing processing-time (wall-clock runtime) of scKB-COPILOT against Cell Ranger on the same scRNA-seq FASTQ datasets, or when reproducing the paper's runtime benchmark table across toy col0, full col0, and PBMC datasets.

name: runtime-benchmarking-across-methods
description: Use when comparing computational runtime or scalability of competing spatial-omics feature-detection methods across multiple platforms, or when verifying that a new method's runtime matches published benchmark claims.

name: runtime-benchmarking-across-sample-sizes
description: Use when comparing the wall-clock runtime of significant genetic meta-marker miners (HOGImine, SiNIMin, FastCMH) across subsampled biobank sizes, or when validating that a faster miner outputs the same patterns as a baseline.

name: runtime-benchmarking-clustering-methods
description: Use when you need to measure or verify the runtime and cluster-count scalability of an scRNA-seq clustering method on a large (100k+) cell dataset, with sparse big-data mode enabled.

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-bioinformatics-tools
description: Use when a paper claims a new tool is substantially faster than an existing method and you must reproduce or verify the runtime comparison on the same datasets and hardware (e.g., 4 CPU cores).

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-computational-methods
description: Use when comparing execution speed of two implementations of the same method suite (e.g., R vs Python decoupleR) on large simulated omics matrices, or when reproducing a scalability benchmark reported as ms/sample/regulator.

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-feature-selection-methods
description: Use when you need to compare wall-clock runtime of feature/marker-selection algorithms on the same datasets at an identical number of selected features, e.g. reproducing or extending the paper's Table 2 speed comparison.

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-implementations
description: Use when two implementations of the same decomposition (e.g. JIVE variants) must be compared for computational efficiency on identical data, and runtime/memory gains must be validated against equivalence of the fitted decomposition.

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-tcr-models
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of TCR-transcriptome integration methods (mvTCR, CoNGA, tessa) on datasets of varying size, or when deciding whether a model can scale to atlas-level (>60k cell) immune profiling data.

name: runtime-benchmarking-of-ti-methods
description: Decision support for choosing a TI method when the input atlas exceeds ~10^5–10^6 cells (e.g. MOCA-style organogenesis data) and runtime plus preservation of global connectivity across parameter choices must be compared against baselines like PAGA, Palantir, STREAM and Monocle3.

name: runtime-benchmarking-on-subsampled-atlas-datasets
description: Use when you need to show that a single-cell integration method scales to atlas-level (~1 million cells, ~147 batches) cross-species data by measuring wall-clock runtime against deep-learning baselines at multiple subsample sizes.

name: runtime-comparison-visualization
description: Use when comparing computational cost of spatial transcriptomics clustering methods on the same samples and K grid, e.g. showing an EM-based method like iSC.MEB is faster than MCMC-based BASS/BayesSpace.

name: runtime-comparison-visualization
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of several feature-prediction or SVG methods across multiple spatial transcriptomics datasets, and you need per-method elapsed wall-clock times rendered as a comparison figure.

name: runtime-latency-profiling
description: Use when comparing inference speed and memory of malignant cell annotation tools on scRNA-seq count matrices subsampled to 100–1,000,000 cells, on a fixed GPU/CPU hardware platform.

name: runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when choosing or justifying a metacell construction tool for large scRNA-seq datasets — you need CPU time and peak memory as a function of cell count across methods such as MC2, SuperCell, and SEACells.

name: runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when validating that a per-cell metric computed over scRNA data (e.g. TEI via orthomap2tei.get_tei) remains tractable on datasets tiled to millions of cells, or when producing runtime/memory scaling tables for a sparse-matrix implementation.

name: runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when benchmarking a new algorithm implementation — e.g., KMD linkage runs across k values on simulated datasets — and you must log per-run timing and peak memory to verify computational-feasibility claims such as O(n^2) memory independent of k.

name: runtime-memory-profiling
description: Use when evaluating a binning-directory index (IBF/MIBF) for approximate sequence search: you must trade off index size (1-8 GiB), (19,19) vs (23,19) minimizers, compression, and partitioning against build time, query time, peak memory, and false-positive assignments.

name: runtime-memory-profiling-of-bioinformatics-pipelines
description: Use when a claim about a bioinformatics tool's speed or memory footprint (e.g. '7x faster', '15 min for 300M reads') must be independently reproduced across scaling points, with matched thread settings and per-fraction measurements.

name: runtime-memory-profiling-scrnaseq-tools
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of scRNA-seq rare-cell detection methods: you need running time and peak memory measured across subsampled datasets spanning ~1,000 to ~68,000 cells.

name: runtime-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the total computational runtime of two sketching/subsampling methods on a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., Sphetcher-H vs geometric sketching on the 2,026,641-cell MOCA dataset), especially when per-stage timing breakdowns are needed.

name: runtime-performance-benchmarking
description: Use when an exact computation with known excessive runtime (e.g. 20 min–3 h per affinity matrix) must be replaced by an approximation and you must quantify the speedup without degrading a defined accuracy metric.

name: runtime-performance-curve-plotting
description: Decision support for choosing scRNA-seq sample size and candidate-TF budget before running scGATE_logic(): when you must verify inference quality saturates (log10 BF plateau) and how runtime scales with cell count and TFs per target.

name: runtime-performance-profiling
description: Use when you need to show a pipeline's runtime scales practically with dataset size, e.g. validating that Spaco colorization completes within bounded time on single-cell-resolution SRT datasets up to 100,000 cells.

name: runtime-performance-profiling
description: Use when quantifying how mapping or integration runtime scales with cell count, e.g. benchmarking Symphony reference builds (20K-1.39M cells) and query mappings (1K-100K cells) against de novo Harmony integration.

name: runtime-performance-profiling
description: Use when a pipeline step (e.g., SVD inside JIVE) is suspected to be a computational bottleneck on large data and you must quantify how much a partial/approximate solver reduces runtime before adopting it.

name: runtime-performance-profiling-large-datasets
description: Use when you must verify that a dimensionality-reduction method scales to a million-plus-observation dataset by timing it against a baseline algorithm with a fixed timeout (e.g., 24 hours for Barnes-Hut t-SNE).

name: runtime-performance-profiling-of-annotation-pipelines
description: Use when benchmarking how quickly automated cell-type annotation methods run on the same clustered scRNA-seq data, or when justifying a method choice by both speed and accuracy across multiple datasets.

name: runtime-profiling-across-clustering-methods
description: Use when comparing clustering runtimes and resource costs of single-cell methods on identical inputs — e.g. FFC vs SC3/Seurat on Splatter-simulated data or FFC vs pegasus/scanpy on the Mouse Cell Atlas — while also recording ARI/purity quality.

name: runtime-profiling-of-imputation-pipelines
description: Use when imputation methods must be benchmarked for scalability on tens of thousands of cells (e.g., 62,893-cell, 91.9%-dropout droplet data) and a wall-clock runtime ordering is required alongside accuracy scores.

name: runtime-profiling-of-integration-methods
description: Decision support for choosing a multimodal integration method when run time matters: datasets such as CITE-seq CBMCs (GSE100866) processed with identical pre-processing, clustered at matched Louvain resolution, and timed per method.

name: runtime-profiling-of-sequence-tools
description: Use when choosing a sequence-search tool for FASTQ/FASTA data where sequencing errors may cause exact matchers to miss targets, and you need runtime and sensitivity measured head-to-head on identical input.

name: runtime-scalability-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to empirically characterize the computational scalability of a clustering or embedding method — e.g., verifying a claimed linear-time behavior or comparing runtimes of competing methods like scMDC and Specter as cell number grows.

name: runtime-scalability-benchmarking-of-single-cell-methods
description: Use when reproducing or extending runtime scalability comparisons of single-cell correction methods across increasing subsample sizes of a large dataset (e.g., ~500,000-cell Heart Cell Atlas).

name: runtime-scalability-profiling
description: Use when choosing an imputation method for a large scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., the 162,490-cell Darrah dataset) and you need to establish which methods complete in reasonable time versus failing with out-of-memory errors.

name: runtime-scaling-analysis
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of imputation or similar single-cell methods on datasets of hundreds of thousands of cells, where runtime-not accuracy-is the question and single-core timings must be isolated.

name: runtime-scaling-benchmark-across-cell-counts
description: Use when comparing computational runtime scaling of dimensionality-reduction methods (LDA/HSS-LDA, PCA, UMAP, PHATE) on single-cell data as cell counts increase, or when judging whether a supervised LDA embedding trades acceptable runtime for class-separation quality (silhouette, PCE).

name: runtime-scaling-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify or verify how penalized regression runtimes in HDMAC (R/Shiny) scale with number of observations and high-dimensional variables, or to reproduce the paper's computing-time table.

name: runtime-scaling-visualization
description: Use when a paper claims an algorithm scales linearly (or better) with input size and you need to empirically reproduce the runtime-versus-size curve on downsampled datasets before applying the method to large SRT data.

name: runtime-scaling-visualization
description: Use when comparing the computational cost of cell-type annotation methods on scRNA-seq data, or when reproducing a runtime scaling benchmark across varying training-set (e.g. 500–10,000 cells) and testing-set (e.g. 1,000–50,000 cells) sizes.

name: runtime-speedup-quantification
description: Use when you must quantify how much faster an optimized C++/OpenMP backend runs versus R's single-threaded baseline (e.g., %*%), across varying core counts, with reproducible timing over many repetitions.

name: runtime-vs-sensitivity-tradeoff-analysis
description: Decision support for choosing SCSit tolerance settings: when you need to know whether enabling more than one mismatch and one indel in SPLiT-seq barcode identification gains enough reads to outweigh the extra runtime.

name: saliency-map-gene-attribution
description: Use when a trained Cancer-Finder ST or scRNA checkpoint must be interrogated for which genes drive malignant-vs-non-malignant predictions, e.g. to derive a ranked tumor-interface gene signature like the ccRCC 10-gene list.

name: sam-alignment-file-processing
description: Use when alignment reads are supplied as SAM files (collapsed or uncollapsed) and must be processed by small RNA counting tools, or when comparing counting runtimes across tools on the same alignment inputs.

name: sam-alignment-name-sorting-preprocessing
description: Use when running CircAST downstream of tophat2 alignments: the pipeline requires accepted_hits.bam sorted by read name and converted to accepted_hits.sorted.sam before isoform assembly and quantification.

name: sam-alignment-sorting-and-bam-conversion
description: Use when RiboSeq (or similar) alignment output exists as merged SAM files from conjoint genome/transcriptome alignment and indexed, uniquely-mapped BAM files are needed for downstream counting, P-site, or QC steps.

name: sam-bam-name-sorting-and-conversion
description: Use when a CircAST-style circular isoform assembly pipeline has produced accepted_hits.bam from TopHat2 paired-end alignment and the downstream assembly tool requires a read-name-sorted SAM file.

name: sam-file-umi-position-extraction
description: Use when UMI-containing FASTQ reads have been aligned to a genomic reference (e.g. STAR with no introns) yielding a sorted SAM file, and you need each UMI's complete list of genomic mapping positions to measure mapping-shift distances between reads sharing a UMI.

name: sam-flag-based-multimapper-removal
description: Use when merged SAM alignment files from the conjoint HISAT2/Bowtie2 genome-transcriptome alignment must be reduced to uniquely mapped reads and converted to sorted, indexed BAM files.

name: sam-flag-field-interpretation
description: Use when a BAM-handling step needs to route aligned reads by strand or read-group: e.g. building strand-specific or per-RG BAM partitions from a single input BAM prior to downstream peak calling or pileup analyses.

name: sam-merge-and-mapped-read-filtering
description: Use when a ribosome profiling pipeline aligns the same FASTA with two mappers (HISAT2 then Bowtie2) and the resulting SAM outputs must be merged, filtered to mapped reads, and converted to BAM/BAI.

name: sam-significance-testing
description: Use when you have a background-subtracted microarray expression matrix with a class-encoded response vector (e.g. WT vs. mutant samples) and need to call differentially expressed genes at a specified FDR cutoff.

name: sam-to-bam-conversion
description: Use when raw WES/WGS reads of a tumor-normal pair have just been aligned to GRCh37/GRCh38 with BWA v0.7.17 and the SAM output must be converted to BAM before GATK v4.2.0.0 processing and Mutect2 variant calling.

name: same-group-level-similarity-scoring
description: Use when scoring candidate 2D embeddings (e.g., PCA, t-SNE, UMAP) for trajectory-inference suitability and you need to measure whether local neighbor structure in the embedding respects pre-computed cell cluster/group assignments.

name: same-workstation-wall-clock-benchmarking
description: Use when measuring how much a GPU-accelerated reimplementation (e.g. cudaMMC vs 3D-GNOME) reduces wall-clock time for generating 100-model chromatin 3D ensembles per chromosome on one fixed workstation.

name: sample-covariance-matrix-estimation
description: Use when the input is a sparsity-filtered cell-gene expression matrix and the goal is to expose its eigenvalue density for comparison against random matrix theory universality (Marchenko-Pastur) predictions.

name: sample-distribution-boxplot-comparison
description: Use when you have probe-level expression matrices (e.g. GEO datasets like GSE4786) and need to visually confirm that normalization to an internal reference gene reduced per-sample distribution differences.

name: sample-index-barcode-demultiplexing-impossible-combinations
description: Use when FASTQ data from multiplexed single-cell libraries on a patterned flow-cell machine (HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq) must be checked for swapped read fraction, especially with a same-library HiSeq 2500 control available.

name: sample-level-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when single-cell or pathomics data are summarized per sample as cell-cluster/structure proportions (plus cluster medians in PCA space) and you need an unsupervised sample-level distance matrix W to cluster samples or infer disease trajectories.

name: sample-level-genotype-qc
description: Use when preparing per-sample biallelic SNP calls from RNA-seq VCFs for allele-specific expression analysis, where homozygous, low-coverage, or allele-imbalanced genotype calls must be excluded before statistical testing.

name: sample-level-niche-score-computation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq study identifies a multi-cell-type disease niche and you need one scalar per sample (sum of cell-type percentages) to test group differences, e.g. EAD vs non-EAD across cold preservation and portal reperfusion stages.

name: sample-loading-hierarchical-clustering
description: Use when you have a completed Tensor-cell2cell decomposition (e.g., rank-6 on a 4D communication tensor) and want to check whether sample loadings across factors resolve clusters concordant with phenotype labels such as condition or severity.

name: sample-metadata-batch-annotation
description: Use when a merged multi-study microarray matrix shows dominant variance driven by study-of-origin (data series/platform) and the known batch must be removed while retaining the biological signal (e.g. MDI differentiation time course).

name: sample-outlier-detection-percentile-thresholding
description: Use when a raw barcode counts table (e.g. from BARtab or a GEO deposit such as GSE246611) needs sample-level and barcode-level QC before downstream barcoding analysis.

name: sample-permutation-baseline-analysis
description: Use when validating RNA-seq variant calls against an orthogonal genotyping platform and you need a null (randomly-paired) concordance baseline to prove that high self-by-self genotype agreement is not an artifact of SNP overlap alone.

name: sample-score-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when rRoma.R has produced a ModuleMatrix of sample scores for tested gene sets and you need to display per-sample module activity as a clustered heatmap annotated with sample-group labels to confirm which modules are shifted or overdispersed.

name: sample-similarity-visualization-euclidean-distance
description: Use when you have run SAM significance testing (e.g., Sig_GenesSAM with fdr.cutoff 0.4) on background-subtracted microarray data and need to visually check whether samples cluster by response class using the significant genes.

name: sample-size-inverse-estimation
description: Use when planning scCODA differential abundance experiments and you must know how many biological replicates are needed to detect a compositional shift of a given log-fold change, especially for rare vs abundant cell types.

name: sample-specific-network-construction
description: Use when per-patient (personalized) co-expression networks are needed from TCGA RNA-seq expression matrices, e.g. before running per-patient WMDS.netP driver-gene identification.

name: sample-to-sample-variability-analysis
description: Use when you have raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices spanning multiple samples and conditions (e.

name: sample-wise-pseudobulk-expression-aggregation
description: Use when you have an adjusted single-cell expression matrix from multiple samples and conditions and need valid sample-level differential state testing per cell type rather than naive per-cell differential expression.

name: samplewise-optimal-tsne-embedding
description: Use when an EMBEDR perplexity sweep (e.g. sweep_values=[25, 100, 250]) has been fit to single-cell data (e.g. Tabula Muris marrow scRNA-seq) and you need a per-cell adaptive embedding for downstream clustering or visualization.

name: samtools-faidx-sequence-retrieval
description: Use when you have genomic coordinates (e.g., FWHM of the LOESS-smoothed coverage peak of a differentially expressed uTAR) and need the underlying FASTA sequence for homology-based annotation.

name: samtools-unmapped-read-extraction
description: Use when starting from 10x scRNAseq cellranger count output (possorted_genome_bam.bam) and you need the host-unaligned reads, with barcodes and UMIs, to realign against a viral or bacterial pathogen reference.

name: sanger-concordance-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a computationally inferred IGHV mutation status or dominant-clone IGHV gene call against available clinical Sanger-based classification for the same CLL samples.

name: sankey-diagram-visualization
description: Use when you have per-cell predicted labels from a classifier (e.g., SciBet Bet predictions) plus known true labels and need to visualize label-to-label correspondence, such as cross-species mapping results.

name: sars-cov-2-gene-annotation-mapping
description: Use when scPathoQuant per-gene pathogen UMI outputs exist for the same 10x samples under two alignment options (bbmap default and -align bowtie2) and you need to verify that per-gene SARS-CoV-2 UMI quantifications are consistent across aligners.

name: saverx-denoising-ablation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure how much SAVER-X denoising contributes to cTP-net protein-imputation accuracy, or to compare the denoising ablation against other parameter tweaks on a CITE-seq holdout benchmark.

name: saverx-scrna-count-denoising
description: Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., CITE-PBMC, CITE-CBMC, REAP-PBMC, HCA MantonCB1/MantonBM1, or van Galen AML counts in Seurat v3 format) will be fed to cTP-net protein imputation and must first be denoised with SAVER-X.

name: savitzky-golay-width-curve-smoothing
description: Use when rendering branching single-cell trajectories as stream plots whose branch width must be proportional to the total number of cells at a given pseudotime, and when gene-expression overlays along branches are needed.

name: saw-pipeline-spatial-data-processing
description: Use when the input is a SAW-processed Stereo-seq spatial dataset (unmapped FASTQ with outUnMappedFq=1, e.g. Zenodo 10685805) and the goal is per-spot lineage barcode annotation and spatial clone territory mapping.

name: sbml-model-export-and-validation
description: Use when a generic genome-scale reconstruction (e.g. Recon2.04 or Recon3D_01) must be made flux-consistent and exported as SBML to serve as the COBRA-format input for context-specific reconstruction with rFASTCORMICS.

name: sbml-qual-model-export
description: Use when a finalized, refined GRN (e.g., an adjacency matrix of signed gene-gene interactions) needs to be turned into a draft Boolean Network in SBML file format for simulation or manual editing.

name: sc-clustering-enhancement-from-external-labels
description: Use when you already have cluster labels for a scRNA-seq dataset from another method (Seurat, CIDR, etc.) and want to improve their accuracy rather than cluster de novo.

name: sc-rna-seq-circadian-phase-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (droplet-based like 10X Genomics Chromium or plate-based) lack sample-time labels and circadian phase per cell must be estimated from expression of core clock genes plus de novo-identified cyclers.

name: sc-rna-seq-data-preprocessing
description: Use when loading raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g. .h5 matrices with cells×genes layout) as input to scCAD or its HVG/HIG ensemble feature selection, and the matrix has not yet been gene-filtered or log-normalized.

name: sc-rna-seq-expression-normalization
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., a GEO download like the GSE113197 Ind4 breast epithelial sample) must be QC-filtered and normalized in R before clustering, annotation, or activity() scoring.

name: sc-rna-seq-multimapping-aware-alignment
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-Seq data for transposable element expression analysis, where default gene-alignment pipelines discard multi-mapping reads originating from repetitive TEs.

name: sc-rna-seq-preprocessing-filtering-logtransformation
description: Use when preparing raw or lightly processed scRNA-Seq count matrices (e.g. GEO downloads like GSE59739 CPM or GSE102962 TPM) before NMF dictionary learning, knowledge transfer, or downstream clustering such as SC3.

name: sc-rna-seq-subpopulation-mapping
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced/unspliced layers contains a proliferative subpopulation (e.g. Leiden cluster 0 in human fibroblasts) and the goal is to resolve the G1-to-G0 exit path and its marker genes.

name: sc-rna-seq-unique-read-fraction-quantification
description: Use when processing raw scRNA-seq FASTQs (e.g. 10X human PBMC, Tabula Muris, lemur lung, mole rat spleen, sea urchin embryo) and you need to measure how many uniquely mapped reads fall outside current gene annotations (uTARs) to assess annotation completeness.

name: sc-rnaseq-cluster-annotation
description: Use when a processed Seurat object carries broad clusters (or SCISSORS-revealed subclusters) that need cell-type labels, and you want markers specific to the target cluster rather than generic upregulated genes.

name: sc-rnaseq-communication-inference
description: Use when you have a normalized single-cell (or spatially resolved) transcriptomics matrix with cell group labels and want to infer neuron-neuron communication networks, especially neurotransmitter signaling absent from protein-only ligand-receptor databases.

name: sc-rnaseq-library-size-normalization
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., counts_dt from splatSimulate, or the 3005-cell mouse cortex/hippocampus matrix) must be depth-normalized and log2-transformed before running endr, UMAP, or t-SNE.

name: sc-rnaseq-quality-control-and-normalization
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE149614 HCC01T/HCC03N .h5ad or similar) require QC, normalization, and HVG selection before batch correction or DEG analysis.

name: sc-st-embedding-transfer-learning
description: Use when you have SC count matrix plus ST counts with spot spatial coordinates and cell-type labels, and need single-cell spatial mapping, pseudo-spatial adjacency, or colocalization of cell types (e.g., TSKs vs endothelial cells in hSCC).

name: sc-st-mapping-matrix-inference
description: Use when you have normalized SC and ST datasets and need to map every single cell to a spatial coordinate on ST spots — e.g. to build a single-cell level spatial transcriptomic landscape or run cell-type-specific spatial DE along a tissue axis.

name: scaffold-simulation-dataset-generation
description: Use when you need simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks with known ground truth — e.g., testing whether a trajectory-suitability check correctly flags trajectory-free simulations (homogeneous cells) while not falsely flagging linear-trajectory simulations.

name: scalability-analysis-of-clustering-pipelines
description: Use when quantifying how a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method's runtime and peak memory grow with cell count — e.g. comparing a correlation-based method against correlation-free baselines at 10k/100k/1M-cell scales.

name: scalability-benchmarking-of-clustering-methods
description: Use when comparing how clustering/batch-correction methods scale with many batches and tens of thousands of cells, or when a candidate method must be ruled in/out on computing time or memory (e.g. a 32 GB limit).

name: scalability-curve-visualization
description: Use when you need to show a tool's runtime scales acceptably with dataset size — e.g., colorizing single-cell-resolution SRT datasets of 1k–100,000 cells within a bounded time budget.

name: scalability-performance-evaluation-omics-methods
description: Use when comparing execution-speed scaling of two implementations of an omics method across large simulated datasets, where runtime must be normalized per sample and per regulator.

name: scale-free-degree-distribution-fitting
description: Use when comparing GRN inference methods (e.g., SCING vs. GRNBOOST2, ppcor, PIDC) on topology quality, or when judging whether inferred single-cell network structures approximate a scale-free degree distribution.

name: scale-free-network-soft-thresholding
description: Use when you need unsupervised gene program/module discovery from scRNA-seq data and want to benchmark against or replace factorization methods like ICA or NMF, starting from an annotated Seurat object.

name: scale-free-topology-assessment
description: Use when a gene co-expression network or module has been inferred (e.g. via SCANet/BioNERO WGCNA) and you need to validate that its graph topology is biologically plausible before selecting hubs or downstream modules.

name: scale-free-topology-fitting
description: Use when you have a constructed gene co-expression or differential co-expression network (adjacency or edge list) and need to validate that its degree distribution approximately follows a scale-free topology before downstream driver-node analysis.

name: scale-invariant-aggregation-optimization
description: Use when raw CT values or normalized expression matrices for multiple candidate reference genes (internal controls) are available and a single optimally weighted virtual reference gene is needed for ΔΔCT normalization.

name: scaled-entropy-distribution-comparison
description: Use when validating whether predictive entropy from classifiers trained on labeled cells can flag cells whose ground truth labels were corrupted, e.g. simulating annotation mistakes before self-training cell selection.

name: scaled-expression-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually validate temporal expression patterns of differentially expressed genes and their linked regulators (activators vs repressors) across omics layers from simulated or real multi-omics count data.

name: scaled-variance-batch-mixing-assessment
description: Use when you need to score or compare batch integration of multiple embedding methods (e.g., corralm vs. PCA+Harmony) on multi-batch scRNA-seq data, such as the SCMixology 10X/Celseq2/Dropseq CellBench dataset.

name: scaling-analysis-cell-count-vs-runtime
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of scRNA-seq methods: multiple tools must be run on size-graded subsamples of one dataset (e.g. the 68k PBMC set) and runtime/peak-memory curves plotted against cell number.

name: scaling-benchmark-measurement
description: Use when reproducing an integration pipeline at atlas scale and you must verify the reported computational efficiency (runtime and memory scaling) against baselines such as scJoint and Seurat.

name: scanorama-batch-correction
description: Use when training and test scRNA-seq datasets come from different studies, platforms, or gene panels (e.g., Lemur 4 vs. Lemur 1, Muris FACS vs. Lemur 2) and batch effects may obscure cross-dataset cell type annotation with OnClass.

name: scanorama-expression-integration
description: Use when a multi-dataset scRNA-seq collection must be integrated purely from expression profiles as a batch-correction/integration baseline — e.g., to test whether annotation-score embeddings cluster cells by cell type better than expression-level integration.

name: scanpy-covariate-regression
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has continuous nuisance covariate scores (e.g., cell cycle or sex scores) that must be regressed out as a pre-processing baseline before clustering or trajectory analysis.

name: scanpy-expression-normalization
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be preprocessed for Cancer-Finder inference — e.g. applying the model at scale to external scRNA-seq datasets such as the 152 CancerSCEM databases.

name: scanpy-gene-scoring-equivalence
description: Use when re-implementing or auditing SenePy's score_hub on an AnnData object and you need a scanpy.score_genes-equivalent configuration (binarize=False, importance=False) as a ground-truth comparison for per-cell signature scores.

name: scanpy-hvg-marker-selection
description: Use when benchmarking unsupervised marker selection for single-cell RNA-seq data — e.g., reconstructing the full transcriptome from k=50 markers on CITE-seq, Mouse Brain, Paul, or Zeisel datasets — and a Scanpy HVG baseline is needed to compare against MarkerMap, RandomBaseline, or PERSIST.

name: scanpy-lognormalization-preprocessing
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices (AnnData) from scRNA-seq datasets need normalization to comparable expression scales prior to cell-type scoring, marker identification, or label transfer.

name: scanpy-normalization-qc-preprocessing
description: Use when raw count matrices (e.g., CSV count tables for SC or ST data) must be normalized, log-transformed, and QC-metric'd before feeding a mapping/integration model, or when a median-genes dropout rate is needed.

name: scanpy-pbmc3k-dataset-loading
description: Use when a workflow needs the canonical PBMC 3K raw count matrix as a starting object — e.g. to estimate Splatter generative parameters, run the scanpy standard preprocessing pipeline, or benchmark cluster-significance methods like Cytocipher.

name: scanpy-preprocessing-highly-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (imported as a Scanpy AnnData object) must be reduced to a compact, informative feature set before batch-integration methods such as scDREAMER, scVI, or INSCT are trained on multi-batch datasets.

name: scanpy-preprocessing-pipeline
description: Use when raw count matrices from one or more scRNA-seq batches must be converted into a normalized, log-transformed AnnData object with top-2000 HVGs before training an integration model such as scDREAMER, scVI, or INSCT.

name: scanpy-scrna-seq-data-handling
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g. 10X matrix.mtx with barcodes.tsv/genes.tsv) must be loaded into an AnnData object and pre-processed (normalize_per_cell, log1p, HVG selection) before dimensionality reduction or imputation.

name: scanpy-single-cell-data-loading
description: Use when a scRNA-seq analysis pipeline starts from raw count/expression data that must be read into an AnnData object (e.g. an h5ad file via scanpy.read_*) before scoring, smoothing, or visualization can proceed.

name: scanpy-single-cell-data-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (AnnData/h5ad, e.g. the NEURIPS bone marrow dataset) must be filtered, normalized to 10,000 counts, log-transformed, and reduced to ~3500 highly variable genes before integration or benchmarking.

name: scanpy-single-cell-embedding-analysis
description: Use when you have precomputed single-cell embeddings (e.g. mvTCR, RNA-only, TCR-only, Harmony-corrected) and need to quantify how well Leiden clusters align with antigen-specificity annotations on the 10x Genomics >60k-cell dataset.

name: scanpy-single-cell-preprocessing-pipeline
description: Use when raw single-cell gene expression count matrices (e.g., MCA or PBMC h5ad/count matrices) must be normalized, reduced to highly variable genes, and converted into affinity matrices or low-dimensional embeddings before clustering.

name: scanpy-workflow-scripting
description: Use when scoring gene sets on single-cell RNA-seq data stored as Scanpy AnnData (h5ad), when per-cell or per-group scores are needed in adata.obsm, or when smoothing sparse scRNA-seq counts via a nearest-neighbor graph before scoring.

name: scanvi-semisupervised-cross-dataset-integration
description: Use when several independently annotated single-cell datasets (e.g. per-study JOINTLY labels from Tabula Sapiens, Jaitin GSE128518, Vijay GSE129363, Hildreth GSE155960, Emont SCP1376, Barboza) must be harmonised into a consensus atlas of cell types and subtypes.

name: scatac-accessibility-matrix-loading
description: Use when an analysis needs to run VIA or other TI methods on Buenrostro scATAC-seq hematopoiesis data preprocessed with TF-motif or k-mer Z Scores protocols and must first load these matrices into a VIA-compatible AnnData container.

name: scatac-scrna-adt-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw count matrices of scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, and/or CITE-seq ADT data must be normalized and preprocessed before training or applying scButterfly cross-modality translators.

name: scatac-seq-accessible-peak-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data must be paired with scATAC-seq peaks and TF motif scans to filter out non-relevant TFs and construct a base GRN parquet (e.g. Cusanovich2018_Spleen_peak_base_GRN_dataframe.parquet) for downstream scGATE logic-gate inference.

name: scatac-seq-activity-matrix-preparation
description: Use when raw scATAC-seq peak data has already been converted to a gene activity matrix (e.g. via Signac) and must be TF-IDF transformed onto scRNA-seq common genes before scBridge label transfer.

name: scatac-seq-base-grn-parsing-and-summarization
description: Use when a base GRN built from scATAC-seq data and TF binding motif analysis (a .parquet file of candidate TF–target links, e.g. Cusanovich2018_Spleen or Buenrostro2018) must be loaded and summarized before running scGATE on scRNA-seq counts.

name: scatac-seq-chromvar-tf-activity-scoring
description: Use when validating DICE-predicted primed cell states and their candidate regulatory factors (e.g. Runx2, Zfhx3, Foxo3, Lmo7) in matched scATAC-Seq profiles, by testing whether motif-derived TF activity is higher in primed versus unprimed cells.

name: scatac-seq-fragment-quality-control
description: Use when starting an scATAC-seq analysis from a fragments file (e.g. BMMC dataset) and low-quality cells, doublets, and high-dimensional tile/peak matrices must be filtered and reduced before clustering.

name: scatac-seq-gene-accessibility-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-Seq-derived cell assignments or marker gene lists must be validated against matched scATAC-Seq data by testing whether target genes of lineage regulators (e.g. GATA1, KLF1, IRF8) show higher chromatin accessibility in the predicted cells.

name: scatac-seq-gene-activity-inference
description: Use when the input is scATAC-seq data and pseudo-space reconstruction is needed but no spatial ATAC-seq reference is available, requiring conversion to a gene activity matrix (via Signac) so ST data can serve as the spatial reference in scSpace.

name: scatac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-analysis
description: Use when input is a scATAC-seq dataset converted to a cell-by-gene activity score matrix and the goal is cell clustering and marker-gene identification via differential expression of the resulting clusters.

name: scatac-seq-gene-activity-matrix-conversion
description: Use when integrating paired or unpaired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq data (e.g. the 10X Genomics PBMC multi-omic dataset) with tools that operate on gene-by-cell matrices rather than peak matrices.

name: scatac-seq-peak-accessibility-processing
description: Use when a scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix must be reduced to an informative peak subset before clustering or trajectory inference, and standard HVF selection is suspected to obscure cell type structure.

name: scatac-seq-peak-calling-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking scATAC-seq peak callers against a known set of ground-truth peaks (e.g. scReadSim synthetic BAM from the sci-ATAC-seq dataset), or when choosing a peak caller for single-cell ATAC data.

name: scatac-seq-peak-plus-te-feature-construction
description: Use when analyzing 10x scATAC-seq (or multi-omics) data and you want clustering/benchmarking feature matrices that combine accessible-chromatin peaks with locus-specific TE counts from MATES, alongside TE-only and multi-mapping-TE-only perspectives.

name: scatac-seq-te-accessibility-quantification
description: Use when scATAC-seq BAM files (e.g. FACS-purified mouse cell samples) should be characterized by TE open-chromatin content alone, to test whether TE accessibility recovers known cell identities or reveals TE-specific openness.

name: scatac-tfidf-lsi-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing scATAC-seq data (binary cell-by-bin accessibility matrix) to feed into cross-modality integration (e.g., with scRNA-seq via uniPort's coupled-VAE) alongside log-normalized gene expression.

name: scatc-topic-modeling-on-scatc-seq-chromatin-accessibility
description: Use when analyzing scATAC/SNARE-seq chromatin accessibility as a cell-by-peak matrix (e.g. ~31,758 cells x 575,265 peaks) and you need unsupervised topics and clusters in the chromatin modality before assigning cell types.

name: scatter-plot-figure-generation
description: Use when comparing a per-cell quality metric (e.g. silhouette coefficient against true cluster labels) between an original data representation and alternative feature constructions, and a scatter/diagonal visualization with a fraction-above-diagonal summary is needed.

name: scatter-quadrant-threshold-visualization
description: Use when two independent feature-ranking metrics (e.g., expression magnitude vs. variance-based loadings) must be compared to decide whether they identify the same significant features, and you need quadrant counts plus a correlation statistic as evidence.

name: sccaf-self-projection-accuracy-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking cross-species single-cell RNA-seq integration strategies (e.g. LIGER, LIGER UINMF, fastMNN, SeuratV4, scANVI, scVI) and you need to measure whether integration overcorrects and blends distinct cell types, reducing cell type distinguishability.

name: sccatch-object-construction
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix plus cluster assignments and need to wrap them into a scCATCH object (or convert a Seurat object) to run findmarkergene/findcelltype annotation.

name: sccrispr-synthetic-data-simulation
description: Use when validating a perturbation-effect estimator on scCRISPR-seq data where true cellular response and cluster proportions are known by construction, i.e. simulation benchmarks sweeping bias parameters such as cluster distance d and ratio change r.

name: scdbm-training-schedule-implementation
description: Use when fitting scDBM/BoltzmannMachines models to scRNA-seq count matrices and you need per-gene negative-binomial inverse dispersion (θ) estimates refreshed periodically during deep-Boltzmann-machine training.

name: scdesign2-count-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction or clustering methods requires simulated count matrices with reliable ground-truth cluster labels, e.g. building an extended evaluation collection alongside real datasets like Zheng, Koh, Kumar, or Trapnell.

name: scdesign2-count-model-fitting
description: Use when a synthetic scRNA-seq benchmark needs realistic UMI count matrices as ground truth and cells belong to distinct clusters, so a cluster-aware count simulator can be trained on real UMI count data.

name: scdesign2-synthetic-count-scaling
description: Use when you need synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data whose throughput (cell number) or library size (sequencing depth) is systematically scaled around a real reference dataset to study pseudo-bulk coverage or guide experimental design.

name: scdha-vae-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when benchmarking a single-cell clustering or dimensionality reduction method on synthetic scRNA-seq count data for which simulated ground-truth cell-type labels exist (e.g. scMOSim output), so clustering accuracy can be scored by ARI.

name: scdisinfact-dataset-construction
description: Use when you have a raw gene-expression count matrix (numpy array, ncells x ngenes) plus a meta_cells dataframe containing batch IDs and one or more condition-type columns, and need to feed them into scDisInFact training.

name: scdna-scrna-cell-association-mapping
description: Use when you have paired scDNA-seq copy-number and scRNA-seq gene-expression matrices (genes as rows, cells as columns, optionally clone labels per DNA cell) and need to assign RNA cells to DNA cells or clones, e.g. for intratumor heterogeneity analysis on scTrio-seq data.

name: scdrs-gene-set-based-cell-scoring
description: Use when you need to score individual cells for association with a GWAS trait using a fixed disease/gene set, or to test whether alternative gene-prioritization methods improve scDRS cell identification.

name: scds-cxds-bcds-doublet-scoring
description: Use when a Seurat/SingleCellExperiment droplet dataset needs per-cell doublet scores from cxds and bcds, either for overkill pre-filtering or as GBM predictors in Chord.

name: scenic-coexpression-module-detection
description: Use when you have a normalized, clustered scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. Louvain clusters in Seurat) and need to identify cluster-specific regulons and transcription factor activation patterns via GRN reconstruction.

name: scgan-generative-model-training
description: Use when you need to train a non-conditional GAN (scGAN) on single-cell RNA-seq count data to generate realistic synthetic cells for augmentation or fidelity studies, and the data is available in .h5/.h5ad format.

name: schema-joint-cell-embedding-integration
description: Use when you have paired single-cell multimodal data (same cells assayed by scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq) and need unified per-cell embeddings to construct a pseudotime-directed cell-state DAG for downstream causal analysis.

name: scib-metric-computation
description: Use when multiple data-integration or label-transfer methods have been run on the same reference-query split and you need a ranked, metric-based comparison of their embeddings (e.g., on a pan-cancer tumor-infiltrating myeloid AnnData).

name: scibet-multinomial-classification
description: Use when a labeled scRNA-seq reference exists and cell types must be predicted for newly sequenced cells or clusters, including cross-platform transfer (full-length vs UMI, e.g., 6 ordered human pancreas training-test pairs), with benchmarking against Seurat v3 and scmapCluster.

name: scientific-task-formulation
description: Use when a candidate sub-task must be scoped to verifiable evidence — e.g. formulating the question of whether HEDGES-MSA overtakes HEDGES only above a specific i.i.d. error rate in the read/write Pareto frontiers.

name: scientific-task-formulation
description: Use when a source article describes a newly released analysis tool or software package (e.g. RCAT for circadian clock genes) and the agent must decompose the article's claims, delivery artifacts, and workflow into a reusable, executable skill definition.

name: scimpute-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix contains dropout zeros that must be imputed before dimension reduction, normalization, clustering, differential expression, or time-series analysis.

name: scinsight-cartesian-combined-condition-baseline
description: Use when benchmarking multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq disentanglement against scINSIGHT, i.e. when a common/condition-specific NMF decomposition must be trained on the same held-out simulated configuration as scDisInFact and scored with ARI and ASW-batch.

name: scissors-derived-marker-gene-selection
description: Use when a heterogeneous Seurat cluster needs rare subclusters resolved and a specific marker-gene signature, or when such a signature must be applied de novo to score bulk RNA-seq samples into subtypes.

name: sclane-trajectory-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when a fitted single-cell trajectory (Slingshot lineages or Monocle3 pseudotime on an Escort-recommended embedding) needs gene-level trajectory differential expression testing to identify dynamically expressed genes along lineages.

name: sclc-neurod1-expression-subtyping
description: Use when SCLC ATAC-Seq/RNA data are available and you need to confirm ecMYC-driven MYC amplification and check whether expression patterns match the NEUROD1-high (SCLC-N) subtype.

name: scmap-cluster-cell-type-classification
description: Use when you need to classify annotated scRNA-seq cells against a labeled reference with scmapCluster and compare classifiers or feature-selection methods by repeated hold-out accuracy.

name: scmap-label-transfer-annotation
description: Use when annotating cells in a target scRNA-seq dataset by transferring labels from an independently collected, labeled reference dataset (e.g., inter-study PBMC annotation) and benchmarking against supervised methods.

name: scmm-latent-space-umap-visualization
description: Use when you have a trained scMM latent representation from paired transcriptome & surface protein (CITE-seq) counts and need to visualize the joint space and its high-resolution cluster partition in 2D.

name: scmmgan-generated-data-evaluation
description: Use when scMMGAN-generated data (e.g. `output_fake2` mapping scRNA-seq into the spatial domain) must be biologically validated by comparing gene-gene correlation rankings against the original modality to separate spurious artifacts from novel associations.

name: scna-seq-null-model-generation
description: Use when you must demonstrate that signalling entropy (SR) depends on network-constrained expression: i.

name: score-based-gene-expression-decomposition-via-langevin-sampling
description: Use when spot-level ST data (e.g., Visium, ~55 µm spots with multiple cells) must be decomposed into per-cell whole-transcriptome expression using an unpaired or paired scRNA-seq reference.

name: score-based-generative-decomposition-pipeline
description: Use when seq-based ST data (e.g. 10x Visium, Slide-seq V2) must be decomposed to single-cell resolution using a paired scRNA-seq reference, or when image-based ST data need transcriptome-wide expression inference.

name: score-based-generative-decomposition-spatial-transcriptomics
description: Use when you have nucleus-segmented or singlet/doublet-classified spatial transcriptomics spots plus a labeled scRNA-seq reference and need transcriptome-wide per-cell expression beyond spot-level resolution.

name: score-based-generative-dropout-correction
description: Use when seq-based ST data (Slide-seq V2, Visium) has dropout or sparse gene expression and a paired scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference is available, and you need to recover/impute whole-transcriptome expression and benchmark the correction.

name: score-based-generative-model-training
description: Use when you need a trained conditional score network from a single-cell RNA-seq reference before running SpatialScope's Langevin-dynamics posterior sampling for gene expression decomposition or imputation.

name: score-curve-aggregation-across-clusterings
description: Use when many candidate clusterings exist for a trajectory-inference benchmark and you must compare selection criteria (e.g. connectivity+VRC vs ASW vs VRC vs random) by how trajectory quality degrades over the top-n ranked candidates.

name: score-matrix-integer-rounding
description: Use when you have a phenotype x feature score matrix M (e.g., from a scRNA-seq dataset like Tabula Muris, mouse cortex, or HCA) and need every phenotype pair (i,j) distinguished at least K times by selected markers.

name: scorecard-plot-reconstruction
description: Use when scorecard_functions.scorecard(df,param_dict) has already generated the four single-quadrant assignments and plots and you need the assembled full scorecard image per pairwise comparison, e.g. VAN/CPT/DEL/LZD vs control.

name: scorecard-quadrant-classification
description: Use when a CSV contains per-gene log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns for pairwise treatment-vs-control comparisons (e.g. VAN/LZD/CPT antibiotics, AGXX vs silver coatings) and you need data-driven identification of extreme or moderately changing genes without preselecting them.

name: scorecard-region-of-interest-gene-assignment
description: Use when a CSV holds pre-computed log2 fold-change and padj columns for pairwise condition comparisons and you need to identify statistically significant extreme gene regulation (down- or up-regulated) per quadrant across multiple antibiotic or treatment contrasts.

name: scpathoquant-cli-parameterization
description: Use when a user has a completed cellranger count output for 10x scRNAseq data and wants pathogen (viral or bacterial) reads aligned, quantified per cell, and appended to the filtered/raw feature-barcode matrices without leaving the host pipeline.

name: scphere-model-training-and-inference
description: Use when very large scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., 35,699-cell RGC or 599,926-cell HCL droplet data) need low-dimensional embeddings that preserve global hierarchical structure, or when mapping new batches/patients batch-invariantly.

name: scpred-eigengene-classifier-training
description: Use when a benchmark dataset has known ground-truth cell-type labels and per-cell supervised annotation accuracy must be quantified against other tools (e.g., EasyCellType, Garnett, SingleR).

name: scqa-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., SMARTer, Smart-Seq2, CEL-Seq2, inDrop data from GEO/ArrayExpress accessions like GSE81608 or E-MTAB-5061) need cell type clustering and cluster-specific key gene identification without knowing the number of cell types in advance.

name: scran-count-normalization-and-cell-filtering
description: Use when a raw UMI count matrix (e.g., from Cell Ranger or Fluidigm C1 scRNA-seq) must be cleaned and normalized before trajectory inference, time-series differential expression, or cell-subcluster identification.

name: scran-pool-deconvolute-normalization
description: Use when a raw digital gene expression matrix (UMI counts, genes x cells, e.g. from Cell Ranger) has been gene/cell filtered but not normalized, signaled by 'indication' = 'none' or 'filtered' in scTITANS.

name: scrb-seq-query-data-loading
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix (query dataset) must be ingested and formatted as a Seurat object prior to Run.ProjecTILs reference-map projection.

name: scree-plot-elbow-artifact-identification
description: Use when a scree plot of a highly sparse cell-gene matrix (e.g. ~95% zeros) shows an elbow or upper-edge eigenvalue deviations, and you must determine whether these are real signal or sparsity artifacts before interpreting PCs.

name: scribble-annotation-semi-supervised-learning
description: Use when you have Visium or ST spatial transcriptomics data with a Space Ranger output (filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 + spatial/ files) and either expert scribbles on histology images or a non-spatial clustering backbone (e.

name: scrispr-seq-infected-proportion-bias-correction
description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data (e.g. CROP-seq with perturbation matrix Y and control matrix Z) where cluster proportions differ between gRNA-perturbed and control groups, distorting fold-change estimates of perturbation response.

name: scrna-ann-data-expression-aggregation
description: Use when a Scanpy/AnnData scRNA-seq object already carries gene age class annotations (an orthomap matched via oggmap) and the goal is relative expression per age class aggregated by cell type or sampling timepoint.

name: scrna-anndata-processing
description: Use when a pre-existing orthomap (gene age class per gene) must be joined with single-cell expression data in a Scanpy AnnData object to compute per-cell TEI or partial TEI profiles across stages or cell types.

name: scrna-batch-mixing-ilisi-quantification
description: Use when comparing batch mixing of two embedding spaces (e.g., BEENE vs PCA) on scRNA-seq data with batch labels and optionally biological labels, to test which space more sensitively detects batch effects via iLISI/kBET.

name: scrna-cluster-confidence-separation-tuning
description: Use when producing a 2D graph embedding of scRNA-seq cells with known cluster labels and the layout is either too diffuse for same-class cells or overly collapsed, requiring adjustment of -c, -k, -d, -z, -l.

name: scrna-count-matrix-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking dimensionality reduction or PC-selection methods on scRNA-seq data by simulating lower sequencing depth (e.g., downsampling deeply sequenced datasets, TGC > 25,000 per cell, to ~5,000 TGC/cell) and comparing reduced embeddings of original vs. downsampled data.

name: scrna-count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq/CITE-seq counts (e.g., a sparse adata.X from a .h5ad file) must be converted into a dense, normalized, scaled matrix before training a marker-selection or generative model.

name: scrna-count-matrix-quality-control
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (CSV or JLD2) must be cleaned before embedding: sparse genes, low-content cells, or high mitochondrial-read cells would otherwise distort downstream PCA/UMAP signal detection.

name: scrna-count-normalization-log1p-transform
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices must be converted to the sf-log1p representation expected by scTab/TabNet-style cell type classifiers trained on CELLxGENE census data.

name: scrna-cpm-normalization-log1p-scaling
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., an AnnData .h5ad such as the 5273-cell HBMP3-spleen-CC2 HuBMAP dataset) must be transformed to a scaled log-CPM representation before PCA, UMAP, or Leiden clustering.

name: scrna-data-loading-and-preprocessing
description: Use when scRNA-seq training/test data must be loaded from h5ad files and preprocessed for ontology-based cell type annotation, especially when cell type labels are free text and need mapping to Cell Ontology IDs.

name: scrna-dataset-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type identification methods on scRNA-seq count matrices and you need training sets of 500–10,000 cells and testing sets of 1,000–50,000 cells, or ~10,000-cell stratified subsets.
