name: scrna-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking dimensionality-reduction embeddings of small UMI count matrices to test whether a vMF/hyperspherical latent space avoids the origin-crowding seen with normal-prior VAEs and t-SNE/UMAP/PHATE.

name: scrna-dropout-imputation
description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq count matrix contains excessive zero dropouts and the goal is expression-matrix completion that retains true (biologically silent) zeros rather than overwriting them.

name: scrna-gene-filtering-thresholding
description: Use when a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (.csv, cells as rows, genes as columns) must be converted into the pre-processed 1000-gene matrix format consumed by AutoImpute.py before imputation.

name: scrna-mapping-quality-assessment
description: Use when query cells have been projected onto a ProjectSVR reference (ref.umap attached) and you must decide which cells to retain for label transfer or downstream tests, e.g. via mean.knn.dist < 1.6 or mapQ.p.adj < 0.1.

name: scrna-pseudobulk-cluster-aggregation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data stored as a Seurat object must be collapsed into pooled, non-sparse per-cluster transcriptomic profiles before applying a predictor (e.g., miRNA inference) to each cell type.

name: scrna-reference-distribution-learning
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics dataset (Visium, Slide-seq V2, MERFISH) must be integrated with a cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq reference and a generative model of single-cell expression distributions is needed for cell type identification or gene expression imputation/decomposition.

name: scrna-scatac-joint-clustering-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression matrix (E) and scATAC-seq openness matrix (O) come from separate samples of the same mixed cell population, and clustering should be informed across datatypes — optionally with bulk H3K27ac HiChIP loops.

name: scrna-scatac-multimodal-integration
description: Use when paired or separate scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrices with time-stage/fate annotations must be integrated and used to reconstruct a bifurcating trajectory and detect terminal cell fates.

name: scrna-scatac-preprocessing-and-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq count matrices must be QC-filtered and normalized with modality-specific recipes (log1p/PCA for RNA, TF-IDF for ATAC) before cross-modality integration.

name: scrna-seq-3utr-isoform-quantification
description: Use when raw 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (FASTQ/BAM from 10x Genomics or Microwell-seq chemistry) must be converted into sparse gene-level and 3'UTR isoform count matrices for APA/UTR-length analysis.

name: scrna-seq-and-proteomics-matrix-loading
description: Use when the task requires ingesting a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq matrix or an experiment-by-protein proteomics matrix (tsv/csv, hundreds of thousands of rows) as input for FAVA network inference or a PCC baseline on the same data.

name: scrna-seq-anndata-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq matrices or downloaded dataset files (e.g. the 5800-cell Setty CD34+ bone-marrow data from the VIA Datasets repo) must be loaded as AnnData with PCA precomputed before running VIA.

name: scrna-seq-annotation-confidence-thresholding
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq cells with a hierarchical classifier (e.g. scATOMIC run_scATOMIC() output) and you need per-class confidence cut-offs derived automatically from each class's score distribution rather than fixed thresholds.

name: scrna-seq-annotation-integration
description: Use when a cancer scRNA-seq dataset (counts matrix, Seurat object, csv/rds/h5, or 10X folder) needs automated cell-type annotation within the tumor microenvironment and batch-effect-corrected integration before downstream analyses like inferCNV.

name: scrna-seq-bam-barcode-splitting
description: Use when input is one 10x Genomics barcoded BAM file (e.g., pbmc_8k) plus barcodes.tsv.gz and per-cell BAM files are required for downstream per-cell analyses such as geneBodyCoverage.pl.

name: scrna-seq-batch-correction-embedding-inference
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq batches or studies (e.g., 9-batch pancreas atlas, immune or lung atlas datasets) need batch-corrected embeddings, or when new query datasets must be annotated against a pre-trained reference atlas without retraining.

name: scrna-seq-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when a Scanpy AnnData object with raw scRNA-seq counts plus per-cell batch labels shows cells separating by batch rather than by cell type (e.g. skewed cell types across batches, nested batch effects, or >10 batches), and an unsupervised integrated embedding is needed.

name: scrna-seq-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., three cell lines across CEL-seq2, 10x Chromium, Drop-seq) has unknown cell types and batch effects must be corrected while clustering cells and benchmarking ARI against alternative integration methods.

name: scrna-seq-batch-effect-simulation
description: Use when you need a controlled scRNA-seq integration benchmark with simulated large batch effects, or to verify reported LB-scenario iLISI/50-RNN values for BATMAN, Seurat V3.0, MNNcorrect, and Scanorama.

name: scrna-seq-batch-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq batches or species (e.g., human–mouse atlas data up to ~1M cells) and you need to compare integration methods' batch mixing, cell-type conservation, and runtime.

name: scrna-seq-benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Use when you have a ranked DEG list from singleCellHaystack's `haystack` function (sorted by log.p.vals via show_result_haystack) and want to validate that top-ranked genes are enriched for known, high-confidence cell-type marker genes.

name: scrna-seq-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when testing whether engineered clustering features (e.g., Spearman-correlation features from SSCC) stay consistent with true cell-type labels across fluctuating subsampling rates of a benchmark scRNA-seq dataset.

name: scrna-seq-cell-annotation
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (rows = genes, columns = cells) and need per-cell activity scores of biological-process PPINs for cell annotation, UMAP embedding, or pseudotime inference.

name: scrna-seq-cell-cycle-effect-removal
description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression data shows within-cell-type heterogeneity from the cell cycle that obscures cell-type differences, and a known set of cell-cycle genes (mouse or human) is available for control-gene annotation.

name: scrna-seq-cell-embedding-extraction
description: Use when trained cross-species cell-type classification models are available (e.g. TACTiCS from Zenodo) and you need per-cell embeddings from scRNA-seq data to assess cell-type alignment across species.

name: scrna-seq-cell-label-annotation
description: Use when you have a small selected marker-gene panel (e.g., a 15-marker panel) plus per-cell expression data and cell type labels, and you need to verify the panel preserves 13-way (or similar) cell type separation in a 2-D t-SNE embedding.

name: scrna-seq-cell-type-aggregation
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression with cell-type labels must be collapsed to per-cell-type profiles to score ligand-receptor interactions between sender and receiver cell types at a single time point.

name: scrna-seq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when training scRNA-seq data with known cell labels exist and every test cell must receive exactly one of the K reference labels, especially with closely correlated cell types.

name: scrna-seq-cell-type-classification-benchmarking

name: scrna-seq-clustering-based-deg-prediction

name: scrna-seq-clustering-evaluation

name: scrna-seq-cna-simulation

name: scrna-seq-count-data-simulation-with-batch-effects-and-dropout

name: scrna-seq-count-matrix-preprocessing

description: Use when a raw or minimally processed scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Veres et al. stage-5 beta-like differentiation, 25,299 cells) must be turned into a cell-type-annotated adata object before running FateCompass.

name: scrna-seq-preprocessing-sctransform
description: Use when the input is a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. from NGDC HRA000084 or GEO GSE84133) that must be preprocessed before building a cell-to-cell KNN graph and training a graph autoencoder.

name: scrna-seq-preprocessing-workflow
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (10X-style droplet data) must be aligned and converted to gene-by-cell UMI count matrices and then quality filtered non-arbitrarily, especially when spliced/unspliced matrices are needed for RNA velocity or trajectory inference.

name: scrna-seq-pseudoalignment-quantification
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq FASTQ files from a 3'-end tag chemistry (e.g. 10xv2/10xv3) must be converted to gene- and UTR isoform-level count matrices without whole-transcript alignment.

name: scrna-seq-qc-filtering-and-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq count matrices (e.g. filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 plus ATAC fragments .tsv.gz) must be QC-filtered and normalized in R/Seurat/Signac before multimodal integration or pairing.

name: scrna-seq-quality-control
description: Use when reprocessing 10x Genomics 3'-end scRNA-seq FASTQs with scUTRquant and you must verify that gene counts from a truncated UTRome reference remain concordant with Cell Ranger before trusting downstream UTR-isoform quantification.

name: scrna-seq-quality-control-and-imputation
description: Use when input is a raw gene-by-cell expression profile plus per-cell perturbation annotations (e.g. crop_stimulated or 10X perturb_GSM2396857 format) that must be QC'd and imputed before MUSIC topic modeling.

name: scrna-seq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when starting from raw single-cell count matrices (e.g. .h5ad from GEO deposits like GSE149614 or Figshare-hosted atlas datasets) that need cleaning before batch correction, clustering, or differential expression.

name: scrna-seq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (10x-formatted mtx directory or CSV) must be filtered for cells with <200 expressed genes, genes in <3 cells, and high mitochondrial fractions before normalization and clustering.

name: scrna-seq-quality-matrix-construction
description: Use when building the compact percentile-coverage matrix from SkewC gene body coverage output (coverage.r) as input for SkewC plotting, trim clustering, and typical-vs-skewed cell classification.

name: scrna-seq-rare-cell-scoring
description: Use when the goal is to detect rare cell populations in a scRNA-seq count matrix (thousands to ~68k+ profiles) and no annotated clusters exist yet; FiRE gives a per-cell continuous rareness score in seconds where RaceID/GiniClust scale poorly.

name: scrna-seq-read-pseudoalignment
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (e.g., 10x Genomics v3 FASTQ, such as sample GSM4626009 from GSE152766) need fast alignment and quantification into spliced and unspliced count matrices for downstream quality filtering with COPILOT.

name: scrna-seq-run-statistics-collection
description: Use when a scKB pseudoalignment run on 10xv3 FASTQ data (e.g. the 80 MB toy_data from GSM4626009, GSE152766) has finished and you must verify and gather its 8 output files for downstream COPILOT input.

name: scrna-seq-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the runtime and memory footprint of pluripotency/scRNA-seq scoring tools (ORIGINS, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) on GEO count matrices (breast GSE113197, colon GSE125970, hematopoietic GSE117498, lung GSE161383).

name: scrna-seq-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing scalability of clustering or cluster-merging methods on scRNA-seq data: you need wall-clock runtime on a fixed, small, cell-type-labelled subset to contrast with AUROC performance on the full dataset.

name: scrna-seq-self-supervised-representation-learning
description: Use when you need to cluster or embed a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. tens of thousands of cells, like the 43,095-cell 10x PBMC dataset) and standard pipelines underperform, or to benchmark deep-learning representation learning against Scanpy/Seurat/scVI.

name: scrna-seq-similarity-learning
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (cells x genes matrix with ground-truth labels available for evaluation) and noisy/high-dropout expression makes naive cell-to-cell similarity unreliable; need NMI/ARI gains from similarity learning.

name: scrna-seq-sparsity-comparison-across-technologies
description: Use when comparing synthetic-data quality from small pilot sub-samples between scRNA-seq technologies (10x Genomics vs Smart-seq2), specifically to quantify whether sparsity degrades small-to-large inference via DBI, ARI, and cluster-proportion metrics.

name: scrna-seq-spatial-mapping
description: Use when you need to link scRNA-seq cells to spatial coordinates/positions via optimal transport — e.g., mapping 1297 Drosophila embryo cells onto 3039 seqFISH/in situ spatial positions from geometry.txt and dge_normalized.txt/bdtnp.txt inputs.

name: scrna-seq-spectral-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix with known cell-subpopulation labels (e.g., embryonic stages) is available and you must quantify whether imputation improves cell-population clustering accuracy against no-imputation and competitor imputers.

name: scrna-seq-splicing-status-prediction
description: Use when scRNA-seq reads labeled 'ambiguous' (compatible with both spliced and unspliced transcripts) need a probabilistic spliced/unspliced resolution, e.g. PBMC1k-style reads aligned to a spliceu augmented reference.

name: scrna-seq-stage-wise-dice-dynamics
description: Use when a time-course or staged single-cell RNA-Seq dataset spans a known or suspected lineage bifurcation (e.g., retinal progenitors splitting into neuronal vs epithelial fates) and the exact transition/tipping stage must be resolved.

name: scrna-seq-stemness-scoring
description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix must be ranked by pluripotency/stemness to identify stem or progenitor cells, e.g. to pick trajectory-inference origins or to check whether a potency method recovers a known cellular hierarchy (HSC > MPP > GMP, stem vs TA).

name: scrna-seq-stratified-cross-validation
description: Use when benchmarking supervised cell-type identification methods on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and a fair, repeated train/test comparison of accuracy across datasets is needed.

name: scrna-seq-study-data-preparation
description: Use when importing new scRNA-seq (RNA-, ATAC-, or CITE-seq) studies into Cellenium, i.e. when raw/normalized single-cell data must be converted to annotated H5AD files with semantically organized study metadata.

name: scrna-seq-subclone-clustering-tsne-visualization
description: Use when deposited scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., drug-sensitive vs. resistant HMCL pairs like U266P vs U266VR) must be clustered into subclones and screened for drug-target gene enrichment to prioritize combination therapies.

name: scrna-seq-subset-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking the wall-clock runtime of scRNA-seq imputation methods (ALRA, MAGIC, DCA, scImpute, SAVER) as a function of cell count, requiring random subsets of a large filtered expression matrix.

name: scrna-seq-technology-parameter-extraction
description: Use when building a reference table of supported single-cell RNA-seq chemistries and their barcode/UMI read-layout settings, or when verifying which technology a FASTQ input corresponds to.

name: scrna-seq-temporal-data-handling
description: Use when you have metabolic labeling scRNA-seq data (e.g., scEU-seq rpeLabeling.h5ad with separate labeled, unlabeled, and total count matrices plus a labeling-time vector) and need paired time-point inputs for RNAForecaster.

name: scrna-seq-to-bulk-3prime-seq-concordance
description: Use when scUTRquant 3'UTR isoform quantification from scRNA-seq must be validated against bulk 3'-seq reference TPMs (e.g., ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7391 HSC or PolyASite-annotated ESC bulk data) to establish concordance.

name: scrna-seq-to-scatac-seq-label-transfer
description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq (annotated source, h5ad with obs['CellType']) and scATAC-seq (unlabeled target) data to transfer cell-type labels, e.g. SNARE-seq or mouse-atlas benchmarks.

name: scrna-seq-train-test-split-preparation
description: Use when a labeled cancer scRNA-seq dataset must be partitioned into training and testing sets to benchmark cell-type or cell-subtype annotation tools on the same cells, e.g., before computing per-cluster accuracy/F1 against original study annotations.

name: scrna-seq-training-dataset-construction
description: Use when building a supervised malignant-vs-normal epithelial training set from labeled scRNA-seq datasets where the raw 'Malignant'/'Tumor' annotations may be noisy and need refinement via cancer signature activity.

name: scrna-seq-uncertainty-measurement
description: Use when a pre-trained source classifier's soft probability outputs exist for scRNA-seq target cells and you need a per-cell uncertainty score to detect which cells belong to known cell types versus novel types.

name: scrna-seq-variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when a UMI count matrix (cells x genes) needs low-dimensional embedding for visualization, batch correction across multiple batch factors (e.g., 30 patients x 3 health statuses x 2 locations), or mapping of held-out individuals.

name: scrna-seq-yan-dataset-processing
description: Use when a Yan (or similar scRNA-seq) expression matrix and SSRE-inferred cluster labels are available and the goal is validating that the clustering supports downstream DEG detection via Kruskal-Wallis testing.

name: scrna-seq-zero-entry-partitioning
description: Use when preprocessing a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix before imputation and you need to decide, per zero entry, whether it is a dropout event or a true zero rather than imputing all zeros indiscriminately.

name: scrna-stage-aggregation-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData object already contains per-cell TEI (or similar gene age-weighted index) in obs and the goal is to summarize and plot mean index per developmental stage to detect an hourglass pattern.

name: scrnaseq-accession-data-retrieval
description: Use when a benchmark requires the original Yan, Goolam, or Deng embryo scRNA-seq count matrices and only a GEO/ArrayExpress accession (e.g. GSE36552) is known.

name: scrnaseq-alignment-with-star
description: Use when input is paired Smart-Seq single-cell RNA-seq data named *_1.fastq/*_2.fastq and a genome reference (.fa) plus GTF are available, and per-cell alignments are needed for fusion or splice-aware analysis.

name: scrnaseq-annadata-construction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq studies must be combined into a single AnnData with explicit batch (source study) and cell-type annotation columns before training scETM or running batch-integration benchmarks.

name: scrnaseq-batch-effect-quantification
description: Use when comparing batch-integration/dimension-reduction methods (e.g., corralm, corralm+Harmony, corralm+MNN, multibatch PCA, Seurat) on multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices and you need paired metrics of cell-type separation (ASW_celltype) vs batch mixing (1-ASWbatch).

name: scrnaseq-batch-integration-mixing-evaluation
description: Use when two scRNA-seq datasets from different species (e.g., human and mouse primary motor cortex raw counts) must be integrated into one latent space and you need a mixing metric plus cross-species cell-type matching recall to judge embedding quality.

name: scrnaseq-batch-integration-model-training
description: Use when you have raw count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches (e.g. .h5ad AnnData, ≥2 batches, up to ~1M cells) and need an unsupervised integrated embedding plus an ablation-based attribution of which adversarial components drive batch correction vs bio-conservation.

name: scrnaseq-bifurcation-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing accuracy of pseudotime inferred by bifurcation-capable trajectory methods on a single-cell RNA-seq differentiation dataset, using marker genes as an external pseudotime reference (e.g. Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlation with ENO3, MEF2C, MYH2).

name: scrnaseq-cell-cycle-pseudo-time-recovery
description: Use when you have unsynchronized scRNA-seq expression data and need to order cells along the cell cycle (G1/S/G2-M) or associate another single-cell modality (e.g., bisulfite methylation) with a recovered cell cycle pseudo time-series.

name: scrnaseq-cell-group-label-permutation-simulation
description: Use when running NeuronChat (or its shared CellChat/CellPhoneDB workflow) on scRNA-seq or spatial transcriptomics and you must decide which inferred ligand-receptor communication links are statistically significant, or when testing p-value stability across permutation counts (M=100 vs M=1000).

name: scrnaseq-cell-subsampling-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when you must determine the minimum cell count needed for reliable logic-gate/GRN inference from scRNA-seq, or characterize how inference quality and runtime saturate with sample size and candidate TF-set size.

name: scrnaseq-cell-type-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq data across multiple samples/conditions and need to build a cell count matrix (e.g., via sccoda.util.cell_composition_data.from_pandas or from_scanpy) as input for compositional differential abundance analysis.

name: scrnaseq-cell-type-label-assessment
description: Use when you need to quantitatively judge how well a dimension-reduction/visualization method separates known cell-type labels in scRNA-seq data, e.g. benchmarking an embedding against PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, or SCANPY.

name: scrnaseq-cluster-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing automatic cell type annotation of scRNA-seq clusters (scCATCH vs Seurat-based one-against-all markers), especially to quantify pseudo marker gene effects on annotation consistency.

name: scrnaseq-cluster-stability-assessment
description: Use when scRNAseq clusters must be validated for reconstruction robustness — e.g. after clustering with an SCA-encoded space (TF/miRNA/kinase targets) on datasets like setA, or when comparing a variant latent space (e.g. vSCA) against a baseline SCA run via QCM/QCC trajectory superimposability.

name: scrnaseq-condition-wise-subsetting
description: Use when a pooled single-condition-agnostic scRNA-seq matrix with cell-type annotations and patient/condition labels must be divided into separate disease-state groups before per-group ligand-receptor inference (e.

name: scrnaseq-confounder-corrected-pca
description: Use when preprocessing 10X scRNA-seq matrices (matrix.mtx/gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) prior to clustering, to correct confounders like cell cycle or mitochondrial load and to choose the number of PCs via shuffled-data simulation.

name: scrnaseq-confounding-factor-correction
description: Use when a scRNAseq expression matrix shows unwanted variation (e.g. ERCC spike-in confounding or cell-cycle effects) and downstream clustering must recover known biological groupings from corrected data.

name: scrnaseq-count-aggregation-by-cell-type
description: Use when a scRNA-seq anndata (.h5ad) matrix with per-cell metadata (cell_type, donor_id, condition) must be reduced to pseudo-bulk counts per sample and cell type before calling DEGs between conditions.

name: scrnaseq-count-data-modeling
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices need a denoised, low-dimensional latent feature representation that explicitly models zero inflation (dropout) before downstream cell-type clustering.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-loading
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices must be ingested into R before SCEVAN analysis — e.g., GSE131928 GBM samples (MGH102, MGH104, MGH105, MGH106) or multiple myeloma 10X data destined for pipelineCNA or multiSampleComparisonClonalCN.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-melting
description: Use when a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) with one column per gene must be reshaped into a tall cell-gene-value table before Parquet serialization and downstream scSPARKL analysis on low-memory hardware.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when you have a per-cell sparse k-mer abundance matrix (from jellyfish counts) and a pre-built CKG look-up table, and need reference-free CKG-level cell features for downstream cell type classification.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw unfiltered droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (.h5 or .mtx) must be shaped for EmptyNN cell-calling or PU-learning based filtering of cell-free droplets.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix is sparse and dropout-prone and must be filtered, HVG-selected, and normalized to [0,1] before binarization or landmark construction.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g. GEO accession like GSE81682 mouse HSPC) must be normalized and converted with cellexalvrR into CellexalVR-consumable input files.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when input is a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix (gene x cell CSV) that must be quality-filtered and reduced to highly variable genes before imputation or K-means clustering evaluation.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when two cross-species scRNA-seq datasets (count matrices) must be preprocessed and paired with a gene similarity distance matrix as input to a cell type matching model such as TACTiCS.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-simulation
description: Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq gene-by-cell count matrix to validate penalized Latent Dirichlet Allocation (pLDA) topic modeling, or to sanity-check topic-word probability estimation on data with known latent structure.

name: scrnaseq-count-matrix-simulation
description: Use when you need a simulated scRNA-seq benchmark dataset with known cell-type labels and controllable cluster sizes (e.g., a rare population <5% of cells) to evaluate clustering accuracy and robustness.

name: scrnaseq-count-simulation
description: Use when an evaluation needs synthetic scRNA-Seq count data with known ground-truth cell-cluster labels — e.g. benchmarking clustering or transfer-learning pipelines where ARI can only be computed if true labels exist.

name: scrnaseq-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a cell-cycle or latent-factor removal method on scRNA-Seq data where ground-truth effect assignments (which PCs are cell-cycle, which genes are cell-type) must be known exactly.

name: scrnaseq-cross-platform-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when several labeled scRNA-seq studies of the same tissue exist and you need to quantify how annotation accuracy transfers between studies/platforms (inter-study annotation) across competing classifiers.

name: scrnaseq-data-formatting
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq data (e.g. GEO accession GSE116753 or similar) must be reshaped into MDIC3's exp.txt/metadata.txt input format before GRN inference with GNIPLR and communication scoring.

name: scrnaseq-data-input-format-preparation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with cell-type and time-point metadata must be formatted into the expression/cell-type/time-point files that dsCellNet requires before running datainput and downstream network inference.

name: scrnaseq-dataset-harmonization
description: Use when several scRNA-seq datasets with expression matrices, dataset-of-origin labels, and cell-type labels must be combined to test whether cell types (e.g. neurons vs non-neuronal cells) replicate across studies via AUROC.

name: scrnaseq-dataset-retrieval-geo-scp
description: Use when a benchmark or method comparison requires raw scRNA-seq count matrices with ground-truth cell labels and the paper lists source repositories (GEO/SCP accession numbers, e.g. Table 1 of the scDHA article) to fetch them.

name: scrnaseq-dataset-subsetting
description: Use when benchmarking PAS/scoring tools on million-cell-level scRNA-seq data where full-dataset computation is impractical, and a fixed-size random cell subset (e.g., 100k cells from the >1.2M-cell lupus atlas) suffices for validation.

name: scrnaseq-dataset-subsetting-and-downsampling
description: Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. a whole-tumor immune atlas) must be narrowed to a biologically relevant population (immune cells) and a fixed number of cells (e.g. 5000) before per-cell scoring.

name: scrnaseq-doublet-detection-ensemble-analysis
description: Use when processing droplet-based scRNA-seq data (Seurat/SingleCellExperiment objects) that lacks experimental doublet labels (no cell hashing, MULTI-seq, or demuxlet), and doublets must be called computationally per sample before downstream clustering or trajectory analyses.

name: scrnaseq-dropout-masking
description: Use when benchmarking gene-imputation methods on scRNA-seq count matrices (h5 format) under controlled synthetic dropout, e.g. to verify a method recovers masked non-zero entries better than baselines.

name: scrnaseq-dropout-masking-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking an scRNA-seq imputation method on controlled dropout recovery — i.e., you have complete pre-processed count matrices and need to quantify NMSE/RMSE/MAE recovery at artificially masked non-zero values.

name: scrnaseq-embedding-suitability-evaluation
description: Use when fitting trajectories (e.g., Slingshot, Monocle3) on scRNA-seq data and you must decide among candidate embeddings from feature selection (number of highly variable genes) and dimension reduction choices, or need to know if a trajectory is appropriate at all.

name: scrnaseq-entropy-model-implementation
description: Use when implementing or validating an entropy-based cluster purity score for scRNA-seq clusters, i.e. computing single-gene sample entropy, LOESS-derived ds residuals, and aggregating them into ROGUE.

name: scrnaseq-expression-matrix-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices for a labeled training set and a testing set (e.g., ASD snRNA-seq patients vs controls) must be normalized and restricted to their shared genes prior to annotation or benchmarking.

name: scrnaseq-expression-matrix-permutation
description: Use when you must verify that a matrix-imputation pipeline (e.g., SERM) is invariant to the arrangement of cells and genes — i.e., row/column permutations of a scRNA-seq count matrix yield near-identical Pearson correlations to the reference.

name: scrnaseq-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when a single-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix (anndata object) and Step 1 cell phase posteriors are available and genes not yet labeled cyclers must be screened for de novo circadian rhythmicity before being added to the current cycler set.

name: scrnaseq-half-sample-resampling
description: Use when comparing marker-selection methods (e.g. G-PC, CEM-PC, mRMR, ReliefF, F values) on scRNA-seq expression matrices and you need to quantify how reproducible each method's selected feature sets are across repeated random resampling.

name: scrnaseq-homogeneity-detection
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is about to undergo trajectory/pseudotime inference and you must first verify it actually contains a continuous trajectory (i.e., is not homogeneous cells or disconnected clusters).

name: scrnaseq-imputation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing imputation methods on scRNA-seq count matrices to test whether imputation improves cell-type separation or preserves biological zeros, e.g. before-vs-after classification error on downsampled Zeisel/Baron/Chen/La Manno data.

name: scrnaseq-latent-space-construction-from-target-sets
description: Use when a scRNAseq counts table with cell-cluster assignments (e.g. setA, clusters 1-5) must be functionally annotated by reconstructing clusters in an encoded space derived from validated target/signature sets rather than gene expression alone.

name: scrnaseq-library-size-offset-normalization
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq count matrices (UMI or read counts) across cells with varying sequencing depth, and a Tweedie/GLM-style model requires a library-size offset log(S) instead of pre-normalizing counts.

name: scrnaseq-log-normalized-matrix-handling
description: Use when feeding raw perturbation (Y) and control (Z) cell-by-gene count matrices into scDecouple or similar scCRISPR-seq pipelines that require log-normalized, HVG-subtracted matrices as input.

name: scrnaseq-log2-transformation-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (rows = cells, columns = genes) must be pre-processed and log2-transformed before dropout imputation or before measuring K-means cell-clustering accuracy with ARI.

name: scrnaseq-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when clustering a scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Chen, Xin, Gierahn benchmarks) requires per-cluster marker genes with explicit fold-change, significance, and expression-prevalence cutoffs to drive automatic cell-type annotation.

name: scrnaseq-marker-selection-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing marker-selection methods on scRNA-seq phenotype-classification tasks: you have count matrices with cell-type/phenotype labels and need discriminative marker sets plus downstream classifier F1 scores.

name: scrnaseq-mixed-transcriptional-profile-simulation
description: Use when a paired scRNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics dataset is available and cell type proportions must be simulated with known ground truth to train or benchmark a deconvolution model (e.g., SpatialDDLS on 10x Visium/Chromium data).

name: scrnaseq-multi-resolution-louvain-clustering
description: Use when an scRNA-seq dataset must be clustered and there is no principled resolution choice: cluster across a resolution grid, compute marker specificity per configuration, and pick the resolution maximizing the specificity index.

name: scrnaseq-neighborhood-scale-analysis
description: Use when selecting a t-SNE perplexity/kEff for single-cell embeddings, or when characterizing whether scRNA-seq data have one or multiple intrinsic neighborhood scales via per-sample EMBEDR p-value sweeps.

name: scrnaseq-normalized-expression-processing
description: Use when constructing ligand-receptor communication edges from a normalised single-cell expression matrix and need an explicit, reproducible definition of gene 'expression' per cell type before edge extraction.

name: scrnaseq-normalized-matrix-qc-processing
description: Use when the input is a barcoded scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. GEO accession GSE99915) needing a QC-filtered, normalized expression matrix plus cell-ID-to-barcode-ID lineage annotations before lineage inference or memory-gene analysis.

name: scrnaseq-preprocessing-quality-control
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data must be filtered (min/max genes per cell, min cells per gene, mitochondrial percentage, HVG dispersion) before single-cell drug-response prediction with scDEAL.

name: scrnaseq-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether denoising or imputation of scRNA-seq data preserves biological structure, by comparing principal component subspaces of original vs. perturbed/imputed matrices.

name: scrnaseq-pseudotime-gene-expression-modeling
description: Use when a sample-level trajectory (PILOT diffusion-map embedding + EIPLGraph pseudotime, e.g. from myocardial_infarction.h5ad) already exists and you must rank cell populations changing along progression and identify cluster-specific genes via Wald tests.

name: scrnaseq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when a raw counts matrix or Seurat object (csv/rds/h5 or 10X folder) enters a scRNA-seq workflow and cells must be filtered for quality before annotation, clustering, or gene-set scoring.

name: scrnaseq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing 10X Genomics scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO samples GSM3453537/GSM3453538) before building a CellChat object, and cells must be filtered by UMI count, gene count, and mitochondrial fraction thresholds.

name: scrnaseq-random-subsampling-pilot-design
description: Use when planning scRNA-seq experiments from small pilot data: you need to test whether generative models trained on sub-sampled pilot datasets can produce synthetic data whose clustering, cell-type proportions, and per-gene distributions match a larger ground-truth dataset.

name: scrnaseq-read-alignment-star
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (.sra/.fastq, e.g., from the Kim dataset) must be mapped to HUMAN reference (read_length 100) to produce BAMs feeding featureCounts and GATK-based SNV calling.

name: scrnaseq-read-simulation
description: Use when a study needs synthetic scRNA-seq reads (BAM/FASTQ) that mimic real data at both read-sequence and read-count levels, e.g., benchmarking UMI deduplication tools or comparing read-coverage fidelity against simulators like minnow.

name: scrnaseq-reference-based-deconvolution
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., Visium spots with multi-cell content, or Slide-seq singlet/doublet spots) must be assigned cell-type labels using a paired, cell-type-annotated scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq reference, and accuracy must be benchmarked per slice vs. jointly across slices.

name: scrnaseq-reference-based-proportion-estimation
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq read counts from a complex tissue and a matching scRNA-seq reference with cell type annotations, and need cell type proportion estimates without pre-selected marker genes.

name: scrnaseq-reference-based-spot-deconvolution
description: Use when a seq-based ST dataset (e.g., 10X Visium spots) needs per-spot cell type proportions estimated from a matched scRNA-seq reference, or when cell-type composition must be obtained before Splane spatial-domain identification.

name: scrnaseq-reference-curation
description: Use when deciding whether an available scRNA-seq reference (e.g., one missing key cell types like neurons, or an atlas from a different tissue such as mouse brain) is fit for reference-based deconvolution of multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data.

name: scrnaseq-reference-mapping
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq (or spatial MERFISH) dataset must be annotated by transferring labels from a matched reference scRNA-seq atlas sharing the same tissue, especially when batch effects separate the two datasets.

name: scrnaseq-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of rare-cell identification methods on scRNA-seq data, or when judging whether a method can process datasets in the tens-of-thousands-of-cells range.

name: scrnaseq-similarity-matrix-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually compare cell-type or developmental-stage separation produced by different learned cell-to-cell similarity matrices on scRNA-seq data, e.g. benchmarking SSRE against Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR on the Goolam or Yan datasets.

name: scrnaseq-simulation-with-ground-truth-subclusters
description: Use when validating or benchmarking a cluster-merging / cluster-significance method (e.g. Cytocipher cluster-merge) on simulated scRNA-seq data where the true subcluster structure is known and an AUROC against ground-truth labels is the target metric.

name: scrnaseq-summary-statistics-construction
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data are available and gene-level DE effect sizes (beta coefficients and their variances) must be generated as input for iDEA's joint DE and gene set enrichment analysis.

name: scrnaseq-time-series-trajectory-inference
description: Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq dataset with collection time-point labels needs a balanced subsample before trajectory inference, especially to exclude cells whose pseudotime disagrees with their collection time point.

name: scrnaseq-transfer-learning-clustering
description: Use when clustering a small scRNA-Seq target dataset (e.g. rare cell types, 300–600 cells) for which a large, well-annotated source dataset from a related tissue or context exists.

name: scrnaseq-trimean-expression-aggregation
description: Use when preparing per-cell-group average expression of ligands, receptors, and cofactors from scRNA-seq data before inferring cell-cell communication probabilities with CellChat or a reimplementation of its mass-action model.

name: scrnaseq-wasserstein-distance-computation
description: Use when you have a multi-sample scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. patient biopsies with cell-type annotations, PCA embedding, patient and disease-status columns) and need sample-level distances to detect disease-associated patient subgroups without patient labels.

name: scrtcna-dimensionality-reduction-baseline-comparison
description: Use when a single-cell transcriptomics dataset ships with pre-computed dimensionality reductions and manual cell-type annotations, and you must show whether a new embedding or clustering method beats those baselines on unsupervised cell-type recovery.

name: scte-mode-comparison-validation
description: Use when scTE differential TE calls (e.g. ≥2-fold change, FDR < 0.05 between ESCs and MEFs) need robustness checks against TE annotation mode, especially to test whether intronic TE reads drive specificity.

name: sctransform-normalization
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices from one or more plant samples (e.g. Arabidopsis, Oryza sativa, Zea mays roots) must be variance-stabilized and normalized with SCTransform prior to PCA/UMAP, clustering, or CCA/RPCA-based cross-species integration.

name: sctransform-sample-integration
description: Use when multiple scRNAseq samples (e.g., a time series such as GSE223109) must be normalized and integrated before joint clustering, and per-sample SCTransform normalization plus a shared integration feature set is needed to remove batch effects.

name: scvalue-rf-oob-data-value-computation
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq AnnData (.h5ad) with cell-type labels must be subsampled for a downstream ML/DL task (annotation, label transfer, deconvolution) and cell-level informativeness should guide which cells enter the sketch.

name: scvelo-dynamical-and-stochastic-velocity-estimation
description: Use when a benchmark requires traditional linear RNA velocity baselines — e.g., comparing against LatentVelo on dyngen synthetic AnnData (spliced/unspliced layers) or real scRNA-seq with spliced and unspliced counts.

name: scvelo-dynamical-model-benchmarking
description: Use when spliced/unspliced AnnData from a hematopoietic or erythroid differentiation dataset yields suspicious or reversed velocity directions from scVelo, and a benchmark against a unified-time method is needed.

name: scvi-continuous-covariate-correction
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain quantifiable continuous nuisance covariates (e.g., cell-cycle or sex scores) and a latent-space batch-correction baseline is needed to compare against gene-level filtering methods.

name: scvi-prior-sampling-implementation
description: Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq observations with a trained VAE (scVI) but you want generation independent of the original observations, i.e., sampling directly from the prior of the latent space rather than the posterior.

name: scvi-tools-style-differential-testing-implementation
description: Use when you have trained a VEGA model with gene-module-informed latent posteriors and need to call gene modules significantly differentially active between two cell groups via a Bayes Factor.

name: second-order-derivative-gap-distance-scoring
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. tens of thousands of cells) must be scanned for rare cell clusters without clustering the whole dataset, and clusters must be ranked by a gap-based distance score (skewness > 2).

name: second-order-derivative-statistic-computation
description: Use when you have a precomputed cell-to-neighbour distance matrix for a scRNA-seq dataset and need to derive ∆D/∆∆D statistics and per-k skewness to identify candidate rare cluster sizes.

name: secondary-metabolite-class-profiling
description: Use when a comparative-genomics pipeline needs BGC-level absence/presence features across many bacterial genomes — e.g. annotating .gbk files with Prokka then mining secondary metabolites with antiSMASH and BiG-SCAPE before lifestyle association.

name: secondary-structure-feature-ablation
description: Use when asked whether a specific feature group (e.g. the 6 SSFs) contributes to a trained XGBoost model's performance and you need a full-vs-reduced-feature ablation table with accuracy, precision, MCC and specificity on a held-out FASTA set.

name: secondary-structure-kmer-feature-generation
description: Use when training or predicting with LncDC with secondary structure features enabled (the '-r' flag), so RNAfold foldings must be converted into ss k-mer score tables at k=1..k=5.

name: secreted-protein-annotation
description: Use when building or extending a ligand-receptor database (e.g. connectomeDB2020-style two-column Ligand/Receptor CSV) where each ligand must be classified as secreted or plasma-membrane before edge extraction.

name: secretory-protein-classification-model-training
description: Use when the goal is to train protein-sequence deep learning classifiers on FASTA-derived encoded matrices and compare architecture performance (e.g. six-class bacterial secreted protein classification) with reported hyperparameters.

name: seed-controlled-in-silico-dataset-generation
description: Use when a benchmark needs multiple simulated single-cell datasets with known ground truth (trajectory, progression times, cell-specific GRNs) across diverse backbone topologies and reproducible seeds.

name: seed-gene-selection-from-cell-type-markers
description: Use when starting CASCC feature selection on a normalized single-cell RNA-seq matrix and you need a biologically grounded seed gene (from known cell-type markers) to launch findAttractor.adaptive.

name: seed-match-counting-in-3utr-transcript-sequences
description: Use when a DESeq2 RNA-seq results table from an siRNA treatment needs to be annotated with predicted seed matches (mer7m8, mer8) in 3'UTRs, or when you must test whether seed-match gene sets show a cumulative down-shift in log2FoldChange versus background.

name: seed-varied-ensemble-network-training
description: Use when evaluating whether ensembling seed-varied neural ODE forecasts improves accuracy over a single RNAForecaster network, or when forecasting simulated/BoolODE single-cell expression futures where single-network log MSE must be reduced at later time points.

name: segment-mean-expression-computation
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. MGH106 from GSE131928) must be aggregated from gene-level expression to per-cell segment mean values over the breakpoints shared across cells, as input to downstream CNV state classification.

name: segment-type-annotation-eval-types
description: Use when you hold hyb-format hybrid records from miRNA/target ligation experiments (e.g. qCLASH, CLASH) and need per-record segment-type and miRNA annotations before tallying hybrid types or miRNA characteristics across replicates.

name: segmentation-benchmark-against-annotations
description: Use when manually annotated cell boundaries exist for multiplexed tissue images and you need quantitative agreement metrics (DSC/JSC) to compare candidate segmentation methods at image and individual-cell level.

name: segmentation-dice-jaccard-evaluation
description: Use when per-cell segmentation masks from multiplexed tissue images (MIBI or multiplexed IF) must be scored against manually annotated ground truth via image-level DSC and JSC distributions.

name: segmentation-mask-quantification
description: Use when two segmentation implementations (or a pipeline and ground-truth annotations) have produced membrane/cell masks over the same multiplexed immunofluorescence TMA sub-images and per-image agreement statistics (DSC/JSC) must be computed and aggregated.

name: segmentation-overlap-metric-computation
description: Use when a predicted cell-border segmentation must be quantitatively compared against manual annotations (or another segmentation method) at the image level to report segmentation accuracy.

name: segmentation-quality-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have segmented-cell masks (_connected.tif) and cell-gene matrices (expr_mat.csv) from a spatial transcriptomics run and need to quantify or compare segmentation quality across methods or ablation configurations.

name: selection-rule-based-read-filtering
description: Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be classified and quantified against GFF3/GTF feature annotations while resolving overlapping features or distinguishing miRNAs from isomiRs at single-nucleotide precision.

name: self-distillation-deep-learning-model-training
description: Use when running Anchored-fusion with default filtering on paired-end RNA-seq FASTQ data and a retrained HVLD filter is desired, or when benchmarking HVLD against bi-LSTM, Transformer, MLP, SVM, and HVL baselines on chimeric-read classification.

name: self-mapping-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when evaluating how accurate and stable a reference-mapping classifier (e.g. scID) is in a controlled self-mapping setting, where published cluster labels exist and ARI against them is the metric of interest.

name: self-supervised-segmentation-model-training
description: Use when segmenting individual cells from subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium transcripts.csv.gz + morphology_mip.ome.tif) without ground-truth labels, and when evaluating loss-component contributions via ablation.

name: self-training-semi-supervised-cell-annotation
description: Use when a small ground-truth-annotated single-cell training set (e.g. 100 actively selected cells) exists but many unlabeled cells remain, and you want to test whether adding confidently self-labeled cells improves F1 cell type annotation.

name: self-training-uncertainty-quantification
description: Use when you have a labeled single-cell training set and need to quantify per-cell annotation uncertainty (predictive entropy) to identify or flag potentially mislabeled cells before self-training.

name: selu-activation-self-normalization
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing the scDHA second module (stacked Bayesian autoencoder) or a modified VAE that projects filtered single-cell data onto a 15-dimensional latent space and needs self-normalizing activations for stable AdamW training.

name: semi-continuous-count-normalization-log1p
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g., 10X matrix.mtx/genes.tsv/barcodes.tsv) must be transformed into semi-continuous normalized form before feeding the AE-TPGG autoencoder or comparing with highly-variable-gene filtering.

name: semi-profiled-data-fidelity-evaluation
description: Use when inferred or semi-profiled single-cell profiles (e.g., inferred_cells.h5ad for target samples like AP1) must be validated against real-profiled ground-truth cells or a representative-vs-target baseline before downstream use.

name: semi-profiling-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a semi-profiled (AI-inferred) single-cell cohort has been generated from bulk data plus representative samples and must be validated against a real-profiled ground-truth cohort before downstream use.

name: semi-profiling-error-normalization
description: Use when evaluating a semi-profiling or sample-inference pipeline on a cohort (e.g., COVID-19, representative counts 4–28) and you need a normalized error EN that is comparable across datasets and baseline schemes.

name: semi-simulated-st-data-construction
description: Use when you need paired SC-ST data with known spot-level cell-type ground truth to validate spatial mapping/deconvolution methods, starting from single-cell data with global x/y coordinates.

name: semi-supervised-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq AnnData has cell type annotations for only a fraction of cells (e.g. 10/20/50% missing labels) and labels must be predicted for the unlabeled remainder.

name: semi-supervised-cell-type-annotation-via-gating
description: Use when integrating heterogeneous scRNA-seq samples (e.g., TIL collections across tumor types) where only partial or noisy cell-type labels exist and you want gating-derived priors to drive semi-supervised integration.

name: semi-supervised-em-mixture-model-clustering
description: Use when filtering droplet-based snRNA-seq data where hard count cutoffs or EmptyDrops fail to remove ambient/debris RNA, and you need expression-profile-based clustering that fixes low-count droplets as debris before fitting a mixture model.

name: semi-supervised-gene-weighting-clustering
description: Use when analyzing paired control/perturbed scRNA-seq data (e.g. gene knock-outs, treatments) where the goal is to identify cell states unique to the perturbed condition without a priori knowledge of marker genes or cell states.

name: semi-supervised-integration-with-cell-type-labels
description: Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq datasets where partial or imperfect cell type labels exist for at least a reference subset, and preserving cell-type biology (e.g., CD8 T cell subtypes) while removing batch effects matters.

name: semi-supervised-label-propagation
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq cells already have partially confident labels from a consensus of annotation tools (e.g. scPred, SingleR, ScType, SCINA, scSorter) and you need to propagate those labels to unconfident cells with a graph convolutional network.

name: semi-supervised-leiden-clustering-with-frozen-clusters
description: Use when refining label-transfer annotations of a query scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., HBMP2-spleen-2 against an annotated HBMP3-spleen-CC3 reference) where unconstrained Leiden clustering alone disagrees with reference labels and a semi-automatic, expert-guided correction is acceptable.

name: semi-supervised-louvain-clustering
description: Use when clustering a perturbation scRNA-seq AnnData where control cells already have trusted cluster labels (e.g. from Louvain on controls) and treated cells must be assigned without letting them distort the control-defined states.

name: semi-supervised-scissors-reclustering
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering (e.g., Seurat Louvain) yields broad clusters suspected of containing rare or low-abundance subtypes that standard resolution sweeps miss.

name: semi-supervised-scrna-seq-integration
description: Use when integrating multiple scRNA-seq batches where partial or imperfect cell type labels are available and preserving cell-type biological variance (e.g., celltype ASW, CiLISI) is a priority alongside batch mixing.

name: semi-synthetic-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing signal-removal methods on a semi-synthetic single-cell dataset where a known nuisance signal (e.g., cell cycle) and a ground-truth biological attribute (e.g., subclone labels) are both annotated, so removal and conservation can be scored quantitatively.

name: semi-synthetic-response-construction-transcriptomic
description: Use when benchmarking high-dimensional regression methods (e.g. SuffPCR vs sparse linear models vs non-sparse PCR) on real omics data where no true response exists, and ground-truth feature selection is needed.

name: senescence-marker-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have cell-type-specific senescence hub gene networks (e.g. from SenePy's Tabula Muris Senis analysis) and need to quantify enrichment of the 180 literature-curated known CS markers to validate each hub.

name: senescence-marker-panel-validation
description: Use when a workflow must reproduce or verify age-dependent CS marker behavior across cell types in Tabula Muris Senis or human aging atlases using senepy hub scoring.

name: senescence-signature-importance-weighting
description: Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes with a SenePy senescence hub signature and you want per-gene contributions scaled by hub-network connectivity rather than treating all signature genes equally.

name: senescence-signature-scoring-of-spatial-transcriptomics
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics spots or single-cell transcriptomes must be scored for senescence using cell-type-specific hub signatures (e.g., mapping senescence burden onto Visium sections or with fibrosis markers like Col1a1).

name: sense-antisense-expression-combination-annotation
description: Use when you have CCIVR Table.csv output containing cis-NAT pairs with expression profiling columns (fold_change, padj) and need to tabulate pair counts per expression combination to find inversely correlated (down-up) pairs.

name: sensitivity-analysis-across-simulation-scenarios
description: Use when you must quantify and compare detection sensitivity of pathway analysis tools across a controlled panel of simulated two-population scRNA-seq comparisons with an implanted target pathway.

name: sensitivity-analysis-of-gene-handling-options
description: Use when porting the BloodGen3 probe-level repertoire to gene-level inputs (e.g. RNA-seq) or when deciding whether duplicate genes mapping to multiple modules must be resolved before running Groupcomparison fingerprints.

name: sensitivity-auc-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking statistical methods on spike-in ground-truth simulations (e.g., XDE along pseudotime on null HCA-BM data) and you need empirical FDR calibration plus a sensitivity-vs-real-FDR AUC to rank methods by power and honesty.

name: sensitivity-fdr-curve-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating TFBS or regulatory-element predictions against a ChIP-sep gold standard by ranking candidate motif sites and quantifying sensitivity at controlled FDR levels, especially to compare predicted vs. true DH or baseline rankings.

name: sensitivity-ppv-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when quantifying the detection limit of a genotype/chimerism assignment method — e.g. how low a minor donor fraction SNV-based assignment can detect in single-cell UMI count data.

name: sensitivity-specificity-computation
description: Use when reproducing or validating malignant-cell-identification benchmarks on labeled scRNA-seq test sets (e.g., test_cancerCellLine.h5ad and test_TabulaSapiens.h5ad) where ground-truth malignant/normal labels exist and method sensitivity/specificity must be quantified.

name: sensitivity-specificity-curve-visualization
description: Use when comparing how reliably signature-fitting algorithms detect low-contribution signatures in simulated catalogs with known ground-truth contributions, and you need sensitivity/specificity curves per algorithm.

name: sensitivity-specificity-metric-computation
description: Use when RNA-seq CNV calls (chromosome-arm, segment, or gene-level from CaSpER) must be validated against an independent DNA-based gold standard such as genotyping-array calls, reporting TPR/FPR and PPV per event category.

name: sensitivity-threshold-analysis
description: Use when sweeping a parameter (e.g. proportion of control genes influenced by a latent effect) to find the minimal proportion at which ccRemover's bootstrap Δj test reliably detects and removes that effect.

name: seqfish-dataset-processing
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics task requires reproducing seqFISH+ mouse cortex communication analysis or validating that a communication-predicted gene (e.g., CPLX1) shows elevated expression where two cell types (L5/L6 eNeurons) are spatially adjacent.

name: seqscope-fastq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw Seq-Scope FASTQ files must be converted into spatial coordinate files, STARsolo barcode whitelists, HDMI density QC plots, and digital expression matrices — i.e., 1st-seq spatial-barcode FASTQ plus 2nd-seq cDNA FASTQ pairs are the starting point.

name: seqspec-region-annotation-extraction
description: Use when you need to determine where a specific library element (cell barcode, UMI, sequence) is encoded in an assay's read structure, given a seqspec YAML specification file.

name: seqspec-yaml-schema-validation
description: Use when a seqspec YAML assay specification must be schema-validated before downstream preprocessing (e.g., cellatlas/kb count), or when a batch of library specs needs per-file pass/fail correctness reports.

name: sequence-copy-padding-encoding
description: Use when protein or lncRNA sequences of variable length must be transformed into fixed-length CNN-compatible inputs for lncRNA-protein interaction prediction or similar sequence-pair classification.

name: sequence-database-query-benchmarking
description: Use when measuring how query time/throughput on a large sequence-database index changes with index configuration (e.g., zero/one/two Aggregated Bloom Comb trees) across query batches of similar, dissimilar, and random sequences.

name: sequence-dataset-query-scoring
description: Use when you need to determine which of thousands of indexed FASTA/FASTQ datasets contain a query sequence, and how many k-mers the query shares with each dataset.

name: sequence-feature-encoding-pseudonucleotide-composition
description: Use when building RNA modification (m5C) predictors that need fused informatic sequence profiles from raw FASTA-like training sequences before classifier training or F-score feature selection.

name: sequence-fragment-alignment-and-centering
description: Use when you need to test whether m5C-containing fragments show distinctive sequence motifs vs non-m5C fragments by comparing per-position nucleotide enrichment across cytosine-centered, equal-length flanking sequences.

name: sequence-information-theory-analysis
description: Use when reads in UMI libraries show mapping shifts and you need to test whether cluster size correlates with sequence complexity, e.g. computing Shannon Entropy and Mutual Information per UMI-read cluster in run_171108.

name: sequence-padding-truncation
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be turned into fixed-length autoregressive token sequences for tGPT: rank genes by descending expression, tokenize, and pad/truncate to 64 or 128 tokens.

name: sequence-read-query-execution
description: Use when a set of sequencing reads must be searched against a pre-built Raptor IBF/MIBF index over 64 or 1,024 bins, and run time, memory, and bin-assignment accuracy must be measured per index size.

name: sequence-search-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing approximate sequence search tools (Raptor, COBS, Mantis) over large binned nucleotide collections and you need construction time, search speed, RAM/disk, and specificity measurements.

name: sequence-similarity-clustering
description: Use when curating RNA/DNA sequence benchmark sets for ML training and testing where redundant sequences could cause overfitting, and a similarity cutoff (e.g. <80%) must be enforced per dataset.

name: sequence-structure-expression-feature-based-mirna-selection
description: Use when you have a uniform-format list of miRNA/precursor candidates (output from miRNATranslate in iwa-miRNA's Galaxy framework) and need to prioritize true positives before manual curation.

name: sequencing-artifact-heteroskedasticity-assessment
description: Use when input is raw (untransformed) NGS/RNA-seq expression data (e.g., TCGA, GTEx count-style feature tables) showing high variance in high-read-count features, and a preprocessing/normalization choice must be made before correlation analysis.

name: sequencing-cost-estimation
description: Use when a semi-profiling workflow needs a defensible dollar figure for sequencing only representative samples versus the whole cohort, or when judging whether the 1/10–1/3 cost-savings target of scSemiProfiler was achieved.

name: sequencing-depth-fold-change-simulation
description: Use when validating that a single-cell cluster-purity metric (e.g., ROGUE) is insensitive to sequencing-depth fold changes between replicates or to variation in cell number, by simulating replicate mixtures and comparing ROGUE/S against silhouette.

name: sequencing-depth-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell velocity model's outputs must be shown stable under technical noise, specifically when perturbing raw count matrices by downsampling to reduced sequencing-depth proportions.

name: sequencing-depth-stratified-recall-evaluation
description: Use when a large single-cell dataset with deposited predefined cell labels is available and you need to quantify whether per-cell UMI counts (sequencing depth) bias the accuracy of an automatic annotation tool such as deCS.correlation().

name: sequencing-depth-variance-simulation
description: Use when evaluating how an estimator (e.g., allelic proportion or expression estimates) performs at reduced sequencing depth, by simulating low-coverage data via random per-cell read down-sampling from full-depth counts.

name: sequencing-error-markov-chain-modeling
description: Use when benchmarking isoform quantification methods (e.g. Longcell, Sicelore2, FLAMES, wf-single-cell, IsoQuant) on simulated Nanopore reads where per-read error processes must be modeled at controlled low/middle/high quality regimes with a ground-truth cell-by-isoform matrix for scoring.

name: sequencing-error-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating UMI recovery/collapse methods (e.g., Longcell iterative clustering vs DBSCAN eps=2) where you need error-laden simulated reads with known ground-truth UMI counts across amplification levels.

name: sequencing-instrument-swapping-control-comparison
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries have been sequenced on both a patterned-flowcell instrument (HiSeq 4000/HiSeq X/NovaSeq) and a non-patterned control (HiSeq 2500), and you need to quantify or rule out excess inter-sample cell-barcode sharing.

name: sequencing-noise-modeling
description: Use when building simulated single-cell sequencing benchmarks that must preserve haplotype structure and amplification artifacts while challenging BAF/phasing-based CNA callers with realistic noise.

name: sequencing-platform-swap-control-analysis
description: Use when a barcode-swapping fraction has been estimated on a patterned flow-cell instrument (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) and you need a same-libraries control on a non-patterned instrument (HiSeq 2500) to attribute swapping to the sequencer rather than the libraries.

name: sequencing-protocol-stratified-benchmarking
description: Use when a cell type classifier trained on 10x 3'/5' scRNA-seq must be evaluated on cells from other sequencing protocols (STRT-seq, Smart-seq2, BD Rhapsody Targeted mRNA) to quantify protocol-specific generalization loss.

name: sequencing-read-quality-assessment
description: Use when starting a sequencing analysis (DNA-seq or RNA-seq) from raw FASTQ data and the downstream pipeline needs quality-checked, adapter-free, length- and quality-filtered reads before alignment or genotyping.

name: sequencing-read-region-property-checking
description: Use when a seqspec specification (YAML) file for a genomics assay library must be schema-validated before use in preprocessing, or when auditing a curated library of assay specs for missing required Region fields.

name: sequencing-read-structure-interpretation
description: Use when you need to know where a genomics assay encodes its cell barcodes, UMIs, or cDNA across R1/R2 reads and Illumina indices — e.g. before preprocessing with cellatlas/kb, or when a spec must be annotated or validated.

name: sequencing-saturation-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how deeply the gRNA library was sequenced in a CROP-seq/single-cell CRISPR screen and determine the read depth (e.g. 34%, 59%, 92% saturation) required for reliable gRNA-to-cell assignment.

name: sequencing-substitution-error-introduction
description: Use when scReadSim has produced synthetic scRNA-seq reads and you need realistic sequencing-error profiles added before benchmarking read-level tools such as UMI deduplication or alignment.

name: sequencing-technology-cross-platform-classification-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation classifiers across multiple scRNA-seq datasets generated by different sequencing technologies, to compare accuracy, computational efficiency, and model complexity per method per dataset.

name: sequencing-tool-runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing a barcode demultiplexer when large noisy long-read datasets (e.g. 61M-read PromethION FASTQ with 1022 true plus 10000 decoy barcodes) must be processed under wall-clock and memory constraints.

name: sequential-batch-correction-with-sample-tree
description: Use when integrating many single-cell RNA-seq datasets (e.g., hundreds of samples, hundreds of thousands of cells) with partial cell type annotations, where batch effects must be corrected while preserving cell-type-specific biology.

name: sergio-single-cell-simulation
description: Use when a gene set scoring or cell-type recovery method needs benchmarking on simulated scRNA-seq data with known cell type labels and tunable dropout/noise conditions.

name: serum-small-rna-expression-ranking
description: Use when raw serum/plasma small RNA-seq FASTQ files need adapter trimming, quality filtering, genome alignment, small RNA annotation, and a ranked RNA-by-sample read count matrix, especially when miRNAs and other small RNA classes (<200 nt) must be profiled together.

name: set-difference-significant-interaction-comparison
description: Use when evaluating whether a joint two-condition DCI method (e.g. scHiCDiff NB/ZINB) recovers differential bin pairs more reliably than independently thresholding significance calls in each condition and subtracting the resulting interaction sets.

name: set-intersection-upsetplot-visualization
description: Use when you have per-sample-pair or per-run lists of selected candidate reference genes and need to quantify pairwise set overlap and duplication rate, flagging genes covered in more than 80% of the pairs.

name: seurat-alignment-score-computation
description: Use when comparing batch-effect correction or dimension-reduction methods (ComBat, MNN, CCA, CCA anchor, Harmony, scPhere, scVI, Cell BLAST/DIRECTi) on scRNA-seq dataset combinations with overlapping cell types and you need a quantitative batch-mixing metric.

name: seurat-anchor-based-label-transfer
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell cell-type classifiers against Seurat v3, or when transferring cell-type labels from an annotated reference scRNA-seq dataset to a query dataset with FindTransferAnchors + TransferData.

name: seurat-anchor-based-transfer-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating crossmodal prediction of surface proteins from transcriptome-only input on a CITE-seq batch, and you need the Seurat anchor-based baseline (Jaccard index per protein) to compare against a deep generative model such as scMM.

name: seurat-anchor-based-transfer-learning
description: Use when benchmarking protein imputation from paired RNA/ADT CITE-seq data against a non-neural transfer-learning baseline, or when comparing predictions in holdout (10%/90%) and out-of-cell-type splits.

name: seurat-batch-alignment-of-scrnaseq
description: Use when two or more scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. AMB2016 and AMB2018 visual cortex) must be matched at the cell-population level by scHPL, since batch effects make cross-dataset comparison unreliable without prior alignment.

name: seurat-cidr-initial-label-integration
description: Use when you already have initial cluster labels from another method (e.g., Seurat or CIDR) on an scRNA-seq dataset and want to refine/enhance them rather than run de novo clustering, evaluating gains in ARI/NMI.

name: seurat-clustering
description: Use when you need a reference (ground-truth) clustering partition on original scRNA-seq data to benchmark synthetic datasets via DBI and ARI, or when labeling synthetic cells by nearest-original-cell mapping in UMAP space.

name: seurat-clustering-and-marker-analysis
description: Use when a combined gene+TE scRNA-Seq expression matrix needs clustering and marker discovery to define cell populations via known markers (e.g., Zscan4c/Tcstv3 for 2C-like cells).

name: seurat-clustering-and-umap-visualization
description: Use when a cancer scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object, counts matrix in csv/rds/h5, or 10X folder) needs clustering into clusters/subclusters and UMAP plots colored by predicted cell type or subtype within scWizard.

name: seurat-clustering-pbmc-workflow
description: Use when a raw 10x filtered gene-barcode matrix (e.g. pbmc3k_filtered_gene_bc_matrices) must be normalized, scaled, and clustered in Seurat before marker-based cell-type annotation such as ScType.

name: seurat-clustering-umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a gene + TE cell-by-locus/family count matrix (e.g., from SoloTE or scTE) must be clustered and embedded in 2D to check whether TE expression recovers known cell populations, or to find cluster marker TEs.

name: seurat-dataset-alignment-for-label-transfer
description: Use when combining annotated scRNA-seq datasets generated by different labs or sequencing protocols (e.g., Saunders, Zeisel, Tabula Muris) into one classification tree, and per-cell label prediction must transfer across batch-corrected data.

name: seurat-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when investigating why one-against-all differential expression produces pseudo marker genes shared across clusters, or when benchmarking cluster-marker-based annotation accuracy against manually assigned cell type labels on scRNA-seq data.

name: seurat-dimension-reduction-clustering
description: Use when the input is a c-CSN-transformed conditional network degree matrix (CNDM, m genes x n cells) and the goal is standard scRNA-seq downstream analysis — t-SNE visualization, clustering, and ARI scoring against known cell labels.

name: seurat-dimensionality-reduction-processing
description: Use when raw single-cell counts need to be converted into a Seurat object with normalized, scaled data, variable features, PCA, and a t-SNE or UMAP 2D embedding — e.g. before detecting dubious embeddings or optimizing hyperparameters with scDEED.

name: seurat-expression-matrix-extraction
description: Use when you have a Seurat object with cell-level metadata (e.g. 'milestone' bins along a pseudotime trajectory, stimulation time points, or cell-type labels) and need per-population expression matrices to feed into SCPA multisample pathway comparison.

name: seurat-findallmarkers-filtering-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking DEG-prediction methods on artificial single-cell datasets with known/planted DEGs, and you need Seurat FindAllMarkers results — both with default filtering and unfiltered — as a cluster-based comparison baseline.

name: seurat-findmarkers-workflow
description: Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices with malignant/non-malignant cell annotations from multiple cancer datasets (e.g., RCC, HNSCC, melanoma, LUAD, BC) and need a consensus marker gene feature set for cell-type classification.

name: seurat-hto-assay-processing
description: Use when a pooled multi-sample scRNA-seq experiment has a cell-hashing (HTO) assay stored in a Seurat object and cells must be assigned singlet/doublet/negative hashtag identities, especially with many hashtags or imbalanced sample sizes where cutoff calling dominates negative assignment.

name: seurat-htodemux-singlet-doublet-negative-calling
description: Use when a cell-hashing CITE-seq experiment yields a hashtag oligo count matrix (e.g. from CITE-seq-Count) and cells must be assigned to hashed samples with doublet/negative calls, as in gExcite's hashing deconvolution step.

name: seurat-log-count-preprocessing
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from two scRNA-seq batches (e.g., Muraro CEL-Seq2 and Segerstolpe Smart-Seq2 pancreas data) must be normalized to log-counts before batch correction or before computing Euclidean distances between cells in gene space.

name: seurat-lognormalize-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., HCA MantonCB1/MantonBM1 or CITE-seq PBMC) as input to cTP-net protein imputation, after SAVER-X denoising and before running the pre-trained 24-protein model.

name: seurat-louvain-graph-clustering
description: Use when benchmarking clustering methods on UMI-based simulated scRNA-seq data — especially detecting a rare subpopulation — and you need a graph-based baseline to compare against k-means on PCA/scVI latent spaces and SIMLR.

name: seurat-louvain-leiden-clustering
description: Use when benchmarking a new scRNA-seq clustering framework (e.g., DeepCCI) against baselines, and you need Seurat Louvain/Leiden results on the same labeled datasets to compute comparative ARI/NMI scores.

name: seurat-marker-detection
description: Use when comparing transcriptional profiles of barcode groups defined by different cell-calling methods (e.g., All-retained vs EmptyNN-retained vs EmptyNN-removed) from a raw scRNA-seq count matrix.

name: seurat-marker-detection-findallmarkers
description: Use when you have a gene+TE (or feature-by-cell) expression matrix with cluster identities and need per-cluster marker TEs/genes with log2FC and adjusted P-values, or when benchmarking a quantification method's marker-recovery rate against known cluster labels.

name: seurat-marker-gene-selection
description: Use when you have a preprocessed count matrix plus manually annotated cell-type labels and need top positive marker genes per cell type to run marker-supervised methods (SCSA, MarkerCount, SCINA) or evaluate marker-based identification.

name: seurat-multimodal-reference-mapping
description: Use when a STARsolo-derived DGE has spatial barcodes too sparse (few UMIs each, e.g. SeqScope ~1M barcodes/mm2) for direct clustering, and cell-type labels must be transferred from a reference onto grid-collapsed spatial segments.

name: seurat-normalization-and-clustering
description: Use when the input is a raw single-cell count matrix (e.g. from GEO accessions like GSE124395 or GSE63473, or 10x filtered_gene_bc_matrices) and you need normalized, clustered, UMAP-embedded cells as input to marker-based cell-type annotation.

name: seurat-normalization-dimensionality-reduction-clustering
description: Use when raw spliced/unspliced gene-by-cell UMI matrices from the scKB/kallisto pipeline need non-arbitrary QC followed by Seurat normalization, PCA, UMAP, and clustering, e.g. Arabidopsis root datasets.

name: seurat-object-cluster-processing
description: Use when you have a Seurat object with graph-based clustering already performed and need to extract a cluster-specific differential expression gene list for enrichment analysis with E.PAGE.

name: seurat-object-construction-and-manipulation
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI counts (e.g. 10x cellranger filtered_bc_matrix or gene-by-cell tables) must be converted into a Seurat object for QC, normalization, scaling and variable-feature detection.
