name: seurat-object-construction-from-spatial-dge
description: Use when a DGE plus spatial coordinates at ultra-high resolution (e.g. Seq-Scope, >1M barcodes/mm2 with very low UMI per barcode) must be aggregated into grid-level Seurat objects before dimension reduction and clustering.

name: seurat-object-downstream-analysis
description: Use when a preprocessed Seurat object from a plant single-cell experiment (e.g., Arabidopsis root scRNA-seq) is available and trajectory inference, cell-type annotation, deconvolution, or cross-species integration is the next analysis step.

name: seurat-object-manipulation
description: Use when a Seurat-format scRNA-seq object must be normalized (LogNormalize, scale.factor=10000) and passed to scPagwas for pathway activation transformation, or when comparing gene-level vs pathway-level matrix sparsity.

name: seurat-object-manipulation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is stored as a Seurat object and you need to subset cells, downsample, or attach per-cell signature scores (e.g. Tcell, Myeloid, NK, Plasma_cell) via AddModuleScore_UCell.

name: seurat-object-processing
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is stored as a Seurat object but the downstream doublet-detection tool (Chord/scds) requires a SingleCellExperiment object, or when preparing per-sample Seurat objects for Chord.

name: seurat-object-single-cell-data-handling
description: Use when working with plant scRNA-seq data (e.g., Arabidopsis thaliana root atlas from Zhang et al., 2019) inside the scPlant pipeline and you need to hold expression matrices, cluster labels, GSEA results, and topic models in one R object.

name: seurat-object-wrangling
description: Use when multiple spatially resolved transcriptomics samples are held as Seurat objects (e.g. DLPFC Visium sections in seuList) and must be converted into an iSCMEBObj with an adjacency matrix list for iSC.MEB clustering.

name: seurat-pca-clustering-pipeline
description: Use when you have a log-normalized single-cell Seurat object with a biologically informed feature set (e.g., DUBStepR optimal features) and need PCA-based graph clustering to resolve discrete cell subtypes.

name: seurat-pca-clustering-workflow
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices from PBMC (e.g. GEO accessions like GSE149689) must be clustered and cell-type annotated to determine which immune subsets show differential expression of genes such as MCEMP1 and HLA-DRA.

name: seurat-sample-integration-clustering
description: Use when multi-patient scRNA-seq samples (e.g., 2 Pre-T ALL patients vs 3 healthy controls from GSE132509) must be integrated across batches, clustered, and cell-type-annotated before per-cluster differential expression and drug scoring.

name: seurat-scrna-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Hydra dataset counts, Tabula Muris marrow counts, PBMC GSE132044 matrices) must be converted into a normalized, scaled, PCA-reduced Seurat object before running t-SNE/UMAP hyperparameter optimization or embedding-quality assessment.

name: seurat-scrnaseq-clustering
description: Use when starting from raw 10x scRNA-seq counts (e.g., Cell Ranger filtered_gene_bc_matrices or an RDS Seurat object) and unsupervised clusters are needed as input for ScType marker-based cell-type annotation or SNV-score assignment.

name: seurat-scrnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g. Tabula Muris thymus) must be normalized, HVG-selected, scaled, and embedded via PCA before trajectory or DEG analysis downstream.

name: seurat-single-cell-analysis
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq counts (e.g., 10x PBMC, bone marrow, MERFISH spatial) must be normalized, clustered, and embedded in Seurat before cell-type annotation with accordion() or accordion_disease().

name: seurat-single-cell-clustering
description: Use when you have two adjusted gene-barcode UMI matrices from paired single-cell processing pipelines and need to compare their cell-clustering outcomes quantitatively via ARI.

name: seurat-single-cell-object-handling
description: Use when running Chord or its built-in detectors (scds, DoubletFinder) on scRNA-seq data: the input must be a Seurat object, and scds additionally requires an sce obtained via creatSCE(seu).

name: seurat-umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO-deposited 10x-style BALF counts) must be reduced to a low-dimensional embedding for clustering and cell-type annotation before severe-vs-mild differential expression testing.

name: seurat-v3-standard-workflow
description: Use when a sparse count matrix of single-nucleus droplets (e.g., 10X mouse brain snRNA-seq) has been pre-filtered by DIEM, EmptyDrops, or a quantile-based hard count cutoff and you need to check for residual background/debris clusters downstream.

name: seurat-wilcoxon-marker-detection
description: Use when computing case-vs-control differential expression per cell cluster from integrated Seurat objects as input to drug repurposing, or when benchmarking DE methods (Wilcoxon vs Limma/DESeq2/edgeR) by downstream AUC.

name: seurat-wnn-multimodal-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a decision-level or ensemble single-cell integration method against a joint-latent-space baseline, especially for RNA plus a second modality (splicing PSI, ADT, ATAC) where modality-specific subclusters are expected.

name: severe-vs-mild-expression-contrast
description: Use when re-analysing processed expression matrices from COVID-19 severity cohorts (e.g. GSE155454, GSE157103) to find genes consistently differentially expressed between severe and mild patients.

name: severe-vs-mild-gene-expression-comparison
description: Use when severe-vs-mill or severe-vs-mild gene expression data from a transcriptomic cohort (e.g. GEO RNAseq matrices) is available and the goal is to test whether a fixed two-gene signature discriminates disease severity, including cross-cohort or cross-pathogen validation.

name: sex-and-age-covariate-adjustment
description: Use when a replicated single-cell dataset is analyzed with Scanpro and donor demographics such as sex or age may confound condition-associated cell-type proportion changes.

name: sex-covariate-batch-adjusted-design-matrix-construction
description: Use when running multi-sample pseudotime differential testing (e.g., lamian_test_h5 with testvar=2) on a multi-sample scRNA-seq atlas where a biological covariate such as sex must be tested while batch/technical variables are adjusted for.

name: sgd-training-hyperparameter-configuration
description: Use when a normalized single-cell gene expression feature matrix (e.g. scanpy HVG .npz) must be embedded into a latent feature space via self-supervised MoCo contrastive training of a DenseNet encoder with SGD.

name: sgrna-knockout-efficiency-evaluation
description: Use when preprocessing Perturb-seq/CROP-seq data before model building and you need to remove cells whose sgRNA-induced knockout failed (20-30% show wild-type phenotype) or perturbations represented by too few cells.

name: shannon-entropy-computation
description: Use when UMI-read clusters (reads sharing a UMI, mapping within ≤3 bp around a modal position) must be characterized for sequence complexity, i.e. per-cluster Shannon Entropy and Mutual Information are needed to test whether low-complexity/tandem-repeat reads predict the mapping shift artefact.

name: shannon-entropy-filtering
description: Use when per-nucleotide structure calls must be derived from RSCanner sliding-window BPC and median Shannon entropy values, e.g. to select low-entropy/high-BPC positions from a CT or dot-bracket structure scan of HCV_Jc1 or any long RNA.

name: shannon-entropy-median-smoothing
description: Use when you have per-nucleotide Shannon entropy values (e.g. from base pairing probabilities) alongside a CT or dot-bracket RNA secondary structure and need a smoothed entropy profile to visualize local structural dynamics.

name: shannon-entropy-percentile-thresholding
description: Use when you have per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values (from a CT or dot-bracket structure plus a shannon.txt file) and need to binarize positions into 'structure counts' using percentile cutoffs before building heatmap/histogram summaries.

name: shannon-index-potency-heterogeneity-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq populations (e.g. hESC vs NPC) must be stratified into discrete potency states and their heterogeneity quantified as a Shannon index, without marker genes or timepoints.

name: shape-change-outlier-sample-coincidence-analysis
description: Use when you have a SCISSOR ScissorOutput object (sample IDs, GSC/LSC outlyingness scores) plus public mutation calls and need to test whether annotated variants like splice site mutations explain detected shape changes, or to audit mutation-call annotation quality.

name: shapley-based-annotation-integration
description: Use when multiple conflicting clustering annotations (e.g., Leiden at resolutions 1/2/3 on RNA and ATAC AnnData objects) must be mix-and-matched into a single stable, biologically coherent cell-population labeling that consensus ensemble methods cannot achieve.

name: shapley-coalitional-annotation-selection
description: Use when a single-cell dataset has two or more conflicting per-cell annotation columns (different clustering algorithms, resolutions, or reference label transfers) that must be reconciled into one definitive per-cell cluster label.

name: shapley-value-feature-attribution
description: Use when a fitted Keras/TensorFlow CLOUDe NN classifier exists and you need model-agnostic per-feature importance (Shapley values) on expression features to identify which genes' features drive class discrimination.

name: shared-cell-type-filtering-across-samples
description: Use when building a 4D-communication tensor from single-cell data spanning multiple samples or contexts and the cell-type annotations differ between samples, so dimensions must match before Tensor-cell2cell decomposition.

name: shared-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when integrating two single-cell modalities (e.g., MERFISH spatial data with matched scRNA-seq) that must be fed a common gene set as input features, or when a shared-encoder integration model requires identical features across datasets.

name: shared-nearest-neighbor-clustering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI counts (e.g., 10x Genomics 68k PBMC) have been embedded into a low-dimensional ZINB-WaVE W matrix and you need cell-population clustering robust to dropouts and over-dispersion.

name: shared-vs-unshared-latent-factor-evaluation
description: Use when you have shared-bio and unshared-bio factor matrices from a disentanglement-test run plus ground-truth cell-type and batch labels, and you must quantify cell-type preservation (ARI) and batch removal (ASW-batch) per factor class.

name: shell-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a scRNA-seq target cell sub-cluster (e.g., AML1_cluster1, 100 cells x 4K genes) must be mapped onto a reference cell atlas via the CCI repository's shell scripts, and a CCI score must be produced.

name: shift-vs-overdispersion-module-classification
description: Use when quantifying gene set activity from a normalized expression matrix and needing to statistically distinguish coordinated-variance (overdispersed) from mean-shift (shifted) pathway activation in omics data.

name: shifted-z-score-calculation
description: Use when permutation test results show a significant colocalization between region sets (e.g., m6A methylation sites and stop codon regions) and you must verify the association peaks exactly at the original region positions rather than being a diffuse positional effect.

name: shiny-gui-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you need to execute methylR locally via its containerized Shiny GUI for Illumina 450K/EPIC array analysis, or when reproducing the paper's downstream modules (DMC plots, GO, KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways enrichment) without writing R code.

name: shiny-interactive-gui-operation
description: Use when a practitioner needs to execute differential methylation analysis and its downstream feature modules (volcano plot, chromosome map, PCA/MDS, gene ontology, pathway enrichment) through an interactive GUI rather than writing R code.

name: shiny-interactive-plot-rendering
description: Use when a bioinformatics pipeline needs a browser-based interactive figure (e.g. GO enrichment plots, volcano plots, chromosome maps) with tunable parameters, produced from a Shiny app served via Docker.

name: shm-mutation-enumeration-in-ighv
description: Use when a de novo assembled Ig transcript (FASTA) needs its top germline IGHV gene, percent identity, SHM count, and mutated/unmutated (mCLL/uCLL) call determined from RNA-seq data.

name: short-edge-gap-closing
description: Use when assembling isoforms from barcoded RNA-seq linked reads (read clouds per barcode) and a per-barcode subgraph contains short low-coverage edges interrupting otherwise continuous isoform paths.

name: short-read-alignment-of-cdna-inserts
description: Use when raw FASTQ files from droplet scRNA-seq (e.g. SRA SRP073767, 2x75 paired-end NextSeq500 output) must be converted into per-cell gene counts and Read1 must first be placed on a reference genome.

name: short-read-alignment-to-barcode-reference
description: Use when barcode-bearing reads have been extracted and trimmed and must be assigned to a known synthetic barcode reference library (e.g. SPLINTR barcodes in FASTA) to produce per-barcode alignment counts.

name: short-read-reference-alignment
description: Use when raw tumor-normal WES/WGS FASTQ reads have been adapter-trimmed and must be aligned to a human reference genome to produce BAM files for downstream somatic SNV/INDEL calling.

name: shuffled-data-null-false-discovery-control
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (e.g., LCMV1/LCMV2 10X CD44+ T cell matrices with selected PCs) and you must pick a clustering resolution without over-discovering spurious clusters.

name: siamese-network-architecture-construction
description: Use when implementing or reproducing ivis's dimensionality-reduction model, i.e. when a scalable neural embedding that preserves local (KNN) and global structure must be trained with a triplet loss on high-dimensional single-cell or general tabular data.

name: siamese-network-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when visualizing or embedding high-dimensional single-cell expression data (CyTOF/scRNA-seq matrices) while needing to preserve global inter-cluster distances, or when new cells must be mapped into an existing embedding.

name: signal-robustness-perturbation-testing
description: Use when an RMT-based noise-filtering pass (e.g., on ZhengMix PBMC or similar sparse scRNA-seq data) has flagged candidate signal dimensions and you need a data-driven threshold to keep only robust, biologically meaningful signals before UMAP embedding.

name: signaling-family-network-subdivision
description: Use when a filtered ligand-receptor connectome (e.g. from CreateConnectome + FilterConnectome) must be broken down by signaling family to identify which cell types dominate production or reception of specific modes such as PDGF, EGF, CSF/chemokine, or VEGF/ANGPT signaling.

name: signaling-hub-centrality-analysis
description: Use when a CellChat communication network has been computed (significant L-R pairs at p<0.05) and you need to rank cell groups as dominant senders/receivers/mediators/influencers or pinpoint the hub cell state.

name: signaling-pathway-network-simulation
description: Use when scRNA-seq-derived Boolean regulatory rules exist for a pathway topology (GRAPHML or KEGG) and the goal is to map individual cells to characteristic signaling states (attractors) of that pathway.

name: signalling-entropy-potency-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq profiles must be ordered by differentiation potency without markers or timepoints — e.g. snapshot data of complex tissues, high-dropout datasets, or identifying cancer stem-cell/drug-resistant phenotypes.

name: signalling-entropy-vs-connectome-agreement-analysis
description: Use when you have single-cell expression data with SCENT signalling entropy (SR) values and want to test or use the CCAT connectome-correlation score as a fast proxy for SR/differentiation potency.

name: signature-autocorrelation-report-rendering
description: Use when a completed VISION/PhyloVision analysis object is available and the goal is to deliver or share results as an interactive web report, locally or on a remote server.

name: signature-classification-accuracy-validation
description: Use when a predicted cell type-specific signature from single-cell RNA-Seq data (e.g., SINCERA signature.prediction output) must be validated for its ability to separate cells of the given type from all other types before export or reuse.

name: signature-matrix-construction-from-marker-genes
description: Use when you have a curated marker gene set (e.g., from G-PC/phenotype-cover, RankCorr, or scGeneFit) plus a scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels, and you need to assess how well those markers support deconvolution of bulk or pseudo-bulk mixtures.

name: signature-presence-calling-from-nonzero-ci
description: Use when fitting reference mutational signatures to individual cancer samples (especially hematological malignancies with low-burden or overlapping processes like SBS9/AID) and you need a specific presence/absence call rather than a point estimate.

name: signature-score-differential-t-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from tumor immune microenvironment samples has been scored for MetaTiME MeC signatures and the goal is to compare per-cell-state-cluster signature activity across two condition groups (pre/post treatment, responder/non-responder).

name: signature-score-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (expression matrix plus spot coordinates) should be scanned for spatially clustered TME gene signatures — e.g. detecting TLSs or tumor capsules — in R with scCancer2.

name: signature-set-construction
description: Use when you need to define a new cell-type or process gene signature (curated marker gene list) or extend an existing signature set so it can be scored per cell with UCell, including over pre-calculated rankings.

name: signed-power-deflation-transform
description: Use when scRNAseq count data are overdispersed relative to Poisson expectations and you need to deflate a CA chi-squared residual matrix (Pearson or Freeman-Tukey) before SVD in a corral preprocessing stage.

name: silent-gene-identification-across-subtypes
description: Use when a batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression matrix has multiple labeled subtypes and the goal is to flag genes that are silent specifically in one subtype (SDG) rather than subtype-enriched marker genes.

name: silhouette-ari-purity-metric-computation
description: Use when benchmarking cell embeddings from paired multi-omics integration methods and you need comparable embedding (silhouette) and clustering (purity, ARI) scores across methods and datasets.

name: silhouette-based-cluster-heterogeneity-evaluation
description: Use when a Seurat object has broad Louvain clusters that may mask rare cell types, and you need a quantitative criterion (per-cell silhouette score distributions) to decide which clusters are heterogeneous enough to recluster.

name: silhouette-based-cluster-number-selection
description: Use when performing unsupervised clustering of single-cell expression data and you need a quantitative, unbiased criterion (silhouette score) to pick K instead of fixing cluster resolution ad hoc.

name: silhouette-based-clustering-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction or batch-integration methods for scRNA-seq (e.g., corralm vs PCA vs Seurat on multi-batch data) and you need a quantitative cell-type-preservation vs batch-mixing trade-off metric on cell embeddings.

name: silhouette-based-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g., Bfimpute vs scImpute/DrImpute/PBLR outputs) on datasets with known cell type labels and you need silhouette-based clustering quality metrics.

name: silhouette-based-clustering-validation
description: Use when you need to quantify whether an engineered/derived cell feature representation (e.g., Spearman or Pearson correlation, cosine, Euclidean, autoencoder features) improves consistency with known cell-type labels in scRNA-seq data.

name: silhouette-cluster-quality-assessment
description: Use when comparing two clusterings of the same scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 5% vs 10% cell subsamples processed by SCC or SSCC) and you need a numeric measure of clustering consistency and per-cell cluster quality.

name: silhouette-cluster-separability-evaluation
description: Use when you have annotated single-cell expression matrices (e.g. Jurkat-293T with CD3D/XIST marker annotations, Zeisel with nine major classes) in raw vs. imputed versions and need to assess whether imputation improves cell-type subpopulation separability.

name: silhouette-cluster-separation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing single-cell denoising or feature-selection methods and a ground-truth cell-phenotype labeling exists, so cluster separation can be quantified as mean silhouette score per method and latent dimension.

name: silhouette-cluster-separation-evaluation
description: Use when comparing manifold projection methods (topoAE, VAE, AE, UMAP) on single-cell modalities and you need a class-separation metric for each low-dimensional embedding, alongside KL0.01/KL0.1/KL1 density scores.

name: silhouette-cluster-separation-metric
description: Use when running hsslda::runHSS feature selection on single-cell marker data (e.g., CyTOF metabolic markers) and you want subset scoring based on cluster cohesion vs. separation of a priori class labels rather than euclidean distance.

name: silhouette-clustering-agreement-scoring
description: Use when simulated scRNA-seq data (e.g. Splatter two- or six-group, 200 genes, 2000 cells, with dropout) has ground-truth celltype labels and you must numerically judge whether a denoiser (DCA ZINB vs MSE autoencoder) recovers celltype structure.

name: silhouette-coefficient-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when comparing two cell embeddings (e.g., OnClass pred_Y_all score-PCA vs Scanorama-integrated expression) on labeled scRNA-seq data and you need a per-dataset, statistically testable measure of cluster separation by cell type.

name: silhouette-coefficient-computation
description: Use when you have 2D UMAP coordinates plus cell-type labels from gene-annotation-based KNN/Seurat clustering and want to test whether an alternative feature space (e.g., uTAR reads outside gene annotations) clusters cell types comparably to annotated gene expression.

name: silhouette-coefficient-computation
description: Use when benchmarking batch-effect correction methods on scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and you need an unsupervised measure of corrected-data separation quality beyond adjusted Rand index.

name: silhouette-coefficient-computation
description: Use when scRNA-seq clustering output must be validated against known cell-type labels, or when testing whether engineered features (e.g., Spearman-correlation features from sscClust) remain consistent across subsampling rates.

name: silhouette-coefficient-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a cluster-purity or clustering-quality metric (e.g., ROGUE) against silhouette coefficients on simulated or real scRNA-seq populations, especially to test robustness to sequencing-depth or cell-number differences.

name: silhouette-evaluation-of-embeddings
description: Use when comparing 2D embeddings of scRNA-seq data for rare cell type separation, where a silhouette index computed over 100+ replicated runs (e.g., EDGE mean 0.851 vs UMAP 0.801 vs t-SNE 0.838 on PBMC) is needed as an objective metric.

name: silhouette-index-cluster-evaluation
description: Use when comparing 2D embeddings (e.g., EDGE, t-SNE, UMAP) of labeled single-cell RNA-seq data and you need a quantitative, replication-averaged measure of how compactly and separately each cell type is projected.

name: silhouette-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction or visualization methods for scRNA-seq data and you need a label-referenced metric of cell-type separation for each 2D embedding.

name: silhouette-index-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq feature selection or clustering method and you need a label-based quantitative score of cluster separation across feature set sizes (e.g., 50-4000 genes).

name: silhouette-score-cell-type-evaluation
description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction or VAE embeddings of scRNA-seq data with known cell-type labels and you need a quantitative, per-method separation metric to supplement visual checks for crowding or overlap.

name: silhouette-score-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare clustering performance of DR methods (e.g., scLENS vs Seurat/Scanpy PCs) on single-cell datasets with known ground-truth labels across varying sparsity or TGC variability.

name: silhouette-score-computation
description: Use when comparing cross-platform scRNA-seq integration quality — e.g. after Seurat integration of platform-specific gene-by-barcode matrices (GBMs) with a reference GBM — by scoring cluster separation alongside kBET.

name: silhouette-score-distance-matrix-validation
description: Use when a patient/specimen-level distance matrix (Wasserstein/EMD between cell-cluster distributions) has been computed and you need an unsupervised quality metric of that matrix, or when benchmarking distance methods with ARI/Silhouette/AUCPR/Spearman metrics.

name: silhouette-score-embedding-assessment
description: Use when a joint embedding of annotated scRNA-seq and unlabeled scATAC-seq cells (e.g., scBridge output or a corrupted/downsampled source run) needs a quantitative embedding-quality metric alongside label transfer accuracy.

name: silhouette-score-evaluation
description: Use when a Seurat/SCISSORS clustering must be assessed for heterogeneity, when comparing clusterings across methods with violin plots of per-cell silhouettes, or when deciding which broad clusters to recluster for rare subpopulations.

name: silhouette-score-evaluation-of-cell-type-clustering
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq integration/annotation pipelines (e.g., 16 MASI variants of raw vs. PlinerScore matrices, marker vs. HVG features) and you need a numeric, statistically testable measure of whether cell-type structure is resolved.

name: silhouette-score-heterogeneity-assessment
description: Use when you have preprocessed bulk RNA-seq data for a cohort (e.g., < 100 samples) and need to decide how many representative clusters exist so that all representatives can be selected in one batch instead of multi-round active learning.

name: silhouette-significance-testing
description: Use when validating joint clustering/embedding of paired scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq against surrogate ground truth labels from bulk data, e.g. comparing CoupledNMF joint t-SNE to Cell Ranger or Seurat V3 label transfer via silhouette index.

name: silhouette-width-batch-mixing-analysis
description: Use when comparing imputation/denoising methods on multi-batch scRNA-Seq data to quantify batch-effect removal while confirming cell-type separation, e.g., merging batches of the same cell type.

name: silhouette-width-celltype-assessment
description: Use when evaluating a batch-corrected/embedded Seurat object (e.g. STACAS output) to determine whether cell type structure survives integration, or when demonstrating that batch-mixing metrics like iLISI reward overcorrected embeddings.

name: silhouette-width-cluster-label-validation
description: Use when you have external cluster labels (e.g., from a different modality or a GMM fit) and need to quantify how well-separated those clusters are in an expression matrix, such as testing whether denoising recovers structure lost to dropout.

name: silhouette-width-cluster-separation-analysis
description: Use when you need to validate that a learned feature space (e.g. ANN deep features) yields more compact within-group and better separated between-group clusters than a baseline feature space on the same labeled samples.

name: silhouette-width-cluster-separation-assessment
description: Use when comparing low-dimensional representations (e.g., PCA vs ZIFA vs ZINB-WaVE) of scRNA-seq data for a fixed set of known cell-type labels, and you need a single cluster-separation score per embedding.

name: silhouette-width-evaluation
description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq clustering has produced per-cell cluster memberships (e.g., the mem output of BAMM-SC) and you must report cluster tightness as average silhouette width, and cluster stability as APN under gene-perturbation reruns, to compare against competing methods.

name: silhouette-width-metric-computation
description: Use when evaluating single-cell integration embeddings (e.g. stored in adata.obsm['delta']) for whether cell-type structure is preserved (ASW) and whether batches are over- or under-corrected (ASW-beta).

name: silverman-rule-bandwidth-selection
description: Use when smoothing nx1 pseudotime and nx1 marker-signal vectors from n single cells into a joint density (e.g., via jointDensityPseudotimeY.m for MAPiT) and Gaussian kernel bandwidths must be set per dimension.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: simhash-fingerprint-grouping
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq reads (BAM/FASTA) have been converted to a sparse k-mer matrix and cell features must be compressed, reference-free, into CKG groups before classification.

name: similarity-learning-pipeline-execution
description: Use when the goal is to cluster pre-annotated or simulated scRNA-seq count matrices (gene-by-cell) by learning an enhanced cell-to-cell similarity matrix and to benchmark the clusterings with NMI/ARI against competing methods.

name: similarity-matrix-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when you have learned decomposition patterns (e.g., ACTIONet archetypes or cNMF usage matrices) and need to quantitatively compare them against labeled bulk reference profiles via a correlation similarity matrix.

name: similarity-matrix-construction
description: Use when multiple candidate subnetworks/modules have been recovered from the same benchmark data (seed genes or gene P-values) and you need a quantitative, pairwise overlap assessment across methods, e.g. Jaccard index on node sets assembled into a 7x7 matrix.

name: similarity-network-fusion
description: Use when multiple low-dimensional latent matrices of single-cell data are available and a single robust cell-cluster assignment must be derived by fusing per-representation cell-similarity networks.

name: similarity-network-fusion
description: Use when multiple gene co-expression networks per condition (e.g., Euclidean-distance and Pearson-correlation networks) must be combined into a single fused network per cancer type using SNF.

name: similarity-weighted-term-sampling
description: Use when constructing a synthetic pathway-enrichment benchmark where a known set of dysregulated/true-positive terms must be chosen with controlled functional redundancy, given a pathway-term dataframe and a similarity matrix.

name: simpleaf-cli-configuration
description: Use when you need to run alevin-fry-based single-cell preprocessing through simpleaf's CLI — e.g. configuring ALEVIN_FRY_HOME, setting executable paths, or building a splici/spliceu reference index from genome FASTA + GTF.

name: simplex-visualization-of-mixture-weights
description: Use when gene-level scBASE mixture weights (πg·s proportions of the seven ASE pattern classes P, B, M, PB, BM, MP, PBM) must be plotted per developmental stage, e.g. to show a gene's trajectory from maternal monoallelic to bi-allelic expression.

name: simulated-atac-seq-read-length-benchmarking
description: Use when validating or benchmarking ecDNA breakpoint reconstruction from ATAC-Seq under controlled read lengths/depths, or when reproducing the paper's robustness claim (F1 = 0.93 at 30× local depth with reads as short as 35 bp).

name: simulated-benchmark-validation
description: Use when validating that a trajectory-suitability or trajectory-detection step correctly discriminates between simulated scRNA-seq datasets with no true trajectory (homogeneous cells or disconnected clusters) and datasets with a known trajectory signal.

name: simulated-bulk-expression-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type decomposition robustness under simulated gene-specific bias between bulk RNA-seq and a snRNA-seq reference, e.g. to quantify how R and RMSD degrade as bias variance sigma increases.

name: simulated-bulk-mixture-generation
description: Use when benchmarking deconvolution or cell-type proportion estimation and you need synthetic bulk profiles with known true mixing proportions, e.g., 100 random mixtures over the five GSE28490 cell types.

name: simulated-cell-mixture-dilution
description: Use when a labeled two-population scRNA-seq mixture is available and you need a controlled simulation of rare-population abundance (e.g. 0.5–5%) to benchmark rare-cell detection tools with F1 scores.

name: simulated-cite-seq-data-generation
description: Use when you need synthetic CITE-seq ADT data with known cluster-level variation structure to evaluate how a purity metric or clustering parameter (e.g., LinQ-View's rank parameter) behaves as the number of surface-protein features changes.

name: simulated-data-cluster-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing TE-expression quantification tools against known ground-truth labels using simulated single-cell data, specifically to test whether expected cell clusters are recovered from gene/TE expression matrices.

name: simulated-data-quality-evaluation
description: Use when a .pth-trained GRouNdGAN checkpoint has produced simulated.h5ad cells and you must verify resemblance to held-out experimental cells (e.g., PBMC-CTL, Dahlin, Tumor-ALL) via cosine, Euclidean, MMD, RF AUROC, and miLISI metrics.

name: simulated-dataset-dimension-validation
description: Use when regenerating or receiving simulated scRNA-seq datasets for benchmarking (Splatter/PROSSTT output) and you must confirm each file is a valid CSV/h5ad count matrix at the canonical 2000×5000 dimension.

name: simulated-doublet-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking HTO-based demultiplexing methods against a known ground truth is needed — e.g. the input is a cell line mixture experiment with HTO and RNA count matrices and you must simulate weak HTO signal and known multiplets.

name: simulated-doublet-training-set-labeling
description: Use when fitting an ensemble doublet classifier (Chord GBM/AdaBoost) that requires labeled training data built from simulated doublets scored by existing detection tools rather than experimental ground truth.

name: simulated-dropout-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating how marker-based annotators behave when a cell type's marker signatures are deleted from a ScTypeDB-format marker database, and you must score which methods correctly report Unknown versus misassigning the perturbed type.

name: simulated-fusion-read-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing fusion gene detection sensitivity across tools on simulated paired-end RNA-seq reads, especially to establish minimum detection coverage for specific fusion genes like BCR-ABL1 or CIC-DUX4.

name: simulated-gene-expression-data-generation
description: Use when a controlled ground truth is needed to compare subnetwork detection methods: generate simulated case/control expression data with a known planted perturbed module inside a reference network.

name: simulated-gene-network-topology-generation
description: Use when benchmarking gene co-expression network methods (scLink, glasso, glasso-r, glasso-f) against ground truth: single-cell count data must be simulated over a power-law or hub-based topology to provide known true edges for AUPRC/AUROC evaluation.

name: simulated-ground-truth-label-comparison
description: Use when a clustering or cell-identification method must be benchmarked on simulated scRNA-seq data where the true cell-type assignments are known by construction, e.g. reproducing scDHA's ARI 0.949 result on six simulated cell types.

name: simulated-mixed-profile-generation
description: Use when a cell-type deconvolution model needs supervised training data but no ground-truth spatial compositions exist, and a single-cell RNA-seq reference with cell type annotations is available.

name: simulated-mutation-catalog-generation
description: Use when you need catalogs of known ground-truth signature composition (e.g., dilution series of SBS2 1–10% or SBS-MM1 1–20% into an average MM background) to benchmark signature fitting or bootstrap CI coverage.

name: simulated-omics-data-generation
description: Use when a scalability or performance benchmark of decoupleR's activity-inference methods is needed and a controlled synthetic omics matrix must be produced instead of real perturbation data.

name: simulated-randomers-training-data-augmentation
description: Use when building training datasets for ONT dRNA basecalling/anomaly models from public or IVT data of questionable quality, and inference artefacts or 'hallucinations' from near-identical modified structures must be mitigated before training NanoListener/IsolationForest models.

name: simulated-read-background-splicing
description: Use when benchmarking a fusion-gene detection tool and you need test FASTQs containing known fusion junctions at controlled expression/coverage levels embedded in realistic sequencing background.

name: simulated-read-benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Use when comparing transcriptome assemblers on complex multi-isoform genes (e.g., GYPC, MAPT, BIN1) from simulated barcoded RNA-seq reads, and you need per-gene full-length isoform recovery counts to rank standard bulk assemblers vs barcode-aware methods.

name: simulated-read-demultiplexing-benchmark
description: Use when benchmarking or reimplementing barcode demultiplexing on simulated long-read FASTQ data, or when the analysis goal is to verify that a demultiplexer reproduces Flexiplex's unique--match assignment behaviour and reported accuracy.

name: simulated-read-truth-evaluation
description: Use when comparing barcode demultiplexing tools on simulated single-cell long-read data where ground-truth read-barcode labels and a true barcode whitelist are available, and accuracy/FDR must be scored per edit-distance setting.

name: simulated-rnaseq-labelled-data-preparation
description: Use when a supervised combination of DEG detection methods is needed and no labelled RNA-seq data exist, requiring simulated spike-in/training data with known DEG truth labels.

name: simulated-rnaseq-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing IPA-detection tools on RNA-seq data with no matched 3'-end-seq or Iso-seq ground truth, or when assessing how sequencing depth (10X–50X) affects identification accuracy and PAU quantification error.

name: simulated-rnaseq-truth-label-comparison
description: Use when you need to evaluate or tune how multiple DEG detection methods (DESeq2, NOISeq, limma) are combined, by comparing vote-threshold or combined-FDR calls against simulated RNA-seq data with known truth labels.

name: simulated-scrna-seq-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing cell-embedding methods (e.g., scGAE vs scDeepCluster, DCA, scVI, Ivis, SAUCIE, scGNN, ZINB-WaVE, PCA, PHATE) on simulated scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cluster labels are available and clustering quality must be quantified by NMI.

name: simulated-scrna-seq-clustering-benchmark
description: Use when a simulated single-cell gene expression matrix must be clustered without a pre-specified cluster count, and cluster-merging behavior must be traced against the d_bar/2 adaptive stopping criterion.

name: simulated-scrna-seq-count-matrix-generation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-type annotation tools requires scRNA-seq datasets with known ground-truth labels (e.g. simulated PBMC count matrices at varying cell counts) so per-cell annotation accuracy can be computed without manual curation.

name: simulated-scrna-seq-quality-evaluation
description: Use when you have simulated scRNA-seq cells (e.g., simulated.h5ad from GRouNdGAN --generate) and must verify they are realistic and non-collapsed — especially on heterogeneous multi-cell-type references like PBMC-All.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-benchmark-data-handling
description: Use when comparing runtime and memory efficiency of scRNA-Seq TE quantification tools (e.g., SoloTE vs scTE) on the same simulated BAM inputs across genome versions such as hg38 and mm10.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when a simulated scRNA-seq AnnData with high-resolution Leiden labels must be used to benchmark enrichment-scoring methods on per-cluster binary classification, or to verify that negative-gene-set-subtraction variants outperform standard scoring.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-cell-type-benchmarking
description: Use when a simulated or pre-labeled scRNA-seq count matrix plus cell-type marker list are available and the goal is to quantitatively rank multiple cell-type identification methods by accuracy and F1-score.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify whether a cell-cell similarity-driven embedding (cMAP) improves clustering of simulated scRNA-seq expression matrices over PCA or Leiden baselines, using adjusted Rand index against ground-truth cell labels.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-count-data-generation
description: Use when you need to benchmark gene/feature-selection methods on synthetic scRNA-seq count data with known informative genes and controlled subpopulation rarity.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-count-generation
description: Use when you need a controlled scRNA-seq simulation fixture (known clusters, target/control gene partition, true labels) to evaluate confounding-effect removal or control-gene-set robustness for scPLS-type methods.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking source-to-target transfer clustering (e.g., NMF dictionary transfer + SC3) requires synthetic count matrices with exact ground-truth labels, or when comparing complete / incomplete / no-overlap source-target cell-type overlap settings.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-ground-truth-matching
description: Use when simulated single-cell expression matrices (with known TE-cell labels and ground-truth log2(FC)) must be scored against a tool's recovered markers, e.g. benchmarking SoloTE vs scTE in Fig 3.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-ground-truth-validation
description: Use when evaluating or comparing clustering methods on scRNA-seq data where simulated ground-truth cluster labels exist, especially to test whether a method resolves rare subpopulations placed close together.

name: simulated-scrnaseq-trajectory-generation
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference or RNA-velocity-based methods against known ground truth, or when replicated simulated datasets (e.g., 785 cells x 600 genes cycle-tree) are needed to quantify pseudotime accuracy.

name: simulated-scseq-cluster-count-evaluation
description: Use when you need to benchmark single-cell clustering methods on data with known ground-truth cell-type labels, especially to test whether a method recovers the correct number of clusters without a predetermined K.

name: simulated-single-cell-expression-data-generation
description: Use when you need controlled-size dense scRNA-seq test data (e.g., 1,000 to 250,000 cells, 10,000 genes) to benchmark query runtimes of AnnSQL, AnnData (backed or in-memory), or Seurat without depending on real atlas files.

name: simulated-spatial-dataset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking the scalability or runtime of a spatial colorization method (e.g., Spaco) and you need controlled synthetic SRT inputs with known cell counts and labels instead of real tissue sections.

name: simulated-st-benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Use when benchmarking cell type deconvolution methods on simulated ST data where ground-truth per-spot cell type proportions are known, or when reproducing SPACEL/Spoint benchmark metrics (PCC/SSIM/RMSE/JSD/AS) on the 32 pseudo-spot datasets.

name: simulated-st-data-validation
description: Use when a deconvolution method for multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data must be quantitatively benchmarked against ground-truth cell-type proportions, especially when a matched scRNA-seq/MERFISH reference is or is not available.

name: simulated-test-data-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking deletion-target classifiers or parameter predictors on simulated expression test sets with known 'Redundant'/'Unique' labels and true OU parameters, or when measuring robustness to added noise.

name: simulated-toy-dataset-generation
description: Use when validating or benchmarking a clustering algorithm (e.g. KMD linkage) against known structure: you need reproducible synthetic datasets with controllable cluster shapes before testing on real biological data.

name: simulated-umi-subsampling-dropout-benchmarking
description: Use when quantifying how accurately a gene-expression imputation or dropout-correction method recovers spatial expression of marker genes from deliberately degraded (subsampled-UMI) ST data against a known ground truth.

name: simulated-visium-spot-analysis
description: Use when evaluating cell type identification accuracy on simulated multi-slice Visium spots where ground-truth per-cell labels exist and you need to test whether joint analysis of all slices outperforms per-slice analysis.

name: simulated-vs-experimental-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when you have a trained generative scRNA-seq simulator's output (.h5ad) plus the original reference dataset and need to verify that developmental trajectories, transitional states, and pseudotime ordering were preserved before downstream use.

name: simulation-based-benchmark-evaluation-scrnaseq
description: Use when benchmarking an scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising method (e.g. AutoClass vs DCA) against a known ground truth, or when testing robustness to hyperparameters such as bottleneck size, pre-clustering number K, or classifier weight.

name: simulation-based-cna-caller-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare precision and sensitivity of single-cell CNA callers against simulated ground-truth events (200 kb–5 Mb single-copy losses/gains) on high-coverage scWGS benchmark data.

name: simulation-based-de-power-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating or comparing DE method power on single-cell RNA-seq data where simulated ground truth (known DE genes, coverage rate, tau1/tau0 parameters) is available, or when reproducing iDEA power-gain results.

name: simulation-based-estimation-error-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a scalable algorithmic variant (e.g. chunked E-step with Chunk=TRUE, chunk.size=500 or 1000) reproduces the accuracy of a reference implementation while reducing runtime, or when benchmarking confounding-factor inference on simulated scRNAseq grids.

name: simulation-based-gene-recovery-validation
description: Use when you need to verify that a Bayesian-FDR intrinsic/differential gene selection procedure recovers known true DE genes in simulation and yields biologically interpretable enriched pathways on real data.

name: simulation-based-grn-method-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-specific network inference methods (e.g. LIONESS with Pearson, SSN, pySCENIC) and synthetic ground truth is required because real single-cell data lacks a known regulatory network reference.

name: simulation-based-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing cell-type deconvolution or clustering methods on spatial transcriptomics data where ground truth is unavailable in real tissue, by simulating multi-cellular pixels with known cell-type proportions and evaluating RMSE of estimated proportions.

name: simulation-based-method-comparison
description: Use when you need to rank or validate differential abundance testing methods against ground truth on synthetic compositional count data, e.g. at low replicate numbers where FDR control is critical.

name: simulation-based-method-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a CNA caller's sensitivity/precision across variant sizes and coverages, or choosing bin size and depth for scWGS analysis using simulated data with known truth events.

name: simulation-based-method-validation-against-ground-truth
description: Use when a new distance-estimation or differential-state method must be checked for accuracy and calibration: simulated data with known per-cell-type true distances are available or can be generated (here via scDist::simData with nct=10, N1=N2=5).

name: simulation-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when evaluating a circRNA full-length assembly/quantification tool against simulated paired-end FASTQ reads with known ground-truth circular isoforms, to characterize how sequencing depth or read length affects assembly sensitivity, precision, and F1.

name: simulation-benchmark-stratification
description: Use when evaluating assembly/quantification accuracy on simulated data where performance may depend on structural complexity (e.g., overlapping genomic regions among circRNAs), requiring metrics stratified by a complexity bin such as RI 1-4 vs RI > 4.

name: simulation-condition-grid-configuration
description: Use when you need controlled simulated scRNA-seq benchmarks to quantify how varying batch-effect and cell-type effect strengths (plus balanced vs unbalanced cell-type proportions) affect batch-correction tool performance.

name: simulation-noise-parameter-tuning
description: Use when benchmarking enrichment methods (pareg, MGSA, FET, topGO, blitzGSEA) on simulated differential-expression studies where robustness to noise must be quantified at a fixed recall target.

name: simulation-parameter-estimation
description: Use when you need sensitivity benchmarks for a pathway or gene-set method on synthetic scRNA-seq data with a known implanted target pathway, and ground-truth recovery can be scored per scenario.

name: simulation-parameter-fitting-from-umi-counts
description: Use when benchmarking normalization or differential-expression methods on scRNA-seq requires simulated datasets with known ground-truth logFC whose mean/variance/library-size structure matches real UMI count data.

name: simulation-parameter-fitting-to-real-data
description: Use when a simulation must be calibrated to a specific real scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Zeisel UMI cortex counts) so downstream benchmarks or experimental-design curves reflect realistic depth, dropout, and variability.

name: simulation-parameter-series-design
description: Use when benchmarking a circRNA assembly or isoform-quantification method against known ground truth, or when validating that regenerated simulation datasets match a published design (depths, read lengths, loci, conditions).

name: simulation-parameter-sweep
description: Use when benchmarking a method whose performance may depend on simulation settings (e.g. differential-expression level, rarity of a cell population) and multiple synthetic datasets with ground-truth labels are needed across a parameter grid.

name: simulation-parameter-sweep
description: Use when benchmarking lineage reconstruction quality against simulation parameters, e.g., sweeping mutation rate or dropout settings on TedSim-simulated barcode data with a known ground-truth tree.

name: simulation-parameter-sweep-analysis
description: Use when validating a perturbation-effect estimator on synthetic scCRISPR-seq benchmarks: construct two-cluster data with known cluster proportions and per-gRNA responses, sweep bias-generating parameters (d, r), run many seeded replicates, and score estimation loss.

name: simulation-parameter-sweep-design
description: Use when benchmarking community detection (or similar inference) methods on simulated multi-subject dynamic networks and you need to isolate the effect of information-sharing levels (r_subject, r_time) and time horizon T on accuracy.

name: simulation-reference-dataset-comparison
description: Use when simulated single-cell count data (e.g. from dyngen's SSA simulation) must be shown to match the technical characteristics of a real transcript-count dataset before using it for benchmarking.

name: simulation-replicate-method-concordance
description: Use when you have DS analysis result tables from multiple differential methods (e.g., pbDS/edgeR/limma vs. mmDS) run over simulation replicates per DS category, and need to quantify and visualize which genes are jointly vs. uniquely detected at FDR < 0.05.

name: simulation-scenario-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) analysis methods and you need synthetic multi-sample scRNA-seq data whose properties are anchored to a real reference SingleCellExperiment.

name: simulation-scenario-parameterization
description: Use when validating that a TWAS or gene-based test controls type I error before applying it to real GWAS data, or when designing simulation grids over p_causal and h_e2 for null or power calibrations.

name: sine-profile-dynamics-parameter-optimization
description: Use when fitting gene dynamics models from scRNA-seq expression data lacking splicing information, by optimizing sine-profile kinetic parameters per target gene via a generalized EM algorithm over TF weights and latent times.

name: single-cell-4i-data-preprocessing
description: Use when a preprocessed 4i/protein imaging single-cell dataset (.h5ad, e.g. RPE 2759 cells x 241 imaging-derived features) must be loaded and subsampled into representative neighborhoods before feature-module discovery.

name: single-cell-active-learning-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking how many cells must be manually annotated to reach high annotation F1, comparing active learning classifiers/search strategies, or testing whether unlabeled novel cell types are flagged by predictive entropy.

name: single-cell-aggregation-consistency-checking
description: Use when verifying that a database-side aggregation of single-cell expression data (e.g. per gene and cell type averages from a sparse PostgreSQL table) matches values computed directly from the original AnnData (H5AD) expression matrix.

name: single-cell-allelic-count-processing
description: Use when scRNA-Seq reads from a CAST×B6-style F1 hybrid must be converted into maternal/paternal allelic count matrices (e.g., 122 blastocyst cells, 8,290 genes) that feed bursting or ASE-state models, and multi-mapping reads would otherwise be discarded.

name: single-cell-alternative-splicing-event-identification
description: Use when input is single-cell SMART-seq BAM (or junction/SJ.out.tab) files and the goal is an unsupervised, annotation-free AS-based view of cell identity that gene-expression clustering misses.

name: single-cell-annotation-benchmark-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or extending the active learning benchmark for single-cell cell type annotation, specifically comparing RF vs LR classifiers with random initial 20-cell training selection.

name: single-cell-annotation-metadata-parsing
description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix must be paired with a cell-label metafile so that expression can be aggregated per cell type prior to cell-to-cell communication analysis.

name: single-cell-annotation-scoring
description: Use when you have reference data with cell-type labels ('cell_type' column in AnnData) and need to annotate a query single-cell dataset by scoring cells against ranked marker genes rather than training a model.

name: single-cell-annotation-stabilization
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object has root-node cell-type predictions from a Census pretrained model and noisy per-cell labels need to be stabilized using UMAP clusters and prediction contours before continuing hierarchical annotation.

name: single-cell-annotation-tool-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how accurately established cell-annotation tools (e.g. ACTINN, SingleR, SCSA) classify tumor T/NK or myeloid scRNA-seq cell subtypes relative to scWizard on independent datasets.

name: single-cell-annotation-transfer
description: Use when a newly generated scRNA-seq query dataset must be labeled by transferring annotations from a curated reference AnnData, and interpretable per-cell attention (e.g., TF-regulon tokens for trajectory analysis) is desired.

name: single-cell-apd-dynamics-interpretation
description: Use when a PACdataset of single-cell poly(A) sites (e.g. from Sierra or scAPAtrap) exists and the goal is to interpret APA dynamics — 3'UTR shortening, differential pA usage, or APA markers — across cell types or biological stages.

name: single-cell-as-probability-matrix-imputation
description: Use when a single-cell AS probability matrix (rows = AS sites, columns = cells) produced from junction reads contains NA entries from dropouts and an imputed, NA-indicator-annotated matrix is needed before unsupervised clustering.

name: single-cell-atac-peak-frequency-filtering
description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (cells × peaks, AnnData with peaks as n_vars) must be normalized and denoised before feeding a variational autoencoder or cross-modality translation model.

name: single-cell-atac-tf-activity-estimation
description: Use when a single-cell ATAC-seq peak matrix (e.g. from a paired multiome Seurat object such as coembed.trajectory.rds) must be converted into per-cell TF activity scores to prioritize candidate TFs for enhancer-based GRN inference.

name: single-cell-autoencoder-latent-space-training
description: Use when you need to functionally mine scRNAseq clusters with a knowledge-biased autoencoder: you have a filtered, log10-transformed counts table plus reference cluster assignments and want per-cluster reconstruction quality (QCC/QCM) and TF signatures.

name: single-cell-barcode-deconvolution
description: Use when starting a single-cell long-read analysis: you have packaged FASTQ files from PacBio or ONT runs plus a barcode-to-celltype assignment file (e.g. from Seurat on the paired 10x v2 short-read data), and need barcoded, cell-type-labeled reads.

name: single-cell-barcode-downsampling
description: Use when you need to determine the minimum number of cells from a deconvoluted single-cell cluster that still supports reliable genetic identification, e.g. testing identification sensitivity on 10X barcodes_reduced.txt files.

name: single-cell-barcode-extraction
description: Use when raw paired-end single-cell amplicon FASTQ from an expressed synthetic barcoding experiment must be converted into per-cell lineage barcode annotation and clone-size tables, e.g. to cross-validate an existing pipeline like FateMap.

name: single-cell-barcode-oligo-assignment
description: Use when input is hashed single-cell CITE-seq ADT FASTQ data (I1/R1/R2) and per-cell hashtag oligo UMI counts are needed as input to hashing demultiplexing.

name: single-cell-barcode-pcr-chimera-filtering
description: Use when processing single-cell lineage-barcode reads where PCR chimeras inflate barcodes-per-cell and UMI sequencing errors inflate UMI counts, and an accurate per-cell barcode annotation table is needed.

name: single-cell-barcode-qc-visualization
description: Use when processing single-cell (10x-style) FASTQs containing expressed synthetic lineage barcodes and you need chimeras removed, UMIs error-corrected, cells annotated with barcodes, and QC plots of barcodes per cell.

name: single-cell-barcode-quality-control
description: Use when starting from a raw, unfiltered droplet-based scRNA-seq count matrix (mtx or h5, e.g. neurons_900_raw.h5) and you need to define the P/U barcode sets that EmptyNN requires before training its classifier.

name: single-cell-barcode-table-processing
description: Use when you have barcoded single-cell profiles with a table of unique cell IDs and assigned barcodes, and you want clonal relationships to inform clustering (alpha) or UMAP embeddings (Warp Factor s in 0-10).

name: single-cell-barcode-umi-position-indexing
description: Use when FASTQ reads must be routed into a single-cell preprocessing tool (STARsolo, kb/kallisto bustools) that needs explicit barcode/UMI/cDNA start,end,strand positions, and an assay spec.yaml exists or can be authored.

name: single-cell-batch-correction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing how well batch-effect correction methods mix datasets with overlapping cell types while preserving cell-type resolution, e.g. reproducing Cell BLAST Fig. 2a-style integration benchmarks.

name: single-cell-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when raw read-count matrices from multiple scRNA-seq batches show batch separation (e.g., in t-SNE colored by batch) and the goal is corrected counts plus cell-type clustering without a priori subtype labels.

name: single-cell-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple scRNA-seq protocols or batches must be integrated for clustering, and batch mixing must be quantified (e.g., ASW) against baselines such as DESC, Harmony, MNN, scVI or Scanorama.

name: single-cell-batch-effect-embedding-training
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from multiple batches requires a nonlinear lower-dimensional embedding that explicitly models batch effects for downstream batch-effect assessment metrics like iLISI or kBET.

name: single-cell-batch-effect-integration
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple batches (e.g., pancreas, human immune, lung, heart atlas) must be integrated to remove batch effects while conserving cell types, trajectories, or rare populations.

name: single-cell-batch-effect-quantification
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data span multiple batches (e.g. 10X 3pV1/3pV2/5p, five islet platforms inDrop/Fluidigm C1/Smart-Seq2/CEL-seq/CEL-seq2) and you need rejection-rate and mixing metrics in both PCA and nonlinear embedding space.

name: single-cell-batch-integration
description: Use when two scRNA-seq count matrices from different technologies (e.g., CEL-Seq2 and Smart-Seq2) need batch correction before joint analysis, and cell-type mixing (iLISI), cell-type consistency (cLISI), and local-structure retention (k-RNN) must be quantified.

name: single-cell-batch-integration
description: Use when a paired control/perturbed scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. GSE164240 PMC cells treated with MK-886, or simulated control + simulate.perturb cells) must be clustered so treatment-affected states are resolved across conditions.

name: single-cell-batch-integration-benchmarking
description: Use when quantitatively comparing data-integration methods (Scanorama, scVI, Seurat) against a trajectory-tree-alignment method on paired single-cell datasets, measuring biological variance conservation with the ATC score.

name: single-cell-batch-integration-joint-clustering
description: Use when multi-donor or multi-batch scRNA/snRNA-seq datasets must be integrated for joint clustering, and interpretable gene factors/modules (not just a latent embedding) are needed for cell-type annotation or marker comparison.

name: single-cell-batch-integration-topic-modeling
description: Use when a perturbation single-cell atlas spans multiple sequencing batches with cell states batch-confounded (e.g., wild-type vs Tal1-/- chimeric mouse embryo batches) and PCA-based latent spaces fail to mix batches while preserving cell-type separation.

name: single-cell-batch-mixing-metric-implementation
description: Use when evaluating batch mixing of integrated single-cell RNA-seq datasets with imbalanced cell type proportions, where standard cell type-agnostic iLISI scores are mis and a per-cell-type normalized metric is needed.

name: single-cell-batch-subsampling
description: Use when you need to test whether an integration method's clustering or batch-mixing metrics depend on how many donor batches (or which subsets) are provided as input, e.g., for consensus-PCA-based methods where each sample's initial decomposition depends on the other samples.

name: single-cell-benchmark-dataset-handling
description: Use when a new or adapted scRNAseq method needs objective evaluation against known cell identities: benchmark datasets with published ground-truth labels and ARI-based cluster recovery scoring.

name: single-cell-benchmark-dataset-loading
description: Use when a study needs the Goolam or Yan scRNA-seq matrices (or the MPSSC benchmark .mat sets) with cell/true_labs labels to benchmark similarity learning and clustering methods.

name: single-cell-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when inferred trajectories (e.g. MST-based trajectories from clustered single-cell data) must be scored against known ground-truth topologies from the dynverse Zenodo benchmark deposit (10.5281/zenodo.1443566).

name: single-cell-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell-type classification methods on labeled scRNA-seq datasets: you need a repeated 7:3 train/test benchmark with per-dataset accuracy/balanced-accuracy tables aggregating 50 repeats.

name: single-cell-benchmark-result-reproduction
description: Use when a benchmark table of per-dataset annotation accuracies is available with dataset metadata (cell counts, cell type counts, label distributions) and a reported correlation (e.g., accuracy vs. DKL) must be independently reproduced.

name: single-cell-benchmarking-f1-evaluation
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare a single-cell (scRNA-seq, snRNA-seq, or snATAC-seq gene activity) cell type classifier against established baselines using held-out validation F1 on annotated, pre-split benchmark datasets.

name: single-cell-bisulfite-methylation-quantification
description: Use when single-cell bisulfite methylation matrices must be coupled to an independently recovered single-cell ordering (e.g., reCAT pseudo time-series from paired scRNA-seq) to visualize methylation dynamics along a cyclic biological process.

name: single-cell-boolean-network-rule-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (log2(TPM+1)-style matrix with cell IDs and condition labels) must be converted into executable Boolean models of KEGG (or custom GRAPHML) signaling pathways to prioritize high-impact genes.

name: single-cell-boxplot-significance-annotation
description: Use when you have cell-level group assignments (e.g., DICE-derived primed vs unprimed TACs) plus continuous per-cell scores such as Palantir fate probabilities or chromVAR TF activity, and need boxplots with annotated one-sided Wilcoxon significance.

name: single-cell-branch-probability-extraction
description: Use when a VIA trajectory has been run on single-cell omics data and you need per-cell fate assignments or branch probabilities toward detected terminal states to score lineage/fate resolution against annotations.

name: single-cell-bulk-gep-correlation-matching
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq-derived tumor sub-cluster GEPs plus LINCS L1000 bulk perturbation profiles and need to identify drug combinations killing the maximum number of tumor sub-clusters.

name: single-cell-cancer-signature-module-scoring
description: Use when cells have already received a cancer-type annotation from scATOMIC's terminal layer and you must separate malignant cells from normal cells sharing the same tissue of origin in a tumour biopsy.

name: single-cell-cell-communication-inference
description: Use when the input is time-course or pseudotime-ordered single-cell RNA-seq without definitive cell types (e.g. pre-blastocyst embryos) and the goal is to infer causal ligand-receptor communication and its link to temporal TF programs.

name: single-cell-cell-count-simulation
description: Use when you need to determine how many pseudo-replicates Scanpro's bootstrapping should use for an unreplicated single-cell dataset, given an estimate of total cells per condition.

name: single-cell-cell-cycle-scoring
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., the 145-cell Llorens-Bobadilla neural stem cell data) contains quiescent G0-like cells that standard cell-cycle analysis does not detect and must be removed before pseudotime inference.

name: single-cell-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (Seurat object) needs fully automated cell-type labels, or when cancer datasets need malignant cell identification and cell-of-origin inference, without manual marker curation.

name: single-cell-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a pre-processed, clustered Seurat object from plant single-cell data needs cell-type labels without manual curation, especially when a reference atlas (e.g., PRJNA517021, PRJNA706435) or a marker gene data frame is available.

name: single-cell-cell-type-annotation-transfer
description: Use when raw source scRNA-seq data are unavailable (privacy/storage) but pre-trained source model weights exist, and target data may contain novel cell types requiring source-free annotation.

name: single-cell-cell-type-classification
description: Use when you have raw (unnormalized) single-cell count data (Seurat .rds, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x cellranger output) and annotated cell type labels to train on, or a pretrained Pollock module to assign cell type labels to new cells.

name: single-cell-cell-type-interpretability-scoring
description: Use when you have a trained Pollock VAE classification module (e.g. scRNAseq_brca_panimmune) plus raw-count .h5ad/.RDS cells and need the interpretability scores identifying which genes drive each predicted cell state.

name: single-cell-cell-type-label-transfer
description: Use when a query AnnData needs cell type labels transferred from an annotated reference (e.g. resolving monocyte subtypes in pan-cancer tumor-infiltrating myeloid data), and you want interpretable, pathway-token-based predictions with per-cell probabilities.

name: single-cell-cellstate-label-transfer
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts of T cells (or other cell types with a pre-built reference map) must be annotated with reference-defined cell states, e.g. assigning tumor-specific CD8 TILs to Tex/Tpex/EM states on the murine TIL atlas.

name: single-cell-celltype-annotation-by-correlation
description: Use when you have a 10x 3' gene-cell-barcode count matrix (e.g. from Cell Ranger) and need per-cell type labels by matching expression profiles to reference populations, or to stratify cell types by host/donor genotype.

name: single-cell-classifier-training-caret
description: Use when a single-cell (RNA or CyTOF) expression matrix needs a probabilistic classifier for active learning uncertainty sampling, pseudo-labelling, or entropy-based mislabel detection.

name: single-cell-clonal-genotyping-from-transcriptomes
description: Use when single-cell gene expression data carry linked per-cell mutation calls (GoT) that are noisy (false negatives from shallow sequencing, false positives from ambient RNA) and the goal is to reconcile genotype-based clone labels with transcriptional cell-type annotations.

name: single-cell-clonal-subset-comparison
description: Use when single cells have already been assigned to clones/subclones (e.g., mtDNA subclones clone1.MT0 vs clone1.MT1) and the goal is to test whether those subclones are biologically distinct via DE genes and Hallmark pathway enrichment.

name: single-cell-clone-calling-from-lineage-barcode-data
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data carry integrated lineage barcodes (e.g. CellTag lentiviral captures from 10x Chromium runs) and you must group cells into clones for state-fate or clonal GRN analyses.

name: single-cell-cluster-annotation
description: Use when a preprocessed and clustered Seurat object or count matrix from scRNA-seq or imaging-based spatial data (e.g., MERFISH mouse brain) needs cell type labels per cluster or per cell, and marker-gene-based annotation with interpretable results is desired.

name: single-cell-cluster-annotation
description: Use when a Seurat (or equivalent) single-cell object has been clustered (e.g. 11 BALF clusters from GSE145926) and cluster labels must be assigned to cell types before stratified DE testing.

name: single-cell-cluster-annotation-propagation
description: Use when a clustered scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., a Seurat object like demo_sc_data) lacks cell-type labels and cell-cell communication analysis with scCrossTalk requires a per-cell sc_celltype character vector.

name: single-cell-cluster-assignment-counting
description: Use when evaluating sequence-search or demultiplexing tools on single-cell FASTQ data by measuring how many cells in a known cluster are recovered via their barcodes after matching target sequences such as BCAS4-BCAS3, E1A, or a variant allele.

name: single-cell-cluster-biomarker-ranking
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been clustered into cell subtypes (e.g. CD163-high macrophage clusters identified by scNovel) and you need pathway-level (GO/GSEA) interpretation of condition-dependent differential expression per cluster.

name: single-cell-cluster-connectivity-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset or 2D embedding must be screened before trajectory fitting — e.g., before Slingshot/Monocle3 — to flag disconnected clusters or homogeneous cells with no trajectory signal.

name: single-cell-cluster-count-aggregation
description: Use when starting PILOT-style sample-level analysis: you have a cell-by-cluster annotated .h5ad (e.g. clusters_col 'cell_subtype', sample_col 'sampleID') and need per-sample cluster probability distributions for Wasserstein distance computation.

name: single-cell-cluster-count-validation
description: Use when a published scRNA-seq result specifies an exact cell count and cluster number for a defined cell compartment (e.g., 44,799 T/NK cells in 32 clusters) and the goal is to independently reproduce and check those values in Seurat.

name: single-cell-cluster-count-verification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has been deliberately over-clustered with Leiden at high resolution (e.g. 3.5) and you need to verify how many significantly different clusters remain after Cytocipher merging and whether intermediate cell states were recovered.

name: single-cell-cluster-functional-annotation
description: Use when a clustered scRNAseq counts matrix needs functional annotation — e.g. identifying which TFs, miRNAs, kinases, or immune signatures drive cell clusterization, or extracting minimal COMET marker gene panels (≤4 genes) for specific clusters.

name: single-cell-cluster-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have an AnnData object with predicted cell-cluster labels from a scRNA-seq clustering method and need per-cluster marker genes to annotate cell types against a curated marker database like CellMark.

name: single-cell-cluster-homogeneity-quantification
description: Use when a scDEED-optimized t-SNE/UMAP visualization raises the question of whether a visual cluster is trustworthy or should be divided, and you need a numeric purity score per cluster and per merged cluster combination.

name: single-cell-cluster-interpretation
description: Use when a learned SIMLR similarity matrix (or single-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix with high noise/dropout) must be converted into 2-D/3-D low-dimensional coordinates and scatter plots that reveal subpopulations.

name: single-cell-cluster-label-aggregation
description: Use when you have a latent cell embedding (e.g. from a dual denoising autoencoder) and K basic clusterings with varying k, and need a single consensus partition that is stable across random seeds and cluster counts.

name: single-cell-cluster-label-mapping
description: Use when synthetic single-cell observations must be assigned cluster identities for fidelity evaluation, and ground-truth cluster labels (e.g. from Seurat clustering on UMAP of PBMC4k or Segerstolpe data) exist only for the original cells.

name: single-cell-cluster-label-validation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq clustering method (e.g., SSRE) has produced cell type labels and you need to confirm the labels are biologically meaningful by recovering known marker genes via differential expression testing.

name: single-cell-cluster-level-statistics
description: Use when CITE-seq data with normalized RNA and ADT matrices plus per-cell cluster assignments needs a quantitative per-cluster purity assessment in both transcriptome and surface protein modalities.

name: single-cell-cluster-marker-identification
description: Use when a Seurat/scMiko scRNA-seq object has author- or algorithm-defined cluster labels (e.g. 'sub_cluster') and you need cluster-specific DEGs, or want to benchmark CDI (binary DEG) markers against Wilcoxon markers for specificity.

name: single-cell-cluster-marker-identification
description: Use when a clustered scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., Seurat object with FindClusters-defined clusters) needs cluster-level marker genes to feed downstream annotation tools such as deCS that accept either gene lists or z-scored expression profiles.

name: single-cell-cluster-marker-roc-analysis
description: Use when you have a count matrix plus cluster assignments (e.g., ClonoCluster hybrid clusters across alpha values) and need to quantify marker sensitivity/specificity via AUC or identify reorganization markers (reorg-AUC > 0.80).

name: single-cell-cluster-pooling-and-preparation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data stored as a Seurat object must be converted into pooled, cluster-level transcriptomic profiles (rows = genes, columns = clusters) before predicting miRNA expression with miRSCAPE or a similar trained model.

name: single-cell-cluster-reconstruction-quality-metric-evaluation
description: Use when an scRNAseq or spatial transcriptomics counts table has been clustered (e.g., 9 SIMLR clusters on a Visium breast cancer section) and you need to determine which clusters the SCA autoencoder reconstructs for the majority of cells before downstream functional annotation.

name: single-cell-cluster-specific-network-inference
description: Use when you have a scATAC-seq-derived base GRN edge list plus a scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. Mouse sci-ATAC-seq Atlas with the Biddy et al. 2018 MEF-to-iEP data) and need per-cluster regulatory networks.

name: single-cell-cluster-stability-integration
description: Use when an AnnData object carries ≥2 conflicting cell-cluster annotation columns (e.g. Leiden at different resolutions, Seurat3/Monocle3/ICGS2, cellHarmony label transfers, or RNA/ADT modality labels) and a single high-confidence reconciled assignment is needed.

name: single-cell-cluster-visualization
description: Use when single-cell profiles (e.g. CSV expression matrix plus discrete class labels) must be visualized in 2D while preserving both cluster structure and differentiation pathways, especially when t-SNE/PCA/MDS fail to reveal trajectories.

name: single-cell-clustering-accuracy-evaluation
