description: Use when you need to judge whether a single-cell clustering/joint-embedding method (e.g. CoupledNMF, Cell Ranger, Seurat V3) produces subpopulations consistent with external labels derived from FACS-sorted bulk signatures.

name: single-cell-clustering-across-multiple-individuals
description: Use when clustering raw UMI count matrices from droplet-based scRNA-seq (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium) generated for several individuals or donors, and naive pooling would cause batch effects or Cell Ranger aggregation downsampling would lose information.

name: single-cell-clustering-across-treatments
description: Use when a single-cell perturbation dataset contains control cells plus one or more treatments and you need control-anchored, interpretable cell states — especially when standard integration workflows might erase perturbation-unique responses.

name: single-cell-clustering-algorithm-benchmarking
description: Use when you have precomputed cell embeddings (e.g. SnapCCESS snapshots across ensemble sizes) for multimodal single-cell data and need to compare clustering algorithms against known cell-type labels using ARI and NMI.

name: single-cell-clustering-algorithm-comparison
description: Use when comparing clustering method performance on single-cell (mass cytometry or scRNA-seq) datasets with known cell-type labels, or when testing whether a clustering method stays accurate at large scale via subsampling.

name: single-cell-clustering-and-dam-annotation
description: Use when a combined gene + TE single-cell expression matrix needs clustering, UMAP visualization, and cell-cluster annotation, e.g. identifying DAM clusters in the APP/PS1 AD mouse model via Cst7, Lpl, and Clec7a.

name: single-cell-clustering-based-subsampling
description: Use when a single-cell expression dataset is highly imbalanced and a small, balanced subsample of cells must be chosen for manual labeling, with or without prior marker gene knowledge.

name: single-cell-clustering-benchmark-against-known-cell-types
description: Use when a clustering (or cell-state) assignment on scRNA-seq data must be validated against an external reference cell-type labeling, e.g. marker-derived labels for PBMCs, using ARI/NMI/purity metrics.

name: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a rare-cell or sub-cluster reclustering method against baseline scRNA-seq clusterers on datasets with known or suspected rare populations, e.g. PBMC3k or simulated pancreas data with rare closely placed clusters.

name: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing clustering performance of multiple single-cell (multimodal or single-modal) methods on datasets with known ground-truth cell-type labels, in single-batch or multi-batch settings.

name: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq/multiome data (~10,000-cell PBMC or large-scale MCA) and you need to compare cluster quality (ARI, purity) against baselines or quantify label-confidence filtering gains.

name: single-cell-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing normalization/confounding-removal methods (e.g. scPLS vs RUV, LMM, PCA, scLVM) on scRNA-seq data with known cell labels, and you need ARI-based clustering performance per downstream method.

name: single-cell-clustering-for-parameter-estimation
description: Use when fitting bursting kinetic parameters (kon, koff, s) from scRNA-seq counts with an MCMC/Gibbs sampler that assumes all cells share the same kinetics, and cells must first be divided by clustering.

name: single-cell-clustering-interpretation
description: Use when a trained scMM model's latent dimensions need biological interpretation, e.g. associating multimodal regulatory programs with individual latent dimensions via pseudocell traversal and TF motif enrichment.

name: single-cell-clustering-metric-evaluation
description: Use when translated or imputed single-cell profiles (e.g. scRNA↔scATAC cross-modality predictions) must be scored for preservation of cellular heterogeneity against ground-truth cell-type labels.

name: single-cell-clustering-of-pbmc-transcriptomes
description: Use when a gene-cell-barcode matrix from droplet scRNA-seq (tens of thousands of cells) must be partitioned into cell subpopulations and characterized by cluster-specific marker genes.

name: single-cell-clustering-partition-analysis
description: Use when raw multimodal single-cell count data (RNA matrix X1 plus ADT matrix X2, e.g. h5 from GSE128639/bmcite) must be partitioned into unlabeled cell clusters and characterized by per-cluster marker/gene-set analysis.

name: single-cell-clustering-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a trained scETM or p-scETM model has produced cell embeddings and you must quantify clustering quality (e.g., ARI/NMI on 'cell_types' labels), compare against competing integration tools, or check that a regularized variant is not compromised.

name: single-cell-clustering-performance-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking a clustering or imputation method (e.g., scGCL, scTAG) on labeled scRNA-seq h5 data and you must quantify which KNN graph settings (k in {5,10,15,20,25}; city-block, cosine, euclidean, L2, manhattan distances) maximize ARI/NMI.

name: single-cell-clustering-quality-scoring
description: Use when many candidate clusterings exist (e.g. Totem's ~10k CLARA runs over a range of k) and an appropriate clustering must be automatically selected before constructing the trajectory MST.

name: single-cell-clustering-result-annotation
description: Use when scQA (or similar) clustering outputs exist for a scRNA-seq dataset and you must confirm that each cluster's key genes match known markers/DEGs to biologically annotate clusters.

name: single-cell-clustering-robustness-quantification
description: Use when you need to quantify the robustness or reproducibility of clusters produced by repeated stochastic single-cell clustering runs (e.g., SCA runs in rCASC), or when implementing cluster-stability validation metrics with a 0.5 explainability threshold.

name: single-cell-clustering-sweep
description: Use when benchmarking a pseudo-time reconstruction (e.g. consensus-TSP vs arbitrary insertion or Oscope) on cell-cycle-labeled scRNA-seq data across a sweep of cluster numbers k, needing correlation-scores per k.

name: single-cell-clustermining-with-autoencoder
description: Use when scRNAseq counts (e.g. setA, 10XGenomics UMI tables) have pre-computed cell clusters and the goal is to discover which biological knowledge (TF, miRNA, IS, kinase targets) drives clusterization, or to test whether combining knowledge groups improves cluster reconstruction.

name: single-cell-cna-calling
description: Use when analyzing PTA-amplified or low-coverage scWGS BAM files to call allele-specific CNAs, especially at small size scales (200 kb–5 Mb), or when comparing single-cell CNA callers on simulated or brain/meningioma datasets.

name: single-cell-cna-detection-from-scrna
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (10x Genomics droplet-based or Smart-seq2) from a tumour sample must be profiled for allele-specific CNAs (copy gain, copy loss, copy-neutral LOH) and subclones reconstructed from sparse, low-coverage data.

name: single-cell-cnv-analysis-quality-control
description: Use when preparing single-cell WGS (e.g., PTA- or MDA-amplified) data for CNA calling and an assay-specific minimum bin size must be chosen from measured allelic dropout, or when verifying that single-cell CNA calls pass QC thresholds (mappability, MAPQ, VAF filters).

name: single-cell-cnv-calling-from-rnaseq
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq data (e.g., 430-cell GBM dataset) to call large-scale CNVs per cell, identify mutually exclusive/co-occurring CNV subclones within a patient, and derive a CNV-based clonal phylogenetic tree.

name: single-cell-cohort-representative-sampling
description: Use when a cohort's bulk sequencing data (e.g., preprocessed COVID-19 cohort bulk RNA-seq from the scSemiProfiler example_data folder) must yield all representative samples in one batch, and multi-round active learning is impractical or would introduce batch effects.

name: single-cell-combinatorial-indexing-assay-annotation
description: Use when you have a seqspec YAML for a combinatorial-indexing single-cell assay and need to identify where the cell barcode is encoded (e.g. Illumina index regions) before preprocessing FASTQs.

name: single-cell-communication-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data (genes x cells) plus cell-type labels need unsupervised cell-cell communication inference without relying on predefined L-R pairs, e.g., non-human species or benchmarking against CellChat/CellPhoneDB/iTALK.

name: single-cell-communication-network-thresholding
description: Use when building or visualizing a cell-to-cell communication network from single-cell expression data plus cell-type labels and you must decide which ligand–receptor edges pass detection (e.g. >20% of cells), specificity, and expression cutoffs before drawing.

name: single-cell-communication-quantification
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression, cell-type labels, and (optionally) time-point annotations and need to infer and compare cell-cell interaction networks, especially to test how L-R aggregation schemes affect interaction recovery.

name: single-cell-community-flux-modeling
description: Use when you have a patient-partitioned scRNA-seq object with cell-type annotations and want community-aware metabolic fluxes per cell type (e.g. glucose uptake across myeloid, B, T, epithelial cells) rather than per-cell or bulk fluxes.

name: single-cell-comparative-regulatory-analysis
description: Use when you have four single-cell datasets (one scRNA-seq and one scATAC-seq from each of two conditions/populations) and need to identify subpopulation-specific differential regulatory relations between transcription factors and target genes.

name: single-cell-copy-number-baseline-subtraction
description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes on rows, cells on columns) and need to remove the normal-cell expression baseline so that cell-specific copy number signal can be segmented, without manually identifying reference cell clusters as inferCNV requires.

name: single-cell-copy-number-calling
description: Use when calling allele-specific somatic CNAs from paired single-cell + matched bulk WGS BAMs (PTA-amplified, ~20-30x scWGS), when small (200 kb-5 Mb) or subclonal CNAs must be resolved, or when benchmarking single-cell CNA callers.

name: single-cell-copy-number-inference
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from tumor biopsies (Smart-seq2 or 10X Chromium) must be automatically segregated into malignant and non-malignant cells and subcloned by copy-number architecture without a manually identified reference-cell cluster.

name: single-cell-count-aggregation-by-cell-type
description: Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment objects contain sparse gene and 3'UTR isoform count matrices at single-cell resolution and counts must be summed per cell type before pairwise differential testing.

name: single-cell-count-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking co-expression inference methods (e.g., CS-CORE vs Pearson, Spearman, locCSN, normalisr, NoiseRegularization) against a known true network, or when evaluating whether estimation bias harms downstream clustering/PCA via simulations with controlled n, p, and cluster structure.

name: single-cell-count-imputation
description: Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts must be denoised/imputed prior to kinetic parameter estimation (kon, koff, s) with the RJAGS Gibbs sampler, or when scVI/MAGIC imputation is needed to meet modeling assumptions.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-correlation-analysis
description: Use when an alternative scRNA-seq quantification workflow must be benchmarked against a standard pipeline like Cell Ranger by comparing gene-level UMI count matrices across the same cells and genes.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-downsampling
description: Use when you need to test stability of a fitted single-cell dynamical model (e.g. scKINETICS velocities) against technical noise in transcript capture by perturbing raw counts at reduced sequencing depths and refitting.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-gene-filtering
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices must be converted into descending expression-ranked gene-symbol sequences for autoregressive transformer models like tGPT.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-generation
description: Use when raw FASTQ files (or Cell Ranger BAMs convertible via bamtofastq) from any UMI-based scRNA-seq platform must be processed into gene-by-barcode matrices under one uniform pipeline, e.g. for cross-platform integration benchmarks.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when pooled scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq droplets have been labeled with hashtag oligonucleotides and you need to load HTO and RNA count matrices, derive per-droplet detected-gene totals, and check HTO-vs-gene correlations before demultiplexing.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count matrices (cells in rows, genes in columns, CSV or similar) must be normalized and rescaled before scGATE inference, or when base GRN .parquet files need read_base_GRN() summarization.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw single-cell gene expression count matrix must be preprocessed to remove an annotated unwanted signal (batch, cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, healthy-reference trajectory) before downstream analysis.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw scRNAseq count matrix must be pre-processed into standardized residuals prior to SVD/CA — e.g., to address overdispersion of counts instead of applying log(x+1) followed by PCA.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw per-individual UMI count matrices from 10x Chromium scRNA-seq need gene filtering, top-1000 HVG selection, and marker-based approximated ground-truth cell-type labels before clustering benchmarking.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., scEU-seq or BoolODE simulated data, genes x cells) are about to be fed into RNAForecaster and still contain high sparsity, non-log-transformed counts, or Float64 values.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix must be converted into a normalized, feature-selected expression matrix (anndata/Scanpy) as input to a graph-based clustering pipeline such as scMGCA.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when a raw cells × genes scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris '00_facs_raw_data/FACS/{tissue}-counts.csv') must be converted to a numeric numpy array and paired with a signal-free null dataset for empirical hypothesis testing of embedding quality.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GSE57872 glioblastoma cells with batch and patient labels) must be modeled without preliminary normalization, especially when batch and biology are partially confounded and covariates like detection rate must be included.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-quality-control
description: Use when raw spliced/unspliced gene-by-cell count matrices (e.g. from scKB/kallisto-bustools) need quality filtering, doublet removal, and downstream Seurat analysis before cell-type annotation.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-quality-control
description: Use when raw 10x Genomics single-cell or multiome (RNA+ATAC) count matrices (h5/CSV) must be filtered and normalized (log CPTT for RNA, CLR for ADT) before Leiden clustering and scTriangulate integration.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-quality-control
description: Use when starting from a raw scRNA-seq count matrix downloaded from GEO (e.g., GSE113197 breast epithelial cells) that must be filtered for low-quality cells and genes and normalized before clustering or marker-based cell annotation.

name: single-cell-count-matrix-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking integration or differential-state detection methods needs synthetic two-condition, two-batch single-cell count data with known injected DS genes at controlled logFC (1.1–2) and prevalence (5% and 10%).

name: single-cell-count-matrix-smoothing
description: Use when single-cell expression data (Scanpy AnnData .h5ad) is too sparse/noisy for per-cell gene set scoring, and a smoothed neighbor-averaged matrix is needed before applying methods like singscore or ssGSEA.

name: single-cell-count-modeling
description: Use when modeling scRNA-seq gene-level count distributions (UMI or non-UMI) with heavy tails and point mass at zero, and you need platform-adaptive fitting with automatically estimated gene-specific index parameter p.

name: single-cell-count-normalization
description: Use when a raw UMI count matrix (e.g., from GEO GSM4905334) must be library-size normalized to the clone's median UMI count before signature scoring, filterGenesFano gene selection, or Geary's C autocorrelation analysis.

name: single-cell-count-normalization
description: Use when a raw single-cell count matrix (e.g. a Seurat object or SingleCellExperiment such as the untreated PDAC snRNA-Seq dataset SCP1089) must be log-normalized with size factors and variable features scaled before clustering or LEADER subsampling.

name: single-cell-count-normalization
description: Use when an AnnData h5ad (e.g. the Macosko Mouse Atlas, 4.4M cells) is too large for in-memory Scanpy QC, and you need cell filtering, library-size normalization, and log transformation via AnnSQL SQL operations.

name: single-cell-count-normalization
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g., CELLxGENE census 2023-05-15 extracts) must be converted to the scTab sf-log1p representation — 10,000-count size factors plus log1p over 19,331 protein-coding genes — before model training, augmentation-vector computation, or inference.

name: single-cell-count-preprocessing-for-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking gene network inference methods on raw single-cell count matrices: each method demands different preprocessing (e.

name: single-cell-count-simulation
description: Use when you need ground-truth scRNA-seq count data with known celltype labels and an applied dropout model to quantify whether a denoiser (DCA vs. an MSE autoencoder) recovers the true cell structure.

name: single-cell-cpm-count-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (.csv or .parquet) has already been quality-filtered in a scSPARKL/Spark pipeline and cell counts must be made comparable across cells prior to gene selection, PCA, and clustering.

name: single-cell-crispr-grna-cell-assignment-interpretation
description: Use when single-cell CRISPR screen (CROP-seq) data has gRNA assignments labeled as intact/spacer-mutant/scaffold-mutant and you must confirm functional impact of gRNA mutations on target gene downregulation.

name: single-cell-crispr-screen-association-testing
description: Use when analyzing UMI read count + gRNA assignment matrices from a pooled single-cell CRISPR screen (e.g., high-MOI CROP-seq/Perturb-seq with thousands of gRNAs) to compute unbiased gRNA-gene associations with logFC, P values, and Q values.

name: single-cell-crispr-screen-cell-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing single-cell CRISPR screening data (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq expression profile plus perturbation information) to remove invalid-edit cells and low-cell-count perturbations before model building.

name: single-cell-crispr-screen-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw input is a gene-by-cell expression profile (e.g. expression_profile.txt) plus per-cell perturbation labels (perturb_information.txt), or 10X barcodes/genes/matrix files with a cbc_gbc_dict, and cells must be QC'd, imputed, and filtered before perturbation ranking.

name: single-cell-crispr-screen-quality-control
description: Use when a single-cell CRISPR screen (e.g. CROP-seq) gRNA library BAM must be quality-controlled for mutant gRNAs and cells must be assigned gRNAs mutation-aware, beyond Cell Ranger feature barcoding.

name: single-cell-crispr-screening-perturbation-ranking
description: Use when you need to validate that a single-cell CRISPR screening pipeline's perturbation-effect ranking (e.g., MUSIC's Rank_overall) is stable under control-cell label noise, or to reproduce the reported robustness figures before trusting downstream ranking-driven conclusions.

name: single-cell-cross-modality-translation
description: Use when raw count AnnData matrices from a single modality must be translated into another (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq peaks, or ADT), including unseen cell types, batch-shifted data, or chained multi-modality inference.

name: single-cell-cytometry-data-handling
description: Use when you have single-cell data (cells x markers, e.g. CyTOF) with a priori class labels (cell type, cell-cycle phase, time point) and need an interpretable, non-stochastic low-dimensional visualization that maximizes class separation.

name: single-cell-data-augmentation-with-cell-type-labels
description: Use when the number of paired training cells for scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (or scADT-seq) translation is limited and clustering quality of translated profiles must be preserved, especially in five-fold down-sampling designs.

name: single-cell-data-format-conversion
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq object (Seurat or AnnData) must be made loadable in CellexalVR, which requires exported CellexalVR input files rather than native R/Python object formats.

name: single-cell-data-integration-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing a homologous-gene mapping and integration algorithm when integrating scRNA-seq datasets across species, especially when species divergence time, number of species, or one-to-one vs in-paralog homology strategies may affect integration quality.

name: single-cell-data-value-sketching
description: Use when a large scRNA-seq atlas (.h5ad, tens of thousands to millions of cells) must be subsampled before downstream ML/DL tasks such as cell-type annotation (scANVI, scPoli, CellTypist, ACTINN), label transfer, CellHint harmonization, or bulk deconvolution, and uniform or geometric sketching.

name: single-cell-dataset-alignment
description: Use when multiple annotated scRNA-seq datasets must be combined to learn a hierarchical classification tree, and batch effects are expected between the datasets (e.g., different PBMC studies measured on different platforms).

name: single-cell-dataset-benchmark-table-construction
description: Use when a cell can belong to multiple inferred trajectories and you need to quantify whether its inferred pseudotime is consistent across those paths, benchmarked per dataset.

name: single-cell-dataset-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking the scalability of a reference-mapping pipeline (e.g. Symphony/Harmony) and you need matched downsampled expression/metadata subsets at multiple cell counts as controlled inputs.

name: single-cell-dataset-label-matching
description: Use when a single-cell count matrix needs a biologically interpretable, cell-type-separating embedding: e.g., the MCA dataset must be embedded via the 137 marker GEPs and benchmarked against PCA, scDHA, or scMGCA using Davies-Bouldin and Calinski-Harabasz scores.

name: single-cell-dataset-subset-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking execution time of single-cell methods across growing sample sizes: subset a raw cell-by-gene count matrix at fixed increments and record single-core wall-clock time and failures per method per size.

name: single-cell-deg-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare DEG prediction methods on single-cell RNA-seq data with known ground truth — i.e., artificial datasets with planted DEGs where AUC and elapsed runtime per method per dataset size can be tabulated.

name: single-cell-demultiplexing-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix plus per-droplet detected-gene counts for regression mixture model demultiplexing, and initial class labels or outlier flags are needed before model fitting.

name: single-cell-denoising-method-benchmarking
description: Use when a sparse single-cell expression matrix with known cell-phenotype labels (e.g., 95% sparse PBMC or mouse cortex data) must be denoised and you need to verify whether RMT feature selection outperforms MAGIC, scImpute, ZIFA, ZIMB-WaVE, scVI, DCA, Seurat, or HVG baselines.

name: single-cell-detection-rate-thresholding
description: Use when filtering ligand-receptor pairs in single-cell expression data so a gene counts as 'expressed' in a cell type only if detected in more than 20% of its cells (NATMI --detectionThreshold default 0.2).

name: single-cell-diagonal-integration
description: Use when you have unpaired single-cell modality pairs (e.g. scRNA-scATAC, scRNA-protein, scRNA-smFISH, scRNA-morphology) from the same biological condition and need a shared cell embedding without converting features across modalities.

name: single-cell-differential-abundance-analysis
description: Use when two annotated single-cell RNA-seq datasets processed in SingCellaR (e.g., eFL and FL HSPC objects with existing UMAP embeddings and cell-type labels) must be compared for cell-subpopulation abundance shifts, and per-cell DA scores plus a DA UMAP figure are the desired outputs.

name: single-cell-differential-activity-prediction
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, spatial transcriptomics, or trajectory data in h5ad/Seurat form with an embedding or coordinate space (PCA, pseudotime, 1D-3D spatial) and need clustering-independent detection of features with non-random activity patterns.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have partitioned droplet-based scRNA-seq barcodes into cell-calling groups (e.g. All-retained, EmptyNN-retained, EmptyNN-removed) and need to test whether a cell-caller's retained barcodes are transcriptionally similar to confirmed cells.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been partitioned by a binary event (e.g., presence/absence of a fusion such as TMPRSS2-ERG) and you must test association with treatment or differential gene expression to quantify the fusion's transcriptional impact per cell.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data or DE summary statistics (per-gene beta coefficient and variance) are available and gene-level differential expression calls between cell types or conditions are needed, especially when power or cross-method consistency is a concern.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing DE methods on UMI or non-UMI scRNA-seq count data (synthetic via Splatter templates from Islam et al. 2011 and Klein et al. 2015, or published GEO datasets) to measure power and FDR control.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-filtering
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset has been clustered (e.g., with scPlant/Seurat) and you need cluster-specific marker genes as input for promoter motif-enrichment analysis such as PMET on SCENIC regulons.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when a clustered single-cell AnnData object needs cluster-level marker/DE genes — e.g. to assign a cell type to a Leiden cluster via enrichment of its top differential genes.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when annotated single-cell RNA-seq data with malignant/non-malignant labels is available and a robust, dataset-independent gene feature set (e.g., TMGs/NMGs) is needed for downstream cell classification.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when comparing two conditions of a single-cell dataset (e.g., IFN-stimulated vs. control PBMCs) and you need per-cell-type significance of ligand/receptor perturbation before scoring differential signaling edges.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when a user defines two or more cell groups over a single-cell gene expression matrix and marker genes must be ranked by statistical significance to build a clustered heatmap or DE table.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell expression matrix with cell type/cluster assignments and need to identify cell type-specific DE genes or TFs (e.g., Welch's t test p < 0.05) to feed signature or regulatory-network analysis.

name: single-cell-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when you have a library-size-normalized, log-transformed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell cluster labels and need per-cluster marker ligand/receptor statistics (log2FC, adjusted P) to feed cell-cell communication inference.

name: single-cell-differential-gene-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a log2-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with cluster labels and need to interpret clusters biologically via DE genes, GO terms, and KEGG pathways.

name: single-cell-differential-gene-expression-testing
description: Use when comparing scRNA-seq imputation methods on biological interpretability: you have raw and imputed expression matrices for the same cells and want to test whether imputation yields clearer DEG patterns and better recovery of disease-related KEGG pathways.

name: single-cell-differential-regulation-testing
description: Use when sc_compreg has produced empirical likelihood ratio scores for TF-TG differential regulation and you need calibrated p-values and FDR control for them.

name: single-cell-differentiation-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when single-cell gene expression data (e.g. ME, MMP, MFG, or MH datasets) must be ordered along pseudotime and multiple bifurcation events of cellular differentiation need to be detected.

name: single-cell-dimension-reduction
description: Use when a learned cell-to-cell similarity matrix from SIMLR's multi-kernel optimization is available and a low-dimensional embedding is needed to visualize and interpret cell populations in scRNA-seq data.

name: single-cell-dimension-reduction
description: Use when reducing dimensions of raw scRNAseq count matrices (SingleCellExperiment objects) to embed cells for clustering and cell-type recovery, and standard log(x+1)+PCA pipelines distort count data or overdispersion is a concern.

name: single-cell-dimension-reduction
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (cells × genes matrix) must be compressed to a low-dimensional embedding for visualization, clustering, or as input to classification or pseudo-time inference, especially with high dropout and technical noise.

name: single-cell-dimension-reduction
description: Use when you have a temporal scRNA-seq gene-by-cell count matrix with a cell-by-time-point binary time table and need a 2D visualization that preserves developmental trajectories and resolves intra-time-point subpopulations.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (wide format, e.g. tens of thousands to millions of cells from 10x Genomics data) exceeds single-machine memory and you need Spark-native PCA cell embeddings compatible with downstream Parquet-based UMAP/t-SNE steps.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF markers, scRNA-seq PCs) come with a priori class labels such as cell type, cell-cycle phase, or experimental time point, and the goal is a supervised visualization whose axes separate those labels.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when an annotated single-cell Seurat object must be subsetted to a compartment (e.g., T/NK cells from the 12 liver transplant samples) and re-embedded/re-clustered via PCA -> UMAP and graph-based clustering to reproduce reported cluster counts.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-and-clustering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., ZF1_F3_DrImpute) must be converted into cluster labels and state lineages that downstream lineage-tree methods like LinRace NJ_asym_Dif require as inputs.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
description: Use when benchmarking a supervised graph-embedding visualization (e.g. GraphDDP) against unsupervised and pseudotime baselines on single-cell data with prior cluster labels, to show which pathways baselines miss.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
description: Use when assessing whether a dimensionality-reduction method can handle a million-plus-cell scRNA-seq dataset within practical runtime, by timing ivis against Barnes-Hut t-SNE with a 24-hour timeout.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-coordinate-handling
description: Use when dense dimension-reduction plots (UMAP/tSNE/DDRTree of scRNA-seq data, e.g. >30k cells) must support freehand per-cell selection or per-point raycast hit detection in Unity, and attaching native colliders to every point is infeasible.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-embedding
description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., the Ind4 breast epithelium sample from GEO GSE113197, genes as rows and cells as columns) must be projected to low-dimensional space (PCA, then UMAP) before graph-based clustering and marker-based cell annotation.

name: single-cell-dimensionality-reduction-pca-lsi
description: Use when you need a low-dimensional cell representation of a single-cell count matrix (scRNA counts, protein ADT, or scATAC peak matrix) to feed a kNN graph, integration method, or label-consistency metric like kNN agreement.

name: single-cell-disentangled-latent-model-training
description: Use when a multi-batch scRNA-seq dataset contains cells measured under multiple biological conditions and you need to jointly remove batch effect while preserving condition effect in latent factors.

name: single-cell-distance-metric-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to validate that a proposed cell-to-cell similarity/distance measure captures same-cell-type affinity more strongly than a conventional pipeline baseline (e.g., HVG+PCA Euclidean distance), by quantifying deviation from a permutation null.

name: single-cell-distance-metric-computation
description: Use when quantifying how closely inferred (semi-profiled) single-cell data matches real-profiled ground truth, or when scoring per-sample inference difficulty Dsc to drive active-learning representative selection on a bulk+single-cell cohort.

name: single-cell-dna-rna-cell-assignment-stability-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq and scDNA-seq cells from the same samples have been assigned with MaCroDNA but no paired ground truth exists, and you need statistical significance and stability of those assignments.

name: single-cell-dna-rna-count-matrix-handling
description: Use when paired scDNA-seq copy-number and scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. the CRC dataset from Bian et al.) must be prepared as gene-by-cell dataframes for MaCroDNA cell-association or runtime/memory benchmarking.

name: single-cell-dna-rna-integration
description: Use when you have independent single-cell DNA copy-number and RNA expression matrices from the same sample (genes as rows, cells as columns) and need to associate RNA cells to DNA cells or infer cell-to-clone assignments.

name: single-cell-donor-based-data-splitting
description: Use when training or evaluating cross-tissue cell type classifiers on multi-donor scRNA-seq corpora where test cells must come from donors never seen during training.

name: single-cell-doublet-ensemble-scoring
description: Use when droplet-based scRNA-seq data may contain heterotypic doublets that destabilize downstream clustering or trajectory inference, and single-method doublet scores vary across datasets — an ensemble (GBM-boosted) score is needed before filtering.

name: single-cell-downstream-fidelity-evaluation
description: Use when a computationally inferred or semi-profiled single-cell cohort must be validated against a real-profiled cohort by comparing downstream outputs such as marker genes, GO enrichment, CellChat interaction matrices, and Monocle3 pseudotime.

name: single-cell-dropout-event-modeling
description: Use when reconstructing the decoder of the scMGCA graph convolutional autoencoder, or when a count-matrix generative loss must account for high-probability dropout events without assuming a zero-inflated negative binomial model.

name: single-cell-dropout-imputation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has extensive simulated or observed dropouts (e.g. 0.1%–10% sampling efficiency) and accurate imputation is needed before clustering, visualization, or pseudotime analysis.

name: single-cell-dropout-modeling
description: Use when pre-training or adapting a single-cell classification model on raw scRNA-seq count matrices and a loss must capture the mean-dispersion-dropout structure (zero-inflation) of gene expression counts.

name: single-cell-dropout-probability-estimation
description: Use when an scRNA-seq raw count matrix contains dropout-driven false zeros and you need to estimate which gene-cell entries are affected by dropout before imputation, rather than altering all expression values.

name: single-cell-drug-repositioning
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from diseased tissue (e.g., TNBC PDX models or patient samples like GSE123926/GSE161529) needs FDA-approved drug recommendations that account for multiple heterogeneous cell clusters.

name: single-cell-drug-response-inference
description: Use when you have untreated disease-state scRNA-seq data with cell-type annotations, a known drug target gene (e.g. Smo for vismodegib, Ctsk for tanshinone IIA), and need to rank which cell types are most drug-responsive.

name: single-cell-drug-response-prediction
description: Use when you have a clustered scRNA-seq AnnData object (scanpyobj.h5ad) and need cluster-wise drug sensitivity estimates (IC50) and cell-kill percentages for GDSC drugs.

name: single-cell-embedding-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be clustered and interpreted through topics — e.g. identifying topics differentially expressed between disease and control conditions or across cell types.

name: single-cell-embedding-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a single-cell embedding method (e.g., DIRECTi, DCA, PCA, tSNE) preserves cell-type resolution in scRNA-seq latent space, by computing MAP of nearest-neighbor cell retrieval between query and reference datasets.

name: single-cell-embedding-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing how well alternative low-dimensional embeddings of simulated scRNA-seq preserve cell-cell topological structure, evaluated as trajectory (pseudotime) recovery measured by Kendall correlation against a known ground truth.

name: single-cell-embedding-clustering
description: Use when inferring a tree-shaped trajectory from single-cell data and a diverse set of candidate clusterings is needed to construct minimum spanning trees and estimate cell connectivity, as in the Totem workflow.

name: single-cell-embedding-clustering-accuracy-assessment
description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods (e.g., scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, scVI, scDML, scDREAMER) on integrated single-cell embeddings where ground-truth cell-type labels exist and you need quantitative clustering/bio-conservation and batch-mixing metrics.

name: single-cell-embedding-clustering-evaluation
description: Use when comparing cell embeddings/clusterings from multiple single-cell multi-omics integration methods and need quantitative embedding (silhouette, purity) and clustering (ARI across resolutions) metrics.

name: single-cell-embedding-distance-computation
description: Use when cell embeddings (e.g. adata.obsm['scace_emb']) and cluster labels are available and you must quantify cluster separation by size-weighted inter-centroid distance to decide which clusters to merge or when merging stops.

name: single-cell-embedding-extraction
description: Use when you need comparable cell embeddings from multiple single-cell foundation models (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer, scFoundation) for a downstream benchmark such as batch-effect correction scored by scIB avgBIO.

name: single-cell-embedding-extraction-transformer
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices or per-cell gene expression rankings must be converted into fixed-length cell embeddings for clustering, UMAP visualization, or batch-effect benchmarking without explicit normalization or batch correction.

name: single-cell-embedding-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object needs a t-SNE or UMAP 2D visualization and the hyperparameters (perplexity, min.dist, n_neighbors) are unvalidated, or when dubious cell embeddings must be detected before interpreting 2D cluster layout.

name: single-cell-embedding-quality-assessment
description: Use when a t-SNE or UMAP visualization of single-cell data must be quality-controlled or its hyperparameters (perplexity, min.dist, n.neighbors) chosen objectively, e.g. when cluster adjacency or distances in the 2D plot need to be judged trustworthy.

name: single-cell-embedding-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq count matrix (e.g. Tabula Muris marrow FACS counts, 10x PBMC scATAC peak matrix) and need to judge which parts of a t-SNE/UMAP embedding reflect biological signal versus distortion, or to choose embedding hyperparameters.

name: single-cell-embedding-quality-classification
description: Use when a 2D scRNA-seq embedding (UMAP, t-SNE, diffusion maps) must be judged fit for trajectory/pseudotime inference, or when a UMAP run exhibits disconnected or unexpectedly grouped small clusters that would bias Slingshot/Monocle3 pseudotime.

name: single-cell-embedding-quality-evaluation
description: Use when comparing a novel embedding (e.g., GRN module AUCell scores) against batch-correction baselines on annotated snRNA-seq data, to quantify batch mixing vs retention of annotations like diagnosis, sex, or batch/sample.

name: single-cell-embedding-reliability-scoring
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (Seurat object) and want to detect dubious 2D cell embeddings from t-SNE/UMAP, or to grid-search perplexity / min.dist / n_neighbors by minimizing the number of dubious cell embeddings.

name: single-cell-embedding-silhouette-evaluation
description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction/visualization quality of scRNA-seq embeddings (e.g., scMGCA latent space vs PCA, t-SNE, UMAP) on datasets with ground-truth cell-type labels, quantified by average silhouette width (ASW).

name: single-cell-embedding-transfer
description: Use when a processed SingCellaR object already contains Harmony/UMAP embeddings and Louvain cluster labels, and trajectory or pseudotime ordering (e.g. HSC/MPP to erythroid differentiation) is needed in Monocle3.

name: single-cell-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix needs a 2D embedding and visualization to compare which method (EDGE vs. t-SNE vs. UMAP) preserves cell-type structure and separates rare populations.

name: single-cell-embeddr-pvalue-estimation
description: Use when a dimensionality-reduced single-cell embedding (t-SNE/UMAP of scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq counts) needs per-cell statistical quality assessment, hyperparameter (perplexity/kEff) optimization, or separation of biological signal from embedding artifacts.

name: single-cell-entropy-based-cell-ranking
description: Use when you have scRNA-Seq or bulk RNA-Seq expression data and need to rank cells/samples by differentiation potency or detect cancer stem-cell/drug-resistant phenotypes without marker genes or timepoint labels.

name: single-cell-error-rate-comparison
description: Use when multiple cell type identification methods must be compared on spatial transcriptomics data with known ground-truth single-cell labels, especially to test whether joint multi-slice analysis improves accuracy over slice-by-slice analysis.

name: single-cell-expression-aggregation
description: Use when a per-cell scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., cortex_data from Yao 2021) must be collapsed into group-level expression per cell subclass so ligand and target abundances can be scored against NeuronChatDB interaction entries.

name: single-cell-expression-cpm-normalization
description: Use when preparing a raw single-cell UMI count matrix (e.g. Tabula Muris or Tabula Muris Senis) as input to NATMI's ExtractEdges.py, which expects CPM-normalized expression profiles with a cell-annotation metafile.

name: single-cell-expression-denoising
description: Use when a sparse scRNA-seq or dropout-simulated count matrix needs denoising/imputation, or when comparing DCA vs MAGIC/SAVER/scImpute recovery of known gene associations.

name: single-cell-expression-dotplot-visualization
description: Use when comparing expression of selected genes across multiple scRNA-seq studies whose cell annotations must be aligned to a shared standardized cell-type vocabulary (CellO) and a concise cross-study overview plot is required.

name: single-cell-expression-imputation
description: Use when raw or dropout-affected scRNA-seq count matrices (h5 files with expression values and true labels) need imputation to improve downstream clustering (ARI/NMI) or gene-expression recovery under synthetic dropout.

name: single-cell-expression-matrix-analysis

name: single-cell-expression-matrix-preprocessing

name: single-cell-expression-preprocessing

name: single-cell-expression-preprocessing

name: single-cell-expression-resampling-bootstrapping

name: single-cell-expression-subsampling

name: single-cell-expression-subsetting

name: single-cell-expression-thresholding

name: single-cell-expression-trajectory-simulation

name: single-cell-feature-embedding-analysis

name: single-cell-gene-expression-decomposition

name: single-cell-gene-expression-filtering

name: single-cell-gene-expression-modeling

name: single-cell-gene-expression-reconstruction

name: single-cell-gene-expression-trend-verification

name: single-cell-gene-fusion-detection

name: single-cell-gene-list-interpretation

name: single-cell-gene-network-inference

name: single-cell-gene-perturbation-clustering

name: single-cell-gene-signature-marker-extraction

name: single-cell-genotype-phenotype-modeling

description: Use when you need to label individual cells as malignant or non-malignant in human tumor scRNA-seq data without a reference, especially across pan-cancer TISCH datasets or to benchmark annotation speed against CNV-based tools.

name: single-cell-manifold-alignment
description: Use when two single-modality single-cell datasets (e.g. ATAC source, RNA target) share no overlapping cells or features and must be aligned into a common latent space for label-matching or integration scoring.

name: single-cell-marker-based-cell-type-scoring
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq counts (AnnData) need standardized cell-type labels via reference-derived marker genes, especially for million-scale datasets on limited compute or when model-based methods (Seurat, Harmony, scNym, scArches) are too costly.

name: single-cell-marker-based-loss-computation
description: Use when training or reproducing BIDCell-style segmentation on SST data (e.g. Xenium transcripts.csv.gz + morphology_mip.ome.tif) and you need per-component and total biologically-informed loss values on real image patches.

name: single-cell-marker-gene-differential-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has already been normalized, dimensionality-reduced and clustered (e.g. SF clusters on PBMC3k), and per-cluster marker genes are needed for cluster annotation or functional enrichment.

name: single-cell-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when you have a trained Miscell encoder on scRNA-seq data (e.g., Smart-seq HVG matrix) with cell cluster labels and need cluster-specific marker genes via attribution scores rather than differential expression tests.

name: single-cell-marker-gene-identification
description: Use when annotating cell types of scRNA-seq clusters automatically and you need cluster marker genes that are upregulated in exactly one cluster, avoiding pseudo markers (e.g. CCL22, SWAP70, KLRF1) that arise from one-against-all comparisons and impair annotation consistency.

name: single-cell-marker-selection-solver-execution
description: Use when given a simulated or real scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type labels and a target marker panel size (e.g., 50 markers), and you must run scGeneFit to extract selected gene indices and measure solver runtime.

name: single-cell-marker-weighted-annotation
description: Use when single-cell or spatial RNA-seq data (Seurat object or raw/normalized count matrix) must be annotated with interpretable, consistency-weighted markers, or when disease-critical cell types such as leukemic stem cells must be scored.

name: single-cell-matrix-factorization-usage-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking matrix-factorization-based GEP discovery (e.g., cNMF) against network-based GEP identification (e.g., SingleCellGGM) on a labeled single-cell dataset, to quantify how many programs are cell-type-specific versus shared activity programs.

name: single-cell-matrix-serialization
description: Use when a single-cell dataset stored as an AnnData (.h5ad) object or a Scanpy sample dataset must be converted into a persistent, SQL-queryable on-disk database so expression matrices and metadata can be joined and filtered with SQL.

name: single-cell-mean-expression-aggregation-by-celltype
description: Use when you must reproduce or de-novo compute the weight_norm edgeweight of every Connectome edge from per-celltype mean normalized expression, or when validating ligand×receptor product scoring on scRNAseq data.

name: single-cell-mec-space-projection
description: Use when you have a tumor scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., TISCH cohorts like BCC pre/post-ICB or BLCA responder/non-responder) and need consistent, interpretable cell-state scores rather than manual marker-based labeling.

name: single-cell-meta-component-interpretation
description: Use when annotating data-driven single-cell gene programs (86 MetaTiME MeCs) with candidate transcriptional regulators using TF ChIP-seq binding evidence, or when validating TF prioritizations for tumor immune cell states.

name: single-cell-metacell-construction
description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. 10X/h5ad from GEO like GSE114953) and need to compress hundreds of thousands of single-cell profiles into ~75-cell metacells for downstream atlas-level analysis.

name: single-cell-module-scoring
description: Use when you have Hotspot-identified heritable gene modules (e.g., from phylogenetically autocorrelated genes in a lineage-traced tumor clone) and need a per-cell score for each module to overlay on phylogeny or expression projections.

name: single-cell-module-scoring-ssgsea
description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix and defined gene signatures (meta-modules or cell-cycle sets) and need per-cell module scores plus dominant-module calls to annotate clusters from an unsupervised clustering such as RCC.

name: single-cell-mosaic-multiomics-integration
description: Use when a dataset contains multiple single-cell batches that jointly profile different subsets of modalities (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, CITE-seq protein, chromVAR motifs), especially with unequal cell-type composition across batches.

name: single-cell-mtdna-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking mtDNA variant-calling tools against known ground-truth clonal variants in simulated Smart-seq2-like scRNA-seq data, or when generating simulated single-cell mtDNA BAMs with controlled clone counts, allele frequencies, and lineage trees.

name: single-cell-multi-batch-dataset-integration
description: Use when concatenating multiple scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., Baron, Lawlor, Muraro pancreas datasets) with batch and cell-type annotations and you need joint low-dimensional embeddings that both preserve cell-type separation and integrate batches for comparison against PCA-based pipelines.

name: single-cell-multi-omic-model-fitting
description: Use when paired transcriptome and surface protein (CITE-seq/REAP-seq ADT) data are available for training and the goal is to impute relative surface protein abundances from UMI-based scRNA-seq counts alone.

name: single-cell-multi-omics-preprocessing
description: Use when paired single-cell modality matrices (e.g. DBIT-seq transcriptomic/proteomic or granulocyte scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq count matrices) must be preprocessed before training scMMGAN or its CycleGAN/CMAE baselines.

name: single-cell-multi-table-correspondence-analysis
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq count tables (batches, samples, or platforms) sharing a common gene feature space must be integrated into a joint low-dimensional embedding, especially when PCA+Harmony shows poor batch mixing.

name: single-cell-multimodal-clustering-integration
description: Use when you have multimodal single-cell data (e.g. CITE-Seq, Multiome, TEA-Seq) with multiple conflicting annotation sets from Leiden clustering at different resolutions, and need a reconciled per-cell population assignment.

name: single-cell-multimodal-data-integration
description: Use when two single-cell omics matrices (e.g., snRNA-seq counts and snATAC-seq peak counts from the same study but unpaired barcodes, such as 10x Multiome PBMC data) must be co-embedded and cross-modal cell pairing is needed.

name: single-cell-multimodal-data-preprocessing
description: Use when raw single-cell datasets with paired TCR sequences and gene expression must be annotated (cell type, tissue, cancer source) and filtered before training mvTCR or building a multi-study reference atlas.

name: single-cell-multimodal-deep-clustering
description: Use when you need to jointly cluster RNA+ADT (CITE-seq) data and assess whether a learned latent space separates cell types while removing batch effects across batches.

name: single-cell-multimodal-embedding-analysis
description: Use when you have paired CITE-seq data (RNA gene counts CSV + raw protein ADT counts CSV, rows = cells, columns = genes/proteins) and need joint cell embeddings or want to quantify complementary, modality-specific information across cells.

name: single-cell-multimodal-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq data and need to quantify whether a multimodal latent embedding improves downstream prediction (antigen specificity, binding avidity from pMHC multimer counts) or cluster identification relative to unimodal baselines.

name: single-cell-multimodal-trajectory-branch-subsetting
description: Use when a single-cell multimodal dataset forms a tree-like or branching differentiation trajectory and you need to ablate topology — testing whether full-trajectory DAG inference or individual branch sub-DAGs explain the observed locus-gene signal.

name: single-cell-multimodal-vae-inference
description: Use when you have single-cell transcriptome count data (RNA_count.mtx with gene.tsv/barcode.tsv) from a CITE-seq experiment and need to predict paired surface protein abundances from a pretrained multimodal VAE, then quantify prediction accuracy against measured protein counts.

name: single-cell-multimodal-wnn-clustering
description: Use when a droplet-based single-cell dataset contains matched mRNA and antibody-derived tag (ADT) measurements and you need a joint cell clustering whose dependence on protein normalization (e.g., dsb vs. CLR) must be evaluated.

name: single-cell-multiome-count-preprocessing
description: Use when raw paired RNA-seq + ATAC-seq single-cell multimodal counts (e.g. 10x Multiome, SHARE-seq, SNARE-seq, sci-CAR) must be normalized and filtered before peak-gene link analysis.

name: single-cell-multiome-data-partitioning
description: Use when you need held-out likelihood evaluation of batch-wise single-cell models (e.g., MIRA RP models on the 13-batch NEURIPS 10x Multiome bone marrow data) and must split cells per batch into train/test sets.

name: single-cell-multiome-subpopulation-linking
description: Use when you have four single-cell data sets (one scRNA-seq plus one scATAC-seq from each of two conditions, e.g. CLL donor vs healthy control) and need to identify and compare condition-specific subpopulations and their regulatory programs.

name: single-cell-multiomic-alignment-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you have aligned single-cell embeddings from multiple alignment methods (e.g. scTopoGAN, UnionCom, MMD-MA) on paired-modality datasets (RNA/ATAC PBMC, RNA/ADT BM) and must rank them on clustering and cross-modality prediction performance.

name: single-cell-multiomic-cell-assignment
description: Use when you have two independent single-cell datasets from the same sample — scDNA-seq copy-number profiles and scRNA-seq expression profiles — restricted to a shared gene set, and need a one-to-one cell correspondence or RNA-cell-to-DNA-clone mapping.

name: single-cell-multiomic-data-integration
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq analysis has predicted primed cells and candidate regulatory factors (e.g. GATA1, KLF1, IRF8 in fetal liver MPPs) and matched scATAC-Seq data from the same cell types is available for epigenomic validation.

name: single-cell-multiomic-peak-gene-linking
description: Use when you have paired scATAC-seq/scRNA-seq data from a dynamic single-cell process and need to rank candidate chromatin peak-gene regulatory links by causal strength rather than correlation.

name: single-cell-multiomic-preprocessing
description: Use when raw unprocessed RNA-seq and ATAC-seq AnnData objects from a paired single-cell multimodal assay must be normalized and filtered to define valid candidate peak-gene pairs for downstream GrID-Net or pseudotime analysis.

name: single-cell-multiomics-count-preprocessing
description: Use when raw or minimally processed CITE-seq or SMAGE-seq h5 count matrices need per-modality normalization (mRNA vs. ADT/ATAC) before feeding a deep clustering model such as scMDC.

name: single-cell-multiomics-data-integration
description: Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics count matrices (e.g. RNA + surface protein CITE-seq, or RNA + ATAC peaks) and need joint dimensionality reduction, cross-modal prediction, or interpretable latent dimensions.

name: single-cell-multiomics-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking CITE-seq clustering methods (scMDC vs. TotalVI, Seurat V4 WNN, SC3, scDCC, BREM-SC, CiteFuse, Specter) requires controlled mRNA+ADT data with ground-truth labels, or for linear-runtime scalability tests.

name: single-cell-multiomics-generative-model-training
description: Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics raw count matrices (RNA and ATAC or CITE-seq) in mtx format with gene/peak/barcode annotation files and need joint representations or crossmodal prediction between modalities.

name: single-cell-multiomics-integration
description: Use when integrating unpaired annotated scRNA-seq (source, h5ad) with unlabeled scATAC-seq gene activity data (target, h5ad) for label transfer, atlas-scale joint embedding, or discovering scATAC-seq cell types absent from scRNA-seq annotations.

name: single-cell-multiomics-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing paired single-cell multi-omics data (e.g. 10X Multiome, CITE-seq, TEA-seq) for integrative methods like Mowgli: raw count matrices per modality need QC, normalization, and feature selection.

name: single-cell-multiomics-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating single-cell multi-omics integration, clustering, or GRN-inference methods requires synthetic scRNA-seq + scATAC-seq data with known differential expression, co-expression patterns, and regulatory ground truth.

name: single-cell-multiplet-detection
description: Use when an (HTOs x droplets) hashtag-oligonucleotide count matrix from pooled cells/nuclei must be assigned to samples of origin with error probabilities, uncertain-droplet discarding, and multiplet (singlet/doublet) detection.

name: single-cell-nanopore-error-correction
description: Use when single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore long-read alignments suffer from read truncation, misaligned small internal exons, or sequencing-error-driven false-positive novel isoforms that must be corrected before isoform quantification.

name: single-cell-nearest-neighbor-graph-construction
description: Use when preparing single-cell RNA-Seq count data for ELVAR differential abundance testing: a Seurat-processed count matrix with PCA is available and an igraph state-manifold with condition attributes is needed for cell-attribute aware community detection.

name: single-cell-neighbor-preservation-evaluation
description: Use when you have one or more 2D embeddings (e.g. UMAP, t-SNE, MDS on subsets of highly variable genes) of scRNA-seq data and must decide which embedding is suitable for pseudotime/trajectory inference before fitting Slingshot or Monocle3.

name: single-cell-neighborhood-graph-construction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with a pre-computed RNA velocity field (e.g., scVelo on an AnnData object with cluster annotations) must be converted into a probabilistic cell-to-cell transition graph for fate/trajectory simulation.

name: single-cell-neighbour-distance-processing
description: Use when a scRNA-seq rare-cell workflow needs candidate minor-cluster sizes derived from an inter-cluster gap signal, i.e. a precomputed cell-to-neighbour distance matrix is available and k must be estimated via ∆∆D skewness.

name: single-cell-network-flow-entropy-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data along a differentiation trajectory (e.g. progenitors vs mature cells) must be ordered by potency of individual cells, using per-cell network entropy rather than expression-only scores.

name: single-cell-network-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing gene regulatory/co-expression network inference methods on scRNA-seq count matrices, especially for quantifying robustness via half-sampling agreement and wall-clock runtime/memory on 10X or Smart-seq2 data.

name: single-cell-noise-signal-decomposition
description: Use when a sparse single-cell expression matrix (e.g. scRNA-seq counts with ~95% zeros) must be split into noise, sparsity-driven artifacts, and true biological signal without assuming i.i.d. noise distributions.

name: single-cell-omics-dataset-acquisition-and-preprocessing
description: Use when a task requires downloading a public multimodal single-cell dataset (TEA-seq/CITE-seq RNA + ADT) and preprocessing it into the features-by-cells modality format expected by SnapCCESS before embedding generation.

name: single-cell-online-label-transfer
description: Use when new scRNA-seq query datasets with batch effects must be annotated against an existing reference atlas, and retraining a model or re-fitting the classifier for each arriving dataset is impractical.

name: single-cell-ontology-based-annotation
description: Use when annotating single-cell RNA-seq data against a controlled vocabulary (Cell Ontology), especially when the query data may contain cell types absent from the training annotations.

name: single-cell-overdispersion-decomposition
description: Use when fitting per-gene mixed models to multi-subject scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts and you need to separate between-subject from within-subject overdispersion, or test whether covariates (e.g., age, sex, AD status) explain subject-level variation.

name: single-cell-pathogen-quantification-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (CPU/wall-clock time) of pathogen quantification tools—scPathoQuant, ViralTrack, PathogenTrack, Venus—on an identical 10x scRNAseq sample to rank them from fastest to slowest.

name: single-cell-pathogen-read-alignment
description: Use when you have 10x scRNAseq data already processed with cellranger count and need to detect, quantify, and differentiate viral or bacterial pathogen reads per cell in a single operation.

name: single-cell-pathway-activity-comparison
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression matrices from two populations (e.g. healthy vs disease, blood vs tissue) and need to rank pathway perturbations by distributional change rather than enrichment.

name: single-cell-pathway-activity-scoring
description: Use when you must compute PAS for a large pathway collection (>10^3 gene sets) across a large scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 100k+ cells, million-cell atlases) and existing scorers like UCell, AUCell, or AddModuleScore are too slow or memory-hungry.

name: single-cell-pathway-distribution-testing
description: Use when comparing pathway activity between scRNA-seq conditions (e.g. resting vs 24h-activated naive CD4+ T cells) and you need distribution-level perturbation signals, not gene-set over-representation.

name: single-cell-pathway-dysregulation-analysis
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells, log2(TPM+1)-style), cell-level metadata with 1/0 condition labels, a contrast file, and you need to identify which signaling pathways are dysregulated per cell type across conditions.

name: single-cell-pathway-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when comparing pathway activity across multiple conditions, time points, or pseudotime phases in scRNA-seq data — especially when enrichment-based methods miss pathways with distributional shifts but little fold change.

name: single-cell-pathway-score-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been quality-controlled and cell-annotated and you need to quantify a signaling pathway (e.g., angiogenesis) per cell, rank cell types by score, and highlight pathway-high subpopulations in the tumor microenvironment.

name: single-cell-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when two (or more) scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10X PBMC 8k and Pan T cells) need a common low-dimensional embedding before batch-correction or integration comparison, and cells must be represented as points in N-dimensional space for distance-weighted matching.

name: single-cell-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a normalized/scaled count matrix of barcoded single cells must be reduced to PC space before building a transcriptome nearest-neighbor graph for clustering or visualization (e.g., prior to ClonoCluster hybrid clustering or UMAP).

name: single-cell-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix over unannotated transcriptionally active regions (uTARs) and need to determine which regions carry cell-type-defining signal via PC loadings.

name: single-cell-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a scRNA-seq pipeline needs PCA on highly variable genes with a data-driven, permutation-based choice of PC count, after read.data quality filtering and get.variable.genes.

name: single-cell-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when preparing synthetic or real single-cell expression data (e.g., dyntoy datasets of ~1000 cells) for trajectory inference, where methods like VIA consume low-dimensional PC embeddings rather than full gene-expression matrices.

name: single-cell-pca-latent-space-projection
description: Use when a cell-by-gene or cell-by-peak AnnData matrix must be embedded before clustering or label transfer, e.g., scATAC-seq gene activity scores or a query dataset being projected onto a reference PCA via scanpy Ingest.

name: single-cell-perturbation-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when comparing drug-responsive cell-type prioritization methods on scRNA-seq perturbation data where ground-truth target cell types are known and paired pre/post-treatment baselines must be evaluated against untreated-only inference.

name: single-cell-perturbation-differential-testing
description: Use when comparing perturbed vs control single-cell RNA-seq cells and asking which pre-annotated gene modules/pathways (GMT-defined GMVs) are significantly differentially active, with module-level significance and a GSEA cross-check.

name: single-cell-perturbation-prediction
description: Use when a multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., 3-batch COVID-19 atlas with age and disease severity condition types) requires predicting counts toward a held-out condition/batch combination, in-sample or out-of-sample.

name: single-cell-perturbation-response-decoupling
description: Use when analyzing scCRISPR-seq data (cell-by-gene matrices Y = perturbation group, Z = control group) where differing infected-cell cluster proportions between perturbation and control groups make fold-change perturbation effects unreliable and per-gRNA cellular response must be estimated.

name: single-cell-plasticity-quantification
description: Use when you have a reconstructed single-cell phylogeny (cells as leaves) plus per-cell categorical metadata (e.g., clone, site, or state labels from GEO metadata) and want a per-cell numeric score of how plastic (mixed) the ancestral context of each category is along the lineage.

name: single-cell-pluripotency-quantification
description: Use when you need per-cell stemness/pluripotency scores from a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells) to identify stem/progenitor cells as trajectory origins, or to compare ORIGINS, LandSCENT, and CytoTRACE scores.

name: single-cell-polya-expression-track-rendering
description: Use when you need a per-gene genome-browser view (e.g., Fig. 1C) showing where poly(A) sites sit in a gene's 3'UTR and how single-cell pA counts and bulk BAM coverage change across sample groups such as SC/RS/ES.

name: single-cell-population-frequency-quantification
description: Use when you hold a scRNA-seq reference atlas with a cell-to-type identity file (e.g., the CCI distribution's data_ref/ cell-type and identity files for healthy BMMCs) and must report or verify the percentage composition of each annotated population.

name: single-cell-population-rejection-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether a hierarchical single-cell classifier detects truly novel populations: hold out a known population (e.g. 'Group 3' with four AMB nodes at tree layers 2 and 3) and measure the fraction of its cells rejected as unseen under alternative node classifiers.

name: single-cell-population-separation-assessment
description: Use when a trained deep learning model (Keras model JSON + weight bin, e.g. tmpMod./tmpWeight.bin) has classified single-cell gene expression data (e.g. Zheng sorted, Pancreas, CellBench) and you need to visually assess whether learned representations separate cell populations.

name: single-cell-preprocessing-and-louvain-clustering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells x genes) need preprocessing and initial Louvain clustering prior to rare cell-type detection, e.g., as stage 1 of the scCAD cluster-decomposition workflow.

name: single-cell-preprocessing-qc
description: Use when raw CITE-seq count matrices (transcriptome + surface-protein/ADT) from 10x Genomics or similar must be cleaned and prepared — e.g. pbmc_1k_protein_v3-style datasets — before pairwise-distance fusion and Louvain clustering in LinQ-View.

name: single-cell-probability-calibration
description: Use when a trained SIMS model must emit per-cell classification confidences, or when novel/unseen cell types in the target AnnData should be flagged as 'unknown' instead of receiving a forced label.

name: single-cell-projection-outlier-detection
description: Use when query cells have been projected into a reference atlas embedding (e.g., via ProjectSVR's ProjectNewdata with a ref.umap reduction) and you must determine which mapped cells are well-placed versus low-quality outliers before downstream label transfer.

name: single-cell-proportion-null-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking false-positive control of cell-type proportion analysis: null datasets with unchanged cluster proportions are simulated and accuracy (fraction of unchanged clusters correctly called non-significant) is scored per replicate or pseudo-replicate count.

name: single-cell-protein-ambient-noise-correction
description: Use when raw ADT/protein count matrices from CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, or TEA-seq experiments show antibody-specific background from unbound antibodies, and both a cell protein matrix and an empty-droplet protein matrix are available.

name: single-cell-proteomic-imaging-data-processing
description: Use when processing preprocessed single-cell proteomic imaging (4i) .h5ad datasets (e.g., PDAC cell lines or RPE with 241–253 imaging features) to select features that preserve cell cycle phases or cellular trajectories prior to trajectory inference.

name: single-cell-pseudo-space-reconstruction
description: Use when you have paired scRNA-seq and ST data (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) and need to map single cells into spatial coordinates or identify spatially variated cell subpopulations that traditional single-cell pipelines miss.

name: single-cell-pseudo-temporal-ordering
description: Use when a cell-to-landmark trajectory graph already exists and individual cells must be sequenced along developmental paths between adjacent landmark states to recover a pseudo-time axis.

name: single-cell-pseudo-time-inference
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq count matrix captures cells from ordered developmental stages and the goal is to infer cell ordering (pseudo-time) and quantify it against known capture/stage time.

name: single-cell-pseudobulk-aggregation
description: Use when a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. H5ad/HDF5/loom) must be converted into pseudo-bulk representative cells per cell type/sub-cluster before gene co-expression network inference with SCANet/WGCNA.

name: single-cell-pseudobulk-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether different scRNA-seq DS methods (edgeR/DESeq2/limma-voom pseudobulk vs MAST/dream mixed models) agree on top-ranked detections at FDR < 0.05, or when benchmarking muscat's pbDS/mmDS engines on simulated multi-sample data.

name: single-cell-pseudobulk-count-aggregation
description: Use when you have raw scRNAseq count matrices with circadian (or other periodic) time labels and need bulk-like profiles so a predictor trained on bulk RNAseq or microarray data can score the samples.

name: single-cell-pseudobulk-missingness-masking
description: Use when individual-cell type pairs in scRNA-seq pseudobulk data have <=10 cells so ctp/ctnu entries were set to missing, and CTMM fitting requires a complete expression and noise-variance matrix.

name: single-cell-pseudobulk-value-projection
description: Use when pseudotime and branch probabilities were computed at the pseudobulk (neighbourhood) level via vdjPseudobulk and must be mapped back to individual cells in a miloR SingleCellExperiment, especially when some cells are unassigned to any neighbourhood.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-assignment
description: Use when snapshot scRNA-seq data (e.g. h5ad count matrices) lacks direction information and you need high-resolution, multi-branch trajectories plus per-cell pseudotime, especially with intricate topologies like parallel differentiation routes.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-estimation
description: Use when a processed AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers and scvelo RNA velocity plus Cytopath consensus trajectory steps are available and per-cell pseudotime and cell fate probabilities must be quantified.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix from a cross-sectional cohort must be ordered along a one-dimensional biological progression without capture times, especially when covariates (stimulus, mutation, drug) may perturb the trajectory.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix (cells × genes) must be ordered along a developmental trajectory, visualized in 2D, or split into branching differentiation paths.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-ordering
description: Use when single cells have a sparse binary/eeSNV feature matrix with subgroup labels and the goal is a continuous genotype-based ordering (primary-to-metastasis trajectory) plus detection of subgroup-specific branches.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from multiple processing batches (e.g. the 10,878-cell human monocyte dataset) must be ordered along pseudotime without batch effects confounding the trajectory.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when you have a single-cell scRNA-seq count matrix with a differentiation hierarchy (e.g., basal-to-differentiated epithelium) and need to root a trajectory objectively by pluripotency scores rather than a priori marker assumptions.

name: single-cell-pseudotime-visualization-on-umap
description: Use when a TFvelo velocity result (e.g. rc.h5ad from a completed run on pancreas or another dataset) needs pseudotime ordering, streamplot arrows on UMAP, and phase-portrait fitting plots for validation and manuscript figures.

name: single-cell-qc-cell-filtering
description: Use when running gExcite (or its embedded scAmpi module) on hashed 10x PBMC samples where cell-level QC from the gene-expression layer must gate downstream CITE-seq/ADT analysis and antibody-positive cell calls.

name: single-cell-qc-filtering
description: Use when raw Cell Ranger gene-expression matrices (e.g., the eFL_1 fetal liver sample) must be pre-processed into a high-quality cell population before clustering, using UMI/gene-count/mito-fraction thresholds and scrublet doublet removal.

name: single-cell-qc-metrics-computation
description: Use when raw droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g. 10x GemCode, SRA SRP073767) must be turned into per-cell QC statistics such as median genes/UMIs per cell, capture efficiency, and multiplet rates.

name: single-cell-qc-summary-reporting
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (spliced and unspliced from scKB/kallisto/bustools) have been quality-filtered with COPILOT and you need to report or verify cell-filtering, mitochondrial thresholds, and doublet removal statistics in a CellRanger-3.1-comparable summary.

name: single-cell-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from scKB (spliced/unspliced 10x-format matrices) need background-noise/dying-cell removal before downstream Seurat analysis, RNA velocity, or trajectory inference.

name: single-cell-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ reads need barcode/UMI identification and quality filtering, and more retained, mappable reads are needed than the original filter that discards reads whose last 6 bases fail to match the barcode.

name: single-cell-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. GEO datasets like GSE145926, GSE132509, GSE123926/GSE113197) must be QC-filtered and normalized prior to Seurat integration, clustering, and downstream ASGARD drug scoring.

name: single-cell-quality-control-preprocessing
