description: Use when raw single-cell counts (10x/h5ad) of representative samples must be quality-filtered and normalized, or when bulk cohort data must be preprocessed (normalize_total, log1p, top-HVG + markers, PCA) before scSemiProfiler VAE-GAN training or active-learning clustering.

name: single-cell-query-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating unlabeled scRNA-seq query cells against a curated reference with known cell types, especially across datasets with batch effects, and when negative queries (cell types absent from the reference) must be rejected.

name: single-cell-query-mapping-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a reference-mapping workflow (Symphony/Harmony) scales to large atlases and need wall-clock timings of reference building, query mapping, and de novo integration baselines.

name: single-cell-rank-based-scoring
description: Use when you need per-cell enrichment scores for gene signatures (e.g., cell-type or T-cell/myeloid marker sets) on a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix, SingleCellExperiment, or Seurat object, and want scores invariant to dataset composition.

name: single-cell-rare-cell-labeling
description: Use when you already have a per-cell FiRE rareness score vector and need a binary rare-cell label (0/1) per cell via the paper's IQR-based thresholding criterion.

name: single-cell-rare-cell-type-identification
description: Use when scRNA-seq count or log-normalized expression matrices (cells x genes, e.g. .h5 with X/Y/gn/cn fields) need rare sub-populations below ~1% detected beyond global clustering.

name: single-cell-rare-cluster-reclustering
description: Use when a Seurat object contains a broadly-defined cluster suspected to be heterogeneous (low median silhouette scores) and rare subpopulations of very low abundance may be masked by standard unsupervised clustering.

name: single-cell-read-alignment-without-annotation-indexing
description: Use when starting from raw scRNA-seq FASTQs and the goal is to quantify reads mapping outside gene annotations (uTARs) to assess annotation incompleteness, e.g. across human, mouse, lemur, mole rat, or sea urchin datasets.

name: single-cell-read-barcode-assignment
description: Use when demultiplexing noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g. a 61M-read PromethION FASTQ) against a barcode list of true and decoy barcodes, and you need read-barcode assignments plus computational cost comparison across tools.

name: single-cell-read-count-simulation
description: Use when a benchmark needs simulated scRNA-seq read counts with ground-truth logFC or a co-expression-free null matrix — e.g. quantifying normalization/DE bias across expression bins or testing nonlinear confounder detection.

name: single-cell-read-downsampling
description: Use when evaluating how an estimator of cell-level quantities (e.g., allelic proportions) performs under reduced per-cell sequencing depth, using full-depth single-cell read counts to create matched low-coverage replicates.

name: single-cell-read-downsampling
description: Use when planning or budgeting single-cell mtDNA clonality experiments: the input is an analysis-ready cell-barcoded BAM and the goal is to determine the minimum reads-per-cell depth at which variant calling (MQuad) and clonal assignment (vireoSNP) remain adequate.

name: single-cell-read-labeling-qc
description: Use when raw paired-end SPLiT-seq FASTQ files need preprocessing to label reads with combinatorial barcodes and UMI, and identified-read counts/ratios must be reproduced or compared to published values.

name: single-cell-read-pseudoalignment
description: Use when raw 10x scRNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., SRR12046119/SRR12046120 Arabidopsis col0 with cDNA_introns_10xv3.idx, or human pbmc_1k_v2) must be pseudoaligned quickly and converted into raw spliced and unspliced gene-by-cell count matrices.

name: single-cell-read-splicing-status-prediction
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq reads aligned to a transcriptome need their spliced/unspliced status predicted, or when multi-gene mapped reads must be resolved to a single gene of origin.

name: single-cell-read-to-feature-assignment
description: Use when quantifying TE expression or accessibility from single-cell RNA-seq or ATAC-seq alignments (unfiltered BAM/SAM with CB/CR and UB/UR barcode/UMI tags) and a cell-by-feature count matrix is needed.

name: single-cell-reclustering-low-purity-clusters
description: Use when an scRNA-seq clustering partition contains clusters of questionable homogeneity and you need to quantify cluster purity with ROGUE and re-cluster low-purity clusters into purer subtypes.

name: single-cell-reduced-dimension-analysis
description: Use when you need to assess whether condition labels (e.g., treatment vs control) are locally imbalanced across a single-cell reduced-dimension representation before running trajectory-level differential topology or abundance tests.

name: single-cell-reference-atlas-building
description: Use when constructing a reusable integrated reference from large single-cell RNA-seq (or CITE-seq) expression matrices so that future query datasets can be mapped and annotated without re-running de novo integration.

name: single-cell-reference-atlas-model-construction
description: Use when constructing a reference mapping model for a single-cell atlas (e.g. mTCA, DISCO PBMC, pan-cancer T cell landscape) by learning gene-set score → embedding relationships with ensemble SVR, to later project query scRNA-seq data without re-running integration.

name: single-cell-reference-atlas-projection
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq clusters (e.g., a leukemia sub-cluster such as AML1_cluster1) must be assigned a healthy counterpart cell type from a reference atlas to infer lineage stage, leukemia subtype, or stemness.

name: single-cell-reference-atlas-projection
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (10x format or Seurat objects) must be interpreted in the stable coordinate system of a curated reference atlas, or when cell subtype composition of a query condition must be quantified and compared.

name: single-cell-reference-based-purity-scoring
description: Use when evaluating a segmentation method's cell-gene matrix for expression purity or cross-cell contamination, e.g. measuring B cells expressing T-cell markers (CD4, CD8A, CD8B, CD3D, CD3E) in Xenium breast cancer data.

name: single-cell-reference-based-segmentation-annotation
description: Use when reproducing or extending the cross-platform generalisability benchmark of BIDCell on CosMx or MERSCOPE data, or when single-cell reference data are needed to guide biologically-informed segmentation and assess B-cell/T-cell marker contamination.

name: single-cell-reference-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when segmenting subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. Xenium breast cancer) with BIDCell and a single-cell reference plus marker files are needed to pre-annotate cells for biologically-informed training or cross-replicate cell type proportion comparison.

name: single-cell-reference-deconvolution
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq ExpressionSet data must be deconvolved into cell type proportions and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference (ExpressionSet or SingleCellExperiment) with cell type and subject annotations is available.

name: single-cell-reference-mapping
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (Seurat object, e.g. .qs/.rds) must be placed into a published reference atlas space for cell-type label transfer, cross-protocol batch-effect correction, pseudotime projection, or group composition comparison.

name: single-cell-reference-mapping
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (e.g., a new 10x technology or donor) must be placed into an existing integrated reference embedding for label transfer, without re-running de novo integration on all raw cells.

name: single-cell-reference-matrix-subsetting
description: Use when building or reproducing a malignancy-classifier gene panel by intersecting pan-cancer bulk RNA-seq DE genes (e.g. TCGA edgeR top-5000 lists) with high-variance genes from an integrated scRNA-seq matrix, and subsetting that matrix into a classifier-ready reference.

name: single-cell-reference-profile-generation
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq or snRNA-seq counts with cell-type and individual labels from the same tissue as your bulk RNA-seq samples and need a reference profile for cell-type proportion estimation (decomposition).

name: single-cell-reference-proportion-estimation
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq read counts from complex tissue (e.g., 89 Fadista pancreatic islet donors) and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference (e.g., E-MTAB-5060 Segerstolpe data), and need cell type proportions to test trait associations.

name: single-cell-reference-proportion-estimation
description: Use when you have a bulk or pseudobulk RNA-seq cohort (e.g., 124-sample COVID-19 pseudobulk) plus a single-cell reference (annotated representative samples or public dataset) and need cell-type proportions comparable against ground truth.

name: single-cell-reference-subsampling
description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-querying/annotation method remains tractable as the reference dataset grows to hundreds of thousands of cells, by timing queries across a range of subsampled reference sizes.

name: single-cell-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when evaluating how well CSNI methods (e.g. pySCENIC, LIONESS, SSN) recover cell-specific regulatory interactions, and simulated single-cell data with known cellwise ground-truth GRNs is available for quantitative AUROC/AUPR evaluation.

name: single-cell-reprogramming-data-analysis
description: Use when analyzing scRNA-seq time courses of TF-mediated reprogramming (e.g., 10x Chromium data with Monocle-annotated trajectory states) to identify and rank regulators of successful fate conversion.

name: single-cell-rna-count-denoising
description: Use when raw UMI-based scRNA-seq counts (e.g., CITE-seq/REAP-seq RNA matrices, cTPnet_demo 4000-cell demo) must be denoised before protein imputation or other downstream modeling.

name: single-cell-rna-count-normalization
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq UMI counts (e.g. 10x h5/h5ad matrices from GEO like GSE117825 or Synapse syn26320732) must be converted into log CPTT-normalized AnnData before scTriangulate integration.

name: single-cell-rna-denoising-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how well a denoising method recovers true expression profiles from severely downsampled scRNA-seq data (70% transcript removal), particularly for rare cell states like pericytes, microfold cells, or microglial cells.

name: single-cell-rna-expression-classification
description: Use when you have labeled cell-by-gene single-cell RNA-seq matrices (AnnData .h5ad or CSV) with a 'class_label' annotation and need automated label transfer to unlabeled cells, especially with many cell types or imbalanced labels.

name: single-cell-rna-label-transfer
description: Use when you need to transfer cell-type annotations from a labeled single-cell RNA-seq reference (e.g., .h5ad AnnData with a 'class_label' column) to unlabeled query cells, even across datasets with different gene panels or cell lines.

name: single-cell-rna-reference-mapping
description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq reference (e.g., Allen Institute cortical taxonomy or Whole_miniatlas_meta.csv BRCA annotations) must be projected onto a 10x Visium slice to resolve per-spot cell-type composition and localize structures like TLS or cortical layers.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a cell-type or cell-state classifier trained on scRNA-seq data (.h5ad anndata, e.g. PBMCs-BS top-3,500 scaLR features) must be scored on a held-out test set, or when benchmarking prediction accuracy across annotation pipelines.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-alignment-and-pcr-duplicate-removal
description: Use when input is full-length scRNA-seq FASTQ data (e.g., SMART-seq2, such as the E-MTAB-9801 human fetal bone marrow dataset) and per-cell sorted BAM alignments free of PCR duplicates are needed for downstream isoform/IPA analysis.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-anchor-based-integration
description: Use when multiple scRNA-seq samples or datasets need batch correction and integration, and prior (even partial or noisy) cell type annotations are available to preserve biological variance.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating or comparing cell-type annotation methods on scRNA-seq data with simulated ground-truth labels, or when deciding between EasyCellType-style marker-database querying and supervised tools like scPred or SingleR.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing wall-clock runtime or novel-cell-detection performance of scRNA-seq annotation tools as dataset size grows from ~1k to million-scale cells, e.g. showing whether a tool scales efficiently versus scmap-cluster/scPred.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-subsampling-replicates
description: Use when comparing the wall-clock runtime of cell-cell interaction inference methods (dsCellNet, NATMI, CellPhoneDB, SingleCellSignalR) on identically sized scRNA-seq inputs, and the original dataset cell count differs from or exceeds the target benchmark size.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when raw or normalized scRNA-seq/spatial count data (Seurat object or count matrix) needs automated cell type labels, and marker-based annotation with interpretable top marker genes per cluster is required.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating newly sequenced scRNA-seq cells or clusters against labeled reference data (e.g., human pancreas, PBMC, Tabula Muris), or when benchmarking cross-platform classification against Seurat v3 and scmap.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating human single-cell RNA-seq cells with standardized, ontology-grounded cell type labels without supplying marker genes or a user-labeled training set, especially when uncertain cells should be placed at ancestral ontology nodes.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating cells from cancer scRNA-seq data (counts matrix, Seurat object, h5, or 10X folder) into tumor microenvironment major cell types and subtypes, or when benchmarking annotation accuracy against original study labels.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-classification
description: Use when training or evaluating cross-tissue scRNA-seq cell type classifiers on the CELLxGENE census (e.g., scaling 1.7M vs 16.2M-parameter scTab models) and reporting macro F1-score on held-out donors.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-classification
description: Use when gene-by-cell count matrices from tumour biopsies need cell-type labels across cancer, immune, and stromal populations, especially when CNV inference alone is insufficient or the tissue of origin is unknown.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-classification
description: Use when classifying cell types in scRNA-seq data without aligning reads to a reference genome, or when benchmarking compressed k-mer group (CKG) features against gene expression features with standard classifiers.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-classification
description: Use when cell-type labels must be transferred from a labeled scRNA-seq training set to an independent test set — especially cross-dataset (e.g. Baron, Segerstolpe, Muraro, Xin, Wang pancreas data) — or when benchmarking a classifier against ML baselines.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-classification
description: Use when labeled scRNA-seq expression datasets (e.g. Zheng sorted, Pancreas, CellBench) need supervised cell-type classification with a deep learning model, and when overall test accuracy must be benchmarked or reproduced.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cell-type-subsetting
description: Use when building or benchmarking GRN inference methods on snRNA-seq data where a specific cell type must be isolated from an annotated single-cell object and split into train/test sets to assess network generalization.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cluster-mean-aggregation
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-to-cluster annotations and need pseudo-bulk per-cluster average profiles as input to a transcriptome-based cell-cell communication framework.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-cluster-significance-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq data have been log-cpm normalised with a tentative high-resolution Leiden clustering producing deliberate over-clustering, and you need to determine which cluster pairs are not significantly different so they can be merged.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices need unsupervised clustering into cell populations, especially when batch effects are present but batch labels are unavailable or should not be explicitly supplied.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-clustering
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals (e.g., 10x Genomics Chromium droplet data) must be clustered into K cell types while correcting batch effects and unbalanced sequencing depth across donors.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-clustering-annotation
description: Use when a published 10x Chromium MEF-to-iEP reprogramming scRNA-seq count matrix must be reprocessed into PAGA clusters with marker-based annotation of fibroblast, transition, dead-end, and reprogrammed iEP states.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantitatively compare scRNA-seq clustering methods against ground-truth cell-type annotations on datasets with 15-30k cells, using ARI/AMI/NMI and number-of-cluster accuracy metrics.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-clustering-stability-analysis
description: Use when you have raw vs. imputed scRNA-seq expression matrices with known cell-type labels and must quantify whether imputation improves or distorts cell clustering quality and gene-level dispersion.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-confounder-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression matrices contain unmeasured confounders (e.g. cell cycle, batch) and a set of annotated control genes is available; benchmark against PCA, LMM, RUV, scLVM.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-data-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic scRNA-Seq datasets with known cell-type labels to benchmark clustering or transfer-learning methods, especially across controlled source-target cell-type overlap scenarios.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-emulation
description: Use when simulated molecular abundances must be transformed into a count matrix whose library sizes, fraction of zeros, and mean-variance behaviour match a real single-cell omics reference dataset for benchmarking.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-imputation
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI counts (e.g., UC mucosa cells) need denoised/imputed expression values via the scPhere decoder, and when dropouts must be reduced without introducing false-positive expression of marker genes.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-loading
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. .h5ad, PBMC interferon-beta or TICA subsets) for GeneVector, which requires raw (unnormalized) counts in AnnData .X before discretize_genes() and GeneVectorDataset construction.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-matrix-loading
description: Use when starting an scRNAseq analysis from raw benchmark count data (Zhengmix, SCMixology) and a SingleCellExperiment object with a standardized feature set is needed before dimension reduction with corral or glmPCA.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when starting from a raw scRNA-seq read count matrix (Rds/CSV of genes x cells, e.g., Fluidigm C1 alpha cells) that must be gene-filtered, covariate-annotated, and formatted before surrogate-variable or marker-gene analysis.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-matrix-quality-comparison
description: Use when a simulated scRNA-seq count matrix must be shown to have data characteristics (library size, zero fraction, dispersion, correlations) matching a real reference count matrix.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-matrix-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., data1-data5 scenarios with defined zero-inflation levels) to benchmark dimensionality-reduction or clustering methods before running them on real data.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-normalization
description: Use when a sparsely-connected autoencoder (SCA) or similar cluster-level analysis must be run on a raw UMI counts matrix and you need to test whether input normalization changes cluster quality metrics or near-threshold cluster calls.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-preprocessing
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., AnnData .h5ad from a multi-batch atlas like the NEURIPS bone marrow challenge) must be cleaned, normalized to 10000 counts per cell, log1p-transformed, and reduced to highly variable genes before topic-model or VAE training.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., Mouse Cell Atlas bone marrow) must be converted into SINGE-compatible .mat files with expression matrix X, gene_list, pseudotimes, and an optional TF-only regix before GLG network inference.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-simulation
description: Use when you need controlled scRNA-seq test data with known per-cell circadian phases to benchmark phase-inference algorithms or study how library size and sampling design affect phase-estimation error.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-simulation
description: Use when you need a synthetic sparse count matrix with a known perturbation (e.g., swapped genes) to validate whether a comparative GRN workflow detects true signal without spurious findings.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-simulation
description: Use when you need gold-standard scRNA-seq count matrices with known population structure, DE genes, or parameter ground truth to benchmark clustering/DE methods or to plan experiments for rare-population detection.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-count-simulation
description: Use when you need controlled synthetic two-batch scRNA-seq benchmarks with known batch-effect magnitude, dropout rates, batch sizes, or cell-type composition for evaluating integration or batch-correction methods.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-covariate-modeling
description: Use when an (HTOs x droplets) count matrix and the total number of genes detected per droplet are both available, and more accurate probabilistic droplet assignment is needed than a naive HTO-only model provides.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-harmonization
description: Use when cell-type labels must be compared across two or more scRNA-seq studies with matching labels (e.g., excitatory vs inhibitory neurons), and you need quantitative AUROC evidence of cross-study replicability.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
description: Use when evaluating a cluster-purity metric (e.g., ROGUE) against sequencing-depth differences or cell-number variation, by generating simulated replicate scRNA-seq mixtures with known ground-truth purity.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
description: Use when you must benchmark cross-timepoint cell annotation methods under controlled scenarios (shifted compositions, disappearing or emerging cell types) with ground-truth labels and Monte Carlo replicates.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction or clustering tools requires ground-truth labels plus controlled sparsity and CV of TGC, e.g. testing robustness to >90% zeros and dropout-driven variability.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking spatial subpopulation or spatial-domain methods against a known truth: simulated paired scRNA-seq/ST data with ground-truth subcluster labels are needed for ARI-style evaluation.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking scalability of a single-cell method: you have a cell x gene expression matrix (e.g., PBMC Multiome from the Human Blood Atlas) and need runtime vs. cell-number measurements on nested subsamples.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-data-subsetting
description: Use when building synthetic rare-cell detection benchmarks by subsampling known cell types from a large scRNA-seq expression matrix, or when probing how few DE genes preserve rare-cell identity.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-integration
description: Use when two raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g. 10X PBMC 8k and Pan T cells) need batch integration in gene space, with quality judged by mean iLISI and mean 50-RNN metrics.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-mapping
description: Use when two library-depth-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrices (e.g. TPM/CPM gene-by-cell data frames) exist, one with known reference clusters, and target cells must be assigned to equivalent reference cell types, especially with batch effect or imbalanced cell numbers/library sizes.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-splitting
description: Use when training a FAVA VAE (or similar latent-space model) on single-cell RNA-seq data and you need to demonstrate the model generalizes to unseen cells rather than memorizing the training set.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dataset-subsampling
description: Use when comparing cell type matching methods (e.g., TACTiCS vs SAMap) whose reference performances were computed on differently sized datasets, and you need equal-sized per-species subsets to control for dataset size effects.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-deep-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data have already been embedded by a pre-trained graph autoencoder and cell-level cluster labels are needed, with simultaneous learning of embedding and cluster assignment.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when two or more single-cell groups (e.g., cells assigned to mtDNA variants/clones by MQuad+vireoSNP) need to be compared transcriptomically to report up-/down-regulated genes with adjusted p-value cutoffs.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dimension-reduction
description: Use when noisy scRNA-seq count matrices (with high dropout) need unsupervised dimension reduction to 2D for cell-type visualization, k-means clustering benchmarks, or lineage/pseudo-time recovery.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dimensionality-reduction-embedding
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris FACS marrow counts) needs 2D embedding with t-SNE/UMAP and a statistically grounded, per-cell assessment of whether the visible structure is real rather than stochastic.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-downsampling
description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-type perturbation statistic (e.g., nDEG from pseudobulk DE testing or scDist distance) remains stable under varying numbers of cells per cell type in scRNA-seq data.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-dropout-imputation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix has extensive dropouts (40%-90% missing values) and downstream tasks such as cell clustering, t-SNE visualization, differential expression, or pseudotime/trajectory inference are degraded by zero inflation.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-embryo-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when you have a merged, quantile-normalized single-cell expression matrix from a temporal biological process (e.g. mouse pre-implantation stages, oocyte to late blastocyst) and need pseudotime ordering that reflects developmental progression.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-emt-lineage-inference
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g., Smart-Seq2 SCC EMT) needs attractor decomposition into multiple stable/hybrid states and quantification of transition flux through intermediate cell states between epithelial and mesenchymal attractors.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-entropy-modeling
description: Use when you need to determine whether an scRNA-seq cluster is a pure cell population, e.g. assessing purity loss from batch effects such as aggregating control and IFN-beta stimulated PBMCs or cells from multiple unrelated individuals (Kang et al., GSE96583).

name: single-cell-rna-seq-expression-binning-discretization
description: Use when a quantitative, rank-trend-based low-dimensional gene representation is needed from normalized scRNA-seq data, i.e., when binning continuous expression values into discrete levels to group quasi-trend-preserved genes.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-expression-scoring
description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type labels and need to compute, rank, or compare expression-based ligand-receptor interaction scores across CCC methods and prior-knowledge resources.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-feature-representation-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking whether feature construction/extraction methods improve the accordance between engineered cell features and true cluster labels in scRNA-seq data, measured via silhouette values against original data.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-gene-detection-rate-filtering
description: Use when a raw single-cell read count matrix is highly zero-inflated (e.g. ~70% zeros) and must be filtered to well-detected genes prior to normalization, correlation estimation, or network inference with scLink.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-global-scaling-normalization
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from a droplet-based scRNA-seq experiment (e.g. 10x cellranger filtered_bc_matrix or gene-by-cell tables) need QC, normalization, scaling and variable-feature detection prior to PCA/clustering.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-hidden-layer-representation-extraction
description: Use when a trained DL model (e.g., RFCN on the Zheng sorted scRNA-seq dataset) exists and you need its last hidden layer outputs projected into a 2D UMAP space to inspect cell-population separation by known cell-type labels.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation
description: Use when a droplet-based scRNA-seq expression matrix has a large fraction of false zeros (dropout) and downstream analyses such as cell-cell distance or correlation computation are degraded by undetected transcripts.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-imputation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix is highly sparse (>80% or even 95% zeros) and true expression levels behind excess zeros must be recovered computationally, treating all zeros as missing values.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-in-silico-data-simulation
description: Use when a runtime or performance benchmark must be repeated on controlled synthetic scRNA-seq data with the same dimensions as an existing benchmark (e.g., dataset_sizes = [1000..250000] cells × 10000 genes), especially to isolate the effect of UMI-count sparsity.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-kinetic-model-fitting
description: Use when raw UMI or non-UMI scRNA-seq count matrices must be converted into gene-level transcription kinetic parameter distributions (kon, koff, s) for simulation or bursting analysis.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-label-noise-injection
description: Use when you must quantify sensitivity of marker gene selection or cell-type classifiers to mislabeled training cells in scRNA-seq data (e.g. .h5ad AnnData with a group_by annotation column), at controlled corruption percentages for k selected markers.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-library-normalization
description: Decision support for choosing between RAW, TC, TMM, or FQ normalization before scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction (PCA, ZIFA, ZINB-WaVE), when the analysis goal is to quantify how normalization choice affects clustering quality.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-log-normalization
description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) that must be scaled by cell library size and log-transformed before embedding, similarity search, or feature gene selection.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-marker-selection
description: Use when a scRNA-seq AnnData dataset needs a small panel of marker genes (e.g., k=50 or fewer than 10% of genes) that maximize cell type classification accuracy, as in spatial transcriptomics panel design or marker benchmarking studies.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-marker-selection
description: Use when scRNA-seq data contain many cell types/tissues with overlapping DE genes and you need one global marker set that discriminates every phenotype pair (e.g., cell-type/tissue combinations in IPF, mouse cortex, or human cell atlas datasets).

name: single-cell-rna-seq-minmax-rescaling
description: Use when an scRNA-seq expression matrix is normalized but unscaled and will feed a non-negative-kernel autoencoder or neural-network feature-selection/dimensionality-reduction step that requires bounded, non-negative input values.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-multi-dataset-integration
description: Use when several independently generated scRNA-seq datasets (different labs, platforms, or batches) must be merged so cells group by biological cell type rather than by study of origin.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices must be normalized before association testing (DE, co-expression, or CRISPR screen) and unbiased, uniformly distributed null P values across gene expression levels are required.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization
description: Use when a scRNA-Seq expression matrix shows strong within-cell-type heterogeneity driven by cell-cycle genes (e.g. cells cluster by cell-cycle stage instead of cell type) and you need a corrected matrix before clustering.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (e.g. CD34_sc from MetacellAnalysisToolkit) must be normalized and embedded prior to building metacells or computing QC metrics like purity, compactness, or separation.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-scaling
description: Use when a scRNA-seq Seurat object has already been through a coarse doublet-removal (overkill) step and you need normalized, scaled, PCA-embedded data to build k-means clusters for artificial doublet simulation.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-normalization-and-scaling
description: Use when a raw Seurat object of single-cell RNA-seq data must be prepared for Connectome's CreateConnectome — i.e. before ligand-receptor z-score calculation on the panc8, ifnb, or similar annotated scRNA-seq objects.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-object-merging
description: Use when you have two or more independently pre-processed SingCellaR objects from biological replicates and need a single integrated object for downstream clustering, UMAP visualization, and cell-type annotation.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-perturbation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a differential-state method (e.g., Augur) inflates false positives as patient-level variability (tau^2) grows, by simulating null scRNA-seq data with beta=0 and comparing against scDist's calibrated p-values.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices (e.g. cancer scRNA-seq from 10X or RDS) must be quality-filtered, normalized, and scaled before cell-type annotation, malignancy prediction, or feeding an XGBoost model in scCancer2.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing single-cell count matrices (e.g., capital.dataset.setty19, velten17, paul15) for branched pseudotime trajectory inference or trajectory-tree alignment, where denoised, dimension-reduced expression is required.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
description: Use when an .h5ad Anndata from velocyto lacks imputed spliced/unspliced moments and must be prepared before running DeepCycle or scVelo-based cell cycle fitting.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
description: Use when an expression matrix (scRNA-seq counts or qPCR values) must be normalized before fitting Cyclum or before running baseline methods (PCA, Slalom, Cyclone, reCAT, Oscope, Cyclops) on periodic-process data.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw single-cell RNA-Seq expression matrix (genes x cells, FPKM/TPM) plus a per-cell sample table must be quality-filtered and normalized on a desktop/laptop before cell clustering and cell type identification.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing-and-clustering
description: Use when raw single-cell expression files must be filtered, clustered into cell-type/subpopulation labels (e.g., microglia vs. DAM), and aggregated into per-sample counts feeding a compositional differential-abundance model such as scCODA.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing-and-normalization
description: Use when a dissociated scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq matrix (e.g. AD middle frontal neocortex snRNA-seq, ~122,606 nuclei, loaded via scanpy/anndata) must be normalized before a supervised spatial-domain or 2D-location prediction model.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing-normalization
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (genes x cells or cells x genes, e.g. .h5) needs filtering and log-normalization before running rare cell detection methods such as scCAD, CellSIUS, EDGE, FiRE, or SCA.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing-normalization
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from scRNA-seq (e.g. Fluidigm C1, SMART-seq2, CEL-seq/2 or PBMC datasets) must be normalized, HVG-filtered, and standardized before clustering with DESC or similar deep-embedding methods.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-preprocessing-seurat
description: Use when a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GEO-supplied counts such as GSE141259 or the Hydra input_counts matrix) must be normalized, scaled, variable-feature-selected, and PCA-reduced before running scDEED or t-SNE/UMAP embedding.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-priming-quantification
description: Use when a snapshot or pseudotime-ordered scRNA-Seq dataset contains a multipotent (MPP/TAC) population plus two or more competing downstream lineages, and the goal is to detect lineage-primed states, rank candidate regulatory factors/pairs, and call individual primed cells.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-processing
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices from GEO deposits (e.g. GSE145926 BALF or PBMC scRNA-seq) need QC filtering, LogNormalize normalization, PCA/UMAP embedding, graph-based cluster annotation, and severe-vs-mild differential expression testing.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix of a differentiating lineage needs pseudotime ordering or linear/branched trajectory detection, and development-related GO genes plus cell-type labels (e.g. llorens_labels) are available for benchmarking.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-quality-control
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices (e.g., GSE123139 MARS-seq melanoma or GSE120861 Perturb-seq) are the input to Normalisr differential-expression or co-expression analyses and low-read/low-gene cells, sparsely detected genes, or outlier cells must be filtered first.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count data must be filtered (mitochondrial content, gene/cell detection thresholds) and normalized (TPM, log1p, HVG selection) prior to trajectory-preserving feature selection or trajectory inference.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix from peripheral blood (e.g. GSE149689 PBMCs) must be QC-filtered and normalized in Seurat prior to Harmony integration, UMAP embedding, and cell-type-level differential expression.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-quality-control-filtering
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (.csv or .parquet) need QC summarization and low-quality cell/gene removal as a preprocessing step before normalization, HVG selection, and clustering.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-quality-filtering
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., AnnData .h5ad from HuBMAP datasets) must be cleaned of low-quality cells and sparsely/ubiquitously expressed genes prior to normalization, PCA, and Leiden clustering.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-read-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking read-level scRNA-seq tools (UMI deduplication, aligners) requires synthetic reads (BAM/FASTQ) with ground-truth UMI count matrices, learned from a real BAM + GTF rather than untrained simulator defaults.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-reference-subsetting
description: Use when evaluating whether a reference-based cell type annotator can flag unseen cell types as 'Unknown': remove one cell type from the training reference and check predictions on held-out cells of that type.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when a new differential expression / differential pseudotime method must be evaluated for FDR control and power against gold-standard spike-in signals on multi-sample scRNA-seq data with pseudotime and a condition design matrix.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference algorithms on scRNA-seq data and reliable ground truth is needed, or when realistic in-silico scRNA-seq data with imposed TF-gene regulatory dynamics is required.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking pathway-analysis methods on single-cell data: you need controlled simulated two-population comparisons with a known implanted target pathway so detection sensitivity can be measured as a fraction of recovered scenarios.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when a new or existing rare-cell detection method needs quantitative benchmarking against competitors, and no real dataset with validated rare-cell ground-truth labels of controlled size and differential-expression level is available.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking how many DE genes are needed for a method (e.g. FiRE) to detect a rare cell subpopulation (~5% of cells) in simulated scRNA-seq data, or when building AUC-ROC sensitivity curves over DE-gene counts.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when a benchmark with known ground-truth cell types and latent progression is needed to compare unsupervised feature selection or trajectory inference methods on simulated scRNA-seq data.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-simulation-scdesign2
description: Use when you need a synthetic scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth trait-relevant cells (e.g., monocyte count) to quantify precision of per-cell scoring methods against GWAS-prioritized gene sets.

name: single-cell-rna-seq-umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (e.g. log-cpm normalized AnnData from scanpy) needs a low-dimensional UMAP embedding for visualizing over-clustered Leiden labels and verifying Cytocipher cluster-merge results.

name: single-cell-rna-spatial-data-integration
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq reference data with spatial transcriptomics (e.g., STARmap, MERFISH, 10x Visium) to obtain shared latent embeddings or deconvolve spatial spot cell-type proportions via an optimal transport plan.

name: single-cell-rna-velocity-baseline-evaluation
description: Use when you need to benchmark TF-based velocity estimation against splicing-based scVelo velocities, or test whether TF expression linearly explains RNA velocity on a scRNA-seq dataset with spliced/unspliced counts.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-age-binned-aggregation
description: Use when you have an aggregated multi-tissue, multi-age single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object and need to algorithmically derive cell-type-specific signatures of an age-associated cellular state (e.g., senescence) from age-dynamic expression changes.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-autoencoder-clustering
description: Use when clustering raw or normalized scRNA-seq count/expression matrices (rows = cells, columns = genes) with tens of thousands of genes or millions of cells, especially when the number of cell types is unknown and rare cell types may be present.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-batch-effect-correction
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with strong batch effects across many batches (e.g., 30 samples), when batch information is unavailable, or when scaling to tens of thousands of cells and needing runtime/memory comparisons of correction methods.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-cluster-annotation
description: Use when an unsupervised clustering of scRNA-seq data (e.g., BUSseq with K chosen by BIC) has yielded clusters without labels and you must assign cell-type identities using marker-gene expression and reference datasets such as Haemopedia.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-cluster-count-benchmarking
description: Use when a spectral-clustering similarity matrix exists for a scRNA-seq dataset and you must determine or benchmark the number of clusters without using ground-truth labels for fitting.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-cluster-purity-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq clusters need a quantitative purity score (e.g. ROGUE > 0.9 as pure) or when low-purity clusters (ROGUE < 0.8) must be detected and re-clustered into refined subtypes.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-clustering
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq dataset (e.g. severe COVID-19 vs healthy bronchoalveolar/peripheral cells, smokers vs non-smokers airway epithelium atlas) needs Seurat graph-based clustering before DE gene extraction for E.PAGE enrichment.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-clustering-and-annotation
description: Use when raw or unannotated scRNA-seq data (e.g., GEO-accessioned BALF, breast epithelial, or TNBC samples) must be quality-controlled, clustered, and assigned cell-type labels before downstream drug repurposing or per-cluster DEG computation.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq dataset with known cell type labels is available and the goal is to test whether clustering the c-CSN-transformed degree matrix (CNDM) outperforms clustering the gene expression matrix (GEM), measured by ARI.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-co-expression-inference
description: Use when you have raw UMI count matrices from scRNA-seq (e.g., a Seurat object like blish_covid.seu.rds) and need unbiased cell-type-specific co-expression networks, or donor-level differential co-expression between conditions such as COVID-19 vs. healthy.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw or processed scRNA-Seq expression matrices (e.g. hESC/progenitor populations like Chu et al.) must be prepared for network-based potency estimation with SCENT, requiring gene mapping to a signalling interaction network before computing per-cell signalling entropy.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking batch-effect correction or cell-type preservation methods and controlled synthetic scRNA-seq data are needed with known ground-truth cell types, batches, and effect magnitudes.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-data-loading-and-qc
description: Use when starting from a 10x Chromium scRNA-seq matrix processed with Cell Ranger v6.0.1 and it must be prepared as input for CellOracle GRN inference/simulation or Capybara cell identity classification.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-data-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw single-cell gene expression matrix needs filtering (min_cells=3, min_genes=200), total-count normalization, log1p and scaling before feeding into scAce or computing ARI/NMI clustering benchmarks.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-dataset-acquisition
description: Use when a benchmark or classification task requires downloading publicly available scRNA-seq datasets identified by GEO accession numbers (e.g., GSE104276, GSE108989) or supplement tables, and normalizing them per assay type before cell-type identification.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-denoising-model-training
description: Use when you need to demonstrate or verify that an scRNA-Seq denoising/imputation model's results (t-SNE patterns, ASW, ARI, MSE, zero-recovery) are insensitive to hyperparameter choices, benchmarked against DCA.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., GSE84133 Baron pancreas) and need a low-dimensional embedding that preserves inter-population centroid distances and developmental trajectory structure rather than only local neighbor structure.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-distance-estimation
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix plus per-cell metadata (condition, patient, cluster/cell-type label) with replicates, and you need a statistically rigorous per-cell-type distance between condition means rather than a differential-abundance or classifier-based.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-doublet-detection
description: Use when a scRNA-seq doublet analysis needs to boost Chord beyond its three built-in tools by appending scores from any external doublet detector to the saved chord() objects and re-running the ensemble.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-downsampling
description: Use when benchmarking computational performance (runtime, peak memory) of a scoring method across dataset sizes and you need controlled, identically sized single-cell expression matrices rather than testing only on the full million-cell atlas.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-imputation
description: Use when a log2-transformed, library-size-normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x top-1000 high-dispersion genes) contains dropout zeros that impair downstream clustering, expression recovery, or variance stabilization analyses.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-simulation
description: Use when assessing robustness of bulk deconvolution (MuSiC) to zero-inflation in the single-cell reference: apply a dropout grid to a scRNA-seq ExpressionSet, re-estimate proportions with music_prop, and score against real proportions.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-dropout-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-Seq imputation/denoising method against a known ground truth, or reproducing ablations (e.g., classifier-necessity test) that require paired dropout and dropout-free count matrices with known cell-group labels.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when an AnnData object with log-cpm normalized counts and over-clustered (high-resolution) Leiden labels needs statistically grounded merging of non-significantly different cell populations.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-feature-ranking
description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., the Mouse cortex MC/Zeisel et al. dataset) with phenotype labels and need a per-gene score to rank all features before selecting a discriminative marker set.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-feature-selection
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X pbmc_1k_v2 counts) and you need an optimal, non-redundant feature gene set to improve cluster separation and DE-gene detection before PCA/clustering.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-fusion-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating fusion gene detection performance on single-cell RNA-seq data with low sequencing depth, e.g. reproducing HVLD AUC values on K562 or multiple-myeloma scRNA-seq cohorts against competing models.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-fusion-simulation
description: Use when evaluating or comparing fusion detection methods on simulated single-cell RNA-seq data, or when quantifying how deep-learning/statistical filtering affects scFusion's precision and F-score.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-imputation-with-autoclass
description: Use when raw scRNA-Seq count matrices (e.g., simulated Splatter data, Villani PBMC, Baron pancreatic islet) suffer from dropouts, noise, or batch effects and you need distribution-agnostic imputation/denoising with downstream clustering or batch-merging evaluation.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-library-size-filtering
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. Drop-seq, thousands of cells) contains extreme-depth cells or very sparse genes that would distort downstream imputation or Gini-distribution comparisons.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-log2-preprocessing-and-gene-filtering
description: Use when raw or low-level-normalized scRNA-seq count/TPM matrices feed an ensemble clustering or feature-selection pipeline and need normalization plus removal of low-level expressed genes.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-network-analysis
description: Use when a scRNA-seq gene expression matrix must be transformed into per-cell direct gene-gene association networks, or when cell-specific hub genes/module structure (e.g., Gokce neural-differentiation hubs) need to be identified.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-normalization
description: Use when an annotated scRNA-seq count matrix must be converted to a comparable expression scale before gene selection or cell type classification, and the protocol (full-length vs UMI) dictates TPM+log1p or size-factor-10,000 normalization.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-normalization-handling
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices must be converted to a comparable feature space (sf-log1p) before training or evaluating cell type classifiers such as scTab, TabNet, XGBoost, MLP, or linear baselines.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-null-gene-set-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking whether gene set enrichment methods (iDEA, fGSEA, PAGE, GSEA, CAMERA) produce well-calibrated null p-values on zero-inflated scRNA-seq-like data, or when studying how gene set size / coverage rate affects calibration.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a normalized and scaled gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix (e.g. PBMC3k with VST-derived variable features) needs PCA followed by t-SNE/UMAP 2D embeddings in a Seurat/SCALA workflow.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-per-gene-descriptive-statistics
description: Use when comparing synthetic scRNA-seq datasets against original count matrices to quantify per-gene distribution fidelity and to expose failures such as unreproduced bimodal gene distributions.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-posterior-coverage-assessment
description: Use when you have per-cell posterior samples of a circular (24 h) quantity such as circadian phase from a Bayesian single-cell method and need to verify that credible-interval uncertainty quantifications are well-calibrated against known true phases or sample-collection times.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when droplet-based 10X Chromium scRNA-seq data (mouse aorta light-dark cycle, hepatocyte time course) must be loaded as anndata objects and subset to cell types for circadian phase inference.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing
description: Use when raw 10x scRNA-seq FASTQ files (with optional CITE-seq ADT and hashing data) must be converted to a filtered, clustered, cell-type-annotated expression matrix via a reproducible end-to-end workflow.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing-and-clustering
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrices (e.g., from liver transplant or SRA cohorts such as SRP313633) need normalization, clustering, and annotation into cell populations before downstream cell-cell communication or trajectory analysis.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing-filtering
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data (e.g., GEO datasets like GSE117872) must be cleaned prior to bulk-to-single-cell drug response prediction, and cells/genes failing QC thresholds must be removed without discarding heterogeneity.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-preprocessing-normalization
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq counts must be prepared as a log-normalized (genes x cells) matrix for full-dimensionality kernel methods (e.g. q-diffusion) that require no feature selection or dimensionality reduction.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-qc-filtering
description: Use when raw scRNAseq FASTQ/output from a time-series (e.g., GSE223109 mouse dermis) must be QC-filtered, integrated across samples, clustered, and annotated into major cell types with marker genes.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-quality-assessment
description: Use when a 10X Genomics barcoded BAM file (with barcodes.tsv.gz from outs/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/) needs per-cell quality assessment based on gene body coverage skewness before downstream scRNA-seq analysis.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-quality-control
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts (Seurat object, csv/rds/h5 counts matrix, or 10X folder) enter the scWizard workflow and low-quality cells must be filtered prior to annotation of TME cell types.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-read-alignment
description: Use when scRNA-Seq FASTQs must be aligned to hg38/mm10 for downstream TE expression analysis with SoloTE or scTE, where multi-mapping reads across repetitive elements must be retained rather than discarded.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-reference-loading
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq reference (e.g. 10x Chromium, GSE173778) and a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. 10x Visium slides) must be ingested as the starting point of a SpatialDDLS deconvolution workflow.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-reference-pretraining
description: Use when building a reference-based cell-type annotation model from multiple scRNA-seq datasets generated on different sequencing platforms and you need batch-effect-free, pre-trained weights for downstream label transfer.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-signal-filtering
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data contain a nuisance or confounding signal (cell cycle, sex, spatial zonation, batch, healthy reference) that must be removed at the gene-expression level while preserving the biological attribute of interest.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-similarity-learning
description: Use when you have a noisy single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix (with dropouts and outliers) and need a cell-to-cell similarity/distance metric for de novo clustering, dimension reduction, or 2-D/3-D visualization of heterogeneous populations.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-cycle correction or latent-factor removal methods on synthetic scRNA-Seq data, or when testing how sparse an effect (fraction of control genes influenced) must be before a PCA-based detector like ccRemover misses it.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-simulation
description: Use when you need controlled synthetic scRNA-seq data with known cell types, patients, and true condition distances to benchmark differential-state methods or test scalability.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-subclustering
description: Use when a broad Seurat cluster is suspected to contain rare subpopulations (e.g. low median silhouette score, known rare cell types like CAF subtypes absent from original annotations) and standard Louvain clustering failed to resolve them.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-synthetic-data-generation
description: Use when a small pilot scRNA-seq count matrix is available and larger synthetic data of the original study size is needed to plan downstream analyses such as clustering or cell-type abundance estimation.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-topic-modeling
description: Use when the input is a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq count matrix and the goal is to decompose expression into interpretable topics corresponding to latent biological functions.

name: single-cell-rnaseq-validation-splitting
description: Use when tuning the scSHARP GCNModel (batch size, neighbor count k, EdgeConv layer count l, embedding size e) on scRNA-seq data with upstream consensus confident labels, and you need held-out cells to score candidate configurations.

name: single-cell-rsec-clustering
description: Use when single-cell count data must be partitioned into cell-type/identity clusters that will be supplied as labels to a trajectory-inference method such as Slingshot, especially after projecting cells into a ZINB-WaVE low-dimensional space.

name: single-cell-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when a single-cell trajectory/dynamics method offers a pre-processing aggregation option for large datasets and you must quantify runtime speedup while verifying that downstream dynamical quantities (landscape, transition probabilities, path likelihoods) are preserved.

name: single-cell-runtime-memory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing runtime, memory usage, and clustering performance (ARI) of scRNA-seq integration/clustering methods across increasing dataset sizes, or quantifying device speed-up (CPU vs GPU) of a deep-learning single-cell model.

name: single-cell-sample-clustering-benchmarking
description: Use when multiple sample-level single-cell/pathomics methods must be compared on patient clustering and trajectory accuracy across many datasets with uniform metrics and statistical ranking.

name: single-cell-sample-level-prior-modeling
description: Use when you have multi-sample single-cell count data with sample-level metadata (e.g., disease status) and need a latent embedding whose sample-specific transformations are modeled as a function of condition, enabling downstream vector field and TF activity analyses.

name: single-cell-sample-metadata-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq samples already have cell-type annotations and you must attach per-sample quantitative metadata (cell-type percentages, composite niche scores, biological labels) for downstream group testing.

name: single-cell-scngs-read-extraction
description: Use when constructing simulated single-cell scWGS benchmark data that must preserve allele-specific haplotype structure, controlled phase-switch error rates, and real WGA artifacts — e.g., before evaluating BAF/phasing-based CNA callers on ground-truth events spanning 200 kb to 5 Mb.

name: single-cell-scrnaseq-synthetic-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-state decomposition or clustering method recovers known planted identity and activity patterns from synthetic scRNA-seq data with planted ground truth.

name: single-cell-senescence-signature-scoring
description: Use when scoring single-cell transcriptomes (AnnData, normalized but unscaled) for cellular senescence with cell-type-specific signatures, e.g., quantifying senescent-cell burden across ages or disease conditions.

name: single-cell-seurat-object-processing
description: Use when starting from raw or unprocessed scRNA-seq data — Seurat objects, .rds count matrices, or paired count/metadata files — that must be loaded, normalized, and clustered before cell-type annotation with the scMiko/Miko scoring pipeline.

name: single-cell-signalling-entropy-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-Seq expression matrices need potency ordering of single cells (e.g. pluripotent vs multipotent vs differentiated, developmental stage ordering, cancer-vs-microenvironment contrast) without prior marker or timepoint knowledge.

name: single-cell-signature-annotation
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data (AnnData object) must be scored or annotated for cellular senescence per cell type, or when literature-curated in vivo senescence gene signatures (e.g. Lung-fibroblast hubs) need to be extracted, searched, or merged.

name: single-cell-similarity-matrix-transformation
description: Use when a raw gene/protein expression CSV matrix (e.g. prot_expression.csv) plus class labels (target.csv) must be transformed before building the GraphDDP/GraphEmbed similarity graph.

name: single-cell-simulation-anchored-to-reference-dataset
description: Use when benchmarking differential state (DS) methods requires simulated multi-sample scRNA-seq data that faithfully mimic a reference dataset's characteristics (mean-dropout, mean-variance, sample-to-sample variability).

name: single-cell-simulation-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing annotation accuracy of marker-database-based cell-type annotation methods on data with known ground-truth labels (e.g. a simulated PBMC dataset), or when deciding which marker database (CellMarker, PanglaoDB, Clustermole) to trust for easyct-based annotation.

name: single-cell-simulation-benchmarking
description: Use when a computational method for trajectory inference, trajectory alignment, RNA velocity, or cell-specific gene regulatory network inference (CSNI) must be evaluated quantitatively against fully known ground truth.

name: single-cell-simulation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing interaction-detection performance of a new trajectory method against DE-based alternatives on simulated single-cell datasets with known ground-truth interaction labels, as in Fig 1f.

name: single-cell-sketch-sampling
description: Use when a scRNA-seq expression matrix is too large for downstream tools (clustering, trajectory inference) and an evenly covering cell subsample is needed, e.g. hundreds of thousands to millions of cells in CSV form.

name: single-cell-snn-graph-construction
description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized, scaled scRNA-seq object with variable features and PCA coordinates must be converted into a cell-to-cell SNN graph to enable graph-based (Louvain) clustering and downstream marker identification.

name: single-cell-snp-genotyping
description: Use when you have a 10x possorted_genome BAM plus barcodes.tsv from a multi-person cell mixture and need per-cell SNP genotypes to genetically separate contributors into individual-specific clusters.

name: single-cell-snv-calling
description: Use when starting from raw scRNA-seq reads (GEO SRA/FASTQ) and you need per-cell SNV calls and gene count matrices as SSrGE inputs, e.g. to build eeSNV features for cancer subpopulation identification.

name: single-cell-snv-calling
description: Use when a 10x Genomics cell-barcoded tumor scRNA-seq sample (e.g., AML patient) must be split into malignant vs non-malignant populations directly from expressed somatic variants rather than from expression clustering alone.

name: single-cell-snv-read-count-likelihood-modeling
description: Use when joint inference of a tumor clonal tree is needed from SNV read counts where bulk DNA WES alternative/total matrices must be combined with scRNA-seq counts whose zeros arise from bursting, dropouts, or non-cancerous cells.

name: single-cell-spatial-cell-type-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how well a spatial transcriptomics integration method identifies cell types or decomposes spot-level gene expression on simulated benchmarks with ground-truth single-cell assignments.

name: single-cell-spatial-coordinate-mapping
description: Use when you have a paired single-cell RNA-seq matrix and ST spot-level count matrix with spot coordinates (e.g. Visium, SeqFISH-derived ST) and need to assign each single cell pseudo-spatial coordinates or infer SC-SC spatial adjacency.

name: single-cell-spatial-dissimilarity-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq matrix (cells x genes) plus a spatial dataset with coordinates for a small set of measured genes, and need to build cost/distance matrices before solving a spatial optimal transport mapping.

name: single-cell-spatial-location-reconstruction
description: Use when a query SC dataset (e.g., .h5ad) lacks coordinates but a matched ST reference (SeqFISH/Visium-like) with truth x/y locations and overlapping genes is available, and spatially-aware downstream analyses such as co-localization or CCC are needed.

name: single-cell-spatial-reconstruction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data must be mapped onto 2D/3D tissue coordinates without marker genes or a reference atlas, e.g. BDTNP dge.txt/geometry.txt pairs where spatial fidelity should be validated against FISH.

name: single-cell-spliced-expression-aggregation
description: Use when noisy per-cell scVelo RNA velocity needs smoothing before trajectory graph construction, i.e., an AnnData object with a spliced count matrix and velocity is available and meta-cell-level outputs are required.

name: single-cell-splicing-landscape-clustering
description: Use when single-cell SMART-seq (bam or junction-file) data must be partitioned into cell subpopulations where gene-expression-based clustering fails, e.g. TNBC tumor cells, embryonic hepatoblasts, or heterogeneous tumor-associated CD4/CD8 T cells.

name: single-cell-splicing-psi-quantification
description: Use when single-cell (e.g., Cell Ranger-aligned FASTQ to hg19) exon-exon junction reads are available and the goal is to resolve modality-specific splicing-defined subpopulations not detectable from gene expression alone.

name: single-cell-sql-query-execution
description: Use when an AnnData/.h5ad single-cell dataset has been converted into an AnnSQL DuckDB database and you need to run SELECT-style SQL (including joins on layer tables) and capture results as a DataFrame, AnnData object, or Parquet file.

name: single-cell-state-binarization
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (log2(TPM+1)-style, cells as columns) must be converted into Boolean states for simulating a prior-knowledge signaling network and mapping each sequenced cell to a characteristic pathway attractor.

name: single-cell-stratified-subsampling
description: Use when you need to reduce a large scRNA-seq AnnData (e.g. the 89,429-cell mTC mouse T cell .h5ad) to a per-cell-type sketch, and you must choose or reproduce a DV-guided within-type selection strategy (FB, MTB, or TP) given the number of cell types present.

name: single-cell-study-integration-metadata-harmonization
description: Use when multiple single-cell RNA/ATAC/CITE-seq studies in H5AD format must be imported into a common queryable database and a gene's specific expression must be compared across studies to identify the annotated cell types it marks.

name: single-cell-subclustering-louvain
description: Use when a coarse cell-type annotation (e.g., 'dermal condensate') must be resolved into finer transcriptional states, and downstream tools like CellChat require state-resolved cell groups as input.

name: single-cell-subpopulation-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells need to be grouped into subpopulations using either SNV-based features (eeSNVs from SSrGE) or raw gene-expression matrices, and when cluster quality must be benchmarked against known labels with AMI over bootstrap runs.

name: single-cell-subpopulation-selection
description: Use when a processed scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-level metadata (cell type, patient outcome) must be narrowed to one cell type before co-expression network inference, e.g. isolating classical monocytes from PBMCs.

name: single-cell-subsampling-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing sketching/subsampling methods on large scRNA-seq datasets (tens of thousands to millions of cells) with metrics like runtime, Gini coefficient, Hausdorff distance, or downstream deconvolution/annotation accuracy.

name: single-cell-subtype-annotation-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking deep-learning cell annotation on tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq data, specifically to test whether major-type prediction followed by Seurat subclustering improves T/NK or myeloid subtype accuracy over direct per-cell annotation.

name: single-cell-supercell-construction
description: Use when building a GRN from large single-cell transcriptomics data (e.g. snRNA-seq count matrices from a specific cell type like microglia or whole visium data) where full-transcriptome GRN inference is computationally intractable and per-cell sparsity must be reduced.

name: single-cell-synthetic-spectra-handling
description: Use when a continuous positive separation/threshold parameter (Delta) must be tuned so that same-label samples stay closer than different-label samples in a reduced marker subspace, with accuracy on a held-out test split as the objective.

name: single-cell-te-expression-quantification
description: Use when you have 10x-style scRNA-seq BAM files (Cell Ranger CB:Z/UB:Z or STARsolo CR:Z/UR:Z tags) and need per-cell TE expression counts to study TE heterogeneity during development, reprogramming, or differentiation.

name: single-cell-te-quantification
description: Use when single-cell short-read data (10X scRNA, Smart-seq2 scRNA, scATAC-seq, Visium, multi-omics) requires TE quantification where multi-mapping reads from repetitive TEs must be accurately assigned to specific loci rather than collapsed to subfamily level.

name: single-cell-temporal-binning-factor-profiling
description: Use when multi-batch single-cell data has a continuous per-cell time axis (e.g. scVelo latent time) and you need to test whether learned interpretable factors (JOINTLY modules) show stage-specific or monotonic temporal activity.

name: single-cell-to-bulk-aggregation
description: Use when raw single-cell GEO datasets (e.g. GSE81861 CRC, GSE72056 melanoma, GSE86146 embryonic) must be converted into bulk-aggregated expression matrices to validate cell-abundance inference or run bulk deconvolution baselines.

name: single-cell-to-bulk-decomposition
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression counts from a large cohort plus snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq data from a subset of the same tissue (e.g., DLPFC), and need estimated cell-type proportions for phenotype association testing.

name: single-cell-to-bulk-transfer-learning
description: Use when you have a Miscell encoder trained on single-cell RNA-seq and a bulk tumor expression cohort (e.g., Mariathasan ICB or TCGA pan-cancer) whose clinical outcomes you want to link to latent features.

name: single-cell-to-cell-type-aggregation-nonzero-fraction
description: Use when raw single-cell expression data must be collapsed to cell-type-level sender/receiver scores per ligand-receptor pair before assembling communication tensors across multiple samples or contexts.

name: single-cell-to-spot-mapping-matrix-inference
description: Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., MERFISH) must be deconvolved to single-cell resolution by mapping each SC profile onto ST spots, after both datasets share a trained embedding space.

name: single-cell-topic-model-training
description: Use when you need to integrate and cluster large-scale scRNA-seq datasets while obtaining interpretable topic-pathway associations from a cells-by-genes AnnData matrix with batch annotations.

name: single-cell-trajectory-backbone-construction
description: Use when you have a clustering of single cells (from CLARA k-medoids) plus a low-dimensional cell embedding and need an acyclic tree-shaped trajectory topology connecting the clusters.

name: single-cell-trajectory-cell-cell-communication-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data span a developmental time course without definitive cell types (e.g., early embryo pre-blastocyst stages), and the goal is to find development-related ligand-receptor pairs whose expression co-varies or causally regulates TF activity along pseudotime.

name: single-cell-trajectory-data-visualization
description: Use when a pre-processed scRNA-seq anndata object with 'clusters' annotations and an scVelo RNA velocity field must be turned into a directed differentiation trajectory with per-population fate probabilities and terminal-state visualizations.

name: single-cell-trajectory-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you need a low-dimensional (d=2 or 3) manifold embedding and plot of single cells for trajectory visualization, starting from a preprocessed N cells × D genes expression matrix and the DTFLOW API.

name: single-cell-trajectory-fate-probability-estimation
description: Use when time-series scRNA-seq data with time-point labels and cell type annotations is available and the goal is to predict cell fate bias — the probability a cell enters a particular fate given its initial state — including under simulated perturbations.

name: single-cell-trajectory-fate-selection-testing
description: Use when a slingshot SingleCellExperiment/trajectory object exists with per-cell lineage curve weights across ≥2 conditions and the goal is to test whether condition shifts the proportions of cells committed to each lineage.

name: single-cell-trajectory-file-formatting
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has per-cell RNA velocity vectors (spliced/unspliced-derived) that must be exported alongside 3D DR coordinates so CellexalVR can visualize trajectories as animated arrows/particles.

name: single-cell-trajectory-gradient-visualization
description: Use when you need to quantify how an in silico TF perturbation (e.g., Gata1 KO) shifts simulated cell-state transitions relative to the reference differentiation gradient in a scRNA-seq trajectory dataset.

name: single-cell-trajectory-inference
description: Use when single-cell transcriptomic data from two or more conditions must be compared along a dynamic process (e.g., differentiation, EMT), and you need to decide whether a common trajectory suffices or conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection, or gene expression.

name: single-cell-trajectory-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq (or CyTOF/scATAC/imaging) data must be ordered along pseudotime and cell fates/terminal states auto-detected — e.g. rare delta cells in E15.5 pancreatic endocrinogenesis or dendritic subtypes in CD34+ hematopoiesis.

name: single-cell-trajectory-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a differentiating progenitor population must be ordered into a multi-branching trajectory with landmark states, without a priori temporal ordering of subsets, to detect branching fate decisions.

name: single-cell-trajectory-inference-with-flow-networks
description: Use when snapshot single-cell RNA-seq data spans multiple cell states (e.g., HSC-to-neutrophil/erythroid differentiation) and you need multi-state, transition-centered trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations without knowing branch counts a priori.

name: single-cell-trajectory-mapping
description: Use when new or perturbed cells (e.g. Gfi1-/-, Irf8-/-, double-KO GMP scRNA-seq count matrices) must be assigned to branches of an existing wild-type reference trajectory to quantify fate-biased allocation.

name: single-cell-trajectory-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing RNA-velocity-based trajectory inference (Cytopath) against topology-constrained baselines on a scRNA-seq dataset with pre-computed velocity and known root/terminal cell states and a known cell type ordering.

name: single-cell-trajectory-reconstruction
description: Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple stable and transitional cell states and the goal is to reconstruct trajectories between any two chosen subpopulations (e.g., HSPC-to-erythroid/GMP, B-cell/mono-DC-to-HSPC reprogramming) that linear or single-branch tools cannot resolve.

name: single-cell-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking trajectory inference or pseudotime methods (e.g., CellPath, Slingshot, VeTra, CellRank) against a known ground truth that real scRNA-seq data cannot provide.

name: single-cell-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when you have longitudinal scRNA-seq data (normalized expression, time-point labels, cell type annotations, e.

name: single-cell-trajectory-tree-alignment
description: Use when two scRNA-seq datasets each contain branching pseudotime trajectories and you need to globally compare their cell-state transition trees, or benchmark how topological/clustering changes affect alignment.

name: single-cell-trajectory-tree-inference
description: Use when you have a multi-sample scRNA-seq dataset with per-cell sample annotation and a low-dimensional embedding (e.

name: single-cell-trajectory-visualization
