description: Use when an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced counts has been fitted with UniTVelo (or scVelo) and you must render the velocity stream, latent time, phase portraits, or direction-correctness metrics to judge the trajectory.

name: single-cell-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when a latent space model (LatentVelo) has produced spliced_velocity and latent trajectories and you need to visualize dynamics — e.g., streamlines colored by latent_time, diverging trajectories toward multiple fates, or terminal-state comparisons on a UMAP embedding.

name: single-cell-transcriptional-velocity-estimation
description: Use when you have scRNA-seq expression data (e.g. GSE207943: 5501 cells x 15497 genes) plus a gene-gene regulatory mask or coexpression prior and Phenograph cluster labels, and need per-cell velocity vectors and cluster-specific regulatory interaction matrices.

name: single-cell-transcriptome-dynamics-modeling
description: Use when the goal is to infer attractor basins, cell-fate transition paths, and transition cells from single-cell transcriptome data by modeling cell-state dynamics as a Markov random walk across cell-cell and cluster-cluster scales.

name: single-cell-transcriptome-projection
description: Use when you need cell expression profiles and Cell Ontology cell-type terms to share one embedding space, e.g. to classify cells to unseen ontology terms or compute marker genes per ontology category.

name: single-cell-transcriptomic-sketching
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes/PCs) is too large for downstream clustering, trajectory inference, or visualization, and a fair, size-controlled cell subset that evenly covers the transcriptomic space is needed.

name: single-cell-transcriptomics-data-handling
description: Use when input consists of dyngen-simulated single-cell transcriptomics profiles (e.g. the 42 dyngen datasets from 14 backbones × 3 seeds) with paired cell-specific ground-truth GRNs, for network inference benchmarking.

name: single-cell-transfer-learning
description: Use when a trained single-cell embedding model must be applied zero-shot to a new tissue or species AnnData (cells-by-genes .h5ad with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' obs columns) and clustering quality on the target must be quantified against ground-truth cell types.

name: single-cell-transition-regulator-identification
description: Use when single-cell trajectory data (e.g., CellRouter multi-state trajectories) and a CLR/CellNet-style GRN edge list are available and the goal is to identify transcriptional regulators driving or mediating specific cell-fate transitions.

name: single-cell-transposable-element-quantification
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, multi-omics, Visium, or long-read data need locus-specific TE count matrices, especially when multi-mapping reads from repetitive TE sequences must be resolved beyond subfamily-level or random/-map assignment.

name: single-cell-trs-background-correction
description: Use when scoring individual cells for GWAS trait association from a Seurat scRNA-seq object — i.e., after trait-relevant genes (top 1,000 by Pearson correlation with gPASsum) are prioritized and per-cell p-values are needed (scPagwas singlecell = TRUE).

name: single-cell-trs-score-computation
description: Use when a ground-truth scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels and pruned GWAS summary statistics (e.g. monocyte count GWAS) must be scored per cell to measure how precisely trait-relevant cells are retrieved.

name: single-cell-umap-annotation-visualization
description: Use when an integrated scRNA-seq object (e.g. Human_HSPC normalized UMI matrix) needs cell-type annotation via AUCell enrichment of lineage signature GMT sets, with results rendered as a UMAP colored by assigned lineage labels.

name: single-cell-umap-clustering
description: Use when you have a per-cell TE count matrix (from scTE or scTEATAC on scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq BAMs) and need to verify that cells cluster by known identity using TE features alone.

name: single-cell-umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when running gExcite's CITE-seq/ADT analysis layer on paired GEX+ADT (e.g. 10x hashed PBMC) data and you need cell-level similarity embeddings from one or both modalities, or joint BremSC clustering inputs.

name: single-cell-umap-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when comparing whether an alternative single-cell feature space (e.g., uTAR or aTAR expression) clusters cell types comparably to annotated gene expression, via silhouette coefficients on 2D UMAP embeddings.

name: single-cell-umap-visualization
description: Use when a trained single-cell multi-omics embedding (e.g., Mowgli latent dimensions on TEA-seq, PBMC 10X, OP Multiome, OP CITE, or BM CITE data) needs 2D visualization to inspect cell-type separation, compare methods, or overlay factor weights.

name: single-cell-umi-count-matrix-filtering
description: Use when the input is a raw (unfiltered, unnormalized) gene-by-cell UMI count matrix, e.g. a Cell Ranger raw digital gene expression matrix, that must be cleaned and normalized before trajectory or downstream scRNA-seq analysis.

name: single-cell-umi-count-matrix-simulation
description: Use when simulating synthetic scRNA-seq UMI count matrices from real gene-by-cell count matrices (e.g., produced by Utility.scRNA_bam2countmat with UMI_modeling=True) to create a deduplication benchmark ground truth.

name: single-cell-umi-count-modeling
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., PBMC4k 4182 cells × 1000 highly variable genes) must be modeled with per-gene negative-binomial dispersion, specifically to estimate or refresh the inverse dispersion parameter θ during deep generative model training.

name: single-cell-umi-count-normalization
description: Use when raw UMI read count matrices from scRNA-seq (e.g., GSE120861 highmoi Perturb-seq) must be normalized at both mean and variance levels before linear association testing such as DE, CRISPR screen, or co-expression inference.

name: single-cell-unspliced-rna-layer-processing
description: Use when an scRNA-seq anndata contains spliced/unspliced count layers and downstream analysis (DeepCycle cell-cycle phase assignment, motif activity from unspliced counts) requires scVelo-computed moments.

name: single-cell-unsupervised-clustering
description: Use when clustering unlabeled single-cell transcriptomes (e.g. small organ tissue samples from the Tabula Sapiens atlas with manually annotated phenotypes) and you want to capture high-order gene coexpression interactions rather than rely on PCA/scVI reductions.

name: single-cell-unwanted-variation-filtering
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain nuisance biological signals such as cell cycle or sex effects that must be removed before downstream analysis while preserving biological signal (e.g., genes of interest in corrected HVGs).

name: single-cell-utr-enrichment-annotation
description: Use when you have aligned single-cell reads (BAM, e.g. 10x Chromium) plus a canonical GFF/GTF annotation and need novel or improved 3' UTR end calls, especially to benchmark against tools like GETUTR or UTRme.

name: single-cell-variant-allele-frequency-inference
description: Use when you have per-cell mutation VAF and coverage matrices from scRNA-seq variant calling that suffer from low coverage and allelic bias, and the goal is inferring corrected genotypes/VAFs or cell lineages.

name: single-cell-variant-calling-with-molecular-barcodes
description: Use when you have eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs and 10x Chromium BAMs from cells known to be wild-type (e.g., healthy donor bone marrow), and need to estimate per-site false-positive rates of scRNA-seq mutation calling.

name: single-cell-variant-read-count-processing
description: Use when scRNA-seq somatic SNV read counts (Rs, Xs) and bulk WES counts (Rb, Xb) must be subsetted to mutations with estimable bursting kinetics before running Canopy2 tree inference.

name: single-cell-vdj-preprocessing
description: Use when raw scVDJ-seq contigs (e.g. AIRR/contig formats) must be merged with a SingleCellExperiment GEX object and cells without complete, productive TCR information filtered out before pseudobulking or trajectory analysis.

name: single-cell-velocity-benchmarking
description: Use when you have velocity matrices from two or more RNA velocity methods plus per-cell cluster annotations and need a quantitative, dataset-wide comparison of velocity field quality via local neighbor consistency.

name: single-cell-viral-count-comparison
description: Use when scPathoQuant has been run twice on the same cellranger output with -align bbmap and -align bowtie2, and you need to test whether per-gene pathogen UMI quantifications are aligner-independent per sample.

name: single-cell-visualization
description: Use when you have tGPT feature embeddings (or another single-cell representation) plus cell type annotations in AnnData and need to render cluster/cell-type UMAPs or developmental trajectory maps (HSC→erythroid/DC-monocyte branches).

name: single-cell-web-report-generation
description: Use when a completed VISION/PhyloVision analysis object (expression + lineage + signatures) must be rendered as an interactive HTML web report for sharing and exploration.

name: single-core-compute-profiling
description: Use when comparing the computational scalability of imputation pipelines on large single-cell expression matrices (tens of thousands of cells) and needing a runtime-vs-cell-count profile under controlled single-core execution.

name: single-core-execution-time-profiling
description: Use when comparing runtime scalability of scRNA-seq rare-cell detection algorithms as input cell count grows from ~1k to tens of thousands of expression profiles, under single-core execution.

name: single-core-performance-profiling
description: Use when validating a scalability claim such as 'runtime scales linearly with the number of spatial locations': timing a method across a grid of downsampled dataset sizes (e.g. 200–3639 Visium spots, 1000–53208 Slide-seqV2 beads) on one processor core.

name: single-cpu-runtime-profiling
description: Use when a benchmark requires measuring and comparing classification/annotation runtime of single-cell label-transfer tools as dataset size scales, and elapsed wall-clock time and throughput are the primary metrics.

name: single-gene-splicing-analysis
description: Use when you need to detect, inspect and quantify known or novel isoforms for one gene at a time from long-read RNA-seq data (PacBio or Nanopore BAM), without prior knowledge of splice sites, and reproduce reported isoform counts.

name: single-layer-neural-network-weight-scoring
description: Use when you must perform feature selection for scRNA-seq classification under low resources: an .h5ad/anndata gene-expression matrix is too large to train one model on all features, so per-subset weight scoring is needed to pick top-K genes.

name: single-node-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing statistical methods for co-expression detection and needing per-method wall-clock runtimes measured on identical simulated scRNA-seq inputs on one node.

name: single-nucleotide-variant-classification-of-small-rnas
description: Use when demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be resolved into distinct features such as miRNAs vs isomiRs (or piRNAs vs siRNAs from the same locus) at single-nucleotide precision, rather than counted as a single aggregated miRNA category.

name: single-nucleus-multiomic-data-integration
description: Use when you have single-nucleus RNA and ATAC assays from the same tissue (e.g. human heart post-myocardial infarction Seurat objects: snRNA.rds, snATAC.rds, gene.activity.rds) and need a joint embedding for clustering, trajectory, or GRN inference.

name: single-nucleus-rna-seq-cell-calling
description: Use when you have a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) from a droplet-based snRNA-seq experiment and must decide which barcodes are nucleus-containing droplets versus cell-free droplets with ambient RNA.

name: single-nucleus-rnaseq-ambient-rna-classification
description: Use when a 10X raw droplet count matrix (e.g. raw_feature_bc_matrix from fresh mouse brain nuclei) shows extranuclear RNA contamination and you must decide which droplets to keep versus remove as background.

name: single-nucleus-rnaseq-data-processing
description: Use when you have a snRNA-seq (or scRNA-seq/spatial transcriptomics) count matrix for a specific cell type — e.g. human prefrontal cortex microglia — and need a directed GRN covering the full transcriptome rather than a small pre-selected gene set.

name: single-nucleus-rnaseq-decomposition
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples must be decomposed into cell-type proportions and a snRNA-seq/scRNA-seq reference with cellType and SubjectName labels is available for some individuals (e.g., the 8 paired DLPFC individuals), especially under known single-cell vs. bulk technical variation.

name: single-sample-transcriptomic-normalization
description: Use when converting a bulk RNA-seq gene x sample matrix (human gene symbols as row names, non-negative normalized values) into sample-normalized reaction activity scores (MRAS) that feed METAFlux's compute_flux step.

name: singlecellexperiment-data-handling
description: Use when single-cell VDJ/scRNA-seq data are stored in SingleCellExperiment objects (e.g. demo_sce, sce_vdj, miloR neighbourhood objects) and colData-level columns such as pseudotime or CD4+/CD8+ branch probabilities must be added, inspected, or projected onto cells.

name: singlecellexperiment-object-construction
description: Use when raw gene-by-cell scRNA-seq count data (e.g. a matrix loaded with data.table) must be wrapped into a SingleCellExperiment with a 'counts' assay as input to UCell signature scoring and downstream UMAP plotting.

name: singlecellexperiment-object-manipulation
description: Use when scVDJ-seq data (gene expression + AIRR/contig receptor data) must be combined into a SingleCellExperiment object and its assays, reducedDims, or colData manipulated for R-based immune repertoire trajectory analysis.

name: singlecellhaystack-differential-activity-execution
description: Use when you need clustering-independent detection of differentially active features (e.g. spatially variable genes in 2D spatial coordinates, trajectory DEGs, pathway activities) from continuous single-cell or spatial expression data.

name: singlecellhaystack-result-ranking
description: Use when you have `haystack` result objects (p-values per gene) and need to rank genes by significance and/or benchmark the ranked list against a curated marker database such as CellMarker.

name: singlesample-gsea-scoring
description: Use when per-cell scRNA-seq counts (h5ad AnnData) must be scored against a two-part UP/DN .gmt signature with a ranked, single-sample method, especially when sparsity blurs signal and neighbor-graph smoothing is an option.

name: singlet-doublet-classification-slideseq-spots
description: Use when processing Slide-seq (or other sub-cellular-spot, image-free) ST data where no nucleus segmentation is possible and each spot's cell count must be estimated before cell-type mapping or gene decomposition.

name: singlet-doublet-negative-label-assignment
description: Use when you have normalized per-hashtag counts plus per-hashtag cutoffs and must classify each barcode as singlet, doublet, or negative to demultiplex a cell hashing experiment.

name: singlet-doublet-negative-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when a task requires comparing HTO demultiplexing tools (HTOdemux, MULTI-seq, GMM_Demux, BFF, DropletUtils, HTOreader) by singlet/doublet/negative rates on the same hashtag dataset, especially datasets with degraded hashtag staining.

name: singlet-multiplet-classification
description: Use when a CROP-seq-style gRNA library must be assigned to cell barcodes from a filtered cell list, with singlet/multiplet distinction needed and per-guide UMI thresholds fitted automatically.

name: singscore-rank-based-scoring
description: Use when per-cell gene set scores are needed from a Scanpy AnnData object (e.g. h5ad) and cells must be scored on ranks rather than raw counts — especially when count sparsity or sequencing-depth variation would destabilize bulk-style scoring.

name: singular-value-decomposition-benchmarking
description: Use when a pipeline (e.g., JIVE) repeatedly computes only the 1–10 singular components on large matrices and you must decide whether a partial SVD replaces full svd without changing results.

name: singular-value-decomposition-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a cell-by-cell similarity matrix (e.g., a Bhattacharyya kernel over RWR diffusion distributions) must be converted to a low-dimensional embedding for visualization or downstream pseudotime ordering.

name: singular-value-decomposition-of-expression-matrix
description: Use when inferring cell-cell communication from a genes×cells scRNA-seq expression matrix with MDIC3: SVD of A supplies the singular matrix Σ needed to solve the right submatrix W=(RΣ)+A.

name: singular-value-spacing-rank-estimation
description: Use when a rank-k SVD approximation of a library/log-normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix is needed and k must be chosen automatically from the data rather than fixed by hand.

name: singular-vector-subspace-distance-computation
description: Use when benchmarking co-expression estimators on simulated data with known ground-truth co-expression structure, and you need a metric for recovery of the dominant principal subspace (e.g., top four singular vectors) beyond value-level correlations.

name: sinusoidal-autoencoder-modeling
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression should be modeled as a circular/periodic trajectory (e.g., cell cycle) to infer per-cell pseudo-time wrapped to [0, 2π], or to nominate genes by their circular-pattern magnitude.

name: sirna-class-co-production-resolution
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads from multiple biologically distinct classes (e.g., C. elegans 22G- and 26G-RNAs) derive from the same genes and must be resolved into separate per-feature count tables rather than merged.

name: sirna-off-target-mechanism-analysis
description: Use when RNA-seq differential expression results (e.g. DESeq2 output with gene_id, log2FoldChange, padj) from an siRNA treatment should be checked for cumulative down-regulation attributable to siRNA seed-region pairing in 3'UTRs.

name: sirna-seed-match-counting
description: Use when you have DESeq2 differential expression results from an siRNA perturbation (e.

name: sirna-seed-region-definition
description: Use when you have an siRNA guide sequence and need to define its seed region (e.g., mer7m8) and count guide matches — canonical or non-canonical with wobbles/bulges/3'-compensatory — across transcript/UTR sequences to interpret seed-mediated off-target effects in RNA-seq data.

name: sirna-seed-sequence-extraction
description: Use when you have a 23 bp, 5'→3' oriented siRNA guide sequence (e.g., "UUAUAGAGCAAGAACACUGUUUU" targeting rat Ttr) and need to derive the mer7m8 seed to drive seed-match counting in SeedMatchR.

name: sirv-benchmark-coordinate-comparison
description: Use when evaluating the accuracy of a long-read isoform caller with known-truth spike-in transcripts, e.g. quantifying exon-coordinate accuracy and recall of known isoforms on SIRV data.

name: sirv-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking isoform detection/quantification tools on spike-in or synthetic standards (e.g. SIRVs) with PacBio long reads, needing exact-match counts against a known isoform set and cosine similarity of abundance profiles.

name: sirv-benchmark-reproducibility-analysis
description: Use when quantifying how a VIsoQLR parameter (e.g. read threshold 0.25%–3%) affects isoform detection counts and quantification accuracy on SIRV spike-in benchmarks, or when validating a published VIsoQLR run.

name: sirv-isoform-annotation-matching
description: Use when benchmarking isoform-detection tools on a long-read dataset with a known ground-truth isoform set (e.g., PacBio SIRV reads) and you need to count how many of the 68 known SIRV isoforms each tool correctly detects.

name: sirv-spike-in-gold-standard-comparison
description: Use when evaluating the accuracy of an isoform detection/quantification method using SIRV spike-in transcripts with known isoform counts and gold-standard abundances as ground truth.

name: size-factor-log-normalization
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (h5) must be library-size corrected and reduced to ~2048 highly variable genes before imputation, clustering, or graph-based modeling as in scGCL.

name: size-factor-normalization-benchmarking
description: Use when a simulated or real scRNA-seq read count matrix with known cell-specific size factors (or ground-truth cell types) is available and you need to evaluate whether BUSseq's cell-specific size factors outperform DESeq, TMM, library-size, or deconvolution normalization.

name: size-weighted-centroid-distance-analysis
description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq embeddings and you need a data-adaptive criterion to decide which cluster pairs to merge and when merging stops, without pre-specifying the cluster count.

name: skewness-based-rare-cluster-candidate-flagging
description: Use when running GapClust on a scRNA-seq neighbour-distance matrix and you need to determine which candidate cluster sizes k (1..K) correspond to a genuine inter-cluster gap harboring rare cells.

name: skewness-minimization-via-scale-factors
description: Use when base-level RNA-seq coverage pileup data (e.g., SCISSOR TOY_data pileup matrix) is right-skewed and a log shift parameter must be chosen automatically to variance-stabilize data prior to SCISSOR global/local shape change detection.

name: skipped-composite-ipa-event-discrimination
description: Use when running InPACT's read module on coordinate-sorted BAM files to classify candidate intronic terminal exons as skipped or composite IPA events and predict novel IPA isoforms.

name: slide-seq-digital-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when input is a Slide-seq DGE plus spatial coordinates (e.g., STtools 'example data 3') and the goal is cell-type clustering and spatial cluster maps at cellular scale, comparing simple aggregation vs sliding-window bins.

name: slide-seq-spatial-data-loading-anndata
description: Use when starting from a Slide-seqV2 puck (e.g. Stickels_hippo mouse hippocampus, accession SCP815) consisting of a gene-by-bead count matrix plus a 2D coordinate file, and you need an AnnData object with spatial coordinates attached for downstream SVG detection.

name: sliding-window-base-pair-content-calculation
description: Use when you have an RNA secondary structure in CT or dot-bracket format plus a positional Shannon entropy file, and need per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed SE profiles to locate structured vs. dynamic regions of a long transcript.

name: sliding-window-cell-count-estimation
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (cells x features in an anndata object) already has an inferred branching graph and pseudotime, and you need to render a stream plot whose branch width is proportional to the total number of cells at each pseudotime position.

name: sliding-window-matrix-imputation
description: Use when a dropout-affected gene expression matrix (e.g. 'data_observed_10perc.mat') must be imputed after a distribution (Gaussian, Rayleigh, or exponential with decay parameter λ) has already been fitted to the reconstructed data.

name: slingshot-curve-weight-extraction
description: Use when a slingshot trajectory object (sds) with multiple lineages is available and you need each cell's lineage-membership probabilities as input to condiments' fateSelectionTest for differential fate selection.

name: slingshot-pseudotime-trajectory-fitting
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq matrix plus cell cluster labels must be ordered along a continuous differentiation dynamic — after an embedding choice (dimension reduction + HVG selection) has been evaluated, e.g. by Escort scoring > 0.

name: slingshot-trajectory-reconstruction
description: Use when single-cell data is expected to follow a continuous developmental or bifurcating trajectory and you need lineage/pseudotime inference, or when validating that filtering steps (e.g. doublet removal) did not distort branch structure.

name: slingshot-unsupervised-pseudotime-trajectory-inference
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data contains multiple branching developmental lineages with unknown endpoints, and you need to reconstruct trajectories unsupervised from a reduced-dimension representation rather than supervised from known progenitor/terminal markers.

name: small-orf-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when you need to test whether an lncRNA/coding-potential classifier handles transcripts with small ORFs, by benchmarking it against established methods on the species-specific sORF test sets from the LncCat study.

name: small-rna-hierarchical-classification-rules
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads must be assigned to features by ordered precedence — e.g. separating canonical miRNAs from 5'-shifted isomiRs or partial-overlap fragments — rather than counted by simple overlap.

name: small-rna-read-assignment
description: Use when assigning demultiplexed small RNA-seq reads (FASTQ) to features from GFF3/GFF2/GTF annotations, especially when loci produce multiple small RNA classes (piRNA vs siRNA) or when miRNA/isomiR variants must be distinguished by single-nucleotide precision.

name: small-rna-read-count-quantification
description: Use when STAR-aligned BAM files from small RNA-seq (e.g. hg38-mapped qualified reads) need to be converted into per-molecule read counts for six small RNA classes, or when deciding whether a read mapping to multiple loci/RNA types should be counted once or per RNA.

name: small-rna-read-preprocessing-and-mapping
description: Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ/FASTQ files (e.g. SRR5049781) must be adapter-trimmed, normalized, length-filtered, and mapped to a reference before phasiRNA phase prediction with PhasiHunter.

name: small-rna-reference-annotation
description: Use when you have STAR-aligned BAM files from human small RNA-seq data (e.g. hg38/hg19) and need to classify reads into miRNA, piRNA, tRNA, snRNA, snoRNA and circRNA classes with per-molecule counts.

name: small-rna-seq-mirna-prediction
description: Use when you have SRA accession numbers or FASTQ files of small RNA sequencing datasets and a reference genome plus annotation for a plant species, and you need to predict miRNA precursors and select credible candidates genome-wide.

name: small-rna-seq-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., 50 nt serum reads) must be processed end-to-end into per-sample RNA-type count profiles, including case-vs-control differential expression on RNAs <200 nt.

name: small-rna-seq-preprocessing
description: Use when small RNA-seq FASTQ files (demultiplexed, optionally .gz) must be reduced to unique sequences with counts before genomic alignment and feature counting in the tinyRNA workflow, or when adapter-derived degenerate bases need trimming.

name: small-rna-seq-quality-control
description: Use when raw small RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. 50 nt reads from serum small RNA kits like NEXTflex) need adapter removal, ligation-base trimming, and low-quality read filtering before genome alignment or small RNA annotation.

name: small-rna-seq-read-alignment
description: Use when quality- and adapter-trimmed single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ reads must be uniquely aligned to a customized genome index to identify small RNA loci (e.g., tncRNAs) while avoiding ambiguous multi-mapping to repetitive regions.

name: small-rna-seq-read-classification-summarization
description: Use when processing single-end Illumina sRNA-seq FASTQ reads (14–50 nt) from plant samples and you need to classify them into tRF/tRNA-half subtypes and reconcile per-species totals against published reference counts.

name: small-rna-seq-read-counting
description: Use when demultiplexed small RNA-seq FASTQ or SAM/aligned reads plus GFF3/GTF reference features must be counted into distinct small RNA classes (miRNAs, isomiRs, piRNAs, siRNAs such as 22G-/26G-RNAs, tRNA/rRNA fragments) produced from the same loci.

name: small-rna-target-prediction
description: Use when you have a set of conserved plant small RNAs (e.g. tRF-5/tRF-3 series 18–25 nt) and need to predict their putative mRNA targets and test whether targets are enriched in specific biological processes.

name: smart-seq2-alignment-deduplication
description: Use when starting from raw Smart-seq2 scRNA-seq FASTQ files that must become analysis-ready BAMs before variant pileup (e.g. for the MQuad cellSNP–MQuad–vireoSNP clonality pipeline).

name: smart-seq2-rdr-baf-anndata-loading
description: Use when input is Smart-seq2 scRNA-seq data for the BCH869 glioma sample (489 malignant + 3 non-tumour cells) already processed by xcltk into RDR and BAF matrices that must be loaded as anndata for XClone.

name: smfish-gene-imputation-evaluation
description: Use when integrating unpaired scRNA-seq with smFISH spatial data to impute and validate spatial expression patterns for genes measured in one modality but not the other, or to benchmark diagonal integration methods on held-out spatial gene predictions.

name: smoke-test-training-on-citeseq-data
description: Use when implementing or reconstructing the MarkerMap marker-selection module and you need to verify it trains end-to-end on a real scRNA-seq/CITE-seq AnnData object and returns exactly k marker indices.

name: smoking-gene-module-interpretation
description: Use when you have a DE gene list or a clustered Seurat object (e.g. smokers vs non-smokers airway epithelium) and want to find statistically enriched environmental gene modules, especially cigarette smoking, airway epithelium, or COPD modules.

name: smote-class-imbalance-oversampling
description: Use when preparing disease/stress and control tab-separated expression matrices for BoostDiff and one condition has far fewer samples than the other (below the recommended ~30 per condition or below BoostDiff's min_samples=15 default).

name: smote-minority-cell-synthesis
description: Use when preparing a reference cell-by-gene expression matrix (e.g., SELINA xx_expr.txt + xx_meta.txt) for classifier training where some cell types are far less abundant than the majority and would otherwise be ignored during modeling.

name: smote-minority-celltype-oversampling
description: Use when a scRNA-seq reference atlas has imbalanced cell-type abundances and rare types (e.g., CD4T, plasma, mast, pDC) are mis-annotated or ignored during model training.

name: snakemake-pipeline-configuration
description: Use when raw 10x 3'-end FASTQ/BAM scRNA-seq inputs must be quantified for 3'UTR isoforms via the scUTRquant Snakemake pipeline, requiring a config.yaml with target, tech, strand, whitelist, and min_umis settings plus a sample_sheet.csv.

name: snakemake-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a multi-person 10X scRNA-seq mixture (possorted_genome_bam + barcodes.tsv) must be separated into per-contributor cell clusters and genotyped VCFs via a reproducible Snakemake pipeline.

name: snakemake-preprocessing-rule-implementation
description: Use when a Snakemake workflow must turn raw FASTQ reads per (sample, seqtype, group) into trimmed, gzipped pre-processed reads plus QC reports prior to HLA genotyping or variant calling.

name: snakemake-workflow-configuration
description: Use when you need to run the circlehunter ecDNA-calling pipeline on one or more ATAC-Seq samples (simulated, cell-line, or negative-control) via its Snakemake workflow and YAML configuration.

name: snakemake-workflow-configuration-and-execution
description: Use when the goal is to run neoantigen prediction end-to-end from raw FASTQ (WES and/or RNA-seq) and produce per-sample predicted neoepitope output tables under results/<sample>/prioritization/.

name: snapccess-embedding-partitioning
description: Use when SnapCCESS variational-autoencoder embeddings of multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA/ADT) have already been generated and the goal is to partition cells into clusters and quantify clustering quality against known cell-type labels.

name: snatac-gene-activity-representation

name: snatac-seq-cell-type-activity-matrix-handling
description: Use when a pooled snATAC-seq candidate enhancer BED (e.g. 286,777 heart enhancers) has per-cell-type activity columns and you need cell-type-resolved enhancer–gene links with a generalized ABC score.

name: snatac-seq-gene-activity-classification
description: Use when the input is snATAC-seq data expressed as gene activity (not peak calls) and the goal is cell type classification or benchmarking against Pollock's snATACseq pretrained modules.

name: snn-graph-construction

name: snn-graph-manifold-learning

name: snp-based-cell-clustering

name: snp-based-mixture-deconvolution

name: snp-dataset-subsampling
description: Use when the goal is to reproduce or extend runtime benchmarks of SNP pattern miners — i.e. measuring how running time scales with number of samples n and SNPs per gene l across HOGImine (k=1, k=2), SiNIMin, and FastCMH.

name: snp-gene-pair-interaction-testing
description: Use when you have RNA-seq expression counts, SNP genotype data, a SNP-to-gene map, and sample metadata (including patientID) and need to test whether genotype effects on gene expression differ by infection condition.

name: snp-genotype-dosage-scoring
description: Use when you need to rank germplasm accessions by resistance-allele burden against a pathogen from VCF genotype data plus a curated table of resistance-SNP effect sizes, e.g. to reproduce top-5 resistant accession tables for C. gregata, F. graminearum, F. virguliforme, M. phaseolina, or P.

name: snp-informed-genome-reconstruction

name: snp-null-set-matching-maf-and-location-bin
description: Use when you have a significant sQTL catalog (sqtlseeker2-nf FDR < 0.05) and need a variant control set to test whether sQTLs are enriched in splice sites, chromatin marks, or GWAS LD hits.

name: snp-to-gene-mapping
description: Use when per-tissue significant ASE SNP coordinate sets are available and the goal is to convert SNP-level ASE calls into gene-level ASE calls, or to quantify cross-tissue overlap at the gene rather than SNP level.

name: snrna-seq-data-loading-and-object-construction

name: snrna-seq-droplet-quality-assessment
description: Use when raw 10X droplet snRNA-seq data (e.g. CellRanger output from fresh/frozen nuclei preparations) contains ambient extranuclear RNA contamination and droplets must be classified as nuclear vs background before downstream clustering or cell-type calling.

name: snrna-seq-nuclear-contamination-quantification

name: snrna-seq-rdr-baf-input-construction

name: snrnaseq-cell-type-annotation

name: snrnaseq-debris-score-interpretation

name: snv-based-chimerism-genotype-assignment

name: snv-calling-from-scrnaseq-reads

name: snv-calling-from-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a mixed-genotype or mixed-species sample (e.g. Jurkat/293T mixtures or transplant host/donor chimerism) must be deconvolved at single-cell resolution using sequence variation rather than gene expression markers.

name: snv-callset-qc-filtering
description: Use when raw breast cancer (GSE75688, SRP067248) or glioblastoma (EGAS00001001880) bulk WES and single-cell/bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files must be converted into QC-filtered somatic SNV read count matrices for Canopy2 input.

name: snv-expression-signature-cell-calling
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data from a tumor sample needs per-cell tumor/normal labels and copy-number-based calling is unavailable or unreliable (e.g., normal-karyotype AML lacking CNAs), or when validating CNA-based calls against SNV/expression evidence.

name: snv-fraction-cell-genotype-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from a mixed-cell or chimerism sample requires per-cell genotype assignment from transcriptome SNVs, especially when no distinguishing marker genes exist or marker-based calls need orthogonal validation.

name: snv-gene-expression-linkage
description: Use when you have per-cell SNV calls (e.g. .vcf-derived binary matrix) coupled with single-cell gene expression counts and need SNV-derived features that link genotype to expression phenotypes.

name: snv-gene-linkage-modeling-with-lasso

name: snv-short-indel-variant-calling

name: soft-clustering-membership-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell expression dataset has been coarse-grained into K attractor basins (e.g., K_cluster from Eigen-Peak Index or Louvain/Leiden priors) and cells must be assigned fractional membership across basins to distinguish stable from transition cells.

name: soft-clustering-probability-assignment
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data with DESC and you need per-cell cluster assignment probabilities to identify high-confidence cells or reveal pseudotemporal structure.

name: soft-thresholding-power-selection
description: Use when constructing a weighted gene co-expression network from a bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g. the 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex+hippocampus or 38-sample 3xTg-AD hippocampus datasets) and a soft-thresholding power must be chosen before adjacency and module detection.

name: softmax-pseudo-probability-cell-labeling

name: softmax-thresholded-binary-classification

name: somatic-hypermutation-status-classification

name: somatic-mutation-enrichment-testing

name: somatic-mutation-feature-engineering

name: somatic-mutation-feature-matrix-modeling
description: Use when you have COSMIC somatic coding mutation data and need to classify genes into TSG/OG categories from mutation-type features, or to predict new driver genes among unlabelled genes.

name: somatic-mutation-sample-filtering
description: Use when starting from raw COSMIC somatic coding mutation records and you need to exclude hyper-mutated samples (>2000 mutations) or restrict to primary tissues with >1000 samples before driver-gene modeling.

name: somatic-snv-indel-calling
description: Use when you have a tumor-normal pair of cleaned, aligned, recalibrated BAM files and need to detect somatic SNVs as well as INDELs for downstream neoantigen or mutation analysis.

name: somatic-snv-mutation-frequency-calculation
description: Use when you have a list of predicted driver genes plus TCGA somatic SNV calls and need to classify genes as rarely- vs frequently-mutated per cancer type, e.g. to validate a driver-discovery method against CGC.

name: somatic-snv-subclonal-frequency-analysis
description: Use when per-cell genotype matrices for somatic SNVs (from cb_sniffer or VarTrix on 10x Chromium data) exist and you need to estimate subclonal frequencies and check sensitivity against bulk VAFs.

name: somatic-snv-validation-across-donor-cohorts
description: Use when you have a panel of eWGS-discovered somatic SNVs from paired tumor/normal sequencing and need to show the variant-detection approach does not falsely call them in cells known not to harbor them (healthy donor scRNA-seq).

name: somatic-snv-variant-calling
description: Use when raw bulk DNA WES and paired scRNA-seq or bulk RNA-seq FASTQ data must be turned into mutation-by-sample read count matrices (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) of QC-filtered somatic SNVs for downstream clonal tree inference.

name: somatic-variant-cell-labeling-with-dropout-awareness
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq reads must be classified per cell as mutant or unknown for pre-called somatic SNVs, and one must reason about why wild-type calls are impossible.

name: somatic-variant-effect-annotation
description: Use when you have somatic SNV/INDEL calls (e.g., GATK Mutect2 VCFs from tumor-normal WES/WGS) and HLA typing, and need amino-acid-level variant annotation plus peptide-MHC binding/immunogenicity scoring for neoantigen prediction.

name: source-free-transfer-learning-model-adaptation
description: Use when labeled source scRNA-seq data are unavailable (privacy/storage constraints) but pre-trained source model weights exist, and target cells must be annotated including detection of novel cell types.

name: source-sink-path-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing perturbation strength of several extracted directed subnetworks (e.g., seven CAT modules) by testing source-to-sink path significance on case/control RNA-seq data and assembling a comparative table of ACEs%, combined path P-values, and DEG counts.

name: soybean-fungal-stress-transcriptomics
description: Use when you have a filtered soybean RNA-seq expression matrix spanning multiple fungal-pathogen stress conditions and need to build an unsigned coexpression network whose gene-module structure supports GWAS-guided candidate resistance gene prioritization.

name: space-informed-cell-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells must be partitioned into subpopulations reflecting spatial variation, and a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) is available to reconstruct a pseudo-space.

name: space-informed-clustering-of-scrna-seq
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been assigned pseudo-space coordinates from a spatial transcriptomics reference (Visium, STARmap, Slide-seq) and the goal is to detect spatially variated subpopulations that traditional transcriptome-only clustering misses.

name: spark-dataframe-column-sanitization
description: Use when loading a raw wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (.csv) into Apache Spark and column headers contain periods, commas, or spaces that would break Spark schema compatibility.

name: spark-dataframe-expression-reshaping
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices (.csv or .parquet) are too large for in-memory tools like Seurat or Scanpy, and downstream Spark-based filtering, normalization, or PCA requires melted tall-format or reshaped wide-format DataFrames.

name: spark-distributed-dataframe-processing
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data (tens of thousands to millions of cells) exceeds in-memory tool limits and the analysis must run on Spark with .csv or .parquet inputs.

name: spark-distributed-gene-filtering
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data has been melted to tall format in Spark and low-quality cells/genes must be filtered in parallel before normalization and HVG selection.

name: spark-executor-memory-and-core-configuration
description: Use when benchmarking or executing scSPARKL (or another Spark-based pipeline) on scRNA-seq count data in .csv/.parquet form and you must configure executor cores and driver/executor memory for the available hardware first.

name: spark-x-spatial-statistics-execution
description: Use when you need per-gene spatially variable gene (SVG) rankings from spatial transcriptomics data — e.g., a Slide-seqV2 gene-by-bead puck matrix with 2D coordinates — to benchmark against singleCellHaystack's ranks.

name: sparse-adjacency-matrix-serialization
description: Use when a pre-processed scRNA-seq expression matrix (normalized HVGs, one row per cell) must be converted into a cell-cell graph for graph-based learning, and the adjacency needs to be persisted in sparse .npz format.

name: sparse-adjacency-matrix-symmetrization
description: Use when two directed or asymmetric weighted GRN adjacency matrices must be converted to symmetric form before spectral manifold alignment or eigen-decomposition of a joint Laplacian.

name: sparse-and-bayesian-polygenic-model-training
description: Use when only summary-level eQTL statistics plus an LD reference panel are available (no individual-level expression genotypes) and per-gene GReX imputation weights are needed for downstream TWAS Stage II testing.

name: sparse-attention-entmax-implementation
description: Use when building a cross-tissue single-cell RNA-seq cell type classifier on tabular gene expression data where interpretable, sparse per-input feature attention is required.

name: sparse-binary-matrix-perturbation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq count matrix contains RMT-detected signal dimensions possibly inflated by stochastic dropout events, and a data-driven, imputation-free criterion is needed to decide which signal eigenvectors to keep.

name: sparse-cell-population-augmentation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation has been severely downsampled (e.g. 150 erythrocyte cells reduced to 13) and you need to restore the original cell count so trajectory or graph analyses recover their structure.

name: sparse-co-expression-edge-extraction
description: Use when single-cell gene expression data has been normalized (library size 10^6), genes filtered to ~500 candidates, and a sparse gene co-expression network must distinguish direct from indirect gene associations via a Gaussian graphical model.

name: sparse-count-matrix-construction
description: Use when processing 10x molecule information files from libraries multiplexed on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) and you need barcode-swap-corrected per-sample sparse gene-by-cell count matrices.

name: sparse-decoder-variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when you need an interpretable latent space for scRNA-seq where each latent dimension corresponds to a pathway, TF regulon, or cell-type gene set, and you must infer gene module activities per cell (in-sample and out-of-sample).

name: sparse-expression-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix in .csv format must be converted into the pre-processed <dataset_name>.{mat, csv} format expected by AutoImpute.py before dropout imputation.

name: sparse-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when a large, sparse single-cell expression matrix must be reduced to per-cell nearest-neighbour distance statistics (D(m,k)) so GapClust can score second-order distance changes for rare cell detection.

name: sparse-gene-coexpression-network-inference
description: Use when analyzing sparse single-cell RNA-seq count matrices where Pearson/Spearman correlations are unreliable due to excessive zeros, and you need a sparse gene co-expression network or comparison of networks across conditions/time points.

name: sparse-graph-convolution-implementation
description: Use when you have a directed gene regulatory network (e.g. DawnNet edge list) plus a gene feature matrix and must compute directed graph convolution outputs while keeping all adjacency matrices sparse.

name: sparse-graphical-model-selection-via-bic
description: Use when fitting scLink to a filtered single-cell expression matrix and you must pick the regularization strength (lda) for the sparse co-expression network objectively, e.g. via BIC rather than a hand-tuned edge cutoff.

name: sparse-grn-structure-filtering
description: Use when you have time-stamped cross-sectional (TSCS) single-cell qPCR or RNA-seq expression data from consecutive time points and need a stable, sparse, signed, directed gene regulatory network despite imprecision in estimating sample mean and covariance.

name: sparse-kmer-matrix-processing
description: Use when a sparse k-mer abundance matrix derived from scRNA-seq raw reads (BAM/FASTA via jellyfish) must be converted into reference-free CKG features because the reference genome is incomplete or insufficient.

name: sparse-linear-regression-matrix-recovery
description: Use when you have TSCS single-cell expression data (qPCR or RNA-seq) at two or more consecutive time points and need to reconstruct a directed, signed, sparse GRN driving a cell-state transition without constructing pseudo-time trajectories.

name: sparse-masked-decoder-construction
description: Use when building an interpretable VAE decoder whose latent variables must correspond one-to-one to user-supplied gene modules (GMT membership) rather than to free-form latent dimensions.

name: sparse-matrix-memory-optimization
description: Use when running RMT-based dimensionality reduction (e.g. scLENS) on whole-gene scRNA-seq matrices where eigenvalue computation exhausts CPU/GPU memory, and median-scaling with sparse storage is an acceptable trade-off.

name: sparse-matrix-minmax-scaling
description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix must be turned into bounded, normalized encoder input for scButterfly's dual-aligned VAE — binarize, filter rare peaks, TF-IDF, then scale to [0,1].

name: sparse-matrix-multiplication
description: Use when per-cell scRNA-seq count data (e.g. a Scanpy AnnData h5ad) are sparse and noisy and a per-cell mini-pseudobulk profile is needed before gene set scoring with methods like ssGSEA, singscore, or mean_z.

name: sparse-matrix-random-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking imputation methods like LATE/TRANSLATE: you hold a ground-truth matrix (e.g., example.hd5, 10,000 genes x 10,000 cells) and need a masked input with a controlled 10% nonzero rate.

name: sparse-matrix-rank-truncation
description: Use when converting a large-scale sparse single-cell expression matrix into a cell-by-pathway PAS matrix via within-cell rank statistics (UCell-style), but the dense rank matrix would exceed memory.

name: sparse-pcr-model-fitting
description: Use when fitting regression or classification models on high-dimensional, correlated omics data (e.g. transcriptomic microarrays with n << p) where sparse feature selection and strong prediction MSE are both required.

name: sparse-principal-component-regression
description: Use when regressing (or classifying) a phenotype on high-dimensional, correlated transcriptomic features where marginal-correlation screening is unreliable and you need both accurate prediction and feature-sparse, gene-level interpretability.

name: sparse-regression-coefficient-extraction
description: Use when you already have extracted gene communities (e.g. 'IC_'+tumor+'.csv' files for KIRC, LIHC, PRAD) and need a sparse, smaller gene signature per community for a classification task.

name: sparse-single-cell-matrix-handling
description: Use when scoring gene signatures on sparse gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrices (sparse matrix or SingleCellExperiment) and per-cell rank-based, dataset-composition-independent scores are required, or when reproducing ScoreSignatures_UCell numerically.

name: sparse-subspace-optimization-admm
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq analysis needs a robust cell-to-cell similarity matrix for spectral clustering of cell types, especially with high-noise, high-dropout data where pairwise-only similarities are unreliable.

name: sparse-subspace-representation-clustering
description: Use when the goal is unsupervised cell-type detection from a cell-by-gene scRNA-seq expression matrix with high noise and dropouts, or when benchmarking a similarity-enhancement step against the original sparse subspace representation.

name: sparse-subspace-similarity-learning
description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq expression matrices to identify cell types where high noise and dropout rates degrade naive pairwise similarity, or when tuning/validating SSRE's rho/lambda penalty ratio.

name: sparse-umi-count-dataset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell analysis tools and you need controlled, in silico UMI-count datasets whose shapes (cells x genes) match real or randomly generated data, especially to isolate the effect of sparsity on runtime or memory.

name: sparsity-constrained-optimization-with-slack-variables
description: Use when you need to select exactly s individual genes as markers from labeled scRNA-seq data by solving a linear program with L1 sparsity and slack constraints, rather than weighted gene combinations.

name: sparsity-driven-feature-selection
description: Use when a cell-gene expression matrix is highly sparse (e.g., ~95% zeros in scRNA-seq) and localized eigenvectors must be separated into sparsity-induced artifacts versus true biological signal before RMT denoising.

name: sparsity-induced-localization-filtering
description: Use when a sparse cell-gene expression matrix yields covariance eigenvectors that localize outside Marchenko-Pastur expectations, and genes driving spurious (sparsity-induced) directions must be discarded before signal gene selection.

name: sparsity-randomization-control-analysis
description: Use when a highly sparse (~95%) cell-gene expression matrix shows eigenvalues deviating from Marchenko-Pastur/Tracy-Widom predictions and you must decide which deviations are sparsity artifacts versus real biological signal.

name: sparsity-tgc-stratified-dataset-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq dimensionality reduction or clustering tools requires datasets whose sparsity and total gene count variability are systematically varied, isolating robustness of methods like scLENS to dropout.

name: spatial-adjacency-embedding-gene-pathfinding
description: Use when a trained STEM model (e.g. on the E1z2 SeqFISH spinal-cord trajectory with 351 genes) and reconstructed pseudo-spatial coordinates are available, and the goal is interpretable attribution of which genes drive each cell's spatial placement rather than expression-only differential testing.

name: spatial-adjacency-hit-number-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a method's inferred single-cell spatial coordinates or SC-ST mapping reproduce the true spatial neighborhood structure of cells, using semi-simulated SC/ST data with known ground-truth positions and adjacency.

name: spatial-adjacency-permutation-null-testing
description: Use when ligand-receptor interactions inferred from scRNA-seq must be validated against spatial transcriptomics — e.g. checking whether top-ranked CCC pairs occur more often between adjacent/colocalized cell types.

name: spatial-adjacency-stratification-of-cell-type-pairs
description: Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data with known cell-type labels (e.g., seqFISH mouse organogenesis, 10x Visium mouse brain) plus a source–target CCI probability matrix, and you need to test whether predicted interaction strengths track physical spatial proximity.

name: spatial-apa-gene-set-integration
description: Use when you have an stAPAminer object with DEAPA, LSAPA and SVAPA calls (e.g., ST-MOB Replicate 11) and need a combined non-redundant gene set, its k-means spatial pattern clusters, and GO terms.

name: spatial-apa-pattern-clustering
description: Use when you have an stAPAminer object with DEAPA, LSAPA, and SVAPA gene calls and need to classify genes into layer-specific spatial APA usage patterns and enrich them for GO terms.

name: spatial-apa-pattern-recognition-benchmarking
description: Use when you must stress-test a KNN imputation of spatial APA usage (RUD) matrices against artificial dropout (10%–90% spots masked or subsampled) and quantify sensitivity of spatial pattern recovery and Moran's I before vs. after imputation.

name: spatial-autocorrelation-testing
description: Use when you have spot-level coordinates and per-spot gene signature enrichment scores from a spatial transcriptomics map and need to detect whether TME signatures are spatially organized and where those structures lie.

name: spatial-axis-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have mapped single cells to spatial coordinates on a ST section (e.g. via STEM's all_coord) and need to identify genes differentially expressed along a spatial axis within one cell type, or fit spatial expression curves for landmark markers.

name: spatial-barcode-grid-aggregation
description: Use when a STARsolo digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates has too few UMIs per spatial barcode for direct cell-type clustering (Seq-Scope, Slide-seq), and you need binned Seurat objects at super-cellular resolution.

name: spatial-boundary-delineation
description: Use when spatially resolved data (Cell2location-deconvolved Visium spots or multiplexed single-cell imaging such as CyCIF/MCMICRO output) must be partitioned into communities with explicit boundaries and per-point region labels.

name: spatial-cell-type-proportion-visualization
description: Use when you have LDA-derived per-pixel cell-type proportions (theta) and pixel positions from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data and need to inspect where each inferred cell type localizes spatially, e.

name: spatial-clone-territory-mapping
description: Use when an SAW-processed spatial dataset (e.g., Stereo-seq with outUnMappedFq=1) carries expressed synthetic lineage barcodes and per-spot clone territories must be annotated and overlapped with matched bulk (GEO) and single-cell barcode annotations.

name: spatial-cluster-map-visualization
description: Use when a Seq-Scope, Slide-seq, or VISIUM spatial transcriptomics dataset has been clustered in Seurat (Step C3) and you need to visualize cell-type cluster identities across tissue coordinates, or to qualitatively compare MSSW versus simple-aggregation map resolution.

name: spatial-clustering-of-st-spots
description: Use when an imputed APA index (RUD) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data (spots × poly(A) sites) needs to be partitioned into tissue layers, e.g., MOB sections, before layer-wise DEAPA or LSAPA tests.

name: spatial-colocalization-zscore-estimation
description: Use when spot-level spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10x Visium slides of murine brain cortex or triple-negative breast cancer) must be converted into colocalized vs non-colocalized cell-type pairs to validate ligand-receptor predictions.

name: spatial-community-clustering
description: Use when single-cell x/y coordinates and marker intensities (e.g., MCMICRO-processed CyCIF data) are available and marker-positive populations must be grouped into spatial communities to delineate tumor boundaries and nested regions.

name: spatial-coordinate-based-feature-screening
description: Use when you have an expression matrix (e.g. a Visium AnnData/h5ad) with 2D spatial coordinates and want to rank all genes by non-random spatial activity, or compare SVG calls across methods like singleCellHaystack vs SPARK-X.

name: spatial-coordinate-mapping-to-brain-atlas
description: Use when an imaging-based spatial dataset (e.g., MERFISH mouse brain sections with per-cell x/y coordinates) needs anatomical registration to a reference atlas (Allen CCF 2020) to validate cell type annotations spatially.

name: spatial-coordinate-plotting
description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics gene expression matrix plus per-cell spatial coordinates and need a 2D scatter/heatmap of one gene's expression across specified cell types to validate predicted cell–cell communication.

name: spatial-data-visualization
description: Use when visualizing single-cell spatial omics data (e.g., Stereo-seq axolotl brain, STARmap, seqFISH, IMC datasets) and default color assignments from Seurat, Scanpy, Giotto, Squidpy, matplotlib, or ggplot2 produce perceptual ambiguity between neighboring, biologically distinct cell types.

name: spatial-distance-stratified-marker-expression-analysis
description: Use when you have a segmented cell-by-gene matrix from subcellular spatial data (e.g. Xenium) plus cell-type labels, and you need to test whether cell boundaries leak transcripts between adjacent cells.

name: spatial-domain-clustering-model-selection
description: Use when multiple spatial-domain clusterings (e.g. across alpha_options 0.05–0.95) must be ranked without ground-truth labels or manual ARI computation, to pick the optimal model configuration.

name: spatial-domain-detection-semi-supervised-training
description: Use when running ScribbleDom training on Visium or ST spatial transcriptomics samples (e.g. bcdc_ffpe, melanoma, human DLPFC) with either expert manual_scribble.csv or Mclust-generated automated scribbles, and you need to tune the scribble-dropout rate beta.

name: spatial-domain-identification-baseline-evaluation
description: Use when you must quantify whether scSpace's space-informed clustering outperforms existing clustering or spatial-domain identification methods on data where ground-truth subcluster labels (e.g., Splatter simulations) are available.

name: spatial-domain-identification-gcn
description: Use when you have several spatial transcriptomics slices (e.g., 12 human DLPFC 10X Visium sections) with Spoint-derived per-spot cell type proportions and need uniform spatial domain labels across slices, plus a quantitative joint-vs-single comparison.

name: spatial-domain-recovery-in-snrnaseq
description: Use when you have single-cell/single-nucleus RNA-seq data lacking spatial coordinates and a trained CeLEry spatial-domain model (e.g., LIBD DLPFC sections), and need to assign each cell to a tissue layer or spatial domain.

name: spatial-expression-map-visualization
description: Use when you need to render gene expression as 2D spatial maps keyed to spot/cell coordinates — e.g. visually validating CeLEry-predicted 2D coordinates against known spatial gradients (ERBB2, ESR1, GATA3) or inspecting VAE-generated ST replicates against originals.

name: spatial-expression-matrix-processing
description: Use when raw FASTQ reads from ultra-high-resolution ST platforms (Seq-Scope <1μm, Slide-seq 10μm, VISIUM 100μm) must be converted into a spatially annotated DGE with millions of spatial barcodes per mm².

name: spatial-expression-matrix-scaling
description: Use when a sparse APA usage (RUD) matrix from spatially barcoded ST data must be imputed using spot–spot distances derived from a scaled gene-spot expression profile (e.g., count.csv + APA.RDA inputs).

name: spatial-feature-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data (e.g. 10x Genomics Visium spots with GetTissueCoordinates) and need to identify spatially patterned genes without first defining spot clusters.

name: spatial-feature-plotting-in-heart-tissue-sections
description: Use when TF expression in spatial transcriptomics spots is too sparse to visualize directly and you need to map a regulome-level activity (aggregated GRN target genes) onto heart tissue sections to localize fibrotic regulatory programs.

name: spatial-gene-expression-pattern-visualization
description: Use when a diagonal integration predicts expression for genes absent from one spatial modality (e.g. smFISH) and you need to inspect the imputed spatial patterns and quantify their agreement with held-out measurements.

name: spatial-gene-expression-prediction
description: Use when you have paired non-spatial scRNA-seq data and spatial in situ/spatial transcriptomics measurements of a subset of genes (e.g., Drosophila embryo bdtnp.txt with geometry.txt) and need to predict spatial expression of unmeasured genes or benchmark reconstruction accuracy by LOOCV.

name: spatial-gene-expression-visualization
description: Use when a predicted cell–cell communication pair (e.g., immature B cells–fibroblasts, L5–L6 eNeurons) needs spatial validation by overlaying a specific gene's expression on cell coordinates from spatial transcriptomics data.

name: spatial-gene-regulatory-inference
description: Use when non-spatial scRNA-seq data has been equipped with a spatial cell–cell distance matrix (e.g., via SpaOTsc optimal transport) and the goal is to infer which gene in one cell affects which gene in a neighbor cell across spatial ranges.

name: spatial-interlacement-graph-analysis
description: Use when single-cell spatially resolved transcriptomics data (SRT) has been clustered and cell-type colors must be assigned so that spatially interlaced/adjacent clusters get maximally contrasting colors from a limited palette.

name: spatial-interlacement-quantification
description: Use when analyzing cellular-resolution SRT data (e.g., STARmap, seqFISH, Stereo-seq, IMC) to quantify how interlaced two cell-type clusters are, or to verify that DOI-guided colorization yields color differences proportional to spatial interlacement.

name: spatial-kde-density-weighting
description: Use when analyzing spatial transcriptomics data (e.g., 10x Visium stxBrain anterior1) to find GO/pathway gene sets whose activity is spatially organized across or within transcriptomic clusters, including high-order patterns missed by cluster-centric analysis.

name: spatial-kernel-construction-from-coordinates
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics slides come with per-cell spatial coordinates and the goal is to remove local spatial-neighborhood effects to reveal global cell subpopulations hidden by spatial autocorrelation.

name: spatial-layer-origin-assignment
description: Use when you need to recover the spatial origin (e.g., cortical layer L1–L6) of individual cells from non-spatial scRNA-seq data by mapping them onto a spatially resolved dataset with layer annotations via optimal transport.

name: spatial-mapping-baseline-benchmarking
description: Use when a supervised location-recovery model (e.g., CeLEry) must be compared against mapping baselines on the same spatial transcriptomics/scRNA-seq splits, using pairwise-distance Pearson correlation as the headline metric.

name: spatial-marker-gene-expression-comparison
description: Use when STEM (or another SC-ST mapper) has assigned cells/labels to ST spots and you need to confirm localization of a rare cell type by testing marker-gene expression differences between localized and non-localized spots.

name: spatial-marker-gene-validation
description: Use when an OT-plan or label-transfer deconvolution of a spatial slice (e.g., 10x Visium) yields per-spot cell-type proportions and you must confirm biological plausibility against layer anatomy and marker-gene expression before accepting the result.

name: spatial-nearest-neighbor-assignment
description: Use when cells with x/y coordinates from a rolled (Swiss-rolled) intestinal tissue image must be mapped onto an ordered, user-selected backbone so that along-line arc position and radial offset (wall thickness) are retained.

name: spatial-neighbor-hit-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction methods (CellContrast, SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, Tangram) on data with truth cell locations, e.g. SeqFISH mouse gastrulation sections in AnnData .h5ad with .obs[['x','y']].

name: spatial-neighbor-score-computation
description: Use when you have single-cell-resolution spatial transcriptomics coordinates (e.g., Seq-Scope mouse colon) plus a cell type label vector and need neighbor-influence scores per cell type to feed CPPLS cell-cell communication modeling.

name: spatial-neighborhood-consensus-filtering-of-spot-labels
description: Use when expert scribbles are unavailable for Visium/ST spatial transcriptomics data and an automated scribble (mclust_backbone.csv) must be derived from an initial non-spatial Mclust clustering.

name: spatial-neighborhood-graph-construction
description: Use when fitting spatial-domain clustering models (iSC.MEB, SC.MEB, BayesSpace, SpaGCN) on SRT sections and an explicit spatial adjacency/neighbor graph must be built from spot coordinates before model fitting.

name: spatial-neighborhood-label-refinement
description: Use when annotating malignant vs non-malignant regions on spatial transcriptomics spots from spot-level malignancy probabilities and image features, and neighboring spots' labels need spatial-coherence refinement.

name: spatial-neighborhood-ligand-expression-aggregation
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been equipped with a SpaOTsc-derived spatial cell-cell distance matrix and you need to quantify at what spatial distance a known ligand explains downstream target gene expression (signaling range inference).

name: spatial-nucleus-segmentation-he-images
description: Use when processing seq-based ST data (e.g., 10x Visium) that has matched H&E images, and per-spot cell counts plus per-cell spatial locations (cell_locations) are needed to resolve spot-level data (~55 μm spots) to single-cell resolution.

name: spatial-plot-rendering-scanpy
description: Use when an AnnData object with cell spatial coordinates and cell-type labels needs to be visualized as a spatial map with a custom cluster-to-color mapping, e.g., after Spaco colorization.

name: spatial-point-pattern-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic ground-truth 2D point-cluster layouts with known spatial relationships to validate or compare spatial-awareness metrics (DOI, Wasserstein, LISI, KDE-Jaccard) or spatial colorization algorithms like Spaco.

name: spatial-prediction-accuracy-evaluation-auc-rmse-spearman
description: Use when a method maps scRNA-seq cells to spatial positions and you must quantify how accurately held-out genes' spatial patterns are recovered against a spatial reference map.

name: spatial-reconstruction-benchmarking
description: Use when you have SC data plus an ST reference with known coordinates (e.g., 10X Visium h5ad spots) and must quantify how well cell spatial relationships are reconstructed versus competing methods.

name: spatial-region-annotation-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when a multiplexed single-cell dataset (e.g., MCMICRO output with per-cell coordinates and phenotype markers such as SOX10+ tumor and CD3D+ immune cells) must be partitioned into spatial subregions to quantify region composition or tumor-immune spatial relationships.

name: spatial-regularization-alpha-blending
description: Use when you already have a trained SpatialDDLS model and spot-level intrinsic predictions and want to spatially regularize proportions using neighborhood information (10x Visium spots with spatial coordinates).

name: spatial-signal-filtering-single-cell
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics slides (count matrix + spatial coordinates per cell) contain a local spatial signal that masks global cell subpopulations, and the goal is to expose those global migratory or regenerative subpopulations.

name: spatial-slice-alignment-3d
description: Use when multiple adjacent tissue slices profiled by seq-based ST (e.g., 10x Visium) must be combined into a single 3D coordinate system before cell type identification or spatially informed modeling.

name: spatial-spot-quality-filtering
description: Use when a spatially barcoded ST dataset (e.g., MOB ST from SRA SRR3382373, ~260–262 spots) is being prepared for poly(A) site identification with scAPAtrap and downstream stAPAminer APA usage quantification, and low-count spots must be excluded.

name: spatial-tile-projection-of-cell-clusters
description: Use when a spatial proteomics (CODEX) dataset has per-cell coordinates and you need to render expression-derived clusters on the tissue image and validate their spatial adjacency.

name: spatial-trajectory-pseudotime-trend-correlation
description: Use when single-cell spatial coordinates have been reconstructed from an SC-ST mapping (e.g., via all_coord on netsc2st) and you must verify the ordering is biologically faithful against ground-truth pseudo time before trusting downstream SDG/DEG calls.

name: spatial-transcriptome-cell-type-deconvolution
description: Use when you need spot-level cell type proportions from seq-based ST data such as 10X Visium, especially as the cell-type-composition input Splane requires before spatial domain identification.

name: spatial-transcriptome-slice-perturbation
description: Use when evaluating how robustly a 3D ST alignment method reconstructs a tissue stack from slices with simulated defects (rotations, flips, translations, crop ratios up to 0.25), or when reproducing the SPACEL Scube STARmap benchmark.

name: spatial-transcriptomic-deconvolution
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. 10x Visium, ST microarray, STARmap spots) must be deconvoluted into cell-type proportions using an annotated scRNA-seq reference and the datasets share only a subset of genes.

name: spatial-transcriptomic-embedding-training
description: Use when you have matched single-cell RNA-seq and spatial transcriptomics count matrices (e.g., SMART-seq SC + MERFISH or Visium ST) and need to transfer spot-level spatial coordinates or zonation information onto individual cells.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-3d-manifold-prediction
description: Use when consecutive spatial transcriptomics slices have already been aligned into stacked 3D coordinates (e.g., by Scube) and the goal is to model and visualize continuous 3D gene-expression surfaces or identify spatially varying genes in 3D.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-automated-scribble-generation
description: Use when expert-provided scribbles are unavailable for a spatial transcriptomics sample (Visium or ST) and you need to bootstrap ScribbleDom from mclust's non-spatial clustering instead of manual histology annotation.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-batch-integration
description: Use when integrating a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. MERFISH on mouse hypothalamus) with a matched scRNA-seq reference, needing batch-effect removal that preserves biological signal, or benchmarking integration methods with scIB metrics.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-batch-pair-construction
description: Use when you have an ST AnnData with truth coordinates in .obs[['x','y']] and need to train a contrastive model whose encoder representations encode cell-cell spatial proximity for downstream SC spatial reconstruction.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-cell-communication-inference
description: Use when you have spatial transcriptomics data with single-cell resolution (gene expression matrix U, spatial coordinate matrix O, cell type labels D) and need to infer which neighboring cell types regulate HVG expression and build a directional MIMO communication network.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-clustering-interpretation
description: Use when a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., Visium counts table) already has spot-to-cluster annotations (e.g., from SIMLR) and the goal is to test which clusters encode interpretable transcription-factor programs.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-colorization
description: Use when visualizing cell-type clusters from single-cell-resolution SRT data (STARmap, Stereo-seq, seqFISH, IMC) where default palettes (Scanpy/matplotlib) cause perceptual ambiguity between spatially adjacent or interlaced cell types.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-coordinate-processing
description: Use when spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv from the Figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.24452812 deposit) are available and an N x N ground-truth adjacency target is needed for STEM's spatial-relationship reconstruction.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-data-analysis
description: Use when paired spatial-transcriptomics and scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. MDA-MB-231-GFP xenograft spatial spots plus Chromium 10X scRNA-seq) must be integrated to infer spatial patterns or cross-domain gene correlations at single-cell resolution.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-data-handling
description: Use when you have a poly(A) site-by-spot matrix plus a gene-spot expression matrix and spot coordinates from spatially barcoded ST data, and you need APA usage quantification, KNN imputation, spot clustering, or imputation benchmarking against scDaPars.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-data-processing
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data (expression matrix with spot coordinates) must be processed to detect and localize TME spatial structures such as TLSs or tumor capsules using gene-signature spatial autocorrelation.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-dataset-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking computational scalability of an SRT method — e.g. verifying a claim that runtime scales linearly with the number of spatial locations on datasets with thousands or more spots or beads.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-deconvolution-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare ST deconvolution methods on datasets with known ground-truth cell type proportions, or measure runtime and peak RAM of SpatialDDLS vs RCTD vs cell2location on identical inputs.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-differential-activity-detection
description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g., 10x Visium) with an expression matrix and 2D spatial coordinates, and need to rank spatially variable genes cluster-independently or compare rankings across SVG methods.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-domain-clustering
description: Use when integrating and spatially clustering multiple SRT sections (e.g., 12-sample human DLPFC 10x Visium) into known domain counts, or when benchmarking clustering accuracy (ARI/NMI) against methods like BASS, SC.MEB, BayesSpace, SpaGCN, Louvain.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-expression-normalization
description: Use when analyzing Space Ranger count matrices from 10X Visium spots (e.g., 747 day-4 chicken heart spots from 5 hearts, 1995 day-14 spots) where spatial uTAR expression must be compared on a common log scale with gene markers such as TNNT2, COL1A1, or HBZ.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-feature-filtering
description: Use when constructing a SpatialDDLS object from paired scRNA-seq (SingleCellExperiment) and spatial transcriptomics (SpatialExperiment) data and you must define the feature set via logFC-based per-cluster filtering before simulating mixed transcriptional profiles.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-figure-reproduction
description: Use when validating cell-cell communication predictions against spatial transcriptomics data — e.g., correlating LIANA-ranked LR interactions with spot-level cell-type colocalization (Visium/SPOTlight) or neighborhood enrichment (seqFISH/merFISH).

name: spatial-transcriptomics-gene-filtering
description: Use when preparing spot-level count matrices (e.g. a SpatialExperiment with raw counts) for SVG detection or spatial clustering, where low-expression and mitochondrial genes must be removed to reduce runtime and improve p-value calibration.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-gene-imputation
description: Use when a low-plex spatial assay (e.g., 153-gene MERFISH hypothalamus data) needs prediction of unmeasured genes from a matched scRNA-seq reference across random training/test gene splits.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-gene-ranking-interpretation
description: Use when you have per-gene SVG rankings (e.g., LR_stat and rank columns from nnSVG's rowData output) and need to interpret them, select top-ranked or significant genes, or assess agreement between methods' rankings.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-malignant-region-identification
description: Use when analyzing tumor ST spot-level data to locate malignant regions against pathologist annotations, especially when comparing spot-region calls to benchmarks such as Cancer-Finder.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-malignant-spot-annotation
description: Use when you have 10x Visium spot-level count matrices (slides with suspected malignant regions) and need reference-free malignant/non-malignant spot calls without a reference or spatial deconvolution.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-network-inference
description: Use when building interpretable GRNs from whole-brain Visium or other spatial transcriptomics count matrices (e.g. mouse AD plaque/age data) and scoring network modules per spot for spatial or disease association.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-pathway-activity-scoring
