description: Use when analyzing Visium spatial transcriptomics data to identify biological pathways (gene sets) whose per-spot activity levels are non-randomly distributed across tissue coordinates, rather than testing individual genes.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-pipeline-execution
description: Use when raw Seq-Scope 1st-seq/2nd-seq FASTQ files (spatial barcodes in Illumina sequence identifiers plus cDNA reads) must be converted into DGE matrices, Seurat objects, clustering, and subcellular plots at ultra-high spatial resolution (>1M barcodes/mm2).

name: spatial-transcriptomics-preprocessing
description: Use when raw ST count matrices (10x Visium, MERSCOPE, MERFISH, Xenium) must be normalized and filtered before training CeLEry for 2D location or spatial domain recovery, or before VAE-based data augmentation.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-reconstruction
description: Use when reconstructing 2D spatial gene expression maps from single-cell expression data (e.g., mouse cerebellum slide-seq, 46,293 locations) without marker genes, and when benchmarking reconstruction accuracy vs number of CCSF components.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-reference-preprocessing
description: Use when reconstructing pseudo-space from scRNA-seq with scSpace and the candidate spatial reference (Visium/STARmap/Slide-seq) may differ architecturally from the target tissue, e.g., DLPFC vs agranular dACC lacking cortical layer 4.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-regulome-scoring
description: Use when TF expression is too sparse in spatial transcriptomics spots (e.g. Kuppe et al. 2022 myocardial infarction data) to map TF activity directly, and an inferred GRN edge list of TF-target links is available to build target-gene regulome scores per spot.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-rexel-parcellation
description: Use when you have spatial scRNAseq data (e.g., MERFISH cell coordinates + log-normalized cell-by-gene matrix) and need to segment tissue into spatial regions by comparing neighborhoods as transcriptome distributions rather than single cells.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-rgb-visualization
description: Use when you have a digital expression matrix with spatial coordinates (e.g., Seq-Scope Velocyto-format DGE from STARsolo alignment) and need to visualize marker gene sets or subcellular spliced/unspliced read patterns at sub-micrometer resolution.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-scrnaseq-mapping
description: Use when separately measured single-cell domains (spatial RNA-seq and scRNA-seq, e.g. Chromium 10X from tumor xenografts) must be aligned so that mapped points retain per-sample correspondence to their inputs, not just distribution-level similarity.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation
description: Use when validating a spatial-pathway or spatial-relevance method on ST data where no ground truth exists: simulate tissue patterns with SRTsim (or SERGIO-style scripts from the manuscript repo), plant known spatially relevant gene sets, and test whether the method separates them from random sets.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation-framework
description: Use when benchmarking or validating an SVG detection method's p-value calibration and sensitivity — e.g., measuring FPR at nominal 0.01/0.05/0.1 cutoffs, running coordinate-shuffle ablations, or building coordinate-permuted null simulations for spatially-resolved transcriptomics data.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-simulation-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when you need ground-truth-controlled ST data to test whether a deconvolution method recovers known cell-type proportions or condition-specific gene-expression changes (e.g., age-associated macrophage Cd274/Clec4d up, Coro1a down) from pixel mixtures.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-splicing-concordance
description: Use when validating that exon-level splicing changes (delta-PSI) found between brain regions in single-cell ScISOrSeq data reproduce in spatial transcriptomics data with ONT long-read alignments, e.g. HIPP vs PFC on a defined exon set.

name: spatial-transcriptomics-spot-clustering
description: Use when you have a spot-level ratio matrix (e.g., RUD APA usage from stAPAminer) plus spot coordinates from spatially barcoded ST data (e.g., MOB) and need to cluster spots, embed them, and validate clusters against tissue layer annotations.

name: spatial-tumor-microenvironment-fraction-analysis
description: Use when you have region-annotated single-cell data from multiplexed imaging (e.g., MCMICRO output) and need per-subregion fractions of marker-defined cell populations, such as Ki67+/SOX10+ or MITF+/SOX10+ fractions across tumor core, peripheral bands, or invasive-front subregions.

name: spatial-variable-gene-pvalue-interpretation
description: Use when comparing SVG calls from two methods (e.g., singleCellHaystack vs SPARK-X) on the same 2D spatial coordinates and count matrix, to identify high-sensitivity hits one method ranks poorly and produce a merged rank/p-value comparison table.

name: spatial-zonation-signal-filtering
description: Use when single-cell liver data contains a spatial zonation signal that confounds reconstruction of a temporal (circadian/regeneration) trajectory, and prior knowledge of zonated genes or a cell-to-location spatial mapping is available to define the signal to remove.

name: spatially-restrained-signaling-cell-extraction
description: Use when significant ligand-receptor interactions detected on spatially reconstructed SC data (spatialDM p ≤ 0.05) must be traced to specific cells and tissues, e.g. recovering the heart/liver cells carrying IGF2-IGF2R signals in the E9.5 mouse embryo scRNA-S1 sample.

name: spatially-smoothed-cell-type-identification-potts-model
description: Use when integrating spot-level ST data (Visium or Slide-seq) with an scRNA-seq reference to resolve per-cell cell type labels with a spatial smoothness prior, e.g. producing CellTypeLabel_nu10.csv for downstream decomposition.

name: spatially-variable-gene-detection
description: Use when you have an imputed APA usage (RUD) matrix or a gene-spot expression count matrix over ST spots and need to identify genes whose APA usage or expression varies spatially (adjusted P < 0.05).

name: spatially-variable-gene-detection
description: Use when you have a spatial transcriptomics count matrix with 2D (or 2-3D) spatial coordinates and need per-gene SVG rankings and p-values without pre-clustering cells or imposing a detection threshold.

name: spatially-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when preprocessing 10x Visium, MERFISH/MERSCOPE, or 10x Xenium spatial data as training input for CeLEry 2D location recovery: after two-step normalization, pick the informative gene panel (spaGCN rank_genes_groups for 2D location recovery) before training the deep neural network.

name: spearman-correlation-analysis
description: Use when testing whether a gene-expression signature (e.g., aggregate TMG or NMG scores from the 73/186 DEGs) is associated with a continuous drug-response phenotype such as GDSC IC50 across cancer cell lines.

name: spearman-correlation-analysis
description: Use when validating predicted per-cluster or per-lineage drug sensitivity scores (e.g. AUC_prediction.csv from scDrug --model PRISM) against an observed ordered response such as treated-vs-control cell-proportion changes, without assuming linearity.

name: spearman-correlation-benchmark-scoring
description: Use when comparing alignment methods (e.g. scTopoGAN vs UnionCom, MMD-MA, SCOT) on their ability to predict one modality from another — ATAC↔RNA on Full PBMC or ADT↔RNA on BM — from unsupervised aligned embeddings.

name: spearman-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how well predicted reaction/metabolite fluxes (e.g., from METAFlux compute_flux on NCI-60 RNA-seq) agree with matched experimental flux measurements, via rank-based Spearman correlation.

name: spearman-correlation-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing feature-imputation methods on unpaired multimodal single-cell data where held-out features (e.g. smFISH-measured genes) have ground-truth spatial or quantitative values to correlate against predictions.

name: spearman-correlation-cell-similarity
description: Use when mapping leukemia/carcinoma sub-cluster cells onto a reference scRNA-seq atlas (e.g., AML1_cluster1 onto normal BMMCs) and a rank-based, outlier-robust expression similarity term is needed as one component of a composite statistic.

name: spearman-correlation-cost-function
description: Use when implementing or re-implementing CAPITAL's dynamic-programming tree alignment and you must score candidate matched nodes between two branched trajectory trees by expression similarity rather than nearest-neighbor cell pairing.

name: spearman-correlation-dimension-reduction
description: Use when clustering large-scale scRNA-seq data with a subsampling-clustering-classification strategy (e.g. k-means on 20-80% subsampled cells) and you need a dimension-reduced feature space that retains clustering accuracy (NMI/ARI) better than PCA or raw expression.

name: spearman-correlation-feature-computation
description: Use when building the CRIT feature matrix and you need a gene-level circRNA co-expression score from paired mRNA/circRNA FPKM matrices (e.g., MiOncoCirc fpkm_matrix.csv) to quantify gene–circRNA regulatory coupling.

name: spearman-correlation-feature-projection
description: Use when clustering large-scale scRNA-seq data (e.g., tens of thousands of cells) with subsampling, and raw-expression clustering accuracy or 10%-vs-50% subsample consistency is poor; the goal is to cluster in a Spearman-correlation feature space instead.

name: spearman-correlation-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have OnClass prediction probability matrices (e.g. pred_Y_seen.released.npy, pred_Y_all.released.npy) plus single-cell expression data and need to identify or validate marker genes for seen and unseen Cell Ontology terms.

name: spearman-correlation-of-factor-loadings
description: Use when Tensor-cell2cell (or similar TCA) factor loadings must be compared against a reference decomposition or a context-level phenotype such as COVID-19 severity, and a rank-based, distribution-free agreement metric is needed.

name: spearman-correlation-protein-rna-association-testing
description: Use when you have imputed surface protein abundances per cell (from cTP-net on denoised scRNA-seq) and need to test protein-space cell-state structure, e.g., opposing CD56/CD16 gradients separating CD56bright and CD56dim NK subpopulations.

name: spearman-correlation-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when comparing denoising performance of scRNA-seq methods against a ground-truth full-depth profile, especially to test whether a method that denoises cells independently outperforms neighbor-aggregating methods on rare cell populations.

name: spearman-correlation-robustness-assessment
description: Use when you need to measure how much adding or deleting a percentage of edges in a regulatory or kinase-substrate network changes downstream activity inference, and whether the change is statistically significant.

name: spearman-correlation-trajectory-progression
description: Use when you have a reconstructed gene regulatory network (CLR/CellNet-style edge list) plus per-cell trajectory progression values from CellRouter and want to rank regulators driving or mediating specific cell-state transitions.

name: spearman-correlation-weight-initialization
description: Reference for initializing TF weight matrices when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics models, where candidate TFs (ENCODE/ChEA) need expression-correlation-based starting weights per target gene.

name: spearman-cross-correlation-lr-tf-covariation
description: Use when you have two single-cell trajectories (e.g. EPI and PE lineages from blastoid/blastocyst scRNA-seq ordered by monocle3), a ligand-receptor pair list, and RTN master-regulator results, and need to find co-varying LR–TF pairs prior to Granger causal testing.

name: spearman-distance-k-medoids-clustering
description: Use when you have simulated (or real) per-feature expression/accessibility profiles across multiple cell types and need to verify that features with shared simulated regulatory programs group into coherent profile clusters.

name: spearman-fold-difference-correlation-analysis
description: Use when validating inferred miRNA activity against measured single-cell or purified-cell-type miRNA profiles, by correlating predicted vs observed fold-differences between cell-type pairs across miRNAs.

name: spearman-global-distance-correlation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking SC-to-ST spatial reconstruction methods (e.g., CellContrast vs SageNet, CeLEry, CytoSpace, NovoSpaRc, Tangram) on test sections with truth locations, to quantify global distance-structure recovery alongside neighbor-hit and JSD metrics.

name: spearman-pearson-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing read-level coverage tracks of synthetic vs real scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq data binned into genomic windows (e.g., 1000-bp bins on chr1) to quantify simulator fidelity.

name: spearman-rank-correlation
description: Use when you have per-sample gene-signature scores and a continuous per-sample metadata variable (purity/VAF) in a pdacR dataset and need a rank-based association with rho, p-value, and n.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have per-node scores (e.g., scBONITA node importance from rule inference on KEGG networks) plus graph-derived node statistics and need to test their association via Spearman rank correlation.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing pseudotime (or any ranked) orderings between a full single-cell dataset and repeated random cell subsamples, to measure ordering robustness of trajectory-inference methods such as DTFLOW, Scanpy, or Monocle2.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a multimodal single-cell dataset (e.g., CITE-seq RNA + ADT) is available and you need to test whether an imputation or transformation in one modality makes its pairwise cell distances more consistent with distances in the other modality.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when pseudobulk 3'UTR isoform counts from scRNA-seq samples (e.g., FACS-sorted HSCs or ESCs) need to be benchmarked against bulk 3' end sequencing TPMs via rank correlation.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have ranked gene lists from two or more SVG/HVG identification methods on the same dataset and need to quantify rank agreement via Spearman correlations plus top-n (n = 10, 20, 50, 100, 200) overlap counts.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-computation
description: Use when a continuous or ordinal data matrix and response are given and you need fast, robust, nonparametric quantification of feature-response and feature-pair associations to feed a correlation-based filter (RRCT, mRMR_Spearman).

name: spearman-rank-correlation-computation
description: Use when paired CITE-seq data (ADT protein + RNA counts) is available and you need a ground-truth-based readout of whether scRNA-seq denoising improves protein-mRNA co-expression, e.g. CD3E detection vs CD3 protein.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-gene-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices need a quantitative low-dimensional cell representation built by clustering genes with akin expression-rank trends, as in scQA's LC2 module.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-network-construction
description: Use when you need a cross-dataset cell-cell similarity network from scRNA-seq expression data for a gene set (e.g. GOmouse, HVGs) as the first step of MetaNeighbor neighbor voting or AUROC estimation.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-of-enrichment-profiles
description: Use when two alternative lineage groupings (e.g., GEMLI-predicted vs. ground-truth barcode lineages) must be compared at the level of gene-category enrichment rather than per-gene lists, to quantify recovery of memory gene GO-terms.

name: spearman-rank-correlation-of-spatial-distances
description: Use when evaluating global spatial reconstruction quality of SC-to-ST mapped single-cell data — i.e., checking whether predicted pairwise cell-cell distances preserve the rank ordering of true coordinates in a query h5ad with truth locations in .obs[['x','y']].

name: species-coverage-summary-tabulation
description: Use when you need to quantify how many species are covered by oggmap's precomputed gene age assignments across Ensembl, eggNOG, or PLAZA sources, or to verify reported coverage totals before relying on shipped orthomaps.

name: species-divergence-time-correlation-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking cross-species integration strategies (e.g. BENGAL tasks) and you need to test whether biology conservation, measured as ALCS from SCCAF self-projection, degrades with increasing species divergence time.

name: species-mixing-metric-evaluation
description: Use when you have integrated single-cell data from two or more species in a joint latent space (e.g., via scVI, scANVI or SeuratV4) and need to quantify species mixing versus biology conservation to compare integration strategies.

name: species-scaling-trend-analysis
description: Use when evaluating how the number of species involved in a cross-species integration affects cell type distinguishability, e.g. detecting overcorrection of few-species cell types by nearest-neighbour methods via iso_F1 trends.

name: species-tissue-dataset-organization
description: Use when building species- and tissue-stratified sequence benchmark sets from site-level modification calls, and redundancy must be removed before balanced train/test partitioning (e.g., CD-HIT <80% cutoff).

name: specificity-stratified-aggregation
description: Use when you have a cell-level embedding score for >60k paired TCR/transcriptome cells (10x dataset) with specificity annotations (e.g., GILGFVFTL, GLCTLVAML, IVTDFSVIK, ELAGIGILTV) and want per-epitope summaries plus correlation with TCRdist similarity.

name: specificity-weighted-cell-pair-ranking
description: Use when a NATMI ExtractEdges.py output folder of per-pair specificity/expression edge weights is available and the goal is to identify the top communicating cell-type pairs or communities (e.g. Fig. 5 Tabula Muris cardiac Nppa-Npr3).

name: spectral-clustering-cell-grouping
description: Use when running Bfimpute on an unlabeled scRNA-seq count matrix and the number of cell types is known (e.g., k=7 for the Chu et al. 2016 dataset), so cells must be grouped before group-wise imputation.

name: spectral-clustering-execution
description: Use when an scRNA-seq expression matrix needs cell-type clustering via spectral clustering on a learned or enhanced similarity matrix, and clustering quality must be scored with NMI and ARI against provided cell-type labels.

name: spectral-clustering-of-2d-embeddings
description: Use when you have 2D t-SNE or UMAP cell embeddings (original and hyperparameter-optimized) for scRNA-seq data with annotated cell type labels and need an objective cluster-vs-label agreement metric such as ARI.

name: spectral-clustering-of-as-matrices
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq junction/AS matrices are QC-filtered and imputed and the goal is unsupervised discovery of splicing-defined cell subpopulations that gene-expression clustering misses.

name: spectral-clustering-of-generated-expression-profiles
description: Use when you have GAN-generated single-cell expression profiles produced by mapping spatial transcriptomics data (x1) into the scRNA-seq domain, and you need to verify or derive spatially informed structure at single-cell resolution.

name: spectral-clustering-of-single-cells
description: Use when an scRNA-seq count matrix must be partitioned into known or estimated cell-type groups before Bfimpute imputation, and the number of cell types is known (e.g., 7 for Chu et al. 2016).

name: spectral-clustering-of-splicing-landscapes
description: Use when the goal is to define unsupervised cell subpopulations from single-cell RNA-seq junction/AS data (e.g., SMART-seq BAMs), especially where gene-expression clustering fails to separate transitional states such as precancerous epithelium.

name: spectral-clustering-on-learned-similarity
description: Use when you have a gene-by-cell scRNA-seq expression matrix with known number of cell types and need cell-type clusters whose quality depends on an engineered/learned similarity matrix rather than raw expression distances.

name: spectral-community-detection
description: Use when the input is a multi-dimensional adjacency tensor (S subjects x T time points, e.g. a 16 x 8 x 500 numpy array) and the goal is to infer time-varying personalized network modules, especially when subjects share little or no apparent information.

name: spectral-eigendecomposition-of-similarity-matrices
description: Use when a cell-to-cell similarity or affinity matrix has been learned (e.g. by SSRE, SSR, MPSSC/SIMLR-style methods) and the cluster number must be estimated from its Laplacian eigenvalue spectrum rather than pre-annotated cell-type counts.

name: spectral-embedding-of-normalized-laplacian
description: Use when a cell-cell similarity matrix is available and a low-dimensional (e.g., 2D) cell embedding must be initialized before SGD-based refinement, as in EDGE on scRNA-seq data.

name: speedup-ratio-computation
description: Use when comparing imputation-method runtimes on the same expression matrix to quantify a speedup ratio, e.g. verifying that SERM is >=10x faster than MAGIC, mcImpute, AutoImpute, or DeepImpute.

name: spermatogenesis-developmental-stage-annotation
description: Use when a mouse germ-cell scRNA-seq query (WT or knockout, e.g. Zfp541-KO) needs developmental stage annotation or pseudotime placement along spermatogenesis by mapping onto the mTCA reference atlas.

name: spermatogenesis-stage-ordering
description: Use when single-cell APA data from mouse sperm cells (SC, RS, ES) should be visualized as a RUD-score gradient on 2D UMAP embeddings to reveal 3'UTR shortening during differentiation.

name: sphere-cover-thresholding-algorithm-execution
description: Use when reproducing or benchmarking the scalability of Sphetcher-H versus geometric sketching on a million-scale single-cell expression matrix (e.g., 2,026,641-cell MOCA), recording per-stage and total runtimes at a fixed sketch size such as 20296 (1% of cells).

name: spherical-vmf-latent-embedding
description: Use when scRNA-seq droplet UMI count matrices need a 2D latent embedding where cells of distinct types should not overlap at the origin, or when sparse data effectively lies on a hypersphere under cosine distance.

name: spheroid-radial-density-modeling
description: Use when transforming single-cell pseudotime from dissociated multicellular spheroids into spatial distance-from-surface coordinates, requiring a spherical-shell radial cell-density distribution as the MAPiT target.
tools: Kernel Density Estimation with Linked BCs

name: spike-and-slab-bayesian-inference
description: Use when testing covariate effects (e.g., health status) on cell-type compositions from scRNA-seq count data with few experimental replicates, and you need explicit control of false discoveries via spike-and-slab effect shrinkage rather than univariate tests.

name: spike-and-slab-bayesian-regression-implementation
description: Use when you have genetic association data across multiple traits (individual-level genotypes/phenotypes, or summary statistics with an LD matrix plus effect sizes/standard errors or z-scores and sample sizes) and need joint fine-mapping and colocalization in the presence of allelic heterogeneity.

name: spike-and-slab-credibility-assessment
description: Use when scRNA-seq cell-type counts are available per sample (especially with few replicates, e.g. 4 healthy / 3 moderate / 6 severe COVID-19 BALF donors) and you need differential abundance calls that control false discoveries under compositionality.

name: spike-and-slab-posterior-indicator-estimation
description: Use when a fitted BUSseq model is available and the goal is to detect intrinsic genes that differentiate cell types at a controlled Bayesian false discovery rate (e.g., alpha = 0.05) from posterior indicator probabilities.

name: spike-in-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a synthetic RNA-seq dataset with known ground truth (e.g. External RNA Controls Consortium spike-in transcripts) is available and you need to quantify which DEG method or combination maximizes F-measure and logFC accuracy.

name: spike-in-benchmark-fusion-recovery-analysis
description: Use when evaluating a single-cell fusion detection pipeline against a spike-in ground truth, to quantify sensitivity (e.g., 27/27 spike-ins recovered) and false discovery via bulk chimeric-read support fractions.

name: spike-in-classifier-performance-evaluation
description: Use when a trained multi-method DEG integration model (e.g. Naïve Bayes over per-gene p-value vectors) must be benchmarked on independent data with ground-truth DEG/non-DEG labels, such as spike-in experiments.

name: spike-in-control-gene-selection
description: Use when an scRNAseq dataset contains ERCC spike-in measurements that must be filtered and designated as the control-gene set before applying control-based confounding-removal methods like scPLS, RUV, or scLVM.

name: spike-in-read-alignment-to-ercc-reference
description: Use when validating droplet-based scRNA-seq sensitivity with ERCC synthetic spike-ins: FASTQ reads from spike-in-only GEMs must be aligned to the ERCC reference (not a genome) to count UMIs per ERCC transcript.

name: splat-parameter-configuration
description: Use when simulated scRNA-seq data with known differentially expressed (feature) genes and a rare/common two-cell-type structure is needed to benchmark feature gene detection or dimensionality reduction methods.

name: splatter-parameter-configuration
description: Use when you need controlled, simulated two-batch scRNA-seq count matrices to benchmark batch-effect correction tools, and you must reproduce a specific effect design (large batch shift, elevated dropout, unequal batch sizes, small batch effects, or multi-cell-type structure).

name: splatter-parameterized-simulation
description: Use when regenerating the simulated scRNA-seq scenarios needed to benchmark scGAE, or when controlled-dropout synthetic single-cell count matrices of exactly 2000 cells x 5000 genes are required.

name: splatter-scrna-count-simulation
description: Use when a benchmark requires simulated scRNA-Seq counts with known ground truth (true counts before noise, DE gene labels, group assignments) so imputation quality can be scored against a reference.

name: splatter-scrna-seq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq data generation method (e.g. scGAN) against Splatter on the same real training cells, evaluating with MMD and random-forest discrimination AUC (RF-AUC).

name: splatter-scrnaseq-pathway-simulation
description: Use when you need simulated single-cell RNA-seq data with continuous differentiation structure and known pseudotime to benchmark clustering, pseudotime, or label-uncertainty methods against a ground truth.

name: splatter-simulated-data-handling
description: Use when a simulated single-cell RNA-seq benchmark is needed to evaluate EDGE or other embedding methods (t-SNE, UMAP), or when a raw gene-by-cell count matrix must be log-normalized before calling endr().

name: splatter-simulation-of-scrna-seq
description: Use when a clustering benchmark requires a large simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth labels — e.g. stress-testing a method's scalability to ~1,000,000 cells when real annotated data of that size is unavailable.

name: splatter-single-cell-rnaseq-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking feature selection or trajectory inference methods on scRNA-seq data where ground-truth cluster labels, DE genes, and latent step pseudotime must be known and noise must be systematically varied via BCV.

name: splice-aware-alignment-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify recall/precision of novel splice-junction detection against held-out AStalavista truth events, or compare align-and-count vs pseudoalignment runtime/memory on tens to hundreds of millions of RNA-seq reads.

name: splice-aware-alignment-parameter-tuning
description: Use when building or adapting a Snakemake neoantigen/variant pipeline that must align RNA-seq reads splice- and chimeric-aware (for fusions, exitrons, indels) and DNA-seq reads genome-wide, with defined STAR chimera parameters and per-branch BAM indexing.

name: splice-aware-genome-alignment
description: Use when raw or adapter-trimmed RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be mapped to a reference genome while correctly handling splice junctions across introns, prior to transcript quantification (RSEM) and DEG calling (DESeq2).

name: splice-aware-multimapping-read-alignment
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-Seq reads (FASTQ) for transposable element expression analysis where TEs are repetitive and multi-mapping must be retained rather than filtered, e.g., building BAMs for SoloTE or benchmarking against ground truth.

name: splice-aware-read-alignment
description: Use when preprocessing Nanopore single-cell or spatially barcoded long reads for isoform-level analysis and you need spliced alignments that respect known transcript junctions before UMI/barcode denoising and isoform counting.

name: splice-aware-ribosome-footprint-genome-alignment
description: Use when aligning rRNA-depleted ribosome-footprint reads (e.g. 25-35 nt RPFs) to a genome whose transcripts contain exon junctions, requiring splice-aware mapping followed by a less strict remapping of unaligned reads.

name: splice-aware-rna-seq-read-alignment
description: Use when starting from RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g., SRA accessions like SRR307911) and you need genome-aligned BAMs that preserve splice junctions for transcriptome assembly, especially when integrating multiple aligner mappings.

name: splice-event-filter-evaluation
description: Use when you have per-sample splice-junction read counts (e.g., STAR split-read *.csf.splicing.txt* outputs) plus known pathogenic mis-splicing events and need to benchmark read-count or singleton-based event filters.

name: splice-graph-construction-from-alignments
description: Use when integrating BAM alignments from multiple splice-aware aligners (e.g., Hisat2 --dta and STAR) over a gene locus and you need an exon/junction graph whose edges carry aligner-capture labels and averaged read-support weights.

name: splice-graph-path-search-implementation
description: Use when you have a labeled splice graph built from integrated mappings of multiple aligners (labels 1, 2+, 2-) and need to extract transcript-representing paths, particularly to recover lowly expressed transcripts.

name: splice-graph-transcript-assembly
description: Use when RNase R-treated paired-end RNA-seq data have back-spliced junctions detected by CIRCexplorer2, CIRI2, or UROBORUS and you need full-length circRNA transcript sequences with FPKM/TPM isoform-level quantification.

name: splice-junction-linear-rna-normalization
description: Use when you need linear RNA expression estimates from ribo− RNA-seq that are directly comparable to circRNA expression at the same gene loci, e.g. to compute a CIRCscore from paired FPBcirc/FPBlinear values.

name: splice-junction-matrix-construction
description: Use when starting from per-cell BAM files or STAR SJ.out.tab junction files from single-cell SMART-seq data and you need a cells-by-sites junction matrix plus a 5'/3' AS probability matrix before imputation or clustering.

name: splice-site-combination-enumeration
description: Use when reconstructing fortuna's Step B fragment-set construction (F from F1:1 and Fmax) from a preprocessed GTF, or when verifying that a fragment set is correct (all fragments derivable from T) and complete (any length-l read is mappable).

name: splice-site-mutation-annotation-matching
description: Use when you have SCISSOR shape-change results plus a public mutation-call repository and need to check whether annotated splice-site mutations are supported by significant coverage-shape changes.

name: splice-site-mutation-interpretation
description: Use when SCISSOR (or similar) has called sample-level RNA coverage shape changes and you need to determine which aberrations coincide with annotated mutations (e.g., splice sites, exon skipping, intron retention, in-frame indels) and which are novel.

name: splice-site-strength-pwm-scoring
description: Use when testing whether cis genetic variants overlapping splice junction motifs alter donor/acceptor site strength, and whether the strength change scales with sQTL effect size (md).

name: spliceai-splice-impact-scoring
description: Use when building a prioritized set of ClinVar VUSs predicted to alter splicing (acceptor/donor gain/loss) as input for tissue-suitability or RNA-seq re-inspection analyses such as MRSD scoring.

name: spliced-read-alignment-hisat
description: Use when reconstructing mRNA 3' end cleavage sites from Microwell-seq (MCA/HCL) FASTQ data at single-nucleotide resolution, after PEAR merging and poly(A) removal, before peak calling.

name: spliced-read-alignment-with-uniquely-mapped-filtering
description: Use when raw paired-end spatially barcoded ST reads (e.g., MOB ST, SRA: SRR3382373) must be mapped to a reference genome before poly(A) site discovery, and downstream tools require unambiguous mapping.

name: spliced-read-fraction-statistical-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking cell-calling methods on single-nucleus RNA-seq raw unfiltered count matrices and you need a contamination-sensitive quality metric (spliced-read fraction) to compare retained barcodes across methods.

name: spliced-read-realignment
description: Use when a pseudoalignment-based quantification (fortuna --quant) left reads unmapped and a spliced aligner such as STAR has detected novel acceptor (AA) or donor (AD) splice sites in those reads that must be counted and annotated.

name: spliced-unspliced-adata-preparation
description: Use when an AnnData object must be structured with spliced_key='spliced' and unspliced_key='unspliced' layers (plus optional batch_key and celltype_key) before running LatentVelo RNA velocity estimation or benchmarking against scVelo.

name: spliced-unspliced-moments-smoothing
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (h5ad) must be filtered, normalized, graph-smoothed, and paired with candidate TF-target sets (ENCODE/ChEA) prior to RNA velocity or TF-based dynamic model fitting.

name: spliced-unspliced-phase-portrait-analysis
description: Use when you have a UniTVelo-fitted AnnData with latent_time and velocity and need per-gene diagnostic phase portraits to check model fit or explain MURK/kinetic genes.

name: spliced-unspliced-read-classification-setup
description: Use when preparing the reference index for scKB/kallisto so single-cell RNA-seq reads can be classified as spliced or unspliced (e.g., for RNA velocity or trajectory inference from splicing dynamics).

name: spliced-unspliced-transcript-compatibility-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq reads aligned to a spliceu transcriptome need a probabilistic spliced/unspliced/ambiguous status, or when multi-gene mapped reads must be resolved to a single gene of origin.

name: spliced-unspliced-umi-quantification-per-droplet
description: Use when processing raw 10X snRNA-seq droplet data (e.g. CellRanger outs/raw_feature_bc_matrix) to quantify per-droplet contamination via percent-spliced reads and estimate the sample-specific nuclear/background midpoint.

name: spliceosome-go-annotation-interpretation
description: Use when building the CRIT feature matrix for candidate circRNA-regulating RBPs and you need to quantify each gene's functional proximity to mRNA splicing via GO annotation and semantic similarity.

name: spliceu-augmented-transcriptome-alignment
description: Use when scRNA-seq reads must be aligned to an augmented spliced+unspliced transcriptome so per-read splicing status can be predicted or evaluated, or when uniquely genome-mapped and fully exonic (ambiguous) read sets are needed.

name: spliceu-reference-construction
description: Use when preparing a scRNA-seq splicing-status analysis (e.g., Forseti prediction) that requires reads to align to both spliced and unspliced transcript versions; triggered by having a genome .fasta and .gtf but no augmented spliceu index.

name: splici-reference-generation
description: Use when starting from a raw genome FASTA plus matching GTF annotation and needing an expanded (splici) reference and mapper index for alevin-fry USA-mode single-cell quantification.

name: splicing-based-velocity-baseline-benchmarking
description: Use when you have per-cell velocity vectors from a new velocity method plus a pseudotime-defined state-transition axis, and need a fair head-to-head comparison against splicing-based methods like scVelo, VeloVAE, and UniTVelo.

name: splicing-prediction-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating a splicing-status predictor for scRNA-seq reads: you need negative-control baselines (constant or random splice_prob) to demonstrate that model AUC reflects genuine prediction rather than chance.

name: splicing-qtl-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you have an sQTL catalog (e.g. from sQTLseekeR2 on GTEx) plus RBP eCLIP peaks and want to test whether sQTLs change RBP binding motifs more than matched non-sQTL variants.

name: splicing-signature-count-aggregation
description: Use when you already hold fortuna signature-count output (cnt.tsv with '|' joined subexon IDs and counts) and need DEXSeq-compatible per-subexon counts for alternative splicing analysis.

name: splicing-status-prediction-modeling
description: Use when you need per-read splicing probabilities for single-cell RNA-seq alignments—especially reads labeled ambiguous ('A') by alevin-fry/STAR workflow logic—so that spliced/unspliced quantification or downstream velocity analyses can resolve fundamentally ambiguous reads.

name: spliseq-read2-barcode-index-kmer-matching
description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ to extract cell-type barcodes and UMI from Read2, especially when reads may contain insertions or deletions in the 8-nt barcode index regions.

name: split-pool-barcoding-layout-interpretation
description: Use when one or more seqspec spec.yaml files are available and the goal is to interpret a library's ordered sequence elements or to compare library structures across assays — e.g. checking which split-pool barcode rounds are shared between two modalities.

name: split-seq-combinatorial-barcode-identification
description: Use when preprocessing raw SPLiT-seq paired-end Illumina FASTQ reads to label each read's cellular origin by identifying combinatorial barcodes (three 8 nt rounds) and UMI, especially when the original method's filters would discard too many reads.

name: splitseq-read-barcoding-preprocessing
description: Use when preprocessing SPLiT-seq paired-end FASTQ data (e.g., SAMN08567259–SAMN08567264) to identify combinatorial barcodes and UMI fault-tolerantly, and to compare STAR mapped-read counts against the original BLAST/BWA-based SPLiT-seq filtering.

name: spot-adjacency-matrix-construction
description: Use when preparing SRT data (e.g., Visium DLPFC sections) for spatial clustering methods that need a neighbor graph — iSC.MEB requires adjacency matrices derived from spot coordinates before model fitting.

name: spot-coordinate-distance-computation
description: Use when ST data provides spot spatial coordinates (e.g. simu_st_metadata.csv from the Figshare deposit DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.24452812) and you need the N x N row-normalized spatial adjacency matrix as a prediction target.

name: spot-lattice-adjacency-construction-from-coordinates
description: Use when generating automated scribbles via AutoScribbleDom and you need neighbor adjacency to label-spot consensus-filter an initial non-spatial Mclust clustering on Visium or ST platform data.

name: spot-level-cell-type-visualization
description: Use when you have an optimal-transport label-transfer matrix mapping spatial spots (10x Visium coordinates) to reference scRNA cell types and need per-spot cell-type composition maps on the tissue slice.

name: spot-level-pcc-rmse-error-rate-computation
description: Use when comparing predicted vs ground-truth spatial assignments of cell types or gene expressions on simulated spatial transcriptomics benchmarks with per-cell/spot-level labels.

name: spot-level-spatial-expression-visualization
description: Use when validating that uTAR signals recapitulate tissue biology in 10X Visium data — i.e., when spot-level expression of annotation-independent TARs must be compared against marker genes (e.g., TNNT2, COL1A1, HBZ) via spatial colocalization or correlation.

name: spot-similarity-distance-ranking
description: Use when you have a sparse spot-by-poly(A)-site RUD matrix from ST data plus a gene-spot count matrix for the same spots, and missing RUD entries must be imputed before downstream spatial APA analyses.

name: spot-to-cell-zonation-score-transfer
description: Use when you have trained STEM embeddings for paired scRNA-seq and Visium ST data and need to assign each single cell a pseudo-spatial coordinate or transfer spot-level scores (e.g., PV-CV zonation) to cells for cell-type-specific spatial DE testing.

name: spotlight-cell-type-deconvolution-of-visium-spots
description: Use when spot-level spatial data (e.g. 10x Visium slides) need cell-type proportion estimates from a matched scRNA-seq reference, to derive colocalization z-scores for validating CCC predictions against spatial adjacency.

name: spurious-interaction-generation-from-variable-genes
description: Use when stress-testing the robustness of CCC inference (e.g. CellChat, CellPhoneDB, SingleCellSignalR run via LIANA) to corruption of the prior-knowledge ligand-receptor resource rather than to noise in the expression data or cell-type labels.

name: sql-aggregation-querying
description: Use when a cells x genes single-cell matrix (e.g. from an AnnData/H5AD file) is loaded into PostgreSQL and per-gene or per-cell-type expression summaries must be computed or queried efficiently across integrated studies.

name: sql-based-single-cell-aggregation
description: Use when aggregative operations (per-cell count sums, gene counts, group-by expression averages, multi-gene filtered queries, table joins) on a single-cell AnnData matrix are too slow or memory-bound in AnnData/Scanpy backed mode or Seurat — e.g. datasets larger than memory such as the 4.

name: sql-convenience-view-join-construction
description: Use when building an AnnSQL database from an AnnData object and you need single-table SQL access to gene expression joined with cell metadata (obs), e.g. group-by queries on cell_type with per-gene averages.

name: sql-database-runtime-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing runtime or memory performance of a SQL-based single-cell database engine (AnnSQL/DuckDB) versus AnnData across filter/query operations, including re-testing on sparser simulated datasets.

name: sql-query-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing query/filter runtime of SQL-based single-cell query engines (AnnSQL/DuckDB) versus AnnData backed or in-memory operations across dataset sizes, to find crossover points and speedup ratios.

name: sqlite-gene-expression-database-construction
description: Use when a Seurat or Scanpy/AnnData object must be turned into CellexalVR-ready input files (expression sqlite3 DB, .mds DR coordinate files) placed in a CellexalVR Data folder.

name: sqtl-catalog-functional-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a catalog of sQTLs (e.g. sqtlseeker2-nf nominal/permuted output at FDR < 0.05) exists and the goal is to identify which functional annotations — splice sites, histone marks, GWAS hits — are over-represented among sQTLs versus matched non-sQTLs.

name: sqtl-effect-size-stratified-analysis
description: Use when nominal sQTL test output (all-tests.nominal.tsv) and FDR-thresholded sQTL labels are available and the goal is to test whether sQTLs alter splice site strength more often/strongly than non-sQTLs, scaling with md effect size.

name: sqtl-mapping-pipeline-execution
description: Use when you need to identify genetic variants associated with multivariate splicing phenotypes (intron excision ratios) from genotype and transcript expression data in a reproducible, containerized workflow.

name: sqtls-effect-size-pearson-correlation
description: Use when you have per-tissue significant sQTL catalogs (e.g. sqtls-*fdr.nominal.tsv from sqtlseeker2-nf) and need to measure to what extent sQTLs are shared across GTEx tissues, or whether a tissue group such as brain has a distinct sharing pattern.

name: sqtls-fdr-threshold-classification
description: Use when you have sqtlseeker2-nf sQTL mapping output (nominal per-variant tests plus FDR-significant sQTL tables) and need binary sQTL/non-sQTL labels for downstream functional-enrichment comparisons such as splice-site PWM strength analysis.

name: squidpy-neighbourhood-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have spatially resolved single-cell or spot-level data (seqFISH, merFISH, 10x Visium) with cell-type labels and need to test whether prioritized CCC interactions are enriched between spatially adjacent cell types.

name: sra-fastq-data-retrieval
description: Use when raw RNA-seq data for a study must be fetched from NCBI SRA via SRR/ERR run accessions or a study accession (SRP) before quantification with tools like Seq2Fun 2.0.

name: sra-fastq-retrieval
description: Use when reproducing a published RNA-seq analysis and raw reads must be fetched from SRA before trimming, alignment (STAR), and quantification (RSEM/DESeq2); triggered when a supplemental accession table lists the samples.

name: sra-rnaseq-data-retrieval
description: Use when reproducing the UMI mapping-shift analysis or Table 1 cluster-size read fractions and raw FASTQ files for any of run_171108, run_170420, SCRB, La Manno, Yanai1, or Yanai2 are needed.

name: srna-read-mapping-workflow-execution
description: Use when running the PhasiHunter preprocess module to produce .map files from sRNA FASTQ data against transcriptome/genome references, or when benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools with the Bowtie index/mapping step held constant.

name: srna-read-stack-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually inspect read stacks, expression boxplots, and arm-selection events for candidate plant miRNAs (e.g., ath-MIR156b) to support manual curation decisions.

name: srnaseq-read-alignment-to-reference-genome
description: Use when you have sRNA-Seq data (SRA accession numbers or FASTQ files) for a plant species WITH a reference genome and need to predict novel miRNA precursors from mapped reads.

name: ssgsea-pathway-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor or LINCS drug-induced profiles) must be transformed into per-sample FM activity scores at the pathway level as part of the GSFM four-quantifier (GSFM_Up/Down/ssGSEA/TF) active-matrix construction.

name: ssrge-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have fitted SSrGE on paired SNV (n_cells x n_SNVs binary) and gene-expression matrices and need a ranked gene list (with SNV ids) to select top-ranked eeSNV genes for subpopulation markers or pathway enrichment.

name: ssrge-linear-model-fitting-with-cnv-predictors
description: Use when you have per-cell SNV matrices and gene expression matrices from scRNA-seq (or coupled RRBS/RNA-seq) data and need to identify expressed SNVs (eeSNVs) associated with gene expression, with or without copy-number predictors.

name: st-reference-contrastive-model-inference
description: Use when SC cells lack coordinates but an ST reference (e.g. SeqFISH embryo ST h5ad with .obs[['x','y']]) exists, and reconstructed per-cell spatial locations are needed for downstream co-localization or cell-cell communication analyses.

name: st-super-pixel-data-enhancement
description: Use when preparing a 10x Visium training reference for CeLEry 2D location recovery, e.g. the mouse posterior brain dataset, where spot-level resolution or a limited gene panel would limit spatial-location prediction accuracy.

name: stability-curve-benchmark-comparison
description: Decision support for choosing how many reference genes to aggregate in qPCR normalization: when you need to compare SD-vs-k stability curves of a weighted (geom_sd_hybrid) versus unweighted (geom) virtual RG to find the crossover point.

name: stability-measure-minimization-sd-cv
description: Use when you have a raw CT matrix (rows = internal controls, columns = samples) for a chosen reference-gene combination and need per-gene weights that minimize the SD or CV of the weighted mean instead of taking a simple unweighted average.

name: stability-selection-ensembling
description: Use when inferring gene regulatory networks from pseudotemporally ordered single-cell expression data (.mat with sparse X, ptime, optional regix/branches) where single regression runs are unstable and ensembling with modified Borda aggregation is needed.

name: stacked-ensemble-model-training
description: Use when building a binary RNA-modification (e.g., m5C) predictor from balanced 41-bp sequence datasets where a single RF- or SVM-based model underperforms and ensemble stacking should be benchmarked.

name: stacked-evolutionary-profile-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA dataset (Scanpy AnnData) has a gene age class annotation (orthomap) and you need to show which evolutionary age classes drive the global TEI across stages or cell types — e.g. testing whether youngest, species-specific classes peak in early embryos.

name: stage-effect-correlation-matrix-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq pseudobulk data span an ordered trajectory (e.g. iPSC-to-endoderm stages CT1–CT4) and you need to test whether adjacent-stage interindividual correlations of cell type-specific expression effects exceed those between more distant stages.

name: standalone-platform-execution-with-matched-parameters
description: Use when comparing a local stand-alone small RNA-seq pipeline against a web-based tool on identical FASTQ files and the comparison requires parameters matched to the reference tool for a fair tool-vs-tool evaluation.

name: star-alignment-of-short-rna-reads
description: Use when a small RNA-seq FASTQ (adapter- and quality-trimmed by COMPSRA QC) must be mapped to hg19/hg38 to enable annotation of miRNA, piRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, tRNA and circRNA molecules with COMPSRA.

name: star-log-metric-extraction
description: Use when you have STAR alignment log files (Log.final.out) from multiple RNA-seq samples and need per-sample or per-group comparison of uniquely mapped, 'too short' unmapped, and chimeric read percentages to diagnose tissue- or condition-specific mapping problems.

name: star-multimapping-read-alignment
description: Use when quantifying transposable element expression in scRNA-Seq data, since reads from repetitive TEs must be aligned and multi-mapping reads kept to avoid losing TE signal.

name: star-rnaseq-genome-alignment
description: Use when processing UMI-tagged single-end FASTQ reads (e.g. after fastq_qual_filter and fastq_umi_clipper) and a position-sorted SAM file is needed to quantify UMI collisions and mapping-shift artefacts.

name: star-split-read-alignment
description: Use when RNA-seq FASTQs must be converted into per-sample splice junction counts (chr-start-end SJIDs) for MRSD calculation, junction coverage estimation, or evaluation of read-count/singleton filters on mis-splicing events.

name: starred-spatial-data-distance-matrix-construction
description: Use when pairing scRNA-seq data (e.g., Allen Brain Atlas mouse_VISp_2018-06-14_exon-matrix.csv) with a spatial dataset like STARmap and you need a pairwise distance matrix among spatial positions as an optimal-transport input.

name: starsolo-alignment-dge-generation
description: Use when raw SeqScope-style 2nd-seq cDNA fastq.gz files and a STARsolo-compatible barcode whitelist are available and a digital expression matrix is needed for spatial transcriptomics analysis.

name: starsolo-high-throughput-alignment
description: Use when raw Seq-Scope 2nd-seq FASTQ pairs must be aligned and converted to digital expression matrices at ultra-high resolution (>1M spatial barcodes/mm2), especially within the STtools Step A3 stage.

name: state-transition-topology-comparison
description: Use when a reconstructed cell-state transition network (e.g. Mpath's MDP-CDP-preDC cascade) must be shown robust to clustering or graph-pruning parameter changes before downstream biological interpretation.

name: statistical-agreement-reproducibility-checking
description: Use when you have per-method regulator activity score matrices from multiple inference methods (e.g. decoupleR on transcriptomics or phospho-proteomics benchmarks) and need to quantify whether methods agree.

name: statistical-distribution-analysis
description: Use when a per-cell uncertainty or score distribution (e.g. scEMAIL E-scores from entropy, confidence, consistency) must be tested for unimodality vs. bimodality to make a binary presence/absence decision about novel cell types.

name: statistical-distribution-fitting
description: Use when you need to find simulation parameters that reproduce the statistical properties (gene CV/mean distributions, zero fraction, SD) of a real scRNA-seq dataset, for either UMI or non-UMI protocols.

name: statistical-filtering-of-cluster-pairs
description: Use when cross-replicate or cross-dataset scRNAseq clusters must be matched: after assess.cluster.similarity computes FC-vector correlations, to discard non-reproducible cluster pairs before building a meta-cluster map.

name: statistical-hypothesis-testing-for-cluster-annotation
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has reCAT-derived mean cell-cycle scores and you need to flag and remove a quiescent/G0-like cell group (no prior algorithm existed for G0-like detection) before pseudotime reconstruction.

name: statistical-link-concordance-comparison
description: Use when you need to test whether regression-based (linear + interaction term) differential gene–gene links are also recoverable by a non-linear dependence measure such as k-NN mutual information, on matched subgroup data.

name: statistical-power-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when you need to quantify whether enlarging the class of discoverable meta-markers (higher-order gene interactions, k>=2) yields more significant patterns than single/low-order miners under the same FWER criterion.

name: statistical-power-curve-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify whether modeling replicates confers robustness against a single outlier sample versus pooling counts, by tracing detection power as sample size increases under simulated data.

name: statistical-pvalue-reproduction-from-score-tables
description: Use when a paper reports a significance p-value (e.g. Wilcoxon p = 1.2e-7) comparing score distributions over a labeled table, and you have the score table to verify it.

name: statistical-results-table-generation
description: Use when you have a per-dataset performance metric matrix (e.g., ARI) for a proposed method plus baselines over a fixed benchmark and must produce a paired significance-test table.

name: statistical-significance-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when a new differential abundance method must be validated against established competitors on shared single-cell datasets, requiring comparable per-cell-type DA statistics and captured-cell-fraction metrics.

name: statistical-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing method performance across multiple scRNA-seq benchmark datasets and you must show the winner's advantage is statistically significant, e.g. via one-sided Wilcoxon tests on per-dataset scores.

name: statistical-significance-testing-ttest
description: Use when comparing a proposed method's averaged detection/classification metrics (e.g. AUROC at C^novel=1-4) against baseline methods across benchmark datasets and you need to confirm the improvement is significant, not noise.

name: statistical-testing-with-wilcoxon-mast-deseq2
description: Use when a QC-filtered, normalized, clustered scRNA-seq object (e.g., PBMC3k with Louvain labels) needs per-cluster marker genes ranked by log2 fold-change against all remaining cells.

name: statistical-threshold-filtering-gene-expression
description: Use when a RiboSeq pipeline has produced normalized count matrices (e.g. HTSeq-count count_matrix_by_transcript_IDs.csv) and you must define significance cutoffs (p-val, logFC) to accept/reject differential expression calls against a reference condition.

name: steiner-tree-backbone-extraction
description: Use when you have gene differential-expression P-values (seed genes) plus a reference interactome and need a minimal connected subnetwork capturing perturbed condition-specific signal for downstream enrichment scoring.

name: steiner-tree-subnetwork-analysis
description: Use when you have seed/disease genes plus group-labeled RNA-seq data and need a data-driven directed subnetwork whose significant causal paths (Bonferroni-corrected ACE testing) explain disease perturbation.

name: stemness-score-benchmark-verification
description: Use when you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix with cell-type annotations and must verify that stemness/pluripotency scores (ORIGINS activity, LandSCENT SR, CytoTRACE) rank expected stem/progenitor types highly.

name: stepwise-feature-selection
description: Use when single-cell data (e.g., CyTOF markers) has a priori class labels (e.g., time points day0–day5) and you need to automatically tune the feature set input to LDA for visualization instead of manually picking markers.

name: stepwise-regression-gene-selection
description: Use when you have a computed GGC matrix from normalized scRNA-seq data and need a minimally redundant seed feature set for DUBStepR-style guilt-by-association feature expansion.

name: stepwise-regression-seed-feature-identification
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq data and you need a non-redundant seed set of well-correlated, cell-type-specific marker genes to drive feature selection (e.g., on a log-normalized 10X PBMC matrix in Seurat).

name: stereoseq-spatial-barcode-extraction
description: Use when processing a SAW-generated unmapped FASTQ from a Stereo-seq sample to recover expressed lineage barcodes per spatial spot and map the spatial territories of abundant clones.

name: stft-spectrogram-conversion-of-ionic-currents
description: Use when raw nanopore dRNA signals (fast5/pod5 chunks, e.g. 3000-sample chunks, pA scale) must be preprocessed into spectrogram-like inputs for a speech-to-text-style transformer that calls canonical and modified bases.

name: stimulus-condition-comparative-analysis
description: Use when multiple transcriptomic conditions from one cell type under distinct stimuli/blocking treatments must be compared for ligand-receptor communication amplitude against a common reference panel.

name: stochastic-copy-and-error-model-sampling
description: Use when evaluating a DNA storage pipeline design under simulated synthesis/sequencing noise: you need per-oligo copy counts and error draws (substitutions, deletions, decode failures) parameterized by a JSON fault configuration before decoding.

name: stochastic-gradient-descent-embedding-optimization
description: Use when a cell-cell similarity matrix (e.g., ensemble weak-learner similarity S from EDGE) must be converted into an optimized low-dimensional embedding for visualization or downstream clustering of scRNA-seq data.

name: stochastic-network-edge-weight-normalization
description: Use when a per-cell gene-gene network (e.g. from c-CSN) must be converted into a stochastic flow matrix and summarized into a single entropy-based potency score per cell, e.g. to order Wang NPC Day 0-30 or Yang E10/E17 differentiation stages.

name: stochastic-reaction-network-conversion
description: Use when a defined gene regulatory network must be turned into stochastic biochemical reactions to simulate single-cell, single-transcript resolution dynamics with known ground truth.

name: stochastic-trial-aggregation
description: Use when assessing whether model outputs (e.g., scKINETICS per-cell transcriptional velocities) are stable under technical noise, by repeating a stochastic perturbation such as downsampling raw counts across multiple independent trials per proportion and aggregating deviation statistics.

name: stoichiometric-constraint-formulation
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq samples require sample-specific metabolic flux estimates over a genome-scale model, and gene expression (MRAS) plus a nutrient medium must be translated into E-Flux style bounds for a QP-constrained FBA solve.

name: stop-codon-region-extraction-custompick
description: Use when a permutation colocalization test needs transcriptome regions of interest (e.g. stop codons) that are not provided directly as a GRanges set and must be picked per-transcript from UCSC hg19 TxDb annotation for features with unknown isoform association.

name: strand-aware-read-partitioning
description: Use when a pipeline consumes a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium output) and downstream analysis, such as truncation-point pileups or per-strand peak calling, requires reads to be separated by strand and read group before processing.

name: strand-clustering-minhash-edit-distance
description: Use when decoding DNA storage sequencing reads where each encoded strand has multiple noisy copies, and you must aggregate copies toward a consensus before reversing the inner encoding.

name: strand-insensitive-tar-labeling
description: Use when you have groHMM HMM bed features (chr*_HMM.bed) and a refFlat gene annotation, and need a per-TAR aTAR/uTAR label based on genomic start/stop overlap regardless of strand.

name: strand-specific-cis-nat-pair-extraction
description: Use when you have a CSV of gene annotations (id, Chr, Strand, Start, End) from Ensembl, optionally with TPM/FPKM/fold_change/padj columns, and need to enumerate sense-antisense overlapping pairs with structural classification.

name: strand-specific-feature-counting
description: Use when generating a per-cell count matrix over groHMM-defined TARs from strand-specific paired-end scRNA-seq alignments (e.g., Smart-seq2), where read orientation must be preserved for correct quantification.

name: strand-specific-genomic-coverage-computation
description: Use when you have a STAR-aligned scRNA-seq combined BAM and groHMM-predicted transcribed regions, and need per-region, strand-aware read counts to apply a retention cutoff for annotation-free TAR discovery.

name: strand-specific-read-coverage-analysis
description: Use when aligned strand-specific reads in BAM format (e.g. 10x Chromium runs where signal concentrates at 3' UTR distal ends) must be converted into candidate intervals of significant coverage as the basis for annotating novel 3' UTRs.

name: strand-specific-read-end-tallying
description: Use when a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium) contains soft-clipped bases with polyA-tails, and precise strand-specific UTR end-base coordinates are needed for downstream 3' UTR annotation.

name: strand-specific-rnaseq-parameter-configuration
description: Use when running Tiglon (or evaluating its assembly) on Hisat2- or STAR-aligned BAM files and you must set the -s orientation flag to match the library type (paired-end first/second/unstranded or single-end single_forward/single_reverse/single_unstranded).

name: stranded-rnaseq-bam-preprocessing
description: Use when you have raw paired-end RNA-Seq reads (e.g. firststrand Illumina libraries) destined for aptardi polyA-site prediction and need to produce a sorted BAM aligned with HISAT2 plus a StringTie-reconstructed input transcriptome.

name: stratified-fraction-aggregation-by-cell-type-and-length
description: Use when a per-call result table already exists (e.g., classified Ginkgo CNA calls in 65 PTA-amplified brain cells) and the analysis goal is summary fractions broken down by cell type and call-length bins, as in HiScanner Fig. 4d–j.

name: stratified-holdout-cross-validation
description: Use when benchmarking a supervised cell-type classifier (e.g., SciBet vs scmap vs Seurat v3) on labeled scRNA-seq datasets and a repeated, class-balanced hold-out estimate of classification accuracy is needed.

name: stratified-train-test-splitting
description: Use when benchmarking cell type annotation or cell selection methods on labeled single-cell expression data and repeated, class-balanced performance estimates (e.g. balanced accuracy, F1) are needed to compare strategies fairly.

name: stratified-train-test-splitting
description: Use when a small, imbalanced RNA-modification dataset (e.g., RMBase v2.0 Ψ sites vs. 10x negatives) must be split into training and test sets while preserving class ratios and removing homologous sequences that would inflate evaluation performance.

name: streaming-read-normalization-via-fifo
description: Use when single-cell library read structure cannot be expressed as one fixed barcode/UMI offset — e.g. barcodes split across two segments like '1{b[16]u[12]b[4]x:}' — yet the underlying mapper only supports simple geometry.

name: stress-condition-composition-comparison
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq expression matrices plus sample metadata for samples spanning distinct stress treatments, and an annotated single-cell reference atlas, and you need to quantify how cell-type composition changes across conditions.

name: stress-condition-replicate-sample-selection
description: Use when preparing a count matrix of tncRNA expression for DESeq2 stress contrasts and you must pick which control/treatment samples qualify, ensuring ≥3 biological replicates per condition.

name: string-gene-association-network-construction
description: Use when validating that gene modules recovered from single-cell feature selection (e.g., DELVE dynamic vs. static modules on CD8+ T cell LCMV data) carry experimental evidence of co-regulation rather than noise.

name: string-network-density-normalization
description: Use when quantifying how connected a protein is within the human STRING interaction network, or when reproducing/validating reported network density percentages (e.g. HSPH1 = 78% from Fig. 1C of Kahraman et al., Scientific Reports 2020).

name: string-ppi-data-integration
description: Use when you have disease isoform switching results (dMDT gene lists whose isoforms lose domains) and need to map those domain losses onto protein-protein interactions from STRING to identify disrupted edges.

name: string-style-score-calibration-curve-fitting
description: Use when raw association scores (e.g. FAVA PCC scores from scRNA-seq or bulk proteomics data) need to be calibrated into interpretable confidence probabilities for network filtering at STRING-style confidence cutoffs.

name: stringtie2-long-read-transcript-assembly
description: Use when benchmarking long-read isoform assemblers on GMAP-aligned PacBio/ONT BAM data against a known reference isoform set (e.g. 68 SIRV isoforms), where StringTie2 must serve as the transcriptome-based comparator.

name: structural-similarity-index-computation
description: Use when evaluating 2D ST slice alignment quality: you have spatial coordinate systems of consecutive slices (e.g., STARmap mouse brain) transformed by a tool like Scube and need a per-slice similarity score against a ground-truth 3D stack.

name: structure-count-percentile-thresholding
description: Use when you have per-window BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values (e.g., from RSCanner's 51-nt centered sliding windows on a CT or dot-bracket structure plus a Shannon file) and need to flag highly-structured positions and quantify structure density per genomic bin.

name: structure-counts-classification
description: Use when per-nucleotide BPC and smoothed Shannon entropy values are already computed for an RNA (e.g. HCV_Jc1 from a .ct or dot-bracket file plus a shannon.txt), and positions must be labeled as structure counts under RSCanner's filtering rules.

name: structure-density-heatmap-visualization
description: Use when you have per-nucleotide BPC and Shannon entropy (e.g. from a .ct or dot-bracket file plus shannon.txt) and need to map where structure-dense regions fall along the transcript.

name: structured-table-curation
description: Use when a published article tabulates per-entity configuration values (e.g., per-technology cell barcode length, UMI length, and special-case flags) that must be reproduced as a structured, row-per-item table for downstream automation.

name: student-t-embedding-affinity-computation
description: Use when a per-cell, local assessment of embedding quality is needed: high-D Gaussian affinities (perplexity = 10% of samples) must be paired with Student-t affinities in 2D t-SNE/UMAP embeddings to compute per-cell KL divergences for data and null embeddings.

name: student-t-soft-assignment-clustering
description: Use when scRNA-seq data (CSV or h5) must be clustered without cell labels and the goal is an unsupervised, graph-aware embedding with soft cell-to-cluster assignments.

name: students-t-soft-cluster-assignment
description: Use when a pre-trained graph autoencoder embedding of scRNA-seq cells must be made clustering-friendly by jointly refining embeddings and cluster assignments via soft-assignment KL loss with Louvain-initialized centroids.

name: subcellular-location-annotation
description: Use when constructing an intercellular communication interaction database or when filtering candidate protein-protein/ligand-receptor pairs so that only proteins with compatible subcellular localizations (e.g., extracellular region, plasma membrane) are paired.

name: subcellular-location-annotation-mapping
description: Use when you have a list of key interactor genes/proteins from an interactome or GMM-cluster assessment and need to label each with a protein type and a UniProt subcellular compartment.

name: subcellular-spatial-transcriptomics-cell-segmentation
description: Use when you have SST data (Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE, Stereo-seq) with a transcripts file and DAPI/nuclei image and need cell-level segmentation and a per-cell gene expression matrix.

name: subcellular-spliced-unspliced-plotting
description: Use when you have a Velocyto-format DGE with spatial coordinates from Seq-Scope (or other <1μm ST data) and need to visualize subcellular spliced/unspliced read patterns at ~1μm²/pixel resolution.

name: subclonal-allele-specific-cna-groundtruth-evaluation
description: Use when a simulated scRNA-seq dataset with known ground-truth subclonal CNA labels (e.g., scCNASimulator chr3 loss on GX109-T1c) is available and caller accuracy must be quantified by AUROC.

name: subclone-expression-signature-verification
description: Use when genotyped cells expressing a specific somatic SNV are available for a scRNA-seq sample and you need to test whether the mutant subclone has an associated expression signature, including by extending mutation labels to non-genotyped cells via density in embedded/clustered space.

name: subclone-mutual-exclusivity-analysis
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq from a heterogeneous tumor (multiple cells per patient/sample) should be decomposed into CNV-defined subclones, and mutually exclusive vs co-occurring CNV events plus a clonal tree are the target outputs.

name: subclone-signature-overlap-analysis
description: Use when you have two gene lists — one from subclonal mutation-associated expression (scRNA-seq) and one from bulk expression correlation (e.g., TCGA AML, q < 0.001) — and need to test for a significant regulon-level overlap.

name: subgenome-homeologous-group-clustering
description: Use when annotating miRNA precursors in a polyploid genome with distinct A/B/D (or other) subgenomes and you need homeologous-group structure, subgenome counts, and complete-triad fractions from curated precursor sets.

name: subgraph-skeleton-representation
description: Use when a VR visualization must make every cell individually selectable in dimension-reduction plots containing >30k points, or when a selection must be captured as a cell/neighborhood sub-graph for downstream analysis.

name: subgroup-eesnv-gene-ranking
description: Use when cell subgroups (e.g. normal vs cancer cells or known cancer subtypes) are predefined and you need eeSNV and gene rankings plus significance tests per subgroup from an already-fitted SSrGE model.

name: subgroup-specific-edge-table-extraction
description: Use when normalized RNA-seq counts and clinical metadata grouped by a subgroup variable (e.g. TCGA-BRCA SUBTYPE like BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) must be reduced to group-specific gene-gene interaction edge lists after expression-based node filtering.

name: subgroup-specific-feature-ranking
description: Use when cells have been clustered or ordered into subgroups (e.g., PDX-pRCC vs Pt-mRCC vs PDX-mRCC branches of a Monocle-style MST) and you need the eeSNVs and impacted genes significantly enriched in each subgroup.

name: subgroup-specific-network-comparison
description: Use when you have normalised count data plus metadata for two or more phenotype subgroups (e.g., BRCA_Her2 vs BRCA_LumA) and want the subgroup-specific gene-gene interactions as a feature list for ML models.

name: subgroup-specificity-labelling-of-gene-links
description: Use when a coarse pathway-level result (e.g. Ras signaling upregulation in HER2-positive BRCA) needs to be resolved to specific, subgroup-restricted gene-gene interactions from a DEGGs differential network.

name: subject-smoothing-regularization-modification
description: Use when analyzing multi-subject dynamic networks with MuDCoD where subjects fall into natural groups (e.g., healthy vs diseased), and the global β subject-smoothing term inappropriately pulls subjects toward an all-subject mean.

name: submodular-optimization-sampling
description: Use when applying the sampling-based extension of KMD clustering to a large dataset (e.g. >100k cells) and you want to test whether a structurally diverse core subset outperforms uniform random subsampling at a fixed sample budget.

name: subnetwork-gene-feature-subsetting
description: Use when you have SEMtree/SEMgraph-extracted active subnetworks (e.g. ST/STr2z variants) and a binary-labelled expression matrix (GSE172114 critical vs non-critical), and need per-subnetwork classification accuracy and predictor-gene parsimony (Table 3).

name: subpopulation-annotation-from-latent-space
description: Use when a temporal scRNA-seq dataset (cell-by-time-point time.table available) has been fitted with a TCM latent map and cells at a terminal time point must be split into subpopulations and annotated with known marker genes.

name: subpopulation-cell-type-selection
description: Use when comparing imputation methods on scRNA-seq data by intra-subpopulation variance stabilization: cell-type annotations and raw/imputed log-transformed count matrices (cells x genes) are available for datasets like Jurkat-293T, Usoskin, Kolodziejczyk or PBMC.

name: subpopulation-defined-trajectory-endpoint-selection
description: Use when reconstructing single-cell trajectories between biologically defined cell states (e.g., CMP to erythroid vs GMP in Paul et al. GSE72857) and prior algorithms cannot target arbitrary endpoints.

name: subpopulation-gene-expression-quantification
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells have been assigned to subpopulations (e.g., by DC3 coupled clustering) and subpopulation-specific expression levels in FPKM are required for candidate transcription factor selection or network construction.

name: subpopulation-specific-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have cluster assignments plus per-gene subpopulation scRNA-seq p-values and cluster-specific HiChIP loop counts, and need a per-subpopulation ranked gene list or GO enrichment characterization.

name: subpopulation-specific-response-interpretation
description: Use when analyzing multi-sample, multi-condition scRNA/snRNA-seq data with cell subpopulation annotations (sample_id, group_id, cluster_id) and the goal is to find genes and cell types showing condition-specific state changes at the sample level.

name: subsample-replicate-ensembling
description: Use when tuning the cost/accuracy trade-off of a SINGE run: you must decide how many subsampled replicates per hyperparameter combination are needed before precision-recall performance plateaus on pseudotemporal single-cell expression data.

name: subsample-stability-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how a reference-gene weighting method's stability performance degrades at low qPCR sample sizes, e.g. reproducing a Figure 2C-style mean-SD-versus-n comparison via repeated random subsampling.

name: subsampled-benchmark-evaluation-against-full-data
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset is too large to analyse directly (tens of thousands to millions of cells) and you must decide which subsampling method (scValue, Uniform, GeoSketch, Sphetcher, Hopper, KH, scSampler) preserves downstream-task structure, judged against a full-data reference.

name: subsampled-pilot-dataset-replicate-aggregation
description: Use when you need to quantify convergence of synthetic-data cluster proportions toward ground truth as pilot size grows, and must collapse many stochastic sub-sampling repetitions into one stable summary value per model–dataset–size combination.

name: subsampling-based-clustering-resolution-selection
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data must be clustered but the Louvain resolution is not known a priori and an objective, subsampling-based choice among resolutions 0.4–1.4 is required (e.g., sub-clustering tumor cells in an h5ad AnnData object).

name: subsampling-based-clustering-strategy
description: Use when clustering large-scale scRNA-seq data (e.g., PBMC 68k) where naive full-data clustering is too slow or memory-heavy, and when subsampling bias must be mitigated to preserve or improve clustering accuracy.

name: subsampling-clustering-classification-pipeline
description: Use when clustering large scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., tens of thousands of cells like the 49,300-cell Macosko retina matrix) where full O(n^2) clustering is infeasible, or when clustering consistency across subsampling ratios (e.g., 5% vs 10%) must be assessed.

name: subsampling-robustness-analysis
description: Use when comparing the robustness of pseudotime inference methods (e.g., DTFLOW, Scanpy, Monocle2) on a single-cell dataset where orderings from random cell subsamples should be checked against the full-data ordering.

name: subsampling-robustness-assessment
description: Use when validating that features engineered from scRNA-seq data (e.g., Spearman-correlation features from sscClust) are robust to subsampling fluctuations before trusting a subsampling-based clustering strategy.

name: subspace-angle-computation
description: Use when comparing low-dimensional structure (top-k PCA subspaces) between an original scRNA-seq matrix and its downsampled or imputed version, to test whether imputation preserves the signal.

name: subspace-regression-gene-imputation
