description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g., CPM/TPM/FPKM values) contains zero entries suspected of being dropout events, and the goal is to improve downstream cell-type clustering (k-means ARI) before imputation-vulnerable analyses.

name: subtype-classification-cross-validation-evaluation
description: Use when a supervised RNA-seq subtype classifier (mLR with Lasso/L1 or Ridge/L2) has been fitted on a feature-selected gene space and you need CV accuracy, held-out test accuracy, and per-class recall/precision tables to compare feature spaces.

name: subtype-classifier-comparative-evaluation
description: Use when a trained subtype classifier (e.g., DeepCC labels from get_DeepCC_label) has been applied to validation cohorts with clinical metadata and you must show its clinical relevance equals or exceeds a benchmark system like PAM50.

name: subtype-concordance-evaluation
description: Use when subtype calls produced by AWCA or mLR models on RNA-seq expression matrices (TCGA RSEM, GSE96058 FPKM, PanCA, GSE81538) must be scored against published PAM50 labels or against another caller's calls via concordance/accuracy.

name: subtype-marker-identification
description: Use when RCC (or another consensus clustering run) has produced cluster assignments on an expression matrix and you need per-cluster marker genes and signature-enrichment evidence to characterize novel subtypes.

name: subtype-marker-selection
description: Use when building subtype classification templates for pre-clinical CRC models (cell lines, organoids, PDXs) where microenvironment-derived gene signals must be excluded from the marker set.

name: subtype-similarity-pattern-validation
description: Use when reproducing a cross-dataset cell label similarity map (e.g., B cell subtypes across HCC, NSCLC, BRCA references) and checking whether recomputed Jaccard values reproduce a reported pattern from the scCancer2 paper.

name: subtyping-comparison-visualization
description: Use when you need to cross-compare intrinsic breast cancer subtype callers (Prosigna, standard PAM50, AWCA-based PAM50) on the same RNA-seq profiles and visualize call concordance plus ROR prognostic agreement.

name: sugar-diffusion-scrna-generation
description: Reference for comparing deep-learning scRNA-seq generators (scGAN/cscGAN) against SUGAR and Splatter on distributional fidelity (MMD) and realism (RF-AUC) on multi-cell-type data such as PBMCs.

name: summarizedexperiment-data-access
description: Use when a dataset is loaded as a SummarizedExperiment object and you need the gene-by-cell count matrix (assays(x)$count) plus per-cell metadata such as time.table or sample_alias to run temporal single-cell analyses like TCM.

name: summarizedexperiment-data-handling
description: Use when a processed, gene-level expression matrix must be packaged with its homogenized sample metadata as a SummarizedExperiment object, or when retrieving the curatedAdipoArray datasets through ExperimentHub.

name: summary-statistic-fine-mapping-with-allelic-heterogeneity
description: Use when you have summary statistics (z-scores or betas+SEs) plus a reference LD matrix for multiple traits/tissues over the same variants, and need fine-mapping with colocalization where multiple causal alleles may mask tissue specificity.

name: summary-statistics-zscore-to-pvalue-conversion
description: Use when OTTERS Stage II per-gene TWAS Z-scores from five training models must be rescaled via genomic control and converted to p values for downstream ACAT-O omnibus aggregation.

name: summed-up-rank-scoring
description: Use when per-cell gene set scores are needed from smoothed scRNA-seq AnnData and a simple rank/count-sum statistic should serve as the score, or when a one-dimensional score threshold (e.g., the median) must classify cells by condition such as LPS treatment.

name: sunburst-enrichment-visualization
description: Use when you have InterCellar functional annotation of int-pairs for ≥2 conditions and need a per-condition sunburst view of terms significant at p < 0.05 (e.g., reproducing Fig. 6 for COVID-19 critical vs moderate).

name: super-kmer-extraction
description: Use when building or querying a PAC index and you need k-mers grouped by minimizer into super-k-mers, split into 4^p partition files, and resolved via per-partition inverted Bloom filters.

name: supervised-cell-label-benchmarking
description: Use when training scRNA-seq data with known cell labels are available and you must quantify whether a supervised annotation method (e.g. NeuCA) outperforms existing supervised or unsupervised alternatives under varying train/test splits or conditions.

name: supervised-cell-type-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to compare classification speed or accuracy of cell type identifiers (e.g. SciBet vs scmap vs Seurat v3) across scRNA-seq datasets of increasing size, or to reproduce the Fig. 2e timing benchmark.

name: supervised-classifier-retraining-on-scrna-seq
description: Use when evaluating whether poor reference/training labels—rather than classifier architecture—limit malignant-cell annotation accuracy, by retraining Cancer-Finder or ikarus on a signature-calibrated .h5ad training set and comparing to originally reported metrics.

name: supervised-classifier-training-and-evaluation
description: Use when cell-type labels are available for scRNA-seq data and you need to benchmark classification performance of alternative feature sets (e.g., CKG vs gene expression) across multiple classifiers and train/test splits.

name: supervised-dimensionality-reduction-lda
description: Use when single-cell data (cells-by-markers matrix) has known a priori class labels (e.g., day0-day5 time points, cell-cycle phase, cell line) and the goal is a low-dimensional, interpretable visualization or projection of unlabeled cells onto axes trained on labeled cells.

name: supervised-label-transfer-ingest
description: Use when an unannotated query single-cell dataset has a closely related annotated reference (e.g. HuBMAP spleen data) and reference-based label transfer is preferred over de novo clustering.

name: supervised-machine-learning-inference-on-genomic-bins
description: Use when you have a sample-specific transcriptome (GTF), genome-aligned RNA-Seq (sorted BAM), and genome FASTA, and need de novo polyA site prediction via machine learning rather than assembler coverage heuristics or annotated polyA site databases.

name: supervised-model-application-to-empirical-data
description: Use when a pre-trained supervised model (e.g., CLOUDe NN classifier/predictor in .hdf5 format) must be applied to an empirical test dataset of deletion events formatted as a space-delimited N+1 x 3m expression matrix to recover per-event classes and parameters.

name: supervised-multiclass-classifier-training
description: Use when a labeled global RNA-seq gene-expression matrix (e.g., 19,737 TCGA genes) must be mapped to predefined classes and no reference sample cohort is available, requiring a comparative ML survey of classifiers.

name: supervised-multinomial-classifier-training
description: Use when annotating single-cell TME data at fine subtype resolution across five compartments (T.cells, Myeloid.cells, B.cells, Fibroblast, Endothelial) and you need a supervised classifier trained on published reference datasets with cross-validated accuracy/kappa evaluation.

name: supervised-pca-integration-embedding-handling
description: Use when a SingCellaR object already contains Supervised PCA embeddings plus cell-metadata covariates (e.g. sample/batch), and multiple scRNA-seq samples must be batch-corrected and clustered into a single integrated embedding.

name: supplementary-figure-reproduction-from-manuscript-code
description: Use when a manuscript ships a code/data repository (GitHub + Zenodo) and a target supplementary figure must be reproduced by executing the authors' scripts and comparing outputs to the paper's reported values.

name: supplementary-file-benchmarking-across-journals
description: Use when you need to benchmark a corpus of published supplementary files (e.g. from Mark Ziemann's gene_name_errors dashboard) for a recurring data-integrity defect, and report screened/affected/autocorrected counts per journal and in total.
tools: Mark Ziemann's gene name errors dashboard

name: supplementary-table-comparison
description: Use when validating a clustering benchmark from a scRNA-seq paper: simulated or real datasets with ground-truth labels exist, and the goal is to reproduce the published NMI/ARI values in supplementary comparison tables for the proposed method vs. competitors.

name: supplementary-table-data-compilation
description: Use when a reproduction task requires assembling per-method performance metrics (F1, accuracy, G-mean, Cohen's Kappa, MCC) and rare-identification success counts from multiple method outputs into a single benchmark table.

name: supplementary-table-enrichment-result-reproduction
description: Use when a FAVA protein association network edge list must be partitioned into functional clusters via MCL and the cluster-level functional enrichment results must be reproduced to match Supplementary Table S1.

name: supplementary-table-reproduction
description: Use when a paper reports a numeric summary table (e.g. marker-overlap percentages) and the goal is to independently regenerate those values from source data rather than trust the reported numbers.

name: support-vector-regression-ensemble-training
description: Use when a reference atlas (e.g. mTCA.seurat.slim.qs) has a low-dimensional embedding and you must train the mapping from gene-set score matrices to UMAP_1/2 coordinates.

name: surface-marker-enrichment-testing
description: Use when single-cell RNA-Seq data has both per-cell signalling entropy scores (from SCENT) and known surface-marker annotations (e.g. CD34/CD96), and you must verify that top-entropy cells correspond to the marker-defined CSC population.

name: surface-protein-imputation-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when the input is a UMI-based scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Seurat v3 object from HCA CBMC/BMMC or AML samples) and cell-surface protein levels such as CD56, CD16, CD57, CD34, CD38 are needed but CITE-seq/REAP-seq was not performed.

name: surface-protein-imputation-model-retraining
description: Use when benchmarking how preprocessing choices (skipping SAVER-X denoising, altered normalization) affect cTP-net protein-imputation accuracy on paired CITE-seq transcriptome–protein data.

name: surrogate-groundtruth-label-construction
description: Use when you need to validate clustering or joint embedding of scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq from a heterogeneous population (e.g., healthy donor BMMC) for which FACS-sorted bulk cell-type signatures are already available.

name: surrogate-variable-gene-association-testing
description: Use when IA-SVA has returned a significant surrogate variable on scRNA-seq count data and you need the marker genes driving that SV (e.g., SV1 marker-gene table from alpha-cell counts).

name: surrogate-variable-inference-from-scrna-seq-counts
description: Use when scRNA-seq read-count matrices are suspected to contain hidden factors (e.g., cell-cycle stage, doublets, patient-specific effects) correlated with known covariates, and a surrogate variable plus associated gene set is needed while adjusting for patient_id and library size.

name: surrogate-variable-significance-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq read-count data appear homogeneous after known covariate adjustment but residual heterogeneity is suspected, and you need to test significance of hidden factors and estimate how many SVs to keep.

name: survival-analysis-cox-proportional-hazards
description: Use when TCGA gene expression matrices and patient clinical metadata (vital status, days to death, days to follow-up) are available and gene sets (e.g. network-derived IC genes) must be tested for prognostic association with overall survival and compared via Concordance statistic.

name: survival-association-analysis
description: Use when you have per-sample bulk-transcriptome embeddings or attention-head features from tGPT plus TCGA overall survival annotations, and you need to test prognostic significance per cancer type.

name: survival-curve-plot-rendering
description: Use when a fitted dipm or spmtree tree (e.g., anorexia continuous-outcome or GBSG2 survival-outcome trees) needs per-node treatment-group plots rendered via partykit::plot.

name: survival-data-preprocessing
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq or microarray expression and matched survival data must be cleaned and normalized before building marker gene-pair (IMGP) prognostic models, e.g., TCGA SKCM06 melanoma cohort input.

name: survival-log-rank-pvalue-zscoring
description: Use when building the CRIT feature matrix for candidate circRNA regulators/RBPs and you need to quantify, per gene, how significantly its alterations (mutation/CNV) impact TCGA patient survival.

name: survival-logrank-pvalue-comparison
description: Use when you need to judge which batch correction method preserves biologically meaningful (survival-relevant) gene signals, by comparing log-rank survival P values of method-specific DEG signatures against TCGA bulk transcriptomes.

name: survival-tree-fitting
description: Use when analyzing censored survival outcomes (Surv time-to-event data) from a clinical study with a treatment arm, to find covariate-defined subgroups where one treatment underperforms.

name: svd-based-pca-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model with sample-specific manifold parameter matrices (model$params$Qi) and need a low-dimensional sample-level embedding to visualize how samples cluster by donor or technology.

name: svd-based-pca-module-projection
description: Use when a normalized gene expression matrix (genes as rows, samples as columns) must be reduced to per-gene-set activity scores with statistical significance, distinguishing shifted from overdispersed modules.

name: svd-based-principal-component-extraction
description: Use when analyzing a scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Lawlor alpha cells, 101 cells) and you need the singular vectors/PCs — e.

name: svd-cross-validation-component-number-selection
description: Use when a normalized, scaled scRNA-seq matrix has been PCA-transformed in Seurat and the number of informative PCs feeding t-SNE/UMAP or clustering must be chosen objectively rather than by eye.

name: svd-low-rank-approximation
description: Use when a normalized scRNA-seq count matrix (cells as rows, genes as columns) contains a large fraction of zeros (e.g. >90% with droplet-based data) and you need a low-rank approximation to complete technical zeros before adaptive thresholding.

name: svd-pathway-activation-score-computation
description: Use when a normalized gene-by-cell scRNA-seq matrix must be transformed into a pathway-by-cell activity matrix (pca_scCell_mat) prior to downstream association testing, or when quantifying how pathway-level aggregation reduces single-cell sparsity.

name: svg-methods-vs-hvg-feature-ranking
description: Use when comparing feature-selection strategies (SVG-ranking methods vs HVGs) as inputs to unsupervised spatial clustering, and you need a quantitative ARI comparison against annotated tissue domains on spatially-resolved transcriptomics data.

name: svg-rank-reproducibility-evaluation-against-known-markers
description: Use when replicating or auditing an SVG-detection result on spatially-resolved transcriptomics data where published per-gene rankings, adjusted p-values, and recovery of known biological marker genes must be verified.

name: svg-recovery-overlap-analysis
description: Use when Splane-style spatial domain labels exist for Visium slices (e.g., the 12 human DLPFC slices) and you must quantify how many annotated layer SVGs each domain-detection method recovers.

name: svm-cell-type-annotation-cross-validation
description: Use when you have scATAC-seq profiles (e.g., PBMC multiome held-out test cells) whose RNA equivalents were translated by scButterfly-C and you need automatic cell type annotation with cross-validated performance metrics.

name: svm-cell-type-classification
description: Use when comparing how well alternative single-cell multiomics embeddings support supervised cell-type identification — e.g. testing whether scME's joint representation beats Seurat, totalVI, MOFA+, or unimodal embeddings on labeled CITE-seq data.

name: svm-classifier-training
description: Use when you have per-sample cell-type abundance estimates (e.g., from DCNet deconvolution of TCGA bulk RNA-seq) and need to classify samples into discrete subtypes such as LUAD vs LUSC.

name: svm-kernel-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when training an RBF-kernel SVM on fused sequence-encoded features (e.g., PSP, k-mer, PCPseDNC, PseEIIP) and default hyperparameters underperform, so C and gamma must be optimized against 10-fold CV accuracy.

name: svm-phase-classification-and-age-regression
description: Use when benchmarking feature selection methods on proteomic-imaging single-cell data with ground truth labels, to test whether a top-p feature subset (e.g. p=30) preserves biologically meaningful signals like cell cycle phase and continuous cell age.

name: svm-sgd-recursive-feature-elimination
description: Use when a single-cell expression matrix (CSV) with user-defined class labels must be reduced to discriminative features prior to graph embedding or correlation transformation, especially when class filtering (--min_threshold 5 / --max_threshold 300) has already been applied.

name: swapped-molecule-exclusion-in-10x-experiments
description: Use when running a negative control for the swapped-molecule removal algorithm on non-multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet datasets, or when validating that molecule exclusion does not over-remove on HiSeq 2500-sequenced data.

name: swapped-molecule-fraction-quality-control
description: Use when running the swapped-molecule removal algorithm as a control on non-multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet scRNA-seq samples (e.g. HiSeq 2500-sequenced mouse epithelial cells from ArrayExpress E-MTAB-6854) to verify that molecule removal is negligible.

name: swapped-molecule-fraction-thresholding
description: Use when multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries (e.g. sequenced on patterned flow-cell HiSeq 4000) share molecule information files and you must remove or reassign reads mislabelled by barcode swapping (~2.5% on HiSeq 4000).

name: swapped-read-fraction-regression-estimation
description: Use when raw demultiplexed scRNA-seq FASTQs from patterned flow-cell machines (HiSeq 4000/X/NovaSeq) are available with per-sample index barcodes, and you need to quantify the fraction of barcode-swapped (mislabelled) reads or validate that swapping is machine-specific.

name: sweep-pvalue-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when you have fitted an EMBEDR_sweep object over multiple perplexity/kEff values (with n_data_embed>=3 and null embeddings) and need to summarize which scales yield the largest fraction of minimal EMBEDR p-values.

name: sweep-summary-visualization
description: Use when an EMBEDR_sweep over perplexity/kEff values has been fitted and you need to visualize per-sample p-value distributions across scales or summarize p-value trajectories by annotation groups (e.g. Tabula Muris cell types).

name: switching-permutation-null-network-generation
description: Use when a dense subnetwork has been extracted from a TF-target adjacency matrix and its edge-density objective value must be tested against a null distribution of random networks that preserve each node's in- and out-degree.

name: symmetrized-multiclass-error-computation
description: Use when cluster-labeled single-cell profiles exist and you need to quantify, per cluster pair or triple (e.g. C5-C6-C7 vs C2-C3-C4), whether a transition pathway is supported by class-confusability rather than geometry alone.

name: symphony-query-mapping
description: Use when an mRNA-only query dataset must be placed into an existing integrated reference atlas (e.g., a CITE-seq memory T-cell reference of ~395,373 cells) to transfer cell-type annotations or infer modalities absent from the query, such as surface proteins.

name: symsim-parameter-configuration
description: Use when you need ground-truth single-cell RNA-seq benchmark data with known cell-type labels and latent pseudotime to evaluate whether feature selection methods preserve cell types and cellular trajectories.

name: synapse-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when reproducing the scTriangulate benchmarking analyses that rely on alternative clustering results (ICGS2, Monocle3, Seurat3, curated annotations) from a prior study deposited only in Synapse, not regenerable from GEO raw counts.

name: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-evaluation
description: Use when a gold-standard synthetic single-cell dataset with known ground-truth trajectory topology (e.g. two bifurcations) and true pseudotime is available, and multiple trajectory-inference methods must be compared on branching detection and pseudotime ordering.

name: synthetic-benchmark-dataset-generation
description: Use when you must compare clustering algorithms under known ground truth: non-convex low-dimensional shapes (ring, half-moon) or Gaussian mixtures where reference labels are available for purity computation.

name: synthetic-benchmark-pair-generation
description: Use when you need reproducible paired trajectory-tree datasets with known topology to benchmark branched pseudotime alignment methods, or to stress-test alignment robustness against topological and clustering disruptions.

name: synthetic-chimera-sequence-construction
description: Use when you need to quantify how well a transcriptome assembly filtering pipeline (e.g. Bellerophon's TPM, CD-HIT-EST, TransRate-C steps) removes chimeric versus nonchimeric contigs, by planting known synthetic chimeras whose fate can be traced.

name: synthetic-compositional-data-generation
description: Use when benchmarking differential abundance/compositional testing methods on single-cell count data, when ground-truth cell-type effects must be known, or when testing performance at low replicate numbers (n0=n1∈{1..5}).

name: synthetic-data-distribution-comparison
description: Use when comparing synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data generated by deep generative models (scDBM, scVI) against original count matrices to assess per-gene distribution fidelity, including detecting bimodality failures.

name: synthetic-data-label-assignment
description: Use when preparing a reference cell-by-gene matrix (e.g., xx_expr.txt with xx_meta.txt labels) for classifier training and some cell types are too rare relative to Nmax, causing models to ignore minority classes.

name: synthetic-data-quality-evaluation
description: Use when you have synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data generated by scDBM or scVI (prior/posterior variants) from pilot sub-samples (e.

name: synthetic-data-reference-matching
description: Use when a simulated single-cell dataset must be shown to have count-level characteristics (library sizes, dropouts, dispersions, correlations) comparable to a real scRNA-seq reference dataset.

name: synthetic-dataset-file-generation
description: Use when a benchmark of batch-integration tools needs controlled two-batch scRNA-seq count matrices where batch magnitude, dropout rate, batch-size imbalance, or cell-type composition must be varied systematically.

name: synthetic-dataset-generation
description: Use when benchmarking a clustering method against ground truth and no labeled real data is available; controlled synthetic problems with tunable noise and cluster shape are needed to expose failure modes of general-purpose algorithms.

name: synthetic-dataset-generation
description: Use when you need to benchmark a feature-selection algorithm on data where the truly relevant features are known by construction, e.g. to measure false discovery rate on probe-laden synthetic matrices.

name: synthetic-differential-expression-perturbation
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell drug repurposing pipelines (e.g., ASGARD vs. Alakwaa's vs. Guo's) for AUC robustness across simulation grids where ground truth must be known by construction rather than inferred.

name: synthetic-differentiation-trajectory-simulation
description: Use when you need a controlled single-cell count dataset with known data-generating expression rates and batch-confounded cell states to test whether a batch-correction or disentanglement method recovers the truth.

name: synthetic-dyngen-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a dynamics-aware latent model batch-corrects cell states and velocities better than gene-space correction (ComBat, scGen) on multi-batch synthetic data with a bifurcating trajectory.

name: synthetic-gaussian-cluster-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking whether a clustering method can infer newly emerging clusters in streaming out-of-sample data, and you need controllable ground-truth labels and tunable cluster-count/noise conditions.

name: synthetic-gene-dynamics-simulation
description: Use when validating an RNA velocity or gene regulation model on data with known ground truth, specifically to test recovery of signed TF-target regulatory weights and RNA velocity from simulated counts.

name: synthetic-gene-expression-matrix-generation
description: Use when a biclustering benchmark requires controlled synthetic test data with known implanted bicluster positions, e.g. Types I-VI (trend-preserving, column-constant, row-constant, shift-scale, shift, scale) planted in N(0,1) backgrounds.

name: synthetic-genotype-data-generation
description: Use when you need controlled synthetic GWAS data (SNP matrix × binary phenotype) with known planted associations to benchmark pattern-mining methods such as HOGImine, SiNIMin or FastCMH under FWER control.

name: synthetic-ground-truth-benchmark-scoring
description: Use when evaluating a GRN-inference or multi-omics integration method on MOSim-simulated bulk or single-cell data where the simulated active regulatory relationships serve as ground truth for benchmarking.

name: synthetic-ground-truth-count-generation-for-deduplication-benchmarking
description: Use when you need a synthetic scRNA-seq UMI count matrix as deduplication ground truth: you have real gene/inter-gene by-cell UMI count matrices (BAM-derived) and cells falling in distinct clusters or continuous trajectories.

name: synthetic-ivt-basecalling-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a basecalling model ab initio distinguishes modified nucleotides (I vs m6A vs canonical) on synthetic constructs where ground-truth modification sites are known.

name: synthetic-lethality-pair-identification
description: Use when you have context-specific metabolic models with a viral biomass objective function and need to enumerate gene pairs whose joint knockout eliminates viral biomass while single knockouts remain viable.

name: synthetic-moons-dataset-simulation
description: Use when a clustering algorithm or intrinsic clustering-quality measure needs benchmarking on non-globular (interleaved crescent) clusters where ground truth is known and noise level can be controlled.

name: synthetic-multi-view-data-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking or validating JIVE/scJIVE decompositions against known ground truth: you need simulated multi-view matrices with controlled joint rank, individual ranks, and residual error to measure runtime differences or agreement of joint/individual/residual variance proportions.

name: synthetic-network-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking multi-subject dynamic community detection (e.g. MuDCoD) and you need synthetic S x T x N adjacency tensors with known node labels across subjects and time points.

name: synthetic-null-coexpression-dataset-generation
description: Use when a null dataset with known ground-truth expression proportions and no true gene co-expression is needed to calibrate or benchmark normalization and co-expression/confounder-detection methods on scRNA-seq read counts.

name: synthetic-perturbation-batch-effect-disentanglement
description: Use when integrating multiple batches of synthetic (dyngen) or real single-cell spliced/unspliced data where one batch carries a perturbation (e.g., gene-module knockout) and batch effects must be separated from perturbation effects in a joint latent space.

name: synthetic-posterior-verification-design
description: Use when implementing or validating a Bayesian differential activity test (e.g., VEGA's Bayes Factor test on VAE latent GMVs) and you need a ground-truth scenario with one known-differential and one known-non-differential module.

name: synthetic-sc-rnaseq-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq differential expression methods on synthetic data with known ground truth (pDE genes), e.g. comparing power/FDR across UMI (CPLM) vs non-UMI (ZICP) platform regimes.

name: synthetic-scrna-seq-network-benchmarking
description: Use when a new GRN inference method must be validated against baselines on synthetic scRNA-seq data where the true TF-target network (BoolODE toggle-switch ground truth) is known, so AUROC/AUPRC/EPR can be computed exactly.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking malignant/non-malignant classification methods on synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground-truth labels, especially when quantifying robustness to dropout noise via F1 scores.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-dataset-merging
description: Use when evaluating cancer-cell prediction on data lacking mixed ground truth: you have one all-malignant and one all-normal scRNA-seq matrix and need a labeled mixed benchmark to compute FPR, FNR, accuracy and AUROC.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-graph-generation
description: Use when implementing or validating a graph-based scRNA-seq model (e.g. scGAE) and you need a small synthetic count matrix plus a KNN cell graph to run dimension-checked forward-pass tests before touching real datasets.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-pairwise-alignment-evaluation
description: Use when a tree/trajectory alignment method must be quantitatively compared to data-integration baselines over many synthetic dataset pairs, using ATC scores and Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values as the benchmark metric.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-pattern-recovery-evaluation
description: Use when you need to validate that a cell-state decomposition recovers a known number of ground-truth identity/activity patterns (e.g., 13 activity patterns) on synthetic single-cell RNA-seq data with controlled noise.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking rare-cell detection methods needs ground-truth controls — e.g. an artificial ~1% rare population (splatter, group.prob c(0.99, 0.01)) or DE-gene titration on a subsampled dataset like 1%Jurkat.h5.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking temporal scRNA-seq visualization or trajectory methods on data with known ground truth — you need synthetic gene-by-cell count matrices with defined lineage and time-point labels.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-simulation-data-handling
description: Use when a simulated scRNA-seq count/expression matrix with synthetic cell-type labels (dozens of classes, thousands of genes) must be analyzed to measure how marker-panel size affects label recovery and wall-clock runtime.

name: synthetic-scrnaseq-simulation-splat
description: Use when you need ground-truth-controlled scRNA-seq datasets (known batches, known cell types) to reproduce or validate integration-metric behavior, e.g., checking whether iLISI favors overcorrected embeddings.

name: synthetic-single-cell-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has simulated/labelled doublets and known simulated-DEG labels, and you need to rank doublet-detection or removal methods by downstream DEG accuracy rather than doublet-call metrics alone.

name: synthetic-single-cell-label-classification
description: Use when a synthetic or real scRNA-seq dataset has many (tens of) cell labels and you must decide whether joint, label-aware marker selection outperforms per-label one-vs-all gene scoring for label classification.

name: synthetic-single-cell-rna-seq-simulation
description: Use when a decomposition choice (e.g., ICA vs NMF) must be validated for program recovery on single-cell expression data, or when designing simulation-based benchmarks with known embedded transcriptional signatures.

name: synthetic-single-cell-rnaseq-simulation
description: Use when a trajectory-inference method must be evaluated on controlled synthetic scRNA-seq data with known structure, using gene-expression smoothness metrics along pseudotime rather than only qualitative figure comparison.

name: synthetic-single-cell-simulation-training
description: Use when you need a ground-truth benchmark of transcriptomic forecasting accuracy where the true future expression states of cells are known, using simulated single-cell data (e.g. BoolODE random 10-gene networks with paired t=0/t=1 count matrices).

name: synthetic-sparse-matrix-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking a scRNA-seq preprocessing pipeline's signal detection: you need a controlled sparse synthetic matrix with a known TGC bias to test whether normalization creates or removes artificial eigenvalue signals.

name: synthetic-toggle-switch-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when validating a logic-based GRN inference method on synthetic scRNA-seq data where the ground-truth Boolean regulatory rules are known (e.g. BoolODE toggle-switch simulations), and you need to confirm recovered gates match designed AND/OR/NOT logic.

name: synthetic-trajectory-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing TI algorithms on simulated single-cell trajectories (e.g., multifurcating, cyclic, disconnected, or converging topologies) where dyntoy gold-standard milestone/pseudotime/cell-fate labels exist and a composite accuracy ranking is needed.

name: synthetic-trajectory-tree-generation
description: Use when a branched-trajectory alignment method needs a controlled noise-robustness or accuracy benchmark and real paired scRNA-seq datasets are unavailable.

name: t-cell-development-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when analyzing single-cell RNA-seq from differentiating T cells (e.g. DN to CD4+/CD8+ SP thymocytes) and you need clustering-independent DEG prediction along a pseudotime trajectory rather than between predefined clusters.

name: t-cell-differentiation-pseudotime-visualization

name: t-cell-naive-effector-subtype-annotation

name: t-cell-state-annotation

name: t-nk-cell-subsetting-from-integrated-object

name: t-test-predictor-filtering
description: Use when a binary-outcome dataset has many predictors (P >> n) and you must pre-select features before lasso/elastic-net fitting while keeping performance estimates unbiased under nested CV.

name: tabnet-based-cell-type-classification

name: tabnet-deep-learning-training

name: tabnet-feature-mask-interpretability

name: tabnet-model-training

name: tabula-muris-count-matrix-ingestion
description: Use when raw Tabula Muris FACS per-tissue count CSVs (e.g., Diaphragm-counts.csv from the Figshare deposit) must be loaded into a cell-by-gene count matrix before QC, normalization, and PCA.

name: tabula-muris-dataset-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing or validating cluster-purity benchmarks on the Tabula Muris brain dataset, or when testing whether ROGUE-guided re-clustering resolves impure oligodendrocyte/neuron clusters into pure subtypes.

name: tabula-sapiens-cell-type-annotation-matching
description: Use when evaluating whether an embedding or kernel method improves unsupervised cell-type recovery on Tabula Sapiens organ tissues (<10,000 cells, PBMCs screened out), with ARI against expert manual annotations.

name: tabular-cell-type-classifier-training
description: Use when training or benchmarking a cross-tissue cell type annotation model on normalized tabular scRNA-seq data, or testing whether data augmentation improves holdout-donor generalization.

name: tabular-deep-learning-inference

name: tabular-deep-learning-model-training

name: tabular-expression-data-ingestion

name: tabular-feature-index-export

name: target-perturbed-network-in-silico-perturbation

name: target-tissue-prioritization-for-disease-loci
description: Use when you have GWAS summary statistics for a complex trait plus eQTL summary statistics for many tissues, a reference LD matrix, and you need to identify which tissue's regulatory effects explain a disease locus.

name: tarone-fwer-pruning-threshold-updating
description: Use when mining high-order genetic interaction patterns (binary or additive encoded SNPs within mapped gene intervals) with a CMH test and you must avoid enumerating the full pattern space while controlling FWER.

name: tcga-alteration-feature-interpretation

name: tcga-barcode-sample-matching

name: tcga-bulk-rnaseq-cohort-stratification

name: tcga-cancer-network-evaluation
description: Use when you have constructed gene co-expression or differential co-expression networks (e.g. from TCGA tumor/normal RNA-seq) and need to verify they approximately satisfy a scale-free topology before downstream driver-node analysis.

name: tcga-clinical-data-integration
description: Use when a tumor subpopulation gene signature (e.g., top DEGs from a Scanpy cluster like Cluster 4 with PTMA and STMN1) must be validated against TCGA patient survival data to assess prognostic significance.

name: tcga-clinical-metadata-harmonization

name: tcga-clinical-survival-analysis

name: tcga-clinical-survival-data-analysis

name: tcga-clinical-transcriptome-data-integration

name: tcga-gtex-cohort-harmonization

name: tcga-lung-cancer-subtype-comparison

name: tcga-multi-omics-data-integration

name: tcga-mutation-call-curation

name: tcga-rna-seq-matrix-processing

description: Use when TCGA RNA-Seq FPKM data must be turned into normalized gene expression matrices for network analysis, and background/noisy genes must be removed via a mean zFPKM > -3.0 activity threshold.

name: tcga-sample-metadata-merging
description: Use when TCGA pan-cancer sample-level flux features must be joined to an external per-sample signature table (e.g., Winter hypoxia scores) by TCGA sample barcode before association testing.

name: tcga-somatic-mutation-data-processing
description: Use when the analysis needs TCGA somatic mutation data downloaded and screened to a survival-analysis-ready design matrix — e.g., genes mutated in ≥1% of patients with patient overall survival times and censoring indicators as the outcome.

name: tcga-survival-clinical-data-harmonization
description: Use when sample-level pseudotimes or trajectory scores must be tested against TCGA overall survival outcomes, requiring clinical covariate adjustment and stratification (e.g. by ER status) via Cox regression.

name: tcga-survival-stratification
description: Use when you need to quantify whether gene signatures derived from batch-corrected scRNA-seq data (e.g., tumor-vs-normal DEGs) preserve clinically meaningful survival signal, as benchmarked across methods like scCobra, Seurat, Harmony, Scanorama, and scVI.

name: tcga-train-test-split-evaluation
description: Use when you need to reproduce or extend the RMSE comparison of DCNet/autoencoder cell-landscape variants across a TCGA train/test split and an independent single-cell validation set such as GSE81861.

name: tclust-alpha-parameter-tuning
description: Use when running SkewC's 2_SkewC.sh trim-clustering step and you need to choose or adjust the alpha trimming proportion (e.g., alpha=0.04 with k=1 for the 1k Brain Cells E18 Mouse dataset) to control the typical/skewed cell split.

name: tcn-rna-editing-site-classification-inference
description: Use when you have tabix-indexed REDItools outTables from RNAseq BAMs and need to classify A-to-G substitutions as genuine A-to-I RNA editing vs RNA variants/sequencing artifacts without coupled DNA sequencing.

name: tcr-cdr3-sequence-preprocessing
description: Use when paired single-cell transcriptome + TCR data must be prepared for antigen specificity prediction or clustering, and TCR input must be restricted to CDR3β for fair method comparison (e.g., mvTCR vs tessa).

name: tcr-clonotype-assignment-per-mouse
description: Use when paired single-cell transcriptome plus full-length TCR sequencing of CD8 TILs (e.g. >3500 cells from seven tumor-bearing mice, GSE116390) must be grouped into clonotypes per mouse before comparing clonal overlap across transcriptomic states.

name: tcr-fate-prediction-benchmarking-against-annotations
description: Use when a T-cell trajectory method (e.g., VDJ feature space vs expression-only PCs) must be validated by comparing predicted cell fates against existing cell-type annotations such as CD8+T, CD4+T, DP(P)_T and DP(Q)_T labels.

name: tcr-modality-contribution-quantification
description: Use when a trained mvTCR joint model is available and you need cell-level attribution of TCR information in the shared embedding, or to check if modality contribution correlates with TCR sequence similarity across antigen-specificity groups.

name: tcr-transcriptome-integration-analysis
description: Use when paired scRNA-seq + TCR-seq data (e.g. 10x dataset with >60k cells) with specificity or pMHC multimer avidity annotations is available and the goal is antigen-specificity classification or pMHC read-count regression from a joint embedding.

name: tcrdist-similarity-computation
description: Use when you have paired single-cell TCR data stratified by antigen specificity (e.g., epitope groups like GILGFVFTL, GLCTLVAML) and need a sequence-similarity measure per group or a similarity metric to correlate against embedding-based scores.

name: te-expression-quantification-benchmarking
description: Use when validating or comparing a single-cell RNA-Seq transposable element quantification method against known ground truth, especially when assessing accuracy on repetitive young TEs where multi-mapping read assignment is problematic.

name: te-index-construction
description: Use when starting a scTE-based analysis: you have a genome assembly (mm10, hg38, panTro6, macFas5, dm6, danRer11, xenTro9) and need a TE index from RepeatMasker rmsk annotation, or a custom TE BED plus gene GTF, before counting reads.

name: te-locus-coverage-vector-construction
description: Use when you need per-locus flanking read-context features for TE quantification from STAR/STARsolo-mapped single-cell BAMs, e.g. to train MATES' AE/MLP or predict locus-specific multi-mapping ratios alpha.

name: te-marker-association-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell TE count matrix (locus-specific, e.g. from MATES) is available and cell populations have been clustered, and you need to test which TE loci act as markers of those populations or of co-expressed gene markers.

name: te-read-locus-enrichment-binomial-testing
description: Use when validating locus-specific TE quantification: after assigning TE reads to loci in single-cell data, test whether reads of a candidate marker TE family are significantly enriched in bins flanking known marker gene loci (e.g., Zscan4c/Zscan4d in mouse 2CLC).

name: te-read-overlap-quantification
description: Use when starting from CellRanger- or STAR-processed scRNA-Seq BAM files and needing to add locus-specific TE expression (not just family-level metagenes) to a gene-by-cell expression matrix for downstream tools like Seurat.

name: te-subfamily-correlation-analysis
description: Use when comparing TE quantification methods on short-read single-cell data and matched long-read (scNanoRNAseq or PacBio) data exist from the same cells/tissue to serve as ground truth for subfamily-level accuracy validation.

name: te-te-expression-correlation-analysis
description: Use when single-cell BAM/SAM files from a differentiation or development time course are available and you need to verify TE quantification quality or detect coordinated TE programs by correlating cell-by-TE counts.

name: te-tool-benchmarking-scrnaseq
description: Use when evaluating or selecting a computational tool for TE expression quantification in scRNA-Seq data, or when validating that a new TE tool recovers biologically expected marker TEs in a defined cell population.

name: te-vs-gene-clustering-agreement-ari-nmi
description: Use when you have independently clustered the same cells from a TE count matrix and a gene expression matrix and need to measure concordance, or when validating that a TE quantification method (e.g., MATES) reproduces known cell states like the mouse 2CLC population.

name: technical-confounder-regression-scrna-seq
description: Use when raw UMI scRNA-seq count matrices must be normalized for downstream association testing (DE, CRISPR screen, co-expression) and nonlinear library-size effects need removal at mean and variance levels.

name: technical-effect-augmentation-of-generative-models
description: Use when a count-based generative model (Negative Binomial likelihood, e.g., MIRA RP topic models) must be trained or evaluated on multi-batch single-cell data where technical effects would otherwise distort the held-out likelihood comparison.

name: technical-noise-parameter-sweep
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell RNA-Seq analysis methods (e.g., differential expression detection) and you need to determine how performance degrades with fewer cells or lower capture efficiency.

name: technical-variation-modeling
description: Use when you have a simulated or real true-count matrix (genes x cells) and need to generate realistic observed scRNA-seq read/UMI counts reflecting capture efficiency, PCR amplification bias, gene length bias, and sequencing depth.

name: technical-variation-pca-scoring
description: Use when evaluating whether a batch-correction/integration method (e.g. scMerge2) actually reduced technical variation across datasets, protocols or technologies, or when comparing raw vs adjusted matrices for label-mixing in PCA space.

name: technology-geometry-string-formatting
description: Use when preprocessing single-cell RNA/ATAC/tag/protein FASTQs (e.g. dogmaseq-dig SRR18677638–SRR18677644 runs) and the tool-compatible technology/geometry string must be derived from the assay's seqspec spec.yaml rather than hand-written.

name: tei-calculation-sparse-annadata
description: Use when you have gene ages (an orthomap from OrthoFinder or eggNOG) matched to a scRNA-seq AnnData object and need a per-cell transcriptome evolutionary index, especially for very large datasets (thousands to millions of cells) where dense per-cell computation would be intractable.

name: temperature-scaling-post-hoc-calibration
description: Use when a trained SIMS (TabNet, PyTorch Lightning) classifier must emit trustworthy per-cell probabilities, and low-confidence cells — e.g., cell types withheld from training — need to be labeled 'unknown' via a user-adjustable threshold.

name: template-gene-set-construction
description: Use when constructing a nearest-template-prediction gene set for classifying pre-clinical models (cell lines, organoids, PDXs) and you must purge markers driven by immune/stromal tumor compartments.

name: temporal-and-subject-heterogeneity-parameterization
description: Use when benchmarking multi-subject dynamic community detection (e.g., MuDCoD) and you need simulated S x T x N gene co-expression networks with controlled similarity between adjacent time points and between subjects, plus ground-truth community labels.

name: temporal-communication-score-simulation
description: Use when validating a context-aware CCC deconvolution method: you need synthetic communication scores with embedded known temporal patterns and a ground-truth rank to test rank selection and factor recovery.

name: temporal-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data are collected at multiple timepoints (e.g., t0/t1 CASiList with Group and Time metadata) and the goal is genes whose expression changes over time or by a time-by-condition interaction, or when comparing tDEG calls with DESeq2/MAST/Seurat.

name: temporal-expression-profile-clustering
description: Use when simulated (or otherwise ground-truth-labeled) bulk time-course gene count data must be checked for faithful recovery of its assigned temporal expression patterns via unsupervised clustering.

name: temporal-fate-bias-quantification
description: Use when simulating TF overexpression with PRESCIENT across multiple time points (day 0–6) or starting populations (e.g., SOX2+, NKX6.1+, NEUROG3 subpopulations) and you need fate-bias shifts toward endocrine lineages per condition.

name: temporal-gene-expression-wave-detection
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq time course (e.g. 0/24/48/72 h myoblast differentiation) already has a trajectory/branch structure and you need to order cells to identify sequential temporal waves of gene regulation along the path.

name: temporal-latent-space-convolution
description: Use when scRNA-seq data span multiple time points (a cell-by-time-point binary time.table is available) and you need one 2D latent space that preserves global developmental trajectories and separates subpopulations within each stage.

name: temporal-reconstruction-correlation-analysis
description: Use when a known confounding spatial signal must be filtered from single-cell expression data and recovery of a hidden temporal trajectory is quantified by Pearson correlation against reference temporal marker profiles.

name: temporal-scrnaseq-dimension-reduction
description: Use when the input is a gene-by-cell count matrix from a temporal scRNA-seq time course (e.g., guo, guo2, loh, trapnell, iPSC, petropoulos, deng datasets) with a complete cell-by-time-point binary time.

name: temporal-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when input is a temporal scRNA-seq count matrix with a complete cell-by-time-point binary time.table and the goal is to preserve lineage trajectories and resolve subpopulations within stages that t-SNE or diffusion maps crowd together.

name: temporal-wave-clustering-of-differentially-regulated-genes
description: Use when cells have been reordered along a pseudo-temporal developmental trajectory and you need to identify how many distinct temporal waves of gene regulation exist and which genes (e.g. mitosis, DNA synthesis, MHC-II) occupy each wave.

name: ten-fold-cross-validation-assessment
description: Use when building clinical outcome prediction models on a cross-platform transcriptome training set and you need 10-fold cross-validation metrics plus transfer-test evaluation on an external validation dataset.

name: tensor-decomposition-network-denoising
description: Use when multiple PC-regression-derived scGRNs have been built from random cell subsamples (e.g., 10 networks x 500 cells) and edge-weight noise must be smoothed before downstream comparison or recall evaluation.

name: tensor-denoising-of-multilayer-networks
description: Use when you have constructed multiple candidate scGRNs per condition (e.g., 10 networks from 500-cell subsamples via pcNet/makeNetworks) and need a single denoised network per condition before aligning conditions or testing differential regulation.

name: tensor-dimensionality-reduction-pooling
description: Use when a trained Keras model's hidden-layer outputs have rank > 2 (e.g., CNN feature maps from dict-encoded protein sequences) and you need a 2-D UMAP embedding to inspect representations layer by layer.

name: tensor-factorization-decomposition
description: Use when you have communication scores from multiple contexts (e.g., 12 BALF COVID-19 samples: 3 control, 3 moderate, 6 severe) and need to deconvolve them into context-driven communication patterns simultaneously.

name: tensor-factorization-of-communication-scores
description: Use when you have per-context communication scores (e.g., CellChat LR-pair scores for control/moderate/severe COVID-19 BALF samples) and need to deconvolve them into factors that vary jointly across LR pairs, cell types, and patient contexts.

name: tensorflow-autoencoder-training
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq count matrices (preprocessed with scanpy/anndata, HVG-selected) where dropout events are high and cell-cell topology should be preserved, or when reproducing scMGCA's multinomial decoder training.

name: tensorflow-custom-layer-implementation
description: Use when a generative model for scRNA-seq must output expression vectors constrained to a target per-cell library size, and the architecture requires a custom differentiable layer rather than an off-the-shelf normalization op.

name: tensorflow-gan-training-workflow
description: Use when a scRNA-seq subpopulation is too sparse for reliable downstream analysis (e.g. classifier F1 degradation after downsampling) and synthetic cell generation with a GAN is needed.

name: tensorflow-graph-session-execution
description: Use when implementing or reproducing a multi-loss GAN (adversarial + cycle + correspondence) in TensorFlow 1.x-style graph/session mode where generator and discriminator must be optimized in a strict per-iteration order with logged diagnostics.

name: tensorflow-keras-model-training
description: Use when building a supervised binary classifier (viral vs. human) over fixed-length sequence fragments (e.g., 48 bp RNA-seq reads) with TensorFlow/Keras, or when retraining baseline models on an identical training split for a fair benchmark.

name: tensorflow-keras-network-construction
description: Use when constructing a denoising autoencoder in TensorFlow/Keras to learn latent embeddings from raw scRNA-seq count matrices, explicitly modeling zero inflation (dropout) via a zero-inflated negative binomial reconstruction loss.

name: tensorflow-neural-network-training
description: Use when a raw scRNA-Seq count matrix needs deep-learning-based denoising/imputation and you must reconstruct the AutoClass architecture (autoencoder + classifier branch with pre-clustering) in TensorFlow.

name: tenx-scrnaseq-sample-preparation
description: Use when starting from raw 10x scRNAseq data from an infected sample and you need cellranger-produced host-aligned outputs plus the unaligned read pool ready for pathogen alignment and UMI quantification (e.g., HIV, SARS-CoV-2 samples).

name: term-enrichment-ranking
description: Use when a pre-computed CCI dataset of enriched ligand-receptor int-pairs must be linked to Gene Ontology and pathway terms, e.g. to build InterCellar's function-verse ranked-term annotation table.

name: term-similarity-based-pathway-sampling
description: Use when generating synthetic benchmark data for enrichment methods where ground-truth active pathways must reflect realistic inter-pathway redundancy (e.g. shared genes), so performance can be evaluated as a function of pathway-similarity structure.

name: terminal-region-clustering-assignment
description: Use when after thresholding root/terminal probabilities (Pr, Pt) at 0.99 on the La Manno-style stationary states, the selected terminal cells must be partitioned into terminal regions to initialize trajectory simulations.

name: terminal-sister-node-merging
description: Use when a fitted DIPM tree (e.g. from dipm() on the MASS::anorexia weight-change data) contains terminal sister leaves whose optimal treatment assignments coincide and you want a smaller tree that preserves all treatment recommendations.

name: terminal-state-and-lineage-reconstruction
description: Use when a single-cell omics dataset (AnnData with PCA in obsm['X_pca']) needs pseudotime, automated terminal state prediction, and lineage/branch probabilities, especially for tree-like, cyclic, or disconnected topologies.

name: terminal-state-and-root-cell-definition
description: Use when a dandelionR trajectory run on a pseudobulked VDJ feature space (pb.milo) needs an explicit root and terminal states before DiffusionMap/DPT and markovProbability can be invoked.

name: terminal-state-auto-detection
description: Use when scRNA-seq (or CyTOF/scATAC) data requires automated identification of end-state cell fates and branch probabilities without manually assigning terminal states, especially for rare lineages in multifurcating or disconnected trajectories.

name: terminal-state-identification-markov-chain
description: Use when a pre-processed anndata object with cluster annotations and an RNA velocity field is available and you must determine which populations are terminal fates (e.g. which endocrine populations are absorbing states for Ngn3-low EP progenitors).

name: terminal-state-lineage-f1-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking how robustly a trajectory-inference method recovers rare terminal cell fates (e.g., mDC, pDC) under varying KNN/ncomps parameters, and when validating detected lineages by marker gene trends.

name: terminal-state-recovery-validation
description: Use when validating Cytopath trajectory inference outputs on a dataset with known terminal cell identities (e.g. pancreatic endocrinogenesis alpha/delta states) and expected co-occurring processes such as cell cycling.

name: terminal-state-supervised-simulation
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with RNA velocity should be resolved into directed differentiation trajectories whose endpoints are known terminal cell states (e.g. annotated alpha/beta/gamma/delta endocrine clusters), especially with cycling or convergent topologies.

name: ternary-simplex-coordinate-mapping
description: Use when you have a discrete cluster-target label per cell (CSV) and want to test whether one of three specific clusters is transitional between the other two, by converting per-class errors into simplex coordinates and a confusion score.

name: tesla-benchmark-pairwise-group-comparison
description: Use when you have a table of TESLA pMHC pairs with predicted binding/immunogenicity scores and experimental immunogenicity labels, and need a significance test comparing score distributions between groups.

name: tessa-functional-landscape-model-execution
description: Use when benchmarking antigen specificity prediction or clustering against a clonotype-level TCR-only baseline, or when a Bayesian TCR functional landscape estimate supervised by scRNA-Seq is required on preprocessed T cell data.

name: test-mse-and-feature-count-aggregation
description: Use when comparing feature-selecting sparse regression methods on high-dimensional omics data and you need a reproducible summary of average test MSE and selected feature counts across repeated random splits.

name: test-set-prediction-error-evaluation
description: Use when comparing penalized or latent-factor regression methods in a p >> n setting and you need unbiased out-of-sample generalization error (test MSE) plus feature-recovery quality on a synthetic or held-out benchmark.

name: tf-activity-expression-correlation-along-trajectory
description: Use when working with paired scRNA-seq/scATAC-seq (e.g., Seurat coembed.trajectory.rds) along a pseudotime trajectory and you must select candidate TFs for GRN inference, since chromVAR activity alone cannot separate TFs of the same family with similar motifs.

name: tf-activity-gradient-concordance-analysis
description: Use when you have a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell atlas with a fitted GEDI model and prior TF-gene networks, and need to test whether TF activity gradients (e.g., SPI1, CEBPA, SP1) concord with the disease vector field in a defined cell type.

name: tf-activity-inference-from-scrna-seq
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts (dgCMatrix) are available together with a TF-gene regulatory prior (e.g., DoRothEA sets A/B/C) and per-TF activity scores per cell are needed, or when TF activities must be validated against TF perturbation labels.

name: tf-affinity-summarisation-per-gene
description: Use when you have a non-overlapping candidate region bed-file with per-cell-type activity columns and need gene-level TF affinity features for downstream modelling such as INVOKE expression prediction.

name: tf-binding-affinity-pwm-scanning
description: Use when you have fine-mapped GWAS/SCZ variants with genomic coordinates and need to predict which transcription factors' binding affinities are disrupted by the risk allele versus the reference allele, specifically to prioritize variants with large (≥20-fold) motif affinity changes.

name: tf-database-candidate-selection
description: Use when fitting TFvelo gene dynamics or any per-gene model that needs a priori candidate TF regulators per target gene from ENCODE/ChEA, with a capped number of TFs per gene.

name: tf-dna-binding-motif-scanning
description: Use when you have scATAC-seq peaks linked to target genes and need to filter the universe of TFs down to a per-target-gene candidate pool before inferring a TF–gene network (e.g. as the base GRN input for scGATE).

name: tf-motif-activity-estimation-with-chromvar
description: Use when you have a paired/single-cell multiome Seurat object with an ATAC peak assay and need per-cell TF activity scores (e.g., to select candidate TFs and compute TF-gene correlations for eGRN construction along a pseudotime trajectory).

name: tf-motif-binding-evidence-integration
description: Use when building a GRN from single-cell multiome (snRNA-seq + snATAC-seq) data where candidate TF–gene interactions must be filtered by enhancer–promoter linkage plus TF motif occurrence in linked peaks, as in scMEGA's eGRN assembly.

name: tf-motif-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when scMM latent dimensions from single-cell multiomics (e.g. CITE-seq transcriptome + surface protein, or ATAC-seq accessibility) lack biological interpretation and you need to link each latent dimension to enriched TF motifs via decoded pseudocells.

name: tf-motif-enrichment-scoring
description: Use when scATAC-seq cells have been assigned to DC3 subpopulations and you need to rank transcription factors as key regulators per subpopulation from open-chromatin motif enrichment plus FPKM expression evidence.

name: tf-motif-pseudotime-trend-visualization
description: Use when you have VIA pseudotime, terminal states, and single-cell branch probabilities on scATAC-seq (or analogous single-cell) data and need to visualize TF-motif activity dynamics along lineages and validate the hierarchy.

name: tf-motif-scanning-with-pwms
description: Use when building a candidate TF–target regulatory mask from bulk ATAC-seq peaks and a PWM motif database (e.g. CisBP), to serve as an epigenetic prior for GRN inference methods such as scKINETICS.

name: tf-perturbation-velocity-scoring
description: Use when you have a fitted scKINETICS model (GRN matrix A plus original per-cell velocities) and need single-cell TF activity scores to identify regulators of a state-transition process, e.g. acinar-to-ductal metaplasia.

name: tf-regulatory-weight-normalization
description: Use when converting a gene expression matrix (e.g., TCGA tumor/normal or LINCS drug-induced profiles) into a GSFM active matrix and you need network-level FM activity via TF regulation, complementing GSFM_Up/Down and GSFM_ssGSEA.

name: tf-regulon-masked-attention-interpretation
description: Use when you need biologically interpretable cell-level attention over TF regulons from a trained TOSICA model — e.g., to order cells in pseudotime by regulon attention or compare regulon dominance between cell states or disease conditions.

name: tf-target-chipseq-overlap-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether single-cell co-expression network edges are biologically supported, by overlapping inferred TF–gene edges against known ChIP-seq TF–target interactions across cell types.

name: tf-target-database-annotation-filtering
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq data for TFvelo and each target gene needs a curated candidate TF set drawn from ENCODE/ChEA regulatory pairs before fitting TF-based gene dynamics.

name: tf-target-enrichment-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a co-expression inference method on scRNA-seq data (e.g., AD snRNA-seq or COVID PBMC) by checking that its significant co-expressed gene pairs capture known TRRUST transcription factor-target relationships more than benchmark methods.

name: tf-target-enrichment-fisher-testing
description: Use when computing the network-level GSFM_TF column of a GSFM active matrix, i.e., when a gene expression matrix and a curated TF-target regulatory database (Garcia-Alonso et al.) must be combined to quantify FM activity at the transcriptional regulatory network level.

name: tf-target-enrichment-testing
description: Use when you need to validate that a fitted gene-wise LASSO model over candidate TFs recapitulates known regulatory databases, e.g. by one-sided t-test enrichment of non-zero-weight TFs in ENCODE/ChEA TF-target sets.

name: tf-target-network-encoded-representation
description: Use when the goal is to functionally interpret scRNAseq cell clusters by encoding them with a TF-target-biased (e.g., TRRUST) autoencoder latent space and to identify which clusters the TF network can reconstruct (mean QCC and QCM >= 0.5 across runs).

name: tf-target-network-inference
description: Use when you have a preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix plus a candidate list of TFs (optionally a base GRN .parquet from scATAC-seq/motif data) and need directed, cell-type-specific TF-target edges with Bayes-Factor-ranked Boolean logic gates.

name: tf-target-network-inference-bayes-factor-ranking
description: Use when you have a small (<200 gene) scRNA-seq matrix, a candidate TF list, and an optional scATAC-seq/motif-derived base GRN parquet, and you need a directed, BF-ranked TF–target network for a specific tissue or cell type.

name: tf-target-prior-mask-construction
description: Use when building a candidate TF-target prior network from ATAC-seq peak sets (e.g. scKINETICS epigenetic prior), where TF motif scan results must be converted to a binary TF-by-gene mask restricted to expressed genes.

name: tf-target-weight-inference-evaluation
description: Use when a synthetic benchmark has known signed TF-target weights (e.g., 10 TFs per target gene) and you must quantify recovery of regulatory weights, velocities, and edges via Spearman correlation, F1, and AUROC.

name: tf-tg-regulatory-relationship-merging
description: Use when an initial GRN adjacency matrix inferred from expression data must be refined before Boolean Network conversion, and curated database interactions are available for the organism.

name: tfbm-motif-file-export
description: Use when refining an inferred GRN and you need de novo TFBM discovery over regulon promoters plus a validated exported motif file as an auxiliary refinement output.

name: tfbs-prediction-from-predicted-dnase-hypersensitivity
description: Use when TFBSs must be predicted for a sample with gene expression (FPKM matrix) but no matched DNase-seq data, and predicted DH can substitute for experimental accessibility to rank motif sites.

name: tfidf-feature-transformation
description: Use when an unnormalized scATAC-seq gene activity matrix (h5ad) must be converted into the TF-IDF-normalized target input scBridge expects, prior to intersection with scRNA-seq common genes and integration training.

name: tfidf-gene-expression-transformation
description: Use when a LogNormalized single-cell expression matrix (AnnData) and a ranked marker list must be converted into a per-cell, per-reference-cell-type score matrix for marker-based label transfer in MASI.

name: tfidf-log-count-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when comparing synthetic single-cell count matrices (e.g., from scReadSim or SCAN-ATAC-Sim) against real scATAC-seq counts in a shared low-dimensional space to compute mixing metrics such as miLISI.

name: tfidf-normalization-of-scatac-counts
description: Use when a raw scATAC-seq peak-by-cell count matrix (AnnData with cells as n_obs and peaks as n_vars) must be prepared as encoder input for a cross-modality translator such as scButterfly before modality-specific pretraining.

name: tg-oriented-boolean-function-transfer
description: Use when a refined GRN adjacency matrix must be turned into a draft Boolean Network model, and curated logical rules (Cell Collective) should be reused where possible with generic fallbacks elsewhere.

name: thresholding-based-radius-binary-search
description: Use when a large single-cell RNA-seq expression matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes/PCs) must be reduced to a fixed-size representative subset that preserves rare cell states and covers the transcriptomic space, rather than uniform subsampling.

name: tidyverse-tabular-data-wrangling
description: Use when a task requires counting, filtering, or joining the E.PATH curated database tables (gs_genes, annotations tibbles) or intersecting E.PAGE enrichment results (results$stats) across query gene lists in R.

name: til-subtype-composition-quantification
description: Use when a scRNA-seq query of T cells (e.g. tetramer+ CD8 TILs or LCMV P14 cells) needs cell subtype frequencies, or when comparing perturbation effects on T cell state proportions (e.g. KO vs WT).

name: time-course-correlation-change-analysis
description: Use when a single scRNA-seq dataset spans multiple time points (e.g. GSE75748 definitive endoderm 0/12/24/36/72/96 h) and the goal is to quantify co-expression correlation changes or hub-gene degree shifts between time points.

name: time-course-scrna-seq-data-processing
description: Use when the input is a time-course scRNA-seq expression matrix (cells sacrificed at each time point, no cell-to-cell correspondence) and the goal is per-cell lineage tracing, cell fate prediction, or dynamic gene-network/critical-gene discovery.

name: time-course-simulation-design
description: Use when benchmarking circadian or cell-cycle phase-inference methods on droplet-based scRNA-seq data and you need controlled simulations with ground-truth phases across library sizes, cell counts, and sampling conditions.

name: time-dependent-covariate-modeling
description: Use when analyzing time-series scRNA-seq data where cell asynchrony must be corrected via pseudotime and the goal is to identify genes or cell subclusters whose abundance fluctuates significantly over pseudotime.

name: time-lag-edge-direction-sign-estimation
description: Use when a time-series RNA-Seq count table has been discretized and pairwise mutual information computed for candidate edges, and undirected edges must be oriented TF->TG with a regulation sign.

name: time-lapse-microscopy-trajectory-comparison
description: Use when a MAPiT-transformed pseudotime trajectory must be validated against ground-truth real-time kinetics, e.g. geminin trajectories reconstructed from static flow cytometry that should match single-cell time-lapse microscopy data (Paper Fig 2).

name: time-resolved-gene-module-annotation
description: Use when you have subject- and time-point-specific gene modules from multi-subject dynamic network inference (e.g. 79 donors x 4 time points) and need to identify which GO biological processes dominate at each stimulation time point.

name: time-series-interpolation-cellalign
description: Use when pseudo-bulk or stage-ordered LR-score and TF-activity series from time-course scRNA-seq are too sparse/discontinuous for Granger causality testing and must be interpolated before running lmtest::grangertest.

name: time-series-scrna-seq-filtering-and-normalization
description: Use when a time-series scRNA-seq analysis starts from a raw digital gene expression matrix (genes × cells) and the matrix must be filtered and normalized prior to trajectory inference (e.g., Monocle3) and pseudotime-based DEG/subcluster identification.

name: time-series-scrnaseq-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from time-course scRNA-seq experiments (e.g., GSE52529 HSMM, GSE67310 MEF, GSE126954 CEED) need DEG and differential subcluster identification along pseudotime rather than per-timepoint comparisons.

name: tisch-single-cell-cohort-loading
description: Use when an analysis requires downloading and loading a tumor microenvironment scRNA-seq cohort with immunotherapy condition annotations (pre/post ICB, responder/non-responder) as input for MetaTiME MeC scoring or differential signature testing.

name: tisch-training-corpus-handling
description: Use when retraining or robustness-testing MetaTiME meta-components over the TISCH tumor scRNA-seq corpus — e.g., leave-one-out cohort exclusion, cross-cohort MeC correlation, or comparing recovered component counts against the 86-MeC full-set reference.

name: tissue-mapping-rate-statistical-comparison
description: Use when RNA-seq reads from multiple tissue groups have been aligned (e.g., STAR Log.final.out files) and you need to quantify whether mapping-quality metrics such as % uniquely mapped or % 'too short' reads differ systematically by tissue.

name: tissue-sample-cohort-selection
description: Use when preparing multi-tissue RNA-seq genotype and transcript expression matrices (e.g. GTEx V7) for sQTL mapping and you must decide which tissues/samples pass a minimum sample-size threshold for powered within-tissue QTL testing.

name: tissue-sharing-stratification-of-causal-components
description: Use when you have CAFEH z-mode results for genome-wide significant GWAS loci across multiple tissues (GTEx) and need to quantify whether tissue-specific vs tissue-shared eQTL components differ in colocalization with disease loci.

name: tissue-specific-clustering-visualization
description: Use when you have per-sample tncRNA detection data (e.g. Supplementary sheets 5.1–5.4) across plant tissues and want to test whether tncRNA composition clusters by tissue via 2D non-linear embedding.

name: tissue-specific-dataset-handling
description: Use when benchmarking or deploying m6A site predictors on tissue-specific 41-nt RNA segment datasets from human, mouse, or rat, or when cross-tissue/cross-species comparisons require consistent dataset splits and encodings.

name: tissue-specific-driver-gene-prediction
description: Use when somatic mutation data can be split by primary tissue of origin (tissues with >1000 samples) and the goal is to predict cancer-type-specific driver genes rather than pan-cancer drivers.

name: tissue-specific-feature-matrix-construction
description: Use when COSMIC somatic coding mutation data can be split by primary tissue of origin and the goal is to identify tissue-specific TSGs/OGs by reusing a pan-cancer cTaG model on per-tissue feature matrices.

name: tissue-specific-marker-database-matching
description: Use when scRNA-seq data are already clustered and each cluster needs automatic, reproducible cell type annotation via a literature-backed tissue-specific marker database instead of manual marker inspection.

name: tissue-specific-reference-matching
description: Use when annotating scRNA-seq clusters by matching identified marker genes (e.g. from a paired one-against-all comparison) against a curated tissue-specific reference of literature-reported markers to filter pseudo markers and rank candidate cell types.

name: tissue-specific-xgboost-model-training
description: Use when you have a large cohort of paired bulk miRNA and mRNA matrices for one tissue (e.g., TCGA skin, breast, or kidney) and need a trained regression model to infer miRNA expression from mRNA-only profiles such as pooled scRNA-seq.

name: tissue-specificity-classification-across-gtex-tissues
description: Use when re-quantifying eQTL tissue sharing from GTEx v8 cis-eQTL summary statistics and the goal is an LD-aware, per-gene tissue-specific vs shared classification robust to allelic heterogeneity.

name: tissue-specificity-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have CAFEH results tables (cafeh.{mode}.results) with per-(SNP, study) pip/alpha/rank/pi fields and want to assess functional validity of fine-mapped variants against Roadmap chromatin states.

name: tls-signature-based-spot-scoring
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics spots contain detected TLS structures and you need to know which immune cell subtypes (e.g. plasmablasts, memory B cells, dendritic cells) compose them.

name: tma-core-image-tiling-and-subimage-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking cell segmentation pipelines on TMA cores or other large tissue images that must first be divided into uniform tiles (e.g., 512x512) to match an evaluation scheme.

name: tma-core-multiplexed-image-processing
description: Use when single-cell segmentation and per-compartment marker quantification is needed on multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images, especially TMA cores with columnar epithelial cells and incomplete membranes that nuclei-dilation or Voronoi methods undersegment.

name: tmb-cna-burden-association-testing
description: Use when testing whether per-sample viral status (e.g., IIV31 positivity in UCEC) differs between groups in TMB, chromosome-level CNA burden, CIBERSORT CD8+/Treg fractions, Kaplan-Meier survival, or TV co-occurrence.

name: tmm-bulk-rnaseq-normalization
description: Use when matched bulk RNA-seq replicates (e.g. GSE52529 Trapnell myoblast bulk data with three biological replicates) must be normalized to define true-zero / expression-level bins against which scRNA-seq dropout imputation is judged.

name: tncrna-cleavage-position-composition-analysis
description: Use when you have classified tncRNA reads (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) mapped to tRNA loci plus flanks and want to test whether cleavage is precise/codon-dependent rather than random tRNA degradation, or to find a conserved tRF-5::tRNA interface motif.

name: tncrna-count-aggregation-per-species
description: Use when you have per-sample tncRNA classification tables from a tncRNA Toolkit run and need species-level summaries of total and unique tncRNA counts per subtype for cross-species comparison.

name: tncrna-feature-annotation
description: Use when small RNA-seq reads have been mapped to a tRNA-masked artificial genome (BAM + reference FASTA available) and per-tncRNA nucleoside modification annotations (e.g. m3C, pseudouridine, dihydrouridine, m2G) are needed.

name: tncrna-interface-motif-discovery
description: Use when you have classified per-sample tncRNA catalogs (tRF-5, tRF-3, tRF-1, 5'tRH, 3'tRH) plus progenitor mature tRNA sequences with 50 bp flanks, and the goal is to distinguish specific endoribonucleolytic cleavage from random tRNA degradation and recover a conserved cleavage motif.

name: tncrna-presence-absence-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have tissue-level tncRNA abundance/presence data (e.g., Supplementary sheets 5.1-5.4) for plant samples and need sample-by-sequence binary feature matrices for tissue-specific clustering or dimensionality reduction.

name: tnseq-log2fold-change-threshold-filtering
description: Use when a CSV of pre-computed log2 fold changes and adjusted p-values per gene must be screened for extreme variations across pairwise antibiotic-vs-control conditions (e.g., VAN, CPT, DEL, LZD vs untreated) using dual fold-change and significance cut-offs.

name: tool-benchmark-accuracy-comparison-analysis
description: Use when two miRNA-inference or similar transcriptomic-prediction tools must be benchmarked head-to-head on the same paired expression cohorts, with per-feature accuracy tables and scatter plots as deliverables.

name: tool-unique-mirna-validation-in-independent-cohort
