description: Use when two small RNA-seq pipelines have been run on the same samples and you must determine which tool's tool-unique miRNA calls are better supported by an external dataset.

name: top-gene-list-jaccard-consistency-analysis
description: Use when comparing DE gene lists from multiple scRNA-seq DE methods (e.g., MAST, edgeR, zingeR, iDEA) to measure cross-method consistency of ranked DE calls at a fixed list size.

name: top-k-candidate-benchmark-evaluation-against-validated-labels
description: Use when you have a ranked list of predicted peptide-MHC candidates and an external gold-standard set of experimentally validated immunogenic labels (e.g., TESLA syn21048999), and you need to quantify whether top-k selection enriches true immunogenic neoantigens above baseline.

name: top-ranked-pair-comparison-across-weightings
description: Use when you need to show that a cell-communication network's top-ranked ligand–receptor pairs depend on the edge-weighting metric (expression vs. specificity), e.g. to expose housekeeping-edge inflation in expression-ranked networks.

name: top-variable-feature-selection-sample-level
description: Use when a per-sample parameter/feature matrix (rows = parameters, columns = samples) must be reduced to its most variable features before training or evaluating a cross-cohort classifier on sample-level labels.

name: top-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when preparing raw scRNA-seq count matrices (cells x genes) as input to EDGE or a similar ensemble feature-extraction method, and you need log-normalization plus a top-variable-gene filter to reduce dimensionality of the candidate gene space.

name: top-variable-parameter-selection
description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model's sample-specific manifold parameter matrix (Q) and need a sample-level 2D embedding showing that samples cluster by one covariate after regressing out another.

name: topic-association-matrix-extraction
description: Use when a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic model is available and you need per-topic gene rankings from the beta matrix to test whether a topic captures a specific cell-type identity program or to interpret topics biologically.

name: topic-based-gene-set-selection
description: Use when an interpretable scRNA-seq topic model (MIRA/CODAL) has been fitted and you need a gene set representing one topic's biological program, plus a background, to test motif or pathway enrichment among topic-ranked genes.

name: topic-gene-loading-interpretation
description: Use when scETM topics have been flagged as differentially expressed (e.g., AD topics 12 and 58 at permutation p ≤ 1e-5) and their biological character must be confirmed from gene loadings.

name: topic-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have an Ntopics x Ngenes topic association matrix (beta) from a fitted CODAL/MIRA topic model and need to interpret an individual topic as a gene program, e.

name: topic-gene-scoring-from-embeddings
description: Use when you have trained an scETM model (e.g. 100-topic model on HP, AD, or MDD AnnData) and need interpretable per-topic gene rankings to test topics against known pathway gene sets via GSEA.

name: topic-marker-gene-annotation
description: Use when STdeconvolve has produced per-topic transcriptional profiles (beta) and cell-type proportions (theta) from multi-cellular pixel-resolution ST data and the recovered topics must be biologically labeled via marker genes.

name: topic-model-based-perturbation-effect-ranking
description: Use when analyzing Perturb-Seq/CROP-seq expression profiles plus per-cell perturbation labels (control labeled 'CTRL') to quantitatively prioritize individual gene perturbation effects at single-cell granularity.

name: topic-model-input-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing pooled CRISPR screening combined with single-cell RNA-seq data (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CROP-seq expression profile + sgRNA perturbation assignments) for topic modeling, and you must remove cells with invalid sgRNA edits and under-represented perturbations.

name: topic-model-unsupervised-training
description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count data in an AnnData object with batch_indices (and optionally cell_types) and need unsupervised cell embeddings for clustering, batch integration, or downstream benchmarking against methods like Harmony, LIGER, scVI, or Scanorama.

name: topic-number-model-selection
description: Use when fitting graded LDA topic models to single-cell CRISPR screening (Perturb-seq/CROP-seq/CRISP-seq) expression data and you must choose the optimal topic number in a data-driven manner rather than fixing it arbitrarily.

name: topic-word-probability-estimation
description: Use when you have a scRNA-seq count matrix (genes × cells) and want robust, interpretable latent topics via penalized LDA, e.g. reproducing the pLDA vignette simulation and exporting topic-word distributions.

name: topological-autoencoder-embedding
description: Use when single-cell RNA/ATAC/ADT modalities must be reduced to a structure-preserving latent space (e.g., PCA-reduced PBMC RNA, LSI-reduced PBMC ATAC, BM RNA/ADT matrices) before manifold alignment or benchmarking projection methods.

name: topological-loss-computation
description: Use when training or evaluating scTopoGAN: you need to quantify how well the topology of the source ATAC manifold is preserved after projection into the RNA target space, at training checkpoints (epochs 500–1000).

name: topological-overlap-matrix-clustering
description: Use when a multi-sample bulk RNA-seq count matrix (e.g., 192-sample 5xFAD/C57BL/6J cortex and hippocampus data with age, genotype, tissue, sex traits) needs to be partitioned into co-expression modules tied to sample traits.

name: topology-guided-gan-training
description: Use when two single-cell modalities must be aligned into a common latent space without overlapping cells or features, using topology-guided GAN training on separately computed topoAE manifolds.

name: toppgene-enrichment-querying
description: Use when a ranked differential-expression gene list (e.g., scTITANS SigGenes at fdr 0.01) needs functional interpretation via GO biological-process enrichment, especially for non-model organisms like Caenorhabditis elegans.

name: torch-geometric-graph-data-preparation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq imputation or representation-learning pipeline needs a cell-cell graph (nodes = cells, edges = k nearest neighbors) built from a normalized, HVG-filtered expression matrix before graph contrastive learning.

name: torch-serialized-object-handling
description: Use when resuming PRESCIENT workflows from the `prescient process_data` output or when a downstream task (fate simulation, TF perturbation screen, UMAP plotting) needs the bundled data_pt contents.

name: total-counts-per-cell-quality-assessment
description: Use when recursively forecasting single-cell expression over many time steps (e.g., 72 hourly steps with predictCellFutures) and you must verify the neural ODE's predictions have not exploded beyond biologically realistic expression levels.

name: total-variation-expression-profile-smoothing
description: Use when a gene-by-cell relative expression matrix (baseline-subtracted scRNA-seq counts ordered by genomic position) must be denoised while preserving piecewise-constant breakpoints prior to copy number segmentation.

name: toxic-chemical-gene-module-annotation
description: Use when you have a short list of differentially expressed genes (e.g. ~27 DE genes from a toxicant-exposure microarray study like cobalt-exposed rat liver cell lines) and want to test whether environmental toxic-chemical gene modules are enriched.

name: toy-dataset-validation-of-optimization-solver
description: Use when implementing or debugging a marker-selection optimization (e.g., scGeneFit's slack LP from Eq. 4) and you need a minimal labeled toy expression matrix plus a concrete expected marker output to verify solver correctness.

name: tp-fp-fn-accuracy-evaluation
description: Use when a locus- or family-level TE quantification tool needs an accuracy benchmark against simulated ground-truth data, especially where multi-mapping of young TEs complicates read assignment.

name: tp53-intron-retention-interpretation
description: Use when a single sample shows a SCISSOR-detected local shape change near a TP53 splice junction and you must test whether a junction-proximal insertion is associated with retained-intron reads versus exonic reads.

name: tpfp-ratio-evaluation-of-network-predictions
description: Use when you have ranked protein interaction lists (e.g., from FAVA, scLink, hdWGCNA, PCC) on scRNA-seq datasets and need a comparable accuracy metric against curated references such as KEGG or BioGRID.

name: tpm-abundance-aggregation
description: Use when raw paired-end FASTQ files from the disease RNA-seq datasets (GSE203206, GSE128177, GSE205867, PRJNA433105) must be converted into transcript-level TPM values compatible with CanIsoNet's transcript isoform definitions.

name: tpm-expression-data-handling
description: Use when a transcript-level TPM matrix from an RNA-seq disease dataset (e.g. GSE203206 Alzheimer's) must be reduced to per-sample dominant isoforms to call disease-specific dMDT isoform switching events.

name: tpm-expression-filtering-of-contigs
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome assembly (e.g., Trinity FASTA plus RNA-Seq reads) contains lowly expressed contigs that should be removed prior to CD-HIT-EST redundancy filtering, following Bellerophon's default TPM cut-off of 1.

name: tpm-expression-normalization
description: Use when a raw gene counts matrix (Ensembl IDs, sample columns) must be converted to TPM/log2(TPM+1) before computing GSVA scores or integrating expression with TCGA clinical data.

name: tpm-expression-quantification
description: Use when you have per-gene MRSD scores (*.results.mrsd.txt) and matching GTEx TPM values and need to test whether relative expression level adequately predicts required sequencing depth.

name: tpm-expression-ranking
description: Use when Ig-transcript contigs from de novo assembly must be expression-quantified and TPM-ranked to mark the dominant clone, e.g. for mCLL/uCLL classification from RNA-seq.

name: tpm-gene-expression-table-generation
description: Use when tumor RNA-Seq FASTQ reads must be aligned and quantified into a TPM table so downstream neoantigen filtering can exclude genes with TPM < 1.

name: tpm-log2-count-transformation
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices (e.g., 10x Genomics h5 count data) must be converted into a stable, log-scaled input for training the VASC variational autoencoder or similar dropout-aware deep models.

name: tpm-normalization
description: Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment UMI counts must be placed on a transcript-per-million scale to compare 3'UTR isoform abundance against bulk 3' end sequencing (e.g., ArrayExpress E-MTAB-7391 HSC or PolyASite ESC) TPM values.

name: tpr-fpr-benchmark-against-dna-ground-truth
description: Use when evaluating CNV calls from RNA-seq data against matched DNA-seq absolute copy-number ground truth, e.g. single cells with simultaneous RNA and copy-number measurements.

name: tpr-fpr-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing the sensitivity and specificity of two cell-classification stages on scRNA-seq data — e.g. testing whether scID's stage-3 weighted-score assignment raises the true-positive rate over stage-2 DPR training-cell selection without inflating false positives.

name: tpr-fpr-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking an SVG-detection method's false positive behavior — e.g. validating that simulated noise genes are not called significant and that coordinate-permuted null data yields FPR near nominal thresholds.

name: tracy-widom-marchenko-pastur-universality-comparison
description: Use when analyzing a sparse single-cell expression matrix with PCA/RMT and you need to separate noise bulk, sparsity-induced artifacts, and true low-rank signal via eigenvalue deviations from MP/TW laws.

name: tracy-widom-threshold-estimation
description: Use when analyzing sparse scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., Z8eq.csv.gz) and a data-driven signal-vs-noise cutoff for dimensionality reduction is needed instead of manual or heuristic PC selection.

name: train-test-generalization-assessment
description: Use when a trained FAVA VAE model must be checked for overfitting to the input scRNA-seq cells, i.e. you need evidence that latent-space performance generalizes to unseen cells.

name: train-test-holdout-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking GRN inference methods on snRNA-seq data and you need to determine which method generalizes to held-out cells rather than merely fitting the training data, via a cosine similarity test/train ratio.

name: train-test-pair-benchmark-design-across-datasets
description: Use when evaluating whether a single-cell classifier generalizes across datasets rather than within one batch: multiple labeled scRNA-seq datasets of the same tissue exist, and each dataset should serve once as training and test set to form all pairwise combinations.

name: train-test-partition-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing a reference-mapping annotation method against supervised cell type classifiers across cross-technology or held-out-donor single-cell RNA-seq splits, e.g. replicating Abdelaal et al.'s PbmcBench benchmark with Symphony references.

name: train-test-split-benchmarking-across-datasets
description: Use when two or more feature representations must be compared for the same classification task across several scRNA-seq datasets (e.g., Chuang, Karaayvaz, PBMC3k, Lee), using held-out test partitions and metrics such as accuracy and weighted-F1.

name: train-test-split-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating a supervised cell-type classifier on annotated AnnData single-cell/nuclei data where you need quantified accuracy on held-out cells and cross-sample generalization bounds.

name: train-test-split-simulation-design
description: Use when benchmarking cell-annotation or classification methods under controlled sample-size conditions, especially to stress-test them on closely correlated classes versus easy low-correlation classes.

name: train-test-split-stratification
description: Use when a classifier trained on pathway-module-derived features (e.g., GSVA scores of high-weight MOFA pathways) must be assessed for generalization on held-out samples and an independent bulk RNA cohort.

name: train-validation-split-by-sample-source
description: Use when training a supervised malignancy or cell-type classifier on multi-sample scRNA-seq data and held-out performance must reflect generalization to unseen patients/samples rather than unseen cells from already-seen samples.

name: train-validation-split-stratification
description: Use when training a neural-network classifier on high-dimensional transcriptomic data (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer cancer-vs-normal labels) and you need a defensible train/validation split before sweeping the number of ranked features to find where accuracy plateaus.

name: trainable-parameter-count-verification
description: Use when re-implementing a published neural architecture in Keras/TensorFlow and you need objective confirmation that layer configurations (filters, kernel sizes, dense units) reproduce the paper's reported model exactly.

name: training-loss-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when training uniPort's coupled-VAE (uniport.Run with default lambda_s=0.5, lambda_recon=1.0, lambda_kl=0.5, lambda_ot=1.0, iteration=30000) and you must confirm the composite VAE + Minibatch-UOT loss decreases rather than diverges.

name: training-subset-scaling-curve-analysis
description: Use when you need to determine whether model performance scaling with training corpus size reflects added cells or added donor/batch diversity, by comparing subsampling regimes on a donor-stratified dataset.

name: trait-cell-type-association-matrix-construction
description: Use when you have preprocessed GWAS trait-associated gene lists (e.g., from 51 GWAS summary datasets) and want to map traits to associated human cell types via CTgene enrichment.

name: trait-relevance-score-computation-single-cell
description: Use when per-cell scores for trait association are needed from scRNA-seq data given GWAS summary statistics, e.g., to identify trait-relevant cells against a scDesign2 ground truth or real disease data.

name: trajectory-accuracy-benchmarking
description: Use when you must decide which 2D embedding (t-SNE/UMAP/MDS over 20/40/100% HVGs) to feed Slingshot or Monocle3, or when benchmarking inferred pseudotime against ground truth on simulated scRNA-seq data.

name: trajectory-assignment-deviation-analysis
description: Use when cells are assigned to more than one CellPath trajectory (cellpath_obj.pseudo_order) and you need to quantify whether inferred pseudotime is consistent across those paths per dataset.

name: trajectory-based-gene-regulatory-dynamics-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq differentiation data (pre-processed adata with cluster annotations and optionally RNA velocity) plus a TF binding-site matrix must be converted into time- and lineage-specific TF activity estimates along cell-fate decision trajectories.

name: trajectory-based-tf-gene-correlation-analysis
description: Use when single-cell multiome (RNA+ATAC) data contain an ordered cell state transition (e.g. naive-to-memory CD4 T cells, SCARA5+ fibroblasts to myofibroblasts) and you need TF-gene regulatory relationships along that trajectory.

name: trajectory-condition-imbalance-visualization
description: Use when a single-cell dataset with a low-dimensional embedding (e.g. Dim1/Dim2 coordinates) and binary condition labels needs a per-cell diagnostic of where condition imbalance concentrates along a trajectory, before formal differential topology or progression testing.

name: trajectory-conservation-evaluation-across-batches
description: Use when integrating multi-batch scRNA-seq data (e.g., ten donor batches of human bone marrow/PBMC immune cells) and the key question is whether a known developmental continuum across batches survives integration, or when benchmarking integration methods on trajectory conservation.

name: trajectory-conservation-scoring
description: Use when benchmarking cross-species scRNA-seq integration of whole-body embryonic atlases and you need to test whether stage progression / developmental trajectory is maintained after integration, e.g. xenopus–zebrafish Embryo_xt_dr.

name: trajectory-differential-expression-and-go-enrichment
description: Use when a trained LatentVelo (or similar latent-dynamics) model has produced latent trajectories and you need the genes driving each lineage path plus GO term interpretation, e.g. endothelial/erythroid/mesenchyme/neural gastrulation trajectories.

name: trajectory-differential-topology-assessment
description: Use when single-cell data from multiple conditions has been embedded in low-dimensional space and clustered, and you must decide whether trajectories can be jointly inferred or are differentially organized across conditions.

name: trajectory-gene-expression-variation-analysis
description: Use when a paired snRNA-seq/snATAC-seq co-embedded object has an inferred pseudotime trajectory (e.g. SCARA5+ progenitors to myofibroblasts) and you need candidate genes as input for enhancer-based GRN inference.

name: trajectory-graph-edge-traversal
description: Use when a landmark-based trajectory graph (landmark coordinates, connecting edges, and cell-to-landmark transition assignments) is already built and cells must be given a pseudo-temporal ordering along each edge of the tree.

name: trajectory-graph-feature-evaluation
description: Use when you have dynamic seed features from DELVE Step 1 and need to rank all features by how well their expression varies smoothly along the underlying cellular trajectory graph rather than by variance.

name: trajectory-inference-aucpr-evaluation
description: Use when you have a sample-level distance matrix (e.g., Wasserstein distances between cluster distributions from .h5ad single-cell/pathomics cohorts) and need to infer a disease trajectory and score it by AUCPR and Spearman correlation against known severity labels.

name: trajectory-inference-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing single-cell trajectory/pseudo-time inference methods on scRNA-seq data with known capture or developmental stages, to quantify which tool's ordering explains real time via R-squared.

name: trajectory-inference-method-benchmarking
description: Decision support for choosing a trajectory inference method when a branching single-cell dataset has trusted ground-truth population labels and lineage marker genes (e.g. Gata1, Pax5) to score branch assignments against.

name: trajectory-inference-method-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare a new or existing trajectory-inference algorithm against baseline methods on synthetic single-cell data, replicating a published benchmark such as Supplementary Fig. 4g,h.

name: trajectory-inference-method-comparison
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction/trajectory methods on temporal scRNA-seq data where the goal is to quantify subpopulation separation within each time point, e.g. deciding whether TCM better preserves subpopulations than t-SNE or diffusion map.

name: trajectory-inference-method-comparison-on-scrna-seq
description: Decision support for selecting a TI method when a scRNA-seq dataset has a known or published branch/cell-type structure and the goal is to determine which of several TI methods (e.g., Monocle3 vs Mpath) reconstructs the true trajectory before downstream pseudotime analysis.

name: trajectory-inference-parameter-sweep
description: Use when you need to assess how sensitive a clustering-based trajectory inference method (e.g. Totem) is to its clustering-count and k-range parameters, by running a grid of parameter combinations with multiple random seeds against a benchmark ground truth.

name: trajectory-inference-pseudotime
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data has been processed in SingCellaR (Harmony-supervised embeddings plus Louvain clusters) and you need pseudotime ordering of immature-to-differentiated cells along a lineage such as hematopoietic stem/progenitor to erythroid.

name: trajectory-inference-pseudotime-reconstruction
description: Use when analyzing time-series scRNA-seq count matrices where cell asynchrony must be corrected via trajectory inference and pseudotime to identify genes and subclusters that vary over time.

name: trajectory-inference-terminal-state-detection
description: Use when a bifurcating or multi-fate single-cell trajectory (scRNA-seq, scATAC-seq, integrated, or cytometry) must have its terminal fates and branch probabilities detected automatically without prior fate labels.

name: trajectory-inference-with-monocle3
description: Use when a time-series scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. UMI counts from Fluidigm C1 or 10X) needs branch/pseudotime reconstruction before time-dependent covariate DEG or subcluster testing.

name: trajectory-inference-with-slingshot
description: Use when paired lineage-barcode and scRNA-seq data need a cell-state tree (state_lineages) over k-means clusters of top-50 PCs, so a lineage-reconstruction method like LinRace can map mutations onto state transitions.

name: trajectory-interpolation-alignment-between-lineages
description: Use when you have two lineage-specific single-cell trajectories (e.g. Seurat objects with EPI/PE identities and a monocle3 cds) and need to test whether LR pairs co-vary and causally precede master TFs along pseudotime.

name: trajectory-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing trajectory/pseudotime inference tools on scRNA-seq data with known cell type labels, to quantify which method recovers developmental ordering on neuronal or hematopoietic datasets.

name: trajectory-path-simulation-between-clusters
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell DEG prediction methods on simulated data where cluster structure and continuous trajectories between clusters are both required, and ground-truth DE labels are needed for accuracy evaluation.

name: trajectory-pseudotime-inference
description: Use when you need per-cell PPIN activity scores for 18 preloaded biological processes and want to embed cells in activity space (UMAP) and assign pseudotime along differentiation.

name: trajectory-root-cell-selection-and-correction
description: Use when inferring developmental pseudotime on a plant scRNA-seq atlas with scPlant (RunMonocle2, RunMonocle3, RunSlingshot, RunCytoTRACE) and a biologically plausible origin — such as meristem cells — must be chosen or validated against a tool's automatic root prediction.

name: trajectory-simulation-perturbation-benchmarking
description: Use when validating a trajectory-level differential test (e.g. progressionTest) against realistic trajectory-inference errors, or when reporting how much pseudotime noise and lineage misassignment a method tolerates.

name: trajectory-step-consensus-state-matching
description: Use when an AnnData object with spliced/unspliced layers and scvelo-estimated RNA velocity has already been processed through Cytopath's Markov simulation and consensus-step construction, and you need cell-level scores against the inferred trajectories.

name: trajectory-suitability-assessment
description: Use when starting a scRNA-seq trajectory analysis and you need to decide whether fitting a trajectory is appropriate — e.g. datasets may be homogeneous or contain disconnected cell populations with no underlying dynamic.

name: trajectory-topology-testing
description: Use when scRNA-Seq data from ≥2 conditions (e.g. control vs ILD) are projected onto a common slingshot trajectory and you must test whether conditions differ in topology, pseudotime progression, fate selection between lineages, or gene expression along lineages.

name: trajectory-tree-alignment-across-species
description: Use when comparing pseudotime trajectories between related scRNA-seq datasets from different species (or conditions) whose trajectories contain branches, and you need to ask whether cell-type marker gene expression dynamics are conserved along aligned pseudotime.

name: trajectory-tree-topology-filtering
description: Use when building benchmark synthetic scRNA-seq data for branched trajectory alignment and only simulations whose cluster-derived MST has a specified topology (e.g., exactly four leaves) should enter the benchmark.

name: transcript-abundance-quantification
description: Use when RNA-seq reads must be quantified against an augmented transcriptome that includes InPACT-reconstructed novel IPA isoforms, and per-site IPA usage (PAU) values are needed downstream.

name: transcript-abundance-quantification
description: Use when a de novo Trinity assembly has produced candidate Ig transcripts that must be abundance-quantified and ranked by TPM to identify the dominant B-cell clone from RNA-seq data.

name: transcript-abundance-quantification-and-gene-level-import
description: Use when starting from raw bulk RNA-seq FASTQ files (e.g. anti-PD-1 vs control CD8 TIL samples from GSE62771) and gene-level counts or a differential expression ranking are needed for GSEA or signature enrichment.

name: transcript-annotation-querying
description: Use when transcriptome elements (e.g., POSTAR3 m6A sites, miCLIP-seq peaks) carry only genomic coordinates and the specific isoform transcript they belong to is unknown, and isoform-aware randomization or colocalization testing is needed.

name: transcript-assembly-and-expression-quantification
description: Use when RNA-Seq fastq files from a tumor sample must be aligned and quantified to gene/transcript TPM values that will filter neoantigen candidates from unexpressed genes (TPM < 1).

name: transcript-assembly-benchmark-evaluation-against-refseq-annotation
description: Use when you have GTF transcript assemblies from multiple assemblers run on the same RNA-seq alignments (e.g., Hisat2/STAR BAMs) and need to quantify which assembler recovers more reference-annotated (RefSeq) transcripts correctly.

name: transcript-assembly-comparison
description: Use when you must objectively compare isoform-detection performance of multiple transcript assembly tools on the same long-read dataset with a known ground-truth isoform annotation.

name: transcript-boundary-extension-quantification
description: Use when comparing isoform calls from StringTie2 and VIsoQLR on the same BAM alignments (e.g., SIRV spike-ins or a PAX6 minigene ONT assay) and transcript start/end coordinates disagree between tools, or when StringTie2 fails to call isoforms that lack certain exons.

name: transcript-count-matrix-generation
description: Use when raw single-cell RNA-seq FASTQ reads must be pseudoaligned to a transcriptome and converted into spliced/unspliced UMI count matrices, especially when Cell Ranger runtime is prohibitive or RNA velocity/trajectory inference is planned.

name: transcript-coverage-decay-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether a 10x Chromium 3' (v2) or 5' (v1) workflow supports calling variants distal to the capture end, or when reproducing coverage-decay curves from per-cell UMI counts.
tools: 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 3' (v2) Gene Expression
10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 5' (v1) Gene Expression

name: transcript-expression-tpm-thresholding
description: Use when a transcript-level TPM expression matrix (trId, geneId columns) is being prepared for sQTL mapping and unreliable genes/transcripts must be removed before association testing.

name: transcript-isoform-identifier-resolution
description: Use when a dMDT entry or isoform switching event is named by gene code and transcript number (e.g. HSPH1-002) and the corresponding ENST accession must be resolved before querying CanIsoNet or STRING.

name: transcript-quantification-filtering
description: Use when an aptardi (or assembler-generated) GTF has been quantitated and redundant/false-positive 3'-terminal transcripts must be filtered by an expression count threshold across replicate samples before differential analysis.

name: transcript-query-set-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking a pre-filter such as Raptor on RNA-Seq collections and you need reproducible transcript query sets of increasing size plus ground-truth membership calls to compute false-positive rates.

name: transcript-recovery-evaluation-at-locus
description: Use when assessing whether a specific annotated RefSeq transcript (e.g., XR_929880.3) missed by single-aligner assemblers can be recovered by integrating alignments from multiple aligners such as Hisat2 and Star.

name: transcript-reference-annotation-handling
description: Use when assembled transcript contigs must be assigned to a reference isoform annotation (e.g. GENCODE GTF) to quantify isoform-level precision and recall of a de novo assembler, as done with IsoQuant in the cloudrnaSPAdes evaluation.

name: transcript-reference-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking the query scalability of an indexed sequence-collection search structure (e.g. PAC) and you need realistic, size-graded query workloads drawn from a reference transcript database.

name: transcript-sequence-deduplication
description: Use when preparing a custom kallisto target transcriptome (GTF + FASTA + kdx + merge table) for 3' UTR isoform quantification from 10X Chromium 3'-tag scRNA-seq data, where reads are short and must be anchored near cleavage sites.

name: transcript-sequence-encoding
description: Use when lncRNA vs protein-coding transcript (PCT) FASTA sequences need to be converted into numeric feature vectors, or when verifying via dimensionality-reduction visualization that ORF-attention features separate the two classes.

name: transcript-to-gene-map-preparation
description: Reference for preparing a spliced+intronic (splici) reference and its 3-column transcript-to-gene mapping from a reference genome FASTA and GTF before single-cell quantification with alevin-fry/simpleaf.

name: transcription-factor-activity-inference
description: Use when you need to score TF activities from RNA perturbation compendia (e.g. Holland et al. 2020 transcriptomics data) using a prior-knowledge gene regulatory network like DoRothEA and rank inference methods by sensitivity.

name: transcription-factor-activity-inference-from-autoencoder-latent-space
description: Use when a counts table with pre-defined cell/spot clusters (e.g., SIMLR annotations over a Visium breast cancer section) must be linked to specific transcription factors via an autoencoder latent space.

name: transcription-factor-activity-inference-linear-model
description: Use when you have preprocessed single-cell RNA-seq (Scanpy/scVelo adata) plus a TF binding-site matrix and want to estimate time- and fate-specific TF activities along stochastic cell-fate differentiation trajectories.

name: transcription-factor-activity-projection
description: Use when you have a pre-processed single-cell count matrix (e.g. PBMC SingleCellExperiment) plus a TF-target prior such as DoRothEA, and want cell-level TF regulon activity scores and projections.

name: transcription-factor-binding-motif-enrichment
description: Use when converting a co-expression network (GCN) to a directed GRN and candidate TF→TG edges (e.g. from GRNBoost2/GENIE3-style regression) must be filtered by cis-regulatory motif enrichment to keep only motif-supported regulators.

name: transcription-factor-binding-motif-refinement
description: Use when an initial MI-based GRN (e.g., from RNA-Seq time series) should be filtered or upgraded with motif evidence from upstream promoter sequences, or when reproducing Augusta's 'with refinement' benchmark.

name: transcription-factor-binding-site-matrix-construction
description: Use when preparing FateCompass inputs from single-cell transcriptomics (e.g., a pre-processed AnnData from Dyngen simulation or pancreatic endocrine differentiation) and you must supply the TF/motif-vs-expressed-gene binding-site matrix needed for TF activity inference.

name: transcription-factor-candidate-selection
description: Use when a cell type has already been identified in a scRNA-Seq dataset (SINCERA S4 object) and you need to find its driving forces — key transcription factors — from differential expression and network centrality.

name: transcription-factor-cluster-activity-analysis
description: Use when a time-course single-cell dataset needs TF activity profiles aligned to ligand-receptor dynamics — e.g. to test whether co-varying LR pairs are causally linked to temporal TF clusters.

name: transcription-factor-composite-ranking
description: Use when DC3 has assigned scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq cells to subpopulations and you need to rank transcription factors driving each subpopulation by joint expression and motif enrichment evidence.

name: transcription-factor-database-selection
description: Use when running TFvelo on scRNA-seq data and you need to restrict the TF pool per target gene — e.g., preparing the gene regulatory input before weight initialization and velocity inference.

name: transcription-factor-hit-prioritization
description: Use when you have a fitted PRESCIENT model (data_pt) on time-series scRNA-seq and need to identify which transcription factors significantly bias differentiation toward a target fate before designing an in vitro perturbational screen.

name: transcription-factor-marker-prioritization
description: Use when scRNAseq clusters have been defined (e.g., via rCASC clustering) and the goal is to identify transcription factors whose target-derived latent representation drives cluster aggregation, rather than generic differential expression markers.

name: transcription-factor-motif-enrichment
description: Use when a Mowgli factor's H(atac) matrix rows must be biologically annotated: top-weighted peaks per factor are tested for TF motif over-representation to name the factor's putative regulator.

name: transcription-factor-motif-enrichment-interpretation
description: Use when assigning functional titles or annotations to BloodGen3 (or similar fixed) module gene lists, and transcription-factor motif enrichment (e.g. RcisTarget) is needed as convergent evidence alongside ontology/pathway enrichment.

name: transcription-factor-network-analysis
description: Use when a transcriptomics (or phospho-proteomic) dataset must be summarized into per-regulator activity scores and the user runs multiple inference methods simultaneously and needs one consensus estimate per regulator.

name: transcription-factor-network-inference
description: Use when a CellexalVR in-session cell group needs a TF-only co-expression network: the input is expression values for the selected cells and the goal is a tf_network.txt consumed by the VR TF network generator.

name: transcription-factor-panel-verification
description: Use when a TF-based SCA latent-space frequency matrix plus cluster assignments (e.g., setA clusters 1 and 2) are available and the goal is to extract and verify an optimal gene marker panel (≤4 genes, negations allowed) per cluster with COMET.

name: transcription-factor-perturbation-analysis
description: Use when you have a trained PRESCIENT model on time-series scRNA-seq data and need to test whether perturbing candidate TFs (e.g. neutrophil or monocyte regulators) shifts simulated cells toward or away from expected terminal fates.

name: transcription-factor-regulatory-network-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic single-cell expression count matrices with known branched trajectory trees — e.g. to benchmark trajectory or tree-alignment methods where ground-truth topology and pseudotime are required.

name: transcription-factor-regulatory-potential-computation
description: Use when you have four single-cell datasets (one scRNA-seq + one scATAC-seq from each of two populations) with consistent cluster assignments, and you need to detect subpopulation-specific differential TF-target regulation.

name: transcription-factor-target-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether inferred gene regulatory network edges are biologically meaningful — e.g., testing if a TF's neighbors in a cell-type-specific network match its ENCODE-validated targets.

name: transcription-factor-target-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when you have a list of predicted circRNA/RBP candidate regulators and a gold-standard regulator list, and need to test shared transcription factor modulation (or related Harmonizome associations) to validate the candidates.

name: transcription-factor-weight-bounded-regression
description: Use when modeling a target gene's RNA dynamics as a weighted function of candidate TF expressions (from ENCODE/ChEA) and you need bounded, solvable TF weight estimates during EM-based gene dynamics fitting.

name: transcription-factor-weight-ranking
description: Use when TFvelo has been run on a scRNA-seq dataset (rc.h5ad with TF weight matrix) and you need to identify the top-weighted regulators or verify TF weight signs on pathway genes.

name: transcriptional-bursting-parameter-interpretation
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrix needs gene-level kon/koff/s kinetic parameter estimates (e.g., to parameterize SymSim's Beta-Poisson model, or to characterize transcriptional bursting per cell cluster).

name: transcriptional-module-co-clustering
description: Use when a fixed module repertoire needs a two-tier organization — grouping modules into aggregates based on similarity of activity profiles across the reference datasets that were used to build the repertoire.

name: transcriptional-network-master-regulator-analysis
description: Use when you need to infer which transcription factors drive temporal gene programs in scRNA-seq trajectories (e.g. blastocyst EPI/PE lineages) so ligand-receptor pairs can be causally linked to TF activity downstream.

name: transcriptional-regulatory-network-inference
description: Use when a single-cell RNA-seq analysis needs cell type-specific TF-TF/TF-TG regulatory networks and ranked key regulators (driving forces) after cell types and signatures have been defined.

name: transcriptional-regulatory-network-inference-from-scrnaseq
description: Use when you have a time-course or trajectory-ordered scRNA-seq dataset with cell-type labels and need to identify upstream temporal transcription factors (e.g., as downstream targets of LR signaling) via TRN inference plus MRA.

name: transcriptional-strand-bias-testing
description: Use when a mutational signature call from fitting (mmsig, deconstructSigs, MutationalPatterns) needs independent confirmation — e.g., platinum signature SBS35 in therapy-related AML — and WGS data with strand annotations are available.

name: transcriptional-time-lag-edge-orientation
description: Use when you have a time-series RNA-Seq count table (e.g., DREAM 4 100-gene/21-sample, C. beijerinckii 6 time points) and need to assign direction (TF→TG) and sign (activation/repression) to mutual-information-derived edges.

name: transcriptome-3-prime-truncation
description: Use when building a custom pseudoalignment target for 3'-end tag scRNA-seq data (e.g., 10X Chromium) where reads do not span cleavage sites and full-length transcripts would collapse 3'UTR isoforms.

name: transcriptome-assembly-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when comparing transcriptome assembler output on the same RNA-seq reads: you have multiple GTF assemblies (e.g., from single-aligner runs and merged-alignment runs) and need correct-transcript counts, precision, and F-score against a known reference.

name: transcriptome-assembly-filtering
description: Use when you have a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g. Trinity output) plus the original RNA-Seq reads and need to remove low-expression, redundant, and chimeric contigs without a reference genome.

name: transcriptome-chimera-filtering-pipeline-execution
description: Use when a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g. Trinity contigs from FASTQ reads) needs chimera removal and quality improvement before downstream gene discovery or differential expression analyses.

name: transcriptome-chimera-identification-blastx
description: Use when you have a de novo assembled transcriptome (e.g. Trinity FASTA) with no reference genome and need to count or mark chimeric transcripts to assess or benchmark assembly filtering.

name: transcriptome-clustering-comparison
description: Use when you need to quantify whether parallelizing RCC's consensus clustering across multiple CCP processes changes clustering accuracy (ARI) or processing time relative to a single-process run with more repeats.

name: transcriptome-evolutionary-index-calculation
description: Use when single-cell RNA data (Scanpy AnnData) needs a gene age-weighted expression index per cell, stage, or cell type — e.g. to detect whether young gene age classes peak in early embryos — or when per-class partial TEI / relative expression profiles are required.

name: transcriptome-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have only sequencing reads and a de novo transcriptome assembly (no reference genome) and need a baseline assembly-quality score before filtering chimeric or low-evidence contigs.

name: transcriptome-quantitation-with-rsem
description: Use when sample-specific transcriptomes (e.g. aptardi or StringTie/Ensembl GTFs) need per-transcript expression counts for filtering or differential expression analysis.

name: transcriptome-read-simulation
description: Use when a de novo transcriptome pipeline (e.g., chimera removal) must be benchmarked against a known ground truth: a reference transcriptome and expression profile are available to simulate reads from.

name: transcriptome-reconstruction-from-rnaseq
description: Use when you have genome-aligned (or alignable) RNA-Seq reads and need a sample-specific GTF transcriptome with accurate 3'-ends/polyA sites for downstream quantitation or APA analysis.

name: transcriptome-reconstruction-stringtie
description: Use when you have a sorted BAM of genome-aligned RNA-Seq reads (e.g. HISAT2 --dta output) and need an initial GTF transcriptome as input for aptardi polyA site prediction or sample-specific 3'-end refinement.

name: transcriptome-reference-index-preparation
description: Use when quantifying transcript abundances with Kallisto from RNA-Seq FASTQ files and an Ensembl transcript cDNA reference must first be converted into a Kallisto index that matches downstream isoform-switching analysis.

name: transcriptome-region-overlap-counting
description: Use when counting overlaps between transcriptome region sets or between isoform-ambiguous genomic features and transcriptome regions of interest (ROI), and when RgnTX's overlapCountsTx / overlapCountsTxIA measures must be reproduced or verified.

name: transcriptome-region-randomization
description: Use when you need null/randomized region sets that respect transcriptome annotation (e.g., for permutation tests of RNA element colocalization) or want to benchmark shuffling runtime over region-count grids.

name: transcriptome-versus-genome-reference-prediction
description: Use when benchmarking phasiRNA prediction tools' runtime on the same sRNA library (e.g., rice SRR5049781) across cDNA and gDNA references, or when deciding whether multithreading (e.g., -j 4) is needed to make genome-based prediction tractable.

name: transcriptome-wide-pseudouridine-prediction
description: Use when you need transcriptome-wide, base-resolution prediction of novel RNA pseudouridine sites in human protein-coding genes using a trained sequence-plus-secondary-structure deep learning model.

name: transcriptome-wide-similarity-search
description: Use when you have a single-cell expression matrix for one study (e.g. H5AD-imported study in Cellenium) and want to find, for a query gene, all genes with correlated expression across cells.

name: transcriptomic-biomarker-set-comparison
description: Use when two or more gene/biomarker candidate lists from the same transcriptomic cohort (e.g., TCGA pan-cancer RNA-seq) need intersection analysis to quantify agreement between feature-selection algorithms.

name: transcriptomic-csv-matrix-handling
description: Use when loading raw RNA-seq/microarray expression .csv files (sample names in first column, labels in last column) that contain missing gene values and must be imputed and quantile-normalized before cross-platform training in Ciclops.

name: transcriptomic-feature-selection-verification
description: Use when reproducing a published nested-CV glmnet model on RNA-Seq data and you need to verify which genes the automatically refitted final model retains and that their ranked coefficients match the published output.

name: transcriptomic-gene-list-annotation
description: Use when a fitted suffPCR model on transcriptomic data yields feature-sparse loadings and the nonzero feature list must be mapped to genes and grouped into functional families for interpretation.

name: transcriptomic-vector-field-computation
description: Use when you have a fitted GEDI model over a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell dataset (e.g., healthy vs severe COVID-19) and need a cluster-free, per-cell-type direction/magnitude field of the condition effect plus TF activity gradients.

name: transfer-component-analysis-batch-correction
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq-derived gene activity data with an ST reference (Visium, Slide-seq, STARmap) whose platforms and batch effects prevent direct joint analysis for pseudo-space reconstruction.

name: transfer-cut-graph-partitioning
description: Use when a consensus clustering must be derived from many base partitions of a single-cell latent embedding (the SDDA output Z), combining sample and cluster nodes in a bipartite graph and solving via transfer cut. Triggers: K-means ensemble inputs, ARI/NMI consensus evaluation.

name: transfer-learning-across-transcriptomic-platforms
description: Use when training data and validation data come from different transcriptomic platforms (e.g., RNA-seq vs. microarray) and you need clinical outcome models that generalize across platforms.

name: transfer-learning-classifier-training
description: Use when matching/aligning cell types across species from scRNA-seq data: you have two scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. human/mouse/marmoset motor cortex) and want to train a within-species classifier then propagate labels cross-species.

name: transfer-learning-label-propagation
description: Use when aligning cell types across two species from scRNA-seq data (e.g. human vs mouse primary motor cortex) where one-to-one orthologous subclasses must be matched and label-transfer recall quantified.

name: transfer-learning-model-evaluation
description: Use when you have two cross-species scRNA-seq datasets (e.g. human, mouse, marmoset motor cortex), a gene similarity distance matrix, and trained TACTiCS models, and need to quantify cell type matching performance via ADS and recall.

name: transfer-learning-pretraining-on-reference-scrna
description: Use when a sparse scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., example.msk90.hd5 / PBMC_G949_10K) must be imputed and a labeled reference dataset from the same platform (e.g., ref_example.mdk50.hd5) is available to initialize the autoencoder.

name: transformer-architecture-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing a modification-aware ONT direct-RNA basecaller from archived .h5 weights and their .h5.cfg files, or when adapting keras.io speech-to-text transformer code to raw ionic current signals.

name: transformer-attention-weight-extraction
description: Use when you have tokenized transcriptome ranking sequences (e.g., top-62-expressing gene lists) and need the raw attention weights of tGPT's 8 transformer layers to derive per-head entropy, head importance, or token attribution features.

name: transformer-based-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq AnnData with known cell labels must annotate an unlabeled query dataset, when rare/unseen cell types should be flagged as 'Unknown', or when batch-insensitive integration with interpretable attention is needed.

name: transformer-decoder-architecture-implementation
description: Use when reproducing or adapting tGPT and you need the exact decoder stack (8 layers, 1024 hidden, 16 heads) and config hyperparameters for autoregressive pretraining on ranked gene sequences.

name: transformer-model-training
description: Use when a reference scRNA-seq dataset with known cell type labels (AnnData) must be used to train an interpretable annotation model that transfers labels to query datasets across batches.

name: transformer-model-training-single-cell-rnaseq
description: Use when a labeled single-cell reference AnnData must be turned into a cell type annotation model (e.g., training TOSICA with GMT masks on mouse/human data), or when comparing convergence of knowledge-based masks vs random masks as in Supplementary Fig. 8.

name: transformer-multi-head-self-attention-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reproducing a masked self-attention cell-type annotation model that maps n input genes to k pathway tokens and returns per-cell attention matrices and cell-type probability vectors.

name: transformer-sequence-tokenization
description: Use when raw single-cell count matrices (e.g., HCL, GSE134355) must be converted into autoregressive transformer input sequences, and gene expression rankings — not raw expression values — are the desired model input.

name: transition-cell-score-computation
description: Use when MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis has returned attractor basins and optimized membership functions rho*(x) for a dataset, and you need to order cells along a specific state transition i->j, distinguish stable (attractor) cells from transition-layer cells, or feed per-cell TCS into downstream.

name: transition-cell-type-identification-along-pseudotime
description: Use when single-cell cluster labels have already been assigned (e.g., via FFC.fit()) and the goal is to detect cells with ambiguous labels — candidate novel transition cell types — along a developmental pseudo-time manifold.

name: transition-driver-gene-classification
description: Use when you have MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins, coarse-grained transition matrix, optimized membership function ρ*(x)) for a specific attractor-to-attractor transition and need the genes marking or driving that transition.

name: transition-entropy-cell-state-bifurcation-analysis
description: Use when a single-cell trajectory dataset (e.g. time-course iPSC induction data) is suspected to contain a cell-fate bifurcation and you need to localize the critical transition point via attractor-basin membership entropy.

name: transition-entropy-quantification-from-membership
description: Use when a MuTrans DynamicalAnalysis output (attractor basins Sk* and optimized membership ρ*(x)) is available and you need to score each cell's transition propensity, e.g. to locate saddle points between attractors in a cell-fate dynamical manifold.

name: transition-gene-classification-td-ih-ms
description: Use when a stable-attractor-to-attractor transition has been defined (e.g., states i and j from MuTrans dynamical analysis) and you need to identify which genes drive the transition, mark transient/hybrid cells, or label meta-stable cells.

name: transition-path-likelihood-comparison
description: Use when a large single-cell dataset makes full MuTrans dynamical_analysis slow, and you must verify that DECLARE-aggregated micro-states reproduce coarse-grained transition probabilities and transition path likelihoods computed on all cells, plus measure the speedup.

name: transition-path-theory-lineage-inference
description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data has been reduced to attractor basins via MuTrans multi-scale rwTPM analysis and you need to reconstruct transition trajectories/lineage between a defined starting and target attractor state, e.g. bifurcating lineages.

name: transition-path-theory-trajectory-likelihood-quantification
description: Use when single-cell transcriptome data has been multi-scale analyzed (attractor basins and coarse-grained transition probabilities from MuTrans dynamical_analysis) and you must infer lineage/transition path likelihoods between states, e.g. routing E->M flux through intermediate cell states.

name: transition-probability-estimation-single-cell
description: Use when scRNA-seq data capture a differentiation process and you need quantitative fate probabilities from progenitor clusters to terminal states, using RNA velocity or a biologically defined differentiation potential as the biasing force.

name: transition-specific-gene-expression-scoring
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data contain annotated subpopulations and you need transition-specific ranked lists of overexpression or knockdown candidates for a defined start-to-target cell-state transition, such as reprogramming B-cells or monocytes/DCs to HSPCs.

name: transitory-and-flat-temporal-profile-simulation
description: Use when building a ground-truth bulk multi-omics simulation over a time-series or two-group design, where DEGs must carry labeled temporal profiles (scaled fold change, transitory, or flat) and regulator layers must reflect activator/repressor coupling.

name: translated-read-alignment-to-kegg-ortholog-database
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ files come from a species without a reference transcriptome, and the goal is KO-level read quantification and functional profiling instead of de novo assembly plus annotation transfer.

name: translated-read-to-ortholog-mapping
description: Use when raw RNA-seq FASTQ reads from any eukaryotic (especially non-model) species must be quantified and functionally annotated without a reference transcriptome, by mapping translated reads directly to KO orthologs.

name: transposable-element-expression-matrix-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-Seq BAM files (CellRanger or STAR output) need TE expression quantified per genomic locus, or when comparing locus-specific vs family-metagene TE quantification for cell-type marker discovery.

name: transposable-element-expression-quantification
description: Use when you have single-cell RNA-seq (or ATAC-seq) BAM/SAM alignments from Cell Ranger or STARsolo and need per-cell TE expression counts alongside gene counts, e.g. to detect cell-type-specific or branch-restricted TE expression.

name: transposable-element-locus-expression-quantification
description: Use when you need locus-specific TE expression quantification from scRNA-Seq BAM files (STAR or CellRanger) to identify TE markers of cell populations, especially repetitive-element activity in subpopulations like 2C-like cells or cancer clusters.

name: transposable-element-read-simulation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantify how accurately a TE quantification method recovers locus-specific abundances by comparing against simulated reads with known ground-truth locus expression, e.g., simulated ~300 bp Alu repeats.

name: transposon-insertion-sequencing-differential-expression-interpretation
description: Use when analyzing pre-computed log2 fold-change and adjusted p-value columns from bacterial transposon insertion sequencing or RNA-seq datasets with multiple antibiotic treatments, and you need a data-driven, quadrant-based summary of extreme gene changes.

name: treated-vs-control-gene-ranking
description: Use when you have Cyclum-fitted pseudo-time for matched treated and control single-cell datasets and want to nominate target genes by differential circular expression patterns.

name: treatment-arm-subsetting-of-clinical-rnaseq
description: Use when you need the >16,000-gene rituximab-arm RNA-seq subset (n=68) from E-MTAB-11611 as a binary-classification input matrix for nested CV or feature-selection benchmarks.

name: treatment-effect-split-structure-verification
description: Use when a fitted DIPM tree (e.g. on GBSG2 with Surv(tyears, status)) must be checked against a published subgroup finding, confirming the split variables and thresholds match the reported treatment-effect pattern.

name: treatment-effect-subgroup-verification
description: Use when a randomized or observational dataset has a treatment assignment variable, a response outcome, and covariates, and the goal is to identify subgroups with differential treatment effects (precision medicine setting).

name: treatment-outcome-association-visualization
description: Use when bulk tumor transcriptomes have been converted to tGPT attention features and you need to test and visualize whether per-head entropy/importance differs across immunotherapy response groups (CR/PR/SD/PD).

name: treatment-recommendation-tree-fitting
description: Use when a treatment-subgroup analysis needs a fitted classification tree (e.g., on weight-change data like MASS::anorexia) whose leaves give optimal treatment assignments per subgroup.

name: treatment-response-association-analysis
description: Use when a cell-type perturbation signature discovered in single-cell immunotherapy cohorts (e.g., scDist FCER1G+ NK cells) must be tested against survival and radiologic response in independent bulk RNA-seq cohorts with clinical metadata.

name: treatment-response-linear-regression-coefficient-testing
description: Use when a scRNA-seq time-series has treated vs untreated conditions across timepoints (e.g., cisplatin X1–X4 in TNBC PDX) and GeneVector metagenes must be classified as treatment-specific using regression coefficients on module scores.

name: treatment-subgroup-boxplot-visualization
description: Use when a fitted subgroup tree (e.g. dipm on anorexia with a continuous outcome, or spmtree on GBSG2 with a survival outcome) needs terminal-node plots showing how treatment groups differ within each node.

name: tree-alignment-dynamic-programming
description: Use when two single-cell datasets each have pseudotime trajectories with multiple branches (trajectory trees) and a global node-to-node correspondence between the trees is needed, e.g. comparing differentiation dynamics across species or conditions.

name: tree-based-feature-importance-ranking
description: Use when you need to rank features from two alternative feature representations (e.g. CKG cell matrices and gene expression matrices) with tree-based models and quantify overlap between their top-ranked features.

name: tree-stability-assessment-across-batch-orders
description: Use when multiple annotated, aligned datasets (e.g. simulated batches or PBMC-FACS) are combined with scHPL and you need to quantify how batch presentation order or missing populations affect the learned tree, or to compare linear SVM vs one-class SVM node classifiers.

name: tree-topology-comparison-across-methods
description: Use when comparing trajectory inference methods for tree-shaped (linear, bifurcation, multifurcation) single-cell topologies on a common benchmark set, requiring standardized scoring with dynverse metrics and topology-stratified statistical testing.

name: tree-topology-vertex-degree-analysis
description: Use when you have a set of clusterings from Totem's CLARA k-medoids step, each converted to an MST via Slingshot, and need per-cell connectivity values to rank clusterings or identify trajectory leaves and branch points.

name: trend-preserving-bicluster-discovery
description: Use when the input is a continuous gene expression or synthetic numeric matrix and the goal is to detect trend-preserving biclusters whose rows maintain relative order of values across a subset of columns.

name: trimean-ensemble-expression-aggregation
description: Use when a gene-by-cell expression matrix with pre-defined cell-group labels (e.g., cortical subclasses from Yao 2021 cortex_data) must be reduced to robust per-group expression values before ligand/target abundance or communication-strength scoring.

name: trimmed-clustering-of-coverage-profiles
description: Use when per-cell gene body coverage profiles (e.g. .geneBodyCoverage outputs from geneBodyCoverage.pl) are available and cells must be classified into typical vs skewed groups with a robust, trimming-based clustering.

name: trinucleotide-electron-ion-pseudopotential-encoding
description: Use when converting 41-bp RNA sequence segments (e.g., m5C candidate sites from A. thaliana or M. musculus) into PseEIIP numerical features for machine learning input.

name: triplet-loss-implementation
description: Use when implementing or reproducing ivis-style triplet-loss dimensionality reduction: a siamese network must be built, triplets must be sampled from KNN structure (positives from the KNN vector, negatives from outside it), and pn-loss must be minimised.

name: triplet-loss-siamese-network-training
description: Use when you need to embed high-dimensional single-cell expression data (e.g. CyTOF BMMC marker panels or scRNA-seq) into 2D while preserving local and global structure, and when new cells must be added to an existing embedding without rerunning the algorithm.

name: trna-derived-fragment-query-selection
description: Use when you have a cataloged plant tncRNA pool and need to choose conserved/common tRF-5 and tRF-3 sequences (18–25 nt) as queries for miRNA-like target prediction workflows.

name: trna-fragment-classification-interpretation
description: Use when single-end sRNA-seq FASTQ reads must be assigned to tRF-5/tRF-3/tRF-1/tRNA-half classes against progenitor mature tRNA loci, or when testing whether tRNA cleavage is non-random and codon/anticodon-dependent.

name: trna-modification-signature-annotation
description: Use when sorted BAM alignments of tncRNA-derived small RNA reads to an artificial tRNA-plus-flank genome are available and per-tncRNA nucleoside modification calls and modification types are needed.

name: trs-background-correction-pvalue-computation
description: Use when scPagwas has produced a gPAS/TRS per cell from GWAS summary statistics plus scRNA-seq data and you need per-cell p-values corrected against a background of control TRSs to call trait-relevant individual cells.

name: true-discovery-rate-curve-evaluation
description: Use when you have simulated or spike-in single-cell count data with a known ground-truth differentially expressed gene set, and need to compare TDR of competing DE methods across a threshold grid.

name: true-positive-rate-false-discovery-rate-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating how well DS detection methods (aggregation-based, mixed-model, cell-level) recover known differential state genes, e.g., how TPR and FDR control vary with number of cells per subpopulation-sample.

name: true-zero-fraction-quantification
description: Use when matched bulk and single-cell RNA-seq data are available and you must test whether an imputation method preserves biologically silenced (true-zero) genes while still correcting dropout events.

name: truncated-normal-mixture-model-fitting
description: Use when a per-cell segment-level smoothed expression matrix (e.g. CNAmtx from SCEVAN's joint segmentation) must be discretized into the five CNV states via an EM-fitted truncated-normal mixture rather than ad hoc thresholding.

name: truncation-point-pileup-aggregation
description: Use when you have a strand-split BAM of aligned reads (e.g. from 10x Chromium) and need per-position counts of polyA/soft-clip-driven read endpoints to locate precise UTR termination sites.

name: tsne-2d-embedding-generation
description: Use when a Seurat object has been preprocessed (NormalizeData, ScaleData, FindVariableFeatures, RunPCA with K PCs chosen via ElbowPlot) and a 2D t-SNE visualization is needed, e.g., as input to scDEED dubious-embedding detection or perplexity optimization.

name: tsne-cluster-boundary-visualization
description: Use when you have BAMM-SC posterior cluster probabilities per cell and need to quantify and spatially validate clustering uncertainty, e.g. confirming ambiguous cells sit at cluster boundaries on a t-SNE plot.

name: tsne-cluster-visualization
description: Use when you have DESC soft-assignment probabilities for scRNA-seq cells (e.g. Kang et al. PBMC data) and need t-SNE plots to inspect cluster coherence, assignment confidence, and control-vs-stimulus mixing.

name: tsne-clustering-visualization-of-recovered-barcodes
description: Use when you have EmptyNN-retained barcodes (e.g., 885 recovered barcodes below a Cell Ranger v.2 cutoff of 200 total counts) and need to visualize and identify their cell-type clusters via t-SNE.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when a raw (dropout-containing), noisy, or imputed scRNA-Seq matrix needs a 2-D visualization of cell-type clusters, or when computing average silhouette width (ASW) on the t-SNE embedding to compare imputation methods.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when sample-wise small-RNA profiles (e.g. tncRNA sequence presence per tissue sample) need non-linear 2D embedding to test whether samples cluster by tissue of origin.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have cells projected onto a small selected marker-gene panel (e.g. scGeneFit's 15 CBMC markers) plus cell type labels, and need a 2-D visualization to check that cell populations remain separated.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-cell-shape-latents
description: Use when single-cell shape features are already encoded as autoencoder latent vectors (e.g., MIRIAM pipeline output) and you need a 2D t-SNE embedding to test whether similar geometries cluster and whether marker-positive cells form discrete populations.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-of-scrna-seq
description: Use when you have normalized scRNA-seq count data (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC, 4500 cells, 9 immune cell types) and need a 2D embedding to assess whether imputation or preprocessing improves subpopulation separation.

name: tsne-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually compare separability of predicted cancer/non-cancer driver gene classes across alternative graph-network embedding representations, especially for genes ranked by neighborhood discrete entropy.

name: tsne-embedding-computation
description: Use when benchmarking dimensionality-reduction scalability on a large scRNA-seq or CyTOF matrix (e.g. the 1.3M-cell 10X Genomics mouse brain dataset), or when a t-SNE baseline embedding is required for comparison against ivis.

name: tsne-embedding-of-cell-similarity-matrices
description: Use when you have cell-to-cell similarity matrices from scRNA-seq methods (e.g. SSRE vs Corr, SIMLR, MPSSC, SSR, native t-SNE) and need 2D embeddings to visually compare how well each separates known cell types/stages.

name: tsne-embedding-of-real-and-generated-cells
description: Use when validating scGAN or cscGAN generated single-cell RNA-seq data: embeddings must show generated cells overlapping real validation clusters and recapitulating cluster/marker-gene structure.

name: tsne-embedding-of-scrna-seq-counts
description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g., Tabula Muris FACS counts CSV) and need a 2D t-SNE embedding whose per-cell quality can be statistically assessed against a signal-less null.

name: tsne-embedding-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when a high-dimensional single-cell feature matrix (e.g., latent representations from Miscell, Seurat, Scanpy, or scVI) needs a fast 2D embedding for visualization and downstream clustering on datasets up to ~55,656 cells.

name: tsne-embedding-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when single-cell expression matrices (e.g., Villani PBMC, Baron pancreatic islet) need a 2-D visualization of cell-type separation or batch mixing, or a t-SNE embedding is required before KMeans clustering for ASW/ARI/NMI/purity evaluation.

name: tsne-embedding-on-similarity-matrix
description: Use when a cell-to-cell similarity matrix (e.g. learned by SIMLR from scRNA-seq expression data) must be turned into low-dimensional coordinates for visualizing and interpreting subpopulations.

name: tsne-embedding-quality-validation
description: Use when generated or augmented scRNA-seq cells (e.g. from scGAN/cscGAN) must be checked for realism against held-out real cells before downstream analyses such as marker gene detection or classifier training.

name: tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when comparing batch-correction methods on multi-batch scRNA-seq matrices and a visual QC of batch mixing versus cell-type separation is needed to accompany quantitative metrics.

name: tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you have BUSseq-fitted corrected read counts (from corrected_read_counts) and need to validate that the batch-effect correction succeeded before downstream analysis.

name: tsne-embedding-visualization
description: Use when assessing whether simulated single-cell RNA-seq data (e.g., GRouNdGAN output vs 1000 held-out test cells) resembles the reference distribution, as the qualitative counterpart to metric-based evaluation in --evaluate.

name: tsne-embedding-visualization-of-single-cell-clusters
description: Use when you have a log-transformed gene-cell-barcode matrix from tens of thousands of droplet-based 3' mRNA counting cells and need a 2D map that shows whether k-means clusters (e.g., k=10 on 50 PCs) form spatially distinct subpopulations.

name: tsne-latent-space-visualization
description: Use when a learned single-cell latent embedding (e.g., from scMDC on CITE-seq RNA+ADT data) must be visually assessed for cell-type separation and batch-effect removal before/instead of relying solely on quantitative clustering metrics.

name: tsne-perplexity-grid-optimization
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq object (e.g., Tabula Muris marrow, CAR-T GSE125881, Hydra) needs an optimized t-SNE perplexity, or when comparing hyperparameter optimization by scDEED vs EMBEDR via dubious-embedding counts and KNN/KNC preservation metrics.

name: tsne-perplexity-hyperparameter-sweep
description: Use when a t-SNE (or UMAP) embedding's quality depends on an unknown scale hyperparameter and you need to pick perplexity/kEff or detect characteristic neighborhood scales using per-sample p values rather than visual inspection.

name: tsne-perplexity-hyperparameter-verification
description: Use when a single-cell count matrix has been embedded with t-SNE and you must verify or report how dubious/trustworthy embedding fractions change between an original and a scDEED-optimized perplexity setting.

name: tsne-perplexity-tuning
description: Use when benchmarking a supervised or class-informed embedding (e.g. GraphDDP) against unsupervised baselines and you must demonstrate that t-SNE's perplexity choice can erase cluster/class structure on labeled single-cell data.

name: tsne-spurious-cluster-contrast
description: Use when evaluating whether a dimensionality-reduction method artificially fragments homogeneous data into compact clusters, or when validating that global structure (cluster shapes and relative locations) survives 2D embedding of high-dimensional data.

name: tsne-umap-dimensionality-reduction-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing dimensionality-reduction embeddings (scPhere vs t-SNE vs UMAP) on large scRNA-seq count matrices and you need a quantitative global-structure metric, e.g. k-NN accuracy to major cell types, rather than visual inspection.

name: tsne-umap-embedding-generation
description: Use when a normalized/scaled scRNA-seq matrix with detected variable features already has PCA scores and you need 2D/3D cluster-visualizing cell projections (t-SNE and UMAP coordinates per cell).

name: tsne-umap-neighborhood-hyperparameter-optimization
description: Use when comparing t-SNE and UMAP embedding quality at default (k=15) versus optimized neighborhood sizes on single-cell data, or when per-cell optimal perplexity/n_neighbors values are needed to distinguish real structure from algorithm-induced noise.

name: tsne-visualization-of-cell-clusters
description: Use when an imputed or raw single-cell expression matrix must be visually inspected for cluster compactness and separation across cell types, e.g., alongside ARI/Jaccard/NMI/purity benchmarks.

name: tsne-visualization-of-latent-embeddings
description: Use when a high-dimensional scRNA-seq embedding (e.g. a 20-dimensional scGAE latent space) must be rendered in 2D to visually verify cluster separation or resolve subpopulations before/after re-clustering.

name: tsne-visualization-of-scrnaseq-latent-space
description: Use when you have a low-dimensional per-cell representation (e.g., ZINB-WaVE W factors) and need a 2D t-SNE visualization of cell populations for clustering inspection or publication figures.

name: tsne-visualization-of-simulated-counts
description: Use when you have run SymSim's SimulateTrueCounts for discrete or continuous populations on a phyla tree (e.g. Phyla5()) and need to verify the simulated cell organization reflects the tree, or to inspect how Sigma changes population heterogeneity.

name: tsne-visualization-of-single-cell-profiles
description: Use when you have translated or measured single-cell profiles (e.g., predicted ADT from consecutive epigenome→transcriptome→proteome translation) and need a 2-D embedding to visually assess cell-type separation.

name: tsne-visualization-single-cell
description: Use when a normalized c-CSN-derived CNDM (m genes x n cells, e.g. >20,000 Tabula Muris droplet cells) needs dimension reduction and 2D visualization to confirm that cells segregate by known origin or cluster structure.

name: tss-anchored-motif-coordinate-analysis
description: Use when you have predicted core promoter elements anchored to annotated TSSs across multiple species and need to compare element position/score distributions to assess conservation or motif positioning quality.

name: tss-coordinate-sequence-extraction
description: Use when you have a set of TSS coordinates (e.g. EPDnew, GSE221852 csRNA-seq, GSE89299 RAMPAGE) and need promoter windows around each TSS as FASTA for motif-position analysis.

name: tss-dataset-quality-assessment
description: Use when you have a set of TSS annotations (e.g. from EPDnew/CAGE, csRNA-seq GSE221852, or RAMPAGE GSE89299) and want to judge dataset quality or compare TSS sources by the stringency of core promoter element positioning.

name: tss-enrichment-cell-filtering
description: Use when starting a scATAC-seq analysis from a fragments file (e.g. BMMC data) and you must exclude low-quality cells — low transcription start site (TSS) enrichment or too few unique nuclear fragments — before building the peak-count matrix and running LSI.

name: tss-proximal-peak-aggregation
description: Use when a mosaic dataset contains scATAC-seq batches but lacks scRNA-seq matrices for some batches (None placeholders in the counts dictionary), so that gene activity scores can substitute for missing gene expression.

name: tss-tts-distance-normalization
description: Use when profiling how far UMI-collapsed transcript coverage extends from transcript ends in 10x Chromium scRNA-seq data (e.g., to justify detecting SNVs up to ~10 kbp from the capture site).
tools: 10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 3' (v2) Gene Expression
10x Genomics Chromium Single Cell 5' (v1) Gene Expression

name: ttest-feature-filtering-within-cv-loop
description: Use when high-dimensional transcriptomic data (P >> n, e.g. RNA-seq expression matrices) must be filtered to a small top-variable set before fitting glmnet/elastic-net models, and you need an unbiased performance estimate rather than the optimistically biased inner-CV metric.

name: tuft-cell-marker-gene-enrichment
description: Use when a GapClust (or similar) rare-cluster detection run on scRNA-seq data yields candidate minor clusters whose identity must be confirmed by enrichment of known marker genes (e.g. Dclk1/Trpm5 for tuft cells).

name: tukey-hsd-posthoc-testing
description: Use when you have per-method, per-condition activity-inference scores (e.g. Spearman correlations to unperturbed activities across normal, edge-addition and edge-deletion networks) and need an omnibus ANOVA plus pairwise Tukey HSD comparison of group means.

name: tumor-boundary-delineation
description: Use when multiplexed single-cell data with x/y coordinates (e.g., MCMICRO-processed CyCIF output) needs region-based analysis requiring tumor/stromal region boundaries and per-cell region labels.

name: tumor-cell-classification-scrna
description: Use when you have raw scRNA-seq count matrices (Smart-seq2 or 10X Chromium) from tumor biopsies and need a fully unsupervised malignant/non-malignant cell classification without manually identified reference cell clusters.

name: tumor-cell-filtering-in-scrna-seq-clusters
description: Use when annotating normal cells within a tumor scRNA-seq dataset (e.g. TNBC GSE176078) and malignant clusters must be excluded first so cluster markers and cell-type calls reflect non-malignant biology only.

name: tumor-cell-fraction-quantification
description: Use when a marker-intensity single-cell table from multiplexed imaging (e.g. MCMICRO output of a CyCIF slide) must be scored per-cell for proliferation status (MPI in {-1, 0, 1}) and the fraction of a tumor-cell type such as SOX10+ cells with MPI = 1 quantified.

name: tumor-cell-malignancy-classification
