description: Use when you have normal-tissue scRNA-seq reference data with cell-type labels and tumor scRNA-seq test data, and need to identify malignant cells as those left unassigned by cell-type classifiers.

name: tumor-cell-malignancy-classification-benchmarking
description: Use when scRNA-seq tumor samples with matched bulk WGS/WES copy-number ground truth are available and you need to quantify accuracy of CNA inference or malignant-cell classification against methods like SCEVAN, inferCNV, and CopyKAT.

name: tumor-cluster-ground-truth-curation
description: Use when benchmarking malignant-cell identification tools against published scRNA-seq tumor datasets where ground truth must be derived from marker-defined clusters (SOX2, OLIG1, GFAP, S100B) or prior malignant annotations.

name: tumor-immune-microenvironment-cell-interaction-inference
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq or microarray data with matched overall survival (or immunotherapy response) information and cell-type marker lists, and you need to infer which immune cell-cell interactions drive favorable/unfavorable prognosis.

name: tumor-immune-regulator-prioritization
description: Use when you have pretrained MetaTiME MeC gene-weight tables (86 MeCs) and want to identify and rank putative TF regulators of a cell-state or signaling component using ChIP-seq binding evidence.

name: tumor-infiltrating-lymphocyte-subtype-classification
description: Use when scRNA-seq data from tumor-infiltrating T cells (human or mouse) must be annotated into stable, reference-defined functional states, or when comparing TIL composition across cohorts, tissues, or perturbation conditions.

name: tumor-isolation-index-quantification
description: Use when you have spatially resolved single-cell coordinates with tumor and immune markers (e.g., SOX10+, CD3D+) from a multiplexed imaging sample and need the fraction of tumor cells in regions without immune infiltration.

name: tumor-keratinocyte-colocalization-analysis
description: Use when you have paired SC and ST data from human squamous cell carcinoma (e.g. Figshare DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.24452812) and need to test spatial proximity of rare cell types such as TSKs and immune cells at single-cell resolution.

name: tumor-marker-expression-annotation
description: Use when a broad tumor/epithelial cluster in a Seurat scRNA-seq object shows low silhouette scores suggesting hidden heterogeneity, and rare malignant subclones or subtype identities (e.g., basal-like PDAC) must be resolved and annotated.

name: tumor-marker-gene-feature-selection
description: Use when preparing malignant vs non-malignant cell classification input: you have a normalized scRNA-seq expression matrix (genes x cells, TPM/CPM) and need DEG features (TMGs/NMGs) selected and [0,1]-scaled.

name: tumor-microenvironment-cell-identification
description: Use when annotating human scRNA-seq cells whose exact types may be missing from the classifier's training set (e.g. endothelial, fibroblast, plasmacytoid dendritic cells in LX675/LX679/LX682 lung tumor samples), and hierarchical Cell Ontology-consistent labels are wanted.

name: tumor-microenvironment-cell-subtype-classification
description: Use when a processed tumor scRNA-seq Seurat object (LogNormalize, 5000 vst features) needs major-type and fine subtype labels, or when subtype labels from different published references must be compared for similarity.

name: tumor-microenvironment-cluster-annotation
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells form one transcriptional cluster (e.g., tumor cells in a TNBC UMAP) but you need to reveal heterogeneous biological programs — such as mitotic cell cycle, DNA replication, DNA repair, or immune response — active in different regions of the cluster.

name: tumor-microenvironment-landscape-inference
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq expression matrix (rows = human gene symbols, columns = samples, e.g. TCGA) and need cell-type abundance estimates across ~434 TME cell types to cluster patients into TME subtypes.

name: tumor-microenvironment-region-partitioning
description: Use when a multiplexed imaging dataset (e.g., CyCIF MEL1, ~1.1M cells) has per-cell markers like SOX10+ (tumor) and CD3D+ (immune), and the goal is to split the ROI into tumor/immune subregions or compute a tumor isolation index.

name: tumor-microenvironment-subtype-classification
description: Use when annotating cells from cancer scRNA-seq data (Seurat object, counts matrix in csv/rds/h5, or 10X folder) into tumor-microenvironment major types and subtypes, especially T/NK and myeloid subtypes, without marker-based manual labeling.

name: tumor-normal-cohort-stratified-model-validation
description: Use when evaluating a trained RNA-seq-to-miRNA prediction model on large paired bulk mRNA/miRNA cohorts and you need cohort-wise accuracy (e.g., 5-fold CV Spearman per TCGA cancer type) rather than a single pooled score.

name: tumor-normal-differential-network-comparison
description: Use when the goal is sample-level comparison of pathway connectivity (e.g., EGFR pathway degree density between TCGA-LUAD tumor and adjacent normal samples) from RNA-seq expression matrices, requiring one network per sample.

name: tumor-normal-sample-pair-processing
description: Use when processing paired tumor-normal WES/WGS FASTQ through TSNAD v2.0 and HLA class I allele typing (4-digit HLA-A/B/C via OptiType 1.3.5) must be run per sample before neoantigen prediction.

name: tumor-phylogeny-inference-from-bulk-and-single-cell-snv
description: Use when you have matched bulk DNA WES and scRNA-seq SNV read counts (Rs, Xs, Rb, Xb) for the same tumor and need to infer subclone number, mutational profiles, cell-of-origin, and cell-to-clone assignments jointly.

name: tumor-phylogeny-reconstruction-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a Bayesian tumor phylogeny inference method (e.g., Canopy2) recovers true clonal configurations Z and single-cell clone assignments Ps better than competing methods across simulated bursting-kinetics settings.

name: tumor-purity-association-analysis
description: Use when scoring a bulk PDAC RNA-seq signature in TCGA-PAAD and asking whether its expression reflects tumor content rather than stromal/normal contamination, via correlation with ABSOLUTE purity.

name: tumor-purity-immune-score-estimation
description: Use when you need to quantify immune infiltration or tumor purity from bulk RNA-seq (e.g., TCGA RSEM-normalized expression) and test whether marker gene-set expression correlates with microenvironment features.

name: tumor-rnaseq-sample-processing
description: Use when processing tumor RNA-Seq FASTQ files to quantify gene/transcript expression (TPM) as a prerequisite for filtering neoantigen predictions by gene expression, following the TSNAD v2.0 module.

name: tumor-subclone-classification
description: Use when starting from a raw scRNA-seq count matrix of a tumor sample and you need unsupervised malignant/non-malignant classification plus subclone-level copy-number substructure and clone phylogeny.

name: tumor-subclone-identification-in-lymphoma-scrna
description: Use when a multi-timepoint (e.g., pre- vs post-treatment) scRNA-seq dataset such as MCL specimens has t0 cell labels transferred via CrossTimeAnnotation and you need to flag emergent tumor subclones among t1 cells.

name: tumor-subregion-proliferation-index-annotation
description: Use when a multiplexed imaging single-cell table (e.g. MCMICRO output from the MEL1 melanoma sample, 1,110,585 cells) has SOX10/Ki67/MITF marker intensities and region annotations, and the goal is per-subregion Ki67+/SOX10+ and MITF+/SOX10+ fractions as in Figure 3D/E.

name: tumor-suppressor-oncogene-classification
description: Use when classifying genes into TSG vs OG classes from a somatic mutation feature matrix (e.g. 37-feature COSMIC-derived pan-cancer matrix) with CGC labels, and per-class accuracy/precision/recall/F1 metrics are required.

name: tumor-vs-healthy-bp-coactivation-comparison
description: Use when per-cell scRNA-seq activity profiles for the 18 ORIGINS2 biological processes are available for tumor and healthy samples and the goal is to detect which BP pairs are correlated vs anti-correlated per condition.

name: tumour-immune-fraction-deconvolution
description: Use when bulk RNA-seq tumour samples (e.g. log2(TPM+1) TCGA data) are being ordered along a covariate-modulated pseudotime and you need per-sample immune cell fractions to validate or annotate the trajectory.

name: twas-null-calibration-analysis
description: Use when you need to verify that simulated TWAS Z-scores or p-values are consistent with the null (KS p > 0.05 vs Uniform(0,1)), with FWER ~0.05 and genomic inflation lambda ~1.

name: twas-power-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when comparing TWAS training frameworks' power or GReX imputation accuracy, e.g., testing whether summary-level reference weights outperform individual-level baselines like FUSION.

name: twas-power-estimation-across-ld-panels
description: Use when evaluating how TWAS power or type-I error changes when eQTL weight-training LD and TWAS testing LD come from a different reference panel than the GWAS LD, or when planning TWAS power analyses.

name: twas-power-estimation-across-parameter-grid
description: Use when you need to compare TWAS power across prediction models or quantify how power scales with GWAS/eQTL sample size, eqtl-h2, h2ge, and number of causal eQTLs before choosing weights for a real TWAS.

name: twas-simulation-execution
description: Use when the task requires simulating a complex trait from real 1000G Phase 3 PLINK genotypes and producing GWAS/TWAS statistics for evaluating TWAS method performance or power at settings like --ngwas 100000 and --nqtl 500.

name: twas-type1-error-estimation
description: Use when you need to verify that a gene-based association (TWAS) test controls false positives under the null, before applying it to real GWAS summary statistics.

name: tweedie-model-gene-level-fitting
description: Use when performing differential expression on scRNA-seq UMI or non-UMI count matrices (or other omics counts) between two conditions, especially when data are sparse, zero-inflated, or heavy-tailed and standard NB-based methods underperform.

name: tweedie-profile-likelihood-estimation
description: Use when fitting per-gene (or per-feature) GLMs to sparse, semi-continuous count or abundance data where the optimal Tweedie index parameter p is unknown and must be estimated automatically within the constrained interval (1, 2).

name: tweedie-semicontinuous-count-modeling
description: Use when the input is a sparse, semi-continuous omics feature-by-sample matrix (counts or relative abundances) with point mass at zero and heavy tails, and you need per-feature differential testing between conditions.

name: two-cluster-gaussian-simulation-analysis
description: Use when analyzing a simulated two-cluster perturbation/control parameter grid varying cluster distance d and ratio change r, to verify that infected proportion bias on PCs scales linearly with d and r as derived in Equations 14-15.

name: two-means-differential-expression-clustering
description: Use when comparing cell-cycle-corrected vs. original scRNA-Seq matrices and you need DE genes plus a signature-gene enrichment statistic (odds ratio, hypergeometric p, 95% CI) to judge whether recovered substructure is biologically meaningful.

name: two-sample-distribution-testing-between-conditions
description: Use when cells from two conditions share a single slingshot trajectory and you must test whether lineage-membership weight distributions differ, i.e., whether conditions allocate cells to lineages in different proportions.

name: two-sample-t-test-cell-correlation-testing
description: Use when annotating t1 scRNA-seq cells against a t0 label set (via CASi's neural network) and you need to flag cells that may belong to newly emerged cell types rather than forcing known labels.

name: two-stage-adamw-warmup-training
description: Use when transforming a filtered, non-negative single-cell representation (e.g., from the non-negative kernel autoencoder) into a low-dimensional compressed latent embedding for downstream clustering, visualization, classification, or pseudo-time inference.

name: two-stage-gan-pretraining-procedure
description: Use when building or retraining a CausalGAN-style simulator for scRNA-seq where a masked causal controller must first be pretrained as a non-conditional WGAN-GP generator before the GRN-structured model is trained end-to-end.

name: two-stage-recursive-cell-type-estimation
description: Use when deconvolving bulk RNA-seq from tissues containing closely related cell types whose expression collinearity breaks single-stage NNLS deconvolution, and a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference is available.

name: type-i-error-and-power-assessment
description: Use when validating a differential topology/proportion test on multi-sample scRNA-seq data: simulated perturbations (e.g., removing myeloid cells from 0–80% of samples' cells) must show controlled type I error at 0% and monotonically increasing power.

name: type-i-error-qq-plot-calibration-assessment
description: Use when benchmarking a statistical method on null/permuted data and you need to verify that its p-values are Uniform(0,1)-calibrated rather than inflated (false positives) or deflated (lost power).

name: type-i-ifn-score-interpretation
description: Use when whole-blood transcript levels (e.g. MCEMP1, HLA-DRA, ETS1) must be correlated sample-wise with clinical severity predictors — CRP, lymphocyte counts or the 28-gene type I IFN score — in the Ong et al. COVID-19 cohort.

name: uberon-tissue-standardization
description: Use when integrating marker databases or cell-sorting marker collections whose tissue annotations use non-standard nomenclature and need to be mapped to a common anatomy ontology before cross-source aggregation.

name: ucell-module-scoring-of-scrnaseq-cells
description: Use when a JOINTLY (or similar NMF-based) joint clustering run has produced interpretable gene modules that must be quantified per cell to annotate cell types, map factor activity, or compare module gene specificity against traditional markers.

name: uci-benchmark-dataset-preparation
description: Use when benchmarking filter FS algorithms (mRMR, CFS, JMI, RELIEF, RRCT, etc.) and you need the study's real-world datasets — Spambase, SPECTF, SRBCT, Ovarian cancer, Cardiotocography, Handwriting, Relathe, Lymph — loaded in matrix form.

name: ucsc-table-browser-gene-model-retrieval
description: Use when SkewC's shipped reference files (hg38_Gencode_V28.norRNAtRNA.bed, mm10_Gencode_VM18.norRNAtRNA.bed) do not match your genome assembly and a custom gene model without rRNA/tRNA entries must be built.

name: umap-2d-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq dataset has been reduced to a high-dimensional embedding (e.g. 40 PCA dimensions) and a 2D visualization is needed to inspect or display Leiden cluster structure, as done for the HuBMAP HBMP3-spleen-CC2 dataset.

name: umap-activity-colormap-visualization
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells already have a UMAP embedding and per-cell activity scores from a PPIN (with or without negative-regulator edges) need to be visualized as a color scale and compared across cell-type populations.

name: umap-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when single-cell data (mass cytometry, scRNA-seq, or spatially reconstructed transcriptomics) have a priori class labels and you need to decide whether supervised LD axes separate labeled structure better than unsupervised UMAP/PCA/PHATE embeddings.

name: umap-cell-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq dataset has already been quality-controlled and dimension-reduced (PCA or iterative LSI) and a 2D visualization of cells colored by Louvain/Seurat cluster identity is needed.

name: umap-cluster-label-propagation
description: Use when a Seurat object has root-node hierarchical predictions from a pretrained Census model (or analogous classifier) and per-cell labels need smoothing/denoising before proceeding to the next node in the cell-type hierarchy.

name: umap-coordinate-mapping
description: Use when reconciling multiple single-cell clustering/annotation sets stored outside an AnnData object, requiring prior cluster labels and UMAP embeddings be registered as obs/obsm fields before decision-level integration.

name: umap-dimension-reduction-embedding
description: Use when constructing low-dimensional embeddings of single-cell RNA-seq data with UMAP as an input choice for trajectory inference and you need to verify the embedding is not disconnected before fitting pseudotime with Slingshot or Monocle3.

name: umap-dimension-reduction-single-cell
description: Use when single-cell expression data needs a low-dimensional embedding for downstream similarity or clustering tasks — e.g. computing per-cell-type 20-dim UMAP vectors for CASi's correlation-based novel-cell detection.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when you have high-dimensional per-transcript feature vectors (e.g., codon-, GC-, sequence-, peptide-, or BERT-encoded ORF-attention features) and need a 2D scatter visualization to check whether lncRNAs and PCTs form separable clusters.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when preprocessing scRNA-seq count data (e.g., PBMC4k or Segerstolpe) for clustering-based evaluation of synthetic data, or when synthetic observations need cluster labels assigned via nearest-neighbor mapping in a reduced space.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq data has per-cell clonal barcode assignments and you want 2D UMAP embeddings in which cells sharing a barcode progressively coalesce as clone influence is tuned up.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-embedding
description: Use when a single-cell (scRNA-seq or scATAC-seq) count matrix has been normalized and feature-selected, and you need a 2D embedding for cluster visualization, annotation, or Monocle 3 trajectory topology.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-spatial-proteomics
description: Use when a CODEX or other spatial proteomics cell-by-protein expression matrix (e.g., AnnData) must be embedded for downstream Leiden clustering and spatial tile visualization, without prior normalization.

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when running SCASL on single-cell SMART-seq junction/AS matrices and you need a 2D visualization of spectral-clustering results on the imputed AS probability matrix (dimension_reduction_method='umap' in configs/srr.yaml).

name: umap-dimensionality-reduction-visualization
description: Use when annotating cells at a later timepoint (t1) against known labels from an initial timepoint (t0) and you need a 2D UMAP projection to inspect whether novel-cell calls or annotation assignments form coherent clusters.

name: umap-embedding-and-signature-score-visualization
description: Use when per-cell signature scores have been computed (e.g., UCell scores stored in altExp(sce,'UCell') or Seurat metadata) and you need to visualize signature enrichment across cells in 2D to interpret clusters.

name: umap-embedding-evaluation
description: Use when benchmarking how well cell-cell communication features (UMAP embeddings or tensor factor loadings) separate phenotypic contexts such as COVID-19 status and severity, using a supervised classifier's cross-validated AUC.

name: umap-embedding-mixing-assessment
description: Use when you have cell-by-gene expression matrices (e.g. expr_mat.csv) segmented independently from two replicate spatial transcriptomics sections and need to quantify whether segmentation output is replicable across replicates.

name: umap-embedding-of-layer-representations
description: Use when a trained deep learning model (e.g. a protein-sequence CNN built with autoBioSeqpy) needs its hidden-layer outputs visualized in 2-D UMAP space for layer-by-layer inspection, diagnosis or refinement of representations.

name: umap-embedding-of-predicted-expression-profiles
description: Use when RNAForecaster (or another gene-dimensional forecaster) has produced future/perturbed expression profiles and you need to verify they occupy biologically plausible expression space by checking co-clustering with real or simulated post-perturbation cells.

name: umap-embedding-of-single-cell-data
description: Use when two or more a priori class labels capture distinct biological sources of variance in single-cell data and you need one unsupervised embedding that preserves all of them simultaneously.

name: umap-embedding-overlay-of-apa-scores
description: Use when single-cell poly(A) site data (PACdataset) has computed per-cell APA indices like RUD and you need to check spatial coherence of those scores on the cell embedding.

name: umap-embedding-overlay-visualization
description: Use when per-cell scores (DA-seq differential abundance scores, cluster or severity annotations) need to be visualized in low-dimensional space on a UMAP built from scMerge2-adjusted single-cell expression data.

name: umap-embedding-parameter-sensitivity-analysis
description: Use when evaluating whether cell-type annotations from an embedding-dependent annotation method (e.g. Census, whose label-stabilizing step uses UMAP clusters and prediction contours) remain stable across UMAP hyperparameter variations like n.neighbors and min.dist.

name: umap-embedding-projection-and-distance-computation
description: Use when benchmarking UMI deduplication or read-level count-recovery tools against a ground-truth gene-by-cell UMI matrix and you need a cell-position-level accuracy metric (mean Euclidean UMAP distance per tool) rather than only correlation statistics.

name: umap-embedding-visualization
description: Use when an integrated scRNA-seq embedding (AnnData with an integrated latent representation and batch/cell-type annotations) needs a 2D UMAP visualization to qualitatively verify batch mixing and cell-type separation after integration.

name: umap-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a trained autoBioSeqpy/Keras model (tmpMod., tmpWeight.bin, parameters.txt) must be validated or diagnosed by visualizing its hidden-layer activations as a 2D UMAP scatter plot colored by class labels.

name: umap-embedding-visualization
description: Use when single-cell scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GSE149689 PBMCs) have been normalized, PCA-reduced and batch-integrated, and you need a 2D embedding to assign cell-type labels and localize gene expression changes to specific immune subsets.

name: umap-embedding-visualization
description: Use when you have a learned low-dimensional joint embedding (e.g. scConfluence latent space in MuData obsm) and need a 2D visualization to inspect cell-type organization, subclusters, or modality alignment.

name: umap-embedding-visualization
description: Use when a fitted GEDI model's integrated cell space or sample-specific manifold parameters need a 2D UMAP visualization annotated by donor, technology, sample, or cell type.

name: umap-embedding-visualization-of-integrated-data
description: Use when you have an integrated or batch-adjusted single-cell expression matrix (scRNA-seq or CyTOF) and need to visually verify that datasets are mixed within shared cell types and that cell-type-specific populations are preserved.

name: umap-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when 2D UMAP visualizations of deep-learning (e.g. RFCN) hidden-layer representations of scRNA-seq cells look unstable or poorly separated and you need to determine whether n_neighbors or min_dist drives the clustering before trusting the embedding.

name: umap-hyperparameter-grid-search
description: Use when a Seurat scRNA-seq or CyTOF object needs UMAP visualization and the analyst must choose min.dist and n.neighbors objectively rather than by default, e.g. when 2D cluster layout trustworthiness is in question.

name: umap-integration-visualization
description: Use when you have raw and scMerge2-adjusted expression matrices from a multi-sample, multi-condition single-cell atlas (e.g. 20 COVID-19 studies, 1298 samples, 963 donors) and must demonstrate integration quality via UMAP embedding plots and technical-label PCA metrics.

name: umap-re-embedding-of-subsampled-data
description: Use when assessing annotation robustness to sample size: after down-sampling cells (e.g., 5–500 per UMAP cluster), each subsampled dataset must be re-projected to a new UMAP before re-running cell-type prediction.

name: umap-visualization-of-cell-type-annotations
description: Use when a scanpy AnnData query (e.g. GSE171524, 116,314 cells) has scNovel novelty labels and cell-type annotations, and visual confirmation is needed that known types (B cell, T cell) are rarely flagged novel while AT1/AT2 are detected as novel.

name: umap-visualization-of-da-scores
description: Use when two processed single-cell datasets (e.g. early fetal liver eFL and fetal liver FL HSPC objects) have been integrated and annotated, and you need to identify and visualize which cell subpopulations are differentially abundant between them via DAseq scores on UMAP.

name: umap-visualization-of-forecast-trajectories
description: Use when you have recursive future-expression predictions from RNAForecaster (predictCellFutures output) and need to qualitatively verify that predicted cell states reproduce lineage structure, e.g. bifurcation into two branches.

name: umap-visualization-of-imputed-protein-abundance
description: Use when scRNA-seq cells (e.g. van Galen AML or normal bone marrow) have had surface proteins imputed by cTP-net and you need a 2D embedding to order cells along a differentiation trajectory or annotate immunophenotype clusters.

name: umi-based-misalignment-correction
description: Use when Nanopore long reads aligned with minimap2 yield spurious isoforms from wrongly mapped small internal exons (e.g., VPS28-201) or truncated ends, and read-level counts must be corrected within UMI clusters before isoform quantification.

name: umi-based-variant-quality-filtering
description: Use when calling SNVs from UMI-based scRNA-seq data (e.g. Cell Ranger-aligned 10x droplet data) to classify individual cells by genotype, quantify chimerism or multiplets, or need variant quality criteria tied to UMI/cell-barcode support rather than read depth alone.

name: umi-cell-barcode-consensus-generation
description: Use when single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM alignments must be deduplicated into per-UMI per-cell consensus gRNA sequences before variant calling, e.g. to reproduce the 28.4% mutant molecule fraction.

name: umi-cell-barcode-gene-combination-deduplication
description: Use when droplet-based 10x Genomics libraries from multiple samples were sequenced together on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) and swapped molecules sharing UMI, cell barcode, and gene across samples must be removed.

name: umi-cell-barcode-synthesis
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq UMI deduplication or read-level tools on 10X-style data and you need synthetic reads whose true UMI counts and cell barcodes are known (e.g. from a 10X BAM with CB/UMI structure).

name: umi-cellbarcode-gene-collision-resolution
description: Use when processing molecule information files from multiplexed 10x Genomics droplet libraries sequenced on patterned flow-cell instruments (HiSeq 4000, HiSeq X, NovaSeq) where ~2.5% of reads may be mislabelled between samples via barcode swapping.

name: umi-cluster-size-scatter-reduction
description: Use when quantifying isoforms from single-cell or spatially barcoded Nanopore long reads with high per-base error (85-99%), where UMI scattering inflates UMI counts and fixed-edit-distance collapsing would overestimate expression.

name: umi-consensus-sequence-construction
description: Use when processing a single-cell CRISPR screen gRNA library BAM (mapped to the designed gRNA cassette reference) whose reads carry cell barcodes and UMIs, and you need per-UMI consensus sequences before calling mutations or assigning gRNAs to cells.

name: umi-count-aggregation-per-phase
description: Use when phase-annotated h5ad data (adata.obs['cell_cycle_theta'] from a DeepCycle run) is available and you need to verify that UMI counts per cell increase roughly 2-fold along the cell cycle prior to the mitotic drop.

name: umi-count-inflation-benchmark-analysis
description: Use when recovering true UMIs from error-prone Nanopore single-cell long reads, or when testing whether a UMI collapsing strategy (e.g. DBSCAN at eps=2) inflates UMI counts at high PCR amplification.

name: umi-count-matrix-construction-from-bam
description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq BAM file aligned to mm10, a gene annotation GTF (e.g., gencode.vM10.annotation.gtf), and a chromosome size file, and you need gene- and inter-gene-by-cell UMI count matrices as ground truth for simulation or benchmarking.

name: umi-count-matrix-integration-10x
description: Use when you have a cellranger count output folder for a 10x scRNAseq sample (e.g. HIV donor or SARS-CoV-2 airway data) and need pathogen UMI counts merged into features.tsv.gz/matrix.mtx.gz so Seurat or standard single-cell pipelines can analyze infected cells downstream.

name: umi-count-matrix-processing
description: Use when the input is a raw single-cell UMI count matrix and you need zero-inflation- and over-dispersion-aware low-dimensional signal extraction without a preliminary normalization step.

name: umi-counting-and-error-correction
description: Use when processing droplet-based scRNA-seq FASTQ data with cell barcodes and UMIs (e.g. 10x GemCode/Chromium), to deduplicate reads into molecule counts or to quantify conversion efficiency against known ERCC spike-in inputs.

name: umi-deduplication-benchmarking
description: Use when synthetic scRNA-seq reads with known ground-truth UMI counts are available and you must rank UMI deduplication tools by accuracy and runtime, reproducing the scReadSim Nature Communications 2023 benchmark (Fig. 4a-d).

name: umi-duplicate-collapsing
description: Use when counting molecules from UMI-tagged RNA-Seq alignments: a sorted SAM file exists and duplicate UMI at identical genomic positions must be merged into single observations before per-gene counting.

name: umi-error-correction-and-collapsing
description: Use when processing single-cell amplicon sequencing data for expressed lineage barcodes and you must remove PCR chimeras and collapse UMI sequencing errors before per-cell barcode annotation.

name: umi-extraction-and-pcr-duplicate-removal
description: Use when processing paired-end FASTQ from spatially barcoded ST data (e.g., MOB ST, SRA: SRR3382373) to attach barcode/UMI identifiers to read 2 and deduplicate PCR artifacts before poly(A) site identification.

name: umi-normalization
description: Use when a cellranger gene-expression matrix has been loaded into a SingCellaR object and passed through filter_cells_and_genes (UMI, detected-gene, percent-mito thresholds, doublet removal), and counts must be scaled before variable-gene fitting or clustering.

name: umi-normalization-and-confounder-regression
description: Use when a QC-filtered SingCellaR object (raw UMI matrix, e.g. after merge of replicates like eFL_1 and eFL_2) needs comparable per-cell expression values with library-size and nuisance-factor effects removed before PCA/UMAP/clustering.

name: umi-quality-correction
description: Use when generating or auditing 3' UMI counting matrices from GemCode/Chromium scRNA-seq FASTQ data where barcode synthesis/sequencing errors must be corrected before counting UMIs per cell barcode.

name: umi-read-cluster-collapsing
description: Use when processing quality-filtered, UMI-clipped single-end RNA-Seq data (e.g., sorted SAM alignments of P. patens SCRB-Seq reads) where reads sharing a UMI must be collapsed to per-molecule counts despite mapping to slightly different genomic coordinates.

name: umi-read-clustering-with-edit-distance-threshold
description: Use when processing UMI-containing single-cell RNA-Seq FASTQ/SAM data (e.g. SCRB-Seq, CEL-Seq2, tagmentation libraries) and you need to collapse duplicate UMI reads at the same genomic position into molecule counts before gene-level quantification.

name: umi-threshold-barcode-set-partition
description: Use when starting from a raw unfiltered count matrix (mtx or h5) and you need to define PU-learning training sets for distinguishing cell-free from cell-containing droplets by total UMI count.

name: umi-threshold-based-cell-filtering
description: Use when you have raw gene-by-cell spliced/unspliced UMI count matrices from scKB (kallisto/bustools) and need to remove low-quality or empty droplets non-arbitrarily before downstream Seurat or RNA-velocity analysis.

name: umi-validity-filtering-and-hamming-correction
description: Use when processing droplet scRNA-seq FASTQ reads (e.g. 10x Genomics GemCode/Chromium data) into a UMI count matrix and you need to remove invalid UMIs and collapse sequencing-error UMIs to avoid inflating molecule counts.

name: umi-vs-non-umi-protocol-zero-inflation-analysis
description: Use when validating that a Bayesian scRNA-seq count model reproduces observed batch-level zero rates, or when assessing whether an explicit zero-inflated dropout component is justified versus a plain negative-binomial fit.

name: umicount-matrix-preprocessing
description: Use when raw UMI count matrices from multiple individuals' droplet scRNA-seq libraries (10x Chromium) must be formatted and zero-gene filtered before population-level clustering with BAMM-SC.

name: umiread-cluster-collapse-thresholding
description: Use when UMI-to-genomic-position mappings (e.g. umi_positions.txt from umi_analyzer_uthash) must be grouped and collapsed so reads sharing a UMI that map within 3 bp count once instead of as multiple molecules.

name: unaligned-read-remapping-with-bowtie2
description: Use when a Ribo-seq pipeline leaves reads unmapped after a first splice-aware genome alignment (HISAT2) and you want to salvage them with a second, less stringent ungapped mapper like Bowtie2.

name: unassigned-label-fraction-analysis
description: Use when benchmarking scRNA-seq cell annotation methods on data where all true cell types are known, to check whether each method assigns labels exhaustively or dumps many cells as 'unassigned'/'intermediate'.

name: unbalanced-cluster-cell-grouping
description: Use when scRNA-seq/snRNA-seq counts for a cell-type subcluster have highly unbalanced cells per subject (e.g., AST3 cells from only ~4 of 30+ subjects) and naive per-cell differential or marker testing would inflate false positives.

name: unbalanced-sinkhorn-divergence-regularization
description: Use when integrating unpaired single-cell modalities (e.

name: uncertainty-scoring-with-expert-ensemble
description: Use when annotating target scRNA-seq cells with a pre-trained source-free classifier and you need per-cell uncertainty scores to detect whether novel cell types are present without manually defined thresholds.

name: unclassifiable-sample-counting-across-cohorts
description: Use when comparing subtype classifiers by how many samples they cannot assign (max posterior probability at or below a cutoff), e.g. DeepCC vs the random-forest CMS classifier on CRC cohorts.

name: unified-vs-independent-velocity-mode-selection
description: Use when running UniTVelo on a count-matrix AnnData and you must decide between the unified latent time model and gene-independent latent time, e.g. for simple differentiation vs complex multi-branching systems like bone marrow differentiation.

name: unimodal-baseline-model-training
description: Use when benchmarking a multimodal TCR+transcriptome model against unimodal baselines on specificity-annotated single-cell data, to test whether modality fusion improves pMHC antigen specificity prediction.

name: unimodal-vs-multimodal-comparison-analysis
description: Use when multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT, or RNA+ADT+ATAC from the same cells) is available and you must decide whether integrated multimodal clustering beats per-modality unimodal clustering.

name: union-threshold-gene-selection
description: Use when after computing dCor and MIC correlations of every gene's expression profile against redPATH pseudotime, you must retain genes significantly linked to proliferation/differentiation (e.g. recover Foxm1, Tubb5, Nek2 in the Llorens-Bobadilla NSC dataset).

name: univariate-cox-survival-analysis
description: Use when a bulk transcriptomic dataset has matched survival (event + time-to-event) information and you must test each gene-pair or marker-pair score individually for prognostic association before building a directed gene-gene network.

name: univariate-ttest-feature-filtering
description: Use when building a glmnet/caret predictive model on high-dimensional biomedical data (P >> n) with a binary outcome and you must restrict predictors to the strongest univariate signals without leaking test-fold information.

name: unix-pipe-chaining-of-bioinformatics-tools
description: Use when a read-level analysis requires two or more sequential operations (e.g. selecting reads containing a variant, then demultiplexing cell barcodes) and the tools involved can read from stdin and write to stdout, so intermediate FASTQ files can be avoided.

name: unknown-cell-type-detection-assessment
description: Use when evaluating whether an annotation method correctly reports 'Unknown' for cell types whose marker signatures are absent, via leave-one-cell-type-out tests on simulated scRNA-seq count matrices with known ground truth.

name: unknown-label-abstention-benchmarking
description: Use when evaluating whether a label-transfer annotator handles truly unseen cell types: a cell type is deleted from the training reference and held-out query cells of that type should be reported as 'Unknown' instead of receiving a wrong label.

name: unlabeling-rate-quantification
description: Use when benchmarking automatic cell-type identification methods on labeled scRNA-seq test data and you need to expose methods that abstain too often, complementing accuracy and F1-score on cross-platform or cross-validation splits.

name: unmapped-read-extraction-from-aligned-rnaseq
description: Use when you have TCGA (or similar) paired-end RNA-seq FASTQs that have been aligned to hg19, and you need the unaligned fraction as FASTQ input for alignment-free viral read detection.

name: unmapped-read-microbiome-profiling
description: Use when you have small RNA-seq FASTQ data processed through QC and human-genome alignment (e.g., STAR) and need to quantify microbial RNA species from the unmapped reads in the four supported taxons: archaea, bacteria, fungi and viruses.

name: unpaired-data-augmentation
description: Use when training scButterfly on unpaired samples — e.g., unpaired control and stimulated PT_PBMC scRNA-seq for perturbation-response prediction — and cell-type labels are available in adata.obs to enable scButterfly-T pairing.

name: unpaired-multiomics-diagonal-integration
description: Use when cell populations were profiled in separate cells per modality (diagonal integration), cross-modality feature connections are rare/noisy, and some cell types may be present in only one modality.

name: unpaired-students-t-test
description: Use when two sample groups' circRNA expression values (e.g., CIRCscore or FPBcirc per circRNA from CLEAR quant.txt files) must be compared for a statistically significant distributional shift, as in HCC vs paired-normal ribo− RNA-seq.

name: unreplicated-dataset-bootstrapping
description: Use when a single-cell dataset (e.g., an AnnData/h5ad object with clustered, annotated cell types) has no replicate samples for all conditions, and you need differential cell-type proportion analysis with p-values and significance calls.

name: unsampled-cell-classification-projection
description: Use when a large-scale scRNA-seq matrix was clustered on a random subsample and the remaining unsampled cells must be assigned to clusters without rerunning the base clustering algorithm on the full dataset.

name: unseen-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when the query scRNA-seq data may contain cell types absent from the reference training set and every Cell Ontology term — including unseen ones — needs a per-cell confidence score.

name: unseen-cell-type-benchmark-evaluation
description: Use when evaluating whether a cell-type annotation method can assign cells to Cell Ontology terms absent from the training set, especially on Tabula Muris Senis Muris droplet data with controlled unseen-term proportions.

name: unseen-cell-type-detection
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset (AnnData) contains cell types not represented in the reference used for MASI label transfer, e.g. query annotations exceed reference cell types (Oetjen et al. 16 types vs 10x PBMC 12 types).

name: unshared-encoder-weight-norm-extraction
description: Use when a trained scDisInFact model exists on multi-batch multi-condition scRNA-seq counts and per-gene rankings of condition-associated key genes are needed for one or more condition types.

name: unshared-feature-augmentation-for-integration
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple species via BENGAL/LIGER UINMF and genes lacking annotated ENSEMBL homology should be retained as unshared features instead of being dropped.

name: unspliced-count-sparsity-quantification
description: Use when loading a new scRNA-seq h5ad into TFvelo_run_demo.py and you need to measure zero-fraction in unspliced counts to justify applying a regulation-based (TF) velocity model instead of a splicing-based one.

name: unspliced-spliced-dynamics-fitting
description: Use when a velocyto/scVelo-processed scRNA-seq dataset (h5ad with Mu/Ms layers) shows cycling patterns in the unspliced-spliced space of GOterm cell_cycle genes and you need a continuous, circular cell cycle trajectory per cell.

name: unspliced-spliced-gene-pattern-fitting
description: Use when scRNA-seq data with spliced/unspliced layers (velocyto + scvelo.pp.moments) shows cycling patterns in unspliced-spliced space of cell-cycle genes and you need a high-resolution continuous cell cycle phase per cell.

name: unspliced-spliced-phase-seeding
description: Use when scRNA-seq data preprocessed with scvelo.pp.moments (Ms/Mu layers) should be assigned a continuous high-resolution cell-cycle phase per cell, and a cycling base gene (e.g. Nusap1 or MELK) is available for phase initialization.

name: unstructured-annotation-serialization
description: Use when a Scanpy AnnData object (.h5ad or in-memory) needs to be persisted as a queryable relational DuckDB database, including unstructured uns mappings that have no natural table form.

name: unsupervised-cell-clustering
description: Use when clustering raw single-cell RNA-seq count data (genes x cells matrix) with unknown cell labels, or when benchmarking scDHA against SC3, SEURAT, SINCERA, CIDR, SCANPY, or k-means on datasets with known cell types using ARI.

name: unsupervised-cell-type-annotation
description: Use when annotating clusters in a normalized/scaled scRNA-seq matrix (e.g., a Seurat object) without a labeled reference, and only a marker database plus the expression data are available.

name: unsupervised-clustering-annotation-comparison
description: Use when you have a simulated or labeled scRNA-seq count matrix with known cell-type labels and a marker list, and you need to rank clustering-then-annotation baselines (Seurat, SC3, PhenoGraph, densityCut, dynamicTreeCut) against marker-based or eager-learning classifiers.

name: unsupervised-feature-selection-for-scrnaseq
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq expression matrices where all genes cannot be treated as equally significant and insignificant genes must be filtered out without using cell-type labels.

name: unsupervised-gene-prioritization
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq expression data has been clustered or embedded with SIMLR and you need to identify the genes that explain differences across the inferred sample populations without pre-selecting gene subsets of known function.

name: unsupervised-marker-selection
description: Use when you must pick a minimal gene panel (e.g. k=50 markers) from scRNA-seq data without cell-type labels, and want to benchmark unsupervised selectors on full-transcriptome reconstruction loss.

name: unsupervised-scrna-seq-clustering-reclustering
description: Use when the input is a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. 10X PBMC3k) whose initial unsupervised clusters appear heterogeneous, and rare or low-abundance cell populations must be resolved without prior labels.

name: unsupervised-trainer-training-loop
description: Use when an AnnData cells-by-genes matrix needs unsupervised scETM training (e.g., MousePancreas.h5ad with 'batch_indices' and 'cell_types' in adata.obs) before embedding extraction or zero-shot transfer to a target dataset.

name: upset-plot-method-comparison-visualization
description: Use when comparing which genes multiple DS analysis methods (pseudobulk pbDS engines vs. cell-level mmDS mixed models) call significant at FDR < 0.05, and you need to visualize set intersections across methods and replicates.

name: uridine-centered-fragment-filtering
description: Use when scanning transcriptome-wide RNA sequences for candidate pseudouridine (Ψ) sites and you need to restrict deep-learning scoring to uridine-centered 51-base fragments.

name: utar-coverage-peak-fwhm-extraction
description: Use when a set of differentially expressed uTARs (e.g., Wilcoxon rank-sum hits) must be assigned functional or gene-level annotations via nucleotide sequence homology of their coverage peaks.

name: utar-feature-expression-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq alignments must be quantified against annotation-independent genomic TARs, and when deciding whether pseudo-bulk uTAR expression or single-cell PC loading better flags biologically significant uTARs.

name: utar-genomic-overlap-matching
description: Use when spatial Visium count matrices and a TAR+reference genome annotation are available and you must confirm that scRNA-seq-discovered uTARs are spatially detectable and colocalize with known marker genes.

name: utility-based-obd-selection
description: Use when running or reproducing a phase I/II immunotherapy dose-finding trial/simulation that must pick an OBD by jointly balancing binary DLT and efficacy outcomes via a utility function, after a toxicity-exploration stage has defined an admissible dose set.

name: utr-annotation-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to measure whether improved 3' UTR annotation (e.g. peaks2utr output with source=peaks2utr) translates into better per-cell genes captured and UMI counts in a 10x Chromium scRNA-seq quantification pipeline.

name: utr-annotation-from-bam-reads
description: Use when you have an aligned scRNA-seq BAM (e.g. 10x Chromium, UTR-enriched) plus a GFF/GTF gene model and need to annotate or reannotate 3' UTRs beyond the canonical annotation.

name: utr-cds-genomic-background-construction
description: Use when a region set of transcriptomic features (e.g. m7G/m6A methylation sites with unknown isoform origin) must be tested for colocalization against 5'UTR or CDS regions using permutation-based null models in R/RgnTX.

name: utr-cds-metagene-segmentation
description: Use when you need a canonical 5'-UTR-CDS-3'-UTR metagene of CLIP (eCLIP/STAMP) binding density on mature mRNA, rather than Metadensity's custom pre-mRNA feature models such as branchpoints or polyadenylation sites.

name: utr-enrichment-peak-detection
description: Use when annotating 3' UTRs from aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium BAM signal concentrated at UTR distal ends) and you need to identify candidate regions of significant read coverage before UTR end determination.

name: utr-sequence-seed-match-counting
description: Use when you have a DESeq2 results data.frame and an siRNA guide sequence, and need per-gene counts of a defined seed (e.g., mer7m8) across 3'UTRs to test for seed-mediated off-target activity.

name: utr-truncation-point-pileup-annotation
description: Use when a GFF/GTF gene annotation plus a BAM of aligned reads (e.g. 10x Chromium, where signal concentrates at UTR distal ends) must be converted into novel 3' UTR annotations.

name: utrome-transcriptome-target-handling
description: Use when running scUTRquant on 10x Genomics or Microwell-seq-style 3'-end scRNA-seq FASTQs and a UTRome/CS-annotated target (e.g. utrome_mm10_v2) must be chosen, built, or configured for gene and 3'UTR isoform quantification.

name: vae-based-cell-embedding-clustering
description: Use when an annotated or unannotated single-cell gene-expression matrix must be clustered and embedded without pre-specifying the number of clusters, e.g. reproducing scRNA-seq ARI benchmarks like Fig. 3A.

name: vae-gan-neural-network-implementation
description: Use when multi-batch scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., pancreas: 16382 cells, 14 cell types, 9 batches) must be integrated via a contrastive VAE-GAN whose decoder emits batch-corrected outputs in the original gene space.

name: vae-gan-single-cell-generative-modeling
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq for a cohort plus single-cell data for one representative sample and need single-cell-resolution profiles (e.g., .h5ad) for non-sequenced target samples.

name: vae-gan-single-cell-inference-training
description: Use when a cohort has bulk sequencing data for all samples but single-cell data for only a few representatives, and single-cell-resolution profiles must be generated for the remaining target samples.

name: vague-cell-threshold-identification
description: Use when a BAMM-SC clustering run on multi-individual droplet scRNA-seq data (e.g., human PBMC) needs per-cell uncertainty quantification or localization of cells with ambiguous cell-type assignments.

name: validation-set-hyperparameter-tuning
description: Use when comparing multiple penalized high-dimensional regression methods (e.g. suffpcr vs glmnet competitors) so each is tuned identically on held-out validation data before test-set evaluation.

name: variable-feature-selection-in-single-cell-data
description: Use when a normalized and scaled scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. PBMC3k) must be reduced to its most informative genes before running PCA and non-linear 2D/3D embeddings in Seurat or SCALA.

name: variable-gene-selection-benchmarking
description: Use when you need to quantitatively compare feature/gene-selection methods on synthetic scRNA-seq data with known informative genes, e.g. validating an entropy-based selector against HVG, Gini, M3Drop, SCTransform, Fano, or RaceID3 via AUC.

name: variable-gene-selection-scrnaseq
description: Use when preparing a raw single-cell RNA-seq count matrix for zero-inflated or latent-factor dimensionality reduction (ZINB-WaVE, ZIFA, PCA) and you must restrict the feature space to the most informative genes first.

name: variance-based-candidate-gene-ranking
description: Use when a gene expression matrix (DataFrame, e.g. tab-separated GSE text or lab mouse brain SHED vs salt data) needs a stably expressed internal reference gene for normalization and no Python-based screening method has been applied yet.

name: variance-based-permutation-testing-for-dynamic-expression
description: Use when applying DELVE Step 1 to preprocessed single-cell data (e.g. .h5ad of RPE 4i imaging features) to find the subset of dynamically-expressed features that recapitulate cellular trajectories before trajectory inference.

name: variance-explained-correlation-analysis
description: Use when you have scRNAseq data with control genes (e.g. 629 annotated cell-cycle genes on 182 ESCs) plus known per-gene PVE and need to benchmark hidden-factor inference methods by r^2 against true PVE.

name: variance-explained-parameterization
description: Use when constructing simulated scRNAseq count matrices whose confounding and biological latent factors must each explain a specified proportion of variance (PVE) so removal methods can be benchmarked under controlled effect sizes.

name: variance-explained-quantification
description: Use when a JIVE (or similar joint/individual) decomposition has been fitted and you need the proportion of variation explained by joint, individual, and residual components — e.g., to verify two implementations yield equivalent decompositions.

name: variance-explained-quantification
description: Use when PCA on a multi-study microarray or expression matrix is suspected to be dominated by batch (e.g. study of origin) and you must measure variance explained per PC and covariate–PC correlations to confirm removal.

name: variance-stabilizing-feature-selection
description: Use when starting a GapClust rare-cell detection run on a raw scRNA-seq expression matrix loaded into R, and you need to select informative feature genes via variance-stabilising transformation prior to PCA embedding.

name: variance-stabilizing-transformation-of-counts
description: Use when an scRNAseq count matrix is overdispersed relative to the multinomial/Poisson assumption underlying standard CA and you need a variance-stabilized residual matrix (or power-deflated residuals) prior to SVD-based dimension reduction.

name: variance-stabilizing-transformation-of-proportions
description: Use when performing differential proportion analysis (PA) on single-cell cluster proportions (AnnData input) and raw per-cluster counts must be variance-stabilized via logit or arcsin-sqrt before ANOVA/t-test calls, particularly when pseudo-replicates are generated by bootstrapping.

name: variant-allele-frequency-matrix-analysis
description: Use when a cells-by-variants VAF matrix from scRNA-seq variant calling contains missing entries, and the goal is to measure type I expressional drop-out (low expression / shallow coverage) before lineage reconstruction.

name: variant-allele-frequency-purity-proxy
description: Use when analyzing bulk PDAC transcriptomic samples (e.g., the Puleo 2018 FFPE primary cohort in pdacR) and you need a per-sample tumor purity proxy without matched normal sequencing, to validate that a gene signature tracks tumor content.

name: variant-calling-from-scrna-alignment-bam
description: Use when you have a Cell Ranger genome BAM from scRNA-seq data and need de novo SNV genotypes per cell — e.g. to determine host vs donor origin in post-transplant bone marrow samples without a known donor genotype.

name: variant-calling-from-wes-tumor-normal-pairs
description: Use when you have paired tumor/normal WES or WGS FASTQ files and need somatic SNV/INDEL calls as the starting point for downstream neoantigen prediction.

name: variant-calling-quality-filtering
description: Use when possorted_genome_bam and barcodes files from 10x scRNA-seq of a cell mixture must be genotyped and quality-filtered to yield per-cell SNP counts for contributor clustering.

name: variant-coverage-fraction-calculation
description: Use when you have per-gene MRSD scores from MRSDexplorer (.results.mrsd.txt) plus a list of VUS-harboring genes and need the fraction of variants assayable at a given read-depth threshold.

name: variant-flanked-sequence-extraction
description: Use when you have a set of fine-mapped variant positions plus REF/ALT alleles and need allele-specific sequence windows centered on each variant for motif scanning (e.g., FIMO PWM analysis of binding-affinity disruption).

name: variant-of-uncertain-significance-prioritization
description: Use when preparing a ClinVar-derived VUS input set for RNA-seq or MRSD-based analysis of splice-altering variants, or when reproducing the paper's 352,011 -> 185,119 -> 7,507 variant curation workflow.

name: variant-splice-site-interval-intersection
description: Use when sQTL mapping results (e.g. all-tests.nominal.tsv from sqtlseeker2-nf) must be restricted to variants overlapping annotated donor/acceptor splice-site intervals so their effect on splice-site strength can be quantified and compared.

name: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation
description: Use when high-dimensional, sparse, redundant scRNA-seq or proteomics matrices (AnnData-compatible TSV/CSV) must be compressed into a dense low-dimensional latent space before correlation-based network inference.

name: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation
description: Use when building or reproducing an end-to-end marker selection model for single-cell RNA-seq (.h5ad / AnnData) data that must select exactly k genes and support supervised (loss_tradeoff=0), unsupervised (=1), or joint (=0.5) objectives.

name: variational-autoencoder-architecture-implementation
description: Use when building a dynamics-based latent-space model of RNA velocity from spliced/unspliced AnnData layers, where lineage-dependent dynamics require a latent regulatory state (zr) with state-dependent conditioning h.

name: variational-autoencoder-cell-embedding
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data has been preprocessed into an AnnData object and you need low-dimensional cell embeddings plus cluster labels without knowing the number of clusters in advance.

name: variational-autoencoder-clustering
description: Use when clustering a raw single-cell gene expression matrix (AnnData) and the number of cell types is unknown, or when benchmarking against methods that require K.

name: variational-autoencoder-dimension-reduction
description: Use when raw single-cell UMI/expression matrices (e.g. 10x Genomics PBMC3k, ~2700 cells with high dropout rate) need nonlinear 2D embedding to separate cell types or resolve rare sub-populations like FCGR3A+ vs CD14+ monocytes.

name: variational-autoencoder-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when clustering single-cell RNA-seq data (tens of thousands of genes per cell) where dropout noise and high dimensionality make direct clustering unreliable, and a compressed latent cell representation is needed before network-fusion clustering.

name: variational-autoencoder-embedding-of-omics-matrices
description: Use when the input is a large, sparse, redundant omics matrix (scRNA-seq tsv/csv or AnnData, >0.5 million conditions/cells, or bulk proteomics) and the goal is protein functional association network inference that outperforms Pearson correlation.

name: variational-autoencoder-gene-expression-augmentation
description: Use when training a spatial location recovery model on Visium-type ST data and the training sample is limited or the scRNA-seq query data is noisy, so synthetic ST replicates are needed to augment the training set.

name: variational-autoencoder-implementation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq matrix (rows = cells, columns = genes) has already been filtered by the non-negative kernel autoencoder and a low-dimensional compressed embedding is needed for clustering, visualization, classification, or pseudo-time inference.

name: variational-autoencoder-joint-embedding
description: Use when you have paired RNA + ADT (CITE-Seq/TEA-Seq) counts and want a joint low-dimensional embedding from which to cluster cells, or when benchmarking decision-level integrators (scTriangulate) against data-level VAE-based joint embedding.

name: variational-autoencoder-latent-dynamics-inference
description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData with spliced/unspliced layers exhibits multi-lineage or transient dynamics (bifurcation, trifurcation) where linear velocity models fail, and latent-space velocities or trajectories are needed.

name: variational-autoencoder-latent-embedding-learning
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices from multiple batches (e.g., pancreas 16,382 cells, immune 33,506 cells, heart atlas 486,134 cells) need batch-corrected latent embeddings for atlas-level or cross-species integration.

name: variational-autoencoder-latent-sampling
description: Use when a generative model must select a discrete subset of k genes (or features) during training and the selection must remain differentiable — e.g., scRNA-seq AnnData in adata.X with cell-type labels in adata.obs['annotation'].

name: variational-autoencoder-latent-sampling
description: Use when generating synthetic scRNA-seq count matrices from a trained scVI model while avoiding the posterior-sampling bias that amplifies artifacts of small pilot datasets.

name: variational-autoencoder-latent-space-correlation
description: Use when you have a high-dimensional scRNA-seq or proteomics expression matrix (e.g. tsv/csv of gene x condition values, AnnData-compatible) and need a ranked protein-protein association network, especially when simple co-expression on the raw matrix is degraded by sparseness and redundancy.

name: variational-autoencoder-marker-selection
description: Use when scRNA-seq AnnData needs a small informative gene panel: supervised or unsupervised marker selection, cell-type classification from k markers, or full-transcriptome reconstruction quality comparison against baselines like scVI.

name: variational-autoencoder-model-training
description: Use when a raw or preprocessed scRNA-seq expression matrix (e.g. h5/H5-loaded counts from Hemberg-group, Biase, Goolam, Pollen, Yan, or 10x Genomics datasets) must be reduced to a 2D-or-larger latent representation while explicitly modeling technical dropout events.

name: variational-autoencoder-model-training
description: Use when paired (or unpaired) scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq raw count matrices are available and a cross-modality translator must be trained to infer one modality from the other, e.g. for annotation or imputation.

name: variational-autoencoder-pytorch-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing or extending VEGA: you have a Scanpy-wrapped single-cell dataset plus a GMT gene-module file and need a PyTorch VAE whose decoder mirrors user-provided gene modules.

name: variational-autoencoder-snapshot-generation
description: Use when multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT or SHARE-seq/SNARE-seq RNA+ATAC) needs embeddings for unsupervised cell clustering or benchmarking against totalVI, MultiVI, MOFA+, or Jvis-learn.

name: variational-autoencoder-st-data-augmentation
description: Use when training a CeLEry spatial-location model on limited ST training data (e.g., one tissue section) and you need to boost robustness to Gaussian/expression noise in the scRNA-seq test cells, or when the number of training sections is too small for merged-slice training.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when single-cell RNA-seq data with spliced and unspliced count layers (AnnData .h5ad) requires RNA velocity or trajectory inference in scenarios where linear steady-state/dynamical models fail, e.g. multiple lineages, transcriptional boosts, or reprogramming bifurcations.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when selecting a small set of gene markers (e.g. k=50) from scRNA-seq data in AnnData/h5ad form, needing cell-type-informative markers with whole-transcriptome reconstruction via a nonlinear VAE.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when clustering cells from multimodal single-cell omics data (e.g. CITE-seq RNA+ADT feature-by-cell matrices) requires generating multiple latent-space embedding snapshots via variational autoencoders for ensemble consensus clustering.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when you have annotated raw single-cell counts (Seurat .RDS, scanpy .h5ad, or 10x matrix) and must train a new Pollock module from scratch or reproduce the paper's disease-specific/generalized/pan-immune models.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when single-cell expression matrices from paired time points (e.g., BoolODE simulations or metabolic-labeling scRNA-seq) are available and you need to benchmark latent-embedding (VAE) inputs against by-gene neural ODE inputs for forecasting future expression states.

name: variational-autoencoder-training
description: Use when the goal is to infer protein functional association networks from sparse, redundant high-dimensional omics data, or to verify that a FAVA VAE model does not overfit by benchmarking train vs. test splits against KEGG pathway co-membership.

name: variational-bayes-model-fitting
description: Use when fitting a Bayesian trajectory model whose posterior is intractable or multi-modal — e.g. PhenoPath on scRNA-seq with a stimulation covariate — and a fast, scalable approximate posterior is needed instead of MCMC.

name: variational-em-approximate-inference
description: Use when fitting a probabilistic latent-space model (e.g., TCM) to temporal scRNA-seq count matrices with a cell-by-time-point binary time table, especially when exact inference of prototype-based generative models is intractable.

name: variational-generative-model-training-scrna-seq
description: Use when scRNA-seq query data must be projected into a batch-corrected low-dimensional embedding trained on a reference dataset (e.g. h5ad inputs via Cell_BLAST.data), and cell-to-cell similarity must be scored for cell-type querying.

name: variational-inference-convergence-monitoring
description: Use when fitting PhenoPath to single-cell or bulk expression matrices (e.g. log2(TPM+1) TCGA-BRCA data) and you must confirm the variational posterior has converged before extracting interaction effects or trajectories.

name: variational-inference-model-training
description: Use when you have paired single-cell multiomics data as an RNA gene counts CSV and a raw protein ADT counts CSV (rows = cells, columns = genes/ADTs) and need a joint cell embedding that preserves both shared and modality-specific information.

name: variational-inference-posterior-optimization
description: Use when unsupervised circadian phase inference is needed on droplet- or plate-based scRNA-seq data, and the goal is an optimized approximate joint posterior q(theta, beta) with calibrated uncertainty rather than heuristic phase ordering.

name: variational-posterior-parameter-extraction
description: Use when a PhenoPath model fit (e.g. on Shalek et al. dendritic cell LPS/PAM stimulation data) is already trained and you need per-gene interaction effect sizes, posterior SDs, and significance calls.

name: variational-topic-model-training
description: Use when fitting an interpretable topic model to multi-batch single-cell expression data where technical effects (batch, donor, sequencing site) must be disentangled from biological cell states, or when latent cell representations are needed for downstream clustering.

name: vartrix-allele-per-cell-matrix-generation
description: Use when you have a set of pre-called variants (VCF), a Cell Ranger BAM with CB tags, and a cell barcodes file, and need to assign variants to single cells/clusters for malignant-cell identification.

name: vascular-roi-annotation-and-arterial-smc-identification
description: Use when a Visium ST section contains a vascular region of interest and you must assign SMC subtype identity (arterial vs venous) using an unpaired snRNA-seq atlas reference and single-cell-resolution decomposition output.

name: vcf-parsing-and-haplotype-genome-construction
description: Use when performing allele-specific read assignment from RNA-seq FASTQ data: a per-sample VCF genotype directory and a reference FASTA are available and reads must be aligned to both haplotype-modified personal genomes.

name: vcf-provenance-augmentation-and-merging
description: Use when consolidating variant calls from multiple callers/modules in a pipeline (e.g. ScanNeo2's SplAdder, ScanExitron, transIndel, Mutect2, Arriba outputs) into per-variant-type VCFs that must carry caller-provenance INFO keys (GRP, SRC) for source-attributed downstream analysis.

name: vcf-variant-comparison-against-wes-reference
description: Use when a deconvoluted single-cell cluster VCF (e.g. cells_merge_clusters.vcf) must be matched against a WES reference VCF to compute matching-SNP fractions and identification likelihood ratios for each contributor.

name: vcf-variant-filtering
description: Use when you have per-tissue multi-sample VCFs (e.g., GATK HaplotypeCaller g.vcf output merged by tissue) and need to remove low-quality variants, indels, indel-proximate and multiallelic SNPs before ASE or allele-count-based testing.

name: vcf-variant-quality-filtering
description: Use when a raw multi-sample VCF (e.g., from GATK HaplotypeCaller) must be cleaned of low-confidence, indel-proximate, multiallelic, and homozygous calls before per-sample allele-based statistics such as ASE binomial tests.

name: vdj-chain-productivity-filtering
description: Use when a paired scRNA-seq + scVDJ-seq SingleCellExperiment object (e.g. Suo et al. fetal immune atlas with contig data merged via scRepertoire) must be filtered to cells with productive, unambiguous immune receptors before VDJ pseudobulking.

name: vdj-feature-space-trajectory-analysis
description: Use when a SingleCellExperiment with a miloR-pseudobulked VDJ feature space (e.g. pb.milo from vdjPseudobulk, mode_option='abT') needs pseudotime and CD4/CD8 branching probabilities projected back to cells.

name: vdj-gene-usage-pseudobulk-tabulation
description: Use when single-cell VDJ data has been pseudobulked into miloR neighbourhoods and you need a gene-usage feature matrix (VDJ genes x pseudobulks) for downstream PCA/diffusion-map trajectory analysis.

name: vdj-recombination-identification
description: Use when analyzing single-cell T cell scRNA-seq (Smart-Seq FASTQ) and the goal is to detect V(D)J recombination fusions marking MAIT cells that bulk RNA fusion methods miss.

name: vdj-trajectory-inference-cross-language-reproducibility
description: Use when porting a Python-based scVDJ-seq trajectory pipeline (Dandelion/Palantir) to R (dandelionR) and you need to quantify cross-language output concordance via cell counts, Pearson/Kendall correlations, and Lin's CCC.

name: vega-lite-specification-authoring
description: Use when rendering a gene-by-cell-type expression comparison across studies, or when a task requires a declarative vega-lite spec (e.g., dotplot) with size/color channels bound to aggregate statistics derived from an scRNA-seq expression matrix.

name: velocity-directional-coherence-scoring-cbdir-iccoh
description: Use when benchmarking RNA velocity models on multi-batch data and you need to quantify whether inferred velocities remain directionally coherent after batch correction, not just whether cell states are integrated.

name: velocity-metrics-aggregation-across-topologies
description: Use when comparing RNA velocity methods on synthetic dyngen AnnData with ground-truth velocities across multiple developmental topologies and a combined benchmark table is required.

name: velocity-model-refitting-with-fixed-mask
description: Use when you need to test whether inferred transcriptional velocities (e.g., from scKINETICS on raw UMI counts such as GSE207943) are stable under technical noise in gene expression, specifically perturbed transcript capture rates from downsampling.

name: velocity-recovery-benchmarking
description: Use when assessing whether scKINETICS-inferred per-cell velocities and GRNs are stable to user-defined hyperparameter choices (initiating sigma) or perturbation of prior inputs (coexpression matrix A^), before trusting downstream regulator calls.

name: velocity-stream-visualization
description: Use when an AnnData object contains estimated velocities and cell-type labels and you need to visually verify that an inferred trajectory (e.g., OPC→OL maturation, retinal branches PR/RGC/AC-HC, Fev+→Delta transitions) is recovered.

name: velocity-vector-nearest-neighbor-analysis
description: Use when comparing velocity inference methods (e.g. scKINETICS, scVelo, VeloVAE, UniTVelo) on the same single-cell dataset and you need a quantitative, cluster-resolved measure of velocity-field smoothness to show one method's vectors are more locally concordant.

name: velocyto-spliced-unspliced-count-matrix-generation
description: Use when starting from raw single-cell RNA-seq reads (e.g. Burns et al. GSE71982, 157 neonatal mouse inner ear cells) and you need spliced/unspliced count layers for RNA velocity estimation and Cytopath trajectory inference.

name: venn-diagram-overlap-visualization
description: Use when comparing lists of significant features (e.g., ASE SNPs or ASE genes) across two or more tissues or conditions and you need intersection counts, overlap fractions, and Venn diagrams to report shared vs. tissue-specific results.

name: vienna-dot-bracket-fold-parsing
description: Use when a CLASH/qCLASH workflow requires reading predicted secondary-structure data in Vienna (dot-bracket) or CT format, or pairing each fold record with its corresponding hyb record (e.g., to detect hyb/Vienna sequence mismatches before analysis).

name: vienna-fold-annotation-merging
description: Use when a qCLASH/CLASH analysis requires each hyb-format hybrid record to carry its predicted folding pattern (dot-bracket) and energy from a paired Vienna or CT file, e.g. before Fold Analysis of miRNA folding patterns.

name: villani-dendritic-subtype-classification
description: Use when FiRE-scored rare PBMC cells need dendritic sub-type resolution against Villani reference signatures, e.g. when rare-cell clusters must be assigned to DC1/DC3/DC4/DC6 identities.

name: villus-zone-trajectory-visualization
description: Use when spatial scRNA-seq data with prior zone/position labels (e.g., villus zones) must be organized into a coherent linear differentiation trajectory, and PCA/UMAP alone give spatially incoherent orderings of landmark genes.

name: violin-plot-benchmark-visualization
description: Use when benchmarking multiple DA-testing methods on scRNA-Seq data and you need to display the full distribution of DA z-statistics per method/dataset to compare sensitivity.

name: violin-plot-gene-expression-visualization
description: Use when you have an annotated single-cell RNA-seq object (e.g. Seurat with cell-type labels) and need to determine which cell subsets show differential expression of specific marker genes.

name: violin-plot-gene-expression-visualization
description: Use when you need to visually confirm that specific genes (e.g., DEFA1/DEFA3) are expressed exclusively in one subset of cells grouped by a metadata variable such as tissue, after a pathway or differential analysis flags them.

name: violin-plot-visualization-of-stage-distributions
description: Use when you need to visually assess whether one marker gene's expression distribution discriminates cell cycle stages in single-cell RNA-seq data (overlapping violins = insufficient marker).

name: viral-biomass-objective-integration
description: Use when building infected-host metabolic models that must carry a viral biomass reaction (e.g. for FBA-based viral essentiality or drug repositioning), starting from a generic reconstruction plus a published VBOF.

name: viral-biomass-objective-knockout-scoring
description: Use when you have infected context-specific genome-scale metabolic models with a VBOF (e.g. SARS-CoV-2 lung models) and need to enumerate essential genes or synergistic gene pairs as drug-target candidates.

name: viral-infection-t-cell-subtype-composition-analysis
description: Use when scRNA-seq data of virus-specific T cells (e.g. P14 cells from LCMV chronic infection under perturbations like CD4 T cell depletion) must be assigned to reference subtypes (SLEC, Tpex, Tex) and their composition compared between conditions.

name: viral-read-classification-model-training
description: Use when building or retraining an alignment-free viral-read classifier on fixed-length RNA-seq fragments (e.g., 48 bp), or when all models must be retrained on identical training fragments for a fair comparison on a shared test set.

name: viral-read-contig-assembly
description: Use when unmapped RNA-seq reads (48 bp fragments in *_unmapped.fastq) have been scored by the viRNAtrap TensorFlow model and predicted viral reads must be extended into contigs for downstream viral identification.

name: viral-read-discrimination
description: Use when unmapped RNAseq reads must be classified as viral vs. human without alignment, or when predicted viral contigs need to be assembled from deep learning model scores.

name: viral-reference-genome-preparation
description: Use when running scPathoQuant on 10x cellranger output and a pathogen (e.g. HIV, SARS-CoV-2, metapneumovirus) reference genome must be packaged into the -p2genome folder with clean FASTA headers.

name: vireosnp-clonal-assignment
description: Use when a SNP-by-cell AD/DP mtDNA matrix (from cellsnp-lite/cellSNP) has been filtered by MQuad and you need per-cell clone labels from mitochondrial variants.

name: virtual-tumor-in-silico-gene-perturbation
description: Use when benchmarking cell-cycle removal methods on scRNA-seq data where no true mixed-subclone tumor sample exists, by simulating perturbed gene expression in mESC cells and measuring subclone delineation accuracy.

name: virus-read-classification-from-rnaseq
description: Use when you have RNA-seq reads already unmapped to hg19/phiX (as *_unmapped.fastq files) and need to detect expressed viruses, including divergent ones missed by alignment-based methods, across tumor samples such as TCGA cancer types.

name: visium-count-matrix-normalization
description: Use when raw 10x Visium spot count matrices must be normalized prior to Cancer-Finder infer.py inference with an ST checkpoint, or when reproducing the paper's 82.00–97.37% per-slide spot-annotation accuracies.

name: visium-dlpfc-data-processing
description: Use when input is a Visium spatial transcriptomics dataset (e.g. Visium_humanDLPFC from STexampleData) loaded as a SpatialExperiment, and gene filtering/normalization is needed before running nnSVG.

name: visium-h5-preprocessing-highly-variable-genes
description: Use when you have a Space Ranger output directory with a filtered_feature_bc_matrix.h5 and spatial/ folder for a Visium sample (e.g. bcdc_ffpe) and need PCA-transformed spot data plus an automated scribble before running ScribbleDom.

name: visium-spatial-expression-visualization
description: Use when Visium spatial transcriptomics data with spot-level counts and 2D coordinates is available and you need to find and visualize gene sets/pathways whose module-score activity is non-randomly distributed across tissue spots.

name: visium-spot-data-preprocessing
description: Use when preparing a 10x Visium slice (e.g. the 2518-spot, 17,943-gene human breast cancer slice) and a scRNA-seq reference so that both are normalized, scaled, and share 2000 common HVGs before coupled-VAE/Minibatch-UOT integration.

name: visualization-method-benchmarking
description: Use when comparing dimension-reduction/visualization methods (e.g. scDHA.vis vs PCA, t-SNE, UMAP, SCANPY) on scRNA-seq data where cell-type labels are available to quantify embedding quality.

name: vitellogenin-ortholog-identification
description: Use when an EcoOmicsDB ortholog group (like vitellogenin s2f_0005567) aggregates too many genes to yield gene-level insights and must be subdivided into clusters before downstream annotation or expression analysis.

name: vmf-distribution-sampling
description: Use when reimplementing or verifying scPhere's hyperspherical VAE: you need vMF posterior sampling, the closed-form vMF-vs-uniform-sphere KL, or the NB observation model with softmax means.
