name: vmf-vae-spherical-embedding-of-scrnaseq
description: Use when embedding very large, sparse droplet scRNA-seq UMI count matrices (e.g., RGC ~35,699 cells or HCL ~599,926 cells) where a normal-prior VAE or 2D t-SNE/UMAP crowds cells and distorts hierarchical global structure.

name: volcano-plot-gene-set-reproduction
description: Use when a publication reports a volcano-plot-style set of up/down-regulated genes within specific cell clusters (e.g. COVID vs healthy in Macrophage clusters 3, 5, 12) and the goal is to regenerate that exact gene list with direction labels.

name: volcano-plot-generation
description: Use when you need per-gene log2 fold change and adjusted p-values for a two-cohort comparison (A vs B) from a pdacR-style parsed dataset, and a volcano plot visualizing differential expression with gene-set members labeled.

name: volcano-plot-visualization
description: Use when you have a two-group differential expression table (gene, log2FC, p-value, adjusted p-value) — e.g. Seurat FindMarkers output between mtDNA-defined subclones — and need to visualize which genes are both significant and large-effect.

name: volcano-plot-visualization-of-differential-activity
description: Use when VEGA's Bayesian differential module activity test yields per-module log_e(Bayes Factor) values for a two-condition single-cell comparison and you need to visualize and flag significantly activated gene modules.

name: volcano-plot-visualization-of-differential-methylation
description: Use when you already have a differential methylation (DMC) results table from Illumina 450K/EPIC array analysis and need to visualize and extract significant CpGs by adjusted-P and logFC thresholds.

name: von-mises-fisher-spherical-latent-modeling
description: Use when scRNA-seq count matrices must be embedded on a hypersphere to avoid Gaussian-VAE cell crowding, corrected for multilevel batch factors (e.g., 30 patients x 3 disease statuses x 2 locations), or mapped from unseen individuals.

name: voom-differential-expression-analysis
description: Use when gene-level RNA-seq read counts (featureCounts output for the Prensner PCa cohort) need cancer-vs-normal DE testing with voom and conversion to log2(Pvalue)×(-10)×regulation values for FunHoP KEGG node scoring.

name: voronoi-rexel-parcellization
description: Use when you have spatial single-cell data (e.g. MERFISH cell-by-gene matrix with (dims x cells) coordinates) and need cell-grouped spatial units for distribution-level segmentation such as LDS.

name: voronoi-tessellation-nuclei-seeded-segmentation
description: Use when a quick, membrane-agnostic whole-cell segmentation baseline from nuclei seeds is needed on multiplexed immunofluorescence or MIBI tissue images, especially to benchmark against membrane-aware segmenters or to quantify undersegmentation in crowded epithelia.

name: vote-threshold-classifier-tuning
description: Use when combining results of multiple DEG detection methods (DESeq2, limma, NOISeq) in ExpHunter Suite and needing to select an optimal vote-threshold cut-off for robust DEG calling, benchmarked against known ground truth.

name: voting-classifier-ensemble-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking whether a stacked ensemble outperforms majority-vote aggregation over combinations of base classifiers (SVM, XGBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTree, GBDT) under 10-fold cross-validation.

name: vst-variable-gene-selection
description: Use when building a Symphony reference from scRNA-seq count/expression matrices (e.g., pbmcs_exprs_small) and you need a shared variable-gene panel before scaling, PCA, and Harmony integration.

name: wald-test-differential-expression
description: Use when you have fitted per-gene Tweedie-family GLMs (CPLM or ZICP) to scRNA-seq count data and need coefficient-level significance testing with multiplicity adjustment to call differentially expressed genes.

name: wald-test-gene-cluster-differentiation
description: Use when you have PILOT pseudotime plus robust-regression fits of gene expression per cell cluster (from pl.tl.genes_importance) and need to rank genes with cluster-specific trajectories, e.g. genes dropping only in healthy cardiomyocytes.

name: wald-test-inference
description: Use when a fitted Compound Poisson (CPLM) or zero-inflated Compound Poisson (ZICP) model needs per-gene or per-feature H0: beta_g = 0 testing with p-values, q-values, and DE calls in a two-group design.

name: walktrap-graph-clustering-of-perturbation-profiles
description: Use when you have a perturbation-by-gene matrix of zdWUI z-scores (or analogous effect-size profiles) and need to group perturbations that cause similar patterns of 3'UTR shortening or lengthening across response genes.

name: wall-clock-runtime-measurement
description: Use when quantifying the computational cost or parallel speedup of nested cross-validation (default 10 x 10 outer/inner folds) on high-dimensional datasets, e.g. RNA-Seq matrices with P >> n where full nested CV is expensive.

name: wall-clock-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational cost (wall-clock minutes) of cell-cell communication inference tools on the same scRNA-seq input, e.g. justifying dsCellNet's efficiency on 10,000-cell developmental datasets.

name: wall-clock-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing computational efficiency of lineage reconstruction methods across dataset sizes, e.g. timing LinRace vs LinTIMaT on simulated barcode-expression data of 1024 and 2048 cells.

name: wall-clock-runtime-profiling
description: Use when comparing the computational cost of pareg versus standard enrichment methods, or when deciding whether pareg's ~30-minute parallelized runtime is acceptable for a given enrichment analysis.

name: wall-clock-speedup-analysis
description: Use when a FrameD fault-injection pipeline configuration (e.g. RS(9,47) code, 25x read depth, 10% fault rate, 368 simulations) must be benchmarked from 1 core to many MPI ranks to demonstrate scalability.

name: wall-clock-time-and-memory-profiling
description: Use when comparing the computational cost (runtime and peak memory) of two or more pipelines on the same input files, e.g. benchmarking SoloTE vs scTE on simulated scRNA-Seq BAMs.

name: wall-clock-timing-measurement
description: Use when benchmarking the computational cost of imputation pipelines on scRNA-seq matrices, e.g. timing SERM against baselines on the 12162x2422 observed matrix (data_observed_10perc.mat) or large HCL/MCA datasets.

name: wall-clock-timing-measurement
description: Use when comparing computational scalability of scRNAseq dimension reduction methods (e.g., CA via corral vs glmPCA) and you need reproducible per-dataset wall-clock timings on standardized count matrices.

name: wallclock-and-memory-profiling-of-pipelines
description: Use when comparing multiple cell type annotation pipelines for a benchmark table and you must report, per pipeline, prediction accuracy together with wall-clock execution time and maximum memory usage under fixed hardware (e.g. 12GB GPU / 128GB RAM / 8 CPU VM).

name: ward-hierarchical-clustering-of-cell-type-profiles
description: Use when building a custom Census cell-type annotation model from a scRNA-seq reference (e.g., Tabula Sapiens) and you need a biologically intuitive cell-type hierarchy to organize the per-node xgboost classifiers.

name: wasserstein-metric-evaluation-of-simulated-populations
description: Use when a generative model simulates a held-out intermediate timepoint of a scRNA-seq time series (e.g., PRESCIENT day-4 rollforward from day 2) and you must quantify recovery of the true marginal population.

name: watershed-segmentation-replacement
description: Use when multiplexed tissue images contain columnar epithelial cells whose watershed segmentation is fragmented by internal (aberrant) membrane segments, and cell objects must be remerged/split per MIRIAM's resegmentation logic.

name: weakened-marker-kernel-robustness-testing
description: Use when you must quantify robustness of a signal-filtering or integration method to weakened prior knowledge — e.g., testing whether replacing marker genes in a cell cycle/sex kernel destabilizes iLISI-based filtering quality.

name: weighted-adamic-adar-similarity-imputation
description: Use when a sparse cell-to-cell similarity matrix learned from scRNA-seq data (e.g., via sparse subspace representation) has zero/missing entries that must be imputed before spectral clustering of cell types.

name: weighted-binarized-gene-set-scoring
description: Use when scoring single-cell or spatial-transcriptomics data (AnnData/scanpy) against SenePy senescence hub signatures, e.g. to flag senescent spots in Visium myocardial-infarction sections using mouse heart hub signatures.

name: weighted-co-expression-graph-construction
description: Use when building a fixed transcriptional module repertoire from multiple blood transcriptome cohorts: you have several GEO expression matrices and need a co-clustering-derived weighted graph to segment transcripts into modules.

name: weighted-cross-entropy-classifier-warmup
description: Use when reconstructing scBridge's heterogeneous transfer loop: annotated scRNA-seq (.h5ad, obs['CellType']) plus unlabeled scATAC-seq activity matrix must first be fitted by a supervised encoder/classifier before GMM reliability estimation and prototype alignment.

name: weighted-density-spatial-kld-testing
description: Use when spatial transcriptomics data with spatial coordinates is available and you must decide whether a gene set/pathway shows spatial organization beyond chance, rather than just cell-type enrichment.

name: weighted-dominating-set-optimization
description: Use when you have paired expression matrices (e.g., TCGA tumor vs normal) as a differential co-expression network and need to identify key driver nodes of transcriptome programs.

name: weighted-f1-benchmark-comparison
description: Use when benchmarking single-cell label-transfer/integration methods on query datasets with weighted F1, e.g. reproducing Fig. 6b-e pancreas comparisons (scCobra 0.95, SCALEX 0.95, TOSICA 0.94, scVI 0.92).

name: weighted-geometric-mean-aggregation
description: Use when qPCR CT data contain two or more internal controls (e.g. RNU48, hsa-miR-16-5p) that must be combined into one normalization reference, or when the unweighted geometric mean of reference genes fails to yield stable target normalization (e.g. non-significant ΔΔCT results).

name: weighted-kde-spatial-relevance-testing
description: Use when analyzing 10X Visium spatial transcriptomics data to test whether curated gene sets/pathways follow anatomical or high-order spatial patterns, without clustering spots.

name: weighted-knn-imputation-of-as-probability-matrices
description: Use when a single-cell scRNA-seq-derived AS probability matrix (per-site PSI-like values from Leafcutter junction reads) contains NA dropouts that must be filled before unsupervised cell clustering.

name: weighted-knn-missing-value-imputation
description: Use when a single-cell AS probability matrix (rows = AS sites, columns = cells) contains NA entries from dropouts and the values must be recovered before spectral clustering, or when imputation fidelity under forced dropout must be quantified.

name: weighted-marker-aggregation
description: Use when a query scRNA-seq dataset in AnnData format must be scored against a ranked cell-type marker list from a reference (e.g., MASI reference data) to produce per-cell cell-type scores and labels for downstream annotation.

name: weighted-nearest-neighbor-multimodal-clustering
description: Use when a droplet-based single-cell experiment (CITE-seq, ASAP-seq, TEA-seq) has paired mRNA and ADT matrices and you need joint clustering to test whether a protein normalization method (e.g., dsb vs CLR) resolves a specific cell population.

name: weighted-network-aggregation-thresholding
description: Use when a NeuronChat run has produced per-interaction communication networks (x@net) and you need one aggregated cell-group connectivity matrix, e.g. to benchmark predicted connectivity against retrograde-tracing labels.

name: weighted-network-edge-percentile-thresholding
description: Use when you have edge-weighted undirected co-expression networks (e.g. Euclidean distance or Pearson correlation based) that are too dense for downstream fusion or community detection and need data-driven edge pruning.

name: weighted-nonnegative-least-squares-deconvolution
description: Use when estimating cell type proportions in bulk RNA-seq from a multi-subject scRNA-seq reference, especially when closely related cell types cause collinearity and methods like CIBERSORT or BSEQ-sc lack power to resolve them.

name: weighted-overlap-colocalization-measure
description: Use when testing association between transcriptome region sets where the query features lack clear isoform association (e.g. miCLIP-seq m6A sites) and isoform-derived regions such as stop codons, and you need a TxIA-aware weighted overlap statistic rather than a raw genomic overlap count.

name: weighted-principal-component-analysis
description: Use when bulk expression samples must be decomposed into cell-type relative abundances but no single-cell reference profile is available—only marker genes with per-gene weights (e.g., log fold-change) per cell type.

name: weighted-random-cell-subsampling
description: Use when benchmarking clustering or dimensionality reduction tools needs datasets with known cell-type composition, by subsampling pre-sorted cells (e.g., Zheng mixtures) at controlled cluster sizes and ratios.

name: weighted-utr-isoform-usage-analysis
description: Use when scUTRquant SingleCellExperiment outputs (gene + 3'UTR isoform count matrices) cover multi-UTR genes across two or more cell types or perturbations and differentially used/lengthened 3' ends must be called and compared to DGE gene sets.

name: weighted-vs-unweighted-artifact-comparison-visualization
description: Use when metacell-level (rather than single-cell-level) differential expression, differential abundance, or dimensionality reduction is planned and metacells have unequal sizes, to quantify and visualize the type I/II errors introduced by disregarding metacell size weights.

name: welch-t-test-asynchrony-comparison
description: Use when comparing whether peak-gene pairs ranked by a Granger-causal method show significantly longer chromatin-to-expression pseudotime lags than pairs ranked by Pearson or pseudocell correlation.

name: welch-t-test-cell-proportion-testing
description: Use when PILOT's Wasserstein-distance-based Leiden clustering has assigned patient samples to clusters (e.g., the PDAC 11 control / 14 Tumor 1 / 10 Tumor 2 split) and you need to test which cell-type proportions differ between clusters.

name: welch-t-test-de-testing
description: Use when a clustered single-cell RNA-seq AnnData object needs a per-cluster DE profile to assign a cell type, e.g. testing one Leiden cluster against the rest before GO/KEGG/MSigDB enrichment.

name: welch-t-test-differential-expression
description: Use when each cell in a single-cell dataset (scRNA-seq or a scATAC-seq cell-by-gene activity matrix) already has cluster labels and you must identify marker genes per cluster via one-vs-rest testing, ranked by fold-change for marker or enrichment analysis.

name: welch-two-sample-t-testing
description: Use when cells have been assigned intact or mutant gRNAs by GiRAFR and you need to test whether mutant gRNA cells fail to downregulate their target genes relative to intact gRNA cells.

name: wes-vs-wgs-signature-concordance-evaluation
description: Use when paired WGS and WES SNV catalogs exist for the same samples and you need to test whether exome capture regions distort COSMIC v3.1 signature contributions (e.g. non-coding signatures like SBS9 or flat signatures like SBS-MM1) before reporting WES-based fits.

name: wes-wgs-read-based-genotyping
description: Use when a tumor-normal WES/WGS pipeline needs patient HLA class I typing from sequencing reads (not clinical HLA reports) so that pMHC binding/immunogenicity prediction can be restricted to the patient's own HLA alleles.

name: wgcna-co-expression-module-detection
description: Use when you have an RNA-seq table of counts plus sample phenotype metadata (e.g., mutant/wild-type Lafora disease samples) and want to find co-expressed gene groups (CEGs) that correlate with phenotypic data.

name: wgcna-co-expression-module-detection
description: Use when input is a processed single-cell expression matrix with cell-level metadata and the goal is to infer co-expression modules and identify which modules track a trait such as patient survival status.

name: wgcna-coexpression-network-inference
description: Use when the input is a preprocessed single-cell expression matrix (e.g. .h5ad/HDF5/loom) with cell metadata and the goal is to infer gene co-expression modules and hubs for specific cell types or conditions.

name: wgcna-gene-module-detection
description: Use when a cell-type-specific co-expression matrix (e.g., from CS-CORE or diff_CSCORE) needs to be partitioned into co-expressed gene modules for downstream GO enrichment of disease-relevant pathways.

name: wgcna-module-detection
description: Use when you have a bulk RNA-seq count matrix across many samples (e.g. 38 female hippocampus 3xTg-AD/WT samples) and need to find co-expressed gene modules and correlate them with external traits.

name: wgcna-module-trait-association-testing
description: Use when a PyWGCNA co-expression network has already been built and you need module–trait correlations (e.g., module eigengene vs. genotype or age/time point) plus GO/KEGG/REACTOME enrichment of the correlated module.

name: wgs-read-quality-trimming
description: Use when raw tumor-normal WES/WGS FASTQ reads are about to be mapped to a reference genome (GRCh37/GRCh38) and adapter or low-quality artifacts must be removed first.

name: wgsim-read-simulation-coverage-scaling
description: Use when constructing synthetic benchmark RNA-seq datasets with known fusion transcripts at graded expression/coverage levels, or when evaluating fusion-detection sensitivity across low-to-high sequencing depth.

name: wheat-microrna-precursor-subgenome-assignment
description: Use when you have a curated list of wheat (Triticum aestivum) miRNA precursors with genomic coordinates and need to quantify their A/B/D subgenome distribution and homologous-group (triad) structure.

name: white-adipose-tissue-reference-atlas-construction
description: Use when multiple independent white adipose tissue (or comparable multi-donor tissue) scRNA-seq datasets must be uniformly annotated and integrated into a single reference atlas with cell type/state labels.

name: whitelist-filtering-of-cellular-barcodes
description: Use when you have noisy long-read single-cell RNA-seq data with discovered cellular barcodes and a short-read-derived whitelist, and need to filter against the whitelist and remove empty droplets.

name: whole-genome-duplication-warning
description: Use when running XClone's combine module on merged RDR and BAF results from scRNA-seq data and you need to check whether allele-specific CNA patterns (e.g., widespread LOH plus copy gains) indicate whole-genome duplication.

name: wide-to-tall-dataframe-reshaping
description: Use when a wide-format scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes, .csv) must be converted into a Spark-optimized tall (cell, gene, count) format before downstream filtering or normalization.

name: wilcoxon-differential-expression-marker-selection
description: Use when you need cell-type-specific marker gene sets from scRNA-seq cluster data — e.g., ten highly specific plus ten low-specificity markers per cell type via Wilcoxon rank-sum — as input to ScType gene_sets_prepare/sctype_score.

name: wilcoxon-differential-signaling-gene-testing
description: Use when preparing scRNA-seq data for CellChat communication inference: clustered cell groups exist and over-expressed signaling genes must be identified before computing ligand-receptor communication probabilities.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-association-testing
description: Use when bulk tumor expression profiles have been projected through a single-cell-trained Miscell encoder (moco-dim 64) and you must test each latent feature for responder-vs-non-responder differences in an ICB cohort, or generally when comparing two patient groups on non-normal feature scores.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-cluster-comparison
description: Use when a processed Seurat scRNA-seq object with cluster/subcluster labels (e.g. PBMC3k) needs a cluster-specific marker gene list, and genes shared with background clusters must be excluded.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-deg-testing
description: Use when you need cluster-level DEGs from a single-dataset scRNA-seq Seurat object and want per-gene discrimination metrics (AUC, sensitivity, specificity), e.g. to benchmark a binary marker method like CDI against a standard Wilcoxon baseline.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-differential-expression-testing
description: Use when a scRNA-seq cell population has been binarized by pathway activity (e.g., GSDensity compute.cell.label PAL labels) and you must test whether a gene of interest is differentially expressed between the pathway-positive and pathway-negative cells.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-gene-screening
description: Use when you have per-spot/per-cell normalized spatial transcriptomics expression with assigned spatial-domain labels and need domain-enriched genes or SVG candidates, e.g. recovering DLPFC cortical-layer SVGs.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
description: Use when comparing a continuous per-region metric (e.g. novel/structured RNA fraction of dsRID-predicted dsRNA regions) between two independent sample groups such as AD and control brain, without assuming normality.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-group-comparison
description: Use when you have a per-sample table with a binary viral-status grouping (e.g., IIV31-positive vs -negative from Source Data file 4) and continuous per-sample quantities (TMB, CNA burden, immune fractions) whose between-group differences must be tested without distributional assumptions.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-marker-testing
description: Use when you need a clustering-based DEG baseline for benchmarking: cells can be clustered into biologically meaningful groups and per-cluster marker genes (e.g. via FindAllMarkers) must be ranked by p-value to compare against an alternative method.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-multiple-testing-correction
description: Use when you need to derive a robust, pan-dataset malignant-vs-non-malignant marker gene feature set by intersecting statistically significant DEGs across multiple annotated cancer scRNA-seq training datasets.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-comparison
description: Use when comparing two methods' distributions of per-run statistical significance (e.g. DA-test P-values over 100 simulation replicates) and you need a non-parametric rank-based test of whether one method attains systematically smaller P-values.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-significance-testing
description: Use when you have per-pair predicted scores (e.g. DeepHLApan binding/immunogenicity scores) plus binary experimental labels and must test whether the scores separate the labeled groups non-parametrically.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-stage-comparison
description: Use when per-cell NFE (or similar potency) scores have been computed for cells grouped into developmental stages and you need a non-parametric statistical test of whether earlier-stage cells are systematically more potent than mature-stage cells.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when comparing two independent score or expression distributions without distributional assumptions — e.g., testing whether 800-gene-set AUROCs exceed 100-gene-set AUROCs, or identifying marker genes by comparing subtype cells against all other interneurons within one study.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing
description: Use when identifying per-cluster marker genes from a clustered single-cell RNA-seq matrix prior to cell type annotation, and when avoiding pseudo marker genes that are upregulated in multiple clusters.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-of-cell-proportions
description: Use when you have per-cell state labels from a single-cell classifier (e.g. TILPRED on GSE120575 CD8 T cells) paired pre/post treatment across a handful of patients, and need a p-value for state-proportion shifts between responder and non-responder groups.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-testing-of-tissue-type-expression
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq or microarray samples from multiple pancreatic compartments (normal pancreas, primary PDAC, PDX, CAF lines, metastasis) and need to test which tissue types drive a curated gene signature's expression.

name: wilcoxon-rank-sum-two-group-testing
description: Use when a single-cell gene expression matrix has cells split into exactly two user-defined groups and in-session differential expression markers are needed to order a heatmap.

name: wilcoxon-ranked-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing clustering quality between two or more single-cell clustering solutions — e.g., per-cell silhouette scores from SCISSORS, Seurat, SAFE, or GiniClust3 — and you need paired significance testing on the score distributions.

name: wilcoxon-ranksum-per-cluster-deg-calling
description: Use when you have a gene expression matrix plus scBGEDA cluster assignments (e.g. the QS_Heart dataset) and need to nominate per-cluster marker genes for cell-type annotation via known marker databases.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-hypothesis-testing
description: Use when two paired measurements were taken on the same samples (e.g., silhouette widths in deep-feature space vs. the 273-gene CMS signature space) and you must test whether one representation is significantly more compact/separated than the other without assuming normality.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing
description: Use when two methods are each evaluated on the same paired set of datasets (e.g., 44 atlas-scale normal/cancer tissues with per-dataset F1, balanced accuracy, or overall accuracy) and a nonparametric significance test of the metric differences is required.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-paired-testing
description: Use when two paired measurements over the same items (e.g., CIEDE2000 color differences per adjacent cell-type pair under two palettes) must be compared without assuming normality, and a one-sided ity claim is needed.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing paired per-replicate runtime (or other paired measurement) values across methods — e.g. three replicate subsamples per tool — and you need a distribution-free significance call without assuming normality.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when two or more classifiers have been run on the identical reference and validation datasets and per-sample (paired) performance scores exist, and you must test whether the performance gap for one class (e.g., cancer-cell F1) is significant.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-significance-testing
description: Use when comparing two methods' per-sample performance metrics (e.g., CCC/Pearson/RMSE over the same 124 pseudobulk samples) and a paired, one-sided significance assessment of whether one method outperforms the other is required.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-test-reproduction
description: Use when reproducing the decoupleR perturbation-benchmark weights ablation, i.e. when paired per-method with-weights vs without-weights perturbed-regulator recovery scores are available and a one-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test must be run on the paired deltas.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when per-event predictions from CLOUDe (classifications and theta1, theta2, log10(sigmaSq/(2*alpha)) values) must be statistically compared across deletion classes or against simulated expression distributions.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when you have paired perturbed/unperturbed expression samples from matched cells (e.g., GRouNdGAN knockout vs control) and need per-edge significance of TF-gene regulation with multiple-testing correction.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when comparing a paired metric (e.g., recall of GTEx eQTL-supported enhancer-gene pairs) between two scoring methods measured on the same small set of units (four heart cell types plus K562) and a non-parametric paired significance test is needed.

name: wilcoxon-signed-rank-testing
description: Use when comparing two methods evaluated on the same set of benchmark datasets and you need a paired, non-parametric significance test on per-dataset scores (e.g. mean ARIs of scISR 0.571 vs raw 0.504, MAGIC 0.461, scImpute 0.286, SAVER 0.423, scScope 0.165, scGNN 0.279).

name: winning-fraction-cluster-pruning
description: Use when scTriangulate has produced per-cell winning annotations and raw winning clusters need filtering by winning fraction (win_fraction_cutoff) or minimum size (abs_thresh) before downstream analysis.

name: within-batch-versus-cross-batch-evaluation-design
description: Use when benchmarking perturbation-prediction methods on multi-batch scRNA-seq data where the held-out matrix may differ in batch from the input, and you must separate condition-only accuracy from condition+batch accuracy.

name: within-cell-type-scatter-visualization
description: Use when benchmarking protein imputation methods (cTP-net vs Seurat v3 anchor transfer) on CITE-seq PBMC data and you need per-cell-type visual comparison of predicted vs measured ADT levels, e.g. reproducing Fig. 2b-c.

name: within-class-mean-averaging-across-cohorts
description: Use when building a predefined external gene-by-subtype centroid reference for PAM50-style classification of RNA-seq breast cancer samples, and you need the reference to be independent of the arbitrary composition of the training cohort.

name: within-cluster-variance-penalty-computation
description: Use when one or more candidate spatial-domain clusterings of ST/Visium spots (e.g., Mclust automated scribbles or ScribbleDom model outputs over an alpha_options grid) must be ranked by a single scalar score in the absence of ground-truth labels for ARI.

name: wnt-pathway-overrepresentation-enrichment
description: Use when upregulated genes from a clone-versus-normal differential expression comparison (e.g., Clone 1 vs Normal in XClone-annotated TNBC1 scRNA-seq data) need to be tested for significant Wnt-pathway over-representation via an over-representation test.

name: workflow-manifest-validation-and-execution
description: Use when a multi-step single-cell processing pipeline (splici/spliceu reference construction, piscem indexing, mapping, permit-list generation, collate, quant) must be declared as a validated JSON manifest and executed end-to-end rather than run as ad-hoc commands.

name: workflow-template-retrieval-from-registry
description: Use when a user needs to reproduce or run a configurable alevin-fry single-cell processing pipeline end-to-end and prefers a curated, versioned workflow template over hand-composing simpleaf/alevin-fry/piscem commands.

name: worm-embryo-dataset-handling
description: Use when the input is the CEED (GSE126954) C. elegans single-cell embryogenesis dataset (or another time-series worm scRNA-seq matrix) and the goal is to identify time-varying differential genes and cell subclusters with scTITANS.

name: xenium-data-preprocessing
description: Use when you have a raw Xenium output bundle (transcripts.csv.gz and morphology_mip.ome.tif) and need to generate BIDCell training inputs (nuclei segmentation, expression maps, patches, cell-gene matrix) before model training.

name: xenograft-artifact-gene-filtering
description: Use when building CMS subtype prediction templates for cell lines, organoids or PDXs, where original CMS markers driven by immune/stromal expression fail to classify CMS1/CMS4 groups.

name: xgboost-classifier-training
description: Use when labeled mRNA+CDS and lncRNA FASTA training sets (human, mouse, or a model organism) are available and a binary coding-potential classifier must be trained and serialized for LncDC-style prediction.

name: xgboost-classifier-training
description: Use when scRNA-seq tumor data lacks internal confidential reference malignant cells and cells must be labeled malignant vs nonMalignant, or when comparing XGBoost, ElasticNet, and neural network classifiers on gene-expression features.

name: xgboost-model-prediction
description: Use when RNA transcript sequences are in FASTA format and you need binary lncRNA vs mRNA classification with an alignment-free XGBoost model, including ablation conditions (full features vs SIF+PF only vs SSF-only).

name: xgmml-network-export-and-cytoscape-visualization
description: Use when a runmodule result (global or local RNC) needs to be persisted as a network file and visually inspected; trigger on any detected module object that must be shared, visualized, or validated in Cytoscape.

name: xor-basis-cosine-statistic-computation
description: Use when the goal is to detect subtype-downregulated genes (SDG) from batch-corrected gene-by-sample expression data — i.e., genes with near-zero mean expression in exactly one subtype and elevated expression in every other subtype.

name: xy-coordinate-imaging-data-processing
description: Use when the input is a CODEX-exported .csv (or similar) containing x and y coordinates of cells from rolled intestinal tissue and the goal is to map the spiral onto a linear proximal–distal / serosa–luminal axis.

name: yaml-config-driven-pipeline-parameterization
description: Use when adapting or re-running a scdrake scRNA-seq/SRT pipeline run for new parameters or cell groupings — e.g. changing a MAD threshold, restricting DRAKE_TARGETS, or setting CONTRASTS_SOURCES in contrasts.yaml.

name: yaml-pipeline-configuration-for-segmentation
description: Use when running BIDCell on subcellular spatial transcriptomics data (Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE, Stereo-seq) and file paths, cpus, model backbone, or single-cell reference settings must be specified in a .yaml config before segmentation.

name: yaml-sample-manifest-authoring
description: Use when running the circlehunter ATAC-Seq ecDNA pipeline on a new cohort (e.g., 14 normal-muscle negative controls or 547 GEO tumor samples) and a sample manifest must list each sample and its output path.

name: young-old-te-divergence-stratification
description: Use when TE loci carry divergence-from-consensus values in a RepeatMasker-derived BED annotation and cluster recovery of young vs old TEs must be assessed separately across genomes or TE-detection tools.

name: z-score-differential-expression-thresholding
description: Use when converting a processed cancer or drug-induced gene expression matrix into the gene-level (GSFM_Up, GSFM_Down) components of a GSFM active matrix, i.e. when per-sample ratios of significantly up- or down-regulated genes per functional module are needed.

name: z-score-normalization-across-methods
description: Use when decoupleR has been run with multiple methods simultaneously and their per-regulator activity estimates must be aggregated into one consensus score, or when benchmarking whether the consensus recovers perturbed regulators better than individual methods.

name: z-score-normalization-of-expression-matrices
description: Use when an expression matrix (e.g. TCGA-style microarray gene-by-sample data or single-cell RNA-seq counts after read-count filtration) shows non-normal or bimodal feature distributions and features must be put on a comparable, zero-centered scale.

name: z-score-significance-testing
description: Use when building a sample-specific (personalized) differential co-expression network: you have normal and tumor expression matrices and need to test, per patient, whether each gene-gene edge's Δr_ij is statistically significant (P < 0.05).

name: zdwi-utr-usage-statistical-testing
description: Use when scRNA-seq data has been quantified at 3'UTR isoform level (e.g. SingleCellExperiment from scUTRquant with the utrome_hg38_v1 target) and you need to test which genes show significant 3'UTR shortening/lengthening per condition or perturbation relative to controls.

name: zebrafish-embryo-cell-type-annotation-matching
description: Use when the goal is to infer cell-cell communication from scRNA-seq of a species outside human/mouse (e.g., 4 hpf zebrafish embryo) where no prior L-R database applies, given a gene-by-cell expression matrix and cell-type labels.

name: zebrafish-embryo-lineage-annotation
description: Use when integrating multiple zebrafish embryo scRNA-seq time-course datasets (e.g., Wagner et al. and Farrell et al.) against an end-point reference marker list to recover lineage emergence timings across developmental stages.

name: zenodo-dataset-retrieval
description: Use when a paper states its data are deposited on Zenodo (a doi:10.5281/zenodo.* DOI) and you must download the package, parse the deposited metadata/annotation tables, and verify reported dataset statistics.

name: zero-inflated-compound-poisson-modeling
description: Use when modeling scRNA-seq read counts (non-UMI, e.g. SMART-Seq2 or Fluidigm C1 plate-based protocols) with excess zeros, or when gene-specific Tweedie index parameter p must be estimated and compared across experimental platforms.

name: zero-inflated-count-model-fitting
description: Decision support for selecting between NB and ZINB noise models before denoising a scRNA-seq count matrix, when sparsity/dropout structure suggests possible zero-inflation.

name: zero-inflated-count-simulation
description: Use when you need synthetic zero-inflated, over-dispersed scRNA-seq counts with known true parameters (ln(mu), pi) to benchmark a model's robustness to misspecification of K, V, or dispersion.

name: zero-inflated-dimensionality-reduction
description: Use when scRNA-seq count data show dropout-driven zero inflation and PCA components appear driven by technical effects (sequencing depth, detection rate), and you need a low-dimensional representation reflecting biology.

name: zero-inflated-mixture-likelihood-fitting
description: Use when modeling continuous scRNA-seq expression of a target gene as a mixture over candidate TF logic combinations, where scRNA-seq dropouts require a point mass at zero and per-rule likelihoods (as in Loregic/LogicTRN) would be computationally prohibitive.

name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-count-simulation
description: Use when benchmarking DE or gene-set enrichment methods on scRNA-seq data and you need null count matrices with realistic zero inflation, or when calibration of null p-values across coverage rates must be tested.

name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-gene-sampling
description: Use when benchmarking perturbation-analysis methods like ICAT and you need synthetic control/perturbed AnnData pairs with known ground-truth perturbed cell states and tunable perturbation severity.

name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression
description: Use when comparing single-cell Hi-C normalized read counts between two conditions (rows = bin pairs, columns = cells) and you need statistically principled DCI calls that handle the excessive zeros typical of scHi-C data.

name: zero-inflated-negative-binomial-regression-implementation
description: Use when a task requires implementing or refitting a zero-inflated negative binomial regression to distinguish true fusion candidates from background technical chimeric-read noise in per-cell scRNA-seq candidate feature tables with expression and GC-content covariates.

name: zero-inflated-poisson-count-downsampling
description: Use when you need to synthetically downsample scRNA-seq count profiles to create a degraded input (with a known ground-truth full-depth counterpart) for benchmarking denoising methods such as scPRINT, MAGIC, or KNNsmoothing2.

name: zero-inflated-tweedie-model-fitting
description: Use when input is a raw scRNA-seq read-count matrix (e.g. Ygc) with excessive zero counts from a plate-based protocol, and a per-gene differential expression test between two groups is needed.

name: zero-inflation-diagnostics
description: Use when you have generated simulated single-cell count data (e.g., parameterized from Cuomo et al.

name: zero-inflation-dropout-layer-benchmarking
description: Use when you must quantify whether an explicit dropout-modeling component improves reproducibility of a VAE's low-dimensional embeddings, e.g. comparing NMI/ARI boxplots over ≥20 repeated runs on small scRNA-seq datasets like Biase, Goolam, Pollen, and Yan.

name: zero-inflation-dropout-tuning
description: Use when you need synthetic scRNA-seq data at multiple controlled zero-inflation levels (e.g., ~12-30% dropouts) to stress-test a method's robustness to dropout, as in scGAE's scenario4 benchmarks.

name: zero-preserving-low-rank-matrix-imputation
description: Use when a scRNA-seq normalized expression matrix shows extreme sparsity/dropout (zeros can exceed 90% with droplet techniques) and you need marker-gene recovery that preserves biological zeros at exactly zero.

name: zero-shot-cell-embedding-transfer
description: Use when a pretrained single-cell embedding model (e.g. scETM trained on MousePancreas.h5ad) must be applied to an aligned target dataset without retraining, and clustering quality of the transferred embeddings must be benchmarked.

name: zero-shot-foundation-model-evaluation
description: Use when comparing foundation models' zero-shot embedding quality on batch effect correction, e.g. when a task asks to reproduce the scIB aggregated (avgBIO) benchmark on pancreas/lung open-problems data without fine-tuning.

name: zero-shot-foundation-model-grn-inference
description: Use when inferring a gene network from scRNA-seq cells without training a model, or when benchmarking foundation-model-derived GRNs (scPRINT, scGPT, Geneformer) against GENIE3/DeepSEM on a ground truth like genome-wide perturb-seq K562.

name: zga-gene-set-enrichment-analysis
description: Use when a curated list of ligand-receptor pair genes (e.g. eLRs from early embryo scRNA-seq analysis) must be validated against reference gene sets (essential, housekeeping, ZGA) with over-representation tests.

name: zga-inhibition-perturbation-comparison
description: Use when testing whether cell-cell communication strength of candidate ligand-receptor pairs depends on a transcriptional process (e.g. ZGA) by comparing interaction scores between drug-perturbed and unperturbed embryo conditions.

name: zifa-latent-embedding-of-marker-genes
description: Use when you have an scRNA-seq dataset plus a marker gene set defining expected cell types, and you need a low-dimensional marker-gene embedding to seed pseudo-labels and pairwise constraints for constrained clustering.

name: zinb-autoencoder-denoising
description: Use when a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (e.g. gene x cell CSV/TSV or AnnData h5ad) is sparse with dropouts and you need a denoised/imputed matrix that preserves count structure for downstream visualization or clustering.

name: zinb-autoencoder-denoising
description: Use when pre-training a source classification model on labeled scRNA-seq count data and a denoising module that models dropout and count dispersion (ZINB NLL) is required before source-free adaptation.

name: zinb-autoencoder-dropout-estimation
description: Use when scRNA-seq expression data contain dropout events that need imputation prior to downstream clustering or gene-expression analysis, and a distribution-aware (ZINB prior) reconstruction is preferred over simple smoothing.

name: zinb-autoencoder-loss-composition
description: Use when clustering scRNA-seq count data with partial pairwise prior knowledge (must-link/cannot-link pairs) that should softly shape the latent embedding instead of hard-constrained clustering like COP K-means.

name: zinb-autoencoder-variant-configuration
description: Use when dissecting which scGCL component (ZINB encoder, graph convolution, AFGRL contrastive learning) drives clustering/imputation results, i.e. an internal component-ablation on Adam/Romanov h5 scRNA-seq data rather than a cross-method benchmark.

name: zinb-decoder-autoencoder-training
description: Use when benchmarking decoder choices for scRNA-seq clustering, e.g. reproducing the scMGCA ablation that swaps the multinomial decoder for a ZINB likelihood on count matrices.

name: zinb-differential-chromatin-interaction-testing
description: Use when you have a normalized scHi-C count matrix (rows = bin pairs, columns = samples/cells) plus a two-condition factor vector and need single-cell DCI calls that handle excessive zero counts.

name: zinb-gene-expression-likelihood-modeling
description: Use when building or reimplementing a VAE-based single-cell integration model (e.g., scDREAMER) where the decoder must reconstruct raw UMI counts with a ZINB likelihood and KL-regularized latent terms.

name: zinb-low-dimensional-signal-extraction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq counts need dimensionality reduction that handles zero inflation without prior normalization, or when unwanted variation (e.g., batch, detection rate) must be removed while preserving biological structure such as patient or cell-type effects.

name: zinb-model-estimation-single-cell
description: Use when you have a raw scRNA-seq count matrix (cells x genes) and need a low-dimensional embedding that models zero inflation and over-dispersion, e.g. for clustering, t-SNE input, or batch-effect removal.

name: zinb-model-fitting-count-data
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count data show zero inflation (dropouts) and over-dispersion, and you need model-based estimates of mean counts, zero probabilities, and dispersion, or a goodness-of-fit comparison of ZINB vs NB/hurdle count models.

name: zinb-model-fitting-scrnaseq
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq UMI count matrices need dimensionality reduction that models zero inflation and over-dispersion directly, replacing PCA or ZIFA without a preliminary normalization step.

name: zinb-noise-model-parameterization
description: Use when denoising or imputing sparse, overdispersed scRNA-seq count matrices where dropout zero counts must be modeled explicitly and classical imputation with defined missing values is unsuitable.

name: zinb-reconstruction-loss-implementation
description: Use when reconstructing, retraining, or verifying Pollock's VAE in PyTorch: the decoder must reproduce counts via a ZINB loss weighted by --zinb-scaler, alongside KL and classification terms.

name: zinb-reconstruction-loss-modeling
description: Use when training a deep autoencoder (e.g. scMDC-style multimodal denoising autoencoder) on raw single-cell count data whose mRNA/ADT/ATAC matrices are zero-inflated and over-dispersed, and reconstruction must model dropout rather than use a plain Gaussian/MSE loss.

name: zinb-scrna-seq-data-reconstruction
description: Use when you have bulk RNA-seq data for cohort samples plus a single-cell reference (e.g., sequenced representative AP6) and need inferred single-cell profiles (.h5ad) for target samples at true single-cell resolution.

name: zinb-to-nb-loss-replacement-in-autoencoder
description: Use when you need to run or reproduce a ZINB-vs-NB loss ablation in a scRNA-seq deep clustering model, i.e. when the analysis goal is to determine whether explicit zero-inflation modeling changes clustering performance (NMI/ARI).

name: zinb-wave-latent-factor-extraction
description: Use when raw scRNA-seq count matrices (e.g., GEO GSE95601 olfactory epithelium data) need a low-dimensional representation that handles zero inflation and over-dispersion without prior normalization, especially as input to clustering or Slingshot lineage inference.

name: zinb-wave-signal-extraction-on-raw-counts
description: Use when scRNA-seq raw count matrices need low-dimensional signal extraction or dimensionality reduction, and preliminary normalization (TC, TMM, FQ) is undesirable or unknown.

name: zinq-reconstruction-loss-optimization
description: Use when integrating scRNA-seq batches where some (10/20/50%) or all cell type labels are available and the latent embedding must be guided by a cell type classifier loss on top of an adversarial VAE ELBO.
